Conditions are given under which an optimal control always exists. It is shown that the optimal control is linear in the system state. A convergent algorithm is developed for computing the optimal feedback gains. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Kleinman D.L."]

Title: METHODOLOGIES OF PATTERN RECOGNITION. PROCEEDINGS OF THE INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE, JAN 24-26 1968, UNIV OF HAWAII, HONOLULU
Abstract: Topics discussed are-statistical analysis as a tool to make patterns emerge from data, learning and computation, biological and mechanical pattern recognition, designing pattern categorizers with extremal paradigm information, adaptive systems of pattern recognition, informational analysis and feature selection.
Name: ["WATANABE ED S"]

Title: State Space Models of Remote Manipulation Tasks
Abstract: A state variable formulation of the remote manipulation problem is presented, applicable to human-supervised or autonomous computer‚Äìmanipulators. A discrete state vector, containing position variables for the manipulator and relevant objects, spans a quantized state space comprising many static configurations of objects and hand. A manipulation task is a desired new state. State transitions are assigned costs and are accomplished by commands: Hand motions plus grasp, release, push, twist, etc. In control theory terms the problem is to find the cheapest control history (if any) from present to desired state. A method similar to dynamic programming is used to determine the optimal history. The system is capable of obstacle avoidance, grasp rendezvous, incorporation of new sensor data, remembering results of previous tasks, and so on. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Whitney D.E."]

Title: Two memory bounds for the recognition of primes by automata
Abstract: This paper establishes two bounds for the rate of growth of memory in automata which recognize the set of primes. ¬© 1969 Swets & Zeitlinger B.V.
Name: ["Hartmanis J.", "Shank H."]

Title: Parameter and State Estimation of a Nonstationary Process
Abstract: A class of nonstationary processes which changes dynamic characteristics in a discrete Markovian way and a method to identify a parameter and to estimate a state variable is proposed. This method is based on the mean-square error criterion using the conditional probability approach under the assumption that the conditional probability distributions of both the parameter and the state variable are Gaussian. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Furuta K.", "Paquet J.-G."]

Title: Automaton model of digital transmission line and its application to logical code conversion
Abstract: A digital transmission line with intersymbol interference extending over multiple time slots can be expressed equivalently by a primary- information lossless automaton so far as the relationship of input- output conversion is concerned. This automation model is applied to the area of code logical conversion, and the precoder logical construction in the partial response communication system of E. R. Kretzmer is explained. A description of how to determine the precoder state- transition diagram for given line impulse response, line code and source code is given.
Name: ["KANAYA F"]

Title: MODELS OF PURE TIME-SHARING DISCIPLINES FOR RESOURCE ALLOCATION
Abstract: Pure time sharing (PTS) disciplines are those which involve in some way the simultaneous sharing of a processor or other service facility by more than one job at a time. By studying the behavior of mathematical models, it is shown how these disciplines can be applied to static processor scheduling problems in which total schedule time is to be minimized. Application of these disciplines to queueing systems is also examined, yielding characterization which classify the performance measures optimized. The PTS disciplines discussed include one which bases scheduling decisions on the elapsed times of jobs and one which decisions one the expected remaining processing times of jobs.
Name: ["COFFMAN JR EG", "MUNTZ RR"]

Title: Synthesis of Time-Optimal Control by Time Interval Adjustment
Abstract: An iterative procedure for time-optimal control of linear plants with constrained control amplitudes is presented. It is assumed that the nth-order state-equation coefficient matrix has real eigenvalues, so that the time-optimal control is of the known bang-bang form with n switchings. The first step in the procedure is to arbitrarily choose n switching times (including the final time), and to calculate a precise constant control function which although not necessarily satisfying the amplitude constraints does bring the plant to the desired terminal state. In the following steps the switching times are systematically adjusted until the control function closely approximates the bang-bang form. The procedure is simple to implement, and experiments have shown fast convergence. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Yastreboff M."]

Title: On the Functional Identification of Nonlinear Systems from Input-Output Data Records
Abstract: The problem of determining the functional model of a time-invariant nonlinear analytic system is considered. A new approach to the identification, based on a new functional series expansion relating the input and the output function of an analytic system, is presented. The results obtained are compared with other methods. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Marchesini G.", "Picci G."]

Title: ALGEBRA OF DERIVATIONS AND A SEMITHUE PARSER
Abstract: While derivations are used to formally generate sentences from the productions of a grammar, the structure, or structural descriptions, which the grammar imposes on a sentence is the entity of general interest. In particular there is an equivalence relation on derivations such that the equivalence classes are a representation of sentence structure for semithue languages. A slightly different equivalence relation provides sentence structure for context sensitive grammars. There is a parse tence structure for context sensitive grammars. There is a parser for context free and semithue languages which is closely allied to the equivalence class representation of sentence structure. The parser is exemplified, described, and shown to find each structure assigned t the input sentence exactly once.
Name: ["BENSON DB"]

Title: NON-PARAMETRIC RECURSIVE IDENTIFICATION ALGORITHM FOR FINITE- MEMORY LINEAR SYSTEMS
Abstract: The problem of identifying a linear, finite-memory, discrete- time system with noisy input and output is considered. A recursive algorithm is proposed which gives asymptotically unbiased estimates of the system parameters. The procedure does not require any specific knowledge of the noise statistics, in contrast to other proposed algorithms which generally need some knowledge of the statistics in order to obtain unbiased parameter estimates.
Name: ["BAR-SHALOM Y", "SCHWARTZ SC"]

Title: RECOGNITION AND REPRESENTATION OF PARALLEL PROCESSABLE STREAMS IN COMPUTER PROGRAMS-II
Abstract: The techniques of recognizing and representing parallel processable tasks within a single job stream (program) are studied. The reasons for and problems associated with parallel processing are given. The distinctions between global and local parallelism, and between explicit and implicit parallelism, are explained. Desirable attributes for specifying explicit parallelism are considered and some technological problems that accrue from parallelism are discussed. The factors involved in compiling a conventionally written program for multiprocessing are examined.
Name: ["RAMAMOORTHY CV", "GONZALEZ MJ"]

Title: Comments on ‚ÄúApplication of Results from the Absolute Stability Problem to the Computation of Finite Stability Domains‚Äù
Abstract: An error is corrected, and new material is added on maximizing the extent of the estimate of the stability region. In an example it is shown that the maximum-area estimate coincides with the estimate constructed by Kalman's method. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Weissenberger S."]

Title: SPTIAL FILTERING INTHE WAVE-VECTOR DOMAIN
Abstract: Spatial data can be represented in the two-dimensional frequency domain. This simplifies the achievement of any desired transfer response in linear digital filter. Similar results are obtained approximately by convolution in space with a weighted coefficient set. The equivalence of wave-vector filtering and a special form of convolution filtering is demonstrated. The regional trend is rmoved from data prior to wave-vector filtering which gives one solution to problems arising at the edge of the data. A computationally convenient form of the two-dimensional fast Fourier transform is given for certain arrays.
Name: ["BLACK DI", "SCLLAR I"]

Title: AUTOMATION TECHNIQUES FOR LARGE SCALE INTEGRATION SYSTEM DESIGN
Abstract: Highly-automated computer techniques are described which may be applied to selected logical graphs to generate the Boolean functions representing the logical graphs. These functions are cataloged into discrete classes. A set of logic functions are then selected from the complete list of discrete classes. Each logical function can cover one or more of the classes in the list. These functions can be automatically imposed on the original logic graph for evaluation. The automated system is set up to allow rapid evaluation of parameter changes such as function size, and number of function types. The evaluation of functions leads to a set that may be used as the building blocks for implementation of a machine. Examples are given of the use of these techniques.
Name: ["MCMAHON MT", "WAXMAN R", "BORECKI D", "PREUSS R"]

Title: Coordinability of Dynamic Systems
Abstract: Coordination is defined as the decision problem of a control unit embedded in a hierarchical multilevel system. The strategy for coordination is derived by using two principles termed the interaction balance and the interaction prediction principle, respectively. A family of interacting subsystems is then considered as coordinable via a coordination principle and relative to an objective valid for the overall system if the lower level control problems can be influenced so that the overall task is achieved. Necessary and sufficient conditions for the coordinability of a class of dynamic systems are derived using a variational approach. The results are applied to systems described by differential equations. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Takahara Y.", "Mesarovic M.D."]

Title: An Algorithm for Nonlinear System Parameter Identification
Abstract: An algorithm for system parameter identification will be presented in this paper. The method is applicable to linear and nonlinear systems with known structures. It is applied in this paper to systems in which both system and measurement noises can be neglected. The algorithm requires less time per iteration and less computer storage than the quasilinearization method. A shaft position control system with multiple nonlinearities will be used to illustrate the method. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Medler C.L.", "Hsu C.-C."]

Title: CHARACTERIZATION OF TWO-WAY DETERMINISTIC CLASSES OF LANGUAGES
Abstract: It is shown that a class of languages id defined by a class of two- way deterministic balloon automata (2DBA) if and only if that class is closed under marked union, marked Kleene closure and the inverse mappings performed by GSM's that move two ways on the input. Hence, the context sensitive languages and various time and tape complexity classes are equivalent to classes of 2DBA.
Name: ["AHO AV", "ULLMAN JD"]

Title: A case study in programming for parallel-processors
Abstract: An affirmative partial answer is provided to the question of whether it is possible to program parallel-processor computing systems to efficiently decrease execution time for useful problems. Parallel-processor systems are multiprocessor systems in which several of the processors can simultaneously execute separate tasks of a single job, thus cooperating to decrease the solution time of a computational problem. The processors have independent instruction counters, meaning that each processor executes its own task program relatively independently of the other processors. Communication between cooperating processors is by means of data in storage shared by all processors. A program for the determination of the distribution of current in an electrical network was written for a parallel-processor computing system, and execution of this program was simulated. The data gathered from simulation runs demonstrate the efficient solution of this problem, typical of a large class of important problems. It is shown that, with proper programming, solution time when NP processors are applied approaches 1/NP times the solution time for a single processor, while improper programming can actually lead to an increase of solution time with the number of processors. Storage interference and other measures of performance are discussed. Stability of the method of solution was also investigated. ¬© 1969 ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Rosenfeld J.L."]

Title: LEARNING OF PARAMETERS FOR GENERATING COMPOUND CHARACTERIZERS FOR PATTERN RECOGNITION
Abstract: NO-ABSTRACT
Name: ["UHR L", "JORDAN S"]

Title: Reading Aids for the Blind: A Special Case of Machine-to-Man Communication
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: The development of a reading machine for the blind offers insight into current problems of computer-to-man communications and poses a technical and humanitarian challenge. Approaches to the problem include compiled speech, reformed speech, and synthesis by rule. Of these methods, synthesis by rule may offer the best long-term tradeoff between quality of the speech and cost and complexity of its production. Implementation of a high-performance reading machine will involve a central service facility that can generate tape recordings or provide voice responses to remote print scanners. Technical problems, especially in providing remote on-line service, seem formidable, but the organizational problems of matching central facilities to the blind user's needs may prove to be even more so. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Cooper F.S.", "Gaitenby J.H.", "Mattingly I.G.", "Umeda N."]
Affiliations: ['University of Connecticut', 'Haskins Laboratories New York', ' Ministry of International Trade and Industry']

Title: Augmented stepwise discriminant analysis applied to two classification problems in the biomedical field
Abstract: Stepwise discriminant analysis is applied to the machine karyotyping of chromosomes using arm-length measurements and functions of these as the basis for classification, and machine differential diagnosis of gynecological diseases based on a set of twenty-six signs and symptoms. When the karyo-typing procedure is augmented by a reordering scheme which takes advantage of the required number of objects per class, a reproduction of human performance with approximately 6% error is achieved. For the gynecological diseases, under certain circumstances, an error rate of 15% is achieved. This is an error rate of least equivalent and probably lower than that realized by humans. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Enslein K.", "Neurath P.W."]

Title: Construction of nonlinear discriminant functions of many- valued patterns
Abstract: The system Phi of functions is formulated by extending the finite system of Walsh functions to the case of many- valued variables, and it is shown that an arbitrary discriminant function of many- valued patterns can be expressed by a linear combination of some elements of the system Phi. A discussion of obtaining the optical set of weight coefficients to construct an optimal discriminant function is given. An algorithm to choose functions from the system Phi to construct an optimal discriminant function for a given set of patterns is formulated.
Name: ["UESAKA Y"]

Title: COMPUTER PROCESSING OF BINARY MAPS OF SEM IMAGES
Abstract: The computer processing system for handling SEM images has been enlarged, improved, and extended. Changes include the addition of a new digital recording system and software modifications for the rapid processing of images into computer readable data from tape. Methods of smoothing to account for electronic noise, specific problems of light and dark fields, and sectoring either up or down on intensity distribution have been considered in the present version of the program. The binary maps of the SEM images produced by the computer allow both the shapes and areas of simple andnd complex particles to be reconstructed. The specific problem of contiguous particles and reentrant particles constitutes the main improvement in the technique.
Name: ["MCMILLAN RE", "JOHNSON JR GG", "WHITE EW"]

Title: Formulation of learning automata and automata games
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate various properties of some learning automata operating in random environments. Based on the strategies of "many-armed bandit problems," two sequential learning models, A<sub>r,k</sub> and B<sub>r,k,b</sub>, having deterministic and stochastic transition rules, respectively, are formulated. Automata using these strategies have shown the desired learning behavior, which is similar to the performance of linear-strategy automata and certain type of stochastic automata. Furthermore, the learning behavior of fuzzy automata in random environments is also considered. Comparison among various models has been made. Computer-simulated examples for the application of proposed models include games against nature and games between automata. The results from simulation have been considered quite satisfactory.‚Ä°Presently with IBM, Kingston, New York. ¬© 1969 American Elsevier Publishing Company, Inc.
Name: ["Fu K.S.", "Li T.J."]

Title: TWO CHARACTERIZATIONS OF THE CONTEXT-SENSITIVE LANGUAGES
Abstract: An n-dimensional bug- automaton is generalization of a finite state acceptor to n-dimensions. With each bug B, one associates the language L(B) which is the set of top rows of the n-dimensional rectangular arrays accepted by B. One-dimensional bugs define trivially the regular sets. Two-dimensional bugs define precisely the context-sensitive languages, while bugs of dimension 3 or greater define all the recursively enumerable sets. Author considers finite state acceptors with n two-way nonwriting input tapes. For each such machine M, let domain (M) be the set of all strings which arethe first component of some n-tuple of tapes accepted by M. For any n greater than or equal to 1, the domains of n-tape two- way finite state acceptors are precisely the same as the languages definable by n-dimensional bugs, so as a corollary, the domains of two-tape two- way finite state acceptors are precisely the context-sensitive languages.
Name: ["FISCHER MJ"]

Title: RECENT RESEARCH IN THEORY OF BOOLEAN MATRICES
Source: Economic Computation & Economic Cybernetics Studies & Research
Abstract: Development of algorithm for computation of matrix Ap-**1 equals Ap equals . . . , of single line or of submatrix of matrix Ap-**1, where A is Boolean matrix with 1 on main diagonal and method is extended to case that Boolean matrix A has element on diagonal which is not equal to unity, or matrix A represents distances or direct capacities between nodes of transport network.
Name: ["TOMESCU I"]

Title: Optimal estimation for nonlinear systems
Source: AIAA Guidance, Control, and Flight Mechanics Conference, 1969
Abstract: For some nonlinear problems, such as orbital estimation using optical measurements, a linear-ized Kalman filter is unstable unless empirical methods of augmenting stability a r e used. An alternate approach is to recognize that nonlinear systems cause the estimation error to become non gaussian, so that more general estimation methods are required. The estimation error probability density can be approximately expressed as a gaussian density multiplied by a finite expansion of Hermite polynomials. Using this formalism and the Bayes approach, a non- ‚Äò linear filter is derived which estimates the system mean, covarian‚Äôce. and third central moments. This filter consists of coupled nonlinear differential equations to be integrated between measurements, and updating equations involving tensor products to be solved at the measurement times. bital navigation problem, and attained close to theoretically optimal accuracy. ¬© 1969, American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics Inc, AIAA. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Culver C.O."]

Title: DETERMINISTIC CONTEXT-SENSITIVE LANGUAGES
Abstract: Knuth has defined the class of LR(k) grammars, and shown that they generate exactly the class of languages recognized by deterministic pushdown automata. This paper extends his methods to context- sensitive grammars (CSGs). Authors will define a class of grammars- called CS(k) grammars-that are equivalent to the deterministic linear bounded automata (DLBAs) and present some of their properties.
Name: ["WALTERS DA"]

Title: On the Optimal Control of Discrete-Time Linear Systems with Random Parameters
Abstract: This work is concerned with the optimal control of a discrete-time linear system with random parameters. It is assumed that the parameters of the system vary randomly during the process, namely, the parameters constitute sequences of random variables. These random variables are not necessarily independent. An important particular case occurs where there are unknown constant parameters in the system. The measurements of the state of the system contain additive noise. A quadratic function of the state and controller, with appropriate weighting, servesas the criterion function. The solutions for the open-loop controller and the open-loop feedback controller are presented. The method of solution is based on the dynamic programming approach which leads to functional recurrence equations. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Bar-Shalom Y.", "Sivan R."]
Affiliations: ['Technfon‚ÄîIsrael Institute of Technology', ' Technion-Israel Institute of Technology']

Title: FAIL-OPERATIONAL LANDING COMMANDS USING KALMAN FILTERING
Abstract: The development of a multi-sensor data processing technique using the real time error analysis inherent in the Kalman filter to provide fail-operational landing guidance commands, is reported. The models assembled to establish feasibility of the concept are described, together with a summary of results obtained to date. Follow-on effort is currently being directed toward simulation of an integrated three-dimensional model both on digital computer and in real-time hybrid simulation incorporating Boeing 747 dynamics and pilot's situation monitor.
Name: ["HAFNER DJ", "BROWN JL", "DOFFING CG"]

Title: MODEL OF VISUAL ORGANIZATION FOR GAME OF GO
Abstract: Computer program which plays GO uses an information processing model to produce perceptual features which are seen by human GO players, and is capable of several responses to the recognition of significant configurations of these perceptual features. Study is designed to provide new insight into human perceptual and problem solving abilities as well as foster the development of new techniques for artificial intelligence.
Name: ["ZOBRIST AL"]

Title: GAIN ADAPTATION IN AN INPUT-PERTURBATION, EXTREMUM- SEEKING SYSTEM
Abstract: The gradient of a unimodal objective function, estimated by sinusoidal perturbation, is used to move the inp%ut toward a value which optimizes the objective function. The gain of the extremum- seeking loop, which depends upon the shape of the objective function, has been found to vary considerably in certain applications. A plant-adaptive loop is proposed to adjust the gain by compensating for shape variation. This additional loop makes use of information extracted by the same perturbation. System performance is demonstrated by hybrid-computer simulation and by implementation in a laboratory catalytic reactors.
Name: ["WHITE JW", "FOLEY GJ", "ALTPETER RJ"]

Title: PATTERN CLASSIFICATION BY THE TIME PATTERN CLASSIFICATION BY THE TIME-VARYING THRESHOLD METHOD
Abstract: NO-ABSTRACT
Name: ["AIDA S", "KINOSHITA G"]

Title: TWO-WAY SEQUENTIAL TRANSDUCERS AND STACK AUTOMATA
Abstract: In this paper a device called a 2-way sequential transducer is defined. Such a device is a natural generalization of the wellknown 1-way sequential transducer, though its behavior is much more complex. Many of the properties of this transducer are derived, and it is shown, for example, that such a transducer maps regular sets and context free languages into the context sensitive languages. The intimate relationship between the class of 1-way stack automata and the 2-way sequential transducer isshown by presenting a new grammar which generates exactly the 1-way stack languages in a perfectly natural way, and it is indicated how several of the properties of 1-way stack languages are obtained from its grammars.
Name: ["EHRICH R", "YAU SS"]

Title: ITERATIVE LEAST-SQUARES ALGORITHMS FOR SIGNAL EXTRACTION
Abstract: Presentation of recursive algorithms for calculating the optimum least-squares weight vector directly from the measured data. Two algorithms are presented. Comparison of algorithms with that of B. Widrow's and L. J. Griffiths'.
Name: ["MANTEY PE", "GRIFFITHS LJ"]

Title: FORMAL MODELS FOR SOME FEATURES OF PROGRAMMING LANGUAGES
Abstract: Formal linguistic objects corresponding to programs are defined via sets of functional equations; two interpretations of such an object are given, one in classical mathematics, and one in terms of an abstract machine that executes the program. Within this framework author examines flow charts, recursion, parameterization, and declaration.
Name: ["ZEIGER HP"]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF STOCHASTIC PARAMETERS BY EXACT NONLINEAR FILTERING OF VECTOR NOISY MEASUREMENTS
Abstract: Extension of author's previous work (see Engineering Index 1968 p 192) to vector case; case where there is no disturbing noise acting is considered; continuous vector measurements z(t) are made of state over interval of time !O,T! in additive gaussian white noise environment; result is given in terms of exact conditional probability density, nonlinear functional of observation vector z(t) taken over interval of time !O,T! and is of such form that it can be programmed on computer.
Name: ["KROY WH", "JR"]

Title: QUEUEING MODEL FOR MESSAGE-SWITCHING NETWORKS WITH CONSTANT- LENGTH MESSAGES
Abstract: Expressions are given for the first and second moments of the queue- length distribution of the single-server queue with constant service time and general arrival distribution. General relationship between moments of queue-length and message- delay distributions holds in the particular case of a first-come- first- served queue discipline. The results for a single queue enable mean message delay to be estimated for a network of queues, with both deterministic and adaptive routing doctrines. Criteria for the rational choice of a deterministic doctrine for a given network and traffic matrix follow directly.
Name: ["SILK DJ"]

Title: HIERARCHICAL GRAPH MODEL OF SEMANTICS OF PROGRAMS
Abstract: Model is based on the use of hierarchies of directed graphs to represent both programs and data. Definition of concepts of '%'level'%' and '%'path'%' which serve as important structural concepts in the application of H-graphs to the description of programming languages. Basic sematic model is introduced by structuring further the '%'atomic units'%' which lie at the lowest level of the hierarchy. Examples illustrate informally how a number of semantic features of actual programming languages may be represented.
Name: ["PRATT TW"]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF DYNAMIC CHARACTERISTICS OF MAN AS OPERATOR IN MANUALLY CONTROLLED SYSTEMS, | [IDENTYFIKACJA DYNAMICZNYCH WLASNOSCI CZLOWIEKA JAKO OPERATORA W UKLADACH STEROWANIA RECZNEGO]
Abstract: Commonly used mathematical models are discussed; linear and nonlinear, stationary and nonstationary models are taken into consideration; quasi-linear models, statistical identification methods due to correlation analysis; frequency responses of human's operator linear model are computed for some typical plants and different bandwidths of random input.
Name: ["FIRLA AP", "MORAWSKI J"]

Title: Automated Chemistry Laboratory: Application of a Novel Time-Shared Computer System
Abstract: A promising strategy for providing a hospital information system is the gradual development and subsequent integration of well-defined information processing modules. A computer system which is suitable and economical to serve one or more of these modules has been developed. Its unique feature is that it uses an interpretive language for all the application programs both in the developmental and service modes of operation. The interpretive language, which has been designed specifically for data management applications, facilitates the creation and debugging of programs; in addition, it allows the time-sharing of a relatively small computer with a negligible overhead for switching control from one program to the next. The multiterminal, real-time remote-access computer system has been in service operation at the Clinical Chemistry Laboratory of the Massachusetts General Hospital since the early Fall of 1968. Presently, the system accepts typed-in requisition information, creates patient files, and generates schedules for centrifuging blood samples and for the performing of all tests; the system also accepts test results and provides reports on individual patients. In the near future all test results will be manually entered into the machine, which will then generate cumulative test reports each day. The on-line connection of automated laboratory equipment (Auto Analyzers) will soon follow. Analysis of the system performance shows that the use of an interpretive language is suitable for this application, and it also indicates that the system has sufficient capacity for serving additional information processing needs, Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Katona P.G.", "Pappalardo A.N.", "Marble C.W.", "Barnett G.O.", "Pashby M.M."]
Affiliations: [' M.I.T.', 'Case Western Reserve University', ' Harvard Medical School']

Title: A three state Markov model for discrimination learning
Abstract: Previous treatments of discrimination learning have been ineffective in predicting both marginal responding and reinforcement effects in two-stimulus probability learning. A three state Markov model is proposed which is designed to account for these results. The basic assumption of the theory is that the subject is reinforced for behaving appropriately to a distinctive cue rather than for making a specific motor response. Empirical results that include variations of œÄ, Œ≤, and cue similarity are accounted for by the model. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Massaro D.W."]

Title: COMPACTION OF NAMES BY X-GRAMS
Abstract: Method of compacting proper given names for computer storage uses x- rams which are combinations of from one to eight letters; rather than spelling names letter by letter, they are '%'spelled'%' with x- grams; algorithm has been implemented in computer program and used to obtain sets of x-grams for two large (42,165 and 43,875) given name samples; using x-grams obtained, it was possible to represent names from one sample in 1. 78 bits/original character and in 2. 1 bits /original character in second sample.
Name: ["WALKER VR"]

Title: RECOGNIZING CONVEX BLOBS
Abstract: Recognizing two dimensional binary objects.
Name: ["SKLANSKY J"]

Title: ADAPTIVE PATTERN RECOGNITION
Abstract: NO-ABSTRACT
Name: ["HAUFF P", "NEIDHART E"]

Title: ALGORITHMS OF ONE-DIMENSIONAL ADAPTIVE EXTREMUM CONTROLLER
Abstract: General algorithms are given a double-perception scheme with sensitivity model is proposed to solve the problem of adaptive control of dynamic processes with extremum static characteristics. Possible simplfications are given along with possibilities of speeding up identification.
Name: ["KOCHISH YA"]

Title: MACHINE PERCEPTION AND DESCRIPTION OF PICTORIAL DATA
Abstract: NO-ABSTRACT
Name: ["FISCHLER MA"]

Title: The inverse problem of stationary covariance generation
Abstract: The paper considers the problem of passing from a stationary covariance, or spectral matrix, associated with the output of a constant linear finite-dimensional system excited by white noise to the set of all possible systems of minimum possible dimension which will generate this covariance. The problem, originally posed by R. E. Kalman in 1965, is solved by identifying each possible system with the solution of a quadratic matrix inequality; an algorithm for the solution of the inequality is also presented. ¬© 1969 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Anderson B.D.O."]
Keywords: ["covariance generation", "linear system", "minimal realization", "network theory", "quadratic matrix inequalities"]

Title: A Method for Solving Arbitrary-Wall Mazes by Computer
Abstract: A method for solving mazes with extended open areas and arbitrarily placed walls is described. This method reduces large open areas containing many possible paths to a small set of shortest paths. It is then possible to use Moore's algorithm of which the paper includes a summary. A computer simulation of a vehicle exploring an unknown maze is discussed. Crude navigation and measurement are sufficient for maze solving with the techniques described. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Sutherland I.E."]

Title: TECHNIQUE OF QUASI-OPTIMAL CONTROL OF NONLINEAR STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS
Abstract: This paper considers the quasi-optimal control of a nonlinear stochastic system whose nonlinearity is characterized by a small parameter. A technique of combining the methods of equivalent linearization and perturbation to obtain a quasi-optimal feedback law is presented, thereby a two-point boundary value problem is side-stepped in obtaining solutions for the problem. A quadratic cost function is used.
Name: ["LOH NK", "ARIARATNAM ST"]

Title: FUNDAMENTAL CONSIDERATIONS ON STATISTICAL CLASSIFIER
Abstract: Fundamental characteristics of statistical classifier are studied from point of system organization and recognition ability; system performance is evaluated by means of concept information processing capacity and a% information processing capacity.
Name: ["NOGUCHI S", "SATO M", "OIZUMI J"]

Title: FUNDAMENTAL CHARACTERISTICS OF SPATIAL NETWORKS
Abstract: Consideration of stability of backward coupled networks; analysis obtained here gives interesting results for input and output relation such as Mach and Broca-Sulzer phenomena; authors obtain fundamental data which is necessary to utilize spatial networks in field of pattern recognition.
Name: ["TAKEDA H", "NOGUCHI S", "OIZUMI J"]

Title: Optimal Estimation in the Presence of Unknown Parameters
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics
Abstract: An adaptive approach is presented for optimal estimation of a sampled stochastic process with finite-state unknown parameters. It is shown that, for processes with an implicit generalized Markov property, the optimal (conditional mean) state estimates can be formed from 1) a set of optimal estimates based on known parameters, and 2) a set of ‚Äúlearning‚Äù statistics which are recursively updated. The formulation thus provides a separation technique which simplifies the optimal solution of this class of nonlinear estimation problems. Examples of the separation technique are given for prediction of a non-Gaussian Markov process with unknown parameters and for filtering the state of a Gauss-Markov process with unknown parameters. General results are given on the convergence of optimal estimation systems operating in the presence of unknown parameters. Conditions are given under which a Bayes optimal (conditional mean) adaptive estimation system will converge in performance to an optimal system which is ‚Äútold‚Äù the value of unknown parameters. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Hilborn C.G., Jr.", "Lainiotis D.G."]

Title: DESIGN OF MODEL FOLLOWING SYSTEMS USING THE COMPANION TRANSFORMATION
Abstract: A new approach to the model following problem for single-input, linear, time-invariant systems is presented. The advantages of this technique over those requiring minimization of an integral square error between the system and model outputs are that no system simulations are r%equired, no averaging time for the integration is required; the results is independent of the system input as a time function, and the system and model need not be repeatedly excited in real time optimization (as in some model reference adaptive schemes).
Name: ["WILKIE DF", "PERKINS WR"]

Title: STABILITY OF A CLASS OF PULSE-FREQUENCY MODULATED CONTROL SYSTEMS
Abstract: The problem of asymptotic stability of a class of pulse-frequency modulated (PFM) control systems is considered. The PFM system is first transformed into a more suitable form. Then a Popov related stability criterion is derived, which gives sufficient conditions for the asymptotic stability of the transformed PFM systems. Two examples of the application of this stability criterion are presented. The second example is shown to be a counter-example to Aizerman's conjecture for sampled-data systems.
Name: ["SHORTLE JR GE", "ALEXANDRO JR FJ"]

Title: Suboptimal control of plants with uncertain parameters
Abstract: A two-level technique for optimal system design is proposed, in which trajectory sensitivity cost is included with state and control variable terms. The resulting optimal system would be less sensitive to plant-parameter variations than one designed without such a trajectory-sensitivity cost term. ¬© 1969, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Rao S.G.", "Soudack A.C."]
Affiliations: [' University of British Columbia', 'Department of Electrical Engineering Technion']

Title: PERFORMANCE OF KILGOUR'S TRUNCATION ALGORITHM WHEN APPLIED TO BIBLIOGRAPHIC RETRIEVAL FROM LIBRARY CATALOG
Abstract: Algorithm for machine retrieval from large bibliographic files was tested for performance in matching user-supplied, unedited search clues to bibliographic data contained in library catalog; in testing, by manual simulation, on data derived from 126 case studies of actual searches of catalog at Yale Univ Library, algorithm achieved 70% recall when compared to results of conventional manual searching; precision was not determined.
Name: ["STANGL P", "TAYLOR BALIPETZKF"]

Title: TRANQUIL. LANGUAGE FOR ARRAY PROCESSING COMPUTER
Abstract: TRANQUIL is the algorithmic language which will be used to write programs for ILLIAC IV, a parallel computer which is array of 256 coupled processing elements (PE's) arranged in four quadrants in each of which the 64 PE's are driven by instructions emanating %from a single control unit. Language enables user to express array type computation processes in terms of arrays and parallel operations. Major features of language, its compiler and its implementation.
Name: ["ABEL NE", "BUDNIK PP", "KUCK DJ", "MURAOKA Y", "NORTHCOTE RS", "WILHELMSON RB"]

Title: AUTOMATIC MODEL FOR PURCHASE DECISIONS
Abstract: Decision-making model to control the entire expenditure by Rolls-Royce Aero Engine Div with outside suppliers. Package for determining the size of orders to be placed on suppliers, the length of time into the future these orders should stretch, the best price break information to ask for, and the extent to which changes in demand within Rolls-Royce should be suppressed to cushion the suppliers from unnecessary fluctuations. A conservative estimate of savings which result from implementing a model of this nature is that purchase bill is reduced by at least 5% and the inventory by somewhere in the region of 15%.
Name: ["CANTELLOW DG", "BURTON SL", "LAING RM"]

Title: The Linear Estimation of Completely Unknown Signals
Abstract: The estimation of completely unknown signals is studied. Signals which have no probabilistic structure propagate through a linear system. The output of the linear system is observed in the presence of white noise. A sampled-data linear filter is found which estimates the signals at discrete points in time. The estimate is optimum in the sense that it is unbiased and the variance of the estimate is minimized (Fisher estimate). Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Glover J.D."]

Title: Optimal Adaptive Filter Realizations for Sample Stochastic Processes with an Unknown Parameter
Abstract: Techniques are given for realizing optimal learning systems for filtering a sampled stochastic process in the presence of an unknown constant or time-varying parameter. It is shown how the nonlinear Bayes optimal (quadratic sense) adaptive filters can be directly realized for continuous parameter spaces by real-time analog systems. Examples are given for both constant and time-varying unknown parameters. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Hilborn C.G., Jr.", "Lainiotis D.G."]

Title: PROPOSAL FOR SERIAL, ARCHETYPE-DIRECTED PATTERN RECOGNITION
Abstract: A pattern recognition system is proposed which appears suitable for practical applications such as optical character recognition and machine perception by robots. The principal advantages of the system are that it offers great economy in feature extraction rocess and that it provides efficient recognition of patterns in the presence of background noise, such as other patterns or irrelevant objects. For simplicity, the system is described in terms of the recognition of two-dimensional patterns. Extension to three- dimensional objects is considered. The basic recognition procedure is to create one stored archetype for each sandard pattern and to recognize a given pattern by finding, in the set of stored archetypes, one which matches the pattern.
Name: ["NOTON D"]

Title: The Design of Optimal Convolutional Filters Via Linear Programming
Abstract: Computational algorithms are given for the design of optimal, finite-length, convolutional filters with finite-length input sequences. Design techniques are developed for minimum-weighted-mean-square-error filters (MWMSE), for minimum-weighted-absolute-error filters (MWAE), and for filters which minimize the maximum output error (minimax). It is shown that the coefficients of the MWAE and minimax filters can be obtained by using standard linear programming methods. Next, the problem of developing a filter whose function is to ‚Äúsharpen‚Äù a particular input waveform is considered. The filter input sequence is assumed to be derived from a Ricker wavelet of the velocity type and the desired output is the Dirac delta function. Convolutional filters are developed for this problem using each of the three performance criteria described above. The output sequences of each of the three optimal filters are discussed. It is shown that the minimax filter gives significantly better discrimination than can be obtained from either the MWAE or MWMSE filters. Copyright 1969 by the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Cavin R.K., III", "Ray C.H.", "Thomas Rhyne V."]

Title: Linear sequential estimation with unestimated parameters
Abstract: The linear sequential equations for estimating the state of a system given noisy measurements are derived for the case in which the system is not randomly perturbed, though some parameters of the system are uncertain. The uncertain parameters are not explicitly estimated, but the state estimate is optimal taking into account the parameter uncertainty. The equations are compared with those obtained for the case in which the uncertain parameters are estimated. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Schwartz L."]

Title: CONSIDERATION ON THE SYSTEM PERFORMANCE OF A TWO-STAGE SEQUENTIAL PROCESSING SYSTEM
Abstract: A processing system is considered in which two processing units are connected in tandem. Analysis of the states in the system is carried out by means of queueing theory, and the maximum processing and utilization rates are derived from the state transitions. In the model, storage or waiting rooms are provided between the two processing units and assumptions are made that the computing-time distribution of one unit is arbitrary, the computing time of the other unit is the exponential type, and to obtain the maximum processing rate, the system is saturated with jobs.
Name: ["AONO S", "NOGUCHI S", "OIZUMI J"]

Title: On a convex function useful in determination of linear discriminant functions
Abstract: The problem of determining a linear discriminant function to minimize probability of error in distinguishing between two measurement classes may, as is well known, often be approximated by a problem of minimizing some convex function. Many particular convex functions have been proposed for this purpose. While the relations between the real problem and the approximation are of critical importance, such relations are frequently unclear or even unsatisfactory. Here we examine a particular choice and show that it has a collection of desirable attributes, relating to the real problem, which are not known to be possessed by any other choice. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Butz A.R."]

Title: Decomposition of a matrix as the sum of direct products. Applications to neural networks
Abstract: The rank of a matrix can be expressed as the least number of sums of direct products into which the matrix can be decomposed. Some applications to nets of linear threshold elements are given. ¬© 1970 IAC.
Name: ["de Luca A.", "Ricciardi L.M."]

Title: Correlation Characteristics and Dimensionality of Speech Spectra
Source: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Abstract: Statistical properties of spectral samples derived from the continuous speech of six talkers and summarized by means of covariance matrix eigenvectors are used to study the dimensionality of the data space. The importance of eliminating low level samples by means of a fixed threshold is emphasized, and criteria for selecting such a threshold are presented. Measurements of spectral correlations stabilize after about 30 sec of speech, suggesting that short term examination of a talker's output may prove sufficient to calculate parameters useful in recognition schemes. Some features of the correlation matrix, which are readily displayed via isocorrelation contours, appear to be related to talker characteristics, while others are talker independent. The results suggest that the separation of speech data into gross classes prior to the application of statistical procedures will enhance the performance of processing schemes. ¬© 1969, Acoustical Society of America. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hughes G.W.", "House A.S."]

Title: Forced model equation for turbulence
Abstract: An artificial random force is introduced into Burgers' model equation for turbulence. This forced model equation is solved numerically as an initial-value problem. Both the driving force and initial velocity field are assumed Gaussian and are generated by a white noise process. Many statistical properties of this model for turbulence are studied. By adjusting the external force, the turbulence can reach an equilibrium state. The velocity correlation function and energy spectrum are calculated for the equilibrium turbulence. It is found that the energy spectrum falls off as the inverse second power of the wavenumber. The velocity correlation function is similar to the result obtained in real turbulence experiments. With Gaussian random driving force and Gaussian initial velocity field, it is found that the velocity field remains very nearly Gaussian by comparing the fourth-order velocity correlation with the quasinormal assumption. Although the process remains very nearly Gaussian, it is found that the projection of the process on the initial white noise process becomes smaller and smaller. This is to be expected, since the dynamic system is escaping from the original random base.
Name: ["Jeng D.-T."]

Title: TECHNIQUE FOR CONTROL OF TRAFFIC AT CRITICAL INTERSECTIONS
Abstract: An algorithm for control of queue lengths at oversaturated intersections oriented toward delaying spillback across upstream intersections as long as possible is described. It is based on determining the change in queue and the allotment of available green time so as to keep the ratio of actual queues to the maximum link storage space on both phases equal. The mathematical development of the algorithm is described in terms of Z transform analysis, and the conditions for stability are derived.
Name: ["GORDON RL"]

Title: ESTIMATING THE CONDITIONAL PROBABILITY DENSITY OF THE PHASE COORDINATES FROM INCOMPLETE INFORMATION
Abstract: Differential equations are derived for the sufficient characteristics of the conditional probability density of the phase coordinates in the presence of a continuous arrival of random information which depends linearly on the phase coordinate vector of a multivariate nonlinear dynamic system. The parameters of a certain multivariate normal probability density and the coefficients of the linear combination of the Hermite polynomials are chosen as the characteristics; the product of the combination of Hermite polynomials and the multivariate normal probabilitydensity serves as an approximate representation of the conditional probability density. The algorithms given in the paper can be used to estimate the parameters of motion of various plants during the process of obtaining measurement information, in synthesizing stochastic control, and in identifying a dynamic system during its operation.
Name: ["BOGUSLAVSKII IA"]

Title: Adaptive Nonparametric Classification
Abstract: A method of adaptive nonparametric classification based on counting known points ‚Äúobserved‚Äù within a hypersphere inserted in the character space is described. It is shown that an optimal single-hypersphere decision process exists, and that the proposed procedure converges stochastically to the optimal process. The latt)er in turn convrrges at maximum rate to the likelihood ratio decision rule. Sampling experiments on multivariate normal populations indicate that the efficiency of the method when the parametric model holds is about the same as that of the standard parametric procedure. ¬© 1969 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Pelto C.R."]

Title: Comments on Linear Feature Extraction
Abstract: The problem considered is that of finding the best linear transformation to reduce a random-data vector z to a vector of smaller dimension. It is assumed that the original data are Gaussian under either of two hypotheses, and that one wishes to use the transformed data to distinguish the hypotheses. The Bhattacharya distance is used to measure the information carried by the transformed data. A compromise solution is obtained for the case in which the data have both different means and different covariances under the alternative hypotheses. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All Rights Reserved.
Name: ["Henderson T.L.", "Lainiotis D.G."]

Title: COMPUTERS LEARN TO ROLL STEEL
Abstract: Adaptive technique devised by Westinghouse Electric Corp now aims at a logic refinement that is immediate, automatic and cumulative. If a computer is not correct in predicting the initial roll settings for a piece of steel, the deviation is noted. A correction factor is cranked into the model that controls initial settings. This is automatically applied the next time the same product is rolled. How system differs from conventional control. Practical examples are given.
Name: ["MCMANUS GJ"]

Title: Identification in automatic control systems
Abstract: There are many concepts of system identification, and in this paper a comparison is made between different approaches based primarily on experimental identification with respect to the criteria of optimality selected for achieving identification, the mathematical models considered, the computing techniques used, and the kind and form of the input signal selected. Linear, non-linear, dynamic, and noisy systems are considered as well as adaptive models and stochastic approximations. It is concluded that although significant progress in system identification has been made, many problems remain, and among them is the determination of modeling accuracy especially for non-linear, noisy systems. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Balakrishnan A.V.", "Peterka V."]
Affiliations: [' University of California', ' Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences']

Title: Performance bounds for discrete-time stochastic optimal control problems
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to obtain some upper and lower bounds for the optimal performance of discrete-time stochastic optimal control problems with incomplete state observation and/or with unknown constant parameters. These bounds are useful for evaluation of various suboptimal policies. For a discrete-state case, √Östr√∂m (l965) has shown two theorems which give these bounds. Our methods are extensions of his in several ways. Utilizing the result of our methods, an evaluation of the state information obtained from the observation signal is also developed. ¬© 1969, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Sawaragi Y.", "Yoshikawa T."]

Title: An Algorithm to Determine the Reliability of a Complex System
Abstract: The method most often suggested for determining the reliability of a system is to construct a reliability network, enumerate from the network all mutually exclusive working states of the system, calculate the probability of occurrence of each working state, and sum these probabilities. For a complex system this is not a practical method for there is a very large number of working states. Esary and Proschan suggest a lower bound approximation to reliability that requires the enumeration of a much smaller set of system states. These states are called minimal cuts. An algorithm is presented to determine the set of minimal cuts and thus calculate a lower bound to system reliability. The algorithm is intended for digital-computer implementation and computational times are provided. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Jensen P.A.", "Bellmore M."]
Affiliations: [' University of Texas', ' The Johns Hopkins University']

Title: A parameter-adaptive control technique
Abstract: Control of linear stochastic systems with unknown parameters is accomplished by means of an approximate solution of the associated functional equation of dynamic programming. The approximation is based on repeated linearizations of a quadratic weighting matrix appearing in the optimal cost function for the control process. This procedure leads to an adaptive control system which is linear in an expanded vector of state estimates with feedback gains which are explicit functions of a posteriori parameter probabilities. The performance of this controller is illustrated with a simple example. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Stein G.", "Saridis G.N."]
Affiliations: [' Research Dept.', ' Department of Electrical Engineering']

Title: Complexity of Decoders: I‚ÄîClasses of Decoding Rules
Abstract: Several classes of decoding rules are considered here including block decoding rules, tree decoding rules, and bounded-distance and minimum-distance decoding rules for binary parity-check codes. Under the assumption that these rules are implemented with combinational circuits and sequential machines constructed with AND gates, OR gates, INVERTERS, and binary memory cells, bounds are derived on their complexity. Complexity is measured by the number of logic elements and memory cells, and it is shown that minimum-distance and other decoders for parity-check codes can be realized with complexity proportional to the square of block length, although at the possible expense of a large decoding time. We examine tradeoffs between probability of error and complexity for the several classes of rules. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All Rights Reserved.
Name: ["Savage J.E."]

Title: STOCHASTIC DIGITAL COMPUTING
Abstract: Recently, interest has developed in digital computing methods that do not use a coded number representation, such as the binary code. One such method is stochastic (or probabilistic) computing, which combines many of the advantages of analog and digital computers. Simple hardware, well suited to LSI, is used, and the main application will probably be in special-purpose computers. It is claimed that for many purposed, stochastic computing should be superior to general-purpose coded digital computing in terms of performance, and speed of design.
Name: ["REDDAWAY SF", "FRENCH M"]

Title: Identification of Linear Sampled Data Systems by Transform Techniques
Abstract: A technique for application of the popular fast Fourier transform (FFT) to the system identification problem is outlined. Smoothing is obtained inherently in the transform and additionally by redundancy in the data. An iterative technique is discussed for the case of nonzero initial conditions and to avoid problems due to the circular nature of convolutions cosaputed by the discrete Fourier transform (DFT). Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Eiectrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Butcher W.E.", "Cook G.E."]

Title: INSENSITIVITY OF GRADIENT METHODS IN THE SOLUTION OF LINEAR PROBLEMS ON ANALOG COMPUTERS
Abstract: The possibility is proved of small variations of the coefficients of the integrators in gradient methods intended for the solution of systems of linear algebraic equations, systems of linear inequalities, and linear programming problems, for which convergence is not disturbed and the limiting solutions are not changed.
Name: ["RYBASHOV MV"]

Title: OPTIMUM CONTROL OF NONLINEAR DISTRIBUTED-PARAMETER SYSTEMS
Abstract: Optimum control of systems which can be described by nonlinear partial differential equations with time t and k-dimensional space vector x as variables is discussed. The controls, which depend on time only, are related to the nonlinear equation and its boundary conditions through intermediate time functions satisfying certain ordinary first-order differential equations. A particular case is considered when inertialess controllers are used for control on some boundaries of the analyzed system. An algorithm is proposed for approximate calculation of the optimum control. An example is considered of optimum control of heating a one-dimensional plate by internal heat sources.
Name: ["GOLUB NN"]

Title: Algorithm for matching 1-dimensional patterns in multidimensional space, with application to automatic speech recognition
Abstract: An algorithm is described which selects corresponding points on two curves in multidimensional space. This simplifies comparison of two curves which have been derived as functions of an independent parameter (usually time), where this parameter does not vary in the same way along each curve. The problem arises in matching utterances for the purpose of automatic speech recognition. ¬© 1969, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Ellis J.H."]

Title: Continuous-time probabilistic automata
Abstract: The concept of a continuous-time probabilistic automaton is presented in the paper. The probability distribution over the state space of this kind of automaton can change in each moment of the considered time interval. In this case, such notions as input word, event, regular event undergo respective modifications. It is also useful to consider the infinitesimal-state diagram instead of the ordinary one. For the automata thus defined, the events accepted, the conditions of connectivity, as well as their discrete approximations are discussed. To conclude, examples of systems are given that belong to the axiomatic framework of continuous-time probabilistic automata. ¬© 1969 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Knast R."]

Title: CONTROLLABLE SEMI-MARKOVIAN PROCESSES WITH FINITE NUMBERS OF STATES AND OF CONTROLS
Abstract: This treats a problem in optimal control of a semi-Markovian process. Application of dynamic programming is investigated for the solution of this problem with chief attention focused on the question of its realization in processes with a large number of possible states. Examples are given.
Name: ["TEPLITSKII MG"]

Title: PERFORMANCE AND STABILITY OF PROCESS COMPUTER CONTROL SYSTEMS WITH CONSTRAINTS ON THE CHANGE OF THE MANIPULATED VARIABLES, | [REGELGUETE UND STABILITAET VON REGELSYSTEMEN MIT PROZESSRECHNERN BIE BESCHRAENKUNG DER STELLGROESSENAENDERUNGEN]
Abstract: Various frequently used methods of delivery of manipulated variables for direct digital control (DDC) contain constraints on the change of the manipulated variables. This results in special forms of nonlinear behavior in DDC control loops, which are explained by some examples. From this there flows a heuristically derived stability criterion for systems with numerical approximations of analog PID algorithms and a new graphic representation of such control operation. W.T.Lee'srule for the choice of sampling intervals for plants with dead time is investigated with respect to the limits of its validity. Various other effects in DDC controls, which are known in the literature, are interpreted.
Name: ["SCHOENE A"]

Title: CUBATURE METHOD OF COMPUTING PROBABILITY MOMENTS
Abstract: Two m-dimensional cubature formulas are developed for computing the initial moments of the output coordinates of an automatic control system. The respective formulas are exact if the coordinates in question are polynomials of degree seven or nine in the m input random variable%s.
Name: ["DOBRODEEV LN"]

Title: CONVERGENCE OF LEARNING ALGORITHMS
Abstract: General conditions are established for the convergence of both search and search free algorithms. These conditions cover the case where some functional expressing the purpose of learning has a unique optomal point, segment, or, finally, a finite number of optimal points. On the basis of the concept of stochastic approximation theory, it is pointed out that a negligible change in the classical convergence conditions permits the case of nonunique optimum point to be covered.
Name: ["DEVYATERIKOV IP", "KAPLINSKII AI", "TSYPKIN YAZ"]

Title: Self-Optimizing target control system
Abstract: A ‚Äútime-optimized‚Äù control system to drive meson targets into critical positions has been developed and used in the Zero Gradient Synchrotron (ZGS). A current drive coil reacts with the magnetic guide field to hold the target in any desired vertical position. This position is repeated each cycle regardless of operational changes of magnetic field, times of targeting, etc. This system achieves proper ‚Äúbang-bang‚Äù acceleration and deceleration by learning and storing information regarding its behavior on previous cycles. At the end of its 20 ms optimized travel, a linear servo mode takes control to maintain the position reached. In the linear servo mode, programmed variations in target height may be made to compliment an experiment. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Potts C.W.", "Marcks D.F."]

Title: On stochastic automata and languages
Abstract: This paper is mainly concerned with two problems in the area of stochastic languages. For the Œª-stochastic languages, a flexible stochastic experimental procedure based on Chebyshev's inequality is proposed. Then, the class of maximum-likelihood stochastic languages is defined on the basis of the maximum-likelihood final-state distribution. Properties of this class of languages and its relationship to Œª-stochastic languages are investigated. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Fu K.S.", "Li T.J."]

Title: GENERAL REGULARIZED SEQUENTIAL UNCONSTRAINED MINIMIZATION TECHNIQUE
Abstract: The extension of the method described is obtained via the regularized auxiliary function and a proof of convergence of the resulting sequential interior method is given. A regularization of the auxiliary function utilized in SUMT is given as an example.
Name: ["FIACCO AV"]

Title: A Technique for Suboptimal Feedback Control of Nonlinear Systems
Abstract: A simple easily implemented method is developed for obtaining a suboptimal control law for the optimization problem associated with minimizing a quadratic cost functional for nonlinear systems. The suboptimal control law is derived using a Taylor's series representation for the feedback gain matrix after modeling the nonlinear system by a linear system at each instant of time. The resultant control law is of feedback form and is nonlinear in state. The suboptimal control is obtained without using iterative techniques or any true optimal solutions. A second-order numerical example illustrates the effectiveness of the method and gives a comparison to the results of previous methods. Title: Optimal Control of Linear Systems with Time-Delay and Observation Noise
Abstract: The problem of controlling a linear system to minimize a quadratic cost criterion is investigated when the system output is a delayed linear combination of system states corrupted by additive observation noise. It is shown that the optimal control is generated by the cascade combination of a Kalman filter and a least mean-squared predictor. Expressions are derived for the minimum cost and for the state variances. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Eiectrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.

Title: An Adaptive Control Algorithm for Linear Systems
Abstract: A modified gradient procedure is presented for adjusting parameters in a linear control system in the absence of complete knowledge of the plant dynamic characteristics. The algorithm operates to make discrete-time changes in the adjustable parameters during the normal course of system operation and incorporates the best available information on the unknown quantities. Sufficient conditions for the error corrective properties of the algorithm are derived, and the results of a simulation study are discussed. Source: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
Abstract: The problem of minimizing a function f(x) subject to the constraint œÜ{symbol}(x)=0 is considered. Here, f is a scalar, x an n-vector, and œÜ{symbol} a q-vector. A sequential algorithm is presented, composed of the alternate succession of gradient phases and restoration phases. In the restoration phase, a nominal point y not satisfying the constraint is assumed; a displacement Œîy leading from point y to a varied point {Mathematical expression} is determined such that the constraint is restored to a prescribed degree of accuracy. Title: Unified Intervals Classification and Unified 3-Classification for Associative Memories
Abstract: Algorithms for a unified interval classification and a unified 3-classification for use in associative memories are presented. The former, which is more generally known as between-limits classification, achieves the classification of the words of an associative memory into those within and those without an interval marked by two given limits; the latter achieves the classification of the words into the three classes, between the given limits, above the upper limit, and below the lower limit. Title: System Identification with Threshold Measurements

Abstract: A method has been developed to analyze systems which have threshold properties. The only information about the system response that is used in the analysis is whether or not this response exceeds a fixed threshold of unknown magnitude. There are many biological systems that fall into this category of systems, for example, the auditory system, the visual system, electrical stimulation of nerve cells, etc. However, any network to which an arbitrary amplitude has been assigned and which the response has to exceed as an artificial threshold could be analyzed with the methods outlined in this paper. The cases of a simple linear system and first- and second-order photochemical reactions are discussed extensively. It is shown that due to the limited output information available, often no unique system characterization is possible. However, the method can be a powerful aid in the selection between various alternatives. The influence of possible nonlinear operators in the system has been analyzed, and the result turns out to be very dependent upon the location and character of these operators. Title: A Dual Maximum Principle for Discrete-Time Lines Systems with Economic Applications
Abstract: A discrete-time linear optimal control problem with given initial and terminal times, state control constraints, and variable end points is set forth. Corresponding to this primal control problem, or maximization problem, is a dual linear control problem, or minimization problem. A dual maximum principle is proved with the aid of the duality theory of linear programming, where the dual of the Hamiltonian of the primal control problem is the Hamiltonian of the dual control problem. A discrete-time analog of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation is derived and economic applications are discussed. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.

Title: A Hyperstability Criterion for Model Reference Adaptive Control Systems
Abstract: This paper considers the stability problem of the model reference adaptive control systems by means of the properties of hyperstable systems. A theorem concerning the hyperstability of model reference adaptive control systems is presented. This theorem directly gives a structure of the adaption mechanism. The results presented here include all the results obtained by Butchart, Shack-cloth, Parks, Winsor, Roy, and Dressler. The hyperstability approach presented in this paper also allows for other solutions to the adaption mechanism and represents a general method for studying this type of adaptive systems. The results are directly applicable to the design of model reference adaptive control systems and they were verified for some particular cases by analogical simulation. Title: A Monte Carlo Method for Stochastic Time-Optimal Control
Abstract: An analog computer is used to apply a Monte Carlo method of solution to the parabolic partial differential equations that arise in stochastic time-optimal control theory. Using this method, an iterative technique called approximation-in-policy-space is applied to find the optimum switching curve. An example of a second-order inertial plant is considered, and the results are found to agree with those found by a perturbation given by Dorato et al. [1]. Title: Note on fuzzy languages
Abstract: A fuzzy language is defined to be a fuzzy subset of the set of strings over a finite alphabet. The notions of union, intersection, concatenation, Kleene closure, and grammar for such languages are defined as extensions of the corresponding notions in the theory of formal languages. An explicit expression for the membership function of the language L(G) generated by a fuzzy grammar G is given, and it is shown that any context-sensitive fuzzy grammar is recursive. For fuzzy context-free grammars, procedures for constructing the Chomsky and Greibach normal forms are outlined and illustrated by examples. ¬© 1969.

Title: ALGORITHMS FOR CODING OF ASYNCHRONOUS AUTOMATED UNITS, | [ALGORITHMES DE CODAGE DES AUTOMATES ASYNCHRONES]
Abstract: The author reports on two simple partially programmed algorithms for the coding of asynchronous automated units, such coding eliminating any critical motion. These methods employ graph theory techniques, in particular algorithms of a graph in an n-cube, and have been simplified.

Title: Analysis and Optimization of a Queueing Model of a Real-Time Computer Control System
Abstract: A single processor provides service to jobs of several different priority classes. The priority ordering remains constant over time; however, the type of priority, i.e., preemptive or nonpreemptive, may depend upon the stage of processing of the job occupying the processor. We allow these preemptible and nonpreemptible intervals to be specified in a relatively arbitrary fashion. If a job is interrupted, a setup time must be incurred before processing can be continued on the job. If arrivals from all classes constitute independent Poisson streams, we are able to obtain expressions for the steady-state expected time in system for jobs of each class. These expressions are then analyzed to determine the optimum manner for assigning the preemptible and nonpreemptible intervals. When setup times are zero and preemptible portions are preemptive-resume, the optimal policy is fairly simple. When setup times are nonzero, the form of the optimal policy is not clear; however, numerical evaluations suggest that at high loads, e.g., greater than 0.9, one should allow much less preemption or time-sharing than one might suspect. Title: Some considerations on fuzzy automata
Source: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: In this paper, we show: The threshold of fuzzy automata can be changed arbitrarily. The fuzzy sets of input sequences characterized by fuzzy automata constitute a distributive lattice, and the complement of the fuzzy set can be characterized by an optimistic fuzzy automaton. ¬© 1969 Academic Press, Inc.

Title: MATHEMATICAL MODEL FOR PATTERN VERIFICATION
Source: IBM Journal of Research and Development
Abstract: Pattern verification is mathematically defined, an appropriate decision function is derived, and a measure of system evaluation is given. Two basic postulates are set forth to fully define a verification system-each known class is expected, with nonzero probability, to be verified under the correct class label; and the pattern vector extracted during verification should be descriptive of the given class, independent of which class lab%l was entered into the system.

Abstract: Logical systems are often represented using the Turing-machine concept. A design method is described whereby the normal transition tables for a Turing machine may be translated into a state table defining the control unit as a finite-state machine, and a special shift-register configuration in place of the computing tape. Design equations and circuits are given for a 4-state Turing machine embodying a 2-symbol alphabet. ¬© 1969, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.

Title: STABILITY OF SYSTEMS HAVING '%'CONSERVATIVE'%' PLANTS
Abstract: An examination is made of problems in the stability of a certain class of systems used for the automatic control of conservative plants. Problems of this kind develop in investigating the dynamic properties of automatic satellite control. Problems of the stability of a system consisting of a one-parameter linear conservative plant and a nonlinear controller are similarly examined. On the basis of the second Lyapunov method, a special method is given for constructing the Lyapunov function; it is shown that under these conditions one obtains a system satisfying the hypothesis of linear associated systems.

Title: The Design of Minimum-Cost Survivable Networks
Abstract: We consider the problem of designing a network which satisfies a prespecified survivability criterion with minimum cost. The survivability criterion demands that there be at least rij node disjoint paths between nodes i and j, where (rij) is a given redundancy requirement matrix. This design problem appears to be at least as difficult as the traveling salesman problem, and present techniques cannot provide a computationally feasible exact solution. A heuristic approach is described, based on recent work on the traveling salesman problem, which leads to a practical design method. Algorithms are described for generating starting networks, for producing local improvements in given networks, and for testing the redundancy of networks at each stage. This leads to networks which are locally optimum with respect to the given transformation. Randomizing the starting solution ensures that the solution space is widely sampled. Abstract: The problem is considered of Phi-machine synthesis for pattern recognition, using potential functions. The possibility is studied of interpolating unknown functions in the learning process using certain concrete forms of potential functions.

Title: NONTRACKING AUTOMATIC OPTIMIZATION OF A CERTAIN CLASS OF NONMINIMAL- PHASE SYSTEMS
Abstract: An algorithm with a simplified reference model is suggested, which represents a modification of the inverse-model method and retains its simplicity of hardware implementation and effectiveness. For practical systems an algorithm with a simplified reference model is given without the inverse model for the case in which it is not possible to implement the inverse model. The algorithm investigated allows the performance of nontracking automatic optimization and selfadaptation of nonminimal-phase systems which are characterized by delay.

Abstract: Methods are presented for designing threshold gate networks with error-correcting capabilities. The particular method presented is an extension of the tree method for realizing a Boolean function. A primary realization is a realization for some function on the tree such that either the separating function or the gaps are assigned without knowledge of any other realizations on the tree. It is shown that a realization obtained by the tree method corrects t errors of gates in the system if and only if all primary realizations are selected so that they correct t errors of gates in the primary realizations. Title: Distinguishability Criteria in Oriented Graphs and Their Application to Computer Diagnosis-I
Abstract: Discrete sequential systems like the functional elements of a digital computer can be represented by directed graphs. In this paper we study an application of graph theory to computer diagnosis. Specifically, we develop the distinguishability criteria in directed graphs and derive bounds on the number of test points needed to locate faults in a sequential system. Abstract: Extremal systems with diverse search algorithms are compared, and recommendations for their usage are given.

Abstract: A computer-oriented algorithm is presented based on a topological development for determining loops and paths in a Mason signal flowgraph (1, 2). The utility of the algorithm in the analysis of linear networks and systems with the desired expressions in symbolic and symbolic/numerical forms is discussed. Abstract: The Bayesian decision procedure is given to determine a finite sequence of n m-ary (m >2) digits that have been transmitted through a channel that has memory and introduces additive noise. Minimum probability of digit estimation error is used as the criterion of goodness. Intersymbol interference at the receiver input is assumed to exist between L successive digits. Title: An entropy model of the developing brain
Abstract: From experimental work on fetal development of neural processes, a qualitative entropy model of the brain is derived. Abstract: The n-tuple method of pattern recognition has been simulated on a somewhat larger and more comprehensive scale than previously reported. The nonweighted version has been found to work better than the maximum likelihood weighted version, and to achieve about 93 percent successful recognition of unconstrained hand-printed numerals, but at the cost of about 42 million bits of storage. ¬© 1969 IEEE.
