The major innovations include a full, formal description of the syntax of a transformational grammar, a directed random phrase structure generator, a lexical insertion algorithm, an extended definition of analysis, and a simple problem-oriented programming language in which the algorithm for application of transformations can be expressed. in this paper we present the system as a whole, first discussing the general attitudes underlying the development of the system, then outlining the system and discussing its more important special features. References are given to papers which consider some particular aspect of the system in detail. ¬© 1969, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Friedman J."]
Keywords: ["computational linguistics", "language analysis", "language processing", "lexical insertion", "natural language syntax"]

Title: Randomized binary search technique
Abstract: A mathematical model is developed for the mean and variance of the number of trials to recover a given document in a randomly received list of files. The search method described is binary in nature and offers new potential for information retrieval systems. ¬© 1969, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Arora S.R.", "Dent W.T."]

Title: Liapunov Function of a Sixth-Order Nonlinear System
Abstract: A formulation of a liapunov function is given for the stability study of a sixth-order system characterized by a nonlinear function (x). fifth-order and fourth-order systems with a nonlinear function 4/(x) are given as special cases. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.

Title: Invariant imbedding and sequential interpolating filters for nonlinear processes
Source: Journal of Fluids Engineering, Transactions of the ASME
Abstract: Suppose imprecise observations are made on imprecisely defined nonlinear processes, and one wishes to estimate the state of the process at certain fixed instants of time lying within the interval of observation. Furthermore, assume that it is required to update these estimates as additional observations become available. This is precisely the problem of sequential interpolation. The equations of the sequential interpolating filter, when a least-squares estimation criterion is used, are obtained in this paper. The interpolation problem is first shown to be equivalent to a two-point boundary-value problem. The two-point boundary-value problem is converted to an initial-value problem using invariant imbedding. The initial-value problem leads directly to a sequential filter. ¬© 1969 by ASME.
Name: ["Kagiwada H.H.", "Kalaba R.E.", "Schumitzky A.", "Sridhar R."]
Affiliations: ['The RAND Corporation', ' University of Southern California', ' California Institute of Technology']

Title: Some New Approaches to Machine Learning
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics
Abstract: Five different but interrelated models of learning have been established within a complex computer program. These models incorporate mechanisms that optimize response patterns on algorithmic and heuristic bases; make abstractions at different levels; produce value judgements; recognize, modify, store, and retrieve geometrical patterns; and exhibit, in general, many aspects of intelligent behavior. Both the teacher and the learner are simulated in the machine. In one model, the program follows a qualitatively new kind of learning process in generating its own strategy and improving it on the basis of experience. The method enables the learner to exceed the playing quality of the teacher. It is suggested that the methods and techniques employed in the project may be useful in mechanizing some problem-solving activities that can be reduced to pattern recognition, such as meteorological forecasting, medical diagnosis, traffic control, and so on. No deliberate attempt has been made to imitate humans. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Findler N.V."]

Title: Concepts of an Estimation System, an Adaptive System, and a Network of Adaptive Estimation Systems
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics
Abstract: A clear distinction is made between two concepts. One concept is called an estimation system and the other an adaptive system. Using these two concepts as building blocks and a Bayes minimum conditional risk approach, it is possible to give meaning to the concept of a network of adaptive estimation systems. Under the framework of the approach, unsupervised estimation (estimation without a teacher) is a classical statistical problem as is supervised estimation. Also, supervised estimation is a degenerate case of estimation and a special case of adapting. In general, adapting without a teacher is impossible. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Patrick E.A."]

Title: ESTIMATION OF DYNAMIC ACCURACY OF AUTOMATIC CONTROL BY SEMIPROPORTIONAL CONTROLLERS
Abstract: Analog computer simulation of dynamic errors of automatic control systems with time delay and controllers operating in case of increased signals across modules, such as used for pi-controllers.
Name: ["SEMIKH VV"]

Title: Unate Cellular Logic
Abstract: A fundamental problem in ‚Äúcellular logic‚Äù is to be able to ‚Äúsynthesize‚Äù ‚Äúcellular arrays‚Äù for arbitrary switching functions that minimize a set of design parameters like size of the arrays and complexity of the individual cells and of the interconnection pattern on the cells. This paper is an attempt to develop ‚Äúminimization algorithms for cellular arrays.‚Äù The particular cellular array considered in this paper is a unate cellular array which is a one or two-dimensional arrangement of two-input one-output combinational cells, each of which is capable of being set to give any one of the fourteen unate functions of its two inputs, that is, excluding EXCLUSIVE-OR and EQUIVALENCE. The main results obtained are as follows. 1) A theorem is proved which says that the output of a unate cascade is a unate function. 2) A simple test procedure is suggested for checking whether or not a given switching function is unate cascade realizable. The procedure needs a maximum of n iterations for testing an n-variable switching function. The procedure being constructive, an algorithm is obtained for getting all the unate cascades which realize a given function. 3) An arbitrary single-output or multiple-output switching function can be realized by using one or more unate cascades arranged in a two-dimensional array. An algorithm is presented for obtaining the minimal cascade realizations of a given function or a set of functions. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Mukhopadhyay A."]

Title: Extrapolation of Tracking Data
Abstract: Errors in the measurement of a trajectory produce errors in the model of the trajectory and its extrapolation. This correspondence presents the extrapolation accuracy of four trajectory models as a function of the extrapolation, the number of independent measurements, and the accuracy of the measurements. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Lorens C.S."]

Title: Derivation of a Matrix Identity
Abstract: In problems of linear digital filtering and recursive estimation, a matrix identity (1) is often met. Here this matrix identity is derived by use of matrix projection operator's and their properties. This deviation is novel, straightforward, and of tutorial value. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hemami H."]
Affiliations: ['Dept. of EIec. Engrg. Ohio State University']

Title: NOTE ON OPTIMUM DESIGN OF NONLINEAR SAMPLED-DATA CONTROL SYSTEMS, | [UEBER DIE OPTIMALE SYNTHESE NICHLINEARER ABTASTREGELUNGSSYSTEME]
Abstract: Procedure for optimum design of class of nonlinear sampled-data control systems, proposed by J. Meksawan and G. J. Murphy is investigated; by counter-example it is shown that given strategy is not necessarily optimal.
Name: ["POKOSKI JL"]

Title: CHARACTER RECOGNITION BY MEANS OF OPTICAL FILTERING
Abstract: A method of character recognition employing optical matched filters is described. Some experimental results are given as an indication of the performance of the filters and the difficulties involved with their application. A simple example of word detection is included to emphasize a parallel processing capability.
Name: ["DYE MS"]

Title: RECOVERY OF FUNCTION IN CLASS OF FUNCTIONS WITH REPRODUCING KERNEL
Abstract: The problem is investigated of recovering a function from values distorted by noise on the assumption that the function belongs to the class of functions with reproducing kernel. On this hypothesis the basic recovery algorithms are similar to the algorithms of the potential functions method and converge for fairly broad assumptions.
Name: ["PETERSEN IF"]

Title: A markov model for quality control plan selection
Abstract: A Markov chain model is developed which provides a measure of the cost of using alternative plans to control the output quality of productive processes. Such a model provides a yardstick for selecting the ‚Äúbest‚Äù control plan structure for a given process. The model structure is explained by presenting the example of a two-state process controlled by a plan which executes corrective action on the first defective sampled. ¬© Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Lave R.E., Jr."]

Title: SYSTEMATIC METHOD OF FINDING DIAGNOSTIC TEST FUNCTIONS
Abstract: A new method of representing machines is proposed. The method describes the structure of the machines and affords operational analysis for combinatorial logical systems (combinatorial machines) composed of logical-product, logical- sum and negation units. Using this, a method of classifying defective machines systematically, due to stationary binary defects of components, as well as of deriving defect-testing functions mechanically is clarified. Since these processes can all be carried out by computers, a new technique of mechanizing diagnostic operations is established.
Name: ["ICHIKAWA T", "WATANABE T"]

Title: Relationship between Kalman‚ÄîBug State Estimation and Blended-Model State Estimation
Abstract: This correspondence shows the relationship between Kalman-Bucy (K-B) state estimation and blended-model state estimation‚Äîa technique used in the aerospace industry. The purpose in presenting this comparison is to aid in the interpretation of the K‚ÄîB filter when used in a control system and, hopefully, to give the designer a more intuitive ‚Äúfeel‚Äù for application of the K‚ÄîB filcer. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gieseking D."]

Title: On the optimization of linear, time-variant, multivariable control systems using the contraction mapping principle
Source: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
Abstract: The problem of optimizing a linear, time-variant, multivariable control system with quadratic cost functional is first phrased in the context of functional analysis. It is shown that the optimum control is given implicitly as the solution of a matrix integral equation. After the fixed-point contraction mapping theorem is invoked, an iterative method for solving this equation is developed and conditions for its convergence to a unique optimum are derived. Techniques for transforming the system operator are discussed so that, when convergence of the original sequence of iterations cannot be assured, that of the transformed system can. However, it is shown specifically that there is always a finite optimization interval for which the procedure may be used. Bounds are also given for the errors, in the sense of norms, between the control after n iterations and its ultimate value and between the cost functional after n iterations and its ultimate value. These bounds are used to decide when to terminate the sequence. Solutions of the iterative scheme using a hybrid computer in parallel and serial modes are discussed and the delays inherent in both methods calculated. It is concluded that the method can be used to track an optimum control system, which drifts from optimum because of parameter variations, with little delay and particularly when the optimization interval is extrapolated only a little into the future. Comparison of the proposed scheme with the steepest-descent approach developed by Balakrishnan shows that the present scheme requires one-third of the computations per step and, therefore, may converge more quickly. ¬© 1969 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Freeman E.A."]

Title: Low Sensitivity Filters for State Estimation in the Presence of Large Parameter Uncertainties
Abstract: Three minimax sensitivity criteria are used to synthesize filters for estimating the state of a simple first-order plant when large uncertainties in dynamic and/or statistical parameters of the plant and measurement system are present. Two design examples involving unknown plant bandwidth and unknown plant input noise covariance are worked out in detail. Graphical comparison of the error performance of the three minimax sensitivity filters with that of the optimal filter is presented for each case. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["D'appolito J.A.", "Hutchinson C.E."]

Title: DETERMINATION OF OPTIMAL WEIGHTING FUNCTION OF LINEAR DYNAMIC SYSTEM BY STATISTICAL CRITERIA IN PRESENCE OF CONSTRAINTS
Abstract: A method is proposed for determining the weighting function of an optimal dynamic system by various statistical criteria on condition that the values of the weighting function lie in a prescribed bounded closed region. Necessary and sufficient conditions are obtained in the form of nonlinear integral equations defining the optimal weighting function of the dynamic system.
Name: ["ANDREEV NI"]

Title: Associative Parallel Processing for the Fast Fourier Transform
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: An associative memory is proposed as a parallel processing unit for the fast Fourier transform; such a processing unit is well suited to implementation in large-scale integrated circuit technologies. Formulas are derived for the number of memory operations required to execute the algorithm and are tabulated for a range of the number of data points being transformed. It is shown that a 1024 word by 64 bit memory with an operation time of 100 ns could execute a 1024 point transform in 8.4 ms. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Wesley M.A."]

Title: Inversion of Multivariable Linear Systems
Abstract: A new algorithm for constructing an inverse of a multi-variable linear dynamical system is presented. This algorithm, which is considerably more efficient than previous methods, also incorporates a relatively simple criterion for determining if an inverse system exists. New insight into the structure of a system inverse is gained by consideration of the inverse system representations resulting from the algorithm. A precise bound on the number of output differentiations required is obtained as well as a bound on the total number of Integrators and differentiators necessary to realize the inverse. This latter bound is equal to the order of the original system. A further advantage of the algorithm. and theory developed is that it is applicable to both time-invariant systems and time-variable systems which satisfy certain regularity conditions. One application is also given: A complete description of the set of initial states necessary and sufficient for a specified function to be the output of an invertible system. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Silverman L.D.M."]

Title: A note on a set of functions for information retrieval
Abstract: An information retrieval system for experimental use is considered and a notation is introduced to help in its description. The system is experimental in that it is designed to facilitate the examination of the effect of different keyword classifications on retrieval performance. The notation derives from the basic operations encountered in information retrieval and examples are given of its use in a system which has already been implemented on a computer. These operations and their relevance to retrieval system is described in detail. Consideration is given to store allocation in the implementation of such a system and a simple method of automatic allocation is presented. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Jackson D.M."]

Title: An experimental anatomy computer system
Abstract: Future computer systems, to assist the practicing physician, may take many forms. Some may, as independent automata, prepare and present specific diagnoses or identify and recommend specified courses of therapy. Others may assist by augmenting the physician's processes of reasoning to enhance both his diagnostic ability and his therapeutic decisions. Such systems will serve as prosthetic extensions of human cognition and will function as integrated manmachine systems combining the unique features of both the man and machine to the solution of diagnostic and therapeutic problems. This latter type of synergetic automaton must have the ability to answer any question submitted by the physician within its information content. Thus, it must be able to interpret the question and derive the answer in a simulation of the human ability to use knowledge. To achieve this, basic research is needed to develop a general system for the organization of disciplinary information and general programs for its utilization. Such research involves the development of a simulation, suitable for computer application, of the primitive pattern of human objectification and the fundamental processes of organization. This paper presents the first operational stage of a computer system constructed for the study of one aspect of this problem. The study involved the modeling of gross objects of the physical world, their attributes and relationships; the subject area used was human gross anatomy and the object set, a male human body. The output of the computer system is demonstrated, comments are given, the system is described, and plans for subsequent research discussed. The paper is written primarily as a progress report on the first operational stage of an experimental system. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Fiege Jr. H.R.", "Smith R.S.", "Palit D.", "Kruger E."]
Affiliations: [' University of Wisconsin Medical', ' University of Wisconsin', ' University of Wisconsin']

Title: Computer simulation of a self-preserving and learning organism
Abstract: The objective of the present work is to describe a technique general enough to be applied to the simulation of a fairly wide range of biological phenomena rather than the explicatory-predictive treatment of a specific problem. A model of an organism is built and studied by computer simulation. The organism has a major goal, survival, and various subgoals, such as optimization of its state of health, maximization of pleasure, minimization of pain, exploration and control of its environment, etc. It perceives a set of stimuli and emits a set of responses the quality of which improves with experience. Various learning processes are incorporated in the "cognitive mechanism" of the organism. The description of the model is followed by an outline of the computer program and, finally, the results of a trial run are discussed. ¬© 1968 N. Rashevsky.
Name: ["Findler N.V.", "McKinzie W.R."]
Affiliations: [' State University of New York at Buffalo']

Title: Optimization of Control Systems with Discontinuities and Terminal Constraints
Abstract: The ‚Äúsuccessive sweep method,‚Äù a Newton-Raphson algorithm in function space, based upon [1]‚Äì[3], is applied to the computation of optimal solutions to control problems which are characterized by terminal constraints and discontinuities in the control functions. The computational technique of using piecewise constant gains is introduced for the successive sweep method in order to reduce computer storage. Two examples are considered. The first example concerns the three-dimensional attitude control of an orbiting vehicle. The second example is the two-dimensional transfer of a low thrust vehicle in a gravitational field. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Dyer P.", "McReynolds S.R."]
Affiliations: ['Jet Propulsion Laboratory California Institute of Technology']

Title: SIMULATION OF RANDOM STATIONARY FUNCTION WITH SPECIFIED ONE- DIMENSIONAL DISTRIBUTION LAW
Abstract: Method is suggested for obtaining stationary random function; technique consists of treating trajectory of point that performs random walk from level to level as realization of random function whose one-dimensional distribution law is related to limiting probabilities of transition matrix; block diagram and description of device for implementing method are given.
Name: ["ZRAZHEVSKII AYU", "MAKHLIN IS", "ROZENFEL'D DKH"]

Title: ANALYSER-CODER FOR MACHINE RECOGNITION OF HUMAN SPEECH
Source: J Inst Telecommun Eng New Delhi
Abstract: Paper deals with the design of an analyzer-coder for construction of a digital code pattern from a human speech input suitable for the use of computers from which the intelligence content can be extracted without any human intervention. Major functions necessary in any pattern recognition system are noted, aspects of decision theory as pertinent to the present work are mentioned and a theoretical model for speech analysis by synthesis is described, including the experimental part of the system, human speech analyzer and matrix coder. The underlying theme of the work is to design a frequency quantized, continuous, short-term spectrum analysis echnique capable of extracting statistically invariant properties of the human speech pattern to a binary quantized representation produced by the measurement apparatus and used as the input data to the categorizer portion of the recognition system.
Name: ["MAJUMDAR DD", "DUTTA AK"]

Title: REALIZATION OF TIME-OPTIMAL SYNTHESIZING FUNCTIONS FOR CLASS OF LINEAR THIRD-ORDER SYSTEMS
Abstract: Method is proposed for design of regulator approximately realizing time-optimal control law; examples and modeling results are given.
Name: ["VOLODIN LA", "MOROZ AI", "OGUL'NIK MG"]

Title: SPEED OF STEP SYSTEMS OF AUTOMATIC SEARCH WITH DRIFT PRESENT IN PLANT'S EXTREMAL CHARACTERISTICS
Abstract: As speed characteristic, author has chosen mean time of transition from state to state; formulas have been obtained for determination of mean time of transition in terms of probabilities of single- cycle transitions of Markov process of state change of search system; results obtained are illustrated in terms of example of extremal system whose object (plant) has piecewise-linear characteristic.
Name: ["GALASHOV NF"]

Title: CLASS OF MULTIPHASE SERVING SYSTEMS FOR STRUCTURAL-TEMPORAL ANALYSIS OF DIGITAL COMPUTERS
Abstract: For purpose of investigating structural-temporal properties of digital computers, certain multiphase queueing system is introduced for which necessary and sufficient conditions of correct operation are determined consisting in constraints on server discipline; upper and lower bounds are found on productivity of model which are invariant with respect to its structure.
Name: ["DEGTYAREV EK"]

Title: PROOF OF ALGORITHM FOR SECONDARY PROCESSING OF INFORMATION
Abstract: Algorithm for secondary processing of information, by which target coordinates in following scan are predicted from results of observations in previous scanning cycles, and space gate centered at this point is generated, is proved; target motion was approximated by model having stationary and independent n-th order increments.
Name: ["LIKHAREV VA", "FURMAN YAA"]

Title: FILTERING OF SIGNALS DEFINED BY DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS WITH VARIABLE COEFFICIENTS
Abstract: Authors consider solution of problem of optimal filtering of random signals defined by differential equations with variable coefficients that contain white noise.
Name: ["DMITRIEV SP", "DOLGINTSEVA GYA", "IGNATOV AA"]

Title: On a mathematical procedure for detecting significant parameters in the classification of a statistical ensemble of phenomena and its applications
Abstract: The paper is concerned with a procedure for detecting the uncorrelated linear combinations of a given set of random variables. The linear transformation which is used is related to the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix for the original random variables. If the significant non correlated signals are in number less than the original ones (which have often a high degree of redundancy) the possibility arises for an application of this procedure to some branches of communication theory. The most important applications should be to vocoder for a further compression of information, for masking messages and also for building a machine which should be able to classify a statistical ensemble after suitable coding. The procedure has been tested by trying to extract significant parameters from a special coding of spoken Italian vowels in view of an improvement in the efficiency of speech recognition. ¬© 1969 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Favella L.F.", "Reineri M.T.", "Righini G.U."]
Affiliations: [' della Universit√° di Torino and Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare-Sezione di Torino', " Istituto elettrotecnico Nazionale 'Galileo Ferraris'"]

Title: ON TIME SERIES ANALYSIS OF VISUAL ACUITY A STATISTICAL MODEL
Abstract: Instantaneous visual acuity is defined and treated as a stochastic process. The properties of this process can be studied indirectly in another, realizable, process. This is generated by letting the outcome of a trial govern the difficulty of the next object. An analysis of this process makes it possible to determine if the mean and dispersion describe the visual performance satisfactorily or not. 1969 Institution Acta Ophthalmologica Scandinavica
Name: ["KRAKAU C.E.T."]

Title: Some Lower Bounds on Signal Parameter Estimation
Abstract: New bounds are presented for the maximum accuracy with which parameters of signals imbedded in white noise can be estimated. The bounds are derived by comparing the estimation problem with related optimal detection problems. They are, with few exceptions, independent of the bias and include explicitly the dependence on the a priori interval. The new results are compared with previously known results. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Ziv J.", "Zakai M."]

Title: SOME CONSIDERATIONS ON A TYPE OF PATTERN RECOGNITION USING A NONSUPERVISED LEARNING PROCEDURE
Source: Electronics & Communications in Japan (English translation of Denshi Tsushin Gakkai Ronbunshi)
Abstract: Little has been published on machines involving unsupervised learning, such as is encountered in detection problem in communications. One method of approaching this problem is to use decision-directed system in which supervisory role is exercised by machine itself. The paper analyzes this method, determining the recognition error rate and the final convergence form. This analysis shows that the decision-directed method does not converge to the optimum form for the case of a known pattern. Several machine methods are proposed to achieve improved functioning.
Name: ["TANAKA K", "TAMURA S", "HIGUCHI S"]

Title: FILTERING OF NONSTATIONARY PROCESSES TAKING OBSERVATIONAL COSTS INTO ACCOUNT
Abstract: Paper considers optimal control of observation; it is shown that this problem leads to use of usual methods of optimization for controls and functionals which depend on a posteriori characteristics.
Name: ["YASHIN AI"]

Title: STATISTICAL EQUIVALENCE OF STOCHASTIC AND NONLINEAR SYSTEMS
Abstract: It is proved that linear system with random parameters can be considered as system with input and output having statistics precisely same as statistics of nonlinear system; method of describing nonlinearities is investigated for both static systems (systems without memory) and dynamic syste.
Name: ["WOODSIDE SM"]

Title: OPTIMAL DISTRIBUTION OF RESOURCES IN PLANNING OF SETS OF OPERATIONS
Abstract: Algorithm is proposed for constructing graph of feasible states (GFS) of set of operations; equivalence is shown of problem of minimizing arbitrary additive and minimax quality criteria and problem of finding shortest and minimax paths in GFS, respectively.
Name: ["GOLIKOV AI", "DEMENCHUK VM"]

Title: ON THE GENERAL SOLUTION OF A STATE-CHARACTERISTIC EQUATION OF FINITE AUTOMATA
Source: Electronics & Communications in Japan (English translation of Denshi Tsushin Gakkai Ronbunshi)
Abstract: Necessary and sufficient condition for minimal solution of linear equation in semiring of language space to be only solution is found. Representation of general solution having certain degree of freedom is given in case where given linear equation has more than one solution. In this case, another linear equation which is equivalent to given one and has only one solution that is equal to minimal solution of given linear equation can be found. Method to obtain such a linear equation from original is established.
Name: ["MINE H", "TAKAOKA T"]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF OPTIMAL DIRECTION FINDING SYSTEMS
Abstract: Possibility of defining optimum direction finding system based on representation of bearing as multivariate Markov process is studied; cases of white and narrow-band noise disturbances are investigated; it is claimed that systems using differential radiation patterns for direction finding are special cases of obtained optimum system.
Name: ["BAKLITSKII VK"]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF AIRCRAFT MODAL CONTROL SYSTEMS HAVING REAL OR COMPLEX EIGENVALUES
Abstract: Modal control is concerned with the design of control loops for systems with governing equations that can be adequately approximated by linear vector-matrix equations. In this paper a design procedure is developed that makes it possible to alter both the real and imaginary parts of any number of pairs of conjugate complex eigenvalues and any number of the real eigenvalues of the system matrix of a plant controlled by a single input if the system is controllable. The theory is applied to the problem of synthesizing a longitudinal autopilot for pitch angle and short-period oscillation mode control.
Name: ["CROSSLEY TR", "PORTER B"]

Title: Rank Permutation Group Codes Based on Kendall's Correlation Statistic
Abstract: A coding scheme based on the properties of rank vectors is presented. The new codes are based on the theory of per-mutation groups by introducing a new notation for the group operation that simplifies the generation and decoding of desirable rank codes. The use of group theory is made possible by the introduction of the Kendall correlation coefficient as a measure of the distance between code words. This technique provides a method for the choice of rank vector code words superior to those that have been proposed in the past. Much of the terminology used in block coding can also be used to describe rank vector codes, but the actual quantities involved are quite different. The rank vector codes discussed in the paper offer the advantage of low sensitivity of the probability of error to the noise distribution because of the nonparametric character of rank vector detection schemes. Bounds that have been verified by extensive computer simulation have been derived for the probability of error. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Chadwick H.D.", "Kurz L."]

Title: CHOOSING PARAMETERS OF REALIZATION OF RANDOM STATIONARY PROCESS IN CALCULATING ESTIMATE OF ITS CORRELATION FUNCTION
Abstract: Study is made of class of exponential correlation functions; parameters of correlation functions (length of realization and frequency with which data are read) are determined directly from form of realization as function of specified accuracy with which correlation function is estimated.
Name: ["ITSKOVICH EL", "TSATUROVA IA"]

Title: Image enhancement: A review
Abstract: We first describe the basic linear and non-linear mathematical operations underlying most image enhancement techniques, and compare the hardware available for carrying out these operations which includes digital computers, optical set-ups and special electro-optical devices. Then we give a brief account of the commonly used image enhancement techniques, such as contrast enhancement, crispening, noise elimination, and inverse filtering. Finally, we mention some examples of image enhancement in the biomedical area. ¬© 1969 Chapman and Hall.
Name: ["Huang T.S."]

Title: SIMULATION OF SEQUENCE OF UNEVENLY SPACED SAMPLES FROM GAUSSIAN RANDOM PROCESS
Abstract: Paper examines procedure for simulation of sequence of random values of multidimensional Markov gaussian random process and stationary gaussian process with fractional rational spectrum; procedure is designed for direct probabilistic simulation of informational and control systems with arbitrary behavior of given data and it can also be used in numerical integration of differential equations with random right-hand member.
Name: ["POLLYAK YUG"]

Title: Properties of Optimal Linear Smoothing
Abstract: The problem in considered of characterizing the improvement in estimating the state of a linear system when filtering is replaced by smoothing. It is found that when the optimal filter is exponentially asymptotically stable, a smoothing lag equal to several time constants associated with this filter yields practically all the possible improvement. The extent of improvement, as measured by an error variance matrix, is also found. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Anderson B.D.O."]

Title: PARTITIONING OF GRAPHS
Abstract: Problem is posed of partitioning graph into subgraphs minimally connected with each other; method proposed can be used to solve problem of distribution of program in computing machine.
Name: ["GORINSHTEIN LL"]

Title: Fuzzy Logic and its Application to Switching Systems
Abstract: Fuzzy logic deals with propositions which may be ascribed values between falsehood and truth (0 and 1) subjectively in either a continuous or a discrete fashion. This is in contrast to ordinary logic (two-valued or k-valued logic) in which a given proposition is ascribed values objectively using either deterministic or probabilistic approaches. An analysis and synthesis of fuzzy logic functions is presented and their electronic implementation is discussed in some detail. Suggestions for possible uses of fuzzy logic in quality control, industrial processes, component testing, and pattern recognition and classification are offered. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Marinos P.N."]
Keywords: ["fuzzy logic fuzzy sets fuzzy systems multivalued logic", "synthesis fuzzy", "systems fuzzy", "logic deals", "fuzzy logic"]

Title: Selecting state variables to minimize eigenvalue sensitivity of multivariable systems
Abstract: It often happens that linear, time invariant, multivariable systems must be simulated or synthesized using digital and analog computers. The simulation may require accurate reproduction of the simulated system, and the synthesis may demand faithful representation of a mathematical model. Because of the degradation introduced by such factors as the finite wordlength constraints of digital computers and the temperature variation of amplifier gains in analog computers, the computer realization will differ from its original model. In this paper a simple method is presented for minimizing the deviation in the eigenvalues of the computer realization when all elements of the system matrix are subject to simultaneous variations. This procedure involves the selection of a suitable set of state variables, the choice depending simply on the location of the system eigenvalues. When the system is realized using the state vector obtained by this method, greater component variations and shorter computer wordlengths can be tolerated before stability is sacrified and satisfactory behavior is compromised. As a result, utilization of the algorithm discussed in this paper can result either in relaxation of computer tolerances, and hence reducing the cost of realization, or in more faithful reproduction of the original system. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Singer R.A."]

Title: Feedback Control of a Class of Linear Systems with Jump Parameters
Abstract: A class of linear systems are studied which are subject to sudden changes in parameter values. An algorithm similar in form to Kushner's stochastic maximum principle is derived and the relationship between these algorithms discussed. Systems in which the performance measure is quadratic are investigated in detail and a differential equation is derived which yields the optimal feedback gains. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Sworder D.D."]

Title: The Human as an Optimal Controller and Information Processor
Abstract: A mathematical model of the instrument-monitoring behavior of the human operator is developed. The model is based on the assumption that the operator behaves as an optimal controller and information processor, subject to his inherent physical limitations. The resulting model depends explicitly on the control task and the control actions. Provision is made for the ability to obtain information from the peripheral visual field. There are no restrictions on signal coupling. The specific characteristics of the operator's visual sampling behavior are predicted by solving a nonlinear, deterministic optimization problem. A two-axis compensatory tracking example is investigated, and the results exhibit the general characteristics expected of a human operator performing a similar task. Copyright 1969 by the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Baron S.", "Kleinman D.L."]

Title: OPTIMAL ESTIMATE OF PARAMETER OF SIGNAL IN PRESENCE OF NOISE WITH FLUCTUATING SPECTRAL DENSITY
Abstract: Recursion formula has been obtained that makes it possible to calculate a posteriori probability density of estimated parameter of signal at receiver in background of nonsteady-state uncorrelated noise, spectral density of which is Markov random process with given coefficients of drift and diffusion.
Name: ["KULIKOV EI", "TRIFONOV AP"]

Title: ESTIMATE OF LIMITING POSSIBILITIES FOR REALIZATION OF FORMAL NEURONS
Abstract: Estimate is given for limiting values of constructional parameters of nondegenerate formal neurons as function of number of inputs, and possibilities of their technical realization are discussed.
Name: ["POTAPOV VI"]

Title: Automatic patching for analog and hybrid computers
Abstract: This paper describes the results of an investigation into the feasibility of an automatic patching system for an analog or hybrid computer. The objective of the study is to reduce the number of switches required to a ‚Äúrea sonable‚Äù number. Actual design of hardware is not con sidered. The final result is a ‚Äúpaper‚Äù design, which is evaluated by attempting to program several problems to see if enough paths exist. The proposed design uses about 8,000 switches for an EAI-680-sized computer, which is far fewer switches than are required by any previously proposed system. The evaluation shows that this system is more than adequate and that, in fact, about 2,000 switches could be saved by modifying the design slightly. ¬© 1969, Sage Publications. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hannauer G."]

Title: Computer operations and the structure of Information
Abstract: A simple statement of the function of a computer may be formulated in terms of reading, writing, and arithmetic. The 'arithmetic' must be seen to cover logical operations as well as addition and subtraction, and a whole set of operations can be expressed as a program of algorithms. The rules of operation for these algorithms are exactly laid out in the syntaxes of the various computer languages but the syntax of the data upon which the operators operate is poorly formalized. The proper development of medical data-syntax is seen to be a field of work upon which depend the proper validation of data base scientific work, the design and ordering of equipment, the planning of data systems, the disposition of resources, and the safety of patients.
Name: ["Knox E.G."]

Title: DETERMINATION OF PARAMETERS OF DISCRETE SYSTEM USING PREDICTION MODEL METHOD
Abstract: Exact and approximate corrective controls are obtained, which correspond to quasi-stationary operating conditions; technique of investigation of model correcting dynamics is illustrated by example.
Name: ["KRUT'KO PD"]

Title: OPTIMAL REGULATION OF NONLINEAR DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS
Abstract: Paper deals with optimal control of autonomous systems of nonlinear differential equations; control functions represent feedback devices which operate upon instantaneous state of system to generate control signals which automatically return system to prescribed state of equilibrium whenever impulsive disturbance occurs in state; these regulator devices are widely used in aircraft flight controls and many other control systems,
Name: ["LUKES DL"]

Title: An adaptive automaton controller for discrete-time markov processes
Abstract: The computation of an optimal feedback controller characteristic for a non-linear stochastic system may be facilitated by the use of a stochastic automaton as a system model. A problem of particular interest is that of a long duration stationary Markov process in which the state is observable but the process dynamics and disturbance characteristics are initially unknown. The determination of a suitable control algorithm, in the form of an adaptive automation in the feedback loop, is considered in this paper for such a process. Since the algorithm is to be used on-line to perform simultaneously the functions of estimation and control, it must constitute an efficient convergent multi-stage dual control strategy. It is shown that an existing method for dual control of a repetitive single-stage stochastic process may be extended to apply to the present case. A method is introduced of calculating successive policy estimates recursively, so that the task of updating the estimated optimal feedback policy at each stage of the process is rendered feasible. The application of the automaton controller is illustrated by the simulated adaptive control of a non-linear conditionally stable heat treatment process disturbed by multiplicative noise. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Riordon J.S."]

Title: USE OF AUTOMATIC CLASSIFICATION METHOD FOR INDIVIDUAL PREDICTION OF POWER KLYSTRON LIFETIMES
Abstract: Method is proposed for individual prediction of reliability characteristics of microwave power devices, based on use of automatic classification algorithms; results are presented of experimental test of this method for prediction of service life of power klystrons.
Name: ["GORENKOV EV", "DOROFEYUK AA", "ZHITKIKH IM"]

Title: OPTIMAL SYSTEM OF SEARCH FOR MINIMUM
Abstract: Method is described for constructing search system for minimum of output quantity of inertia object; time optimal control rule is implemented in system, rule being invariant with respect to parameter changes of control object. i
Name: ["FITSNER IN"]

Title: Some Swedish experience in the development of interactive computer systems
Abstract: Since the advent of the computer the data processing field has been growing at an ever-increasing rate. One part of this field‚Äîperipheral systems permitting real-time, interactive, man-machine communication‚Äîhas started to grow in an explosive way which surpasses all expectations of a few years ago. This paper reviews the logical development of a requirement for multi-programming, multi-processor systems, in order to match the computational speed and facilities of the computer to those of the man, and to enable man and machine to interact co-operatively as a decision-making team. The requirement for cooperative decision-making arose very early on in air traffic control, and the system concepts described are exemplified through a description of the CENSOR computer system developed by Standard Radio & Telefon for the Swedish Air Force. Recently one of these systems has been installed in the Karolinska Hospital in Stockholm for patient monitoring in an intensive care ward. The modularity of the system, both in hardware and software, largely gained through the multi-processor approach using satellite machines, has been an important factor in enabling a variety of complex systems to be built up with experience for problems which were, initially, incompletely specified. ¬© 1969, Academic Press Inc. (London) Limited. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Mellberg K."]

Title: Information Processing of Remotely Sensed Agricultural Data
Abstract: Systems utilizing sensors on aerospace platforms for the purpose of surveying earth resources have been under study recently. In this paper research on the information processing portion of such a system for agricultural resources is described. In particular the application of pattern recognition techniques to multispectral data is proposed and example results are presented. Good classification accuracy on crop species identification of some 40 000 samples in a five square mile area was achieved in one example. Other examples show results in feature selection and nonparametric classifier algorithms. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Fu K.S.", "Landgrebe D.A.", "Phillips T.L."]

Title: Creating holographic filters for automatic recognition systems
Source: Proceedings of SPIE - The International Society for Optical Engineering
Abstract: The holographic process is well known. But the efficient creation of ‚Äúholographic filters‚Äù for optical automatic pattern recognition devices demands little-known technique refinements. Problems of making filters and their solutions are discussed. Basic equipment requirements and significant variants are presented for filter generation and processing systems. Filtering results are shown for typical reconnaissance targets and for fingerprint identification. A proposed automatic device is depicted for recognizing and counting reconnaissance targets. A list of recommendations is given to those just be-ginning work in the field. ¬© 1969, SPIE.
Name: ["Thomasson J.T."]

Title: APPROXIMATIONS IN PROBLEMS OF CONSTRUCTIONS OF FUNCTIONS AND OF PATTERN RECOGNITION
Abstract: Required information consists in knowledge of coordinates of points of teaching sequence, where teaching is either not done at all or consists in tuning of net of samples according to rule indicated; experimental data are included that show efficiency of algorithm as compared with machine execution of algorithm of potential functions.
Name: ["MALKINA RM", "PERVOZVANSKII AA"]

Title: Computerized Learning Machines Applied to Chemical Problems Molecular Formula Determination from Low Resolution Mass Spectrometry
Abstract: A computerized learning machine has been applied to the chemical problem of determining molecular formulas from low resolution mass spectra. Learning involves applying feedback to a decision process to minimize the probability of undesired responses. The basic concepts of learning machine theory are presented, along with the computer programs which, using a training set of low resolution mass spectra, empirically develop pattern classifiers to correctly determine molecular formulas. Statistically varied spectra are used to demonstrate the high reliability of the system, and some possible applications of learning machines to other aress of chemical data interpretation are discussed. ¬© 1969, American Chemical Society. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Jurs P.C.", "Kowalski B.R.", "Isenhour T.L."]

Title: DETERMINATION OF THE STATIC AND DYNAMIC CHARACTERISTICS OF A PLANT WITH A CONSTANT DELAY PORTION
Abstract: Author solves the problem of identification of a system consisting of a constant delay and a linear dynamic portion, as well as of a system which additionally contains a nonlinear lagless part with linear dynamic part. The moments of the correlation functions are used for determining first the static characteristics of the system, and then the delay and the dynamic characteristics of the linear part, the results are extended to the case of many inputs.
Name: ["VOYTSENKHOVSKII VB"]

Title: The DDA integrator as the iterative module of a variable structure process control computer
Abstract: The present trends in computer organization, control technology and large-scale integration are evaluated to deduce the features of a new computer for process control purposes, and to propose an actual design. The proposed computer will have a variable structure organization, with a fixed part, a GP computer, and a variable part composed of an array of DDA integrators, acting as processor elements. The latter can well be implemented as LSI circuits, to form iterative modules. The topology of the computer is of the partially interconnectible, decentralized type. The machine lends itself particularly well to the application of advanced reliability strategies. The problem domain which can be solved is relatively broad, and although the proposed organization does not comply strictly with the criteria of Shannon or Holland, its practical facilities for control applications are not impaired, while implementation and programming are rendered easier. An appropriate autocode for programming the computer is based on the differential calculus, and it would be particularly suitable for the application of Newell's problem-solving techniques. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Hatvany J."]

Title: Computer simulation of stochastic processes through model-sampling (Monte Carlo) techniques
Abstract: A simple Monte Carlo simulation program is outlined which can be used for the investigation of random-walk problems, for example in diffusion, or the movement of tracers in the blood circulation. The results given by the simulation are compared with those predicted by well-established theory, and it is shown how the model can be expanded to deal with drift, and with reflexion from or adsorption at a boundary. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Sheppard C.W."]

Title: EXAMPLES FOR ADAPTIVE PROCESS CONTROL KNOWN STRUCTURE OF PROCESS MODEL
Abstract: Process optimization according to given performance index and adaptive open loop control under varying environment conditions are problems of automation, which can be solved by process computer; for this purpose it is necessary to have dynamic mathematical model of process stored in computer; static mathematical model is favored above dynamic one; some mathematical methods are discussed, which can be used for choice of model structure and for on-line identification.
Name: ["POPOVIC DB"]

Title: ON TOURS OF TRAVELING SALESMAN
Abstract: Adjacency properties of tours on their convex hull are discussed; rule is given by which it can be tested whether any two tours are adjacent vertices on this convex hull or not; based on this rule algorithm is described for generating all adjacent tours of given tour.
Name: ["MURTY KG"]

Title: CODING OF CLASSES IN DIAGNOSTIC PROBLEMS
Abstract: The merits of proposed coding are that the most essential properties of a class are revealed, along with a quantitative estimate of their information content and the rules and instrumentation for recognition are simple. Recognition can be effected with code tables. It is possible to select the most informative parameters (from the sum of the resolutions of all the intervals of values), and to select and estimate the necessary number of intervals in a simple way.
Name: ["OSIS YAYA"]

Title: OPTIMAL ESTIMATION OF PIECEWISE-CONSTANT VECTOR PARAMETERS
Abstract: A stepwise procedure is proposed for calculating estimates and the error correlation matrix.
Name: ["DMITRIEV SP"]

Title: ENERGETIC (POWER) ESTIMATIONS OF COMPLEXITY OF LOGIC NETWORK PEFORMANCE
Abstract: The method of complexity estimation of realization of an arbitrary Boolean function in logic networks is given. The method takes into account energy losses, associated both with signal transmission and processing in the network. Some theorems of upper and lower asymptotic bounds of energetic complexity of realization of an arbitrary Boolean function are proved.
Name: ["GORYASHKO AP"]

Title: Dynamic scheduling in the process industries by predictive control
Abstract: The objective of this paper is to apply the technique of predictive control in order to obtain approximate solutions for the on-line scheduling problems, both "static" and "dynamic", which can account for disturbances in plants which are complex and whose dynamics are significant. The predictive controller relies on repetitive simulation to enable it to choose among possible control or scheduling alternatives. Heuristic methods for choosing schedule changes in response to disturbances may be derived from analogous techniques of optimal control. Application of the techniques to a problem from the paper industry is described and numerical results are presented which compare the improved performance to that obtainable from static scheduling alone. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Long C.F.", "Schoeffler J.D."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF PARAMETERS OF NONLINEAR AUTOMATIC SYSTEMS
Abstract: A method for the synthesis of the parameters of nonlinear automatic systems containing one nonlinearity is proposed. The method is based on linearization of nonlinearities, based on the representation of functions by an exponential polynomial and the minimization of the integral quadratic error.
Name: ["STANKEVICH VI"]

Title: OPTIMAL SINGULAR CONTROL OF SYSTEMS WITH VARIABLE FEEDBACK
Abstract: It is shown that if the switching of control parameters is done in a certain logical order in a bang-bang fashion and if certain constraints are fulfilled, then in the state space of the object there exists a hyperplane, such that the state point after reaching it will move along it in an exponential manner into the origin of space. This movement is optimal in the sense of minimizing an integral quadratic performance index. As an example, optimization of a second-order system with variable damping is discussed.
Name: ["MORSZTYN K", "BROWN WA"]

Title: MARKOV PHOTOGRAPHIC NOISE
Abstract: Study of photographic noise from viewpoint or continuous-parameter Markov chains; model predicts new relation between rms density and average density; distribution of number of developed grains is shown to correspond to special nonstationary probability of grain development and is not Poisson distribution.
Name: ["YU FTS"]

Title: GENERALIZED PROBLEMS IN STOCHASTIC APPROXIMATION
Abstract: Two theorems on probability convergence of process that is generalization of stochastic approximation process are given.
Name: ["BRUSIN VA"]

Title: ANALYSIS OF NONLINEAR DISCRETE SYSTEMS BY METHOD OF SEPARATION OF MOTION
Abstract: Principal attention is given to the algorithm of the motion separation and the phase-plane analysis of the relay type discrete systems. It is shown, that the relay type discrete systems may have limit cycles which occupy rhombuses and rings in the phase plane. Presence of the limit cycles explains the fact that a quasi- periodic motion is the most characteristic of the discrete systems.
Name: ["GERASHCHENKO EI"]

Title: ON-LINE OPTIMAL CONTROL USING A HYBRID COMPUTER
Abstract: The optimal controller uses the method of steepest descent to optimize the control with amplitude constraints over a constant future time interval, for a given performance index. The effect that the optimization period and the plant parameter changes have on performance of the controller is investigated. The performance of a fourth-order plant, controlled to optimize a quadratic performance index, is compared with its performance when controlled to optimize a modulus performance index. It is shown that the use of the modulus performance index has several advnatages over the use of thequadratic performance index. The controller is more easily realizable and the resulting performance is improved due to the faster rate of convergence of the control toward the optimum for small errors in the plant state.
Name: ["YASTREBOFF M"]

Title: Electronic eye
Source: Japanese Journal of Medical Electronics and Biological Engineering
Abstract: This is a technical survey of the researches on synthesizing a model of the visual system of an animal, or an electronic eye such as a pattern recognizer for which ingenious mechanisms of biological systems are heuristics. These researches are reviewed from a standpoint of visual information processing. This survey includes the models of photoreceptors, the models of neural interactions, in a retina, the models of the visual feature extraction from optical patterns, and the models of the recognizing system which have an ability to learn characters or figures. ¬© 1969, Sage Publications. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Fukushima K."]

Title: The Mean Accuracy of Pattern Recognizers with Many Pattern Classes
Abstract: Hughes [1] presented some curves relating the mean performance of a pattern classifier averaged over all pattern recognition problems of given complexity, when there are two classes of patterns to be distinguished. In this correspondence the mean recognition probability is computed for the case of q pattern classes when the a priori probabilities of the classes are equal. When the a priori probabilities are unequal, the mean performance will improve over the performance with equal a priori probabilities, so these curves provide a lower bound to the performance of recognizers with more than two pattern classes. Some comments on the appropriateness of these statistics to common recognition problems are made. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Kain R.Y."]

Title: THE CONCEPT OF INVERSE IMAGES & THEIR ROLE IN RESOLUTION
Source: Indian Journal of Pure and Applied Physics
Abstract: Method has been described for converting a density function of any unit (of which a composite density function is composed) into an inverse function, so that the composite function can be analyzed for the units in order to find their positions. This inverse function is obtained by computing the inverse matrix of the unit function. This method should be particularly useful to the x-ray crystallographers and for information retrieval.
Name: ["MCLACHLAN JR D"]

Title: An algorithm for straight-line representation of simple planar graphs
Abstract: An algorithm is developed for drawing straight-line planar graphs which are isomorphic to a convex polyhedron and simple (i.e. a connected graph with no self-loops or multiple branches). The construction of such graphs is outlined in three stages. Stage 1 determines all the independent cycles of the graph plus one dependent cycle by Goldstein's algorithm. Stage 2 orders the cycles in such a way that they may be drawn in sequence with a given cycle as external. Stage 3 constructs the graph by successively assigning coordinates to the vertices which were placed in order according to the result of Stage 2. An iterative procedure is used for shifting the coordinates to eliminate crossings of edges. Results show that practically all these planar connected graphs up to 22 cycles can be drawn provided that the longest cycle is chosen as the external one. In addition, in the event of failure of the iteration procedure for graphs with a large number of cycles, a heuristic decision involving man-machine interaction is introduced to adjust the partially completed straight-line graph. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Woo L."]
Affiliations: ['International Business Machines Corporation New York Scientific Center']

Title: Extending the Definition of Prime Compatibility Classes of States in Incomplete Sequential Machine Reduction
Abstract: A procedure is illustrated to reduce the number of classes of internal states to be considered in the state minimization problem for incompletely specified sequential machines. The procedure leads to an extension of the definition of prime compatibility classes of states. It is based on the updating of the logical closure constraints for prime classes due to previous eliminations of nonprime ones. An additional, more complex elimination mechanism is also presented. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Luccio F."]
Keywords: ["additional elimination rules", "extended prime classes", "prime compatibility classes of states", "reduction of incomplete sequential machines", "updating of the logical closure constraints"]

Title: METHOD FOR AUTONOMOUS NAVIGATION OF ARTIFICIAL SATELLITES
Abstract: A method is proposed for autonomous navigation of artificial satellites of planets. It is shown that all the elements of the orbit can be determined comparatively simply from the measurements selected. An algorithm is presented for solving the navigation problem by the method of successive approximations; the uniqueness of the solution and the convergence of the iterative process are demonstrated. Examples are given of navigation systems found by this method/
Name: ["ZYBIN YUN"]

Title: The application of Bayes's theorem when the true data state is uncertain
Abstract: This paper discusses the application of Bayes's theorem to those cases where the true state of the world is not known with certainty. An algorithm is proposed that relaxes the requirement of Bayes's theorem that the true data state be known with certainty by postulating a true but unobservable elementary event, œâ, which gives rise to posterior probabilities which reflect the uncertainty of the data. A derivation is presented for the calculation of Bayesian posterior probabilities which uses as its input these probabilities, rather than the true event, œâ, which is assumed to be unavailable. Suggestions are made as to the application of this modification of Bayes's theorem to cascaded inference processes. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Gettys C.F.", "Willke T.A."]

Title: Learned specification of concept neurons
Abstract: The referential aspect of a concept can be defined by a disjunction of conjunations of attributes. A single neuron can represent a disjunction of conjunctions of attributes if the assumption that neurons are single-threshold devices is discarded. Instead, one must assume that such concept neurons are composed of hundreds or thousands of (high-threshold) receptive areas, each containing tens or hundreds of synaptic sites. When essentially all of the sites of a receptive area are activated in close temporal contiguity, the receptive area generates a local (spike) response which is assumed to be sufficient to fire the cell body and axon of the neuron. If we assume that all concepts possessed by a single human being can be encoded by single neurons in this manner, there are enough neurons in the human cortex only if we assume that most of these concept neurons are specified by learning. Genetic specification is ruled out by the enormous (infinite?) nember of possible concepts humans appear to be able to learn. Therefore, a speculative neural mechanism is presented regarding how "free" neurons could become specified by learning. ¬© 1968 N. Rashevsky.
Name: ["Wickelgren W.A."]

Title: OPTIMAL NONLINEAR FILTERS FOR SMOOTHING, PREDICTION, AND DIFFERENTIATION USING FINITE NUMBER OF DISCRETE VALUES
Abstract: Examination is made of structure of optimal nonlinear digital smoothing filters that perform prediction and differentiation under conditions when measured quantity has uniform probability distribution over restricted range of values, and useful signal remains constant or varies according to linear law over restricted time interval.
Name: ["KORSHUNOV YUM"]

Title: APPROXIMATION METHOD FOR FOURIER TRANSFORM INVERSION APPLIED TO DISTRIBUTED PARAMETER SYSTEMS
Abstract: The problem of transform inversion to obtain the impulse and step responses of a distributed parameter system is considered where the responses are to be reconstructed later with a minimum of computation and with an estimate of error. It is found that the use of symmetry conditions allows the Fourier transform of the impulse response to be approximated by a weighted sum of Hermite polynomials having, for Gaussian weighting, a simple inverse. An inequality, giving the maximum estimated error as a function of the integral errorsquared is derived which, when combined with a qualitative appreciation of the form of the frequency domain error, gives a good estimate of the error distribution in the time domain. An expression for deriving the approximated step response from the approximated impulse response is given.
Name: ["JEFFRESON CP"]

Title: DECOMPOSITIONAL DYNAMIC OPTIMIZATION OF PRODUCTION WITH HIERARCHIAL CONTROL STRUCTURE. CONTROL OF GROUP OF STATIONARY SUBSYSTEMS
Abstract: Optimal control algorithms are considered for complex hierarchically coupled nonstationary dynamic plants; in present article decomposition principle is extended to group of stationary subsystems.
Name: ["PLISKIN LG"]

Title: CONTROL OF SPACE-VEHICLE MOTION DURING RE- ENTRY INTO THE ATMOSPHERE
Abstract: Problem of controlling the descent of a space vehicle in the atmosphere at velocities of the order of the second cosmic velocity. A multistep adaptive algorithm is constructed for controlling range during the descent. The results of the simulation of the algorithm on a digital computer are presented. It is shown that the algorithm provides adequate accuracy for control and yields a sufficiently smooth control process in the presence of considerable variations in the distribution of the parameters of the atmosphere.
Name: ["OKHOTSIMSKII DE", "BUKHARKINA AP", "GOLUBEV YUF"]

Title: ON ESTIMATION OF GAUSSIAN CONVOLUTION PROBABILITY DENSITY
Abstract: It is shown that certain type of expansion can always be obtained, with coefficients expressed as product of two terms-one function only of unknown distribution and other term dependent on gaussian density; rates of convergence and comparison with other methods of density estimation are discussed.
Name: ["SCHWARTZ SC"]

Title: APPLICATION OF A RESOLVENT IDENTITY TO A LINEAR SMOOTHING PROBLEM
Abstract: By using a result of Siegert a new identity is derived for the resolvent of a covariance function. This identity is used to obtain a simple relation between the smoothed and filtered linear-least- squares estimates of a signal process in additive uncorrelated white noise.
Name: ["KAILATH T"]

Title: FEATURE DETECTION METHOD FOR OPTICAL CHARACTER RECOGNITION
Abstract: A method of optical character recognition is presented that may be suitable for the recognition of hand-printed alphanumeric characters. It overcomes some of the problems of distortion, misregistration, orientation and sensitivity to variations in stroke thickness. The technique has been simulated on Myriad and results with machine printed upper-case alphanumeric characters are encouraging.
Name: ["HOSKING KH"]

Title: BOUNDS ON MULTIPROCESSING TIMING ANOMALIES
Abstract: Author studies typical model of multiprocessing system, and determines precise extent by which execution time for set of tasks can be ifluenced because of timing anomalies; special case of model is shown to generate interesting number-theoretic question.
Name: ["GRAHAM RL"]

Title: RANDOM SEARCH METHOD
Abstract: A multistep random search for the minimum of a function of many variables is considered. At each step of the search it is proposed to project repeatedly the set of values of the objective function of various coordinates axes for subsequent conclusion as to the possibilities of dichotomizing the region with respect to one or several coordinates. Experimental data are presented concerning the effectiveness of the method.
Name: ["ZAKHAROV VV"]

Title: ON THE REMOVAL OF ILL-CONDITIONING EFFECTS IN THE COMPUTATION OF OPTIMAL CONTROLS
Abstract: It is shown that the seeming ease with which nonlinear programming algorithms can be applied to di#ming algorithms can be applied to discrete optimal control problems is deceptive and that severe ill- conditioning may occur due to the exponential nature of solutions of a difference equation, and that it is possible to make very effective use of nonlinear programming results, such as the convergence theory of Zangwill and the anti-zigzagging precautions introduced by Zoutendik in conjunction with geometric ideas of optimal control theory. The algorithmsresulting from the approach can be used for solving a large variety of problems, such as minimum time, minimum energy and minimum fuel problems for linear dynamical systems with constraints both on the control and on the trajectory.
Name: ["POLAK E"]

Title: STABILITY OF LINEAR INTERCONNECTED NETWORKS
Abstract: This paper is concerned with linear interconnected networks which are spatial networks and are a generalization of the network model of the mutually inhibitory mechanism which plays the most important role in the pattern-recognition process of the visual nerve system. In order to explore the practical application of linear interconnected networks to the engineering field, a physical realization condition is established by using the concept of parent function and the decomposition of a linear interconnected network into unit systems. A condition for a linear interconnected network to be stable in a specified manner is also established.
Name: ["YAMASHITA K", "OKAMOTO J"]

Title: LEVEL-ADAPTIVE SPEECH CODING SYSTEM
Source: Electronics & Communications in Japan (English translation of Denshi Tsushin Gakkai Ronbunshi)
Abstract: A speech coding system for pulse-code modulation is proposed in which the binary information output of the coder is divided into sections of time length T, the short-time level of the input speech is discriminated for each section, the coding reference voltage to be used in the next section is varied according to the above level, and all available bits are effectively utilized over the entire operating range of input speech power so that a quality improvement of about 1 bit is achieved.
Name: ["OMORI T", "MASUDA I"]

Title: MODIFICATION OF (U, V, W) SYSTEM
Abstract: Analysis showing degree of adherence of Wyszecki's system to equal visual intervals; modification is proposed, yielding formula for computation of color differences for pairs of similar colors; formulas for specifying whiteness for practical purposes, based on modified system.
Name: ["SATO M", "HIOKI R"]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF STOCHASTIC SYSTEM
Abstract: The problem of the identification of a plant with single output, subject to random variation in the process of functioning is considered. A model is applied to the description of the behavior of the plant in the form of a system of noncoupled secondorder differential equations whose coefficients are stationary random functions. The methods for finding the statistical characteristics of the damping factors are illustrated. The results of solving the identification problem may be used to estimate system reliability in the presence of slowly varying parameters.
Name: ["DIMENTBERG MF"]

Title: Modeling Nonstationary Random Processes with an Application to Gyro Drift Rate
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: The problem of estimating the a priori statistics of a nonstationary process is considered using finite-time averages of experimental data. A model of the form of a linear time-invariant difference equation with a stationary independent random sequence driving function is proposed and investigated. Finite-time averages are calculated and then used in a steepest descent method to determine the coefficients of the difference equation. Methods are presented for transforming this model to the state-spaceformat necessary for Kalman filtering, and an example is givenusing actual gyro drift-rate data. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Van Dierendonck A.J.", "Brown R.G."]

Title: CLOSED FORM RECURSIVE LEARNING FILTER FOR A CLASS OF PROCESSES WITH UNKNOWN PARAMETERS
Abstract: This paper shows that a closed form recursive solution analogous to the Kalman-Bucy solution, can exist for the combined parameter identification and state estimation problems, provided that the system states form an independent sequence of events.
Name: ["CAMERON AV"]

Title: PRE-PROCESSING OF DATA FOR CHARACTER RECOGNITION
Abstract: Article considers the preprocessing of data for character recognition and describes character defects which affect the method of feature detection. Some account of other work on preprocessing is given and an investigation into one of these approaches is described. A possible hardware implementation is outlined.
Name: ["ALCORN TM", "HOGGAR CW"]

Title: ALGORITHM ON CONTROL WHICH IS CLOSE TO OPTIMAL FOR N-TH ORDER SYSTEMS
Abstract: Estimate is given for closeness of control by increments to optimal control; system parameters are found which provide minimum possible transient time; algorithm is discussed for simultaneous control by increments and by structure; principal realization of proposed algorithms is given, and certain properties of systems are noted.
Name: ["ALEKSANDROV VM", "NESTEROV AA"]

Title: Relating Remote Sensor Signals to Ground-Truth Information
Abstract: This paper describes two computer-based methods for data handling and display which significantly simplify the task of relating remote sensor signals to that ground-truth information which can be derived from aerial photographs of the ground scene. These techniques have been applied successfully to microwave radiometer and infrared spectrometer flight-test data. Results indicate that the digital computer, with its associated storage and display capabilities makes possible systematic and accurate analysis of remote sensor data in large volume at low cost. In one approach, the computer is used to determine and display, on aerial photographs, the exact path of the sensor boresight over the ground scene. Using this display, an investigator can observe visually certain simple correlations between the sensor return and the ground scene. In the second approach, the analyst uses a special light-pen console to put ground-truth information (in graphical form) into the computer. Using techniques described here for storing, retrieving and processing graphical data, the computer automatically converts the ground-truth information into a form where it can be correlated directly with the remote sensor signals. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Eppler W.G., Jr.", "Merrill R.D."]
Affiliations: [' Lockheed Electronics Co.', ' Lockheed Palo Alto Research Laboratory']

Title: On a General Relationship Between Estimation, Detection, and the Bhattacharyya Coefficient
Abstract: A general and fundamental relationship between esti-mation, detection/pattern recognition, and the Bhattacharyya coefficient is established. Specifically, it is shown that a functional of the likelihood ratio necessary for Bayes optimal detection/pattern recognition is the Bayes-optimal mean-square estimate of the indicator variable {3, where {3 = 1, 0, for hypotheses H 1, H 0, respectively, The Bhattacharyya coefficient is then shown to be the expected value of the estimation error standard deviation. ¬© 1969 IEEE
Name: ["Lainiotis D.G."]

Title: UNIFIED APPROACH TO NONLINEAR ESTIMATION
Abstract: A unified approach to the dynamic nonlinear estimation problem is presented. General algorithms for filtering, smoothing, and prediction for both continuous and discrete nonlinear systems are derived. The continuous problem is treated first by a direct approach which yields an exact solution. A similar approach is then applied to the more complex discrete estimation problem. It is shown that in the continuous measurement limit, the derived discrete and continuous nonlinear filtering algorithms are identical.
Name: ["GURA IA", "HENRIKSON LJ"]

Title: RANDOM LOGICAL NETS-1, 2, 3
Abstract: Certain methods are considered for the passage from the '%'microscopic'%to the '%'macroscopic'%' description of complex systems consisting of a large number of elements, using the example of random logical nets. The equations of random logical nets are considered and methods for their simplification are discussed. Author defines a special class of homogeneous nets, and investigates their subclass, the symmetric nets and considers in detail the example of a symmetric net constructed of McCulloch-Pitts neurons.
Name: ["ROZONOER LI"]

Title: DETERMINING ORDER OF EXECUTION OF INDEPENDENT OPERATIONS ON PARALLEL MACHINES
Abstract: One of the problems of scheduling theory formulated as an extremal problem on a graph is considered. A combinatorial method is proposed for the exact solution of the problem, using a procedure of tagging the nodes of the graph.
Name: ["ZAK YUA"]

Title: Optimal Synthesis of Distributed Parameter Systems
Source: IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques
Abstract: A technique is developed for the synthesis and design of a distributed parameter system guiding waves from one point in space to another. The parameter distributions are assumed to be unrestricted except for the upper and lower bounds resulting from the imposition of physical realizability. The problem is similar to the ‚Äúsensitivity‚Äù problem encountered in the optimal control of the systems. An improved version of the first-order gradient technique is used to obtain the optimal distributions of the parameters. The first-order gradient technique is sensitive to the form of the arbitrary distributions assumed at the start of the iterations. This technique has serious convergence problems associated with it. The problem is particularly severe and is encountered in ‚Äúsingular‚Äù optimal control problems. The algorithm devised here improves the first-order gradient technique so that it becomes less sensitive to the initial assumed distributions and virtually eliminates the convergence problems generated because of the bounds on the parameter distributions. A transmission line with distributed series r, 1 and shunt c is a particular case of the distributed parameter system. The optimal design of a notched filter employing a thin film circuit is a successful example of the application of the improved gradient technique. These distributions have been obtained by the use of a hybrid computer. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Karnik A.R.", "Cohen G.H."]

Title: TOWARDS UNIQUE DECOMPOSITION OF GRAPHS
Abstract: In effort to define indexing system for linear graphs, approach taken to obtain ordering of graphs is to split any graph uniquely into two subgraphs in such way that ordering may be defined recursively; consideration is given primarily to connected graphs, since in general graph connected components may be considered as separate entities.
Name: ["SNOW CR", "SCOINS HI"]

Title: Stimulus-response theory of finite automata
Abstract: The central aim of the paper is to state and prove a representation theorem for finite automata in terms of models of stimulus-response theory. The main theorem is that, given any connected finite automaton, there is a stimulus-response model that asymptotically becomes isomorphic to it. Implications of this result for language learning are discussed in some detail. In addition, an immediate corollary is that any tote hierarchy in the sense of Miller and Chomsky is isomorphic to some stimulus-response model at asymptote. Representations of probabilistic automata are also discussed, and an application to the learning of arithmetic algorithms is given. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Suppes P."]

Title: REDUCTION OF STOCHASTIC LINEAR DISCRETE CONTROL SYSTEMS
