Title: Additional Features of an Adaptive, Multicategory Pattern Classification System
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics
Abstract: Some additional features of an adaptive, multicategory pattern classification system are presented. No a priori knowledge of the class probability densities or a priori probabilities of occurrence of the categories is required. The system utilizes a set of functions selected by the user to form discriminant functions. Adaptation of the system is accomplished using a set of independent pattern samples of known classification in such a manner that the system discriminant functions form minimum mean-square approximations to the Bayes discriminant functions as the number of samples of known classification increases. The convergence rate of the system is examined, and conditions are established under which the expected loss due to misclassification by the system is asymptotically equivalent to the minimum loss achievable when using the Bayes discriminant functions. In addition, a simulation of the system for a three-category problem is presented to demonstrate system performance for a finite number of adaptions. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Pitt J.M.", "Womack B.F."]

Title: Asymptotically Optimal Discriminant Functions for Pattern Classification
Abstract: The two category classification problem is treated. No a priori knowledge of the statistics of the classes is assumed. A sequence of labeled samples from the two classes is used to construct a sequence of approximations of a discriminant function that is optimum in the sense of minimizing the probability of misclassification but which requires knowledge of all the statistics of the classes. Depending on the assumptions made about the probability densities corresponding to the two classes, the integrated square error of the approximations converges to 0 in probability or with probability 1. The approximations are nonparametric and recursive for each fixed point of the domain. Rates of convergence are given. The approximations are used to define a decision procedure for classifying unlabeled samples. It is shown that as the number of labeled samples used to construct the approximations increases, the resulting sequence of discriminant functions is asymptotically optimal in the sense that the probability of misclassification when using the approximations in the decision procedure converges in probability or with probability 1, depending on the assumptions made, to the probability of misclassification of the optimum discriminant function. The results can be easily extended to the multicategory problem and to the case of arbitrary loss functions, that is, where the costs of misclassification are not necessarily equal to 1. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Wolverton C.T.", "Wagner T.J."]

Title: IMPROVEMENT OF VARIABLE-STRUCTURE SYSTEM TIME RESPONSE BY COMBINATION OF '%'SLIPPING'%' HYPERPLANES
Abstract: The problem of improving the dynamic indices of a variable- structure system (VSS) is considered. A method is proposed for improving the speed of the system without increasing the tendency to oscillate in the transient processes, based on the application of a piecewise-continuous formation of the '%'slipping'%' plane. The method is illustrated by the example of a third-order VSS.
Name: ["MAKAROV IM", "RAKHMANKULOV VZ"]

Title: Recognition of characters subject to spatially independent transformations
Abstract: Binary valued characters, defined over a discrete subset of two-dimensional space, are assumed to be contaminated by spatially independent random errors at each point in space. The errors are described as random transformations. That is, a probability distribution over the possible transformations is assumed at each point. With this definition of the contaminating error process, the optimal Bayes recognition procedure is developed. The optimal recognition rule is linear in the character observations. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Gray Jr. K.B."]

Title: A Bound on the Output of a Circular Convolution with Application to Digital Filtering
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: When implementing a digital filter, it is important to utilize in the design a bound or estimate of the largest output value which will be obtained. Such a bound is particularly useful when fixed point arithmetic is to be used since it assists in determining register lengths necessary to prevent overflow. In this paper we consider the class of digital filters which have an impulse response of finite duration and are implemented by means of circular convolutions performed using the discrete Fourier transform. A least upper bound is obtained for the maximum possible output of a circular convolution for the general case of complex input sequences. For the case of real input sequences, a lower bound on the least upper bound is obtained. The use of these results in the implementation of this class of digital filters is discussed. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Oppenheim A.V.", "Weinstein C."]

Title: The Principle of Minimum Information
Abstract: The principle of maximum entropy for assignment of estimated probabilities is intriguing. Since entropy is the negative of information, the principle was renamed. The formalisms for discrete and continuous random variables are described and illustrated. The problem of complete ignorance is discussed and the concept of quasi-ignorance is introduced as a substitute. Constraints on the probabilities, beyond the minimum, are a source of constemation and a stumbling block to the application of the principle, Many questions are raised, but no answers are given. At present, the principle cannot be evoked to solve practical problems in reliability. Theoreticians should apply themselves to find realistic tractable constraints that do not involve logical contradictions. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Evans R.A."]

Title: Two Stochastic Approximation Procedures for Identifying Linear Systems
Abstract: A Robbins-Monro [1] stochastic approximation procedure for identifying a finite memory time-discrete time-stationary linear system from noisy input-output measurements is developed. Two algorithms are presented to sequentially identify the linear system. The first one is derived, based on the minimization of the mean-square error between the unknown system and a model, and is shown to develop a bias which depends only on the variance of the input signal measurement error. Under the assumption that this variance is known a priori, a second algorithm is developed which, in the limit, identifies the unknown system exactly. The case when the covariance matrix of the random input sequence is not positive definite is also considered. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Holmes J.K."]

Title: Error Analysis, Sensitivity, and Prior Statistics
Abstract: Methods of statistical interference including estimation and modern filter theory are finding ever-increasing application in electrical engineering problems. Two problems which occur when methods of modern estimation theory are applied to a physical problem are the choice of prior statistics and the choice of a mathematical model for the system. This paper provides a fundamental and tutorial discussion of the role of error analysis, sensitivity, and prior statistics in classical point estimation. Thus, it provides the framework for study and research into varied aspects of this problem in more difficult and realistic situations. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Sage A.P."]

Title: EFFECT OF THE ERRORS OF CONTROL OF A SEARCH SYSTEM ON THE CHARACTERISTICS OF SIGNAL DETECTION
Abstract: A search system with random errors of control is investigated. The characteristics of detection and correct determination of the position of the signal are found. Their dependence on the number of cycles of surveying a given region is investigated. Some examples are presented.
Name: ["KUKSENKO HP", "REPIN VG"]

Title: Application of non-uniform quantization to closed-loop digital systems
Source: Journal of Physics E: Scientific Instruments
Abstract: When a digital computer acts as an on-line computational device in a closed-loop measurement or control system, the performance is degenerated by the quantization errors incurred in reading continuous data into the machine. The analysis presented in the paper shows that the increase in steady-state mean square error introduced by this degenerative effect can significantly be reduced by employing non-uniform quantization of input data. The resulting deterioration in transient performance is negligible. It is shown, under small signal conditions, that the spectrum of non-uniform quantization errors is essentially white. As a result, the expected maximum accuracy improvement in a given system can be easily evaluated. As a means of verifying the analysis, the performance of a practical direct digital control system employing non-uniform quantization is compared with a counterpart having uniform quantization. The steady state response to a spectral input shows an accuracy improvement equivalent to 7 bits. The technique of non-uniform quantization described in the paper is readily implemented to improve the steady state accuracy of an existing system, or alternatively for a given design-consistent accuracy, to economize in analogue-to-digital converter bit capacity.
Name: ["Edwards R.", "Durkin J."]

Title: APPLICATION OF STOCHASTIC APPROXIMATION ALGORITHMS TO AUTOMATIC CONTROL PROBLEMS IN PRESENCE OF STRONG INTERFERENCE
Abstract: It is assumed that interference dispersion is infinite, but that lower-order moment exists; convergence of stochastic approximation processes to desired point with probability one and in mean is proved.
Name: ["KRASULINA TP"]

Title: Reconstruction of fiducial marks and cameras utilizing simultaneously all the photographs available
Abstract: We describe in this paper a program to calculate a posteriori the coordinates of a set of points photographed by n cameras, together with the positions and orientations of the cameras, also not known a priori. The coordinates of the cameras are obtained by an unique fit, requiring the points measured on the pictures to be images of true points, existing somewhere in space. The coordinates of the points photographed are then easily obtained. ¬© 1969 The American Institute of Physics.
Name: ["Negri P."]

Title: STABILITY CONDITION OF AUTOMATIC CONTROL LOOP WITH DELAY TIME
Abstract: Approximate method for estimating stability of an automatic control loop with delay time is shown. The differences from other conceivable methods are described.
Name: ["TACHIBANA M"]

Title: DECOMPOSITIONAL DYNAMIC OPTIMIZATION OF PRODUCTION WITH HIERARCHIAL CONTROL STRUCTURE-2
Abstract: Adaptive control of group of nonstationary subsystems; Dantzig- Wolfe decomposition is extended; to form optimization algorithms for various methods of organizing control of complex nonstationary subsystems and to formalize definition of optimal number of levels in hierarchy in decompositional optimization; example is given.
Name: ["PLISKIN LG"]

Title: STOCHASTIC MODELS OF COMPUTERS FOR CHOICE OF FAST MEMORY PARAMETERS
Abstract: A twophase queueing model is studied -a computer model having fast memory devices. By investigation of the semi-Markov process connected with the system, expressions are obtained for the state probabilities and the mean serving time for one demand with various serving disciplines, corresponding to the application of fast memory devices of a given volume and different functions.
Name: ["DEGTYAREV EK"]

Title: On equal matrix languages
Abstract: A generative grammar called equal matrix grammar which generates a class which meets both context-sensitive and context-free languages is defined and the formal power series generated by context-free grammars is extended to grammars of this system. The Parikh mapping of this family of languages is shown to be semilinear. The Boolean and closure properties of a certain subfamily are examined. For this subfamily, the generative power of equal matrix grammar is higher than that of context-free grammars. For certain inherently ambiguous context-free languages, including that of Parikh, unambiguous grammars of this class exist. The application of equal matrix grammar to the generation of Tamil kernel sentences is given in the appendix. ¬© 1969 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Siromoney R."]

Title: EXPERIMENTAL MULTIFRONT PAGE READER
Abstract: The design concepts of an experimental page reader are described. Some indication of the performance expected and relative complexity is given. More detailed descriptions of particular procedures within the recognition logic may give a clearer impression of the manner by which features are located and character structures coded. Mention is made of logic simulation methods being used to design and prove hardware implementations previous to construction. Applications of the reader are discussed.
Name: ["THOMPSON J", "ALCORN TM"]

Title: STEADYSTATE MOTIONS IN AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS WITH A DEVIATING ARGUMENT
Abstract: A scheme of successive approximations for the exact solution over an infinite time interval is constructed; sufficient conditions for the existence of a steadystate solution are derived. Such systems occur frequently in the theory of nonlinear vibrational-rotational motions in systems whose parameters vary within a narrow range.
Name: ["AKULENKO LD"]

Title: THE DETERMINATION OF OPTIMAL CONTROL SEQUENCES FOR LINEAR DIGITALLY- CONTROLLED CONTINUOUS SYSTEMS USING A SUM-OF- ABSOLUTE- ERROR INDEX
Abstract: Bellman's principle of optimality is used to derive a feedback law in a multivariable sampled-data system with a sum- of- absolute- error performance index taken at sampling and intersampling instants. The optimum feedback coefficients and performance functions are calculated in reverse time by a computer program. The method is applicable to systems of any order, although the amount of computation required becomes prohibitive with high order systems. Two examples are presented, including a comparison with quadratic index design, and the advantages of the absolute value index are illustrated.
Name: ["BROWN WA"]

Title: An adaptive predictor of river flow for on line control of water resource systems
Abstract: The centralized control and administration of water systems including rivers, reservoirs, hydro-power plants and water gates has recently been considered in Japan for the purpose of the optimal control of water resource and the protection of damage by a flood. Forecasting of river flow is a fundamental problem to realize a real time control of water system. An adaptively modified model that represents the dynamic characteristics of process is used for prediction of river flow. The predictor is developed to satisfy the requirement for controlling reservoirs release. The computer system and its operation in the centralized control of the Sagami River is briefly introduced, and it has been successfully operated since April 1967. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Toyoda J.", "Toriumi N.", "Inoue Y."]

Title: COMPUTER SIMULATION OF LINEAR FILTERS AND OF THE TRANSMISSION OF RANDOM PROCESSES THROUGH THEM
Abstract: Using the envelope method and representing the filter impulse response and input voltage in discrete form, expressions are obtained for the response of a linear filter, that provide more convenient algorithms for use on digital computers. A method is suggested for selecting the sampling interval in the time domain.
Name: ["LIKHAREV VA"]

Title: SHAPE RECOGNITION DYNAMICS AND QUANTUM LOGIC
Abstract: A finite description of the shapes of objects belonging to a Hilbert space is sought. A model is presented in which the formalism of quantum mechanics is employed to '%'dynamically'%' extract shape and structure information from well defined mathematical objects that simulate stimuli from the outside world. These objects are assumed to have finite norm energy. The sensor system are transformed in such a way as to maximize the observalbe truncated norm. The structural and ergodic invariants that are used to describe compactly the shape of the objects under analysis.
Name: ["LOWITZ GE"]

Title: Tree generating regular systems
Abstract: Trees are defined as mappings from tree structures (in the graph-theoretic sense) into sets of symbols. Regular systems are defined in which the production rules are of the form Œ¶ ‚Üí œà, where Œ¶ and œà are trees. An application of a rule involves replacing a subtree Œ¶ by the tree œà. The main result is that the sets of trees generated by regular systems are exactly those that are accepted by tree automata. This generalizes a theorem of B√úchi, proved for strings. ¬© 1969 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Brainerd W.S."]

Title: Stimulus sampling learning models described as continuous-time stochastic processes
Abstract: In a previous work, an extension of the stimulus sampling theory to continuous-time learning models was introduced. A noncontingent reinforcement schedule occurring according to a Poisson process was then considered. The present article thoroughly investigates first properties of four continuous-time models which differ in their reinforcement schedules. Two are noncontingent and two are simply contingent; two occur according to a Poisson process, the other two are equally spaced in time. The response process is always two-valued and continuous in time. Fundamental equations are derived from the axioms, conditional probabilities computed and estimation procedures provided for the parameters. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Donio J."]

Title: Postsynaptic membrane response predicted from presynaptic input pattern in lobster cardiac ganglion
Abstract: Given the pattern of impulses impinging on a neuron, it should be possible to predict its output firing pattern if enough is known about pre- and postsynaptic properties. A quantitative reproduction of the first part of this input-output conversion is reported, namely the translation of input pattern into a sequence of postsynaptic membrane potential variations.
Name: ["Hartline D.K.", "Cooke I.M."]

Title: Some problems of information processing and models of the visual pathway
Abstract: The manner in which sensory information is processed depends on the structure as well as on the dynamic characteristics of the sensory organ and the processing stations in the sensory pathway. Some problems of visual information processing, arising from our presently available data, are formulated. They fall into the areas of information input, information processing in the retina and beyond the retina. Models relating to these problems are discussed with a view to obtaining a unified picture of information transfer in the visual pathway. The models are concerned, in particular, with psychophysical observations bearing on the serial capacity and the statistics of the information input, the static and dynamic characteristics of retinal receptive fields and a suggested approach to information processing beyond the retina. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Leibovic K.N."]
Affiliations: [' State University of New York at Buffalo']

Title: GENERALIZED TRANSFER CHAIN, (DIE VERALLGEMEINERTE UEBERTRAGUNGSKETTE
Abstract: For generalized feedback chain, eigen-, open loop- , reference and noise behavior and for generalized control chain reference behavior are described directly in such way that determinant and matrix calculus are avoided; idea of functional structural generalization of feedback and control principle originates from idea of information flow in intercerebral and efferent nerve fibers.
Name: ["STARKERMANN R"]

Title: Nonlinear estimation for partial differential equations
Abstract: The sequential estimation of the states of a process described by a set of nonlinear hyperbolic or parabolic partial differential equations subject to both stochastic input disturbances and measurement errors is considered. A functional partial differential equation of Hamilton-Jacobi type is derived for the minimum least square estimate error, which is solved approximately in the region of the optimal estimate by a second-order expansion. The optimal estimate is given as the solution of an initial value problem. In the linear case the estimator equations represent analogs of the well-known Kalman filter equations for lumped parameter systems. The determination of the state of a process governed by one-dimensional heat equation from noisy measurements is considered. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Seinfeld J.H."]

Title: MULTIPLE-WIRING ALGORITHM
Abstract: This paper proposes an algorithm for automatic design of patterns for aluminum interconnections and printed wiring in integrated circuits. In algorithms thus far proposed for this purpose, the wiring order is sequential and no consideration can be given to the effects of wires added later in the sequence. To overcome this disadvantage the algorithm proposed in this paper provides for calculation of the probabilities of all wiring patterns of the circuit and at the same time simplifies the calculation procedures for relocation of wiring.
Name: ["NISHIKAWA S", "UTSUNOMIYA T"]

Title: Information-processing analysis of perceptual processes in problem solving
Abstract: Proposed a theory to explain, in information-processing terms, some common phenomena in the initial perceptual phases of problem solving, to show that some existing computer programs for heuristic search and learning already contain basic processes that will produce these phenomena, and to show how simple organizations of the processes enable the programs to parallel human behavior. The theory is particularized in a computer program to simulate the eye movements, during the 1st 5 sec., of Ss choosing a move in chess. The application of the theory is illustrated and its consistency is shown with data on memory of chess positions and with existing knowledge of short-term memory parameters. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2006 APA, all rights reserved). ¬© 1969 American Psychological Association.
Name: ["Simon H.A.", "Barenfeld M."]
Keywords: ["problem solving visual information processing analysis computer program", "perceptual processes", "basic processes", "analysis perceptual", "processing analysis"]

Title: A Theory of Bayesian Learning Systems
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics
Abstract: Efforts are made to simplify the implementation and to improve the flexibility of Bayesian learning systems. Using a truncated series expansion to represent a pattern class, a simplified structure is shown with nearly optimal performance. A criterion of determining the learning sample size is given so that after taking a sufficient number of learning observations, the system may elect to learn by itself without relying on the external supervision. A time-varying random parameter is approximated by the polynomial with random coefficients. The Bayes estimates of the coefficients are obtained sequentially from the useful information in the learning observations. The condition for convergence of the unsupervised learning is established and shown to be closely related to the selection of the characteristic features. The system retains the same structure in both supervised and unsupervised learning processes with either the stationary or the time-varying random parameter. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Chen C.-H."]

Title: EXPERIENCE IN THE PRACTICAL REALIZATION OF ALGORITHMS FOR THE RECOVERY OF LIKELIHOOD FUNCTIONS BY THE POTENTIAL-FUNCTION METHOD
Abstract: Questions are considered in connection with the practical realization of algorithms for the recovery of confidence functions by the potential-function method. A model problem is used to investigate the influence of the choice of potential functions, the U-series, the order of arrival on the choice of potential function and the construction of the decision rule for the confidence function.
Name: ["GUKOVSKII DE", "RAEV AG"]

Title: HEURISTIC METHODS OF SOLVING CERTAIN SUPPLY CONTROL PROBLEMS
Abstract: Using example of problem of attaching consumers to suppliers certain theoretical difficulties often encountered in problem of supply control and planning are discussed; considerations are advanced in support of elaboration of heuristic algorithms for this kind of problem and basic ideas and most important details of heuristic algorithms for attachment problem are discussed.
Name: ["LERNER AYA", "TSEL'MAN FKH"]

Title: Optimal Synthesis of Arbitrary Switching Functions with Regular Arrays of 2-Input 1-Output Switching Elements
Abstract: Most switching functions are not realizable by a single cascade of 2-input 1-output switching elements, even if repeated inputs are allowed. However, arrays of such cascades feeding a single collector cascade of AND or OR cells can be used to synthesize any function. This paper is concerned with optimal array realizations of this form. A procedure is given which allows one to generate rather efficiently all prime cascade realizable functions which imply a given switching function. These prime functions may be restricted to those realizable by a single cascade either with or without repeated inputs. To solve problems of optimal single output array synthesis, allowing incompletely specified functions, it is necessary only to select a minimum cost cover from the set of prime cascade realizable functions. Each function used in the cover may be realized very easily, and the resulting cascades supply the inputs to the collector cascade. Extensions are made to the simultaneous realization of several switching functions, each being the output of a separate collector cascade fed from the same array. ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Weiss C.D."]
Keywords: ["input 1-output switching elements", "arrays of cascades", "incompletely specified functions", "multiple output realizations", "optimal array realizations"]

Title: Calculated Quantizing Noise of Single‚ÄêIntegration Delta‚ÄêModulation Coders
Abstract: We calculate the granular quantizing noise for a delta modulator that has unequal positive and negative step sizes. The asymmetry leads to a highly colored noise spectrum. We perform this calculation by adding a ramp function of time to the input of a symmetrical coder. The resulting formulas can also be used for uniform DPCM and PCM coders. The idle‚Äêchannel spectrum consists of discrete lines which scatter somewhat irregularly in amplitude and frequency, they can be regarded as the result of sampling (aliasing) a sawtooth wave. These lines are phase‚Äêmodulated by a coder input. For a sinusoidal input, discrete side frequencies are produced which again have an irregular progression of amplitudes. Gaussian inputs lead, to gaussian line shapes; the lines broaden as input power is increased. A totally white spectrum (as is often assumed in connection with delta‚Äêmodulation‚Äêsystem considerations) cannot be attained, however, before the onset of slope overload. We give a numerical example that uses a coder suitable for telephone applications. One can see that step asymmetry can be very advantageous in attaining low noise. ¬© 1969 The Bell System Technical Journal
Name: ["Iwersen J.E."]

Title: Optimum Estimation of Nonstationary Gaussian Signals in Noise
Abstract: This paper treats the problem of estimating a signal s (t) in the presence of noise n (t) where s (t) and n (t) are independent nonstationary Gaussian processes. Specifically, we present the maximum likelihood and the minimum mean-square estimates of s(t) for each t, T1< t< T2, by observing the entire signal-plus-noise waveform x(¬∑) during the interval [T1, T2]. Under the condition that the signal cannot be detected perfectly in the presence of noise, we explicity prove that both estimates, denoted by s(t), are given by E{s(t)|x(.)}, the conditional expectation of s(t) given x(.) With the use of simultaneously orthogonal expansions of x(t) and n(t) we further obtain explicit expressions in the form of infinite series for s(t) and e(t) = E|s (t) - s(t)|2, the minimum mean-square error. Moreover, if the integral equation ¬© 1969 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Kadota T.T."]

Title: Automatic determination of crystal structure
Abstract: Several crystallographic computer programs have been organized into one large automatic program for solving crystal structures. The emphasis of this organization has been to produce a noninteractive system, that is, to have all decisions made by the computer. Input data are the raw intensity data, cell constants, space group, chemical formula, and other miscellaneous items. The output is a stereo picture of the contents in a unit cell. The program, operating in a noninteractive mode, has successfully solved compounds of unknown structure; in addition, for a test compound of completely unknown composition, this program deduced the correct structure with an average error in bond distance of 0.05 angstrom and an average error in bond angle of 7¬∞.
Name: ["Johnson Q.", "Smith G.S.", "Kahara E."]

Title: On the Length of Programs for Computing Finite Binary Sequences: Statistical considerations
Abstract: An attempt is made to carry out a program (outlined in a previous paper) for defining the concept of a random or patternless, finite binary sequence, and for subsequently defining a random or patternless, infinite binary sequence to be a sequence whose initial segments are all random or patternless finite binary sequences. A definition based on the bounded-transfer Turing machine is given detailed study, but insufficient understanding of this computing machine precludes a complete treatment. A computing machine is introduced which avoids these difficulties. ¬© 1969, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Chaitin G.J."]

Title: Application of Coupled Films to Memory Elements
Abstract: A review of multilayer film applications to memory elements is given. Among the topics discussed are the development of creep-free elements by use of multilayer or composite films, the application of magnetostatica1ly coupled films and of exchange coupled films for DRO and NDRO memories, and finally the potential applications of multilayer films to magnetooptic memories. The latter includes multilayer films made of two strongly ferromagnetic films separated by a low-Curie-temperature intermediate layer. Their coercivity changes rapidly with temperature and this original property can be used to make magnetooptic memories. ¬© 1969, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Bruyere J.-C.", "Massenet O."]

Title: A Model for Generating On‚ÄêOff Speech Patterns in Two‚ÄêWay Conversation
Abstract: This paper describes a model that generates on‚Äêoff speech patterns representative of those in experimental two‚Äêway telephone conversations. The model assumes a conversant to occupy one of three speaking or one of three silent states. Transitions among the states arc determined by Poisson processes governed by six parameters (one for each state). The validity of the model is tested by comparing the model computer simulation of 16 conversations with 16 real conversations. Cumulative distribution functions are compared for ten events (such as talkspurts, pauses, mutual silences, and so on) defined on the speech patterns. The model yields good fits to all events except ‚Äúspeech before interruption‚Äù when an interruption occurs, a model speaker tends to interrupt the other's talkspurt later than a real speaker does. Theoretical behavior of the model is also studied. All events consist of concatenations of exponentially distributed ‚Äústate durations,‚Äù even though most events are not themselves exponential. For some purposes, the exponential distribution is a satisfactory empirical fit to talkspurts, but not to pauses. Possible applications of the model include studying people's motivations to talk and fall silent on different circuits, and predicting statistical behavior of voice operated devices on the circuits. ¬© 1969 The Bell System Technical Journal
Name: ["Brady P.T."]

Title: ADVANCES IN INFORMATION SYSTEMS SCIENCE.
Abstract: Learning systems which play an important role in artificial intelligence research are first considered, and basic principles for a unified approach to the problem of designing these systems are presented. The data-processing requirements of pattern recognition and machine learning are then presented, and the concept of stochastic computing through the representation of analog quantities by the probabilities of discrete events is introduced. Recent research on the semantics of programming languages is reviewed. Detailed attention is also given to information storage and retrieval systems. Finally, some characteristics of human information processing, which is useful in the study of man-machine systems, are dealt with.
Name: ["Tou Julius T."]

Title: On synchronous variable length coding for discrete noiseless chrannels
Abstract: A method is presented for finding the shortest variable length codes with a given bit per symbol ratio for discrete noiseless channels. The central feature of the procedure is a dynamic programming algorithm for determining the optimal code paths. Bounds are found for the channel capacity. ¬© 1969 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Franaszek P.A."]

Title: ASSIGNMENT PROCEDURE IN AUTOMATIC MILTI-RADAR OBSERVATION SYSTEMS, | [DAS ZUORDNUNGSVERFAHREN IM AUTOMATISCHEN MULTI- RADARBEOBACHTUNGSSYSTEM]
Abstract: With a flying object being tracked independently by two radars of a MULTI-RADAR- System, the problem arises, how to recognize the tracks as representations of the same object. A possible assignment precedure is described.
Name: ["GALLREIN D"]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF A CLASS OF OPTIMAL DISCRETE SYSTEMS FOR TRAJECTORY CORRECTION OF DYNAMIC SYSTEMS IN THE PRESENCE OF CONSTRAINTS, MEASUREMENT ERRORS, AND ERRORS IN GENERATING THE CONTROL PARAMETERS
Abstract: The miximum deviation of a certain function in the presence of arbitrary type restrictions is minimized. For the case of small disturbances the problem is reduced to standard linear programming algorithms with the help of a special choice of the scheme of calculation. The structure of the optimal solution of the problem for the cases of incomplete, complete, and redundant information is defined.
Name: ["KUZMAK GE", "CHARNYAVSKAYA IYU"]

Title: An Algorithm for Minimum Energy Control
Abstract: This paper presents a very effective, large step, parametric method for solving fixed time, minimum energy, discrete optimal control problems with linear plants, and convex constraints on the terminal state. The reason for using parametrization is that it removes the usual severe ill-conditioning effects. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Elijah Polak E.P.", "Deparis M."]
Affiliations: [' University of California', 'Service Technique de Construction des Armes Navales']

Title: Computer-oriented automation in chemical analysis of soils
Abstract: The requirements of equipment to extend the Technicon system of automated analysis to provide digital results for computation are discussed. A system of commercial modules, which permits peak values to be sensed, digitised and transmitted to either a computer or a paper tape punch, is described. Regression methods are used to fit calibration graphs for accurate interpolation of unknown samples. Further advantage is gained from the system if subsequent calculations are to be made on the computed concentrations.
Name: ["Keay J."]

Title: THE PROBLEM OF OPTIMAL CONTROL FOR THE DESCENT OF A SPACE VEHICLE IN THE ATMOSPHERE
Abstract: Problem of controlling the descent of a spacecraft. Reduction to problem of the optimal control of the final state of a stochastic system. The control algorithm is constructed with the use of the nominal trajectory and g-force measurements are considered to be the information source. The problems of programming the nominal trajectory of the motion and achieving the conditions under which it can in fact be realized are considered jointly.
Name: ["VLASOV AG", "MITROSHIN EI", "UKOLOV IS"]

Title: Time optimal control of time varying third order plants
Abstract: It has been shown that time invariant third order plants can be time optimally controlled by a hybrid computer. The computer generates a time optimal switching surface, which it then uses to control the plant. [1]. This paper presents an extension of this approach to slow time varying plants, by automatically updating the switching surface. The effects that parameter changes have on the response of the plant and on the switching surface are investigated. It is shown that by rescaling the switching surface, the effects of parameter changes on the plant's response could be minimised. A method is then presented for the time optimal control of time varying plants. The method consists of on-line identification of the time varying parameters and the continuous updating of the switching surface to maintain time optimal control. ¬© 1969 Presses Acad√©miques Europ√©ennes, Brussels.
Name: ["Yastreboff M."]

Title: The Block-Oriented Computer
Abstract: LSI will have a profound effect on the design of computer systems ranging from evolutionary changes in implementation to revolutionary changes in basic architecture. This paper discusses a computer composed of an array of processors. Entire wafers are used, rather than wafers diced into chips. The computer utilizes software to substitute process elements for the purpose of compensating for imperfect yield on the wafer. The computer organization possesses a property called block orientation which permits the use of whole LSI wafers with low yields without requiring a secondary metalization manufacturing step. Through the use of a unique computing algorithm, the parallelism and communication problems inherent to array processors are minimized. Processing systems of the sort discussed can possess a self-healing capability. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Campeau J.O."]
Keywords: ["array processor", "computer organization", "high reliability", "implicit function generation", "large-scale integration"]

Title: NOTE ON TOTALLY UNATE STATE ASSIGNMENT FOR SEQUENTIAL MACHINE
Abstract: The problem of assigning states in such a way that the state function for a sequential machine is unate for each of the variables is an interesting problem since it is related to the complexity involved in realizing a state function by means of a single threshold element or by use of more than one decision element. A method is described whereby the authors set up various conditions to narrow the range of possibility and finally conclude by carrying out some state assignments. A sequential machine with less than eight states and a single input variable is considered in this note.
Name: ["DOHI Y", "TOHMA Y"]

Title: A learning model for inventory of slow-moving items
Abstract: Probabilistic inventory models assume that demand follows a stable distribution with known parameters. This assumption is reasonable where substantial demand history is available under stable conditions. However, for slow-moving items, such as maintenance items, usually little history is available. In such cases, the assumption of known parameters seems unnecessarily arbitrary. We present here a model that takes into account the uncertainty of the unknown parameters, determines the optimal inventory decision, updates the original distribution assumptions as the passage of time increases our information concerning the parameters, and determines optimal policy. ¬© Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Smith B.E.", "Vemuganti R.R."]

Title: On the mean square approximation of a function with a linear combination of exponentials
Abstract: This paper deals with the problem of finding the 2N coefficients of a linear combination of N exponentials which minimizes its mean square error from a given function f(t). The real difficulty lies in the determination of the optimal exponents. A real function of N real variables is constructed, such that the points where it is minimal give the optimal exponents. Such a function may be considered as the sample for t = T of the response to f(T‚Äît) of a simple system. This implementation allows a significant simplification of the given problem from a computational point of view, for instance by hybrid methods. ¬© 1969 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Marzollo A."]

Title: On startup or learning curves: An expanded view
Abstract: The startup or learning curve literature has in the past concentrated mainly on the algebraic power function or on versions based on this function. This concentration is not unusual because the power function has proven, in numerous studies, to fit empirical data quite well. However, other easy-to-apply algebraic functions should also be analyzed and considered. One such function, an exponential function, is discussed and is shown to provide a better fit to several sets of empirical data than the traditional power function. In addition to providing a better fit, this exponential function is easy to apply in practice. ¬© Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Pegels C.C."]

Title: BOOLEAN LOGIC AND AUTOMATED DOCUMENTATION, | [LOGIQUE BOOLEENNE ET SEMANTIQUE DOCUMENTAIRE]
Abstract: The fundamental principle of this system is the use of a boolean searching logic which examines the words of the textual data. Searching is not limited to descriptors or keywords. Thus, since the data base contains the language of the original document, the search questions or profiles can use the same kind of normal language words.
Name: ["DUBON RJ"]

Title: Sch√§tzung der Bestimmungsgr√ºnde von Rangfolgen
Abstract: We assume that every ranking is determined by a "ranking criterium", which is a linear function of certain independent variables. As in the case of multiple regression, the form of this function is determined from past experience. However, other than is the multiple regression, we assume that the dependent variable, the ranking criterium, is unknown and that it can be inferred by comparisons only. The estimation is done using linear programming. Practical applications are given. ¬© 1969 Physica-Verlag.
Name: ["Grassmann W.K."]

Title: CORNELL IMPLEMENTATION OF THE SMART SYSTEM
Source: Cornell Univ-Dept of Computer Science -Sci Report ISR-16
Abstract: The SMART system is design for the exploration, testing and measurement of proposed algorithms for document retrieval. The systems organization of the SMART programs is discussed as implemented for operation in a batch processing mode on the IBM 360/65. Covered in particular are the basic input and text analysis routines, the document clustering programs, the search routines and the feedback operations. Sample computer output is shown in each case to illustrate the operations.
Name: ["WILLIAMSON D", "WILLIAMSON R", "LESK M"]

Title: BIBLIOGRAPHIC DATA AS AN AID TO DOCUMENT RETRIEVAL
Source: Cornell Univ-Dept of Computer Science-Sci Report ISR-16
Abstract: The hypothesis that bibliographic data added to a SMART style document collection will improve retrieval effectiveness is tested. Two uncommon kinds of biblimgraphic data, authors and place of publication, are used to build concept matrices. These matrices are used with associated queries in a typical retrieval environment involving relevance feedback. With the aid of a new statistic, it is found that these matrices actually do aid retrieval.
Name: ["MCNEILL JW", "WETHERELL CS"]

Title: METHOD OF DIAGNOSTIC TEST GENERATION
Abstract: In method of generating test cases for diagnosing a machine using high density circuitry, minimal and sufficient set of path tests can be generated by a simple algorithm working on a graph representation of the machine. Combinational logic networks can be diagnosed by a set of test input patterns generated by a procedure described. Logic simulator which uses a general purpose programming language as the simulator media, and several methods of fault location.
Name: ["CARROLL AB", "KATO M", "KOGA Y", "NAEMURA K"]

Title: MACHINE GENERATION OF INFORMATION RETRIEVAL INDEXES
Abstract: The computer processes utilized at the University of Tulsa for generating printed indexes to the Petroleum Abstracts bulletin are described. An Alphabetic Subject Index is generated at monthly intervals, in which the titles of the various abstracts are given multiple listings, under appropriate descriptor headings. In addition, Dual Dictionary Coordinate Indexes are prepared at 4-mo intervals, for more sophisticated searching. Master Record Tapes for computer searching are also issued at 4-mo intervals. Thesesearching tools have resulted in improved retrievability of desired information, and have greatly increased the value of the abstracting operation.
Name: ["MARTINEZ SJ", "ANIS M", "BUTHOD P", "HELANDER DP"]

Title: GENERATING VARIABLE-LENGTH CODES FROM GRAPHS
Abstract: This paper presents a method for obtaining a variable-length D- nary exhaustive prefix code X given a weighted, nondirected graph. It is seen that such a code may be decoded by a network determined from the structure of the given graph. It is demonstrated that a given graph also defines an additional exhaustive prefix code X', called the dual code of X. For one terminal-pair planar graphs, relationships resulted in additional flexibility in the decoding of graph theoretic variable-length codes.
Name: ["BOBROW LS", "HAKIMI SL"]

Title: EXPERIMENTS WITH A FAST ALGORITHM FOR AUTOMATIC CLASSIFICATION
Source: Cornell Univ-Dept of Computer Science-Sci Report ISR-16
Abstract: An algorithm is described for automatically classifying items in a document collection into useful clusters in a reasonably amount of time. The algorithm is first presented in a general form, and a proof is given which describes how the time needed to classify a given collection is related to the number of documents in the collection. Clusters are produced for two different document collections, and the results are evaluated by performing centroid searches on the clustered collection. Finally, a new evaluation measure is defined, and comparisons are made with clusters produced by other automatic methods.
Name: ["DATTOLA RT"]

Title: Reduction of context- free grammars
Abstract: The problem of fining the simplest grammar among the grammars which generat the same language as a given context- free grammar (FG)is treated. It is theoretically possibleto find the simpest grammar fromthestrucurally equivalent context- free grammars. Several propertie of %the simplest grammar which s structurally equivalent to the given CFG are studied. By utilizing thoseproperties, a fairly efficient method is developed for the reduction of th grammars. It is also proved that there exists no general algorithm which will find the simplest among the context- free grammars which are weakly equivalent to a given CFG.
Name: ["TANIGUCHI K", "KASAMI"]

Title: LEADER RETRIEVAL SYSTEM
Abstract: Service-oriented prototype designed to meet the retrieval needs of research scientists provides very highly user-oriented facility for the negotiation of open-ended inquiries and interactive browsing. System includes on-line processing of requests, using a novel and relatively inexpensive hardware configuration, and serialorganizes its output in the form of document references, citations to documents, and complete textual passages selected from one or several documents, in any way that the user specifies. Principal design features and system implementation.
Name: ["HILLMAN DJ", "KASARDA AJ"]

Title: ON THE PROBLEM OF COMPUTATIONAL TIME AND COMPLEXITY OF ARITHMETIC FUNCTIONS
Abstract: NO-ABSTRACT
Name: ["AVIZIENIS A"]

Title: CONSTRUCTION OF AN OPTIMAL ACCESS TREE FOR DATA ORGANIZATIONS WITHIN A DATA BASE, | [DIE KONSTRUKTION EINES OPTIMALEN ZUGRIFFSBAUMES FUER DATENORGANISATIONEN INNERHALB EINER DATENBANK]
Abstract: Linear data organizations are discussed along with the nonlinear structure of records and segments in data bases. The segmented records of a file are stored and retrieved according to a procedure given by E.H.Sussenguth. An algorithm is presented to minimize the expected value of the access number.
Name: ["WEDEKIND H"]

Title: RECOGNITION SYSTEM USING PROBABILISTIC DECISIONS BASED ON EXTRACTED FEATURES
Abstract: NO-ABSTRACT
Name: ["MURDEN P", "SYMONS M"]

Title: STABILITY OF SYSTEMS WITH CONSERVATIVE PLANTS, | [STABILNOSC UKLADOW Z OBIEKTAMI KONSERWATYWNYMI]
Abstract: Dynamic properties of automatic feedback control systems with linear conservative plants are investigated; it is assumed that controllers are of certain nonlinear types; conditions of asymptotic stability of equilibrium points.
Name: ["PALUSINSKI O"]

Title: Computer-program description general least-squares program for fitting functions to data
Abstract: A program is described which attempts to fit any function specified in a procedure, to a set of data. The values of a fixed number of disposable constants are systematically adjusted to minimise the sum of squares of differences between values and corresponding points of the function. An example is given of the use of the program in the analysis of an experimental autocorrelation function. ¬© 1969, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Murgatroyd P.N."]
Affiliations: ['H. H. Wills Physics Laboratory University of Bristol Royal Fort']

Title: CERTAIN METHOD OF SEQUENTIAL SEARCHING FOR EXTREMUM OF REGRESSION FUNCTION WHICH BELONGS TO LIPM 1 CLASS, | [0 PEWNEJ METODZIE SEKWENCYJNEGO POSZUKIWANIA EKSTREMUM FUNKCJI REGRESJI KLASY LIPM 1]
Abstract: Properties of approximation of regression function constructed in form of bands are investigated; it is assumed that regression functions taken into consideration belong to LipM 1 class; approximating bands are determined on base of confidence limits which estimate values of regression function at certain points; method is derived which makes it possible to solve problem of searching for extremum of regression function which belongs to given class.
Name: ["KACPRZYNSKI B"]

Title: ADAPTIVE FILTER. A COMPONENT FOR USE IN PATTERN RECOGNITION AND TRAINABLE SYSTEMS
Abstract: A method for implementing an adaptive filter which can be trained to seek an optimal center frequency is described. The method uses a novel combination of an operational amplifier and digital-to-analog converters to achieve the desired adaptive bandpass characteristics. A detailed description of the adaptive filter is given, and its application in pattern recognition systems is discussed.
Name: ["IDELSOHN JM", "NADON DJ", "MOORE J"]

Title: MACHINE IDENTIFICATION CONCEPTS OF PATH SENSITIZING FAULT DIAGNOSIS
Abstract: It is demonstrated that the path sensitizing diagnosis method is equivalent to a Moore type '%'machine identification'%' experiment for a machine class which contains good and faulty copies of a transmission path submachine of a complete machine. For memoryless irredundant machines the fault resolution power of a complete set of path sensitizing tests is, nevertheless, the maximum which is possible if no submachine with a fault is used as a sensitizing vehicle. The use of the pathsensitizing method in irredundant sequential machines with memory, on the other hand, may not yield the maximum fault resolution power.
Name: ["KRIZ TA"]

Title: INFORMATION RETRIEVAL AND NATURAL LANGUAGE
Abstract: Arguments for automated information retrieval systems which use various scientific linguistic methods in their underlying systems to analyze and interpret structure and semantic content of each sentence; techniques used and experience gathered in course of building two models for use of English language for information retrieval purposes; several proposals for dealing with ambiguity of natural language sentences.
Name: ["MOYNE JA"]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR DETERMINING CHROMATIC NUMBER OF FINITE GRAPH
Source: Economic Computation & Economic Cybernetics Studies & Research
Abstract: Generalization of procedure given by D. Welsh and M. Powell for obtaining upper bound of chromatic number of finite graph, as well as algorithm allowing accurate measurements of chromatic number and of partition realizing it, by building rooted tree which takes into account maximal independent sets of graph; algorithm, as well as application of concept of pushdown stack, are described.
Name: ["TOMESCU I"]

Title: THRESHOLD LOGIC. A SIMPLIFIED SYNTHESIS BY A RECURSIVE METHOD
Abstract: The scope of this paper is to describe the theoretical basis of a direct and efficient synthesis method for a threshold function(s) from its Boolean expression. A set of recursive formulas of weight and threshold is thus derived. This method is capable of handling a relatively large number of Boolean variables, whether the Boolean expression is a single threshold function or compound threshold functions. The minimal realization of the Boolean threshold function can also be obtained.
Name: ["SHA RT", "SZE TW"]

Title: TERMINAL CONTROL OF LINEAR DISTRIBUTED PARAMETER SYSTEM BY LINEAR PROGRAMMING
Source: Kansas State Univ-Institute for Systems Design & Optimization-Report 17
Abstract: Literature on the optimal terminal control of linear distributed parameter systems by means of the linear programming technique is reviewed. Some suggestions are made which may facilitate computational aspects of the problem. A brief account of the theory of linear programming is also given.
Name: ["HUANG HS", "FAN LT", "HWANG CL"]

Title: CLUSTER MAPPING WITH EXPERIMENTAL COMPUTER GRAPHICS
Abstract: This paper deals with a cluster approach to unsupervised estimation of the component probability density functions (PDF) of a mixture of PDF's. It is assumed that vector samples are independently drawn from a finite mixture of multivariate gaussian, class conditional PDF's. The samples from the mixture, which are in the observation space, are mapped to the parameter space containing the fixed but unknown parameters characterizing the mixture. Each sample vector is mapped to a point in the parameter space. The mapping is such that samplesfrom a single component distribution map to a tight cluster in the parameter space. The tight clusters in the parameter space can be displayed on a computer out%put display for interactive identification of the classes.
Name: ["PATRICK EA", "FISCHER FP", "II"]

Title: ON STOCHASTIC AUTOMATA AND LANGUAGES
Abstract: For the conventional lambda-stochastic languages, a flexible stochastic experimental procedure based on Chebyshev's inequality is proposed. Then, the class of maximum-likelihood stochastic languages is defined on the basis of the maximum-likelihood final- state distribution. Properties of this class of languages and its relationship to lambda-stochastic languages are investigated.
Name: ["FU KS", "LI TJ"]

Title: FACTORS AFFECTING TIME BOUNDS OF PARSING PROCEDURES
Abstract: The time complexity of context-free parsing procedures is studied in the framework of reduction systems for problem solving. It is shown how variations in the time bounds of these procedures are related to, and can be explained in terms of, differences in their control mechanisms.
Name: ["KORENJAK AJ", "WALTERS DA"]

Title: GENERAL CONTROL-SYSTEM ANALYSIS BY DIGITAL COMPUTER USING OPERATIONAL-ARRAY TECHNIQUE
Abstract: A novel approach called the 'operationalarray technique' in the frequency domain is outlined. The aim is to p%rovide computer- aided system analysis and synthesis translated into control- engineering terms in a readily usable computational form. All instructions are given to the computer through the data. Changing the zeros and poles for optimization purposes or introducing compensation networks with additional zeros and poles becomes a matter of changing the arrays in the data, leaving the main program untouched. The method may be extended to time response, and root- locus computation. An example shows how the scheme is implemented in the frequency domain.
Name: ["N-NAGY FL", "AL-TIKRITI MN"]

Title: DENSE AND NON-DENSE FAMILIES OF COMPLEXITY CLASSES
Abstract: Turing machine model introduced by J. Hartmanis and R. E. Stearns is used. It uses separate input, output and work tapes and uses the standard finite control over a finite alphabet. Authors consider the class of all such machines over all finite alphabets.
Name: ["BORODIN A", "CONSTABLE RL", "HOPCROFT JE"]

Title: TASK-INDEPENDENT EXPERIENCE- GATHERING SCHEME FOR A PROBLEM- SOLVER
Abstract: NO-ABSTRACT
Name: ["QUINLAN JR"]

Title: ON A GENERALIZATION OF THE HO-KASHYAP ALGORITHM TO MULTI- CLASS PATTERN CLASSIFICATION
Abstract: A new algorithm is proposed for multiclass pattern classification which is a generalization, without constraint, of the Ho-Kashyap dichotomization algorithm. It is different from the generalization due to W. G. Wee and K. S. Fu; for large number of training patterns, it requires the generalized inverse of a smaller matrix and hence may be advantageous for some problems.
Name: ["TENG TL", "LI CC"]

Title: ON THE REPRESENTATION OF FORMAL LANGUAGES USING AUTOMATA ON NETWORKS
Abstract: Each normal network N provided with a one-way input tape determines a family of languages Nl. A representation theorem, analogous to the Chomsky-Schuetzenberger representation theorem for context free languages, is proved for the class Nl. One consequence is that Nl is a principlal full AFL generated by a closed set (one that contains all its prefixes). The converse is also proved, thereby establishing an equivalence between families of languages defined by normal networks and principal full AFLsgenerated by closed sets. The representation theorem is applied to the push-down store and Turing machine networks to obtain a stronger version of the Ginsburg, Greibach, and Harrison representation theorem for recursively enumerable sets.
Name: ["FISHER GA", "RANEY GN"]

Title: QUERY CLUSTERING IN A LARGE DOCUMENT SPACE
Source: Cornell Univ-Dept of Computer Science-Sci Report ISR-16
Abstract: The Cranfield 424 document collection is clustered using queries and known relevance judgments. This clustering method is compared to a full search of the collection, and several searches using a standard clustering technique. Several new evaluation parameters are defined and applied to the experiment.
Name: ["WORONA S"]

Title: ON PROBABILISTIC AUTOMATA WITH STRUCTURAL RESTRICTIONS
Abstract: Two generalizations of the theory of loop-free decomposition of stochastic finite-state systems formulated by G. Bacon are presented. It is shown that there exist stochastic finite-state systems which admit a loop-free decomposition for a proper subset of the set of all initial distributions on their state set, while both Bacon's theory and first generalization hold for the set of all initial distributions. Sufficient conditions are given in both cases. Linear probabilistic automata (LPA) are introduced. It is shown that if a mod-2 LPA has a critical cutpoint, then this cutpoint is unique.
Name: ["GELENBE SE"]

Title: SIGNAL FLOW GRAPHS AND THEIR NODAL IMAGES, | [GRAPHES REI ET LEURS IMAGES NODALES]
Source: Rev Roumaine des Sciences Techniques-Series Electrotechnique at Energetique
Abstract: Use of graphs and their nodal images for development of new type of man-machine '%'dialog'%'. Graphs may be used for constant and permanent visualization of computer control states whose studied function is displayed by simultaneous use of two elementary geometric structures, i. e. radial and in series structures. Generality of these two concepts is shown and example of economic application discussed.
Name: ["DIMO P"]

Title: Stochastic sampling character-recognition system
Abstract: The sampling of characters by segments of a maximum-length sequence is the basis of an adaptive multifont character-recognition system. The results of simulation experiments are included. ¬© 1969, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Buykes J.", "Mau A.", "Stein A.", "Thompson L.", "Youssef T."]

Title: ROBOT CONTROL STRATEGY
Abstract: Experimental test of behavioral theory of information processing based on ethological observations by programming robot control system.
Name: ["FRIEDMAN L"]

Title: SINGLE PASS CLUSTERING METHOD
Source: Cornell Univ-Dept of Computer Science-Sci Report ISR-16
Abstract: In information retrieval, several complex clustering methods exist which require extensive processing time and computer memory. A cheap clustering method is developed which requires only one pass over the document collection to generate clusters. The one-pass clustering method is investigated using the ADI collection of 82 documents and 35 queries which is available on-line in the SMART system. Clusters formed are not of uniform size; one or two early clusters are exceptionally large. Variation of the minimum correlation cutoff value is an adequate control for the number of clusters generated. The effect of document order on theclustering method is investigated, and the results are inconclusive. Overall, the single-pass clustering method is surprisingly effective and compares favorably with more complicated clustering methods.
Name: ["RIEBER S", "MARATHE VP"]

Title: OPTIMUM PREFILTERING IN RANDOMLY-SAMPLED DATA SYSTEMS
Abstract: The problem of simultaneous optimum meansquare linear prefiltering and postfiltering for randomly-sampled processes is considered. The optimum prefilter is shown to satisfy an integral equation. For a class of input signals, using the Poisson sampling scheme, the optimum prefilter is shown to truncate the input spectrum to within a finite interval. The discussion is then extended to include jitter, random skips, and sampling errors in amplitude.
Name: ["MASRY E", "LIU B"]

Title: Optimization of a time-variable, constrained control matrix
Source: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
Abstract: The problem posed is to choose, in a optimal manner, a time-variable, bounded, linear transformation defining the velocity of a state point in n-dimensional space in terms of the state. The two-point boundary-value problem which arises from an application of the Pontryagin maximum principle is explicitly solvable; hence, a formula is derived showing that the optimal trajectories in state space are equiangular spirals in two-dimensional subspaces of R<sup>n</sup> and also describing the boundary of the set of attainability. This formula is used to solve the problem of minimal-time transfer between any two given points, and the optimal control is specified both as an open-loop and a closed-loop controller. The solutions to the problem of maximizing a linear payoff function of the final state and of maximizing the angle of rotation of the state vector about the origin are also given. ¬© 1969 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Lawden G.H."]

Title: PATHFINDING ALGORITHM FOR AUTONOMOUS ROVING VEHICLE
Abstract: Paper discusses routing algorithm-consisting of global and local mode-which has been proposed for controlling roving vehicle; applicable in unmanned exploration of Martian surface.
Name: ["KIRK DE", "LIM LY"]

Title: OPTIMIZING CONTROL USING ADAPTIVE MODEL
Abstract: Authors give a realization of the concept for the adaptive optimization using a static model in the steady state optimizing control of a process, and present the necessary conditions which the adaptive model must satisfy, and give the analytical representation for the effectiveness of the adaptation technique.
Name: ["HARUNA K", "ISHIKAWA T"]

Title: DISCRETE CONTROL AS A TRANSPORTATION PROBLEM
Abstract: Previous work has made possible the discretization of the state space and control space such that corresponding to any discrete initial state, there is a unique control sequence which takes the initial state to zero in n steps. Based on the control requirements, it is possible to induce a norm-determined, neighborhood topology on the state space which yields the discretization. The results provide for the formulation of a class of control problems which can be considered in terms of sequential routing problems in transportation systems.
Name: ["MICKLE MH", "VOGT WG"]

Title: NETWORK SENSITIVITY MINIMIZATION, AN ALTERNATE FORMULATION
Abstract: A formulation is given for the synthesis of component parameters for a given network structure, so that a sensitivity criterion for parameter variation effects is a minimum for the resulting network. The method uses a gradient type parameter adjustment procedure, with parameter increments confined at every step to values consistent with some network function invariance conditions, with accuracy specifications, and with passivity conditions. The network invariance conditions relate to the first order term of a Taylor series expansion for the network function.
Name: ["SAHASRABUDDHE HV", "KESAVAN HK", "VETTER WJ"]

Title: ON THE DETERMINATION OF THE OPTIMAL CONSTANT OUTPUT-FEEDBACK GAINS FOR LINEAR MULTIVARIABLE SYSTEMS
Abstract: This research is concerned with the optimal control of linear time- invariant systems with respect to a quadratic performance criterion. The problem is posed with the addition constraint that the control vector is a linear time-invariant function of the output vector rather than of the state vector. The performance criterion is then '%'averaged'%' and algebraic necessary conditions for minimization are found.
Name: ["LEVINE WS", "ATHANS M"]

Title: DERIVED GRAMMARS WITH APPLICATION TO SYNTACTIC ANALYSIS
Abstract: Precedence relations are useful in locating the handle of a string when the language is specified by a precedence grammar. They are still useful when multiple relations exist between one or more ordered pairs. In this case the parsing algorithm must have a backtracking mechanism. Very often the number of ordered characters having multiple relations can be reduced by means of two devices introduced in this paper. A successor relation limits theup parse. This is done by looking at the derived grammar which defines the set of LR bottom-up parses for the language. Next, precedence relations are extended to indicate which grammar rules could have produced a handle which the relation is capable of marking. Used jointly, the two devices are capable of eliminating some of the multiple precedence relations.
Name: ["HADLOCK F"]

Title: An Adaptive Receiver Implementation for the Gaussian Scatter Channel
Abstract: To implement the minimum probability of error receiver for M-ary frequency-shift-keyed (FSK) communications over a Gaussian scatter channel, a minimum mean-squared error estimate of the scattered channel output signal must be constructed. It has been difficult to construct the optimum receiver since the correlation function of the scattered signal must be measured, and the impulse response of the estimation filter must then be found by solving a difficult integral equation. Stochastic approximation methods are used to develop an on-line algorithm for generating a self-optimizing filter. This filter is then used in the minimum probability of error receiver to estimate the sample function at the output of an ultrasonic model of a needles scatter channel. Experiments have been performed which indicate that the proposed adaptive receiver structure can be of practical utility because of its ease of implementation and speed of operation. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Sakrison D.J.", "Mcaulay R.J.", "Tyree V.C.", "Yuen J.H."]
Affiliations: ['1 University of California', ' Lincoln Laboratory', 'Jet Propulsion Lab', 'California Institute of Technology']

Title: NOVEL AUTOMATIC FINE TUNING CONCEPT, | [EINE NEURATIGE SCHALTUNG FUER DIE AUTOMATISCHE FEINABSTIMMUNG VON FERNSEHEMPFAENGERN]
Abstract: Previous methods of automatic fine tuning have the disadvantage that the discriminator zero and the sound trap are shifted towards different frequency points through aging. A newly developed circuit locks the sound carrier to the point of maximum suppression. When if the sound trap tuning frequency is shifted, the sound carrier remains hi%ghly suppressed so that the picture reception remains undisturbed. The complete integrated circuit that comprises a discriminator at intercarrier frequency (5.5 MHz), is described.
Name: ["JANSSEN PJH"]

Title: OPTIMIZATION IN DISTRIBUTED PARAMETER CONTROL SYSTEMS. DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING APPROACH-1, 2, 3
Source: Rev Roumaine des Sciences Techniques-Serie de Mecanique Appliquee
Abstract: Optimization is discussed of a control system described by a linear integro-partial differential equation of parabolic type with a delayed argument. Dynamic programming approach is used to find necessary conditions for the optimality of an admissible policy. Examples are considered. Using previous results pertaining to application of the principle of optimality and the establishment of first variations, necessary conditions for the optimality of an admissible policy are found and terminal and averaging controls are given.
Name: ["OGUZTORELI MN"]

Title: The development of a self-adaptive forecasting technique
Abstract: Exponential smoothing is one of the most successful naive forecasting schemes, but it suffers from the inability to select the smoothing constants quantitatively without making crucial assumptions about the time series. The method presented, called SAFT, utilizes a modified evolutionary operation first to evolve the smoothing constants directly from the data and then to monitor them to account for changing influences in the data. SAFT provides good forecast accuracy and a more advantageous dynamic response than other forecasting schemes. Because of the modest information storage and computation time, SAFT is recommended when a large number of forecasts are needed on a routine basis. ¬© Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Roberts S.D.", "Reed R., Jr."]

Title: INCOMPLETELY-SPECIFIED FINITE- STATE STOCHASTIC SEQUENTIAL MACHINE EQUIVALENCE AND REDUCTION
Abstract: The stochastic sequential machine is invariably treated as the stochastic extension of the completely-specified deterministic machine. This paper investigates the incompletely-specified finite-state stochastic sequential machine from the viewpoint of machine equivalence and reduction. Definitions are chosen and procedures developed so that they reduce to the conventional forms in the special cases of complete specification and/or deterministic machines.
Name: ["LOVELL BW"]

Title: ON THE FEEDBACK COMPLEXITY OF AUTOMATA
Abstract: The existence of a hierarchy for the size measure for the general case of simulation is established. The formulation developed makes explicit the connection between the logical net and algebraic parameters. It is shown that nets with feedback indegree (where the feedback indegree of a point is the number of input lines it receives from points is the same strong component) is less than or equal to one, cannot homomorphically realize all transition functions.
Name: ["ZEIGLER BP"]

Title: Some studies in machine learning using the game of checkers. II-Recent progress
Abstract: A new signature-table technique is described together with an improved book-learning procedure which is thought to be much superior to the linear polynomial method. Full use is made of the so-called "alpha-beta" pruning and several forms of forward pruning to restrict the spread of the move tree and to permit the program to look ahead to a much greater depth than it otherwise could do. While still unable to outplay checker masters, the program's playing ability has been greatly improved.tplay checker masters, the. ¬© 1969.
Name: ["Samuel A.L."]

Title: Strong stability problems for probabilistic sequential machines
Abstract: The strong stability problem for a machine A and some behavioral equivalence ‚â° is to characterize the input symbol transition matrices of all machines A‚Ä≤ formed from the input symbol transition matrices of A such that from any initial distribution A ‚â° A‚Ä≤. The strong stability problem is studied herein for the behavioral equivalences ‚â°<sub>I</sub> (indistinguishability) and ‚â°<sub>N</sub> (N-moment equivalence). The concepts of strong stability transformation and error matrix are introduced to formalize the perturbations which are allowed in the input symbol transition matrices. Necessary conditions for the existence of any strongly stable transformations are studied using the concept of invariant error matrix. Title: ADAPTIVE APPROACH TO SMOOTHING, FILTERING AND PREDICTION
Abstract: A cybernetic approach to the processes of smoothing, filtering and prediction which are of considerable interest in control and data processing, is presented.
Name: ["GILSTRAP LO", "JR"]

Title: DEFINITE STOCHASTIC SEQUENTIAL MACHINES AND DEFINITE STOCHASTIC MATRICES
Abstract: The major mathematical tool is developed. Some properties of definite stochastic matrices are sstablished. Sets of stochastic matrices are discussed. Convex sums of stochastic matrices are considered.

Title: DETECTION OF SPARSE, NOISY SAMPLED DATA
Abstract: It is shown that a uniform distribution may be a more accurate assumption in many cases. Game theory is suggested as a decision technique for improved matching of statistics. Using a Brown approximation solution, the reliable estimates needed for the matched filter detection are obtained.

Title: SEQUENTIAL DETECTION PROCEDURE BASED ON THE GAMBLER'S RUIN PROBLEM
Abstract: The procedure is applied to the problem of the discrimination between shift alteratives when the probability distribution function of the data samples is symmetric about the median. The procedure is shown to have the desirable properties of ease of implementation, the capability of finding the exact decision thresholds for achieving a desired performance and being applicable to a broad class of distributions. It is also shown that the performance of the proposed detector is better than that of thenonsequential detector based on the same test statistic and compares favorably with efficient nonparametric rank vector detection procedures.

Title: On the Potential Function Method and the Increment Error Correction Rule in Pattern Classification
Abstract: Based on the basic property that the solution weight vector of the linear pattern classifier can be expressed as a linear function of the training patterns, it is shown that the increment error correction algorithm is a special case of the potential function method. For linearly separable training patterns, a form of potential function which appears to be useful is also proposed. Copyright ¬© 1969 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.

Title: PROPERTIES OF BOUNDS ON COMPUTATION
Abstract: Authors show that for any recursive function t, there are recursive functions t' which (except at a rapidly vanishing percentage of arguments) can be made arbitrarily much larger than t, such that any running time function bounded above by t' is in fact bounded above by t. The proof is based on the construction of difficult to compute characteristic functions which take the value one very infrequently. I

Title: SOME PROPERTIES OF A PREDICTIVE QUANTIZING SYSTEM
Abstract: This paper presents some theoretical properties of a predictive quantizing system for the transmission of random signals. Expressions for the mean-squared error are derived for some input processes, and several bounds are also derived. The gaussian case is discussed in detail, and it is shown that the predictive system gives no improvement over the conventional communication system. The class of linear Markov processes is also considered. In this case, an example is presented3hich clearly illustrates the limited region of improvement for the predictive system. The relation of the improvement to the correlation of the input samples is also illustrated.

Title: MEDICAL RECORD ACQUISITION, SCREENING AND RETRIEVAL USING NATURAL LANGUAGE DATA PROCESSING TECHNIQUES
Abstract: Natural language '%'batch'%' and '%'on-line'%' data processing techniques for acquiring narrative text and for the subsequent data screening, editing and information retrieval operations are used for patient record information. Details are given for the operations of data acquisition and display, document screening and editing, spelling and content analysis, file maintenance, and retrieval. Results are given for preliminary experience with the system.

Title: SYNTHESIS OF AN ON-BOARD HYBRID COMPUTER FOR AN ADVANCED HELICOPTER FIRE CONTROL SYSTEM
Abstract: Analytical/empirical solutions of the equations of motion describing the dynamics of a projectile fired from a moving helicopter are obtained and used to establish the weapon aiming requirements for an advanced fire control system. Turrent pointing angles are generated by composite signals obtained from manual inputs at the sighting station and corrections calculated by an on-board computer. All sensor outputs are converted to digital format where required and sequentially enter a special purpose digital computeras fire control computation inputs. All arithmetic operations are effected by the machine, reconverted to analog signals, and input to the servo loops to provide instantaneous correction angles to drive the turret relative to the sight.

Title: OPTIMIZING FLOATING POINT ARITHMETIC VIA POST ADDITION SHIFT PROBABILITIES
Abstract: In the processing of binary floating point addition and subtraction, there exist two possible shift operations, first to align the binary points before addition or subtraction, and second, to normalize the result. In processing these shifts there are several options as to method, and sequencing of operations within a given method. To choose the variation that optimizes the program it is necessary to know the probability of occurrence of the various length shifts possible. Method for estimating the required probabilities, and an example of their application in subprogram optimization.
Name: ["FIELD JA"]

Title: Predictive Adaptive Control
Abstract: A control system is described which employs an adaptive modeler to estimate the state, dynamics, and future trajectory of an unknown plant. Control is automatically synthesized to minimize a performance index involving the estimated future. The effects of perfect and imperfect modeling and of optimal and suboptimal instrumentation are considered. Experimental results are presented.
