Abstract: The AMTRAN system (Automatic Mathematical TRANslator) is a multiterminal conversational mode computing system which enables the mathematically oriented user to interact directly with the computer in a natural mathematical language. In connection with the project of implementing a multiconsole version on an IBM 1130 computer, the AMTRAN language has been revised and formally defined at the University of Georgia Computer Center. The programming language AMTRAN is defined and its basicfeatures are described. A comparative study between AMTRAN and other high level languages is divided into two parts. Only language features are compared with batch mode languages, whereas the whole AMTRAN-system is taken into account for a comparison with other interactive systems.
Name: ["REINFELDS J", "ESKELSON N", "KOPETZ H", "KRATKY G"]

Title: ARCHITECTURE OF A LARGE ASSOCIATIVE PROCESSOR
Abstract: A processor for information storage and retrieval apparently must be large to be practical. Two solutions are presented to several problems associated with large processors. One solution is the segmentation of a processor, and the other is a system of processors. The architectures have low propagation delay, provide for fast loading and unloading data in parallel from different I/O channels, and permit highly parallel programming. The diagnosis of cells is briefly considered. It is apparent that both architectures are capable of operating in the presence of some cells found to befaulty. Further, a graceful degradation of performance occurs when most cells are faulty. The results presented apply to a number of associative memory processors, and may also apply to future iterative processors that broadcast instructions in a channel, even though they do not use the associative search operation as associative processors do.
Name: ["LIPOVSKI GJ"]

Title: The inverse modeling problem
Abstract: In simulation modeling of very large-scale systems, such as social and natural systems, reductions in scale must be so severe that state variables of the abstraction (model) often cannot be translated back to variables that have real-world significance. Model behavior may not much resemble anything that occurs naturally. If y is a real system and x a model of it, the two can be viewed as related by a set of homomorphic corres pondences M. Then, xMy means x ‚Äúis a model of‚Äù y. Behavior of x pertains to that of y only as M is a valid model, and the relationship is implicit in an inverse model M<sup>-1</sup>, defined from the fact that xMy implies yM<sup>-1</sup>x (y ‚Äúis modeled by‚Äù x). To make it explicit, that is to interpret model behavior in terms of real-world variables, means in some sense to be able to identify M<sup>-1</sup>. One approach to estimating it is suggested, but a definite solution is not reached. ¬© 1970, Sage Publications. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Patten B.C."]

Title: Time- and tape-bounded turing acceptors and AFLs
Source: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: Complexity classes of formal languages defined by time- and tape-bounded Turing acceptors are studied. Sufficient conditions for these classes to be AFLs are given. Further, it is shown that a time-bounded nondeterministic Turing acceptor need have only two storage tapes. ¬© 1971 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Book R.V.", "Greibach S.A.", "Wegbreit B."]
Affiliations: [' Harvard University', ' University of California', ' Harvard University']

Title: What's ahead in robot quality control
Abstract: This article deals with complex, highly sophisticated, automatic lines for packaging very broad variety of products with the use of automatic controls. Several examples of control devices, based on optical- electronic, electromagnetic, etc. , operational principles. Pneumatic air stream control system is also included. Brief description of automated production lines incorporating various robot- type quality control devices is presented.
Name: ["ANON"]

Title: Synthesis of adaptive sub-optimal feedback control lawsj
Abstract: In this paper a method for synthesizing a sub-optimal feedback controller which is sensitive to variations in plant parameters is presented. The structure of the sub- optimal control is a linear combination of suitably chosen basis functions multiplied by coefficients which are functions of the varying plant parameters. The coefficient multipliers are determined by the minimization of a mean-square error using data obtained from numerically computed optimal trajectories. The controller may be called adaptive since it uses identification of the varying plant parameters to modify the coefficient multipliers. Examples are included which show that with relative sensitivity as the criterion the method is superior to other methods of suboptimal control design. ¬© 1970 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Raju G.V.", "Brueggemann W.M."]

Title: A Feature Extractor for Curvilinear Patterns
Abstract: A feature extractor for a pattern recognizer which can effectively process curvilinear drawings has been synthesized. It is a multilayered parallel network composed of analog threshold ele ments, and consists of six layers in cascade. In the final layer of the network, the curvature of the input drawings is extracted. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Fukushima K."]

Title: Change of error criterion in mean square optimisation
Abstract: System error is defined as the output of a linear time-invariant filter H(s) whose input is the system input minus the system output. The effect of changes of His) on the resulting optimum mean-square error system is studied. ¬© 1970, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Shelton R.D.", "Jones T.J."]
Keywords: ["error analysis", "filtering and prediction theory", "optimisation", "error criterion", "error defined"]

Title: Retrieval optimization by feedback
Source: Handling of Nuclear Information, Proc Symp
Abstract: The retrospective searching and selective dissemination routines employed in the EURATOM Nuclear Documentation System are described. Figures are given for precision and recall ratio, cost and turnover time. The effect of reformation of search queries on these parameters as a result of user response is evaluated. Automatic reformulation by term weighting as a result of partial relevance assessment has yielded surprisingly good results, so that this procedure is presently applied.
Name: ["VERNIMB C"]

Title: A Multimodel and Computer Oriented Methodology for Synthesis of Sequential Discrete Systems
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics
Abstract: The synthesis of sequential discrete systems involves two major steps: 1) the abstract synthesis that yields a state-transition diagram, and 2) the structure synthesis that yields a realization. The structure synthesis, where the minimum state-transition diagram is assumed to be given, is discussed. Classically, two different models are in use to perform the structure synthesis: the finite-state model with memory span k=1, and the finite-memory model. These classical models (the finite-state model extended for k‚â•1), are considered and other models are introduced that may be used for the structure synthesis. The latter, combined models with memory span k (k‚â•1), sometimes yield a better realization (according to specific engineering requirements) than the classical models. Structure synthesis based on the combined models and a rough evaluation of all the considered models from the standpoint of their realization is included in this paper together with an outline of a FORTRAN IV program being developed to automate the complete structure synthesis. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Klir G.J.", "Marin M.A."]
Affiliations: [' University of California', ' University of California']

Title: ON OPTIMAL ALLOCATION AND GUIDANCE LAWS FOR LINEAR INTERCEPTION AND RENDEZVOUS PROBLEMS
Abstract: This paper considers the problems of guiding N interceptors so that they intercept or rendezvous with N targets at the same time T. It is assumed that the interceptors and targets are described by linear time-varying differential equation (deterministic or stochastic). Under certain assumptions both the optimal (static or dynamic) interceptor-target allocation and the guidance of each interceptor for the optimal allocation can be obtained with modest real-time and storage computer requirements.
Name: ["ATHANS M"]

Title: Fully parallel computer for radar data processing
Source: National Aerospace and Electronics Conference, Proceedings of the IEEE
Abstract: The architecture of a global, highly- parallel machine designed for real- time track data processing in advanced radar systems is described. The machine consists of an unstructured ensemble of an indefinite number of processing elements operating under common control.
Name: ["GITHENS JA"]

Title: Discrete stochastic optimal control model of the human operator
Source: National Aerospace and Electronics Conference, Proceedings of the IEEE
Abstract: A discrete stochastic optimal control model of the human operator is developed for the single- loop compensatory/pursuit tracking situation. A comparison between model and experimental normalized tracking error and power spectral density data confirms the model capability of matching and predicting operator performance with sufficient correlation to warrant its application as a tool in manual vehicular control system design.
Name: ["PASKIN HM"]

Title: Biologically derived model for image classification utilizing Walsh functions
Source: National Aerospace and Electronics Conference, Proceedings of the IEEE
Abstract: An image classification model based on cross- correlation and discrete Walsh- Fourier techniques is presented, and shown to have biological relevance. A review of some known properties of Walsh functions, and a discussion of sequency filtering are included. A computer simulation of the model (using handwritten capital letters as images) and the results obtained from the simulation are described.
Name: ["CARL JW"]

Title: Hybrid computation of the optimal control for an entry vehicle with three degrees of freedom
Source: National Aerospace and Electronics Conference, Proceedings of the IEEE
Abstract: This paper presents an optimal control solution for a dynamic entry vehicle along a planar trajectory which was determined on a hybrid computer. The most important characteristics of hybrid simulation are discussed and related to this problem solution. The optimal control problem is described and the effects of hybrid computation on the optimal control algorithm (conjugate gradient) is discussed.
Name: ["BRINKER JA", "JOHNSON RW", "STAPLES JR ME"]

Title: Hybrid vs digital synthesis of optimal boost vehicle controller
Source: National Aerospace and Electronics Conference, Proceedings of the IEEE
Abstract: This study determines the efficiency of the solution of realistic optimal control problems on a hybrid computer. It essentially compares the speed of optimal solutions obtained by both digital and hybrid means, and investigates the techniques that spped up or retard convergence to a solution. The problem consists of determining the optimal open loop controller for the minimum fuel trajectory of a solid booster, considering the effects of pitch dynamics.
Name: ["CARPINELLA R", "EBELTOFT A", "JOHNSON RW"]

Title: Real- time multisensor data display
Source: National Aerospace and Electronics Conference, Proceedings of the IEEE
Abstract: Perfectly registered, real- time video has been obtained at visual and thermal IR wavelengths. These signals have been recorded in parallel and have been presented to observers both independently and in various composite modes, some of which use color coding of the video information. Subjects exhibit statistically significant performance improvement for target recognition in the composite modes, particularly when color cueing is used.
Name: ["FAUBERT DB", "LEONARD JR KC"]

Title: Cognitive model of problem-solving in chess
Abstract: By performing a series of five experiments with two subjects, several aspects of one of the subject's behavior in solving chess problems were found to be predictable, and a model was developed to explain this predictability. The heuristics used in this model may be applicable in developing future computer programs for chess play.
Name: ["Scurrah M.J.", "Wagner D.A."]

Title: Control-function optimisation using quadrature integrations for positive semidefinite state cost matrix Q
Abstract: A new technique for control-function optimisation has recently been proposed for linear dynamical systems with quadratic-performance indices which have positive definite state cost matrix Q. Its advantage is that the only integrations needed are quadratures. A modified technique for when Q is positive semidefinite is described here. ¬© 1970, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Wright J.C.A."]

Title: Pattern learning in humans and electronic learning nets
Abstract: The letter reports on a previously unseen similarity between an associative memory model recently proposed for the brain and some electronic systems that have been developed for practical learning machines. This similarity is analysed, and its implications are discussed. Results of a comparison between the learning behaviour of an electronic network and a group of human subjects in a pattern-recognition task are given to complete the comparative study. ¬© 1970, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Aleksander I.", "Fairhurst M.C."]

Title: Microcircuit learning nets: Hamming-distance behaviour
Abstract: A probabilistic method based on the Hamming distance is presented for calculating the pattern-recognition response of a class of single-layer microcircuit learning nets. The prediction of the behaviour of a 12-element machine is shown to agree with measured responses. The method is also used to explain the characteristics of nets trained on translated versions. ¬© 1970, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Aleksander I."]

Title: Vision information center: A user-oriented data base
Abstract: In response to the information needs of scientists and physicians who work in the field of vision, we have developed a direct-access, on-line specialized information retrieval system which combines computer-assisted instruction and bibliographic retrieval. An essential feature of the system is its accessibility via remote computer terminal. The key to the data base is a thesaurus which contains specific terminology arranged in a hierarchical structure. The thesaurus is used both for indexing the literature and for retrieving the information stored in the computer. Courses of instruction on selected subjects in ophthalmology have been programmed and form part of the data base. A search of the literature retrieval system by single subject, or by a combination of several subjects chosen from the thesaurus, retrieves the appropriate bibliographic citations. The response to the service offered by the Vision Information Center indicates that the center should expand its facilities to satisfy the needs of its clients.
Name: ["Eichhorn M.M.", "Reinecke R.D."]
Affiliations: [' Harvard Medical School', 'Vision Information Center', ' Union University']

Title: AUTOMATIC CONTROL OF PNEUMATIC JIG, BASED ON ASH CONTENT OF COAL CONCENTRATE, | [AUTOMATISCHE REGELUNG EINER LUFTGEPULSTEN DURCHSETZMASCHINE NACH DEM ASCHEGEHALT DES KOHLEAUSTRAGS]
Source: Gluckauf: Die Fachzeitschrift fur Rohstoff, Bergbau und Energie
Abstract: Since coals of similar density can differ substantially in their ash content an apparatus has been developed that provides for automatic based on ash content, control of separating various coal concentrates, produced in a pneumatic jig. Its design and operation are described.
Name: ["PADBERG W", "SCHANNE L"]

Title: OPTIMAL MODEL-FOLLOWING CONTROL- SYSTEM SYNTHESIS TECHNIQUES
Abstract: Three synthesis methods in which optimization techniques are used to design controllers that make the closed-loop system behave like a specified ideal system or model are considered. The background theory is summarized, and the techniques of real and implicit model- following are discussed, especially their practical and computational aspects. A simpler algebraic form of the implicit- model-following performance criterion is presented. It is shown that, provided certain conditions are satisfied, this formulation yields a control law that is easily computed, unique, and useful in practice.
Name: ["MARKLAND CA"]

Title: SYDOLAB, a loboratory documentation system, (SYDOLAB, systeme de documentation de laboratoire)
Source: Handling of Nuclear Information, Proc Symp
Abstract: SYDOLAB is a computer- based automatic searching system which facilitates the joint use of a bibliographic index by several research workers interested in a number of clearly defined subjects. It can be used to find a document from a subjective description. Searching is based on the use of key words and authors' names, connected by logic operations and, in some cases, by references.
Name: ["GERVAIS C", "GILET R", "SCHAUER G"]

Title: A man-machine approach toward solving the traveling salesman problem
Abstract: The traveling salesman problem, (form a cir-cuit through N points with no subloops in such a way as to minimize the length of the circuit), is a close kin to many board wiring problems. It has been attacked by many mathematical methods with only meager results. Only for special forms of the problem or for problems with relatively few points can it be solved exactly evin using very large amounts of computer time. Heuristic procedures have been proposed and tested with only slightly better results. This paper will describe a computer-aided heuristic technique which uses only a modest amount of computer time in real time to solve large (100-200) point prob-lems. This technique takes advantage of both the computer's and the human's problem solving abilities. The computer is not asked to solve the problem in a brute force way as is the case in many of today's heuristics but it is asked to organize the data for the human in a fashion that allows the human to solve the problem easily. The techniques employed in this paper require that the computer and the hjiman cooperate to find the solution to the problem in reasonable amounts of both of their times. The computer initially uses a series of heuristics that produce groups of points and some partial connections of these points. The human is asked to connect the points within the groups and then connect the groups in a manner that produces a circuit and appears to the human to maximize the ratio of enclosed area to perimeter. The computer takes this solution and uses another set of heuristics to make im-provements. The solution is displayed to the hijtman and if he is satisfied the procedure stops; if not the former procedure is repeated until the human is satisfied that cost for finding a better solution exceeds his estimate of the best possible improvement that eould be obtained by further work. The heuristic procedures seek to group points around information obtained from solving a series of mathematical programming problems (assignment problems) and some observed correlations between these problems and the traveling salesman problem. The results are very good. The man-machine interaction solution for all problems in the literature is within one per cent of the solution for a fraction of the computer time. The experi-ence to date indicates that the technique can be taught to inexperienced persons and their results, after training, are similar to those of the authors'. ¬© 1970 Proceedings - Design Automation Conference. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Krolak P.", "Felts W.", "Marble G."]

Title: Simulation of the traffic action on signal- controlled road networks, (Simulation des Verkehrsgeschehens auf signalgeregelten Strassennetzen)
Abstract: A computer pogram, called QUWAIT, is described. It allows the computation of probability distributions of traffic jam lengths and waiting times at all signals of a road network.
Name: ["FISCHER D", "STOOP K", "SCHULTZ E"]

Title: Control considerations and smooth flow in vehicular traffic nets
Abstract: Analysis, constraints, and problem areas in the formal structure of control on the signalizationassignment level of a multilevel macroscopic controller. A '%'smoothflow'%' control philosophy is presented, and some consequent controllers for aterials and for networks are demonstrated. Some formal constraints and difficulties in structuring the control problem are treated; these include cycle length definition, predictor requirements, and the problem of, and bounds on, the closure integers.
Name: ["MCSHANE WR", "YAGODA HN", "PIGNATARO LJ", "CROWLEY KW"]

Title: Problem of reproduction of random vibrations
Abstract: Solution is given to the problem of determination of optimum links in an automatic control system of a random vibration test stand. The use of these links allows the reduction of errors in the vibration process being reproduced. The correcting links are found by using the method of statistical optimization. The exponential consinusoidal characteristic of autocorrelation functions of input signals is taken into consideration, these functions constituting analogs of registered signals of actual operational vibrations.
Name: ["BOZHKO AE"]

Title: Application of Optimal Control Theory to Satellite‚ÄêBased Oceanic Air Traffic Control
Abstract: This paper describes the application of stochastic optimal control theory to the design and analysis of a satellite‚Äêbased Air Traffic Control (ATC) system for the North Atlantic. The longitudinal and lateral motion of several oceanic aircraft is simulated by postulating the existence of an ATC system, part of which is derived from optimal control considerations. The simulated environment includes such factors as errors arising from navigation, wind and surveillance. The control algorithm includes a Kalman filter in tandem with an optimal regulator, with adjustable update and command rates, and command thresholds. The analytical tool that is developed herein can be used as a basis for deriving the expected separation standards to be used with a future satellite‚Äêbased system. In addition, it can be used to determine the impact of design trade‚Äêoffs on system performance. 1970 Institute of Navigation
Name: ["STARR S.H.", "HOROWITZ B.M."]

Title: Proceedings symposium on nonlinear estimation theory and its applications, San Diego, Calif, Sept 21- 23 1970
Abstract: Proceedings include 42 papers (four with abstracts only given) on many aspects of nonlinear estimation theory and applications, such as the status of radar tracking algorithms,analytical methods for performance evaluation of nonlinear filters, state estimation in nonlinear distributed parameter systems, and design of navigation filtering algorithms in a mobile ground vehicle. Individual papers are indexed separately.
Name: ["PROC"]

Title: Convergence of certain training algorithms for adaptive threshold elements with imperfect weight components
Abstract: A proof of the convergence of an adaptive algorithm based on the concept of characteristic vector is presented. It is shown that the adaptive algorithm will converge even when imperfections existing in the components of the ATE and the imperfections are within certain finite limits. ¬© 1970 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Babu C.C.", "Chan W.-C."]

Title: Realization of a computer controlled traffic control system, (Realisierung einer computergesteuerten Verkehrsregelungsanlage)
Abstract: The Hasler traffic control system with dataflex CONTRA is described. The small computer is capable of centrally controlling the light signal of a medium- sized city. The central equipment, the possibilities of data acquisition and transmission, the control equipment at individual intersections, and the available programs are discussed.
Name: ["LUESCHER B"]

Title: AUTOMATIC GENERATION OF TESTS CASES
Abstract: Discussed is the '%'syntax machine,'%' a program for automatically generating syntactically correct programs (test cases) for checking compiler front ends. The notion of '%'dynamic grammar'%' is introduced and is used in a syntax-defining notation that provides for contest-sensitivity. Examples demonstrate use of the syntax machine.
Name: ["HANFORD KV"]

Title: Computer identification of systolic time intervals
Abstract: A digital computer program is described for automatic identification of the points in the electrocardiogram, phonocardiogram and exterrally recorded carotid pulse wave which are necessary for estimation of the major systolic time intervals. The logic of recognition is designed to locate these points whenever they are clearly defined. Independent error checks are made throughout the program to insure that the measurements made on the points identified are accurate estimates of the systolic time intervals. The measurements calculated on the points identified by the pattern recognition program conform closely to those obtained by careful visual identification. ¬© 1971.
Name: ["Kyle M.C.", "Freis E.D."]
Affiliations: [' Georgetown University School of Medicine', ' Georgetown University School of Medicine']

Title: A New Analog-Digital Filtering Method for Real-Time Speech Recognition
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: Using the low-pass filtering properties of a particular new type of analog-to-digital converter, we have developed a numerical filtering method which permits us to obtain, by programming, a large scale of passband filters. The procedure involved is very simple, fast, and consequently very well adapted to real-time treatment. It consists of sampling the analog signal at different rates and then linearly combining the samples thus obtained. These filters have a number of very interesting characteristics: For example, the frequency response curves resemble very closely the response of the basilar membrane. This combination of analog-digital coding and passband filtering seems especially well adapted to the treatment of the speech signal; we are presently applying the method to the problem of real-time speech recognition. ¬© 1970, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Maissis A.", "Fievet F.", "Walrave P.H."]

Title: BRANCH AND BOUND ALGORITHM FOR THE CONTINUOUS PROCESS JOB SHOP SCHEDULING PROBLEM
Abstract: The continuous process job shop scheduling problem (CPJS) arises typically in the following way; a set of M machines or production facilities is available; a set of N jobs is to be processed through these machines in accordance with a technological matrix; the machines associated with a given job must all be used simultaneously for the completion of this job; a predetermined production time is required for each job; the objective is to determine a production schedule which minimizes the total completion time (makespan) of all jobs. A branch and bound type algorithm for the solution of the CPJS problem is presented.
Name: ["BOZOKI G", "RICHARD JP"]

Title: COMPUTER TEXTURE ANALYSIS
Abstract: The given geometric object (for example, a polyhedron or a geometric combination of polyhedra) is recognized by a hierarchical identification of its projections-first the relevant vertices are recognized, then the meaningful edges, and then the main regions. From the geometric nature and mutual relationships of regions one infers or guesses the geometric identity of the object.
Name: ["BAJCSYOVA R"]

Title: AI in CAI: An Artificial-Intelligence Approach to Computer-Assisted Instruction
Abstract: The main purpose of the research reported here is to show that a new and more powerful type of computer-assisted instruction (CAI), based on extensive application of artificial-intelligence (AI) techniques, is feasible, and to demonstrate some of its major capabilities. A set of computer programs was written and given the name scholar. Due to its complexity, only the conception and educational aspects of this system (including an actual online protocol) are presented in this paper. In what may be called conventional ad hoc-frame-oriented (AFO) CAI, the data base consists of many ‚Äúframes‚Äù of specific pieces of text, questions, and anticipated answers entered in advance by the teacher. By contrast, an information-structure-oriented (ISO) CAI system is based on the utilization of an information network of facts, concepts, and procedures; it can generate text, questions, and corresponding answers. Because an ISO CAI system can also utilize its information network to answer questions formulated by the student, a mixed-initiative dialogue between student and computer is possible with questions and answers from both sides. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Carbonell J.R."]

Title: A Linear Filtering Approach to the Computation of Discrete Fourier Transform
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: It is shown in this paper that the discrete equivalent of a chirp filter is needed to implement the computation of the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) as a linear filtering process. We show further that the chirp filter should not be realized as a transversal filter in a wide range of cases; use instead of the conventional FFT permits the computation of the DFT in a time proportional to N log2 N for any N, N being the number of points in the array that is transformed. Another proposed implementation of the chirp filter requires N to be a perfect square. The number of operations required for this algorithm is proportional to N3/2. ¬© 1970, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Bluestein L.I."]

Title: Computer detection of ventricular ectopic beats
Abstract: An algorithm has been developed for performing a beat-by-beat real-time analysis of electrocardiograms for the purpose of ectopic beat detection. A multipatient version of this algorithm has been implemented on a small digital computer. Examination of the results indicate close agreement of analysis by computer and cardiologist. The noise suppression features of the program permit continued operation under diverse clinical conditions. ¬© 1971.
Name: ["Feldman C.L.", "Amazeen P.G.", "Klein M.D.", "Lown B."]
Affiliations: [' Worcester Polytechnic Institute', ' Worcester Polytechnic Institute', ' Harvard School of Public Health']

Title: Digital Synthesis of Speech and Music
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: Electronic music has developed in response to sophisticated music listeners' desire for change. The seeds of change arose in the symphonic music of Stravinsky, Sch√∂nberg, and von Webern before World War I. Some excellent early analog music was composed by Badings and Var√®se at Philips in 1958 and is reproduced on the associated stereo disk. Good digital computer music was composed on the IBM 7090 at the Bell Telephone Laboratories about 1960. An example by Mathews and a 1969 composition on a third-generation computer by Risset is demonstrated. The electronic evolution is affecting the symphonic repertoire and popular music. This paper also discusses and demonstrates recent advances in speech synthesis, including speech analysis and synthesis by the cepstrum method and speech synthesis from printed words by a new process developed in the Bell Telephone Laboratories. ¬© 1970, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Beranek L.L."]

Title: Optimal control of systems with known distribution functions of parameters
Abstract: The optimal control for the system with uncertain or random slowly- varying parameters whose probability density functions are known is dealt with. The necessary conditions for the optimal control are derived. In particular, for the linear quadratic problems, it is shown that the necessary condition results in the linear integral equation. A numerical example is presented to illutrate the proposed method. The method is compared with other methods for the same problems utilizing the sensitivity analysis.
Name: ["KANESADA F", "ISHIHARA T"]

Title: Identification and control of a class of stochastic systems with unknown parameters
Abstract: We consider the recursive estimation of the unknown parameters in the stochastic differential equation describing the system utilizing the observations of the state of the system. We show that the unknown parameters can be divided into two groups so that the true values of the members of the first group can be recovered instantaneously whereas the true values of the members of the second group cannot be recovered in finite time. We derive the recursive equations for the conditional mean and covariance of the unknown parameters of the second. Then we consider the determination of the optimal feedback control function for minimizing a suitable criterion function. We will show that the optimal feedback control is a function of the current state measurement, the conditional mean and variance of the unknown parameters. We mention a method of approximation of the optimal feedback control function and the results of the simulation of the control scheme. ¬© 1970 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Kashyap R.L."]

Title: Experiments on probabilistic information processing
Abstract: Probabilistic information processing, the modification of prior beliefs under the impact of new observations, has been studied experimentally over the last ten years using Bayesian decision theory as frame of reference. Experiments related to the two basic approaches - probability revision and deferred decision making - are reviewed, while a critical examination is made of the basic research paradigms used. An evaluation of the fruitfulness of the underlying research strategy is attempted. ¬© 1970.
Name: ["Manz W."]

Title: Cost-effectiveness as a guide in developing indexing rules
Abstract: To date, the many decisions among alternatives that are required in the course of developmental efforts to improve indexing have, with few exceptions, been guided primarily by criteria related to effectiveness, as measured by some objective method or as judged subjectively. Although effectiveness-type criteria may be adequate for work intended solely to advance the state-of-the-art, when the goal is to develop indexing techniques appropriate for operating services, it seems highly desirable to employ some criterion that takes cost as well as effectiveness into consideration. The central problem of operating services can be reduced to either that of producing the best indexing possible at a given cost or that of producing indexing of a given level of effectiveness at least cost. In our current effort to develop rules for human, machine and man-machine indexing, we employ a cost-effectiveness type of criterion in making the critical developmental decisions. The general approach is described and illustrated with examples of how measures of cost and of effectiveness were considered jointly in decision making, primarily for how to reduce cost of indexing at a given level of effectiveness. Problems of defining cost are also discussed, such as how to divide indexing into discrete steps, the effects of long-term vs. short-term activity in humans and small-batch vs. large-batch considerations for machines. ¬© 1970.
Name: ["Schultz C.K."]

Title: Formulating a model of multilane traffic flow
Abstract: A formulation of a model of multilane traffic using Markov renewal theory. The model considers the movements of individual vehicles within a given traffic environment that is described by a bivariate probability distribution of platoon lengths and speeds. Outputs of the model include average vehicle speed, vehicle delay, and lane- changing intensities and patterns.
Name: ["BULLEN AGR", "WORRALL RD"]

Title: ON-LINE ADAPTIVE CONTROL TEACHES COMPUTERS TO ROLL METALS
Abstract: Many computers that control rolling mills require much off-line data analysis and adjustment of model constants to make the necessary improvements in the mill setups to give good production performance. The learning procedure that is now being used on several rolling mills does the necessary adjusting of the model predictions on-line as data is collected during the rolling of each piece. A system of classifying, testing and storage improves the mill setups for future rolling of similar products. Short-term fast learning is used to take care of current variations and a slower trending is used to improve the long term mill setups.
Name: ["SMITH AW"]

Title: LISTAR. LINCOLN INFORMATION STORAGE AND ASSOCIATIVE RETRIEVAL SYSTEM
Abstract: LISTAR is primarily an on-line interactive system which permits a user to define, search, modify, and cross associate data files to suit his own special interests and needs. The system assumes an oper-ended library of users' files which can be called from auxiliary storage for processing by a name designation. A collection of files which have a common directory (Master File) is called a '%'file set'%'. Each file set contains, in addition to its data files, the directory information required for their interpretationand processing. The user is free to define, modify, augment, delete, and cross associate data in files as his interests dictate. In addition to direct support of the terminal user, the system allows information storage and retrieval functions to be performed at the request of independent task programs. Details are given for the structure and operation of the system and its implementation on an IBM 360/67 computer.
Name: ["ARMENTI A", "GALLEY S", "GOLDBERG R", "NOLAN J", "SHOLL A"]

Title: INFORMATION THEORY APPROACH TO THE SOURCE APPROXIMATION PROBLEM
Abstract: The problem of approximating a random time series is considered from an information theory point of view. McMillan's theorem and the entropy concept form the basis for the theory developed. Two classes of approximation processes are studied-finite order unifilar Markov sources and renewal processes. Both classes are shown to possess certain desirable properties for approximation purposes.
Name: ["ERICSON T"]

Title: OPTIMIZATION OF THE INDUSTRIAL PROCESS BY ADAPTIVE PROGRAMMING
Abstract: One of the possible variants of a generalized algorithm of dynamic optimization is proposed, that can be used fo%r solving the problem of adaptive optimization of multivariable nonlinear control systems. The algorithms are based on the use of perception.
Name: ["KOCHISH YA"]

Title: STUDY OF HEURISTIC LEARNING METHODS FOR OPTIMIZATION TASKS REQUIRING A SEQUENCE OF DECISIONS
Abstract: The learning problem is viewed as one of associating states of the environment, defined by some set of stimulus variables to which the problem solver is attending, with strategies for performance. The question examined is whether significant learning can be accomplished on a very complex optimization task if the stimulus environment is represented by a state vector of some of the most obvious relevant stimulus variables and only ordinal feedback is used. a computer program, used to study a project scheduling problem, consists of two closely interacting routines, a performance routine and a learning routine. The performance routine is designed to find the shortest path through the tree of feasible solutions, i. e. , feasible job schedules. The learning program evaluates paths through the tree of feasible solutions by comparing them with the bench mark solution (best solution so far), and it alters the tables of connections on the basis of these evaluations. Three experiments with this learning program are described and results are evaluated considering the effects of positive and negative reinforcement. The relationship to human learning is mentioned.
Name: ["HUESMANN LR"]

Title: NATURAL LANGUAGE INQUIRY TO AN OPEN-ENDED DATA LIBRARY
Abstract: A new computer system and language, '%'MUSE'%', is designed to enhance the time-shared computer environment by providing a natural language for machine-user communication. It is designed to provide the manager with a medium of interaction with a large common data base, loaded and maintained by the '%'MUSE'%' system. '%'MUSE'%' is capable of performing as a simulation model builder, statistical tool, data screening and sorting aid, and report organizer for non- routine, creative use. The system is described in terms of five functional modules-normal interactionodule, teaching module, data loading and maintenance module, metalanguage processor, and report generator. Each of these modules, in turn, is constructed of submodules, many of which are used in common by the larger, functional modules.
Name: ["POTTS GW"]

Title: Time-Optimal Control of Sampled-Data Systems
Abstract: The matrix pseudoinverse is used to obtain a minimum-time control law for a general nth-order linear time-invariant completely state-controllable sampled-data system with r inputs. The control law is unique only in certain special cases. In the general case several time-optimal control sequences may exist; the particular control law obtained is shown to require minimum Energy. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Grainger J.J.", "Pandy K.G."]

Title: A formal approach to code optimization
Abstract: We examine from a formal point of view some problems which arise in code optimization and present some of the results which can come from such an approach. Specifically, a set of transformations which characterize optimization algorithms for straight line code is presented. Then we present an algorithm which produces machine code for evaluating arithmetic expressions on machines with N ‚â• 1 general purpose registers. We can prove that this algorithm produces optimal code when the cost criterion is the length of machine code generated. ¬© 1970, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Aho A.V.", "Sethi R.", "Ullman J.D."]

Title: OPTIMUM SOLUTION OF MODEL-REDUCTION PROBLEM
Abstract: Conditions are given for synthetizing a reduced model for a multivariable time-invariant linear system by minimizing a functional of the error between the output vector of the reduced model and the original model. It is shown that, when the system has s single output or single input and the eigenvalues of the reduced model are specified, the synthesis simplifies to a linear problem. A simple example is presented. Paper 6181 C.
Name: ["WILSON DA"]

Title: CONTRIBUTION TO THE IDENTIFICATION OF INDUSTRIAL OBJECTS
Abstract: A practical method of identification is proposed as a first step towards the control optimization. The identification proposed, based on measurements of the characteristics of the controlled objects, resulted in the establishment of the controlled system model. The derivation of a respective algorithm is described.
Name: ["KOCHISH YA", "ALMASHI G"]

Title: COMPUTER INSTRUCTION REPERTOIRE. TIME FOR A CHANGE
Abstract: A study to determine how current machine instructions were being used led to the conclusion that the two major areas to be attacked in the development of a job-oriented computer are excessive data editing and fixed length instructions. A proposed solution involves a technique of automatic editing for the first area, and a system of variable length commands for the second. These techniques are detailed. Results are given for the concept verification, in which three bench mark problems, which were previously programmed for a conventional computer, were recodedin the proposed Litton Polyprocessor instruction set. In all cases the Polyprocessor could accomplish the same result with fewer instructions and a diminished program space requirement.
Name: ["CHURCH CC"]

Title: Computer Simulation of Synthesizing Images by Digital Phased Arrays
Abstract: A method of synthesizing images by digital phased arrays is proposed. Following this method a numerical experiment of image synthesis is conducted to simulate arrays of 64 √ó 64 by computer. Each array element is assigned a binary digit, that is, it is either excited or nonexcited. ¬© 1970, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Aoki Y."]

Title: Models of information processing in the cerebellum
Abstract: An approach for effectively modeling the nervous system is described. When applied to the cerebellum the result is analogous to a spatial filter.
Name: ["CALVERT TW", "MENO F"]

Title: Learning probabilities of events. An analysis of the problem and its relevance for the study of decision making
Abstract: The problem of learning to associate events with their probabilities of occurrence is discussed in the context of decision making under uncertainty. Knowledge of probabilities of hypothetical states of the world is essential for adequate decision making. Subjective probabilities assigned to these hypothetical states may be revised using available probabilistic information, which often has a differential diagnostic impact on each hypothesis. Prior probability distributions, as well as conditional probability distributions representing the diagnostic impact of a set of data on a single hypothesis, may be learned by subjects in the process of observing a random sequence of events E<sub>t</sub> occuring with different relative frequencies œÜ<sub>i</sub>. It is assumed that during the observation of such a random sequence the subject through a perceptual learning process associates the events with subjective probabilities of occurrence. This is called multiple probability learning. Possible different structures of the event sequence are considered and various questions are asked concerning the effects on learning of several important characteristics of the observed probability distribution. ¬© 1970.
Name: ["Vlek C.A.J."]

Title: An algorithm for bus scheduling problems
Abstract: The problem arose in the context of devising a schedule for buses to be operated by a State Transport Corporation. An algorithm for obtaining a schedule to minimize the number of buses required is described, in which computational advantage is taken of the special structure of the problem. A computer program has been written and some results of its use are described.
Name: ["SAHA JL"]

Title: Gradient identification for linear systems
Abstract: Identification refers to the characterization of a system. In the second or dynamic situation, identification is required as a prelude to action. Action results from decisions and modifications. Sequential identification procedures make use of information as it becomes available. Sequential identification algorithms are closely related to pattern recognition training algorithms. Different information is available in the identification and pattern-recognition problems. This chapter discusses the identification of stationary and time-varying features from perfect input-output measurements. In the case of identification of stationary parameters, conditions under which the identification error approaches zero (in the limit) can be satisfied by careful design of the matrix of gains. The convergence of the gradient algorithm is also studied in the chapter and was demonstrated for the class of slowly varying parameters; however, the study was inconclusive for the class of rapidly varying parameters. The chapter presents the identification algorithms for the noisy measurement situation. ¬© 1970, Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Mendel J.M."]

Title: Selection of Pattern Features by Mathematical Programming Algorithms
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics
Abstract: The selection of a ‚Äúbest‚Äù subset of features from a given set is considered for the case where a multiplicity of constraints are present in the two-class pattern recognition problem. The problem can be formulated with a Lagrangian multiplier and an efficient iterative technique used in conjunction with dynamic programming procedures to obtain a solution when two constraints are present. The problem can be formulated in integer programming terms and use made of available integer programming computer algorithms for solution when multiple constraints are present. The Lemke-Spielberg zero-one integer algorithm is particularly useful, but other integer programming algorithms can be used also. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Nelson G.D.", "Levy D.M."]
Affiliations: [' South Dakota State University', ' University of Iowa']

Title: Ein multistabiles Gewichtselement f√ºr lernf√§hige Systeme
Source: Zeitschrift f√ºr angewandte Mathematik und Physik ZAMP
Abstract: By the addition of a second staircase generator to a frequency dividor an up-down counter can be realized. The information stored in the counter is accessible as an analogue voltage by the addition of a simple circuit. The analogue voltage can then be easily used for the generation of discriminant functions in classifying systems. Circuits of this type, generating multistable weighting functions, were tested in a simple learning machine. ¬© 1970 Birkh√§user-Verlag.
Name: ["S√©quin C.", "Minder R.", "Baldinger E."]
Affiliations: ['Institut f√ºr Angewandte Physik der Universit√§t Basel']

Title: Automatical classification of signals by a probability-theoretical decision model | [Classification automatique de signaux bas√©e sur un mod√®le probabiliste th√©orique de d√©cision | Automatische signalklassifikation durch ein wahrscheinlich-keitstlieoretischcs entscheidungsmodell]
Abstract: The probability-theoretical decision model, which is developed here, describes the automatic inclusion of signals in meaning classes if all the possible meanings of these signals are known, but no technical measurement criteria for this meaning assignment is given, that is if no one-one mapping of meaning classes onto a given set of initial signals exists. With the probability distribution (Pa) and the distribution of the conditioned probability (Pu/a) the conditioned probabilities (Pa/u) can be computed according to the Bayes Laplace theorem. They state, for every signal at the analyzer output, the probabilities with which the corresponding input signal has transmitted each of the given meanings. Then the mapping matrix (Cg/u) of the assigner can be determined by weighting with suitably chosen cost factors. This results in the desired unique transformation of an input signal into an output signal. ¬© 1970 S. Karger AG, Basel.
Name: ["Backhausen W.J."]

Title: On the Asymptotic Improvement in the Outcome of Supervised Learning Provided by Additional Nonsupervised Learning
Abstract: This paper treats an aspect of the learning or estimation phase of statistical pattern recognition (and adaptive statistical decision making in general). Simple mathematical expressions are derived for the improvement in supervised learning provided by additional nonsupervised learning when the number of learning samples is large so that asymptotic approximations are appropriate. The paper consists largely of the examination of a specific example, but, as is briefly discussed, the same procedure can be applied to other parametric problems and generalization to nonparametric problems seems possible. The example treated has the additional interesting aspect that the data does not have structure that would enable the machine to learn in the nonsupervised mode alone; but the additional nonsupervised learning can provide substantial improvement over the results obtainable by supervised learning alone. A second purpose of the paper is to suggest that a new fruitful area of research is the analytical study of the possible benefits of combining supervised and nonsupervised learning. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Cooper D.B.", "Freeman J.H."]
Keywords: ["adaptive statistical decision making", "adaptive systems", "data clustering", "statistical estimation", "statistical pattern recognition"]

Title: Some results on sparse matrices
Abstract: A comparison in the context of sparse matrices is made between the Product Form of the Inverse PFI (a form of Gauss-Jordan elimination) and the Elimination Form of the Inverse EFI (a form of Gaussian elimination). The precise relation of the elements of these two forms of the inverse is given in terms of the nontrivial elements of the three matrices L, U, UÀúl associated with the triangular factorization of the coefficient matrix A; i.e., A = L- U, where L is lower triangular and U is unit upper triangular. It is shown that the zero- nonzero structure of the PFI always has more nonzeros than the EFI. It is proved that Gaussian elimination is a minimal algorithm with respect to preserving sparseness if the diagonal elements of the matrix A are nonzero. However, Gaussian elimination is not nec essarily minimal if A has some zero diagonal elements. The same statements hold for the PFI as well. A probabilistic study of fill-in and computing times for the PFI and EFI sparse matrix algorithms is presented. This study suggests quantitatively how rapidly sparse matrices fill up for increasing densities, and emphasizes the necessity for reordering to minimize fill-in. ome Results on Sparse Matrices* By Robert K.
