In particular, two mapping operations are used which together prove especially effective for discriminating alveolar septa from background ‚Äúnoise‚Äù. The mapped images, therefore, lend themselves to simplified analysis which the computer can perform. Finally, two lungs are processed using the computerized method, and the results are compared statistically to the corresponding data produced by humans. The results are shown to be sufficiently accurate to warrant more extensive lung-tissue analysis by computer. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Levine M.D.", "Reisch M.L.", "Thurlbeck W.M."]

Title: HEURISTIC ALGORITHM FOR THE N JOB, M MACHINE SEQUENCING PROBLEM
Abstract: The search for a solution to the problem of finding an optimal or near optimal sequence of jobs being scheduled in a flow shop type situation has given consideration to both exact and approximate techniques of solution. Exact techniques, which usually require an electronic computer, have been developed to minimize some well definee criterion on problems involving a limited number of jobs. This paper describes a simple algorithm for the solution of very large sequence problems without the use of a computer. It produces approximate solutions to the n job, m machine sequencing problem where no passing is considered and the criterion is minimum total elapsed time.
Name: ["CAMPBELL HG", "DUDEK RA", "SMITH ML"]

Title: Formal algorithms for continuous-time non-linear filtering and smoothing
Abstract: Kalman‚Äôs formal limiting procedure is applied to some recent results in sequential discrete time non-linear filtering and smoothing to obtain the corresponding estimation algorithms for continuous-time non-linear dynamic systems. The resulting filtering algorithm is found to agree with the well-known Detchmendy Sridhar filter which was obtained via another method. The present smoothing algorithm is a new result. It is argued that the combined filter-smoothing results here lead to an estimation algorithm which Is second order in both system dynamics and measurement function non-linearity. ¬© 1970 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Meditch J.S."]

Title: Computer approaches to protein structure I. Analysis of atomic distances
Abstract: X-ray crystallography has yielded the detailed three-dimensional geometry for a number of proteins. In order to interpret the atomic interactions within a protein molecule, it is usually necessary to construct molecular models. Another means of acquiring information concerning molecular structure would be to recast the X-ray data into a more meaningful form. Computer programs, which convert the coordinates of the atoms into a form that facilitates the study of preferred atomic interactions, are described. In this approach the local atomic environment for each atom of the protein is calculated and printed in a manner that makes information of specific atomic interactions readily accessible. ¬© 1970.
Name: ["Tometsko A.M."]

Title: COMPUTER-CONTROLLED MESSAGE SYNTHESIS
Abstract: A system of message synthesis in which a computer speaks to people has been developed. The computer controls the output of an audio announcement system, so that responses are made with natural- sounding voice messages.
Name: ["TRUPP RD"]

Title: OPTIMUM TIME COMPRESSION IN PROJECT SCHEDULING
Abstract: An algorithm based on convex programming is developed for optimum time compression in network scheduling systems. The development allows for the activity time-cost trade- off functions to be any differentiable convex function. Decomposition theory is then applied to reduce the amount of computation necessary. This, along with a limited number of rules to structure any incoming vector, makes the algorithm amenable to time compression in large project networks.
Name: ["LAMBERSON LR", "HOCKING RR"]

Title: An asynchronous digital controller
Source: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics and Control Instrumentation
Abstract: With the advent of new solid state techniques it becomes feasible to design special purpose preprogrammed digital computers. One application for such a device is in the area of industrial process control. The trend in the field is toward computer control of all industrial processes. To have a single central computer control hundreds of continuous processes in a single plant could be a problem of insurmountable proportions if all problems such as computer failure, subsystem failures, etc. were to be accounted for. One way to alleviate the large central processor from continuous online process computations is to have ‚Äúmicrocomputers‚Äù at each control sight for controlling a particular process. The central computer is then relegated to monitor and ‚Äúset point‚Äù calculations. The size of this microcomputer is to be on the order of a cigarette package with a cost approximately a hundred dollars. The computer would perform the functions of proportional plus rate plus reset, much as its analog counterpart now does. The advantage is that all elements would now have a digital format. There are many ways to design such a computer. Asynchronous logic is used in this instance to design a particular computer. The advantage of such logic is that the computer is called to perform only when necessary. The phenomenon which makes this method of design feasible is that control calculations in general need not be extremely accurate. Thus a ‚Äúshort‚Äù word machine can be used. A three bit word is used as an example. Four or five bits would certainly be more than adequate in most cases. The design procedure as illustrated holds equally for longer words. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Frank A.A."]

Title: A branch-and-bound algorithm for flow shop scheduling problems
Abstract: This article is concerned with the solution of the flow shop scheduling problem in which all jobs have the same machine ordering. A branch-and-bound algorithm is developed for finding the sequence of J jobs to be processed on M machines which minimizes the schedule time. Thib algorithm consists of branching and bounding processes, but without the backtracking process which guarantees optimality. The procedure employed is that in constructing a subset of feasible sequences, a node representing a partial sequence is branched. Selection of the node depends on the lower-bound concept as a decision rule. This lower bound is based on resolving the conflict of jobs on the last machine. By using this algorithm, the number of explored nodes is considerably reduced and, hence, the computational effort involved in obtaining an optimal or near-optimal solution is decreased. High quality of solutions is obtained. Computationally, this algorithm extends the size of problems that can reasonably be solved. ¬© 1970 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Ashour S."]

Title: PATTERN RECOGNITION WITH ORTHONORMAL SERIES EXPANSIONS, | [MUSTERERKENNUNG MIT ORTHONORMALEN REIHENENTWICKLUNGEN]
Abstract: Pattern recognition is treated with analytical methods on the basis of orthonormal series expansions. Recognition of handwritten numerals was chosen as an example. Three criteria are given to find an appropriate system of functions. The derived systems are compared according to the expenditure necessary for classification. With a statistical test optimality of the classifier is investigated and shown to be optimal for handwritten numerals. The size of the random sample is determined by considering confidence intervals.
Name: ["NIEMANN H"]

Title: Optimal process control with random termination time
Abstract: Control of a random process is considered whose duration is not known exactly. A procedure is given for the optimal algorithm of process control with possible loss due to observation and to control taken into account as well as loss related to the deviation from the nominal of the controlled process. See also English translation in Automat Remote Contr n 6 June 1970 p 907-14
Name: ["KLEMENT'EV AA"]

Title: One method of multiple differentiation applied to a signal in automatic regulation systems
Abstract: With the plant parameters known, the approach allows one to take into account additional information concerning the control action. A plant whose parameters are unknown is replaced by a sufficiently generalized mathematical model. The filter built for this mathematical model is recommended for use in the approximate differentiation of an output signal from a plant whose parameters are unknown. See also English translation in Automat Remote Contr n 6 June 1970 p 890-6
Name: ["KALACHEV MG"]

Title: Stochastic automata as models of learning systems
Abstract: Finite automata can be used as mathematical models for systems with finite number of states that admit at discrete time intervals certain inputs and emit certain outputs. Stochastic automata for which the inputs are constant are called autonomous stochastic automata. An autonomous stochastic automaton can be interpreted as a finite-state Markov chain with the same set state. The formulation of stochastic automata can also be employed to describe the behavior of deterministic automata with random inputs. The state and automata equivalence relations and minimization problems in deterministic finite automata can be extended to the case of stochastic automata. The basic idea used in the synthesis of stochastic automata follows the formulation of deterministic automata with random inputs, that is, autonomous stochastic automata are synthesized as deterministic automata with random inputs. Because of the stochastic nature in state transitions and input-output relations stochastic automata are considered suitable for modeling learning systems. Stochastic automata models find its application in pattern recognition, multimodal search, and learning control. ¬© 1970, Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Fu K.S."]

Title: Informativeness of a set of attributes
Abstract: It is pointed out that regardless of the fact that a set of low- information attributes can be highly informative under certain conditions, this conclusion is invalid for the case where the attributes take on the values plus or minus one. Upper and lower bounds on the informativeness of a set of two attributes, expressed in terms of the informativeness of each of them, are presented. See also English translation in Automat Remote Contr n 6 June 1970 p 1009-12
Name: ["GUL'CHAK MG"]

Title: Computer control of non-linear systems with varying performance criteria
Abstract: A non-linear system, or process whose parameters are adjustable, is considered. The system is supposed to work under varying performance specifications. Stability is to be maintained at all times, of course. An algorithm combining Popov‚Äôs stability criterion and a non-linear programming technique is proposed. Using this algorithm the system‚Äôs parameters may be adjusted using a time-sharing console connected to a central computer and to the control system. Examples of non-linear third- and fourth-order systems are solvod in detail. It is clear that the algorithm may be easily extendod to higher-ordor systems. ¬© 1970 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Tabak D."]

Title: ON POSSIBILITIES OF DATA PROCESSING BY MEANS OF DIGITAL COMPUTERS, | [UBER MOEGLICHKEITEN DER MESSWERTVERARBEITUNG MIT HILFE DIGITALER RECHNER]
Abstract: The principal construction of modern digital computers is outlined. Modes of operation and function characteristics of data processing by means of a digital computer are described. A scheme of classification for computer-operated data processing is mentioned. Solutions of a system for a combined action between computer and measuring equipment are shown. From Science Abstracts.
Name: ["NAUMANN G"]

Title: TRACKING BY '%'EYE CONTROL'%'
Abstract: Because the eye is quicker than the hand, a pointing and tracking system based on human eye motions can have valuable aerospace applications. The development of a system which employes an ingenious infrared electro-optical tracker called on Oculometer is reported.
Name: ["VAUGHAN W"]

Title: Automatic checking of packages by code readers, (Automatische Kontrolle von Verpackungen durch Codeleser)
Abstract: As automation grows and the number of units and packaging rates increases, the need arises for checking operations that are independent of human effort. For this purpose the goods to be packaged are given code marks which are detected during the packaging process by code readers, and checked for correctness. The paper describes the electrical and mechanical design of a code reader.
Name: ["RATSCH J"]

Title: TRANSCRIPTION AND CORRECTION OF TEXTS ON PUNCHED TAPES, | [ERFASSEN UND KORRIGIEREN VON TEXTEN AUF LOCHSTREIFEN]
Abstract: Experience with the preparation of the Latin text of the Bible for the computer. One of the main difficulties associated with the application of automatic data processing methods in philology is data acquisition. The author describes a typewriter-punched paper tape-based method which has been successfully applied with the transcription of the text of the Vulgate. The method is compared with the punched card approach.
Name: ["OTT W"]

Title: Spectral analysis of the convolution and filtering of non-stationary stochastic processes
Abstract: A unified theory is presented that deals with the spectral description, the convolution, and the filtering on non-stationary stochastic processes. Two time-dependent spectrum definitions, the physical spectrum and the instantaneous spectrum, are discussed in detail. The physical spectrum is an easily interpreted, non-negative, frequency-time decomposition of the expected energy of a process; it is a natural extension to non-stationary processes of the usual stationary process power spectrum defined as under(lim , T ‚Üí ‚àû) E [frac(1, T) | underover(‚à´, t - T / 2, t + Œ•{hooked} / 2) x (u) e<sup>- 12 œÄ f u</sup> d u |<sup>2</sup>]. The instantaneous spectrum is a partially negative frequency-time decomposition of the expected energy of a process; it is a simple generalization of the stationary process power spectrum defined as the Fourier transform of the (ensemble average) autocorrelation function. Simple, exact, linear-system input-response relations for the instantaneous spectrum are derived for both deterministic and stochastic systems. A band-limited white definition based on the instantaneous spectrum is provided for non-stationary processes. For any desired time (or frequency) resolution, we show that the physical spectrum can be generated from the instantaneous spectrum by appropriately smoothing the instantaneous spectrum in the frequency-time plane. We also derive relationships that show how to generate the physical spectrum from (ensemble average) autocorrelation functions taken either in the time domain or the frequency domain. A discussion of non-stationary white processes is provided. Frequency-time duality is stressed throughout. Applications of the work to active sonar, passive sonar and structural vibrations are discussed. ¬© 1970 Academic Press Inc. (London) Limited.
Name: ["Mark W.D."]

Title: GENERALIZED LEARNING ALGORITHMS
Abstract: The concept of a complex learning goal is introduced as the extremum of the mathematical expectation of some function of a random functional and the mathematical expectations of other random functionals for distribution densities not known in advance. Generalized learning algorithms are found that permit the learning goal to be attained. Earlier known results areobtained from these generalized algorithms as partial results.
Name: ["TSYPKIN YAZ"]

Title: Linear control with incomplete state feedback and known initial-state statistics
Abstract: A method is proposed for the design of a linear, time-invariant state feedback control for a linear, time-invariant, finite-dimensional system with infinite duration of control (regulator problem).Which makes use of only those state variables which are available for measurement, providing that these are sufficient to render the system stable. The expected value vector and the covariance matrix for the initial state are presumed to be known. The cost function is quadratic and is expressed in terms of the initial state statistics and the cost-weight matrix. The necessary conditions are derived for the minimization of the expected value of the cost. The minimization results in a set of m simultaneous polynomial equations in m unknowns where m is the product of the number of the available state variables and the number of control signals formed out of these. The theory is illustrated by a simple example of a third-order system. ¬© 1970 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Dabke K.P."]

Title: A psycholinguistic model of syntactic complexity
Abstract: Previously developed psycholinguistic notions of syntactic complexity, involving depth, degree of nesting and node/terminal node ratio are reviewed. The authors' own system, based on transformational generative grammar, is presented. This system employs a quantitative unit measurement based on the fundamental logical operations underlying phrase- and transformation-rules. Each rule is thus seen to comprise a given number of units, and any English sentence can be quantitatively ‚Äú measured ‚Äù in this way. Evidence is cited to support the contentions (1) that this system provides hypotheses which have been testable in experimental language performance tasks and (2) that it comes closer to common-sense notions of complexity than the three other approaches. Problems germane to both theoretical foundations and practical application of the system are listed and discussed. These include the total number of transformations, usage, depth, degree of nesting, non-syntactic variables and the question of linearity. ¬© 1970, Sage Publications. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Frank S.M.", "Osser H."]

Title: IMAGE RECONSTRUCTION FROM PHASE INFORMATION ONLY
Abstract: A quantitative analysis is given of the effect on holographic image reconstruction of discarding the amplitude information contained in wavefront reflected by a diffusely reflecting, coherently illuminated surface image reconstruction from a phase record alone is analyzed for the cases of perfect and imperfect phase matching.
Name: ["KERMISCH D"]

Title: CERTAIN CRITERIA FOR THE ABSOLUTE STABILITY OF CONTROLLED SYSTEMS
Abstract: The mathematical problem of M. A. Aizerman for an automatic control system with one nonlinearity reduced to a canonical form, is discussed. Certain classes of systems for which the problem has positive solutions are defined.
Name: ["MAIGARIN BZH"]

Title: ALGORITHMIC APPROACH TO EFFICIENT REDUNDANCY OF INFORMATION SYSTEMS
Abstract: The problem is considered of the efficient determination of the reliability level of the devices in an information system, starting from the reliability imposed on a number of algorithms. There is proposed an approach to the solution of this problem and a method for the optimal distribution of reliability among the devices of an algorithmic network.
Name: ["KOGAN LM", "TSEITLIN VA"]

Title: CANONICAL REPRESENTATION OF RANDOM FUNCTIONS IN RELIABILITY PROGNOSI
Abstract: By computer simulation the problem is solved of a random process attaining boundaries on condition that, as a result of a check, its state at a certain instant (instants) has become known. The investigated random process is represented in the form of a canonical expansion. Results are presented of a simulation of a queueing system using the proposed prognosis method.
Name: ["KUDRITSKII VD"]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR FINDING SHORTEST ROUTES FROM ALL SOURCE NODES TO A GIVEN DESTINATION IN GENERAL NETWORKS
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present an algorithm for solving the problem in which the distances fo some arcs are negative.
Name: ["YEN JY"]

Title: DESIGN OF SELF-OSCILLATORY ADAPTIVE SYSTEM OF VARIABLE STRUCTURE
Abstract: A method of synthesis is proposed for an adjustment algorithm of an adaptive device for a self-oscillatory system that is based on the describing function technique. The theoretical results are illustrated by examples.
Name: ["ALEKSANDROV AD", "VAL'KOV LS", "GAVRILIN MG", "MALEN'KII LYA", "SABUROV NV", "KHABAROV VS"]

Title: IMPROVED ALGORITHM FOR DIRECT DIGITAL CONTROL
Abstract: A digital algorithm which eliminates the effect of dead time is not penalized by sampling. This can be accomplished by including an analytical predictor in the feedback path, to estimate the value of the process output one half sample in the future. Corrective action is based on the predicted rather than the actual output.
Name: ["MOORE CF", "SMITH CL", "MURRILL PW"]

Title: Robot data screening, an automatic search technique
Abstract: The problem of extracting useful information from a motley of data aggregates is investigated in the light of traditionally applied statistics. Robot data screening and the requirements of automatic scale procedures are then considered in detail. Using the concepts of entropy and predictability the Robot Data Screening Program endeavours to establish a procedure for applying automated data processing for obtaining useful information, particularly in problems which do not fit comfortably within traditional statistical thinking. ¬© 1970.
Name: ["Sterling T.D.", "Haberman S.", "Pollack S."]

Title: WORD-RECOGNITION MACHINE
Abstract: An equipment that is capable of recognizing the digits 0 to 9, spoken by a wide range of speakers, is described. Recognition scores of the order of 95% are achieved for male speakers of British origin. It is suggested that, in a phoneme-based recognition scheme, improvements in feature extraction are of greater importance than the optimization of decision strategies. Future improvements must depend on the wider use of adaptation by the machine to the talker, and the forms this adaptation might take are discussed.
Name: ["SCARR RWA"]

Title: Linear systems analysis of the limulus retina
Abstract: The remarkable sensitivity of the Limulus eye to moving patterns can be explained by the dynamics of the neural mechanisms that transduce light to the firing of nerve impulses. The excitatory generator potential results from the superposition of small discrete potentials triggered by photon absorptions. This mechanism specifies both the frequency response to time‚Äêvarying stimuli and the spectral properties of the intrinsic noise. The response to higher frequencies is enhanced by two inhibitory synaptic mechanisms; self‚Äêinhibition that is local to photoreceptors, and lateral inhibition that depends on the activity in neighboring photoreceptors. Analysis of these mechanisms yields a mathematical model that accounts for both the deterministic and the stochastic components in the spike train. Copyright ¬© 1970 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.
Name: ["Dodge F.A.", "Shapley R.M.", "Knight B.W."]

Title: A predictive time-optimal controller for second-order systems with time delay
Abstract: This paper presents a method of interactive or real-time predictive control which can be implemented without a stored program computer. By restricting the process dy namic model to a second-order-plus-dead-time format, a configuration which is satisfactory for many chemical or petroleum processing systems, a time-optimal controller can be built entirely on a small analog/hybrid computer. For set-point changes, the controller utilizes an analog model of the process to search out the predicted optimum input switching sequence and continuously maintains the process on the time-optimal trajectory. Because of the predictive nature of the method there is no necessity to include the time-delay term in the high-speed model; the predicted switches in the process input are simply ad vanced in time by the amount of the time-delay. ¬© 1970, Sage Publications. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Mellichamp D.A."]
Affiliations: ['Department of Chemical and Nuclear Engineering University of California']

Title: On Feature Selection in a Class of Distribution-Free Pattern Classifiers
Abstract: A feature-selection procedure is proposed for the class of distribution-free pattern classifiers [1], [2]. The selection procedure can be readily carried out on fixed (large) training samples using matrix inversion. If direct matrix inversion is to be avoided, the approximation method [4] or the stochastic-approximation procedure [2] can be applied to the training samples. The proposed procedure, aside from furnishing a statistical interpretation, has a mapping interpretation. It has the unique property of designing a pattern classifier under a single-performance criterion instead of the conventional division of receptor and categorizer. It enables the system to come closest to the minimum-risk ideal classifier. In particular, for two-class problems having normal distributions with equal covariance matrices, equal costs for misrecognition, and equal a priori probabilities, the proposed procedure yields the optimum Bayes procedure without the knowledge of the class distributions. Furthermore, the proposed feature-selection procedure is the same as that of the divergence computation. Experimental results are presented. They are considered satisfactory. Name: ["Wee W.G."]

Title: STATISTICAL TECHNIQUES FOR CLASSIFICATION.
Abstract: Consideration is given to some statistical techniques that are or may be related to automated multiphasic health testing. The usage and possible development of discrimination and classification techniques are discussed. Also, various multivariate techniques which may have some use for examining the large amounts of multivariate data which automated multiphasic health testing may generate are examined.
Name: ["Fisher Jr. Lloyd D."]

Title: Algorithmic Solution of the Change-Making Problem
Abstract: The change-making problem (assemble a total of C cents using the least number of coins) is representative of a frequently encountered class of optimization problems. A recursive algorithm is developed for solving that problem. A much simpler--but not universally applicable--algorithm is also presented, and a procedure is described for testing its validity for any specified set of parameters. ¬© 1970, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Chang S.K.", "Gill A."]
Affiliations: [' Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences']

Title: Nonlinear time-domain models of human controllers
Source: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
Abstract: Data from a compensatory tracking task are analyzed by using time-domain models. The linear time-domain results are transformed and compared with frequency-domain results. The nonlinear time-domain model of the same data reduced the remnant or residual power by only a small amount. The need for testing models on independent data is discussed. A novel, but attractive, method of generating functions for an efficient functional expansion of time-domain models is offered. ¬© 1970 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Taylor Jr. L.W."]

Title: A theory of pattern perception based on human physiology
Abstract: The grOBS connectivity, patterns of information pathways in the primate and human visual systems, when examined by an information proeessing engineer, bear a curious resemblance to the two-dimensional-pattern optical computers which he builds himself in an attempt to achieve pattern recognition. The portions of the visual system inferior to the primary visual cortex are essentially a topologically accurate homeo-morphic mapping of the retinal image, at least in the vioinity of the fovea. Analysis of the topological espects of the visual scene and hence Pattern Recognition' must therefore take place in the primary visual cortex and successive cortical areas. We have previously reported how intra- and intor-cortioal connectivity could support a combined memory and computation scheme capable of performing pattern recognition by a variation of two-dimensional -cross correlation. This paper is a report of an extension of the previous model enabling it to perform pattern recognition by computing the two-dimensional Fourier transform of input images in a manner isomorphic to computation of the 'Fraunhofer diffraction pattern in optioal computers. It is shown that the use of the Fourier transform of an unknown pattern in a subsequent correlation scheme results in a pattern recognition system which is not easily faulted by the small local mutilations of input patterns whioh badly compromise straight oorrelation pattern recognition schemes. ¬© 1970 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Kabrisky M.", "Turman O.", "Day C.M."]
Affiliations: ['Wright Patterson Air Force Base', 'U.S. Air Force Institute of Technology']

Title: On filtering and smoothing algorithms for non-linear state estimation?
Abstract: This paper discusses a summary derivation of maximum a posteriori estimation for continuous and discrete non-linear systems. It is known that with Gaussian a priori statistics, the maximum a posteriori estimate is equivalent to an appropriate least squares fit. Filtering, fixed interval and fixed point smoothing algorithms for approximate non-linear estimation are obtained for the least squares curve fit using ' running time ' and ' fixed time ' invariant embedding. Examples illustrating the use of the algorithms are presented. ¬© 1975 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Sage A.P.", "Ewing W.S."]

Title: RELATIONS BETWEEN MATRIX-SOLUTIONS THAT ARE USED IN PROGRAMS FOR AUTOMATIC LENS DESIGN, | [ZUSAMMENHAENGE DER IN PROGRAMMEN ZUR AUTOMATISCHEN KORREKTION VERWENDETEN LOESUNGSMATRIZEN]
Abstract: The linearized dependence of aberrations on system parameters is given by the variation matrix A. The dependence of parameter changes on required aberration changes is given by the matrix solution L. The solution of the adaptive procedure by Glatzel and the least-squares solution are each the generalized inverse of the variation matrix. The damped least squares solution by Girard and Wynne is a modification of the least-squares solution.
Name: ["KRAUTTER M"]

Title: An Efficient Context-Free Parsing Algorithm
Abstract: A parsing algorithm which seems to be the most efficient general context-free algorithm known is described. It is similar to both Knuth's LR(k) algorithm and the familiar top-down algorithm. It has a time bound proportional to n<sub>3</sub> (where n is the length of the string being parsed) in general; it has an n<sub>2</sub> bound for unambiguous grammars; and it runs in linear time on a large class of grammars, which seems to include most practical context-free programming language grammars. In an empirical comparison it appears to be superior to the top-down and bottom-up algorithms studied by Griffiths and Petrick. ¬© 1970, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Earley J."]

Title: General Repetitive Events and Machines
Abstract: A finite automaton is a general repetitive machine if there is a path in the state graph from every final state to the start state. In this paper general repetitive events are defined in terms of certain factorization properties of the associated regular expressions, and a one-to-one onto correspondence is shown between general repetitive machines and general repetitive events. Name: ["Reynolds B.G."]
Keywords: ["automaton", "finite automaton", "general repetitive event", "general repetitive machine", "automaton general"]

Title: On the Uniqueness of Minimal-State Stochastic Sequential Machines
Abstract: A necessary and sufficient condition for a minimal-state stochastic sequential machine to be unique (up to renumbering the states) is described. Furthermore, a geometric characterization of the class of state-equivalent machines is given. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Nieh T.T."]

Title: INFLUENCE OF A PREDICTIVE DISPLAY ON THE DISTRIBUTION DENSITY AND POWER DENSITY FUNCTION DURING THE MANUAL CONTROL OF A RATE-CONTROL SYSTEM, | [DER EINFLUSS EINER VORANZEIGE AUF VERTEILUNGSDICHTE-UND LEISTUNGSDICHTEFUNKTIONEN BEI DER MANUELLEN FOLGEREGELUNG EINES BESCHLEUNIGUNGSSYSTEMS]
Abstract: The control of a roll motion of a VTOL aircraft is made easier because the pilot is no longer forced to estimate himself the extrapolated control error. It is shown how a predictive display effects the autocorrelation and power density function of the human input and output signal control error and stick signal. Distribution function of control error and stick signal are given for tests with and without additional predictive display.
Name: ["JOHANNSEN G"]

Title: IDENTIFICATION IN A CLASS OF RANDOM FUNCTIONALS
Abstract: The identification is considered of nonlinear functionals that allow finite dimensional local linear approximation by known functionals with a random approximation error. On the basis of finitely many observations with correlated noise author determines a linear (in the observations) and unbiased estimate of the functponal to be identified with a minimum mean-square error.
Name: ["PETERSEN IF"]

Title: APPLICATION OF MARKOV-PROCESS THEORY TO THE DETERMINATION OF STATISTICAL CHARACTERISTICS OF NONLINEAR SAMPLED-DATA SYSTEMS
Abstract: Integro-difference equation are derived for the determination of the one-dimensional distribution law (for a single arbitrary time) for a multidimensional random process whose components are considered at fixed equidistant times. For the case of a Markov process the equation derived is a generalization of the Fokker- Planck-Kolmogorov equation to processes with the components indicated.
Name: ["VOLOSOV ID"]

Title: ADAPTIVE SYSTEM FOR TRACKING VARYING PARAMETERS OF A FUNCTIONAL TRANSFORMER'S CHARACTERISTIC
Abstract: See also English translation in Automat Remote Contr n 2 Feb 1970 p 209-14; A condition is obtained for selecting the correction step U, this condition being necessary for the reproduction of the process by which the transformer's parameters change. An expression is found for the mean-square tracking error which permits the optimal correction step to be defined. An algorithm is considered for the automatic tuning of parameter U during the course of the system's operation, based on the use of the procedure of stochastic approximation.
Name: ["LETSKII EK"]

Title: APPLICATION OF THE KALMAN FILTER TO CONTINUOUS SIGNAL RESTORATION
Abstract: The R. E. Kalman filter is applied to the inverse filtering or deconvolution problem. The derivation given of the Kalman filter emphasizes the relationship between the Kalman and N. Wiener filter. This derivation is based on the representation of systems by state variables and the modeling of random processes as the output of linear systems excited by white noise. Illustrative results indicate the applicability of these techniques to a variety of geophysical data processing problems.
Name: ["BAYLESS JW", "BRIGHAM EO"]

Title: OPTIMAL FILTERING OF MULTIALTERNATIVE SIGNALS
Abstract: For the description of a useful signal a two-dimensional Markov process with m states is assumed. A method of transition is demonstrated.
Name: ["KUL'MAN NK"]

Title: Note on tape reversal complexity of languages
Abstract: The number of tape reversals required for the recognition of a set of inputs by a 1-tape Turing machine (TM) has been proposed before as a measure of complexi. It is shown that if a set is recognizable by a multi-tape TM with no more than R(n) tape reversals, where n is the input length, then the set is recog. It is also shown that if a set is recognizable by a multi-tape TM within time T(n), then the set is recognizable by a 1-tape off-line TM with no more than. Upper bounds on the number of reversals necessary for the recognition of a number of well-known classes of languages are also obtained. ¬© 1970 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Kameda T.", "Vollmar R."]

Title: STATISTICAL SYNTHESIS OF LOGICAL CIRCUITS FOR PATTERN RECOGNITION
Abstract: A method is proposed for the construction of logical circuits intended for the recognition of patterns from their observed coordinates (features), represented in the form of binary codes. In the synthesis the conditional distribution laws of the observed coordinates for each of the recognized pattern are assumed known. A method is described for the synthesis of optimal and close-to- optimal circuits with respect to a chosen statistical criterion.
Name: ["BURDIN NM", "YARUSHEK VE"]

Title: MINIMAL LENGTH OF UNIQUELY-CONTINUABLE INPUT- OUTPUT SEQUENCE REALIZED BY AUTOMATA
Abstract: It is pointed out that in any deterministic automation with pairwise distinguishable states, uniquelycontinuable input-output sequences are realized of length not exceeding 2n-(log//2n).
Name: ["RUDNEV VV"]

Title: RELIABILITY OF A HIERARCHICAL CONTROL SYSTEM
Abstract: Expressions are obtained for the reliability of a control system with hierarchical structure as a function of the reliability characteristics of the apparatus and the number of control levels. The model is reduced mathematically to a homogeneous Markov process with finite number of states. Conditions are derived for which passage to a hierarchical structure is useful for reliability considerations.
Name: ["KOEKIN AI"]

Title: RELATIVE SEMI-INVARIANTS IN THE FILTERING OF PROCESSES WITH STEP COMPONENTS
Abstract: Algorithms for approximate determination of the optimum estimates are devised. Examples are given.
Name: ["YASHIN AI"]

Title: APPLICATION OF METHODS OF AUTOMATIC CLASSIFICATION TO THE CONSTRUCTION OF A STATIC MODEL OF A PLANT
Abstract: The problem is considered of constructing a mathematical description of a static plant in a situation where the number of known values of the output paameter is substantially smaller than the number of known vectors of the input parameters, and there is no a priori information about the character of the relation to be recovered. A method is proposed for the solution of the problem using automatic classification algorithms. The efficiency of the method is illustrated by the example of the process of high pressure ethylene polymerization.
Name: ["DOROFEYUK AA", "KASAVIN AD", "TORGOVITSKII ISH"]

Title: MULTIPLE REGRESSION WITH UNBALANCED DATA
Abstract: Regression analysis has become a very popular method for analyzing existing plant and research data. The existance of correlations among the independent variables is recognized as a major pitfall in the proper interpretation of such data%. This paper outlines the errors in interpretation that may result when specific degrees of correlation exist. The situation is examined for two-variable case, fitting first and second degree models to data from sources of varying complexity. A computer was used to generate and anzlyze the data.
Name: ["HINCHEN JD"]

Title: AO, 1 ALGORITHM FOR CITY PLANNING
Abstract: A model for the allocation of research funds to a series of urban experiments whose outcomes determine the ultimate disposition and allocation of greater amounts of money for urban housing projects. It is shown that the allocation model is a particular application of a technique which can be applied in the design of statistical experiments, and the paper describes the algorithm for solving the 0,1 integer programming problem which results from the formulation of the urban model. An association matrix was derived which expresses the likelihood that certain experimental procedures will be paired in actual practice.
Name: ["FIERING MB"]

Title: An automatic computational procedure for calculating natural frequencies of skeletal structures
Abstract: This paper describes an infallible method of finding all required natural frequencies of undamped vibration of linearly elastic skeletal structures, when the members are analysed as continuous and uniform, using dynamic stiffnesses, and not as an approximately equivalent lumped-mass system. The natural frequencies are, in general, those for which |K| = 0, where K is the dynamic overall stiffness matrix. In this case K is a transcendental function of the frequency œâ and will have an infinite number of zeros, some of which may be coincident. Furthermore |K| may become infinite. Thus in general |K| is a highly irregular function of œâ and this poses problems when writing general-purpose computer programs, which must be capable of finding the natural frequencies of an infinite variety of possible structures. The authors' method completely overcomes these problems by finding, with virtually no extra work, how many natural frequencies have been exceeded at each iteration. Furthermore, this information will usually reduce the number of iterations needed, leading to a saving in total computation time. The method is developed explicitly for rigidly jointed plane frames, but space frames, grillages, etc. can be included without extension of the principles. ¬© 1970.
Name: ["Williams F.W.", "Wittrick W.H."]

Title: Random matrices and neural networks
Abstract: In connection with some problems that arise in the study of neural networks random matrices are considered and the probability for them to have certain rank is investigated. Two models are studied in a simple-minded approach to problems of this type. ¬© 1970 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["de Luca A.", "Ricciardi L.M.", "Vasudevan R."]
Affiliations: ['Laboratorio di Cibernetica del C.N.R.', "Istituto di Fisica Teorica dell'Universita"]

Title: Adaptive Linear Classifier by Linear Programming
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics
Abstract: A linear classifier based on linear programming which is adaptive to a change in the set of input vectors is discussed. Different from other linear classifiers, this one maintains the maximum reliability of its operation, provided that the set of pattern vectors is linearly separable. A procedure of deriving an optimum structure of the linear classifier for a change in the set of input vectors is a modification of the ordinary simplex method and yields an optimum structure in much fewer iterations than the straightforward application of the ordinary simplex method does. The adaptive procedure is then extended to the case in which a linear classifier maintains the minimum number of erroneously classified input vectors even if the set of input pattern vectors is not linearly separable. This is based on Gomory's algorithm for integer linear programming. The feasibility and efficiency of these linear classifiers are computationally proved by some examples. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Ibaraki T.", "Muroga S."]
Affiliations: [' University of Illinois', ' University of Illinois']

Title: Entropy and Data Compression
Abstract: An optimum compression ratio (OCR) is defined for a source, leading to ‚Äúefficiency‚Äù of a compression algorithm and resulting in a good evaluation of data-compression schemes. Applications to first- and second-order Markov sources, in conjunction with the ‚Äúfan‚Äù and ‚Äúzero-order hold‚Äù compression schemes, are also presented. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Tzannes N.S.", "Sarantakis A.J.", "Farr E.H."]

Title: On the Difficulty of Computations
Abstract: Two practical considerations concerning the use of computing machines are the amount of information that must be given to the machine for it to perform a given task and the time it takes the machine to perform it. The size of programs and their running time are studied for mathematical models of computing machines. The study of the amount of information (i.e., number of bits) in a computer program needed for it to put out a given finite binary sequence leads to a definition of a random sequence; the random sequences of a given length are those that require the longest programs. The study of the running time of programs for computing infinite sets of natural numbers leads to an arithmetic of computers, which is a distributive lattice. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Chaitin G.J."]

Title: Simplification of the Covering Problem with Application to Boolean Expressions
Abstract: It is well known that the covering problem can be formulated as a system of linear inequalities together with a linear expression to be minimized; a technique for simplifying this system of inequalities is analyzed. Specifically, the conditions for replacing two inequalities by a single inequality are investigated. A lower bound on the number of inequalities in a simplified system is derived. A statistical analysis of the reduction procedure is presented. Experimental results dealing with the effectiveness of the reduction technique and on the solution of the covering problem in both reduced and unreduced form are given. Finally, a specific covering problem, namely that of simplifying Boolean expressions, is considered. Techniques for taking into consideration fanout constraints are introduced, and the simplification of this new problem is considered. ¬© 1970, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Breuer M.A."]
Keywords: ["boolean simplification", "covering problem", "integer linear programming", "mathematical programming", "simplification techniques"]

Title: THRESHOLDED CONVOLUTION OPERATIONS
Abstract: Thres holded convolution operations occur frequently in picture- processing algorithms and in special picture-processing hardware, such as image storage tubes. A number of theorems revealing some of the effects of combining the thresholding operation with the convolution operation are derived. In particular it is shown that a discrete convolution operation takes binary-valued functions into binary-valued functions if and only if it is a translation or identically zero. It is also shown that no thresholded nonzero convolution (i. e. a nonzero convolution followed by a thresholding) is equivalent to an unthresholded discrete convolution.
Name: ["SKLANSKY J"]

Title: Some Algebraic Properties of Speech Signals
Abstract: Although the set of all recognizable speech signals is not closed under superposition. certain subsets are found experimentally to have vector space properties, and hence may be discriminated by means of annihilation transforms. Experimental results are described for speech phoneme discrimination using time-domain annihilation filters. ¬© 1970, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Moshier S.L."]

Title: AUTOMATIC INTERCEPT SYSTEM USING PRERECORDED SPEECH SEGMENTS
Abstract: A telephone intercept service system featuring automatic assembly of prerecorded words, phrases, and syllables is described. The objective is to automate the telephone intercept service which is being handled by intercept operators. When a cusomter is reassigned to a new number for some reason, any other customer who dials the previous number will be advised that the number is no longer working and he should dial the new number. This interception service will be continued on the discontinued number for a period long enough to ensure that very few calls intended for a previous number will be routed to the number.
Name: ["SUEYOSHI H", "ICHIMURA A"]

Title: Diffraction-Pattern Sampling for Automatic Pattern Recognition
Abstract: This paper describes diffraction-pattern sampling as a basis for automatic pattern recognition in photographic imagery; it covers: Diffraction-pattern generation. diffraction-pattern/image-area relationships, diffraction-pattern sampling, algorithm development (using an interactive computer-graphic based facility), facility description, and experimental results which have been obtained over the last few years at General Motors‚Äô AC Electronics-Defense Research Laboratories, Santa Barbara, Calif. Sampling the diffraction pattern results in a sample signature‚Äìa different one for each sampling geometry. The kinds of information obtainable from sample signatures are described, and considerations for developing algorithms based on such information are discussed. A tutorial section is included for the purpose of giving the reader an intuitive feeling for the kinds of information contained in a diffraction pattern and how it relates to the original photographic imagery. ¬© 1970, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Lendaris G.G.", "Stanley G.L."]

Title: TIME-OPTIMAL CONTROL OF A LINEAR DISTRIBUTED PARAMETER SYSTEM
Source: J Inst Eng (India) Electron Telecommun Eng Div
Abstract: Paper is devoted to the problem of time-optimal control of systems whose dynamic behaviors are characterized by linear partial differential equations and the control functions are subject to a general norm constraint. The problem is analyzed by the methods of functional analysis, and reduces to one in nonlinear programming. The method is illustrated by a diffusion process solving it numerically using the method of steepest descent.
Name: ["SINGH RNP"]

Title: COMPUTER-CONTROLLED QUEUEING PROCESS WITH CONSTANT- ACCESS CYCLE
Abstract: A process in which the queue has feedback is examined. The process has a Poisson input, exponential servers and a first-come- first- served queue discipline, but the services must start at an access point because of the computer control. A simple model of the queueing process is presented. The fundamental equations and the generating function for the stationary-state probability distribution of the queueing process are derived, and a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a stationary distribution is obtained. Paper 5991 E.
Name: ["CHAN WC"]

Title: EXTENSIONS OF QUADRATIC MINIMISATION THEORY. THE DISCRETE-TIME CASE
Abstract: A covariance condition is shown to be a necessary condition for the existence of a finite control law associated with discrete-time quadratic loss-minimization problems. Sufficient conditions (including the covariance condition) are then determined which extend the range of optimal-control problems, for which a well defined control law may be calculated. The results may also be applied to solving problems in filtering and stability theory.
Name: ["MOORE JB", "COLEBATCH PM"]

Title: CLASS OF GENERAL RELIABILITY GROWTH PREDICTION MODELS
Abstract: In structuring reliability growth prediction models as Markov chains, it is shown that the computation of the reliability after n trials and possible associated repairs Rn may be accomplished with any of several different methods. The paper considers a class of models that accommodates variations in several important factors, such as the interdependencies of assignable cause failure modes, inclusion of an inherent failure mode, the repair policy, and the distribution of initial states of the system.
Name: ["BARR DR"]

Title: MINIMIZING THE NUMBER OF OPERATIONS IN CERTAIN DISCRETE-VARIABLE OPTIMIZATION PROBLEMS
Abstract: The paper deals with the solution to a discrete optimization problem by decomposition. It develops a criterion for ranking the decomposition procedures, discusses the properties of the optimal decompositions, and gives an algorithm for finding the best decomposition in the case of no storage limitation.
Name: ["BRIOSCHI F", "EVEN S"]

Title: APPLICATIONS OF THE FOLDANT ALGORITHM TO NETWORK ANALYSIS
Abstract: Certain algebraic operations of a lower triangular matrix of a graph G are called foldant operations. The algorithm to find the sum of k-tree products is constructed using foldant operations. The method for calculating all the y-parameters of a passive four- terminal network simultaneously using the algorithm, and the method for obtaining the number of all subgraphs g(i, k) of G that contain i independent closed paths and have the separation number k are described. The calculation of the probability that certain terminals are connected in a multiterminal network is also described.
Name: ["HATTORI Y", "SASAKI T"]

Title: METHOD OF AUTOMATIC GENERATION OF COMPILERS
Abstract: A new method of automatic generation of compilers based on the theory of automata is reported. A new algorithm for translating regular expressions into corresponding state graphs by means of list processing techniques is presented. An application of the algorithm to a language syntax analyzer is described in order to demonstrate the usefulness of the method.
Name: ["FUJINO K"]

Title: Scheduling to Reduce Conflict in Meetings
Abstract: Conflicts in scheduling can be treated as defining an undirected linear graph independently of the relation of the activities in conflict to additional constraints of time and space. Each connected component of such a graph, which can be found by an algorithm described by Gotlieb and Corneil, corresponds to a set of events that must be scheduled at different times. ¬© 1970, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Grimes J.E."]

Title: ADAPTIVE CONTROL OF INFLATION AND UNEMPLOYMENT.
Source: IEEE, Northeast Electronics Research & Eng Meeting, NEREM Record, Tech Application Papers
Abstract: The U. S. economy can be modeled as an adaptive control system with unknown plant parameters, where the state and control are the rates of inflation and unemployment. Optimal Bayesian control policies for adaptive systems, however, can be obtained only for special cases. The purpose of this paper is to present an approximation for adaptive control problems with linear plant equations and quadratic performance indices. The distinguishing feature of the approximation is that the solution to the modified problem can be given an economic interpretation.
Name: ["MacRae C.D.", "MacRae E.C."]

Title: On the structure of subrecursive degrees
Source: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: Subrecursive degrees are partitions of computable (recursive) functions generated by strong reducibility orderings. Such reducibilities can be naturally characterized in terms of closure operations. Closure operations corresponding to standard reducibilities such as "primitive recursive," etc., are computation time closed. It is shown that if the closure operation defining a strong reducibility satisfies certain axioms, then the partial ordering of the subrecursive degrees contains dense chains. ¬© 1970 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Basu S.K."]

Title: STATUS OF REAL-TIME ESTIMATION TECHNIQUES AND THEIR APPLICATION TO TRACKING AND NAVIGATION.
Source: IEEE, Northeast Electronics Research & Eng Meeting, NEREM Record, Tech Application Papers
Abstract: The prevalence of digital computers has provided the impetus for application of real-time estimation techniques. The challenge to the engineer designing such systems is to provide the best performance under often severe constraints on computational capability. The abundance of estimation methods suitable for real-time applications aids in the design by providing many options, but also hinders the designer by making his process of choice a potentially costly undertaking. It is the purpose of this review to consider the many estimation techniques on the basis of the modeling complexity required to apply the technique. The modeling of the measurement process, disturbances, and statistics of the measurement environment are discussed.
Name: ["O'Donnell J."]

Title: Monte Carlo techniques for prediction and filtering of non-linear stochastic processes
Abstract: This paper deals with the estimation of state variables for non-linear stochastic discrete-time processes. For the prediction problem, a direct evaluation of the Chapman-Kolmogorov equation may be prohibitive while the Monte Carlo approach offers an elegant alternative solution. The system is simulated and relevant data collected in order to estimate some parameters of the probability density function an arbitrary number of time steps ahead. The conjecture of inefficiency inherent in Monte Carlo work is invalidated with two variance reduction techniques. The non-linear filtering problem is discussed within the framework of the Bayesian approach. The problem of estimating the conditional mean of the posterior density function is formulated as a multidimensional integral. The control variate method presented shows that the Monte Carlo approach can successfully be adapted to estimate the approximation error of existing non-linear filtering equations and to improve their accuracy significantly. ¬© 1970.
Name: ["Handschin J.E."]

Title: A one-sided stochastic model of search problem
Source: Trabajos de estadistica y de investigacion operativa
Abstract: The underlying process is a cyclic, 3 State Semi Markov with general holding time distributions. The supplementary variable technique [1] has been employed to solve the model. The generating functions of the State probabilities have been obtained in terms of Laplace transforms [2]. In the end, it is shown that the limiting probabilities of the system in 3-State are proportional to the mean holding times in corresponding States, from which the asymptotic rate of scoring hits is obtained for a particular case. ¬© 1970 Springer.
Name: ["Arora S.D."]
Affiliations: ['Dte of Scientific Evaluation Ministry of Defence']

Title: STUDY PROGRAM DETERMINATION BY DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING
Abstract: The problem this paper deals with is the selection of an optimal study program or curriculum, tailored to an individual student, by maximizing educational potential. Educational potential in a subject area is defined as a non‚Äêlinear function of the number of courses taken in the respective subject area. Parameters of the educational potential function include a type of learner parameter, a type of teaching parameter, and a subject area parameter. The latter is a function of the number of courses available in the subject area. The educational potential or learning function is based on a body of empirical data accumulated by experimental psychologists, and has the shape of a stretched‚Äêout letter S. The optimal study program is obtained by finding the maximum sum of the subject areas' educational potentials. The technique used to find this maximum sum is called dynamic programming. A computer program was written to perform the solution procedure on a digital computer. Copyright ¬© 1970, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved
Name: ["PEGELS C.C."]
Affiliations: ['State University of New York at Buffalo']

Title: A model for cortical memory
Abstract: Information in the nervous system is coded into patterns of firing in specific collections of neurons. We assume without proof that memorization is the conversion of these firing patterns into spatially distributed patterns (such as changes in the transmission properties of the synapses or cell membranes). We also assume that recall is the synthesis of a copy of the firing patterns which occurred during storage. It is the purpose of this paper to develop a network called a memory block which can store, search for, and recall these firing patterns. The storage mechanism of the memory block closely resembles the holographic storage process. Information which is stored in a particular memory location is distributed throughout all the neurons of that location. Damage to large numbers of neurons in a given memory location does not destroy the stored information but merely reduces the fidelity of the recalled patterns. When a specific piece of information is required from the memory block, a similar information pattern is sent to every memory location. Each memory location correlates the test pattern with its stored patterns and returns a signal which is proportional to the similarity between the test pattern and the corresponding stored pattern. A high signal indicates a close match and locates the stored information. Recall is immediately possible. To convert between temporal firing patterns and spatial neuronal changes, a memory timing mechanism is introduced. This mechanism is a wave of activity in the nonneuronal medium which inactivates all but a thin layer in the network. During storage, the active layer moves through the appropriate memory location. In this way, the time of input is converted into position within the storage network. During recall, the memory timing mechanism is again used, this time to convert between position of storage and time of output. A learning network is then presented which utilizes the memory block as a storage network. This network differs from other learning models in several prominent ways. Not only are all input patterns permanently stored, but the memory traces remain unchanged for the life of the system. Learning and forgetting are independent of the memory traces themselves but depend on the threshold of recallability of information from the individual memory locations. We conclude with a brief discussion of some physiological and biological questions posed by the model. ¬© 1970.
Name: ["Baron R.J."]

Title: On bounds on the number of steps to compute functions
Source: Proceedings of the Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
Abstract: Let f be a partial recursive function defined in terms of other functions gi-gn such that f converges if and only if some well defined assertions about the convergency of g,.,gn hold: then we can find a total function (depending on the number of steps required to compute gi,.,gn) that bounds the step counting function of f almost everywhere f is defined. It is also shown that, in that case, to compute the bound to the step counting function is not much harder than computing the step counting function itself. ¬© Proceedings of the 3rd ACM Symposium on Operating Systems Principles, SOSP 1971. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Ausiello G."]

Title: Input-Adaptive Kalman-Bucy Filtering
Abstract: The theory of nonlinear filtering (Stratonovitch, Kushner, and Bucy) is applied 1) to real-time identification of the covariance matrix of the input noise in the process model used by Kalman and Bucy [1] and 2) to adaptive mechanization of the matrix Riccati equation and the gain matrix in the Kalman-Bucy filter. ¬© 1970 IEEE

Title: The Innovations Approach to Detection and Estimation Theory
Abstract: Given a stochastic process, its innovations process will be defined as a white Gaussian noise process obtained from the original process by a causal and causally invertible transformation. The significance of such a representation, when it exists, is that statistical inference problems based on observation of the original process can be replaced by simpler problems based on white noise observations. Seven applications to linear and nonlinear least squares estimation. Gaussian and non-Gaussian detection problems, solution of Fredholm integral equations, and the calculation of mutual information, will be described. The major new results are summarized in seven theorems. Some powerful mathematical tools will be introduced, but emphasis will be placed on the considerable physical significance of the results.
