Examples are presented to demonstrate the procedure in action and show that, even in cases where the system has been carefully numbered, considerable improvement can be achieved. The procedure is also applicable to band matrix solution techniques. Copyright ¬© 1970 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd
Name: ["King I.P."]

Title: On the Input and Output Reducibility of Multivariable Linear Systems
Abstract: By introducing into a constant linear system (F, G, H) with input vector u and output vector y an open-loop control u = Pv and observer z = Qy, a new constant linear system (F, GP, QH) results which has input vector v and output vector z. The problem investigated is one of constructing (F, GP, QH) so that v and z have minimal dimension, subject to the condition that the controllability and observability properties of (F, G, H) are preserved. It is shown that when the scalar field ‚Ñ± (over which the system is defined) is infinite, the minimal dimensions of v and z are essentially independent of the specific values of the input and output matrices G and H. It is also shown that this is not the case when ‚Ñ± is finite. Furthermore, an algorithm is presented for the construction of the minimal input (minimal output) (F, GP, QH), which is directly represented in a useful canonical form. ¬© 1970 IEEE
Name: ["Heymann M."]

Title: Application of Stochastic Approximation to On-Line System Identification
Abstract: A nonparametric stochastic approximation type of algorithm for on-line identification is considered. By on-line, it is meant that the system is driven by an arbitrary known input, the control, in addition to an input noise disturbance. Thus, the control effort proceeds in conjunction with identification and is in no way restricted by the requirements of identification. The system is assumed to be all-pole with unknown poles, unknown gain, and noiseless output measurement. Consequently, the procedure is useful when the degree of inaccuracy in the knowledge of the system is much larger than possible output measurement errors. Adaptive control using this procedure is discussed, together with a numerical example. ¬© 1970 IEEE
Name: ["Bar-Shalom Y.", "Schwartz S.C."]

Title: Search for the optima of stochastic functions
Abstract: A method is proposed for search for extrema in stochastic systems. Search algorithms which were developed and are successful in. noise-free systems are used in the noise - eorrupted systems except that minimum variance estimators are substituted for direct functional measurements. The optimal programme of estimators is obtained by solving a variational calculus problem. Ail example showing significant improvement in search response over traditional stochastic approximation methods is presented. ¬© 1970 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Luecke R.H."]

Title: On system identification from noise-obscured input and output measurements
Abstract: This paper deals with maximum-likelihood system identification when both the input and the output signals are corrupted by Gaussian observation noise. A derivation of exact maximum-likelihood estimation for this problem is included, but the difficulty of implementing it numerically precludes its practical evaluation at this time. A new approximate method is introduced, called the ‚Äòoutput reference‚Äô method, in which the input noise is referred to the output, and an iterative gradient search method used. This technique requires no a priori knowledge of the noise covariance matrix. The method of Koopmans‚ÄîLevin, which does require knowledge of the noise covariance matrix, is then reviewed in detail, and experimental results are presented for the white noise case which indicate that the output reference method is more accurate. ¬© 1970 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Rogers A.E.", "Steiglitz K."]

Title: Near-optimal non-linear filtering using quasi-moment functions
Abstract: In previous publications (Fisher and Stear 1967 a, b), the authors dealt extensively with the general non-linear filtering problem. This paper utilizes tho very desirable properties of the expansion of a probability density function in terms of its quasimoment functions to obtain near-optimal ‚Äòsolutions‚Äô to the general dynamical equation of tho non-linear filtering problem. Specifically, stochastic differential equations are derived for the near-optimal non-linear filter using the theory of approximation of a probability density function by its lower-order quasi-moment functions. In addition, the result of approximating the conditional density function by a Gaussian density function is compared with the frequently used method of linearizing the non-linear equations about a nominal solution and applying Kalman linear filtering techniques. ¬© 1970 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Fisher J.R.", "Stear E.B."]

Title: STOCHASTIC COMPUTERS SOLVE MORE PROBLEMS FASTER
Abstract: Simulation of complicated economic orders and real-time automatic control of industrial processes, aircraft, missiles and spacecraft ae tasks that can make the best digital computer look slow in operation, and the best analog computer look inaccurate, bulky and expensive. One new concept in computer technology that could be much more suited to these latest applications is discussed. Called stochastic computing, it is a concept that could find realization with the latest developments in integrated circuits, particularly if there is a marked drop in their price.
Name: ["HALLIWELL J"]

Title: System theoretic analysis of models: Computer simulation of a living cell
Abstract: In modeling a biological system for computer simulation one must often reduce the complexity of the system in accord with practical considerations of computer size and length of computation time. In our model of a living cell (Weinberg & Zeigler, 1969) we found the formal concepts of systems theory valuable in this regard. In particular, the notion of homomorphism is applicable to the problem of assuring that the model preserves interesting properties of the system under study while at the same time being simpler with respect to computer implementation. To develop our model of the cell we simplified the state space and transition function by aggregating co-ordinates of the state description while at the same time reducing the state sets of the new lumped co-ordinates. Certain aspects of the transition function of the model could be determined beforehand, but full specification of the transition function had to be determined by trial and error. In general, testing the model for homomorphism is equivalent to validating the model by comparing its behavior with the behavior of its real world counterpart. The process of aggregation by which we simplified our model, while well-known to economists, has been little appreciated by simulators of biological systems. This paper discusses the application of these system theory concepts to biological models for computer simulation. ¬© 1970.
Name: ["Zeigler B.P.", "Weinberg R."]

Title: Analysis of Digital Predictive Compensation
Abstract: The analysis and dynamic behavior of a predictive type learning control system are considered. An output transform is derived for a system containing a digital predictor, and examples are given of the system's dynamic performance. The output transform is then modified to describe a realistic situation in which time delay is required for input identification by means of a template matching technique. ¬© 1970 IEEE
Name: ["Light W.R.", "Mcvey E.S."]
Affiliations: ['U.S. Army Electronics Command', ' University of Virginia']

Title: Switching Strategy for Optimal Adaptive Third Order Control Systems
Abstract: The conventional design of bang bang control systems for time optimal performance involves an accurate mathematical model of the system and complex computations to determine the optimal switching conditions. Such a design is normally based on the assumption that the system parameters remain fairly constant. Recomputation of optimal trajectories becomes necessary for any change in the parameters. This paper describes a simple adaptive-optimal control strategy for systems representable in phase space and can be easily adopted on a digital controller. Projections of optimal curves are obtained by storing sections of actual system trajectories in the form of tables in the computer memory. Optimal switching instants are determined by shifting and comparing the stored trajectory with the actual trajectory. Since no manipulations are required and the switching curves are obtained by constantly storing and updating the system trajectories, the control remains optimum even when there is a change in parameters. The proposed strategy requires only measurement of error in the system, derivatives of error are formed by using the difference equations, a method well suited for digital formulation of state variables. ¬© 1970, The Institute of Measurement and Control. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Mohleji S.C.", "Thomas P.A.V."]

Title: A New Design Procedure for Traffic Signal Control Policies
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics
Abstract: A procedure for the design of traffic signal control policies which results in minimal average delay and queue length is presented. The procedure is applicable to preset and sampled data controllers. The optimal policy is computed from measurements of the average demand in each flow direction during some interval (10 minutes to several hours). In many cases, substantial improvements over classical techniques in the areas of intersection performance and safety are obtained. In other cases, the theoretical foundations of the new procedure provide proof that the classical design techniques already generate optimal solutions. Computation time for the procedure is sufficiently small to allow a single automaton to control many (100-1000) intersections in real time. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Morris A.A., Jr.", "Yagoda H.N."]

Title: TRANSIENT ANALYSIS OF LOGICAL NETWORKS APPLIED TO HAZARD DETECTION
Abstract: Paper is concerned with a unified and completely algebraic approach to the transient analysis in both combinational and sequential logical networks through a systematic use of some Boolean differential operators. The transient-analysis procedures described are applied to the detection of various types of hazards which can occur in gate-type networks which operate with level input signals, also called fundamental-mode networks.
Name: ["THAYSE A"]

Title: On A Priori Error Estimates of Some Identification Methods
Abstract: This paper examines in detail the estimation errors of two algorithms proposed by Koopmans [1] and Levin [2] for identifying linear systems described by an nth-order scalar difference equation. Necessary and sufficient conditions are established for the strong consistency of the estimates that these algorithms generate. A priori error bounds on estimation error are obtained to provide a quantitative basis for comparing these algorithms in relation to the maximum likelihood estimates. Computational results are also presented to supplement the theoretical discussions. ¬© 1970 IEEE
Name: ["Aoki M.", "Yue P.C."]

Title: ADAPTIVE TECHNIQUES FOR IMPROVING COMMUNICATION SYSTEMS PERFORMANCE
Abstract: The theory and application of a class of least mean squared error (LMSE) algorithmic or adaptive techniques to problems in the communications field is discussed. The basic theory is reviewed in a tutorial manner up to and including the idea of recursive LMSE solutions. Original work is presented in the use of LMSE algorithms with probabilistically defined input vectors and their applications.
Name: ["GERHARDT LA"]

Title: Algorithm for variable- length proper- name compression
Abstract: Viable on- line search systems require reasonable capabilities to automatically detect variations between request format and stored format. An important requirement is the solution of the problem of matching proper names, not only because both input specifications and storage specifications are subject to error, but also because various transliteration schemes exist and can provide variant proper name forms in the same data base. This paper reviews several proper name matching schemes.
Name: ["DOLBY JL"]

Title: ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY MANIPULATIONS
Abstract: A numer of manipulation methods of various search and retrieval operations are described using certain set of symbols.
Name: ["FENG TY", "LEE CC"]

Title: MONTE CARLO PROGRAMMING. RANDOM SEARCHING IN THE SOLUTION OF PARAMETER OPTIMIZATION PROBLEMS
Abstract: Optimality requirements to maximize the expected rate of convergence of the local random search technique are derived for selected test objective functions. These analytical results are synthesized into a general strategy for modulating the step size of the local random search technique. The strategy adopted is implemented in a local random search algorithm suitable for either digital or hybrid computation. Analysis indicates that the usefulness of the global random search technique is severely limited by the large number of objective function evaluations required.
Name: ["LAWSON GP", "LAVI A"]

Title: CONSTRUCTION OF MINIMAL LINEAR STATE-VARIABLE MODELS FROM FINITE INPUT/OUTPUT DATA
Abstract: It is shown that the resulting realization in essence models the transient response of the unknown system. If the unknown system is linear, this technique can be used to find a smaller dimensional linear system having the same transient characteristics. If the unknown system is nonlinear, the technique can be used either to determine a useful nonlinear model, or determine a linear model both of which approximate the transient response of the nonlinear system.
Name: ["TETHER AJ"]

Title: APPLICATION OF CONJUGATE GRADIENT METHOD TO THE ESTIMATION OF VTOL AIRCRAFT PARAMETER AND STATE
Abstract: Unlike other interative methods such as an extended Kalman filtering and the quasilinearization method, the conjugate gradient algorithm requires no inversion of a matrix nor a solution of a system of linear equations in each iteration. Furthermore, regardless of the initial estimate, this scheme features a rapid convergence to a local minimum. The feasibility of using this method for the parameter estimation of a VTOL aircraft is demonstrated and comparisons with other techniques are given.
Name: ["CHEN RTN", "WEINGARTEN N", "MESIAH C", "CLOSE V"]

Title: Programmable indexing networks
Abstract: These networks have the ability to arbitrarily reorder a set of n input cells into m output cells with the repetition or deletion of any cell allowed. Blank cell values may be arbitrarily placed in any of the output cells, thereby allowing the construction of arbitrary contiguous sets of data separated by blanks in the output. These networks have a special cases previously studied permutation and sorting networks. The networks described here are extremely general in nature and should have many different areas of application, particularly, in areas needing networks for routing and transferring data. The solutions suggested here areprogrammable (utilizing the output position mask), as fast, and utilize less hardware than the previously suggested shift registers permuters.
Name: ["THURBER KJ"]

Title: DISTRIBUTED PARAMETER IDENTIFICATION USING THE METHOD OF CHARACTERISTICS
Abstract: Both the very real problems of noisy measurements and limited available measurement transducers are discussed. Convergent algorithms are developed using a Robbins-Munro stochastic approximation scheme. The extension of these methods to the identification of functions, multidimensional systems and diffusion terms is considered.
Name: ["CARPENTER WT", "WOZNY MJ", "GOODSON RE"]

Title: Self- operating filter for hybrid inertial navigation systems
Abstract: A number of hybrid systems, such as pure Inertial- Doppler, Loran- Inertial and Doppler- Loran- Inertial, are briefly discussed. In addition to improving the stability and damping characteristics, the external velocity and/or position measurements increase overall navigational performance. In this context, since the navigation problem is one of measurement and estimation, optimal filtering is used to reduce navigational errors. The implementation problem and some basic properties are summarized for different types of filters, such as polynomial filters, the Wiener filter and the relatively new filtering technique known as the Kalman filter. This structure can beasily implemented on the airborne digital computer which constitutes a part of the hybrid- inertial navigation system.
Name: ["SIDAR M"]

Title: Model Predictive Time-Optimal Control of Second-Order Processes
Source: Industrial and Engineering Chemistry Process Design and Development
Abstract: Set point changes for second-order processes are implemented using a hybrid computer and a fast-time model of the controlled process to search out the time-optimal trajectory. Process outputs are used as initial conditions to monitor the process transition in continuous, closed loop fashion. Model scan rates up to 100 per second (with convergence to the optimal solution in milliseconds) furnish a continuous updating of predicted switch times for the controlled process and make possible the multiplexing of a single hybrid controller to a large number of controlled processes. The controller has excellent characteristics for set point changes and also as a regulator with both analog simulated processes and an experimental two-tank liquid level system. ¬© 1970, American Chemical Society. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Mellichamp D.A."]

Title: ON THE BEHAVIOR OF OPTIMAL LINEAR SAMPLED-DATA REGULATORS
Abstract: Optimal sampled-data controls for linear processes with quadratic criteria are determined through application of the discrete minimum principle. The effect of sampling on the closed loop system's performance is investigated and the asymptotic behavior of the optimal cost for large sampling periods is determined. The resulting design method is applicable to continuous, sampled-data, and discrete regulators.
Name: ["LEVIS AH", "ATHANS M", "SCHLUETER RA"]

Title: On-Line Computers for Speech Research
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: On-line computers offer powerful interactive computing, flexible control of laboratory instruments, and cost economy for a wide range of speech experiments. This paper describes the hardware and software of one such on-line facility which was specially designed for simple self-service operation by speech scientists who are not always computer experts. Examples are given of the use of on-line facilities for the study of speech analysis, speech synthesis, and speech perception. ¬© 1970, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Denes P.B."]

Title: GRADIENT BIASED RANDOM SEARCH
Abstract: The gradient biased random search technique that has been proposed in this study was developed as an extension to both the random search and the Kiefer-Wolfowitz stochastic approximation search. From the point of view of an extension of the random search, the addition of a gradient biasing term permits the resulting algorithm to be optimized with respect to its convergence rate on a noisy, unimodal index of performance surface. It has also been shown that a gradient biased random would result whenever an n-dimensional stochastic vector is added to the n-dimensional Kiefer- Wolfowitz stochastic approximation search technique.
Name: ["PENSA AF", "MCMURTRY GJ"]

Title: GENERAL LINEAR SEQUENTIAL FILTER
Abstract: A Kalman filter that accounts for time-correlated noise without augmenting the state vector or differencing the measurements is derived. The resulting filter equations demand less computer storage space and computation time than previously derived equations based upon state augmentation and measurement differencing. Solving the matrix Wiener-Hopf equation under the constraint that the noise states are not solved for gives the required formulation.
Name: ["JOHNSON DJ"]

Title: CONSTRUCTION OF REGIONS OF STABILITY FOR NONLINEAR SYSTEMS CONTAINING TIME DELAYS
Abstract: A method is presented for constructing regions of stability for nonlinear systems containing time delays. This method, based on modified Lyapunov stability theore%ms, is applicable to higher- dimensional systems containing several time delays or time-varying delays. Computational results for a simulated chemical reactor indicate that physically significant regions of stability could be constructed despite the presence of large time delays.
Name: ["SEBORG DE", "JOHNSON EF"]

Title: An Algorithm for Real-Time Computer Control of a Tracking System with a Nonlinearity
Abstract: A tracking antenna control system with a nonlinearity is considered. The system is uniformly sampled and the control signal is computed at each sampling interval to achieve optimal position alignment with minimum energy expenditure. A direct minimization method permitting efficient real-time implementation is adopted. ¬© 1970 IEEE
Name: ["Tabak D."]

Title: Efficient Smoothing of Digitized Measurements in a Large Real-Time System
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: In a recently developed system, involving extensive real-time measurement and digital computation subsystems, each measurement is quality checked to establish reasonableness, edited to remove ‚Äúbad‚Äù samples, and filtered to attenuate noise. These functions are achieved under severe restrictions on computer time and storage. The quality of a sample is determined by comparison with a simple prediction, which is used in editing the sample if the original sample is deemed ‚Äúbad.‚Äù A five-point recursive filter having optimally selected coefficients for each measurement is employed. Comprehensive tests have proven the acceptability of the smoothing process. ¬© 1970, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Blanton H.E."]

Title: MAN-MACHINE INTERACTION FOR THE DISCOVERY OF HIGH- LEVEL PATTERNS
Abstract: A high-level pattern is a partition of the set of individuals into subsets within which a common set of linear, additive, noninteractive relationships holds. That is, although there may be no significant correlations among variables for a certain sample of individuals, it is possible that there exists a partitionof the sample into subsets with in each of which there exist very strong correlations between variables. A computer program, called INTERFORM, has been written (for the GE time-sharing system) to carry out an interactive search for patterns of this type. The program provides the researcher with a set of simple commands, which are to be used heuristically-he can try arranging individuals in one way, see what happens, try another, and so on. Some of the available commands are given with a description of statistical operations they perform. The applicability of this scheme to data analysis in the social sciences is discussed.
Name: ["FOSTER DF"]

Title: APPLICATION OF SPECIFIC OPTIMAL CONTROL TO THE DESIGN OF DESENSITIZED MODEL FOLLOWING CONTROL SYSTEMS
Abstract: Control law designed are characterized by partial state feedback, perfect model following when theoretically possible, relative insensitivity of the compensated plant to mathematical modeling inaccuracies, and plant-model realignment in the presence of state disturbances. The feasibility of the design technique is demonstrated by the design of a nontrival aircraft control problem.
Name: ["WINSOR CA", "ROY RJ"]

Title: ON PARALLEL PROCESSING NETWORKS
Abstract: Author discusses the problem of finding the duration of a network, given the duration of the processes, for the case of full parallelism, and for the case of simulation by a conventional computer. Author also discusses the cost of this simulation as a function of the processes and how to simulate the network in the minimum cost.
Name: ["COHEN D"]

Title: DUALITY OF LINEAR ESTIMATION AND CONTROL
Abstract: The present paper is intended to provide a link between the concepts of duality in mathematical programming and of duality of linear stochastic estimation and deterministic unconstrained linear regulator problems discussed by Kalman and Bucy and thus allow a rigorous extension of the latter to special problems such as colored-noise estimation and singular regulator problems.
Name: ["SIMON KW", "STUBBERUD AR"]

Title: SINGULAR OPTIMAL CONTROL OF DISCRETE-TIME SYSTEMS
Abstract: The problem considered is that of the minimization of a performance index which is quadratic in the state only with the scalar input to the system subject to a magnitude constraint. The possibility of a singular region of control existing and the determination of this singular control is obtained in a direct manner without recourse to Pontryagin's principle. The remaining or nonsingular control is obtained by application of the discrete maximum principle.
Name: ["GRAHAM JW", "D'SOUZA AF"]

Title: AUTOMATIC DISCRIMINATION OF NOISY AND QUASIPERIODIC SPEECH SOUNDS BY THE PHASE PLANE METHOD
Abstract: The possibility of automatic discrimination of noisy and tonal speech sounds by their phase images is explored. A block diagram of an experimental model of the discriminating apparatus is given, along with an assessment of the discrimination efficiency.
Name: ["LOBANOV BM"]

Title: Information Networks in Generative Computer-Assisted Instruction
Abstract: An environment is described in which a computer dynamically generates simple instructional and remedial sequences for nonnumeric topics such as geography and biology. This environment is described in detail and consists of a structured pool of information and sets of mechanisms (skeleton patterns) that extract data from the pool. The environment is implemented in the form of an interactive ALGOL program on the Burroughs B5500, and examples of interactions with students are included. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Wexler J.D."]

Title: SCHEDULING PROCEDURE FOR PARALLEL PROCESSORS IN THE PAPER INDUSTRY
Abstract: The paper describes a heuristic schedule generator for parallel processors ehich process jobs having precedence constraints. The algorithm considers parallel processors which are similar but not necessarily identical. For example, machines of the same type but where age difference will reflect technical innovation. Paper industry processes are discussed but the procedure is relevant to other manufacturing processes which perform in parallel. The objective function which the schedule generator attempts to maximize is process utilization; however, other scheduling criteria are discussed.
Name: ["MOODIE CL", "WALTER JM"]

Title: Numerical Analysis of Electroencephalographic Data
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: Correlation of electroencepholographic data recorded simultaneously from several different regions, although promising important insights into the nature of the EEG generating process had been impeded by the prohibitive cost of special equipment or computer time until the introduction of the FFT. Now one is able to analyze the statistical structure of an EEG and explore the biological meaning of its parameters. Power spectra of EEGs in mono- and dizygotic-twins are shown to illustrate how modern techniques can be used to assess the individuality of the spontaneous working EEG. Other examples show the possibility of investigating the relations between simultaneous recordings from different parts of the brain while awake and asleep. EEG analysis is still at its beginning, subject to the data gap between the gross activity from macroelectrodes and the electrical activity from microelectrodes at individual neurons. ¬© 1970, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Dumermuth G.", "Kleiner B.", "Huber P.J.", "Gasser T."]
Affiliations: ['University of Z√ºrich', 'Swiss Federal Institute of Technology', ' Princeton University']

Title: STATIC OPTIMIZATION OF MULTICOUPLED SYSTEMS OF LARGE DIMENSIONALITY- 1, 2, 3
Abstract: An algorithm is given for solving linear problems of the type considered having a large number of dimensions, based on the use of specific features of the given problems. Some nonlinear problems of the static optimization of multicoupled plants are considered, reducing to problems of convex programming and to multiextremal problems of a special form. Algorithms are proposed for the solution of problems of high dimensionality. A method is proposed for solving linear problems ofstatic optimization of multicoupled plants on electrical network models or by certain matrix schemes without the use of additional devices for modeling the constraints.
Name: ["MEEROV MV", "LITVAK BL"]

Title: An Improved Algorithm for High Speed Autocorrelation with Applications to Spectral Estimation
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: A common application of the method of high speed convolution and correlation is the computation of autocorrelation functions, most commonly used in the estimation of power spectra. In this case the number of lags for which the autocorrelation function must be computed is small compared to the length of the data sequence available. The classic paper by Stockham, revealing the method of high speed convolution and correlation, also discloses a number of improvements in the method for the case where only a small number of lag values are desired, and for the case where a data sequence is extremely long. In this paper, the special case of autocorrelation is further examined. An important simplification is noted, based on the linearity of the discrete Fourier transform, and the circular shifting properties of discrete Fourier transforms. The techniques disclosed here should be especially important in real-time estimation of power spectra, in instances where the data sequence is essentially unterminated. ¬© 1970, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Rader C.M."]

Title: Computer Simulation of an Automatic Adaptive Equalizer for Real Telephone Channels and Free Data Format
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: Following a short introduction to two important principles of adaptive channel equalization, a computer simulation of a complete linear transmission and equalization scheme is presented. The model includes the transmitter, a time-dispersive noise-free channel, and an adaptive receiver based on the minimum mean-square error criterion. The equalization algorithm described in the paper allows the transmission of time-discrete analog data pulses at a speed of 3600 baud or more while following slow time variations of channel characteristics. It is shown how the measured frequency characteristics of real telephone lines can be used in the simulation process. Some examples are given of the convergence time and of the ratio of output signal-to-intersymbol interference noise, both as a function of equalizer length. ¬© 1970, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Eggimann F."]

Title: STUDY OF WEIGHTED AND OPERATOR MODIFIED LMSE ALGORITHMS FOR PROBABILISTICALLY DEFINED INPUTS
Abstract: Algorithmic procedures which minimize the mean squared error (LMSE) as an index of performance, find application in communications, controls, and systems theory because of the need for an adaptive capability to provide continual updating and the sequential nature of the data involved.
Name: ["GERHARDT LA", "WALBESSER WJ"]

Title: OPTIMAL CONTROL OF PROCESSES CONTAINING PURE TIME DELAYS
Abstract: A survey of previous work is given and the necessary conditions for optimality are extended to a more general class of processes than previously covered. Various computational techniques are discussed, and a conjugate gradient control vector iteration algorithm is proposed and testedon a CSTR example. '%'Optimal'%' start-up policies are found for both constant and variable time delays.
Name: ["RAY WH", "SOLIMAN MA"]

Title: NEAR-OPTIMAL FEEDBACK CONTROL OF DISTRIBUTED PARAMETER SYSTEMS BY TRAJECTORY APPROXIMATION
Abstract: After the system equation is reduced to an approximating system of ordinary differential equations by the Galerkin-Kantorovich method, Pontryagin's maximum principle is applied. It is shown that the feedback control law is linear and can be obtained by solving a matrix Riccati equation. Numerical results and graphs are presented for the control of a heat exchanger with wall heat flux forcing. They indicate that three or four sampling probes are sufficient to attain almost total optimality.
Name: ["ZAHRADNIK RL", "LYNN LL"]

Title: Composite Signal Decomposition
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: A technique for decomposing a composite signal, which consists of the superposition of known multiple signals overlapping in time, is described. Decomposition includes determining the number of signals present, their epochs (arrival times), and amplitudes. The procedure is investigated for the noise-free and noisy situation. The computation algorithm employs the fast Fourier transform to determine the decomposition filter from a knowledge of the signal waveshape and the specified pulse output. The latter is used to recognize the signal arrival time; the amplitude of which is proportional to the signal amplitude; and the number of such pulses denotes the number of individual signal waveforms that make up the composite signal. Digital data processing problems such as filter realizability, signal resolution capability, the effects of additive noise, frequency (spectrum) compatibility between signal waveform and filter response pulse, and possible additional processing in certain cases are discussed. Applications are decomposition or resolution of signals or echoes in radar and sonar, seismology, brain waves, and neuroelectric spike data. Examples of results are presented for decomposition for noiseless and noisy cases for specified signals. In addition, results are tendered for the decomposition of brain waves evoked by visual stimulation. ¬© 1970, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Childers D.G.", "Perry N.W., Jr.", "Varga R.S."]

Title: Finite-Memory Hypothesis Testing-A Critique
Abstract: In this correspondence, we critically examine some recent papers that attempt to obtain optimal finite-memory solutions for some hypothesis-testing problems. We point out that these solutions contain hidden memory-consuming elements, and hence are not optimal. We present and examine various possible definitions of finite memory from a finite-state-machine viewpoint. ¬© 1970, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Chandrasekaran B."]

Title: LEARNING WITH AN IMPERFECT TEACHER
Abstract: A decision rule for classifying patterns with an imperfect teacher is derived. Using nonparametric estimators for the unknown densities appearing in the decision rule, a procedure for learning to recognize patterns with an imperfect teacher is given. It is shown that the proposed learning scheme has an asymptotic average risk equal to the Bayes' minimum risk. The proposed learning scheme is simulated on the computer for some simple density functions and the results are presented.
Name: ["SHANMUGAM K", "BREIPOHL AM"]

Title: DESIGN OF OPTIMAL-ADAPTIVE DIGITAL AUTOPILOT
Abstract: Re-entry vehicle motion is described by linear differential equations whose parameters change over a very wide range during the flight and are unknown except for some a priori guess. An identification algorithm based upon discrete orthogonal functions is used to identify the flight motion parameters. An optimization algorithm based upon quadratic performance index determines the closed-loop characteristic polynomial, which when combined with identified flight motion parameters yields the suitable compensation.
Name: ["PURI NN"]

Title: An Alternate Realization of the Near-Ideal Predictor
Abstract: An alternate method of realization of a near-ideal predictor for use in digital control systems is described which offers a considerable reduction in the time required for realization. An analytical approach is used to develop an algorithm which replaces the proposed parameter optimization routine with a few simple operations. ¬© 1970 IEEE
Name: ["Pracht C.P.", "Ook G."]

Title: AUTOMATIC CONTROL OPTIMIZATION CLASS OF TRILINEAR DIFFERENTIAL GAMES
Abstract: Differential games where the control vec%tor of each player lies on a strictly concave manifold are considered. In one class of such games no time paths of the control variables under optimal play depend parametrically upon the initial values of any state variable except time.
Name: ["CLEMHOUT S", "WAN JR HY"]

Title: LINEAR OPTIMAL CONTROL OF A LINEAR SYSTEM WITH STATE-AND CONTROL- DEPENDENT NOISE
Abstract: Both the finite and infinite terminal time cases are considered. Two precise representations of the controlled stochastic process are considered. For the case with no correction terms, the optimal control is shown to be a linear feedback of the system state variables. Uniqueness and stability conditions are presented for this problem.
Name: ["MCLANE PJ"]

Title: Optimum Line Shape Analysis by Least-Square Approximation and Linear Transformation Processes
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: The problem of optimum analysis of overlapping signals by means of least-square approximation techniques and by linear transformation processes, like resolution enhancement by inverse convolution, is considered. It is shown that optimum accuracy is obtained by employing, before doing a least-square fit, a transformation process which transforms the random noise into white noise. This particularly implies that in any process of artificial resolution enhancement, a loss of accuracy occurs. Examples from the field of spectroscopy are given to demonstrate the achievable accuracy and the requirements with respect to signal-to-noise ratio. ¬© 1970, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Ernst R.R.", "Benz H."]
Affiliations: ['Laboratorium f√ºr Physikalische Chemie ETH', 'Borer and Company']

Title: A discrete-time differential dynamic programming algorithm with application to optimal orbit transfer
Abstract: Recently, the notion of Differential Dynamic Programming has been used to obtain new second-order algorithms for solving nonlinear optimal control problems. (Unlike conventional Dynamic Programming, the Principle of Optimality is applied in the neighborhood of a nominal, nonoptimal, trajectory.) A novel feature of these algorithms is that they permit strong variations in the system trajectory. In this paper Differential Dynamic Programming is used to develop a second-order algorithm for solving discrete-time dynamic optimization problems with terminal constraints. This algorithm also utilizes strong variations and, as a result, has certain advantages over existing discrete-time methods. A nonlinear computed example is presented, and comparisons are made with the results of other researchers who have solved this problem. The experience gained during the computation has suggested some extensions to an earlier, previously published Differential Dynamic Programming algorithm for continuous time problems. These extensions, and their implications, are discussed. ¬© 1970, American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Inc., All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gershwin S.B.", "Jacobson D.H."]
Affiliations: [' Division of Engineering and Applied Physics']

Title: OPTIMAL CONTROL SURFACE LOCATIONS FOR AIRCRAFT FLEXURE CONTROLLERS
Abstract: The basic physical relationships involved in control of a flexible aircraft disturbed by random wind gusts are used in formulating the surface location problem as one in optimal control of a distributed system, using a limited number of point-force controllers. The three phases of this problem-- estimation, control, and surface placement, are then solved by means of the matrix minimum principle and the calculus of variations. The variational equations are greatly simplified and the order of the problem considerably redced by use of optimalontrollers at each stage in the search for optimal surface locations. A computer program has been written which uses these equations in solving the surface location problem for winged aircraft. Results of a trial study based on a 14 order model of the Lockheed C-5A transport aircraft are reported.
Name: ["JOHNSON TL", "ATHANS M", "SKELTON GB"]

Title: PROBLEM OF THE OPERATIONAL RELIABILITY OF FLIGHT CONTROL SYSTEMS AND AUTOMATIC PILOTING OF AIRCRAFT
Abstract: Problems created by increasing complexity and sophistication of automatic pilots are discussed. The malfunction of mechanisms is discussed generally, and malfunction statistics on flight control systems and their component parts are given. A model design of highly reliable flight control system is presented and discussed in detail.
Name: ["PETERS O"]

Title: OPTIMAL STOCHASTIC CONTROL PROBLEM WITH OBSERVATION COST
Abstract: The problem of simultaneously determining an optimal control strategy and an optimal observation strategy for a linear system is considered. Quadratic costs on state and control and on '%'on- off'%' type observation cost are assumed. Dynamic Programming is used to obtain a solution. An example is provided which shows some interesting relations between the optimal observation strategy and various system parameters.
Name: ["COPPER CA", "NAHI NE"]

Title: On the Design of Optimal Constrained Dynamic Compensators for Linear Constant Systems
Abstract: The design of linear time-invariant dynamic compensators of fixed dimensionality s, which are to be used for the regulation of an nth-order linear time-invariant plant, is dealt with. A modified quadratic cost criterion is employed in which a quadratic penalty on the system state as well as all compensator gains is used; the effects of the initial state are averaged ont. The optimal compensator gains are specified by a set of simultaneous nonlinear matrix algebraic equations. The numerical solution of these equations would specify the gain matrices of the dynamic compensator. The proposed method may prove useful in the design of low-order s compensators for high-order n plants that have few r outputs, so that the dimension of the compensator is less than that obtained through the use of the associated Kalman‚ÄìBucy filter n or the Luenberger observer n ‚Äì r. ¬© 1970 IEEE
Name: ["Johnson T.L.", "Athans M."]

Title: NEW ADAPTIVE CONTROL SYSTEM BASED UPON THE AREAS ENCLOSED BETWEEN THE INPUT AND OUTPUT PLOTS
Abstract: An adaptive and optimal time control method for processes with time varying coefficient is given. The method permits first the process identification by an equivalent linear transfer function with time delay during a real control transient, and second, to calculate an input signal within any given physical limitation for an optimal minimum time response. The method is primarily based on the area formed between the curves representing the input and output variables of a controlled process and on their physical meaning for a processo be controlled. An approach to the control problem is given in which a process disturbance is to be taken as an unbalance in control impulse. The new balance can be restored by giving to the process the control impulse that it lacks.
Name: ["OBRADOVIC IJ"]

Title: ON AVERAGE-OPTIMAL NONLINEAR FEEDBACK CONTROL SYSTEMS
Abstract: A procedure for synthesizing suboptimal feedback controls is presented. The optimization problem considered is that of controlling a linear time-invariant system with a cost functional which is nonquadratic but convex. The synthesis of the feedback control will involve the storage of the switching surfaces in a computer plus the off-line computation of the optimal feedback gains.
Name: ["DEBS AS", "ATHANS M"]

Title: OPTIMAL LINEAR FILTER AND ITS RELATION TO SINGULAR OPTIMAL CONTROL
Abstract: The linear filtering problem is formulated into a deterministic optimization problem, and the solution requires the use of the general technique of solving a singular optimal control problem. Both the case of white measurement noise and the case of correlated measurement noise are considered. It is found that the equation which represents the singular surface also gives the orthogonality condition which is to be satisfied by the optimal linear filter. The formulation of the filtering problem is especially suited for the design of a suboptimal filter.
Name: ["LEE JS"]

Title: APPROXIMATE OPTIMAL CLOSED LOOP CONTROL OF NONLINEAR SYSTEMS VIS PARAMETER SEARCH
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present a simple straight forward procedure for obtaining a near optimal closed loop algorithm for nonlinear system and compare it with linear design via optimal control theory.
Name: ["FOURNIER CD", "GROVES FR"]

Title: OPTIMIZATION OF COUPLED NONLINEAR SYSTEMS
Abstract: A coupling perturbation method is developed for near optimum design of nonlinear systems. A scalar parameter epsilon is introduced in an nth order systems such that for epsilon equals O the system decouples into two (or more) independent low order subsystems. By the same procedure epsilon is introduced into the performance index. The near optimal control is defined as truncated power series in epsilon. It is shown that each term of the series can be sequentially obtained by separate subsystem calculation. Two examples are presented and the results compared with those obtained by conventional iterative methods. applicability of the method to problems which cannot be solved by conventional methods is discussed.
Name: ["KOKOTOVIC PV", "SINGH G"]

Title: DISCRETE ESTIMATION ALGORITHMS FOR RANDOMLY SAMPLED STOCHASTIC SIGNALS
Abstract: Reformulation of the original problem leads to an interesting correlation between plant and measurement noise which requires a special sequential algorithm. Effects on estimation error variance by varying the ratio of the discrete sample period to the average of the random sample period are discussed. An example is given to illustrate the techniques presented.
Name: ["STEINWAY WJ", "MELSA JL"]

Title: Property of the Equation-Error Approach to Parameter Identification
Abstract: This correspondence demonstrates an unusual property associated with the equation-error approach to parameter identification. This property, which is usually a liability of the equation-error formulation, is shown to be an asset for a specific application. ¬© 1970 IEEE
Name: ["Mendel J.M."]

Title: Toward Objective Phonetic Transcription-An Online Interactive Technique for Machine-Processed Speech Data
Abstract: The derivation of phonetic transcription is one component of speech processing that can utilize man-data techniques. This involves the assignment and time location of phonetic symbols to speech data. Conventional transcription methods are suspect in at least two respects. First, the symbols assigned are often based on ‚Äútalker intention,‚Äù or what ‚Äúshould be,‚Äù rather than on physical evidence; and, second, symbol location is usually related to subsequent machine processing only minimally. An exploratory procedure is described that operates online, in an interactive mode, utilizing a graphic display with an IBM System/360 model 40. Available for display are a digital sound spectrogram, the power spectrum at a given time sample, an average spectrum for a given sound class, and correlations of a current spectrum with average spectra. Using this technique, location and assignment of phonetic symbols are less dependent upon operator expertise (and/or bias) and highly related to subsequent processing. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Dixon N.R.", "Tappert C.C."]

Title: LIMITING FORMS OF OPTIMUM STOCHASTIC LINEAR REGULATORS
Abstract: By means of a limiting process it was shown that a meaningful stochastic control law may result for a linear process with a quadratic performance criterion whnn the control is not weighted, or when the observations are noisefree. Although the calculations were carried out for the special case in which the process is time- invariant and the control interval is infinite, the extension of these results to the more general case of a time-varying process with a finite control interval would appear to be relatively straightforward.
Name: ["FRIEDLAND B"]

Title: COMPUTING DEVICES FOR DETERMINING THE MEAN SQUARE ERROR OF THE CONTROL SYSTEMS SUBJECTED TO RANDOM NOISE
Abstract: A method is proposed for determining the mean square errors of linear systems with variable parameters by analog technics. The most commonly occurring random processes with exponential correlation functions are analyzed, presenting examples of practical systems.
Name: ["LUR'E ZYA"]

Title: ON THE STABILITY OF A CLASS OF DISTRIBUTED, SAMPLED-DATA NONLINEAR SYSTEMS
Abstract: A frequency domain stability criterion '%(sufficient condition) for a class of distributed parameter, sampled-data systems containing a memory-less, nonlinear feedback element is presented. This criterion for absolute stability of the class of distributed systems considered here parallels the criterion for lumped systems obtained by Jury and Lee. An example is given to illustrate the applications of the stability criterion.
Name: ["NAGARAJAN N", "KHATRI HC"]

Title: Algorithm for producing half- tone computer graphics presentations with shadows and movable light sources
Abstract: The LINESCAN algorithm processes a graphical image into a half- tone final image from two data sets derived from the three- space structure, first the set of all plane equation coefficients for the polygonal surfaces of the structure and, second the perspective projections of the edges of the surfaces on the viewing plane. The construction of the final half- tone image is done in a television- like manner where a crt beam scans across the image line- by- line and exposes a raster of points. As the beam moves across the scanline, the intersectionpoints on the scanline corresponding to the viewable edges of the original structure will dictate changes in the tone (intensity) of the scanning beam from that point to the next intersection. The extended version of the LINESCAN algorithm for solving the shadow problem includes two scanning operations. The primary scanning movement is the original scan operation where the three- space structure data is processed to provide the final image structure. The additional or secondary scanning operation processes, in a parallel manner, the shadow three- space structure to produce data which will be combined with the primary scan data to form the scanline intensity data for the final image.
Name: ["BOUKNIGHT J", "KELLEY K"]

Title: Termination of programs represented as interpreted graphs
Abstract: In this study of the termination problem of interpreted graphs, an interpreted graph is considered as an abstract model of algorithms. It consists of a directed graph. The main result is a sufficient condition for the termination of interpreted graphs defined by means of well- ordered sets. This result has applications in proving the termination of various classes of algorithms. he results are illustrated in proofs for termination of programs and recursively defined functions. 51878% 721- 723 EI 71 /AUTOMATA THEORY/ //GRAPH THEORY// COMPUTERS Codes Algorithm for caryless quibinary shifting addition; R. ZUSSMAN (Naval Applied Science Lab, Brooklyn, NY), J. F. WEISS; IEEE Trans Comput v C- 18 n 12 Dec 1969 p 1140- 2; An algorithm developed by the authors for quibinary addition is described. This algorithm is applicable to processors employing a binary- coded- decimal (BCD) numbering scheme. Quibinary addition for each digit is accomplished without carries. Error detection is obtained by odd and even parity checks.
Name: ["MANNA Z"]

Title: REAL-TIME HYBRID SIMULATION OF AN ADAPTIVE- CONTROL TECHNIQUE
Abstract: Paper describes the simulation of an adaptive scheme based on leastsquares methods, incorporating a hybrid computer. The analog computer simulates the process dynamics, while the online digital machine effects the adaptive control via a. d. c. and d. a. c. interfaces. The scheme is shown to be realistic, and to have application to relatively fast-responding systems. The process is repeatedly identified as a series of quasilinear optimal- feedbackcontrol law. This control law, valid for a discrete- timenvironment, is shown to have application in continuous time. A novel approach to the problem of inaccessible states is investigated.
Name: ["SANDOZ DJ", "SWANICK BH"]

Title: Observation and Control of Linear Systems with Constant Disturbances
Abstract: The problem of regulation in the presence of a fixed but unknown disturbance is considered. The control law is designed as if the disturbance were known, and an estimate given by an observer is used in the control law. A system results having as many integrators as outputs. ¬© 1970 IEEE
Name: ["B√âlanger P.R."]

Title: APPROACH TO THE REGULATOR PROBLEM FOR NONLINEAR CHEMICAL PROCESSES
Abstract: The method uses linear realization theory to replace the original system by a linear model which is assumed to approximate the dynamic behavior of the system near specified steady-state values. Linear control theory is then used to generate a control sequence for the original nonlinear system.
Name: ["KALLINA C"]

Title: On the Convergence of Lion's Identification Method with Random Inputs
Abstract: An interesting identification scheme for scalar-input‚Äìscalar-output linear systems, proposed by Lion in [1], is investigated for a wide class of random inputs. The inputs include the class of functions u(t) = Œ£kiui(t), where {u1(t), ‚Ä¶, uk(t)} is a Markov process which is asymptotically stationary. An invariant set theorem for random systems [2] is used to prove convergence (in probability) of the identification algorithm proposed in [1]. Indeed, in view of the power of the deterministic invariant set theorem, it is of great interest to study methods of useful application of the stochastic analogy. One of the main contributions is the illustration of its potential power, via the vehicle of the identification problem. ¬© 1970 IEEE
Name: ["Kushner H.J."]

Title: ON TREATMENT OF SAMPLES OF RANDOM PROCESSES GIVEN BY THEIR ENVELOPES
Abstract: Relations for statistical characteristics of a narrowband random process and its envelopes, upper and lower, are given, assuming the process to be gaussian. Knowledge of these relations enables estimation of statistical characteristics of a random process having an '%'average'%component characterized as a stationary random process and a vibratory component being a centered stationary random process given by its envelope. For the estimation of the characteristics of the given process, the knowledge of the corresponding characteristics of both components is necessary. Some examples, proving practical use of the described method, are given.
Name: ["KROPAC O"]

Title: ON FUZZY DECISION PROCESSES AND FUZZY DIFFERENTIAL GAMES
Abstract: The fuzzy dynamic programming proposed by S. S. L. Chang has been extended to fuzzy decision processes involving two decision makers and, in particular, to fuzzy differential games of pursuit and evasion. Only one unknown parameter in the system is considered. A membership function is attributed to the payoff of a game rather than to its unknown parameter. A pair of guaranteed strategies can be determined such that the value of the game played under the fuzzy situation is bounded above and below by the minimal and the maximalguaranteed payoffs respectively where each membership function is equal to unity. A fuzzy linear pursuit problem is discussed as a special case of fuzzy decision process.
Name: ["LI CC", "SIMAAN MA"]

Title: Trajectory Insensitivity of Optimal Feedback Systems
Abstract: It is shown that for a single-input linear time-invariant plant in phase-variable canonic form, such that the control minimizes a quadratic performance index, the integral of a quadratic form of the state sensitivity using feedback control is less than the corresponding one using open-loop control, for any arbitrary positive semidefinite nonzero weighting matrix. Classes of state representations, which are not in phase-variable canonic form for which the relative insensitivity holds, are given. ¬© 1970 IEEE
Name: ["Sundararajan N.", "CRUZ J.B., Jr."]

Title: Quasi-Optimum Proportional Navigation
Abstract: The problem of deriving feedback guidance laws for interceptor type aerodynamically controlled missiles which seek to engage moving targets is considered. These missiles contain target trackers which provide angular information about the relative interceptor-to-target geometry. The performance criterion for this problem is quadratic, but the system equations are nonlinear. Suitable guidance mechanizations are obtained by applying the technique of quasi-optimum control. The efficiency of the resulting guidance system, relative to a linear optimum guidance system and a proportional navigation system, is demonstrated by simulations of attack situations in which the interceptor missile launch conditions depart from the nominal attack geometry. ¬© 1970 IEEE
Name: ["Axelband E.I.", "Hardy F.W."]

Title: IMPROVED ALGORITHM FOR LEARNING SYSTEMS
Abstract: An algorithm is developed for implementing a learning controller based on the concept of a subgoal. The method differs from previous work in that the state space need not be quantized, resulting in vastly reduced memory requirements and shorter learning times. The method is applicable to linear stationary systems with unconstrained control variable wherein the system parameters are specified with uncertainty. Factors affecting the convergence are discussed, and examples are used to illustrate the design.
Name: ["SCOTT RW", "ZAJAC GE", "LINDORFF DP"]

Title: SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS OF DISCRETE DETECTION ALGORITHMS
Abstract: A sensitivity analysis of the algorithms for detection of a Gauss- Markov random signal in the presence of additive Gaussian noise is presented. Algorithms are derived for computing the sensitivity of the mean and variance of the logarithm of the likelihood ratio to modeling errors. Errors are considered in the plant model, and the plant and observation noise covariance matrices. Results are presented for an amplitude modulation example problem.
Name: ["MC LENDON JR", "SAGE AP"]

Title: Upper Bound on the Dimension of Minimal Realizations of Linear Time-Invariant Dynamical Systems
Abstract: A linear time-invariant dynamical system described by means of its transfer function matrix is considered, and an upper bound on the dimension of a minimal internal description of the system is computed. This upper bound is also the minimal dimension of a realization having an invariant structure with respect to the coefficients of the transfer-function matrix for a given location of its distinct poles. Finally, a simple algorithm is proposed for constructing a realization having dimension equal to that upper bound. ¬© 1970 IEEE
Name: ["Roveda C.A.", "Schmid R.M."]

Title: ON-LINE IDENTIFICATION OF LINEAR DYNAMIC SYSTEMS WITH APPLICATIONS TO KALMAN FILTERING
Abstract: The estimates are shown to be asymptotically normal, unbiased and consistent. The scheme is capable of being implemented on line and can be used in conjunction with the Kalman filter. A technique for more efficient estimation by using higher order correlations is given. If the dimension of the system is unknown, a recursive technique is given to determine the order of the system.
Name: ["MEHRA RK"]

Title: MINIMUM COST PATH FINDING WITH INCOMPLETE COST INFORMATION
Abstract: The applications of the problem range from transportation routing problems through feedback control, to artificial intelligence research.
Name: ["CASHIN PM"]

Title: OUTPUT FEEDBACK CONTROL WITH APPLICATION TO UNSTABLE LINEAR SYSTEMS
Abstract: A computational method for the determination of gains for the output-feedback control of fixed, linear systems is presented. The algorithm involves the iterative shifting of closed loop eigenvalues which lie in undesirable portions of the complex plane, e. g. , the right-half plane. Experimental results are cited for a flexible inverted pendulum modelled by a ninth order state equation with only four output variables to be fed back.
Name: ["KOENIGSBERG WD", "FREDERICK DK"]

Title: FIXED CONFIGURATION APPROACH TO THE STOCHASTIC LINEAR REGULATOR PROBLEM
Abstract: A linear filter, possibly of lower than the stochastic system to be controlled, is specified. The control is then required to be a linear transformation of the filter state. optimization is with respect to the filter dynamics, gain, and initial conditions, and the feedback control gains. It is found that performance does not depend on the filter dynamics. An example is presented to demonstrate this result. Another example is presented which indicates that performance possible when a second order plant is controlled by a first order filter.
Name: ["SIMS CS", "MELSA JL"]

Title: Development of a computer technique for the on-line processing of respiratory variables
Abstract: Three analog signals, instantaneous air-flow, O<sub>2</sub> and CO<sub>2</sub> concentration in inspired and expired gas, are transmitted by telephone line to a hybrid computer system. These signals are digitized and processed by on-line computer. The quantities calculated by the computer are: tidal volume, minute pulmonary ventilation, O<sub>2</sub> uptake per breath, O<sub>2</sub> consumption per minute, CO<sub>2</sub> exhaled per breath, and CO<sub>2</sub> exhaled per minute. Problems in processing these signals and the practicality of the automatic technique for handling respiratory data are discussed. The results of a comparative study between the computer technique and the traditional Douglas method are presented. ¬© 1970.
Name: ["Cardus D.", "Newton L."]
Affiliations: ['Baylor College of Medicine', ' University of Texas', ' University of Texas']

Title: DISCRETE STOCHASTIC OPTIMAL CONTROL MODEL OF THE HUMAN OPERATOR
Abstract: A comparison between model and experimental normalized tracking error and power spectral density data confirms the model capability of matching and predicting operator performance with sufficient correlation to warrant its application as a tool in manual vehicular control system design.
Name: ["PASKIN HM"]

Title: ON THE STABILITY OF STOCHASTIC LUR'E SYSTEMS WITH DIFFERENTIABLE NONLINEARITY
Abstract: The method of Popov is extended to derive sufficient conditions for the asymptotic stability in the mean of a Lur'e-type nonlinear feedback systemhaving stochastic parameters in the linear part. It is assumedthat the nonlinear characteristic is specified by known bounds on the slope, as well as on the sector in which it may lie. It is also assumed that the statistics of the random parameters of the linear subsystem are known. The stability conditions developed are analogous to those proved for the deterministic versions of the problem. Paper 6308 C.
Name: ["PURKAYASTHA S", "MAHALANABIS AK"]

Title: Stability of a Class of Multiplicative Nonlinear Systems
Abstract: The problem of input‚Äìoutput stability of a class of systems with multiplicative nonlinearities that arise from a generalization of the Lure problem is considered. Some results are presented that are believed to be new. ¬© 1970 IEEE
Name: ["Satyanarayana N.", "Thathachar M.A.L.", "Srinath M.D."]

Title: All- automatic processing for a large library
Abstract: The all- automatic methodology for processing in a large library is explored. A variety of indexing methods which do not involve human control of the indexing vocabulary are discussed. Automatic creation of a library classification is examined, considering classification algorithms of the hierarchic divisive type, the resulting classification schedule, and evaluation of a classification. Techniques for retrieval through browsing with the aid of a classification schedule are described.
Name: ["PRYWES NS", "LITOFSKY B"]

Title: CONVERGENCE RATES OF OPTIMAL VARIABLE-STRUCTURE STOCHASTIC AUTOMATA
Abstract: The general conditions for achieving optimality are stated and several optimal linear and nonlinear updating schemes are reported. The problem of speed of convergence of automata is discussed and several optimal hybrid schemes with improved convergence rates are proposed.
Name: ["VISWANATHAN R", "NARENDRA KS"]

Title: SUBOPTIMAL CONTROL BY AGGREGATION
Abstract: The study is conducted by constraining the control law to be a linear mapping of the aggregated state and by determining the control gains by satisfying necessary and sufficient conditions for minimizing an '%'averaged'%' quadratic cost functional (which is independent of system initial conditions). Upon observing that the solution to this problem depends on an nth order Riccati type matrix equation, the performance of the overall suboptimal policy is shown to be bounded from below by the true optimal cost and bounded from above by the performance resultingrom a control policy based on an mth order model of the original nth order system. To illustrate the theory, an example of a fifth order process is given.
Name: ["SCHAINKER RB"]

Title: Conditional reflexes and learning machines
Abstract: A proposed learning machine is described which learns by avoidance but also exhibits conditional reflex behaviour. This proposal is an extension of an avoidance learning system described in two earlier papers, Reader (1968, 1969). The design provides for any number of 'conditional reflexes', the mechanisms of which simultaneously share the common memory of the avoidance learning machine. The process of reinforcement-extinction of the 'conditional reflex' is different from the reinforcement-inhibition mechanism of the avoidance learning machine. ¬© 1970.
Name: ["Reader A.V."]

Title: Real time-adaptive control of systems containing inaccessible state variables
Abstract: This paper describes an adaptive scheme for controlling a non-linear process which is attractive from the point of view of implementation in a real time mode. Effective process control can be maintained, even when certain of the state variables are inaccessible, without the need for excessive computation. The process is repeatedly identified as a series of quasi-linear systems. The nature of the control is defined by a model, static or dynamic, set a priori. A ‚Äòsub-optimal‚Äô controller is modified by each successive identification. ¬© 1970 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Swanick B.H.", "Sandoz D.J."]

Title: Optimum Reconstruction of a Randomly Intermittent Signal
Abstract: Unreliable or intermittent electrical connections are considered. A stochastic model for unreliable connections is described. The application of the Wiener-Hopf theory to the reconstruction of a randomly intermittent signal leads to the design of an optimum filter which minimizes the mean-square reconstruction error. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Loo S.G."]

Title: A learning system for terrain recognition
Abstract: A system is described which automatically classifies terrain types from photography. Input is conventional panchromatic single-frame aerial photography of the earth. A flying-spot scanner converts this input to a time-varying video signal suitable for processing by the pattern recognition system. Processing consists of a series of analog and digital operations to arrive at a terrain classification based on spatial texture in the region of the input point. A learning strategy enables the system to refine its processing operations in order to improve classification performance with time. Test results are summarized. ¬© 1970.
Name: ["Idelsohn J.M."]

Title: ESTIMATION OF THE STABILITY BOUNDARIES OF A SYSTEM FOR THE AUTOMATIC CONTROL OF THE PHASE OF AN OSCILLATOR OUTPUT
Abstract: Based on the small-parameter method, estimates are given for the lock-in band and the transient time in a system for the automatic control of the phase of an oscillator output (APCS). In the particular case of a piecewise-linear system the approximate results is compared with the exact result.
Name: ["SHAKHTARIN BI"]

Title: Construction of Minimal Linear State-Variable Models from Finite Input-Output Data
Abstract: An algorithm for constructing minimal linear finite-dimensional realizations (a minimal partial realization) of an unknown (possibly infinite-dimensional) system from an external description as given by its Markov parameters is presented. It is shown that the resulting realization in essence models the transient response of the unknown system. If the unknown system is linear, this technique can be used to find a smaller dimensional linear system having the same transient characteristics. If the unknown system is nonlinear, the technique can be used either 1) to determine a useful nonlinear model, or 2) to determine a linear model, both of which approximate the transient response of the nonlinear system. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Tether A.J."]

Title: New approach to variable metric algorithms
Abstract: An approach to variable metric algorithms has been investigated in which the linear search subproblem no longer becomes necessary. The property of quadratic termination has been replaced by one of monotonic convergence of the eigenvalues of the approximating matrix to the inverse hessian. A convex class of updating formulas which possess this properly has been established, and a strategy has been indicated for choosing a number of the class so as to keep the approximation away from both singularity and unboundedness. A FORTRAN program has been tested extensively with encouraging results.
Name: ["FLETCHER R"]

Title: MULTILEVEL CONTROL SYSTEMS
Abstract: The basic approach to the solution of a problem of optimal control consists in decomposing the problem into simpler problems that are solved at different levels such as ordinary stabilization, and adaptation. The solution of the problem involves the determination of a system structure to which there correspond certain periods of quantization and control algorithms. The criterion of solution is to achieve the best possible compromise between system cost and optimality of control. Since the optimization problem cannot be solved directly, a method of successive solutions is proposed.
Name: ["FINDEISEN W"]

Title: Stopping conditions for iterative control-function optimisation
Abstract: Iterative control-function optimisation for linear dynamical systems with quadratic performance indices is considered. Conditions are given which enable the stage to be determined at which the control function achieved is an adequate approximation to the optimal control function, with respect to the performance index. These yield useful stopping conditions. A computed example is presented. ¬© 1970, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Allwright J.C."]

Title: SCATTER STORAGE SCHEME FOR DICTIONARY LOOKUPS
Abstract: Scatter storage schemes are examined with respect to their applicability to dictionary lookup procedures. Of particular interest are virtual scatter methods which combine the advantages of rapid search speed and reasonable storage requirements. The theoretical aspects of computing hash addresses are developed, and several algorithms are evaluated. Experiments with an actual text lookup process are described.
Name: ["MURRAY DM"]

Title: OPTIMAL FEEDBACK CONTROL OF LINEAR TIME-INVARIANT SYSTEMS WITH QUADRATIC CRITERION
Source: J Inst Eng (India) Electron Telecommun Eng Div
Abstract: Design of optimal feedback control for a linear time-invariant system to drive it from an arbitrary initial state to origin so as to minimize a quadratic performance criterion, requires the solution of the reduced matrix Riccati equation. In this paper, a generalized numerical method for obtaining the required solution of the reduced Riccati equation on a digital computer, is given. The method is illustrated by means of a flow chart applicable for an nth order system. FORTRAN programs and computationalresults for a fourth-order system and the block diagram showing optimal feedback control configuration for the fourth-order system are included.
Name: ["SINGH R"]

Title: A Pseudo-Markov Model for Series of Neuronal Spike Events
Abstract: Spike trains of spontaneous neuronal activity in the rabbit brain are submitted to statistical analyses based on the following pseudo-Markov model. The nerve cell is supposed to alternate between a bursting and a resting state. The numbers of consecutive spikes within each state are assumed to be independent integer-valued random variables with discrete probability distributions. Given the state, the interspike intervals are independent real-valued random variables. The two state semi-Markov model is obtained as a special case when the discrete distributions are geometrical. Statistical second-order properties of recorded spike trains are compared with those predicted by the model on the basis of known first-order properties. For that purpose, serial correlation coefficients and intensity functions for spike trains produced by the model are computed. A comparison between observed and predicted results for the spontaneous activity of 17 brain cells yields a good fit in eight cells and discloses some salient features of the statistical structure in the activity of six other cells. By making it feasible to compute theoretical correlograms, the model may advance the understanding of empirical correlograms. The possibilities for integrating this statistical model of spike trains with a model of the mechanism of spike train production are discussed. ¬© 1970, The Biophysical Society. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Ekholm A.", "Hyv√§rinen J."]

Title: DECISION RULE IN STATISTICAL RECOGNITION THEORY
Abstract: The problem of recognizing a stipulated classification of a set of n-dimensional binary vectors by means of a device which is capable of discriminating the shape of at least k specified components of these vectors (k less than or equal to n) is considered. A certain decision rule is studied which uses the statistics of a learning sequence and allows partial consideration of the dependence of the components of vectors belonging to one class. An estimate is given of the required memory volume of the recognizing device which registers the statistical data of the learning sequence.
Name: ["PODDUBNYI GV"]

Title: EFFECTS OF QUANTIZATION ERRORS IN HYBRID SYSTEMS, | [AUSWIRKUNG VON QUANISIERUNGSFEHLERN IN HYBRIDEN SYSTEMEN]
Abstract: Methods are treated, to determine the effect of quantization-errors on the system output signals. This is done in the time domain and utilizing Z-transform analysis. For this purpose the systems are treated in the state space. The quantization-errors are introduced as stochastic input signals with equal probability distribution.
Name: ["KROGMANN UK"]

Title: Process identification with visual interaction between operator and computer
Abstract: A method of system identification is introduced which involves an operator in an interactive scheme using a graphic display linked to a hybrid computer. Correlation functions of process input/output data are calculated by the digital computer. A model of the system's dynamics is built on the analogue computer, and the model parameters are adjusted, by visual interaction, to obtain a best-fit identification. ¬© 1970, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Williams D.C."]

Title: Signed-Digit Division Using Combinational Arithmetic Nets
Abstract: To meet the challenge created by the advent of large- scale integration, a unique microelectronic arithmetic building element and combinational arithmetic nets, composed of the building elements, have been studied and proposed for arithmetic processor design. A fast division algorithm, particularly suitable for floating-point arithmetic, has also been developed for signed-digit arithmetic. This algorithm is characterized by the need of preprocessing the divisor and then exact generation of quotient digits. This paper describes the implementation of this division algorithm with the arithmetic building element and combinational arithmetic nets. The intention here is to explore the feasibility of applying large-scale integration technology to arithmetic processors. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Tung C."]

Title: GENERALIZATION OF KALMAN'S METHOD TO IDENTIFICATION PROBLEMS
Abstract: The quality of this model is investigated when it is used to predict the plants response, and it is shown that for each time of observation there exists its own optimal (in the sense of prediction precision) modification of the generalized model.
Name: ["PEREL'MAN II"]

Title: Binary Logic for Residue Arithmetic Using Magnitude Index
Abstract: We consider a residue number System using n pairwise relatively prime moduli to represent any integer X in the range The moduli mi are chosen to be of the 2-1 type, in order that the residue arithmetic can be implemented by means of binary registers and binary logic. Further, for each residue number, a magnitude index Pxis maintained for all arithmetic operations. We investigate the properties of such a system and derive the addition, subtraction, multiplication, sign determination, and overflow detection algorithms. The proposed organization is found to improve the operation times for sign detection and overflow detection operations, while rendering multiplication to be a difficult operation. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Rao T.R.N.", "Trehan A.K."]
Keywords: ["base extension index generation logic magnitude index modular adders naturalized form overflow detection residue mult", "plication", "residue number system scale by 2 sign determination", "residue arithmetic", "maintained arithmetic"]

Title: OBSERVERS FOR THIRD-ORDER SYSTEMS
Source: J Inst Eng (India) Electron Telecommun Eng Div
Abstract: The device which constructs the missing state components is called an observer. The observer supplies as estimate of the state-vector at the expense of adding poles to the overall system and is itself a linear system driven by the available outputs of the original system. This paper studies the problem of design and construction of observers for single-input, single- output systems.
Name: ["GOSWAMI S", "DAS GUPTA S"]

Title: Automated system for medical data processing
Abstract: This paper deals with the principles of construction of automated systems for medical data processing. Components of such systems are determined, and function distribution of 'man-and-automation' symbiosis at the stage of system creation and application is considered. Operational problems of the system are described and some preliminary experimental data for individual elements of the systems are cited. ¬© 1970.
Name: ["Popov A.A.", "Yanenko V.M.", "Zaitsev N.G.", "Zaslavsky S.Ja."]

Title: Self-Organizing Approach to the Stochastic Fuel Regulator Problem
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics
Abstract: A self-organizing procedure to achieve a performance adaptive controller with asymptotically optimal properties is proposed for systems with completely or partially unknown dynamics. A physically realizable controller that operates in an unknown stochastic environment is obtained.
