Name: ["Ramamoorthy C.V.", "Chin Y.-H."]
Keywords: ["access time", "binary search", "cost of memory type", "frequency of usage", "frequency partition file"]

Title: Planning and specifying the functions for a process computer with the MADAM program system. (Einsatzplanung, Auftragsabwicklung und Inbetriebnahme eines Prozessrechners mit dem Programmsystem MADAM)
Abstract: The usefullness of process computers for monitoring and control in industrial processes is shown to depend on whether the process functions can be quickly and clearly converted into a system of programs. This is shown to be possible with the MADAM program system which helps to formulate the problem at hand and provides a highly automated sequence for the planning of process computer functions.
Name: ["FALKENBERG EA", "VOLKMANN W"]

Title: \Algorithms for Discrete Sequential Maximum Likelihood Bias Estimation and Associated Error Analysis
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: Optimization theory and discrete invariant imbedding is used in order to derive computationally efficient sequential algorithms for the maximum likelihood estimation of bias errors in linear discrete recursive filtering with noise corrupted input observations and correlated plant and measurement noise. Error analysis algorithms are derived for adaptive and nonadaptive systems with bias and modeling errors. Examples demonstrate the efficiency of the adaptive estimation algorithms and the error analysis algorithms for estimation with bias uncertainty. Copyright ¬© 1971 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Lin J.L.", "Sage A.P."]
Affiliations: [' Southern Methodist University', ' Southern Methodist University']

Title: New algorithms for estimation with sequentially correlated measurement noise
Abstract: This paper derives new estimation algorithms for use with systems with sequentially correlated observation noise. Both single and two-stage correlation are considered. The algorithms appear much like the well known white noise algorithms and are not much more complex. Error analysis algorithms for the analysis of modelling errors made in using those and white noise estimation algorithms are also presented. Those algorithms permit analysis of the effect of making the white noise assumption when the observation noise is really coloured. Examples and associated illustrations are presented to show this effect The newly derived algorithms are compared with existing, more restrictive algorithms, and Bhown to provide equivalent results for problems where both apply. ¬© 1971 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Brown R.J.", "Sage A.P."]

Title: Improved distance measure for pattern recognition
Abstract: The Euclidean distance has often been used to measure the similarity between patterns represented by multidimensional vectors. The Euclidean distance is expensive to implement in hardware, and alternatives have been sought. The letter proposes a new distance measure which is a weighted sum of the city block and square distances. This new distance is a more accurate predictor of the Euclidean distance than are either of its components. ¬© 1971, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Batchelor B.G."]

Title: Error Bounds for a Contextual Recognition Procedure
Abstract: The general problem of the use of context in computer character recognition is briefly reviewed. For the special case where the context is generated by a two-state stationary Markov chain, upper bounds are obtained for the average error probability of an optimal recognition procedure, based on compound decision functions. These bounds are nonparametric and simple functions of the ‚Äúdifferences‚Äù between: 1) the a priori and transition probabilities of the context, and 2) the distributions of the measurements used to identify the characters. Some justifications, applications to systems design, and illustrative examples are given. An improvement is also obtained on a previously derived upper bound for procedures using no context. Copyright ¬© 1971 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Chu J.T."]
Affiliations: ['Department of Industrial Engineering and Operations Research']

Title: Note on Optimal Selection of Independent Binary-Valued Features for Pattern Recognition
Abstract: Given a set of conditionally independent binary-valued features, a counter example is given to a possible claim that the best subset of features must contain the best single feature. ¬© 1971, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Toussaint G.T."]

Title: A Simplex Algorithm for On-Line Computation of Time Optimal Controls
Abstract: The minimum-time regulator problem is solved computationally for general linear-discrete systems by a modification of the simplex algorithm of linear programming (LP). The algorithm presented is faster than the LP solutions devised previously, taking but a single application to solve for the optimal control. An extension of the LP bounded-variable technique further reduces computer time and storage requirements. Application to a sixth-order process with two control inputs shows that the algorithm is sufficiently economical of running time and storage to be implemented on-line with a small process-control computer. Copyright ¬© 1971 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Bashein G."]

Title: A two-tape simulation of turing machines | Zwei-Band Simulation von Turingmaschinen
Abstract: Let M<sub>1</sub> be a Turing machine with k heads on a m-dimensional storage (m‚â•1). Then there exists a Turing machine M<sub>2</sub> with one tape and one stack, simulating t M<sub>1</sub>-steps in at most Œ≥t<sup>2-1/m</sup>lg t+Œ≥‚Ä≤M<sub>2</sub>-steps. This result cannot be improved by more then a factor lg t. ¬© 1971 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Sto√ü H.-J."]

Title: \A Stochastic Approximation Method
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A new algorithm for stochastic approximation has been proposed, along with the assumptions and conditions necessary for convergence. It has been proved by two different methods that the algorithm converges to the sought value in the mean-square sense and with probability one. The rate of convergence of the new algorithm is shown to be better than two existing algorithms under certain conditions. Results of simulation have been given, making a realistic comparison between the three algorithms. Copyright ¬© 1971 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Sinha N.K.", "Griscik M.P."]

Title: Optimal estimator for linear stochastic systems described by functional differential equations
Abstract: The optimal state estimator for linear systems described by functional differential equations is constructed. The problem is solved by deriving equations for the unbiased estimation error as well as for its covariance. A functional of the estimation error at the terminal time is minimized by an optimal choice of the gain matrices of the estimator. It is accomplished by the application of the matrix maximum principle. The applicability of the optimal estimator is illustrated by an example. ¬© 1971 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Koivo A.J."]

Title: Property of dual points
Abstract: Starting from a basic theorem in threshold logic, a condition which must be satisfied by the on set and the off set of a threshold function is found. A property follows which neural networks must possess to be able to realise a reverberation of maximum length. ¬© 1971, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Arcelli C.", "Massarotti A."]
Affiliations: ['Laboratorio di Cibernetica Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche']

Title: A method for optimizing control of multimodal systems using fuzzy automata
Abstract: This paper deals with a new method for optimizing control of multimodal systems by using fuzzy automata. Two classes of fuzzy automata corresponding to the Mealy and Moore type of ordinary automata are formulated in which the transition may be executed on the basis of the membership function between these two states, and these automata are used as the optimizing controller for a global search of the optimum of a multimodal systems. The concepts of the higher order transition in the automata and the partition of the domain of objective function are introduced to the method of optimizing control, and the control systems can hold the true optimum at small hunting loss without keeping any local optimum. The operation of self-organization is performed to optimize the system in the automata. ¬© 1971 American Elsevier Publishing Company, Inc.
Name: ["Asai K.", "Kitajima S."]
Affiliations: ['University of Osaka Prefecture', 'Osaka City University Osaka']

Title: On the speed of response of a model-reference adaptive control system
Abstract: An analytical evaluation of the adaptive loop response of a model-reference adaptive control system is presented using sinusoids as a test signal. A schematic diagram of the feedback system containing a primary control loop and an adaptive control loop are given. ¬© 1971 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Pradhan B.R."]

Title: On Network Linguistics and the Conversational Design of Queueing Networks
Abstract: Network diagrams are a frequent means of problem description in many technical disciplines. However, problem-oriented graphic systems which use network diagrams as the medium of communication require translators. These accept the information provided in the network diagrams, associate mathematical meaning with the symbols of the diagram, and then transform that meaning into a model of the entire network which is capable of computer solution. A formal framework for these operations, constituting a useful linguistic approach to the translator functions, is offered. The approach is illustrated for Markovian queueing networks. ¬© 1971, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Irani K.B.", "Wallace V.L."]
Keywords: ["computer aided design", "conversational graphics", "graphics languages", "man-machine interaction", "markovian systems"]
Affiliations: [' Department of Electrical Engineering', ' Department of Computer and Information Science']

Title: Proceedings of the 1971 International ACM SIGIR Conference, SIGIR 1971
Source: Proceedings of the 1971 International ACM SIGIR Conference, SIGIR 1971
Abstract: The proceedings contain 19 papers. The topics discussed include: the function of semantics in automated language processing; how features resolve syntactic ambiguity; converse natural language data management system: current status and plans; CUE: a preprocessor system for restricted, natural English; full text document retrieval: Hebrew legal texts; quantification in query systems; the relational data file and the decision problem for classes of proper formulas; managing semantic data in an associative net; and a HEATHKIT method for building data management programs.

Title: How features resolve syntactic ambiguity
Source: Proceedings of the 1971 International ACM SIGIR Conference, SIGIR 1971
Abstract: Ambiguity is a pervasive and important aspect of natural language. Ambiguities, which are disambiguated by context, contribute powerfully to the expressiveness of natural language as compared to formal languages. In computational systems using natural language, problems of properly controlling ambiguity are particularly large, partially because of the necessity to circumvent parsings due to multiple orderings in the application of rules. Features, that is, subcategorizations of parts-of-speech, constitute an effective means for controlling syntactic ambiguity through ordering the hierarchical organization of syntactic constituents. This is the solution adopted for controlling ambiguity in REL English, which is part of the REL (Rapidly Extensible Language) System. REL is a total software system for facilitating man/machine communications. The efficiency of processing natural language in REL English is achieved both by the detailed syntactic aspects which are incorporated into the REL English grammar, and by means of the particular implementation for processing features in the parsing algorithm. ¬© 1971 ACM.
Name: ["Dostert B.H.", "Thompson F.B."]

Title: A heathkit method for building data management programs
Source: Proceedings of the 1971 International ACM SIGIR Conference, SIGIR 1971
Abstract: One of the difficulties faced in implementing information management and retrieval systems is that each case seems to present its own special complexities. As a result information retrieval systems typically fall behind their programming schedule and have many bugs when delivered. In this paper a set of basic operations on types of files are defined. These operations are intended to fulfill the same role for information retrieval systems programmers that functions such as LOG(X) fill for mathematical applications programmers.. they should make the job very much easier. The file operations have been implemented as a run‚Äîtime package written in FORTRAN IV and Burroughs Extended Algol. The approach has been used to develop three different information management systems; an APL interactive computing system, a generalized information retrieval system, and a specialized information retrieval system for map oriented data. These systems are described. ¬© 1971 ACM.
Name: ["Hunt E.", "Kildall G."]

Title: The converse natural language data management system: Current status and plans
Source: Proceedings of the 1971 International ACM SIGIR Conference, SIGIR 1971
Abstract: This paper presents an overview of research in progress in which the principal aim is the achievement of more natural and expressive modes of on-line communication with complexly structured data bases. A natural‚Äîlanguage compiler has been constructed that accepts sentences in a user-extendable English subset, produces surface and deep-structure syntactic analyses, and uses a network of concepts to construct semantic inter‚Äîpretations formalized as computable procedures. The procedures are evaluated by a data management system that updates, modifies, and searches data bases that can be formalized as finite models of states of affairs. The system has been designed and programmed to handle large vocabularies and large collections of facts efficiently. Plans for extending the research vehicle to interface with a deductive inference component and a voice input-output effort are briefly described. ¬© 1971 ACM.
Name: ["Kellogg C.", "Burger J.", "Diller T.", "Fogt K."]

Title: RECOGNITION OF IMAGE ELEMENTS.
Abstract: A method is described for the recognition of image elements, using facial photographs as an example, and the results of a digital-computer simulation of this process are presented. The object to be recognized is treated as a collection of component elements.
Name: ["Krymskiy N.K."]

Title: Optimal classification and its consequences
Source: Proceedings of the 1971 International ACM SIGIR Conference, SIGIR 1971
Abstract: A particular classification and retrieval model are considered. A notion is introduced which indicates the extent to which retrieval performance may be improved by a suitable choice of classification within the model. A method for determining the optimal performance for the model is outlined together with an algorithm for constructing the classification which allows this limit to be attained. A treatment of the mathematical preliminaries for a particular class of match function is given. The relevance of the analysis in research on information retrieval systems is discussed. ¬© 1971 ACM.
Name: ["Jackson D.M."]

Title: MINIMIZATION OF MANY-EXTREMAL FUNCTIONS OF SEVERAL VALUES.
Abstract: The problem of finding a global minimum of a function of several variables is examined from the point of view of the theory of decision making. A new algorithm is proposed for a global search, one that is a generalization of the results. The authors give examples of application of the proposed method for minimizing two- and three-dimensional many-extremal functions.
Name: ["Strongin R.G."]

Title: CONVEX APPROXIMATION METHODS IN PROBLEMS OF SEARCH FOR AN EXTREMUM.
Abstract: The problems of increasing the computational stability of search optimization methods are investigated. The algorithms for smoothing and best convex approximation of the models of functionals being minimized are proposed.
Name: ["Gorodetskiy V.I.", "Zakharin F.M."]

Title: RESULT OF AN INVESTIGATION OF ALGORITHMS FOR SELECTING CONNECTING PATHS IN SWITCHING SYSTEMS BY THE MONTE-CARLO METHOD.
Source: Telecommunications and Radio Engineering (English translation of Elektrosvyaz and Radiotekhnika)
Abstract: The use of an algorithm which takes into account the structural characteristics of the switching system ensures effective use of the connecting paths, and thus enables one, for a given quantity of switching apparatus and servicing quality, to transmit a greater load. The algorithm considered here is suitable for choosing connecting paths in switching systems with an arbitrary number of sections. The effectiveness of the algorithm is illustrated using the examples of a four-section switching system operating under individual selection conditions.
Name: ["Arkhipov I.M.", "Yershov V.A."]

Title: ADAPTIVE ALGORITHMS FOR OBSERVATION OF DYNAMIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A procedure is given for synthesizing observation algorithms based on principles of constructing extremal systems for processing information with coordinate control of models. The procedure developed enables the authors to carry out structural and parametric synthesis of algorithms for disturbed and undisturbed observation regimes.
Name: ["Krut'ko P.D."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF VARIABLE-STRUCTURE CONTROL SYSTEMS IN THE PRESENCE OF NOISE.
Abstract: The dynamics of second-order variable-structure systems are studied, with random noise in the switching channel of the logical device. High control performance can be achieved by special construction of the switching line.
Name: ["Ganin I.A.", "Zavedeyev A.I."]

Title: Checking Experiments ror Sequential Machines
Abstract: .Some new procedures for designing efficient checking experiments for sequential machines are described. These procedures are based on the use of four types of sequences introduced, namely, the compound DS, the resolving sequence (RS), the compound. RS, and the simple I/O sequence. Significant reduction in the bound on the length of checking experiments is achieved. Along a parallel line of development, a new procedure, called the state counting method, is presented for detecting faults that can cause an increase in the number of states. for an n-state, m-input symbol machine, this procedure gives a bound on the length of checking experiments that is approximately m<sup>ŒîœÄ</sup>. n times the bound for conventional checking experiments designed strictly under the assumption that no faults increase the number of states, where m > 1 and Œîn is the maximum anticipated increase in the number of‚Äô states due to faults. Copyright ¬© 1971 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Hsieh E.P."]

Title: Process monitoring with the MADAM program system, (Prozessueberwachung mit dem Programmsystem MADAM)
Abstract: A general survey is given to the main computer functions for process monitoring with the MADAM program system, especially of the monitoring of danger states, the logging of switching operations, the selection of data for fault analyses and the cyclical output of analogue values. Apart from modules of the system programs for the processing of analog readings and binar0 signals, use can also be made of the programs for logic functions, fault analysis, cyclical data outputs and text readouts.
Name: ["MUELLER CH", "ZANKL A"]

Title: Ordering algorithm for analysis of data arrays
Abstract: An algorithm for reordering data arrays is presented. The object is to find a one- dimensional ordering of the rows and columns of an array, given no prior information other than the array itself. The algorithm is an iterative one, and, in finding what it considers to be the most satisfactory ordering of an array, it also enables one to determine immediately the most significiant underlying variable.
Name: ["DEUTSCH SB", "MARTIN JJ"]

Title: The Effect of an Erroneous Model of Colored Noise on the Optimal Filtering Algorithm
Abstract: The effect of errors due to incorrect colored noise on optimal filtering algorithms has been investigated. The matrix differential equations have been derived for the computation of the actual covariance. Copyright ¬© 1971 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Saito O.", "Takeda H.", "Fukushima K."]

Title: An Evaluation of Adaptive Step-Size Random Search
Abstract: An evaluation is made of a proposed adaptive step-size random search method to minimize a quadratic function, and the computational results are replicated and improved. Comparing this. Copyright ¬© 1971 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["White L.J.", "Day R.G."]

Title: On the Bounds for State-Set Size in the Proofs of Equivalence Between Deterministic, Nondeterministic, and Two-Way Finite Automata
Abstract: The bounds on state-set size in the proofs of the equivalence between nondeterministic and deterministic finite automata and between two-way and one-way deterministic finite automata are considered. It is shown that the number of states in the subset machine in the first construction cannot be reduced for certain cases. It is also shown that the number of states in the one-way automation constructed in the second proof may be reduced only slightly. Copyright ¬© 1971 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Moore F.R."]

Title: Whirl Decomposition of Stochastic Systems
Abstract: Using a technique based on ‚Äústate splitting‚Äù it is shown that every n-state Markov system is decomposable into a whirl interconnection of n - 1 two-state Markov systems. Copyright ¬© 1971 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Paz A."]

Title: On the representation of weakly continuous stochastic processes
Abstract: A novel approach to obtaining series representations in the stochastic mean for weakly, and therefore mean square, continuous stochastic processes is presented. Two distinct orthogonal series representations are derived for the entire class of weakly continuous stochastic processes over a broad class of Lebesgue sets of the real line, and a constructive procedure to obtain them explicitly is given. They include as particular cases all earlier representations. Also they are shown to converge almost surely in the norm of an L<sub>2</sub> space. Two general results, on which the development of this paper is based, are also presented. ¬© 1971 American Elsevier Publishing Company, Inc.
Name: ["Cambanis S.", "Masry E."]
Affiliations: [' University of North Carolina', ' Information Science University of California at San Diego']

Title: Versatile cellular array for binary arithmetic
Abstract: A cellular array is proposed which can be controlled to perform the arithmetic functions of A plus BD plus C, A minus BD- C, or A/B. This results in a saving of hardware over previous arrays, and by having more terms in each function, a reduction in the overall calculation time can be achieved.
Name: ["WHITE G"]

Title: All zero- one algorithm for a certain class of transportation problems
Abstract: A special class of transportation problems is considered by which the cost is associated with the transportation of the material from each source to each user. Each user is to be supplied by one source only. The problem consists of finding the flow of the material from the sources to the users that satisfies their demands and minimizes the total transportation cost.
Name: ["DEMAIO A", "ROVEDA C"]

Title: Supervised learning in nonGaussian pattern recognition
Source: Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Decision and Control
Abstract: This paper considers supervised learning, structure and parameter adaptive binary pattern recognition when a nonGaussian pattern is observed in Gaussian noise. To facilitate a feasible solution, certain judicious approximations are made use of. Two examples are presented to demonstrate the learning capability of the proposed algorithms. ¬© 1971 IEEE.
Name: ["Rajasekaran P.K.", "Srinath M.D."]

Title: Function restoration using linear programming
Abstract: This paper presents a method for function restoration using linear programming. It is shown that by defining a suitable error function the function restoration problem can be transformed into a linear programming problem. Furthermore, the error correction algorithms reported in the literature can be derived by minimizing the error function by the steepest-descent method. Numerical examples are given for illustration. ¬© 1971 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Chan W.-C.", "Babu C.C."]

Title: A Computer-Based Learning System for Remote Manipulator Control
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A concept of adaptive aiding for performance improvement in remote handling is described. The concept incorporates an autonomous control subsystem (ACS) that is able to supplement the operator's control function. The behavior of the ACS is established through a process of learning by observing the operator's control function in relation to the environment and manipulator output. The computer-based system establishes a decision-making policy which is based on conditional probability. Initially, the output device is totally controlled by the operator, while the computer system acts as a passive observer. As the operation continues, the computer system gradually assumes the role of active controller, reducing the operator's function to that of an action initiator and inhibitor. A pilot experiment Indicates the feasibility of the concept; with a relatively short training period, the ACS was able to assume the bulk of the decision-making load and guide a three-dimen-sional manipulator satisfactorily through a series of manipulative tasks. Copyright ¬© 1971 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Freedy A.", "Hull F.C.", "Lucaccini L.F.", "Lyman J."]
Affiliations: [' University of California.', ' University of California', ' National Institutes of Health']

Title: Computer generation of minimally autocorrelated aperiodic binary signals (for system identification)
Source: J Inst Telecommun Eng New Delhi
Abstract: An algorithm for the generation of binary signals having an aperiodic autocorrelation function, which is progressivly having an aperiodic autocorrelation function, which is progressively approximated to the unit impulse, is presented. System identification with such a signal for injection and crosscorrelation is illustrated and compared with similar identification using pseudorandom binary signals.
Name: ["SESHADRI V"]

Title: Low sensitivity feedback control of non-linear discrete systems
Abstract: The synthesis of a feedback controller of non-linear discrete systems is considered. The control systems designed arc optimal and low sensitive to parameter variations. The first step in the synthesis of the controller is to quasilinearize the non-linear difference equations which describe the nonlinear discrete systems. Dynamic programming is then applied to find the feedback control law with respect to a quadratic performance index which includes the state variable, control variable, trajectory sensitivity function and control sensitivity function as its arguments. The optimal gains in the feedback control law for the non-linear systems are then determined by iteration. An example is studied in detail to show the superiority of this technique over the optimal control system without including the sensitivity functions. ¬© 1971 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Chiang S.-M.", "Shih Y.-P."]

Title: Using the Huffman code for sequential diagnosis
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A specific example of sequential diagnostics is presented for which D. A. Huffman coding can be applied. This optimal code, borrowed from information theory, can replace a dynamic programming approach when appropriate diagnostic tests are available. For both methods of solution required computer memory size is related to the magnitude of the diagnosis.
Name: ["HARDY LM", "OMBERG ER", "WATSON JW", "MAGER GE"]

Title: Associative techniques in the solution of data management problems
Source: Proceedings of the 1971 26th Annual Conference, ACM 1971
Abstract: This paper is concerned with the development of data management systems from an associative point of view. The design utilizes relational set theory applied to information systems. The basic notion involves the mathematical transformation of hierarchical structures of n-ary relations into associative normal form (ANF). This transformation preserves the information content while at the same time allowing the information to be manipulated by an associative memory in a more efficient manner than is possible on a random access memory. Among the advantages that can be realized from this system are the capability of handling many and varied data structures; substantially fewer pointers and directories; a reduction in storage space requirements; and a substantial decrease in query and update time. ¬© 1971 Association for Computing Machinery, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["DeFiore C.R.", "Stillman N.J.", "Berra P.B."]

Title: A preliminary algorithm for determining the order of a linear stochastic dynamic system
Source: Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Decision and Control
Abstract: This paper presents a preliminary algorithm for determining the orders of a linear stochastic dynamic system solely from the observation of the system output. The scalar transfer function of the system contains both poles and zeros, however, no a priori information is available about the numbers and values of these poles and zeros. The driving input of this system is assumed to be white. Such a system is called a mixed type process, since it is a combination of the autoregressive (all-pole) and the moving-average (all zero) processes. The objective of this algorithm is thus to determine the number of poles (order of the autoregressive portion of the process) and the number of zeros (order of the moving-average portion of the process) of the mixed type process. The algorithm suggested in this paper is based on a two stage process: first take those output correlations which follow a repetitive pattern to determine the order of the autoregressive portion, then proceed to estimate the autoregressive parameters and lower the index of the correlation until the significant deviation from the repetitive pattern is observed, the order of the moving-average then can be determined. ¬© 1971 IEEE.
Name: ["Chow J.C."]

Title: Comments on ‚ÄúA Nonlinear Mapping for Data Structure Analysis‚Äù
Abstract: A recent paper by Sammon<sup>1</sup> describes a useful technique for analyzing data and helping find clusters. It consists of a nonlinear mapping of the original data into two dimensions (for visual inspection) which is superior for many purposes to use of the first two principal components. The present correspondence points out that essentially the same mapping can be achieved by a widely used, easily obtainable computer program for multidimensional scaling called M-D-SCAL. ¬© 1971, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Kruskal J.B."]

Title: COMPUTER LEARNING TECHNIQUE FOR DETERMINING CARDIAC OUTPUT
Source: JAAMI J Ass Advan Med Instrum
Abstract: This paper describes an automatic error correcting algorithm for determining cardiac output from indicator-dilution curves. The importance of this technique, as opposed to existing methods, is that the use of error correction eliminates the need for differentiation of the noisy input signal, thus providing a more stable system. In particular, the continuous version of this algorithm has been programmed for analog computation.
Name: ["ROY R", "POWERS JR SR"]

Title: ON THE THEORY OF LOGICAL-DYNAMIC CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The structural properties of logical-dynamic systems are interpreted by means of logic-operator matrices and predicate systems. Logical-dynamic control systems are shown to be a general case of systems relative to continuous systems, pulse systems, and automatic systems with finite automata.
Name: ["Zhuk K.D."]

Title: MULTILAYER STATISTICAL DECISION THEORY.
Abstract: A theorem is proved on the convergence of the multilayered algorithm to the optimal decisions obtained by the complete (one layer) algorithm. According to this theorem, though the analog of the complete description differs from the latter, in general, both these formulas lead to the same optimal decision.
Name: ["Ivakhnenko O", "Spynu Ye.I.", "Dymytrov V.D.", "Patereu S.H.", "Patratiy I.Z."]

Title: Logical Networks for Feature Extraction
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The extraction of features for the purpose of reconstituting a pattern set may be particularly useful in those cases where a large number of patterns can be decomposed into a relatively small set of sub-patterns. By the representation of pattern and feature sets as matrices, the concept of feature determination has been extended to multilevel features and the hierarchical organization of logical networks employing these features. An algorithm is presented to sequentially generate features by an adaptive process of altering weights in a network of thresholdlike logical elements. Experimental results indicate the potential of the algorithm in organizing a recognition network to correspond to the information structure of the pattern set. Copyright ¬© 1971 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Riseman E.M."]

Title: The Reconstruction of Binary Patterns from Their Projections
Abstract: Given the horizontal and vertical projections of a finite binary pattern f, can we reconstruct the original pattern f? In this paper we give a characterization of patterns that are reconstructable from their projections. Three algorithms are developed to reconstruct both unambiguous and ambiguous patterns. It is shown that an unambiguous pattern can be perfectly reconstructed in time m √ó n and that a pattern similar to an ambiguous pattern can also be constructed in time m √ó n, where m, n are the dimensions of the pattern frame. ¬© 1971, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Chang S.-K."]

Title: Nonlinear Estimation Via Kalman Filtering
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: The extended Kalman-Bucy filtering algorithm is applied to the problem of estimating the system parameters of a single-channel missile attitude control system. In particular, noisy observations of body angular rate, normal acceleration, and control surface deflection are used in the algorithm to obtain estimates of body angular rate, angle of attack, control surface deflection, air density, and missile velocity. Computational results obtained for this problem are presented. These results are evaluated to determine the applicability of this estimator as a part of an adaptive control scheme. In addition, a general approach to the formulation of practical nonlinear estimation problems is suggested. Copyright ¬© 1970 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Kappl J.J."]

Title: Simulation neuronaler impulsrhythmen
Abstract: Networks with cyclic inhibition (NW) were introduced in a previous paper (Kling, Szekely, 1968) as models of neural burst-generators with rhythmic output pattern: an arbitrarily number of neuronlike elements is connected to a ring-shaped structure, its basic principle being recurrent cyclic inhibition. An external stimulation of all elements causes a periodical rotation of the excitation (firing) state. - The present paper is a detailed theoretical investigation of the NW, which can be characterized as an asynchronous astable multiflop. Its behaviour can be described by special difference equations over a continuous time axis; characteristic features of periodicity are derived. Particularly the influence of the socalled recovery times (the mutual independent and variable transit times from inhibitory to firing state of each element) is demonstrated. Furthermore, it is shown, that the mean of the stationary time pattern of a stochastic NW (with stochastic varying recovery times) is an analog to a special time pattern of a special (infinite) class of the corresponding deterministic NW. ¬© 1971 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Kling U."]
Affiliations: ['Institut f√ºr Nachrichtentechnik der Technischen Hochschule M√ºnchen', 'Bildungstechnologisches Zentrum Wiesbaden Au√üenstelle Darmstadt - Gruppe CAI']

Title: ON BARRON'S SELF-ORGANIZED CONTROL
Abstract: Self-organizing control (SOC) is analyzed as a conventional controller and the evolution of adaptive SOC from a simple linear system is shown. The development intentionally avoids any reference to the bionics concepts which Barron uses to describe his system. Reply by R. L. Barron.
Name: ["TILLEY EA"]

Title: Robust Detection of a Known Signal in Nearly Gaussian Noise
Abstract: A detector that is not nonparametric, but that nevertheless performs well over a broad class of noise distributions is termed a robust detector. One possible way to obtain a certain degree of robustness or stability is to look for a min-max solution. For the problem of detecting a signal of known form in additive, nearly Gaussian noise, the solution to the min-max problem is obtained when the signal amplitude is known and the nearly Gaussian noise is specified by a mixture model. The solution takes the form of a correlator-limiter detector. For a constant signal, the correlator-limiter detector reduces to a limiter detector, which is shown to be robust in terms of power and false alarm. By adding a symmetry constraint to the nearly normal noise and formulating the problem as one of local detection, the limiter-correlator is obtained as the local minmax solution. The limiter-correlator is shown to be robust in terms of asymptotic relative efficiency (ARE). For a pulse train of unknown phase, a limiter-envelope sum detector is also shown to be robust in terms of ARE. ¬© 1971, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Martin R.D.", "Schwartz S.C."]

Title: Computer improvement of Anger Camera images
Abstract: Data from the Anger Camera were obtained by means of a data acquisition computer or high resolution film reader and stored on magnetic tape. Correction for nonuniformity was obtained for camera flood and stored for processing incoming data. In addition, a method of contrast enhancement which allows the user to visualize the resulting image and its histogram is described. ¬© 1971.
Name: ["Waxman A.D.", "Siemsen J.K.", "Efron E.", "Wright J."]
Affiliations: [' Southern California Medical Center Los Angeles', 'IBM']

Title: Data processing of radioisotope images for optimum smoothing
Abstract: A digital method of data processing radioisotope scan images is used to derive a smoothing function for obtaining the best least mean squares fit of a noisy radioisotope image to the expected image. This is compared to smoothing with a Gaussian function, where it is seen to give a better least mean squares fit. Approximate values for the relevant parameters are derived for a digitized thyroid scan.
Name: ["Barber D.C.", "Mallard J.R."]

Title: Reconstructions of Signals of a Known Class From a Given Set of Linear Measurements
Abstract: This paper investigates the error in reconstructions of a signal based on a given finite set of linear measurements, and presents two schemes that, if there is available a priori knowledge of the class of signals of which the measured signal is a member, can achieve a reduction of this error beyond the best that could be done without such knowledge. The error measure used is the supremum over the class of the ‚Ñí2distance between a signal and its reconstruction. The essence of the proposed reconstruction techniques is a coordinate transformation from the sampling subspace to a new reconstruction subspace known to be efficient for representation of signals of the given class. This study applies the theory of extremal subspaces and n widths of signal classes originated by Kolmogorov. Results are applied to the much studied class of time-concentrated bandlimited signals. The measurement process is here assumed to be the convenient one of Nyquist rate time sampling. For this problem, plots of the error bounds and of several test functions and their reconstructions are presented, both for the proposed reconstructions, and for conventional cardinal-sampling-theorem reconstructions. ¬© 1971, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Parks T.W.", "Meier R.G."]

Title: The Reliability of Linear Feature Extractors
Abstract: This paper introduces the concepts of capacity and reliability of a linear feature extractor. The relationship between the capacity introduced here and the channel capacity in information theory is discussed in some detail. The reliability is associated with the least favorable distributions and gives us a measure of the effectiveness for the worst possible case. It is of particular importance in pattern recognition problems because we have no control over the distributions of the patterns. It is shown that for the family of probability distributions with covariance matrix S, the most reliable (i.e., minimax) feature extractor is the Karhunan-Lo√©ve expansion. The concept of reliability is extended to the two-class pattern recognition problem and is discussed in terms of the Bhattacharyya distance. ¬© 1971, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Young T.Y."]

Title: ON MINIMIZING THE NUMBER OF MULTIPLICATIONS NECESSARY FOR MATRIX MULTIPLICATION
Abstract: This paper develops an algorithm to multiply a p x 2 matrix by a 2 x n matrix. The algorithm minimizes the number of multiplications for matrix of multiplication without commutativity for the special cases p equal 1 or 2, n equal 1, 2, and p equal 3, n equal 3. It is shown that commutativity actually reduces the number of multiplications required.
Name: ["HOPCROFT JE", "KERR LR"]

Title: Linear Optimization in Synthesis of Nonlinear Spatial Filters
Abstract: Generally, the synthesis of coherent spatial filters is restricted to the linear region of the transfer characteristic of a photographic film. However, a technique of synthesizing a nonlinear spatial filter such that the signal detection may be optimum will be described. In this paper, a generalized linear optimization technique is formulated. The application of this optimization technique toward a simple nonlinear spatial filter is demonstrated, and the extension of this optimization technique for a more complicated nonlinear spatial filter is also given. The signal detection by nonlinear optimum spatial filtering is analyzed. Finally, it is concluded that, instead of restricting the spatialFllter recording to the linear region of the transfer characteristic of the photographic film, an optimum nonlinear spatial filter may be achieved. ¬© 1971, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Yu F.T.S."]

Title: Feature Extraction by Golay Hexagonal Pattern Transforms
Abstract: Golay hexagonal pattern transforms are position independent local operators for use in transforming or altering binary images. The hexagonal tessellation is preferred because it removes the connectivity ambiguity present in the square or checkerboard tessellation. Golay transforms also may be applied to multilevel or ‚Äúgray‚Äù images by encoding such images as a registered stack of binary image planes. The general Golay transform creates a new binary image (the output image) from as many as three stacked input images. Simpler Golay transforms merely alter the binary pattern contained in a single image plane, i.e., the same plane acts as both input and out-put. Because it is slow and cumbersome to perform Golay transforms using a general-purpose computer, fast special-purpose computers have been built for this purpose which may be programmed in a new image processing language called Glol (Golay logic language). It has been found, using both synthetic images as well as images taken from the real world, that Golay transforms are useful in feature enhancement and extraction. Several illustrative examples are pro-vided. ¬© 1971, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Preston K., JR."]

Title: Performance optimization of a self-organizing feedback control system in presence of inherent coupling signals
Abstract: This paper deals with optimization of the response of a self organizing feedback control system in presence of inherent coupling signals. The system contains lenses and phototubes as a sensing element and it always orients its front surface in the direction of the tracked object with the help of light signals received. Adaptive Step Size Random Search (ASSRS) has been used and parameter optimization in presence of different coupling signals was achieved. The results obtained are verified by an inverse sensitivity method. Finally the merits of random search technique are compared with those of the inverse sensitivity method. ¬© 1971.
Name: ["Chatterji B.N.", "Chatterjee B."]

Title: Speaker Adaptation in a Limited Speech Recognition System
Abstract: This study examines the feasibility and limitations of speaker adaptation in improving the performance of a fixed(speaker-independent) automatic speech recognition system. A fixed vocabulary of 55 [eCVd] syllables is used in the recognition system, where C is 1 of 11 stops and fricatives, and V is 1 of 5 tense vowels. The results of the experiment on speaker adaptation, performed with 6 male and 6 female adult speakers, show that speakers can learn to change their articulations to appreciably improve recognition scores. The preliminary results obtained also indicate that most of the necessary adaptation can be achieved in a relatively short time, provided that the speakers are instructed in how to change their articulations to produce the desired effects. The recognition scheme is based on the extraction of several acoustic features from the speech signal. This is accomplished by a hierarchy of decisions made on carefully selected parameters that are computed from a spectral description of the speech signal by means of a set of energoids (energy centroids), each energoid representing the center of energy concentration in a particular spectral energy band. ¬© 1971, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Makhoul J."]

Title: Some Geometric Properties of the Likelihoood Ratio
Abstract: A fundamental spatial property is noted that relates the likelihood ratio for random signals in Gaussian noise to conditional-mean parameter estimation. This allows a geometric interpretation of the estimation-correlation operation. Some additional properties exhibited by the likelihood ratio are also presented. ¬© 1971, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hatsell C.P.", "Nolte L.W."]

Title: Convergence to the Rate-Distortion Function for Gaussian Sources
Abstract: In this paper we derive an expression for the minimum-mean-square error achievable in encoding t samples of a stationary correlated Gaussian source. It is assumed that the source output is not known exactly but is corrupted by correlated Gaussian noise. The expression is obtained in terms of the covariance matrices of the source and noise sequences. It is shown that as t ‚Üí ‚àû, the result agrees with a known asymptotic result, which is expressed in terms of the power spectra of the source and noise. The rate of convergence to the asymptotic results as a function of coding delay is investigated for the case where the source is first-order Markov and the noise is uncorrelated. With D the asymptotic minimum-mean-square error and D, the minimum-mean-square error achievable in transmitting t samples, we find ‚à£Dt-D‚à£ ‚â§ 0((t-1log t)1/2) when we transmit the noisy source vectors over a noiseless channel and ‚à£Dt-D‚à£ ‚â§ 0((t-1 log t)1/3) when the channel is noisy. ¬© 1971, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Bunin B.J.", "Wolf J.K."]

Title: Supervised Learning Sequential Structure and Parameter Adaptive Pattern Recognition: Discrete Data Case
Abstract: In a previous paper [1], Bayes-optimal recursive supervised learning structure and parameter adaptive pattern recognition systems were derived for continuous ‚Äúlumped‚Äù Gaussian processes. In this paper, the discrete data case is considered, and the discrete data version of the partition theorem is derived. Several examples are also presented of the application of the adaptive detectors, and computational results are given indicating their learning capacity and convergence rate. ¬© 1971, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Lainiotis D.G."]

Title: Digital synthesis of non-linear filters
Abstract: Practical implementation of discrete-time Bayesoptimal non-linear estimators has not received much attention, since the problems associated with storing probability densities and computing convolution integrals are formidable, and, hence, presumably prohibitive. However, the prevailing technique of designing non-linear estimators based upon Taylor series approximations frequently leads to undesirable, inaccurate or unstable, behavior. Thus there is considerable motivation for proceeding with the development of digital realizations of non-linear filters whose degree of accuracy is under the complete control of the computer program. In this paper techniques are proposed and discussed which solve the basic two subproblems associated with optimal discrete-time non-linear estimators: density storage and Bayes-law computation. For density storage a point mass representation on a floating rectangular grid of indices is proposed, while for the Bayes-law computation a simple and effective convolution summation involving an ellipsoid tracking technique to determine the important points to include in the summation is developed. Monte Carlo experiments with the proposed non-linear estimator reveal significant improvement in mean-square error behavior over some conventional approximation realizations. An example is given which illustrates the application of non-linear estimation to tracking and detection systems. ¬© 1971.
Name: ["Bucy R.S.", "Senne K.D."]

Title: Analog computer for non-linear optimal control
Abstract: In the optimization of a non-linear system one is generally faced with a complicated two point boundary value problem. This two point boundary value problem in the case of a linear system can be solved by breaking it into two one point boundary value problems, by going into the Riccati equation. However in case of a non-linear or bilinear system the solution of the Riccati equation is not a simple undertaking. Thus various iteration methods are often tried. In this paper a method of solving this two point boundary value problem on analog computer has been presented. The steepest descent method is applied here on boundary condition iteration. This method overcomes a past hesitation of using the analog computer for the optimization problems, which require a large computer memory. This method in fact is applicable to any system linear or non-linear. However the size of the computer and the degree of accuracy definitely limit its application. ¬© 1971 Presses Acad√©miques Europ√©ennes, Brussels.
Name: ["Sahni R.N."]

Title: A computational algorithm for the identification of nonlinear systems
Abstract: An automatic computational algorithm for parameter identification is presented. The algorithm has been implemented on a digital computer and identification is made in terms of a nonlinear discrete model which is referred to as the General model. The model is deterministic, time invariant and is constructed by cascading a discrete linear system with memory and two zero-memory nonlinear gain functions. This model is an extension of a discrete form of the Hammerstein model first formulated and applied to the identification problem by Narendra and Gallman. The model parameters are determined (identified) by minimizing the mean square error between the model and plant output by a conjugate gradient search. The algorithm has been extended to include parameter identification of feedback systems. ¬© 1971.
Name: ["Goldberg S.", "Durling A."]
Affiliations: ['Department of Electrical Engineering California State Polytechnic College', 'Department of Electrical Engineering University of Miami']

Title: Performance-Measure Densities for a Class of LQG Control Systems
Abstract: When linear-quadratic-Gaussian (LQG) control problems are solved, the performance measure takes on a probability density function of a type which has received very little attention in the literature because of the nonzero-mean multidimensional character of the state process. This paper combines techniques of the fast Fourier transform, recent results of Baggeroer and Schwartz, and the classic methods of Karhunen-Loeve to present what seem to be the first published curves of such densities. As a vehicle for discussion, a one-parameter family of LQG control systems of the minimal variance type serves both to provide examples of the new density curves and to display certain controlled behaviors of the moments of the densities. Name: ["Sain M.K.", "Liberty S.R."]
Affiliations: [' Universitv of Kotre Dame', ' Texas Tech University']

Title: A new technique for closed loop control of discrete stochastic nonlinear systems
Source: Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Decision and Control
Abstract: A new approach for optimum control of discrete stochastic nonlinear systems is developed from practical engineering assumptions. Systems amenable to this new approach include optimum guidance and navigation systems for space and terrestrial vehicles, optimum closedloop process controllers, and optimum controllers for systems with unknown parameters. The solution is obtained by expansion of the stochastic cost function in a power series around a deterministic trajectory with the assumption of linear perturbation estimation and control about that trajectory. Optimization of the expanded cost function gives necessary conditions dependent on the covariance matrices and the deterministic portion of the cost. When the necessary conditions are solved, a set of openloop controls, perturbation controller gains, and perturbation estimator gains are obtained that can be precomputed and implemented into the system. ¬© 1971 IEEE.
Name: ["Schmidt G.T."]

Title: Suboptimum algorithms for post- detection processing of optical radar signals in the photon- counting mode for estimating target range- 2
Abstract: A suboptimum linear- quadratic post- detection processing algorithm is investigated. See also English translation in Telecommun Radio Eng pt 2 v 26 n 4 Apr 1971 p 104-8
Name: ["TERPUGOV AF", "KHARITONENKO AA"]

Title: Recognizing three- dimensional objects by their silhouettes
Abstract: A method of classifying or identifying a three- dimensional object from one or more of its silhouettes is described. The method is based on a low- cost parallel mechanism for computing the slope density, i. e. , the density of slopes of the edge of the silhouette. Examples of applications of the method are microscopy and aerial navigation. The present study is based on an application of the technique to recognizing aircraft.
Name: ["SKLANSKY J", "DAVISON GA"]

Title: Integrated automatic control of metallurgical furnaces by means of an electronic computer, (La regolazione automatica integrale di forni siderurgici tramite calcolatore elettronico)
Abstract: The results obtained by the application of a mini- computer for the on- line control of a continuous multi- zone furnace for heat- treating of steel bars are reported.
Name: ["BARBA F", "SCHGOER G"]

Title: Process computer in the data and automation systems of discontinuous processes, (Der Einsatz des Prozessrechners in Informations- und Automatisierungssystemen diskontinuierlicher Prozesse)
Abstract: Refers to the most important operational functions for the acquisition, control, and short- term planning of production operations in piece processes that can be realized with a process computer. The functions, their application, and their data traffic with the process and with each other are described. Functions of supervising and autosupervising production facilites are treated.
Name: ["BAHRS M"]

Title: On the Need for and Use of a Measure of State Estimation Errors in the Design of Quadratic-Optimal Control Gains
Abstract: In this correspondence it is shown quantitatively that state estimation error acts like an additional disturbance on the stochastic linear regulator. The closed-loop system's covariance matrix is shown to be an explicit function of the optimal filter's state estimation error covariance matrix. Ways in which this information can be used in design of the feedback gain matrix of the deterministic linear regulator are discussed. Copyright ¬© 1971 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Mendel J.M."]

Title: Etudes sur les Œµ- et œÅ-algorithmes
Abstract: Some methods of accelerating the convergence of sequences are studied herein. It is shown that, in some special cases, the convergence of the Œµ-algorithm of Wynn is assured. A modification of this algorithm is then proposed which may still accelerate the convergence toward the limit. Finally, a new œÅ{variant}-algorithm is given in which the dependence with respect to a parameter is explicitely introduced. ¬© 1971 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Brezinski C."]

Title: On the Stochastic Control of Linear Systems with Different Information Sets
Abstract: This paper deals with the stochastic control of linear systems in which the information available to distinct controllers is different. Constraints on the control structure are imposed. Necessary conditions for optimality of the controller structure parameters are obtained. The results show that the separation theorem does not hold in this case. Copyright ¬© 1971 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Chong C.-Y.", "Athans M."]

Title: The identification of optimum production systems by network analysis and dynamic programming
Abstract: Agricultural and horticultural production systems are made up from combinations of unit operations. These unit operations can be combined in different ways and the number of feasible systems available is likely to be very large. Computer algorithms based on the analysis of a general network and on a simple application of dynamic programming have been developed to identify and evaluate the optimum or near optimum combinations of unit operations from a network representation of feasible systems. The algorithms can take into account such factors as varying levels of production or equipment usage. ¬© 1971, The British Society for Research in Agricultural Engineering. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Boyce D.S.", "Parke D.", "Corrie W.J."]

Title: Some Considerations on the Application of the Volterra Representation of Nonlinear Networks to Adaptive Echo Cancellers
Abstract: In this paper we apply the Volterra representation of nonlinear systems to the echo control problem and propose a generalized adaptive echo canceller which compensates for nonlinear echo paths. We prove that the proposed echo canceller converges and reduces the echo to zero and finally we suggest other applications for the system. ¬© 1971 The Bell System Technical Journal
Name: ["Thomas E.J."]

Title: APPROACH TO SOLVING DISCRETE PROGRAMMING PROBLEMS.
Abstract: The authors propose an approach based on successive decomposition of the set of feasible plans of a problem into subsets, each of which corresponds to some specific feature of the solution. It is estimated how promising the subsets are on the basis of statistics about the influence of the feature of a solution on the value of the objective function. The best feature is fixed, and the corresponding subset is further decomposed. The approach is investigated using the example of constructing the schedule for automatic transport traffic.
Name: ["Ovsievich B.L.", "Pokidova B.I."]

Title: Binary B-trees for virtual memory
Source: Proceedings of the ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data
Abstract: A class of binary trees is described for maintaining ordered sets of data. Random insertions, deletions, and retrievals of keys can be done in time proportional to log N where N is the cardinality of the data-set. Binary B-trees are a modification of B-trees described previously by Bayer and McCreight. They avoid the storage overhead encountered with B-trees and are suitable for processing in a one-level store.
Name: ["Bayer R."]

Title: Bayesian aggregation of independent successive visual inputs
Abstract: Tested the hypothesis that successive, brief visual stimuli are perceptually independent, rather than being increasingly clear. If multiple looks are independent, then the serial position of a discrepant letter should not affect identification accuracy. 5 undergraduates and the 1st author made identification responses to tachistoscopically presented graphemes (a, t, u), presented 1 at a time and 3 times in succession. Many 3-look trials had a discrepant letter in 1 of the 3 serial positions. No effect due to order of the discrepant letter was found, supporting the independence hypothesis. Given evidence for independence, bayes' rule was used as a model for information aggregation to predict 3-look performance from 1-look data. Predictions were very accurate, providing further evidence for the bayesian aggregation model and for perceptual independence. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2006 APA, all rights reserved). ¬© 1971 American Psychological Association.
Name: ["Keeley S.M.", "Doherty M.E."]
Keywords: ["perceptual independence vs increasing clarity of successive brief visual stimuli bayesian aggregation model", "successive visual", "hypothesis successive", "perceptually independent", "stimuli perceptually"]

Title: An algorithm for determining the shortest path on a network graph
Source: USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics
Abstract: AN algorithm for calculating the shortest path in an oriented network graph with a large number of vertices is described; it is based on the idea of counter-solution of the functional equations of dynamic programming. The solving process is in two stages. A numerical example is given, illustrating the effectiveness of the algorithm. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Alekseeva S.M.", "Alekseev O.G."]

Title: On the allocation of inference functions in decision systems
Abstract: Information processing and decision performance by a hierarchal (or cascaded) system was studied under the realistic circumstance in which some input data are of necessity processed intuitively, and some are processed by a man-machine (PIP) combine. The objective was to determine how much use the system is able to make of information that, for one reason or another, must be added to the PIP aggregate "by hand.". Three ranges of such "unanticipated" data were introduced, together with two procedures for handling it: before and after PIP arrived at its opinion (i.e., as an adjustment in the priors for PIP, and as a revision in the PIP posteriors). From a total of 1722 problems the conclusion seems to be that performance does improve with manually aggregated (unanticipated) data, but it asymptotes after relatively few (4-6) such items. This implies a limited human capacity. Order of processing has little or no effect. ¬© 1971.
Name: ["Howell W.C.", "Gettys C.F.", "Martin D.W."]

Title: Mathematical simulation of the electroencephalogram using an autoregressive series
Abstract: A method of fitting an autoregressive series to the EEG is described. Some results from this method of analysis relating to the statistical properties of the EEG are mentioned which show the EEG 'generators' to be changing every 20 seconds, and which suggest the optimum length of an epoch for analysis is from 20 to 30 seconds. Some evidence that the EEG generators and the generators of the evoked potential have certain features in common is presented and that a model set up to the spontaneous ongoing activity of the EEG is able to specify within limits the form of the evoked potential at that point. Finally, a simple model of the cortico-thalamic action seen from the point of view of the autoregressive series is described. ¬© 1971.
Name: ["Fenwick P.B.C.", "Michie P.", "Dollimore J.", "Fenton G.W."]
Affiliations: [' London Great Britain Part of the work was done while the author held a Clinical Research Fellowship', ' the University of London', 'University of London Institute of Computer Science', ' Institute of Psychiatry']

Title: Algorhythms of the preliminary treatment of signals in the visual analyser
Abstract: It is proposed to use the method of synthesis of optimal algorhythms for treating signals in investigating the functional organization and patterns of work of sections of the nervous system. A model has been worked out and the optimal algorhythm for processing the receptor signals synthesized for the neurone ensembles of the visual analyser. A comparison has been made of the optimal algorhythm with the work of the actual ensembles of the nerve cells of the visual analyser. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Petrov A.A."]

Title: A minimization method without the calculation of derivatives
Source: USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics
Abstract: A METHOD of minimizing convex functions converging from any initial approximation, in which the calculation of the gradient is replaced by the calculation of the function at additional points, is presented. It is proved that the rate of convergence of the method is ultralinear. The present paper is a direct continuation of [1], in which a method of minimizing a function of many variables, possessing ultralinear convergence, but requiring the calculation of the gradient of the minimized function, was presented. In a number of problems the calculation of the gradient itself may present considerable difficulties. Hence it is important to consider methods in which the gradient is calculated approximately by calculating values of the function at additional points. Papers on this topic already exist (for example, [2-5]). In the present paper it is shown that by increasing the calculations of values of the function it is possible to generalize the results of !l1 and construct methods with ultralinear convergence, not requiring the calculation of the gradient. Since the ideas and methods used in this paper are similar to the methods in [ll, to avoid repetition, we use all the concepts and notation introduced in [1 !, and this paper must be read together with [1]. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Danilin Yu.M.", "Pshenichnyi B.N."]

Title: I. Constancy of colour perception
Abstract: In natural conditions of observation man recognizes the colour of objects despite the considerable scatter of spectral composition of the light sources. Such recognition must necessarily require comparison of the excitation of several sites on the retina. The present work is concerned with study of certain patterns of this process (psychophysiological experiments and construction of models). In the first part we introduce the main concepts and describe the signs allowing the visual system to "introduce a correction for the character of the illumination". ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Nyuberg N.D.", "Bongard M.M.", "Nikolayev P.P."]

Title: Classification by cascaded threshold elements
Abstract: A method is presented to synthesize threshold element networks by iterative computation of the parameters. The modification of the parameters, which is under the control of a gain function, is carried out sequentially. The training procedure of the whole cascade is subdivided into separate training periods during which only the parameters of one threshold element are modified. The algorithm starts with one threshold element. If a given pattern set is not linearly separable the structure of the classifier is extended automatically to a general cascade. Computer simulations indicate good results. ¬© 1971.
Name: ["Holdermann F."]

Title: Performance of single letters and pairs of letters in short-term recognition experiments
Abstract: The theory of statistical decision is used to describe the recognition of single letters and pairs of letters from verbally presented lists. The results which are explained by means of the memory operating characteristic exhibit that the recognition of homogeneous pairs is predictably better than the recognition of single items. ¬© 1971 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Hauske G."]
Affiliations: ['Institut f√ºr Nachrichtentechnik der Technischen Universit√§t M√ºnchen']

Title: Operations on certain expressions
Source: USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics
Abstract: ALGORITHMS are described for some natural transformations of rational expressions of several which are in general inhomogeneous (the coefficients are integers throughout). With the increasing interest in the transformation of expressions by computer, suitable transformation algorithms need to be developed. The present paper describes some particular algorithms, some of which have been realized in program form by the author. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Abramov S.A."]

Title: A computational problem solver
Source: USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics
Abstract: A PROBLEM-SOLVING program is discussed for the case when the problem description does not contain the solution algorithm in explicit form. The semantic aspect of the problem is represented by a computational model, on the basis of which the algorithm is compiled. Examples are given of solving problems from school geometry and physics. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Tyugu E.Kh."]

Title: Model of psychological functioning
Abstract: A model of psychological functioning, based on the activity of individual neurons, is proposed. A method to identify general patterns of behavior is outlined. A biochemical mechanism to account for synaptic transmission and modification of behavior by experience is suggested and incorporated in a holographic model of memory. A model of some cognitive processes is presented as an illustration of the method of applying the model; a means of extending the model to social organizations is suggested, and implications of the model are briefly discussed. ¬© 1971.
Name: ["Irving D.", "Proctor P."]

Title: Correlative level coding and maximum- likelihood decoding
Abstract: A correlative level encoder is treated as a linear finite- state machine and an application of the maximum- liklihood decoding (MLD) algorithm, which was originally proposed by A. J. Viterbi in decoding convolutional codes, is discussed. Asymptotic expressions for the probability of decoding error are obtained for a class of correlative level coding systems, and the results are confirmed by computer simulations. It is shown that a substantial performance gain is attainable by this probabilistic decoding method.
Name: ["KOBAYASHI H"]

Title: AUTOMATIC READOUT OF GRAPHIC INFORMATION IN A COMPUTER-PLOTTER SYSTEM.
Abstract: Methods are considered for increasing the efficiency of reading out geometrical patterns from a computer-AP (automatic plotter) system. Algorithms are described for automatic storage and readout of graphic information.
Name: ["Sollogub A.V.", "Belyakov V.G.", "Blagodatskikh N.I."]

Title: Loop schemata
Source: Proceedings of the Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
Abstract: We define a class of program schemata arising from the subrecursive programming language Loop. In this preliminary report on Loop schemata we show how to assign functional expressions to these schemata (as one aspect of the problem of assigning meaning to these programs) , and we outline a solution to the schemata equivalence problem. Schemata equivalence is reduced to questions about formal expressions. Certain subcases of the problem are easily shown solvable, and although we claim that the general problem is solvable, we do not present the complete solution here because of its complexity. ¬© Copyright 1971 by ACM Special Interest Group for Automata and Computability Theory.
Name: ["Constable R.L."]

Title: The computation of the shortest path in graphs and appropriate data structures | Die Bestimmung k√ºrzester Pfade in Graphen und passende Datenstrukturen
Abstract: By using appropriate data structures we solve a bookkeeping problem that arises when determining the shortest path in a net. At the same time the difference between the classical algorithms by Moore and Dijkstra is diminished. Besides that we present a way how the computing effort can be reduced when information about the end point is available. ¬© 1971 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Braess D."]

Title: An iteration theorem for one-counter languages
Source: Proceedings of the Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
Abstract: We give a definition of one-counter languages. We show that the smallest full AFL containing this family is principal with full generator D, the semi-Dyck language on two letters. We then give without the proof, which shall be published elsewhere, our main result: An iteration theorem for one-counter languages that yields several corollaries. ¬© Copyright 1971 by ACM Special Interest Group for Automata and Computability Theory.
Name: ["Boasson L."]

Title: GENERAL ORDER MINKOWSKI METRIC PATTERN CLASSIFIER.
Abstract: One general category of multiclass deterministic pattern recognition systems is defined by a linear structure in the input variables and an analytical criterion. This criterion requires the minimization of the average p**t**h power of one Minkowski distance measure of order p in one particular decision space. Analytical reasoning indicates that the criterion yields an error-correcting procedure. This procedure results in a reduction of the number of misclassifications when the order of the criterion metric is increased. This feature renders the criterion particularly well suited to nonseparable problems. It is briefly mentioned how this design criterion may be used to produce optimized decision surfaces in the separable two class case, as it tends to maximize the minimum distance from each class to the decision surface. The Bayesian distribution-free classifier appears as a special case of the general category of classifiers defined by the criterion.
Name: ["Devijver Pierre A."]

Title: The unit-clause proof procedure with equality
Abstract: Besides a rigorous treatment of what we call assignment and which describes more clearly the notion of substitutions done by a computer, a proof procedure is given which extends the scope of the unit-clause procedure to the first order predicate calculus with equality. The main part of the procedure is an algorithm which generates assignments instead of clauses in order to make inferences due to equalities. This procedure is equivalent to the unit-clause procedure extended by paramodulation. A machine proof of a theorem is given in the appendix. ¬© 1971 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Hoffmann G.-R.", "Veenker G."]
Affiliations: ['Zentrum f√ºr Datenverarbeitung der Universit√§t T√ºbingen', 'Gesellschaft f√ºr Mathematik und Datenverarbeitung m. b. H. Bonn']

Title: AUTOMATIC DETECTION OF VEHICLES IN AERIAL PHOTOGRAPHS OF HIGHWAYS.
Abstract: An approach to automating the data reduction process is described. Techniques from the fields of interactive computer graphics and automatic pattern recognition are used in combination to reduce the amount of human effort required. A computer-controlled flying-spot scanner is used to scan the photographs. By means of a graphic tablet and stylus, a human operator selects ground reference points, delineates road boundaries, and may mark vehicles. The computer extrapolates the trajectories of vehicles to predict their positions in successive photographs. Their precise locations are then determined and recorded by applying pattern recognition techniques, matching the vehicle images in the current frame against their recorded images in the previous frame of photography.
Name: ["Raudseps Juris G."]

Title: SEQUENTIAL STRUCTURE AND PARAMETER ADAPTIVE PATTERN RECOGNITION - 1. SUPERVISED LEARNING.
Abstract: Recursive filters for supervised learning Bayes-optimal adaptive pattern recognition with continuous data are derived. Both off-line (or prior to actual operation) and on-line (while in operation) supervised learning is considered. The concept of structure adaptation is introduced and both structure as well as parameter adaptive optimal pattern recognition systems are obtained. Specifically, for the class of supervised learning pattern recognition problems with gaussian process models and linear dynamics, the adaptive pattern recognition systems are shown to be decomposable ( ‚Ä≥partition theorem‚Ä≥ ) into a linear, non-adaptive part consisting of recursive, matched Kalman filters, a nonlinear part - a set of probability computers - that incorporates the adaptive nature of the system, and finally a linear part of the correlator-estimator (Kailath) form.
Name: ["Lainiotis D.G."]

Title: A note on "axioms" for computational complexity and computation of finite functions
Abstract: Recent studies of computational complexity have focused on "axioms" which characterize the "difficulty of a computation" (Blum, 1967a or the measure of the "size of a program," (Blum, 1967b and Pager, 1969). In this paper we wish to carefully examine the consequences of hypothesizing a relation which connects measures of size and of difficulty of computation. The relation is motivated by the fact that computations are performed "a few instructions at a time" so that if one has a bound on the difficulty of a computation, one also has a bound on the "number of executed instructions." This relation enables one to easily show that algorithms exist for finding the most efficient programs for computing finite functions. This result, which has been obtained independently for certain Turing machine measures by David Pager, contrasts sharply with results for measures of size, where it is known that no algorithm can exist for going from a finite function to the shortest program for computing it (Blum, 1967b) (Pager, 1969). In a concluding section, which can be read independently of the above-mentioned results, some remarks are made about the desirability of using a program for computing an infinite function when one is interested in the function only on some finite domain. There is nothing deep in this paper, and we hope that a reader familiar with the rudiments of recursion theory will find this paper a simple introduction to the "axiomatic" theory of computational complexity. Such a reader might do well to begin with the concluding remarks after reading the basic definitions. ¬© 1972 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Young P.D."]

Title: Tabulator-turing machine and complexity | Tabulator-Turingmaschine und Komplexit√§t
Abstract: A new model of a Turing Machine, called "Tabulator Turing Machine", is defined. It can shift its head over several squares of the tape and is therefore more similar to a real computer than a normal Turing Machine. The complexity classes defined by this machine are different from those defined by a normal multitape Turing Machine.
