Abstract: Stability conditions of the orientation process in a rotating coordinate system are investigated. The kinematic problem of orientation is considered, assuming that control is effected by changing the angular velocity component of the coordinate system being oriented. Processes of positioning are investigated for the case where the orientation is achieved according to two control signals.

Title: ON THE APPLICATION OF DIVERGENCE TO FEATURE SELECTION IN PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The problem of feature selection in pattern recognition is viewed as that of mapping of vector samples from n-dimensional feature space to that in m-dimensional space (m less than n) by a linear transformation. A transformation matrix is obtained by maximizing the divergence between a pair of Gaussian distributed pattern classes.

Title: SYNTHESISING NETWORKS.
Abstract: The paper reports the development of an algorithm which can be used to synthesise networks between geometric points. The operation of the algorithm is detailed and its theoretical basis outlined. The use of the algorithm is illustrated by synthesizing different networks between one set of geometric points.

Abstract: The knnearest neighbor classification rule is a nonparametric classification ‚Äòprocedure that assigns a random vector Z to one of two populations œÄl,œÄ2. Samples of equal size n are taken from œÄl and œÄ2‚Äô and are ordered separately with respect to their distance from Z = z. This rule is equivalent to the Fix and Hodges, ‚Äúmajority rule‚Äù [4] or the nearest neighbor rule of Cover and Hart [3]. This paper studies some asymptotic properties of this rule including an expression for a consistent upper bound on the probability of misclassification. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.

Title: Der programmierbare endliche automat
Abstract: The paper deals with finite automata with two tapes, the second tape of which is interpreted as programme tape. For fixed automata those classes: of languages are considered, which can be accepted by variation of the programmes. The representation of all regular sets over some alphabet X by a fixed one-way automaton proves to be impossible. This problem has not yet been solved for automata with rewind instructions and two-way automata, which are strongly more powerful than one-way automata. ¬© 1972 Springer-Verlag.

Title: Automatic Correction of Linear Waveform Distortions in Television Systems. | [AUTOMATISCHE KORREKTUR LINEARER SIGNALVERZERRUNGEN IN FERNSEHSYSTEMEN.]
Abstract: A theoretical analysis of linear transmission distortions in the time domain is presented. General criteria are derived for the measurement of the distortions of a television channel using special test signals and for the project of a correction network. The automatic control of this network by means of a digital computer is analyzed and some theoretical points are discussed for the conception of such a system. Experimental results are included.
Name: ["Fasshauer Peter"]

Title: Observations on the Separability of Control and Estimation. | [UWAGI O ROZDZIELNOSCI STEROWANIA I ESTYMACJI.]
Abstract: An analysis of some questions concerning the theorem on the separability of control and estimation as given by Wonham has led to the following conclusions: 1) It is possible to replace the condition of non-singularity of the observer matrix, needed by the Wonham theorem, with the condition of uniform observability of a process model. 2) If the regularity conditions given in the theorem are satisfied, then in the case of a trajectory tracking the separation principle holds not only for closed-loop systems but also for closed-open-loop ones. 3) The separation property defined in the paper is equivalent to the neutrality of control with regard to estimation within the meaning of the Feldbaums's theorems on dual control. Under additional conditions a closed-loop system can be reduced to an open-loop one with continuous observation of disturbances.

Title: PERFORMANCE OF STOCHASTIC GMDH ALGORITHMS IN ACTUAL EXAMPLES.
Abstract: Some estimation methods are compared relative to the performance of pattern recognition algorithms. It is shown that a stochastic GMDH algorithm with a small number of data points is more efficient than algorithms of the method of potential functions.
Name: ["Patratiy I.Z.", "Shelud'ko O.I.", "Drobotya A.I."]

Title: Optimum Production Scheduling of Multicommodity in Flow Line
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The applications of computer control in production factories have been extended from the control of mass and energy to the production control. The control at this level comprises the formulation and alteration of work schedules in accordance with the progress of work, and it may be called the control of information. This paper deals with the flow line which is the most fundamental production line in the factory and proposes and verifies the optimal scheduling method. In the case of producing multicommodities by a flow line, the optimum schedule is the one which satisfies the demand for the respective products and minimizes the changeover loss. The branch-and-bound method is used to obtain an optimum schedule. The geometrical characteristics of the region in which the feasible schedules exist are used for calculating the lower bound of the objective function for the subset of feasible schedules. Title: A space-efficient list structure tracing algorithm
Abstract: An algorithm for tracing during garbage collection of list structure is presented. It requires only one bit for each level of doubly branching structure traced. Compared to existing trace algorithms, it generally requires less storage-often, substantially less. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Wegbreit B."]

Title: Optimal Planning of Experiments in Problems Involving Extrapolation to a Point. | OPTIMAL'NOE PLANIROVANIE EKSPERIMENTOV V ZADACHAKH EKSTRAPOLYATSII V TOCHKU.
Abstract: Two methods are proposed enablingone to obtain optimal extrapolation plans minimizing forecasting dispersion at a set point of parameter space which is inaccessible to direct measurements. The proposed algorithms of optimal planning do not impose any limitations on the functional form of the regression equations or the form of the planning space.
Name: ["Krug G.K.", "Sosulin Yu.A."]

Title: Adaptive short-term forecasting of hourly loads using weather information
Source: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
Abstract: A comprehensive computer-oriented procedure for probabilistic forecasting of hourly power-system loads with lead times of 1 to 24 hours is described. The forecasts produced are based on both historical load data and information from the latest weather forecast. The methodology combines stochastic load models and adaptive weather-load models optimally to yield an adaptive forecasting procedure especially suited for real-time control of power systems. Name: ["Gupta P.C.", "Yamada K."]

Title: MARTINGALE APPROACH TO LINEAR RECURSIVE STATE ESTIMATION.
Abstract: A new approach is presented to linear recursive estimation (Bucy-Kalman filtering) which we believe may be more elegant and satisfying than extant treatments. The main idea is to exploit the simplier problem of estimating one Martingale from another.
Name: ["Balakrishnan A.V."]

Title: An Improvement to an Algorithm for Computing Aircraft Reference Altitude
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: A recently developed algorithm which is being used to compute an aircraft reference altitude from air data inputs is accurate in a stationary column of air. However, pressure gradients in the atmosphere can introduce significant errors. An improvement (which corrects for pressure gradient errors) has been developed which is based on the equilibrium equation for the motion of the air mass in the presence of pressure gradients. Title: ON THE FLOW-SHOP SEQUENCING PROBLEM WITH NO WAIT IN PROCESS.
Abstract: The optimization problem of minimizing the completion time in flow-shop sequencing with an environment of no intermediate storage is considered. Application of this problem in computer systems is pointed out and techniques are developed to solve the problem.
Name: ["Reddi S.S.", "Ramamoorthy C.V."]

Title: Topical Subject: The Robot in Industry - Friend or Foe. | [DAS AKTUELLE THEMA: INDUSTRIE-ROBOTER - FEIND ODER HELFER?]
Abstract: A discussion with representatives of a well-known manufacturer of automation units and freely programmed industrial robots is based on technical details and is concerned with the possible applications and future developments. Nowadays, robots are used in industry for recurrent actions or for environments, dangerous for human beings. The trend is from stored programmes to what are known as autodidactic automatic machines.
Name: ["Breuer Edmond"]

Title: COMPUTER SCHEDULING OF VEHICLES FROM ONE OR MORE DEPOTS TO A NUMBER OF DELIVERY POINTS.
Abstract: The problem of scheduling delivery vehicles from a number of depots to customers, subject to constraints on load and distance or time, is considered. A new algorithm is presented; this allows routes from several depots to be constructed simultaneously, subject to restrictions on numbers of vehicles at individual depots. Where too many customers require service, a flexible priority rule will select those to be served. Results for the single depot case are compared with other known algorithms; further results are given and discussed for cases of several depots.
Name: ["Wren Anthony", "Holliday Alan"]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF SYNTHETIC ISOLATED VOWELS AND VOWELS IN H-D CONTEXT.
Abstract: This paper describes experiments in which various acoustic features of the h-d context were systematically eliminated in order to locate which parts of the consonants aid this more uniform identification. It is concluded that no one consonantal feature was responsible but that a spontaneous improvement in uniformity of identification occurs when several contextual features combine to achieve a new level of speech-likeness. This paper is concerned with a more detailed examination of the h-d context in an attempt to isolate characteristics which contribute most to the result of an earlier experiment.
Name: ["Millar J.B.", "Ainsworth W.A."]

Title: A versatile clustering algorithm with objective function and objective measure
Abstract: A computer program for nonparametric cluster synthesis, using similarity rather than maximum likelihood as the basis for class membership, is presented. The algorithm utilizes recursive computations to develop a hierarchy or tree of nested clusters. The major components of the program are: (1) a (dis)similarity function. (2) a grouping or merger strategy, based on optimizing a dynamic objective function, and (3) a halting criterion, based on evaluating a dynamic objective measure. Program options permit variations of data normalization, measures of similarity, and clustering strategy. A variety of hard-copy summaries and displays are available to the user. An illustrative application to the classification of human mitotic chromosomes is included. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Prewitt J.M.S."]

Title: A highly parallel algorithm for approximating all zeros of a polynomial with only real zeros
Abstract: An algorithm is described based on Newton's method which simultaneously approximates all zeros of a polynomial with only real zeros. The algorithm, which is conceptually suitable for parallel computation, determines its own starting values so that convergence to the zeros is guaranteed. Multiple zeros and their multiplicity are readily determined. At no point in the method is polynomial deflation used. ¬© 1972, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Patrick M.L."]
Keywords: ["guaranteed convergence", "newtons method", "parallel numerical algorithms", "real polynomials", "real zeros"]

Title: A flexible system for automatic generation of special purpose dichotomous keys, and its application to Australian grass genera
Abstract: The key-generating program KEYGEN has been incorporated in a flexible system whereby special purpose dichotomous keys can be produced rapidly and cheaply from a single data base. The system is applicable to any taxonomic group for which suitable observational data are available. It is currently being applied to Australian grass genera, for which data are now available on 274 attributes representing 120 aspects of leaf morphology and anatomy, inflorescence form, spikelet, flower, and fruit structure. Grass genera are being recorded for variation at world level so that the data can be used (and if necessary extended) in order to make keys for other regions. Examples are given of early efforts at ‚Äòconventional‚Äô and ‚Äòvegetative-anatomical‚Äô special purpose keys, generated from the data via the system described here. ¬© 1972 CSIRO. All Rights Reserved.
Name: ["Watson L.", "Milne P."]

Title: SEQUENTIAL METHOD SEEKING THE GLOBAL MAXIMUM OF A FUNCTION.
Abstract: The method is applicable to an objective function of a single variable defined on a closed interval and such that some bound on its rate of change is available. The method is shown to be minimax. computational aspects of the method are discussed.
Name: ["Shubert Bruno O."]

Title: Some New Techniques for Processing Remotely Obtained Images by Self-Generated Spectral Masks
Abstract: An extension of a new technique that enables parallel, simultaneous processing of remotely obtained images is presented. The technique holds out promise for automatic on-board classification of data. The central feature involves the generation of binary masks, directly from the image, based on object reflectance data, that groups objects into equivalence classes. These masks, called equivalence class masks, can be used in various logical combinations to isolate classes of objects with a priori known reflectance or radiance signatures. Experimental verification of the technique is furnished for simple scenes. A computational scheme, based on a sequence of integrated irradiance measurements on the image, that enables the identification of objects within an equivalence class is suggested. ¬© 1972 Optical Society of America.
Name: ["Stark H.", "Barker R.C.", "Lee D."]

Title: MINIMUM SEARCH TREE STRUCTURES FOR DATA PARTITIONED INTO PAGES.
Abstract: The doubly chained tree structure is an efficient device for organizing a file that must be searched and updated frequently. This paper considers a variation to the doubly chained tree which is more representative of a file in which the data is partitioned into blocks or pages. In this model the cost of searching the next node is 1 if the node is reachable from the same root (i. e. , on the same page), and is k if the next node is the next root (i. e. , on a different page). An algorithm for constructing doubly chained trees having any number of terminal nodes N, with minimal average search length, is developed. A simple closed expression is derived for the minimum average search time as a function of the number of terminal nodes N and the parameter k. A proof of optimality is included.
Name: ["Patt Yale N."]

Title: A manifold imbedding algorithm for optimization problems
Abstract: A manifold imbedding algorithm is described for the solution of two-point boundary value problems arising in optimization problems. A one-parameter imbedding of the initial and terminal manifolds is introduced so that a member of the resulting imbedded class of problems has an immediate solution. This problem is the first of a finite sequence of problems including the original one as last element. By a continuation procedure, these problems are successively solved. In contrast to a previous imbedding technique for solving two-point boundary value problems, the system equations are left unchanged. Intermediate problems therefore keep their physical meaning and the choice of a proper imbedding is easier. Moreover, a reduction of computation time is achieved. The manifold imbedding method may be regarded as a variation of the Newton-Raphson iterative procedure characterized by an extended region of convergence. The resulting reduction of guesswork and the unified approach to a wide range of optimization problems are amongst the favorable features. The minimization of the transfer time of a low-thrust ion rocket between the orbits of Earth and Mars illustrates the application of the method. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Hontoir Y.", "Cruz Jr. J.B."]

Title: Algorithms for Welding Data Computation and their Industrial Application. | ALGORITHMEN ZUR BERECHNUNG VON SCHWEISSDATEN UND IHRE ANWENDUNG IN DER INDUSTRIE.
Abstract: The various algorithms for computing parameters of several welding techniques are tabulated and analyzed. The conditions and fields of their practical applications are discussed.
Name: ["Blume Fritz", "Buder Gerd", "Schwarz Peter"]

Title: Some Applications of the Spectral-Radius Concept to Nonlinear Feedback Stability
Abstract: Several results are derived concerning the input-output stability of nonlinear time-varying feedback systems. These results all share the common feature that they are based on an application of the concept of the spectral radius of a bounded linear operator. Section I contains the preliminary notions, including that of the spectral radius. In Section II, bounds are obtained for the spectral radius of a Volterra integral operator, and these bounds are used to obtain sufficient conditions for the existence of an inverse operator for a type of nonlinear operator. This technique is applied to obtain stability regions for the Mathieu-Hill equation, in order to illustrate the fact that the method proposed here yields less conservative stability bounds than those obtained by standard contraction methods. In Section III, several results are proved regarding the existence of inverse operators for linear operators. In Section IV, the results of Section III are applied to the Lp-stability problem for linear time-varying systems. It is shown that, under certain conditions, the well-known circle criterion implies Lp-stability for all p, rather than just L2-stability. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Vidyasagar M."]

Title: A hybrid computer technique for detecting sharp EEG transients
Abstract: A technique is described which uses a hybrid computer system for the detection of waves in an EEG signal which are relatively sharper than the background activity. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Carrie J.R.G."]

Title: Nonlinear Autonomous Shift Registers as Variable Frequency Dividers. | [NICHTLINEARE AUTONOME SCHIEBEREGISTER ALS VARIABLE FREQUENZTEILER.]
Abstract: Nonlinear autonomous shift registers can also be used as variable frequency dividers for phase or frequency automatic control systems provided the divider ration is small. If derived from the theoretical bases of automatic machines sequences having a maximum length L can be generated by means of linear shift registers, as can reduced sequences by adding a non-linear complement in the return. Transformations of similarity and equivalences of structure still permit an economic design of shift registers with memory numbers n less than 8. A low-channel radio set serves as an example to explain the setup of such a divider for N equals (40 to 49).
Name: ["Klein H.J."]

Title: Controllability of sequential machines
Abstract: A sequential machine is said to be k-controllable if there exists a minimum integer k such that every state transition can be achieved by an input sequence of length k. In this paper properties of controllable sequential machines are discussed. The main results are as follows: (1) An efficient procedure for controllability test is given. (2) It is shown that every uncontrollable strongly connected machine has an autonomous component machine. (3) The upper bound of k in a controllable machine containing a loop of length l is given. (4) The upper and lower bounds of k in k-controllable machines are shown. (5) It is shown that any sequential machine can be realized by a controllable or uncontrollable machine. ¬© 1972 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Kambayashi Y.", "Yajima S."]

Title: Linear Sequential Pattern Classification
Abstract: A nonparametric sequential pathyutern classifier called a linear sequential classifier (LSC) is presented. The pattern_components are measured sequentially and the decisions either to measure the next component or to stop and classify the pattern are made using linear functions derived from sample patterns based on the least mean-square error criterion. The required linear functions are computed using an adaptlon of GrevilJe's recursive algorithm for computing the generalized inverse of a matrix. A recursive algorithm for computing the least mean-square error is given and is used to determine the order in which the pattern components are measured. Under the assumption of two equiprobable classes that are normally distributed with equal covariance matrices, it is shown that the LSC is equivalent to Wald's sequential probability ratio test. Computer-simulated experiments indicate that the LSC is more effective than existing nonparametric sequential classifiers. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Smith S.E.", "Yau S.S."]

Title: Application of Optimum Error-Reject Functions
Abstract: In an optimum pattern-recognition system the error rate is determined by the reject function. This correspondence describes how this property may be exploited to provide quantitative tests of model validity using unclassified test samples. These tests are basically goodness-of-fit tests for a function of the observations. One of these tests is shown to provide an improved estimate of error in Monte Carlo studies of complex systems. Results are given for normal distributions when parameters are estimated. In this case error estimates obtained from the empirical reject rate underestimate the actual error and performance depends on the ratio of design samples to dimension. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Fukunaga K.", "Kessell D.L."]

Title: AUTOMATIC ELECTROCARDIOGRAM INTERPRETATION SYSTEM.
Abstract: A new system automatically analyzes an electrocardiogram (ECG) acquired through an electrocardiograph online controlled by a computer. The electrocardiograph incorporates switches for patient identification and programmed control; the computer accomplishes ECG analysis while doing other work.
Name: ["Shibata Sadayasu", "Egashira Yoshinobu", "Katayama Tomoyuki"]

Title: METHOD FOR AIDING HUMAN OPERATOR PERFORMANCE IN A NONCOMPENSATORY TRACKING TASK.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The method involves the display of information to the operator about his performance as compared with an automatic optimal controller performing the same task. Only a computer simulation of the automatic system is required. The method is applied to a simulated vehicle-following experiment and the results show that the method enables the human operator to perform effectively by providing him with an optimal reference. 10 refs.
Name: ["Gourishankar V.", "Peppard L.E."]

Title: Robust Estimation of Signal Amplitude
Abstract: An iterative estimation procedure involving the use of a light limiter is proposed for obtaining robust estimates of the amplitude of a signal of known form in additive nearly Gaussian noise. In the case of a constant signal the procedure, referred to as the iterative limiter estimator (ILE), is exhibited as a form of stochastic approximation and the procedure is shown to be robust in a well-defined asymptotically min-max sense. The ILE is also shown to be asymptotically robust in terms of efficiency relative to the sample mean. In the case of a time-varying signal the procedure is referred to as an iterative limiter‚Äîcorrelator estimator (ILCE). Simulation results show that both the ILE and the ILCE possess a high degree of robustness for seemingly. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Martin R.D."]

Title: SUBOPTIMAL AND NEAR-OPTIMAL CONTROL OF LOAD-FREQUENCY-CONTROL SYSTEM.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: A method of reduction in the computation for multiarea load-frequency-control systems is considered using the method of aggregation due to M. Aoki. In the case of the nonobservability of some of the states, an observer is constructed, and a controller that is almost an optimal controller is obtained.
Name: ["Moorthi V.R.", "Aggarwal R.P."]

Title: COMPILE-TIME ERROR DIAGNOSTICS IN SYNTAX-DIRECTED COMPILERS.
Abstract: This paper has shown the feasibility of formally specifying compile-time error diagnostics in the grammar of a programming language, and the extent to which the positioning of these messages can be done automatically. This process is easy for a particular class of grammars (LF), but although this class of grammars is large, it appears to be impossible to write some of the more common programming languages into this form directly, though it can be done by relegating some syntactic distinctions to the semantic analysis. However, the general principles outlined can probably be extended to other classes of grammars with suitable criteria chosen for the error message insertion algorithm.
Name: ["Burgess C.J."]

Title: Suboptimal feedback control of a distributed linear regulator with control and observation structure constraints‚Ä†
Abstract: The problem of feedback control of a linear distributed parameter system with quadratic cost where the number of control and measurement locations is finite is considered. An average cost is used to reduce the sensitivity to changes in initial conditions. A suboptimal scheme is developed to evaluate the feedback coefficients. Two examples arc solved where the feedback coefficients are evaluated in a piecewise constant form using the matrix Maximum Principle and matrix gradient. ¬© 1972 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Bhagavan B.K.", "Nardizzi L.R."]
Affiliations: ['Information and Control Sciences Center SMD Institute of Technology']

Title: On the Application of Sensitivity Methods for Parameter Optimization and Identification. | [UEBER DIE BENUTZUNG VON EMPFINDLICHKEITSMETHODEN ZUR PARAMETEROPTIMIERUNG UND PARAMETERIDENTIFIKATION.]
Abstract: Unknown parameters and initial conditions of a system of nonlinear differential equations are determined by extremizing a given criterion. Problems of this class occur also in parameter optimization and identification. The problem can be reduced to the solution of linear algebraic equations by calculation of sensitivity functions. Depending on the criterion to be optimized the system of linear equations can be solved directly or treated by methods of linear or nonlinear optimization. The solution of the system of linear equations is a measure for the improvement of the unknown parameters and initial conditions. The procedure is explained by two practical examples.
Name: ["Paul W."]

Title: Optimal control of linear stochastic systems described by functional differential equations
Source: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
Abstract: The optimal control is determined for a class of systems by assuming the configuration of the feedback loop. The feedback loop consists of an unbiased estimator and controller. The gain matrices of the estimator and the controller are so determined that the mean-squared estimation error and the average value of a quadratic cost functional, respectively, are minimized. This is accomplished by the application of the matrix maximum principle to a distributed parameter system. The results indicate that the optimal estimation and the optimal control can be computed independently (separation principle). ¬© 1972 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Koivo A.J."]

Title: On Variable-Length-to-Block Coding
Abstract: Variable-length-to-block codes are a generalization of run. length codes. A coding theorem is first proved. When the codes are used to transmit information from fixed-rate sources through fixed-rate noiseless channels, buffer overflow results. The latter phenomenon is an important consideration in the retrieval of compressed data from storage. The probability of buffer overflow decreases exponentially with buffer length and we determine the relation between rate and exponent size for memoryless sources. We obtain codes that maximize the overflow exponent for any given transmission rate exceeding the source entropy and present asymptotically optimal coding algorithms whose complexity grows linearly with codeword length. It turns out that the optimum error exponents of variable-length-to-block coding are identical with those of block-to-variable-length coding and are related in an interesting way to Renyi's generalized entropy function. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Jelinek F.", "Schneider K.S."]

Title: Modular Networks and Nondeterministic Sequential Machines
Abstract: The synthesis of sequential machines by interconnections of copies of a fixed module is considered. A family of modules Mr,p for positive integers r and pr is defined. Mr,p can be used to synthesize sequential machines with 2P input symbols. A nondeterministic sequential machine (NSM) is said to be r-bounded if it has one initial state and for no state and input are there more than r choices for the next state. It is shown that the problem of finding a network of modules Mr,prealizing a given event E is equivalent to finding an r-bounded NSM realizing the reverse of E. As a consequence, two upper bounds on the number of copies of the module Mr,p necessary to realize an event E can be shown. 1) If E is defined by an n-state NSM, then E is defined by a network of at most cln2+p logr2 copies of Mr,p 2) If E is defined by an n-state deterministic sequential machine, then E is defined by a network of at most c2nl+v logr2 copies of Mr,p. cl and C2 are constants, about 4. Title: Generalization of Synthesis to Finite Settling Time - 1, 2. | VERALLGEMEINERUNG DES ENTWURFS AUF ENDLICHE EINSTELLZEIT - 1, 2.
Abstract: Control algorithms for sampled data systems are proposed and investigated. These algorithms result from known ones by replacing the requirement of adjusting all state variables of the n-th order system in n steps by the requirement to adjust only m less than n state variables in m less than n steps. The first m components of the state vector of the system transformed to the observable canonical form are chosen as corresponding state variables. It is demonstrated for a special plant that the proposed algorithms can show for special m less than n the same behavior, with respect to the control variable, of a synthesis to finite settling time. Additionally these algorithms avoid certain disadvantages, e. g. control variables too large in magnitude. One can guess that in general all plants with zeros in the actuator transfer function have this advantage.
Name: ["Preusche G."]

Title: COMPUTER-CONTROLLED QUEUING SYSTEM WITH SERVICE INTERRUPTIONS.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: A computer-controlled queuing system with Poisson input, first-come-first-served queue discipline and multiple-exponential servers that are subject to breakdowns and repairs is described. A generating function for the state probabilities of the system and a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of statistical equilibrium for the system are derived. A formula for the determination of the first waiting-time distribution in the system is obtained by the use of the theory of Markov chains.
Name: ["Chan W.C.", "Chung W.K."]

Title: IN-CORE FUEL MANAGEMENT OPTIMIZATION BY HEURISTIC LEARNING TECHNIQUE.
Abstract: The optimization of the multistage refueling decision process was studied by the heuristic approach for four-region batch refueling including shuffling. The final criterion, the average discharge burnup at the end of the whole reactor life can be regarded as a function of the weight and is maximized in the weight space by the hill climbing algorithm. A numerical simulation is given, and the maximum burnup, the refueling scheme, and the optimal weight are discussed in relation to the power-peaking factor constraint. Though the method is not guaranteed as for the optimality, reasonable solutions are obtained and the intuitive understanding of the process is possible by discussing the optimum weight of each rule.
Name: ["Hoshino Tsutomu"]

Title: Feedback control of stochastic systems with a generalized performance index
Abstract: The feedback control of a class of linear systems disturbed by additive white noise is considered. A linear control law is used to minimize a non-quadratic integral performance criterion. The stochastic problem is transformed to a deterministic problem, and a solution is developed using the calculus of variations. ¬© 1972 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Sims C.S.", "Rhoten R.P.", "Mulholland R.J."]

Title: CURVE FITTING WITH PIECEWISE-LINEAR FUNCTIONS.
Source: Proc Inst Radio Electron Eng Australia
Abstract: A method for finding an optimal piecewise-linear approximation to a specified function has been described in a recent paper. The method employs an evolutionary random search technique as one of the minimization steps. A new method is described which converges more rapidly than the random search algorithm. The method utilizes a simple, adaptive, steepest descent algorithm. Furthermore, it is shown that the gradient required in the new algorithm can be easily evaluated.
Name: ["Cantoni A."]

Title: A pseudo Newton-Raphson method for function minimization
Source: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
Abstract: A pseudo Newton-Raphson algorithm for function minimization is presented. As in all such algorithms, an estimate of the inverse Hessian is calculated. In this case, the estimate is of the form XZX<sup>T</sup>, where Z is a diagonal matrix; and this feature permits the use of the simple procedures to maintain the positive definiteness of Z, and hence of the restriction of XZX<sup>T</sup> to the range of X. The algorithm is shown to have finite convergence for quadratic functions and asymptotic convergence for a fairly general class of functions. Some numerical results are presented, and the extension of the algorithm to deal with linear equality and inequality constraints is briefly discussed. ¬© 1972 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Mamen R.", "Mayne D.Q."]
Affiliations: ['Communication Research Council', ' Imperial College of Science and Technology']

Title: Compatible Controllers for Time-varying Linear Plants
Abstract: Problems relating to the optimal control of linear systems with quadratic cost invariably lead to analytic solutions requiring complete state feedback for their implementation. It is often the case in actual practice, however, that only a subset of the entire state vector can be measured. In such cases, one approach is to construct an estimator of the complete state via dynamic feedback elements, whose output is then used to construct a control that asymptotically approaches the optimum. A more general compatible controller theory, described here for optimizing time-varying linear plants, can often be implemented with less complexity than that required of observers or Kalman filter type designs. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Rothschild D.S.", "Grammaticos A.J."]
Affiliations: ['Research Department Grumman Aerospace Corp.', 'Department of Electrical Engineering New York University']

Title: LONGITUDINAL REFERENCE SIGNAL GENERATION FOR AUTOMATIC-VEHICLE CONTROL.
Abstract: A method of reference signal generation for synchronous longitudinal control of automatic vehicles is presented. The principles of operation are given along with some preliminary experimental results which indicate that the technique should be usable on existing roadways.
Name: ["Mayhan R.J.", "Brinner T.R.", "Olson K.W."]

Title: Fault Isolation via Components Simulation
Abstract: The problem of deducing the internal component parameters from external measurements of a large-scale system is studied in the context of the fault isolation problem. By assuming an appropriate algebraic connection model matrix, algebraic necessary and sufficient conditions for the exact determination of the internal component parameters are obtained for both the single-test frequency and multiple-test frequency cases. In both cases the linear independence of the rows or columns of certain matrices may be used to determine appropriate test points and test frequencies. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Saeks R.", "Singh S.P.", "Liu R.-W."]

Title: Comments on ‚ÄúA Stochastic Approximation Method‚Äù
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The results stated in the above paper1 concerning an approved stochastic approximation method are considered. Formulas for the variances of the estimates are derived, and it is found that, in fact, the new algorithm is inferior to previously suggested ones. Name: ["Ljung L."]

Title: Normal and Emergency Control of a String of Vehicles by Fixed Reference Sampled-Data Control
Abstract: A fixed reference control scheme for automated highways is proposed. Each vehicle controls itself; thus multiloop feedback is avoided. A Simple proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller is selected from many alternatives. For emergency stopping, a PI controller using a tachometer on a braked wheel can bring a vehicle with rubber tires to a controlled skid-free stop. Title: EFFECTIVENESS OF CERTAIN EASILY REALIZABLE RANK ALGORITHMS FOR DETECTIONS OF SIGNALS AGAINST A BACKGROUND OF NOISE.
