Name: ["Osman M.Y."]

Title: Optimal stabilization of a multi-machine system
Source: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
Abstract: The optimal linear regulator design technique of determining the weighting matrix Q with dominant eigenvalue shift, developed in a companion paper [6], is applied to the optimal stabilization of a multi-machine system. Two cases are studied, the first is with one optimal controller uEI on one machine of the m-machine system and the other with m optimal controllers uEM for the m-machine system. For comparison a one optimal controller uE on one machine with the rest approximated as an infinite system and m optimal controllers of individual design are also investigated. Nonlinear tests are given. It is found that uEI control is better than uE control, uEM control is better still than uEI control, and individual uE controllers are not good for the overall system. Although multi-machine formulations are available [1‚Äì3, 7], a new one is given in this paper aiming at the reduction of number of matrix inversions and to keep them in low order. All system parameters are retained in the final results which is important to system parameter sensitivity studies. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Yu Y.-N.", "Moussa H.A.M."]

Title: Derivation of weighting matrices towards satisfying eigenvalue requirements
Abstract: The present work is concerned with the problem of designing appropriate weighting matrices for the performance index of the linear regulator optimization problem, guch that the resulting optimal policy satisfies given eigenvalue requirements. The text provides an algorithm for deriving a diagonal state-weighting matrix according to these eigenvalue requirements, the latter often being better defined than the requirements for the stato-weighting matrix. The solution given employs matrix differential calculus and a static gradient minimization sub-routine to minimize an eigenvalue error criterion, thus facilitating optimal control within desired eigenvalue requirements. ¬© 1972 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Gbaupe D."]

Title: Signal Classification Through Quasi-Singular Detection With Applications in Mechanical Fault Diagnosis
Abstract: This paper deals with the classification of signals in terms of their autocorrelation functions. For each of two classes the eigenfunctions of the autocorrelation function are found, and a proper subset of each one is chosen. An unknown signal is classified by comparing the norms of its projections on the two subsets of eigenfunctions. By working with the eigenfunctions corresponding to the smallest eigenvalues, the method approximates singular detection. An application of this technique is shown for the classification of engine-vibration records as a basis for automatic mechanical fault diagnosis. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Fang G.-S.", "Pavlidis T."]

Title: Model reduction for discrete-time dynamic systems
Abstract: The model reduction techniques of Marshall and Davison for linear continuous-time models are extended for use in reducing the order of linear discrete-time models. Two approaches for the reduction of high-order continuous-time models to low-order discrete-time models are presented and evaluated. The resulting reduced order discrete-time models obtained by the two approaches are shown to be equivalent. A simple numerical example is solved to demonstrate the techniques presented. ¬© 1972 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Wilson R.G.", "Fisher D.G.", "Seboeg D.E."]

Title: SEMI-AUTOMATED COMPUTER FINGERPRINT ENCODING AND MATCHING SYSTEM.
Source: Ky Univ, Off Res Eng Serv, Bull UKY BU102. Carnahan Conf on Electron Crime Countermeas, Proc
Abstract: The results of this study provide practical information that may be used in the selection of additional fingerprint descriptors in a fingerprit identification research and retrieval system. The results showing the types of descriptors that are generally usable, the effects of differences due to fingerprint ridge pattern types and the data on multiple finger matching systems may be applied to the design and development or selection of most types of fingerprint identification systems.
Name: ["Solosko Robert B.", "Paley James J."]

Title: PENALTY-FUNCTION PERFORMANCE OF SEVERAL UNCONSTRAINED-MINIMIZATION TECHNIQUES.
Abstract: Three unconstrained-minimization techniques: a non-gradient method, a variable-metric method, and a variant of Newton's method, are employed with five linear-search methods to solve a number of unconstrained-minimization problems, and a number of well-known constrained-minimizatIon problems via a penalty-function approach. A comparison of these methods is made with two different performance criteria: the number of equivalent function evaluations and the execution time on a certain computer. Computational experience has been obtained to answer the question of whether resetting options should be used in a variable-metric method. The execution time as measure of performance is considered.
Name: ["Lootsma F.A."]

Title: Computer Simulation of After-Inhibition in Crayfish Slowly Adapting Stretch Receptor Neuron
Abstract: A theoretical model is described which is able to mimic the responses of slowly adapting stretch receptor neurons of crayfish to applied currents. Its principal feature is postspike inhibition, in which each nerve impulses produces a small inhibitory current that decays with a simple exponential time-course that is long compared with normal interspike intervals. The model was simulated with both an analogue and a digital computer. Parameters for particular model neurons were determined both by an analysis of experimental data obtained from adaptation to constant injected currents, and by matching computer output to the data. Parameter values estimated by the two techniques agreed within ¬±10%. Model parameters determined from adaptation data successfully predicted the magnitude and time-course of posttetanic hyperpolarization (PTH) in the stretch receptor neuron. In addition, model neurons were able to reproduce posttetanic depression (PTD) as seen in stretch receptor cells. ¬© 1972, The Biophysical Society. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Sokolove P.G."]

Title: Adaptive Method of Approximation of Probability Densities by Using Moments. | [EIN ADAPTIVES WAHRSCHEINLICHKEITSDICHTE-APPROXIMATIONSVERFAHREN MIT MOMENTEN.]
Abstract: Series expansions for the approximate representation of a priori unknown non-Gaussian probability densities of stochastic variables, e. g. control variables are employed. The coefficients of these series expansions are formed by measurable characteristic quantities, i. e. moments. The known expansions of Gram-Charlier and Edgeworth which depend strongly on Gaussian distributions give satisfactory solutions only in the case of distributions similar to the Gaussian. Therefore, the author proposes matched series-expansions which are based on the five solutions of the Pearson differential equation that can be modified by parameters. So these expansions are chosen by means of the first four moments. By this method approximation is extended from series which are similar to Gaussian distributions to classes of probability densities which are similar to Pearson solutions.
Name: ["Kuehl B."]

Title: SPEAKER VERIFICATION: A STEP TOWARD THE ‚Ä≥CHECKLESS‚Ä≥ SOCIETY.
Abstract: By analyzing and comparing voice characteristics, a computer can verify the identity of a telephone caller with reasonable accuracy. This paves the way for such services as banking, charge purchases, and access to confidential information by telephone.
Name: ["Lummis Robert C."]

Title: A Theoretical Neural Integrator
Abstract: A neural network model is introduced which approximates the behavior of an integrator. It is developed from cells that are physiologically realistic. Requirements for insensitivity of network function to cell threshold distribution are derived, and network performance as the forward-path element of a neuromuscular control system is analyzed. The response of the ‚Äúintegrator‚Äù to sustained inputs is derived and shown to approximate the desired proportionality of input magnitude and rate of change of output. Finally, deviations from physiological realism are discussed and the visual accommodation system is described as an example of a biological servomechanism in which a neural integrator seems probable. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Rosen M.J."]

Title: RISK OF ESTIMATION BY DATA OBTAINED VIA COMMUNICATION CHANNEL.
Abstract: In a remote-control system including a communication channel, a new limitation on the capabilities of the control system is imposed by the capacity of the communication channel. A discussion is given, assuming static observations through a communication channel with a given channel capacity, of the coding system which minimizes the risk of estimation and reducing the problem of coding to the problem of determining the joint probability distribution of the information source and the observation space, a general fundamental equation is derived for the optimum joint probability distribution, assuming a loss function of quadratic type. A solution of this equation can be given for the case where the information source is Gaussian and a linear method is used for the estimation. The result has revealed that for smaller channel capacities, it is wiser not to transmit those costates which are not important from the viewpoint of the loss function.
Name: ["Ando Kazuaki", "Araki Mituhiko", "Kondo Bunji"]

Title: PROCESS INTERRUPT ALGORITHM.
Abstract: This algorithm allows category specification by bit position for each input signal, so that determination of whether or not the interrupt resulted from an input transition that is of significance may be made rapidly in a common routine.
Name: ["Nagel D.M."]

Title: RECURSIVE METHODS IN PHOTOGRAMMETRIC DATA REDUCTION.
Abstract: An attempt has been made to deal with sequential data reduction problems as they arise in computational photogrammetry. Continuing earlier efforts, an algorithm suitable for cases where the size of the normal equations changes, has been formulated and tested. Also, test results are given to compare times used for sequential solutions compared to batch solutions indicating a cutoff point. Finally, a discussion of the sequential process and nonlinear mathematical models points out the complexity of the problem. A possible scheme is given which, while not exact, yielded quite close results to the exact solution.
Name: ["Mikhail Edward M.", "Helmering Raymond J."]

Title: Computer Model of the Formation of Self‚ÄêOrganizing Systems
Source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English
Abstract: A model of a simple self‚Äêorganizing system is investigated. Mechanisms that are important to a molecular‚Äêbiological understanding of evolution are studied with the aid of the model. Copyright ¬© 1972 by Verlag Chemie, GmbH, Germany
Name: ["F√∂rsterling H.‚ÄêD.", "Kuhn H.", "Tews K.‚ÄêH."]
Affiliations: ['Physikalisch-chemisches Institut der Universit√§t', 'Max-Planck-Institut f√ºr Biophysikalische Chemie']

Title: Spontaneous behaviour in neural networks
Abstract: We set up a general theory of neural networks in which each neuron is treated realistically as a noise generator due to'the spontaneous emission of packets of transmitter substance at the synapses it makes with other neurons. This description allows the time development of firing probabilities, either for single neurons or those composing a net, to be obtained. This is simplest in discrete time, though is still possible in continuous time. The deterministic limit of the discrete time development is obtained and shown to agree with the decision equations of Caianiello. We conclude by some considerations on the importance of spontaneous firing in animal behaviour after introduction of a parameter, called the spontaneity parameter, helpful in describing the amount of spontaneous behaviour of a neuron or net of them. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Taylor J.G."]

Title: A New Approach to Automatic Scanning of Contour Maps
Abstract: The problem of automatic digitizing of contour maps is discussed. The structure of a general contour map is analyzed, and its topological properties are utilized in developing a new scanning algorithm. The problem of detection and recognition of contour lines is solved by a two color labeling method. It is shown that for maps containing normal contour lines only, it suffices to distinguish between so-called ‚Äúeven‚Äù and ‚Äúodd‚Äù lines. The ‚Äútangency problem‚Äù involved in practical scanning is discussed, and a solution based on minimizing computer memory space and simplifying control program is suggested. ¬© 1972, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Mor M.", "Lamdan T."]
Affiliations: ['Israeli Ministry of Defense', 'Weizmann Institute of Science']

Title: ONE-SIDED CONTEXT-SENSITIVE GRAMMARS.
Abstract: This paper defines a restricted context-sensitive grammar, namely a one-sided context-sensitive grammar whose rules are all of the form Av yields uv, u does not equal epsilon , and examines its characteristics. It is found that (i) for any one-sided context-sensitive grammar there exists an equivalent one-sided context-sensitive grammar having a rewriting rule A yields a, A yields BC, or AX yields BX; (ii) the family of one-sided context-sensitive languages properly contains the family of context-free languages and is contained in the family of context-sensitive languages; (iii) the family of one-sided context-sensitive languages is an AFL; (iv) the family of languages generated by the programmed one-sided context-sensitive grammar is identical with the family of context-sensitive languages.
Name: ["Ito Hidenori", "Inagaki Yasuyoshi", "Fukumura Teruo"]

Title: LOW-DIMENSIONAL ESTIMATOR FOR A FINITE-DIMENSIONAL LINEAR TIME-VARYING SYSTEM.
Abstract: A finite-dimensional linear time-varying plant is considered, which is described by the state equations dx(t)/dt equals A(t)X(t) plus B(t)u(t) and Y(t) equals C(t)X(t) plus D(t)u(t). The construction of the deterministic state estimator for this plant is discussed. An estimator is proposed whose dimension is smaller by m than the given plant, provided that the mxn matrix C(t) has a rank C(t) equals m for all t. A salient result is as follows: under the assumption that A(t) is continuously differentiable and C(t) is twice continuously differentiable, the plant state can be estimated using the estimator with reduced dimension which can eliminate the estimation error if and only if the plant is completely observable.
Name: ["Sasano Yoshiro", "Ikeda Masao"]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF FAULT-DIAGNOSABLE LOGICAL CIRCUITS.
Abstract: A method is proposed for computer synthesis of fault-diagnosable logic circuits. The optimal circuit is synthesized on the basis of logical functions defined as a set of independent variables. This synthesis method is, if slightly modified, applicable to logical functions containing forbidden minterms. This method is also applicable to the synthesis of multioutput functions and the realization of sequential circuits.
Name: ["Yamamoto Masaru"]

Title: PROPERTIES OF CONTEXT-SENSITIVE TREE AUTOMATA AND CHARACTERIZATION OF DERIVATION TREES OF CONTEXT-SENSITIVE GRAMMARS.
Abstract: As an extended concept of tree automata, context-sensitive tree automaton is defined. The class of languages acceptable by context-sensitive tree automata is considered and its closure properties are investigated. A modified context-sensitive grammar which has a language-generating capability equivalent to the usual context-sensitive grammar is defined and a derivation tree in the modified context-sensitive grammar is defined in terms of the derivation diagram in that grammar. The set of derivation trees of a modified context-sensitive grammar is characterized in terms of a context-sensitive tree automaton and a mapping called a projection. It is proved that the class of the sets of trees which are acceptable to context-sensitive tree automata is properly contained in the class of inductive sets and includes the class of the sets of trees which are acceptable to tree automata as a proper subclass.
Name: ["Kojima Masaaki", "Honda Namio"]

Title: Mathematical properties of responses of a neuron model - A system as a rational number generator
Abstract: Recently, Nagumo and Sato proposed a mathematical neuron model in the form of a nonlinear difference equation and investigated its response characteristic. The result showed that the input-output relationship of the neuron model is quite complicated and takes the form of an extended Cantor's function. It also explained the "unusual and unsuspected" phenomenon found by Harmon in experimental studies with his transistor neuron model. - In this paper, a fraction representation of a sequence of pulses is proposed. A mathematical treatment of the same neuron model based on the representation gives the same result as in the previous paper. Moreover, many mathematical properties, including the one where the ratio of the number of 1's contained in a cycle of a sequence to the length of the cycle gives any rational number between 0 and 1, were obtained by investigating sequences generated by the model. ¬© 1972 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Sato S."]

Title: EEG correlates of attention in humans
Abstract: An attempt is made in this report to extend the Bremner attention model to human EEG data. Data are present which show changes predicted by the expectancy subset originally defined by animal EEG data. An additional subset, internal focus, is proposed and partially supported by changes in human EEG. It is suggested that this subset is unique to humans. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Bremner F.J.", "Moritz F.", "Benignus V."]

Title: Image replicator
Abstract: The design, operation, alignment and the experimental tests on a prototype of a multiple-objective projection system, by means of which many identical, strictly coordinated images can be obtained at one time are described.
Name: ["Grammatin A.P.", "Dukhopel I.I.", "Ivanov M.A.", "Ivanov A.V."]

Title: A Measure of Computational Work
Abstract: The computational work of a process is measured in terms of the information in a memory for its table-lookup implementation. This measure is applied first to simple logical and arithmetic processes, and then more complicated processes comprising organizations (called synergisms) of several subprocesses. The computational advantages of Cartesian, compositional, and sequential synergisms are investigated and illustrated by means of the work measure. The relation between the work of a process and the work capacity of a facility on which it is implemented is examined, and a concept of efficiency of implementations is formulated. A few areas for further investigation are outlined. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hellerman L."]

Title: DIGITAL CODINGS OF MULTI-DIMENSIONAL INFORMATION SOURCES AND APPLICATIONS TO IMAGE CODING.
Abstract: It is noted that linear-transformation coding and multidimensional predictive coding are available as efficient methods for digital encoding of multi-dimensional information sources, such as still pictures and moving pictures. The decomposition of multi-dimensional coding into one-dimensional codings is considered as a method of reducing the complexity of multidimensional coding, and a procedure for optimal design of such coding system is given. It is shown that the maximum attainable redundancy reduction can be realized by this method. As an example of multi-dimensional sources, homogeneous isotropic still pictures are treated.
Name: ["Nitadori Kazuhiko"]

Title: Considerations of Sample and Feature Size
Abstract: In many practical pattern-classification problems the underlying probability distributions are not completely known. Consequently, the classification logic must be determined on the basis of vector samples gathered for each class. Although it is common knowledge that the error rate on the design set is a biased estimate of the true error rate of the classifier, the amount of bias as a function of sample size per class and feature size has been an open question. In this paper, the design-set error rate for a two-class problem with multivariate normal. distributions is derived as a function of the sample size per class (N) and dimensionality (L). The design-set error rate is compared to both the corresponding Bayes error rate and the test-set error rate. It is demonstrated that the design-set error rate is an extremely biased estimate of either the Bayes or test-set error rate if the ratio of samples per class to dimensions (N/ L) is less than three. Also the variance of the design-set error rate is approximated by a function that is bounded by 1/8N. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Foley D.H."]

Title: ON PROPERTIES OF THRESHOLD NETWORKS.
Abstract: This paper discusses the problem of realization of a logical function by a threshold network composed of a regular arrangement of elements. Any logical function can be regarded, for a suitably given weight vector, as a multiple threshold function with various threshold values, and this paper discusses network realization from the viewpoint of multiple threshold functions. The discussion is mostly concentrated on the cascade, two-level, and hybrid networks in which elements have the same weight vector and adjustable coupling coefficients between the threshold and the element.
Name: ["Imamiya Atsumi", "Noguchi Shoichi", "Oizumi Juro"]

Title: An adaptive random search algorithm for constrained minimization
Abstract: The well-known pattern search method has been randomized by Lawrence and Steiglitz [4] in order to augment its ability to adapt to direction. In this note we introduce other refinements in order to make it more adaptive in step size, and the use of penalty terms is incorporated as so to accommodate constraints. This yields an algorithm that appears to be robust and reliable, as verified by numerical experimentation. Moreover, the method has low storage requirements and is insensitive to the initial choice of a search radius. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Beltrami E.J.", "Indusi J.P."]

Title: NEARLY OPTIMAL INSPECTION POLICY.
Abstract: This paper concerned with an easily computable inspection policy for the detection of the failure of a system. A one-parameter policy is suggested and it is shown that this policy has the property of decreasing (increasing) intervals between successive inspection times if the system has an increasing (decreasing) failure rate. Cost comparisons, using linear cost functions, with a computationally difficult optimal policy which has a minimum expected cost show that the proposed policy compares quite well with the optimal policy.
Name: ["Munford A.G.", "Shahani A.K."]

Title: Uniform Linear Prediction of Bandlimited Processes From Past Samples
Abstract: For x(t) either a deterministic or stochastic signal band- limited to the normalized frequency interval |œâ| ‚â§ œÄ, explicit coefficients {akn} are exhibited that have the property that in an appropriate norm and for any constant intersample spacing T satisfying 0 < T < 1/2; that is, x(t) may be approximated arbitrarily well by a linear combination of past samples taken at any constant rate that exceeds twice the associated Nyquist rate. Moreover, the approximation of x(t) is uniform in the sense that the coefficients {akn} do not depend on the detailed structure of x(t) but are absolute constants for any choice of T. The coefficients that are obtained provide a sharpening of a previous result by Wainstein and Zubakov where a rate in excess of three times the Nyquist rate was required. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Brown J.L."]

Title: Error Probability in Dependent Pattern Classification
Abstract: This correspondence derives an upper bound on the probability of error of the m -class Bayes decision process when the patterns observed have first-order stochastic dependence. The bound is derived by applying an information-theoretic approach in which both the equivocation and the Bhattacharyya coefficient play a role. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Forsyth J.J."]

Abstract: Following is a continuation of the list of titles and authors: Survey of Adaptive Control Using Liapunov Design. By D. P. Lindorff and Robert L. Carroll. Title: Identification of Weighting Function Using Deterministic Input
Abstract: In this paper, a procedure for identifying the weighting function of a system is proposed. The procedure uses a new type of criterion involving a priori information about the weighting function as well as the integral of the squared response error. The optimal weighting function applied in - this criterion can be determined by solving the optimal tracking problem, provided that the output of a linear, free dynamical system is supplied to the plant as an input. The criterion function is also valid from the estimation theory. The computational algorithm of the procedure is presented herein. Numerical computations of several examples have shown that the proposed procedure gives satisfactory results even for the short-time observed data. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Furuta K.", "Ha J.-S."]
Affiliations: [' Tokyo Institute of Technology', ' R.O.K. Merchant Marine College']

Title: SEQUENTIAL GRADIENT-RESTORATION ALGORITHM FOR OPTIMAL CONTROL PROBLEMS WITH BOUNDED STATE VARIABLES - 1, 2.
Abstract: An algorithm for minimizing a functional subject to various constraints is presented. The problem considered was to find the state x(t), the control u(t), and the parameter pi so that the functional is minimized, while the constraints are satisfied to a predetermined accuracy. Six numerical examples are developed in order to illustrate the convergence properties of the sequential gradient-restoration algorithm. Four examples pertain to the fixed-final-time case, and two examples pertain to the free-final-time case.
Name: ["Hennig G.R.", "Miele A."]

Title: Optimal scheduling for two-processor systems
Abstract: Despite the recognized potential of multiprocessing little is known concerning the general problem of finding efficient algorithms which compute minimallength schedules for given computations and m‚âß2 processors. In this paper we formulate a general model of computation structures and exhibit an efficient algorithm for finding optimal nonpreemptive schedules for these structures on two-processor systems. We prove that the algorithm gives optimal solutions and discuss its application to preemptive scheduling disciplines. ¬© 1972 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Coffman Jr. E.G.", "Graham R.L."]

Title: Optimization of constrained dynamic systems using the sequential unconstrained minimization technique
Source: Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement and Control, Transactions of the ASME
Abstract: The development of a computer program for the optimization of dynamic systems subject to parameter and terminal state constraints is presented in this paper. The problem is handled by converting it to an equivalent algebraic optimization problem. The resulting problem is then solved by a modified version (D YS UMT) of the nonlinear programming method S UMT (Sequential Unconstrained Minimization Technique). The available program provides an efficient and convenient analysis tool to aid engineers in the modeling and designing of dynamic systems. ¬© 1972 ASME.
Name: ["Murali B.N.", "Ebbesen L.R.", "Sebesta H.R."]

Title: On the Covering and Reduction Problems for Context-Free Grammars
Abstract: A formal definition of one grammar ‚Äúcovering‚Äù another grammar is presented. It is argued that this definition has the property that G' covers G when and only when the ability to parse G' suffices for parsing G. It is shown that every grammar may be covered by a grammar in canonical two form. Every A-free grammar is covered by an operator normal form grammar while there exist grammars which cannot be covered by any grammar in Greibach form. Any grammar may be covered by an invertible grammar. Each A-free and chain reduced LR(k) (bounded right context) grammar is covered by a precedence detectable, LR(k) (bounded right context) reducible grammar. ¬© 1972, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gray J.N.", "Harrison M.A."]

Title: Matched Signal Detectors for a Certain Class of Detection Problems. | [ANGEPASSTE SIGNALDETEKTOREN FUER EINE BESTIMMTE KLASSE VON ENTDECKUNGSPROBLEMEN.]
Source: AEU Arch Elektron Uebertrag Electron Commun
Abstract: A special kind of signal detection problems frequently occurs in security or supervising systems. The principal feature of these detection problems is that the costs (or losses) appearing when a given signal component is really present in the quantity measured at the detector input strongly depend on the detection time. This implies the existence of a maximum reasonable detection time. A structure for signal detectors is devised which uses this property for optimum noise suppression. Only linear time-invariant systems are taken into account. These detector systems mainly consist of a combination of time-delay and prediction filters. Some computed examples are discussed.
Name: ["Luck Heinz"]

Title: Synthesis of Discrete Devices by Logical Block Diagrams of Algorithms. | [SINTEZ DISKRETNYKH USTROISTV PO LOGIKO-STRUKTURNYM SKHEMAM ALGORITMOV.]
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii, Gornyi Zhurnal
Abstract: A formal description is given of the language of logical bloc diagrams and a method is proposed for the synthesis of discrete devices of the finite automation type on the basis of formal processing of these diagrams. Application in coal mine data processing is mentioned.
Name: ["Gol'din M.A.", "Mikhailovskii O.V."]

Title: Optimization in Deterministic Production Models. | OPTYMALIZACJA W DETERMINISTYCZNYCH MODELACH PRODUKCYJNYCH.
Abstract: A method is investigated of searching for the optimal system of producing a finite number n of different products with minimal costs. It is assumed that all the products are produced in lots. Every product is processed on m or less machines according to some technological sequence restrictions. The problem is to determine the sequence of products providing the minimum or near to the minimum production costs. Two production models with different cost function constraints are constructed. It is shown that for a special class of sequencing problems the form of the cost function makes it possible to reduce the amount of computations n times. Because, for n products, the possible configurations in the sequencing problem are the n! permutations and for large n it is impssible to enumerate all the possibilities, an algorithm based on statistical methods is given. This algorithm may be called a parametrized Monte Carlo chain because at each step it uses the crude Monte Carlo method and in addition the above property of a special class of functions is utilized.
Name: ["Cichocki Krzysztof"]

Title: METHOD OF DUAL MATRICES FOR FUNCTION MINIMIZATION.
Abstract: The method proposed is characterized by employing two matrices at each iteration. One matrix is such that a linearly independent set of directions can be generated, regardless of the stepsize employed. The other matrix is such that, at the point where the first matrix fails to yield a linearly independent gradient, it generates a displacement leading to the minimal point. This represents a saving on the total computational effort required by the conventional algorithms.
Name: ["Huang H.Y."]

Title: Bandwidth Reduction Via Movement Compensation on a Model of the Random Video Process
Abstract: The video-signal bandwidth reduction obtained by inter- frame differential transmission is hindered by rapid movements of the objects and the camera. A simple movement compensation procedure can be obtained by dividing the image into zones and then transmitting for each zone a displacement vector relating the zone to a zone in the previous frame that is maximally correlated with it. The effectiveness of such a procedure is studied on a model of the random video process, obtained as a derivation of a three-dimensional telegraph signal. In particular, it is shown that for this model, the optimal procedure for finding the most correlated zone in the previous frame is the one matching the intersections of the contour lines. The optimal size of the zone for which a single displacement vector has to be transmitted is also determined. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Rocca F.", "Zanoletti S."]

Title: Approximate synthesis method for optimal control of a system subjected to random perturbations. PMM vol. 36, n‚âó5, 1972, pp. 829-839
Source: Journal of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: An approximate method is proposed for synthesizing the optimal control for a dynamical system in the presence of external random perturbations and measurement errors. The synthesis problem posed reduces, as is known, to solving a nonlinear parabolic partial differential equation (the Bellman equation) whose exact solutions are known only in a few cases. It is assumed that either the external perturbations acting on the system are sufficiently small or the measurement errors are large. Under these conditions the Bellman equation contains a small parameter in the leading derivative, and the solution is constructed by means of an expansion with respect to the small parameter. It is shown that the approximate synthesis of the optimal control for perturbed systems can be constructed in explicit form if the solution of the corresponding problem for the perturbation-free system is known. Estimates of the errors in the method are proved. Examples are given. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Solianik A.I.", "Chernous'ko F.L."]

Title: PLAUSIBILITY PLUS PROBABILITY: BAYESIAN STATISTICS.
Abstract: The author defines Bayesian Statistics as statistical decision methods based on Bayes' Theorem concerning joint probabilities per compound events. His aim is to show how to use Bayesian statistics to resolve conflicts between ‚Ä≥observations‚Ä≥ and ‚Ä≥opinions‚Ä≥ in a decision-making context, by not putting all the decision weight either on opinions alone or on observations alone, but rather by considering both. From an example, it is shown that a strong prior opinion (as expressed by high initial odds) concerning some hypothesis cannot easily be reversed by unfavorable data, i. e. , by data in conflict with the hypothesis. However, by observing a sufficient amount of data in conflict with an opinion, the opinion must finally be overthrown. Bayesian statistics is a method of allowing opinions to stand as long as probability calculations from observed data combined with the opinions will substantiate such opinions.
Name: ["Johnson Leonard G."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF DISCRETE OPTIMUM CONTROL SYSTEMS VIA FINITE IMPULSE RESPONSE.
Abstract: In synthesizing optimal discrete control systems using pulse response according to quadratic criteria, two problems are encountered. WThe pulse response is a polynomial of order 20 or more, which makes computation difficult, especially numerical computation. It is very difficult to obtain spectral densities in the form of rational fraction functions. Both these problems are dealt with. The first is solved by a compensation of the system with a special filter. The solution of the second is such that it is sufficient to know only the finite number of values of the autocorrelation function. An example is given.
Name: ["Vostry Zdenek"]

Title: LOCALIZATION PROBLEM IN GEOMETRY AND COMPLEXITY OF DISCRETE PROGRAMMING.
Abstract: The algorithmic complexity of the following problem is investigated: Given an arbitrary point of Euclidean space, we want to determine whether it belongs to a given convex polyhedral set. An application to the theory of discrete programming is discussed.
Name: ["Moravek Jaroslav"]

Title: Optimization of LR(k) parsers
Source: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: Certain techniques for modifying LR(k) parsing tables to decrease their size have been developed by Korenjak [2] and DeRemer [3, 4]. We show that the techniques of the latter can be characterized by two transformations on sets of tables. We then show that the "simple" LR(1) method of DeRemer [4] can be considered a special case of Korenjak's method [2]. ¬© 1972 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Aho A.V.", "Ullman J.D."]

Title: On Translation Algorithms in Residue Number Systems
Abstract: This paper considers translation problems in residue number systems. The conversion from a fixed-base representation to a residue representation can be done using residue adders only; we show that relatively simple combinational logic can be used to replace one level of residue addition. In the reverse translation problem, we examine the conditions under which base extension can be used to compute the fixed-base digits from a residue code number, and we study the efficiency of the algorithm. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Banerd D.K.", "Brzozowski J.A."]
Keywords: ["base extension", "input translation", "modular arithmetic", "output translation", "residue number systems"]
Affiliations: [' University of Ottawa', ' University of Waterloo']

Title: Sorting by Natural Selection
Abstract: A amily of sorting algorithms is proposed, the members of which make Adler use of the memory space and thus yield longer sorted strings. Extensive simulation results are presented, and various implications and lurther application, are discussed. ¬© 1972, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Frazer W.D.", "Wong C.K."]
Keywords: ["algorithm", "expected string length", "sorting by replacement selection", "sorting algorithms", "amily sorting"]

Title: Monte Carlo study of the optimal non-linear estimator: Linear systems with non-gaussian initial states
Abstract: The optimal, in the mean-square sense, estimate of state vector of a linear discrete system that is excited by white zero mean gaussian noise and that has non-gaussian initial state vector is presented. Both the optimal estimate and the corresponding error covariance matrix are given. It is shown that the optimal estimator consists of two parts: a linear estimator which is a Kalman filter and a non-linear part which is a parameter estimator. In addition, the a posteriori probability density function, p(x(k)Œªk), is also given. Finally, a suboptimal procedure that reduces the computational requirements is presented. The results of extensive digital computer simulations including Monte Carlo study have been presented to establish that the non-linear filter presented here is far superior to the best linear Kalman filter. A practical filter design criterion for utilizing this non-linear filter with reduced data processing requirements is also given. ¬© 1972 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Park S.K.", "Lainiotis D.G."]

Title: A New Data Base for Syntax-Directed Pattern Analysis and Recognition
Abstract: The problem of developing an appropriate data base for syntax-directed pattern analysis and recognition is considered. A new data base is introduced by generalizing the notion of concatenation in representing patterns with a relationship matrix. The. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Chien Y.T.", "Ribak R."]

Title: An Axiomatic Approach to Code Optimization for Expressions
Abstract: An axiomatic approach is proposed as a means of specifying precisely what liberties are permitted in evaluating expressions. Specific axiom systems are introduced for arithmetic expressions, which permit free grouping of terms within parentheses, in the spirit of American National Standard Fortran. Using these axiom systems, two algorithms are given for finding optimal equivalent forms of an expression not having multiple references to any variable. The first algorithm is intended for highly parallel computers and is a slight generalization of that of Baer and Bovet. The concept of delay is introduced as a measure of the serial dependency of a computation and the algorithm is shown to minimize delay. This provides, as a special case, a proof of the level minimality claimed by Baer and Bovet. The second algorithm is shown to produce an equivalent expression which can be evaluated with a minimal number of instructions on a computer of the IBM System/360 type. It is an extension of a result of Sethi and Ullman, which relates only to commutative and associative operations. ¬© 1972, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Beatty J.C."]

Title: Optimal Horizontal Guidance Law for Aircraft in the Terminal Area
Abstract: The automation of many of the functions currently performed by the controllers and pilots is essential for a safe and efficient air traffic control (ATC) system. A major aspect of the overall ATC system is the guidance and flight control of aircraft. This paper deals with the horizontal guidance of aircraft in and near the terminal area. The problem of guiding an aircraft in minimum time from an arbitrary point to the outer marker is formulated as a nonlinear optimal control problem, and the control law solution is obtained by the application of the maximum principle. It is found that for some initial states the problem is singular. Furthermore, the extremal controls for this problem are not unique. Consequently, the optimal controls must be obtained on the basis of the value of the performance index. The control law is implemented in the form of a digital computer program which computes the optimal trajectory for arbitrary initial conditions. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Pecsvaradi T."]

Title: REMARKS ON THE OPTIMUM RATE OF CONVERGENCE OF THE ON-LINE IDENTIFICATION OF NON-STATIONARY SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The use of the entropy definition by Fisher for the solution of on-line identification tasks permits the choice of the optimum convergence. Due to its advantageous properties, the statistical convergence optimization criterion with the known expected values can be chosen as identification quality criterion, too; therefore its application in practice is suggested. The algorithms serving for parameter estimation based on the variation of the entropy, are a new trend in research, if the entropy is expressed as a function of sampled values of output and input signals.
Name: ["Bencsik I."]

Title: A Note on the Kalman-Bucy Filtering for Linear Distributed-Parameter Systems
Abstract: In a recent paper Tzafestas [1] considered the filtering: problem of linear distributed-parameter systems corrupted by boundary and volume (system‚Äòs interior) disturbances. It is shown here that the filtering equations for such systems are obtainable in a straightforward manner by using the concept of extended operators in Hilbert space. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Atre S.R."]

Title: NOTE ON GENERATION OF SEQUENCES OF PSEUDORANDOM NUMBERS WITH PRESCRIBED AUTOCORRELATION COEFFICIENTS.
Abstract: A method is discussed allowing the geheration of sequences of pseudorandom numbers with a autocorrelation function near the autocorrelation function of the white noise after filtering by a filter with the transfer function F(p). The white noise is approximated on a digital computer by a telegraph signal S. On S some integral transformation is applied. The experimental results show that the generated autocorrelation coefficients have values near the expected ones. The method allows generation of pseudorandom sequences having a great number of nonzero autocorrelation coefficients.
Name: ["Kral Jaroslav"]

Title: Determination of Volterra kernels from input-output data
Abstract: In this paper a class of system identification problems of non-parametric type is considered. Specifically, given an unknown deterministic system whose input-output relation can be expressed by a Volterra expansion, some basic structural aspects related to the problem of determining Volterra kernels from input-output records are discussed from a coordinate-free point of view. The model adopted for the system input‚Äîoutput relation is general enough to cover a number of situations ranging from problems of identification where the kernels are time-varying to those where the kernels must be constrained in Hilbert spaces of well-behaved functions. The emphasis is on establishing what, in principle, can be recovered of the system kernels through a noiseless identification process, and the ultimate limitations imposed by the presence of observation or measurement noise. An application of the steepest descent iteration to the ill-posed estimation problem resulting from the presence of observation noise is considered. ¬© 1972 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Mosca E."]

Title: A Class of pdf Modeling Algorithms
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The development and comparison of a class of nonparametric probability density function modeling algorithms is presented. Each algorithm iteratively estimates a model of the sampled density function based upon a description of a set of equiprobable regions over the range of the variable of interest. Minimization of computational complexity and memory capacity while maintaining convergence and stability are the principal considerations. Variations of the algorithms are compared as to rate of convergence and limit cycle stability relative to ease of implementation. Results including comparative curves are presented. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Drake K.W.", "Gerhardt L.A."]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR OBTAINING BEST APPROXIMATION ON SETS OF POSITIVE POLYNOMIALS.
Abstract: The problem of finding best mean-squared approximations on bases of the cones of positive polynomials is discussed. An algorithm is developed for finding the best approximations which is based on the Hahn-Banach (separation) theorem. The algorithm also offers prospects as a viable alternative to a gradient scheme in more general situations.
Name: ["Matthews J.W."]

Title: Reconstruction of a defocused image
Source: Optics and Spectroscopy (English translation of Optika i Spektroskopiya)
Abstract: The paper discusses the question of reconstruction of a photographic image obtained in a system whose transfer function has zero and negative values (defocusing, astigmatism, distortion of the image of a moving object, etc.). It proposes a method of reconstruction using two differently distorted photographs which makes it possible to eliminate the information loss at the zero points of the transfer function and to perform the reconstruction over a wide range of spatial frequencies.
Name: ["Shmarev E.K."]

Title: Automatic Subdivision of a Large Network into Partial Systems. | AUTOMATISCHE ZERLEGUNG EINES UMFANGREICHEN NETZWERKES IN TEILSYSTEME.
Source: Wissenschaftliche Zeitschrift der Technischen Unversitat Dresden
Abstract: The analytical method can usefully be applied to digital calculation of the current-voltage relations in large electric power supply networks. After describing such an analytical method, an algorithm is presented which is instrumental in automatic subdivision of a large electric network into partial networks by means of a digital computer. As a result, practical application of the analysis method is considerably improved; error possibilities of manual preparation of partial systems are thus avoided.
Name: ["Siegmund Dietmar"]

Title: Compensation Method of Identification of an Industrial Flotation Process with the Application of Orthogonal Filters. | KOMPENSATSIONNYI METOD IDENTIFIKATSII PROMYSHLENNOGO FLOTOPROTSESSA S UPRIMENENIEM OROTGONAL'NYKH FIL'TROV.
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii, Gornyi Zhurnal
Abstract: A method of erection of a coupling operator of a multidimensional dynamic object is considered. To solve the problem, the method of orthogonal filters is used. Weight coefficients are found by solving a system of linear algebraic equations. The algorithm obtained was used in the identification of the process of coal flotation at the Novo-Irminskaya central flotation plant.
Name: ["Salyga V.I.", "Khadzhikov N.R."]

Title: Description of the maintained activity of single units in the cat visual cortex in terms of a three component model
Abstract: A simple three additive component model that can adequately describe the spontaneous discharge pattern of the neurons in the cat visual cortex is proposed. The different components of the model were related to the observed biological data by examining the activity of single units at different levels of environmental luminance. In this way it was possible to demonstrate some functional characteristics which seem to be peculiar to the visual striate area with respect to nonstriate ones.
Name: ["Agnati L.F.", "Pallotti G.", "Galletti C.", "Riva Sanseverino E."]

Title: Design of Control Circuits Time Response by Hybrid Computer Simulation. | EGYSZERU SZABALYOZASI KOROK TERVEZESE IDOTARTOMANYBAN A HIBRID UZEMMOD SZIMULACIOJAVAL.
Abstract: A program for optimizing a simple single loop linear control circuit is described. The program simulates in structure and function the operation of hybrid computers. It contains an optimizing and a simulating unit with the help of which the optimization of compensation can be achieved in the case of PI and PID controllers by an arbitrary integral criterion even for overshot limitation. A lagging element with a pair of complex conjugate poles and two real poles is considered as the controlled system. The applicability of the program is very flexible, the system can be easily extended.
Name: ["Keviczky Laszlo", "Banyasz Csilla"]

Title: Optimal Restoration of a Stationary Random Process by Discrete Samplings.
Abstract: In Russian.
Name: ["Galitskas A.A."]

Title: Determining Initial Values of Adjoint Systems in Optimally Fast Control of Linear Plants. | [NAKHOZHDENIE NACHAL'NYKH ZNACHENII VSPOMOGATEL'NOI SISTEMY, PRI ZADACHE OB OPTIMAL'NOM PO BYSTRODEISTVIYU UPRAVLENII LINEINYMI OB'EKTAMI.]
Abstract: The fundamental vector 4(0) of adjoint systems, which determines the optimally fast control law of linear plants, is determined by means of the maximum principle. The exact solution comprises three steps: (1) parametric equations of extremal trajectories are deduced: (2) a set of transcendental vectors is examined, the real, non-negative solution of which yields uniquely the instant of switching of the optimal control; (3) a system of linear equalities and inequalities is derived, the solution of which is the set of initial vectors of the adjoint systems determining the optimally fast control.
Name: ["Tsvetanov Iliya P."]

Title: Augmented loop languages and classes of computable functions
Source: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: A classification of all the computable functions is given in terms of subrecursive programming languages. These classes are those which arise from the relation "primitive recursive in". By distinguishing between honest and dishonest classes the classification is related to the computational complexity of the functions classified and the classification has a wide degree of measure invariance. The structure of the honest and dishonest classes under inclusion is explored. It is shown that any countable partial ordering can be embedded in the dishonest classes, and that the dishonest classes are dense in the honest classes. Every honest class is minimal over some dishonest class, but there are dishonest classes with no honest class minimal over them. ¬© 1972 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Machtey M."]
Affiliations: [' Departments of Mathematics and Computer Science']

Title: A Signal-Dependent Error Arising in Digitally Processed Images Due to Quantization
Abstract: A troublesome error has been found in digital data which represents an image renormalized by a computer. The error, which takes the form of anomalous patterns in the switching sequence of certain bits, contributes unnecessary, signal-dependent noise to the data. Experimental results illustrating this phenomenon are shown and a theoretical model is derived. The model shows that the phenomenon results from a quantization or roundoff error inherent in digital renormalization and describes its detailed behavior. A method for rescaling the data which does not lead to the introduction of noise is described. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Carter W.H.", "Brown V.D."]

Title: CRITICAL PATH PROBLEMS WITH CONCAVE COST-TIME CURVES.
Abstract: This paper presents an algorithm for determining the minimum cost schedule of tasks in a critical path network in which task cost-time curves may be concave. A computer program for the case of cost-time curves that are piecewise linear in two segments is described, and a numerical example is presented.
Name: ["Falk James E.", "Horowitz joel L."]

Title: A. D. C. -TIME COMPUTATION ALGORITHM FOR A WORKING REGIME IN SEVERAL SHIFTS.
Source: Econ Comput Econ Cybern Stud Res
Abstract: In applying critical path methods to work scheduling, an analysis of resources, time and the work regime must be interrelated. The proposed algorithm is applicable for a wide range of work shift conditions.
Name: ["Stoica M.", "Bancila I.", "Ciobanu G."]

Title: Index Ranges for Matrix Calculi
Abstract: The paper describes a scheme for symbolic manipulation of index expressions which arise as a by-product of the symbolic manipulaticn of expressions in the matrix calculi described by the authors in a previous paper. This scheme attempts program optimization by transforming the original algorithm rather than the machine code. The goal is to automatically generate code for handling the tedious address calculations necessitated by complicated data structures. The paper is therefore preoccupied with ‚Äúindexing by position.‚Äù The relationship of ‚Äúindexing by name‚Äù and ‚Äúindexing by position‚Äù is discussed. ¬© 1972, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Bayer R.", "Witzgall C."]

Title: A model for data structures and its applications. (Part II)
Abstract: This paper is the second and final part of [6]. Some problems of irregular data structures (list structures) are analysed by means of the proposed model. Operations on data structures are introduced and discussed. The model is applied to a problem in information retrieval. Finally, some general remarks on data-structure problems are made, intended as a justification of the approach taken in this paper. ¬© 1972 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Turski W.M."]

Title: On non-determinancy in simple computing devices
Abstract: This paper studies one-tape Turing machines with k read-only heads which are restricted to the original input. The main result shows that if any set accepted by such a 3-head non-deterministic Turing machine can be accepted by a deterministic Turing machine with more read-only heads, then the deterministic and non-deterministic context-sensitive languages are identical. Several related results are derived and some tantalizing open problems are discussed. ¬© 1972 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Hartmanis J."]
Affiliations: ['Gesellschaft f√ºr Mathematik und Datenverarbeitung mbH Bonn']

Title: On Bad Data Suppression in Estimation
Abstract: Merrill and Schweppe [1] propose a modification of the usual least squares criterion for estimation in order to suppress bad data. It is shown that similar estimators can be obtained from maximum likelihood theory. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Kohlas J."]

Title: Control of stochastic distributed-parameter systems
Source: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
Abstract: A scheme is proposed for the feedback control of distributed-parameter systems with unknown boundary and volume disturbances and observation errors. The scheme consists of employing a nonlinear filter in the control loop such that the controller uses the optimal estimates of the state of the system. A theoretical comparison of feedback proportional control of a styrene polymerization reactor with and without filtering is presented. It is indicated how an approximate filter can be constructed, greatly reducing the amount of computing required. ¬© 1972 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Yu T.K.", "Seinfeld J.H."]

Title: Dynamic Programming Training Period for an MSE Adaptive Equalizer
Abstract: This paper concerns itself with the design of an algorithm that will shotten the training period and adaptation time of an adaptive equalizer. Time-invariant or slowly varying channels with white additive Gaussian noise are considered. An adaptive equalizer in the form of a nonrecursive transversal filter reduces the intersymbol interference. The training period consists of the transmission of isolated pulses between which the equalizer is adjusted. The algorithm uses a minimum mean-squared error criterion with a variable step size on each iteration. A fixed number of iterations is allowed for the error to be minimized. A constraint related to the average excess mean-squared error is included, and the set of step sizes is determined by invoking the principle of optimality in dynamic programming. The resulting algorithm is compared to the popular fixed step-size algorithm. Predicted and experimental results are given. A fairly well conditioned and a poorly conditioned channel are considered. Results show that the new algorithm has a faster adaptation time. It is more complex than the fixed step-size algorithm, but for long transversal filters requires little additional computation time. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Richman S.H.", "Schwartz M."]

Title: On two-state isolated probabilistic automata
Abstract: In this paper we generalize and extend Yasui and Yajima's results on two-state two-symbol probabilistic automata to the two-state multisymbol case. We use a slightly different notion of isolated probabilistic automata independent of the initial distribution. An algorithm is derived to synthesize such automata. Finally we show the existence of a regular language accepted by some completely isolated probabilistic automaton. ¬© 1972 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Tan C.P."]

Title: DYNAMIC MODEL BUILDING SYSTEM USING VIRTUAL MEMORY.
Abstract: A self-contained model building and storage managements system written entirely in FORTRAN IV (at IBM G level) is described. The program control system is the practical result of a particular approach to scientific model building. This approach splits the problem into two parts: the first part is to identify the classes of elementary processes and activities that form the basic functions and operations in the system studied, and the second is to study different ways of organizing these basic operations to reproduce or simulate the behavior of the system under study. The approach was successfully adopted for a project to model the modal choice of travellers faced with a number of alternative ways of making long distance trips.
Name: ["Wigan M.Ramsay"]

Title: On the Stability of Multiloop Feedback Systems
Abstract: Some extensions on recent work in passive stability theory by Desoer and the author are presented. The stability of feedback systems is considered where the forward-loop and return-loop subsystems each have been subdivided into several systems operating in parallel. Results are obtained in the areas of Lyapunov stability, L2-input L2-output stability, and bounded-input bounded-state stability. Before applying these results to a specific multiloop feedback system, a pseudoenergy analysis must be done on each sub sub-system. Two specific types of systems are so analyzed. The first is a general linear first-order time-varying system. The second is a linear time-varying infinite-dimensional system; the analysis of this system takes the form of a Kalman-Yacubovich-type lemma. By using these two new systems, along with several others that have been analyzed previously, stability theorems for many specific multiloop feedback systems can be proven. One such example is given. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Estrada R.F."]

Title: Parallel Task Execution in a Decentralized System
Abstract: The overhead involved in the real-time multiprocessor execution of parallel-processable segments of a sequential program is investigated. The execution follows a preprocessing phase in which the source program is analyzed and the parallel-processable segments are recognized. A number of representations of a parallel-processable program are possible. A table representation is used, and a technique is developed to efficiently interpret this table in a system in which a number of identical processors share a common memory. A number of program graphs based on real problems are used to investigate the overhead involved in parallel task execution. The investigation is conducted in the context of two organizations‚Äîthe centralized, in which processor assignments are totally under the control of the operating system, and the decentralized, in which processors are allowed to determine their own next assignment from the program they are executing. In the decentralized system, processor assignment and other control information is embedded within the program segments themselves. Within each of these organizations, two configurations are examined. In the first, the operating system periodically polls a program to determine if a need for a processor exists; in the second, a program generates an interrupt to request a processor when a task becomes ready. Results of simulation in which the number of processors and the task durations are permitted to vary over a wide range show that the decentralized organization and the polling configuration provide the most improvement over conventional uniprocessor execution. This improvement, which includes consideration of overhead due to table interpretation, exists even when the number of parallel paths is not large, provided the average task duration is not small. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Gonzalez M.J.", "Ramamoorthy C.V."]

Title: On time dependent fuzzy sets
Abstract: This paper extends the concept of fuzzy set, introduced by L. A. Zadeh, to a time dependent setting. Time dependence enters into a number of areas including planning and pattern recognition. Results are given for topologies of fuzzy sets and applied to shadows. Time dependent fuzzy relations are defined and discussed. ¬© 1972 American Elsevier Publishing Company, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Lientz B.P."]

Title: Weighted increment linear search for scatter tables
Abstract: A new linear search for hash tables whose increment step is a function of the key being addressed is presented. Comparisons with known methods are given, in terms of efficiency and computation complexity. In particular, the new method applies to tables of size n = 2<sub>r</sub>. It allows full table searching, and practically eliminates primary clustering at a very low cost. ¬© 1972, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Luccio F."]

Title: Two Channel Service System with Alternation of Priorities and with the Time of Service of Demands Depending on the State of the Processor. | DWUKANALOWY SYSTEM OBSLUGI Z WYMIANA PRIORYTETOW I CZASEM OBSLUGI ZGLOSZEN ZALEZNYM OD STANU PROCESORA.
Abstract: A service system with two input channels and a single processor is considered. Demands enter the system input in batches. The number of demands in separate batches is randomly distributed. The time intervals between batches are independent random variables having the same exponential distribution. An alternating priority discipline and dependence of the service time upon the processor state at the time an arrival enters the system input is discussed. Models of systems with alternating priority and nonzero processor changeover time can be obtained as special cases from the one derived.
Name: ["Libura Marek"]

Title: MINIMIZATION OF THE CROSSING NUMBER IN LOGICAL CIRCUIT GRAPHS.
Abstract: The problem of minimization of the crossing number in logical circuit graphs is discussed. This problem is important for the design of computers with large-scale integrated (LSI) circuits or when designing general-purpose and/or control computers and in automated design of logical schemes and flowcharts. Paper gives an account of new findings as a result of a general multilayer problem study. A new algorithm shows systematic ways to find geometrical layouts of certain switching functions, which may be executed by means of a minimum of layer numbers, and which may be used for the automatic design of LSI circuits.
Name: ["Koryachko Vyacheslav P.", "Mamatov Yuri A."]

Title: ON STEADY STATE MINIMUM VARIANCE CONTROL STRATEGY.
Abstract: Optimal digital regulation of a stationary stochastic plant with single input and single output is investigated. It is assumed that the input-output relation is described by a linear difference equation and that the spectral density of additive stochastic disturbances is rational. The problem is to determine the control law (the algorithm of the digital controller in feedback) so9 that the variance of the plant output be minimum in steady state.
Name: ["Peterka Vaclav"]

Title: Linear Filtering in the Presence of Time-Varying Bias
Abstract: The problem of estimating the state of a linear system subjected to a time-varying bias with sample paths generated from b = F*b is considered, and an optimal filtering algorithm is derived. It is shown that the structure of the optimal estimator is the same as that determined earlier by Friedland for constant bias disturbances, and that the algorithm possesses the same computational advantages over the augmented Kalman-Bucy filter. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Tacker E.C.", "Lee C.C."]
Affiliations: [' Louisiana State University', ' Louisiana State University']

Title: EXAMPLE OF THE FUNCTION (BEHAVIOUR) OF A SYSTEM ELEMENT CONSISTING IN RUDIMENTARY PROPERTIES - 1.
Abstract: The author applies a certain set model to some problems of cybernetics. Attentionis focused on the function of an element from the cybernetical point of view, i. e. of an element of a certain class of cybernetical systems, of an element with given properties. For example the present element has its memory, can operate rudimentary properties, can process its information. A feedback of the element is expressed by means of a wave of activities or of a wave of information. Not only an operating of activities but also information processing, e. g. decision making, are developed in time flow, i. e. they are delayed, in general, etc. The element can, for example, have a certain energy, mass, function, ability, aim, etc. The element can be a worker, an operator, a specialist, a machine, an engine, an industrial product, a device, etc. The purpose of the investigation is to introduce a new description of problems occuring in different cybernetical systems, for example when solving problem of automatic control. The corresponding mathematical expressions are subjects of Part II of the present paper.
Name: ["Dastych Premysl"]

Title: Process Matching System for Multiplex and Programmed Computer Channels. | FOLYAMAT-ILLESZTO RENDSZER MULTIPLEX ES PROGRAMOZOTT SZAMITOGEP-CSATORNAKRA.
Abstract: The paper describes the matching system developed at the Process Control Institute at Budapest Polytechnical University, by the help of which, using the multiplex or programmed input and output channel of a computer, an information exchange can be realized between the computer and the process. With respect to logical operation the matching unit is similar to the operation of the so-called internal interface unit of computers equipped with real-time channels. The user subroutines of the matching system on the one hand permit information exchanges, on the other hand a simple description of information processing changing from case to case becomes possible. The matching system has so far been employed in such problems where the process was a logical network to be checked, or a measuring and data acquisition system CAMAC.
Name: ["Arato Peter", "Kalmar Peter", "Kondorosi Karoly", "Korosi Istvan", "Lantos Bela"]

Title: Introduction into the Theory of Optimal Fast Response Adaptive Systems of Automatic Control. | [VVEDENIE V TEORIYU OPTIMAL'NYKH PO BYSTRODEISTVIYU ADAPTIVNYKH SISTEM AVTOMATICHESKOGO UPRAVLENIYA.]
Abstract: An analysis of the known adaptation algorithms is made. New methods of synthesis of optimal adaptive regulators are proposed and described, and this forms the basis of a classification of these regulators. Problems connected with the methods of analysis of optimal fast response systems are considered. Using these methods it is possible to solve the problem of the necessity of adaptation and of the requirements with respect to an adaptive control system.
Name: ["Shukshunov V.E.", "Pototskii S.I.", "Savin M.M.", "Marinin V.I."]

Title: Adaptive Parameter Identification
Abstract: An extended Kalman filter with a fictitious noise input is developed for tracking time-varying parameters. An adaptation algorithm is used for adjusting the covariance of the fictitious noise according to the magnitude of the measured residuals and applied to the tracking of time-varying VTOL parameters. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.

Title: Identification and Control of a Dynamic Process Using the Method of Least Squares, Modeled on the ODRA 1204 Digital Computer. | IDENTYFIKACJA I STEROWANIE OBIEKTEM DYNAMICZNYM NA PODSTAWIE ZASADY NAJMNIEJSZEJ SUMY KWADRATOW MODELOWANE NA MASZYNIE CYFROWEJ.
Abstract: A method is presented for estimating parameters of a controller which minimizes the variance of the output signal. In the equation of the assumed process, the random variable does not depend upon the input. The control algorithm results from applying linear stochastic control theory, and minimizes the mean value of the sums of the squares of the output signal. Parameters are estimated on the base of normal operating records by applying the least-squares method. Estimators are shown to be consistent. If the random variable is normally distributed then the estimators are maximum likelihood ones and have all the optimal properties of such estimators. Some numerical examples are given.

Title: Solving Navigation Problems with a Hybrid Analog Computer. | [LOESUNG VON NAVIGATIONSPROBLEMEN MIT HYBRIDEM ANALOGRECHNER.]
Abstract: This paper demonstrates the application of a hybrid analog computer to solving some basic problems of navigation. It is shown how optimization can be achieved both quickly and with a sufficient degree of accuracy using the gradient technique.
Name: ["Zartner Albrecht", "Duerr Rolf"]

Title: PORTABLE DATA ACQUISITION UNIT FOR WORD RECOGNITION RESEARCH.
Source: AES: Journal of the Audio Engineering Society
Abstract: A portable recording and digitizing apparatus is described in detail, which permits selectable automatic segmentation of the natural speech signal prior to digitizing and processing at a central computer facility. The flexibility and accuracy of the data acquisition unit are illustrated by describing the complete recording and analysis procedure for a sample word.
Name: ["Levin Herman", "Lord William"]

Title: Algorithm of a Fast, Two-Bit Division of Numbers Represented in the Form of the Complement of Twos. | [ALGORYTM PRZYSPIESZONEGO, DWUBITOWEGO DZIELENIA LICZB PRZEDSTAWIONYCH W ZPAISIE UZUPELNIEN DO DWOCH.]
Abstract: An improvement is described for the division algorithm known as ‚Ä≥Two-Bit Lookahead Non-Restoring Division‚Ä≥ formulated by I. Flores in his book ‚Ä≥The Logic of Computer Arithmetic‚Ä≥ . It is shown by an example that the algorithm of the reference work does not satisfy the condition of convergence of a sequence of partial remainders. There is introduced another method of determining multiplicity of the divisor, subtracted from the partial remainder at each step of the algorithm. Proof is given of the convergence of a sequence of partial remainders of the improved algorithm.
Name: ["Brzoza Wlodzimierz", "Wolski Antoni"]

Title: Determination of Excitation Functions of Elementary Automata. | WYZNACZANIE FUNKCJI WZBUDZEN AUTOMATOW ELEMENTARNYCH.
Abstract: Algorithms are given of the excitation functions of elementary automata. These algorithms make it possible to derive by simple methods the excitation functions for any number of inputs and internal states of a proposed automaton. Examples presented showing the effect of the algorithms. These algorithms have been written in ALGOL-60 and used in the ODRA-1204 computer.
Name: ["Sosnowski janusz"]

Title: CONTRIBUTION TO THE STUDY OF ANTHROPOMORPHIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Definitions, dynamic aspects and stability concepts of anthropomorphic systems are presented. The attempt to synthetize a locomotion mechanism, reproducing with great similarity the human locomotion system, would lead to extremely complex systems, particularly from the control standpoint. Evidently, there arises the problem how to reduce the total number of degrees of freedom at the dynamic level of the locomotion - manipulation system. In the proposed method the synergy of some type of gait is been realized as well as the synthesis of the compensating system, which is necessary to maintain the prescribed synergy. The synergy supposes the synchronization of the system parts relative movement and it is equivalent to introducing supplementary connections (constraints) in the locomotion system mechanism. Due to these connections the total number of degrees of freedom diminishes considerably, and with a prescribed algorithm the system does not possess ‚Ä≥freedom‚Ä≥ in the classical sense; it moves according to a preselected law. Some schemes of perturbed steady gait regime stabilization are also given.
Name: ["Vukobratovic Miomir"]

Title: Measuring two-dimensional complexity: A conceptual structure
Abstract: Two-dimensional complexity is viewed as being analyzable through two-dimensional syntax. This premise is based on the assumption that there is a natural two-dimensional language, which is used for visual data processing and pattern recognition. Based on these assumptions, three measures of syntactic complexity, developed for context-free grammars, are shown to have application to Dacey's two-dimensional languages for simple polygons. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Betak J.F."]

Title: On the Identifiability of Parameters
Abstract: A precise definition of identifiability of a parameter is given in terms of consistency in probability for the parameter estimate. Under some mild Uniformity assumptions on the conditional density parameterized by the unknown parameter, necessary and sufficient conditions for the unknown parameter to be identifiable are established. The assumptions and identifiability criteria are expressed in terms of the density of individual observations, conditioned upon all past observations. The results are applied to linear system identification problems. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Edison T.", "Anton J.J."]

Title: SEQUENCE CONTROL OF ANALOGUE COMPUTERS.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: An inexpensive method of simplifying the control of iterative problem solutions run on parallel-logic analog computers by employing a special-purpose sequence controller is described. The controller stores up to 16 64 bit words, which are transferred in sequence to an output buffer. Most of the bits within each word form the control signals for analog components. This is mechanized by connections from the controller-output buffer to the analog-component control lines via an existing parallel-logic patchboard. Conditional (i. e. comparator-controlled) operations and manual control (using logic switches) are possible with only a limited number of analog components. A compiler for a digital computer enables the user to define the modes and states of analog components as a sequence of events in time. These events, and the periods of time between them, may be defined by a list of digital-program-source statements, or conversationally, by replying to questions typed at the user's teleprinter. Either form of input is compiled into the sequence-controller machine code, which is then loaded into the controller memory ready for execution.
Name: ["Barney G.C.", "Miller D."]

Title: A Note Concerning Nondeterministic Tape Complexities
Abstract: A set of sufficient conditions on tape functions L<sub>l</sub>(n) and L<sub>2</sub>(n) is presented that guarantees the existence of a set accepted by an L<sub>l</sub>(n)-tape bounded nondeterministic Turing machine, but not accepted by any L~(n)-tape bounded nondeterministic Turing machine. Interesting corollaries arise. For example, it is shown that, for integers m ; 0, p ;1, and q ; 1, there is a set accepted by an [n~+(P/q)]-tape bounded nondeterministic Turing machine that is not accepted by any [n<sup>m+(p/(q+l))</sup>]-tape bounded nondeterministic Turing machine. ¬© 1972, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Ibarra O.H."]
Keywords: ["complexity", "context-sensitive language", "deterministic turing machine", "fully constructable", "nondeterministic turing machine"]

Title: On the Optimality of Some Set Algorithms
Abstract: The establishment of lower bounds on the number of comparisons necessary to solve various combinatorial problems is considered. Some of the new results are : (a) given two finite sets of real numbers, A and B, where n = max ( | A |, | B |), O(n.log n) comparisons are required to determine if A = B, even when comparisons are allowed between linear functions of the numbers; and (b) the maximum of a set of n real numbers cannot be computed in fewer than n - 1 comparisons if comparisons of only linear functions of the numbers are permitted, but the maximum can be computed in Ilog2n] comparisons if comparisons are allowed between exponential functions of the numbers. ¬© 1972, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Reingold E.M."]
Keywords: ["determining set equality", "maximum of a set", "optimal algorithms", "combinatorial problems", "optimality set"]
