Name: ["Fuller S.H."]
Keywords: ["disk scheduling", "drum scheduling", "file scheduling", "graph theory", "rotational latency analysis"]

Title: The conversion of limited-entry decision tables to optimal and near-optimal flowcharts: Two new algorithms
Abstract: Two new algorithms for deriving optimal and near-optimal flowcharts from limited entry decision tables are presented. Both take into account rule frequencies and the time needed to test conditions. One of the algorithms, called the optimum-finding algorithm, leads to a flowchart which truly minimizes execution time for a decision table in which simple rules are already contracted to complex rules. The other one, called the optimum-approaching algorithm, requires many fewer calculations but does not necessarily produce the optimum flowchart. The algorithms are first derived for treating decision tables not containing an ELSE-rule, but the optimum-approaching algorithm is shown to be equally valid for tables including such a rule. Both algorithms are compared with existing ones and are applied to a somewhat large decision table derived from a real case. From this comparison two conclusions are drawn. (1) The optimum-approaching algorithm will usually lead to better results than comparable existing ones and will not require more, but usually less, computation time. (2) In general, the greater computation effort needed for applying the optimum-finding algorithm will not be justified by the small reduction in execution time obtained. ¬© 1972, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Verhelst M."]

Title: A method to increase the depth of focus by two step image processing
Abstract: The method to obtain an increased depth of field consists of two steps. The first step is to produce a modified incoherent image of the three dimensional object which, though degraded, has the same degradation for all object planes. The second step is to filter this modified image in a coherent image processor to obtain un undegraded image with increased depth of focus. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["H√§usler G."]

Title: Low-cost associative memory
Source: Digest of Technical Papers - IEEE International Solid-State Circuits Conference
Abstract: THE DEVELOPMENT of LSI technology has made possible wide flexibility in the architecture of information-processing systems. One major result of this is the ability to implement highly parallel, distributed logic and memory computers. One approach that has received considerable attention is the associative or content addressable memory<sup>1</sup>. This is a word organized array of storage elements and logic which allows a comparison of stored information with data applied to the bit lines. Each word provides a logic signal (flag) which indicates whether or not any stored bit in the word does not agree with the state of the corresponding bit line. ¬© 1972 IEEE.
Name: ["Mundy J.L.", "Burgess J.F.", "Joynson R.E.", "Neugebauer C.A."]

Title: ASYMPTOTIC ANALYSIS OF A NONPARAMETRIC CLUSTERING TECHNIQUE.
Abstract: Authors consider a general class of valley-seeking criteria. The results bear a close resemblance to Parzen's theory of probability density estimation. This similarity is exploited to develop sufficient conditions for a criterion to be valley seeking in the asymptotic sense.
Name: ["Koontz Warren L.G.", "Fukunaga Keinosuke"]

Title: A Covariance Approach to Spectral Moment Estimation
Abstract: We are interested in estimating the moments of the snectral density of a complex Gaussian signal process {q(1)i(t)} when the signal process is immersed in independent additive complex Gaussian noise {q(2)(t)}. Using vector samples Q = {q(t1),.,q(tm)}, where q(t) = q(1)(t) + q(2)(t)_ estimators for determinihg the spectral moments, or parameters of the signal-process power spectrum may be constructed. These estimators depend upon estimates at the covariance function R1 (h) of the signal, process at only one value of h ‚â† 0. In particular, if m =2, these estimators are maximum-likelihood solutions. (The explicit solution of the Iikelihood equations for m < 2 is still an unsolved problem.) Using these solutions, asymptotic (with, sample size) formulas for the means and variances of the spectral mean frequency and, spectral width are derived. It is shown that the leading term in the variance computations is identical with the Crame Rae lower bound calculated using the Fisher information matrix. Also considered is the case where the data set consists of N samples of continuous data, each, of finite duration. In this case asymptotic (with N) formulas are also derived for the means and variances of the spectral mean frequency and spectral width. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Miller K.S.", "Rochwarger M.M."]

Title: Z-TRANSFORM ANALYSIS OF NONUNIFORMLY SAMPLED DIGITAL FILTERS.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: An analysis is presented of digital filters operated with nonuniform sample periods. The analysis is applicable to filters using a mean-square definition of transfer function, e. g. moving-target-indicator filters, and also to conventional digital filters. The evaluation of the frequency response of such filters using the analytic results of the paper leads to considerable savings in computation time over direct simultaion methods. Nonuniform sampling of conventional digital filters is shown to result in a reduction of the effective Nyquist frequency, although, within this limited frequency range, additional control of the frequency response is possible for certain filters. A pole-zero diagram may be drawn for a nonuniformly sampled filter, and allows comparisons to be made with the corresponding uniformly sampled case.
Name: ["Thomas H.W.", "Lutte N.P."]

Title: OPTIMAL BINARY IDENTIFICATION PROCEDURES.
Abstract: Binary identification problems model a variety of actual problems, all containing the requirement that one construct a testing procedure for identifying a single unknown object belonging to a known finite set of possibilities. They arise in connection with machine fault-location, medical diagnosis, species identification, and computer programming. Author describes the basic model for binary identification problems and present a number of general results, including a dynamic programming algorithm for constructing optimal identification procedures. The main results of the paper concern identification problems in which the object possibilities are naturally partitioned into similarity classes with available tests of two types; general tests which only distinguish between similarity classes and specific tests which each test for a single one of the possibilities. This structure is utilized to obtain considerable improvement over the general dynamic programming algorithm.
Name: ["Garey M.R."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF OPTIMAL REGULATOR FOR SYNCHRONOUS MACHINE.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: A procedure for the synthesis of a self-adaptive near-optimal controller for small perturbations, subject to a quadratic performance index, of a synchronous generator connected to an infinite busbar is described. The performance of the system with this controller is compared with those having proportional and derivative voltage regulators. The optimal controller extends the stable operating region of the system at low active-power levels, increases the magnitudes of perturbations for which the actual nonlinear system is stable, improves the transient response and reduces the steady-state deviations for a step change in the infinite-busbar voltage.
Name: ["Raman S.", "Kapoor S.C."]

Title: On Identification of Certain Nonlinear Systems
Abstract: In the fields of communication and control there sometimes arises the problem of determining the characteristics of a time-invariant system from discrete records of its input and output during a limited interval of time, where the output data are contaminated with random noise. When this system is linear, we can use the convolution sum to obtain a characterization of the output as a linear combination of past inputs. Hill and McMurtry [4] showed that if we choose a Legendre binary noise sequence as input to a linear system, then the least squares approximation to the characterizing coefficients is expressible in a computationally feasible form, even when a large number of coefficients is involved. In this correspondence we characterize a nonlinear system by a generalization of the convolution sum and show that if we choose Golomb's maximal linear recurring binary-noise sequence [2] as input, then the least squares approximation to the characterizing coefficients is expressible in a computationally feasible form. Thus, the maximal linear recurring sequence occupies the same role in investigating certain nonlinear systems that the Legendre sequence occupies in investigating linear systems. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hayashi H."]

Title: Rotating storage devices as partially associative memories
Source: Proceedings of the ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data
Abstract: It is shown that "associative addressing" is a very natural way for using rotating memories. The concept of "partially associative memory" is defined as a memory on which each item can be addressed via part of its content. A realization of such a memory on rotating devices is proposed, and its performance discussed. Copyright ¬© 1972 by Association of Compuiting Machinery.
Name: ["Minsky N."]

Title: Computer minimization of multivalued switching functions
Abstract: A cubical representation for multivalued switching functions, which is very convenient for digital computer processing, is presented. A p-valued switching function of n variables is represented by an array of cubes. Each cube is composed of a logical coefficient and n coordinates with each coordinate represented by p bits. A set of operators for multivalued logic design (such as sharp, union, etc.) for manipulating arrays of cubes is defined and used for minimizing multivalued switching functions. The idea of ‚Äúcompound literals‚Äù is introduced, which yields a realization with less hardware than the existing methods. Algorithms for finding all prime implicants, essential prime implicants, and a near-minimum cover for multivalued switching functions are presented that are suitable for both computer and hand execution. These algorithms have been programmed in Fortran. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Su S.Y.H."]
Keywords: ["circuit realization of multivalued functions", "combinational circuits", "compound literals", "computer-oriented algorithms", "cubical notation"]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF OPTIMAL RECEIVER STRUCTURE FOR SIGNALS PHASE MODULATED SIMULTANEOUSLY BY TWO BINARY PROCESSES.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: A generalization of a previously described procedure for synthetizing optimal receiver structures is developed and applied to a receiver for signals phase modulated simultaneously by a binary pseudonoise signal and a binary data signal. Both binary signals are represented by discrete Markov processes, and the phase and delay of the signals are represented by continuous Markov processes.
Name: ["Cherdyntsev V.A.", "Davies A.C."]

Title: AIRCRAFT FAULT ISOLATION BASED ON PATTERN OF COCKPIT INDICATIONS: A HUMAN FACTORS APPROACH.
Abstract: It is estimated that the average time for isolating faulty components is about 24 minutes. A concept of fault detection software is proposed, which utilizes graphic aids and involves wide consideration of human factors. Performance results are given showing reduced time to detect flaws and increased accuracy of diagnosis.
Name: ["Burrows A.A.", "Miles W.L."]

Title: Minimizing the computation time for using the technique of sectioning for digital filtering of pictures
Abstract: This note considers the problem of minimizing the computation time required for digital filtering of pictures by the technique of sectioning. Direct enumeration on a computer was used to tabulate the optimum section size, and tables of the optimum section sizes are presented. The tables are compared with previously tabulated optimum sections for one-dimensional filtering; the optimal two-dimensional section sizes have linear dimensions twice as great as the optimal one-dimensional sections. To explain this discrepancy, analytical models are developed for the optimum one- and two-dimensional sections. The analytical models verify the tabulated data on optimum section size, and demonstrate why optimal two-dimensional sections are greater in size than corresponding one-dimensional sections. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Hunt B.R."]
Keywords: ["by sectioning", "digital filtering", "fast fourier transforms", "picture processing", "minimizing computation"]

Title: Invariant Estimates in the Statistical Theory of Optimal Systems. | INVARIANTNYE OTSENKI V STATISTICHESKOI TEORII OPTIMAL'NYKH SISTEM.
Abstract: An attempt is made to apply the methods of the theory of groups for the determination of optimal systems. These methods can be used only if a problem is invariant under some transformation group G such that given conditions are fulfilled. A large class of invariant vector-valued signals is described by a model. A method to determine optimal invariant estimates is described.
Name: ["Shaikin M.E."]

Title: ASSOCIATIVE PARALLEL PROCESSING SYSTEM FOR NON-NUMERICAL COMPUTATION.
Abstract: A systems design is postulated for a symbol processing machine (SPM) employing associative storage principles. The storage requirements, such as data structures and their manipulation, and the need for internal and external communication and control are evaluated. A storage system is proposed, based on a linear array (or string) or storage cells each holding one symbol plus control logic, which may be associatively addressed in parallel. Using this concept a set of cell commands has been developed and the overall storage system shown (using simulation techniques) to have considerable advantages when performing symbolic processing algorithms. Refs.
Name: ["Beaven P.A.", "Lewin D.W."]

Title: PREDICTION AND CONTROL OF TRACTOR STABILITY TO PREVENT REARWARD OVERTURNING.
Source: Transactions of the American Society of Agricultural Engineers
Abstract: A mathematical model was developed to predict rearward overturning behavior of a tractor for any set of initial conditions of angle of tip and angular velocity. The tractor was then simulated on a digital computer using a phase plane approach to determine stability criteria covering a wide range of operating conditions. A control system was designed based on stability criteria.
Name: ["Mitchell B.W.", "Zachariah G.L.", "Liljedahl J.B."]

Title: UNIFILAR SOURCES AND THE SOURCE APPROXIMATION PROBLEM.
Abstract: The problem of giving an approximate description of a discrete time finite alphabet information source is considered. Specifically certain classes of finite state source models are considered. The models are assumed to be unifilar (or state calculable). Special attention is devoted to the class of linear models and to the class of renewel models. Both classes are shown to possess a number of interesting properties which make them useful for approximation purposes. The unavoidable discrepancy between a source and its approximation is discussed. Certain results characterizing this discrepancy are derived and in a heuristic discussion some possible implications to the coding problem are indicated. The problems involved are claimed to be extremely difficult and most of them are leunsolved.
Name: ["Ericson Thomas"]

Title: Adaptive computer control of a glass coating process
Abstract: This paper presents the development and implementation of an on-line adaptive controller in an industrial process. The process, drawing and coating of glass rod used in the manufacture of resistors, is described briefly and the control problem formulated. The proposed control system, based on an on-line digital computer system, is outlined. Synthesis of the adaptive controller, including an identification technique and closed loop optimization strategy, is presented. Software development, testing, and implementation of the controller is described; special emphasis is given to on-line programming techniques. Results of the implementation are presented and the development summarized. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Thomas R.L.", "Goodson R.E.", "Harter E.J."]
Affiliations: [' Process Technology', ' Purdue University', ' Process Technology']

Title: Synchronization for Unknown Signal Sequence by Learning Procedure
Abstract: Methods of synchronization for an unknown signal sequence by learning procedure, which computes a posteriori probabilities for the signal location, are presented. First, to avoid the difficulties of the interference between successive intervals, a signal sequence with ample guard spaces for getting ‚Äòrid of the interference is treated. Next, the case without guard space is treated. To the nonsupervised case, some methods are applied. The methods proposed in this paper have a form of double learning with respect to the unknown signal form and the signal location. Also some results of computer simulation are presented. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Tamura S.", "Tanaka K."]

Title: COMPUTER CONTROL AND DATA ACQUISITION OF A TIDAL MODEL.
Source: Natl Res Counc Can, Div Mech Eng, Mech Eng Rep MH-110
Abstract: A large tidal model of the St. Lawrence River covering the region from Montreal to Ile du Bic is connected directly to a mini computer for data acquisition and control of the tidal boundary. Concepts for the design and operation of a computer based system for this application are described. Details of an adaptive feedback controller for diurnal tides are given.
Name: ["Funke E.R."]

Title: Optimal Discretization of Continuous Signals. | [OPTYMALNA DYSKRETYZACJA SYGNALU GIAGLEGO.]
Abstract: A method of optimal selection of sampling and quantization rates is worked out for continuous signals. It is based on information-quantity criterion and mean-square error estimation. A method is given for evaluating the probabilistic properties of the signal and for determining the error in reproducing the signal from its discrete representation, using the prescribed characteristics of the signal, parameters of discretization and method of interpolation. The problem of optimal discretization of continuous signals subject to additional constraints concerning admissible values of discretization parameters is formulated and solved. Solutions are given in a form convenient for practical applications.
Name: ["Wydro Kornel"]

Title: ON-LINE IDENTIFICATION IN AN UNKNOWN STOCHASTIC ENVIRONMENT.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The problem of parameter estimation for linear discrete-time plants is discussed. The characteristics of the disturbing noise terms are unknown. An algorithm with on-line capability which yields consistent estimates is derived.
Name: ["Wouters Willy R."]

Title: A parameter-free clustering model
Abstract: One way to compare clustering techniques is in terms of the part done by the computer and the part controlled by the user. This paper presents a mathematical formulation of the clustering problem in which no parameters to be controlled by the user are included, thus no outside interference is required. The model was applied to clustering data points defined in a multi-dimentional space. The experiments demonstrate that the partition depends mainly upon the structure inherent in the data set. This approach is particularly useful in the case where no preliminary information, as to the number of categories or their distribution, is available. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Gitman I."]

Title: COLOR DISTANCE AND GEODESICS IN COLOR 3 SPACE.
Abstract: A method is given for determining the ‚Ä≥color distance‚Ä≥ between two arbitrary colors for use in evaluating errors in transmission and processing of color images. The problem of determining the distance is defined by a riemannian metric and a gradient method is shown for computing the geodesics corresponding to the metric. Results are illustrated with graphs and tables.
Name: ["Jain Anil K."]

Title: Effect of random errors on generalized distance computations
Abstract: There is growing interest in devising non-statistical classification algorithms for multivariate populations. Statistical algorithms are not appropriate if an adequate statistical model for the population does not exist. Such algorithms may be sensitive (unstable) to errors in their data. The particular case of populations of objects characterized by binary attributes susceptible to independent and equiprobable errors is examined. The determination of stability requires the prior computation of the expectation of a statistical function of the object-pair similarities. The order and convergence of a numerical approxiamation for determining these expectation with prescribed accuracy is examined in the sub-asymptotic case in which normality does not occur. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Jackson D.M.", "White L.J."]
Affiliations: [' University of Waterloo', ' The Ohio State University']

Title: SIMPLIFICATION OF AND, EXCLUSIVE-OR SWITCHING FUNCTION.
Source: J Inst Telecommun Eng New Delhi
Abstract: The use of Exclusive-Or circuits often lead to significant circuit reduction. However, the minimization of circuit containing Exclusive-Or gates is quite different from the minimization of conventional And-Or circuits. In this paper, a simple tabular method has been presented for the near minimal realization or arbitrary Boolean function by networks composed of And and Exclusive-Or circuits.
Name: ["De Sarkar S.C.", "Bandyopadhyay S.", "Choudhury A.K.", "Ghosh S."]

Title: Locus Procedure for the Estimation of System Parameters in the Time Domain. | ORTSKURVENVERFAHREN ZUM BESTIMMEN VON SYSTEMPARAMETERN IM ZEITBEREICH.
Abstract: A procedure is given to determine the values of the model parameters from the system response of given deterministic test signals. The locus procedure is applicable only in the time domain and is valid exactly for the given corresponding transfer function. Models are indicated for proportional plants which occur often in practise. These models approximate plants of n-th order by substitute plants with only two time constants and corresponding order.
Name: ["Gitt W."]

Title: Polo problem oriented language organizer
Abstract: The design process requires that engineers integrate the operation of several separate but related subtasks. The result of each subtask either creates data for the next lower level in the design, or dictates that earlier decisions be modified before proceeding further. The use of the computer as an aid to design can lead to a number of problems with respect to communication, which do not exist in the conventional design process. Problem Oriented Language (POL) supervisory systems such as ICES and the Translator Generator are available for engineers to use in communicating with the computer. However, a number of problems concerning data management and machine dependence indicate that a second look at POL supervisory systems is needed. The purpose of this paper is to present a brief review of the development of current Pol's and to present the concept of the POLO system. POLO is a machine independent prototype computer system whose purpose is to provide engineers with an environment in which thay can develop their own computer-aided design environment. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Lopez L.A."]

Title: STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS AND THEIR CONNECTIONS.
Abstract: The class of stochastic systems is defined and its closeness with respect to all possible connections by which large-scale systems are composed is proved. The concept of a decision function as the main characteristic of a stochastic system is introduced. The relations between the decision functions of the main types of connections of stochastic systems and those of connected systems are established yielding the means to find the decision functions of any composed stochastic system given the decision functions of the components. The stochastic system can serve as a model of a system with indeterministic behavior in the general statistical theory of control processes. A summary in Russian is included.
Name: ["Pugachev V.S."]

Title: COMPUTATION OF THE LIMITED INFORMATION MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD ESTIMATOR.
Abstract: Computation of the Limited Information Maximum Likelihood Estimator (LIMLE) of the set of coefficients in a single equation of a system of interdependent relations is sufficiently complicated to detract from other potentially interesting properties. A numerically stable estimation scheme based on Householder transformations and the singular value decomposition is presented. The analysis permits a convenient demonstration of equivalence with the Two Stage Least Squares Estimator (TSLSE) in the instance of just identification.
Name: ["Dent Warren", "Golub Gene H."]

Title: Approximate Calculation of Input Functions for Sequential Programming Systems on a Hybrid Analog Computer. | [DIE NAEHERUNGSWEISE BERECHNUNG VON EINGANGSFUNKTIONEN FUER PROGRAMMSTEUERUNGSSYSTEME AUF EINEM HYBRIDEN ANALOGRECHNER.]
Abstract: It is shown how it is possible to obtain approximate solutions of input functions also in case of complex system and complicated programs. Procedures with variable and with constant intervals are differentiated. Two illustrative examples are included.
Name: ["Ljubimow Eduard", "Schoenefeld Reinhold"]

Title: Muscle spindles in muscle control - III. Analysis of adaptive system model
Abstract: As an extension of a previous paper (Inbar, 1972/II) wherein the servo model of muscle control was analyzed and found insufficient in describing muscle control phenomena, an optimal adaptive model is proposed, where muscle spindles serve as the sensors of muscle dynamics. The concept of an adaptive system is defined and illustrated within the framework of an algorithmic adaptive, or "learning" scheme. A speculative attempt is made to correlate the various adaptive model components with the anatomical structures involved in muscle control. The paper concludes with a general discussion of the adaptive system approach to physiological systems. ¬© 1972 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Inbar G.F."]

Title: Comments on ‚ÄúOn the Identification of Variances and Adaptive Kalman Filtering‚Äù
Abstract: It has been found that a modification is required in the test proposed in a paper by Mehra. The purpose of this test is to tell whether or not identification is complete. This modification is described and an example showing the need for the modification is given. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Alspach D.L."]

Title: Real-Time Simulation of Multihead Tape Units
Abstract: The main result of this paper is that, given a Turing machine with several readwrite heads per tape, one can effectively construct an equivalent multitape Turing machine with a single read-write head per tape, which runs at precisely the same speed. This result implies that serial storage may be used to handle files requiring several points of immediate two-way read-write access without interruptions for rewinds, etc. It also yields simplified proofs of several results in the literature of computational complexity. ¬© 1972, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Fischer P.C.", "Meyer A.R.", "Rosenberg A.L."]
Keywords: ["buffer", "computational complexity", "multihead tape units", "multitape turing machine", "real-time computation"]
Affiliations: [' Department of Applied Analysis and Computer Science', ' Project MAC', 'IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center']

Title: On Sampled-Data Optimization in Distributed Parameter Systems
Abstract: A system of parabolic partial differential equations is transformed into ordinary differential equations in a Hilbert space, where the system operator is the infinitesimal generator of a semigroup of operators. A sampled-data problem is then formulated and converted into an equivalent discrete-time problem. The existence and uniqueness of an optimal sampled-data control is proved. The optimal control is given by a linear sampled-states feedback law where the feedback operator is shown to be the bounded self-adjoint positive semidefinite solution of a Riccati operator difference equation. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Lee K.Y.", "Barr R.O."]

Title: ON A GENERALIZATION OF THE STATISTICAL LINEARIZATION METHOD.
Abstract: A method of studying the accuracy of nonlinear, nonstationary stochastic systems based on the statistical linearization of nonlinear functions by means of canonical expansions of random functions is given. The suggested scheme of statistical linearization preserves the coefficients of the canonical expansions. The mathematical expectation and coordinate functions are obtained by minimizing the mean square error. The study of the accuracy of nonlinear, nonstationary stochastic systems is reduced to the investigation of nonlinear, nonstationary deterministic systems for mathematical expectations and coordinate functions.
Name: ["Sinitsin I.N."]

Title: Application of Evolutionary Gradientless Extremum Planning of Experiments for Statical Optimization of Technological Processes of Flotation. | [PRIMENENIE EVOLYUTSIONNOGO BEZGRADIETNOGO EKSTREMAL'NOGO PLANIROVANIYA EKSPERIMENTOV DLYA STATICHESKOI OPTIMIZATSII TEKHNOLOGICHESKIKH PROTSESSOV FLOTATSIONNOGO OBOGASHCHENIYA.]
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii, Gornyi Zhurnal
Abstract: The use of saturated plans for the selection of an extreme point in the investigated region and for the movement towards the extremum, based on this choice, is proposed. It is proved that for a guaranteed selection of an extreme point, taking into account all the triple interactions, it is sufficient to apply the constructed saturated plans in a special way. Rules for the construction of such plans and examples are given.
Name: ["Povolotskii V.S."]

Title: On a Method of Sequential Pattern Recognition
Abstract: In this paper, a multistage linear programming method of pattern recognition is proposed. The usual n-dimensional linear program has been split up into n stages of a one-dimensional linear program in such a way that more and more patterns belonging to two classes A and B are correctly classified as we proceed to higher and higher stages. It has been shown that if the threshold is kept fixed for all the stages, the formulation of the problem entails a preprocessing of the feature coordinates; on the other hand, if the threshold is allowed to be different values in different stages, no such preprocessing is required. The application of the proposed method for the recognition of two handwritten Bengali characters has been discussed and compared with the results of other methods. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Som A.", "Nath A.K."]
Affiliations: [' Bramhananda Keshab Chandra College', ' Jadavpur University']

Title: ON TWO METHODS OF A DISCRETE SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION.
Abstract: The maximum-likelihood method and the generalized least-squares method for the discrete identification are compared. On the basis of algorithms for computers, conclusions are drawn about the possibility of the application of these methods, about their numerical importance for the case of different noise structures. The actual importance of this study is shown.
Name: ["Banyasz Cs.", "Gertler J."]

Title: KALMAN INVERSE FILTER WITH DISCRETE TIME OBSERVATIONS.
Source: Bull Acad Pol Sci, Ser Sci Tech
Abstract: The author derives the algorithms of inverse continuous-discrete and discrete filtering on the basis of the state-space approach. Two cases (white and colored measurement noise) are examined.
Name: ["Porebski W."]

Title: Complexity of Realizing Asymptotically Optimal Codes by Constant Depth Schemes. | SLOZHOST' REALIZATSII ASIMPTOTICHESKI OPTIMAL'NYKH KODOV SKHEMAMI POSTOYANNOI GLUBINY.
Abstract: The complexity of schemes realizing linear codes was studied. It is shown that the scheme G of constant depth can be constructed, which realizes a linear code, with rate R and code distance greater than dn, the complexity of which is not greater than c//1n log n and depth is not greater than c//2 log n, where c//1 and c//2 do not depend on n. Similar lower bounds are also given. These bounds show that it is impossible to receive further essential simplifications of such schemes. The upper bounds, which are more complicated, are received by method of random processes.
Name: ["Gel'fand S.I.", "Dobrushin R.L."]

Title: ADAPTIVE ALGORITHM FOR DETERMINING VARIATIONS OF THE CHARACTERISTICS OF AN OBSERVED RANDOM PROCESS.
Abstract: An adaptive algorithm is proposed for the determination of the variations of the characteristics of an observed random process. It is postulated that the indicated variations behave according to the law of an unobservable homogeneous Markov chain with unknown transition probabilities. The number of states of the Markov chain and the conditional distribution functions for the observed variables are presumed to be known. At each instant (discrete time) the a posteriori distribution with respect to the unobservable states of that chain is computed. An algorithm converging to the true values is described for estimating the unknown transition probabilities of the chain. An example is given of the operation of the formulated adaptive algorithm in the probabilistic model of a Markov chain with observables having a binomial distribution function.
Name: ["Linkin V.M.", "Naumov B.P."]

Title: CONTROL IN NETWORKS WITH A DESIGNATED BRANCH INDETERMINACY.
Abstract: Optimization problems for stochastic networks are considered. Existence and uniqueness theorems for minimum path and maximum flow are deduced under stringent constraints on the network, and the problem of constructing a flow minimizing a special type of penalty function is investigated.
Name: ["Vinogradskii A.S."]

Title: LINE FILTER.
Abstract: An arrangement is shown which will remove or filter the line data i order to simplify the recognition process, in character recognition systems which must recognize characters written on a preprinted line.
Name: ["Kerchmar K."]

Title: Partially automated psychiatric interviewing-a research tool
Source: Journal of Nervous and Mental Disease
Abstract: Computers are currently not capable of conducting useful psychiatric interviews without human assistance. This is because of difficulties involved in extracting meaning from the wide range of verbal expressions produced by psychiatric patients. Fully automated nontrivial interviewing will have to await developments in the field of computational linguistics. In the meantime, a human translator placed in the computer-patient loop can perform the meaning extraction task, enabling the program to conduct interviews with patients. Such a system provides a tool for researchers interested in studying interview theory and psychiatric classification. A prototype interviewing program that was designed to conduct initial psychiatric interviews and which incorporates a human translator has successfully interviewed several hospitalized psychiatric patients. ¬© 1972 by The Williams & Wilkins Co.
Name: ["Hilf F.D."]

Title: Optimal filtering in linear distributed parameter systems with multiple time delays
Abstract: This paper considers the problem of state estimation in a noisy medium of a process described by a linear partial differential equation subject to multiple time delays in the system model as well as in the observation process. The filter equations for the optimal estimate and variance are obtained in the form of partial integro-differential equations, the complexity of which depends on the system. ¬© 1972 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Shukla V.", "Srinath M.D."]
Affiliations: [' Southern Methodist University', ' Sir George Williams University']

Title: Toward a Formal Theory of Modeling and Simulation: Structure Preserving Morphisms
Abstract: A simulation consists of a triple of automata (system to be simulated, model of this system, computer realizing the model). In a valid simulation these elements are connected by behavior and structure preserving morphisms. Informational and complexity considerations motivate the development of structure preserving morphisms which can preserve not only global, but also local dynamic structure. A formalism for automaton structure assignment and the relevant weak and strong structure preserving morphisms are introduced. It is shown that these preservation notions properly refine the usual automaton homomorphism concepts. Sufficient conditions are given under which preservation of the local state space structure (weak morphism) also forces the preservation of component interaction. The strong sense in which these conditions are necessary is also demonstrated. This provides a rationale for making valid inferences about the local structure of a system when that of a behaviorally valid model is known. ¬© 1972, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Zeigler B.P."]

Title: Analysis of a Data Transmission System with Decision Feedback in the Presence of Burst Errors. | ANALIZA SYSTEMU TRANSMISJI DANYCH Z DECYZYJNYM SPRZEZENIEM ZWROTNYM W OBECNOSCI ZAKLOCEN SERYJNYCH.
Abstract: The forward channel in this system is noisy, binary and with memory. The feedback channel is ideal. Description of the forward channel is given by the Gilbert model. Formulas for statistical dependence of two successive received sequences are expressed as a function of sequence length, feedback channel delay time and parameters of the forward channel model. Using the graph method, the probability of a correct ultimate decision and system efficiency is evaluated. The system efficiency is defined as a ratio of the number of transmitted information elements to the number of all the transmitted elements. Systems parameters are determined for a code applied to: 1) bursts of errors detection; 2) detection of independent errors; 3) partial correction and detection of independent errors. Estimated parameters are compared with corresponding ones of an analogous system with memoryless, binary, symmetric forward channel of the same capacity as the memory channel. Computations are performed for two algorithms of the system operation: 1) transmission of a single message and repetition, when errors are detected; 2) transmission of messages in blocks containing M code sequences and repetition of the whole block when errors are detected.
Name: ["Rykaczewski Roman"]

Title: LOW-COST ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY.
Abstract: The design of two high-density MOS associative memory cells is described. The first cell is suitable for data management applications, having three internal states including the DON'T CARE (mask) condition. The second cell is suitable for parallel processing applications and has the capability of selected bit writing. Both cells consume about 20 mil**2 of silicon area, which allows the implementation of 512 bits on a chip. Varactor bootstrapping is used to enhance the storage node voltage for improved cell operation. The use of a compatible bipolar transistor is discussed.
Name: ["Mundy Joseph L.", "Burgess James F.", "Joynson Reuben E.", "Neugebauer Constantine"]

Title: Adaptation and identification by comparison of models | ADAPTION UND IDENTIFIKATION DURCH MODELLVERGLEICH
Abstract: A method for parameter identification of linear or linearizable control systems is pesented. The method is distinguished by simplicity and a relatively short measure time. After this the results of analog simulation are shown. Finally an analysis of the efficiency of the method with a reference to special applications in adaptive control systems is given.
Name: ["Nitsche H."]

Title: Learning characteristics of the human operator in man/machine system (Japanese)
Abstract: This paper deals with the problem of the learning characteristics of the human operator in a compensatory tracking control task. It is already known that the human operator can learn and adapt himself to changes in control dynamics. It is therefore essential for a system designer to analyze the learning behavior of the human operator. However, the process of learning has not been investigated in much detail. A new method to assess the learning process of a human operator is proposed by fitting the experimental curve to logarithmic function. Variations of the coefficients are then considered to provide a measure for the learning speed. The new method of evaluating the learning process is applied to the cases of step response and frequency response. Also, in order to reduce the training interval, the method of performance scores display is used for the detection of the optimal switching point in a relay control system. The results of these investigations are expected to be of use in the design of man made machine systems.
Name: ["Akashi H.", "Hashimoto H."]

Title: Identification of a Dynamic System by the Maximum-Likelihood Method, Using the ODRA 1204 Digital Computer. | IDENTYFIKACJA OBIEKTU DYNAMICZNEGO NA PODSTAWIE ZASADY NAJWIEKSZEJ WIAROGODNOSCI NA MASZYNIE CYFROWEJ ODRA 1204.
Abstract: An algorithm is given for identifying the parameters of a linear dynamic system with m inputs and a single output. It is assumed that the plant operates in the presence of random disturbances with a rational probability density function. Identification is performed on the basis of measured data on inputs and output of the plant Records are taken in the course of normal operation of the plant. An approach is based on the application of the maximum - likelihood principle. An example of the application of the algorithm, using a digital computer ODRA-1204 is given. Difficulties due to accomplishing such a process and a way of assuring the convergence of the algorithm are given. Computational examples are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithm.
Name: ["Siekierski Tadeusz J."]

Title: Continuously valued logic
Source: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: Motivated by the recognized inadequacy of conventional logic for the representationand manipulation of variables in areas related to artificial intelligence, this paper addresses itself to the investigation of the formal systems obtained by extending well-known connectives to continuous arguments. The studied systems, called "soft algebras," are generalizations of Boolean algebras in that they satisfy all the axioms of the latter ones except the laws of complementarity, i.e., x+=1 and x=0. It is shown that every soft algebra is a bounded, distributive and symmetric lattice. A specific soft algebra, the family of all functions of n variables in the closed interval [0, 1], is analyzed in great detail. This particularlalgebra is a formal unification of many recent results concerning "fuzzy" logic. It is shown that every "soft" function can be canonically represented by a pair of normal expressions, i.e., each soft function is representable by a double array of tables (a generalization of the truth-table representation of Boolean functions). Also, a synthesis and two-level minimization procedure, which is a generalization of the Quine-McCluskey method, is given. ¬© 1972 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Preparata F.P.", "Yeh R.T."]
Affiliations: ['Department of Electrical Engineering University of Illinois at Urbana', ' University of Illinois at Urbana', ' University of Texas at Austin']

Title: Minimization of Finite Automata. | MINIMIZATSIYA KONECHNYKH AVTOMATOV.
Abstract: Tow approaches for minimization of finite automata are compared: reduction of the number of their internal states, and minimization of the physical implementation of the automata. Methods of resolving the first problem are reviewed; the second approach is represented by an original algorithm.
Name: ["Shinshkov D.B."]

Title: Image improvement using bidimensional recursive filters of the Wiener type | BILDVERBESSERUNG MIT ZWEIDIMENSIONALEN, REKURSIVEN FILTERN VOM WIENER TYP
Abstract: The relationship between a radioactivity distribution and its scintigram is described by plication. Computer scintigraphy should cancel this plication by suitable filters and thus reconstruct the radioactivity distribution as accurately as possible. Because there are no noise free scintigrams, filters of the Wiener type are used to advantage. These can be divided into 3 classes: frequency filters, plication filters and recursive filters. The present study deals with the latter. Such filters have the advantage over frequency filters of also working in the local area, but they require a smaller number of coefficients than equivalent plication filters and are simple to compute. The algorithm of recursive filters can be derived from inversion of a plication and is therefore adapted to problems of image improvement.
Name: ["Pistor P."]

Title: Search Model. | O PEWNYM MODELU WYSZUKIWANIA.
Abstract: A model of information search is defined, which is based on the probability distribution of the set of all admissible arrangements of elements in a set of places. The fundamental relationships for sequential and dichotomous search are derived for this model. The form of the optimal algorithm of sequential search is derived. It is shown that the algorithm depends on the probabilities of finding the desired element in each place of the set of places. These probabilities, in turn, are functions of the distribution of a random vector (Z//1, Z//2,. . . ,Z//n) where Z//1, (j equals 1,. . . ,n) maps the contents j of this space, and also of the probabilities (P(A/i) which are the indices of the frequencies of location requiring search of an element with the sign i. The mean number of trials for sequential search is determined. For dichotomous search on the basis of the concepts indicated above, it has been proved that in some particular cases, the optimal trial is that which checks the content of the place exactly in the middle of the set of places in question.
Name: ["Subieta Kazimierz"]

Title: The SIFT Algorithm for Fundamental Frequency Estimation
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: In this paper a new method for estimating Fo, the fundamental frequency of voiced speech versus time, is presented. The algorithm is based upon a simplified version of a general technique for fundamental frequency extraction using digital inverse filtering. It is demonstrated that the simplified inverse filter tracking algorithm (hereafter referred to as the SIFT algorithm) encompasses the desirable properties of both autocorrelation and cepstral pitch analysis techniques. In addition, the SIFT algorithm is composed of only a relatively small number of elementary arithmetic operations. In machine language, SIFT should run in several times real time while with special-purpose hardware it could easily be realized in real time. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Markel J.D."]

Title: PROGRAMMING MEANS FOR SIMULATION OF LOGICAL NETWORKS - 1.
Abstract: This is the first of a three-part tutorial aeries on digital-computer simulation. The author considers logical networks as analogous to neural nets. In this part, a simulation program is presented for a first-generation computer and uses the language MOST as it is a typical first generation language which has been applied in the computer ODRA 1013 in the Biophysical Institute of Charles University in Prague, Czechoslovkia.
Name: ["Kindler Evzen"]

Title: Automatic Error Analysis for Determining Precision
Abstract: The problem considered is that of evaluating a rational expression to within any desired tolerance on a computer which performs variable-precision floating-point arithmetic operations. For example, the expression might be œÄ/(œÄ + 1/2 - e) ‚àö2), which is rational in the data œÄ, e, ‚àö2. An automatic error analysis technique is given for determining, directly from the results of a trial low-precision interval arithmetic calculation, just how much precision and data accuracy are required to achieve a desired final accuracy. The techniques given generalize easily to the evaluation of many nonrational expressions. ¬© 1972, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Richman P.L."]

Title: Simplex Algorithm for Nonlinear Programming. | ALGORYTM SIMPLEX PROGRAMOWANIA NIELINIOWEGO.
Abstract: A non-gradient algorithm for unconstrained static optimization is considered, which is based on the Simplex method originally worked out by J. A. Nelder and R. Mead (see Engineering Index 1965 p 432). This algorithm has high accuracy for various ‚Ä≥goal‚Ä≥ functions, and a small approximately linear increase in the extent of the computation of a ‚Ä≥goal‚Ä≥ function for an increase in the dimensionality of the roblem. A modification of the algorithm, suggested by W. Spendley, for certain kinds of ‚Ä≥goal‚Ä≥ functions, is presented. A comparison is made of these algorithms, illustrated by two examples.
Name: ["Olinger Wiktor"]

Title: SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION HISTORY, METHODOLOGY, FUTURE PROSPECTS.
Abstract: System identification methods may be characterized as those which are suitable for real time operation and those which are not. The non-real time methods include frequency response identification, correlation methods, iterative schemes based upon such computational techniques as the gradient methods, etc. These methods are usually not suitable for real time implementation because of computer time requirements. Those system identification methods which are suitable for real time implementation are generally based upon state and sequential filter concepts. Generally, computer requirements are less for these methods than for the non-real time methods. A restriction of the real time methods is that a structure for the system must be asssumed and parameters identified within this structure. Techniques for structure validation are mentioned. System identification problems may be subdivided in several ways and some of these are mentioned. Finally, three general techniques for system identification are presented; techniques based on transfer function identification, learning model identification, and identification based on nonlinear filtering.
Name: ["Sage Andrew P."]

Title: Problem Associated with the Identification of Dynamic Systems in Factor Space. | [ZADACHA IDENTIFIKATSII DINAMICHESKIKH SISTEM V FAKTORPROSTRANSTVE.]
Abstract: The problem of dynamic systems identification over quadratic criteria of closeness is solved. The theorem of existence of generalized solutions being elements of normal factor space is proved. ‚Ä≥Energy‚Ä≥ norm is used in the factor space which permits finding solutions of a rather general form. Similar solutions may not be, for instance, point functions in a conventional sense. An approximate solution of the problem is defined in the normal space. A connection between generalized solutions and incorrectness of the problem is established. The suggested solution of the problem determines another approach for the solution of incorrect problems.
Name: ["Leonov Yu.P."]

Title: EFFICIENCY OF AN OPTIMUM SEARCH SYSTEM.
Abstract: The efficiency of a system which searches a channel carrying a useful signal is investigated. At each step the system scans that channel for which prior calculation shows the maximum a posteriori probability of signal presence.
Name: ["Filosofov L.V."]

Title: SEQUENTIAL TREATMENT OF INFORMATION TRANSMISSION.
Abstract: A situation is considered in which the sender of a message over a noisy channel is aware of what signals have actually been received at the other end. The sender and receiver agree sequentially on a coding which is optimal in that it minimizes the expected number of signals required to bring the receiver to a prescribed degree of certainty as to what message is intended. This process is termed interrogation of sender by receiver, and is a situation occurring in sequential experimentation. The solution to this sequential optimization problem yields automatically the concepts of information measure and of channel capacity, also a certain form of the coding theorems, and a sequential construction for the optimal coding.
Name: ["Whittle P."]

Title: DISPERSION EQUATION OF NONLINEAR PLANT IDENTIFICATION.
Abstract: A general identification equation for a nonlinear plant by random function dispersion methods is obtained. The optimal weighting function of a linearized nonlinear plant is given by a dispersion identification equation. Some practical examples are illustrated.
Name: ["Bunich A.L.", "Rajbman N.S."]

Title: A Digital Hardware Realization of a Random Number Generator
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: A digital random number generator that generates number sequences with either uniform or Gaussian distributions has been constructed in TTL digital hardware for use as a peripheral device to a DDP-S16 computer. The hardware design is based on an algorithm described by Rader, Rabiner, and Schafer [l]. Approximations to the Gaussian distribution are generated by summing NA +1 consecutive numbers from the uniform sequence, where NA (the number of additions) is specified by the user and is in the range 0‚â§NA‚â§213. Measurements of its autocorrelation function, power spectrum, and amplitude histograms indicate that the generator produces uncorrelated samples with amplitude distributions that are very close to the desired uniform or Gaussian distributions. For generating Gaussian numbers, the hardware generator operates at least 600 times faster than an equivalent software realization. Name: ["Perry J.L.", "Schafer R.W.", "Rabiner L.R."]

Title: Understanding natural language
Abstract: This paper describes a computer system for understanding English. The system answers questions, executes commands, and accepts information in an interactive English dialog. It is based on the belief that in modeling language understanding, we must deal in an integrated way with all of the aspects of language-syntax, semantics, and inference. The system contains a parser, a recognition grammar of English, programs for semantic analysis, and a general problem solving system. We assume that a computer cannot deal reasonably with language unless it can understand the subject it is discussing. Therefore, the program is given a detailed model of a particular domain. In addition, the system has a simple model of its own mentality. It can remember and discuss its plans and actions as well as carrying them out. It enters into a dialog with a person, responding to English sentences with actions and English replies, asking for clarification when its heuristic programs cannot understand a sentence through the use of syntactic, semantic, contextual, and physical knowledge. Knowledge in the system is represented in the form of procedures, rather than tables of rules or lists of patterns. By developing special procedural representations for syntax, semantics, and inference, we gain flexibility and power. Since each piece of knowledge can be a procedure, it can call directly on any other piece of knowledge in the system. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Winograd T."]

Title: POSSIBLE USE OF ADAPTIVE PROGRAMMING.
Abstract: Generalized adaptive programming algorithms are presented for process optimization of multivariable continuous plants, according to the optimization of some economical performance index (minimum costs, maximum production effectiveness, etc. ). The term ‚Ä≥adaptive programming‚Ä≥ points out somewhat vaguely the adaptation suggested by Ya. T. Tsypkin and by the necessity of a digital computer for the realization. The actual algorithmic scheme is a fourfold generalized perception scheme devised by a multivariable stochastic approximation method.
Name: ["Kocsis Janos"]

Title: Combination Bayesian and logical approach to analysis of normal and abnormal chromosome spreads
Abstract: Both hardware and software are being developed for a practical, inexpensive system for human chromosome analysis. The hardware allows a relatively untrained operator to generate chromosome arm length measurements directly in a small, dedicated 12-bit computer. Analysis programs using a combination of Bayesian probability and logical techniques perform karyotype analyses and score chromosomal aberrations using the list of arm lengths as their sole input. Performance compares favorably with that of human cytogeneticists using conventional methods of analysis. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Bender M.A.", "Kastenbaum M.A.", "Lever C.S.", "Pelster D.R."]
Affiliations: [' Vanderbilt University Medical School', ' Inc.', ' Operated by Union Carbide Corporation for the U.S. Atomic Energy Commission.Oak Ridge', ' Vanderbilt University']

Title: APPLICATION OF SAMPLING INSPECTION TO CORRECTIVE PLAN FOR PRODUCTION PROCESS.
Abstract: A corrective plan for the maintenance of production process whose capability is deteriorating in service is given. A special analysis, based on the Markov model of production process, is proposed. The dynamic characteristics from the initial state to the corrected state of production process are also analyzed with the Graphical Evaluation and Review Technique (GERT). From these analyses it is shown that the function of sampling inspection can be extended to the measure of process control.
Name: ["Ohta Hiroshi", "Kase Shigeo"]

Title: NUMERICAL EXPERIMENTS ON DUAL MATRIX ALGORITHMS FOR FUNCTION MINIMIZATION.
Abstract: Four algorithms of dual matrices for function minimization presented in an earlier paper are tested through several numerical examples. Three quadratic functions and five nonquadratic functions are investigated. For quadratic functions, the results show the convergence is achieved in at most n plus 1 iterations, where n is the number of variables. For nonquadratic functions, the results show that these algorithms are very stable and efficient. Also, the effects of the stepsize factor on these algorithms are investigated.
Name: ["Huang H.Y.", "Chambliss J.P."]

Title: Stochastic modelling of computer-regulated linear plants in noisy environments
Abstract: The purpose is the discrete-time stochastic modelling of a linear plant in single-loop direct digital feedback control, particularly with a constant reference input. The system receives dynamic inputs by the intrinsic noise of the digital quantizers, and from environmental disturbances, which are assumed to have rational spectral densities. An equation is derived in the deviation from its mean of the random feedback variable, y(k), consisting in a linear difference expression in y(k), a so-called autoregrcssion, equated to a sum of linear difference expressions in white noise sequences, so-called moving averages. The sum of these also is a moving average. The conclusion is The stochastic process of a computer-regulated linear plant in a single feedback loop, whose dynamic inputs are all quantization noise sources and environmental disturbances with rational spectra, can be expressed as a stationary mixed auto-regressive, moving-average (ARMA) model, which also has a rational spectral density. Features of the model useful for identification purposes are discussed. In particular an algorithm for the computation of the autocovariance function is derived for use in a forthcoming paper. ¬© 1972 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Lindberger N.A."]

Title: CONVERGENCE OF POTENTIAL FUNCTION TYPE LEARNING ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: Convergence theorems for some learning algorithms generated by a potential function are dealt with. The kernel function of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) as a potential function is used. The problem of how one may use ‚Ä≥teaching‚Ä≥ several times during the algorithm is considered, along with the case of noisy ‚Ä≥teaching‚Ä≥ . Algorithms are discussed which turned out to be particularly efficient in learning in unambiguous models by potential function type learning algorithms.
Name: ["Gyorfi L."]

Title: A vector cost function for efficient adaptation
Abstract: A vector coat function is proposed which makes adaptive control without complete plant identification more feasible, as the problem of adaptation simplifies to the solution of a set of partial difference equations. The characteristics of the system are defined in terms of matrix arrays, all of which need not be known a priori, but are determined in a learning and adapting loop. Some examples are discussed showing the practical implementation of the proposed algorithm. ¬© 1972 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Sinha N.K.", "Temple V.", "Rey A.J.-C."]

Title: ON FORMULATION OF STATE EQUATIONS FOR LINEAR NONSTATIONARY DISCRETE-TIME SYSTEM.
Abstract: Two compact, non-recursive forms of a state space description from the scalar difference equation of a linear nonstationary discrete-time system are given.
Name: ["Soukup Vaclav"]

Title: A Prototype Intelligent Robot that Assembles Objects from Plan Drawings
Abstract: An intelligent robot that recognizes and assembles three- dimensional objects by means of vidicon cameras, an articulated mechanical hand, and a digital computer is described. Its problem-solving functions include three essential parts: the recognition of macro-instructions from a human master, the recognition of the objects to be handled, and the decision making for executing the necessary tasks. The instruction is in the form of a three-view plan of a simple polyhedral assemblage whose overall spatial configuration is recognized together with its component parts. In this process the set of planes of the assemblage is disassembled into open shells; these are then reconstructed into closed shells to find the parts by solving a linear equation where the shell vectors are taken into consideration. In the object recognition, all the geometric features of polygonal prisms in the field of vision are extracted to find the specific parts required for the assembly. Further computation is made to search for the assembly procedure and is based on the restraint vectors of each object and consequent disassembly tree. Finally, the mechanical hand starts the autonomous manipulation of the parts so as to accomplish the assigned assembly. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Ejiri M.", "Uno T.", "Yoda H.", "Goto T.", "Takeyasu K."]

Title: STATE SPACE APPROACH TO DISCRETE LINEAR CONTROL.
Abstract: The state space approach to the synthesis of a class of discrete linear control systems is given. Both time-optimal and quadratic-cost problems are considered and a comparison to classical methods is made via the technique of pole assignment. The highlight of the paper is the state space theory of the ‚Ä≥output‚Ä≥ problems. This theory is limited to single-input single-output systems. Throughout the paper the following important idea accompanies the theory: optimality does not necessarily imply stability. As a matter of fact, certain measures had to be taken to ensure stability.
Name: ["Kucera Vladimir"]

Title: FACTORIZATION OF MATRICIAL SPECTRAL DENSITIES.
Abstract: A new iterative solution is given, for the problem of inner-outer factorization of matricial spectral density functions. Convergence properties of the solution are stated, and two methods of implementing the solution are given, together with an example.
Name: ["Tunnicliffe Wilson G."]

Title: Analysis of a Chainlike Neural Net with Lateral Inhibitions. | ANALIZA LANCUCHOWEJ SIECI NEURONOWEJ Z OBOCZNYMI HAMOWANIAMI.
Abstract: An N-link chain is considered as an example of a simple neuron-like network with lateral inhibitions. The introduction based on neurophysiological data makes it possible to present the mathematical description of a single link as well as the whole network with its nonlinear threshold characteristic. The network action and stability conditions are described using the Z transform method. Theoretical results are discussed and compared with experimental ones obtained by simulating the chain on a computer. Recent results are shown to justify previous experiments and to provide a basis for deeper and more accurate investigations of chain networks.
Name: ["Macukow Bohdan"]

Title: METHOD OF CONSTRUCTING SELF-LEARNING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: In general, the learning system is characterized by the learning method. The learning method proposed in this paper is one of the nonsupervised learning methods proposed by E. M. Braverman and Ya. Z. Tsypkin, in which the discrimination function is constructed successively by solving the minimization problem of the evaluation function via probability approximation. This learning method is characterized by the self-correcting learning process to which the convergence theorem with probability 1 is applied. Two self-learning systems are derived by this method and their learning capability is examined on the mixture distribution consisting of normal distributions.
Name: ["Watanabe Takashi", "Noguchi Shoichi"]

Title: Proximity measures for the classification of geometric figures
Abstract: A proximity relation is a fuzzy relation which is reflexive, symmetric, but not necessarily transitive. A quantitative measure of the proximity of two n-sided polygons is defined. Various properties of angular and dimensional proximities of triangles are investigated. A method for classifying a triangle as an ‚Äúapproximate right triangle, ‚Äù ‚Äúapproximate isosceles triangle, ‚Äù ‚Äúapproximate isosceles right triangle, ‚Äù ‚Äúapproximate equilateral triangle‚Äù or ‚Äúordinary triangle‚Äù is presented. A method used to classify a quadrangle as ‚Äúapproximate square, ‚Äù ‚Äúapproximate rectangle, ‚Äù ‚Äúapproximate rhombus, ‚Äù ‚Äúapproximate parallelogram, ‚Äù ‚Äúapproximate trapezoid‚Äù or ‚Äúordinary quadrangle‚Äù is also presented. The measures of proximity employed for this purpose have an intuitive interpretation. The results may be of use in pattern recognition, information retrieval and artificial intelligence. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Lee E.T."]

Title: On Determining Optimum Simple Golay Marking Transformations for Binary Image Processing
Abstract: A computer program has been written which is capable of evaluating all possible Golay marking transformations related to a particular pattern recognition task using an exhaustive search technique. Such evaluations are reported for separating two image data sets: one taken from biomedical microscopy; the other, aerial reconnaissance. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Preston K.", "Carvalko J.R."]

Title: Improved holographic matched filter systems for pattern recognition using a correlation method
Abstract: A multi-channel correlator for holographic matched filtering is described. The two-dimensional channels are separated spatially in the Fourier plane. This arrangement allows individual filters to be realized for each channel for different spatial frequency ranges etc. The multi-channel correlator is addressed by a generator of multiple object waves, i.e. by different directions of object illumination. Parallel and sequential evaluation of the correlation signals is possible. The efficiency and signal-to-noise ratio for both modes of operation are discussed. In each channel, linear superimposed multiple Vander-Lugt filters may be introduced to increase the over-all capacity of learning steps. The risk of over-exposure is small because the centres of the frequency spectra are separated on the hologram filter plate. With a multi-channel correlator, combined matched and feature filtering may be performed. Preliminary experimental results show that this method can be succesfully used in some cases where the results of simple matched filtering remain unsatisfactory. The results and discussions are presented from a more general point of view with some remarks concerning comparable methods and possible future aspects. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Winzer G.", "Douklias N."]

Title: A simple method for the control of divergence in Kalman-filter algorithms
Abstract: It is found that, under certain conditions, the estimation errors produced by the Standard Kalman-filter algorithm increase rapidly, and become unbounded, even though the predicted error covariance continues to decrease in accordance with the stability properties of the Kalman filter. A very simple modification, which freezes the filter gain when divergence is suspected, is suggested. The modified algorithm would keep these errors within bound without causing an appreciable increase in the computation burden. ¬© 1972 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Sriyananda H."]
Affiliations: [' The University of Wales Institute of Science and Technology']

Title: Distribution-Free Pattern Verification Using Statistically Equivalent Blocks
Abstract: A nonparametric classification procedure based on distribution-free tolerance regions is presented. Without knowledge of the class probability distributions, the procedure gives information about the expected performance of the classifier through use of only one sample of statistically independent observations from each class. With this procedure, a two-class discriminant can be designed for a given expected false alarm probability or for a given confidence that the false alarm probability is less than a given amount. Three ordering methods are presented that appear intuitively reasonable for minimizing the miss probability. Even though the methods do not, in general, meet this objective, they are easily implemented on a computer and can give good results. A procedure for obtaining a measure of the miss probability is also presented. These methods are applied to the problem of verifying the purported identity of a speaker from a sample of the speaker's voice. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Beakley G.W.", "Tuteur F.B."]
