Title: On the Estimation of Spectra by Means of Non‚Äêlinear Functions of the Covariance Matrix
Source: Geophysical Journal of the Royal Astronomical Society
Abstract: The estimation of spectra of random stationary processes is an important part of the statistics of random processes. There are several books on spectral analysis, e.g. Blackman & Tukey, Hannan, and Jenkins & Watts. As a rule, spectral estimators are quadratic functions of the realizations. Recently Capon suggested a new method for estimation of spectra of random fields, in which a non‚Äêquadratic function of the realization is used: he considered a homogeneous random field Œ∂(t,x<sub>1</sub>,x<sub>2</sub>), i.e. one which is stationary in time and space and a random function of the time and space co‚Äêordinates t, x<sub>1</sub>, x<sub>2</sub>. For the sake of expository convenience we shall consider ordinary stationary processes of time only, Œ∂(t); the generalization of our results to the case of random fields is easy. Comparison of the conventional spectral estimator and the ‚Äòhigh‚Äêresolution‚Äô estimator for an artificial example showed that the latter has less smoothing effect on the true spectrum (Capon). This was later confirmed by examples using real data (Capon). However, it was not clear whether for a finite realization the high‚Äêresolution estimator distorted the true spectrum, i.e. whether it behaved for example like a conventional estimator raised to some power. In the present paper we introduce and study a new class of spectral estimators which are generally non‚Äêlinear and non‚Äêquadratic functionals of the realizations. These estimators include the conventional and high‚Äêresolution ones, for which we shall give the approximate distributions. We derive under rather general conditions the limiting distribution of the new class of estimators, and illustrate them with several examples. As a matter of fact, these new estimators are weighted means of the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix, e.g. the arithmetic mean, geometric mean, and so on. Copyright ¬© 1972, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved
Name: ["Pisarenko V.F."]

Title: Representing program schemes in logic
Source: 13th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory, SWAT 1972
Abstract: Our principle technical results are the development of a family of first order logics (called FILs), the translation of classes of program schemes into these logics and the development of routine decision procedures for these representations. We feel the results are interesting because the class of schemes include a previously studied important class (Paterson's monadic non-intersecting loops class), because the decision procedures are routine and the new logics are natural, and finally because this work provides information and tools for the important problem of designing and compiling highly declarative programming languages. ¬© 1972 IEEE.
Name: ["Cherniavsky J.C.", "Constable R.L."]

Title: ON THE APPLICATION OF DIVERGENCE FOR THE EXTRACTION OF FEATURES FROM IMPERFECTLY LABELED PATTERNS.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The application of divergence as a criterion for the extraction of effective features from imperfectly labeled patterns is examined.
Name: ["Babu C.Chitti"]

Title: Pattern recognition problems in the study of carbon black
Abstract: This paper reviews certain pattern recognition problems associated with the study of carbon black. Two methods are described in which various properties are estimated by visual comparison with two-way charts. For studying fused aggregates, a new method of shape characterization has been developed, which should be of quite general utility. This method is based on representation of the silhouette of the aggregate as an ellipse with equivalent radii of gyration. Computer simulation is used to provide realistic models of aggregates, from which a relation is derived between the projected area of the silhouette (relative to that of a particle) and the volume of the aggregate. Automated methods are discussed for the determination of mean aggregate size and certain particle size parameters. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Medalia A.I.", "Hornik G.J."]

Title: Honest bounds for complexity classes of recursive functions
Source: 13th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory, SWAT 1972
Abstract: A new simplified proof of the McCreight-Meyer Honesty or Naming Theorem is given. Let t be a recursive function, and let F(t) be the set of recursive function computable within time bound t. Then it is shown that an honest recursive t‚Ä≤ can be found which is arbitrarily large on a dense set of arguments such that F(t) = F(t‚Ä≤). ¬© 1972 IEEE.
Name: ["Meyer A.R.", "Moll R."]

Title: AUTOMATION OF REMOTE INSTRUMENTS WITH AN ON-LINE COMPUTER.
Abstract: A discussion is given of the operation of a hierarchical computer system, consisting of host-satellite computers for automation of process and laboratory analyzers. The system applies accurate stream analysis to the overall control strategy of a process plant.
Name: ["Shah M.J."]

Title: SELF-LEARNING ESTIMATOR FOR TRACKING.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A heuristic technique for determining a sequence of estimates of a time-varying quantity, given only noisy observations of the quantity, is presented. The estimates are computed without knowledge of the generating mode of the time variation and without recourse to statistical models of the noise. The heuristic technique presented is called a self-learning estimator for tracking (SLET) because it works with little a priori information and no external supervision. Examples of the SLET tracking ability are presented.
Name: ["Eisenstein Bruce A."]

Title: NOTE ON THE LINEAR REINFORCEMENT SCHEME FOR VARIABLE-STRUCTURE STOCHASTIC AUTOMATA.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The linear reward-inaction scheme proposed previously (see EI 1970 p 233) for variable-structure stochastic automata was shown by a counter-example not to be optimal as concluded. However, the scheme is epsilon optimal and this conclusion detracts very little from the usefulness of the scheme from both mathematical and practical standpoints. A careful study of schemes proposed by others indicates that a method of stability analysis suggested for investigating convergence properties of reinforcement schemes is also incorrect.
Name: ["Viswanathan R.", "Narendra Kumpati S."]

Title: A Two-Level System of Stochastic Automata for Periodic Random Environments
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: ,A class of nonstationary environments with unknown but periodically changing probabilistic characteristics is considered. It is proposed to optimize the performance in an environment from this class by using a two-level system of variable-structure stochastic automata. The first level estimates the unknown period, while the second level operates suitably in the environment for one cycle, assuming that this estimate is the true period of the environment. The average output of the environment in this cycle is used as the input to the first level to determine the next estimate of the period. The optimal performance of this two-level system of automata in periodic random environments is demonstrated through computer simulations. Name: ["Narendra K.S.", "Viswanathan R."]

Title: Sample-based classification procedures derived from density estimators
Source: Journal of the American Statistical Association
Abstract: Parametric or nonparametric density estimators from a mixture of K distributions can be used to estimate the non-error rate of an arbitrary classification rule‚Äîand to construct a rule which maximizes estimated probability of correct classification. (For two multivariate normal distributions with common covariance matrix, this general criterion yields the usual linear discriminant.) Such a sample-based rule is asymptotically optimal under very general conditions. Often its ‚Äúapparent‚Äù non-error rate exceeds its true rate and is even optimistically biased as an estimator of the (unknown) optimal rule‚Äôs non-error rate; but the apparent rate converges to this optimum. ¬© Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Glick N."]

Title: The emptiness problem for automata on infinite trees
Source: 13th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory, SWAT 1972
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to give an alternative proof to the decidability of the emptiness problem for tree automata, as shown in Rabin4. The proof reduces the emptiness problem for automata on infinite trees to that for automata on finite trees, by showing that any automata definable set of infinite trees must contain a finitely-generable tree. ¬© 1972 IEEE.
Name: ["Hossley R.", "Rackoff C."]

Title: Information processing in the visual system
Abstract: In this paper an attempt is made to find a mathematical model for a number of mainly electrophysiological results concerning pattern recognition of mammals. After a short introduction to the applied theory of linear nervous nets, the investigations in the retina and geniculate body are interpreted as filters for space- and time-dependent oscillations. By application of the detection theory a functional model of the cortex regions 17, 18. ¬© 1972, MCB UP Limited
Name: ["Von Seelen W."]

Title: Asymptotic properties of random processes that arise in learning models
Abstract: This paper develops the properties of a stochastic learning model first reported in [1] and [2]. Some mathematical problems that appear to be interesting in themselves have arisen in the analysis of the limiting behavior of this stochastic model. Because of this these problems will be examined in a framework that is broader than that strictly required for model analysis. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Usachev Y.S."]

Title: The Assistant Mathematician: An interactive graphic programming language
Abstract: This paper describes an experimental interactive graphics system called The Assistant Mathematician (TAM). TAM is a prototype computational aid for non-programmers, particularly engineers or scientists, that uses ordinary two-dimensional mathematical notation as its language. The system includes an arithmetic interpreter, incorporating an extensive set of arithmetic operators on constants, variables, and arrays, that accepts hand-printed graphic (two-dimensional) input from a data tablet and supplies two-dimensional output via a projection display system. TAM is one of a class of potential interactive graphics systems useing natural language to improve man-machine communication. ¬© 1972, ACM. All rights reserved.

Title: Recognition of bubble chamber events exemplified by the Heidelberg automatic system
Abstract: Different methods in use for analysing bubble chamber pictures and the problem of automating the event recognition process are discussed. A new program system for fully automatic analysis is described and its capabilities are demonstrated. Starting from a digitization of an entire bubble chamber picture (3 stereo views) the program yields space reconstructed and topologically interpreted events. Finally some trends of the future are outlined. ¬© 1972.

Title: Remarks on the use of citation data in predictive models of scientific activity
Abstract: The relations between data, information and prediction are discussed with reference to a suggested Markov model for forecasting of the structure of scientific activity. A conclusion is that the output of mathematical operations, i.e. the predicted "state" or activity distribution, is not related to the input as a deductive or probabilistic consequence of its real information content, but rather to information attributed to the data by assumptions inherent in the method. This is a general difficulty in futures studies, namely that the openness of explanation of a phenomenon effectively limits the possibilities to extend the understanding of systems behaviour into predictive statements. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Borenius G.", "Schwarz S."]

Title: On learning systems
Abstract: The class of learning systems under consideration uses generalized linear algorithms which evaluate the appropriate parameters after processing the arbitrary groups of data. The algorithms reported earlier are obtained as particular cases. The properties of generalized algorithms are found, optimal algorithms are determined. The algorithms are used in construction of learning systems intended to estimate the characteristics of random sequences, for pattern recognition, communication, etc. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Tsykin Y.S."]

Title: Filtering and control performance bounds with implications on asymptotic separation
Abstract: A bound is derived on the accuracy in causally estimating a Gaussian process from nonlinear observations. Both additive Gaussian noise and Poisson observations are included. The bound is used to study the control of a stochastic linear dynamical system with nonlinear observations of either type and an average quadratic cost. An asymptotic Separation Theorem is established showing that a linear feedback control law, involving a state estimate, is asymptotically optimum as the accuracy of the state estimate approaches the bound. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Snyder D.L.", "Rhodes I.B."]

Title: On mixture distributions in pattern recognition
Abstract: This paper is concerned with the analysis of a class of problems involving mixture variates (functions of several random variables). The explicit inclusion of a mixture as a separate category in pattern recognition problems is studied and plausible forms for the mixing densities in such problems are derived. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Sacco W.J."]
Affiliations: ['U.S. Army Ballistic Research Laboratories Aberdeen Proving Ground']

Title: Computer output display of cells and cell features
Abstract: In recent years, several computer programs have been presented for the extraction of features from biological data in the form of digitized pictures. Most of these programs have dealt with the extraction of features from chromosomes or simple cells. In this paper a procedure and computer program is presented which locates and extracts features from a nerve cell characterized by having a cytoplasm, nucleus, and a nucleolus. The procedure design and use is facilitated because it is implemented in an interactive system where computer output display of digitized cells, histogram of cell optical density, and extracted cell features can be displayed. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Patrick E.A.", "Altman J.", "Wild R."]

Title: Optimizing control using fuzzy automata
Abstract: A method for the optimizing control using the stochastic or fuzzy automata has convergent characteristics which are superior to those of the random search method. In this paper, the convergent characteristics of the optimizing control using the fuzzy automata previously proposed by the authors are investigated with regard to the convergent coefficient of the reinforcement algorithm for the learning operation of the automata. It is shown that the convergent characteristics can be improved if the convergent coefficient is varied with respect to the objective functions. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Asai K.", "Kitajima S."]
Affiliations: [' University of Osaka Prefecture', ' Osaka City University']

Title: A method of computer generation of correlated Gaussian pseudo-random numbers
Source: USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics
Abstract: A METHOD is described for generating stationary and non-stationary sequences of pseudo-random Gaussian numbers with given correlation from sequences of independent bounded pseudo-random numbers with arbitrary distributions. The method is based on computing the discrete Fourier transform of the initial sequence, modified in accordance with the required energy spectrum. As a result of using the fast Fourier transformation algorithm, after N log<sub> 2</sub>N computer operations, N Gaussian numbers can be generated with a given energy spectrum of arbitrary shape; not more than N numbers of the initial sequence are expended in these operations. The method is useful for generating large blocks of high-quality correlated Gaussian numbers. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Mirkin L.I.", "Rabinovich M.A.", "Yaroslavskii L.P."]

Title: Estimation of the quality of the experts designing the training table in the pattern recognition problem
Source: USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics
Abstract: A METHOD is given for estimating the quality (skill) of the experts preparing the initial material for the solution of diagnostic and recognition problems. The method is constructed by variation of the parameters describing the representability of the material introduced by the experts. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Gulyamov D.Kh.", "Zhuravlev Yu.I."]

Title: Path accuracy limitations of inertially based flight trajectory control system in a turbulent environment
Abstract: Parameter optimization is a powerful technique for synthesizing optimal control systems for stochastic, reduced state feedback, fixed configuration control systems. This paper illustrates the application of parameter optimization to optimize inertial measurement based vertical and lateral control systems for a jet transport aircraft. The mean square gust induced path deviation is minimized subject to penalty on the mean square effector activity. The resulting solutions are presented as curves which display minimum RMS position error and parameter values as a function of RMS effector activity. The optimized solutions are compared to the performance achieved by a conventional trajectory control system using Instrument Landing System measurements. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Mackinnon D.", "Madden P."]

Title: Reconnaissance automatique des √©v√©nements sur les clich√©s de chambre √† bulles
Abstract: A new method for automatic scanning of bubble chamber films is proposed. Its main feature consists of using a specialized device for detecting information points as vertices, then allowing a fast image analysis which does not need a big computer. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["de Janti Ph.V."]

Title: Autonomous state classifications by dynamical systems
Abstract: A number of key areas of theoretical biology involve essentially similar formalisms and treat essentially similar questions; among these areas are the theories of (micro- physical) measurement, pattern recognition, classification and discrimination mechanisms, and pattern generation. It is pointed out that, in each of these areas, we must ultimately deal with a dynamical system which is, in some sense, classifying its own states in an unambiguous way, on the basis of its intrinsic autonomous dynamics. We call such systems autonomous state classifiers; we characterize these systems mathematically and deduce a number of their elementary properties. The manner in which these properties manifest themselves in the areas of theoretical biology enumerated above is also briefly discussed. ¬© 1971.
Name: ["Rosen R."]
Affiliations: [' State University of New York at Buffalo']

Title: A discriminant method of clustering
Abstract: A parametric method for dividing a heterogeneous multivariate population into components is proposed. The method includes the following operations: (1) The mixed population is divided into two parts by a linear discriminant function with arbitrary coefficients; (2) The parameters of both parts are evaluated and then a new linear discriminant function is built, determining the second division. This new division is shown to be better (i.e., to provide a less misclassification probability) than the initial one; (3) The change in direction of the dividing hyperplane found in this way is extrapolated until the best division (in the above sense) in this extrapolation course is achieved; (4) A discriminant correction is carried out, determining a new course of extrapolation, and so on. This process may be controlled by analysing the one-dimensional distribution obtained by mapping the multivariate distribution into the line normal to the dividing hyperplane. Division into several components is made by successive dichotomies. Some problems concerning the use of finite samples are discussed. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Urbakh V.Yu."]

Title: A stochastic approach to finding the zero of a function
Source: USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics
Abstract: THE function whose zero is sought is assumed to be the realization of a stochastic process and the conditional probability density (with respect to the computed values of the function) of the root position is determined. When seeking the zero, the function is computed successively at the point where this density has its maximum. The optimality, convergence, and connection with regula falsi, of this procedure are discussed. The algorithm is applied to the case when the function retains the same sign in the neighbourhood of its zero. Considerable attention has been paid in recent years to seeking optimal computational methods for solving problems such as finding the zero or extremum of a one-dimensional function specified in a closed interval. Most results in this field have been obtained by a game-theoretic approach; initially, minimax algorithms were used [1] i.e. algorithms optimal in the "worst" case (the functions to be minimized were assumed unimodal, and the functions whose zeros were sought, monotonie). Later, minimax search strategies that took account of the subtler properties of the function, the possibility of computational errors (see e.g. [2]) and a lag in the results of measurements [3], were devised. The results of [1] were also extended to the case (see e.g. [4]) when, at each search step, the value of the function is determined simultaneously at several points. There was a roughly parallel development in the field of extremum problems (see e.g. [5-7]), in which a probability measure is specified in the class of investigated functions; this provides the basis for using statistical decision theory in the development of optimal computational methods. For instance, step-by-step optimal algorithms were devised in [6-7] for seeking the absolute extremum of a multi-extremal function (including the case when the measurements are distorted by noise). This stochastic approach is extended in the present paper to the problem of finding the zero of a function. In Section 1, a possible means for introducing a probability measure is discussed and the conditional probability density (with respect to the function values computed during the search) of the root position induced by the measure is determined. The point at which the density has its maximum is shown in Section 2 to be approximated by a simple inequality. This inequality, which depends on the computational results at previous search steps, retains its properties when the stochastic description is modified to suit problems in which the function retains the same sign of the interval containing its zero (Section 3). Section 4 proposes recurrent testing (function computation) at each search step, at the point of the interval corresponding to our inequality; the convergence of this algorithm is discussed. Section 5 discusses a test selection criterion, relative to which the asymptotic inequality for the root position proves to be an exact optimal solution. This root search method can be used regardless of the signs of the function at the ends of the interval containing its zero. If these signs are different, the algorithm becomes the same as regula falsi (and a statistical criterion is thus found, relative to which regula falsi is step-wise optimal). ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Strongin R.G."]

Title: Upper bounds for correlations between binary outcomes and probabilistic predictions
Source: Journal of the American Statistical Association
Abstract: There are many types of diverse models that yield probabilistic predictions for outcomes that are binary. We show that a correlation between the 0, 1 binary outcomes and the prediction probabilities can yield meaningful results. The upper bound for the resulting R<sup>2</sup> turns out to be a surprisingly simple expression for a class of situations which contain a quite general assumption on the distribution of the prediction probabilities. Some implications for subjective probability estimates are also given. ¬© Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Morrison D.G."]

Title: Machine recognition of patterns in particle physics
Abstract: In the last decade, computerized data handling techniques have changed the experimental habits of nuclear physics. The important role of digital pattern recognition methods is underlined. The machine recognition and classification problems encountered in particle physics are reviewed and compared with those typical of other fields. Practical achievements are emphasized and an attempt is made to analyse them as part of that body of knowledge normally collected under the headings of "Pattern Recognition". Some state-of-the-art projects and outstanding problems are mentioned together with considerations of possible future developments. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Zanella P."]

Title: An approach to artificial nonsymbolic cognition
Abstract: In this paper we describe an approach to the artificial recognition of events of a nonsymbolic nature, such as the bidimensional perspective views of scenes of our everyday world. Scenes are presented as colored pictures and the objective of the cognitive task is the labeling of the interpreted scene objects. The method is based on three major components: 1. (i) a preprocessed version of the scene (stimulus), 2. (ii) a semantic map and 3. (iii) an algorithm which performs interpretation of the stimulus under the guidance of the semantic map. The algorithm is sequential and proceeds from general to specific, thereby achieving efficient tree-pruning (contextual elimination). Stimulus interpretation is based on attribute-value matching, but classification relies strongly on the accumulated context. Backtracking provisions are available in the sequential cognitive algorithm for correction of earlier wrong hypotheses. Experiments are presented and described. The major weakness of the approach is the present lack of a satisfactory theory of inference. Flexibility, generalizability, and efficiency appear to be valid merits. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Preparata F.P.", "Ray S.R."]

Title: A new optimality criterion for discrete dynamic programming
Source: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: This paper concerns a discrete-time Markov decision model with an infinite planning horizon. A new optimality criterion and the related optimal policy, termed R-optimal one, are proposed. The criterion is much effective comparing with the existing criteria because of its availability both for discounting case and nondiscounting case in the same form. It is shown that there exists a stationary R-optimal policy and it can be found in finitely many steps by the policy iteration method. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Mine H.", "Tabata Y."]

Title: A naturally ordered enumeration of compositions
Source: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A
Abstract: A composition of the positive integer M, with N-parts, is a vector of N non-negative integer components the sum of which is M. The paper presents a transformation that "enumerates" (assigns serial numbers) the set of all possible compositions most densely so that their "natural" ordering is preserved. The transformation is useful for the efficient retrieval and compact storage of probabilities, or functions on probability spaces, in finite memories. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Barnea D.I."]

Title: Applications of sequential methods in pattern recognition to diagnosis
Abstract: The number of decision nodes of a diagnostic decision tree is shown to be reduced by selectively pursuing a path through the decision tree directed by the experience of prior decision outcomes. Two algorithms that provide this selectivity among paths are discussed as applications of sequential pattern recognition theory. One algorithm seeks to minimize the expected decision loss associated with each step in a multistage decision process, while the other algorithm seeks to minimize the uncertainty of a decision at each step. A comparison of the algorithms reveals that the latter provides greater selectivity among decision paths and a corresponding greater reduction in the number of decision nodes. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Krischer J.P."]

Title: Pattern recognition using a hybrid computer
Abstract: A method is developed for hybrid simulation of a linear sequential learning algorithm. Up to 60 weights can be corrected very fast simultaneously. Computing times are mainly dependent on speed of presentation of the patterns to the analogue computer. One type of analogue circuit seemed most suitable for implementation in special purpose hard-ware. The method is convenient for interaction with the user. ¬© 1972 Presses Acad√©miques Europ√©ennes, Brussels.
Name: ["van der Mast C.A.P.G."]

Title: Decomposition of nets
Abstract: An improved mode of representation for networks resulting from process simulation flowcharts is presented based on the signal flowgraph concept. Decomposition of maximal cyclical nets in the digraph by a minimal cut-vertex set becomes a simple three-step procedure of reduction to intervals, elimination of self-loops and processing of node pairs associated with two-way edges. Identification of cyclical nets is obtained as a by-product of decomposition. The procedure is applicable to equation-ordering problems if the output set is selected a priori. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Barkley R.W.", "Motard R.L."]

Title: File ordering and retrieval cost
Abstract: This study proposes and investigates file ordering and retrieval techniques which, it is hypothesized, will (a) reduce the average cost of retrieving records which satisfy a query, and (b) increase the rate of retrieval in the initial portion of the response period. A self-adaptive version of the k-centroids algorithm of MacQueen is used to detect clusters of records, where a member of a cluster is more similar in key content to the other records in the cluster than to records which are not in the cluster. A file, which is usually sequenced in an arbitrary fashion that is neither intended nor expected to affect the retrieval costs, is reordered so that the records in a cluster are assigned to proximate storage locations. A direct access data management (information storage and retrieval) system utilizing some type of index scheme to avoid a serial, exhaustive search of the file is assumed. The effect (a) above is an expected result of reordering the records as described. The effect (b) is to be achieved by reordering and by a search algorithm which utilizes the cluster descriptions to guide the search. Experiments on both artificially generated files and small sample files drawn from the 1960 U.S. Census file indicate that (a) is generally accomplished, but (b) is not consistently attained. The mean retrieval cost per record is decreased, on the average over several queries, by 8-10 per cent, with savings up to 30 per cent occasionally obtained. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Rettenmayer J.W."]

Title: On identification of synchronous sequential machines
Abstract: For a completely specified strongly connected synchronous sequential machine, the problem of constructing the input-output sequences that will be sufficient to identify the machine, given its flow table, is first studied in this paper. An adaptive procedure is suggested, which constructs the identifying sequences of the machine in successive segments. A necessary condition for an input sequence to be able to identify a machine is that the sequence must lead the machine through all the state transitions. To find such an input sequence of minimal length, a matrix approach is finally proposed in the paper. The modified transition diagram (MTD), modified transition matrix (MTM), and higher-order modified transition matrix are defined, and their relevant properties are studied, which are used to find the required sequence of minimal length. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Sheng C.L.", "Das S.R."]

Title: Optimal control of distributed parameter systems with separable controllers
Abstract: This study is devoted to the optimization of distributed parameter systems with separable controllers. This class of distributed parameter systems is characterized by control action having fixed functional dependence upon the independent spatial variables of the system and free functional dependence upon time. This class of system models many physically realizable distributed parameter systems more accurately than those models which permit completely distributed controls. An electrical analog to the boundary behavior of a dense perfectly conducting plasma supported by a magnetic field against gravity provides a detailed example. A comparison is made between the resultant optimal separable control, the ideal distributed optimal control which is not constrained in any of the spatial variables, and an easily implemented feedback control for this system. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Davis J.M.", "Perkins W.R."]

Title: Conditional non-independence of data in a practical bayesian decision task
Abstract: The repetitive use of Bayes' theorem to aggregate data requires that the data be conditionally independent. The robustness of Bayesian analysis to violations of this assumption was tested by comparing Bayesian with other techniques in a practical prediction task. In classifying 861 MMPI profiles as either neurotic or psychotic, two variants of Bayesian analysis techniques, both of which ignored sizable conditional dependence in the data, had cross-validated hit rates as high as comparable analyses which correctly handled the interrelationships among the MMPI scales. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Lichtenstein S."]

Title: The serial design of tandem system observers
Abstract: The problem of observing the states of two tandem-connected linear stationary systems is considered. It is shown that if the tandem systems are observable then the tandem system observer can be composed of two separate systems, each the same order as the corresponding system being observed. Let the state vector of the input system be denoted by d and the state vector of the output system be denoted by x. (See Fig. 1.) The decoupled observer is based upon a Luenberger observer designed for the output system as if d(t) were zero for all time. A second observer is then added which observes d(t). The output of these two observers is then combined to form the observed x(t) with d(t) nonzero. (See Fig. 2.) An advantage of this decoupled observer is that if the input system is changed, then only one of the two observers must be redesigned. An example which demonstrates the construction and operation of this observer is discussed. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Earhart R.J.", "Cavin III R.K."]

Title: Man-machine interactive transit system planning
Abstract: The problem of finding the best fixed routes for node oriented transit systems is used for an initial implementation and evaluation of a man-machine interactive problem solving system. The interactive graphic system enables a planner/analyst to effectively search for and evaluate a large number of alternative designs in a short period of time. This evaluation is based on a modal split model which predicts the system utilization and cost consequences of each alternative design. The model performs a detailed analysis of the components of the trip of each potential trip maker by the alternative modes of travel by transit or private automobile and it is based on values reflecting the average trip makers perception of disutility of the various trip components. After a conceptual discussion of the problem, the interactive graphic problem solving environment and the model underlying the prediction process, the mechanics of the actual implemented system are described, both in terms of computer hardware and software features. The use of the system is then illustrated with a hypothetical problem situation and the ability of the interactive process to assist the resolution of conflicting objectives and to help a policy making body to reach compromises after a value-oriented discussion. Finally, the paper discusses some issues raised in the prototype analysis relative to (1) the role and performance of the human in the interactive process, (2) alternative solution generation schemes and (3) model calibration. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Rapp M.H."]

Title: A general formulation of analogue computer programming and scaling
Abstract: The four basic analogue computer operations are identified and utilized in a vector-matrix format for the computer equations. This format, which is reminiscent of the state equation model for a dynamical system, displays clearly the task of analogue computer programming and scaling for a given system model, the first as a transformation on the structure of the initial system model, the latter as a linear transformation on the system variables in the restructured form to computer variables. Relating to scaling, the formulation leads directly to a simple and easily used scaling procedure which is a variant of the "normalised variable" or "ratio of scale-factor" method. The popular "on-the-diagram scaling" approach is also contained in the results as a particular interpretation. The generality and compactness of the formulation is of particular value for digital computer generated or assisted scaling and patching, for hybrid and data input-output interfaced situations, and for large system studies through subsystem partitions. Manual implementation is, however, equally simple and direct. Scaling, and the formulation presented, is also partinent to some problems of a digital nature. ¬© 1972 Presses Acad√©miques Europ√©ennes, Brussels.

Title: Properties of a cost function employed in a second order optimisation algorithm
Source: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: In the second-order differential dynamic programming algorithm, and the second-variation optimisation algorithm, a new control is generated at each iteration using a linear control policy of the form: u(t) = u<sup>*</sup>(t) + K(t)[x(t) - x ÃÑ(t)], where x(t) is the new and x ÃÑ(t) the old state at time t. Associated with this policy is a cost function. This paper establishes certain properties of the cost function for arbitrary piecewise continuous functions u<sup>*</sup>(¬∑) and K(¬∑), permitting the determination of sufficient conditions for the following statement: "If the distance between the nominal and new control functions is Œµ{lunate}, then the error in the estimated change in cost is of the order Œµ{lunate}<sup>3</sup>.". ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Mayne D.Q."]

Title: On a model of neuronal spike trains
Abstract: Stochastic models of neuronal firing have been proposed previously, in which neuronal firings are determined by the interaction between two renewal processes. This paper proposes a stochastic model of neuronal firing taking account of a threshold level and derives the interval density between two successive firing events. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Osaki S.", "Vasudevan R."]

Title: Model of the dependence of visual acuity on contrast
Abstract: We have investigated a model of the receptive field in which the central receptors of the field through an excitatory link and all the receptors through an inhibitory link converge on a summing output. The outputs of the excitatory and inhibitory links are power functions of their input signals with different indices. Such a model corresponds to an actual receptive field in which the central zone of summation decreases with increase in the contrast. The model of the set of such fields possesses the property of increase in visual acuity with increase in contrast. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Glezer V.D.", "Kuperman A.M."]

Title: The application of list processing techniques to picture processing
Abstract: This paper describes a picture-processing system that was first developed to locate ridge-endings in a fingerprint, but has since been expanded to solve a number of other picture-processing problems. The system extracts from a picture contour a set of features or nodes which are then tied together in a bidirectional list structure. Having the information in this form simplifies elimination of noise. The method used for establishing the list structures provides a convenient means for the performance of summing operations such as accumulation of area or calculation of moments of the picture surface. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Shelman C.B."]

Title: Tracking of DABS-Equipped Aircraft
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: The Discrete Address Beacon System (DABS) is scheduled to replace the Air Traffic Control Beacon System (ATCRBS) as the prime sensing tool for air traffic control in the 1980s. The design of DABS requires knowledge of the tracking accuracy obtainable as a function of various system parameters. In particular, the potential value of air-to-ground telemetry of turn-rate data and its effect on intermittent positive control (iPC) must be assessed. The design of DABS tracking algorithms is discussed, and the results obtained with a Kalman tracker simulation are given. The major finding is that turn-rate telemetry of moderate accuracy can improve tracking by a factor of 6 to 10. ¬© 1972 IEEE. All rights reserved.

Title: MODEL REFERENCE ADAPTIVE SYSTEMS SOME EXAMPLES.
Abstract: Presents some examples of design of model reference adaptive systems (M. R. A. S. ) using the hyperstability approach. The different steps of the design are discussed in detail, pointing out the computational and implementation problems. For the examples discussed throughout the paper, experimental results are given. Title: An Implemented Graph Algorithm for Winning Shannon Switching Games
Abstract: In this tutorial paper a computer program which wins Shannon Switching Games is described. Abstract: A stochastic sequential machine model is employed to investigate some of the problems concerning the reliability of sequential machines. Two methods, using the notions of entropy for stochastic automata and principal entries in their transition matrices, are used and compared for reliability estimates. Abstract: The computation of a number of picture properties which involve connectivity and component counting is considered. The computational model consists of a one-dimensional array of finite-state automata which scans a digital picture, one row at a time, in one-pass. Abstract: In this paper, which continues [1] and [2], we shall construct a sequence of probabilistic automata that approximate a stochastic learning model. That such a replacement is possible (and the estimate of the error involved) follows from Theorems 3.1 and 4.1 of [2], which also gives the definition of a perceptron, of a stochastic learning model (BM) and of a particular case of this model (LBM), as well as the proofs of all the theorems cited below. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.

Abstract: A fast algorithm is given to produce a small set of short sentences from a context free grammar such that each production of the grammar is used at least once. Abstract: Estimation of the state of a nonlinear discrete-time system using quantized data is considered. The results of Monte-Carlo simulations are presented in which the performance of these two algorithms is compared with that of a Kalman filter in which the quantization error is approximated by white noise. Title: SELECTION OF PERFORMANCE INDICES FOR OPTIMAL CONTROL PROBLEMS.
Abstract: Investigates the proper selection of a performance index to satisfy a work statement of desired effect. Title: On feedback stabilizability of decentralized dynamic systems
Abstract: The paper formulates and discusses stabilizability of decentralized linear time invariant dynamical systems with coordination and/or communication among control agents. Decentralized control systems are defined to be dynamical systems with several controllers, each operating on the system with partial information on the states of the systems. This restriction amounts to certain structural constraints on the feedback and other system matrices. With the constraints, controllability of the systems does no longer imply stabilizability. Title: INPUT REQUIREMENTS AND PARAMETRIC ERRORS FOR SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION UNDER PERIODIC EXCITATION.
Abstract: Provides the conditions on periodic system excitation necessary for unique identification using a multiple input state model of a dynamic system. Results include the minimum number of input frequencies necessary to uniquely determine all state and input matrix elements of an n dimensional linear system. Title: Recursive Properties of Abstract Complexity Classes
Abstract: A complexity class Rt is the class of all recursive functions whose computation ‚Äúcost‚Äù is bounded by the function t. The results are extended to complexity classes determined by partial functions, and the properties of these classes are investigated. Properties of effective presentations of complexity classes are also studied. Title: Error analysis algorithms for distributed parameter filtering
Abstract: Interest in estimation in distributed parameter linear systems is increasing. This paper presents the derivation of error analysis algorithms for filtering in distributed parameter systems. ¬© 1972.

Title: A computational approach to the combined problem of optimization and parameter identification
Abstract: Two important areas in systems engineering are process identification and optimization. The optimization problem depends on a mathematical model which in turn is determined by the identification procedure. Each of these problems is computationally difficult, a feature which has led to separate treatment in the literature. This paper attempts to examine the interdependence of these two problems and to develop an iterative computational approach for solving the joint problem which actually arises in practice; namely, the optimization of a plant whose parameters are in fact unknown. An integrated formulation of the two problems based on the theory of multilevel optimization exploits the mathematical similarity of the two problems. Several methods of decomposing the integrated problem into subsystems representing the optimization and identification problems are derived. An example problem is solved and computational results are presented. ¬© 1972.

Title: ON-LINE IDENTIFICATION OF MARKOV PARAMETERS AND DISCRETE LINEAR STATE VARIABLE MODEL FROM FINITE INPUT-OUTPUT DATA.
Abstract: An on-line identification procedure is presented for obtaining multiple linear discrete system models from observations of input and output. The precise information on the dimension of the given system is not always necessary. When the volume of gathered data is not sufficiently large enough for a complete system identification, then only a partial identification is performed. For a partial identification it is shown that both Tether-Ho's algorithm and Budin's modified algorithm can be applied. Markov parameters are identified from the measured data. Tether-Ho's algorithm can be applied on the identified Markov parameters for a system identification. Abstract: This report summarizes the progress made to date applying the convex feedback technique to the assessment of aircraft maneuvers associated with approach and landing, such as flare after acquisition of the instrument landing system (ILS), which is predominantly a pitch plane maneuver. Although specific data used are for the DC-9, the method can be applied to any aircraft. The theory developed has been applied in the form of a computational algorithm which requires the use of measured DC-9 data, instead of working on the differential equations of the system. The optimal criterion chosen here is a weighted quadratic error index. The system identification is based only on direct measurements of the state variables. Title: An algorithm for solving linearly constrained optimization problems
Abstract: An algorithm for minimization of functions of many variables, subject possibly to linear constraints on the variables, is described. In it a subproblem is solved in which a quadratic approximation is made to the object function and minimized over a region in which the approximation is valid. A strategy for deciding when this region should be expanded or contracted is given. The quadratic approximation involves estimating the hessian of the object function by a matrix which is updated at each iteration by a formula recently reported by Powell [6]. This formula enables convergence of the algorithm from any feasible point to be proved. Use of such an approximation, as against using exact second derivatives, also enables a reduction of about 60% to be made in the number of operations to solve the subproblem. Numerical evidence is reported showing that the algorithm is efficient in the number of function evaluations required to solve well known test problems. ¬© 1972 North-Holland Publishing Company.

Title: HYBRID COMPUTER SOLUTIONS WITH MINIMAL ERROR IN ANALOG COMPUTATION AND DATA CONVERSION.
Abstract: Comparing the 'exact' solution method on the digital computer with the hybrid computer solution of linear partial differential equations clearly favors the all digital 'hybrid' simulation. The all digital solution has increased arithmetic at each step over the hybrid solution by six each of the operations; fixed point multiply, store, add and load. However, the real savings is in the noniterative solution on the digital computer while the hybrid simulation is iterative and requires repeated calculation of the same increment values. Abstract: A different approach to dynamic simulation of a social environment is presented. The branch of the physical sciences known as ‚Ä≥systems identification‚Ä≥ is recommended as an approach to social modeling to supplement mathematical techniques which presently predominate. A review of computer systems available for this approach is given. A hypothetical problem is investigated and solved to illustrate the approach.

Title: TWO SOLUTIONS TO THE PROBLEM OF COMPUTER RESOURCE CONFLICTS.
Abstract: The first solution is a Resource Examination Algorithm that advises the computer operator of resource conflicts as they arise. Information is written to the operator for a resolution of the resource conflict that is external to the decision process of the operating system. The second solution is a Job Scheduling Algorithm. The resource matrix is converted to a probability of allocation matrix. A derivation of the probabilistic formulas to calculate the probability of a wait state is given. The components of the matrix are then input to the formula to calculate a wait state probability. An algorithm then orders the job stream by wait state potential so that the probability of a resource conflict is minimal.

Title: Parameter estimation using linear programming and quasilinearization
Source: The Canadian Journal of Chemical Engineering
Abstract: A generalized algorithm for the estimation of parameters in a process model from experimental data is presented in this paper. The algorithm, which combines linear programming with quasilinearization, is formulated and its advantages and limitations are discussed. Examples are included to illustrate application of the algorithm to real engineering problems, one of which was encountered in industry and another of which was encountered in a control study. The examples demonstrate the incorporation of constraints, convergence promotion and reliability estimates into the identification. Copyright ¬© 1972 Canadian Society for Chemical Engineering

Title: DESIGN OF FINITE MEMORY LEARNING CONTROLLER USING LEAST SQUARE APPROXIMATION.
Abstract: A technique of synthesizing a finite memory learning controller for a linear but otherwise unknown plant is introduced. The learning controller has no a priori knowledge of the plant, but it computes a set of weighting functions which characterizes the unknown plant, based on the information it accumulates through the experience of actual operation. When the memory of the controller is saturated, the weighting functions are updated throughout the operation so that the controller is capable of maintaining the desired performance in the presence of parameter variation and environmental changes. Simulation results are provided.
Name: ["Rattan Kuldip S.", "Yeh Hsi-Han"]

Title: STATE ESTIMATION IN LARGE-SCALE SYSTEMS: A COMPUTER NETWORK APPROACH.
Abstract: Certain aspects are considered of problems in the decentralized stochastic control of large-scale dynamical systems. Particular attention is focused on the structure describing the information available to each control unit, and an approach to the problem of decentralized state estimation in a large-scale system is outlined. The state estimator proposed in this paper has certain properties which are desirable from the standpoint of implementation requirements. It is similar to the extended Kalman filter in the sense that the estimates are used to periodically update the interaction modeling section of the filter. This, of course, suggests that the filter may, in some cases, become divergent. These stability questions are presently under consideration.
Name: ["Sanders Jr. Charles W.", "Tacker Edgar C.", "Linton Thomas D."]

Title: Select Properties of the Graph Model of a General Automaton
Abstract: Select properties are presented for a graph model of a general automaton consisting of a processor, environment and time graph. The properties, stated in the form of theorems and corollaries, deal with connectedness, number of points and lines and indegree and outdegree as the model relates to the automaton's sets, functions and characteristics. The properties are illustrated by an example automaton. ¬© 1972, MCB UP Limited
Name: ["Koenig E.C.", "Fredericku T.J."]

Title: More about metrics of subjective spaces and attention distributions
Abstract: A new representation of metrics is presented, competing theories of similarity and their geometric representations are compared, and metrics resulting from averaging individual distances are discussed. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Fischer W.", "Micko H.C."]

Title: An algebraic approach to image restoration filter design
Abstract: The image restoration problem in a linear imaging system is formulated as the problemof minimizing the effective radius of the system point spread function subject to a constraint on relative noise gain. The problem is solved by reducing the imaging system under consideration to an equivalent sampled system and subsequently optimizing the sampled system by algebraic techniques. The analysis applies to unsampled, line scanned, and sampled systems and explicitely accounts for spectrum foldover. Truncation problems are avoided in the discrete case by formulating the optimum processing array as the solution to a finite dimensional eigenvector equation. ¬© 1972 Academic Press, Inc.

Title: Preprocessing of gray-scale pictures
Abstract: A major problem in picture processing is to detect all the contrast boundaries (or edges) in a picture, independently of the particular gray levels involved. Several edge detection methods are described. The boundary elements detected by these methods are characterized by directions in order to speed up nonsystematic search algorithms. Since the detected boundaries tend to be broad bands, a thinning procedure, based on a local distance transformation, has been developed. Finally, the results of a search algorithm which makes use of the direction information are presented. ¬© 1972 Academic Press, Inc.

Title: Recursive definitions of partial functions and their computations
Source: Proceedings of ACM Conference on Proving Assertions about Programs
Abstract: The object of this paper is to present a syntactic and semantic model for recursive definitions, and to study the relation between their computed functions and their fixpoints. The recursive definitions that we consider are syntactic generalizations of those introduced in [2] by Kleene and in [5] by McCarthy. ¬© 1972 ACM.

Title: Evaluation nets for computer system performance analysis
Source: AFIPS Conference Proceedings - 1972 Fall Joint Computer Conference, AFIPS 1972
Abstract: The class of evaluation nets has been informally described. An evaluation net may be treated as an interpreted marked directed graph, where transitions correspond to vertices and the locations correspond to directed arcs. The arcs are capable of holding a single item of structured data at a time. The graph of the net represents the structure of the system and indicates the control of token flow. The transition procedures interpret the action of the vertices. By operating the net, (in a simulation manner), measures of resource utilization, turnaround, throughput, etc., are available for further analysis of the system. An implementation of the nets might include some "automatic" analysis, such as resource utilization figures. The nets are modular and allow varying level of detail of representation. An interactive implementation of evaluation nets might consist of a net editor with graphic and symbolic output. The graphic output would be used by the designer in structural debugging and the symbolic output could be used by an interpreter to simulate the net. Current studies at the University of Washington include the implementation of evaluation nets. A more formal treatment of the nets may be found in Nutt,7 from which this paper is abstracted. Examples are given which model the Boolean functions of two variables and a Turing machine. A comprehensive evaluation net of the CDC 6400 is presented which shows the structure of the machine and which allows an extensive performance evaluation of the machine at the task/resource level. This net includes models of priority queues of arbitrary length and illustrates how queueing algorithms may be handled. Evaluation nets are also compared with Petri nets. Future work, besides the implementation, includes the study of the nets as models for computational processes. ¬© Association for Computing Machinery, Inc 1972. All rights reserved.

Title: Selective attention and the breadth of learning: An extension of the one-look model
Abstract: Notes that when Ss are trained with multiple cues relevant to solution of a discriminative learning or concept identification task, some Ss learn about more than 1 relevant cue, a result that has been considered damaging to "1-look" versions of attention theory. It is demonstrated that, to the contrary, a slightly extended version of the D. Zeaman and B. J. House (see PA, Vol. 38:6426) 1-look model can predict multiple-cue learning in the redundant relevant cues experiment and can accommodate the effects of various task and training factors that have been shown to affect the breadth of learning. Moreover, a new version of the 1-look model that assumes all-or-none learning predicts with quantitative rigor the data of T. Trabasso and G. H. Bower on the breadth of learning by adult humans. Title: EVOLUTIONARY SYNTHESIS OF CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A method is proposed for algorithmic synthesis of control systems. The control system is considered to be in the process of evolution (from simple to complex) with gradual learning of the control at each stage of the evolution. An example of synthesis is presented.
Name: ["Varygin V.N.", "Koval'chuk S.A.", "Chernykh V.S."]

Title: Representation of figures by labeled graphs
Abstract: Figures of arbitrary shape (not necessarily "thin line") can be approximated by polygons which are represented as unions of some of their convex subsets. Such representations can be considered as graphs whose nodes correspond to convex subsets and whose branches connect nodes corresponding to intersecting subsets. The nodes of such graphs are labeled with information related to the structure of the convex set they represent. The paper discusses various properties of such graphs including grammars which may generate them. It is also shown that their analysis can provide information about topological properties of the figure and its shape in general. ¬© 1972.

Title: GENERALIZED MODEL FOR GENERATING MEMORY TRACES.
Abstract: A new generalized method for producing system independent memory traces (Memory Request Sequences) is described. The general model consists of two substructures; a basic memory trace generation model and an extended model which deals explicitly with multiple subprograms. The model is most useful in simulation studies of memory organizations.
Name: ["Thorington Jr. John M.", "Irwin J.David"]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF NONLINEAR SYSTEMS WITH DISCONTINUOUS PARAMETERS.
Abstract: The response error method is applied to the identification of systems containing parameters that are discontinuously nonlinear with unknown discontinuity points. It is shown how valid sensitivity equations containing delta functions as coefficients can be derived and used in the identification of the nonlinear parameters including the location of the discontinuity point.
Name: ["McKinley Henry J."]

Title: CONNECTIVITY MATRIX APPROACH TO FAULT EQUIVALENCE IN COMBINATIONAL LOGIC NETWORKS.
Abstract: An algorithm is given which will determine what faults in a combinational logic circuit cannot be distinguished. The basic tool for this algorithm is the connectivity matrix of structural graph theory. The algorithm presented has one basic advantage over others presented on the subject. That advantage is its ease of programming. Programs can be written by simple matrix manipulation and comparison programming. The overall effect of finding these generated equivalence classes is that fewer tests need be generated to detect circuit faults. A test which detects a given fault will also detect any other fault in the same equivalence class. It should be mentioned that the reachability matrix associated with structural graph theory could have been used instead of the connectivity matrix. It was not used because the algorithm needed was much more complicated and very difficult to program.
Name: ["Stigall Paul D.", "Steury Thomas D."]

Title: Optimal adaptive control: A non-linear separation theorem‚Ä†
Abstract: For the quadratic cost, non-linear, adaptive stochastic control problem with linear plant and measurement models excited by white gaussian noise, and unknown time-invariant model parameters, the optimal stochastic control is obtained and shown to separate (‚Äònon-linear separation theorem‚Äô) into a bank of model-conditional deterministic controller gains and a corresponding bank of known non-linear functional of the model-conditional, causal, mean-square state-vector estimates. This separation may also be viewed as a decomposition of the optimal, non-linear adaptive control into a bank of model-conditional, optimal, non-adaptive linear controls, one for each admissible value fof the unknown parameter Œ∏ and a nonlinear part, namely the bank of a posteriori model probabilities, which incorporate the adaptive nature, of the optimal adaptive control. Results are given for a special case of the above problem‚Äî namely, uncertainty in the measurement matrix‚Äîthat exhibit drastically reduced computational requirements. In this special case, we have explicit separation between control and estimation, and it is shown that only one deterministic controller is required to be used with the non-linear, adaptive, mean-square state-vector estimate. ¬© 1972 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.

Title: Upper and lower probability inferences from ordered multinomial data
Source: Journal of the American Statistical Association
Abstract: Dempster‚Äôs method of upper and lower probabilities represents an attempt to obtain posterior probability statements about parameters without the necessity to incorporate prior information. We apply Dempster‚Äôs method to the case of multinomial data for which there is some natural ordering of the categories. Inferences are derived for the sum of an arbitrary set of categories, the ratio of two such sums, and linear combinations of the category probabilities. Numerical examples are given, and some effort is made to interprete Dempster‚Äôs approach and relate it to the standard approaches to statistical inference. ¬© Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Weisberg H."]

Title: Guidance and control techniques for automated air traffic control
Abstract: A guidance technique has been developed for flying an aircraft automatically along curved trajectories. The technique consists of a set of algorithms for automatically synthesizing flight profiles, i.e., the horizontal trajectory, the altitude and speed profiles, and a time sequence of commands. The flyability Of the synthesized profile under wind disturbances and initial condition error is verified by closing the loop around the synthesized trajectory and flying it in a computer-simulated jet aircraft. A control law having longitudinal, lateral and heading deviation from the synthesized profile in the feedback loops is used for the simulated flight. The performance of the system is excellent, errors that are initially zero never exceed 230 ft and large initial errors are reduced rapidly. The system also behaves quite well under wind disturbance. For example, the longitudinal and lateral deviations never exceed 470 ft for a 10-knot error in estimated wind velocity. This paper presents the flight-profile synthesis algorithms, describes the control law, analyzes the overall system performance under initial errors and error in steady wind estimates, and discusses the simulation results. ¬© 1972 American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Inc., All rights reserved.

Title: A computer assisted study of Go on M √ó N boards
Abstract: The game of Go invites analysis. The rules seem few and simple, suggesting that the game may have helpful theorems. Tens of millions of people play and skill has developed over centuries to extraordinary levels. Thus, computer analysis can be tested against analysis by highly skilled human players. We study M √ó N boards, rather than the usual 19 √ó 19. We begin with the computer-assisted complete tree calculation for the tiniest boards. The analysis extends to slightly larger boards with the aid of various lemmas and concepts of connectedness and symmetry. The usual rules are incomplete. Though difficulties rarely arise from this on a 19 √ó 19 board, they are frequent on small boards. We therefore extend and complete the rules in a way which, we believe, preserves their spirit. We give bounds on the value of the game and on its combinatorial magnitude. We discuss a heuristic strategy based on potential. The flow chart for our computer program is included and may be easily modified for use in human-machine symbiosis. We offer conjectures about the optimal strategies and the value of the game, for somewhat larger boards than those solved. We suggest small-board Go as a progressive testing ground, as M and N increase, for: 1. (1) techniques to yield the complete solution, 2. (2) the power of learning programs and of (positional) evaluation functions, 3. (3) human-machine symbiosis, and 4. (4) human-machine confrontation. ¬© 1972.

Title: Suboptimal feedback control for nonlinear systems
Abstract: A method is presented for synthesizing suboptimal feedback control laws for nonlinear systems optimized with respect to a quadratic performance index. The proposed method allows the designer to easily calculate a second-order approximation to the optimal control. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Garrard W.L."]

Title: DETECTION OF A POINT SOURCE IN THE PRESENCE OF NONGAUSSIAN BACKGROUND NOISE.
Abstract: An optimal method for detecting a pulsed signal in the presence of background noise such as the radiation of a cloudy sky with a non-Gaussian intensity distribution, is presented.
Name: ["Reznik M.Kh."]

Title: SOME PROPERTIES OF MONOTONICITY ON MANY-VALUED LOGIC AND THEIR APPLICATIONS TO THE ANALYSIS OF MANY-VALUED THRESHOLD FUNCTIONS.
Abstract: A concept called a multiply completely monotonic set is introduced which is based on the monotonicity of many-valued functions. It is shown that many-valued threshold logics (including two-valued threshold logic) can generally be discussed using a multiply completely monotonic set that consists of functions from many-valued n-dimensional space to a two-valued space. The investigation begins with the asummability used to formulate a necessary and sufficient condition for a function to be a many-valued threshold function, and proceeds to define the complete monotonicity of a many-valued function.

Title: Model for flicker frequency noise of oscillators
Abstract: A stationary statistical model is proposed for oscillator frequency fluctuations, leading to a flicker power spectral density for frequency fluctuations and to the corresponding time domain frequency instability (logarithmic behavior).

Title: Dynamical systems realizing stationary weighting patterns and time- varying feedback systems
Abstract: An improved necessary and sufficient condition is obtained for a linear time- varying dynamical system to realize a stationary weighting pattern. These results are then used to show that certain time- varying feedback systems will have the input- output mapping of a time- invariant system only in trivial case.

Title: Indirect Approximation Of Probability Densities
Abstract: The integral-square criterion is important from a theoretical standpoint and because of its extensive treatment in the pattern recognition literature; it has an elegantly simple solution. The mean-square criterion poses more computational difficulties, but is more valid in higher dimensions and more accurate where it counts for any dimensionality. The weighted mean-square error can reduce the required complexity of the discriminant by allowing larger approximation errors away from class boundaries. The probability estimates required for the mean-square and weighted mean-square algorithms can be obtained by direct assignment, by adaptive modification, or by potential function (Parzen estimator) techniques. Modified mean-square criteria that minimize the average error only at misclassified sample points lead directly to the algorithms when linearized. The mean-square criteria can be linearized as well and yield two-sided loss functions, which penalize correctly classified samples as well as incorrectly classified samples. The consideration need not be limited to polynomials for approximation; other forms may yield more efficient decision rules. ¬© 1972, Academic Press, Inc.

Title: Transference of Learning Between Recognition Classes
Abstract: To demonstrate transference experiments have been carried out in which the recognition of Highleyman's handprinted numerals was a few percent more accurate when numerals and letters were used as a training set than when only numerals were used as a training set. Title: Man‚ÄêMachine Interaction in Human‚ÄêFace Identification
Abstract: How well can a computer identify a human face which is described by a person who is inspecting a photograph? We give an account of an interactive system that takes advantage both of the human's superiority in detecting and describing noteworthy features and of the machine's superiority in making decisions based on accurate knowledge of population statistics of stored face‚Äêfeatures. Experiments using a population of 255 faces and 10 or fewer feature‚Äêdescriptions showed that the population containing the described individual could be narrowed down to less than 4 percent in 99 percent of all trials. ¬© 1972 The Bell System Technical Journal

Title: Minimization of Fuzzy Functions
Abstract: It is shown that the minimum canonical sum-of-products form of a given fuzzy function is the union of all its prime implicants. Title: Algorithm for the reduction of sensitivity to parameter variations in the linear regulator
Abstract: An optimal linear-regulator problem is augmented by including a quadratic trajectory-sensitivity term in the integrand of the cost function and specifying a linear feedback control comprising both state and trajectory-sensitivity terms. The resulting specific optimal-control problem is solved assuming that the initial state is known. The method leads to a computationally feasible scheme, even for high-order systems. ¬© 1972, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.

Title: Polynomial Representation of Classifiers with Independent Discrete-Valued Features
Abstract: It is shown that for n-valued conditionally independent features a large family of classifiers can be expressed as an (n‚Äîlist-degree polynomial discriminant function. The usefulness of the polynomial expansion is discussed and demonstrated by considering the first-order Minkowski metric, the Euclidean distance, and Bayes‚Äô classifiers for the ternary-feature case. Title: Permutation Codes for Sources
Abstract: Source encoding techniques based on permutation codes are investigated. For a broad class of distortion measures it is shown that optimum encoding of a source permutation code is easy to instrument even for very long block lengths. Also, the nonparametric nature of permutation encoding is well suited to situations involving unknown source statistics. For the squared-error distortion measure a procedure for generating good permutation codes of a given rate and block length is described, The performance of such codes for a memoryless Gaussian source is compared both with the rate-distortion function bound and with the performance of various quantization schemes. The comparison reveals that permutation codes are asymptotically ideal for small rates and perform as well as the best entropy-coded quantizers presently known for intermediate rates. They can be made to compare favorably at high rates, too, provided the coding delay associated with extremely long block lengths is tolerable. ¬© 1972, IEEE. All rights reserved.

Title: Therapy planning aids and computer aided instruction
Abstract: A system of programs has been developed to utilize a large scale time-sharing computer in radiation therapy treatment planning and in the instruction of residents and technicians. In addition to its use within the medical centre, the system is available for remote use of practising radiologists and therapists throughout the state. The system is centred on an RCA Spectra 70/46 computer. Access is through Hazeltine 2000 video terminals (closed circuit TV compatible), which may be equipped with a Hewlett-Packard 7200A remote plotter. The programs, which include external and interstitial dose calculators and a generalized computer aided instruction system, are written in FORTRAN IV. The system was shown to have a high degree of interactivity, allowing graphic input of a patient information (contours, etc.), a facility for replanning cases and computer aided instruction integrated with the treatment planning system. The extended calculating abilities and large storage area of the computer have been utilized to account for mixed multiple fields and inhomogeneities (shielding, lung, bone, etc.) in the beam paths. The time-sharing nature of the system allows two or more therapists to view the same information simultaneously and consult on the planning of treatment.

Title: Admissibility Properties of Gilbert's Encoding for Unknown Source Probabilities
Abstract: Huffman coding provides optimal source encoding for events of specified. source probabilities. Gilbert has proposed a scheme for source encoding when these source probabilities are imperfectly known. This correspondence shows that Gilbert's scheme is a Bayes scheme against a certain natural prior distribution on the source probabilities. Consequently, since this prior distribution has nonzero mass everywhere, Gilbert's scheme is admissible in the sense that no source encoding has lower average code length for every choice of source probabilities. ¬© 1972, IEEE. Title: QUORUM RESTORING UNITS.
Abstract: Subdefinite Boolean functions, called quorum logical functions, are introduced. An algorithm is given for the synthesis of quorum schemes in the OR-NOT basis, which are used, in particular, as restoring units for increasing the realiability of discrete automata.
Name: ["Malev V.A."]

Title: Computer-controlled kinematic simulator of a cobalt radiation therapy unit
Abstract: In the development of an automated cobalt-60 radiation therapy unit, a computer-controlled, <sup>1</sup>/<sub>4</sub> scale kinematic simulator was designed to assist in (a) the planning and testing of a new treatment, the evaluation of collision avoidance programs, control algorithms, etc., (b) trouble shooting the system and (c) the training of system operators, all without interfering with the alternative manual mode of operation of the treatment machine. Axis speeds are simultaneously controlled by a 6 bit command from a Digital Equipment Corporation model PDP-11 computer, which also monitors the position of each axis. Various quantization schemes were evaluated, and maximum loop gains for zero overshoot were determined. Computer control can be transferred from the simulator to the treatment machine at any time by switching the control cables. In the overall system design, the same PDP-11 operating under a version of 'MUMPS', also maintains an on-line departmental patient information system. Relevant items from the treatment administered are entered directly into patient's record. Alternately, information material needed for the next treatment can be rapidly recalled from an on-line disc. The informational system is currently operational and completion of project is scheduled for this summer.
