Title: Spectral Factorization of Random Processes with Multiplicity One
Abstract: A fairly general treatment of the spectral factorization problem for scalar processes is presented. Necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a scalar dynamic system generating a given covariance function and equations whose solutions yield the system parameters are given. The processes considered are of second order with zero mean, Gaussian, and continuous in quadratic mean; initial conditions are relaxed. Copyright ¬© 1972 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Halyo N.", "McAlpine G.A."]

Title: A Newton-like optimization algorithm for digital systems with time delay
Abstract: The design and computation problems of optimum nonlinear digital time-delay control systems is considered. A minimum principle is presented which solves the design problem, and a second-order computational algorithm is developed which solves the computation problem. The minimum principle is shown to be a special case of a generalized minimum principle in. Hilbert space. The computational algorithm is actually a Newton-like hill-climbing technique for iteratively improving the guessed initial values of the conjugate vector Œª so as to satisfy the final condition of the problem. The main advantage of the present algorithm is that it does not require excess memory as in other algorithms. ¬© 1972 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.

Title: A self‚Äêadapting time‚Äêoptimal control algorithm for second‚Äêorder processes
Abstract: A method for performing time‚Äêoptimal control with only limited prior knowledge of specific process dynamics is described. The time constants of the process are identified during the transient period accompanying the desired set point change, and the valve switching times of the control algorithm are calculated based on these time constants. The adaptive features of this method make its use independent of process or operating variation. The effectiveness of the proposed control method was evaluated using digital simulation and experimental techniques. The experimental phase which involved random changes to the temperature set point of a batch reactor was carried out with the aid of an on‚Äêline digital computer. Title: Clustering and linear placement
Abstract: This paper presents two algorithms, one for clustering a set of interconnected nodes and the other for forming a linear placement of clustered interconnected nodes. The linear placement algorithm requires the output of clustering as an input. The two algorithms were designed to analyze the structure of digital logic for automatic placement of logic functions on a MOS/LSI chip as part of an automatic layout system8 and so far have only been used for that application. However, the clustering algorithm could be used to analyze any undirected graph. Both algorithms are noniterative and provide very good results with small amounts of computer time. ¬© 1972 ACM.
Name: ["Schuler D.M.", "Ulrich E.G."]

Title: On linear stochastic differential games with non-linear and noisy information
Abstract: The paper presents some of the results for computing the optimal strategies for a, two-player, zero-sum differential game subject to quadratic cost functional. Each player is assumed to have imperfect information of the strategies of his opponent. The system dynamics are taken to be linear but the measurements are assumed to be non-linear. The resulting optimal minimax stochastic control problem involves the solution of combined optimal control and stochastic estimation problems. Sub-optimal solutions are derived by approximating the measurement non-linear functions by second-order stochastic approximation technique. Some of the recent results in non-linear estimation and control theories are utilized in deriving the optimal strategies. ¬© 1972 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Raja Rao B.V."]
Affiliations: ['Indian Institute of Technology', ' Pilkington Brothers Limited']

Title: Iterative least squares development of discriminant functions for spectroscopic data analysis by pattern recognition
Abstract: Chemical data can be automatically classified into useful chemical categories by computerized learning machines using adaptive pattern dichotomizers. Previous investigations have employed negative, error correction feedback procedures to train the two-class pattern categorizers. This paper reports a new method based on an iterative least squares procedure developed for obtaining the discriminant functions used by the pattern dichotomizers. The iterative least squares method is discussed in detail, and its application to the training of decision makers to classify low resolution mass spectra is demonstrated. It is shown that pattern dichotomizers trained with the method can obtain predictive abilities of 98% in classifying unknown low resolution mass spectra into useful chemical categories. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Pietrantonio L.", "Jurs P.C."]

Title: Statistical analysis of discrete control systems with varying parameters using the method of orthogonal expansions. II
Abstract: The determination of the mathematical expectation and correlation function of the output signal of discrete automatic control systems with varying parameters is considered. The statistical characteristics of the output signal are determined by means of an expansion in a certain specially formulated orthonormalized system of functions. The computing algorithm may be realized on a digital computer. ¬© 1974 Consultants Bureau.

Title: Recognition and retrieval processes in free recall
Abstract: Describes a model of free recall which identifies 2 processes: (a) retrieval, by which S accesses the words; and (b) recognition, by which S decides whether an implicitly retrieved word is a to-be-recalled word. Submodels for the recognition and retrieval processes are described. The recognition model assumes that during the study phase, S associates "list markers" to the to-be-recalled words. The establishment of such associates is postulated to be an all-or-none stochastic process. In the test phase, S recognizes to-be-recalled words by deciding which words have relevant list markers as associates. A signal detectability model is developed for this decision process. The retrieval model is introduced as a computer program that tags associative paths between list words. In 4 experiments, 41 male and 52 female 16-32 yr. old Ss studied and were tested on a sequence of overlapping sublists sampled from a master set of common nouns. Results confirm the prediction that S's ability to retrieve the words would increase as more overlapping sublists were studied, but his ability to differentiate the words on the most recent list should deteriorate. Further predictions derived from the free recall model were also supported. (56 ref.) (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2006 APA, all rights reserved). ¬© 1972 American Psychological Association.

Title: Substructure Search by Set Reduction
Abstract: A PL/1 implementation of a substructure search system based on set reduction is described. The set reduction algorithm is based on set theory and Boolean algebra rather than the graph-theoretic approach described by Sussenguth [J. Chem. Doc. 5, 36 (1965)]. The use of ordered numerical codes for atom properties permits rapid list processing for fast rejection of non-matches, and the formulation of an efficient method for set generation. Time trials with a small file of organic chemical structures indicate that the algorithm can be economically used for substructure (or complete structure) sequential searches on a file containing 30,000-50,000 computer-coded structures. ¬© 1972, American Chemical Society. All rights reserved.

Title: An inferential processor for interacting with biomedical data using restricted natural language
Source: Proceedings of the Spring Joint Computer Conference, AFIPS 1972
Abstract: This paper describes the design and implementation of a natural language system (hereafter referred to as ENGOLISH) which was developed to support and enrich the utilization of computer models of physiological systems. In addition to providing capabilities for interrogating data bases using a subset of English, ENGOLISH also provides capabilities for defining and structuring data bases using this subset of English. In particular, this facility has been used to encode relevant information from documents concerning these models to enrich their utility. ENGOLISH is structured around GOL (Goal Oriented Language) which is a programming language developed by H. Pople to provide a means in which to express algorithms involving heuristic search and problem solving. GOL provides not only the basis for organizing and searching ENGOLISH data structures but also provides the basis for ENGOLISH's heuristic parsing algorithms. For a description of GOL, see Pople. ¬© 1972 by the American Federation of Information Processing Societies, Inc..
Name: ["Isner D.W."]

Title: Comparison of Linear and Quadratic Classifiers Using the Font OCR-A as an Example.. | VERGLEICH LINEARER UND QUADRATISCHER KLASSIFIKATOREN AM BEISPIEL DER SCHRIFTART OCR-A.
Source: NTZ Nachr Z NTZ Commun J
Abstract: An experimental comparison is reported of the performance of linear and quadratic pattern classifiers, statistically adapted to a given recognition problem by means of a modified mean square procedure. The comparison is based on the OCR-A type font. The sample set used (approx. 82,000 characters) originates from the reading machine development. It was scanned directly from actual documents. The experiments show that a simple quadratic classifier is able to reduce the reject rate - with the reject threshold unchanged - by a factor of 100 compared with the linear one.

Title: REASONING ABOUT PROGRAMS.
Abstract: Description of a theorem prover that embodies knowledge about programming constructs, such as numbers, arrays, lists, and expressions. The program can reason about these concepts and its used as part of a program verification system that uses the Floyd-Naur explication of program semantics. It is implemented in the QA4 language; the QA4 system allows many bits of strategic knowledge, each expressed as a small program, to be coordinated so that a program stands forward when it is relevant to the problem at hand. The language allows clear, concise representation of this sort of knowledge. The QA4 system also has special facilities for dealing with commutative functions, ordering relations, and equivalence relations; these features are heavily used in this deductive system. The program interrogates the user and asks his advice in the course of a proof.
Name: ["Waldinger Richard J.", "Levitt Karl N."]

Title: Comparison of methods of parameter estimation using pseudorandom sequences
Abstract: A recently proposed method of parameter estimation of a linear dynamic system with state-variable characterisation is compared with an earlier instrumental variable technique for estimating the parameters of the difference-equation model of the same system. In both methods, a pseudorandom-binary-sequence test signal is used. ¬© 1973, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Macleod C.J."]

Title: TRANSIENT IN A SINGLE-SERVER QUEUING SYSTEM.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: A new approach is presented using the stochastic transition signal-flow graph, for the study of transient in a single-server queueing system with Poisson input, first-come first-served queue discipline. A complete solution is obtained for the state probabilities of the system. Furthermore, the probabilities of waiting and loss, as well as the waiting-time distribution, are determined. The system considered is subject to delay and loss, since the waiting capacity is finite.
Name: ["Chan W.C.", "Chung W.K."]

Title: OPTIMAL CONTROL IN AGE DEPENDENT POPULATIONS.
Abstract: The growth of an age-distributed population system is described by a partial differential equation. An optimal control problem is introduced in which the difference between an actual age profile of the population and a desired equilibrium age distribution is minimized. An open loop optimal control policy is generated using a gradient procedure. A closed loop strategy is proposed.
Name: ["Falkenburg Donald R."]

Title: PREDICTING PLATELET COUNTS IN LEUKEMIA CHEMOTHERAPY WITH THE THEORY OF LINEAR MEAN SQUARED ESTIMATION.
Abstract: Patients with myeloid leukemia have blood platelet counts that, in response to chemotherapy, vary with time. These counts are interpreted as a signal generated by a random process and concepts from linear mean squared estimation are used to describe the morphology of the data curves: Noisy data points are filtered and missing data points are interpolated.
Name: ["Meier George D.", "Lincoln Thomas L."]

Title: DERIVATION OF AGGREGATION MATRICES FOR SIMPLIFIED MODELS OF LINEAR DYNAMIC SYSTEMS AND THEIR APPLICATIONS FOR OPTIMAL CONTROL.
Abstract: The use of simplified models for deriving suboptimal controllers to the original higher order plants need a relationship between the original state vector and the simplified state vector. The relationship is known as the aggregation matrix. It is claimed that there is no unique method available for evaluating the relevant aggregation matrices. This paper presents a procedure for the evaluation of the aggregation matrix for Davison's model and also discusses the applicability of the aggregation matrix concept for solving the linear regulator and the linear tracking problems via simplified models of the plants. The results are demonstrated by a numerical example.
Name: ["Lamba S.S.", "Rao S.Vittal"]

Title: Mean square stability criteria for stochastic feedback systems
Abstract: In this paper several stability criteria are obtained for a class of stochastic feedback systems containing a multiplicative white noise element; continuous time as well as discrete time systems are dealt with. Mean square stability properties are derived by means of Lyapunov theory; the Lyapunov functions are generated by means of the Lyapunov equation, the path integral technique, and the Kalman-Yacoboviteh lemma. Results similar to the Routh-Hurtwitz conditions and the circle criteria for deterministic feedback systems are discussed. Different interpretations of the white noise element (It√≤, Stratonovitch, etc.) are considered. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Willems J.L."]

Title: COMPUTER IMPLEMENTATION OF AN ALGORITHM FOR AUTOMATIC COMPILATION AND ALPHABETICAL ORDERING OF A WORDFORM DICTIONARY USING THE ASSOCIATIVE-ADDRESS METHOD.
Abstract: The machine implementation of an algorithm for automatic compilation and alphabetical ordering of a wordform dictionary using the associative-address method is presented. The structure of the cells of the address parts of the wordform dictionary in the computer memory is described. A block diagram of the automatic compilation and alphabetical ordering program is given. The program is implemented on a Minsk-32 computer.
Name: ["Zinov'ev E.V.", "Ivailovskii Yu.E."]

Title: Sequential Decision Feedback with a MAP Strategy
Abstract: A computer simulation technique is used to evaluate the performance of the MAP strategy for sequential block orthogonal signaling over a Gaussian channel with noiseless and delayless feedback. The system performance is given in terms of the character error probability. The obtained results are compared with those derived using other suboptimum strategies previously proposed. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Benedetto S.", "Biglieri E."]
Affiliations: ['Istituto di Elettronica e Telecomunicazioni del Politecnico']

Title: RAMP CONTROL TO RELIEVE FREEWAY CONGESTION CAUSED BY TRAFFIC DISTURBANCES.
Abstract: The paper examines a class of traffic-responsive ramp control algorithms for adjusting ramp volumes in response to traffic disturbances, e. g. congestion resulting from lane blockages. A large number of traffic-responsive ramp control plans are considered. Each plan is evaluated in terms of freeway service and delay over a fixed control period by simulating the response of traffic to a lane blockage on a macroscopic model of freeway traffic.
Name: ["Payne Harold J.", "Meisel William S.", "Teener Michael D."]

Title: The Recovery of Distorted Band-Limited Stochastic Processes
Abstract: This paper deals with the problem of recovering a band-limited process after it has been distorted by an instantaneous nonlinearity and subsequently band-limited. Several uniqueness theorems for the input-output relationships are derived. In contrast with the deterministic case, no requirement that the nonlinearity be monotonic is made here. An iterative procedure for the recovery of the input is presented. Applications to two-level quantizers are considered, and a new result on the determination of a band-limited Gaussian process from its zero crossings is obtained. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Masry E."]
Affiliations: [' University of California at San Diego']

Title: SOME SEARCH PROBLEMS WITH FALSE CONTACTS.
Abstract: The paper describes and discusses some search problems to provide a foundation for developing a search theory in the presence of false contacts. Properties of the search plan are defined and illustrated by examples. After a general description of false-contact generators and aalternative actions that may be used when contacts are made, the problem is formulated for the case in which false contacts are generated by real stationary objects that are investigated when contacted.
Name: ["Dobbie James M."]

Title: New experimental results in fuzzy clustering
Abstract: This paper is mainly devoted to the description of experiments using improved techniques for clustering data in fuzzy sets. Previous methods provided good fuzzy dichotomies but failed for partitions in a larger number of sets. The modifications presented here resulted in good fuzzy classifications in any, previously established, number of clusters. The modifications are described both theoretically and computationally. The effect of variations in the function that maps the original distance structure in the data space and that prescribed for the classification space is examined. Numerous computational examples are presented. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Ruspini E.H."]

Title: Optimal adaptive control of linear systems with unknown measurement subsystems
Abstract: For the quadratic cost, adaptive stochastic control problem with linear plant and measurement models excited by white Gaussian noise, and with unknown time invariant model parameters in the measurement subsystem, the optimal stochastic control is obtained. It is shown that separation between estimation and control holds in this case. The controller is shown to be linear and deterministic, while the estimator is shown to consist of a bank of known nonlinear functions of model conditional, causal, mean-square state-vector estimates. The estimator can again be partitioned into a bank of linear, model conditional, optimal, nonadaptive estimates, one for each admissible value of unknown parameter vector Œ∏, and a nonlinear bank of a posteriori model probabilities which incorporate the adaptive nature of the optimal adaptive control. The results are presented both for continuous-time and discrete-time systems. A special case of the above problem is also discussed. It is the case of joint detection and control. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Lainiotis D.G.", "Upadhyay T.N.", "Deshpande J.G."]
Affiliations: [' The University of Texas at Austin']

Title: VISION AND MANIPULATION AS A PROGRAMMING PROBLEM.
Abstract: Experiments with a computer-controlled robot are used as a means of studying programming technique. Experimental tasks include simple automatic assembly. The emphasis is on the development of programming language features and facilities for describing to the machine the structures, trajectories and constraints involved. Programs exist for sorting objects by visual appearance, packing objects into a confined space, and stacking rings on a peg.
Name: ["Mitchie D.", "Ambler A.P.", "Barrow H.G.", "Burstall R.M.", "Popplestone R.J.", "Turner K.J."]

Title: SURE STAF: A COMPUTERIZED STAFF SCHEDULING SYSTEM FOR TELEPHONE BUSINESS OFFICES.
Abstract: Scheduling of staff between answering incoming calls and processing paper-work has been a continual problem in telephone company Business Offices. A staff scheduling system has been developed and implemented in Bell Canada on a trial basis. Incoming call load data are recorded automatically and are entered daily into a time share computer terminal. The next day's forecast, by half hour, is made by a cyclic exponential smoothing routine and the number of servers required to take calls is calculated using a queueing model of the Business Office. A schedule of call answering periods for the available staff to match the requirements is made using a heuristic algorithm. Managers are able to choose their objective on the accessibility of the office to incoming customer calls and the staff can organize their work day without unplanned interruptions.
Name: ["Church J.G."]

Title: HIGH ORDER LANGUAGE OPTIMAL EXECUTION PROCESSOR: FAST INTENT RECOGNITION SYSTEM (FIRST).
Abstract: Recently timesharing and interactive systems have begun to bridge the hardware-software generation gap. This paper describes a system which is intended to eliminate the gap by providing a computer which directly executes a powerful language - APL - in a highly efficient manner. The programmer and machine communicate entirely in APL with a fully interactive timesharing operating system integral in the design. In particular this paper focuses on the execution aspects of the computer and relates results obtained by emulating the main processor to conventional computer approaches.
Name: ["Schroeder S.C.", "Vaughn L.E."]

Title: Solving Problems of Air Distribution Control in a Coal Mine Ventilation network on an Analog and Digital Model. | [K RESHENIYU ZADACH UPRAVLENIYA VOZDUKHORASPREDELENIEM V SHAKHTNOI VENTILYATSIONNOI SETI NA ANALOGO-TSIFROVOI MODELI.]
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii, Gornyi Zhurnal
Abstract: A digitally controlled variable-coefficient unit is proposed and realized. It ensures transmission of manipulated variables calculated by the digital part of the model. The analog-digital model of coal mine ventilation control consists of a control digital computer of the UM-1 type and two analog computers of the EMU-10 type. The digitally controlled variable-coefficient unit is a portable device connected by means of 20 plug and socket contacts to the UM-1 and EMU-20 computers. The results of modeling show that the accuracy of solution of the problem is quite acceptable.
Name: ["Svyatnyi V.A.", "Avramenko F.G.", "Merkulov A.P."]

Title: SEMIAUTOMATIC SPEECH SOUNDS AURAL IDENTIFICATION PROCEDURE WITH ITS APPLICATION TO SPEECH ANALYSIS.
Abstract: A semiautomatic aural identification procedure is described which makes maximal use of the computing technique. The procedure employs lay-listeners and includes a listener's check, computation of the confusion matrix and punching on cards the labels of the speech segments which received incorrect responses.
Name: ["Christov Ph.D."]

Title: Identification of Optimum Filter Steady-State Gain for Systems with Unknown Noise Covariances
Abstract: A discrete linear stationary system is considered for which the input noise covariance Q and the output noise covariance R are unknown. A stable filter with a suboptimal gain is assumed. An identification scheme is presented which uses the autocorrelation functions of the innovations sequence of the suboptimal filter to determine the optimum filter steady state gain I‚Äô directly without the intermediate determination of the unknown covariances Q and R. The approach used is to identify an output equivalent representation of the original system which does not involve the unknown covariances directly. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Carew B.", "Belanger P.R."]

Title: NETWORK ANALYSIS USING A SPARSE TABLEAU WITH TREE SELECTION TO INCREASE SPARSENESS.
Abstract: It is shown how, at the price of selecting an appropriate tree from the network graph and finding the f-cutset matrix with respect to this tree, a tableau can be obtained with a unit submatrix in the upper left-hand quarter of the coefficient matrix. With this form, the upper half of the matrix can be bypassed during L/U decomposition, elimination being done only on rows in the bottom half of the matrix. Substantial savings in multiplications can be made during back-substitution since non-zero elements in the upper right-hand quarter are either plus 1 or minus 1, and the upper left quarter submatrix is a unit matrix.
Name: ["Weeks W.T.", "Jimenez A.J.", "Mahoney G.W.", "Qassemzadeh H.", "Scott T.R."]

Title: An application of kalman techniques to aircraft and missile radar tracking
Abstract: A real-time and postflight data reduction and error analysis program is developed with the ability to estimate either aircraft flight paths or missile trajectories with the same state vector and matrix dimension filter equations simply by input selection of the appropriate state transition matrix. A feature of the filter formulation is an analytical technique for computing the effects of measurement error parameters not explicitly included in the filter state vector on both the state vector estimate itself and the state covariance matrix. Examples of the processing of real tracking data for aircraft flight paths, missile trajectories, and some other more unusual applications are presented which illustrate both the data reduction and error analysis modes of program operation. ¬© 1973 American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Aldrich G.T.", "Krabill W.B."]
Affiliations: [' AIAA', ' Navigation and Traffic Control Programs']

Title: Nonparametric Bayes Error Estimation Using Unclassified Samples
Abstract: A new nonparametric method of estimating the Bayes risk using an unclassified test sample set as well as a classified design sample set is introduced. The classified design set is used to obtain nonparametric estimates of the conditional Bayes risk of classification at each point of the unclassified test set. The average of these risk estimates is the error estimate. For large numbers of design samples the new error estimate has less variance than does an error-count estimate for classified test samples using the optimum Bayes classifier. The first application of the nonparametric method uses k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) estimates of the posterior probabilities to form the risk estimate. A large-sample analysis is made of this estimate. The expected value of this estimate is shown to be a lower bound on the Bayes error. A simple modification provides unbiased estimates of the k-NN classification error, thus providing an upper bound on the Bayes error. The second application of the method uses Parzen approximation of the density functions to obtain estimates of the risk and subsequently the Bayes error. Results of experiments on simulated data illustrate the small-sample behavior. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Fukunaga K.", "Kessell D.L."]

Title: Discrete-time fixed-lag smoothing algorithms
Abstract: Kalman filtering results are applied to yield alternative computationally stable fixed-lag smoothing algorithms including reduced order and minimal order fixed-lag smoothers. The reduced order smoothing algorithms are new and clearly have advantages over the more familiar algorithms. The properties of such fixed-lag smoothers are also studied. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Moore J.B."]

Title: A Rate-Distortion Bound on Channel Requirements for Transmission of Parameters of Adaptive Predictive Coders, with Speech Applications
Abstract: A nonstationary signal source can be decomposed into subsources if it exhibits certain characteristics. Adaptive predictive coding is considered as a method of extracting these subsources from the composite source in such a way that the overall communication problem can then be viewed as two different, but connected, communication problems: 1) transmission of predictor parameters, and 2) transmission of the subsource using difference signals. An intermediate fidelity criterion is defined that describes the effects of predictor parameter distortion on the reconstruction of the difference signal. Then a rate-distortion bound on the channel requirements for the transmission of the predictor parameters is found, subject to a dual fidelity criterion. The approach is applicable to a wide range of nonstationary signal classes. The speech process is chosen here because of the wide interests in the information content of speech. The signal class consists specifically of selected voiced phrases. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Jones R.A.", "Gupta S.C."]

Title: Direct Construction of Minimal Bilinear Realizations from Nonlinear Input-Output Maps
Abstract: The paper is concerned with the construction of bilinear state space descriptions from a prescribed nonlinear input-output map. The problem is shown to be equivalent to that of matching an infinite sequence of constant parameters which uniquely identifies the given map. Both the problems of requiring the matching over a finite number of terms of the sequence (partial realization problem) and over the whole sequence (complete realization prob-lem) are treated. In both cases explicit existence criteria and an algorithm for finding minimal realizations are given. The approach is based on the introduction of a suitable infinite matrix formed with the input-output parameters, which can be considered as a generalization of the Hankel matrix usually considered in the realization theory of linear systems. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Isidori A."]

Title: REALIZATIONS OF OUTPUT-OBSERVABLE SEQUENTIAL MACHINES AND THEIR FAULTS DETECTIONS.
Abstract: Consideration of an output-observable sequential machine as one of the machines which are easily diagnosable. Equivalence between output observability and quasi-FSR realizability is shown and a method is described by which a machine can be made output-observable by adding a minimum number of output terminals. It is shown that in a (k)-output observable sequential machine, an input sequence obtained by adding an arbitrary input sequence of length k to an input sequence passing through all transition branches of the state transition diagram is a fault detecting sequence.
Name: ["Fujiwara Hideo", "Kinoshita Kozo"]

Title: ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY: A VERSATILE CIRCUIT ELEMENT.
Abstract: The basic operation of an associative memory (often called a content-addressable memory is explained. The design of an associative-memory integrated circuit containing a 64-bit array of memory cells is described. The design of an experimental associative-memory system is discussed and brief details of possible applications considered.
Name: ["Shead C.J."]

Title: STRUCTURE OF KRON'S POLYHEDRON MODEL AND THE SCATTERING PROBLEM.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: A polyhedron network model or 'automaton' to represent a wide range of physical system problems, proposed by G. Kron, is considered. The model includes a sequence of higher-dimensional structures, each formulated by an orthogonal electrical network with closed and open paths. A set of electromagnetic waves is assumed to propagate across the polyhedron, and many other physical concepts are introduced intuitively into the model, including those concerned with multidimensional 'generalized' machines, thermodynamics, fluid flow and statistical phenomena. The present work highlights the significance of the orthogonal electric network in the polyhedron structure, and it is shown that a similar structure exists in the general scattering representation of a flow process. The formulation of the scattering problem would then appear to provide an analytical basis for many of the physical concepts discussed by Kron. It is also shown to be associated with the system problems concerned with the multimachine power system, least-squares estimation and linear optimal control and filtering. Kron's polyhedron model and the scattering problem thus incorporate similar basic features, which appear to be of fundamental importance in general system theory.
Name: ["Nicholson H."]

Title: ON THE CONTROL OF FLOATING-POINT MANTISSA LENGTH IN ITERATIVE COMPUTATIONS.
Abstract: This report describes strategies to control dynamically the length of floating-point number representation in a specific iterative computation: solution of a polynomial equation by Newton's method. The mantissa length is chosen at each stage as small as possible; a lower limit arises from the objective not to slow down the quadratic convergence of the Newton's method. The consequences of different control strategies are investigated using the statistical theory of roundoff error. This work confirms that dynamic control of the mantissa length is feasible. A new type of termination criteria, independent of floating-point number representation, was developed as a result of the research.
Name: ["Tienari Martti"]

Title: NEW STRATEGIC APPROACH TO REAL-TIME TRAFFIC ROUTING.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A few traffic routing strategies and the results of a computer experiment set up to investigate their merits and characteristics are presented. These strategies are heuristic; some of them rest on a concept referred to as predictive. This concept, broadly stated, consists of using a knowledge of the future evolution of the network to make a decision at the present time. To do this detailed information concerning the origin-destination flows as well as the local network situation is assumed to be available. The computer experiment described refers to a rather simple situation for which the control algorithms and dynamical models are not involved. The results of this experiment lead to the conclusion that traffic controlled according to a predictive strategy achieves superior performance. A rather unique microscopic observation method discloses interesting features of the traffic behavior under different strategies.
Name: ["Filomeni Paolo", "Gnavi Franco", "Secco-Suardo Gian M."]

Title: CONTROL OF COMPLEX PLANTS WITH PREDICTION OPTIMIZATION BASED ON SELF-ORGANIZATION.
Abstract: In control with optimized prediction, each solution is evaluated from the point of view of its effect on the future. In contrast to previous work, synthesis of an optimal controller is carried out here in discrete time. As the first example a plant (hydroelectric station) for which the optimal control can be obtained by dynamic programming or by self-organization (selection) is considered. It is found that the method of self-organization is applicable to more complex plants, with a large number of delayed independent variables and in the case of optimization with a sliding prediction interval. As the second example, a complex stochastic plant (the gaseous conditions of a water reservoir) is treated, for which dynamic programming cannot be used.
Name: ["Ivakhnenko A.G.", "Ovchinnikov V.A.", "Petrache G.", "Gulyan N.V."]

Title: MOTIVATION SYSTEM FOR A ROBOT.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A motivation system for a robot consists of a set of general goals and prohibitions which guide the robot's actions. The necessity of a motivation system presents itself when the robot has a complex task structure and hence must interact with the real world. A linear polynomial is suggested as a means of evaluating choices based on these motivations. Procedures to adjust the polynomial are given. An example is offered to illustrate that reasonable and consistent decisions can be made in situations of moderate complexity.
Name: ["Koplowitz Jack", "Noton David"]

Title: An interactive simulation programming system which converses in english
Abstract: In this paper an experimental system for producing simulation programs through natural language dialogue with a computer is described. With the current version of this system, which operates under CP/CMS on an IBM 360/67, a queuing problem may be stated to the computer in English. The system checks the problem description for completeness, and if necessary, asks questions which may be answered in English. Then it can produce an English description of the problem as it sees it and a GPSS program for performing the simulation. The user may then modify the problem through further dialogue to produce additional programs, as desired. A complete sample problem is included in the paper. ¬© 1973 Proceedings - Winter Simulation Conference. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Heidorn G.E."]

Title: CRITERION OF FREEDOM OF CHOICE OF DECISIONS FOR CONTINUOUS CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: For the most important classes of continuous control systems (deterministic with delay, stochastic, and stochastic with delay), a theory of freedom of choice of decisions is constructed. The results obtained make it possible to determine the most ‚Ä≥thorough‚Ä≥ running control, that maximizes the freedom of choice of subsequent decisions.
Name: ["Stepashko V.S.", "Khylyuk L.F."]

Title: SYNCHRONIZED FINITE AUTOMATA.
Abstract: Finite automata are classified in accordance with the way in which the transient process is organized. The concept of a synchronized finite automation is introduced, and the possibilities for eliminating dangerous hazards by using delay elements are studied.
Name: ["Yakubaitis E.A."]

Title: Tours in Machines and Digraphs
Abstract: A tour in a machine is a shortest input sequence taking the machine from some initial state, through all of its remaining states and back again into its initial state. A best upper bound for tour length is found for two types of machines: n-state sequential machines with unrestricted input alphabet and n-state sequential machines with a two-letter input alphabet. The problem of finding a best upper bound for length of tours in machines is restated and solved using the language of the theory of directed graphs. The solutions to the above special cases restated in this language seem obvious but require a nontrivial proof of their status as solutions. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Dewdney A.K.", "Szilard A.L."]
Keywords: ["directed graph", "finite-state machine", "index terms-circulation", "initial moore machine", "maximum tour length"]

Title: Linear Convex Stochastic Control Problems Over an Infinite Horizon
Abstract: A stochastic control problem over an infinite horizon which involves a linear system and a convex cost functional is analyzed. We prove the convergence of the dynamic programming algorithm associated with the problem, and we show the existence of a stationary Borel measurable optimal control law. The approach used illustrates how results on infinite time reachability [1] can be used for the analysis of dynamic programming algorithms over an infinite horizon subject to state constraints. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Bertsekas D.P."]

Title: SPECTRAL EQUIVALENCE OF FUNCTIONALS AND THE SOLVABILITY OF OPTIMAL STABILIZATION PROBLEMS.
Abstract: An examination is made of those spectral properties of stationary linear completely controllable systems that are associated with the problem of optimal stabilization. A one-to-one mapping of the equivalence classes of quadratic functionals onto the manifold of spectral vectors of an asymptotically stable closed system is constructed. Applications to the solvability of optimal stabilization problems with significantly incomplete information, and with restrictions on the spectrum of the closed system, are examined. A discussion is given of application of the results to certain automatic control problems. An example illustrating the essence of the proposed spectral classification of functionals is included.
Name: ["Gal'perin Ye.A."]

Title: Linear stochastic system identification using correlation techniques
Abstract: The identification of linear, discrete time, scalar output systems which are driven exclusively by white, zero mean, inaccessible noise sequences is discussed. Two principal results are presented. First, two methods (least squares and an autocorrelation technique) for identifying the system characteristic equation coefficients are compared. The least squares approach is shown to be biased except for special cases. In general, the bias cannot be removed. If the state transition matrix is of the phase variable form, bias removal requires a knowledge of the measurement noise variance and all but one of the state driving noise variances. The autocorrelation technique is not biased asymptotically and does not require a knowledge of the noise variances. Secondly, it is shown that the m<sup>2</sup> elements of the state transition matrix cannot be identified uniquely from the scalar output sequence autocorrelation coefficients if the system order is higher than one. The implication of this uncertainty in the state transition matrix on optimal filtering of the output sequence is briefly discussed. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Boozer D.D.", "McDaniel Jr. W.L."]
Affiliations: ['Teledyne Brown Engineering Research Park', ' State College']

Title: ERROR DETECTION AND CORRECTION IN FORMAL LANGUAGES.
Abstract: The error detecting and correcting problems on spelling errors are discussed in the formal language theory. Three kinds of errors are considered. These are: substitution, deletion and insertion errors. The number of errors in a word is assumed to be bounded by a constant k independently of the word length. It is shown that all language classes under the classification by Chomsky are closed under these error operations.
Name: ["Iwamoto Kanji", "Sawano Akio"]

Title: Investigation of Some Control Algorithms for Stationary Operating Modes of Electric Power Systems. | ISSLEDOVANIE NEKOTORYKH ALGORITMOV UPRAVLENIYA STATSIONARNYMI REZHIMAMI ELEKTROENERGETICHESKIKH SISTEM.
Abstract: Two interconnected control algorithms of normal stationary operating modes of an electric power system are investigated: the algorithm of operational calculation of the parameter of the electrical operating conditions of a network by the measurement results and the algorithm of control of the operating conditions of a network by voltage and reactive capacity. The mathematical formulation and algorithms for solving the problems on a digital computer are given. Practical investigations of the effectiveness of the utilized control algorithm are carried out on a modeling set consisting of an a. c. design table and a ‚Ä≥Mir‚Ä≥ digital computer.
Name: ["Venikov V.A.", "Golovitsyn B.I.", "Liseev M.S."]

Title: ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY FOR SPATIO-TEMPORAL PATTERNS.
Abstract: An associative memory system is proposed for spatial patterns which change with time and shows the results of computer simulation of the system. This proposed circuit consists of many threshold elements which represent abstract actions of neural cells. Some connectivities among such elements are fixed and other connectivities are variable. Memory is stored as dispersed variable interconnections of many elements.
Name: ["Fukushima Kunihiko"]

Title: A stopping rule for threshold learning
Abstract: A stopping rule is derived for time-varying training procedures operating on trainable signal detectors and single-feature pattern classifiers. It is assumed that the statistical description of the environment is partially unknown. The stopping rule is baaed on a recently-developed technique for obtaining a bounded-length confidence interval for the expected value of a non-stationary random variable. Training is stopped when this interval falls inside specified limits, thereby assuring a specified minimum performance at a desired confidence level. The rule is illustrated by a numerical example in which the two classes of obser vations overlap. An expression is obtained for the limit to which the probability of acquiring the stopping criterion converges in probability. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Sklansky J.", "Ramanujam H.R."]

Title: EQUIVALENCE AND SIMPLIFICATION OF ANALYZERS.
Abstract: A discussion is given of a method for finding an analyzer which is equivalent to a given analyzer and has a minimum length of LOOK sequence, as well as a method to simplify such an analyzer. It is pointed out that an analyzer is different from a parser and that simplification of an analyzer is more effective in general than that of a parser in obtaining a simple structure.
Name: ["Taniguchi Kenichi", "Kasami Tadao", "Kikuno Toru"]

Title: Computation Times of Arithmetic and Boolean Functions in (d,r) Circuits
Abstract: A (d, r) circuit is d-valued logical circuit in which each element has fan-in at most r and can compute any r-argument d-valued logical function in unit time. In this paper we review results previously published on the computation time of such circuits for addition and multiplication and for computation of general Boolean functions. We also explicitly state hitherto unpublished but known results on the time necessary to divide in such circuits. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Spira P.M."]
Keywords: ["circuits of elements of limited fan-in", "time of arithmetic operations", "time of computation", "functions circuits", "logical circuit"]

Title: Dispatcher Control by Complex Discrete Production Processes. | [STEROWANIE DYSPOZYTORSKIE ZLOZONYMI DYSKRETNYMI PROCESAMI PRODUKCYNJYMI.]
Abstract: The problem of production process control is considered, along with complex production processes and dispatcher control. It is shown that in order to describe processes of the type discussed one has to consider only four basic types of operations: technological processing, assembly, disassembly and transport. The formalization of a dispatcher control is presented. The concept of a dispatcher control of a complex discrete production process realized with the use of a digital computer is discussed. Algorithms for modeling and making optimal decisions are presented. Industrial application of the presented algorithms is exemplified with the material (hot ingots) flow in a metallurgical plant.
Name: ["Bobrzynski Wojciech", "Goscinski Andrzej", "Wala Konrad"]

Title: Cluster validity with fuzzy sets
Abstract: Given a finite, unlabelled set of real vectors X, one often presumes the existence of (c) subsets (clusters) in X, the members of which somehow bear more similarity to each other than to members of adjoining clusters. In this paper, we use membership function matrices associated with fuzzy c-partitions of X, together with their values in the Euclidean (matrix) norm, to formulate an a posteriori method for evaluating algorithmically suggested clusterings of X. Several numerical examples are offered in support of the proposed technique. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Bezdek J.C."]

Title: OPTIMAL OBSERVERS FOR TIME VARYING LINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A method is presented for generating the optimal control of a linear system for measurements of the system input and output. The systems considered are n-th order, time invariant or time varying forced linear systems which are restricted to be bounded and uniformly completely state reconstructible. The control is generated from an estimate of the state vector which is obtained from an observer. The observer dynamics are derived from an optimal estimation formulation which is closely related to the concept of observability. Asymptotic stability of the observer is demonstrated and the effects of initial errors are considered. The result is a practical method of estimating the state of a linear system from noiseless measurements of the input and output. Additionally, theoretical results are obtained concerning the existence of observers for time varying linear systems.
Name: ["Watts A.C.", "McDaniel Jr. W.L."]

Title: SELF-GROWING LEARNING MACHINE.
Abstract: A new function is introduced which repeats local nonlinear processings with self-organization, providing a realizable form for the system to perform the process, and shows, both from general analysis and simulation experiment, that the produced model realizes the required behavior. The newly introduced self-organizing function is one in which the machine defines the connection between elements in a self-organizing way.
Name: ["Nagano Takashi"]

Title: ON-LINE PICTURE PROCESSING OF TEXTILE PATTERNS.
Abstract: Description of a technique of on-line picture processing as applied to the design of textile patterns via man-machine interaction. It is shown that after actual patterns are converted into digitized images, correction and shaping techniques are applied to the digitized gray-level picture. The effectiveness of the method as an image-processing technique for textile production is confirmed.
Name: ["Sakai Toshiyuki", "Nagao Makoto", "Konishi Osamu"]

Title: SCATTERED TREE AUTOMATA AND SCATTERED CONTEXT-SENSITIVE TREE-GENERATING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The authors define the scattered tree automaton, which is an extension of the tree automaton. Results are examined.
Name: ["Ito Hidenori", "Inagaki Yasuyoshi", "Fukumura Teruo"]

Title: ON THE COMPUTER AIDED DESIGN OF CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A computer method is proposed for the design of linear systems. The method combines a new root locus method with direct time response considerations. Computer methods for nonlinear system investigation are described. In particular, a computer implementation of a harmonic linearization method is discussed when a finite number of higher harmonics is taken into consideration.
Name: ["Somlo J."]

Title: IMPROVED STOCHASTIC MODEL FOR OCCUPANCY-RELATED RANDOM VARIABLES IN GENERAL-ACUTE HOSPITALS.
Abstract: The paper presents an improved stochastic model for the behavior of the daily census and associated waiting variables in general-acute hospitals. This increased flexibility is attained via a generalization of the queueing discipline, permitting admissions of elective patients to be suspended when the number of occupied beds reaches a predetermined level.
Name: ["Shonick William", "Jackson James R."]

Title: ITERATIVE UNIVERSAL LOGICAL MODULES.
Abstract: Various bidimensional interative universal arrays are presented and compared under the following performance criteria: area, perimeter (delay), form factor and effective number of external inputs.
Name: ["Davio M.", "Quisquater J.J."]

Title: NEURAL NETWORK MODEL FOR BINOCULAR PARALLAX EXTRACTION.
Abstract: Parallax extraction plays an important role in the binocular mechanism of the living organism. The authors constructed a neural network model for binocular parallax extraction with analog threshold elements which are abstracted neural cells by adopting various properties of neural cells (in particular, the neural cells in the cerebral visual areas) that have been clarified by physiological experiments. The performance of the neural network model was simulated by a digital computer. The results were satisfactory.
Name: ["Hirai Yuzo", "Fukushima Kunihiko"]

Title: Fuzzy sequential functions
Abstract: In this paper, the sequential functions or input-output relations of fuzzy systems which are realizable by maximin machines are studied. Various problems related to these functions are examined, which include characterization and decision Problems, completion problems, extension problems, closure properties and their relations to maximin regular events. Some basic properties of maximin regular events are also presented including the extension of Kleene‚Äôs theorem to the maximin case. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Santos E.S."]

Title: Invariant Gauss‚ÄîGauss Detection
Abstract: The detection of information-bearing Gaussian processes immersed in additive white Gaussian noise (WGN) is an important problem that arises in many signal processing applications. When the level of the WGN is unknown, classical approaches to the problem fail. In this paper a principle of invariance is used to derive a detector with performance that is invariant (or insensitive) to system gain, or equivalently channel attenuation. The detector structure can be realized and detection thresholds set without prior knowledge of the WGN level. When the observation interval is large the detector has the structure of a spectral estimator-correlator, the output of which is compared to an adaptive threshold. The invariance feature of the detector makes it a constant false alarm rate (CFAR) receiver; an ad hoc structure for suboptimal CFAR Gauss-Gauss detection is discussed as well. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Scharf L.L."]

Title: Optimal Planning of the Experiment for the Static and Dynamic Identification of Controlling Objects. | OPTIMALE PLANUNG DES EXPERIMENTES ZUR STATISCHEN UND DYNAMISCHEN IDENTIFIKATION ZU STEUERNDER OBJEKTE.
Abstract: A method is presented for the establishment of continuous D-optimal experimental plans by means of a constant process. The method is used for solving problems associated with the identification of dynamic objects. Several new D-optimal plans and sequences are given.
Name: ["Krug G.K."]

Title: METHOD OF SYNTHESIZING THE STRUCTURE OF A MULTIFUNCTIONAL LOGIC ELEMENT.
Abstract: An algorithm is proposed for synthesizing the structure of a multifunctional logic element that realizes a specified list of functions and has a minimum number of inputs.
Name: ["Yakubaitis E.A.", "Chapenko V.P.", "Kalnberzin A.Ya."]

Title: DISCRETE VELOCITY MODEL OF HIGHWAY TRAFFIC FLOW.
Abstract: This article discusses a Markov chain model of highway traffic flow. The transition probabilities for the vehicle velocity density function are calculated in terms of car following models, the surrounding traffic's velocity, and desired velocity changes.
Name: ["Ward Denham S."]

Title: STATISTICAL DYNAMICS OF MULTIPROGRAMMED COMPUTING SYSTEMS: A MARKOV PROCESS MODEL.
Abstract: This article develops the theory of the statistical dynamics of a fixed degree of multiprogramming Markov process model. The model is a generalization of Buzen's central server model and permits the inclusion of such features as multiple central processing units and direct access storage devices with rotational position sensing and sector queueing.
Name: ["Arthurs Edward"]

Title: Parallel Processing Algorithms for the Optimal Control of Nonlinear Dynamic Systems
Abstract: This paper describes the recent development of parallel processing algorithms for solving optimal control problems for nonlinear dynamic systems. Both the deterministic and stochastic cases are considered. The resulting algorithms are applicable to a large range of parallel architecture computers, including Illiac IV, associative processors, and potential designs based on integrated circuit technology. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Larson R.E.", "Tse E."]

Title: Real-Time Determination of the Cos-Sin Amplitude Spectrum of Fluent Speech with Free Programmable or Fixed Programmed Computers. | [ECHTZEIT-ERMITTLUNG DES COS-SIN-AMPLITUDENSPEKTRUMS AUS FLIESSENDER SPRACHE MIT FREI PROGRAMMIERBAREN ODER FEST PROGRAMMIERTEN RECHNERN.]
Abstract: It is shown that real-time determination of cos-sin-amplitude spectra of fluent speech is only possible with very fast, free programmed (very expansive) computers, such as the IBM 360/195. It is also shown that with cheap, fixed programmed computers the real-time determination is guaranteed. Three methods and their realization are described.
Name: ["Kuehlwetter J."]

Title: Synthesis of Control Devices of Optimal Nonlinear Systems of the Second Order. | SINTEZ UPRAVLYAYUSHCHIKH USTROISTV OPTIMAL'NYKH NELINEINYKH SISTEM VTOROGO PORYADKA.
Abstract: A problem of optimum fast-response control of oscillating and non-oscillating plants of the second order is solved. With the synthesis of many real systems transition to a nonlinear mathematical model of the second order is fully justified. To solve the problem of synthesis, the method of polynomial approximation is applied. The switching line which is the control law, is found in the form of a tabulated function. Realization of the control laws thus obtained can be realized with the aid of analog devices, as well as by using digital computers, by means of preliminary approximation of the said laws, for instance by Chebyshev polynomials.
Name: ["Kolesnikov A.A.", "Shteinikov G.A."]

Title: ARCHITECTURE OF CASSM: A CELLULAR SYSTEM FOR NON-NUMERIC PROCESSING.
Abstract: This paper presents the architecture of a context-addressed cellular system for non-numeric information processing, using an inexpensive, large-capacity circulating memory device. The information structures currently used in existing information systems are described. Then the architecture of the system as a whole is presented, as well as the implementation of these information structures as basic data types and hardware management of storage allocation and garbage collection. The paper intends to demonstrate that distributing intelligence throughout a rotating memory device can decrease the time required for search operations in large data bases.
Name: ["Copeland Jr. George P.", "Lipovski G.Jack", "Su Stanley Y.W."]

Title: Numerical Investigations of the Binary Search Tree. | [NUMERISCHE UNTERSUCHUNGEN AM BINAER-ZUGRIFFSBAUM.]
Abstract: During the organization and managing of data, search trees are of great importance, especially binary search trees. The construction of an optimum search tree can be difficult in case of great reorganization and updating (insertion and delection of data). The reason for this difficulty are the different updating steps, leading from a balanced binary tree to an unbalanced one. This unbalance increases the average search number (number of accesses in order to search a special item). It is shown that the simple binary search tree under the context of a determined rhythm of restructuring is still better than other known and proposed solutions. Particularly, the paper outlines the dependence of the average search number on reorganization and updating.
Name: ["Albrecht W."]

Title: INFORMATION MATRIX AND LOCAL IDENTIFIABILITY OF PARAMETERS.
Abstract: A definition for local identifiability of a parameter is given in terms of consistency in probability for local estimate. The relationship between local identifiability and Fisher's information matrix is established where it is proved that positive definiteness for the average information matrix is sufficient for local identifiability. The eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the matrix determine the region of local identifiability for the parameter. If the matrix has a nonzero null space, it is shown that the null space constitutes a subspace which may be unresolvable from the parameter being sought. Some illustrative examples are given to indicate the implications of the results.
Name: ["Tse Edison"]

Title: Noise Variance for Rounded Two's Complement Product Quantization
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: The Halyo-McAlpine discrete model for product quantization is reconstructed using an error variable set having an even number of members. It is shown in this case that the noise variance associated with a continuous model becomes an upper rather than a lower bound on the variance of the product quantization noise. The modified error set is shown to be more consistent with binary data formats such as two's complement. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Sjoding T.W."]

Title: Solution of Large Sparse Systems by Ordered Triangular Factorization
Abstract: Analysis and/or control problems arising in utility systems are often of high dimensionality. As a result, the usual symbology of formal vector-matrix notation can obscure structural properties of the system or model which might otherwise allow very simple numerical solution. Simultaneous sparse systems arising from a number of different areas are shown to be of this type, including problems of electric power flow, water distribution, mechanical structure analysis, differential equation solution, optimal control, and linear programming. All are highly amenable to efficient solution schemes employing the sparse-matrix method of ordered triangular factorization. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Tinney W.F.", "Meyer W.S."]

Title: Estimation of the Magnitude-Squared Coherence Function Via Overlapped Fast Fourier Transform Processing
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: A method for estimating the magnitude-squared coherence function for two zero-mean wide-sense-stationary random processes is presented. The estimation technique utilizes the weighted overlapped segmentation fast Fourier transform approach. Analytical and empirical results for statistics of the estimator are presented. The analytical ex. pressions are limited to the nonoverlapped case; empirical results show a decrease in bias and variance of the estimator with increasing overlap and suggest a 50-percent overlap as being highly desirable when cosine (Hanning) weighting is used. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Carter G.C.", "Knapp C.H.", "Nuttall A.H."]
Affiliations: [' New London Laboratory', ' University of Connecticut']

Title: Image restoration of blurring due to uniform linear motion by TV techniques
Abstract: A simple method using TV techniques for the image restoration of degradation due to uniform linear motion is described. The restored image is displayed on a TV monitor after simple differential operation for the video signal corresponding to the blurred image. No computer calculation is needed. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Inuiya M.", "Ichioka Y."]

Title: A spectral analysis procedure for model identification and parameter evaluation of dynamic systems
Abstract: A spectral analysis procedure for model identification and parameter evaluation of dynamic systems is given. Assuming the process can be represented as a linear system, an algorithm is given for converting the frequency response to spectra from which the poles and zeros of the process can be identified. The characteristics of the Lorentzian peaks which appear in the spectra can be used to evaluate the location of the poles and zeros in the complex plane as well as the gain and time delay of the dynamic system. Included are several illustrative examples with the fast Fourier transform being used to compute the required spectra. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Kirmse D.W.", "Kiang Y.H."]

Title: Minimum Test Sets to Detect and Locate Single Faults in Combinational Circuits. | [MINIMAL-TESTSAETZE ZUR ERKENNUNG UND ZUR LOKALISIERUNG VON EINZELFEHLERN IN SCHALTNETZEN.]
Abstract: A procedure to derive tests for single permanent faults in combinational circuits is proposed using the knowledge of the indistinguishable s-a-0/s-a-I-faults at the gate inputs and outputs. These faults are said to form equivalence classes. After deriving the equivalence classes, tests for the faults contained are computed from the Boolean difference of the switching function. The resulting reduced test set detects and locates all distinguishable faults. The construction and simplification of the complete fault table is avoided by this procedure.
Name: ["Giesselhardt W."]

Title: Computer as a Conversation Partner. | [DER COMPUTER ALS GESPRAECHSPARTNER.]
Abstract: Data output in the form of spoken words will soon enable millions of telephone subscribers to hear verbal information from a computer. Requirements and requests made of the computer will be fed in numerically coded form via a telephone keyboard and the computer will then answer with a human voice over the telephone receiver. The principles of digital voice output are described and the problems of input and output are treated. Possible applications for this type of computer are considered.
Name: ["Schreiber Alf"]

Title: Influence of Intermittent Failures on the Output Signal of a Combinational Logic Network. | [WPLYW USZKODZEN CHWILOWYCH NA SYGNAL WYJSCIOWY LOGICZNEJ SIECI KOMBINACYJNEJ.]
Abstract: A network in which intermittent failures of its elements may occur is considered. A method for computing the probability of erroneous output signal is given. Damaged logic elements realize constant logic functions true or false with the probability e//i//0 and e//i//1, respectively. It is assumed that failures are independent.
Name: ["Komorowski Witold"]

Title: Computational complexity in partial algebras of finite type | Berechnungen in partiellen Algebren endlichen Typs
Abstract: The method of Shannon and Lupanov to estimate the minimal size of a logical net for the representation of a typical truth function is generalized to computations in partial algebras of finite type. Applications are given to free groups, polynomial rings over finite fields, Boolean rings and to the approximate computation of real numbers. ¬© 1973 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Strassen V."]

Title: THRESHOLD PULSE PARAMETERS FOR AUTOMATIC FREQUENCY AND PHASE CONTROL BY A PULSED RADIO-FREQUENCY SIGNAL.
Source: Telecommunications and Radio Engineering (English translation of Elektrosvyaz and Radiotekhnika)
Abstract: An automatic frequency and phase control system (AFP) is investigated which is controlled by an incoming signal in the form of radio-frequency pulses whose carrier frequency tunes the driving oscillator of the system. A relationship is derived between the threshold parameters of the pulses and the parameters of the system for which stable operation of the AFP system is possible.
Name: ["Blagoveshchenskiy M.V.", "Maslennikov V.V."]

Title: Discrete Optimal Terminal Control. with Application to Missile Guidance
Abstract: The following aspects of discrete optimal terminal control of a linear system with a quadratic performance index are considered: 1) specification of a performance index that will give satisfactory results from an engineering standpoint at the critical terminal time; 2) closed-form algebraic solutions of the control law that are computationally feasible on-line, without necessitating prior lengthy off-line computation and storage. For a linear plant with discrete control, it is shown how a generalized performance index can be modified slightly in order to provide implicit feedback. The original plant and control problem are replaced by an ‚Äúequivalent plant‚Äù (with eigenvalues that are shifted only if those of the original plant are unsuitable) and an ‚Äúequivalent problem.‚Äù The equivalent problem (with a slight restriction) has a performance index whose loss function weights only the control, and is solved for the optimal control in closed form with minimal difficulty from literal matrix inversion. Solution of the optimal control in the original problem is a minor additional step. If the original plant has suitable eigenvalues, as in the case of a missile system with a well-designed autopilot, then the equivalent problem reduces to the original problem because there is no need for implicit feedback via the performance index. For a general missile-guidance problem, the solution of the restricted equivalent problem with discrete control is given. The example is for a missile airframe (without a conventional autopilot) having unsuitable eigenvalues. Performance in terms of rms state variables is sharply improved by making the equivalent plant have eigenvalues that correspond to a fast integral of the squared acceleration error response. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Stallard D.V."]

Title: A translating computer interface for a network of heterogeneous interactive information retrieval systems
Source: Proceedings of the 1973 Meeting on Programming Languages and Information Retrieval, SIGPLAN 1973
Abstract: The need for a network of heterogeneous interactive bibliographic information retrieval systems is projected from the facts of wide acceptance and growing demand for these systems and the limitations of their use caused by limited online data base size. Because of the established characters of the different I-R systems and unlikelihood that a standardized I-R system leading directly to the ultimate uniform network will soon be generally adopted, we propose an intermediate solution in which computer interfaces would provide the networking capability by translating and converting among the diverse languages and data bases of existing systems. We have begun work on such a network in which the computer interface is based on the concept of a common language for commands, indexing vocabularies, and data base structures. In particular, the common language for commands and data base structures is based on identifying the basic or primitive I-R functions and bibliographic data base elements. The conversion among indexing vocabularies is based on the concept of a Master Index and Thesaurus containing the conglomerate thesaurus information from the separate data bases. In addition, the phrase decomposition and stemming of the individual words in the search request and subject index phrases are used as further techniques for automated conversion among diverse vocabularies. An initial experimental interface is described which interconnects the M.I.T. Intrex system, the MEDLINE retrieval system, and the TYMNET computer network using the ARPANET Terminal Interface Processors for intercomputer communication. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Marcus R.S."]

Title: TOPOLOGICAL FORMULATIONS OF SYMBOLIC NETWORK FUNCTIONS FOR LINEAR ACTIVE NETWORKS.
Abstract: Algorithm which is based on the concept of graph-partitioning is presented. This algorithm provides a step-by-step procedure for formulating linear (active or passive) network functions that can readily be adapted for computer implementation.
Name: ["Shieu Shin-Dong", "Chan Shu-Park"]

Title: DIGITAL PROCESSING OF RADIOGRAMS UTILIZING GRAPHICAL MODELS AND SHAPE DESCRIPTORS.
Abstract: The concept of the technique presented here is how to organize a program in such a way that flexibility and logical flow are augmented and how to formulate the structural information about a scene so that it guides the usage of the primitive operations. Program organization will be described by a graph processor called an IAG, image analysis graph. Structural information will be described by a tree structure. Shape analysis utilizes fourier descriptors. The problem considered is the development of an automated system to recognize and analyze radiographic images. Several subclasses of images are considered. These include chest and knee radiograms and brain, liver, lung, and thyroid scans. (An approach which could accurately classify radiographic images could also be applied to other scenes which can be viewed from a fixed frame of reference such as printed circuit board inspection. 11 refs.
Name: ["Harlow C.A.", "Dwyer S.J.", "Eisenbeis S.A.", "Lodwick G.S."]

Title: Fixed-Point Smoothing with a Measurement Process Initiated a Posteriori
Abstract: For discrete linear stochastic systems, a fixed-point smoothing algorithm is given to obtain optimal estimates of the state of the system at time k = i (i fixed) when noisy linear measurements of the state are not available until the time k = j(j > i). An example is included to illustrate smoothing degradation as (j - i) increases. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Priemer R."]
Affiliations: [' University of Illinois at Chicago Circle']

Title: ALGORITHM FOR DETERMINING ADAPTIVE MACHINE-TOOL CONTROL-SYSTEM PARAMETERS.
Abstract: A system for correcting tool trajectory to increase accuracy when machining complex three-dimensional profiles is described. The system algorithm is explained and criteria for evaluating the system and selecting optimum algorithm parameters are considered.
Name: ["Salamandra B.L."]

Title: ON DYADIC INVARIANT SYSTEMS.
Source: Proc Inst Radio Electron Eng Australia
Abstract: A new type of linear system suitable for digital signal processing is described. Dyadic invariant systems are defined over the group of binary vectors and hence are well matched to binary computation. Their implementation on computing machines involves the fast Walsh transform, an algorithm similar to fast Fourier transform used for time invariant systems but as FWT uses only additions and subtractions, it is much faster than FFT. The dyadic analogs of power spectrum, smoothing filters and matched filters will be discussed, as well as applications of dyadic invariant systems outside communications engineering.
Name: ["Yuen C.K."]

Title: Computation of Optimal Controls Using a Piecewise Polynomial Parameterization
Abstract: A class of optimal control problems is treated. The mathematical programming approach is used by employing a special piecewise polynomial parameterization of the control profile. A method for evaluating the gradient of the cost with respect to the various parameters is developed; this enables the optimal values of the parameters to be determined by minimizing the cost through a gradient search method. The algorithm is illustrated by a computed example. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Sirisena H.R."]

Title: STOCHASTIC CONTROL WITH OBSERVATION COSTS.
Abstract: The discrete stochastic linear servomechanism problem is reformulated to include the costs of observations. The optimal control solution to this modified problem is found to resemble the solution for the standard servomechanism problem, but the optimal observation policy requires the solution of a TPBV (two point boundary value problem) which may be computed a priori. The problem is further extended to include the class of nonlinear systems suggested by dynamic population system models. The solution to this extended problem is an iterative solution involving the second order conditional-mean estimation and prediction algorithms and the linear control algorithms which are applied about the linearized predicted trajectories.
Name: ["Sauer Gregory J.", "Melsa James L."]

Title: ON A LANGUAGE FOR THE TRANSFORMATION OF GRAPHS INTENDED FOR THE SPECIFICATION OF AUTOMATA.
Abstract: The notion of a command of bounded complexity intended for graph transformations is introduced. The existence of a finite universal system of commands is proved. The concept of a graph-algorithm, similar to the conception of an algorithm due to Kolmogorov-Uspenskii, is discussed. These concepts form a basis for the development of a general notion of a growing automaton and may also be used for the description of the operation of finite automata.
Name: ["Barzdin Ya.M.", "Kalnin'sh Ya.Ya."]

Title: DATA MANAGEMENT SYSTEM UTILIZING AN ASSOCIATIVE MEMORY.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: Since much of the processing of data management problems involves the manipulation of data by content rather than physical location, it appears that associative memories may be useful for the solution of these problems. In order to demonstrate the feasibility of utilizing a hardware associative memory, a data management system called Information Systems for Associative Memories (IFAM) has been developed and implemented. After presenting a brief description of associative memories, the implementation and capabilities of IFAM are described.
Name: ["DeFiore Casper R.", "Berra P.Bruce"]

Title: OPTIMAL FEEDBACK CONTROL AND KALMAN FILTER DESIGN VIA AN INTERACTIVE COMPUTING AND VISUAL DISPLAY SYSTEM.
Abstract: This article describes a unique, recently developed capability for the interactive design of Kalman filters and optimal feedback controllers for stochastic linear multivariable systems. The main program, termed OPCON for OPtimal CONtrol, is written in FORTRAN and makes full use of the on-line computational capabilities of a Digital Equipment Corporation time-shared PDP-6 computer in conjunction with a PDP-1 visual display unit.
Name: ["Michael Gerald J.", "Dubin Alan P."]

Title: Simulation of an individual making decisions under uncertainty
Abstract: A computer simulation model, SIDTP (Simulation of Individual Decisions through Information Processing), of a person making nine decisions under uncertainty is sketched. Eight of a subject's (S's) choices are consistent with the Laplace or maximize expected value criteria and S's other is consistent with the Savage (minimax regret) criterion (see Luce and Raiffa, 1957).SIDIP implies that the subject does not use the conventional computational processes dictated by those criteria. SIDIP reproduces S's articulated choice behavior:inconsistent use of choice criteria, rejection of some alternatives,and eventual choice from the preferred alternatives. Analysis of information processing models of suboptimal decision behavior suggests operational techniques by which decision making can be improved. ¬© 1973 Proceedings - Winter Simulation Conference. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Tuggle F.D.", "Barron F.H.", "Day R.O."]
Affiliations: [' University of Kansas Lawrcnce', ' University of Kansas Lawrcnce', ' University of Kansas Lawrcnce']

Title: A Parallel Algorithm for the Efficient Solution of a General Class of Recurrence Equations
Abstract: An mth-order recurrence problem is defined as the compu tation of the series x1, X2,‚Ä¶, XN, where xi=fi(xi-1,‚Ä¶, xi-m) for some function fi This paper uses a technique called recursive doubling in an algorithm for solving a large class of recurrence problems on parallel computers such as the Illiac IV. Recursive doubling involves the splitting of the computation of a function into two equally complex subfunctions whose evaluation can be performed simultaneously in two separate processors. Successive splitting of each of these subfunctions spreads the computation over more processors. This algorithm can be applied to any recurrence equation of the form Xi= f(bi, g(ai, xi-1)) where f and g are functions that satisfy certain distributive and associative-like properties. Although this recurrence is first order, all linear mth-order recurrence equations can be cast into this form. Suitable applications include linear recurrence equations, polynomial evaluation, several nonlinear problems, the determination of the maximum or minimum of N numbers, and the solution of tridiagonal linear equations. The resulting algorithm computes the entire series x1, ‚Ä¶, XNin time proportional to [log2/N] on a computer with N-fold parallelism. On a serial computer, computation time is proportional to N. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Kogge P.M."]

Title: A Comparison of Some Theoretical Models of Parallel Computation
Abstract: In this paper we briefly describe and compare a number of theoretical models for parallel computation; namely, Petri nets, computation graphs, and parallel program schemata. We discuss various problems and properties of parallel computation that can be studied within these formulations and indicate the ties between these properties and the more practical aspects of parallel computation. We show how marked graphs, a particular type of Petri net, are a restricted type of computation graph and indicate how some results of marked graphs can be obtained from known results of computation graphs.
