Also, for schemata we discuss the decidability versus undecidability of various properties and several techniques of schemata composition. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Miller R.E."]
Affiliations: [' IBM T. J. Watson Research Center']

Title: RETRIEVAL IN A SET-THEORETICALLY STRUCTURED DATA BASE: CONCEPTS AND PRACTICAL CONSIDERATIONS.
Abstract: By generalizing the concept of inverted file a data base organization is obtained that may easily be described in terms of mathematical sets and relations. The approach offers a number of advantages, among them clarity and precision in the description of the data base organization and the processes within it, a certain degree of adaptability and portability, and above all, by including intermediate language expressions as part of the data base, exceptional flexibility towards changes in the data base.
Name: ["Kraegeloh Klaus Dieter", "Lockemann Peter C."]

Title: A reliability model using markov chains for utility evaluation of computer systems onboard ships
Abstract: Introduction of computers onboard ships to provide a high degree of automation necessitates calculation of computer system reliability to evaluate the utility of the system. The reliability aspect of the system is simulated by a model using Markov chains. Having defined the system state space and the transition rates, the model provides evaluation of the state probabilities. Evaluation of system utility is based on computer task values and the failure probabilities. Application of the analysis model to an existing system reveals information useful in assigning redundancy, eliminating bottle-necks and allocating spare parts. ¬© 1973 Proceedings - Winter Simulation Conference. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Boe C.", "Heimly T.", "Mathiesen T.-C."]

Title: On the Approximation of Optimal Realizable Linear Filters Using a Karhunen-Lo√®ve Expansion
Abstract: The Karhunen-Lo√®ve expansion of a random process is used to derive the impulse response of the optimal realizable linear estimator for the process. The expansion is truncated to yield an approximate state-variable model of the process in terms of the first N eigenvalues and eigenfunctions. The Kalmaa-Bucy filter for this model provides an approximate realizable linear estimator which approaches the optimal one as N ‚Üí ‚àû. A bound on the truncation error is obtained. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Fortmann T.E.", "Anderson B.D.O."]

Title: On Convergence of Distortion for Block and Tree Encoding of Symmetric Sources
Abstract: For symmetric sources we examine the rate of convergence to the rate-distortion function using block codes and tree codes. With block codes the average distortion decreases toward distortion D at a doubly exponential rate in block length for any fixed rate greater than R(D), the rate-distortion function. For tree codes a difference equation for the probability distribution of the distortion is derived with tree depth as an independent variable. Its numerical solution suggests that the same doubly exponential convergence behavior applies to tree codes. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Omura J.K.", "Shohara A."]

Title: A General Dynamic Programming Solution of Discrete-Time Linear Optimal Control Problems
Abstract: An optimal control problem with linear dynamics and quadratic criterion is imbedded in a family of problems characterized by both initial and terminal points. The optimal value function is jointly quadratic in initial and terminal points, and the optimal control is jointly linear. Recursive formulas for the coefficients of these functions are developed. This generalized procedure can be used to solve several versions of the problem not solvable by the standard one-ended imbedding technique. In particular, a procedure doubling the number of stages at each iteration is given for problems with time-invariant coefficients. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Dreyfus S.E.", "Kan Y.C."]
Affiliations: [' University of California', ' University of Louvain']

Title: PRACTICAL FILTER FOR NOISY DYNAMIC SYSTEMS WITH UNKNOWN TIME-VARYING PARAMETERS.
Abstract: The problem of a practical filter for discrete-time, dynamic systems with unknown parameters whose variation cannot be estimated in advance is considered. The modeling errors caused by the unknown parameters degrade the filter performance and sometimes lead to divergence of estimation errors. Divergence is said to occur when the calculated covariance of estimation errors becomes unrealistically small with the actual covariance. A practical filter that modifies the calculated covariance is developed as a technique for controlling the divergence. This is done by testing whether or not the actual residual at each stage is likely to have come from the calculated distribution, and the calculated covariance is modified when the test is rejected. The numerical results of digital simulation indicate that divergence of estimation errors is observed when the a priori information for dynamic systems is in error and that the divergence is prevented by the proposed filter.
Name: ["Soeda Takashi", "Yoshimura Toshio"]

Title: A New Class of Lower Bounds to Information Rates of Stationary Sources via Conditional Rate-Distortion Functions
Abstract: A new class of lower bounds to rate-distortion functions of stationary processes with memory and single-letter vector-valued distortion measures is derived. This class is shown to include or imply all other well-known lower bounds to rates of such sources and distortion measures. The derivation is based on the definition and properties of the conditional rate-distortion function. In addition to providing a unified and intuitive approach to lower bounds, this approach yields several interesting relations among conditional, joint, and marginal rates that are similar to and sometimes identical with the analogous relations among the corresponding entropies. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gray R.M."]

Title: ON CONTROLLABLE PERIODIC SEMI-MARKOV PROCESSES.
Abstract: The optimal control problem for periodic semi-Markov processes is considered. The algorithm presented for the solution of this problem with a finite number of possible states and an infinite time is a generalization of the algorithm due to R. A. Howard.
Name: ["Teplitskii M.G."]

Title: A wait untilalgorithm for general purpose simulation languages
Abstract: Modem simulation languages such as SIMSCRIPT II and SIMULA 67 are very powerful general purpose languages which contain facilities to handle lists and to schedule events in simulated system time (imperative sequencing statements). These languages do not include some of the useful but more specialized features of previous languages (GPSS, CSL, SOL) especially interrogative sequencing statements such as SEIZE <facility> or WATT UNTIL-Boolean expression>; however, the definition capability of the new languages is powerful enough to permit their extension to include the interrogative features. The addition of some features of GPSS to SIMULA 67 was presented at a previous SIMULATION CONFERENCE. The present paper extends that work by describing an efficient algorithm which adds the WAIT UNTIL procedure to SIMULA. ¬© 1973 Proceedings - Winter Simulation Conference. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Vaucher J.G."]

Title: Verification of Long-Term Forecasts of Tehcnico-Economic Indices of Open-Pit Workings by the Methods of the Statistical Theory of Prediction. | [VERIFIKATSIYA DOLGOSROVHNOGO PROGNOZA TEKHNIKO-EKONOMICHESKIKH POKAZATELEI OTKRYTYKH GORNYKH RABOT METODAMI STATISTICHEKOI TEORII PREDSKAZANII.]
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii, Gornyi Zhurnal
Abstract: The statistical theory of prediction develops quantitative methods of forecasting and the ways to improve their accuracy. Forecasting is accomplished by different methods of extrapolation of time series. Under the conditions of the statistical theory of prediction verification of the forecasts is carried out by confirming each forecast by the prediction methods. Three statistical methods of calculation of the prospects for future dynamics are proposed for long-term forecasting of technico-economic indices of open-pit mining works. These are: the method of direct extrapolation of the forecast trend, exponential smoothing in accordance with Brown and adaptive smoothing by Laguerre polynomials.
Name: ["Eremina V.I."]

Title: On the generalization of observers to systems with unmeasurable, unknown inputs
Abstract: The theory of observers for linear, time-invariant systems is generalized to systems where some of the inputs are unmeasurable and statistically unknown. Criteria for the existance of such observers are developed and an example is presented. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Hostetter G.H.", "Meditch J.S."]

Title: DESCRIPTION OF A GENERAL USE AUTOMATED DATA REDUCTION SYSTEM.
Source: Int Congr on Instrum in Aerosp Simulation Facil, 5th, Rec
Abstract: A versatile automated data system has been developed and implemented for use in a laboratory operating arc jet wind tunnels. A digital tape recorder is used, with an analog tape option available for increased time resolution. Data reduction calculations are performed on a timesharing computer using a set of standard programs. Reduced data are listed, and disk data sets are also created for plotting or for use in later calculations. Operational costs of the system are reasonable and both large and small data reduction tasks are handled readily.
Name: ["Wakefield Roy M.", "Pearson Jr. B.Douglas"]

Title: Frequency-Domain Criteria for Stability of a Class of Nonlinear Stochastic Systems
Abstract: The problem of finding frequency-domain conditions that are sufficient to ensure asymptotic stability with probability one (ASWP 1) of a Lur√©-type system with white-noise input disturbance is considered. It is shown that, if the noise is linearly related to the state of the system, a relatively simple frequency-domain inequality that guarantees ASWP 1 of the system exists. The stochastic version of the second method of Lyapunov, along with a Meyer-Kalman-Yakubovich(MKY)-type lemma, is used to derive such a condition, assuming first that only sector information of the nonlinearity is available. A modification of this lemma is subsequently used to derive an improved stability condition, assuming that both sector and slope information of the nonlinearity are available. Finally, the case of a differential system with white-noise parameter perturbation is considered and an illustrative example is presented. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Mahalanabis A.K.", "Purkayastha S."]
Affiliations: [' Indian Institute of Technology', ' Electronics Corporation of India']

Title: Managerial control systems based on learning curve models
Abstract: Human operator output in the performance of repetitive tasks increases with practice, resulting in the ‚Äò learning curve ‚Äô graph well known in industrial engineering circles. This paper describes the construction of a systems model of the learning curve, the model parameters such as the learning time constant being readily estimated graphically from historical data or in advance of the event using a digital computer algorithm. Learning curve models for individual operators, and for groups of operators, are then used as basic elements in a managerial control system, the inputs to this system being operator effort, industrial engineering effort, and material and financial resources, whilst the output will be completed tasks. The managerial control system is designed to increase productivity by considering four separate feedback loops incorporating the monitoring of individual performance, monitoring of training schemes, updating of time standards, and identification of worker spare capacity leading to group incentive and bettor performance. Each loop is illustrated by an example taken from industry, with associated cost benefits estimated directly from the learning curve models. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Towill D.R.", "Bevis F.W."]

Title: Single step detection of blurred images in a coherent optical processor
Abstract: Two important operations that can be performed by coherent optical processing systems are image detection and image restoration. These operations require complex spatial filters, and if both operations are to be performed, cascaded processing stages employing two separate spatial filters are usually needed. Spatial filters are described that will perform in a single step both operations simultaneously, thus eliminating the need of extra processing stages while providing the advantages of higher efficiency and smaller space requirements. The filters are characterized by their simplicity and are easily fabricated using conventional techniques. Experimental results are presented. ¬© 1973 Optical Society of America.
Name: ["Jablonowski D.P.", "Lee S.H."]

Title: Constrained sequential-block search in simulation experimentation
Abstract: This paper describes the application of sequential-block search techniques to simulation experimentation with constrained systems.Two basically different approaches are examined. One approach combines designed experiments,multiple regression,and mathematical optimization to predict a constrained optimum solution, which is then checked by further experimentation in the region of the predicted solution.A second approach employs a sequential optimum-seeking technique,such as gradient search or sequential simplex search, modified to accommodate constraints.These techniques are illustrated with a simple inventory system modeled with the GASP-II simulation language. A comparison of the effectiveness of these approaches is presented. ¬© 1973 Proceedings - Winter Simulation Conference. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Biles W.E."]

Title: Context-free error analysis by evaluation of algebraic power series
Source: Proceedings of the Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
Abstract: Optimal error analysis with respect to a context-free language may be viewed as the evaluation of an algebraic power series. By generalization of the nodal span context-free recognition algorithm, any algebraic power series is computable in O(n) steps. The closure of algebraic power series under sequential transduction yields a generous class of reasonable error measures for which optimal analysis is O(n). Included is minimizing the number of symbol insertions, deletions and/or replacements needed for correction, a special case which has been studied separately. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Teitelbaum R."]

Title: Search Properties of Some Sequential Decoding Algorithms
Abstract: Sequential decoding procedures are studied in the context of selecting a path through a tree. Several algorithms are considered and their properties compared. It is shown that the stack algorithm introduced by Zigangirov and by Jelinek is essentially equivalent to the Fano algorithm with regard to the set of nodes examined and the path selected, although the description, implementation, and action of the two algorithms are quite different. A modified Fano algorithm is introduced, in which the quantizing parameter Œî is eliminated. It can be inferred from limited simulation results that, at least in some applications, the new algorithm is computationally inferior to the old; however, it is of some theoretical interest since the conventional Fano algorithm may be considered to be a quantized version of it. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Geist J.M."]

Title: Suboptimal Control of Linear Systems by Augmentation with Application to Freeway Traffic Regulation
Abstract: The development of on-ramp metering control strategies for a freeway can be aided by the well-developed theory of linear optimal control. However, an adequate model of an appropriate form must be available. Recently developed ‚Äúaggregate variable‚Äù models appear to be best suited to this purpose. In these models the freeway is sectioned into lengths of about ¬Ω mi and traffic is described in terms of the aggregate variables section speed, section density, and volume. The model is used to formulate a linear regulator problem with quadratic cost for the purpose of determining a feedback control rule which returns the freeway to nominal conditions after a disturbance. The solution of the regulator problem involves considerable computation difficulty when the order of the system is large, In a large class of applications the optimal control law has a local structure which can be exploited in a computationally efficient manner to yield a suboptimal control with little loss of system performance. A new technique, the augmentation method, is presented for constructing a suboptimal control from a set of optimal controls for low-order sub-systems. New results are presented which provide a rational and elegant measure for the additional cost associated with an arbitrary stabilizing suboptimal control. Additional results pertain especially to the augmentation procedure. The models and suboptimal control scheme are applied to a specific detailed design for an 8-mi segment of the San Diego Freeway in Los Angeles. Simulations are shown illustrating the effectiveness of such traffic-responsive controls in clearing up congestion due to traffic incidents. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Isaksen L.", "Payne H.J."]

Title: Sequential Non-Gaussian Pattern Recognition with Supervised Learning
Abstract: This paper considers binary pattern recognition of a non-Gaussian pattern in Gaussian noise using supervised learning. The scheme is both structure and parameter adaptive. To facilitate a feasible solution, certain judicious approximations are used. Two examples are presented to demonstrate the learning capability of the proposed algorithms. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Rajasekaran P.K.", "Srinath M.D."]
Affiliations: [' Indian Institute of Technology', ' Southern Methodist University']

Title: Stability Structure for Feedback Systems Having Unstable Open Loops
Abstract: Previous structure for feedback-system stability based upon causal inverse operators on normed linear spaces is extended to include the ‚Äúopen-loop unstable‚Äù case. Simple illustrations are given. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Damborg M.J.", "Naylor A.W."]
Affiliations: [' University of Washington', ' University of Michigan']

Title: Probabilistic reinforcement algorithms for the reconstruction of pictures from their projections‚Ä†
Abstract: Probabilistic reinforcement algorithms are described for the reconstruction of digital pictures, consisting of two or more grey levels, from their projections. The power of those algorithms are illustrated by a few examples, as reconstructed by a digital computer. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Krishnan S.", "Prabhu S.S.", "Krishnamurthy E.V."]

Title: On the Error Probability for a Class of Binary Recursive Feedback Strategies
Abstract: The error probability for a class of binary recursive feedback strategies is evaluated. An exact analysis is given for both a nonsequential and a sequential decision strategy. We obtain the interesting result that even for the nonsequential receiver the error probability vanishes exponentially fast at channel capacity. A similar result had been previously obtained by Horstein for the sequential receiver, but was believed to be a consequence of the sequential nature of his decision strategy. For rates below capacity our feedback strategies have two error exponents, i.e., a lower error exponent E<sup>‚àí</sup>(R) and an upper error exponent E<sup>+</sup>(R). The lower error exponent E<sup>‚àí</sup>(R) exhibits an anomalous behavior in that E<sup>‚àí</sup>(R) increases monotonically from E<sup>‚àí</sup>(0) = 0 to E<sup>‚àí</sup>(C) = E(C) as the rate R increases from 0 to capacity. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Schalkwijk J.P.M.", "Post K.A."]
Affiliations: [' Technological University', ' University of California at San Diego']

Title: On feature extraction in pattern recognition
Abstract: This paper proposes the concept of equivocation from information theory as a criterion for feature selection. An expression for equivocation is derived in terms of class conditional probabilities. By making the assumption that the patterns in each class are normally distributed, a transformation matrix that minimizes the equivocation in the reduced dimension is obtained. Furthermore, a relationship between the equivocation and the expected divergence between any pair of classes is presented. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Babu C.C."]

Title: Automatic classification of mass spectra by means of digital learning nets
Abstract: The method of pattern recognition by means of s.l.a.m. (stored-logic adaptive modules) has been applied to the automatic classification of mass spectra into broad chemical groups, with zero-error results. ¬© 1973, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Stonham T.J.", "Aleksander I.", "Camp M.", "Shaw M.A.", "Pike W.T."]
Affiliations: ['Electronics Laboratories University of Kent', 'Unilever Research Port Sunlight']

Title: Finite fuzzy automata, regular fuzzy languages, and pattern recognition
Abstract: Fuzzy set theory is summarized, and finite fuzzy automata and languages are described. Some results in fuzzy languages based on the "max(min)" rule are discussed. An application of fuzzy languages in syntactic pattern analysis is described and is illustrated by a simple example. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Thomason M.G."]

Title: Application Of Kalman Filtering Technique To Nuclear Reactors
Abstract: This paper deals with the application of Kalman filter for estimating the non-measurable variables of a nuclear pool-type research reactor using noisy measurements of only a few variables. The estimated variables are used to identify two parameters of the reactor dynamics. These estimates are also useful for reactor control, protection, instrumentation, operator information, etc. The filtering technique can be applied to more complex nuclear steam systems. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Godbole S.S."]

Title: The Computational Solution of Optimal Control Problems with Time Lag
Abstract: A gradient computational procedure is developed for discrete-time optimal control problems in which the current cost and rule governing state transitions depend on the entire past history of states and decisions. A condition necessary for optimality is also deduced in two ways and given physical interpretation. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Dreyfus S.E."]

Title: On Subspaces Associated with Partial Reconstruction of State Vectors, the Structure Algorithm, and the Predictable Directions of Riccati Equations
Abstract: The close relations are discussed that exist among the three subspaces that arise in three apparently unrelated problem areas: 1) the subspace associated with the error of state vector reconstruction in informationally decentralized control problems; 2) the subspace associated with the solution of the Riccati equation; and 3) the null space of the certain observation matrix constructed by the structure algorithm. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Aoki M."]

Title: Bounds on the Number of Processors and Time for Multiprocessor Optimal Schedules
Abstract: Two problems of importance for the scheduling of multiprocessing systems composed of identical units are discussed in this paper. 1) Given a partially ordered set of computations represented by the vertices of an acyclic directed graph with their associated execution times, find the minimum number of processors in order to execute them in a time not exceeding the length of the critical path of this graph. 2) Determine the minimum time to process this set of computations when a fixed number of processors is available. A unified formulation for lower bounds on the minimum number of processors and on time is presented. These lower bounds are sharper than previously known values and provide a general framework that gives insight for deriving simplified expressions. A new upper bound on the minimum number of processors is presented, which is sharper than the known bounds. The computational aspects of these bounds are also discussed. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Fernandez E.B."]
Affiliations: [' University of Chile', ' University of California']

Title: Industrial Robots - Workers of Steel. | [INDUSTRIEROBOTER, STAEHLERNE HANDLANGER.]
Abstract: The currently available unintelligent robots and their second and third generation, the intelligent and superintelligent robots, are described. Examples illustrating the use of robots in automobile industry, forging, metal forming, etc. are presented, and economical aspects are dealt with.
Name: ["Schuenemann John"]

Title: RECONSTRUCTION OF BINARY PATTERNS FROM A FEW PROJECTIONS.
Abstract: There are situations in the natural sciences and medicine in which it is desirable to estimate the gray levels of a picture at individual points from the integrals of the gray levels along straight lines at a few angles. In a number of applications it is possible to assume that the picture is a binary pattern. A number of computer algorithms have been proposed to solve this problem. In this paper the author proposes a new algorithm and compares it experimentally to some previously proposed algorithms.
Name: ["Herman Gabor T."]

Title: LOGICAL ORGANIZATION OF A PROBLEM-ORIENTED MICROPROGRAM-CONTROLLED PROCESSOR.
Abstract: A problem-oriented processor is capable of adapting to several problems like, e. g. , the writing of compilers and operating systems. The requirements for the logical organization of a problem-oriented processor are derived and the logical structure is defined by describing the functional units and the microinstruction format. An example for a micro subroutine is given and compared with an equivalent program written in a conventional machine language.
Name: ["Haff Norbert"]

Title: INFORMATION-THEORETIC INEQUALITIES AND SUPEREFFICIENT ESTIMATES.
Abstract: It is proved that superefficient estimates for a matrix loss function do not exist in the class of estimates uniformly at least asymptotically efficient. An analogous result is established for sequential estimates. Integral asymptotic bounds for the estimation risks are also obtained for a large class of loss functions and a priori distribution functions.
Name: ["Ibragimov I.A.", "Khas'minskii R.Z."]

Title: Model Scaling for Nonlinear Dynamic Systems. | SKALOWANIE MODELI NIELINIOWYCH OBIEKTOW DYNAMICZNYCH.
Abstract: A method for determining analog computer equations for modeling nonlinear dynamic systems is presented. The equations derived comply with the scaling factors criteria given in the paper. The amplitude scaling problem is solved using Lyapunov stability theory for estimation of the maximum values of variables. A scaling algorithm which provides a means for determining a program for digital comoputer functioning as a hybrid system is given. The method proposed is illustrated with some numerical examples.
Name: ["Znamirowski Lech"]

Title: Recognizing machines with parametric and nonparametric learning methods using contextual information
Abstract: Pattern recognition systems using information from the pattern which follows the present pattern are discussed. Parametric learning methods in the supervised and unsupervised machines are proposed and compare favorably with conventional methods. Furthermore, a semilinear machine with a nonparametric learning method is considered. The results of computer experiments with artificially generated data and with handprinted alphanumeric characters are given to show that the approach we adopt is quite useful for recognition of Markovian patterns. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Shimura M."]

Title: HAPPE HONEYWELL ASSOCIATIVE PARALLEL PROCESSING ENSEMBLE.
Abstract: The Honeywell Associative Parallel Processing Ensemble (HAPPE) is built to demonstrate the basic simplicity of hardware concepts inherent in parallel associative processing. HAPPE is implemented with the same standard circuit building blocks (MSI's, ROM's, and RAM's) that are used in all conventional computers. By using standard building blocks a long time objection to associative memory systems, that of requiring special purpose (low usage) circuits is overcome.
Name: ["Marvel Orin E."]

Title: MAXIMUM COST TRAJECTORIES IN OPTIMALLY CONTROLLED STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: An algorithm is provided for finding the locally worst case sample paths of an optimally controlled linear jump parameter system. The resulting value of lambda //1(o, omega //o) provides a lower bound on the cost that may accrue to optimal system. This lower bound is useful in situations in which a constraint is placed upon the cost; e. g. , the cost must in no circumstance exceed M. If lambda //1(o, omega //o) greater than M, the locally worst case analysis guarantees that the specification will not be met. Unfortunately, the converse is not always true.
Name: ["Sworder D.D."]

Title: Character recognition by complex filtering in reading machines
Abstract: In order to investigate the possibility of constructing a compact and relatively simple character recognizing reading machine for the blind, a character recognizer has been built and tested with 44 different symbols. This device is based on correlation with a Fourier transform hologram in a coherent optical system. The symbols tested consisted of the lower case Swedish alphabet, the numerals 0-9 and 5 punctuation marks. The results show that, provided an appropriate input device can be constructed, it is possible to build a reading machine capable of reading one printed character at a time with an accuracy sufficient for most reading purposes. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["H√•rd S.", "Feuk T."]
Keywords: ["aids for the blind", "complex filtering", "holography", "optical correlator", "pattern recognition"]

Title: Synthesis of a Class of Self-Oscillating Optimal Relay Systems of Plant Control of the Second Order. | [O SINTEZE ODNOGO KLASSA AVTOKOLEBATEL'NYKH OPTIMAL'NYKH RELEINYKH SISTEM UPRAVLENIYA OB''EKTAMI VTOROGO PORYADKA.]
Abstract: Methods of synthesis of a control device for self-oscillating optimal relay control systems are considered. Special features of the structure of phase trajectories, given one compromise criterion, are investigated. A number of supplementary functions are introduced for the synthesis of the control device. They are used in the logic unit for selecting the control action.
Name: ["Dolgozvyag V.A.", "Fedunets P.D.", "Derevyanko P.F."]

Title: CHOICE OF OBSERVATION LAW IN THE CASE OF AN ARBITRARY DISTURBANCE.
Abstract: An investigation is made of the optimal control of an observation process in the case of an arbitrary correlation matrix of the random disturbances in the observation channel. In the general case, the problem reduces to controlling several deterministic systems, to which the usual methods of optimal control are applicable.
Name: ["Kolmanovskiy V.B."]

Title: HEURISTIC MONITOR FOR COMPUTER-AIDED INSTRUCTION.
Abstract: A CAI (computer-aided instruction) system which is based on algorithms for problem generation and solution is described. (This particular system teaches digital logic design. ) A heuristic monitor has been developed which tailors the path taken by each student through the course concepts in accordance with his previous performance. This monitor is described as well as general techniques for problem generation and solution monitoring.
Name: ["Koffman E.B.", "Walrath S.J."]

Title: REALIZATION OF A HORIZONTAL COLLISION AVOIDANCE SYSTEM.
Abstract: For a two-aircraft encounter, the computer realization of a cooperative horizontal collision avoidance system is analyzed. The system is based on range, relative bearing, relative heading and speed ratio information, and the realization accounts for the turn dynamics of both aircraft.
Name: ["Karmarkar J.S.", "Merz A.W."]

Title: Influence of input quantizer step sizes on the processing gain of digital beamformers
Source: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Abstract: Utilizing a formulation of output power of a digital beamformer with input quantizers of unequal input and output step sizes given previously, the optimum quantizer step sizes which yield maximum processing gain for a typical array were searched by the method of ‚Äústeepest ascent‚Äù with a digital computer. For the case of two-bit /channel quantization with small input SNR (‚©Ω ‚àí 10 dB), the array gain surface as a function of two independent step variables exhibits a maximum which is only slightly greater than the maximum array gain achievable with uniform input quantizers. For larger input SNR, the array gain surface tends to be concave upward, and the performance of uniform quantizers can at the best be a suboptimum. The high theoretical processing gain in the limiting case of very large step sizes is attributed to a threshold effect of the input quantizers. Except for these latter conditions, the optimum uniform quantizing condition previously reported by the author represents essentially valid optimum design. ¬© 1986, American Association of Physics Teachers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Wang H.S.C."]

Title: OPTIMAL MAINTENANCE POLICY OF A MACHINE SUBJECT TO FAILURE.
Abstract: Optimal maintenance policies for a machine with degradation in performance with age and subject to failure are derived using optimal control theory. The optimal policies are shown to be, normally, of bang-coast nature, except in the case when probability of machine failure is a function of maintenance. It is also shown, in the deterministic case that a higher depreciation rate tends to reverse this policy to coast-bang. When the probability of failure is a function of maintenance, considerable computational effort is needed to obtain an optimal policy and the resulting policy is not easily implementable. For this case also, an optimal policy in the class of bang-coast policies is derived, using a semi-Markov decision model. A simple procedure for modifying the probability of machine failure with maintenance is employed. Numerical examples are presented to illustrate the results obtained.
Name: ["Alam M.", "Sarma V.V.S."]

Title: METHOD OF CONCEPT FORMATION BASED ON FUNCTIONAL DECOMPOSITION.
Abstract: An algorithm for concept formation is described and preliminary results are presented. The algorithm attempts to reduce concept formation time by decomposing a concept formation problem into a sequence of smaller problems. The decomposition of a problem produces a hierarchy of concept ‚Ä≥parts‚Ä≥ used in the solution.
Name: ["Towster Edwin"]

Title: DeVILBISS-TRALLFA SPRAY PAINTING ROBOT.
Abstract: An electronically-controlled manipulator designed to replace the human spray gun operator in direct industrial application processes is described in this paper. The unit can be taught a complex number of different instructions in seconds to perform a paint spraying task and becomes ready on its own for as long as required. It remembers all instructions given to it because it has its own magnetic tape memory system.
Name: ["Haugan K.M."]

Title: STRUCTURE OF MEMORY IN CONCEPT FORMATION.
Abstract: This paper presents an approach to simulate one type of the mental processes of the human brain. This process permits immediate perception of concepts which consist of different attributes. A model of concept formation based on the ability of the human brain to find similar attributes in different concepts and different attributes in similar concepts is offered.
Name: ["Khalil T.M.", "Lovitsky Vladimir"]

Title: MINIMIZATION OF BAROMETRIC ALTIMETRY ERROR FOR AIRCRAFT LANDING BY STATISTICAL REGRESSION.
Abstract: The correlations between air pressure at different altitudes are used to calculate a maximum likelihood prediction curve for pressure with respect to altitude by means of statistical regression. The airport pressure is fed before landing into an onboard computer which calculates the altitude from a third order equation. The coefficients of this equation are given which are calculated before flight using correlation coefficients, pressure variances, and a local and seasonal mean pressure profile. As an example the method is applied upon a density profile for lack of sufficient data about pressure correlation.
Name: ["Becker Klaus"]

Title: ITERATIVE QUADRATIC OPTIMIZATION OF NONLINEAR TIME-LAG CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Suboptimal control problems involving nonlinear systems which contain a nonconstant time delay are considered, along with the standard quadratic cost functionals. Instead of attempting to satisfy a set of necessary conditions for optimality, the nonlinear optimization problem is treated heuristically as a perturbation on a linear problem. An iterative procedure that converges rapidly to a suboptimal control is derived.
Name: ["Vidyasagar M.", "Gracovetsky Serge A."]

Title: Optimization of k-Nearest-Neighbor Density Estimates
Abstract: Nonparametric density estimation using the k-nearest-neighbor approach is discussed. By developing a relation between the volume and the coverage of a region, a functional form for the optimum k in terms of the sample size, the dimensionality of the observation space, and the underlying probability distribution is obtained. Within the class of density functions that can be made circularly symmetric by a linear transformation, the optimum matrix for use in a quadratic form metric is obtained. For Gaussian densities this becomes the inverse covariance matrix that is often used without proof of optimality. The close relationship of this approach to that of Parzen estimators is then investigated. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Fukunaga K.", "Hostetler L.D."]

Title: On the use of binary and gray code schemes for continuous-tone picture representation
Abstract: The paper discusses the idea of iterating the conversion of a continuous-tone picture from binary to Gray code representation. A simple recursive function is defined by means of which the value of the ith bit representing a picture point's grey level after the mth iteration is determined. The resulting rearrangement of grey levels as well as that of the bits throughout the planes is discussed next. The iteration is shown to repeat after 2‚Ä≥ steps, where n is the number of bit planes representing the picture. A data compression scheme is developed on the basis that prior to exact repetition, approximate repetitions take place during the iterations, and the resulting picture is almost the same as the original. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Deutsch E.S."]
Keywords: ["binary code", "picture compression", "unit distance code", "code representation", "representation simple"]

Title: Guiding a robot by visual feedback in assembling tasks
Abstract: A system whereby a robot puts a block into a box using visual feedback is described. In this experiment, the difference between the desired position and the actual position of the object is recognized visually and corrected by moving the manipulator. The experimental results show that such visual feedback is effective in performing the precise positioning. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Shirai Y.", "Inoue H."]

Title: ANALYTIC DESIGN OF ADAPTIVE SAMPLING CONTROL LAW IN SAMPLED-DATA SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A unified analytic approach is presented for the design of adaptive sampling control law in sampled-data systems. This is accomplished by introducing an objective function which measures the performance of the sampler over each sampling interval, and then minimizing it to obtain the sampling control law. A total of six different control laws, which are functions of the sampled function, are obtainable from the generalized objective function by selecting different weighting coefficients. More than half of these control laws are identical to existing results. Similar control laws as functions of the system output can be derived as well. An experimental evaluation of the performances of four representative control laws in a second order system is included. The results show that all of them can substantially improve sampling efficiency. It is found that the improvements are nearly the same for all the control laws. This implies that control law with the simplest structure provides the best choice for practical applications.
Name: ["Hsia T.C."]

Title: Possibilities of Suboptimal Control in the Linear-Quadratic Problem. | O MOZLIWOSCIACH STEROWANIA SUBOPTYMALNEGO W PROBLEMIE LINIOWO-KWADRATOWYM.
Abstract: Possibilities of a suboptimal control for the linear problem with the quadratic performance criterion and fixed terminal time are discussed. The suboptimal matrix of feedback gains was chosen as a constant matrix. As a result of this choice, the theorem on the necessary condition for the matrix elements was obtained. The definition of r-suboptimality which makes it possible to compare various suboptimal controls is quoted.
Name: ["Gosiewski Anatol", "Krawczyk Jacek B."]

Title: STABILITY ANALYSIS ALGORITHM FOR LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH n TIME LAGS USING PARAMETER PLANE METHOD.
Source: J Inst Eng (India), Electron Telecommun Eng Div
Abstract: A stability analysis of linear systems with n time lags is discussed. A computer algorithm and program is developed for computing parameters alpha and beta for the stable range of a system with two transport time lags. A system is considered whose characteristic equation depends linearly and nonlinearly on two system parameters.
Name: ["Desai R.C.", "Shah P.C.", "Lalwani C.S."]

Title: Some Aspects of the Inverted Pendulum Problem for Modeling of Locomotion Systems
Abstract: The inverted pendulum can be used as one of the sim-plest models of a biped locomotion system, Problems of stability, periodic motion, and locomotion of the inverted pendulum are con-sidered in this paper. The development algorithms of this paper hopefully can be used for study, simulation, and analysis of more realistic models of biped locomotion systems. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Hemami H.", "Weimer F.C.", "Koozekanani S.H."]

Title: Bayes Decision Rules Based on Objective Priors
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics
Abstract: The problem of statistical decision making under uncertainty is considered. A Bayes approach based upon prior probabilities which are found using an objective inference technique developed by Kashyap is proposed as the basic solution procedure. The problem is formulated in a statistical decision theory format and the general solution technique is outlined. Using this inference technique, it is possible to have different priors for different experiments. A general decision criterion is formulated to handle these situations. It is shown that in situations where the experimentation is fixed and the decision problem is faced repeatedly, but not necessarily an infinite number of times, this approach is justifiable. In situations where there is a choice of experiments, these arguments are not as conclusive; however, the approach still has practical merit as an objective alternative to the minimax approach. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Oberlin T.L."]

Title: A unified algorithm for designing multidrop teleprocessing networks
Source: Data Networks: Analysis and Design - 3rd Data Communications Symposium, DATACOMM 1973
Abstract: The problem or designing minimum cost multidrop lines which connect remate terminals to a concentrator or a central data processing computer is studied. In some cases, optimal solutions can be obtained by using either linear integer programming or a branch-bound method. These approaches are not practical since they lack flexibility and require an enormous amount of computer time for most practical problems. As a consequence, heuristic algorithms have been developed by various authors. In this paper, we point out that all of these algorithms fall into the class of minimum spanning tree problems, constrained by traffic or response time requirements. The difference between them is mainly the sequential order with which a branch or a line is selected into the tree. Without the constraints, all algorithms converge to a minimum spanning tree. With the constraints, they form different sub-trees. Most of the algorithms can be unified into a modified Kruskal's minimum spanning tree algorithm. In the modified algoritm, a weight is associated with each terminal. Let w<sub>i</sub> be the weight associated with terminal i, and d<sub>ij</sub> be the cost for the line directed from terminal i, and terminal j. When the algorithm fetches the cost for the line, it replaces it replaces it with d<sub>ij</sub> - w<sub>i</sub>. In some cases, w<sub>i</sub>'s need to be read-justed in the middle of the algorithm. The difference between all existing heuristic algorithms is in the way w<sub>i</sub>'s are defined. If w<sub>i</sub> is zero for all i, the algorithm reduces to the unmodified Kruskal's algorithm, if w<sub>i</sub> is set to zero whenever a line incident to terminal i is selected as a tree branch, the algorithm reduces to Prim's minimum spanning tree algorithm. An extension of the algorithm to the solution of an associated problem of partitioning the terminals with respect to a predetermined set of concentrators, multiplexers, terminal interface processors, or central computers is also derived. The efficiency of an algorithm depends greatly on how it is implemented. The computational complexity of the unified algorithm is in the order of N<sup>2</sup> log N for the most general case, where N is the number of terminals. By using good heuristics, it reduces to K<sub>l</sub> K log N + K<sub>2</sub> N, where K<sub>1</sub> and K<sub>2</sub> are constants, for many practical applications. The algorithm has been applied to large networks with over 1,000 terminals, yielding excellent results and using only 15 seconds of computer time on a CDC 6600 computer. Designs obtained by using different w<sub>i</sub>'s are compared. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Chou W.", "Kershenbaum A."]

Title: INFORMATION RETRIEVAL LANGUAGE (IRL).
Abstract: An examination is made of the question of developing a language for describing information retrieval systems. A formal description of an information retrieval language and its application in an information retrieval system are included. The organization and basic functions of programs set up for realization of an information retrieval system on a computer are described.
Name: ["Yevseyev V.F.", "Ozhogin B.A.", "Stroganova N.A."]

Title: LOGICAL STRUCTURE OF THE MEMORY RESOURCE IN THE SYMBOL-2R COMPUTER.
Abstract: Described are those aspects of SYMBOL's memory structure that affect direct high-level language implementation. The SYMBOL system is composed of several substantially independent processors, each of which contributes a unique function to the operation of the system. The processors most intimately involved in the implementation of the SYMBOL programming language are the translator, which translates the source program supplied by the user into an internal object program, and the general processor, which then executes the object program. Also involved are the input/output processor and the channel controller, which provide communications between the user and his program. The activities of the various processors are coordinated by a processor known as the system supervisor. The user-oriented processors do not interact directly with core memory, but instead address their requests for memory services to yet another processor, the memory controller. The structure of the memory resource provided by the memory controller is the chief topic of this paper.
Name: ["Richards Jr. Hamilton", "Zingg Roy J."]

Title: Interpreter for the Simulation of Cellular Automata. | [UEBER EINEN INTERPRETIERER ZUR SIMULATION ZELLULARER AUTOMATEN.]
Abstract: Elements of a problem-oriented language are explained. This language is designed to facilitate the simulation of two-dimensional cellular spaces. An example processed by the corresponding interpreter is described.
Name: ["Vollmar R."]

Title: Prime-a processor design for character recognition
Source: Proceedings of the Annual International Symposium on Microarchitecture, MICRO
Abstract: This paper discusses the organization of a processor designed for extraction of spatially oriented features from digital patterns. Several unusual features of the processor are discussed. The design is compared with general purpose processors and with special hardware. ¬© 1973 IEEE Computer Society. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Kimmel M.J."]

Title: ON THE SOLUTION OF GEOMETRIC PROGRAMS VIA SEPARABLE PROGRAMMING.
Abstract: Problem of choosing the ‚Ä≥best‚Ä≥ decision from a number of feasible alternatives, the optimal one being that particular decision which is most attractive based on some measure of effectiveness - such as profits, costs, time or volume. Recently, a relatively general branch of non-linear programming, called geometric programming, has been developed. Application of geometric programming theory spans many of the classical subsets of non-linear programming. However, to date, large geometric programs have been difficult to solve. This paper presents a simplex-based approach to the solution of such programs which is indifferent to the degree of difficulty of the problem. Furthermore, unlike many gradient-search techniques its success is not dependent upon a ‚Ä≥good‚Ä≥ starting point.
Name: ["Kochenberger Gary A.", "Woolsey R.E.D.", "McCarl Bruce A."]

Title: STRUCTURAL APPROACH TO PATTERN LEARNING AND THE ACQUISITION OF CLASSIFICATORY POWER.
Abstract: One approach to the development of pattern recognition systems is to design machines which can learn to differentiate patterns on the basis of self-generated hypotheses about the underlying organizations of the various patterns. This paper is addressed to the two fundamental problems which that approach entails: what is to be learned and how to learn it. A parametric structural representation for the encoding of exemplars is introduced which provides a framework for the analysis of the general pattern learning problem. Several algorithms are then developed which can generate, for any set of encoded exemplars, the total set of possible abstractions from that set. Finally, a principle of predictive power is introduced which enables us to employ the abstraction sets corresponding to different pattern classes to effect the classification of a novel test item.
Name: ["Hayes-Roth Frederick"]

Title: Use of Computer Methods of Synthesis for Linear Automatic Control Systems with Prehistory. | PRIMENENIE MASHINNYKH METODOV DLYA SINTEZA LINEINYKH SAU S PREDYSTORIEI.
Abstract: An approximate method of synthesis is proposed for linear automatic control systems with prehistory, based on the use of small digital computers. Problems of synthesis of a consecutive and a parallel correcting device are solved in a general way for high-order systems with non-unitary feedback under non-zero initial conditions. A general algorithm for solving the problems on a ‚Ä≥Mir-1‚Ä≥ digital computer is obtained.
Name: ["Gudkova N.V.", "Smol'nikov L.P."]

Title: Micro qnulation: When to do it and when not to do it
Source: Proceedings of the Annual International Symposium on Microarchitecture, MICRO
Abstract: In a broad sense, any computer system evaluates user-written (or source language) programs in two broad phases: First, a user program is translated into an equivalent program in some intermediate language, during a compilation phase; this program then becomes a surrogate for the original source program, being executed in its place as often as desired, over any number of interpretation phases. There may be several levels of intermediate languages involved during the translation phase (e.g., parse-tree code emitted by a specific pre-pass syntactic scanner, object code emitted by a specific compiler, relocatable code emitted by a linkage-editor, and machine code emitted by a loader). Similarly, there may be several levels involved during the execution phase (e.g., a micro-programmed CPU might emulate a 360/65, which could be executing a 360-code program which interprets LISP-code). In this paper, we idealize such computer systems as two-phase processing systems in which all of the translational procedures are composed into a single compiler component whose input medium is source language, and whose output medium is a directly executable language (or DEL, see figure 1). This DEL also serves as the input medium to a single interpreter component, and hence is the lowest level into which complete source langu-age programs are translated. ¬© 1973 IEEE Computer Society. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hbevel L."]

Title: Algorithm for the Analysis of Systems Represented by Signal Flow Graphs.
Abstract: In Russian.
Name: ["Tsimbalist E.I.", "Naumov L.A."]

Title: Asynchronous network of specific microprocessors
Source: Proceedings of the Annual International Symposium on Microarchitecture, MICRO
Abstract: The present state of the LSI technology enables the integration of sophisticated functions,such as control functions. However.these functions are still simple.A present micro-computer set offers a low parallelism and a low flexibility in interruption handling. Thus,the typical application of micro-computer sets is the development of inexpensive satellite processors.Two technics become available:-the dynamic microprogramming,-the multiplication of control organs. The efficient use of the dynamic microprogramming supposes the concept of the host machine which can emulate a number of virtual machines (cf B1700). The multiplication of control organs actually needs asynchronous communication procedure and requires specific microprocessors. This paper investigate such a machine. The computer is a collection of specific microprocessors.The communications are handled by an auto-regulating principle. A paged working storage and a communication mechanism are cyclicly shared between the microprocessors. The communication mechanism allows the garbage collecting and the flag locking of the common pages. ¬© 1973 IEEE Computer Society. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Dromard F.", "Noguez G."]

Title: An algorithm for synchronizing entrance ramp vehicles and freeway gaps
Source: Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement and Control, Transactions of the ASME
Abstract: An algorithm for synchronizing ramp vehicles into freeway gaps is developed. It is thought to be an improvement over existing synchronization algorithms because the derivation takes into account the phenomenon of vehicular interaction which is fundamental to any realistic description of the merging process. Attention is focussed on identification of new platoons and characterizing gap propagations within a platoon. The probability of synchronizing a ramp vehicle with an ordered gap of a platoon is formulated in terms of the platooning freeway vehicles‚Äô speeds and arrival times at a shoulder lane detector and is maximized to generate the optimal release time of the ramp vehicle. A numerical example is included. ¬© 1973 by ASME.
Name: ["Klee H.I."]

Title: Virtual Synthesis of Algorithms of Running Control of Operating Conditions of an Electric Power System Based on a Dynamic Model of the Plant. | VIRTUAL'NYI SINTEZ ALGORITMOV OPERATIVNOGO UPRAVLENIYA REZHIMAMI ENERGOSISTEMY NA OSNOVE DINAMICHESKOI MODELI OB''EKTA.
Abstract: A method is proposed for synthesizing the algorithms of permissible control conditions, based on updating statistical relations between the monitored and controlled variables. The method is considered in application to solving the problem of distribution of active capacities in an electric power system.
Name: ["Il'in V.D.", "Salyga V.I."]

Title: Compression algorithms that preserve basic topological features in binary-coded patterns
Abstract: In this paper, some problems related to the recognition of plane, two-tone pictures (e.g. handprinted characters) are considered. It is assumed that suitable algorithms (already described) have been applied to the original picture, in order to obtain linearwise, two-tone figures. A problem that arises at this point is classifying these results in a suitable way; to this purpose, it is necessary to define and perform a set of measurements such that the results obtained by applying them to figures of the same class be the same, the possible ambiguity be minimal and the loss of information be as reduced as possible. In this paper, some algorithms are described that transform the figure into another one of the least possible dimensions, but retaining a set of basic topological and quasi-topological characteristics of the original picture. While implicitly defining a set of measurements to be performed, the "reduction" of the figure is implemented so that several figures having the same basic characteristics give the same "reduced" figure as final result. The considerable reduction of the figure's dimensions may furthermore make the recognition simpler. Several algorithms are described, and the results are compared; all are of parallel type, and therefore particularly suited for hardware implementation. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Sami M.", "Stefanelli R."]

Title: An Online Digital-Computer System for the Semiautomatic Analysis of Golgi-Impregnated Neurons
Abstract: Rapid and accurate measurements of neuronal processes in Golgi preparations are possible with the aid of a small computer (Glaser and Van der Loos, 1965). This paper describes a system for doing this, using a small digital computer which controls stepping motors (0.5-Œºm steps) attached to the stage (x,y axes) and fine focus (z axis) of a microscope. The observer tracks the processes, topological information, such as the location of the soma, dendritic origins, branch points, and ends of processes, is signaled to the computer by special controls, and the x, y, and z coordinates of each are stored in digital format. The computer printout yields 1) individual x, y, and z coordinates with associated topological identifiers; 2) quantitative data for each dendritic segment in order (i.e., primary and secondary branches, etc.); and 3) computes the actual linear dimensions of each segment in microns. An associated oscilloscope display can 1) display the whole neuron, or individual processes, by connecting recorded points by vectors; 2) identify each dendrite; 3) rotate (continuously or by a specified angle) the whole cell, or individual dendrites, around any selected point or axis; and 4) indicate spatial relationships by dynamic rotation, intensity modulation, or stereo pairs. The performance of this system has been evaluated for accuracy and the repeatability of measurements. Measurements of dendritic lengths made on the computer microscope and ‚Äúby hand‚Äù differ by less than 1 percent when the total dendritic tree is considered; when the same cell is measured on different occasions using the computer microscope, the observations differ by only 0.1 percent. An evaluation of the system's errors indicates that these are on the order of 1 percent. The advantages and some potential applications of the system are discussed. Briefly, it permits the rapid accumulation of detailed quantitative data about the processes of neurons and their graphic reconstruction and display. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Wann D.F.", "Dierker M.L.", "Woolsey T.A.", "Cowan W.M."]

Title: Computer Graphics in Three Dimensions for Perspective Reconstruction of Brain Ultrastructure
Abstract: A technique for computer reassembly and plotting of morphological serial sections in three dimensions is described. The computer reconstruction is obtained at a savings in cost and time compared to previous model-processing or isometric drawing methods. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Willey T.J.", "Schultz R.L.", "Gott A.H."]
Affiliations: [' Loma Linda University', ' Loma Linda University', ' The Aerospace Corporation']

Title: Graph algorithms and their application to more general problem classes | Anwendung von Graphenalgorithmen auf allgemeinere Problemklassen
Abstract: For to find out shortest routes in graphs a lot of efficient algorithms have been generated (e. g. see Hu [1], Visotschnig [2], Pape [3]). The favourable properties of these algorithms can be utilized advantageously in a general class of problems given below. These problems can be described by graphs, where the solutions appear as routes and especially as cycles. ¬© 1973 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Perl J."]

Title: DEVELOPMENT OF A MARGINAL ANALYSIS CAPABILITY FOR WATER RESOURCES SIMULATION MODELS.
Abstract: This paper describes a procedure that, given the information obtained from a single run of a simulation model, allows estimation of the gradient vector of a response surface for a water resources planning problem. The basis for the gradient estimator is developed from a probabilistic Markov model of the reservoir state transitions from one time period to another. The marginal analysis capabilities arise by recognizing how the reservoir transitions would be changed by modification of decision variables. The behavior of the gradient estimator is examined under several conditions in application to a simple example problem.
Name: ["McBean Edward A.", "Schaake Jr. John C."]

Title: SIMULATION AND ANALYSIS OF CORE ALLOCATION SCHEMES.
Abstract: Core allocation in computer systems is surveyed. In order to study and evaluate a core allocation algorithm, a simulation model of a core allocation algorithm for a multiprogramming operating system has been devised and programmed. Essential elements which have been included are the job environment, the computer system environment, and user environment. The model is patterned basically after GECOS III, on the H-600/6000 line computer. Some results of the investigation are presented, such as throughput, turnaround, memory utilization and flexibility.
Name: ["Phillips Kathie A.", "Bulgren William G."]

Title: Control of Commutation Fields by Means of Multiple Uniform Structures. | [UPRAVLENIE KOMMUTATSIONNYMI POLYAMI S POMOSHCH'YU KRATNYKH ODNORODNYKH STRUKTUR.]
Abstract: Commutation fields belonging to the class of binary object fields are widely used for commutation of channels in different types of data communication and control systems. The article considers problems of realization of the system of control of multicascade commutation fields by means of multiple uniform structures. One of several possible methods of synthesis of the cells of such structures is proposed for divided commutation fields of a set configuration and with certain operting conditions.
Name: ["Mel'nikov M.S."]

Title: Basic Principles in Computer Structures. | [PRINZIPIEN IN RECHNERSTRUKTUREN.]
Abstract: The essential functions of a data processing system are considered from two viewpoints: the interaction of information streams, i. e. streams of data stored control programs, and the hierarchy of information control, built up step by step by stored programs, functions, structures and configurations. It is shown that information-controlled automata, in spite of their complexity, require only three basic functions: operation control, addressing and program control. This information-based treatment of computer structures and information-controlled automata shows one way in which today's computer techniques may be removed from the realm of empirical facts and placed on a foundation of basic principles.
Name: ["Ganzhorn K."]

Title: Optimal Control of Linear Systems with Continuous and Discrete Observations. | OPTIMAL'NOE UPRAVLENIE LINEINYMI SISTEMAMI PRI NEPRERYVNYKH I DISKRETNYKH NABLYUDENIYAKH.
Abstract: A problem of optimal control of linear systems with quadratic criteria of quality, given continuous and discrete observations, is considered. The kind of optimal control and the value of minimized functional are found. The problem belongs to the range of control problems with incomplete data, which is of interest for technical control tasks.
Name: ["Kolmanovskii V.B."]

Title: SYSTEM DESIGN AND ANALYSIS OF ESGM/SINS NAVIGATION SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The design of reduced state, Kalman filters for an ESGM/SINS (Electrostatically Supported Gyro Monitor/Ships Inertial Navigation System) are described. The first filter is for resetting the SINS with navigation data from the ESGM; the second is for resetting the ESGM with position data from an external source. In the first case considerable test data are available on which to model the Kalman filter, while in the second case the test data are extremely sparse. Two alternative designs are discussed in each case, and the best are utilized in an error analysis of the combined ESGM/SINS.
Name: ["Sandberg Herbert J.", "Dushman Allan"]

Title: MULTICHANNEL ADAPTIVE FILTER THEORY AND APPLICATIONS TO REFLECTION SEISMOLOGY.
Abstract: The two types of adaptive multichannel filters applied to exploration reflection seismograph data are the maximum likelihood filter and the Wiener filter. The techniques to obtain reflection seismograph data in the form suitable for multichannel filtering are described. Examples of both synthetic and real field data processed by these two multichannel filters are presented and evaluated. The equations for the two types of filters are derived and it is demonstrated the maximum likelihood filter equations are identical in form to the Wiener equations and can be solved by the same matrix inversion techniques.
Name: ["Mercado E.J."]

Title: IMPROVEMENT OF CHINESE CHARACTER RECOGNITION USING PROJECTION PROFILES.
Abstract: A previously reported algorithm for the optical recognition of printed Chinese and Japanese kana characters of single font contained a defect, namely the deterioration of recognition when the stroke-width of the character varies. Improvements are proposed to rectify this defect, based on the use of an optimum frequency range, compensation of the stroke-width variation on the frequency domain and the increase of projection directions. The authors also propose an algorithm of quasi-two-dimensional elastic matching for the recognition of multi-font printed Chinese characters.
Name: ["Nakano Y.", "Nakata K.", "Uchikura Y.", "Nakajima A."]

Title: Systems of Learning from the Engineer's Point of View. | LERNENDE SYSTEME IM BLICKFELD DES INGENIEURS.
Abstract: The paper presents an introduction to the problematic character of learning structures, reviewing the fundamental terms of learning, the basic structures of systems capable of learning, and possible applications.
Name: ["Habiger Ernst"]

Title: System independent tracing for prediction of system performance
Source: Proceedings of the 1st Symposium on Simulation of Computer Systems, ANSS 1973
Abstract: Modeling has been frequently used for predicting the effects of hardware or software changes on the performance of an existing computer system. Most simulation models used for this purpose rely on self-driven models (using probabilistic distribution functions) describing the load applied to the computer system. Trace-driven simulation models have also been used for system performance prediction, but the traces obtained were generally greatly influenced by the environment (the operating system and the hardware) in which the traces were obtained. This paper defines the technique of obtaining traces characterizing application programs (jobs) independently of the system on which the tracing was performed. The job profiles so obtained can then be used to drive the simulation model of a computer system in which the software (operating system) and the hardware used are modeled. The software and hardware models can be distinct of the traced system. An implementation of the tracing technology so defined is shown. Finally, the applicability of the trace-driven simulation technology for validation of an operating system model is demonstrated. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Beretvas T."]

Title: DIVERGENCE IN REDUNDANT GUIDANCE, NAVIGATION, AND CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The behavior of command outputs from redundant, independent guidance, navigation, and control (GNC) system channels is studied. It is shown that closed-loop guidance sensitivity to vehicle state, or the presence of pure integrators in a linear GNC system, will cause channel outputs and other intermediate signals to diverge, without affecting overall system stability. Techniques are developed, and mathematical expressions derived, to estimate the magnitude of this channel divergence for sensor bias and scale factor errors and time measurement bias errors. These methods are used to determine the magnitude of divergence for the Space Shuttle vehicle with an independent GNC channel system. The results, which prove to be significant, are then verified by digital simulations. Finally, the problems caused by divergence, and candidate solutions, are discussed.
Name: ["Padinha Henry A."]

Title: CONTINUOUS-DISCRETE DATA FILTER FOR PRE-FILTERED OBSERVATIONS.
Abstract: A sequential filtering algorithm is derived for processing integrated measurements, and the algorithm is applied to data filtering with discrete pre-smoothed measurements. The filter algorithm is similar to the standard continuous-discrete filter, but provides optimal compensation for prefilter time lag and correlation between plant process noise and prefilter observation noise. Consequently, the algorithm enables one to attain large data compression rates with minimum performance degradation, and in a form suitable for filter calculations. Prefilter trade studies with a two dimension system show that the algorithm may provide a large reduction in filter computations with only a small increase in RMS error.
Name: ["Warren A.W."]

Title: OPTIMUM LINEAR ESTIMATES FOR THE REGRESSION COEFFICIENTS OF ISOTROPIC RANDOM FIELDS.
Abstract: Isotropic random fields (fields whose correlation functions are invariant under rotations about a fixed point) are discussed. Linear unbiased estimates optimum in the sense of minimizing the mean-square error are given for the regression coefficients when the random field is observed on a sphere. It turns out, in particular, that the optimum unbiased estimate of an unknown expectation coincides with the average over the sphere. Optimum nonlinear estimates for random regression coefficients are investigated.
Name: ["Yadrenko M.I."]

Title: A Formalization of Transition Diagram Systems
Abstract: The transition diagram systems first introduced by Conway are formalized in terms of a restricted deterministic pushdown acceptor (DPDA) called a nested DPDA. It is then established that the class of nested DPDA's is capable of accepting all deterministic context-free languages. The proof of this involves demonstrating that left recursion can be eliminated from deterministic (or LR(k)) grammars without destroying the deterministic property. Using various structural properties of nested DPDA's, one can then establish equivalence results for certain classes of deterministic languages. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Lomet D.B."]
Keywords: ["automata theory", "context-free languages", "deterministic pushdown automata", "left recursion", "lrk grammars"]

Title: OPTIMIZATION OF MULTIVARIABLE SYSTEMS AND MARKOVIAN PROGRAMMING.
Abstract: It is shown how the mathematical tool of Markovian processes with rewards (the so-called Markovian programming) can be effectively used to solve certain dynamic problems in the optimization of multivariable systems. In this case the optimization problem is reducible to a linear programming problem. The constraint matrix of the linear programming problem thus obtained has the same specifics of signs as in the case of static problems in the optimization of multivariable systems. The Markovian programming problems are of great dimensionality. The constraint matrix is as a rule filled with nonzero elements. Therefore it is very important to use the specific features of the problem.
Name: ["Meerov M.V.", "Litvak B.L."]

Title: MULTI-OBJECT IMAGE DISCRIMINATION.
Abstract: Pattern classification in a multi-object image is formulated as a dynamic programming problem. This approach requires measures of costs of associating elements with given features to different objects. This is in contrast to approaches that require measures of similarity or distance between elements.
Name: ["Lew Art"]

Title: SYMMETRIC GAMES FOR LARGE AGGREGATES OF PROBABILISTIC AUTOMATA.
Abstract: Equations are proposed for the approximate description of a system of interacting automata in which the transition probability of an automaton from one state to another is a symmetric function of the states of all the automata. It is proved that the solution of the approximate equations converges to the exact solution as the number of automata is increased without bound.
Name: ["Sushkov B.G."]

Title: Passive stochastic feedback stability Part I. A general theory‚Ä†
Abstract: The use of passivity concepts is well known in determining the stability of deterministic feedback systems. In this paper (Part I) a parallel theory is developed for feedback systems in which one or more of the sub-systems is stochastic in nature. This theory is compatible with and essentially subsumes one passive stability theory formulation for deterministic systems with a state representation given in recent work by C. A. Desoer and the author. A definition of a stochastic dynamical system is given in the paper. This definition has a generality comparable to many definitions of deterministic dynamical systems which have appeared in the literature. The input and output spaces of such a stochastic system are classes of random processes and its state is intimately connected with Markov concepts. It is shown that, under mild restrictions, a general deterministic dynamical system subject to ensembles of inputs (random processes) also defines a stochastic dynamical system. In this paper the feedback system as well as its sub-systems are assumed to be stochastic dynamical systems. In passive deterministic feedback stability one is required to do a particular type of analysis. In this paper a stochastic version of that analysis is generated and stochastic stability theorems are derived based on this analysis. Three types of stability are discussed for stochastic feedback systems: (1) zero input with probability 1 Liapunov stability, (2) expected L<sub>s</sub>-input produces expected L<sub>s</sub>-output stability, (3) expected bounded-input produces expected bound-state stability. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Estrada R.F."]

Title: Evaluation of the shortest processing time scheduling rule with truncation process
Abstract: This paper discusses the development of a scheduling rule and summarizes the results of the evaluation of its performance with respect to some tardiness related criteria. Studies done on job shop scheduling indicated that the simple dispatching rules which mostly perform well with respect to a criterion of performance may have undesirable results with respect to other criteria. In this paper, a scheduling rule with truncation process called SPT-T is introduced and studied. Simulation results showed that the shortcomings of simple dispatching rules are remedie.d by using the SPT-T scheduling rule. ¬© 1973 AIIE.
Name: ["Oral M."]

Title: INVESTIGATION OF SOME PRINCIPLES OF SIMULATION AND THEIR APPLICATION TO A BIOMEDICAL PATTERN RECOGNITION PROBLEM IN RADIOISOTOPE SCANNING.
Abstract: Simulation techniques are applied to a biomedical pattern recognition application: radioisotope scanning for detection of tumors. Results of a simulation experiment are presented for an idealized model of this application. A description of simulation as a process is given along with an abstract framework which identifies its key constituent elements. One of these, the evaluation criterion, is discussed and its important role in practical simulation experiments is delineated. An example of this criterion is given for the radioisotope scanning application, and its relationship to the theory of stopping rules is mentioned.
Name: ["Klinger Allen", "Rynell Inga"]

Title: ANALYSIS OF TRAFFIC PROBLEMS EMPLOYING CLASSIC GRAPH THEORY FOR AUTOMATED SOLUTION BY DIGITAL COMPUTER TECHNIQUES.
Abstract: This paper presents a pragmatic approach to the application of classical graph theory to the solution of traffic problems. The problem is presented in its traffic format and then transformed into a graph theoretical problem. A new algorithm for solution is presented and proved. The required data structures required for computer solution are likewise presented and developed.
Name: ["Honkanen Pentti A."]

Title: HYPERELLIPTIC DECISION SURFACES FROM THE METHOD OF GENERALIZED PORTRAITS.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The method of generalized portraits, first developed by Vapnik et al. for separating patterns consisting of n binary-valued attributes is modified by allowing pattern vectors with n continuous bounded attributes. Using linear separation in n plus 1 Euclidean space, optimal and unique hyperelliptical decision surfaces are generated which encapsulate training vectors of a given class to the exclusion of all others, if such a separation exists. The resulting algorithm is deterministic and capable of indicating linear inseparability in E**n** plus **1. The implemented algorithm is described in terms of its properties, its (n plus 1)-dimensional geometry, a flow diagram, and examples.
Name: ["Schatzki Thomas F."]

Title: COMPUTER CONTROL OF THE TRANSPORT SYSTEMS IN COAL MINES.
Abstract: A mathematical model of transport in underground coal mines is presented and some problems of optimal control are described. Two general systems are considered: conveyor transport and mixed scheme; conveyor in sections and rail transport on the main roads.
Name: ["Firganek B."]

Title: Errors in System Analysis Due to Stochastically Disturbed Step Responses. | [FEHLER BEI DER SYSTEMANALYSE AUS STOCHASTISCH GESTOERTEN SPRUNGANTWORTEN.]
Abstract: The method starts from equations, which allow the calculation of the coefficients of the plant by regression of the measured step response. The transfer function of the plant is assumed to have constant numerator and a polynomial in the denominator. Assuming that the ideal and exact step response of the system is disturbed by a stochastic signal, it is investigated how the errors of the calculated coefficients depend on characterics of the noise signal and the measurement time. Results are checked by a simulation on a digital computer. It is shown that filtering of the disturbed step response by a low pass filter does not improve the results of the analysis, because the identification procedure has smoothing properties.
Name: ["Lepers H."]

Title: ON THE CONVERGENCE OF AN ALGORITHM FOR FINDING A GLOBAL EXTREMUM.
Abstract: A study is made of the convergence of a one-dimensional algorithm for finding the global minimum of a function.
