Sufficient conditions are found to the search to converge to the global minimum, and estimates of the speed of convergence are made. The results are generalized to the many-dimensional case. The results of experimental comparison of the proposed method with an algorithm based on repeated local descents from randomly chosen initial points are described. The comparison is made using a sample containing 50 two-dimensional test functions.
Name: ["Strongin R.G."]

Title: APPLICATION OF THE RANDOM NETWORK MODEL TO GERMANIUM-CHALCOGENIDE ALLOYS.
Abstract: A random network model based on the tight binding approximation has been developed for amorphous alloys which enables the average positions and widths of the bonding and antibonding bands as a function of alloy composition. The tight binding matrix elements have been evaluated for the Ge-S and Ge-Se systems. For chalcogenide concentrations exceeding approximately 60 at. %, the character of the top of the valence band changes from that associated with bonding orbitals to that associated with lone pair orbitals. This may account for the observed maximum in the optical gap in the Ge-S system at the composition of GeS//2.
Name: ["White R.M."]

Title: FUNCTIONS DESCRIBING INTERACTIVE PROGRAMMING.
Abstract: The authors give a functional description of interactive programming based on a definition of formal dialogs which are produced by an infinite Mealy type automaton. The concrete input sequences are mapped by an interpretation function into a set of abstract inputs which describe executable objects of the dialog. An application function maps the abstract inputs to functions representing both transitions of the dialog-states and outputs. The application function as well as the secondary functions and the commands are defined axiomatically. Axioms are given especially for execution and assign commands and for commands related to interrupts and task control.
Name: ["Kupka Ingbert", "Wilsing Norbert"]

Title: INTERNAL MACHINE.
Abstract: Two results are presented in this paper: an enlargement of the concept of machine languages and a way to design computers based on an inner machine oriented toward interpretation of machine languages in general. Attributes are discussed of ‚Ä≥directly interpretable languages‚Ä≥ and processing mechanisms related to their interpretation. ‚Ä≥Sequential extraction‚Ä≥ allows an instruction to be of arbitrary form, while ‚Ä≥linear decoding‚Ä≥ permits organizing the interpreting routines into structures. This leads to powerful machine language level capabilities. A case is built for the ‚Ä≥internal machine‚Ä≥ approach to computer design. The internal machine (unlike microprocessors) is not oriented towards low level (gate, register) manipulation of data, but its operations reflect elementary actions related to the process of interpretation. The advantages of the internal machine include simplicity, programming interface (as opposed to the interface offered by microprocessors), and the ability to handle directly interpretable languages. A choice can be made among many architectures for the internal machine. An organization based on the execution stack is suggested as the most general solution. The essential ‚Ä≥general purpose‚Ä≥ organizations of the internal machines lend themselves to extensions and specializations which provide extra efficient handling of specific subprocesses related to interpretation.
Name: ["Welin Andrew M."]

Title: EXPERIMENTAL QUERY SYSTEM: SYNTEX.
Abstract: This paper presents a system whose purposes are: universality, evolution capabilities, dynamically variable data-structures, conversational communication, a sub-class of natural language as query language, deductive methods. A prototype system has been implemented. Much of the effort has been towards definiting data-structures representation. At the lower level, atoms and relations are used to define elementary informations. At the upper level, axioms are used to define the data-structure. As a result, the first four points can be satisfied. A query language sub-class of natural language and deductive methods are being developed.
Name: ["Artaud A.", "Nicolas J.M."]

Title: USING THE MINIMUM SPANNING TREE TO RECOGNIZE DOTTED AND DASHED CURVES.
Abstract: An important problem in pattern recognition is the organization into two and three-dimensional space curves of data given as points ( ‚Ä≥dots‚Ä≥ ) or short line segments ( ‚Ä≥dashes‚Ä≥ ). This paper describes a general method for recognizing such dotted or dashed space curves employing the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST). The extension of the method to handle ‚Ä≥dashed‚Ä≥ curves requires only the definition of a closeness measure between dashes which reflects the directional information as well as positional. It is possible to use the method in a layered hierarchy where the MST of dots is used to detect dashes, the MST of dashes to detect short curves without inflections, and an MST constructed from these curves is used to detect larger curves with possible inflections.
Name: ["Zahn C.T."]

Title: Boss simulation of real-time computer systems
Source: Proceedings of the 1st Symposium on Simulation of Computer Systems, ANSS 1973
Abstract: A description of the Burroughs Operational Systems Simulator (BOSS) is given. A BOSS process is shown which models a system disk call. The concept of embedded processes is introduced, exemplified and expanded using a model for retrieval in a message switch. The modeling of virtual memory in a computer system is discussed. A process sets the parameters for the use of a central processing unit (CPU) and then calls an embedded process that handles the events leading to CPU action. All events involved with the model for automatic search for core space and memory overlay are shown. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Meyerhoff A.J.", "Shafer P.E."]

Title: DESCRIPTION AND ASYNCHRONOUS IMPLEMENTATION OF CONTROL STRUCTURES FOR CONCURRENT SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The L-graph is introduced, as a generalization of Petri-nets allowing pipelining of operations; it is directly related to D. Slutz's Flow Graph Schemata. Then an asynchronous, speed-independent implementation of systems, described by L-graphs, is given. An L-graph is translated into a ‚Ä≥single-conflict‚Ä≥ Petri-net, which in turn, as shown, can be directly implemented by networks of asynchronous modules.
Name: ["Grandoni Fabrizio", "Zerbetto Piero"]

Title: An Efficient Parallel Algorithm for the Solution of a Tridiagonal Linear System of Equations
Abstract: Tridiagonal linear systems of equations can be solved on conventional serial machines in a time proportional to N, where N is the number of equations. The conventional algorithms do not lend themselves directly to parallel computation on computers of the ILLIAC IV class, in the sense that they appear to be inherently serial. An efficient parallel algorithm is presented in which computation time grows as log<sub>2</sub> N. The algorithm is based on recursive doubling solutions of linear recurrence relations, and can be used to solve recurrence relations of all orders. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Stone H.S."]
Affiliations: [' Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science']

Title: COMPUTER IDENTIFICATION OF WHITE BLOOD CELLS.
Abstract: The hardware and software problems for an effective image processing system are described, with a real time high speed system solution as the goal. The discriminating power of the algorithms was tested in a simulation made on the PIQUANT film scanner and is between 67 and 92% depending on the definition of accuracy. The results are expected to be of value to firms designing and building commercial equipment and to prospective purchasers of it.
Name: ["Neurath P.W.", "Brenner J.F.", "Selles W.D.", "Gelsema E.S.", "Powell B.W.", "Gallus G.", "Vastola E."]

Title: MODAL APPROACH TO CONTROL LAW REDUCTION.
Abstract: A method is proposed for reducing the complexity of state feedback control laws for high order systems. Using a modal approach, selected state variables are eliminated to give an incomplete state feedback control law. The proposed method for control law reduction is applied to an optimal control system for a tenth order model of a pilot scale evaporator. Simulation and experimental results show that the modal approach is practical and results in better control than methods based on reduced order models or conventional multiloop design techniques.
Name: ["Wilson Robert G.", "Seborg Dale E.", "Fisher D.Grant"]

Title: NEW APPROACH TO THE ‚Ä≥INVERSE PROBLEM OF OPTIMAL CONTROL THEORY‚Ä≥ BY USE OF A GENERALIZED PERFORMANCE INDEX (GPI).
Abstract: By showing the equivalence of quadratic cost functionals to the GPI, a new, straightforward solution to the Inverse Problem is given for linear time-invariant single-input systems. The eigenvalues of the optimal system can be directly determined from the parameters of the GPI. In case of partial feedback, the parameters of a sub-optimal control law can be determined by minimizing the GPI. Using Parseval's theorem, the GPI can be evaluated with little computation effort which is very advantageous for parameter optimization. To give an illustrative engineering example, the altitude control of aircraft is considered.
Name: ["Miski Tuncer"]

Title: Dynamic Identification of Linear Plants. | [O DINAMICHESKOI IDENTIFIKATSII LINEINYKH OB'EKTOV.]
Abstract: A generalized formulation is presented for the problem of dynamic identification of linear systems and possibilities of solving this problem are shown. Four methods of identification are set forth, namely: the classical algorithm using the method of stochastic approximation, two algorithms using quasioptimal convergence coefficients (one of the scalar type and another of the diagonal matrix type), as well as a recurrent algorithm on the basis of the least squares method. The results are shown on the example of a one-dimensional oscillating link.
Name: ["Kochish Ya.", "Etvesh P."]

Title: PROCEDURAL DECISION TABLES AND THEIR IMPLEMENTATION.
Abstract: A new algorithm for conversion of procedural tables, the Line-Mask-Technique, is presented. The DETAB/GT processor (an implementation of this algorithm) shows the characteristics of this technique. In particular the processing of OR-rules (ambiguous tables) and implementation of test aid facilities is shown. In this processor an interpretative assembly language routine is used for program control. This routine consists of only 40 instructions and allows one to obtain good results. A further improvement can be achieved by implementation of the algorithm as microprogram. By using 2 machine instructions the decision table technique becomes a new element for program control on machine language level.
Name: ["Thurner R.", "Bauknecht K."]

Title: GENERATIVE CAI IN HIGH SCHOOL ALGEBRA.
Abstract: A generative computer-aided instruction system for high school algebra is described. The system handles three basic types of problems; manipulation problems, word problems, and graphing problems. Each problem is generated by the use of a probabilistic grammar which takes into account the student's previous work. Solution monitoring is also dependent on the student's prior performance.
Name: ["Gilkey Thomas J.", "Koffman Elliot B."]

Title: APPROXIMATE ‚Ä≥OPEN‚Ä≥ PRIORITY QUEUE MODEL FOR DETERMINING TOTAL DELAY INCLUDING OVERHEAD IN A REAL-TIME VIRTUAL MEMORY SYSTEM.
Abstract: This paper develops an ‚Ä≥open‚Ä≥ , priority queuing model which determines the delay including overhead incurred in a real-time virtual memory system. The model is a n-priority, Markov arrival, general service single-server with finite queue lengths. Further, the mean service time is computed through an interaction of both the cyclic queue model of Shedler and the model discussed in this paper.
Name: ["Johnson Philip Avery"]

Title: NEW GENERALIZED LEAST SQUARES ESTIMATION ALGORITHM FOR SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION.
Abstract: Modified formulations of the generalized least squares estimation algorithm for system parameter identification is presented. Two sets of results are derived: First the existing algorithm is reformulated by eliminating the intermediate filtering procedures and introducing the system's input-output correlation matrices. Then it is shown that the new algorithm can be conveniently simplified to a form which does not require repeated matrix inversions.
Name: ["Hsia T.C."]

Title: Algorithms for discounted stochastic games
Source: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
Abstract: In this paper, a two-person zero-sum discounted stochastic game with a finite state space is considered. The movement of the game from state to state is jointly controlled by the two players with a finite number of alternatives available to each player in each of the states. We present two convergent algorithms for arriving at minimax strategies for the players and the value of the game. The two algorithms are compared with respect to computational efficiency. Finally, a possible extension to nonzero sum stochastic game is suggested. ¬© 1973 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Rao S.S.", "Chandrasekaran R.", "Nair K.P.K."]
Affiliations: [' Case Western Reserve University', ' University of New Brunswick']

Title: Problem of Automatic Detection of Damaged Sections in A District Heating System. | [O ZADACHE AVTOMATICHESKOGO VYYAVLENIYA POVREZHDENNOGO UCHASTKA V TEPLOVYKH SETYAKH.]
Abstract: The possibility of identification of breakdown sections during the process of maintenance of complicated central heating systems by means of a specialized computing machine on the basis of data on the difference in the velocity of pressure changes in conditions of operation and breakdown is demonstrated. One of the ways of constructing an algorithm for the operation of such a computer is presented. The paper appears to be useful for the purposes of automation of dispatch control of district heating systems.
Name: ["Gorskaya N.I."]

Title: RECURSIVE FUNCTIONS NOT DEPENDENT ON THE COMPUTATIONAL RULES.
Abstract: On the basis of some Cadiou-Manna's ideas, a Function Calculus is introduced, where it is shown that functions' independence from computational rules is undecidable. Furthermore a class of functions is introduced, namely the Steady Functions, whose definition is completely syntactical and it is proved that function steadiness is a sufficient condition for function independence from computational rules.
Name: ["De Michelis Giorgio"]

Title: On-Line Learning Optimal Control Using Successive Approximation Techniques
Abstract: The application of learning theory to on-line optimization of unknown or poorly defined plants is discussed. An on-line optimization procedure is achieved by means of a learning algorithm which alters a trainable controller on the basis of an instantaneous performance criterion or subgoal. The subgoal is related to the overall goal, the integral cost, by means of successive approximations to the Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The resulting piecewise linear controller is implemented by means of an encoder consisting of threshold logic units and a classifier consisting of a set of logic switching functions. The classifier is determined by means of an algorithm developed by Arkadev and Braverman. Features of the learning algorithm are illustrated by minimum-time and minimum-time-fuel problems. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Levine M.D.", "Vilis T."]

Title: APPLICATION OF MATHEMATICAL MODELS OF LEARNING IN THE DECISION STRUCTURE OF ADAPTIVE COMPUTER-AIDED INSTRUCTIONAL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The aim of this paper is to contribute to the decision making capability of a CAI-system in a specific instructional task: Teaching Chinese characters. The solution is general to cover any other paired-associate learning task containing independent learning items. The decision structure is based upon a mathematical model. Experimental results indicate that the efficiency of learning can be improved significantly.
Name: ["Laubsch Joachim H.", "Chiang Alice"]

Title: OPTIMUM TUNING OF A CORRECTOR OF DATA-TRANSMISSION SIGNALS.
Source: Telecommunications and Radio Engineering (English translation of Elektrosvyaz and Radiotekhnika)
Abstract: The problems of optimal tuning of a harmonic data transmission signal using the mean-square criterion are considered, taking intersymbol interference and additive noise into account. It is shown that this criterion is related to the error probability when receiving digital data. A method of determining the optimal coefficients in the branches of the harmonic corrector is described. The results of a computer simulation of the operation of the corrector when transmitting data by APSK-SSB.
Name: ["Kleibanov S.B.", "Tsirel'son D.A."]

Title: PROBLEMS IN AUTOMATIC PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: A survey of current interests in pattern recognition is given. First, methods to represent patterns and statistical methods to select features and to determine decision functions are discussed. Next, image processing methods and hardware implementations are regarded. Finally, some applications and results of image processing are illustrated.
Name: ["Kazmierczak Helmut"]

Title: FAULT-TOLERANT COMPUTING BY USING RESIDUE NUMBER SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The error detecting and correcting properties of Redundant Residue Number Systems (RRNS) are discussed, taking into consideration single residue digit and single bit errors. Error detecting and correcting procedures are presented, also yielding additive overflow detection as a byproduct. The fault-effectiveness of the RRNS is analyzed and an approach to introduce reconfiguration and standby spare organization in processors using RRNS is presented.
Name: ["Barsi Ferruccio", "Maestrini Piero"]

Title: A Unified Approach to the Evaluation of a Class of Replacement Algorithms
Abstract: The replacement problem arises in computer system management whenever the executable memory space available is insufficient to contain all data and code that may be accessed during the execution of an ensemble of programs. An example of this is the page replacement problem in virtual memory computers. The problem is solved by using a replacement algorithm that selects code or data items that are to be removed from executable memory whenever new items must be brought in and no more free storage space remains. An automaton theoretic model of replacement algorithms is introduced for the class of ‚Äúrandom partially preloaded‚Äù replacement algorithms, which contain certain algorithms of practical and theoretical interest. An analysis of this class is provided in order to evaluate their performance, using the assumption that the references to the items to be stored are identically distributed independent random variables. With this model, it is shown that the well-known page replacement algorithms FIFO and RAND yield the same long-run page-fault rates. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gelenbe E."]

Title: Set-Theoretical Approach to the Description of Recursively Defined Functions and Automata. | BESCHREIBUNG VON REKURSIV DEFINIERTEN FUNKTIONEN UND AUTOMATEN AUF MENGENTHEORETISCHER GRUNDLAGE.
Abstract: Proceeding from the definition of the function as a set of ordered pairs properties are obtained of recursively defined functions as a special case of a general fixed-point theorem for ordered classes. The method of operation of automata is described with the aid of some examples using a new notation for recursively defined functions. It is shown how to obtain mathematical models for dynamic ystems with the help of recursively defined functions.
Name: ["Ehling H.J.", "Plate H.", "Reinke R."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF SYNTAX-DIRECTED TRANSLATION SCHEMES.
Abstract: Syntax-Directed Translation Schemes (SDTS) are a formalism for describing the process of translation between two context-free grammars. In this paper an algorithm is given which, presented with two grammars G//1 and G//2 and a suitable finite set of examples of translations from strings in L(G//1) to strings in L(G//2), finds, if they exist, two new grammars G prime //1 and G prime //2, such that L(G prime //1) equals L(G//1) and L(G prime //2) equals L(G//2). Such grammars have productions corresponding to derivatives of G//1 and G//2, and can be coupled by a SDTS satisfying the set of examples.
Name: ["Celentano A.", "Della Vigna P.", "Ghezzi C.", "Tisato F."]

Title: A general statistical model for estimating future demand levels of data‚Äêbase utilization within an information retrieval organization
Source: Journal of the American Society for Information Science
Abstract: A statistical model for characterizing the growth patterns of data base utilization and for estimating future utilization levels of demand has been developed for information retrieval organizations. The model developed is Œ≥ = Œ≤ (1‚Äêe<sup>‚àíat</sup>) where Œ≥ is the number of users of a data base at time ‚Ä†, and Œ± and Œ≤ are parameters to be estimated. Illustrations of the model applied to a typical information retrieval organization are given and discussed. Copyright ¬© 1973 Wiley Periodicals, Inc., A Wiley Company
Name: ["Ware G.O."]

Title: MULTIPLIER METHODS FOR CONVEX PROGRAMMING.
Abstract: A combined primal-dual and penalty method is given for solving the nonlinear programming problem. The algorithm generalizes the ‚Ä≥method of multipliers‚Ä≥ and is applicable to problems with both equality and inequality constraints. the algorithm is defined for a broad class of ‚Ä≥penalized Lagrangians,‚Ä≥ and is shown to be globally convergent when applied to the convex programming problem. The duality aspects are explored, leading to geometrical interpretations of the method and its relationship to generalized Lagrange multipliers. The rate of convergence is given and the method is shown to be superior to ordinary penalty methods.
Name: ["Kort B.W.", "Bertsekas D.P."]

Title: HIERARCHICAL SET OF MODELS FOR CONTROL OF A CLASS OF LARGE-SCALE SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Attention is given to the generality of control problems in systems for which the crux of the industrial process consists in moving discrete objects in a network. A hierarchy of models, including deterministic imitation models and linear programming models are proposed for the control of such systems. The principles of construction of models of a hierarchical set are described, and the results of verification of them are given.
Name: ["Ivanishchev V.V."]

Title: Waveform Segmentation Through Functional Approximation
Abstract: (minmax) linear uniform(minmax) approximation. Various algorithms are reviewed and a new one is proposed based on discrete optimization. Ex amples of its applications are shown on terrain profiles, scanning electron microscope data, and electrocardiograms. The processing is sufficiently fast to allow its use on-line. The results of the segmentation can be used for pattern recognition, data compression, and nonlinear filtering not only for waveforms but also for pictures and maps. In the latter case some additional preprocessing is required and it is described in [19]. Waveform segmentation is treated as a problem of piecewiseCopyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Pavlidis T."]

Title: ON THE CONSOLIDATION OF STATES OF SEMI-MARKOV PROCESSES.
Abstract: An examination is made of one method of overcoming high dimensionality of the phase space of a stochastic system. The method consists in shifting to a system in which each state is a set of states of the original system. Necessary and sufficient conditions are found in order that the new system belong to the class of Markov and semi-Markov systems with arbitrary phase spaces. An example is considered.
Name: ["Zakharin A.M."]

Title: FINITE CONTROL OF LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH DISTRIBUTED PARAMETERS.
Abstract: Controlling boundary conditions that ensure shift of a one-dimensional system from one state to another in minimum time have been found for the system described by a second-order partial differential equation. The method permits synthesis of a finite control using only the solution of the differential equation which describes the system.
Name: ["Yefimov S.P."]

Title: The heuristic synthesis of applications-oriented microcode
Source: Proceedings of the Annual International Symposium on Microarchitecture, MICRO
Abstract: This paper describes an algorithm for the synthesis of applications-oriented microcode for a dynamically micropro-grammable computer. The need for such an algorithm is expressed by Reigel, Faber, and Fisher1as an integral step in the solution of the tuning problem, or the problem of modifying a system architecture in order to optimally solve a given problem. This modification of architecture takes place through synthesis of microprograms that are stored in writable control storage. Writable control storage permits each class of user application programs to execute with a specialized instruction set, or architecture. A synthesis algorithm provides a method for generation of these specialized architectures. The required synthesis algorithm should be autonomous, should not require apriori knowledge of user application, and should be adaptable to day-by-day changes in user problems. Current attempts at tuning architectures can be considered as manual tuning. Heuristic tuning is suggested as an auto-mization of the manual tuning process. Several phases of heuristic tuning are summarized. The architecture synthesis phase is considered in depth and an algorithm for microprogram synthesis is given. Several examples of the synthesis algorithm are presented and the expected execution improvements are shown. ¬© 1973 IEEE Computer Society. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Abd-Alla A.M.", "Karlgaard D.C."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF ALGORITHMS FOR DATA COMPRESSION.
Abstract: The problem of data compression is stated in terms of measuring systems invariant to a given class of signals. Such systems are shown to be effectively synthesized through measurement signal structural models. The synthesis of linear algorithms for adaptive signal sampling is given as an example.
Name: ["Vittikh V.A."]

Title: COMPUTER MODEL FOR OPTIMAL FREEWAY ON-RAMP CONTROL.
Abstract: This paper describes the development of a computer program, LINCON, that can determine the desired fixed-time metering rates for a group of on-ramps to be controlled. The linear programming technique is used to formulate a decision model that is then integrated with a previously developed deterministic freeway stimulation model, FREEQ, to become a ramp-control model, RAMPCON.
Name: ["Wang Jin J.", "May Adolf D."]

Title: Representation and Processing of Extensive LISP Programs. | DARSTELLUNG UND BEARBEITUNG UMFANGREICHER LISP-PROGRAMME.
Abstract: An elementary pseudocode is described which allows the representation of LISP functions by a sequence of operation on a cellar. The code is generated by a LISP coded compiler and evaluated by a simple interpreter. The capacity of a conventional LISP system is extended by storing the pseudocode in a paged secondary storage.
Name: ["Luegger J.", "Melenk H."]

Title: A Survey of Indexing Techniques for Sparse Matrices
Abstract: A sparse matrix is defined to be a matrix containing a high proportion of elements that are zeros. Sparse matrices of large order are of great interest and application in science and industry; for example, electrical networks, structural engineering, power distribution, reactor diffusion, and solutions to differential equations While conclusions within this paper are primarily drawn considering orders of greater than 1000, much is applicable to sparse matrices of smaller orders in the hundreds. Because of increasing use of large order sparse matrices and the tendency to attempt to solve larger order problems, great attention must be focused on core storage and execution time Every effort should be made to optimize both computer memory allocation and executmn times, as these are the limiting factors that most often dictate the practicahty of solving a given problem Indexing algorithms are the subject of this paper, as they are generMly recognized as the most important factor in fast and efficient processing of large order sparse matrices. Indexing schemes of main interest are the bit map, address map, row-column, and the threaded list Major variations of the indexing techniques above mentioned are noted, as well as the particular indexing scheme inherent in diagonal or band matrices. The concluding section of the paper compares the types of methods, discusses their suitabihty for different types of processing, and makes suggestions eoneernlng the adaptability and flexibility of the maj or exmting methods of indexing algorithms for application to user problems. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Pooch U.W.", "Nieder A."]

Title: MINIMIZATION ALGORITHM FOR THE DESIGN OF LINEAR MULTIVARIABLE SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A new algorithm for the design of linear multivariable systems is presented. This algoritm constructs a set of minimal-order (McMillan degree) solutions to a proper rational matrix equation. The algorithm has direct application in exact model matching, inverse systems and dynamic observers; in particular, application of the algorithm is made to construct a minimal-order inverse system and to find a lower bound on the minimum order dynamic observer required to estimate a set of linear functionals of the state.
Name: ["Wang Shih-Ho", "Davison Edward J."]

Title: Stability of Computers with Networks Containing negative Resistances. | STABILITE DES CALCULATEURS A RESEAUX COMPORTANT DES RESISTANCES NEGATIVES.
Abstract: Theoretical stability conditions are determined which show the existence of zones of stability and instability according to the values of the negative resistances, the latter having eventually to be ‚Ä≥switched‚Ä≥ . The method for stabilization by ‚Ä≥auxiliary sources‚Ä≥ is also mentioned.
Name: ["Mesnard Guy", "Vo Hoang Hien", "Vidal Jean"]

Title: On the Control of Systems with Unknown Parameters
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics
Abstract: Closed-loop and open-loop controls are found for systems with unknown parameters. Use of the prior information is made by objectively inferring prior probability distributions for the unknown parameters and then selecting the control gains which minimize the resulting risks. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Oberlin T.L."]

Title: Digital Simulation of Random Disturbances with Given Rational Spectral Density Function. | SYMULACJA CYFROWA ZAKLOCEN PRZYPADKOWYCH O ZADANEJ GESTOSCI WIDMOWEJ W POSTACI FUNKCJI WYMIERNEJ.
Abstract: The problem of computer simulation of disturbances which form a stationary stochastic process described by a given rational spectral density function is considered. Principles for the selection of a random number generator to be used for simulation of a stochastic process are described. The method is exemplified by digital simulation of the stochastic process which is the output of a second order filter excited by white noise. An ODRA-1204 computer was used for simulation. The formula for the spectral density function of a stationary stochastic sequence which is the output of a given discrete filter is derived.
Name: ["Rewo Ludomir"]

Title: Synthesis of Quasi-Optimal Control of a System Consisting of an integrating and Two Lag Circuits. | SINTEZ KVAZIOPTIMAL'NOGO UPRAVLENIYA SISTEMOI, SOSTOYASHCHEI IZ INTEGRIRUYUSHCHEGO I DVUKH INERTSIONNYKH ZVEN'EV.
Abstract: The problem of synthesis of a control system which is close to the optimal one as regards fresponse, taking into account the limitations imposed on the control action and the phase coordinate - the position of the control organ - is considered. Expressions are obtained for two variants of the structural scheme and graphs of dependence of the feedback coefficients in the function on the step along the controlled coordinate are obtained, making it possible to realize the quasi-optimal system in a technically simple way.
Name: ["Kolesnikov A.A.", "Gorelov V.N.", "Chernysh P.I."]

Title: DIRECTED SEARCH FOR OPTIMAL TRAJECTORIES IN TWO-DIMENSIONAL SPACE.
Abstract: An examination is made of the method of directed search for optimal trajectories in a two-dimensional space. Sufficient conditions for optimality are found and an algorithm of search for the optimal trajectory is given. The procedure of seeking the optimal trajectory and the extreme simplicity and economy of practical realization of the method are illustrated with an example of choosing an optimal flight trajectory.
Name: ["Maslennikov V.M."]

Title: METHOD OF DESCRIPTION OF ASYNCHRONOUS DISCRETE CONTROL DEVICES.
Abstract: The behavior of asynchronous discrete control devices is described with the aid of two automata: automaton A//1, for which any transition from one state to another is accompanied by a change in the output, and automaton A//2, which represents events at the input of A//1. The problem of decomposition of the original automaton A into automata A//2 and A//2 is solved. The automaton A//2 is described in the form of a superposition of Boolean functions and standard predicates, and a realization of it with a network consisting of logical elements and standard cells (flip-flops, delay lines, samplers, and counters) is given.
Name: ["Yuditskiy S.A."]

Title: PROGRAMING INTEGRAL PULSE FREQUENCY MODULATION SYSTEMS ON THE ANALOG COMPUTER.
Source: Am Soc Eng Educ COED Trans
Abstract: The integral pulse frequency modulation system has many possible applications. It has been used in control systems and in neural modeling. The study of IPFM for possible use as a communications system has lagged behind investigations in other areas. This is due mainly to the problems of using an unclocked system as a communications device. This paper describes the use of an analog computer simulation to study the signal to noise ratios of the IPFM system. It covers the programming of the IPFM system on the computer, the results obtained from the simulation and the problems associated with the system. The signal to noise ratio curves indicate that the IPFM system may be applicable in wideband communications systems if future research and development takes place.
Name: ["Quinn Egbert Lyle", "Kurland Marvin"]

Title: INCOHERENT RADAR TARGET EXTRACTION IN CLUTTER OF UNKNOWN LEVEL BY RECURSIVE INTEGRATION FOR SIGNAL AND THRESHOLD.
Source: NTZ Nachr Z NTZ Commun J
Abstract: Starting from the known covariance of target echo sequences and the homogeneity of clutter, a recursive technique is presented which combines nearly optimum target extraction with clutter-adaptive threshold control using a small amount of cost. The system loss is compared with that of known devices and it is pointed out that no logarithmic preamplification may be used in inhomogeneous clutter environment.
Name: ["Hanle Eberhard"]

Title: ON REFERENCE STRING GENERATION PROCESSES.
Abstract: Efficient memory management is important for optimizing computer usage. The referencing pattern, describing the sequence of memory addresses, is the environment for memory management problems. One referencing model assigns probabilities to positions in an LRU stack of memory pages. ‚Ä≥Local‚Ä≥ behavior is easily described using this model. However, the distinctly different behavior among instruction and data references is lost. In this paper the authors generalize the LRU stack model to an arbitrary number of memory spaces which are selected by the transitions of a Markov chain. The additional detail affects the behavior of the models for a working set management strategy.
Name: ["Arvind", "Kain R.Y.", "Sadeh E."]

Title: OPTIMAL FEEDBACK CONTROL OF SAMPLED-DATA PROCESSES.
Abstract: This paper discusses the application of optimal feedback control theory to sampled-data process control. A procedure is developed for the design of discrete feedback control algorithms. This technique promises significant improvement, in a number of respects, over presently practiced methods of discrete feedback control. The method presented takes into account the effect of unmeasured disturbances, includes integral action and dead time compensation, and substantially simplifies tuning--important considerations in industrial process control.
Name: ["Mollenkamp Robert A."]

Title: DETECTION OF FIXED-ENERGY SIGNALS UNIFORMLY DISTRIBUTED ON A SPHERE OF THE SIGNAL SPACE ON A GAUSSIAN WHITE NOISE BACKGROUND.
Source: Telecommunications and Radio Engineering (English translation of Elektrosvyaz and Radiotekhnika)
Abstract: The synthesis of optimal receivers for detecting uniformly distributed signals of fixed energy on a Gaussian white noise background is discussed.
Name: ["Gurov A.A."]

Title: The Analysis of Radiographic Images
Abstract: The problem considered is the development of a method of scene analysis that employs a descriptive approach in the analysis of pictures. In an effort to facilitate implementation of the algorithm to a wide range of picture classes, a description of the scene is read in as data in the form of a tree structure that guides the search for objects from the largest to the smallest. The algorithm has the following features: the analysis of the scene is top-down; feature extraction and pattern recognition are combined in a reinforcing system; the algorithm contains a description of the class of scenes to be analyzed; region enumeration techniques are used in primitive object identification; principal parameters in the program are self-adjusting; adjusting; and the concept of ‚Äúfield of vision‚Äù is used to locate the boundaries of objects. The algorithm has been implemented and tested on posteroanterior (PA) chest radiograms, anteroposterior (AP) knee radiograms, and lateral brain scans. The analysis of PA chest radiograms is used to describe the implementation of the program. To date, the algorithm has been tested only on radiographic images; however, the method should also be applicable to other image classes. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Harlow C.A.", "Eisenbeis S.A."]

Title: On two-way multihead automata
Source: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: For each positive integer n, let ‚Ñí<sup>N</sup>(n) be the class of sets accepted by a family of automata of type N, each with a read-only input with endmarkers and n two-way input heads. The following result, which is applicable to most types of two-way multihead devices, is proved: If for each positive integer n, there is some integer M<sub>n</sub>>n such that ‚Ñí<sup>N</sup>(n) is properly contained in ‚Ñí<sup>N</sup>(M<sup>n</sup>), then ‚Ñí<sup>N</sup>(n) is properly contained in ‚Ñí<sup>N</sup>(n + c<sup>N</sup>) for each n, where c<sub>N</sub>=1 or 2, depending on the type of the device. As a consequence, it is shown that deterministic two-way finite automata with n+2 heads are strictly more powerful than deterministic two-way finite automata with n heads for each positive integer n. It is also shown that the class of sets accepted by deterministic (nondeterministic) two-way pushdown automata with n heads is properly included in the class of sets accepted by deterministic (nondeterministic) two-way pushdown automata with n+1 heads. ¬© 1973 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Ibarra O.H."]

Title: ON THE EFFICIENCY OF SIMPLE CONTROLLERS.
Abstract: An examination is made of controller schemes for the operation of a homogeneous computational system in the solution of a set of interconnected problems. An analytical estimate is made of the resulting quality of the distribution of the computational labors in the general case. Data regarding statistical estimation of the quy of the distribution are given for several types of computational systems and various criteria of estimation of problems used by a controller.
Name: ["Trusov S.S."]

Title: Optimization of Multiparameter Reference Models by Random Search Procedures. | OPTIMIERUNG VIELPARAMETRIGER BEZUGSMODELLE MIT HILFE VON ZUFALLSSUCHVERFAHREN.
Abstract: In this paper random search techniques for parameter optimization are described. These methods can be applied for the identification of multi-parameter systems by use of reference models. The idea of random search techniques is explained and a comparison with gradient methods is given. Some search algorithms are described in detail and their different convergence properties are mentioned. As an example, the parameter optimization of ‚Ä≥human controller models‚Ä≥ is shown for vehicle control. For this example a combination of local random search with priority direction and global search strategy is used.
Name: ["Johannsen G."]

Title: Evaluation of Real-Time Cepstra for Fast Detection of Voiced Sounds. | [AUSWERTUNG VON ECHTZEIT-CEPSTRA ZUR SCHNELLEN DETEKTION STIMMHAFTER LAUTE.]
Source: NTZ Nachr Z NTZ Commun J
Abstract: A description is given of the assemblage of a real-time voiced-unvoiced detector which is used for automatic recognition of spoken words. The detector operates according to the so-called cepstrum method which is difficult to implement, but provides freedom from disturbance. The theoretical foundations of the ceptrum method as well as the construction and function of the detector are explained. As shown by experimental results and experience the voiced-unvoiced detector is capable of processing in a fast and accurate manner even those speech signals which are superimposed by disturbances and/or limited in the frequency domain.
Name: ["Timme Martin", "Idler Horst", "Lay Theo"]

Title: Partial Reconstruction of State Vectors in Decentralized Dynamic Systems
Abstract: The extent to which the state vector information can be recovered in a decentralized control system from a partial observation record of the state vector measurement and also of the control vectors is discussed. That subspaces associated with partial reconstruction of the state space can be obtained recursively and that they have certain invariance properties is shown. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Aoki M.", "Li M.T."]

Title: The Stabilization Of Two-Dimensional Recursive Filters Via The Discrete Hilbert Transform
Abstract: Two-dimensional recursive filters are useful only if stable, that is, if their outputs remain bounded for bounded inputs. The stability of a recursive filter depends on the phase spectrum of its denominator array. A two-dimensional generalization of the discrete Hilbert transform leads to a scheme producing stability with nominal distortions of the filter's desired amplitude spectrum. The method is therefore an attractive alternate to a least-squares procedure recently described by Shanks et al10. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Read R.R.", "Treitel S."]

Title: SCHEME FOR SOLVING A NONLINEAR PROGRAMMING PROBLEM IN THE CASE OF A UNIMODAL TARGET FUNCTION.
Abstract: The solution of a nonlinear programming problem is reduced to integration of a system of differential equations describing the trajectory of descent along a dominating restriction in the state space. A class of problems that can be solved by this method is exhibited.
Name: ["Razdol'skiy A.G."]

Title: ANALYIS OF QUEUING SYSTEMS WITH NONORDINARY FLOWS OF EVENTS.
Abstract: A study is made of queueing systems in which the appearance and servicing of orders occur in groups. A system of equations is obtained for the probabilities of events in a many-line queueing system with a limited number of waiting places. A procedure is proposed for finding the solutions of this system in special cases. Solutions for certain queueing systems in this class, and formulas for determining the distribution function of the waiting time, are given.
Name: ["Popov V.A.", "Litvinov M.L."]

Title: Exponential Approximation Via a Closed-Form Gauss-Newton Method
Abstract: A convergent gradient descent technique is provided for the approximation of functions of time from their Laplace transforms. The approximation is composed of a finite series of exponential functions. Both the complex coefficients and exponents of the exponential terms are adjusted to reduce the integral squared error at each iteration. The novel feature of the present method is that all parameters are adjusted through the use of explicit formulas. This overcomes the usual numerical difficulties associated with the inversion of ill-conditioned matrices. Finally, the utility of the proposed method is demonstrated by its performance on certain examples chosen to allow comparison with previously developed methods. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Harman R.K.", "Fairman F.W."]
Affiliations: ['Computing Devices of Canada Ltd.', " Queen's University"]

Title: AQVAL/1 - COMPUTER IMPLEMENTATION OF A VARIABLE-VALUED LOGIC SYSTEM VL<sub>1</sub> AND EXAMPLES OF ITS APPLICATION TO PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: AQVAL/1 is a PL/1 program which synthesizes quasiminimal formulas of the variable-valued logic system VL//1 under cost (or complexity) functionals designed by a user from a set of available criteria. A brief functional description of AQVAL/1 is presented, and current results of its application to two pattern recognition problems are reported. Medical applications are discussed.
Name: ["Michalski R.S."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF PROGRAMMED EXTENSIVE CONTROL OF SPATIAL TURNING MANEUVER.
Abstract: A synthesis is examined of a system for programmed extensive control based on the Pontryagin maximum principle. Computational relations are obtained for determining a program for the variation of the moments applied to a vehicle about the body axes to insure performance of a specified turning maneuver in minimum time.
Name: ["Bodner V.A.", "Alekseev K.B.", "Zbarskii I.S."]

Title: Neighborhood search algorithms for finding optimal traveling salesman tours must be inefficient
Source: Proceedings of the Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
Abstract: In this paper, we explore the use of neighborhood search techniques for finding optimal solutions to the symmetric Traveling Salesman Problem. These techniques have been dramatically successful in obtaining near-optimal solutions to this problem for a reasonable expenditure of effort (1,2,3,4,5,6,9,10,12). Extensions of these techniques can be used to obtain the globally optimum solution, but the effort involved is at least an exponential function of the number of cities, n. Indeed, as this paper demonstrates, all local search algorithms that are capable of finding the optimal solution to an arbitrary n-city problem must grow at least as fast as Thus for large problems, these algorithms are computationally inefficient. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Weiner P.", "Savage S.L.", "Bagchi A."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF NONLINEAR SYSTEMS HAVING PRESCRIBED STEP RESPONSES.
Abstract: An n**t**h order step response model for ground stable nonlinear devices and systems is proposed. The model is based upon the assumption that the dynamic component of the system step response is Lebesgue integrable. It is shown that the model converges, in the mean square sense, to an exact representation as n yields infinity . Furthermore, it has an orthogonal feature which, in tradition of Wiener, separates the nonlinearity from the dynamics. The model admits a simple circuit realization, and the parameters which characterize it can all be measured directly. Finally a relatively large class of nonlinear systems satisfying the required stability assumption is identified.
Name: ["Chua Leon O.", "Schilling R.J."]

Title: OPTIMUM FILTERING FOR STOCHASTIC SIGNALS IN STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: An analysis is presented of the input-output relation of stochastic signals in systems having parameters which are stochastic processes themselves. It is shown that the output spectrum is the same as the output spectrum of a deterministic parameter system with additive noise added to the input; the spectrum of this additional input is computed. Continuous as well as discrete filters are considered. This result is used to solve the Wiener filter problem for cases where some parameters of the transmission channel of the signal are stochastic.
Name: ["Willems Jacques L."]

Title: Approximation of Transient Functions of Static Plants and an Algorithm for the Required Computer-Aided Calculations. | [APPROKSIMATSIYA PEREKHODNYKH FUNKTSII STATICHESKIKH OB'EKTOV I ALGORITM VYPOLNENIA NEOBKHODIMYKH RASCHETOV NA ETsVM.]
Abstract: A simple method is proposed for approximating the transient function of a static plant by the transient function of a model whose transfer function has the form of a rational fraction polynomial with multiple real pole. The proposed method can also be applied to reduce the order of complicated transfer functions. An algorithm is presented for implementing the necessary calculations on a digital computer. It ensures simple and effective application of the method. An example illustrating the use of the method is given.
Name: ["Dzhigit G.A."]

Title: Fast on-line integer multiplication
Source: Proceedings of the Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
Abstract: A Turing machine multiplies on-line if it receives its inputs low order digits first and it produces the k-th output digit before reading in the (k+l)-st inputs. We present a general method for converting any off-line multiplication algorithm which forms the product of two n-bi6 binary numbers in time F(n) into an on-line method, and the new algorithm requires time only 0(F(n) log n). Applying this technique to the fast multiplication algorithm of Sch'onhage and Strassen gives an upper 2 bound of 0(n (log n) log log n) for on-line multiplication of integers. Other applications are to the on-line problems of products of polynomials over a finite ring, recognition of palindromes, and multiplication by a constant. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Fischer M.J.", "Stockmeyer L.J."]

Title: NEW ALGORITHM FOR LOCATING SOURCES AMONG DESTINATIONS.
Abstract: The problem considered is the location of m sources among n locations and the assignment of the location requirements to the sources in order that the total transportation cost is minimized. A branch and bound algorithm is developed to achieve an optimal solution. Two lower bounds are developed for the algorithm; one is efficient for small problems while the other is more efficient for larger problems. An illustrative example is given, and a detailed application of the algorithm to the thirty largest metropolitan centers in the United States is presented for various numbers of destination (10, 20 and 20) and sources (2, 4 and 6). The branch and bound algorithm was coded in Fortran IV and tested on a number of problems. Some of the example problems that were tested are included in this paper.
Name: ["El-Shaieb A.M."]

Title: CURRENT PREDICTIVE MODELS OF THE DYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT OF TRANSPORTATION.
Abstract: The current predictive models of the transportation dynamic environment which have been developed for use by Sandia Laboratories. The information sources, methods of building the models, and the method of representation are described. Advantages and limitations of the models are discussed.
Name: ["Foley J.T.", "Gens M.B.", "Magnuson C.F."]

Title: Fast algorithm for finding a forest of a linear graph
Abstract: A new algorithm is described for finding a tree of a connected, or a forest of an unconnected, linear graph. The algorithm is found to be the fastest of known algorithms having the same minimal storage requirements. A short comparison of the algorithm with some other algorithms is included. ¬© 1973, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Jovanovich A.D.", "Chobeljich S.N."]

Title: Combinational and Sequential Cellular Structures
Abstract: Cellular arrays composed of identical cells with uniform interconnections are presented. The basic cell is a switching device with two inputs, two outputs, and two control variables x and T. The cell structure is either purely combinational or with unit delay depending upon the control variable T. The control variable x sets up either a ‚Äúcrossing mode‚Äù or a ‚Äúbending mode‚Äù in the cell. Thus a two-dimensional cellular array without time delays has the connection capabilities of a crossbar switch. Any combinational switching function can be realized by appropriate choice of control variables while the inputs to the edges of the plane are fixed. Alternatively, the control variables can be fixed while the inputs to the edges of the cellular plane are varied from function to function. A cubic array is constructed from a set of identical cellular planes packed one upon the other such that the control variables applied to the first plane will penetrate to all other planes without time delay. It is shown that any k functions of the same variables can be synthesized on such a cubic array. By allowing the control variable T to delay some signals in the array, such a cubic array can be used to realize any synchronous sequential machine with single or multiple inputs and/or feedback functions. Any defective cell in the array can be tested and isolated. The array can be stripped, divided, or interconnected. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Kukreja S.N.", "Chen I.-N."]
Keywords: ["crossbar switch", "cubic cellular arrays", "fault detection", "machine realization", "synchronous sequential machines"]

Title: SHORT-TERM PLANNING OF TRAIN SERVICES BY COMPUTER- ‚Ä≥AIRE-POWER‚Ä≥ .
Abstract: Merry-go-round trains operate between a large number of collieries and a small number of power stations. These trains convey specially constructed wagons which are automatically loaded and discharged while the train moves at slow speed. The variation of demand for movement is such that a new train plan is prepared each week. A computer system has been developed to assist this planning process and to improve its efficieny. The system requires the transmission of data relating to the tonnages to be moved via a data link between the Planning Office in Leeds and the computer center in Crewe. A program has been developed which will verify the data, examine all the alternatives available, and select the optimum based on theoretical costs, and prepare a plan which contains the requirements for individual trains, the locomotive, men's and wagon set schedules. The plan is transmitted back to Leeds where it is printed out to form the working document. The whole process from receiving the tonnage forecast to printing out the plan takes approximately three hours when producing a plan for a week and this is reduced when preparing plans for shorter timescales.
Name: ["Catterall P.V."]

Title: An Innovations Approach to Least-Squares Estimation‚ÄìPart V: Innovations Representations and Recursive Estimation in Colored Noise
Abstract: We show that least-squares filtered and smoothed estimates of a random process given observations of another colored noise process can be expressed as certain linear combinations of the state vector of the so-called innovations representation (IR) of the observed process. The IR of a process is a representation of it as the response of a causal and causally invertible linear filter to a white-noise ‚Äúinnovations‚Äù process. For nonstationary colored noise processes, the ER may not always exist and a major part of this paper is devoted to the problem of identifying a proper class of such processes and of giving effective recursive algorithms for their determination. The ER can be expressed either in terms of the parameters of a known lumped model for the process or in terms of its covariance function. In the first case, our results on estimation encompass most of those found in the previous literature on the subject; in the second case, there seems to be no prior literature. Finally, we may note that our proofs rely on, and exploit in both directions, the intimate relation that exists between least-squares estimation and the innovations representation. Name: ["Kailath T.", "Geesey R.A."]

Title: On evaluating boolean expressions
Abstract: An evaluation algorithm for Boolean expressions is efficient if it recognizes when particular conditions cannot affect the value of the result. Of special interest are efficient algorithms which do not expect the conditions to be evaluated in the order in which they appear in the expression. This is important for selective retrieval from a large data base, when the evaluation (retrieval) order depends on the data organization and not on the order in which the qualifiers appear in the query. Another aspect of data retrieval is that we may repeatedly change part (but not all) of the values of the variables, and wish to re‚Äêevaluate part of the expression. Algorithms are given for representing and efficiently evaluating Boolean expressions both for the sequential and random cases; for the latter, an algorithm for partial re‚Äêinitialization is also given. Copyright ¬© 1973 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd
Name: ["Gudes E.", "Reiter A."]

Title: SPECTRAL ESTIMATOR FOR DYNAMIC-TEST DATA FROM TURBINE-BLADE VIBRATIONS.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: An analysis is presented of the distribution of occurrence times for pulse trains which can arise in the measurement of turbine-blade vibrations. The problem arises where a proximity probe, mounted in the casing, detects the passing of a rotor-blade tip and generates a pulse. Since the pulse timing depends on the magnitude of the blade vibration an irregular distribution of time intervals arises, and here the properties of the pulse-occurrence distribution are related to the blade-vibration statistics. In particular, a spectral estimator is considered and its errors are evaluated. The analysis provides a solution to a general problem in the estimation of the power-spectral-density function of a Gaussian process from observations of crossings at an arbitrary barrier.
Name: ["Nightingale J.M.", "Durrani T.S."]

Title: Computerized Control of a Mine Ventilation System. | [KIEROWANIE PRZEWIETRZANIEM KOPALNI W OPARCIU O ELEKTRONICZNA TECHNIKE OBLICZENIOWA.]
Abstract: Paper stresses the need for broader application of digital computation to the control of mine ventilation systems. The problems involved in the preparation of input data and their verification are discussed. The essential problems whose solution can be accomplished by digital computation and techniques for analyzing the output data are indicated. Paper postulates that in the area of bringing up to date the parameters of the ventilating network the part played by the ventilation supervisory staff cannot be overestimated. A practical example of computer application to the solution of a problem resulting from introduction with the network of a new ventilating mine shaft is presented.
Name: ["Frycz Andrzej", "Sulkowski Jozef"]

Title: SEARCH METHOD FOR OPTIMAL CONDITIONS IN AN INDUSTRIAL CHEMICAL PROCESS.
Abstract: A description is given of a search algorithm base upon the planning of experiments, but also incorporating a priori knowledge, intuition and accumulated knowledge of the investigator, for locating maxima or minima in unknown functions.
Name: ["Kofarov V.V.", "Zaslavskii I.I.", "Ivanov V.G.", "Krivovaz R.A.", "Spivakovskii G.I."]

Title: The dependent shop sequencing algorithm a general algorithm for solving flow shop, job shop, and dependent shop sequencing problems
Abstract: This article describes a heuristic algorithm which will yield an optimal or near optimal minimal makespan solution to a specific type of sequencing/scheduling problem defined as the dependent sequencing problem which includes the pure job-shop and flow-shop sequencing problems. The name ‚Äò dependent sequencing ‚Äô was selected for this model since it reflects the possibility of interdependence between activities of the technological processing order graph (GTPO) not present in ‚Äò pure ‚Äô job -shop or f low-shop sequencing models. There are some approaches to this class of problem which provide optimal solutions, but their time to solutions and/or theoretical approaches make them difficult to understand and apply. Recent articles in the literature have recommended that research in the sequencing/scheduling area be directed toward developing practical approaches which can be easily understood and applied. The dependent shop algorithm utilizes extensions of PERT/CPM techniques which are widely known and therefore, can be easily applied. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Spencer D.L.", "Dudek R.A."]
Affiliations: [' University of Houston', ' Texas Tech University']

Title: COMPUTER-CONTROLLED TRAFFIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A comparison of Signal Plan Generation and Signal Plan Selection systems is made, and hardware sub-systems are discussed. The Signal Plan Selection systems assumes that area traffic flow patterns are analogs of actual traffic flow patterns in one or two main streets. The Signal Plan Generation systems function on the basis of wide-ranging on-line traffic flow pattern samples. The British Motorway Control System is described, and some comments made on the probable future development of area traffic control systems.
Name: ["Howard-Jones R."]

Title: Bias Estimation Errors Induced by Parameter Uncertainties
Abstract: The effect of a class of plant parameter uncertainties upon the state vector estimation of a system driven by a deterministic forcing function is considered. For this problem the minimization of mean-square error and the minimization of bias error are opposing goals. The set of noninferior solutions for the optimal control problem whose performance index has components mean-square error and bias error is considered, and evaluated. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Leondes C.T.", "Pearson J.O."]

Title: Optimal Control of Complex Chemical Plants by Means of Hierarchial Automatic System. | OPTIMALE STEUERUNG KOMPLEXER PRODUKTIONSANLAGEN DER CHEMIEINDUSTRIE DURCH HIERARCHISCHE AUTOMATISIERUNGSSYSTEME.
Abstract: Multilevel optimization applied to a large scale chemical process is considered. Algorithms and feasible optimization are discussed as methods for solution of automated processes.
Name: ["Auerbach D.", "Grauer M.", "Metzing P."]

Title: Application of Digital Computers in Analysis of Nonlinear Control Systems Stability Using Popov Technique. | [ANWENDUNG VON DIGITALRECHNERN BEI DER ANALYSE DER ABSOLUTEN STABILITAET NICHTLINEARER REGELUNGSSYSTEME AUF DER BASIS DES POPOW-KRITERIUMS.]
Abstract: Popov method for calculation of absolute stability of control systems is shown by which an algorithm is derived for digital computer for simplified calculation. The limit curve is determined in which nonlinearities are shown so that by proper selection of values stable control may be obtained.
Name: ["Baltruschewitsch A.W.", "Mueller G."]

Title: Some Characteristics of Universal Cell Nets
Abstract: In this paper, one-output n-input combinatorial nondegenerate networks of cells are analyzed. The networks consist of oneoutput two-input cells that are universal in that they realize all 16 functions of the two-input variables. Such networks have a number of interesting properties, among which is the fact that if network N realizes F(x), it also realizes the dual function Fd(x). Besides the basic properties shown to be possessed by all networks, the number of functions realized by certain network forms are calculated. The network forms discussed lead naturally to a class of networks called disjunctive networks. These are characterized by cell interconnections where cell outputs and network inputs connect to at most one cell input. It is shown that disjunctive networks possess the interesting property that all networks of c cells realize the same number of functions (but not necessarily the same functions). Further, it is shown that all disjunctive networks of c cells realize the same number of functions dependent on all input variables. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Butler J.T.", "Breeding K.J."]

Title: Results of a Study of the Linear Prediction Vocoder
Abstract: The Linear Prediction Vocoder (LIPREDER) System is an analysis-synthesis speech processing system which efficiently converts speech into digital form at voiceband data rates. The objective of our study was to optimize the LIPREDER system in terms of performance and complexity for a wide selection of talkers and sentences at data rates of 3600 and 7200 b/s The optimized LIPREDER system produces synthetic speech quality which represents a substantial improvement over previous voice encoders operating at voiceband data rates. Evaluation results indicate that for most talkers and text there is little or no perceptible quality difference between the synthetic speech produced by LIPREDER systems at 3600 and 7200 b/s Additionally, implementation of the LIPREDER system appears to be technically feasible. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Haskew J.R.", "Kelly J.M.", "Kelly R.M., Jr.", "McKINNEY T.H."]

Title: Algorithms of Learning
Abstract: Learning in various learning systems is accomplished with the help of algorithms. This chapter introduces a method for obtaining the algorithms of learning, not only for simple, but also for complex goals of learning.These algorithms of learning represent stochastic difference or differential equations. The conditions for convergence of the algorithms are evaluated and the methods of treating the constraints are also considered. The chapter presents the learning algorithms, and reviews the algorithmic approach. The algorithms of learning guarantee the attainment of the corresponding goal of learning when the conditions of the stability criteria are satisfied. As the goal of learning is reached in time, the learning system that realizes these algorithms is an asymptotically optimal system. The same goal of learning can be reached by various algorithms of learning, which are simple or modified, with simultaneous or alternative action. ¬© 1973, Academic Press Inc.

Title: ASYMPTOTIC ENLARGEMENT OF THE STATES OF CERTAIN STOCHASTIC AUTOMATA.
Abstract: Let a homogeneous Markov chain having a finite number of states and describing a stochastic automaton depend on a parameter epsilon in such a way that the transition probabilities are continuous functions of epsilon for epsilon equals epsilon //0 and the set of states of the chain for epsilon equals epsilon //0 decomposes into the union of k greater than 1 ergodic sets X//1,. . . ,X//k. A family of Markov processes describing a random walk of the original Markov process on the sets X//1,. . . X//k as epsilon approaches epsilon //0 is constructed.
Name: ["Rotenberg A.R."]

Title: OPTIMIZATION ALGORITHMS FOR DIFFERENT SIZE PROBLEMS WITH UNKNOWN STATISTICAL PROPERTIES OF THE CRITERION FUNCTION.
Source: ACM Urban Symp on the Appl of Comput to the Probl of Urban Soc, 8th Annu, Proc
Abstract: Optimal urban land use is presented as a problem of allocating indivisible resources. Two distinctive models are presented, a market model and a planning model. The former model involves maximizing private profitabilities and is a linear assignment problem. The latter model maximizes the net of profitabilities and positive externalities over transhipment and negative externalities. The solution matrix for each model is a permutation matrix which assigns a whole activity to one location. The planning model is a quadratic assignment problem. The quadratic assignment problem is reduced to the maximization of several linear assignment problems. Two linear assignment algorithms are presented, an exact backtrack method and a simple heuristic method.
Name: ["Gordon Peter", "MacReynolds William K."]

Title: Convergence of the Edited Nearest Neighbor
Abstract: The edited k-nearest neighbor rule (k-NNR) consists of 1) eliminating those samples from the data which are not classified correctly by the k-NNR and the remainder of the data, and 2) using the NNR with the samples which remain from 1) to classify new observations. Wilson has shown that this rule has an asymptotic probability of error which is better than that of the k-NNR. A key step in his development is showing the convergence of the edited nearest neighbor. His lengthy argument is replaced here by a somewhat simpler one which uses an intuitive fact about the editing procedure. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Wagner T.J."]

Title: ASYMPTOTIC PROPERTIES OF LEAST-SQUARES ESTIMATES FOR REGRESSION COEFFICIENTS.
Abstract: The asymptotic normality of least-squares estimates for the coefficients of a linear combination of stochastic functions is verified, along with the existence and convergence of the moments of the estimates. Estimates are formulated from observations of stochastic functions and a linear combination with additive ‚Ä≥noise.‚Ä≥ The stochastic functions and ‚Ä≥noise‚Ä≥ are assumed to be independent Gaussian processes.
Name: ["Dorogovtsev A.Ya."]

Title: PRACTICAL RECOMMENDATIONS FOR THE SPECTRAL ANALYSIS OF STATIONARY GAUSSIAN PROCESSES.
Abstract: Estimates obtained for the spectral density of a stationary Gaussian discrete-time stochastic process on the basis of the differential properties of the estimated spectral density are discussed. It is shown that the rejection of nonnegative weighting functions makes it possible in many situations to diminish significantly the mean-square error of estimation. Recommendations are formulated for the selection of weighting functions in accordance with the number n of readings, which is assumed to be finite.
Name: ["Alekseev V.G."]

Title: DERIVATION OF SWITCHING FUNCTIONS FOR THE STORAGE ELEMENTS OF A FINITE AUTOMATON WITH STATE ENCODING ON THE COLUMNS OF A FLOW TABLE.
Abstract: A simple formula is proposed for the derivation of logic functions for the switching of storage elements of an asynchronous finite automaton with encoding of its states on the column of a flow table.
Name: ["Sapozhnikov V.V.", "Sapozhnikov Vl.V."]

Title: THEORY OF DELAY POLYNOMIALS AND THEIR NULL SEQUENCES.
Source: J Inst Eng (India), Electron Telecommun Eng Div
Abstract: The theory of delay polynomials that describe the sequential behavior of linear autonomous multistable (p-level) systems is outlined. Two methods are discussed to evaluate all the null sequences associated with a given p-nary nth degree delay polynomial irrespective of its factorable features. The analysis is limited to autonomous systems which remain stable in p states, p being a prime integer.
Name: ["Sastri K.S."]

Title: PROJECT OF URBAN TRAFFIC NOISE CONTROL.
Abstract: Physico-mathematical considerations about the shape of the probability distribution functions of the fundamental acoustical magnitudes intervening in a determination of urban traffic noise are presented. The shapes of the functions of the related magnitudes are determined by the assumptions made for one of them. It is deduced that, a priori, it is not possible to postulate that an experimental distribution of sound pressure levels would fit to a normal law. Finally, the features that an automatic system for the acquisition and processing of acoustical signals must accomplish, are analyzed.
Name: ["De Cevallos J.F.G.", "Delgado C.", "Martinez Saez V.", "Santiago J.S."]

Title: TRAJECTORY-SENSITIVITY DESIGN OF LOAD-FREQUENCY CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: A method is described for limiting the trajectory dispersion of a load-frequency control system due to parameter variations with a controller subject to structure constant. The parameter variations are assumed to be small, so that linear sensitivity equations are obtained for the trajectory-sensitivity function. The desensitization problem is then formulated as a suboptimal-control problem with a specified feedback structure and a quadratic performance index which also includes the trajectory-sensitivity function. The controller gain minimizing the cost function is determined by iterative application of an algorithm for parameter optimization based on averaging the performance criterion. Applied to a 2-area system, the design procedure is shown to produce a load-frequency control system with a trajectory sensitivity to the varying-incremental-speed-regulation parameter greatly reduced compared with that of the corresponding suboptimal-control system designed without sensitivity considerations, while maintaining a satisfactory performance.
Name: ["Malek N.G.", "Julich P.M.", "Tacker E.C.", "Tan O.T."]

Title: IMAGE RECONSTRUCTION FROM PROJECTIONS.
Abstract: Several methods of image reconstruction from projections are treated within a unified formal framework to demonstrate their common features and highlight their particular differences. This is done analytically (ignoring computational factors) for the following techniques: the Convolution method, Algebraic Reconstruction, Back-projection, and the Fourier-Bessel approach.
Name: ["Zwick M.", "Zeitler E."]

Title: Machine recognition of handwritten words: A project report
Abstract: A project beginning with publication of the author's book Recognition in 1965 has resulted in a cursive script recognition program which has correctly identified 79 per cent of a test sample of 84 words. This program makes no use of information about sequence of stroke inscription, and segments the cursive line as part of the recognition procedure. It thus compares favorably in performance level with previously reported programs appropriately "normalized", while not requiring input pertaining to stroke sequence and stroke segmentation that is essential to these other programs. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Sayre K.M."]

Title: The netlet theory ani cooperatife phenomena in neural networks
Source: Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement and Control, Transactions of the ASME
Abstract: Many of the observed oscillatory phenomena in biological systems are the result of endogenous neural activity and occur in the absence of any kind of proprioceptive feedback. In certain simple animals such activity is manifested in a stereotyped behavioral response of considerably longer duration than the evoking stimulus. For instance, in Tritonia gilberti (a slug-like nudibranch) even the briefest touch by a predator triggers a powerful escape motion consisting of alternating dorsal and ventral flectionsof the animal‚Äôs body. Physiological studies by A.O. D. Willows revealed that the mechanism responsible for this behaviour is a cooperative effect which requires the interaction between three small pools of neurons. In our earlier publications we have proposed a netlet theory for investigating the dynamics of interacting neuronal ensembles. We found that a variety of cooperative phenomena, such as hysteresis effects, phase transitions, resonances and entrainments exist in such structures. By a combination of mathematical analysis and computer simulation it is shown in this paper that hysteresis effects together with a known property of neurons, namely, accumulating hyperpolarization, give rise to the kind of behavior observed in Tritonia and shed light on some features found in the single unit firing records. ¬© 1973 by ASME.
Name: ["Gseriely T.J.", "Harth E.", "Lewis N.S."]

Title: OPTIMAL CONTROL OF PARTIALLY OBSERVABLE MARKOV PROCESSES OVER A FINITE HORIZON.
Abstract: The paper formulates the optimal control problem for a class of mathematical models in which the system to be controlled is characterized by a finite-state discrete-time Markov process. The formulation is illustrated by a simple machine-maintenance example, and other specific application areas are also discussed. The paper demonstrates that, if there are only a finite number of control intervals remaining, then the optimal payoff function is a piecewise-linear, convex function of the current state probabilities of the internal Markov process.
Name: ["Smallwood Richard D.", "Sondik Edward J."]

Title: PERFORMANCE OF RECURSIVE DIGITAL MOVING-TARGET-INDICATOR RADAR FILTERS WITH BUTTERWORTH FREQUENCY RESPONSE.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: Three sets of results for digital moving-target-indicator radar filters with Butterworth frequency response are presented. These are: (a) the dependence of the improvement factor on the standard deviation of power spectrum of clutter (assumed Gaussian) for filter orders from one to five; (b) the frequency response of a 2nd-order filter for different numbers of hits between Gaussian 3 db points; (C) the dependence of dc attenuation of the number of hits between Gaussian 3 db points; (c) the dependence of dc attenuation of the number of hits between Gaussian 3 db points for filter orders from one to five. These results, which have been obtained by means of a digital computer, show that the improvement in performance of the filter is most marked in going from filter order one to three, beyond which the improvement is less marked.
Name: ["Haykin S.S.", "Boulter J.F."]

Title: The analysis and synthesis of probability transformers
Abstract: A logical network with n inputs and m outputs ((n, m)-network) supplied by a binary random vector may be considered as a device transforming the input probability distribution into the output one. In this paper a method of analysis of such a network is presented. The approach is based on the orthogonal expansions of the logical functions and the corresponding distributions into the Walsh-Rademacher series. On the basis of the results obtained the synthesis problem has been formulated in terms of the spectral approach. ¬© 1973 Noordhoff International Publishing.
Name: ["Laski J."]

Title: An Adaptive Observer for Single-Input Single-Output Linear Systems
Abstract: A full order adaptive observer is described for observing the state of a single-input single-output observable continuous differential system with unknown parameters. Convergence of the observer states to those of the system is accomplished by directly changing the parameters of the observer using an adaptive law based upon Lyapunov stability theory. Observer eigenvalues may be freely chosen. Some restriction is placed upon the system input in that it must be sufficiently rich in frequencies in order to insure conver-gence.
