Name: ["Koffman E.B."]

Title: Machine Learning of Correlation
Abstract: A simple, inexpensive, special-purpose digital computer was built to exemplify the obvious as well as the subtle properties of correlation. The method augmented the usual mathematical introduction of this material. Using such common peripheral equipment as a function generator with V.C.O. capabilities, analog noise generator and oscilloscope, such concepts as auto-and-cross-correlation, stochastic filtering, and signal detection can be dynamically explored. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Taylor F.J."]

Title: QUEUEING THEORETIC MODELS.
Abstract: Tradeoffs between methods of solving analytical queueing models are discussed. It is suggested that representing the multiple (simply defined) resources of a computer system and the sequencing of tasks among these resources gives models which are simple enough to yield to analysis and yet are applicable to systems of interest. Theoretical results from the study of such networks are summarized and directions of future research are briefly discussed. Diagrams show models.
Name: ["Denning P.J.", "Muntz R.R."]

Title: Noisy neural networks: A Summary
Abstract: We build a mathematical model of neural networks which is based on recent physiological data concerning information transmission at the synaptic junction. This transmission is known to occur in nearly all synapses by means of emission of a number of quanta of a chemical transmitter on receipt of a nerve impulse at the pre-synaptic membrane. The work of Katz and his colleagues1 has shown that there is always leakage of transmitter quanta, and that this follows a Poisson law. ¬© 1973, Informa UK Ltd. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Taylor J.G."]

Title: External program control of a laboratory computer to obtain representative criteria for average evoked potentials | [EXTERNE PROGRAMMSTEUERUNG EINES LABORCOMPUTERS ZUR GEWINNUNG REPRASENTATIVER MERKMALE FUR AVERAGE EVOKED POTENTIALS]
Abstract: The algorithm and technical implementation of external control of an average computer are described, permitting one to combine the process of averaging evoked potentials and the derivation of representative criteria for these average evoked potentials (AEP). By virtue of its programmed control of address advance, the system intervenes in the computer's own principle of fixed adjustment of the time interval represented by each address value. This minimizes the address demand for obtaining criteria so that processing can be made by all 4 channels of the computer (storage capacity 400 addresses). Furthermore, the averaged pre analysis interval may be stored for each AEP. To demonstrate the mechanism of external control, its integration into the experimental unit of the neurophysiological test process is described.
Name: ["Gurk C.", "Baumann H.", "Schauer M."]

Title: A Learning Program Which Plays Partnership Dominoes
Abstract: A learning program has been written in BASIC to play four-player partnership dominoes. Because dominoes is a game of incomplete information, the program uses somewhat different principles of artificial intelligence from those used in programs for games of complete information, such as checkers, chess, and go. The program was constructed to use a ‚Äústrategy signature table‚Äù which classifies board situations through the interactions of game parameters. Each entry in the table contains adaptively determined weights indicating the advisability of various strategies. Once chosen, a strategy then employs probability analysis and linear polynomial evaluation to choose a move. Our program wins approximately two-thirds of its games in tournament situations, and has defeated championship players. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Smith M.H."]

Title: Experiences with a test stage free text processing system in pathology using display terminals
Abstract: A system for computerization of surgical pathology findings and autopsy protocols in German clear text is described in detail. It is based on a thesaurus which has been compiled by incorporating more than 44,000 entry words. These words have been encoded according to the Systematized Nomenclature of Pathology (S.N.O.P) thus representing a classified system with a logical structure. FORTRAN programmed processing of the narrative text takes place automatically in a 128 k core storage computer with external random access bulk stores. Evaluations are asked for by a video display unit using a very simplified retrieval language which enables the pathologist himself to specify questions in an on line dialogue. The system has been in test stage operation since 1972. Up to now 8,000 biopsy reports have been analyzed automatically, stored and retrieved by numerous questions combining many variables. Experiences gained during test stage operation give definite hints concerning suitable input media, structure of a thesaurus on different levels of text analysis and indications to the function of a centralized pathology register.
Name: ["Becker H."]

Title: Real-Time Pitch Extraction by Adaptive Prediction of the Speech Waveform
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: With the exception of relatively sophisticated methods such as cepstrum analysis, the problem of reliable pitch-period extraction has remained largely unsolved. This paper examines the feasibility of pitch-period extraction by means of the nonstationary error process resulting from adaptive-predictive quantization of speech. A real-time hardware system that may be realized at low cost is described. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Maksym J.N."]

Title: Design and Simulation of a Speech Analysis-Synthesis System Based on Short-Time Fourier Analysis
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: This paper discusses the theoretical basis for representation of a speech signal by its short-time Fourier transform. The results of the theoretical studies were used to design a speech analysis-synthesis system which was simulated on a general-purpose laboratory digital computer system. The simulation uses the fast Fourier transform in the analysis stage and specially designed finite duration impulse response filters in the synthesis stage. The results of both the theoretical and computational studies lead to an understanding of the effect of several design parameters and elucidate the design tradeoffs necessary to achieve moderate information rate reductions. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Schafer R.W.", "Rabiner L.R."]

Title: Application of a Digital Inverse Filter for Automatic Formant and F0 Analysis
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: In this paper, a new algorithm based upon a digital inverse filter formulation is presented for automatically determining VU, a voiced-unvoiced decision (VU = 0 during unvoiced speech and VU = 1 during voiced speech), F0, the fundamental frequency, and Fi, i = 1, 2, 3, the first three formant frequencies, as a function of time. Formant trajectory estimates are obtained for all speech sounds that satisfy VU = 1. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Markel J.D."]

Title: On-line information retrieval as a scientists tool
Abstract: The use of an on-line information retrieval system by the scientists themselves is described. MEDUSA was designed to allow physicians to interrogate the MEDLARS data base. A brief description is given of the system and details of an experiment to test its effectiveness. Search formulations prepared on-line by medical research workers are compared for recall and precision with the same requests formulated by search editors in the normal way. The results show that physicians can use an on-line system effectively. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Barber A.S.", "Barraclough E.D.", "Gray W.A."]

Title: Observer Reliability and Human Inference
Abstract: This paper presents a formal analysis of the problem of determining the inferential impact of the information in a composite report from a collection of unreliable observers or sensors. Each sensor reports one of a finite number of possible states of a data system linked probabilistically with an ‚Äúobjective system‚Äù whose condition is to be inferred from the data state. The principal assumptions are that the sensors do not ‚Äúcollaborate‚Äù in making their reports and that their reports are conditioned only by the existing data state and not by the actual, unobservable state of the objective system. Use of the notion of conditional independence to express these assumptions gives the analytic expressions a tractable form which sheds light on various inference issues. The paper also briefly discusses current empirical research on the question of how well people actually adjust the impact of inferential evidence to correspond to the unreliability of the sources of information. ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers. Inc.
Name: ["Schum D.A.", "Pfeiffer P.E."]

Title: Acquisition by telemetry and computer analysis of 4-channel long-term EEG recordings from patients subject to "petit-mal" absence attacks
Abstract: A Telemetry EEG Data Acquisition Cart (TEDAC) has been assembled into a complete system for continously monitoring 4 channels of EEG. The system consists of a 4-channel telemetry transmitter (mounted on the patient's head), a receiver, a Minograf EEG machine for continuously writing out the EEG, a tape-recorder for recording the EEG for later playback and analysis by a PDP-12 computer, and a digital clock for establishing a time base to co-ordinate the patient's activity with the EEG signal recorded on paper and tape. We are especially interested in studying the interrelationships between anti-epileptic drugs, psychological factors, clinical seizures, and epileptic discharges on the EEG. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Ives J.R.", "Thompson C.J.", "Woods J.F."]

Title: Constant-False-Alarm-Rate Processors for Locally Nonstationary Clutter
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: A technique for designing normalizing processors for locally non-stationary clutter is discussed. The design procedure assumes the logarithm of the clutter power varies as a polynomial with range. When the actual environment matches the design environment, the false-alarm rate is a constant that is independent of the polynomial coefficients. A measure of the relative target detection capability as a function of the number of normalization cells and the degree of the design-environment polynomial is given. The applicability of the processors to non-Rayleigh clutter is discussed. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Nitzberg R."]

Title: A Descriptive Technique for Automatic Speech Recognition
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: A technique is introduced that analyzes the time evolutions of some parameters of the speech waveform. Suitable algorithms provide a description of these evolutions when a word is pronounced. Descriptions can be seen as the phrases of a language produced by a generative grammar. Recognition is performed by parsing the descriptions. Some experimental results are reported. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["De Mori R."]
Affiliations: [' Centro di Eleborazione Numerale dei Segnali']

Title: MINIMAX STATE ESTIMATION WITH UNCERTAIN PARAMETERS.
Abstract: The problem of analyzing a minimax filter from the viewpoint of designing a state estimator for an n-dimensional system in the presence of large parameter uncertainties is considered. The solution of the minimax filtering problem requires the application of the general techniques developed for solving singular optimal control and bang-bang control problems. Two specially chosen second order examples are presented to illustrate the switchings in the parameters of the minimax filter by solving the associated two point boundary value problem using the Newton-Raphson procedure.
Name: ["Vathsal S.", "Sarma I.G."]

Title: EIGENVALUE SPECIFICATION FOR SYSTEM MATRICES.
Abstract: The problem of assigning the eigenvalues of a real nth-order matrix constrained by the specification of certain zero entries is explored. The problem is subdivided into two principal paths. First, for certain classes of matrices, necessary and in two cases necessary and sufficient conditions are given governing the existence of such a matrix for a specified complex conjugate set of eigenvalues. Secondly, with these conditions implemented as a subprogram designed to screen unrealizable sets of eigenvalues, several algorithms are outlined, the object of which it is to find a real nth-order matrix having as its eigenvalues the specified set. This is accomplished by using the Fletcher-Powell minimization method applied to a suitably defined function of n variables. This problem finds applications in many areas, but it was originally motivated by attempts to obtain desired responses from an nth-order dynamic system governed by a set of linear homogeneous differential equations of the form dY/dt equals AY, where A is the constant real system matrix to be found.
Name: ["Zimmer Hewlon", "Van Ness James E."]

Title: NONPARAMETRIC STOCHASTIC CONTROL AND EXTREMUM-SEARCH ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: Nonparametric statistics is used to develop an approach to the solution of problems of combined control of nonlinear static entities with unknown characteristics, including extremum entities. Results of statistical computer simulation of control processes with training and extremum-search processes are given.
Name: ["Zhivoglyadov V.P.", "Medvedev A.V."]

Title: CHOICE OF A SYSTEM OF INSTRUCTION FORMATS FOR A CONTROL COMPUTER.
Abstract: A procedure is proposed for establishing and selecting a system of instruction formats for a control computer on the basis of a statistical analysis of the quantitative characteristics of control algorithms.
Name: ["Zhuravlev Yu.P.", "Zabubenov V.N."]

Title: An adaptive optimization system applied to machine synthesis
Abstract: The paper presents the foundations of an optimization system for medium size computers. The system may be used to solve technical or economic problems with nonlinear objective functions and constraints. The system contains five algorithms of the deterministic and stochastic category. The master algorithm, based on works of Bush and Mosteller, randomly seeks one of these five. It performs computations for a certain time and examines its effectiveness. This experience is then taken as the basis for modification of the probability vector used in the choice of algorithm. The technical examples solved by different algorithms are presented. The results needed for definition of the initial vector illustrate difficulties met by an engineer in the proper choice of algorithm. These difficulties, which occur often in practical cases, prove the demand for further studies on optimization systems. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Golinski J."]

Title: Modelling error compensation in nonlinear estimation problems
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The problem of using reduced order models in nonlinear estimation problems is considered. It is shown that inclusion of a non linear correction term permits reduction in the variance of errors of estimation without undue increase in the computational burden. Results are presented for both continuous and discrete time systems and are illustrated through numerical examples.
Name: ["Sinha A.K.", "Mahalanabis A.K."]

Title: Computer image processing techniques for automated breast thermogram interpretation
Abstract: The development of an inexpensive technique for automated interpretation of breast thermograms by computer has important implications for the mass screening of breast carcinoma. Success in disclosing the thermographic abnormality is demonstrated using three computer image processing techniques: (1) spatial signature analysis; (2) symmetry measurement using thermal density distributions; and (3) image coding by contour map data structure. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Winter J.", "Stein M.A."]

Title: ADAPTIVE OBSERVER FOR SINGLE-INPUT SINGLE-OUTPUT LINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: An adaptive observer has been demonstrated for single-input single-output systems with constant or slowly varying parameters. Work is currently underway to extend the observer to multivariable systems as well as systems with rapidly varying parameters and systems with noise. It is hoped that the adaptive observer will be eventually used not only for observing the state of an unknown system but in model reference problems and pole placement problems as well. 14 refs.
Name: ["Carroll Robert L.", "Lindorff D.P."]

Title: COMPUTATIONAL ALGORITHM FOR DESIGN OF REGULATORS FOR LINEAR JUMP PARAMETER SYSTEMS.
Abstract: An iterative algorithm is presented for finding the optimal feedback controller for a linear jump parameter system with state dependent transition probabilities. Conditions guaranteeing convergence are provided and two simple examples illustrate the application of the algorithm.
Name: ["Robinson V.G.", "Sworder D.D."]

Title: Control of Industrial Systems by On-Line Computers. | [ASSERVISSEMENT DE SYSTEMES INDUSTRIELS PAR ORDINATEUR ‚Ä≥ON LINE‚Ä≥ .]
Abstract: This paper treats direct closed-loop optimal and sub-optimal control of systems and industrial processes using the modern techniques of electronic, digital and analog theory. A method of reducing computational effort and information processing is proposed for a class of mathematical models. Finally, examples in the chemical and petrochemical industries are given.
Name: ["Kebir M."]

Title: AUTOMATIC INFORMATION EXTRACTION FOR LAND USE AND AGRICULTURAL APPLICATIONS.
Abstract: Some results at the Marshall Space Flight Center in interpretation technique development is summarized and related to applications areas, including land use mapping and agricultural survey and monitor. Comparison of automatic classification results with human photointerpretation indicates certain inadequacies due to reliance on spectral characteristics alone. Work in progress that attempts to account for the spatial properties of the imagery over local regions is described. In particular, the application of a fast template matching algorithm, employing the sequential similariy detection principle, to image registration, linear feature detection and the extraction and enumeration of scene objects, is discussed and illustrated.
Name: ["Bond A.D.", "Thomas D.T."]

Title: Unsupervised learning of the kalman filter
Abstract: It is the purpose of the letter to provide a short description of a general recursive method for learning the optimal stationary Kalman filter Kopt, when the plant and measurement noise covariance kernels, denoted by Q and R, respectively, are unknown. Experimental verification that confirms the theoretical expectations is presented. ¬© 1973, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hampton R.L.T."]
Keywords: ["filtering and prediction theory", "kalman filters", "filter kopt", "filter purpose", "experimental verification"]

Title: PROCESS OPTIMIZATION BY DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING.
Abstract: The technique of dynamic programming for process optimization is explained. The process being analyzed involves the design of a chemical plant to make a new product. The techniques of dynamic programming are used to reduce the number of computations necessary to determine the best decision policies that can be made for a set of operating conditions and constraints. Process description is followed by that of the design technique and a procedure to optimize profit is presented. Sensitivity analysis to evaluate the design at various operating conditions is explained.
Name: ["Morneau H.P.", "Biela J.A.", "Damaskos N.J."]

Title: Stimulation of Linear Time-Invariant Systems. | ZUR SIMULATION LINEARER ZEITINVARIANTER SYSTEME.
Abstract: Linear time-invariant continuous-time systems S represented by their canonical state equations are considered, and a general method of evaluating output samples gamma //k taken at T-second intervals is described. Given an arbitrary finite-dimensional linear space of input segments of duration T, it is shown that, for any input signal mu composed of segments from this space, the corresponding sequence of output samples gamma //k can be obtained as the output sequence of a linear time-invariant discrete-time system consisting of scalers, adders, and delay elements.
Name: ["Othmer Friedrich E."]

Title: Identifying an unknown process by utilizing randomly chosen inputs
Abstract: We investigated the problem of identifying the input-output relationship of an unknown deterministic process. In particular we investigated the problem of identifying solely on the basis of a finite number of input-output data pairs. Under this rather severe but realisitic limitation we have found identifications can be made by using randomly chosen inputs. Furthermore we have found that, if two conditions are met, then the input-output relationship can always be constructed and therefore identified by using randomly chosen inputs. One condition is that the unknown input-output relationship be contained in a class of functions such that any two functions of the class have equal outputs for only an input subset of measure zero. The other condition is that the class of functions be decomposable into a countable sequence of subclasses such that n + 1 input-output data pairs are sufficient for determining at most one member of the n-tb subclass. Classes of functions which meet these conditions include polynomial functions, roots of polynomial functions, roots of the sum of two polynomial functions, and the exponential functions that originate in diffusion or decay problems. Hopefully our results can be extended to problems having observational errors in the input-output data pairs. ¬© 1973 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Stalford H.", "Kullback J."]

Title: COMPLEX-ANALYTICAL PROCEDURE FOR DETERMINING THE SWITCHING INSTANTS IN TIME-OPTIMAL CONTROL OF LINEAR PLANT WITH DISTURBANCES.
Source: Bull Acad Pol Sci, Ser Sci Tech
Abstract: The minimum-time control problem for a single-input, single-output linear time invariant plant affected by a given external disturbance is considered. This disturbance is supposed to be defined as a function of time alone, and there are no restrictions concerning the place in which the disturbance affects the system. A complex-analytical procedure is proposed for determining the switching instants.
Name: ["Pelczewskie W.", "Lawrynowicz J."]

Title: STEPWISE APPROXIMATION OF A CONTINUOUS FUNCTION BY ITS MEAN VALUES DURING INTERVALS OF CONSTANT SIGN.
Source: Telecommunications and Radio Engineering (English translation of Elektrosvyaz and Radiotekhnika)
Abstract: In certain applications, such as the random and adaptive discretization of speech signals, data compression, or processing of experimental results, etc. , a continuous function has to be approximated by its mean values, determined during intervals where it has fixed sign. It is of theoretical and practical interest to assess the accuracy of such an approximation, on very general assumptions regarding the class of approximated function. The authors obtain an expression for the normalized mean square error, on the assumption that the initial function is the realization of a stationary random process, ergodic with respect to its autocorrelation.
Name: ["Nazarov M.V.", "Paramonov Yu.V."]

Title: ANGLE ERROR EXTRACTION FROM FFT PROCESSORS.
Source: IEEE Electron and Aerosp Syst Conv, Rec
Abstract: The application of fast Fourier transform (FFT) techniques to signal processing in tracking radars has led to the question of appropriate methods of extracting angle error information. For mono-pulse radars the answer is straightforward as it depends only on the relative amplitude of the target return in the various channels. For other types of radars, particularly those employing conical scan techniques, the introduction of a sampling or scanning frequency makes the solution less obvious. This paper describes two approaches to conical scan angle error extraction that make use of varying degrees of pre and post FFT processing.
Name: ["Sykes David F.", "Williams Lyle K."]

Title: Computer approaches to protein structure. VI. A multiple option model building program
Abstract: Conformation analysis of proteins is complicated by the presence of thousands of atoms which often are involved in multiple interactions. As a result, complete molecular models of proteins contain a relatively high information density. Computer graphics provides a means of controlling the flow of information by permitting the construction of large numbers of models containing different amounts of structural detail. The multiple option FORTRAN IV program described in this report permits the observer to focus on specific interactions and/or regions of a protein model with all or only specified amino acid side chains present on the backbone. The models can be readily translated, rotated, and adjusted in size, and constructed with specified visibility limits. Minor adjustments in the basic program provides complete families of stereoscopic pairs for three dimensional analysis of the models. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Tometsko A.M."]

Title: A Vocal Data Management System
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: This paper describes an implementation strategy for a vocal data management system (VDMS) being developed by the voice input/output project at the System Development Corporation. VDMS will accept connected speech of a language describable by 25‚Äì50 phrase equations and having a vocabulary of approximately 1000 words formed from about 100 data records. The strategy is based on the concept of predictive linguistic constraints (PLC). The present concepts of fixed directionality in parsing are replaced by a more generalized approach. To facilitate this flexibility, the system comprises a set of near-independent coroutines that are interconnected by a software busing structure. The VDMS acoustic processors verify the predictions. Very loose matching criteria are used for locating the predicted words. Special attention is given to word segments that are experimentally determined to be most invariant. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Barnett J."]

Title: The Influence of Glottal Waveform on the Naturalness of Speech from a Parallel Formant Synthesizer
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: A computer-simulated parallel formant synthesizer has been used to copy short samples of human speech. It is possible to make the synthetic speech almost indistinguishable from the natural in spectrum, waveform, and by earphone listening, provided that the synthetic glottal pulse is derived by inverse filtering a typical natural vowel from the same talker. Various other pulse shapes have been tried, such as the combination of cosine segments suggested by various workers as a close approximation to human glottal pulses. For producing speech acceptable as natural, none of these idealized pulse shapes has been as successful as those derived by inverse filtering. However, the subjective differences are small compared with the differences that would be caused by reverberation when listening to a loudspeaker in an ordinary room with good acoustics; it has been demonstrated that under such listening conditions, the phase structure of glottal pulses is of no importance. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Holmes J.N."]

Title: Suboptimal Algorithms for Nonlinear Smoothing
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: This paper presents second-order algorithms for fixed-point and fixed-lag smoothing problems for nonlinear systems. The algorithms are obtained on the basis of the state augmentation approach, used earlier by the authors, for dealing with linear smoothing problems. Both discrete- and continuous-time forms of solutions are presented and the results are illustrated by considering a radar tracking problem. Some of the advantages of the proposed smoothing solutions compared to existing ones are also discussed. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Biswas K.K.", "Mahalanabis A.K."]

Title: Optimal Tracking of Maneuvering Targets
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: Maneuvering target motion is modeled by introducing a binary random variable in the target state equation. The optimal estimate is shown to be a weighted combination of two Kalman filter estimates with weights depending on the likelihood ratio for the detection of a maneuver. A tracking scheme is proposed for maneuvering target tracking and illustrated in an example. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Thorp J.S."]

Title: A Comparison of Discrete Loinear Filtering Algorithms
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: Seven filter algorithms were presented in a recent survey paper [2], and were compared computationally (operations count) when relatively few observations were to be processed. These algorithms are elaborated further in this paper. Details of the computations are presented, and it is shown that for problems with even moderately large amounts of data, the information matrix and square-root information matrix formulations are computationally more efficient than the other methods considered (conventional Kalman, stabilized Kalman, and square-root covariance mechanizations). It is pointed out that Schmidt's matrix factorization-Householder transformation technique leads to the same equations as those obtained via Potter's method. Several improvements in the equation mechanization are given. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Bierman G.J."]

Title: Compensation of Constraint Effects in Control Systems by Means of Anticipating Correcting Elements - 1. | KOMPENSATION VON BESCHRAENKUNGSEFFEKTEN IN REGELUNGSSYSTEMEN DURCH ANTIZIPIERENDE KORREKTURGLIEDER - 1.
Abstract: In the design of technical control systems it is often necessary to take account of constraints as to bounded amplitude and rate of the control variable. It is well known that the optimal solution of these problems is given by application of the maximum principle of Pontryagin or dynamic programming. But, in general, these methods are too extensive for realization. Therefore, a great number of suboptimal but realizable design procedures have been derived. Different to these procedures, which aim at the complete design of a controller, this paper considers the problem when a controller is given which already fulfills the constraint of control amplitude limitation but which leads to unsatisfactory system behavior if an additional constraint on the control rate is introduced. First it is shown qualitatively that such disturbing limiting effects can be partially compensated by a special correcting element with anticipating behavior. Then an approximate technical realization of this anticipating correcting element is given. The compensating property of this correcting element is illustrated quantitatively for a system with const/s**2 plant. Finally, additional points are discussed.
Name: ["Kiendl H."]

Title: AUTOMATED HANDLING OF REMOTELY SENSED DATA BY THE CANADA CENTRE FOR REMOTE SENSING.
Abstract: A description is presented of the image processing system which consists of a PDP-10 CPU, 32K (36-bit word) memory, two 9-track, 1600 c. p. i. tape drives, console and other peripherals. The special hardware comprises a modified RCA 2 in. video tape recorder used for reading RBV video tapes and an Ampex 28-track 1 in. instrumentation recorder for playing back MSS data recorded at 10000 bits/inch/track. RBV data is corrected in the Radiometric-Geometric Correction Unit (RGCU); MSS data is deskewed, reformatted and radiometrically corrected in a special-purpose computer, the Multispectral Data Processor (MDP). Annotation and ephemeris data derived from NASA orbital prediction elements plus precomputed framing information are combined with MDP processed data in a special controller which directs two Electron Beam Recorders in the production of latent imagery on 70 mm film.
Name: ["Jager M.A."]

Title: Parsing algorithms with backtrack
Abstract: Two classes of restricted top-down parsing algorithms modeling "recursive descent" are considered. We show that the smaller class recognizes all deterministic context free languages, and that both classes can be simulated in linear time on a random access machine. Certain generalizations of these parsing algorithms are shown equivalent to the larger class. Finally, it is shown that the larger class has the property that loops and other "failures" can always be eliminated. ¬© 1973 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Birman A.", "Ullman J.D."]
Affiliations: ['IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center', 'Princeton University']

Title: APPROXIMATE PROBABILITY DENSITY FUNCTION OF RANGE AND ADJUSTED RANGE.
Abstract: Developing the general expression approximately for probability density function and probability distribution function for the random variable range of both the independent random normal variable and dependent random normal variable of the first and second order Markov linear model is presented. The mean, the variance, the skewness coefficient and the excess coefficient of the maximum range approximately obtained by the above method and applying the basic criteria set by Karl Pearson, the approximate probability density function of range is obtained as one of the best fitted from his family of curves.
Name: ["Sutabutr Prathet"]

Title: Discretizing dynamic programs
Source: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
Abstract: Discretizing certain discrete-time, uncountable-state dynamic programs such that the respective solutions to a sequence of discretized versions converge uniformly to the solution of the original problem is shown. Via a random perturbation device, we apply our general approach to a separable nonconvex program. ¬© 1973 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Fox B.L."]

Title: Diagnostic accuracy of a 15 lead hybrid computer aided electro cardiographic system
Abstract: An automated ECG system for multiple hospital data acquisition, on line interpretation, and interactive terminals has been developed. A hybrid system utilizing information from 12 and 3 lead ECGs is in operation in a busy teaching tertiary hospital. Of 4,019 ECGs examined by this method, 95% of important abnormal statements were correctly diagnosed. A hybrid logic system resulted in greater diagnostic accuracy for myocardial infarction and right bundle branch system block than 3 or 12 lead analysis alone. The 3 lead system gave the most satisfactory results for left ventricular hypertrophy and left bundle branch system block, and the 12 lead analysis was the most satisfactory for the diagnosis of ischemia, axis deviation and left anterior hemiblock. It is concluded that both 12 and 3 lead systems (and a combination of these systems) are essential for the computer aided diagnosis of ECGs.
Name: ["Talbot S.", "Dreifus L.S.", "Watanabe Y.", "Reich M.", "Chiang R.", "Morris K."]

Title: A neural system analysis of memory storage and retrieval
Abstract: Contends that from an information-processing viewpoint, memory can be subdivided into cue-access, short-term memory, and long-term memory storage and retrieval systems, which in turn are controlled by a number of operations, (e.g., match-mismatch, decay, and selective attention). Furthermore, it is assumed that specific neural substrates are maximally involved in the modulation of these specific processes essential to efficient mnemonic processing of information. Evidence is presented from previous studies to support this theoretical view of information processing. This evidence suggests that (a) the sensory systems and the cerebral cortex are critically involved in match-mismatch processing of information in the cue-access system, (b) the midbrain reticular formation and association cortex process information in the short-term memory system, and (c) the hippocampus is critically involved in consolidation and read-out of information in the long-term memory system. Evidence is also presented to suggest that after an initial preperceptual analysis information is transferred in parallel to the short-term and long-term memory systems, but that superimposed upon this parallel structure are sequential transfer processes (e.g., rehearsal). Name: ["Kesner R."]
Keywords: ["neural system analysis human information storage  retrieval", "memory systems", "analysis memory", "neural analysis", "term memory"]

Title: Markov model of learning: Length of the first run of incorrect responses
Source: Acta Universitatis Palackianae Olomucensis Facultatis Medicae
Abstract: In this paper the properties of the characteristic are studied, defined as the length of the first run of incorrect responses. The formulae for the probability distribution and the mean value of this characteristic have been derived, in the case of Nh and Sh model. The theoretical results were confronted with the empirical ones. Besides this, the formulae have been derived for the amount of information contained in the sample space of the studied characteristic and the comparison carried out with the amount of information contained in the nonreduced sample space of the original record. In this way, the eventual loss or gain of information can be evaluated resulting from the introduction of the studied characteristic of learning.
Name: ["Komenda S."]

Title: Identification automatique des parametres d'une loi theorique sur petit ordinateur: Application aux lois de distributions de probabilite d'intervalles entre potentiels d'action
Abstract: The authors describe a technique of parameter identification which expresses experimental curves by a theoretical law. They consider, as an example, distribution laws of intervals between neuronal spikes. The algorithm used was written in the assembler language PAL on a small computer PDP8 Digital Equipment. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Pernier J.", "Echallier J.F."]

Title: Computer reduction and analysis of neurophysiological data with special emphasis on evoked potential frequency analysis
Abstract: A hardware and software system is described for the acquisition, reduction and analysis of neurophysiological data. Application pertains to EEG and EEG-derived evoked potential records. Determination is made of frequency component information in the records using a Fast Fourier Transform algorithm. The frequency information is represented as power spectra estimates (PSE), which are later selected, averaged and input to a multivariate discriminant statiscal package. Control of the software system is made via remote terminal and acoustic coupler, allowing the use of off-site computer support. Sample results are provided. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Lewis G.W."]

Title: Identification of a pattern to depict displacements of man's centre of gravity | IDENTIFICATION D'UN MODELE REPRESENTANT LES DEPLACEMENTS DU CENTRE DE GRAVITE DE L'HOMME
Abstract: This paper introduces a new method for on line analysis of the movements of the inertia center of the body. A reliable data acquisition device is proposed. The processing method realizes the identification of a mathematical model of these displacements via Kalman filtering. The parameters of this model characterize the motions observed under some experimental conditions, and allow various interpretations.
Name: ["Gueguen C.", "Leroux J."]

Title: Triage: a logical algorithmic alternative to a non - system
Source: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians
Abstract: Triage, a process of sorting patlents and assigning priorities for medical care, relles on medical judgement. The process is an essential and continual function of any health care service though few have an orderly, medically rational system for accomplishing it. An alternative to non-systematic triage can be provided utilizing algorithms. An algorithm is a set of unamblguous step by step instructions applied to the performance of any specific task. When designed by physicians to insure medical valldity, algorithms can assist minimally trained personnel to perform a variety of tasks previously requiring skill in medical decision making. With the ald of a set of specially designed algorithms, 36 Red Cross volunteers, each with eight hours of instruction, were tralned to perform the triage function at the DeWitt Army Hospital. The system accomplishes the processes of sorting, designating, and assigning of prlorities to an entire unscheduled ambulatory patient population. Adherence to the rules and the steps in the algorithm, not medical decisions, are required of the volunteers. Data disclose that proper triage, including accumulation of Identification information, can be accomplished within two minutes in 45% of patients and within four minutes in 78%. Incidence of error was less than 1%. Application of algorithms to emergency medical triage is promising. ¬© 1973 American College of Emergency Physicians.
Name: ["Larsen Jr. K.T.", "Vickery D.M.", "Collis P.B.", "Folland E.D."]

Title: METHODS OF LOCAL IMPROVEMENT IN STOCHASTIC OPTIMIZATION PROBLEMS.
Abstract: The idea of the method of feasible directions is used to solve stochastic optimization problems with varying levels of initial indeterminacy. The concepts of variation in the space of random vectors and the evolution of their distribution densities, which is determined by the total probability formula, are introduced. These concepts are used to formulate rules for local improvement, successive application of which makes it possible to construct various algorithms for solving stochastic optimization problems. Examples are given.
Name: ["Tsypkin Ya.Z.", "Kaplinskiy A.I.", "Krasnenker A.S."]

Title: FEATURES OF PLANE SIMPLE LOOPS.
Abstract: A simple loop is very important in recognizing an object as a contour on the two-dimensional plane. It contains almost all problems encountered in the field of pattern recognition. This paper studies the feature vector which has a one-to-one correspondence with a simple loop on a given plane, and derives explicit expressions of its position, rotation, size and shape.
Name: ["Kitajima Hideo"]

Title: PERFORMANCE CRITERION AND NETWORK SYNTHESIS FOR OPTIMAL ADAPTIVE CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A performance criterion of a linearized control system is presented, and a connection is established between this criterion and the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial, and the rates of motion of the actuating element and of the system as a whole. Under given constraints on the transient performance, a digital-computer synthesis is carried out of the transfer function of a control system that minimizes the criterion. Network methods for synthesis of optimal (in the sense just mentioned) adaptive linearized control systems are proposed; by using the same approach, it is possible to solve with these methods the problem under consideration in classes of systems with constant adjustment of the controller, and also in self-adjusting systems and in systems of variable structure.
Name: ["Savkin M.I.", "Nikitina M.P."]

Title: Some Problems of Automation of Nuclear Power Plant Using General Purpose Computers and the Prospects of Development of Complex Control and Monitoring Systems. | NEKOTORYE VOPROSY AVTOMATIZATSII ATOMNYKH ELEKTROSTANTSII S PRIMENENIEM UVM I PERSPEKTIVY RAZVITIYA KOMPLEKSNYKH SISTEM UPRAVLENIYA I KONTROLYA.
Abstract: Problems of automation of nuclear power plants (NPP) with high-capacity channel reactors by means of the general purpose computer of the VNIIEM-3M type are considered. Brief characteristics of the system are presented and the specific features of the design and technological base as well as problems of ensuring reliability are discussed. The importance of an integrated approach to the problem of automation of nuclear power plants and up-to-date development of algorithms and software for a system using a general purpose computer is pointed out. The need for setting up an integrated digital-analog and physical test model of a NPP for developing algorithms and elements of an automated control system is noted. The ways for developing NPP automation, using a third-generation computer as the controlling machine in a closed system of control, are analyzed.
Name: ["Adas'ko V.I.", "Kalashnikov V.K.", "Proferansov Yu.D.", "Tanaev M.Ya.", "Urusov I.D."]

Title: CONVERGENCE OF OPTIMUM-TRIAL RANDOM-SEARCH ALGORITHM.
Abstract: The convergence conditions for an optimum-trial algorithm are found in a situation with limited noise and with no noise. In the absence of noise, asymptotic estimates for the rate of convergence to the greatest value are obtained for the linear, central, and quadratic models. It is shown that the optimum-trial algorithm does not converge in the case of unlimited noise, and therefore it should not be used in such cases. 3 refs.
Name: ["Vaisbord Z.M.", "Rastrigin L.A.", "Rubinshtein Ya.S."]

Title: APPROXIMATING PRE-EMPTIVE PRIORITY DISPATCHING IN A MULTIPROGRAMMING MODEL.
Source: IBM Journal of Research and Development
Abstract: The formulation of the closed queueing network model of a multiprogramming computer system is generalized to allow each task to have its own set of facility service rates and I/O device selection probability distribution. In the model, processor sharing is assumed for different types of customers. It is shown through a series of investigations that the model reasonably approximates pre-emptive priority dispatching.
Name: ["Anderson Jr. H.A."]

Title: Sufficient Statistics and Reproducing Densities in Simultaneous Sequential Detection and Estimation
Abstract: -The doubly-compound hypothesis detection problem with finite-dimensional parameter vectors is treated in a general context. It is shown that estimation and detection occur simultaneously, with the detector using the a posteriori densities generated by two separate estimators, one for each hypothesis. No assumptions are made on the estimation criterion and very loose assumptions on the detection criterion. If sufficient statistics and hence natural conjugate densities exist for the unknown parameters, the procedure is quite tractable. In this case, the optimal detector partitions in such a way that the primary processing can be done without knowledge of the a priori parameter distributions. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Birdsall T.G.", "Gobien J.O."]

Title: On the distributed parameter least-squares state estimation theory
Abstract: Some results concerning the state estimation problem of distributed-parameter systems corrupted by white, in time, stochastic disturbances and noises are presented. The least-squares technique is adopted throughout. First, the Gauss-Markov theorem is extended to the distributed-parameter ease and a dynamic estimator is derived governing the minimal variance linear unbiased estimate of the state of the system at hand. Second, the innovations approach to least-squares estimation is invoked and the filtering, fixed-interval, fixed-point, and fixed-lag smoothing problems are studied and solved. Finally, the stability properties of the optimal filter derived are studied by employing the controllability and observability properties of the system under consideration. The results of the paper provide new tools for dealing with distributed data, thus substantially enlarging the existing distributed-parameter estimation theory. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.

Title: Adaptive Channel Memory Truncation for Maximum Likelihood Sequence Estimation
Abstract: Maximum likelihood data sequence estimation, implemented by a dynamic programming algorithm known as the Viterbi algorithm (VA), is of considerable interest for data transmission in the presence of severe intersymbol interference and additive Gaussian noise. Unfortunately, the required number of receiver operations per data symbol is an exponential function of the duration of the channel impulse response, resulting in unacceptably large receiver complexity for high‚Äêspeed PAM data transmission on many channels. We propose a linear prefilter to force the overall impulse response of the channel/prefilter combination to approximate a desired truncated impulse response (DIR) of acceptably short duration. Given the duration of the DIR, the prefilter parameters and the DIR itself can be optimized adaptively to minimize the mean‚Äêsquare error between the output of the prefilter and the desired prefilter output, while constraining the energy in the DIR to be fixed. In this work we show that the minimum mean‚Äêsquare error can be expressed as the minimum eigenvalue of a certain channel‚Äêdependent matrix, and that the corresponding eigenvector represents the optimum DIR. An adaptive algorithm is developed and successfully tested. The simulations also show that the prefiltering scheme, used together with the VA for two different channel models, compares favorably in performance with another recently proposed prefiltering scheme. Limiting results for the case where the prefilter is considered to be of infinite length are obtained; it is shown that the optimum DIR of length two must be one of two possible impulse responses related to the duobinary impulse response. Finally we obtain limiting results for the case where the transmitting filter is optimized. ¬© 1973 The Bell System Technical Journal
Name: ["Falconer D.D.", "Magee F.R., Jr."]

Title: Some Characteristic Features of Digital Computer Modeling of Daily Graphs of Utility Loads by the Statistical Load Method. | O NEKOTORYKH OSOBENNOSTYAKH MODELIROVANIYA NA TsVM SUTOCHNYKH GRAFIKOV KOMMUNAL'NO-BYTOVOI NAGRUZKI METODOM STATISTICHESKIKH ISPYTANII.
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenij i Energeticheskikh Ob''edinenij Sng. Energetika
Abstract: It is shown that when the statistical test method is used for digital modeling of daily graphs of utility loads, special limitations should be introduced to exclude some graphs which do not correspond to actual conditions. Probability characteristics of the random process of change in the reactive capacity of the utility load are revealed. Also, the correlation bond between the random values of the active and reactive load capacities is clarified. The statistical test method is used to obtain probability characteristics of future loads.
Name: ["Soldatkina L.A.", "Fokin Yu.A.", "Abu El'-Kheir M.Kh."]

Title: On the Sensitivity of a Fixed-Point Smoothing Algorithm
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: This paper presents a simple approach to the derivation of sensitivity measures of smoothing algorithms. It is proposed that the known sensitivity results of the Kalman filtering algorithm be utilized along with the state augmentation approach for this purpose. The sensitivity measures so obtained are easier to compute than the ones available in the literature. It is then shown that the fixed-point smoothing algorithm, derived recently by Biswas and Mahalanabis [1], [2], is less sensitive to model parameter variations than the algorithm studied by Griffin and Sage [7], [8]. The case of a satellite tracking problem is presented by way of illustrating the results. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Sinha A.K.", "Mahalanabis A.K."]

Title: Statistically-Optimum Dynamic Server Assignment in Systems with Interfering Servers
Abstract: Cellular mobile radio systems have been proposed that use many base stations to provide radio service over a large geographical area. In such systems, a stored-program processor assigns radio channels to base stations in real time, under certain interference constraints. The capacity and the queueing characteristics of the overall system are strongly dependent on the processor algorithms that are used. This paper presents three algorithms which are in a certain minimax sense statistically optimum. The procedures are quite general, and may be applied to any system that employs many servers, the use of some combinations of which is not allowed. The first algorithm provides for the preferential assignment of a ‚Äústandard‚Äù channel. If all standard channels are busy, a ‚Äúnonstandard‚Äù channel is selected in such a manner that the probability of blocking is minimized in that interferable facility most likely to suffer blocking. The second algorithm provides for the transfer of service from nonstandard to standard channels whenever standard channels become free. The choice of the particular nonstandard channel to be freed is again made in a manner which minimizes the maximum probability of future blockage. The third algorithm provides for the rearrangement of channel assignments in those instances when all assignable channels, both standard and nonstandard, are busy. Such rearrangement can cause channels to become available under certain circumstances. If more than one rearrangement is possible, again the choice of what particular action should be taken is governed by the goal of minimizing the maximum probability of future blockage. All three algorithms attain short-term optimality by enumeration; that is, each candidate for assignment is considered in turn. Under the condition that the given candidate is selected, the conditional probability of future blocking in each of the server groups is calculated, and the maximum of these probabilities is associated with the candidate. After all candidates have been considered, that candidate which has the minimum associated probability is assigned. These algorithms produce, by definition, an instantaneous system state which is always optimum in the above minimax sense. In systems with large numbers of servers, the system changes state rapidly; thus, occasional short-term errors disappear rapidly, and short-term optimization tends to lead to peak performance in the long term as well. Title: RECOGNITION SYSTEMS WITH PREDICTION PATTERNS FOR SIGNAL DETECTION IN RANDOM NOISE.
Abstract: Signal detection in random noise is considered in the case of an algorithm using recognition systems with prediction patterns. The effectiveness of this algorithm is illustrated by examples of detection of deterministic signals. With a comparative analysis of error probabilities it is shown that the proposed method improves detection performance.

Title: APPROXIMATE QUEUEING MODELS FOR MULTIPROGRAMMING COMPUTER SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The approximation consists of replacing the computer system by a single server with a varying service rate that equals the reciprocal of the steady-state expected cycle time of a closed system processing the same number of jobs. This approximate model was compared to the exact result for some simple cases and found to have small relative errors.
Name: ["Avi-Itzhak B.", "Heyman D.P."]

Title: GMDH ALGORITHM FOR SYNTHESIS OF MULTIPLICATIVE MODELS OF COMPLEX SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The regression equation obtained with the aid of GMDH algorithms can be constructed based on various reference functions. Partial descriptions, or trends, are regression equations in each independent variable. There exists a GMDH algorithm with successive separation of trends for which the complete description is the sum of the latter. In this paper, the authors propose a GMDH algorithm in which the complete description is obtained in the form of a product of trends. This algorithm uses orthogonal Chebyshev polynomials. The so-called generalized GMDH algorithm comprises both these algorithms, since it uses both summation and multiplication of trends.
Name: ["Ivakhnenko A.G.", "Deleur Ye.G.", "Yaremenko A.G.", "Patereu S.G.", "Todua M.M."]

Title: ADAPTIVE LEARNING ALGORITHM FOR STATISTICAL PROCESSING OF MEASUREMENTS.
Abstract: The problem of how to arrive at statistical estimates of the performance parameters of a spacecraft and of outer-space variables on the basis of indirect autocorrelated measurements uder a priori indeterminateness conditions is solved. A suboptimal algorithm (within the framework of correlation theory) for processing measurement information is derived. Recurrent procedures for the adaptive algorithm are worked out by correcting the first two moments of the distribution of the parameters and of the correlation matrices of the errors in each channel of the measurements to be processed on the basis of experimental data from successive runs of measurements.
Name: ["Sukhoruchenkov B.I."]

Title: Sequential Estimation of Kinematic Flight Parameters from Radar Data. | SEQUENTIELLE SCHAETZUNG KINEMATISCHER FLUGPARAMETER AUS RADARDATEN.
Abstract: Starting from a general tracking algorithm (Kalman Filter), the class of dynamic target models is extended to cover also stronger correlated modes of target motions. In order to get more precise estimations of kinematic target parameters at times when this can be achieved, a sequential decision procedure is used to solve some divergence problems with mismatched filters. The transient behavior and the decision accuracy can be definitely improved by this technique, which can be easily implemented and described, especially in the case of phased array radars. Numerical examples and theoretical limits of estimation and decision accuracy are given.
Name: ["van Keuk G."]

Title: Comments on ‚ÄúLyapunov Functions for Quadratic Differential Equations with Applications to Adaptive Control‚Äù
Abstract: The adaptation laws existing in known model reference systems are shown to be unfavorably determined by the underlying basic structure. Simulation results are also given, which demonstrate that the adaptivity itself can be limited, if not missing, when the chosen structure implies stability domain restrictions. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Devaud F.", "Caron J.-Y."]

Title: APPROXIMATE CONTROLLER SYNTHESIS METHOD IN THE CASE OF A CONSTRAINED CONTROL PARAMETER.
Abstract: An approximate method is described for analytic design of controllers when the control parameter is subject to a saturation-type constraint. The method is based on dynamic programming and does not require checking the continuity of Lyapunov's function.
Name: ["Kudin V.F."]

Title: Optimal Random Sample Search Methods for the Implementation of Data Systems by Means of Orthogonal Lists - 1. The Implementation of Data Systems by Means of Orthagonal Lists.
Abstract: The applicability of orthogonal list-like organization methods for one-dimensional data structures is shown and advantages are pointed out. Sample search methods for orthogonal lists are developed.
Name: ["Janko W."]

Title: Clustering Using a Similarity Measure Based on Shared Near Neighbors
Abstract: A nonparametric clustering technique incorporating the concept of similarity based on the sharing of near neighbors is presented. In addition to being an essentially parallel approach, the computational elegance of the method is such that the scheme is applicable to a wide class of practical problems involving large sample size and high dimensionality. No attempt is made to show how a priori problem knowledge can be introduced into the procedure. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Jarvis R.A."]

Title: Application of Pattern Recognition to Steady-State Security Evaluation in a Power System
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: Power system operation is outlined and system security is defined. The need for security evaluation in power system operation is discussed, and the evaluation is presented as a pattern recognition problem. A suitable straightforward and quick procedure is used to select a small number of variables as features from a large set of variables which are normally available in power systems. Comparison is made on the security classification performances of a number of different types of classifiers. The training of classifiers is carried out by a search algorithm which seeks to minimize the number of classification errors. The procedure to determine the security functions (classifiers) is illustrated by an example, and simulation results on the steady-state security of the CIGRE 225-kV system show that the pattern recognition approach to security evaluation is encouraging. Some uses of security functions in the control and operation of power systems are outlined. The effect of many of these uses cannot be achieved as easily by other existing methods. Finally, some of the problems associated with the application of pattern recognition to power system security evaluation are discussed. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Pang C.K.", "Koivo A.J.", "El-Abiad A.H."]

Title: DESIGN OF DYNAMICAL AND CONTROL SYSTEMS BY THE METHOD OF INEQUALITIES.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: In the design of dynamical systems, such as automatic regulators and electrical networks, a system is required to satisfy constraints and specifications, which can be represented by a set of simultaneous algebraic inequalities. It is shown how typical design problems lead naturally to the formulation of a set of inequalities, any solution of which characterizes an acceptable system. A numerical process for obtaining a solution of a system of inequalities is developed. Applications of the method of inequalities to the design of automatic control systems are discussed. Specific control problems, in single-variable and multivariable systems, are considered, and designs, obtained by methods of inequalities, are compared with those obtained by standard methods of Nyquist, root locus and optimization.
Name: ["Zakian V.", "Al-Naib U."]

Title: Two-Step Encoding for Finite Sources
Abstract: Any finite information source is given a graph structure, in which two vertices are adjacent whenever the two corresponding source letters are distinguishable by the coder-decoder pair. Usual sources correspond, therefore, to complete graphs. If the associated graph is not complete, however, an e-code for the source can be constructed in two steps: in the first, distinct codewords are given to distinguishable letters only; in the second step, a similar encoding is carried out for the complementary graph, in which distinguishable letters become indistinguishable and the converse. A particularly simple case shows up when nonadjacency is an equivalence relation among the vertices of the graph: each class of nondistinguishable letters can then be considered as a letter in a coarser source alphabet. The two-step procedure is then particularly intuitive. A problem arises when this procedure does not destroy optimality of the resulting a-code; some partial results are given in this direction. The results obtained are largely based on some graph-theoretical ideas and tools. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Longo G.", "Korner J."]
Affiliations: ["Istituto di Elettrotecnica e di Elettronica dell'Universit√† di Trieste"]

Title: Enforcement Policies for Parking Regulations
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: Effective enforcement of no-parking regulations is essential in urban areas. A probabilistic finite-state machine model that relates enforcement to expected levels of compliance is developed, and its simulation results are shown to agree with experimental data. The effects of deterministic and random enforcement policies are described, and a class of implementable policies that yield satisfactory results is analyzed. Finally, these results are used to determine schedules and routes for enforcement officers that increase their effectiveness. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Tartarone S.", "Levis A.H."]

Title: Mathematics of Fuzzy Systems. | [MATEMATYKA TWOROW NIEWYRAZNYCH.]
Abstract: Research associated with the attempts to extend notions of set theory to sets with fuzzy components is discussed, along with the possibility of applying these sets in technical sciences. A distinctive feature of such sets is a so-called membership function ascribing to each element a certain degree of membership in the set. Reference is made to fuzzy logic which makes use of the logical value notion that may be different from truth and falsehood. Attention is directed to fuzzy algorithms, i. e. to inaccurate action instructions, and to the attempts of programming such instructions, and to the attempts of programming such instructions for digital computers.
Name: ["Wajs Karol"]

Title: CONCAVE MINIMIZATION OVER A CONVEX POLYHEDRON.
Abstract: A general algorithm is developed for minimizing a well defined concave function over a convex polyhedron. The algorithm is basically a branch and bound techniue which utilizes a special cutting plane procedure to identify the global minimum extreme point of the convex polyhedron. The indicated cutting plane method is based on F. Glover's general theory for constructing legitimate cuts to identify certain points in a given convex polyhedron. It is shown that the crux of the algorithm is the development of a linear underestimator for the constrained concave objective function. Applications of the algorithm to the fixed-charge problem, the separable concave programming problem, the quadratic problem, and the 0-1 mixed integer problem are discussed. Computer results for the fixed-charge problem are also presented.
Name: ["Taha Hamdy A."]

Title: Hybrid Sparse-Matrix Methods
Abstract: In computer-aided design for large systems, the efficient solution of large sparse systems of linear equations is important. We critically examine two parts of the solution of sparse systems of linear equations: ordering and the factorization of the ordered matrix. After examining several candidates from a theoretical point of view, as well as with examples, we conclude that the Markowitz ordering criteria, with extension for the variability-type problem, is the most practical ordering algorithm. A combination of solution processes provides a very efficient hybrid algorithm for factoring the ordered sparse matrix. The hybrid is outlined so that it may be tailored to minimum storage utilization, minimum central processing unit (CPU) time, or may be built entirely in a high-level language to reduce programming time. A number of examples are included. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Dembart B.", "Erisman A.M."]

Title: DIGITAL CONTROL ALGORITHMS - 2. KALMAN ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: Common practice in the process industries is to use the discrete equivalent of the three-mode proportional-plus-integral-plus-derivative (PID) controller for digital feedback loops. A number of unique discrete algorithms have also been developed. The Kalman algorithm is considered in this article, which is the second in a series comparing the performance of several discrete algorithms with three mode control, for a process in which time constants rather than dead times dominate.
Name: ["Chiu Kuo-Ching", "Corripio Armando B.", "Smith Cecil L."]

Title: Example of a Nonlinear Model-Following Control System. | [EIN BEISPIEL FUER EINE NICHTLINEARE MODELLFOLGEREGELUNG.]
Abstract: Similar to the linear case, the concept of model following control can be used to advantage with nonlinear plants. The application of this method with respect to a modification of the dynamic response of an airplane's longitudinal motion is discussed from a theoretical point of view. Details about the realization of the computer algorithm are given.
Name: ["Kienzle E.", "Schmidt G."]

Title: HOW TO APPLY DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING AND NONLINEAR RECURRENT FILTRATION TO ESTIMATES OF THE SPACE-VEHICLE STATE VECTOR.
Abstract: The Bayes criterion is employed to show that estimating the state vector of a space vehicle reduces, in the general case, to solving a set of nonlinear two-point boundary problems. Equations for estimating nonlinear recurrent filtration, derived through the dynamic programming method and a direct approach to solving nonlinear two-point boundary problems within the framework of the nonlinear theory, are cited. The estimating equations so derived are distinguished by great generality, and correspond most closely to the initial optimality criteria.
Name: ["Nevol'ko M.P.", "Kainov A.F."]

Title: METHOD OF INSTRUMENTATION OF INFORMATION RETRIEVAL AT LOCAL LEVEL.
Abstract: A heirarchical principle of design of information-retrieval systems is considered, and an example is presented of instrumentation of a system at the local level.
Name: ["Mirpayazov U.M.", "Skuridin V.P."]

Title: Analysis of Multimodal Systems
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: The estimation of a multimodal linear system whose mode-to-mode transitions are described by a finite-state Markov chain is described. The problem has application in studying separation standards in an air traffic control environment. An optimal solution is formulated which is computationally infeasible. A suboptimal estimator is then derived which closely approximates the optimal estimator. An example is presented to illustrate the technique. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Bruckner J.M.H.", "Ronald W.S.", "Rea F.G."]

Title: A Parser-Generating System for Constructing Compressed Compilers
Abstract: This paper describes a parser-generating system (PGS) currently in use on the CDC-6500 computer at Purdue University. The PGS is a Fortran-coded program that accepts a translation grammar as input and constructs from it a compact, machine-coded compiler. In the input translation grammar, each BNF syntactic rule corresponds to a (possibly empty) ‚Äúcode generator‚Äù realizable as an assembly language, Fortran or Algol, subroutine that is called whenever that syntactic rule is applied in the parse of a program. Typical one-pass compilers constructed by the PGS translate source programs at speeds approaching 14,000 cards per minute. For an XPL compiler, the parser program and its tables currently occupy 288 words of 60-bit core memory of which 140 words are parsing table entries and 82 words are links to code generators. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Mickunas M.D.", "Schneider V.B."]

Title: CONTENT-ADDRESSABLE MEMORIES BASED ON MAGNETIC-DOMAIN LOGIC.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: The implementation of logic into magnetic-bubble memories, and particularly the realization of a content-addressable storage is proposed. The basic bubble-interactive logic and flip-flop functions are reviewed. The most suitable memory structure is discussed, along with the logical requirements for content addressing. Two cellular bubble logic-in-memory arrays and their operation modes are described. One employs successive, the other simultaneous, data access. A comparison between these two designs and a similarly structured random-access bubble memory device is given with special consideration for bit packaging density, interface terminals and data-access time.
Name: ["Kluge W."]

Title: Some New Algorithms for Recursive Estimation in Constant Linear Systems
Abstract: Recursive least-squares estimates for processes that can be generated from finite-dimensional linear systems are usually obtained via an n √ó n matrix Riccati differential equation, where n is the dimension of the state space. In general, this requires the solution of n(n + 1)/2 simultaneous nonlinear differential equations. For constant parameter systems, we present some new algorithms that in several cases require only the solution of less than 2np or n(m + p) simultaneous nonlinear differential equations, where m and p are the dimensions of the input and observation processes, respectively. These differential equations are said to be of Chandrasekhar type, because they are similar to certain equations introduced in 1948 by the astrophysicist S. Chandrasekhar, to solve finite-interval Wiener-Hopf equations arising in radiative transfer. Our algorithms yield the gain matrix for the Kalman filter directly without having to solve separately for the error-covariance matrix and potentially have other computational benefits. The simple method used to derive them also suggests various extensions, for example, to the solution of nonsymmetric Riccati equations. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Kailath T."]

Title: MULTISERVER COMPUTER-CONTROLLED QUEUING SYSTEM WITH PRE-EMPTIVE PRIORITIES AND FEEDBACK.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: A multiserver computer-controlled queueing system with pre-emptive priorities and feedback was investigated. A formula for the generating function of the state probabilities of the system is derived and a method using the transition probabilities of a Markov chain for determining the first waiting-time distribuion in the system is presented.
Name: ["Chan W.C.", "Chung W.K.", "Maa D.Y."]

Title: Compensation of Time Lags and Nonlinearities in Automatic Control Systems. | [KOMPENSATSIYA INERTSIONNOSTEI I NELINEINOSTEI V AVTOMATICHESKIKH SISTEMAKH UPRAVLENIYA.]
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenij i Energeticheskikh Ob''edinenij Sng. Energetika
Abstract: A graphic method of synthesis of multi-link regulators for the compensation of time lags and nonlinearities in automatic control systems is presented. It is shown that the general system, compensation regulator - nonlinear inertial system, is able to pass input signals of any form (without a stepwise change of the signal) along the control action channel, without form distortion and without time shift. The method is illustrated by the example of the synthesis of a regulator for the compensation of time lags and nonlinearities in a third order system.
Name: ["Basharin A.V.", "Vyaznikov L.A."]

Title: SYNTAX DIRECTED COMPILER.
Abstract: The general design of a compiler is described that is arranged to compile sequences of statements of a high-level machine-dependent language, for generating sequences of object code for the operation of a specific machine.
Name: ["McNabb D.L.", "Walters Jr. J.R."]

Title: Compilation Techniques for Recognition of Parallel Processable Tasks in Arithmetic Expressions
Abstract: With the developments of parallel computer systems, the techniques for the recognition and representation of parallel task streams in a job (program) have become important to enhance the system performance. This paper makes a survey of the previous techniques for the recognition and representation of parallelism within an arithmetic expression and introduces some new techniques. The techniques are classified into three categories: 1) precedent-dependent method; 2) syntax-dependent method; and 3) Polish string-dependent method. This classification is made on the basis of the characteristics of the recognition method. An analysis is also made on them. The advantages and disadvantages of these techniques are discussed. A new technique introduces a procedure, which generates a homogeneous tree with the minimum path length of a specified degree k. The technique is particularly important for large machines that require more than two operands at a time for an arithmetic operation. Another new technique introduced recognizes parallelism within an expression and tests ‚Äúwell formation‚Äù completely in only one pass. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Ramamoorthy C.V.", "Park J.H.", "Li H.F."]
Keywords: ["explicit approach", "form parallelism parse tree polish string recursion", "maximum parallel", "well formation", "parallel task"]

Title: COMPUTER-BASED DISPLAY OF NONDESTRUCTIVE EVALUATION DATA.
Abstract: This paper discusses techniques developed to reduce large amounts of data acquired by automated or semiautomated digital acquisition systems. These techniques include: 1) Automatic generation of three-dimensional plots of characteristics over large surface areas. 2) Contour plotting of significant gradients in data. 3) Use of color to supplement digital enhancement techniques. 4) Multisectioned plots of large bodies to show internal flaw areas.
Name: ["Stiefeld Bernard"]

Title: Utilization of Reliability Measurements in Bayesian Inference: Models and Human Performance
Abstract: Anormative 2-stage model for incorporating reliability measurements of data-reporting sources in a Bayesian inference system is presented. An experiment required human subjects to make intuitive inferences about two hypotheses on the basis of sample data which were reported with a given reliability. When compared with the optimal model, subjects exhibited systematic errors in estimating the diagnostic impact of less than perfectly reliable data. Their responses reflected the use of specific nonoptimal heuristic strategies to process the information. A utility function was added to the normative model to illustrate how a best choice might be made from among potential data-gathering experiments whose costs increase with their reliabilities. Recommendations for using computer aids to enhance efficiency in inference systems are made. ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers. Inc.
Name: ["Johnson E.M.", "Cavanagh R.C.", "Spooner R.L.", "Samet M.G."]
Affiliations: ['U.S. Army Research Institute for the Behavioral and Social Sciences', ' Inc.', 'Office of Naval Research', ' Inc.']

Title: SELF-LEARNING OF FINITE-MIXTURE DISTRIBUTIONS BY STOCHASTIC APPROXIMATION METHOD.
Abstract: This paper discusses a system for learning a finite-mixture distribution of patterns. The analysis is based on the stochastic approximation by which the optimal parameter of the cumulative distribution function is estimated. The learning system proposed in this paper produces several minimal solutions. However, it is proved that parameter vectors successively derived converge to one of these minimal solutions. The proof is based on Devyaterikov's concept. The learning system enables one to learn the recognition function of patterns without supervisors.
Name: ["Isomichi Yoshinori"]

Title: TIME-SHARING COMPUTER PROGRAM FOR THE SOLUTION OF THE MULTIPLE CRITERIA PROBLEM.
Abstract: This article describes a time-sharing computer program written to implement a man-machine interactive algorithm for the solution of the multiple criteria problem. A unique feature of this program is the man-machine dialog which obtains information from the decision-maker through a series of simple, ordinal comparisons.
Name: ["Dyer James S."]

Title: CONSIDERATION ON SYSTEM DIAGNOSIS.
Abstract: This paper describes the fault diagnosis of a system represented by the equivalent SEC-graph. In particular, the author investigates the system diagnosis by means of test S-gates. Consideration is first given to the algorithm for obtaining the set V of vertices under which the faulty vertex can be distinguished uniquely. An algorithm is then presented for a nearly optimum set of vertices, which is an approximate solution. This algorithm is shown to be effective for large-scale systems and to be easily programmed.
Name: ["Yamamoto Masaru"]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF AN OBJECT IN THE CASE OF OPTIMAL CONTROL WITH INCOMPLETE INFORMATION.
