Abstract: A procedure is proposed for identification of an object in the case of optimal control with incomplete information. A theorem is given establishing the form of the design matrix and to avoid transforming the target function.
Name: ["Adler Yu.P.", "Talalay A.M."]

Title: TOPOLOGICAL PROPERTIES IN DIGITIZED BINARY PICTURES.
Abstract: Two features of digitized binary pictures - connectivity number (CN) and coefficient of curvature (CC) - are defined and various topological properties of pictures are derived using them. The basic properties of the NC and CC and the relation among these features and the genus of pictures are considered. The algorithm for shrinking a picture is given and the correctness of the algorithm is proved. The properties of shrunk pictures (called shrunk skeletons) are derived. As an application of this algorithm, a new thinning algorithm is given. The method adopted based entirely on arithmetical treatment and differs from those previously reported in the literature. An algorithm for border following is given and properties of the CN and CC with respect to border following are presented.
Name: ["Yokoi Shigeki", "Toriwaki Jun-ichiro", "Fukumura Teruo"]

Title: DECOMPOSITION OF MULTIVALUED SWITCHING FUNCTIONS AND ITS APPLICATION TO THRESHOLD NETWORKS.
Abstract: This paper proposes a method for realization of three-valued switching functions by networks of minimal ternary threshold gates. First, theoretical aspects of the decomposition of an arbitrary multivalued switching function are described in terms of several simpler component switching functions. Then, on the basis of theorems given in the first part, the method is described and illustrative examples are given for its application.
Name: ["Mine Hisashi", "Fujita Shiro"]

Title: STATISTICAL APPROACH TO THE PROBLEM OF MAXIMIZING A FUNCTION.
Abstract: A study is made of a statistical method of optimizing a function, with allowance for a restriction on the number of possible meaurements of the function being optimized. The method of dynamic programming is used to derive recursion relations for determining the optimal points of measurement of the function. An approximate realization of the optimization method is worked out. An example is given of application of the method proposed, which indicates its efficiency in comparison with the method of stochastic approximation.
Name: ["Aleksandrov V.M.", "Batkov A.M.", "Poreshin P.P."]

Title: SYSTEM DIAGNOSIS BY MEANS OF OUTPUT BLOCKING AND RECOVERING GATES.
Abstract: Graph theory has been applied actively to system diagnosis. This paper proposes output blocking and recovering gates (OBR gates) which block fault signals and recover them to normal signals; also discussed are their basic properties used for system diagnosis. The blocking and recovering states (BR states) of OBR gates and the blocking and recovering cutsets (BR cutsets) are described. The relation between the cover of all edges in graphs by BR cutsets and distinguishability of pairs of vertices is discussed. It is proved that a system is always 1-distinguishable by use of proper pairs of OBR gates.
Name: ["Nakano Hideo", "Nakanishi Yoshiro"]

Title: NETWORK PLANNING ALGORITHM FOR OPERATIONS OF VARIABLE INTENSITY.
Abstract: A dynamic network planning problem is considered that requires allocation of limited flows of (storable and unstorable) resources in such a way that the execution time of the operations is minimal. It is assumed that some of the operations can be interrupted, that all operations can be executed with variable intensity, and that they require several types of resources. It is proposed to solve the problem using an algorithm based on priority rules. Together with the conventional heuristic priority rules, the algorithm uses also a new form of dynamic priority, based on the maximum principle.
Name: ["Zimin I.N."]

Title: Efficient Ordering of Set Expressions for Symbolic Expansion
Abstract: This paper gives an algorithm for efficiently ordering the terms and factors of a set (or Boolean) expression so that the work required for the symbolic expansion of the expression according to the distributive law is minimized. Formulas are given for computing the measure of work associated with any ordering of an expression. It is shown from these formulas that reordering the factors of the intersections can possibly reduce the cost of expansion, but this cost is invariant with respect to the ordering of the terms of the unions. A simple ordering algorithm is given for quickly determining an optimal (not necessarily unique) ordering of an intersection and a union. When this algorithm is applied to all intersections and unions in an expression, the resulting order is shown to minimize the total work over all possible orderings. Thus it is easy to establish an optimal ordering for an expression and estimate the machine time for its symbolic expansion before doing the expansion. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Worrell R.B.", "Hulme B.L."]
Affiliations: [' Assurance Studms Division', ' Numerical Analysis Division']

Title: The Solvability of the Decision Problem for Classes of Proper Formulas and Related Results
Abstract: In connection with the development of an actual question-answering system, the Relational Data File of The Rand Corporation, a class of formulas of the predicate calculus, the definite formulas of Kuhns, was proposed as the class of symbolic representations of the ‚Äúreasonable‚Äù questions to put to this retrieval system. Roughly speaking, the definite formulas are those formulas F such that the set of true substitution instances of F in a finite interpretation I are preserved on passage to a certain special extension I‚Ä≤ of I. The proper formulas are those definite formulas which are supposedly especially suitable for machine processing. It has previously been shown by the author that the decision problem for the class of definite formulas is recursively unsolvable. In this paper, however, it is shown that the decision problem for various classes of proper formulas is solvable. Thus, for each of these classes there is a mechanical procedure to decide of an arbitrary formula whether it is a member of the class. It follows that for each of these classes there is no effective transformation @@@@ which takes an arbitrary definite formula F into a proper equivalent @@@@(F). In addition, it is shown that the decision problems for a number of classes of formulas which bear a structural similarity to any class of proper formulas are recursively unsolvable. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Di Paola R.A."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF AN INFORMATIONAL SYSTEM.
Abstract: An examination is made of the problem of determining the minimum number of measuring devices necessary for ensuring a given quality of control of a technological object. By an information-theoretic approach, this problem is reduced to the standard nonlinear programming problem. A method is described of analyzing a synthesized informational system, for the realization of which there is proposed a recursion algorithm for estimation of the informational connection of two signals.
Name: ["Mamayev D.D.", "Svechinskiy V.B."]

Title: ESTIMATION OF THE NUMBER OF EXCURSIONS OF A RANDOM PROCESS FROM DISCRETE READINGS OF A MIXTURE OF THE PROCESS WITH NOISE.
Abstract: Methods are proposed for determining the number of excursions in a finite realization of a stationary random process, from discrete readings of an additive mixture of the process with noise. Examples of possible algorithms for registration of excursions on a computer are included, and estimates are made of their efficiency. The case of a normal random process and a large number of intersections is examined in detail. The results obtained can be used directly to determine the sampling period from the condition of a given error of registration of the excursions.
Name: ["Baylin A.M."]

Title: USE OF MATHEMATICAL MODEL OF BLOOD COAGULATION PROCESS IN HEALING OF BRAIN INFARCT.
Abstract: The problem is considered of identification of a control system for blood coagulation of humans. Mathematical models are constructed for the obtained types of control system, and a method is proposed for using heparin in healing of brain infarct; this method is brain infarct; this method is based on the obtained model.
Name: ["Mayboroda L.A.", "Vilenskiy B.S."]

Title: FINITELY CONVERGENT RECURSION ALGORITHMS FOR ADAPTIVE IDENTIFICATION OF DISCRETE DYNAMIC OBJECTS.
Abstract: The problem of adaptive identification of a dynamic object is formulated as the problem of solving a system of target inequalities connecting the outputs of the object and the model. This is done with finitely convergent recursion algorithms. A method is described for constructing optimal algorithms for solving these inequalities, which depend on a number of unknown parameters. The algorithms obtained are used for identification of nonlinear objects of several types. Conditions for precise identification are formulated, ensuring convergence of the model parameters to the unknown parameters of the object.
Name: ["Timofeyev A.V."]

Title: ON THE SYNTHESIS OF TERMINAL CONTROL LAWS.
Abstract: The problem is posed, and solved locally, of meeting of the integral curves of nonlinear automatic control systems of a broad class in a bounded time, and independently of the initial state, with a prenamed movable or immovable point in the phase space of the automatic control system. The manifold of terminal control laws that solve this problem is presented. The idea on which the solution is based consists in organizing artificial singular points of a new type at necessary places in the phase space of the dynamic equations of the automatic control system. The results of the article can be used in analysis and synthesis of control systems for various pursuit problems, for control of technological processes, and for mathematical ensuring of the planned development of economic systems whose dynamic equations are known.
Name: ["Grishin A.P."]

Title: ON THE PARTITION PAIR AND DECOMPOSITION BY THE PARTITION PAIR FOR STOCHASTIC AUTOMATA.
Abstract: The partition pair plays an important role in the decomposition of deterministic automata. In view of this, the partition pair is defined and its algebraic properties are presented. Furthermore, a strongly periodic stochastic automaton is defined and, using that notion, a theorem is given for decomposition of a stochastic automaton by a partition pair sequence of period T.
Name: ["Fujimoti Sinti"]

Title: LEARNING OF PREDICTING FUNCTION AND MECHANISM OF IMPROVING RECOGNITION RATE USING CONTEXT.
Abstract: A learning system for a predicting function is examined, and a mechanism for improving the recognition rate in this learning system is discussed. It is concluded that a combination of a self-learning system of recognition function and a learning system for a predicting function enables one to realize a recognizing mechanism having high recognition rate without supervisors.
Name: ["Isomichi Toshinori"]

Title: Industrial Process Identification. | [IDENTIFICATION DE PROCESSUS INDUSTRIELS.]
Abstract: This paper shows how to apply well known methods of industrial process identification to a real case of continuous cement furnace. Due to the problem of getting precise data and because it was impossible to make many test runs only simple models are examined. The methods of deconvolution, of Strejc, and of multiple linear regression are used and the results are discussed.
Name: ["Dubuisson B.", "Marechal C.", "Le The Tanh", "Weber C.", "Ouillade G."]

Title: On the simulation of continuous non-linear filters A comparative study of second- and third-order approximations
Abstract: Among several second-order approximations to the filter of a non-linear system, it is found that the extended Kalman filter is generally the most versatile. The second-order likelihood filter, also known ns the Detchmendy‚ÄîSridhar filter is inferior to the ahove and at the same time involves more computation. In the special ease when analytical expressions For the gaussian expectation integrals of the non-linearities can be found, the extended Kalman filter can be further improved by using stochastic linear approximations as suggested by Sunahara. The third-order likelihood filter derived in this paper is more accurate than the above, but calls for considerable storage space and computing time. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Leung V.P.", "Padmanabhan L."]

Title: Hierarchical Classification of Plane Surfaces and Application of a Placement Problem According to a Heuristic Method. | [RECHERCHE D'UN CLASSEMENT HIERARCHIQUE DE SURFACES PLANES ET APPLICATION A UN PROBLEME DE PLACEMENT SELON UNE METHODE HEURISTIQUE.]
Source: Rev Fr Autom Inf Rech Oper
Abstract: In classifying patterns (geometric or otherwise), it is important to use as little raw material as possible. However, it is difficult to obtain the optimum and takes considerable time when the number of patterns is important. The minimum approach is effected here by a hierarchical classification determined by topological considerations. The authors propose the establishment of a list by a heuristic method. A numerical example is given to verify the proposed solution.
Name: ["Diverrez J.C.", "Du Bois de Meyrignac B.", "Soenen R."]

Title: DEVELOPMENT OF THE ACL LANGUAGE AND ITS IMPLEMENTATION ACL-NOVA.
Abstract: The development of a one-terminal system ACTIV-8 for the PDP-8 computer is first described. The concepts of the dynamic syntax checking of keyboard input from the terminal and the interruption of stored program execution via the communicate statement are presented. The development of the new conversational language ACL and its implementation as a multi-user conversational interpreter ACL-NOVA is then described. The ACL-NOVA system runs as a stand-alone system and provides a powerful conversational computing facility for many users in a time-sharing environment.
Name: ["Bennett N.W.", "Sanger P.L."]

Title: OPTIMAL REPLACEMENT RULES WHEN CHANGES OF STATE ARE SEMI-MARKOVIAN.
Abstract: Investigation of the use of a discrete-time semi-Markov process to model a system that deteriorates in usage. Replacement rules that are state-dependent, state-age-dependent, and age-dependent are proposed. The paper generates semi-Markov decision processes so that optimal policies can be obtained by the policy-iteration method. Sufficient conditions for the existence of an optimal control-limit state-dependent replacement rule are derived.
Name: ["Kao Edward P.C."]

Title: Automated system for testing visual fields
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: An electronic system for automatically testing the human visual field is described in the context of mass screening for visual disorders, such as glaucoma. Present methods of field testing are reviewed. The new system is patient operated and uses a television monitor as the means of presenting the test stimuli and displaying the results. A multilevel map of a patient's retinal sensitivity is produced in a form which is readily interpreted by an ophthalmologist. A data-transfer unit enables the local storage of results and allows direct access to a computer. Preliminary clinical trials show good agreement with conventional field-testing methods, and yield more detailed information than has, in the past, been feasible on a routine basis. | An electronic system for automatically testing the human visual field is described in the context of mass screening for visual disorders, such as glaucoma. Present methods of field testing are briefly reviewed. The new system is patient operated and uses a television monitor as the means for presenting the test stimuli and displaying the results. A multilevel map of a patient's retinal sensitivity is produced in a form which is readily interpreted by an ophthalmologist. A data transfer unit enables the local storage of results and allows direct access to a computer. Preliminary clinical trials show good agreement with conventional field testing methods, and yield more detailed information than has hitherto been feasible on a routine basis.
Name: ["Chaplin G.B.B.", "Edwards J.H.", "Gedye J.L.", "Marlowe S."]

Title: Model Approximations to Visual Spatio‚ÄêTemporal Sine‚ÄêWave Threshold Data
Abstract: Experimental data on visual spatio‚Äêtemporal sine‚Äêwave thresholds obtained by Robson and Kelly are considered. In seeking model approximations to the data it is assumed that the subject's visual threshold to modulation at different spatial and temporal frequencies gives the image of his filter function to within a multiplicative constant. It is further assumed that the data can be approximated by a system with a spatially uniform, isotropic, and temporally invariant response which consists of the difference between an excitatory and an inhibitory term, and that each term is separable into a product of a spatial and a temporal function. ¬© 1973 The Bell System Technical Journal
Name: ["Budrikis Z.L."]

Title: UNIQUE CONSTRUCTION OF REGRESSION CURVE USING A SMALL NUMBER OF POINTS - 2.
Abstract: A theory is developed using sequential projection of the output vectors onto the plane of the independent variables (the theory of projection operators). On this basis it is proved that the error calculated on the training sequence of data decreases monotonically as the number of selection layers of the GMDH increases. It is shown that if a certain freedom of choice (or, more precisely, the projection basis) is given, a multilayer selection algorithm will not differ (in its results and properties) from complete enumeration. Illustrative examples are presented. In addition, a generalized GMDH algorithm with selection of projection operators is described, that makes it possible to reduce the size of the problem to be solved. The basic principles of self-organization theory are considered, and related to the method of solution of controversial scientific problems by selecting an appropriate criterion, or by shortening the size of complete enumeration, or by control with prediction optimization.
Name: ["Ivakhnenko A.G.", "Koval'chuk P.I.", "Todua M.M.", "Shelud'ko O.I.", "Dubrovin O.F."]

Title: Realization of Self-Testing Asynchronous Sequential Circuits. | REALISATION DE CIRCUITS SEQUENTIELS ASYNCHRONES AUTOTESTABLES.
Source: Rev Fr Autom Inf Rech Oper
Abstract: This paper deals with the realization of self-testing asynchronous sequential machines for a certain class of single failures. The synthesis uses a 1-out-of-n code, and the circuit is obtained by connecting sequential cells according to the flow graph; transitions between states are performed on a single wire by a pulse. Two cellular networks are added in order to give the whole system a self-testing property. The first, an iterative cellular network, detects any configuration of the state variables not belonging to the 1-out-of-n code, and it is designed in order to be self-checked. The second one tests the output network of a Moore-type machine by using parity techniques. It will be shown how to make it self-checking.
Name: ["Geffroy J.C.", "Courvoisier M.", "Diaz M."]

Title: OPTIMAL CONTROL OF LINEAR MULTIVARIABLE SYSTEMS BASED ON DISCRETE OUTPUT FEEDBACK.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: The application of a discrete multivariable output-prediction equation to the optimal-control problem is discussed. The dynamic-programming procedure is used to minimize a cost functional defined in terms of the inputs and outputs of the process. A method is described whereby it is possible to effect stabilized control which is based on minimization of a single-state performance criterion. The output-prediction equation is shown to provide an effective basis for the implementation of optimal control.
Name: ["Sandoz D.J."]

Title: Application of the Tichonov regularization algorithm to object restoration
Abstract: Object restoration is recognized as an improperly posed problem and an algorithm developed by Tichonov is employed to numerically stabilize the solution. Some numerical results are illustrated. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Barakat R.", "Blackman E."]

Title: Control of Resultant Stability by Using Cybernetic Methods. | OB UPRAVLENII REZUL'TIRUYUSHCHEI USTOICHIVOST'YU PRIMENENIEM METODOV KIBERNETIKI.
Abstract: One of the possible variants of constructing a system of cybernetic control of resultant stability in a complex electric power system, using automatic turbine speed governors, is considered. Criteria of control optimality are proposed. Algorithms of data processing and formation of control signals of the control system are based on representation of the parameters of the operating conditions of the electric power system in a generalized form.
Name: ["Venikov V.A.", "Zelenokhat N.I."]

Title: TREE DRIVEN DATA INPUT AND ITS VALIDATION.
Abstract: A generalized technique for the input of forms into a computer system, and its implementation in ALGOL is described. The format for any section of a form is parameterized. Each type of form has an associated input format tree which holds the various sets of section parameters. This input format tree is used to decode the data belonging to a form into a data tree.
Name: ["Padgett M.I."]

Title: On the Controllability of Linear Systems of Distributed Parameters and Their Use for the Determination of Optimal Actuating Points. | SUR LA COMMANDABILITE DE SYSTEMES LINEAIRES A PARAMETRES REPARTIS ET SON UTILISATION POUR LA DETERMINATION DE POINTS D'ACTION OPTIMAUX.
Source: Rev Fr Autom Inf Rech Oper
Abstract: The purpose of this paper concerns the controllability of a class of distributed parameter systems which can be controlled by a certain number of points of the spatial domain. The reachable domain of the state space, from a bounded norm control, depends on the choice of actuating points of the system. A method is then proposed, which from the maximization of the domain volume a set of optimal actuating points are derived.
Name: ["Amouroux M.", "Babary J.P."]

Title: A Survey of Applications of Symbolic Network Functions
Abstract: A. survey of applications of symbolic network functions is presented in which some network elements, in addition to the complex frequency s, are represented by variables. The concept of ‚Äúclosed systems‚Äù is generalized. A fundamental theorem on the form of symbolic network functions is proved. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Lin P.M."]

Title: REALIZATION OF FINITE AUTOMATA BY LADDER-TYPE FLOW NETWORKS.
Abstract: Flow networks can be used for the realization of finite automata. Methods are proposed for the design of finite automata using ladder-type flow networks. Parameters of these realizations are presented, as well as the parameters of realizations of counters and registers.
Name: ["Gendler M.B."]

Title: Recursive Ideal Observer Detection of Known M-Ary Signals in Multiplicative and Additive Gaussian Noise
Abstract: This paper presents the derivation of the recursive algorithms necessary for real-time digital detection of Mary known signals that are subject to independent multiplicative and additive Gaussian noises. The motivating application is minimum probability of error detection of digital data-link messages aboard civil aircraft in the earth reflection multipath environment. For each known signal, the detector contains one Kalman filter and one probability computer. The filters estimate the multipath disturbance. The estimates and the received signal drive the probability computers. Outputs of all the computers are compared in amplitude to give the signal decision. The practicality and usefulness of the detector are extensively discussed. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Painter J.H.", "Gupta S.C."]
Affiliations: ['NASA Langley Research Center', ' Southern Methodist University']

Title: LOGICAL REVERSIBILITY OF COMPUTATION.
Source: IBM Journal of Research and Development
Abstract: The usual general-purpose computing automation (e. g. , a Turing machine) is logically irreversible - its function lacks a single-valued inverse. Here it is shown that such machines may be made logically reversible at every step, while retaining their simplicity and their ability to do general computations. This result is of great physical interest because it makes plausible the existence of thermodynamically reversible computers which could perform useful computations at useful speed while dissipating considerably less than kT of energy per logical step. In the first stage of its computation the logically reversible automaton parallels the corresponding irreversible automaton, except that it saves all intermediate results, thereby avoiding the irreversible operation of erasure. The second stage consists of printing out the desired output. The third stage then reversibly disposes of all the undesired intermediate results by retracing the steps of the first stage in backward order (a process which is only possible because the first stage has been carried out reversibly), thereby restoring the machine (except for the now-written output tape) to its original condition. The final machine configuration thus contains the desired output and a reconstructed copy of the input, but no other undesired data. The foregoing results are demonstrated explicitly using a type of three-tape Turing machine. The biosynthesis of messenger RNA is discussed as a physical example of reversible computation.
Name: ["Bennett C.H."]

Title: NONPARAMETRIC FEATURE ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SAMPLED DIFFRACTION PATTERNS.
Abstract: Techniques which allow the pattern recognition experimenter to rapidly develop, compute, and evaluate individual as well as sets of features are discussed. Standard file and data formats enable rapid extraction of new features from an existing data base. Analysis of new features is accomplished using nonparametric statistical measures of class separation based on ranks. The Rank Sum Test, Kolomogorov-Smirnov Test, and Mutual Information are readily computed from sample ranks determined by individual features. These measures are computed for feature vectors using distribution estimates based on statistically equivalent blocks. Several examples illustrate the use of these techniques on real data. Interpretation of the statistical separation results is discussed in the context of selecting a feature set which maximizes the recognition performance.
Name: ["Kasdan Harvey L."]

Title: DISCRIMINATION OF NEURAL CODING PARAMETERS IN THE AUDITORY SYSTEM.
Abstract: Measures of information transmission in the nervous system are developed from statistical decision theory. The information measure is based on the divergence of two distributions and is related to the Cramer-Rao inequality. This measure is applied to the estimation of frequency and amplitude from spike trains in the auditory system.
Name: ["Sanderson Arthur C.", "Calvert Thomas W."]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR A STEP BY STEP MINMAX CONTROL OF LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH POWER-BOUNDED NOISE.
Abstract: For a linear discrete system subject to noise with a power-like bound, a step-by-step min-max control law is derived as an explicit function of the state in which a parameter appears which is easily determined by solving a scalar equation. Some interesting properties are shown of the corresponding trajectories of the state.
Name: ["Maniacco M.", "Marzollo A.", "Pascoletti A.", "Ukovich W."]

Title: MIN-MAX CONTROL OF NORM UNCERTAIN SYSTEMS: POST-ADDITIVE FUNCTIONALS.
Abstract: The problem of the control of a process, which is described by an approximate model, is considered. The problem is reduced to the control of the model whose output is affected by an input dependent error constrained in norm, and a min-max approach is taken. Attention is focused on features of the penalty functional since it is desired to synthesize the min-max control by means of a feedback on the states of the model; for example a quadratic functional has not this property. An L//1 type functional is then proposed, which is not differentiable; by means of duality techniques, however, the minimization can be carried out. The min-max is obtained both by iterative procedures, both as a function of the actual value of the model state: this function is the solution of a set of a partial differential equation. The proposed methods are applied to a numerical example and compared.
Name: ["Milanese M.", "Negro A."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION AND STOCHASTIC CONTROL OF NON - DYNAMIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The paper presents a newly developed theory of identification and stochastic control of linear nondynamic systems (i. e. , linear systems whose transfer functions are not necessarily rational) subject to random disturbance as well as measurement error.
Name: ["Balakrishnan A.V."]

Title: ON THE IDENTIFIABILITY OF LINEAR DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The case is considered in which the unknown parameters of a stationary linear system may be parametrized by a set of unknown parameters. The question thus arises of when such a set of parameters can be uniquely identified on the basis of observed data. This problem is examined both in the case of input and output observations and in the case of output observations in the presence of a white noise input. conditions for local identifiability are derived for both situations, and a sufficient condition for global identifiability is given for the former situation, i. e. , when simultaneous input and output observations are available.
Name: ["Glover Keith", "Willems Jan C."]

Title: APPLICATIONS PROGRAMMING AID.
Abstract: In generating several thousand tests for automatic test equipment (ATE) systems, two principles have been developed that simplify application programming. The first principle is that some tests within most application programs are similar in intent. This factor permits the generation of a set of generalized test procedures that includes most of the tests required for a given unit, with the result that the number of different techniques required is much less than the total number of tests. The second principle is to generate the application program code by automation after defining the test techniques. To do this, an intelligent terminal in an interactive man/machine system has been developed. This paper defines the test technique philosophy and expands on the properties and attributes of the automated system, named the applications programming aid (APA).
Name: ["Colgan John"]

Title: Finite stochastic automata with variable transition probabilities
Abstract: The transition probabilities of the stochastic automata we introduce in this paper are dependent upon the number of times the current state has been passed by. All the possible ways an automaton can develop, are represented by a set of matrices, which is formally characterized. Based on this representation, a method to calculate some probabilities of these automata, is given. ¬© 1973 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Paredaens J.J."]

Title: DIGITAL SIMULATION OF THE OPTIMAL FILTER FOR A STOCHASTIC DISTRIBUTED PARAMETER SYSTEM.
Source: Bulletin of the University of Osaka Prefecture, Series A Engineering and Natural Sciences
Abstract: A digital simulation is presented of an optimal filter for a linear distributed parameter system subject to both additive and state-dependent noises. The quantitative properties of the estimation errors are discussed and a method of determining the observation points and their numbers is proposed.
Name: ["Ohmatsu Shigeru", "Shibata Hiroshi", "Hata Shiro"]

Title: ALGORITHM DYNAMICS.
Abstract: A technique for measuring simple structural properties of algorithms is described. Using these measures, it is found that for a nontrivial class of algorithms there is a quantitative relationship between operators and operands and their usage. Properties of ‚Ä≥Full‚Ä≥ and ‚Ä≥Reduced‚Ä≥ algorithms are then explored, and shown to predict the quantitative relationship observed.
Name: ["Halstead Maurice", "Bayer Rudolf"]

Title: ESTIMATION OF THE 'STATE' OF THE HEART.
Abstract: Methods are described to classify the 'states' of de- and repolarization processes in human hearts into categories with the help of electrocardiograms and by means of automation of human decision-making. The needed algorithms and classification models are trained during a learning period. Clustering methods are used for the choice of the most relevant signal part, pattern recognition is applied to the measurement of the wave duration, and statistical classifiers are used for the estimation of the state of the process. Results are given for learning and test populations of signals and processes.
Name: ["Talmon Jan L.", "van Bemmel Jan H."]

Title: MULTIMODAL SEARCHING TECHNIQUE USING A LEARNING CONTROLLER.
Abstract: A total variable structure probabilistic automaton (variable number of states and variable search probabilities) has been proposed as a model of a controller in an adaptive or learning control system. The learning controller is capable of controlling a plant where a global search of a multimodal noisy performance surface is desired, the entire admissible region of the control action is divided into various different subregions in accordance with the number of states and the search probabilities of the stochastic automaton. The learning controller is able to adjust the search probabilities and the number of states. The adjustment is based on the past values of the index of performance and is nonlinear. The learning controller has the ability to determine the subregion with global minimum and to vary the division of the whole admissible region into subregions so that the subregion with global minimum is maintained if the multimodal noisy performance surface changes. The division of the whole admissible region into subregions (each subregion corresponds to one state of the automaton) is also nonlinear and depends on the desired accuracy of the subregion with the global minimum. The searching technique is effective in a learning control system where the direct functional relationship between the index of performance and the controlled parameters is unknown.
Name: ["Konokovsky R.", "Binder Z."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF A BAUXITE DIGESTION PROCESS BY FOURIER ANALYSIS.
Abstract: The paper describes the approach which has been used to identify the digestion part of an alumina Bayer plant. It shows how Fourier transform analysis can lead to useful and meaningful results for process control applications. In a first stage, a linearized model is built up from simple assumptions. Pulse tests and resulting Bode diagrams are presented. Identification by comparison with synthetic transfer functions makes it possible to verify the assumptions made in building the linearized model and to estimate the parameters. The application of the dynamic model is illustrated.
Name: ["Riffaud J.P.", "Magistry P."]

Title: ON SOME PROBLEMS RELATED TO THE IDENTIFICATION OF AIRCRAFT PARAMETERS.
Abstract: The methods of identification used in the evaluation of aircraft parameters are the equation error method and the output error method. The second method involves the weighted least squares estimation, maximum likelihood estimation, and Bayesian estimation procedures. Both methods are covered by one computing program. The accuracy and sensitivity of various solutions and the effect of certain model errors are discussed and covered by examples.
Name: ["Klein Vladislav", "Williams David A."]

Title: ANALOGUE MODEL IDENTIFICATION OF SYSTEM DYNAMIC ERROR TRANSFER FUNCTIONS.
Abstract: A method based on frequency domain sensitivity functions is presented in flow diagram form suitable for human operator implementation in analog model experiments in which the error between system and model performance is displayed as a Lissajous figure. The method is successfully applied to determine the dynamic error transfer function of a simulated sixth-order radar control system. In deriving the flow diagram, considerable use is made of the fact that many high-order systems are adequately described by a coefficient plane model.
Name: ["Towill D.R."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION TECHNIQUE FOR MULTI-INPUT MULTI-OUTPUT SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A method for real-time identification of multiinput multioutput linear-time invariant systems is presented. Weighting sequence models are experimentally determined from input-output records using delayed data information. Both noise-free and noise-corrupted signals are considered, and expressions for the variances of the estimators are derived. The proposed computational algorithms have the property that errors usually present in numerical deconvolution techniques are greatly reduced.
Name: ["Bilal A.Y.", "Hassan M.F."]

Title: GAME THEORETIC DESIGN OF INPUT SIGNALS FOR PARAMETER IDENTIFICATION.
Abstract: A new concept of designing an optimal input for accurate parameter identification has been developed using the game theory approach, where the input is constrained to the semi-closed form with positive feedback. The property of parameter identifiability is first defined and discussed to investigate whether the design problem makes sense. Two theoretic game approaches to the problem of input design for parameter identification are then presented. The lower bound of the error criterion preserved by the optimal inputs is derived, and the structure of the equation error is examined. Numerical examples are presented.
Name: ["Sawaragi Yoshikazu", "Ogino Katsuya"]

Title: Upon some continuous prediction algorithms. I
Abstract: Three difference-differential processes operating upon an initial value function Œ¶ (Œº) and yielding a sequence of approximations to {Mathematical expression} are described. The processes are confluent analogues of an algorithm related to Romberg's extrapolation procedure, of the œÄ-algorithm, and of the Œµ-algorithm. It is shown that these processes can be modified to yield approximations to the integral {Mathematical expression}, and that in certain circumstances this integral can be evaluated by a process of repeated differentiation involving the function œà(Œº). Discrete algorithms for approximating {Mathematical expression}, for which it is assnmed, that values of the successive derivatives of the function Œ¶ (Œº) are available, are described. It is shown that these algorithms can be applied to the evaluation of the integral {Mathematical expression}, it being assumed that the values of the successive derivatives of the function œà(Œº) are available. A number of examples in which closed expressions for the transformed estimates can be derived are discussed. Algol procedures for implementing the discrete algorithms are given ¬© 1973 Instituto di Elaborazione della Informazione del CNR.
Name: ["Wynn P."]

Title: ON TRACKING LINEAR PLANTS UNDER UNCERTAINTY.
Abstract: A minimax terminal state estimation problem is considered which can be viewed as a mathematical model for an estimation problem in which an attempt is made to track an uncooperative target with basically unknown maneuvering capabilities in a relatively noisy environment. The problem can also be thought of as a stochastic two-person zero-sum game in which the players are the tracker and the evader.
Name: ["Mintz Max", "Basar Tamer"]

Title: GAME THEORETIC APPROACH TO SENSITIVITY DESIGN OF OPTIMAL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Two game theoretic approaches to sensitivity design for a linear regulator problem under large uncertainty are developed, where the equation error in the model system and the feedback controller as assumed to be antagonists. The so-called game theoretic design, which is the worst case design, is developed, and the upper bound of the value of the performance index is derived. A slightly different game design called sensitive game theoretic design is also presented. The problem of determining admissible errors so that the value of the performance index does not exceed some value is discussed by the use of rho -sensitivity.
Name: ["Sawaragi Yoshikazu", "Ogino Katsuya"]

Title: UNUSUAL APPLICATION OF PROGRAM-PROVING.
Abstract: An inductive proof in mathematics may often be expressed as an algorithm and a proof that the algorithm is correct. Especially when the proof proceeds by cases, a recursive pattern-matching language, such as Hewitt's MATCHLESS, is a felicitous language for writing the algorithm. Authors use this idea to prove a new mathematical result, which itself is of interest in computer science.
Name: ["Wand Mitchell"]

Title: SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION USING STOCHASTIC APPROXIMATION.
Abstract: The application of stochastic approximation to the identification of linear systems is discussed. The parameters of a discrete-time model are first determined in a recursive manner from the samples of the observed input and output data contaminated with noise using a recently proposed new algorithm for stochastic approximation. From this model, the parameters of the corresponding continuous-time system are then estimated. Simulation results are presented indicating that the proposed scheme for identification converges much faster than the existing methods based on stochastic approximation, provided that the signal-to-noise power ratio is not less than one.
Name: ["Sinha Naresh K."]

Title: INTERACTIVE INSTRUCTION SIMULATION ON AND OF THE DATAPOINT 2200 COMPUTER.
Abstract: An interactive simulation of the execution of mnemonically entered instructions for the Datapoint 2200 Computer has been developed which runs on this same machine. A representation of the registers, flip-flops, program counter, subroutine stack, and referenced memory cell is shown on the display of the machine. Individual mnemonic instructions may be entered from the keyboard. Both the instructions and their operands are syntactically checked character-by-character as they are entered and all illegal entries are refused. The simulator displays the corresponding octal form of these instructions and modifies the representation of the state of the machine accordingly. Short programs of such instructions may be entered and normal sequential execution simulated.
Name: ["Huebner Paul F.", "Skelton Daniel T.", "Schweppe Earl J."]

Title: APPLICATION OF REALIZATION THEORY TO IDENTIFICATION OF MULTIVARIABLE PROCESS.
Abstract: By introducing the motion of epsilon -practically minimal realization, they are reduced to an equivalent system to the plant with the minimal dimension in the practical sense.
Name: ["Furuta Katsuhisa"]

Title: DUALITY APPLIED TO THE COMPLEXITY OF MATRIX MULTIPLICATIONS AND OTHER BILINEAR FORMS.
Abstract: The paper considers the complexity of bilinear forms in a noncommutative ring. The dual of a computation is defined and applied to matrix multiplication and other bilinear forms. It is shown that the dual of an optimal computation gives an optimal computation for a dual problem. The concept of duality is applied to matrix multiplication.
Name: ["Hopcroft J.", "Musinski J."]

Title: ON THE GENERATION OF SENSITIVITY AND PSEUDOSENSITIVITY FUNCTIONS FOR MULTIVARIABLE SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to unify recent advances in the area of computer generation sensitivity and pseudosensitivity functions and to point out new results which may be obtained from these known achievements. Attention is paid to an extension of the existing results to the generation of pseudosensitivity functions for linear multivariable systems whose mathematical models are given in the state space. The methods of generating pseudo sensitivity functions, discussed in the paper, enable the extension of the methods for identification, parameter optimization and synthesis of adaptive systems, so far extensively used in the cases of single-input, single-output systems, to linear multivariable systems.
Name: ["Bingulac S.P.", "Djorovic M."]

Title: CONTROL THEORETIC APPROACH TO DYNAMIC MEASUREMENTS OF WEIGHT IN INDUSTRIAL WEIGHING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The new idea of dynamic compensation to a noisy industrial weighing system of moving-arm type has been developed from the modern control theoretic point of view, and a Computer-Aided Dynamic Measurement Method (CAMM) has been proposed. Computer simulation studies have been worked out to investigate the effectiveness and usefulness of the present approach form the various aspects of practical applications. The feasibility of CAMM has also been examined through a practical experiment.
Name: ["Ono T."]

Title: COMPUTATIONAL EXPERIENCE WITH THE CENTRAL CUTTING PLANE ALGORITHM.
Abstract: The Central Cutting Plane Algorithm is an algorithm for solving the convex programming problem. The major theoretical results concerning the algorithm are stated. Some preliminary computational experience with an experimental code of the algorithm are reported.
Name: ["Elzinga Jack", "Moore Thomas G."]

Title: ADAPTIVE PROCESSING: TIME-VARYING PARAMETERS.
Abstract: Signal detection problems in which parameters of either or both the signal and the noise are allowed to vary with time in an uncertain manner are considered. The time variations are accounted for by assuming that the parameters can be modeled as a Markov stochastic process.
Name: ["Nolte Loren W."]

Title: METHOD OF ADAPTIVE FILTERING.
Source: Telecommunications and Radio Engineering (English translation of Elektrosvyaz and Radiotekhnika)
Abstract: An adaptive algorithm is described for tuning a Kalman filter when there is incomplete a priori information on the object parameters.
Name: ["Ashinyants R.A."]

Title: COMPARISON OF SEVERAL DATA-RATE-REDUCTION TECHNIQUES FOR SONAR.
Abstract: Three data-rate-reduction (DDR) techniques are investigated. The first is a post-OR integrator, i. e. , a processor which OR-gates the parallel outputs of the filter bank, integrates M temporal samples of the OR-gate output, and thresholds the integrated data for alerting purposes. The second is a maximum likelihood ratio device, i. e. a processor which forms likelihood ratios on the sequence of samples from each of the parallel outputs of the filter bank, OR-gates the likelihood ratios, and then thresholds the OR-gated output. The third technique is a Kolmogorov-Smirnov (nonparametric) device, i. e. , a processor which estimates the difference in the distribution function of the amplitude of noise alone and the distribution function of the amplitudes of the samples in each channel of the filter bank, then OR-gates these estimated differences and finally thresholds the OR-gated output to alert the operator.
Name: ["Dow J.J.", "Brown B.M.", "Reeder H.A."]

Title: Development of a Real-Time Adaptive Control Technique
Abstract: An adaptive technique is described which relies upon identifying the transition and driving matrices of a linear dynamic system. By identifying these matrices a sub-optimal controller is updated so that effective control is maintained. The method may be extended to non-linear and time varying systems by employing quasi-linearization. The simplicity of the algorithm allows real-time control of systems for which there is no a priori knowledge concerning system dynamics. The scheme is illustrated using a hybrid computing system specifically designed for this purpose. Application of this technique to plant is referred to. This paper gives a history of the development of this particular deterministic approach to the adaptive control problem. ¬© 1973, MCB UP Limited
Name: ["Swanick B.H.", "Sandoz‚Ñ† D.J."]

Title: RECENT TREND IN ADAPTIVE SPATIAL PROCESSING FOR SENSOR ARRAYS: CONSTRAINED ADAPTATION.
Abstract: It is shown that a class of suboptimal (i. e. less than fully adaptive) adaptive systems can in many cases give near optimum array performance with a reasonable hardware requirement. It is further shown that suboptimal adaptive array control algorithms should be properly constrained and configured within the context of the signal and interference environment for a specific array. The emphasis is placed on adaptive realization techniques for the general multichannel processor, with applications discussed in terms of specific examples.
Name: ["Owsley Norman L."]

Title: MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD IDENTIFICATION OF ASTROM MODEL BY QUASILINEARIZATION.
Abstract: The application of a quasilinearization technique to the identification of linear stochastic model, proposed by Astrom, is described. By interpreting the maximum likelihood method as finding the coefficients of the prediction model, an iterative algorithm is derived using quasilinearization. The algorithm proposed is very simple for computer application and can be implemented in on-line identification.
Name: ["Furht Borivoje P."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF PROCESSES WITH DIRECTION-DEPENDENT DYNAMIC RESPONSES.
Abstract: Many processes have dynamic responses which are dependent on the direction in which the response variable is moving. The effects of such nonlinear behavior on the weighting function model of the process obtained by crosscorrelation and on the difference equation model obtained by a generalized least-squares procedure are determined theoretically for a process with first-order dynamics perturbed with pseudo-random binary signals. The theory is confirmed by results from a hybrid computer simulation, and computer-simulated results for processes with second-order dynamics are also presented. Experimental work on two pilot-scale processes with direction-dependent dynamics is reported, and further examples from the literature are examined.
Name: ["Godfrey K.R.", "Briggs P.A.N."]

Title: NEW CLOSED SOLUTION DESIGN OF CONSTANT FEEDBACK CONTROL FOR SYSTEMS WITH LARGE PARAMETER VARIATIONS.
Abstract: A new method for designing the feedback part of a linear invariant control system for every desirable design goal is presented. The method has three important advantages: the parameter variations may be arbitrarily large, no sensitivity measure used because sensitivity generally is only a ‚Ä≥local‚Ä≥ property, and a closed solution can be derived.
Name: ["Bux Dieter"]

Title: DESIGN OF DISCRETE MODEL REFERENCE ADAPTIVE SYSTEMS USING THE POSITIVITY CONCEPT.
Abstract: A unified approach to the design of ‚Ä≥parallel‚Ä≥ , ‚Ä≥series-parallel‚Ä≥ and ‚Ä≥series‚Ä≥ discrete model reference adaptive systems (MRAS) is discussed using the representation of these systems as an equivalent feedback system partitioned into a linear time invariant part and a nonlinear time varying part. The design of stable discrete MRAS is consequently converted to the construction of algorithms assuring certain positivity properties separately for each of these two parts. A general procedure for constructing such algorithms is presented. Experimental results are included.
Name: ["Landau I.D."]

Title: OPEN-LOOP - FEEDBACK-OPTIMAL ADAPTIVE STOCHASTIC CONTROL OF LINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The suboptimal stochastic control of linear discrete-time dynamical systems with unknown or stochastically varying parameters is considered. The suboptimal scheme is based upon the use of the open-loop-feedback-optimal (O. L. F. O. ) - method. The state and parameter estimates are generated by an extended Kalman filter algorithm. Numerical results for first-order systems are presented.
Name: ["Ku Richard", "Athans Michael"]

Title: DATA-COMPRESSION FOR ADAPTIVE MODEL IDENTIFICATION OF NONLINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The problem of nonlinear system identification is considered. A method of compressing initial information is suggested which is applicable to systems described by linear differential equations. An example of the application of this method to a nonlinearity problem is presented.
Name: ["Norkin K.B."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION BY PSEUDOSENSITIVITY FUNCTIONS AND QUASILINEARIZATION.
Abstract: The paper treats the identification of nonlinear deterministic multivariable systems by pseudosensitivity functions from the point of view of quasilinearization. The pseudo quasilinearization procedure is introduced and the pseudosensitivity functions, defined previously by other authors, are extended. The cases in which the pseudosensitivity functions lead to the noniterative (one-shot) identification algorithms are defined. A detailed analysis is also performed in order to distinguish between the Gauss-Newton algorithm and an algorithm based on the modified quasilinearization. Finally, combining the modified and pseudo quasilinearization, an algorithm with improved convergency characteristics is proposed.
Name: ["Matausek M.R.", "Milovanovic M.D."]

Title: Clustering of one-dimensional ordered data
Abstract: A set of n ordered real numbers is partitioned by complete enumeration into k clusters such that the sum of the sum of squared deviations from the mean-value within each cluster is minimized. ¬© 1973 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Sp√§th H."]

Title: An automaton framework for neural nets that learn
Abstract: Brindley (1967, 1969, 1972) has discussed nets of several types of formal neurons, many of whose functions are modifiable by their own input stimuli. Because Brindley's results are widely referred to, for example Marr (1970, 1971) and include some of the scarce non-trivial theorems on learning nets, it is important that serious side-conditions be made explicit. The language of finite automata is used to mathematicize the problem of adaptation sufficiently to remove some ambiguities of Brindley's approach. We close the paper by relating our framework to other formal studies of adaptation. ¬© 1973, Academic Press Inc. (London) Limited. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Kilmer W.L.", "Arbib M.A."]

Title: On random observation processes for stochastic approximation
Source: Annals of the Institute of Statistical Mathematics
Abstract: In [1] a new procedure is given to estimate the root of a regression equation. The purposes of this paper are to extend the Lemma 1 in [1] and to give a process involving a randomly determined sequence of observations for finding thermaximum of a regression function. The process is similar to that of [1]. Kiefer and Wolfowitz [2] gave a stochastic approximation procedure for the latter purpose. Their process needs the condition of the unimodality of the regression function which is not required for our case. ¬© 1973 Institute of Statistical Mathematics.
Name: ["Yamazoe S."]

Title: DIGITAL ADAPTIVE CONTROLLERS USING SECOND ORDER MODELS WITH TRANSPORT LAG.
Abstract: The design of a discrete optimal regulator requires the a priori knowledge of a mathematical model for the system of interest. Because a second-order model with transport lag is very amenable to control computations and because this type of model has been used previously to represent certain high-order single input-single output processes, an adaptive controller was designed based upon adjustment of controls computed for such a model. An extended Kalman filter was utilized for tracking the model parameters which were subsequently used to update a set of optimal control gains. Favorable results were obtained in applying this procedure to the control of several examples including a ninth-order nonlinear process.
Name: ["Joshi S.", "Kaufman H."]

Title: TREATMENT OF TIME VARYING STOCHASTIC BIAS IN RECURSIVE FILTERING.
Abstract: The problem of estimating the state x(i) of a linear system in the presence of a time-varying stochastic bias vector b(i) is considered via the Supplemented Partitioning Approach (S. P. A. ) to filtering. The motivation of the S. P. A. method is to use the partitioning philosophy to reduce the computational difficulties associated with computer storage, computing time, and computational errors in the application of Kalman-Bucy filtering theory to state-augmented systems. In the S. P. A. method, two effectively decoupled Kalman-Bucy filters are constructed for the estimation of the system state and the estimation of the bias vector respectively. The interaction between the system state vector and the bias vector is accounted for by supplementing the system, bias and measurement noise vectors as well as the respective noise covariance matrices. These supplementing terms are derived.
Name: ["Shah Mahendra M."]

Title: ON THE IDENTIFICATION OF LINEAR DISCRETE TIME SYSTEM MODELS USING THE INSTRUMENTAL VARIABLE METHOD.
Abstract: The identification of linear discrete time system models using the instrumental variable method requires the generation of an instrumental matrix sequence. A method of using a time invariant, linear, discrete time system model to generate an instrumental matrix sequence is discussed.
Name: ["Finigan Brian", "Rowe Ian H."]

Title: ESTIMATION OF SPATIALLY DISTRIBUTED DECAY PARAMETERS IN A CHEMICAL REACTOR.
Abstract: Discussed are some of the problems of developing practical algorithms for estimation of states and parameters in distributed parameter systems, which will form part of an on-line adaptive control scheme. The specific problem examined is that of a fixed bed catalytic reactor in which the activity is a function of the spatial coordinate as well as time. A method of reduction based on the use of splines to parameterize the model is shown to lead to effective decomposition of the filter matrices. This can be conveniently used in conjunction with a catalyst decay mechanism represented by a simple phenomenological equation characterized by one parameter. The application of a nonlinear filter based on mean value linearization results in an efficient, reliable and stable on-line estimator for this class of problem.
Name: ["McGreavy C.", "Vago A."]

Title: EVOLUTION OF A COMPUTER PROGRAM FOR OBTAINING OPTIMUM COMPUTER SIMULATION SOLUTIONS.
Abstract: For problems which are to be solved by digital computer simulation, an optimum solution is, in general, not obtained by analytic techniques, but rather by a search of the relevant parameter space. This search tends to be overwhelming, especially in those cases where more than three of four parameters are involved. Because of this, an OPTIMIZER computer program has been developed to provide efficient semi-automatic procedures of searching for an optimum computer simulation solution. The development of the OPTIMIZER is described in this paper.
Name: ["Smith Dennis E."]

Title: Optimization of Static Loading and Sizing of Multilevel Memory Systems
Abstract: The following two important aspects of multilevel static memory management are treated: (1) memory loading, and (2) memory sizing. An algorithm is developed for the optimal loading of program and data files in various memory levels of given sizes. The selection of optimal sizes from a given set of finite alternatives is done through a cyclic queueing model, which recognizes the effects of queues and waiting times and helps in deriving a balanced system. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Arora S.R.", "Gallo A."]
Affiliations: [' University of Minnesota', ' Division of Sperry Rand Corporation']

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF DISTRIBUTED PARAMETER SYSTEMS USING THE EPSILON METHOD: A NEW ALGORITHM.
Abstract: The application of the epsilon -method to the state estimation and parameter identification of distributed systems is considered. Using a suitable approximation of the state evolution, a function space algorithm for the minimization of the epsilon -functional is described. Numerical experiments are reported.
Name: ["Di Pillo G.", "Grippo L.", "Lucertini M."]

Title: OPTIMIZING ONE CLASS OF LARGE-SCALE SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Optimal control problems for a complex dynamic plant consisting of a number of subsystems having the same final objective and the same constraint on control actions are considered. Complex nonlinear relationships between plant coordinates and controls are assumed. A linear programming computing algorithm for the approximate solution of such problems is proposed.
Name: ["Meerov M.V.", "Bershchansky Ya.M."]

Title: AUTOMATED ATE PROGRAM PREPARATION FOR ANALOG CIRCUITS.
Abstract: Work undertaken to pursue and solve the problem of applying the capabilities of powerful CAD (computer-aided design) programs to the problem of writing analog Automatic Test Equipment (ATE) test programs is reported. Some of the results of this work are examined. The paper is oriented toward the problem of testing analog circuits because this problem has generally received less attention from the people in the ATE field than has the problem of digital circuits.
Name: ["Greenspan A.M."]

Title: TESTING FLOW GRAPH REDUCIBILITY.
Abstract: This paper presents an algorithm with an almost-linear time bound for determining whether a flow graph is reducible. The algorithm may be used to determine a way to reduce the graph if such a way exists. The method uses depth-first search and a good algorithm for computing disjoint set unions, and it improves upon a previously published algorithm for determining reducibility. The algorithm may be used as a basic subroutine for various code optimization procedures.
Name: ["Tarjan Robert"]

Title: USE OF SIMULATION IN REAL-TIME PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT.
Abstract: A discussion is presented as to how simulation can be used as an effective management tool to reduce costs by predicting many software requirements and design problems that are inherent in the development of real-time computer programs. Historically, simulation has been applied primarily to system performance evaluation and logic verification, and only recently has been formally used to help control the development of the operational program in a U. S. Navy tracking system. Since the technique is still under evaluation, the paper discusses the general concepts.
Name: ["Camp John W.", "Sullivan Richard L."]

Title: ON-LINE IDENTIFICATION OF CONTINUOUS SYSTEMS FROM SAMPLED DATA.
Abstract: The application of a digital computer for on-line identification of the parameters of a linear system from the samples of observed input and output data is considered. A discrete-time model is first obtained using a recursive algorithm such that the values of the parameters may be updated at the end of each sampling interval. From this model a continuous-time model is then derived. The method has been applied to the identification of the parameters of a realistic model of a nuclear reactor.
Name: ["Sinha Naresh K."]

Title: OPTIMUM STELLAR-AIDED INERTIAL PLATFORM STABILIZATION.
Abstract: Two methods of aligning an inertial platform for space missions by means of optical sensors are discussed. The first is that of the maximum likelihood estimation, while the second is that of the optimum linear filtering. The former provides a complete solution to the general case of a nonlinear, non-gaussian estimation problem. The optimization theory uses the well known ‚Ä≥separation theorem‚Ä≥ , namely stochastic estimation and optimal control. In both maximum likelihood and linear estimation, an incorrect model of the signal generating process may lead to bounded estimation errors, especially when the system noise is zero. A comparison of the two methods has shown that the computational requirements of the max likelihood far exceed those of the Kalman-Bucy estimator.
Name: ["Siouris George M."]

Title: MINIMUM TRAJECTORY SENSITIVITY DESIGN OF OPTIMAL CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Two techniques for the minimum trajectory sensitivity design of optimal control systems are discussed. The control law is assumed to be in the form u equals k//o(t) plus K//1(t)x. With such a controller, the first order sensitivity equations do not give rise to higher order sensitivity terms and are exact. One design consists of augmenting the sensitivity equations with the system equations and obtaining the solution optimal to a weighted average of the control criterion and the sensitivity criterion. This procedure directly obtains the optimal k//o(t) and K//1(t). The second technique, called the hierarchical method, consists of first solving the usual optimal control laws corresponding to the different possible programs for k//o and K//1. Out of these control laws, the one that results in minimum trajectory sensitivity is chosen by solving a second optimal control problem defined by the sensitivity equation and the sensitivity criterion. Both designs yield noninferior solutions. They are applied to the linear quadratic optimal regulator problem and numerical results are obtained for the scalar case. The resulting solutions satisfy the terminal constraints exactly for small parameter variations. They are shown to yield for the example smaller trajectory sensitivities throughout the optimization interval compared to the corresponding conventional open-loop and closed-loop solution.
Name: ["Sarma I.G.", "Hole K.E.", "Prasad U.R."]

Title: TWO RESULTS CONCERNING THE POWER OF TWO-WAY DETERMINISTIC PUSHDOWN AUTOMATA.
Abstract: It is shown that there is a two-way, deterministic Pushdown Automaton (2DPDA), U, which is a universal machine for the class of Finite Automata (FA). The method parallels D. Knuth and D. Bigelow's construction of a language which is not context-sensitive but which is the acceptance set of some stack automation, that is, a language is constructed which is not context-free, but which is accepted by a 2DPDA.
Name: ["Martin Daniel", "Gwynn John"]

Title: FORMAL SYSTEMS DESCRIPTION IN INFORMATION SYSTEMS DESIGN.
Abstract: An extension to the theory of formal information systems description, by which dynamical features can be represented, is proposed. A method of information systems analysis is explained, and it is shown how the result of the systems analysis can be expressed in a formal language which serves as input to a computer-based documentation system.
Name: ["Solvberg A."]

Title: ANALYSIS OF THE ACCURACY OF PARAMETRIC ADJUSTMENT OF A SYSTEM FOR ADAPTIVE CONTROL OF MULTIVARIABLE PLANTS IN MODIFIED SENSITIVITY MODELS.
Abstract: An analytic procedure for determining the accuracy of adjustment in adaptive control systems, using sensitivity models for calculating the gradients of the optimality criterion with respect to the adjusted parameters, is given. The procedure provides an opportunity for calculating the steady-state values of the adjusted parameters and the error of adjustment accurately, by using modified sensitivity models. With the aid of this procedure, an optimal structure of modified sensitivity models for different classes of plant input signals may be synthesized.
Name: ["Danev Bozhidar V."]

Title: APPLICATION OF RANDOM SEARCH TECHNIQUES AND STOCHASTIC APPROXIMATION IN HUMAN OPERATOR MODELLING.
Abstract: Off-line parameter optimization techniques for nonlinear multiparameter controller models of the human operator in man vehicular control problems are described. The model parameters (a total of eleven) are estimated for the same time slices of data by means of a random search technique and a stochastic approximation algorithm. The random search technique presented is one which combines directional and step size adaptation. It is contrasted with directional adaptive random search. The stochastic approximation algorithm is of the Kiefer-Wolfowitz type, expanded with step size adaptation and random search features. The techniques are compared with each other regarding their convergence speed, the detection of the global minimum, and the final values of the criterion function.
Name: ["Johannsen Gunnar"]

Title: CONTROL OF MULTIVARIABLE SYSTEMS WITH UNKNOWN BUT CONSTANT PARAMETERS.
Abstract: The problem of designing selfadjusting regulators is approached from the viewpoint of control of systems with constant but unknown parameters. An algorithm is proposed which can be applied to multivariable systems including those with unknown time delay and/or nonminimum phase. The main feature of the approach is the application of orthogonal transformations in order to reduce the observed input-output data. The use of orthogonal transformations makes it possible to obtain an appropriate information state of relatively low dimension. This information state asymptotically gives all second-order statistical characteristics which are required for the solution of the control problem when formulated as control of systems with uncertain parameters.
Name: ["Peterka V.", "Astrom K.J."]

Title: SELECTION OF PERIODIC TEST SIGNALS FOR ESTIMATION OF LINEAR SYSTEM DYNAMICS.
Abstract: The influence of the spectral properties of the test signal on the minimum variance bound (MVB) for the estimation of system parameters has been investigated. The parameters were the coefficients of the differential equation and the time delay. Optimum signals have been synthesized which minimized the trace of the minimum variance bound of the parameter estimates.
Name: ["van den Bos A."]

Title: REAL-TIME IDENTIFICATION USING ADAPTIVE DISCRETE MODEL.
Abstract: A new method for real time identification using a discrete adaptive model is presented. Synthesis of adaptive loops for model parameters is achieved by using hyperstability concepts. Attention is focused on a special treatment of error between model and process outputs which take into account the feedback realized by adaptive loops. Algorithms are written for identification with parallel (output error method) and series parallel (equation error method) models. Performances of these methods are compared and simulation results of parameters variance and biasing in presence of noise are given. Effects on convergence speed are described. Experimental results have been obtained on a heat exchanger. An extension of this method to adaptive filtering is proposed and an application to very high noise-signal ratio measurements is given.
Name: ["Hirsch J.J.", "Peltie P."]

Title: ON INFORMATION MEASURE IN IDENTIFICATION AND PARAMETER ESTIMATION.
Abstract: A new definition for a measure of the amount of information associated with probability distributions is proposed. This measure, called Bayesian distance, appears to be particularly appropriate in statistical decision theory since it is closely connected with the concept of error probability of decision making associated with the Bayes' rule. The properties of the Bayesian distance are investigated in the context of the finite-parameter estimation problem.
Name: ["Devijver Pierre A."]

Title: ESTIMATION OF MULTIVARIABLE RAILWAY VEHICLE DYNAMICS FROM NORMAL OPERATING RECORDS.
Abstract: A procedure developed for parameter estimation in a mathematical model describing the generation of lateral motions of railroad vehicles from measurements under normal operating conditions is discussed. Computations for a cyclical least squares model reference technique are carried out on a hybrid computer. It is shown that the use of two models in parallel can substantially improve the convergence, especially if the system output is disturbed by additive noise.
Name: ["Broersen Piet M.T."]

Title: ADAPTIVE CONTROL AND IDENTIFICATION BY A MODEL.
Abstract: A simple and relatively fast method for parameter identification of linear or linearizable control systems is presented. The results of analog simulation are then shown, and the efficiency of the method is analyzed with a reference to special applications in adaptive control systems. 3 refs.
Name: ["Nitsche H."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF NONLINEAR DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS BY USING AN INVERSE DESCRIBING FUNCTION METHOD.
Abstract: A class of nonlinear distributed systems which exhibit a structure similar to that of the standard loop with lumped parameter is considered. After a review of the principal results obtained by using a new harmonic linearization method recently proposed for these systems, an identification procedure which has been directly derived, by inversion, from this theoretical approach is described.
Name: ["Jumarie Guy"]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF POWER BLOCKS AS NON-LINEAR DYNAMIC OBJECTS.
Abstract: Problems of on-line determining of consumption functions of power blocks are considered, Algorithms are derived for computing parameter estimates of dynamic models, and a stability test for nonstationary intervals of power block characteristics is presented. Identification algorithms are checked using the statistical simulation method. Results for 300 MW power blocks suggest an expedient applicability of the method.
Name: ["Kaminskas Vytautas", "Nemura Antanas"]

Title: STOCHASTIC IDENTIFICATION OF DIGITAL FEEDBACK LOOPS USING A TABLE APPROACH.
Abstract: The identification by discrete-time models of a linear, computer-controlled process and its linear environment by methods of statistical estimation using natural noise data recorded on-line is dealt with. Earlier published methods for the estimation of the parameters of discrete models of DDC computer-regulated linear plants, influenced by multiple noise sources of rational spectral densities are taken into account. The paper discusses 1) a table approach for the identification of a set of primary parameters out of a multitude of possible structures, and 2) the risk of obtaining ambiguous results.
Name: ["Lindberger N.A."]

Title: ESTIMATION OF POWER GENERATOR DYNAMICS FROM NORMAL OPERATING DATA.
Abstract: Data obtained from a power generator during normal operation is analyzed in order to obtain a small-signal dynamic model of a power generator and its environment. A fast-Fourier transform technique is used to investigate causality between certain pairs of variables. Spectral analysis and a maximum likelihood method is applied to determine the transfer function relating angular velocity to electric torque. A fifth-order state space model has been constructed from physical a priori knowledge of the structure. Feedback effects have been included in the structure of the model which has no input but noise. Eight uncertain physical parameters and thirty parameters describing noise have been estimated using a maximum likelihood criterion. The maximum likelihood method is used to estimate parameters in such a fifth-order model describing the generator and its environment.
Name: ["Lindahl Sture", "Ljung Lennart"]

Title: ADAPTIVE ESTIMATION AND CONTROL OF LINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A new method is presented for deriving an estimator which uses a model to obtain an error vector containing both noise and dynamic mistake and minimizes the projection of this error vector in a direction containing only dynamic mistake to yield unbiased estimates for the model. The model is a ratio of polynomials in z, but it has its highest accuracy when interpreted as poles and residues in the z-plane, and the corresponding poles and residues in the s-plane.
Name: ["Smith Otto J.M."]

Title: LIMIT IDENTIFIABILITY OF CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The usability of theoretical methods from the viewpoint of practical accuracy of signal or data measurement is analyzed. It is shown that, in practice, measurements with absolute accuracy are not possible, and the problem of limit identifiability of systems is examined. The problem is treated of whether, at the given level of accuracy of measurement, it is possible to identify a ‚Ä≥sufficiently‚Ä≥ accurate model of the control system from the measured data.
Name: ["Stepan Jaromir"]

Title: EQUIVALENT FILTER IDENTIFICATION FROM AUTOCOVARIANCE ESTIMATES.
Abstract: From an experiment on a time-independent Gaussian process with rational spectrum, the equivalent (shaping) filter is identified. Measurement data are first reduced to an autocovariance estimate, and then filter parameter estimates, asymptotically equivalent to maximum likelihood estimates, are compared. Experimental results from simulated time series are given.
Name: ["Gerdin Krister"]

Title: ON-LINE ESTIMATION OF NON-LINEAR PROCESS PARAMETERS.
Abstract: An on-line sequential parameter estimation technique has been developed and applied to an experimental laboratory-scale chemical reactor system. The estimator is based upon a gradient method of minimizing the sum of squared errors, the objective being to cater for nonlinear systems. The gradient vector is multiplied by a modifying matrix to give a parameter adjustment vector, a suitable fraction of which is used to update the model parameters. Starting with steepest descent convergence given by a unit matrix, successive refinement of the modifying matrix leads to second-order hill-climbing and eventually to an exact correspondence with linear sequential least-squares filters.
Name: ["Jackson A.McN.", "Rippin D.W.T."]

Title: DESIGN AND CHARACTERIZATION OF OPTIMAL TEST SIGNALS FOR LINEAR SINGLE INPUT-SINGLE OUTPUT PARAMETER ESTIMATION.
Abstract: It is shown that the optimal test signal for linear single-input single-output parameter estimation is characterized by its autocorrelation function. This fact has been shown to lead to an efficient algorithm for test signal design. Furthermore, a procedure has been described for arriving at the most appropriate design criteria for any given ultimate use of the model.
Name: ["Goodwin G.C.", "Payne R.L."]

Title: ADAPTIVE MICROSCHEDULER FOR A MULTIPROGRAMMED COMPUTER SYSTEM.
Abstract: The objective of this paper is the description of the development and verification of a new, adaptive method of internal scheduling of resources, with the goal of the optimization of computer system performance. A general system effectiveness measure is defined which parametrically encompasses the prototypical system effectiveness measures to be considered. The adaptive internal scheduler then selects such tasks for resource allocation request fulfillment that a local system effectiveness measure, derived from the general measure, is optimized, leading to semioptimization of the general measure.
Name: ["Pass Edgar M.", "Gwynn John"]

Title: PARAMETRIC INSENSITIVITY AND CONTROLLED INVARIANCE.
Abstract: Parametric insensitivity of state and output trajectories of linear systems is approached by employing an analysis method recently developed for imbedding a large class of structural properties usually expressed in terms of matrices into a unitary geometric framework. Necessary and sufficient conditions useful for determining maximal state and output subspaces, where parameter insensitive trajectories range, are given. A procedure for the synthesis of controllers which discriminate the trajectories according to their insensitivity to various parameters is proposed. It is also shown that such controllers are consistent with completely arbitrary pole assignment.
Name: ["Bonivento C.", "Guidorzi R.", "Marro G."]

Title: ABOUT THE EVALUATION OF THE ERROR MADE WHEN REPRESENTING A LARGE SYSTEM BY A GIVEN-ORDER MODEL.
Abstract: The introduction of both notions of vectorial norms and overvaluing matrices for discrete nonlinear systems is considered. These properties lead to defining an estimator of the error between system and model. It is then necessary to examine different cases leading to an overvaluation of the vectorial norms of the error for linear or nonlinear systems considered under transient or operating conditions. The application of the identification method by assimilating the process to a lower-dimension system is considered for a nonlinear process under operating conditions.
Name: ["Borne P.", "Gentina J.C.", "Laurent F."]

Title: Heuristic Optimization Method Based on the Method of Calculation of Arguments by Sections. | [EIN HEURISTISCHES OPTIMIERUNGSVERFAHREN NACH DER METHODE DER GRUPPENWEISEN ARGUMENTSBERECHNUNG.]
Abstract: The usefulness of employing heuristic elements in computer programs for processing of extensive numerical problems is considered. A method proposed by A. G. Ivakhnenko for solving such problems by means of heuristic algorithms with perception analogous structure is described.
