The application of such an algorithm is illustrated by a novel solution procedure for extensive numerical optimization problems which is based on the method of calculation of arguments by sections.
Name: ["Krepler Karl"]

Title: ON THE SUBSTITUTION OF POLYNOMIAL FORMS.
Abstract: The problem of devising efficient algorithms for computing Q(x//1// prime . . . ,x//r// minus //1// prime P(x//1// prime . . . ,x//r// minus //1)) where P and Q are multivariate polynomials is considered. It is shown that for polynomials which are completely dense an algorithm based upon evaluation and interpolation is more efficient than Horner's method. Then various characterizations for sparse polynomials are made and the subsequent methods are re-analyzed. In conclusion a test is devised which takes only linear time to compute and by which a decision can automatically be made concerning whether to use a substitution algorithm which exploits sparsity or one which assumes relatively dense inputs. This choice yields the method which takes the fewest arithmetic operations.
Name: ["Horowitz Ellis"]

Title: COMPUTATIONAL EXPERIENCE WITH AN ALGORITHM FOR THE LOCK BOX PROBLEM.
Abstract: The lock box problem involves the location of post office boxes within a company's distribution area. Customer remittances are mailed to these boxes and the checks are processed by a local bank. The problem is to locate the boxes in a way that will minimize processing cost and the opportunity costs associated with the remittances while in transit. It is shown that the programming problem can be reduced for m zero-one variables, where m is the number of locations. Computational results are reported for problems involving up to 5050 variables.
Name: ["Bulfin R.L.", "Unger V.E."]

Title: DESIGN OF STATE ESTIMATOR FOR SYSTEMS ORIGINALLY DESCRIBED BY INPUT-OUPUT RELATION.
Abstract: An optimal filter is constructed for systems which are described by an input-output equation. It is shown that the steady-state optimal estimator, which is obtained simply from the system parameters, gives an exact value of the system state.
Name: ["Funahashi Y.", "Nakamura K."]

Title: MINIMAL REALIZATION AND APPOXIMATION OF LINEAR SYSTEMS FROM NORMAL OPERATING RECORDS.
Abstract: A method of identifying a minimal-order state model of a multivariable discrete process from the input-output data is presented. This realization is directly given as a canonical form. From the deterministic point of view, an identifiability condition is mentioned. Experimental results are reported.
Name: ["Barraud Alain", "de Larminat Philippe"]

Title: ADAPTIVE SYSTEM THEORY TODAY AND TOMORROW.
Abstract: The state-of-art in the theory of adaptive systems is summarized, relying on iterative learning algorithms. The outlook for further advances is given.
Name: ["Tsypkin Ya.Z."]

Title: DETERMINISTIC TYPE CONTROLLER FOR A CLASS OF UNCERTAIN PLANTS WITH PARTIAL IDENTIFICATION.
Abstract: A deterministic approach is presented for designing a two-level controller for a class of unknown, nonlinear, multi-input multi-output plants operating in an uncertain environment. / This approach employs the Liapunov synthesis procedure via the introduction of a vector, called ‚Ä≥the characteristic vector‚Ä≥ , which is the characteristics of the unknown plant and its environment. The system is expressed in the state-space form, with an unknown functional relationship, does not require an explicit knowledge of the plant or its uncertain ties, and the design approach may be viewed as a deterministic one. This bypasses some of the rigid restrictions of the stochastic control theory and the existing adaptive techniques.
Name: ["Nikiforuk P.N.", "Gupta M.M.", "Kanai K.", "Wagner L."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF NONLINEAR SYSTEMS THROUGH THE UTILISATION OF DISCONTINUOUS ORTHOGONAL FILTERS IN APPLYING A MULTILEVEL PSEUDORANDOM SIGNAL.
Abstract: A method is proposed which makes it possible to estimate the parameters of a model which approximates the nonlinear no-memory portion of the Hammerstein-type nonlinear memory system by discrete orthogonal Rademacher functions and the linear memory portion of the nonlinear memory system by discrete orthogonal Haar functions, by applying a multilevel, inversely repeated pseudorandom test signal.
Name: ["Sutek Lubomir", "Varga Miloslav"]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF TWO-LEVEL CONTROLLER FOR A CLASS OF LINEAR PLANTS IN AN UNKNOWN ENVIRONMENT.
Abstract: A deterministic design procedure for controlling a class of multivariable linear plants operating in an unknown environment is presented. Use is made of the concept of the 'two-level' controller. The design of the first-level, which operates in a feedforward mode, is a function of the given desired response characteristics of the plant. The design of the second-level, which operates in a conditional feedback mode, employs the Lyapunov type synthesis procedure and is independent of the plant parameters and its uncertainties. To cope with the plant uncertainties a measurable vector, which is characteristic of the plant's unknown environment and is called the 'characteristic vector', is introduced. The design procedure presented may be viewed as a deterministic approach, by-passing some of the rigid requirements of the stochastic control theory and adaptive techniques. It is illustrated by means of two hybrid simulated examples.
Name: ["Nikiforuk P.N.", "Gupta M.M.", "Kanai K.", "Wagner L."]

Title: Consistency of an Estimate of Tree-Dependent Probability Distributions
Abstract: We demonstrate in this correspondence that the procedure introduced by Chow and Liu for estimating tree-dependent probability distributions is consistent. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Chow C.K.", "Wagner T.J."]
Affiliations: ['IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center', 'University of Texas']

Title: TYPE TWO COMPUTATIONAL COMPLEXITY.
Abstract: A programming language for the partial computable functionals is used as the basis for a definition of the computational complexity of functionals (type2 functions). An axiomatic account in the spirit of Blum is then provided. The novel features of this approach are justified by applying it to problems in abstract complexity, specifically operator speed-up, and by using it to define the illusive notion of the polynomial degree of an arbitrary function. New results are obtained for these degrees.
Name: ["Constable Robert L."]

Title: CORRECT AND OPTIMAL IMPLEMENTATIONS OF RECURSION IN A SIMPLE PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE.
Abstract: The object of this paper is to study the mechanism of recursion in a simple, LISP-like programming language, where the only means of iteration is through recursion. The theory of computation developed in Scott provides the framework of our study. It is shown how the implementations of recursion which deserve to be called ‚Ä≥correct‚Ä≥ can be characterized semantically, and demonstrate a general criterion for the correctness of an implementation. An implementation of recursion is described which is both correct and optimal in a general class of sequential languages, and therefore constitutes an attractive alternative to both ‚Ä≥call-by-name‚Ä≥ and ‚Ä≥call-by-value‚Ä≥ .
Name: ["Vuillemin Jean"]

Title: A Path Entropy Function for Rooted Trees
Abstract: The class of rooted trees or arborescences used for modeling hierarchical classification and indexing procedures is considered. An entropy function measuring the complexity of the paths from the root to the terminal vertices is defined. Upper and lower bounds are found for the values of this function, and it is shown to be additive with respect to a tree product operation defined here. The results are extended to the case when the terminal vertices are weighted, and the path entropy function is compared to the information function defined by C. Picard for questionnaires. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Green C.D."]

Title: OPTIMAL LANDING FLARE CONTROL OF AIRCRAFTS WITH SENSITIVITY CONSIDERATION.
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to synthesize the final state of automatic flare control theoretically when the deviations of the mass and velocity from the reference values occur. An automatic closed-loop control system having characteristics of reduced sensitivity is presented which was designed only by measuring the altitude and rate of descent of aircraft. This reduced sensitivity system yielded satisfactory responses under the influence of parameter variations related to flight velocity and mass.
Name: ["Ohta Hirobumi", "Sugiura Ichiro"]

Title: SPECTRAL ANALYSIS OF A CLASS OF RANDOM SIGNALS.
Abstract: It is shown that the Theory of Distributions offers a powerful means of calculation in the study of random signals. The calculation of the mathematical expectation of the nonlinear function of a multidimensional random variable is considered, along with second-order S, random distributions as well as the spectum of a pulse train.
Name: ["Fortet Robert M."]

Title: PROBLEMS OF IDENTIFICATION IN METABOLIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The general problems of identification of metabolic systems in living organisms are considered, where the need is to derive mathematical models which not merely relate independent and dependent variables but also have structure and parameters corresponding to biological features. With the data available unique structure determination and parameters estimates may not be possible. Improved fitting methods are considered together with attempts at obtaining a more complete model specification.
Name: ["Carson E.R.", "Finkelstein L."]

Title: PROCESS FOR REDUCING CLUSTER REPRESENTATIONS AND RETRIEVAL COSTS.
Abstract: A clustered retrieval system is considered, in which documents are classified into homogeneous groups of clusters in order to optimize search efficiency. The documents are represented by a weighted term vector. The value of each component of a vector indicates the degree of contribution of that term to the content of the document. Each cluster of documents is identified by a ‚Ä≥centroid vector‚Ä≥ , the sum of the set of document vectors contained within the cluster. A reduction procedure is described which reveals the dominant features of the cluster by giving more importance to those terms exhibiting strong interrelationships within the clusters, reducing storage requirements and retrieval costs.
Name: ["Crouch Donald B."]

Title: EXTENDED POLYNOMIAL ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: It is shown that standard polynomial algorithms may be applied to a much wider class of functions by making a straightforward generalization of the concept of exponent. The implementation of a computer algebra system from a standard set of polynomial programs which allows for any coefficient or exponent structure is also discussed.
Name: ["Hearn Anthony C.", "Loos Rudiger G.K."]

Title: DECENTRALIZED CONTROL OF DISCRETE-TIME STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: This paper deals with an optimal control problem of a discrete-time linear stochastic system with two controllers, each of which can make certain noisy measurements of the state of the system. These two controllers cooperate in trying to minimize the same performance index. Certain constraints are imposed on the control structure, and so the problem is concerned with determining the optimal values of the structure parameters of the controllers. Both cases, with and without information exchange between the two controllers, are treated. Weak separability is introduced as an extended concept of the separation theorem and sufficient conditions for the problem to be weakly separable are obtained. The usefulness of the concept is illustrated by several numerical examples.
Name: ["Yoshikawa Tsuneo"]

Title: The dynamic clusters method and optimization in non hierarchical-clustering
Source: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
Abstract: Algorithms which are operationnally efficient and which give a good partition of a finite set, produce solutions that are not necessarily optimum. The main aim of this paper is a synthetical study of properties of optimality in spaces formed by partitions of a finite set. We formalize and take for a model of that study a family of particularily efficient techniques of ‚Äúclusters centers‚Äù type. The proposed algorithm operates on groups of points or ‚Äúkernels‚Äù; these kernels adapt and evolve into interesting clusters. After having developed the notion of ‚Äústrong‚Äù and ‚Äúweak‚Äù patterns, and the computer aspects, we illustrate the different results by an artificial example. ¬© 1973, Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Diday E."]

Title: TREATMENT OF BIAS IN THE SQUARE-ROOT INFORMATION FILTER/SMOOTHER.
Abstract: The Dyer-McReynolds square root information filter (see Engineering Index 1970 p 260 abstract 14106) is rederived, using recursive least squares arguments. The result is applied to a system composed partly of biases. The filter ‚Ä≥sensitivity‚Ä≥ matrix, ‚Ä≥computed‚Ä≥ covariance, and ‚Ä≥consider‚Ä≥ covariance for this augmented system are reviewed. A new computationally attractive representation for the smoothed estimates, in terms of a smoothed ‚Ä≥sensitivity‚Ä≥ matrix and a smoothed ‚Ä≥computed‚Ä≥ covariance is presented.
Name: ["Bierman G.J."]

Title: VEHICLE SCHEDULING ALGORITHM USING NON-SERIAL DISCRETE DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING WITH SPACE SHUTTLE APPLICATIONS.
Abstract: The development and operation of a vehicle scheduling algorithm is described. This algorithm has applications to the NASA problem of assigning payloads to space delivery vehicles. The algorithm is based on a discrete, integer-valued, non-serial, dynamic programming solution to the classical problem of developing resource utilization plans with limited resources. The algorithm places special emphasis on incorporating interpayload (precedence) relationships; maintaining optimal alternate schedule definitions (a unique feature of dynamic programming) in the event of contingencies (namely, resource inventory changes) without problem resolution; and, by using a special information storage technique, reducing the computational complexity of solving realistic problems. This information storage technique is demonstrated with a brief example. Reference is made to an operational computer program which solves the problem of assigning payloads to space delivery vehicles.
Name: ["Dupnick E."]

Title: SIMPLE METHOD FOR THE STEADY-STATE IDENTIFICATION OF 2nd ORDER NONLINEARITIES.
Abstract: In this paper a simple method for steady state identification of 2nd order nonlinear systems is considered. The algorithm processes the data on-line and the coefficients of static characteristics can be obtained simply by this algorithm in the case of uncorrelated input signals. The model obtained in such a way can be used for system optimization. On the basis of this method equipment can be made, facilitating appropriate structure estimation of steady state characteristics.
Name: ["Keviczky L.", "Banyasz Cs."]

Title: CONTROLLABILITY AND STABILIZABILITY OF DECENTRALIZED DYNAMIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Controllability and stabilizability of linear decentralized system are examined. The paper examines the manner in which controllable subspaces of local control agents are affected by the control action of the other agent, and applies the results to obtain several necessary and/or sufficient conditions for stabilizing decentralized systems by state feedback or by local output feedback signals. It is shown that an agent can maximize the region of stabilizability by minimizing the controllable subspace of the other agent by proper choice of his own control action. It is also shown that exchange of observation (and control) data and cooperation between agents are important in achieving system stabilization.
Name: ["Aoki M.", "Li M.T."]

Title: ANALYSIS AND ALGORITHM FOR A MINIMAX PROBLEM WITH THERMAL STRESS APPLICATIONS.
Abstract: In some industrial processes the control transients are accompanied by thermal transients which produce damaging thermal stresses in parts of the apparatus. The steam turbine start-up may be cited as an example of such a process. The need arises to schedule the control transients so that the resulting damage be minimized while the requirements of the process are met. This problem is analyzed in the case when the measure of damage is the maximum value of the thermal stress transient at a given location and the admissible controls are constrainted by two time-dependent limits. The system is assumed to be linear and time invariant with thermal stress selected at critical locations. The solution of the minimax problem is obtained for systems whose impulse response function of thermal stress satisfies certain conditions common in thermoelastic problems. The proof of the method of solution and an example of application are also given.
Name: ["Rednarski Stanislaw", "Shen C.N."]

Title: BRANCHING FLOW OF FAILURES IN A CONTROL SYSTEM WITH RANDOM INPUT ACTIONS.
Abstract: A form of failures that are encountered in complex control systems is considered. This form is expressed in an increased-frequency sequence of failures of one type; it is established that in each such sequence the first failure generates all the subsequent ones under certain random input actions. Two models of the flow of failures which allow for the specific features of the failures described above are proposed. Results of statistical processing of actual failure flows in control systems are given.
Name: ["Sobolev Yu.Ya.", "Solyanik B.L.", "Yastrebenetskii M.A."]

Title: EFFICIENCY MODEL FOR COMPLEX RESTORABLE SYSTEMS.
Abstract: An efficiency model is proposed for complex restorable systems that allows for the sequence of appearance of failures in an ensemble of malfunctioning elements. The model generalizes the Markov ‚Ä≥death and birth‚Ä≥ scheme. An estimate is derived for the system efficiency on the basis of the resultant characteristics of the stochastic process.
Name: ["Peterson E.Ya.", "Ettinger B.Ya."]

Title: COMPARISON OF VARIOUS REALIZATIONS OF GRADIENT AND STATISTICAL GRADIENT METHODS.
Abstract: The systematic estimation error for the gradient of a function to be optimized is introduced. Gradient and statistical gradient methods are compared in terms of a criterion that is independent of the number of determinations of the function to be optimized. It is shown that when a paired trial is used it is possible to obtain unbiased gradient estimates in not just a linear field.
Name: ["Talalai A.M."]

Title: RANDOM DELAYS IN OPTIMAL CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The analysis and optimization of sampled-data control systems with randomly delayed control signals are considered. Two classes of random delays are studied: Non-integer random delays that are smaller than the sampling interval, and integer delays, with perfect or delayed information about the delays, where the latter are multiples of the sampling interval. Recursive formulas for the calculation of the optimal control laws are given. Several classes of statistically dependent delays are treated, e. g. sequence delays, where control signals form a queue and are released simultaneously.
Name: ["Davidson Charles"]

Title: FAULT DETECTION AND RECOVERY IN A MULTI-PROCESSOR CONTROL SYSTEM.
Abstract: Principles of achieving reliability in a shared resource system are discussed. Fault detection in the Mark II multiprocessor system is described, along with CPU action after fault detection. Experience gained is reported.
Name: ["Nissen J.", "Owen G."]

Title: OPTIMAL DECISION PROCEDURES FOR FINITE MARKOV CHAINS - 3. GENERAL CONVEX SYSTEMS.
Abstract: This paper is concerned with the general problem of finding an optimal transition matrix for a finite Markov chain, where the probabilities for each transition must be chosen from a given convex family of distributions. The immediate cost is determined by this choice, but it is required to minimize the average expected cost in the long run. The problem is investigated by classifying the states according to the accessibility relations between them. If an optimal policy exists, it can be found by considering the convex subsystems associated with the states of different levels in the classification scheme.
Name: ["Bather John"]

Title: TERNARY POSITIONAL AUTOMATIC CONTROL SYSTEM.
Abstract: A position automatic control system using a stepping motor, ternary variables and ternary coded feedback is studied. It is shown that ternary driving of a stepping motor increases resolution over the same motor with binary driving. Comparative study of parallel and serial error detectors is presented including comments on the tolerances allowed for threshold gates.
Name: ["Moraga Claudio", "Bittner Alberto"]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR THE RESOLUTION OF PULSE SIGNALS.
Abstract: A pulse resolution algorithm is described that has marked advantages over an algorithm based on the classical ‚Ä≥valley‚Ä≥ test. A method is given for calculating the operating characteristics of a system that embodies the suggested method.
Name: ["Vasil'yev N.G.", "Ovsyannikov V.A.", "Smolyanskiy B.Ye."]

Title: EVALUATING COMPUTING SYSTEM CHANGES BY MEANS OF REGRESSION MODELS.
Abstract: This paper describes how a regression model of the Research Center's APL system was constructed and used for evaluating system changes. A model is developed which shows that the size of the workspace, but not the number of workspaces in core, significantly affects the performance of the Research Center's system. In particular, the model indicates that increasing the workspace size from 5 to 7 tracks causes 11 percent of all requests to be degraded by at least 0. 4 seconds under mean load conditions.
Name: ["Waldbaum Gerald"]

Title: OPTIMAL BALANCING OF I/O REQUESTS TO SECTOR SCHEDULED DRUMS.
Abstract: The problem of optimally balancing the total load on a memory hierarchy consisting of sector scheduled or ‚Ä≥slotted‚Ä≥ drums is analyzed by applying Kuhn-Tucker optimization techniques to a set of queueing theoretic models. The results are of interest in cases where it is possible to control the relative load on each device in a hierarchy by physically relocating data files or by altering the backing store management policy used in a virtual memory system.
Name: ["Buzen Jeffrey P."]

Title: Solutions of the singular stochastic regulator problem
Source: Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement and Control, Transactions of the ASME
Abstract: The limiting form of the optimum stochastic regulator is determined which minimizet the steady-state expectation, E<sub>a</sub>(x‚Ä≤Qx + u‚Ä≤Ru), for the linear process, x = Ax + Bu + Gv, given noisy observations y = Hx + w (with v and w being independent white noise processes) when either the control weighting matrix, R, or the spectral density matrix, W, of the observation noise, w, is singular. It is shown that as R tende from a positive-definite matrix to a non-negative definite matrix, the optimum regulator can be synthesized by a system using at most n ‚Äî ks integrators, where n is the order of the system and ks equals the rank of B minus the rank of BR. Similarly, when IP tends from a positive-definite matrix to a non-negative definite matrix, the optimum regulator can sometimes be synthesized by a system using at most n ‚Äî rs integratori where rs equals the rank of H minus the rank of WH. The structure of the regulator is given for each of these cases. ¬© 1973 by ASME.
Name: ["Hutton M.F."]

Title: APL MODELS FOR OPERATIONAL PLANNING OF SHIPMENT ROUTING, LOADING, AND SCHEDULING.
Abstract: A vehicle routing algorithm with an imbedded loading heuristic and movement simulation was developed to provide the interactive capability to plan shipment delivery and returns. The vehicle movement model is a small discrete event fixed interval simulation that uses the APL operators to keep track of loading facility status, truck location, etc. for scheduling purposes. The models operate in a field environment, but are linked to centralized planning models and data bases. They are illustrative of APL's almost unique ability to combine simulation modeling with operational restrictions such as interactive operation by non-programmers.
Name: ["Cuthbert Richard D.", "Peckham Larry"]

Title: HANDWRITTEN CHINESE CHARACTER RECOGNITION BY AN ANALYSIS-BY-SYNTHESIS METHOD.
Abstract: A method for handwritten Chinese character recognition is based on the fact that a Chinese character can be drawn as a sequence of a few types of fundamental strokes and that each stroke in a handwritten Chinese character can also be described in terms of a fairly simple model of penpoint movement during handwriting. The system was tested by computer simulation using a total of 1000 handwritten Chinese characters, the correct recognition rate was 82. 4 per cent.
Name: ["Yoshida Makoto", "Eden Murray"]

Title: ON THE REALIZATION OF AN OPTIMAL DECISION RULE BY MEANS OF A HIERARCHIAL SYSTEM.
Abstract: The realization of a best approximation of an unknown optimal decision rule by means of a self-learning hierarchical system is discussed. This optimization implies the simultaneous use of adaptive estimation and classification techniques. An unsupervised learning discrete algorithm based on stochastic approximation theory is proposed as a solution to this problem. Some applications are suggested, particularly in the field of modeling of static and dynamic nonlinear relationships. Numerical results are given.
Name: ["Do-Tu H.", "Installe M."]

Title: ARCHITECTURE OF VIRTUAL MACHINES.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: A model is developed which represents the mapping and addressing of resources by a process executing on a virtual machine. By deriving properties of the model, one can clarify and contrast existing virtual machine systems. However, the most important result of the model is that its proper interpretation implies the Hardware Virtualizer as the direct natural implementation of the virtual machine model. Some of the characteristics of the Hardware Virtualizer are developed and then the operation illustrated through the use of a concrete example.
Name: ["Goldberg R.P."]

Title: Optimization of the Compression Characteristic of Speech Signal Samples in Pulse Code Modulation Systems. | OPTYMALIZACJA CHARAKTERYSTYKI KOMPRESJI PROBEK SYGNALOW MOWY W SYSTEMACH MODULACJI IMPULSOWO-KODOWEJ.
Abstract: The optimization of segmented compression characteristics is considered. A minimum value of the ratio of the mean signal power to the mean power of the quantization distortion in a given interval of the effective signal value is used as an index of the quality of the compression characteristic. The quality index reaches the maximum value for the optimal characteristic. A calculation method of the parameters of the optimal characteristic is given. A method of the estimation of the accuracy of the optimal solution is also presented.
Name: ["Dobrogowski Andrzej"]

Title: IDENTIFIABILITY OF THE OPTIMAL CONTROL MODEL FOR THE HUMAN OPERATOR.
Abstract: An important problem in manual control concerns the identification of human operator model parameters from measured data. The identifiability properties of the optimal control model structure for the human operator is considered.
Name: ["Phatak A.V.", "Weinert H.L."]

Title: CONVERGENCE PROPERTIES OF OPTIMAL CONTROL ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: The convergence of optimal control algorithms in the sense of control measures is studied, and it is shown, as a corollary, that most optimal control algorithms construct sequences of controls which always converge in cost to a local minimum.
Name: ["Williamson L.", "Polak E."]

Title: CLOSED LOOP CONTROL DESIGN FOR NONLINEAR, NONQUADRATIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The problem of optimal control of a nonlinear system with non quadratic final cost function admits a closed-loop suboptimal solution by approximation of the Lyapunov function by means of the control-equivalent Gaussian sum method. Using the duality between optimal control for deterministic systems and estimation for stochastic systems, the solution is presented as the superposition of solutions of linear subsystems.
Name: ["Dajani M.Z.", "Campion G."]

Title: INTERACTIVE GRAPHICS SYSTEM FOR ANALYSIS OF BUSINESS DECISIONS.
Abstract: An experimental system is described that enables the user, through an intelligent graphics terminal, to construct, modify, analyze, and store decision trees. With this system, business decisions under uncertainty can be analyzed. This paper discusses the system and its capabilities. A brief discussion of decision analysis is included, which represents an aspect of financial modeling. A detailed description of the system command structure is appended.
Name: ["Ravin J.", "Schatzoff M."]

Title: AUTOMATIC MODEL GENERATION AND RECOGNITION OF SIMPLE THREE DIMENSIONAL BODIES.
Abstract: A new approach to picture recognition is described that works where the lighting condition is not ideal, and the background may have no strong contrast to the objects.
Name: ["Nagao Makoto", "Hashimoto Shigeo", "Sakai Toshiyuki"]

Title: EASY VIRTUAL MEMORY TECHNIQUE FOR DATA.
Abstract: An easily implemented virtual memory algorithm for data is described. Its utility and limitations in computer simulation problems are illustrated with examples. Criteria for selection of core buffer size and arrangement of data on the virtual memory device are discussed. The algorithm may be coded in FORTRAN for any computer having a block addressable random access peripheral memory device and has been successfully used on a Varian 620/L with LINC tapes.
Name: ["Amstutz Larry I."]

Title: REDUCED ORDER FILTERING WITH APPLICATIONS IN HYBRID NAVIGATION.
Source: IEEE Electron and Aerosp Syst Conv, Rec
Abstract: The Kalman filter has gained wide acceptance as the best algorithm for mixing data in multisensor navigation systems. Implementation of the Kalman filter for high order dynamic systems, however, often requires excessive real time computer capacity. In this paper an algorithm is presented for a class of suitably constrained reduced-order filters which minimizes the variance of the estimated variables. The algorithm generates both the filter gain history and the true estimation error covariance. The algorithm is illustrated with a multisensor navigation system example involving the mixing of beacon range and range-rate data with a high quality inertial system. The effect of several alternate filter state selections on navigation accuracy is examined in detail.
Name: ["D'Appolito Joseph A.", "Roy Kenneth"]

Title: STRICT DETERMINISTIC VERSUS LR(O) PARSING.
Abstract: The authors introduce part of a more general theory called ‚Ä≥characteristic LR(k) parsing‚Ä≥ . This actually produces parsers which are tuned to the characteristics of a particular family of grammars. The theory is applied to the family of strict deterministic grammars and the result is parsers which are as fast as canonical LR(k) parsers although they are substantially smaller.
Name: ["Geller Matthew M.", "Harrison Michael A."]

Title: STOCHASTIC MODEL OF FLOW VERSUS CONCENTRATION APPLIED TO TRAFFIC ON HILLS.
Abstract: A deterministic model is extended by allowing a probabilistic distribution of concentrations for a given mean value of flow. The specific application is to traffic proceeding up a two-lane hill.
Name: ["Soyster A.L.", "Wilson G.R."]

Title: CALCULATION OF DERIVATIVES IN EXTREMUM PROBLEMS.
Abstract: An algorithm is presented for generating a program for computing values of functions and the matrix of their partial derivatives for an arbitrary system of functions that is represented as a decomposition of differentiable conditionally elementary operations. The effectiveness of the resultant program is predetermined by the possibility of taking account of the degree of ‚Ä≥connectedness‚Ä≥ of the functions in the system, the use of the notion of ‚Ä≥conjugate‚Ä≥ process, and the utilization of the library principle of programming. A specific example is used to consider the application of the algorithm and to evaluate its effectiveness.
Name: ["Ostrovskii G.M.", "Borisov V.V.", "Volin Yu.M."]

Title: Pen direction sequences in character recognition
Abstract: A descriptive, generative model of the pen direction sequences measured during the hand drawing of characters is shown to be useful in recognition. Preprocessing and classification procedures are based on the properties of the model. Results are presented from tests with a realization of these methods as a real time recognition system running in a small computer. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Michael Powers V."]

Title: ON THE PROBABILITY OF DEADLOCK IN COMPUTER SYSTEMS.
Abstract: As the number of processes and resources increases within a computer system, does the probability of that system's being in deadlock increase or decrease? To answer this question, Probabilistic Automata are introduced as a model of computer systems. This allows investigation of the above question for various scheduling algorithms. A theorem is proven which indicates that, within the types of systems considered, the probability of deadlock increases.
Name: ["Ellis Clarence A."]

Title: Parameter Identification in Linear Distributed Parameter Systems
Abstract: Perturbation analysis is used to identify unknown but constant parameters in a linear distributed parameter system. Noisy observations are assumed to be available at a finite number of spatial locations. A numerical example is solved to illustrate the proposed method. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Bhagavan B.K.", "Nardizzi L.R."]
Affiliations: [' SMU Institute of Technology', ' SMU Institute of Technology']

Title: Critical Notes on the Box and Jenkins Method for the Prediction of Nonstationary Stochastic Processes. | [UWAGI KRYTYCZNE O METODZIE BOXA I JENKINSA PREDYKCJI NIESTACJONARNYCH PROCESOW STOCHASTYCZNYCH.]
Abstract: The method given by G. E. P. Box and G. M. Jenkins of one-step-ahead prediction, optimal for a certain class of nonstationary univariate discrete-in-time stochastic processes (containing in particular stationary processes) is described. Critical notes on the method, concerning its computer implementation, are presented.
Name: ["Halicki Henryk"]

Title: NEW METHOD FOR THE FAST COMPUTING OF THE FREQUENCY CHARACTERISTIC OF CONTROL SYSTEM.
Abstract: The new computing method determines the approximate frequency function from the step response function, using the fewest possible points of the time function to get one point of the frequency function. The transformation formulae give the best approximation in the so-called middle frequency range belonging to the environment of the minus 180 degree phase shift, which is the most important part for the design. With the help of this fast computing method the real-time stability-checking of the control system can be performed.
Name: ["Frigyes A.", "Langer L."]

Title: OPTIMAL SOFTWARE TEST PLANNING THROUGH AUTOMATED NETWORK ANALYSIS.
Abstract: This paper describes an automated method for designing an optimal set of test cases which exercise all branches in the source code of the user's software modules. The method has been impleted for FORTRAN source code and is operational on NASA/JSC's Univac 1108 Exec II System. The paper defines ideal criteria for verification, demonstrates the impracticality of attempting to exercise every path, and arrives at a practical, measurable objective: to find the minimum set of paths which exhaustively exercise all logical branches in the module.
Name: ["Krause Kurth W.", "Smith R.W.", "Goodwin M.A."]

Title: GENERALIZED SYSTEM FOR COMPUTER ASSISTED DIAGNOSIS.
Abstract: An interactive computer assisted diagnostic system based on Bayesian analysis and implemented on a small time sharing computer is described. The system accepts any diagnosis problem for which the classes, features, and class conditional probabilities can be defined either by training samples or a priori medical knowledge. The system is updatable so that confirmed test cases can refine the conditional probabilities. 10 refs.
Name: ["Hardigg Jack B.", "Vaughan Randall B.", "Shen Leon Y.L."]

Title: DIGITAL ADAPTIVE MODEL FOLLOWING CONTROL.
Abstract: Development of an implementable digital adaptive control system requires a control law that can be efficiently adjusted during system operation and on identification algorithm that is capable of supplying parameter estimates at an accuracy and rate specified by the controller characteristics. To this effect a control law has been derived based upon the minimization of a single stage weighted combination of the squared error between the states of a linear plant and model and the control energy. To illustrate the utility of such a control law, its application in an adaptive mode to typical linearized lateral aircraft dynamics is currently being considered.
Name: ["Alag G.", "Rondot J.", "Kaufman H."]

Title: SIMULATION APPLIED TO THE SYSTEMS ANALYSIS OF ENGINEERING PROBLEMS.
Abstract: Engineers involved in the design and analysis of complex systems can use computer simulation as a systems analysis and synthesis tool. Discrete event simulation, coupled with dynamic display while the model runs on the computer, and where the user can dynamically interact with the simulation, provides new opportunities for systems insight. One higher order simulation language, GPSS, is used as a base, to which are added data bases, human interactivity, display graphics, and a high order continuous simulation language, CSMP.
Name: ["Reitman Julian"]

Title: PROBABILISTIC PROPERTIES OF R-AUTOMATA FOR ADAPTIVE GENERATION OF RANDOM-SEARCH PARAMETERS.
Abstract: Adaptive generation of the parameters of random-search algorithms by using R-automata with purposeful behavior is considered. The behavior is described by a random-walk process with absorption. Probability characteristics for the operation of these automata are obtained for stationary and nonstationary random media. Simple asymptotic formulas are obtained for these characteristics.
Name: ["Meleshko V.I."]

Title: APPROACH TO MULTI-VALUED SEQUENTIAL LOGIC.
Abstract: A new family of multi-valued memory devices based on a unique set of multi-valued logic operators is presented. The devices are compared to binary memory elements (flip-flops). Synthesis of the memory devices from the set of operators is demonstrated. Operation of the devices is discussed in detail and the devices are shown to be hazard-free during the clocking operation. The set of operators which form the basis for the memory devices is shown to be a sufficient set of operators and thereby is proven to form a multi-valued algebra. Techniques in the design of multi-valued sequential circuits are discussed and examples presented.
Name: ["Irving T.A.", "Nagle H.T."]

Title: ANALYTIC MODEL OF THE HASP EXECUTION TASK MONITOR.
Abstract: The HASP Execution Task Monitor periodically rearranges the OS/360 dispatching chain to give tasks pre-emptive execution priority in inverse order to their CPU utilization history. This paper develops a simple model of the Execution Task Monitor and employs it to study the effectiveness of the monitor in improving system performance. A modified strategy for monitor control is postulated and investigated for the case of task execution in memory of varying speed.
Name: ["Strauss Jon C."]

Title: REASONS FOR ROBOTS.
Abstract: The advantages of robots, especially for use in applications involving high temperature, dust, toxic atmospheres or other hostile environments, are reviewed. Cost factors in robot selection are also evaluated.
Name: ["Heginbotham W.B."]

Title: INFORMATION PATTERNS AND CLASSES OF STOCHASTIC CONTROL LAWS.
Abstract: A discussion of the possible information patterns and the corresponding classes of control laws in stochastic control is presented. The emphasis is on the utilization of past, and mainly, future measurement information. Since the control is restricted to be causal, the only information about the future measurements available to the controller is the future measurement program and the associated statistics. It is shown that the utilization of this type of information distinguishes a stochastic closed-loop controller from a stochastic feedback controller. The ‚Ä≥probing‚Ä≥ and ‚Ä≥caution‚Ä≥ properties that appear in stochastic control problems are discussed. It is pointed out that, when the dual effect is present, a closed-loop type controller has the feature of being actively adaptive: by probing the system, it can reduce the existing uncertainties. The concepts underlying the recently developed closed-loop type control algorithm for nonlinear systems are briefly reviewed.
Name: ["Tse E.", "Bar-Shalom Y."]

Title: Rule-oriented methods in problem solving
Abstract: A heuristic, in the usual sense and certainly in the sense that this term is used in this paper, is a rough guide or principle, or underlying knowledge which is not expressed explicitly. Heuristic methods for solving problems can involve the incorporation of such knowledge into algorithms. This paper describes two methods for finding the solution to problems using heuristic methods. A solution to a problem is represented by a sequence of operators which transpose one problem situation to another. Problems are categorized into four types: reversible regular, irreversible regular, reversible irregular and irreversible irregular problems. The rule-oriented method described were is useful particularly for the reversible regular problems to which heuristic knowledge is applicable. Some examples of the application of heuristics are shown in solving the Missionary-and-Cannibal problem and the Tower-of-Hanoi problem. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Shimura M.", "George F.H."]

Title: INCREASE OF CLOSED-LOOP NOMINAL TRAJECTORY LIKELIHOOD IN UNCERTAIN SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The paper examines how trajectory sensitivity with respect to small perturbations in initial states and plant parameters is affected by using a control implemented as a feedback rather than as the nominally equivalent open-loop control. The uncertainty in initial state x//o and plant parameter q is modeled by jointly normally distributed random variables. Two examples are presented. The first helps visualize the geometrical concepts introduced, while the second is related to a third order system, and illustrates the potential disadvantage of feedback control.
Name: ["Hontoir Y.", "Cruz Jr. J.B."]

Title: MULTILAYERED STOCHASTIC LANGUAGES FOR PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: For obtaining complex and effective descriptions in the problems of pattern recognition, the multilayered stochastic languages, accepted by stochastic automaton with criterion of functioning, are proposed. A method of constructing CF-stochastic grammar generating the considered languages is discussed.
Name: ["Dimitrov Vladimir"]

Title: NUMERICAL ALGORITHMS FOR THE IDENTIFICATION OF SYSTEMS, VIA SPLINES.
Abstract: The identification of linear systems is considered as a problem involving a solution of an ill-posed linear equation. General conditions are given for the regularization of this problem. A numerical solution is obtained in the subspace of cubic splines.
Name: ["Caprihan Arvind"]

Title: APPLICATION OF GENERALIZED SENSITIVITY FUNCTIONS IN ESTIMATING THE REAL-TIME COMPUTATIONAL EXPENSE NECESSARY FOR STABILIZING THE DYNAMICS OF DRIFTING PARAMETER PLANTS BY PROCESS COMPUTER.
Abstract: The relation between the real-time computational expense of the control algorithm and the obtained stabilization of plant dynamics is studied. With this, one assumes a linear nonadaptive control algorithm and a linearizable minimal phase low-pass plant with slowly drifting parameters. In order to obtain practical results, generalized expense and sensitivity indices are introduced. By using suitable approximations for the plant and subsystem functions in time and frequency domain as well as a generalized frequency domain sensitivity function one carries out system synthesis by means of which the generalized indices are numerically related. The method is described and a numerical example is given.
Name: ["Rudolph H."]

Title: SPACE-TIME PROCESSING FOR OPTIMAL PARAMETER ESTIMATION.
Abstract: It is claimed that a great deal of attention has been devoted in recent years to the problem of detecting random space, i. e. , time signals such as those presented to a passive sonar array. The structure and performance capabilities of the optimum detector have been determined and compared with those of suboptimal configurations attractive from the point of view of implementation. This paper deals with the second stage of the signal processing problem, the extraction of information concerning parameter such as bearing and range.
Name: ["Bangs William J.", "Schultheiss Peter M."]

Title: RECURSIVE ESTIMATION OF THE STATES AND THEIR HIGHER ORDER MOMENTS IN NONLINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The problem of determining the minimum mean squared unbiased estimates of the states of a system from noisy measurement data is studied. The conditional probability density of these states is first written as a truncated Gram-Charlier series and, secondly, as the sum of a finite number of Gaussian-like densities. The orthogonal polynomials associated with each of these densities as kernels are derived, and the nonlinear functions are expanded in these polynomials. Retaining terms up to second order in this expansion, recursive algorithms are derived for the state estimates and their second-, third-, and fourth-order moments.
Name: ["Ramani N.", "Balasubramanian R."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF DISTRIBUTED PARAMETERS.
Abstract: A method specially designed for the off-line estimation of distributed parameters in distributed systems, based upon the use of modern control theory in function spaces, is presented. The nonquadratic cost function is minimized by a standard gradient method. Practical application of this method is illustrated by several examples.
Name: ["Chavent G."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF PROCESS DYNAMICS IN THE GLASS INDUSTRY.
Abstract: Two case studies are presented on the application of modern process identification and parameter estimation techniques in the glass industry. In the first example, the dynamics of a glass forming machine are identified using generalized least squares method, and, in the second case, the dynamics of a glass melting process are identified by using analog computer (experimental) technique. The results are compared with those produced by maximum likelihood method. The process models obtained are used to compute the control laws which are then used to set up the controllers.
Name: ["Raja Rao B.V.", "Mather J.", "Lyons B.D."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF PARAMETER AND STATE INSENSITIVE FEEDBACK SYSTEMS WITH CONSTRAINTS BASED ON PIECEWISE CONSTANT LINEAR CONTROL LAWS.
Abstract: Linear time-invariant plants with given differential equations and constraints are considered. A synthesis procedure (based on applying piecewise constant linear control laws) was recently described. The resulting nonlinear feedback systems are suboptimal with respect to a quadratic performance index and can be realized more easily than optimal systems. Now it is shown that it is possible to increase the insensitivity of these systems with respect to parameter and state uncertainty by minimizing suitable simple cost functions for every piecewise applied linear control law.
Name: ["Kiendl Harro D."]

Title: SELECTION PROCESSES AND THEIR RELATION TO AUTOMATA.
Abstract: It is shown that a finite selection transducer can be defined to generate syntactically correct sentences when the selection process is applied to the underlying selection. The pushdown selection and the pushdown selection transducer which is a generator of correct sentences of any context-free language are then defined. Such a device could be used to build an interactive incremental editor-compiler for context free languages with the insurance that the output statements are syntactically correct and parsed.
Name: ["LeBeux Pierre"]

Title: NEIGHBORHOOD SEARCH ALGORITHMS FOR FINDING OPTIMAL TRAVELING SALESMAN TOURS MUST BE INEFFICIENT.
Abstract: This article shows that any exact neighborhood search algorithm for the Traveling Salesman Problem must inspect a prohibitively large number of feasible solutions. Authors begin with a brief discussion of the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) and neighborhood search techniques. They develop a necessary condition for neighborhood search to converge to an optimal solution. They use this result to obtain a lower bound on the effectiveness of neighborhood search as applied to the TSP.
Name: ["Weiner P.", "Savage S.L.", "Bagchi A."]

Title: PLANT-ADAPTIVE PULSE - FREQUENCY MODULATED CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A state-dependent identifier compatible with the pulse-frequency modulator has been developed and applied to the real-time, on-line adaptive control of a pulse-frequency modulated feedback system whose slowly-varying parameters have been estimated at discrete time instants from plant impulse response with the aid of a dual-function controller.
Name: ["Broughton M.Blythe"]

Title: ON INPUT SIGNAL SYNTHESIS FOR LINEAR DISCRETE-TIME SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The problem of how to generate optimal input signal series for the identification of linear discrete-time systems in order to improve the accuracy of the estimate is investigated. The determinant of the covariance matrix is considered as a measure of the error in the parameter estimate. Very simple methods are suggested for the minimization of these criteria in the case of an amplitude-constrained input signal.
Name: ["Keviczky L.", "Banyasz Cs."]

Title: CONVERGENCE PROPERTIES OF THE GENERALIZED LEAST SQUARES IDENTIFICATION METHOD.
Abstract: Convergence properties of the generalized least squares method are analyzed. The method can be interpreted as optimization of a likelihood function. The number of local maximum points of the likelihood function is examined and it is shown that it is influenced by the signal to noise ratio. The theoretical results are illustrated by numerical examples. Plant measurements as well as simulated systems are used.
Name: ["Soderstrom Torsten"]

Title: ON SENSITIVITY REDUCTION IN NONLINEAR FEEDBACK SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The satisfaction of a well known sufficient condition for sensitivity reduction by use of feedback, is shown to imply severe restrictions on the feedback control law, and also on the weighting matrix in the integral-square criterion for closed-loop sensitivity reduction.
Name: ["Kreindler Eliezer", "Jameson Antony"]

Title: CLASSIFICATION OF CORN ODOR BY STATISTICAL ANALYSIS OF GAS CHROMATOGRAPHIC PATTERNS OF HEADSPACE VOLATILES
Abstract: At present corn is graded organoleptically into ‚Äúnormal‚Äù and various ‚Äúoff‚Äêodor‚Äù categories. The possibility of classifying corn odor on the basis of gas chromatographic patterns of headspace volatiles was studied using 60 samples of corn and statistical step‚Äêwise discriminant and regression analyses. Three options for subdividing the patterns into variables and several transformations for quantitation of peak areas were explored. To obtain optimum odor classification, five to seven gas chromatographic features were necessary. When applied to additional samples, classification at an error probability P < 0.05 (above 95% confidence level) was obtained for some statistical models. Thus, an objective system is feasible for classification of grain odor. Copyright ¬© 1973, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved
Name: ["DRAVNIEKS A.", "REILICH H.G.", "WHITFIELD J.", "WATSON C.A."]
Affiliations: [' IIT Research Institute', 'USDA Grain Marketing Research Center']

Title: ON A STUDY OF STABILITY AND SENSITIVITY OF LARGE CONTINUOUS NON-LINEAR SYSTEMS UNDER UNCERTAINTY.
Abstract: Essential properties whose trajectories encompass the process trajectory are defined. A method is proposed which leads to defining the notions of pseudo-overvaluing and pseudo-undervaluing matrices related to a system of nonlinear differential equations. The characteristic properties of such mathematical tools are studied. The choice of various norms brings out spectral properties of these pseudo-overvaluing matrices and defines their structure. This yields a sufficient condition of global asymptotic stability for nonlinear continuous systems. Illustrative examples are included.
Name: ["Gentina J.C.", "Borne P.", "Laurent F."]

Title: RECOVERY SEMANTICS FOR A DB/DC SYSTEM.
Abstract: A unified, systematic view of integrity/recovery is presented as it relates to a data-processing system, whether man, machine, or both.
Name: ["Davies Jr. Charles T."]

Title: TOOL FOR AUTOMATIC PROGRAM RESTRUCTURING.
Abstract: A tool, called LOCALIZER, which improves the locality of programs for multiprogrammed virtual-memory computer systems, is described. The method of critical working sets, which is the basis of the tool, is presented. This method is especially suitable for those systems where primary memory is managed according to the working set strategy. The various modules of the tool are briefly described after a discussion of the general restructuring procedure.
Name: ["Ferrari Domenico"]

Title: SETS THAT DON'T HELP.
Abstract: This paper contains several results yielding pairs of problems which do not help each other's solution, and therefore which may be said to be complex for ‚Ä≥different reasons.‚Ä≥ Statements are formalized and results proved within Blum complexity theory, generalized to relative algorithms. The approach is fairly intuitive.
Name: ["Lynch Nancy", "Meyer Albert", "Fischer Michael"]

Title: CANONICAL STRUCTURES IN THE IDENTIFICATION OF MULTIVARIABLE SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The role of state-space canonical (block-companion) representations in the structural and parametric identification of linear multivariable systems is investigated. Unitary algorithms for the identification of these systems are proposed. Their main advantages are that they can operate on quite general input/output sequences and lead to canonical state-space representations; moreover, the initial state of the system needs not to be zero or known and can be easily estimated. A consistent extension to the case of uncorrelated zero-mean additive noise is also reported.
Name: ["Guidorzi Roberto P."]

Title: MODELING A PARTICULAR CLASS OF MULTIPLE-INPUT/MULTIPLE-OUTPUT BLACK BOXES WITH STOCHASTIC INTEGRAL EQUATIONS AND IDENTIFYING THE REQUIRED PARAMETERS.
Abstract: A method is given for obtaining a mathematical model of a class of black boxes having multiple inputs and multiple outputs in terms of Ito stochastic integral equations. This method is applicable to the class of black boxes having ergodic correlation functions when there is zero applied input. The point of view adopted in this paper is phenomenological in that it is desired that calculations made using the mathematical model should be ‚Ä≥close‚Ä≥ to what is actually observed at the output of the black box.
Name: ["Eyman Earl D.", "Kerr Thomas H.", "Loh Nan K."]

Title: DESIGN OF OPTIMAL LOW-SENSITIVITY FEEDBACK CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A control system of low sensitivity to changes in the plant parameters is considered. The requirement of dynamic property stability is met by introducing the functions of the plant sensitivity relative to a certain parameter vector into the quadratic functional of performance. The optimal synthesis problem is solved with due regard to the specifics of initial conditions for sensitivity functions. Allowance for zero initial conditions of the sensitivity function led to an optimal control law in a form that its implementation does not require the knowledge of current values of the plant sensitivity functions.
Name: ["Yanushevsky R.T."]

Title: MULTIDIMENSIONAL INDUSTRIAL PLANT IDENTIFICATION.
Abstract: A comprehensive identification procedure to be applied to complex industrial plants with a number of input variables and an ‚Ä≥input-output‚Ä≥ relation of a type unknown in advance is proposed. In this procedure, the informative input variables are selected by extremum grouping algorithms. To construct a static model, piecewise approximation algorithms are developed. A possible way of using the procedure for studying dynamic properties of the plant is outlined. The results of three practical solutions are given.
Name: ["Dorofeyuk A.A.", "Kasavin A.D.", "Torgovitsky I.Sh."]

Title: ON THE OPTIMAL EVALUATION OF A SET OF BILINEAR FORMS.
Abstract: Although general theories are beginning to emerge in the area of automata based complexity theory, there are very few general methods or even general problem formulations in the area of arithmetic complexity. This paper proposes and defends a general model for studying bilinear multiplication in order to provide a common framework for discussing a wide class of problems.
Name: ["Brockett Roger W.", "Dobkin David"]

Title: NEW INTERPRETATIONS AND JUSTIFICATIONS FOR WORST CASE MIN-MAX DESIGN OF LINEAR CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Certain equivalences between a stochastic control problem and a zero-sum differential game are demonstrated which made it possible to give a stochastic interpretation to min-max (worst case) design of linear omicron systems. This suggests that the ‚Ä≥pessimistic‚Ä≥ min-max design is not unattractive since it corresponds, in a stochastic setting, to minimization of the expected value of an exponential function of a quadratic form. Another significant result of this equivalence is that the existence of the solution of the stochastic control problem implies and is implied by the existence of the solution of the differential game. It is claimed that these notions can be extended to provide existence results for nonlinear stochastic control problems and nonlinear differential games. Certain asymptotic properties of the gain matrix were also investigated.
Name: ["Jacobson D.H."]

Title: DYNAMIC ANALYSIS OF ADAPTIVE CONTROL THROUGH SENSITIVITY MODELS.
Abstract: A solution is presented to the problem of nonsearching selfadjusting system (NSAS) analysis and synthesis, the system being quasistationary and linear. The sensitivity theory and representation of signals at the output of self-adjusted loop nonlinear elements on the envelope are used in the construction of linear models of NSAS's in order to study the stability and quality of processes in coordinate and parametric disturbances. The envelope transfer function for high-frequency processes is defined.
Name: ["Krutova I.N.", "Yadykin I.B."]

Title: TEST INPUT EVALUATION FOR OPTIMAL ADAPTIVE FILTERING.
Abstract: Average statistical divergence is proposed as a figure of merit for ranking test inputs used in identifying the unknown parameters of a system. Average divergence is a concept taken from communication theory; it can be computed a priori from a recursion relation derived in this paper. Two closed-form analytic examples are presented.
Name: ["Smith Patrick L."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF PARAMETRIC MODELS USING CORRELATION ANALYSIS.
Abstract: A correlation matching method is introduced for the identification of parametric models in Laplace Transfer Function and Difference Equation forms. The basic procedure of the proposed method is the matching of correlation response functions - calculated from a mathematical model - to cross correlation functions evaluated from the system input/output data records. Implementation using interactive computer graphics allows an operator/analyst to match the model's dynamic characteristics to those of the system and at the same time gain deeper understanding of the system's behavior. Practical results are presented for the identification of a boiler-turbine plant together with those obtained from an economic system.
Name: ["Williams D.C.", "Delaney D.G."]

Title: MULTIVARIABLE CONTROL SYSTEMS WITH A STRUCTURAL STEADY-STATE SIGNAL INVARIANCE.
Abstract: Linear, time-invariant feedback control systems in which the controlled plant is affected by unmeasurable stepwise disturbances are analyzed. Necessary and sufficient conditions are given for the existence of a controller such that the control system is asymptotically stable and stead-state output-invariant with respect to disturbances. A synthesis procedure of the controller follows from the sufficiency proof. The minimum number of the integral actions that are needed is also found.
Name: ["Grasselli O.M.", "Nicolo F."]

Title: DELTA-LMS ADAPTIVE ALGORITHM.
Abstract: A new least-mean-squares (LMS) adaptive algorithm, the delta-LMS adaptive algorithm, is developed. Using a two-step iterative process, this new algorithm solves a specific convergence problem that occurs in LMS algorithms when the desired response and the input signals have large mean values. The properties of this new algorithm are illustrated by identification examples. These examples are computer simulations in which tapped delay lines are used to model time invariant, asymptotically stable systems.
Name: ["Timm John Eric"]

Title: ON THE SYNTHESIS OF TRAJECTORY INSENSITIVE LINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Necessary and sufficient conditions are presented for the existence of a linear feedback control law such as to make all possible trajectories of a given linear time-invariant system insensitive to small parameter variations. However, such a control law may entail severe controllability restrictions on the resulting insensitive system; therefore necessary and sufficient conditions are also presented which ensure that the controllability properties of the original system are preserved after the insensitivity generating control law has been implemented.
Name: ["Karlin Alessandro", "Locatelli Arturo", "Zanardini Claudio"]

Title: Efficient Multiprogramming Resource Allocation and Accounting
Abstract: Although sometimes thought of as only a component of time-sharing operation, multiprogramming can involve broader questions of resource allocation, since fairness is not required to meet a response criterion. In a multiprogrammed system, it may serve maximal resource use to be unfair, for example by holding an input/output channel idle for a program while it completes a small amount of processor usage, enabling further use of the channel. Several applications of this principle are given, and it is suggested that a multiprogramming executive might dynamically adjust its allocation algorithms to gain efficiency. Allocation of resources is closely connected to accounting for those resources, raising the problems of repeatability, minimal uncharged overhead, and relative weighting of charges for dependent resources. Since weightings may depend on allocation algorithms, these are not arbitrary accounting parameters. Often the only repeatable accounting is one which omits an extensive overhead; this overhead can be multiple-charged to all programs which benefit from it, so that in the worst case the overhead will be paid, and should multiprogramming prove efficient, overcharges will result. Multiprogramming turns on allocation of the memory resource essential to control of other resources. The general suggestions for allocation and accounting are applied to this question, and some details provided for the case of a monitor which controls a virtual-memory machine. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hamlet R.G."]

Title: TARGET SET CONTROL OF UNCERTAIN SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A linear dynamic system described by an approximated model is studied. The approximation leads to an uncertainty which cannot be modeled by additive noise nor by a parameter bounded variation. A definition of ‚Ä≥uncertainty in norm‚Ä≥ is given. The problem of driving the output in a specified region is investigated. Necessary and sufficient conditions for the solution of the problem and the structure of a linear optimal controller are derived. A method for system approximation which leads to the minimal uncertainty is outlined.
Name: ["Mauro Vito", "Menga Giuseppe"]

Title: ADAPTIVE CONTROL WITH INCOMPLETE IDENTIFICATION.
Abstract: It is argued that adaptive control of a system with incomplete knowledge of the plant is feasible using a vector cost function which is measured continually. The problem of adaptation simplifies to the iterative determination of the parameters of the controller. The characteristics of the system are defined in terms of matrix arrays,all of which need not be known a priori, but are learned in a learning and adapting loop. Using an efficient gradient method, the norm of the vector cost function is minimized in an iterative manner. Several examples show the general procedure for applying the method.
Name: ["Sinha Naresh K."]

Title: APPLICATION OF STOCHASTIC APPROXIMATION TO THE ON-LINE ESTIMATION OF THE PARAMETERS OF NOISY PROCESSES.
Abstract: The application of stochastic approximation to the on-line estimation of the dynamics of noisy processes is dealt with. A finite memory model equivalent to the weighting function of linear, time-invariant systems, is chosen to represent the unknown process dynamics. The identification is effected by the application of a pseudorandom signal superimposed on the system input, and modified forms of the Kiefer-Wolfowitz algorithm.
Name: ["Abbosh F.G."]

Title: METHOD FOR DISCRETE SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION.
Abstract: A method is presented for the estimation of discrete system parameters. It is derived from a maximum descent law and compares favorably with contemporary techniques. Sensitivity models are not required and stability can be insured by correct choice of the adaptive gain.
Name: ["Clarke Raymond", "Green John W."]

Title: PATTERN PROGRAMMING: A METHOD FOR SOLVING GLOBAL CONSTRAINED OPTIMIZATION PROBLEMS.
Abstract: A method for finding a global constrained optimum is described. The proposed method, named ‚Ä≥Pattern Programming‚Ä≥ , consists of the following three phases: pattern measurement, pattern representation and heuristic search method. In each phase, new concepts and algorithms are introduced. The method is illustrated by some examples.
Name: ["Nakahori Ichiro", "Terano Yoshio"]

Title: SCHEDULING METHODS FOR ASSISTING THE DESIGN OF INFORMATION SYSTEMS AND FILE ORGANISATION.
Abstract: The mathematical formulation and algorithms for the problem of optimizing the sequence of random access files on a single disc storage unit are examined. The generalized SPT (shortest-processing-time) rule and its possible applications in data processing are also considered.
Name: ["Savolainen V."]

Title: COMBINED STATE AND PARAMETER ESTIMATION FOR DISTRIBUTED-PARAMETER SYSTEMS USING DISCRETE OBSERVATIONS.
Abstract: An algorithm is presented for the on-line estimation of the state and parameters of a distributed-parameter system in which measurements are made only at a finite number of spatial locations, as well as at discrete times. Using a weighted least square approach, a sequential algorithm for nonlinear filtering of a continuous-discrete distributed-parameter system has been developed which is directly applicable to the combined state and parameter estimation. The continuous-discrete filter circumvents the difficulty of solving a nonlinear Riccati-like operator equation for continuous time measurements.
Name: ["Sherry Howard", "Shen David W.C."]

Title: Reaction time measurements in the study of memory processes: Theory and data
Source: Psychology of Learning and Motivation - Advances in Research and Theory
Abstract: This chapter demonstrates how the study of choice reaction times in continuous (serial) information processing tasks can be very useful in investigating human short-term memory. The subtractive method of Donders and the additive factors method of Sternberg are briefly reviewed. A third method involving the construction and testing of specific process models, which make clear-cut quantitative predictions for carefully designed experiments that fall within the boundary conditions of the process models is presented. The chapter presents a serial, self-terminating memory scanning model to account for human behavior in stimulus identification, naming, choice-reaction, and (memory scanning) character classification tasks. The model assumes that after stimulus information is input, it makes contact very soon with long-term memory, where the information is interrogated and the stimulus is identified. The identification process operates in parallel, the evidence in support of this is that the time to name a character is independent of stimulus ensemble size and stimulus probability. ¬© 1973, Academic Press Inc.
Name: ["Theios J."]

Title: SENSITIVITY DECREASE OF MULTIVARIABLE AUTOMATIC CONTROL SYSTEMS TO THE VARIATIONS OF MEMBER PARAMETERS.
Abstract: The synthesis of linear multivariable automatic control systems is discussed. The required quality of operation at uncontrolled variations (within definite boundaries) of the member parameters is maintained. A synthetic method is suggested based on the introduction of correction communications on sensitivity functions. The possibility is studied for solving the problem with the aid of such an approach.
Name: ["Yermachenko A.I.", "Zdor V.V."]

Title: MODEL STRUCTURE IN SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION FOR FERMENTATION PROCESS DESIGN.
Abstract: The importance of the identification of model structure is emphasized from the point of view of an application-oriented problem. The choice of the model structure of a fermentation process is discussed from the viewpoint of the objects of system synthesis - i. e. , static optimal control, dynamic optimal control, and stability at an equilibrium state. The calculated results show that the model structure which describes a specific growth rate of fermentation microorganisms has a more meaningful role in the description of the system behavior than that which describes the specific production rate.
Name: ["Takamatsu Takeichiro", "Hashimoto Iori", "Shioya Suteaki", "Manago Atsushi"]

Title: INFORMATION STRUCTURE IN DYNAMIC MULTI-PERSON CONTROL PROBLEMS.
Abstract: It is argued that in traditional control problems, an almost universal assumption is the fact that information is centralized. For multi-person optimization problems, such an assumption can only be justified in limited class of problems. Coupled with the additional complication that the information may be dynamic, a host of new conceptual questions arise which have begun to be resolved only recently. These new understandings are not only crucial to any further advance in such areas as differential games and decentralized control theory but also have deepened the insight on the traditional one-person stochastic control problems. The purpose of this paper is to give an introduction to literatures on this topic.
Name: ["Ho Y.C.", "Chu K.C."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION AND SYSTEM PARAMETER ESTIMATION OF DISTILLATION PROCESS - A CASE STUDY.
Abstract: A brief description is first given of the results of a previous study concerning identification and control in the field of distillation. The process of distillation and reflections guiding identification and control are discussed in detail. In particular, it is shown that two types of models are required: a steady state nonlinear model valid in the whole operating domain, and a dynamic linear model efficient for small variations of the inputs in the neighborhood of the operating point. Finally, the steady state identification of industrial distillation columns, and dynamic identification in various situations is studied.
Name: ["Foulard Claude", "Bornard Guy"]

Title: SOME ASPECTS OF HUMAN OPERATOR IDENTIFICATION IN REAL TIME.
Abstract: An approach is presented to real time identification of a human operator, performing a simple closed-loop compensatory task, based on an Astrom type model with time-varying parameters. Possibilities of getting unbiased estimates, of detecting parameter variations, and determining system order and delay are discussed, starting from the Kalman filtering type of algorithm and the instrumental variable method. The implementation on a small digital computer is also described.
Name: ["Stankovic S.S.", "Kouwenberg N.G.M."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION AND CONTROL OF A PILOT-SCALE BOILING RIG.
Abstract: Linear models of a pilot-scale boiler are identified from experimental data and used in the design of controllers. The plant is treated as a two-input, two-output system, whose four transfer functions are identified by the method of generalized least squares from data collected during experiments with pseudo-random binary sequence (PRBS) inputs. Single-loop controllers are then designed from these transfer functions so that a weighted performance index is minimized. Two possible configurations of the controllers are applied to the boiler and it is demonstrated how the controllers can be tuned so as to achieve the best acceptable control. The extension of the method to multivariable systems is outlined.
Name: ["Clarke D.W.", "Dyer D.A.J.", "Hastings-James R.", "Ashton R.P.", "Emery J.B."]

Title: APPLICATION OF THREE-LEVEL-PSEUDORANDOM-SIGNALS FOR PARAMETER ESTIMATION OF NONLINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Some methods are shown which allow the estimation of nonlinear models with different structures. However, the application of these methods is restricted to testing of time-invariant systems. As test-signals, three-level-pseudo-random signals are used. For the approximation models are used consisting of a linear part and a nonlinear gain.
Name: ["Krempl R."]

Title: APPROXIMATION ALGORITHMS FOR COMBINATORIAL PROBLEMS.
Abstract: Simple polynomial-time, heuristic algorithms for finding approximate solutions to various polynomial complete optimization proglems are analyzed with respect to their worst case behavior, measured by the ratio of worst solution value that can be chosen by the algorithm to the optimal value. The results indicate a possible classification of optimization problems as to the behavior of their approximation algorithms.
Name: ["Johnson David S."]

Title: System Identification in Time Domain by Means of Locus Plots. | SYSTEMIDENTIFIZIERUNG IM ZEITBEREICH MIT HILFE VON KENNWERTORTSKURVEN.
Abstract: A locus plot procedure is described for an example of a P-plant, which is excited by triangle pulses. With this locus plot the values of the plant parameters can be estimated. This procedure acting in time domain is appropriate for system identification from measurement data as well as for the approximation of dynamic relationships which are difficult to describe.
Name: ["Gitt W."]

Title: ON THE SYNTHESIS OF UNKNOWN-INPUT OBSERVERS AND INVERSE SYSTEMS BY RECURSIVE ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: The synthesis of unknown-input observers and inverse systems is approached in the state space by using some iterative computational procedures which have been previously developed by the authors in order to detect the most important structural properties of linear time-invariant dynamical systems. An important feature of this approach is the possibility of taking into account the constraint of being stable for the synthesized observer or inverse system. New, simple, necessary and sufficient conditions for unknown-input state observability and invertibility, both without and with stability constraints, are obtained.
Name: ["Basile G.", "Marro G."]

Title: ENGINEERING-TYPE MODELS OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES.
Abstract: The rate-variable approach, which applies the principle of continuity of flow, is introduced and discussed. The development of network models of population dynamics from the rate-variable approach is presented, along with specific, detailed application to the problem of finding optimum control strategies for a very serious endemic disease, snail fever (schistosomiasis). It is shown that in the case of that disease, the modeling results suggest that a threshold exists, below which the endemic will gradually die away, and that the timing of control measures can be crucially important in determining their effectiveness.
Name: ["Lewis Edwin R.", "Lee Keh-Lon"]

Title: L. S. D. - A LINEAR CONTROL SYSTEM DESIGN PROGRAM.
Abstract: A Fortran IV computer program is described which provides the user with a number of different state-space methods for designing linear multivariable continuous control systems; including pole assignment, optimal regulator, model-in-the-system, model-in-the-performance index and optimal servomechanism. The Linear System Design program is intended as an additional tool for the control systems designer; one which is easy to use and can provide a number of state space design alternatives from a single computer run. The various options available in the program have been chosen because of their good potential for application. Thus, the program constitutes a useful basis for the complete preliminary design of either deterministic or stochastic state space controllers for linear continuous-time systems. Several examples are quoted which demonstrate the utility of the program.
Name: ["Young Peter C.", "Levsen Larry D.", "Virdee L.S."]

Title: FIXED DISCRETE FEEDBACK CONTROL LAW FOR A STOCHASTIC SYSTEM WITH VARYING PARAMETERS.
Abstract: The parameters of many processes vary in an ill defined manner, yet within a specified envelope. Typical of such a process is an aircraft in flight where the parameters vary as a function of time due to changes in altitude, velocity, etc. Time varying parameters cannot be specified due to variation of routes, etc. Experimental data are available, however, for sets of discrete ‚Ä≥flight conditions‚Ä≥ . An algorithm is derived for application to a problem wherein the process can be defined by a nominal equation and by ‚Ä≥high and low‚Ä≥ extremes. Weighting terms are introduced so that one condition, typically the nominal one, can be stressed. A control which is satisfactory for the specified nominal and extreme conditions should be satisfactory over intermediate values. It is also demonstrated that use of an optimal control designed specifically for one condition can lead to instability as the plant changes, without correction in the control law. This algorithm can be applied to the design of linear feedback controls with high actuator and sensor failure integrity. In this case the plant with lost sensor/actuator is defined as a separate plant condition, with low weighting.
Name: ["Healey M.", "Jones P.R."]

Title: CONTROL SYSTEM USING ADSOL, AN ON-LINE DIGITAL SIMULATION PROGRAM.
Abstract: ADSOL, a continuous system simulation program, is described which enables a control system to be simulated using a remote terminal attached to a digital computer, and which enables an engineer to interact with the program to obtain information about the performance of the system being simulated. The engineer is then able to apply his expertise to modifying the control system to provide a required level of performance. The program has available both single and multivariable automatic optimization routines, and the user is able to monitor the progress of any optimization run on-line.
Name: ["Revett M.C."]

Title: PHASE TRAJECTORY SIMULATION OF FEEDBACK PULSE CONTROLLED SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The use of a digital computer using high level languages for nonlinear control system simulation is shown to be attractive in terms of the flexibility offered in problem specification and in the corresponding ability to perform retrospective system design. The mathematical models of highly nonlinear control systems are discretized, from which a complete analysis and synthesis program is constructed from a basic collection of numerical algorithms.
