Abstract: We prove the following theorem in this paper: For any real numbers r<sub>1</sub>, r<sub>2</sub>, 1‚â§r<sub>1</sub><r<sub>2</sub>, there is a set A of strings which has nondeterministic time complexity n<sup>r</sup>2, but not nondeterministic time complexity n<sup>r</sup>1. The computing devices are nondeterminsitic multitape Turing machines. ¬© 1973 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Cook S.A."]

Title: General model for the molecular events in synapses during learning
Abstract: In this communication an effort has been made to formulate a general model for the chemical events in the activation of a previously nonfunctional synapse. The purpose is to show that it is possible to present a realistic detailed chemical model for this essential event in memory fixation.
Name: ["Huttunen M.O."]

Title: A nurse-computer assisted preoperative anesthesia management system
Abstract: The digital computer has the potential for valuable support in the field of clinical medicine. Ten patients for elective surgery were interviewed and examined by a certified registered nurse anesthetist aided by a digital computer. Described is the logical design and construction of a computer assisted preoperative anesthesia management system using a series of experimental computer programs (Clinical Decision Support System) developed by IBM. The system consists of a device for gathering and storing patient data and also a system for making logical decisions from this data. Using this data, decisions were made by the computer. This evaluation was compared to the standard physician gathered data. Results indicate that the nurse-computer combination was superior to the physician's in the gathering and recording of patient data. The nurse-computer system also generated more decisions of potential use to the attending anesthesiologist. Program revision was undertaken on the basis of this data to improve the system. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Chodoff P.", "Gianaris II C."]
Affiliations: [' School of Medicine', 'Northwestern University Medical Center']

Title: Online system performance measurements with software and hybrid monitors
Source: Proceedings of the 4th ACM Symposium on Operating Systems Principles, SOSP 1973
Abstract: Two monitors were implemented to collect information about the behaviour of the online system developed and run at Stanford. The response of this online system was slow and main memory was a critical resource. The goal was to extract desired information by a method that requires only a negligible amount of monitored system resources. Results presented in this paper indicate that this effort has been successful. A software monitor that requires less than 700 bytes of main memory collects statistics about utilization of special online system resources and about the scheduler mechanism, detects system deadlocks, and measures online executive overhead. This software monitor helped to discover various facts about the system behaviour; however, to understand the reasons behind certain situations, it was necessary to learn more about properties of individual terminal tasks. Since a software monitor would cause an intolerable system degradation and hardware monitoring is not directly appiicable for such measurements, a hardware/software monitor interface was implemented which enables recording of software events by a hardware monitor. The monitoring artifact is thus kept close to zero. This technique has been applied to measure time a task spends in various states and it has many other uses. ¬© Proceedings of the 4th ACM Symposium on Operating Systems Principles, SOSP 1973. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Svobodova L."]

Title: FUZZY AND PROBABILISTIC CLUSTERING AND THE ANALYSIS OF NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL DATA.
Abstract: A common neurophysiological problem is that of the determination of electrophysiological correlates of physiological and behavioral states. When additional information allows the identification of such states the problem of correlating this information with the electrophysiological records is usually handled using pattern recognition techniques. In other cases, however, the actual purpose of the analysis is the determination of the many possible behavioral and physiological mechanisms underlying the phenomenon in question. It is in these particular instances that cluster analysis can be expected to yield results. Application of fuzzy and probabilistic representation will additionally help to determine transitions between the different states.
Name: ["Ruspini Enrique H."]

Title: MODEL FOR THE PHOTICALLY STIMULATED ELECTROENCEPHALOGRAPHIC SIGNALS.
Abstract: A new mathematical model for the characterization of stimulated and unstimulated EEG alpha waves is proposed and discussed. This model is based on the concept that the phases of the alpha -frequency waves can be aligned (i. e. , re-set to a preferred phase) by the photic stimulus. The incoherence of the phases tends to increase as a function of time, following the most recent aligning stimulus. The average of alpha time samples exhibits the same phenomenon when some references, say the initial peaks of the time samples, are aligned artifically (i. e. , without stimulation). In this model, the propagation rate of the incoherence of phase is defined. The adequacy of the phase uncertainty model has been demonstrated by comparing simulated results with empirical results. The simulated data were obtained by the use of Wiener-Levy process. The experimental results were obtained by using EEG signals recorded from human subjects exposed to photic flashes. The results are well matched.
Name: ["Floyd R.V.", "Lai D.C.", "Anliker J.E."]

Title: COLOR IMAGE CODING WITH THE SLANT TRANSFORM.
Abstract: The slant transform and its application are discussed, along with color image transform coding. It is claimed that slant transform coding of color images provides a substantial bandwidth reduction compared to conventional PCM coding with only a minimal amount of image degradation. The technique is superior from the standpoint of image quality to any other transform coding method using unitary transforms. Preliminary studies indicate that the slant transform color image coder can be implemented for operation up to real time television rates using high speed, parallel digital circuits or by acoustic surface wave devices.
Name: ["Chen Wen-Hsiung", "Pratt William K."]

Title: ASYNCHRONOUS NETWORK OF SPECIFIC MICROPROCESSORS.
Abstract: The efficient use of the dynamic microprogramming supposes the concept of the ‚Ä≥host machine‚Ä≥ which can emulate a number of virtual machines. The multiplication of control organs actually needs asynchronous communication procedure and requires specific microprocessors. Such a machine is investigated in this paper. The computer is a collection of specific microprocessors. The communications are handled by an auto-regulating principle. A paged working storage and a communication mechanism are cyclicly shared between the microprocessors. The communication mechanism allows the garbage collecting and the flag locking of the common pages.
Name: ["Dromard Francois", "Noguez Gerard"]

Title: RECURSIVE MICROPROGRAMMING IN A SYNTAX RECOGNIZER.
Abstract: Description of the microprogrammed architecture of a top-down syntax recognizer using the recursive descent technique for illustrating recursive microprogramming. The recognizer is implemented by a microprogram. The micro-instructions have a vertical format. Recursive microprogramming is described in implementing the recognizer. The microprogram is first described without and then with considerations of timing and synchronization. To illustrate recursive microprogramming, the hardware architecture of a vertically microprogrammed processor where recursive microsubroutines together with a read-write control memory are used is presented.
Name: ["Chu Yaohan"]

Title: On ‚ÄúA General Approach to Linear Mean-Square Estimation Problems‚Äù
Abstract: The application of series representations for random processes to problems of causal least-mean-square estimation on infinite intervals has met with some difficulty in the past. This correspondence brings to light two of the more outstanding difficulties in relation to the contribution of Cambanis, which appears in this issue. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gardner W.A."]

Title: Kinship and identity algorithm of coefficients of identity | [APPARENTEMENT ET IDENTITE. ALGORITHME DU CALCUL DES COEFFICIENTS D'IDENTITE]
Abstract: The concept of inbreeding which is a fundamental notion of population genetics, covers many aspects. The concept of gene identity is one possible approach by which the ancestry common to 2 individuals may be summarized using 15 coefficients of identity, although the coefficients must be calculated practically. This paper proposes an algorithm which is put into efficient computer program form.
Name: ["Nadot R.", "Vaysseix G."]

Title: Continuous speech data base with 14 marked vowel and nasal classes
Source: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Abstract: One of the problems in the design of continuous speech recognition systems is evaluation of the stage which detects occurrences of phonemes in the speech signal. A method of evaluating and optimizing phoneme recognition networks has been developed which uses data obtained by manual ‚Äúmarking‚Äù of phoneme locations on a tape recording of speech. With the aid of a digital computer and display, 1090 occurrences of vowels, nasals, and ‚Äúdon‚Äôt care‚Äù conditions were marked in a five-minute sample of speech. These data, which may be used for measurement of error rates in speech recognition systems, have been included in the IEEE Computer Society repository for data bases. ¬© 1986, American Association of Physics Teachers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Preusse J.W.", "Drucker H."]

Title: Statistical decision theory applied to some auditory phenomena
Abstract: Some results are reported which have been obtained by applying the statistical decision theory to the detection of an auditory signal covered by noise. Based on these general results it was possible to explain in a mathematical form the known experimental fact that it is easier to detect the presence of an auditory signal covered by noise when the period of the signal is constant, than in the case where the period is subject to random variations.
Name: ["Spataru C.", "Vasilescu V."]

Title: Computer counting of lithium-treated metaphase chromosomes a population survey technique
Abstract: Automatic counting of chromosomes by computer is a feasible technique for screening human populations for aneuploidy. This paper presents a system which has been developed around a new lithium-treated chromosome preparation. 35 mm negatives of metaphase chromosome spreads are scanned fully automatically; chromosomes are distinguished from nonchromosomes to get the count for a given spread and then thirty spread counts per patient are pooled in a histogram to find the true chromosome complement. Presumptive sex diagnosis is also made by comparing A-C and D-G group counts. Results are presented from a normal male, a normal female and XO-XYY mosaic. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Freed C."]

Title: An automated particle analysis system
Abstract: A system is outlined which automatically determines size distributions of polydisperse particles such as deposits of atmospheric aerosols, of soils, or of elemental constituents of polydisperse particles. A minicomputer operates a scanning system, and options include the use of an optical microscope television scan, a scanning electron microscope or an electron microprobe. Size distributions of particles are derived from digital images of particle fields. In addition, particles are classified as to shape by extracting features of each particle from the digital image.
Name: ["Blifford Jr I.H.", "Gillette D.A."]

Title: The recognition problem: application to sum of exponentials
Abstract: Consider a stochastic process X(t) = Œº(t) + Œµ{lunate}(t) where Œº(t) is the deterministic part and Œµ{lunate}(t) the purely nondeterministic part. Assume that X(t) is observed at n equidistant time points, œÑ units apart, and that a "model" is given that ascribes to Œº(t) a specific analytic form f(t, Œ∏), where Œ∏ is a parameter vector. If, on physical or other grounds, f(t, Œ∏) can be meaningfully decomposed into nonoverlapping components f{hook}(t)Œ∏ = ‚àë i=1 kf{hook}<sub>i</sub>(t,Œ∏<sub>i</sub> the recognition problem is: how does our ability to recognize the presence or absence of components (without necessarily any parameter estimation) depend on n, œÑ, and k? A general purpose procedure on the way to attack this problem is proposed and applied to the case f{hook}(t,Œ∏) = ‚àë,/op. i=1Œ≤<sub>ie</sub>-Œ±<sub>it</sub>, Œ±<sub>i</sub> > 0. Mathematical complexity necessitates numerical evaluation of the analysis, but some seemingly general results have been obtained: (i) for fixed n and k there is an "optimal" œÑ-interval that increases with n but decreases when k increases; (ii) increase in œÑ affects asymmetrically the recognizability of the components (the system's behavior changes qualitatively with time scale); (iii) the best unbiased estimators (in the Cram√©r-Rao sense) are, for finite œÑ, inconsistent with respect to n but become consistent when œÑ approaches zero; (vi) for fixed n and optimal œÑ the coefficients of variation for the best unbiased estimators increase approximately exponentially with k, suggesting substantial limitations regarding the largest number of components that can be recognized in data. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Bergner P.-E.E.", "Takeuchi K.", "Yin Lui Y."]

Title: CONTROL SYSTEM VIEW OF AUTOMATED PERSONAL DATA SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Potentially harmful effects of automated personal data systems, or computerized data banks containing information about individuals which can be linked to the particular individual involved are analyzed in terms of feedback control mechanisms. It appears, as a result of this analysis, that many of these potentially harmful effects are related to either a real or perceived inability of individuals to provide feedback relating to decisions that may affect them. Based on this analysis, measures are suggested by which feedback mechanisms might be ensured.
Name: ["Salasin John"]

Title: ACID: A USER-ORIENTED SYSTEM OF STATISTICAL PROGRAMS.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: A common problem in any scientific or business effort is to organize large masses of data for human interpretation. This article describes a program system called ACID (Automated Classification and Interpretation of Data), which is designed to do just this. ACID is focused on a somewhat heuristic pattern recognition problem (in the general sense of that term) although the concepts discussed here are certainly not limited to this.
Name: ["Baker R.A.", "Jones T.A."]

Title: MODELS OF COMPLEX STOCHASTIC TRANSPORT NETWORKS AND OPTIMIZATION OF THEIR PARAMETERS.
Abstract: Markov models of the operation of complex stochastic transport networks are proposed. Efficiency indexes characterizing the quality of the system are obtained. Essential network parameters are determined and optimized. The results can be used for the reconstruction of optimum design of networks.
Name: ["Kuchura V.N.", "Pirogov V.V.", "Petrov Yu.P."]

Title: THEORETICAL APPROACH FOR CHARACTER RECOGNITION BASED ON PHENOMENOLOGICAL ATTRIBUTES.
Abstract: The importance of using a theory of characters in the designing of automatic computer character recognition algorithms for hand printed letters is demonstrated. Ambiguously shaped characters or ‚Ä≥difficult cases‚Ä≥ constitute the basis for the theory. It is argued that a theory based on ambiguities, rather than on the classical archetypical shape of letters, leads to algorithms which will perform more accurately.
Name: ["Blesser B.", "Shillman R.", "Kuklinski T.", "Cox C.", "Eden M.", "Ventura J."]

Title: FEATURE SELECTION FOR COMPACT PATTERN DESCRIPTION.
Abstract: The performance of the syntactic pattern recognition method, i. e. recognition error ratio or processing speed partly depends upon the pattern description. In this relation a compact pattern description method is discussed. Corresponding to the feature selection of the decision theoretic approach a definition of a substructure as a feature consisting of primitive elements is based upon its entropy within the given pattern complex. The description organization and parsing order are also controlled by feature entropy measure, so that the object pattern is matched with the least steps.
Name: ["Hanakata K."]

Title: DATA STRUCTURES AND PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: A scheme for reducing two-dimensional arrays obtained from digitized pictures is discussed which enables object-detection and relationship-detection without discarding data useful for pattern-matching. Aspects of several pattern recognition contexts which can be incorporated in this scheme and some related algorithms were discussed.
Name: ["Klinger Allen"]

Title: HARMONIC ANALYSIS OF FINITE AUTOMATA.
Abstract: A method is proposed for analytically describing finite automata that is based on the Fourier expansion of the transition and output functions in a multiplicative orthonormalized basis that arises naturally (when the alphabets of the automation are specially assigned). A classification of automata that is based on this analytic representation is presented.
Name: ["Blyumin S.L."]

Title: MULTIPLE-VALUED VARIABLE-THRESHOLD THRESHOLD LOGIC AND ITS APPLICATION TO THE REALIZATION OF THE SET OF BOOLEAN FUNCTIONS.
Abstract: In this paper some properties of multiple-valued variable-threshold threshold functions are described and these properties are used for the realization of a set of Boolean functions.
Name: ["Aibara T.", "Takamatsu Y.", "Murakami K."]

Title: INCREMENTAL CURVE GENERATION USING MULTIPLE-VALUED LOGIC.
Abstract: A nonparametric curve generation using ternary logic has been presented. By limiting the increments to a single or double unit step along x or y axis, the four ternary logic expressions are derived. In the given method the selection of proper incremental step is not a result of numerical calculations, but is based on the set of conditions detected by the ternary logic. The only required numerical calculation is the updating of the function and its derivatives. Consequently, the method is suitable for fast generation of any given curve.
Name: ["Orsic M."]

Title: DISTANCE MEASURES ON DETECTION TEST SETS AND THEIR APPLICATIONS.
Abstract: The purpose of this article is to shift attention from the faults and to consider relationships between detection test sets. In particular the author is interested in defining distance functions between any pair of input sets. Two such functions are defined, based respectively on the ideas of the function verification and fault detection capabilities of the input sets.
Name: ["Seth Sharad C."]

Title: ROLE OF THE MINICOMPUTER IN PRODUCTION ROBOT CONTROL.
Abstract: This control concept enables accurate positioning, achieved by measurement between robot and environment. No information passes either to or from central system unless either local reflex terminates local motor action and signals central control, or central control may interrupt local motor sequence due to decision based on local sensors signalling central control.
Name: ["Larcombe M.H.E."]

Title: STRONG CONSISTENCY OF MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD ESTIMATES FOR NONLINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Families of stochastic processes indexed by a finite number of alternative parameter values are considered. For general classes of stochastic processes it is shown that maximum likelihood estimates converge almost surely to the correct parameter value. This is established by use of a submartingale property of the sequence of maximized likelihood ratios together with a technique first employed by A. Wald in the case of independent identically distributed random variables.
Name: ["Caines P.E."]

Title: DIGITAL ADAPTIVE FLIGHT CONTROLLER DEVELOPMENT.
Abstract: A digital adaptive flight control algorithm has been developed by combining a weighted least squares estimator with optimal linear regulator control logic designed to minimize a quadratic model-following performance index. Results for a typical fighter aircraft's trajectory over six distinct flight conditions are very promising.
Name: ["Kaufman H.", "Berry P."]

Title: ADAPTIVE UNIVERSAL FAULT TOLERANT CELLULAR LOGIC ARRAYS.
Abstract: Adaptive universal fault-tolerant logic arrays are presented which have cellular structures, low numbers of input-output terminals, and are thus compatible with large scale integration technology. These cellular arrays can implement fault-tolerant digital systems capable of adapting on-line to realize any logic function on a given number of variables. The same simple adaptation algorithm employed to realize either a completely specified or an incompletely specified logic function is also used for dynamic error correction (on-line repair). The adaptive fault-tolerant cellular arrays are based on a proposed redundant decomposition of a switching function. A two-rail scheme of such arrays is shown to be capable of both error detection and dynamic error correction through adaptation. A comparison is carried out, which indicates that the reliability of the two-rail scheme is better than that of TMR (Triple Modular Redundancy) schemes, for a comparable cost in hardware.
Name: ["Iosupovicz A."]

Title: SYSTEMATIC SIMULATORS OF JOINT ORDER UNIFORM VARIATES.
Abstract: The simulation of joint order statistics from the uniform distribution and subsequently from any other distribution, utilizing the probability integral transformation or ‚Ä≥Table Lookup‚Ä≥ method, has been of considerable interest in many Monte Carlo studies. This paper considers several major simulators and compares their relative efficiency with respect to execution time.
Name: ["Mason Robert L.", "Lurie Dan"]

Title: STOCHASTIC CONTROL OF LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH NONCLASSICAL INFORMATION AND AN ARBITRARY NUMBER OF CONTROLLERS.
Abstract: The control of both discrete and continuous time linear stochastic dynamic systems with quadratic cost and with control being exercised by an arbitrary number of controllers each of which is making proprietary noisy measurements is studied. It is assumed that the a priori statistics of the initial state and the measurement and system noise is known. In order to obtain a tractable problem the structure of the controller is constrained to utilize the previous control and state estimate and current measurement. This simplification results in a stage-varying matrix parameter optimization problem. The necessary conditions for the solution are developed. An example consisting of a single stage and first order system is examined. Its solution is determined first by the approach developed here and then by enforcing the separation principle. The first approach, by taking into account all the a priori information available in a joint optimization problem, yields a cost which is less than that resulting from the enforcement of the separation principle.
Name: ["Pisacane V.L.", "VandeLinde V.D."]

Title: OPTIMAL SENSOR CONFIGURATION CONTROL APPLIED TO A MISSILE LAUNCHER CONTROL PROBLEM.
Abstract: A system and sensor configuration control problem has been formulated for a class of linear stochastic control systems corrupted by Gaussian noise. The criterion function is a weighted trace of the terminal error covariance matrix for the optimal linear estimator of the state of the system. A numerical optimization algorithm for this problem has been based on a parameter optimization approach. This approach is applied to a problem of optimal missile launcher control while estimating the relative alignment of two inertial instrument packages.
Name: ["Rains R.G.", "Stubberud A.R."]

Title: SPIDAC: SPECIMEN INPUT TO DIGITAL AUTOMATIC COMPUTER.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: An automatic optical-microscope scanner has been described for on-line input of pictorial data from a glass microscope slide directly into the core memory of a digital computer. An application of the system to chromosome analysis is also given. With the SPIDAC system, one can automatically search to locate all chromosome spreads on a glass slide, and scan to completely analyze the chromosomes of suitable spreads, including some interactive editing of the picture.
Name: ["Ledley Robert S.", "Huang H.K.", "Golab Thomas J.", "Kulkarni Yeshwant", "Pence Gerard", "Rotolo Louis S."]

Title: GENERALIZED MODEL FOR SIMULATING COMMODITY MOVEMENTS BY SHIP.
Abstract: The logic structure and techniques are described which are used in a Simscript program for simulating the movement of ships through a network of locks, reaches, lakes, and ports. The program also provides for endogenous route selection between ‚Ä≥micro-route‚Ä≥ alternatives, i. e. , parallel locks or canals, and for the endogenous scheduling of ship movements, given port-to-port commodity movement demand and fleet mix. The model is basically a general network simulation tool based on the concept of a ‚Ä≥route map‚Ä≥ which describes the sequence of facilities to be traversed between given points in the network. The cardinal mechanism in the model is a Movement Control Module which monitors the route map of each ship during its voyage and sends the vessel to generalized satellite modules where the performance of locks, reaches, lakes, and ports are simulated. Attributes carried by the ship initialize the generalized modules to simulate a specific lock, reach, lake, or port as dictated by the ship's position along its route map. The model is being used to simulate the performance of the Great Lakes System for the Corps of Engineers.
Name: ["Rea John C.", "Nowading David C.", "Buckholts Philip Wade"]

Title: AUTOMATIC DIGITAL CURVE FOLLOWER/DIGITISER WITH CONSTANT AVERAGE TANGENTIAL SPEED.
Abstract: The design and synthesis of a digital instrument which can automatically follow and digitize a given nonintersecting profile or curve are presented. Such a profile or contour-following action is central to the operation of an important class of numerically controlled (NC) machine tools in which a cutter (mechanical, oxy-acetylene flame or laser) is used to replicate a master template out of a given material. The design incorporates several novel features like approximately-constant following-speed, automatic curve acquisition and tracking, and can be adapted to several related applications, such as planimetry, pattern recognition, electrocardiogram analysis, etc. , which may also arise in biomedical research.
Name: ["Rancourt Denis", "Boutet Robert", "Dumais Michel", "Hudon Pierre", "Vallee Jocelin"]

Title: CONTOUR DETECTION IN NOISY PICTURES USING HEURISTIC SEARCH METHODS.
Abstract: A method for detecting contours in noisy pictures is presented. The problem of contour detection is reduced to the problem of finding a minimal-cost path in a weighted graph. A figure of merit takes into account the properties of the contour, and graph searching techniques are used to find the contours which minimize the given figure of merit. Because of the global approach, this method has great flexibility. Some experimental results are given, which show how information about the shape of the object to be detected can be incorporated in the figure of merit, thus allowing the extraction of contours from noisy pictures and the separation of touching objects.
Name: ["Martelli Alberto"]

Title: VDL - A DEFINITION SYSTEM FOR ALL LEVELS.
Abstract: The VDL system for the description of programming languages which was originally used for the definition of PL/I is extended to the description of processors. This paper shows the relationship between the language of definition and the abstract machine over which the semantics of the language are specified.
Name: ["Lee John A.N."]

Title: ALGEBRAIC TECHNIQUES FOR FINDING TESTS FOR SEVERAL FAULT TYPES.
Abstract: Algebraic techniques are used to find tests for loop-free logic networks under a variety of failure models. Fundamental to these procedures is a network representation called the SPOOF, an algebraic notation that expresses the topology of a network as well as its logical function. Both fault-free and faulty behavior are readily characterized by the SPOOF, which is an effective tool for finding tests.
Name: ["Flomenhoft Mark J.", "Si Siu-Chong", "Susskind Alfred K."]

Title: ASSOCIATIVE PROCESSOR APPLICATIONS TO REAL - TIME DATA MANAGEMENT.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: This article describes a research study concerning the potential of associative processing as a solution to the problem of real-time data management. The desired outcome of the research is an evaluation of the comparative advantages of associative processing over conventional sequential processing as applied to general real-time Data Management System (DMS) problems. The specific DMS application framework within which the study is carried out is that of the data management functions of the U. S. Air Force Tactical Air Control Center.
Name: ["Linde Richard R.", "Gates Roy", "Peng Te-Fu"]

Title: ADAPTIVE DIGITAL FILTERS.
Abstract: An adaptive digital filter is discussed. Two representative classes of algorithms are derived using energy and phase information respectively to adjust the filter parameters of center frequency and bandwidth for a second order filter. They do not require external signal information. Nth order filters are best realized by a parallel connection of second order systems. Applications include tracking nonstationary signals such as in seismic and acoustical sensing.
Name: ["Gerhardt L.A."]

Title: STOCHASTIC APPROXIMATION ALGORITHMS AND APPLICATIONS.
Abstract: The conditions of applicability are presented for stochastic approximation algorithms that minimize a mean-square error criterion for identification of a linear discrete-time stationary system without dynamical numerator. The acceleration of the convergence is discussed. Then a tentative is outlined to overcome the previous requirement of states accessibility.
Name: ["Kubrusly C.S.", "Gravier J."]

Title: AVERAGE VARIATION L-STABILITY CRITERIA FOR TIME-VARYING FEEDBACK SYSTEMS - A UNIFIED APPROACH.
Abstract: The problem of developing L//2-stability criteria for feedback systems with a single time-varying gain, which impose average variation constraints on the gain is treated. A unified approach is presented which facilitates the development of such average variation criteria for both linear and nonlinear systems. The stability criteria derived here are shown to be more general than the existing results.
Name: ["Sundareshan M.K.", "Thathacher M.A.L."]

Title: Automaton and Information. | [AUTOMAT UND INFORMATION.]
Abstract: The question of hw much an automatic machine does supply is investigated by means of Shannon's entropy as a measure of information for various types of automatic machines associated with the abstract automata theory. The results are reviewed in tables and explained by examples.
Name: ["Fey P."]

Title: OXYGEN TRANSPORT IN THE BRAIN MICROCIRCULATION BY A HYBRID COMPUTER NONLINEAR MONTE CARLO METHOD.
Abstract: A modification of the Monte Carlo method for application to nonlinear partial differential equations is presented. The hybrid computer nonlinear Monte Carlo method is used to solve a nonlinear unsteady state mathematical model of oxygen transport to the capillaries and tissue of human brain and appears to have much promise as a nonlinear PDE solution technique.
Name: ["Hunt Daniel H.", "Bruley Duane F.", "Bicher Haim H.", "Knisely Melvin H."]

Title: Nonsupervised classification using the principal component
Abstract: This paper presents a mathematical model of a nonsupervised two-category classifier with a nonparametric learning method by using the first principal component. On the assumptions that the patterns of each category are clustered and that the mean point of all patterns used lies between the two clusters, the separating hyperplane contains the mean pattern point and is perpendicular to the line governed by the first principal component. The learning algorithm for obtaining the mean pattern vector and the first principal component is described, and also some experimental results on random patterns are presented. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Shimura M.", "Imai T."]

Title: Algorithm of Technological Process Control at a Wet Magnetic Separation Plant. | [ALGORITM UPRAVLENIYA TEKHNOLOGICHESKIM PROTSESSOM NA FABRIKE MOKROI MAGNITNOI SEPARATSII.]
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii, Gornyi Zhurnal
Abstract: An algorithm of optimal stabilization of the output parameter in the concentrate - the content of the 0. 074mm class - is worked out for the technological process of wet magnetic sepration at the Sokolovsko-Sarbayskiy ore mining and dressing combine. The algorithm uses the dual control theory methods which are considered as the best suited to conditions of control with errors.
Name: ["Chumak S.N.", "Leonov R.E."]

Title: Minimum-Time Control of a Linear System with Delay. | STEROWANIE MINIMALNOCZASOWE PEWNEGO OBIEKTU LINIOWEGO Z OPOZNIENIEM.
Abstract: An n dimensional control system described by the equation dx/dt(t) equals Ax(t) plus plus Bx(T minus tau ) plus Cu(t) is considered. Admissible controls are piecewise continuous bounded functions with the range in a polyhedron including the origin in R**r. It is assumed that the system is controllable to zero in the complete state space. The problem under consideration is to find an admissible control u such that the trajectory x of the system satisfies a given condition. A method of solving the problem is described. The method consists of converting the problem into a finite dimensional minimization problem.
Name: ["Korytowski Adam"]

Title: UNIFIED APPROACH TO GLOBAL PROGRAM OPTIMIZATION.
Abstract: A technique is presented for global analysis of program structure in order to perform compile time optimization of object code generated for expressions. The global expression optimization presented includes constant propagation, common subexpression elimination, elimination of redundant register load operations, and live expression analysis. A general purpose program flow analysis algorithm is developed which depends upon the existence of an ‚Ä≥optimizing function‚Ä≥ . The algorithm is defined formally using a directed graph model of program flow structure, and is shown to be correct. Several optimizing functions are defined which, when used in conjunction with the flow analysis algorithm, provides the various forms of code optimization. The flow analysis algorithm is sufficiently general that additional functions can easily be defined for other forms of global code optimization.
Name: ["Kildall Gary A."]

Title: CONTROL STRATEGY FOR SPATIAL TRADE MODELS INCORPORATING TRANSPORTATION COSTS.
Abstract: A spatial trade model consisting of several suppliers and markets for shipping and receiving a commodity is examined under an assumption of perfect competition. The proposed dynamic model incorporates the effects of transportation costs separating suppliers from markets. Maximization of a suitably defined social pay-off function leads to an optimal control of the dynamic system. The control law is arrived at using a computational algorithm. A numerical example illustrates the application of this algorithm.
Name: ["Garg Devendra P."]

Title: NOTE ON FIXED INTERVAL SMOOTHING FOR LINEAR CONTINUOUS SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Several implementations of fixed interval smoothers are discussed. It is observed that fixed interval smoothing can be performed without storing and inverting covariances of the filtered estimate using numerically stable algorithms. A covariance for the smoothed estimate of process noise is obtained.
Name: ["McReynolds Stephen R."]

Title: SIMPLIFICATION OF LARGE-SCALE LINEAR DYNAMIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A method which reduces large scale linear dynamic systems with a single input and single output to low order models while minimizing the approximation error is proposed. A set of necessary conditions for the optimum reduced model subject to a pulse input is derived. Extensions to a step input are discussed. Numerical results for the proposed method and comparisons with other model reduction techniques are presented for a linear heat diffusion problem.
Name: ["Riggs James B.", "Edgar Thomas F."]

Title: CONTINUITY OF COST FUNCTIONALS IN DIFFUSION PROCESSES AND ITS APPLICATION TO AN EXISTENCE THEOREM OF OPTIMAL CONTROLS.
Abstract: A cost functional which is the integral of a cost rate over a random time is associated with a control system described by a stochastic differential equation. The control policy is confined to measurable Markov controls. In connection to the problem of selecting a minimizing control, two results are shown. The first one is the continuity dependence of the cost functional on controls, i. e. , it is shown that if a sequence of controls convergers weakly to a control then the corresponding sequence of the cost functionals converges to the cost functional corresponding to the limiting control. Using this result, the second one is to show an existence theorem of optimal stochastic controls among an appropriatge set of admissible controls under some assumptions.
Name: ["Yamada K."]

Title: POLYNOMIAL COMPLETE SCHEDULING PROBLEMS.
Abstract: It is shown that the problem of finding an optimal schedule for a set of jobs is polynomial complete even in the following two restricted cases: (1) All jobs require one time unit. (2) All jobs require one or two time units, and there are only two processors. As a consequence, the general preemptive scheduling problem is also polynomial complete. These results are tantamount to showing that the scheduling problems mentioned are intractable.
Name: ["Ullman J.D."]

Title: New Results in Optimizing Surveillance System Tracking and Data Correlation Performance in Dense Multitarget Environments
Abstract: Tracking performance in surveillance systems depends on two interrelated functions: track updating, the process of incorporating a new measurement into the track to update the system state estimate, and retum-to-track correlation, the process of selecting which sensor return, if any, to use for track updating. Because of the presence of a number of targets in the same vicinity and the existence of clutter and false alarms, the correlation function is generally performed imperfectly. Since typical tracking filters such as the Kalman filter do not account for such correlation errors, degraded performance often results as well as unreliable and optimistic estimates of tracking accuracies. This paper examines and provides for optimizing the overall tracking process considering both the correlation and track update functions and their inter-action. General equations for tracking performance of any arbitrary tracking filter used with a broad class of correlation algorithms in dense multitarget environments are developed. A new reoptimized tracking filter is derived which provides, from among a general class of tracking filters using a priori information on sensor return sta-tistics, optimal performance in such environments and which reduces to the Kalman filter when environmental effects are eliminated. The new filter is compared parametrically to both the standard Kalman filter and a computationally simpler version of the optimal filter in terms of tracking accuracy and reliability of the calculated covariance matrix, over a spectrum of environmental conditions. At high densities of sensor returns, the new filter provides considerably improved tracking performance as well as uniquely reliable estimates of this performance. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Singer R.A.", "Sea R.G."]

Title: TWO-WAY PROBABILISTIC AUTOMATA.
Abstract: It is argued that two-way finite automata represent the same class of languages that one-way finite automata represent. The analogous statement does not hold for the corresponding probabilistic automata if a probabilistic (fuzzy) event is taken as the analog of the probabilistic automaton language.
Name: ["Kuklin Yu.I."]

Title: STABILIZATION OF MULTIVARIABLE SYSTEMS WITH CONSTANT-GAIN OUTPUT FEEDBACK.
Abstract: An algorithm is proposed for determining a set of constant output feedback gains to stabilize a linear, time-invariant, multivariable system. This is accomplished by using gradients of the Hurwitz determinants to adjust the values of the gains. The smallest Hurwitz determinant is increased at each iteration, if possible, until either the system is stable or a stationary point is reached (equivalent to a local extremum in an optimization problem).
Name: ["Fortmann Thomas E."]

Title: FEEDBACK CONTROLLER DESIGN FOR MULTIVARIABLE SYSTEMS BY LINEAR PROGRAMMING.
Abstract: The application of linear programming (LP) to the design of state variable feedback controllers for multivariable plants with deterministic inputs is described. The design problem is solved in two steps. The first step consists of an open-loop optimization in which LP is used to determine the plant input vector profile which optimizes the plant response to a specified demand. The performance criterion used is the minimization of the Integral Weighted Absolute Value of the error state vector and of the plant input vector. The second step is a minimum Integral Weighted Absolute Error fitting, through the feedback controller, of the vector profiles (input and feedback vectors) determined in the first step. The second step, also implemented by LP, produces the controller parameters (a matrix of constant gains). The technique is illustrated with an application to the NERVA nuclear rocket engine controller design. The LP program used is the IBM MPS/360 version 2, modification level 9.
Name: ["Porcelli Giacomo"]

Title: MEAN SQUARE STABILITY CRITERIA FOR LINEAR WHITE NOISE STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Lyapunov theory is used to analyze the mean square stability properties of linear systems with white noise stochastic coefficients in the state equations. Discrete time as well as continuous time systems with a finite dimensional state vector are considered. First the single noise case is discussed, then the case of multiple but uncorrelated noise elements is analyzed, and finally the general case of multiple correlated noise coefficients is dealt with.
Name: ["Willems J.L."]

Title: A computational view of perception
Abstract: A computational approach to visual perception is outlined. The investigation centers on two problems. One concerns the shape, and the other the edges, of dot figures. In determining edges it is not possible to delimit arbitrarily the region on which each point computes. So in this context a global computation is defined. This leads to a novel way of investigating clustering. When the edges of a figure have been sequenced to yield the boundary it is then possible to determine its shape. The study of shape has been confined to convex figures. In these an attempt is made to extract global units which correspond to corner like regions. Finally, it is suggested that a theory which evolves in the manner described has a more unitary aspect than other approaches. (Journal received: 28 Nov. 1974)
Name: ["Rosenberg B.", "Langridge D.J."]

Title: OPTIMAL DECISION PROCEDURES FOR FINITE MARKOV CHAINS - 2. COMMUNICATING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A Markov process in discrete time with a finite state space is controlled by choosing the transition probabilities from a given convex family of distributions depending on the present state. The immediate cost is prescribed for each choice and it is required to minimize the average expected cost over an infinite future. The paper considers a special case of this general problem and provides the foundation for a general solution. The main result is that an optimal policy exists if each state of the system can be reached with positive probability from any other state by choosing a suitable policy.
Name: ["Bather John"]

Title: REPRESENTATION OF BOOLEAN FUNCTIONS BY MULTIFUNCTIONAL LOGIC ELEMENTS.
Abstract: A decomposition algorithm is described for an arbitrary Boolean function using a basis of 24 functions which can be implemented by a multifunctional logic element. The optimality criterion for the algorithm is the maximum number of logic-element inputs that are used.
Name: ["Stepanovskaya I.A.", "Uskach M.A."]

Title: FORCING FUNCTION SELECTION FOR IDENTIFICATION IN HUMAN RESPIRATORY CONTROL.
Abstract: Input forcing function selection for discriminating among alternative structural models and for estimating parameters of functional models is considered. The model outputs are corrupted by an additive noise source, which represents the so-called breath-to-breath variation in the observation of a ventilation response to an end-tidal CO//2-O//2 forcing function input. The problem of forcing function selection for model discrimination is formulated around minimizing the probability of error in model selection while the problem of forcing function selection for model parameter estimation is formulated around minimizing the parameter estimation error variance. Forcing function selection is illustrated by considering end-tidal CO//2 inputs that enhance parameter estimation for a functional model that summarizes normoxic respiratory controller behavior.
Name: ["Swanson G.D.", "Bellville J.W."]

Title: TASK-SCHEDULING ALGORITHM FOR A MULTIPROGRAMMING COMPUTER SYSTEM.
Abstract: Presented are a description and analysis of a task scheduling algorithm which is applicable to third generation computer systems. The analysis is carried out using a model of a computer system having several identical task processors and a fixed amount of memory. The algorithm schedules tasks having different processor-time and memory requirements. The goal of the algorithm is to produce a task schedule which is near optimal in terms of the time required to process all of the tasks. An upper bound on the length of this schedule is the result of deterministic analysis of the algorithm. Computer simulations demonstrate the applicability of the algorithm in actual systems, even when some of the basic assumptions are violated.
Name: ["Krause K.L.", "Shen V.Y.", "Schwetman H.D."]

Title: STRONG VARIATION ALGORITHMS FOR OPTIMAL CONTROL PROBLEMS WITH CONTROL AND TERMINAL INEQUALITY CONSTRAINTS.
Abstract: This paper presents several new algorithms for solving optimal control problems with general constraints on the control and inequality constraints on the terminal state. The algorithms are of the differential dynamic programming (strong variation) type. Terminal inequality constraints are dealt with by incorporating features of nonlinear programming algorithms of the feasible directions type.
Name: ["Mayne D.Q."]

Title: MULTIPLE SEQUENCE RANDOM NUMBER GENERATORS.
Abstract: A method is described for converting a single sequence random number generator to a multiple sequence generation. Although many discrete event simulation models utilize a single random number sequence, regardless of the number of random variables included in the model, in many discrete event simulation models, a unique random number sequence is desirable for each random variable in the model. Failure to incorporate this feature may lead to ill-behaved models having a much larger variability than is possible with multiple sequences. An application is included that compares simulation results obtained using a single sequence of random numbers to those obtained using a unique sequence for each random variable in the model.
Name: ["Mize Joe H."]

Title: MINI-COMPUTER BASED WORD RECOGNITION SYSTEM.
Abstract: A speech recognition device is described of the type that replaces the ‚Ä≥typing‚Ä≥ by ‚Ä≥speaking‚Ä≥ .
Name: ["Capel A.C.", "Little W.D."]

Title: ADAPTIVE SYSTEMS RESEARCH IN THE U. S. NAVY.
Abstract: Pattern recognition and its application to ocean surveillance and the near-real-time screening of tactical reconnaissance imagery presented to the pilot are presented as a typical adaptive systems project in the Navy. The performance of a pattern-recognition device is compared with that of a human operator. It is concluded that the human operator will make the final decision, but he will be aided by a pattern-recognition device. The interpretation of unfamiliar information such as radar imagery or radar range profiles poses considerable problems for the human operator, and therefore pattern recognition is needed the most in this area. The basic pattern recognition process is briefly described and an example is given of processing techniques for pattern recognition which have been implemented. The requirements and the need for a pattern-recognition device for ocean surveillance and near-real-time automatic screening of tactical resonnaissance information are outlined.
Name: ["Hueber W."]

Title: REPRESENTATION OF SETS ON MASS STORAGE DEVICES FOR INFORMATION RETRIEVAL SYSTEMS.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: In order to conserve storage space, one method of storing sets of positive integers, namely the Bit Stream Set Representation is described here, which assigns a single binary digit (bit) in storage to each node in the universe.
Name: ["Byrom Stuart T.", "Hardgrave Walter T."]

Title: OPTIMAL INSTANTANEOUS OUTPUT-FEEDBACK CONTROLLERS FOR LINEAR STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The problem of determining a linear feedback control that depends only on the instantaneous value of the system output is solved for a class of linear stochastic systems with quadratic cost criterion. For the finite time (steady-state) version it is shown that a two point boundary value problem (two nonlinear algebraic equations) must be solved to implement the optimal control. The iterative methods to solve the above equations are briefly reviewed. A number of examples solved on a digital-computer are included.
Name: ["Kurtaran Ben-Zion", "Sidar Menachem"]

Title: SEQUENTIAL DIAGNOSIS OF DIGITAL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The problem of generating decision trees for sequential fault diagnosis of combinational digital networks is considered in this paper. Minimal decision trees are derived using the dynamic programming method which becomes inefficient for large networks. Therefore nearly minimal decision trees are constructed using the information gain weighting function. It is shown that the number of computations and the size of computer memory required for deriving the nearly minimal solution are significantly smaller than those required for deriving the minimal solution. Finally, the nearly minimal solution is extended to module level sequential diagnosis in which one has to distinguish among faults in different modules only.
Name: ["Koren Israel"]

Title: An algorithm for pattern classification using the concept of characteristic vector of the output of threshold element
Abstract: This paper presents an algorithm for pattern classification using the concept of characteristic vector of a Boolean function first proposed by Dertouzos for single-threshold element realization. It is shown that the algorithm is convergent for a finite number of iterations. Depending on the choice of a parameter, three correction rules which are the fixed increment rule, the absolute correction rule and the fractional correction rule can be obtained from the algorithm. The quantity (b - b<sup>j</sup>) used in the algorithm is shown to be equivalent to the augmented pattern used in pattern classification in the literature. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Chan W.-C."]

Title: A decomposition algorithm for optimality problems in tree-structured networks
Abstract: In this paper, various optimality problems (such as the shortest route, most reliable route and maximum capacity route problems) are studied in networks which admit a tree-like representation. A general decomposition algorithm is presented which offers important computational advantages over standard matrix-type optimality calculations. Moreover, when implemented for particular classes of decomposed networks, the general algorithm is shown to provide substantial improvements over existing decomposition methods. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Shier D.R."]

Title: Solvable classes of discrete dynamic programming
Source: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: As finite state models to represent a discrete optimization problem given in the form of an r-ddp (recursive discrete decision process), three subclasses of r-msdp (recursive monotone sequential decision process) are introduced in this paper. They all have a feature that the functional equations of dynamic programming hold and there exists an algorithm (in the sense of the theory of computation) to obtain the set of optimal policies. (In this sense, we may call them solvable classes of discrete dynamic programming.) Besides the algorithms for obtaining optimal policies, two types of representations are extensively studied for each class of r-msdp's. Other related decision problems are also discussed. It turns out that some of them are solvable while the rest of them are unsolvable. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Ibaraki T."]

Title: A mathematical model of learning under schedules of interresponse time reinforcement
Abstract: A model is proposed for free responding under schedules of interresponse time reinforcement. Each response generates a pattern of stimuli that changes in an orderly way over time. At any time the changing pattern may be sampled, and the state of conditioning of the sampled pattern determines whether or not a response actually occurs. The prediction of this model for the asymptotic distribution of interresponse times is derived. The predictions are tested against data from ratio, interval, and DRL schedules of reinforcement. The fit of the model is sufficiently good to make it worth-while continuing investigation of the model. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Ambler S."]
Affiliations: [' Now at the University of Auckland']

Title: The use of operator factorization for linear control and estimation
Abstract: The linear filtering, prediction and smoothing problems as well as the linear quadratic control problems can very generally be formulated as operator equations using basic linear algebra. The equations are of Fredholm type II, and they are difficult to solve directly. It is shown how the operator can be factorized into two Volterra operators using a matrix Riccati equation. Recursive solution of these triangular operator equations is then obtained by two initial value differential equations. The proofs of smoothing and optimal control under known disturbances are in this way especially clear and simple. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Hagander P."]

Title: Analysis Technique for Asynchronous Automata. | [METOD ANALIZA ASINKHRONNYKH AVTOMATOV.]
Abstract: A technique is considered which starts with a given system of excitation functions and arrives at transition functions written in the form of a table with generalized input states. The technique can be used for the design of digital control devices where an analysis of their functional algorithms given in the schematic form or as a system of excitation functions of internal elements is necessary.
Name: ["Lagovier V.A."]

Title: Optimal allocation of instructional effort to interrelated learning strands
Abstract: The problem of allocating instructional effort to two interrelated blocks of learning material is studied. In many learning environments, the amount of material that has been mastered in one area of study affects the learning rate in another distinct but related area-for example, the curriculum subjects of mathematics and engineering. A model is developed that describes this phenomenon, and the Pontryagin Maximum Principle of control theory is applied to determine optimal instructional policies based on the model. The nature of this optimal solution is to allocate instructional effort so that the learner follows a maximal average learning rate "turnpike" path until near the end of the study period and then concentrates on only one strand. This strategy, when applied to a more realistic stochastic model, defines a closed-loop feedback controller that determines daily instructional allocation based on the best current estimate of how much the student has learned. This estimate is calculated by a multistage linear filter based on the Kalman filtering technique. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Chant V.G.", "Atkinson R.C."]

Title: On-line identification of distributed parameter systems
Abstract: A method is suggested for the identification of distributed parameter systems. The method is suitable for on-line identification and uses non-linear programming to minimize the integral of the weighted error squared over an observation interval. An exponential form for the weighting function is used. The factors which affect the identification are studied, and an optimal identifier is determined. A closed form expression for the estimated parameters is derived in the case of systems with slowly varying parameters. The effect of noise is studied. Experimental results are given to show the applicability of the methods suggested. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Hamza M.H.", "Sheirah M.A."]

Title: REAL-TIME, THREE-DIMENSIONAL, VISUAL SCENE GENERATION WITH COMPUTER GENERATED IMAGES.
Abstract: This article discusses briefly the general area of visual simulation, of which computer generated images (CGI) is a part. The chronology of developments leading to the present state of the art in this field is covered. The capabilities of systems currently operational or under construction are described in some detail. Problems associated with achieving desired results are discussed with their solutions or current status. Emphasis is given recent developments not previously reported in the literature.
Name: ["Bunker W.Marvin"]

Title: A straight forward and flexible design method for complex data-base management systems
Abstract: Human manipulation of objects generally includes handling knowledge concerning these objects. Knowledge handling requires in its turn the manipulation of documents. Document manipulation will be shown to require information transfer, storage and retrieval. When large amounts of information are to be stored and retrieved, the need arises for the creation of information storage and retrieval systems. This paper presents a description and design method for such systems. The method is based on a modelling technique. A logical system model will be shown to be derivable from the general objectives and the collection of tasks set for a system. It will then be explained how the physical realization of an information storage and retrieval system can be derived from its logical model taking account of hard- and software properties of the computer system and the programming language to be used. Finally a detailed outline will be presented for a design procedure. The practical applicability of this procedure has been proved during the design of several large data-base management systems. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Jonkers H.L."]

Title: On optimal nonlinear estimation part I: Continuous observation
Abstract: A generalization of the Bucy representation theorem, which plays the same role in the case of general optimal estimation for an arbitrary random process as does the Bucy theorem in the case of optimal filtering for a diffusion process, is obtained under very weak hypotheses. It forms the cornerstone of the paper, from which all the other results are deduced. Some properties of optimal smoothing and prediction are briefly discussed. The conditional densities of the smoothing and prediction processes are expressed in terms of the conditional density of the filtering process. Smoothing and prediction for the class of systems which reduce, via the concept of finite dimensional sensor orbits, to the case of linear dynamics are investigated, thereby illustrating the applicability of previous results in order to obtain efficiently computable solutions. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Lo J.T.-H."]

Title: A decision procedure using discrete geometry
Abstract: A decision procedure is given which makes essential use of concepts in discrete geometry. The procedure decides for any one-state Turing machine with three-dimensional tape, whether or not it has an immortal configuration, i.e., it solves the uniform halting problem for such devices. The history and significance of the problem is examined. The solution is given with the main motivation of showing how traditional mathematical concepts can be used in decision procedures. The paper is introductory in the sense that all notions are carefully defined. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Herman G.T.", "Jackowski J.A."]
Affiliations: [' State University of New York at Buffalo']

Title: On the identification of multi-output linear time-invariant and periodic dynamic systems
Abstract: In this paper we describe an efficient computational algorithm for estimating the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of a linear time-invariant multi-output dynamic system, using only output observations, for qualitative analysis of the transition matrix or for evaluating its eigenvalues. We also give some computational results of the identification of those systems using the Ho-Kalman approach. Furthermore, an identification scheme for high-frequency periodic systems of unknown periods is described in detail. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Sameh A.H.", "Heimerdinger W.L."]

Title: Descriptive modeling of subjective probabilities
Abstract: A nonfrequentistic model of subjective probability was tested in an empirical, subjective estimation task. The model relies on a characterization of stimulus similarities as distances in a cognitive space. This representation was independently tested using a multidimensional scaling analysis of similarities data. Subjective probability estimates given by the subjects for a related set of stimuli were then shown to be highly consistent with respect to their similarity judgments, and predictable by the model. The experiment also utilized special transformations on the stimuli to test consistency properties of subject probabilities. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Wise J.A.", "Mockovak W.P."]

Title: Information theory of neural noise in hearing
Abstract: The information capacity of the peripheral auditory system, as limited by the neural noise effect, is computed. The cochlear patterns are taken to be continuous space-time surfaces, with parameters of characteristic length and characteristic time as estimated from mechanical and synaptic transfer functions. The output messages are taken to be the sets of spike counts from small, optimally-dimensional subdivisions of the space-time domain on the auditory nerve. The computed upper and lower bounds on capacity are 5160 and 8500 bits/sec. respectively, in agreement with a previos determination which was based on psychoacoustic measurements of difference limen and masking distance. The agreement implies that the limitation on capacity is peripheral rather than central, and that the physiological phenomenon of neural noise accounts for the psychoacoustic phenomena of limited acuity of hearing. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Rink R.E."]

Title: A technique for machine-aided indexing
Abstract: Subject indexing of text can, in principle, be accomplished in many ways. The technique for machine-aided indexing (MAI) developed at the Defense Documentation Center (DDC) is illustrated on a randomly chosen abstract. Additional text is provided in coded form so that the reader can more fully explore this technique and form his own opinion of the applicability and versatility of this particular procedure. The DDC method for subject indexing is very close to operational status for a data base which grows at the rate of two million words of text per year. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Klingbiel P.H."]

Title: The set of solutions for Boolean equations
Abstract: The set of solutions for Boolean equations are required in certain classes of bivalent programming and deterministic scheduling problems. The purpose here is to determine the set of solutions in a general manner. The aim is not directed toward an optimal solution. General truth table concepts are reviewed and extended. The extensions are threefold: (a) a reinterpretation of the truth table concepts for the designation numbers that identify the vertices of the unit hypercube, (b) a statement of a primitive algorithm for the computation of the set of designation numbers which correspond to the vertices of the solution space and (c) an extension of this primitive algorithm. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Turksen I.B."]

Title: GEOMETRICAL APPROACH TO MULTIVALUED LOGIC FUNCTION SYNTHESIS.
Abstract: The paper presents a new method of multivalued logic function synthesis based on implementation of a simple, practical realization operator ‚Ä≥Two Side Upper Limiter‚Ä≥ . The method is based on assumption that every N valued, n variable function forms a discrete n-dimensions hyper space. The space is divided into convex subspaces which includes points of the same value.
Name: ["Janczewski L.J."]

Title: REGULATORY FEEDBACK CONTROL OF NONLINEAR POPULATION DYNAMICS.
Abstract: Recently developed theory for the noninteracting control of nonlinear systems is applied to a mathematical model for competition between two species. A regulatory feedback control law is derived which enables the automatic regulation of the population to desired levels.
Name: ["Schoenau Greg J."]

Title: MAXIMAL RATE PIPELINED SOLUTIONS TO RECURRENCE PROBLEMS.
Abstract: On a pipelined computer, where the total stage delay in computing f is d//f time units, the solution output rate is one new X//i each d//f time unit. This paper describes a method for increasing this rate to 1 per time unit when the function f has certain simple functional properties. The total stage delay and complexity of the resulting pipelines are also described.
Name: ["Kogge Peter M."]

Title: RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN STATISTICAL RISKS AND THE LEAST-MEAN-SQUARE-ERROR DESIGN CRITERION IN PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: A theoretical justification is provided for the use of the least-mean-square-error design criterion in the context of the feature selection and ordering problem. It is shown that for an arbitrary matrix of costs of misclassification, and for a well chosen objective function, the minimization of the approximation error results in the minimization of an upperbound of the Bayes risk. In the case of equal cost of misclassification, it is shown that the least-mean-square-error is an upper bound on the Bayes error probability. Conditions are obtained under which a) the bound is as tight as possible, and b) the least-mean-square-error is equal to the error probability of the nearest-neighbor decision rule, and to the average conditional quadratic entropy. Some remaining problems are discussed.
Name: ["Devijver Pierre A."]

Title: ON RECONSTRUCTION OF AMBIGUOUS PATTERNS.
Abstract: A number of algorithms are developed related to the reconstruction of ambiguous patterns using the x- and y- projections. Algorithm I identifies the unambiguous subpatterns of a similar pattern, while Algorithm II detects and reconstructs the unambiguous subpatterns from its projections. Properties found in a completely ambiguous pattern and relations to previous results are explored. An algorithm to compute the number of similar patterns is also outlined.
Name: ["Wee W.G."]

Title: NEW MULTICLASS CLASSIFICATION METHOD: MODIFIED MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD DECISION RULE.
Abstract: A new multiclass decision rule is proposed for classification when the conditional density function of each class has multivariate normal distribution with unequal mean vector and different covariance matrix. This new decision rule, called modified maximum likelihood decision rule (MMLDR), will be equivalent to optimum Bayes decision rule when the covariance matrices are equal and the a priori class probabilities are equally likely. The estimated MMLDR works much better than the estimated Bayes decision rule in actual multiclass samples, and when the samples are multivariate normal distributions, the estimated Bayes decision rule has a slightly better classification result than the estimated MMLDR. The error rates for each class for this MMLDR is analyzed. The comparison of performance on both the estimated MMLDR and the Bayes is also presented.
Name: ["Chang J.K.", "Dwyer III S.J."]

Title: INTERACTIVE SIMULATION PROGRAMMING SYSTEM WHICH CONVERSES IN ENGLISH.
Abstract: An experimental system for producing simulation programs through natural language dialogue with a computer is described. With the current version of this system, which operates under CP/CMS on an IBM 360/67, a queueing problem may be stated to the computer in English. The system checks the problem description for completeness, and if necessary, asks questions which may be answered in English. Then it can produce an English description of the problem as it ‚Ä≥sees‚Ä≥ it and a GPSS program for performing the simulation. The user may then modify the problem through further dialogue to produce additional programs, as desired. A complete sample problem is included in the paper.
Name: ["Heidorn George E."]

Title: THEORY OF CHARACTER RECOGNITION BY PATTERN MATCHING METHOD.
Abstract: The pattern matching method is theoretically studied based on the structure of patterns. Secondly, the input pattern is defined in a generalized form including a ‚Ä≥blurring‚Ä≥ parameter. The blurring operation has the merit of suppressing noises accompanying with the input pattern, but has the demerit of decreasing the similarity measure. A new processing method of canonicalization is defined that overcomes this difficulty. Thirdly, the mathematical structure of the similar pattern set of the same category class is studied. A practical optical character reader ASPET/71 capable of reading printed characters with very poor print quality has been designed by the theory described.
Name: ["Iijima Taizo", "Genchi Hiroshi", "Mori Kenichi"]

Title: APPLICATION OF A NONMETRIC MULTIDIMENSIONAL SCALING METHOD FOR FEATURE SELECTION IN PATTERN RECOGNITION SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The results of an analysis of the geometrical relationships between pattern and feature representatives in a joint space are used for the selection of a reduced set of features. A set of data representing handprinted characters of the numerals 0 through 9 is used to illustrate the proposed feature selection procedure. The original starting set of features was reduced by almost fifty percent and the discrimination power of the resulting reduced set of features was slightly improved over that of the full set of features.
Name: ["Milojkovic D.V.", "Goetze A.J.", "Tappert C.C."]

Title: HOLOGRAPHIC PATTERN RECOGNITION: NEW THOUGHTS ON OLD PROBLEMS.
Abstract: Two difficulties which arise in the attempt to apply holographic matched filtering to pattern recognition are that the pattern location is seldom precise enough to permit matched filtering, and that the use of simple threshold circuits to perform the recognition is unreliable. It has been found that when matched filtering is precluded, the next best approach is both easy and useful and that more complicated recognition circuits produce an increase in system reliability.
Name: ["Caulfield H.J."]

Title: COMPUTATIONAL DELAY IN COMPUTER CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The problem of computational delay in the design of computer control systems is considered. Design of digital controllers to satisfy specifications such as minimum settling time, minimum error, etc. often lead to control laws whose output must be calculated from the present sampled value of the input. Since any digital process requires a finite time to accomplish such a calculation, the actual controller output will be delayed from its desired output time. When this computational delay becomes significant, system performance is affected. A modified control algorithm is proposed whereby the effects of the computational delay time are eliminated and yet the dynamics of the designed system are preserved. An example is discussed to illustrate the effects of the computational delay and the advantages of the modified controller.
Name: ["Haberland B.L.", "Rao S.S.", "Eisenberg L."]

Title: State Reduction in Incompletely Specified Finite-State Machines
Abstract: The problem of reducing the number of states in an arbitrary incompletely specified deterministic finite-state machine to k states (for a given k) has proven intractible to solution within ‚Äúreason- able‚Äù time; most techniques seem to require exponential time. Two reduction techniques-state assignment to the DON'T CARE entries, and so-called ‚Äústate splitting‚Äù‚Äìare investigated. For both of the techniques, the question, ‚ÄúCan I achieve an equivalent k state machine?‚Äù is shown to be polynomial complete, with the resulting conjecture that neither is solvable in time bounded by a polynomial function of the size of the machine. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Pfleeger C.P."]
Keywords: ["donr care conditions", "fmite automaton", "incompletely specified finite-state machine", "machine minimization", "maximum compatibles"]

Title: ECONOMICS OF SEGREGATED AND INTEGRATED SYSTEMS IN DATA COMMUNICATION WITH GEOMETRICALLY DISTRIBUTED MESSAGE LENGTHS.
Abstract: Integrating two different message switching systems into one with the resultant integrated system having the combined channel capacity, need not necessarily result in improved performance. This segregated system vs. integrated system question has been adequately answered in a recent communication for the specific case when the message arrivals are Poisson processes and the message lengths for the two systems are (separately) exponentially distributed. Recent investigations indicate that in computer communications traffic, a better approximation of the message lengths is provided by the geometric distribution. This paper presents a new algorithm which establishes the relative superiority of the segregated or the integrated system for the geometrically distributed message lengths.
Name: ["Verma P.K.", "Rybczynski A.M."]

Title: COMPUTER CONTROL FOR MANNED AND AUTOMATED SPACE VEHICLES.
Source: American Astronautical Society, Scientific Technology Series
Abstract: Digital computers are fundamental to the enhancement and replacement of human capability in spacecraft. Past and future progress are discussed in several aspects of computer technology, including computer design, software design, algorithms, the man-machine interface, and system structures. Fifteen years from now, thanks to developments in system structure, software, reliability, and algorithms, the computers and software in space will be able to perform at the level of those on the ground today. With these developments, there will be important advances in the performance of space vehicles.
Name: ["Hopkins Jr. Albert L."]

Title: ENTROPY MINIMAX, A NON-BAYESIAN APPROACH TO PROBABILITY ESTIMATION FROM EMPIRICAL DATA.
Abstract: In this paper, author briefly reviews the entropy minimax concept, describes recent developments in applying it both to potential function analysis and to cluster analysis, and explains its non-Bayesian characteristics. The objective of the entropy minimax method is to use the information contained in the sample observations and general background information to estimate outcome class probabilities as a function of location in ‚Ä≥feature space‚Ä≥ (the ‚Ä≥space‚Ä≥ whose axes are the various quantitative and qualitative features) and the uncertainties in these estimates.
Name: ["Christensen R.A."]

Title: AUTOMATED SYSTEM FOR THE APPRAISAL OF HYDROCARBON PRODUCING PROPERTIES.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: This article introduces an automated system for the appraisal of hydrocarbon producing properties. Simulation of further research in the area of hydrocarbon production, prediction and hydrocarbon property appraisal is emphasized.
Name: ["Leeper Kim D."]

Title: Z-Resolution: Theorem-Proving with Compiled Axioms
Abstract: An improved procedure for resolution theorem proving, called Z-resolution, is described. The basic idea of Z-resolution is to ‚Äúcompile‚Äù some of the axioms in a deductive problem. This means to automatically transform the selected axioms into a computer program which carries out the inference rules indicated by the axioms. This is done automatically by another program called the specializer. The advantage of doing this is that the compiled axioms run faster, just as a compiled program runs faster than an interpreted program. A proof is given that the inference rule used in Z-resolution is complete, provided that the axioms ‚Äúcompiled‚Äù have certain properties. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Dixon J.K."]

Title: ESTIMATION OF THE GRADIENT OF A DENSITY FUNCTION AND ITS APPLICATIONS IN PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: Nonparametric density gradient estimation using a generalized kernel approach is investigated. Conditions on the kernel functions are derived to guarantee asymptotic unbiasedness, consistency, and uniform consistency of the estimates. The results are generalized to obtain a simple mean-shift estimate that can be extended in a k-nearest neighbor approach. Applications of gradient estimation to pattern recognition are presented using clustering and intrinsic dimensionality problems with the ultimate goal of providing further understanding of these problems in terms of density gradients.
Name: ["Fukunaga Keinosuke", "Hostetler Larry D."]

Title: NEW APPROACH TO THE PROBLEMS OF CLICKS OF A PHASE LOCKED LOOP FM DETECTOR (PLL).
Abstract: It is shown that there exists inputs which are not clicks that cause clicks at the PLL output. These inputs which are here called ‚Ä≥subclicks‚Ä≥ can be characterized by certain bounds of their parameters. Subclick existence is proved and the bounds of the parameters are found both analytically and by means of computer simulation. The results of this work may enable one to compute the subclick rate, from which the deterioration of PLL threshold, due to this phenomenon, can be existimated. The existence of subclicks emphasizes the fact that PLL can be not only a filter for clicks at its input, but also a generator for clicks.
Name: ["Bar-Ness Y.", "Baron R."]

Title: COMPUTER SIMULATION OF DIGITAL SYSTEMS WITH DELAYS IN THEIR COMPONENTS.
Abstract: A digital computer program for the simulation of digital circuits considering component delay has been developed. The program uses discrete event simulation techniques and its purpose is to analyze systems using commercial digital IC's data. The final goal of the project is to simulate and diagnose digital systems with a large number of components.
Name: ["Medina-Vaillard Luis Manuel", "Sianez-Gutierrez Jorge"]

Title: RANGE-RATE FROM DME-AIR DATA MEASUREMENTS.
Source: IEEE Electron and Aerosp Syst Conv, Rec
Abstract: A process for estimating the radial velocity of an aircraft to a known DME ground transponder by combining slant range information and air data is discussed. The idea is based on characterizing the flight of an aircraft by a series of connected intervals in which the profile is described by a polynomial in time having stationary coefficients. Radial velocity is itself a function of time dependent on these coefficients and is derived by linear methods from multiple measurements of range.
