A Kalman-Bucy filter mechanization for estimating the radial velocity from multiple measurements of range and air data is also described.
Name: ["Lee Bernard"]

Title: OPTIMIZATION OF LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH TRANSPORTATION LAGS FOR QUADRATIC CRITERIA.
Abstract: Optimization problems for linear systems with transportation lags are considered. The performance criteria are quadratic both in control and state. Besides time and space varying controls, also actuators interpreted as time invariant parameters are admitted. The solution of the optimization problem is based on the maximum principle. For the optimal controls, the optimal parameters, and the optimal trajectories analytical solutions in the time domain are given. From the general results a special case is derived which appears if the transportation process consists of pure time delays. As an example, the optimization of a heat exchanger illustrates the general theoretical results.
Name: ["Lunderstaedt R."]

Title: OPTIMUM TIME-SHARING ALGORITHM FOR A SERVICING DEVICE IN A QUEUING SYSTEM WITH INTERRUPTIONS.
Abstract: A system is considered in which the servicing of any request can be interrupted at any instant and the request is transferred to a queue to await service. A partial criterion for evaluating the optimality of organization of service is introduced.
Name: ["Gerasimov V.I."]

Title: HIGH-SPEED IMAGE PROCESSING METHOD FOR BANKING APPLICATIONS.
Abstract: Image Processing is basically a technique of verifying input document sequence against a list of expected input sequence. The heart of Image Processing is the search algorithm, which must allow for out of sequence or missing documents in the input stream. The search algorithm presented here is significantly different from known systems and is performed independently from a host CPU. This method of Image Processing gives a complete image search of up to 17 images and allows image file refile, without affecting throughput during normal operation.
Name: ["Baldwin B.E.", "Schoeps F.D."]

Title: NOVEL ANALOG-MEMORY CELL FOR APPLICATION IN PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: A novel simple circuit utilizing a pair of complementary IGFETs was used as the basic computation cell for applications in pattern recognition. Each cell has a complete parabolic I-V characteristic. Using suitable connections, a number of paralleled cells gives, in just a single operation, the mean square-deviation between two sets of data. This is also the minimum Euclidean distance between two pattern vectors. Using non-volatile memory devices (MNOS-FETs) in place of the regular IGFETs, one of the pattern vectors can be electrically preset. The operating characteristics of the individual as well as arrayed cells are presented. Abstract only.
Name: ["Yu K.K.", "Reitboeck H.J.", "Brody T.P."]

Title: STRUCTURE AND DESIGN OF LINEAR MODEL FOLLOWING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: This paper investigates the problem of designing a compensating control for a linear multivariable system so that the impulse response matrix of the resulting closed-loop system coincides with the impulse response matrix of a prespecified linear model; this is the Model Following Problem. A new formulation of the problem is developed, and necessary and sufficient conditions for a solution to exist are stated. An upper bound is determined for the number of integrators needed to construct the compensating control and, if the open-loop plant in question possesses a left-invertible transfer matrix, this bound is shown to be as small as possible. The relationship between the internal structure of a model following system and the model being followed is explained and a description is given of the possible distributions of systems eigenvalues which can be achieved while maintaining a model following configuration. This leads to a statement of necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a solution to the problem which results in a stable compensated system.
Name: ["Morse A.S."]

Title: An Innovations Approach to Least-Squares Estimation-Part VI: Discrete-Time Innovations Representations and Recursive Estimation
Abstract: The linear stochastic discrete-time realization problem is to find a white-noise driven finite-dimensional linear system whose output generates a specified separable covariance. The solution to this problem is presented in the form of a causal and causally invertible innovations representation (IR) whose existence depends only on the positive definite nature of the separable covariance. It is also shown that least-squares filtered and smoothed estimates of one process given observations of a related colored process can be expressed as linear combinations of the state vector of the JR of the observed process. The analogous continuous-time problems have been studied earlier, and it has been shown that an important role is played by what is known as the relative order of the co-variance. Here this is defined as the number of differencing operations required to produce a delta function component in the differenced covariance. It is shown that, unlike the continuous-time case, the relative order of the covariance does not necessarily induce similar (relative order) constraints on the impulse response of all models whose responses to white noise have the given covariance. This fact is at the heart of certain differences between continuous-time and discrete-time results. It is shown, however, that the innovations representations obey a number of constraints equal to the relative order of the covariance. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Gevers M.R.", "Kailath T."]

Title: UNIFIED ALGORITHM FOR DESIGNING MULTIDROP TELEPROCESSING NETWORKS.
Abstract: It is shown that all the effective heuristics currently used for designing multidrop teleprocessing networks and a whole class of extensions and combinations of these heuristics can be represented by a simple algorithm. This unified algorithm is more powerful than any of the individual heuristics in that designs obtained using it are at least as good, and almost always better, than those obtained by applying other heuristics separately. Using parametrized w-rules, the solutions are competative in quality with designs obtained by extensive branch exchange and are far more effective in computer time. Futhermore, it can be extended to treat a much broader class of problems with a wide variety of constraints and also to yield good solutions to the associated problem of clustering terminals about multiplexers, concentrators, terminal interface processors, or central computers. The efficiency of an algorithm in both computer core and running time requirements depends on how it is implemented. By using clever sorting and searching techniques, and by employing heuristic maneuvering, both the core and running time requirements grow almost linearly proportionally to the total number of terminals for many practical problems.
Name: ["Chou W.", "Kershenbaum A."]

Title: MODEL REFERENCE ADAPTIVE CONTROL USING ONLY INPUT AID OUTPUT SIGNALS.
Abstract: It is shown how globally stable model reference adaptive control systems may be designed using only the plant's input and output signals. Controllers for single input-single output, nonlinear nonautonomous plants are developed based on Lyapunov's direct method and the Meyer-Kalman-Yacubovich lemma. Filtered derivatives of the plant output replace pure derivatives which are normally required in these systems. An augmented error signal replaces the error previously used which is the difference between the model and plant outputs. However, global stability is assured in the sense that this difference approaches zero asymptotically.
Name: ["Monopoli R.V."]

Title: INTERPRETIVE SOFTWARE FOR A LARGE ONE-OFF PROCESS.
Abstract: The use of interpretive software for computer control is discussed, with particular reference to the multi-computer control system for the new European synchrotron. In this context an interpreter is defined as a computer program which accepts high level control language source code as data input and gives the required control action as output directly, thus bypassing the usual steps of compilation, linking and running. This approach offers many advantages which can greatly reduce software effort, both for applications programming and in system design. The disadvantage is slow execution of interpretive programs or increased computing power requirements for a given application. The advantages and disadvantages of interpretive software are considered in the context of the planned synchrotron computer control system. The application of interpretive software for some prototype work is described.
Name: ["Crowley-Milling M.C.", "Hyman J.T.", "Shering G.C."]

Title: COMPUTERIZED INTERACTIVE FINANCIAL FORECASTING SYSTEM.
Abstract: A computerized interactive forecasting system is described, which has been developed for the Finance Department at the Semiconductor Products Division of Motorola Inc. While being basic in its operation, the financial forecasting system has permitted the analysis of large amounts of data on a timely basis. Interactive profit and loss forecasting models have been developed which represent the various operating levels of responsibility in the Division in both domestic and international areas. The financial analyst, from a remote terminal, can communicate with the computer to access, update and report forecast data as well as manipulate any or all the financial models. The forecasting system was designed to place complete control of operation in the hands of the users, and also to provide flexibility in adapting to constantly changing financial forecasting requirements.
Name: ["Wolfe Philip M.", "Deutsch Donald F."]

Title: INCORPORATION OF FALSE ALARMS IN SIMULATIONS OF ELECTRONIC RECEIVERS.
Abstract: A simple method for simulating false alarms in simulations of electronic receivers is developed. False alarms are an important part of electronic receivers and previously their generation was computationally complex because of their random nature and very small probability of occurrence. The approach derives the probability density function of the time between false alarms and shows how, for typical values of false alarm probability, the density function may be approximated by a discrete uniform density. Procedures are outlined for simulating false alarms both in the absence and presence of jamming. Also, a method is shown for representing the false alarm as having a finite width commensurate with the bandwidth of the receiver. A rapid computer algorithm for obtaining the amplitude of a false alarm is derived.
Name: ["Sobczynski V.P.", "Pearson C.J."]

Title: Model of certain stages of recognition of schematic images
Abstract: The paper outlines model concepts on the recognition of schematic images based on analysis of the work of the visual system of man and higher animals. The main stages in the work of the model are: 1) local detection, 2) synthesis of the fragments of the description, 3) checking, 4) advancement of an hypothesis, 5) verification of the hypothesis. Recognition of two-dimensional images the contours of which constitute broken lines is considered. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Krol' V.M.", "Levashov O.V.", "Reklaitis V.K.", "Tanengol'ts L.I."]
Affiliations: ['Institute of Problems of Control (Automation and Telemechanics)']

Title: Anesthesiologist scheduling using a set partitioning algorithm
Abstract: Applications of a computerized technique for daily assignment of attending anesthesiologists to specific tasks in a large operating room suite is presented. A varying complement of attending anesthesiologists are available each day and must be optimally matched with a variable surgical request load. The problem is attacked by formulating it as a mathematical optimization problem of the set partitioning type. The key to success of this approach is a careful choice of a set of possible tasks and an assignment of a "cost" value to each possible task of each available attending anesthesiologist, which reflects the relative desirability of the task. Results are given which show that good assignments are rapidly and consistently generated in this way. An operating cost comparison with current manual methods is favorable. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Ernst E.A.", "Lasdon L.S.", "Ostrander L.E.", "Divell S.S."]

Title: MODEL AND ITS SOLUTION TOWARD A BETTER TRAFFIC SYSTEM.
Abstract: A model for the traffic network, considering signal stations and the roads connecting these signal stations is introduced. Using this graph model, the paper establishes a hierarchy and partitions the network into sub-networks which may be individually designed for minimum delay and proper distinction of the synchronization of the road traffic signals.
Name: ["Kermani Mehdi B."]

Title: THEORY OF EXTENSIVE ORIENTATION CONTROL.
Abstract: The technique for changing the orientation of the flight of a vehicle by a single rotation of the vehicle about the Euler axis is examined. The kinematic relations presented are used in selecting the control moments which provide the required vehicle rotation. The differential equation of motion of the vehicle which characterizes its dynamic properties during extensive control is derived.
Name: ["Bodner V.A.", "Alekseev K.B.", "Zbarskii I.S."]

Title: A Parallel Picture Processing Machine
Abstract: A parallel picture processing machine (PPM) is presented. The proposed machine can perform local operations of both logical and arithmetical character on three by three neighborhoods of digitized pictures. It is essentially a two-dimensional machine but in a restricted sense it can be regarded as three-dimensional. The instruction repertoire is thoroughly discussed and several program examples are presented. In the last section the implementation of the machine is described and various tradeoffs between speed and economy are discussed. A dynamically programmable microprogram store is shown to give great freedom in program design. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Kruse B."]
Keywords: ["digital picture processing", "feature extraction", "local operations", "parallel processing", "sequential machines"]

Title: HIGH SPEED DIGITAL ADAPTIVE ECHO CANCELLER.
Abstract: The main limitation of echo cancelers, to date, has been their failure to adapt to rapidly varying echo path characteristics. An experimental adaptive echo canceler has been constructed to investigate the feasibility of implementing an improved control algorithm which has a faster tracking capability than previous methods. Experimental results are presented which are in good agreement with the predicted performance. It is demonstrated that, using currently available technology, an echo canceler which uses the improved control algorithm would be able to follow frequency offsets of several Hertz while still maintaining good cancelation.
Name: ["Demytko N.", "Mackechnie L.K."]

Title: An Application of Nonlinear Smoothing to Submarine Exercise Track Reconstruction
Abstract: The reconstruction of submarine tracks for tactical exercises is formulated in this paper as a nonlinear, discrete-time, fixed interval smoothing problem, and the extended Kalman filter is used to obtain a solution. The operation of the smoothing algorithm is illustrated with the reconstruction of a 5-h exercise run. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Crane R.N."]

Title: Interaction Between Segmental and Nonsegmental Factors in Speech Recognition
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: The present study demonstrates that spectrograms of Swedish utterances can be read with great accuracy under nontrivial conditions. This result is to be attributed primarily to the development of a formalized strategy that was designed to make it possible for spectrogram readers to derive information on certain grammatical features of an utterance such as word class, word boundaries, endings, and function elements. The input to this strategy consists of segmental phonetic features that the subjects extract from the spectrographic display and of information on prosodic features such as stress and tonal accent. The latter information is specified on the spectrogram for each syllable. An experimental situation is thus created that differs from the informal recognition of unknown utterances from spectrograms. A subject can base his final identification of lexical items not only on segmental phonetic features but also on an error-free specification of prosodic features and, in so far as he has been able to use the strategy successfully, on grammatical information. Experimental results are reported indicating that subjects improve their performance markedly with the aid of the strategy. In conclusion, attention is drawn to the important role that grammar and prosody appear to play in the present experiments and to the implications of the findings for future work on automatic speech recognition and speech perception. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Lindblom B.E.F.", "Svensson S.-G."]
Affiliations: [' Stockholm University', ' Royal Institute of Technology']

Title: Incorporation of Statistical Information for Polynomial and Transcendental Interpolation
Source: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
Abstract: One of the principal considerations in the implementation of automated testing systems is the ‚Äúcost‚Äù of accumulating test data. Because testing is controlled and recorded by a digital computer, only discrete data points are gathered. Also, an elapsed waiting time is necessary in order to establish the test conditions prior to performing a measurement. Due to these factors, the number of measurements has a major influence on the cost of testing devices automatically. It now follows that automated testing of continuous systems will entail interpolation. This paper treats the situation wherein statistical information is substituted for some of the deterministic data in interpolation and extrapolation procedures. The principle advantage with this approach is that a reduction in the number of measurements required to characterize a device through interpolation and extrapolation is achieved. A consequence of utilizing the statistical data is that the device function is said to lie within statistical bounds. In addition to introducing the proposed approach, this paper describes practical considerations in obtaining the required statistical information. A hypothetical example is given in order to illustrate the application of the proposed techniques. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Herman F.H.", "Kobylarz T.J."]

Title: Dynamic Programming for Job Scheduling Problems. | DYNAMISCHE OPTIMIERUNG BEI REIHENFOLGEPROBLEMEN.
Source: Wissenschaftliche Zeitschrift der Technischen Unversitat Dresden
Abstract: Using the example of three special job scheduling problems, the transferability of the already known dynamic optimization algorithms is investigated. For this purpose statements are made about the validity of the Bellman optimality principle by employing two formulas and by using a counterexample.
Name: ["Terno Johannes", "Ullrich Matthias"]

Title: TIMING AND CONTROL GENERATION USING AN ASSOCIATIVE ARRAY.
Abstract: Complex timing and control logic functions is accomplished using an associative array. By use of an associative array of monolithic array oxide silicon devices, the timing and control is electronically alterable and nonvolatile resulting in hardware count reduction.
Name: ["Nosowicz E.J."]

Title: Continuous Parameter Adaptation for Linear Regression Models. | STETIGE PARAMETERANPASSUNG FUER LINEARE REGRESSIONSMODELLE.
Abstract: Controllers with multidimensional parameters are investigated for compatibility of handling the regression models. Various approaches in the selection process of a sequence are studied. An analog computer simulation is shown as the verification of this approach.
Name: ["Peschel M.", "Schwaar M."]

Title: MINIMIZATION OF THE REPRESENTATION OF TRANSIENTS IN ASYNCHRONOUS AUTOMATA.
Abstract: A procedure is proposed for minimizing the number of segments (pulses and pauses) in the representation of the process of transition of an asynchronous automaton from one stable state to another.
Name: ["Levin V.I."]

Title: COORDINATE REPRESENTATION AND STRUCTURAL INVARIANTS FOR MANY-VALUED SWITCHING FUNCTIONS.
Abstract: The main contribution of this paper is an extension of the coordinate representation, developed for binary logic, to switching functions based on any integer radix. These functions are a direct generalization of the Boolean functions of binary logic and are capable of representing information in a much more compact form than their binary counterparts. The purpose is to expand the geometric representation to include switching functions having any number of truth values and arguments.
Name: ["Allen Christopher"]

Title: ON A PATTERN CLASSIFICATION ALGORITHM OF R. L. KASHYAP.
Abstract: The convergence properties of a stochastic approximation type pattern recognition learning algorithm are investigated. Some results by M. A. Aizerman, E. M. Braverman, and L. I. Rozonoer as well as by R. L. Kashyap are further expanded. Necessary and sufficient conditions for the convergence of the algorithm are given, and it is shown that under certain natural conditions the algorithm does not converge. An estimation for the probability of erroneous classification is also proved.
Name: ["Fritz J."]

Title: Approximate solution of Bellman's equation for a class of optimal terminal state control problems. PMM vol. 37, n‚âó3, 1973, pp. 414-425
Source: Journal of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: We consider the problem of the optimal control of the terminal state of a linear system containing random perturbations in the form of Gaussian white noise. We propose a method for the approximate solution of Bellman's equation for one class of such systems in the case when the solution of the deterministic Bellman equation has discontinuities of the first kind in its values or in the values of its derivatives. As an application of the results obtained we give an approximate solution of Bellman's equation corresponding to one model problem in the control of entry into the atmosphere (see [1, 2]) and we compare the result obtained with the results of the numerical calculations in [2]. Some methods for the approximate solution of Bellman's equation have been studied earlier, for example, in [3-6]. Asymptotic expansions with respect to a small parameter, being the noise intensity, were constructed in [4-6] for the case when the deterministic Bellman equation corresponding to a system without random perturbations has a smooth solution. Exact solutions of Bellman's equation were obtained in [3] in certain cases when the system has a dimension of one. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Bratus' A.S."]

Title: PARALLEL ALGORITHMS FOR OPTIMUM NONLINEAR STATE ESTIMATION.
Abstract: Different parallel algorithms for computing the conditional mean state estimate for nonlinear dynamical systems are described. It is shown how the estimation problem can be reformulated so as to utilize parallel computers effectively to approximate the optimal state estimate. The problem of quantization, which plays an important role in the numerical approximation, is considered. An optimal wide-sense quantizer is obtained which can be realized by simple hardware. The parallel algorthms described in this paper are suitable for a large class of parallel computers.
Name: ["Tse Edison", "Larson Robert E."]

Title: NONSUPERVISED PATTERN CLASSIFICATION BASING ON THE NEAREST NEIGHBOUR RULE.
Abstract: Nonsupervised classification of a sample set of observed patterns should result in a partition which reflects an intrinsic structure of the underlying pattern population. However, the resulting partition may also depend upon random details of the pattern configuration within the sample set. An attempt is made to improve reliability by gradually combining small subsets into larger and larger subsets. It is shown that such a procedure performs especially well if the initial partition is provided by means of the nearest neighbour rule.
Name: ["Paulus Erwin"]

Title: The structure of ill structured problems
Abstract: The boundary between well structured and ill structured problems is vague, fluid and not susceptible to formalization. Any problem solving process will appear ill structured if the problem solver is a serial machine that has access to a very large long-term memory of potentially relevant information, and/or access to a very large external memory that provides information about the actual real-world consequences of problem-solving actions. There is no reason to suppose that new and hitherto unknown concepts or techniques are needed to enable artificial intelligence systems to operate successfully in domains that have these characteristics. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Simon H.A."]

Title: TRANSFORMATIONAL GRAMMARS FOR LANGUAGES AND COMPILERS.
Abstract: Several aspects of programming languages can be described conveniently via transformational grammars. Furthermore corresponding language processors, i. e. compiler modules, can be constructed automatically from these grammars. Restriction to local transformations on trees yields efficient processors, or ‚Ä≥transformers‚Ä≥ . Examples are presented to illustrate the practical use of these grammars, as well as to demonstrate their computational complexity. Open questions for research and development are posed.
Name: ["DeRemer Frank"]

Title: NEW CLASS OF SEARCH ALGORITHMS FOR ADAPTIVE COMPUTATION.
Abstract: An adaptive probability state variable (PSV) parameter search algorithm possessing long-term memory has been formulated to cope with systems that must avoid high performance-penalty operating regions. The information gained from all previous experiments is efficiently encoded in multivariate probability distribution functions (pdf's). This long-term memory capability enables the PSV algorithm effectively to avoid future experiments in high penalty regions. The systems considered are resource-limited, and catastrophic failure may occur if parameter values lying in high penalty regions are implemented. Those cases in which the high penalty regions are not known in advance were investigated. The PSV algorithm has the capability of adaptively learning the location and hypervolume of these regions as the search proceeds. The algorithm is explicitly guided in its internal strategies as a function of the remaining system resources and the updated pdf's. Clustering analysis is used both in the discovery of new operating regions and for updating the pdf's. Experimental results are presented.
Name: ["Mucciardi A.N."]

Title: Automatic Control of Ventilation of Gaseous Coal Mine. | [AVTOMATICHESKII KONTROL' PROVETRIVANIYA GAZOVYKH UGOL'NYKH SHAKHT.]
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii, Gornyi Zhurnal
Abstract: Problems of automatic control of ventilation of gaseous coal mines are considered from a theoretical point of view. Problems evaluation of initial data from an insufficient number of methane detectors and air velocity indicators for automatic control and automatic gas protection are discussed. Block diagrams are given for the relevant data processing.
Name: ["Trop A.E.", "Karalyus A.A.", "Tokpanov E.D."]

Title: The Q<sup>*</sup> algorithm-a search strategy for a deductive question-answering system
Abstract: An approach for bringing semantic, as well as syntactic, information to bear on the problem of theorem-proving search for Question-Answering (QA) Systems is described. The approach is embodied in a search algorithm, the Q<sup>*</sup> search algorithm, developed to control deductive searches in an experimental system. The Q<sup>*</sup> algorithm is part of a system, termed the Maryland Refutation Proof Procedure System (MRPPS), which incorporates both the Q<sup>*</sup> algorithm, which performs the search required to answer a query, and an inferential component, which performs the logical manipulations necessary to deduce a clouse from one or two other clauses. The inferential component includes many refinements of resolution. The Q<sup>*</sup> algorithm generates nodes in the search space, applying semantic and syntactic information to direct the search. The use of semantics permits paths to be terminated and fruitful paths to be explored. The paper is restricted to a description of the use of syntactic and semantic information in the Q<sup>*</sup> algorithm. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Minker J.", "Fishman D.H.", "McSkimin J.R."]
Affiliations: [' University of Maryland', ' University of Massachusetts', ' University of Maryland']

Title: Efficient compilation of linear recursive programs
Source: 14th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory
Abstract: A linear recursive program consists of a set of procedures where each procedure can make at most one recursive call. The conventional stack implementation of recursion requires time and space both proportional to n, the depth of recursion. It is shown that in order to implement linear recursion so as to execute in time n one does not need space proportional to n: ne for arbitrarily small e will do. It is also known that with constant space one can implement linear recursion in time n. We show that one can do much better: n e for arbitrarily small c. We also describe an algorithm that lies between these two: it takes time n.log(n) and space log(n). In this context one can demonstrate a speed-up theorem for linear recursion - given any constant-space program implementing linear recursion, one can effectively find another constant space program that runs faster almost everywhere. ¬© 1973 IEEE.
Name: ["Chandra A.K."]

Title: STEPS TOWARD HANDWRITTEN SIGNATURE VERIFICATION.
Abstract: A system of computer programs to isolate and identify important features on handwritten bank checks is described. The inputs to the process are a picture of the signature portion of the bank check, the correct spelling of the expected name, and some known features of the expected handwriting. Using built-in knowledge of the types of features important to forgery detection, the programs select, locate, and identify features in the handwritten signature for output. The programs which carry out this analysis were written in FORTRAN on a UNIVAC 1108, and make extensive use of the XAP picture processing language.
Name: ["Nagel Roger N.", "Rosenfeld Azriel"]

Title: APPLICATIONS OF A PROBABILITY-BASED MODEL.
Abstract: A model for describing the continually (stepwise) decreasing failure rate associated with the software debugging process is applied to a code reading experiment in novel ways. In these applications, the number of purposely inserted errors (seeded errors) is known, and the other parameter of the model, which is the step size, is determined from the error detection rate observed during an initial period of reading of the code.
Name: ["Jelinski Zygmunt", "Moranda Paul B."]

Title: BIO-MEDICAL APPLICATIONS OF A HOLOGRAPHIC SYSTEM FOR AUTOMATIC SURFACE MAPPING.
Abstract: A holographic image projection and tracking system has been developed which can automatically map a surface with high precision. To illustrate the potential usefulness of this technique to biomedical applications, point coordinate data for preselected points and automatically scanned surface profile data has been taken of a skull geometry model. System design studies on this holographic technique show that dimensions of objects of the order of 1 meter in size can be produced from their image to an accuracy of 1 part in 10**4. Moreover, the precise location of the image surface can unambiguously be determined for even matte, featureless surfaces without the need for surface preparation. The skull model data and suggestions for other biomedical applications are presented.
Name: ["Gara Aaron D.", "Majkowski Richard F.", "Hubbard Robert P.", "McLoed Donald G.", "Stapleton Thomas T."]

Title: ONE PROBLEM OF OPTIMUM CONTROL IN A QUEUING SYSTEM (SALE OF TICKETS IN A TRANSPORT SYSTEM).
Abstract: The problem of optimum control in a system servicing two flows of requests with limited capacity and specified operating time is considered. A theorem regarding the form of the optimum control policy is proved.
Name: ["Gertsbakh I.B.", "Fraiman A.B."]

Title: Optimal Linear Estimates of Expectation Value and Regression Coefficient of Homogeneous and Isotropic Random Fields. | OB OPTIMAL'NYKH LINEINYKH OTSENKAKH MATEMATICHESKOGO OZHIDANIYA I KOEFFITSIENTOV REGRESSII ODNORODNYKH I IZOTROPNYKH SLUCHAINYKH POLEI.
Abstract: A problem is considered in which a homogeneous and isotropic random field with unknown mean value m and known correlation function is observed on a circle with given radius. It is shown that the average random field on the circle has least dispersion among all the unbiased estimates of m. Estimates are considered if the random field is observed on the system of concentric circles or on the set of apices of a rectilinear polygon.
Name: ["Yadrenko M.I."]

Title: KALMAN FILTER APPROACH TO ADAPTIVE ESTIMATION OF MULTISPECTRAL SIGNATURES.
Abstract: Because the signatures of remote sensing data from agricultural crops exhibit significant non-stationarity, so that the performance of fixed parameter classifiers degenerates with time and distance from the initial training data, a class of adaptive decision-directed classifiers is being developed based on Kalman filter theory. The Kalman filter is being used to systematically organize various factors in the problem of adapting a classifier of remote sensing data based on the decisions made by the classifier. Limited results to data on two data sets indicate approximately a 25%-40% reduction in rates of misclassification.
Name: ["Crane R.B."]

Title: A practical filter for systems with unknown parameters
Source: Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement and Control, Transactions of the ASME
Abstract: This paper deals with the problem of a practical filter for discrete-time, dynamic systems with unknown parameters whose variation cannot be estimated in advance The modeling errors caused by unknown parameters dearly degrade the filter performance and sometimes lead to divergence of estimation errors. Divergence is said to occur when the calculated covariance of estimation errors becomes very small comparing with the actual covariance. A practical filter that modifies the calculated covariance is developed as a technique for controlling the divergence. This is done by testing whether or not the actual residual at each stage is likely to have come from the calculated distribution, and the calculated covariance is modified when the test is rejected. The numerical results of digital simulation indicate that divergence of estimation errors is observed when the a priori information for dynamic systems is in error and that the divergence is prevented by the proposed filter. ¬© 1973 by ASME.
Name: ["Soeda T.", "Yoshimura T."]

Title: ADAPTIVE OBSERVER FOR DISCRETE LINEAR TIME-INVARIANT SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The problem of estimating the state of a discrete linear time-invariant system when the noise statistics are unknown is considered. In the absence of any knowledge of the noise statistics, an observer with a fixed gain can be used in estimating the state. When more observation information is accumulated, the estimation performance can be improved by directly adjusting the gain of the observer adaptively. An adaptive observer is developed which will converge in mean square to the optimum filter asymptotically.
Name: ["Tse E."]

Title: DECENTRALIZED CONTROL OF AN INTERCONNECTED ELECTRIC ENERGY SYSTEM SUBJECT TO INFORMATION FLOW CONSTRAINTS.
Abstract: The problem of designing a decentralized feedback controller for a class of interconnected linear dynamical systems is considered. The structure of each local controller is constrained to be such that it can be defined via a constant output feedback matrix, and necessary conditions for the resulting parameter optimization problem are given in the form of simultaneous nonlinear algebraic equations. Two methods for solving these equations are discussed and compared relative to computational efficiency. The design methodology is then illustrated via an application to an interconnected electric energy system.
Name: ["Linton T.D.", "Fischer D.R.", "Tacker E.C.", "Sanders Jr. C.W."]

Title: PATTERN RECOGNITION OF CHEST X-RAY IMAGES.
Abstract: Pattern recognition of chest x-ray films is discussed. First, the outline of the software system for automatic photointerpretation of chest x-ray films is introduced briefly. Then the methods for pattern recognition employed in the system are surveyed. Finally, the recognition procedure of abnormal shadows in lung is described in detail, and some of experimental results for real chest photofluorograms are shown.
Name: ["Toriwaki Jun-ichiro", "Suenaga Yasuhito", "Negoro Toshio", "Fukumura Teruo"]

Title: APPLICATION OF COMPUTER VISION TO A SIMULATED ASSEMBLY TASK.
Abstract: The technical feasibility and potential usefulness of computer vision applied to complex industrial parts was recently demonstrated. In the experiment, a special numerically controlled machine tool was modified to perform the simulated assembly task of automatically mounting wheels onto automobile hubs. The wheel-mounting system consisted of three major hardware-software subsystems concerned with vision, recognition, and manipulation. Each subsystem is described in this paper with particular emphasis being placed on the pattern recognition algorithms that were used.
Name: ["Olsztyn Joseph T.", "Rossol Lothar", "Dewar Robert", "Lewis Norman R."]

Title: ESTIMATION UNDER CONSTRAINED SAMPLING.
Abstract: The fragmentation of computer core cells into alternating blocks of free and occupied cells may be crudely expressed by the ratio of the number of free blocks to occupied blocks. A method of estimating the number of free blocks is given, based on a sample of free blocks. However, the sampling units are not freely accessible. The constraint is that larger blocks must be exhaustively sampled before a smaller block can be sampled. The sample size required for a specified precision in the estimate is given by a sequential sampling rule. The theory is developed independent of computers and a variant of the theory is applied to the core fragmentation problem.
Name: ["Ramanujacharyulu C."]

Title: NOTTINGHAM 'SIRCH' ASSEMBLY ROBOT.
Abstract: In this research machine, an attempt is made to apply visual feedback to a versatile handling system in a way which might be acceptable in an industrial environment. The machine incorporates visual feedback through a vidicon television camera coupled to a small digital computer. The computer, after processing the visual data, provides all the control functions for the machine. The main reason for making this development is to remove the need for orderly orientation and presentation of component parts in order to allow a rapid change in re-programming.
Name: ["Heginbotham W.B.", "Gatehouse D.W.", "Pugh A.", "Kitchin P.W.", "Page C.J."]

Title: DISCRETE-TIME STOCHASTIC REALIZATION PROBLEM: MINIMUM VARIANCE PROPERTY OF THE INNOVATIONS REPRESENTATION.
Abstract: The class of all Markovian realizations of a time-varying separable covariance is determined by the class of all state-variances that obey a set of constraints. The solution with the smallest state-variance is the IR (Innovations Representation). It is shown that it can be obtained by directly solving the constraint equations for their smallest solution using a matrix property. Alternatively the IR can be obtained in the usual way via the Kalman filter equations. That the IR has the smallest variance of all Markovian models follows from the stochastic interpretation of its state as the filtered estimate of the state of any other model. The stochastic interpretation of the maximum variance model is a topic of continuing inquiry.
Name: ["Gevers M.", "Kailath T."]

Title: DECOMPOSITION OF TERNARY SWITCHING FUNCTIONS.
Abstract: An extension of the ideas of Roth and Karp on compatibility techniques is used for the systematic decomposition of a ternary switching function F with an arbitrary number of variables. At each stage, the three types of decompositions allowed are simple disjunctive, simple non-disjunctive, and complex disjunctive. For the partition of the input space A into two disjoint subsets, a method is given to generate the disjoint maximal compatible sets which are used to define the necessary two-place functions alpha .
Name: ["Muzio J.C.", "Miller D.M."]

Title: FAST WALSH TRANSFORM SUBROUTINE.
Abstract: Walsh Functions are playing an increasingly important role in computer signal processing, multiplexing pattern recognition, and many other areas. Both in hardware and software applications these functions have many advantages over the standard orthogonal transformations. It has been shown that the transformation can be factored in a way analogous to the Fast Fourier transform algorithms. The program presented for computing the Fast Walsh transform has been adapted from a modification of an FFT subroutine. This algorithm generates the Walsh transform components in order of increasing sequency. Sequency being the half mean number of changes in sign in the half-open interval.
Name: ["Dromey R.G."]

Title: MULTI-PURPOSE COLLISION TRAJECTORY SENSING.
Abstract: The author discusses radar-logic systems as a means of driver-warning with the output of an audio alarm signal. It is shown how these systems can be utilized in deployment of a restraint system, automatic headway control, or as a backup system on an automated highway. It is maintained that by extending the reasoning to a three-dimensional system, it could also be utilized in collision avoidance for aircraft.
Name: ["Tartaglia Paul E."]

Title: MIXED STOCHASTIC OPTIMIZATION ALGORITHM AND ITS APPLICATIONS IN PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: The problem of the minimization of a functional of several parameters is treated. It is supposed that the gradient of the functional is known but the stochastic approximation method cannot be applied since its convergence is not guaranteed due to the form of the functional. A mixed random search-stochastic approximation method insuring this convergence is developed. The method has been applied to the one-step design of pattern recognition systems, i. e. , when unknown parameters in the data analyzer (i. e. , variables in the feature extraction or feature transforming processes) and in the recognizer (such as the weights of a linear discriminant function) are similtaneously optimized with respect to a single performance index.
Name: ["Devroye L.P."]

Title: Optimal utilization of fixed-capacity channels in feedback control
Abstract: The performance limitations on the linear control of a linear plant, due to the presence of a feedback channel with finite information capacity, are considered in this paper. This situation may arise in such diverse applications as (a) the remote control of a plant, using a digital data link for feedback, (b) where quantization errors and bit errors of a digital controller may be modelled as occurring in a noisy digital channel in cascade with an ideal controller, and (c) in human-operator modelling, where the sensory feedback channels are characterized by fixed information capacity due to neural noise. The principle result obtained is that, given the state-dimension n of the plant and the channel capacity Œµ{lunate}, reliability function E(R), and block encoding time T> > 1 C, the optimum data-rate R satisfies the equation 2R=nE(R). This rate provides the optimum tradeoff between the effects of quantization errors and message errors. It is seen that R<sub>opt</sub>‚ÜíC as n becomes large, but that good channel performance is retained provided that > > n T. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Rink R.E."]

Title: FINITE AND INFINITE MEMORY RANGE LEARNING PROCESSES IN STATIONARY AND NONSTATIONARY ENVIRONMENTS.
Abstract: A generalized Bush-Mosteller learning model is discussed simulating both finite memory range learning and infinite memory range imprinting processes, as well as an ideal learning scheme storing all experiences with equal weight. The learning and imprinting dynamics in stationary and nonstationary environments is studied using as a performance criterion the relative entropy of the true with respect to the system's subjective environmental probabilities. For the stationary case learning and imprinting schemes exhibit a symmetrical performance which is nearly optimal for small deviations from the ideal learning scheme. In the nonstationary case imprinting schemes perform poorly, while proper learning processes are capable of keeping the relative entropy at a low level. Their optimal memory range is calculated in terms of the environmental fluctuation time.
Name: ["Pfaffelhuber E."]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR GLOBAL EXTREMUM SEARCH WITH RECOGNITION OF THE STRUCTURE OF THE FUNCTION TO BE OPTIMIZED.
Abstract: A global extremum search algorithm is proposed which is based on recognition of individual structural elements of the function to be optimized. Each element utilizes its own special algorithm and as a result, the effectiveness of extremum search is greatly enhanced.
Name: ["Gulyaev V.V.", "Sukhanov Yu.N."]

Title: APPLICATION OF FOURIER ANALYSIS TO MULTISPECTRAL/SPATIAL RECOGNITION.
Abstract: Investigation of spectral response from materials is made by the approach of the spatial features. It was concluded that the Fourier Transform may be used in a one-dimensional to multi-dimensional analysis of more than one channel of data. The two-dimensional transform represents the Fraunhofer diffraction pattern of the image in optics and has certain invariant features. Physically the diffraction pattern contains spatial features which are possibly unique to a given configuration or classification type. Different sampling strategies may be used to either enhance geometrical differences or extract additional features.
Name: ["Hornung Richard J.", "Smith James A."]

Title: PATTERN RECOGNITION APPROACH TO THE CLASSIFICATION OF NONLINEAR SYSTEMS FROM INPUT-OUTPUT DATA.
Abstract: A method of classifying nonlinear stochastic systems, using pattern recognition and a pattern vector constructed from the input-output data, is proposed for six stated classes of low-order nonlinear systems. The method is capable of extension to additional classes of nonlinear systems. Various applications of the classification procedure are given, particularly in the areas of systems modeling, self-organizing control systems, and learning control systems.
Name: ["Saridis G.N.", "Hofstadter R.F."]

Title: FAULT DIAGNOSIS IN UNIFORM MODULAR REALIZATIONS OF SEQUENTIAL MACHINES.
Abstract: It has been shown that all stuck-at faults inside a tree can be modeled as stuck-at or OR faults on control inputs. The required input sequences have been shown to be of minimal length. When the trees are faulty and faults are such that the set of faults is equivalent to a single module being faulty, then the fault detection test has been extended to perform fault location from the point of view of partial utilization of faulty trees.
Name: ["Prasad B.A.", "Gray F.G."]

Title: LINEAR CONTROL ALGORITHM FOR A FLAT GLASS ANNEALING LEHR.
Abstract: The algorithm demonstrated was tested and has shown the ability to predict the flue temperature corrections required to achieve a preselected temperature profile. The supervisory algorithm is based on the heat transfer between the flue gas and the section of the ribbon directly beneath that flue.
Name: ["Sisoler Gabriel M.", "Wilkins George", "Perryman Richard"]

Title: CONTROL OF STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS WITH NON-MARKOV PARAMETER PROCESSES.
Abstract: One class of systems with non-Markov parameters is considered. A simple artifice is used to obviate some of the difficulties in defining the basic probabilistic structure. The structure of the resulting controller is analysed both qualitatively and quantitatively.
Name: ["Sworder D.D."]

Title: OPTIMAL SEQUENCE ESTIMATORS FOR STATISTICALLY UNKNOWN BINARY SOURCES AND CHANNELS.
Abstract: An information source is considered which is an i. i. d. binary sequence governed by unknown probability measures. The information sequence is transferred through a memoryless binary channel with unknown cross-over probabilities. The channel model also represents those cases in which an input represents those cases in which an input quantizer is always used, so that the incoming information-bearing observations are threshold crossings of the observation process, and the unknown cross-over probabilities are associated with uncertainties concerning the signal-to-noise ratio. The optimal (under a minimum error-probability criterion) sequence estimator (which utilizes the observed threshold crossings) is derived and studied. The receiver is described by a practically implementable algorithm which involves a shortest path calculation, which is performed using the Viterbi algorithm, and appropriately incorporates the sufficient statistics of the unknown parameters. Its similarity to unsupervised decision directed learning procedures is noted.
Name: ["Rubin I."]

Title: Feature lists and confusion matrices
Abstract: This report compares three feature list sets for capital letters, previously proposed by different investigators, on the ability of each to predict empirical confusion matrices. Toward this end, several variants of assumed information processes in recognition were also compared. The best model incorporated: (1) variable feature retrieval probabilities, (2) a goodness-of-match lower threshold below which guessing determines response, and (3) response bias on guessing trials. This model, when combined with one particular proposed feature list set, produced stress values of less than 9% in comparisons to empirical matrices for each of three different Ss. The feature retrieval probability vectors associated with these minimum-stress predictions were highly correlated ( {Mathematical expression}), suggesting considerable generality of process and feature sets between Ss. ¬© 1973 Psychonomic Society, Inc.
Name: ["Geyer L.H.", "DeWald C.G."]
Affiliations: ['Human Factors Program', ' State University of New York at Buffalo']

Title: LOGIC PARTITION FOR MULTI-EMITTER TWO-LEVEL STRUCTURES.
Abstract: Because the efficient use of high-speed logic modules depends on logic designs in which the fan-numbers are kept small and the number of logic delays held to a minimum the authors have developed a logic partition technique, based on the simple decomposition methods of Ashenhurst, which allows the efficient use of a multi-emitter two-level logic structure. The authors describe briefly the circuit operation of a ‚Ä≥Multi-Emitter Two-Level Logic‚Ä≥ configuration (METLL) and present an algorithm for partitioning the logic for single output two-level combinatorial networks. The application of the algorithm is illustrated by some specific examples, which include full adders and an iterative multiplier.
Name: ["Thompson P.M.", "Elmasry M.I."]

Title: An Analytic Comparison of Random Searching and Gradient Searching for the Extremum of a Known Objective Function
Abstract: The relative efficiencies of random searching and gradient searching for the extremum of a known function can be measured by a so-called search loss measure developed by Rastrigan [1]. It will be shown that a simple modification to the basic random searching strategy [1] can lead to a significant relative improvement in the efficiency, i.e., rate of convergence, of the random search. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Lawrence J.P., III", "Emad F.P."]

Title: Computer discrimination of cells in serous effusions. II. Peritoneal fluid
Abstract: The feasibility of discriminating between 'normal mesothelial cells' in peritoneal fluids, reactive mesothelial cells, and ovarian and esophageal tumor cells by means of digitized image analysis is investigated. Satisfactory classification results were attained in both training and object sets; the image properties most suitable for discrimination, error rates, and likelihoods for correct recognition of individual cells are given for each of the cell types.
Name: ["Jahoda E.", "Bartels P.H.", "Bibbo M.", "Bahr G.F.", "Holzner J.H.", "Wied G.L."]

Title: ROBUSTNESS OF LINEAR LEAST-SQUARES FILTERING ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: Some sufficient conditions are given under which the mean-square error of linear least-squares (l. l. s. ) estimates converges to its true steady-state value despite perturbations due to uncertainties in initial conditions, round-off errors in calculation, etc. For state-variable estimators, this property, called robustness, is implied by the exponential asymptotic stability of the estimating filter, but this latter property though desirable is of course far from necessary for the more basic (since mean-square error is the ultimate criterion) property of robustness. A general sufficient condition is presented for robustness of l. l. s. predictors of stochastic processes. This condition is then specialized to l. l. s. estimators for processes described by state-variable models and by autoregressive-moving average difference equation models. It is shown that these conditions can establish robustness in cases where previous criteria either fail or are inconclusive.
Name: ["Aasnaes Hans Bent", "Kailath Thomas"]

Title: OPTIMAL FEEDBACK CONTROL LAW FOR REGULATOR PROBLEMS WITH LINEAR STATE INEQUALITY CONSTRAINTS.
Abstract: A feedback control law for time-invariant regulator problems with linear state inequality constraints is derived by using an interior penalty method. The existence of solutions for arbitrary initial states inside the constrained region is discussed. By uniformly decreasing a penalty parameter, the technique always yields feasible solutions which converge to the optimum.
Name: ["Zeskind R.M.", "Vimolvanich V."]

Title: SCHEDULING WITH PARALLEL PROCESSORS AND LINEAR DELAY COSTS.
Abstract: This paper deals with the sequencing problem of minimizing linear delay with parlallel identical processors. The theoretical properties of this m-machine problem are explored, and the problem of determining an optimum scheduling procedure is examined. Properties of the optimum schedule are given as well as the corresponding reductions in the number of schedules that must be evaluated in the search for an optimum. An experimental comparison of scheduling rules is reported; this indicates that although a class of effective heuristics can be identified, their relative behavior is difficult to characterize.
Name: ["Baker Kenneth R.", "Merten Alan G."]

Title: ONE RANDOM-SEARCH ALGORITHM FOR OPTIMIZING SYSTEMS WITH CONSTRAINTS.
Abstract: A local random-search algorithm with proportional coordinate-by-coordinate training is considered. The memory vector of the system is constructed allowing for variations in the target and constraint functions. To enhance the dynamic quality of readjustment of the memory vector in complex search situations, author employs a variable forgetting factor. The algorithm is adjusted in terms of response; the results are generalized. An example is given which involves the calculation of the optimum construction parameters for a system of nonsimultaneous loads.
Name: ["Valuiskikh V.P."]

Title: SEARCHING A COMPRESSED INDEX.
Abstract: A method is presented for building and searching an index of compressed keys. The difficulty with indexes built with compressed keys is that they must be searched in a sequential fashion. The average number of entries which must be examined is one-half N, where N is the total number of entries. This search can be improved by building a multilevel index, thereby reducing N in a given block. To minimize the number of index levels and reduce the number of entries examined, a directory to each index record may be provided. Instead of constructing a separate directory, it is shown how entries within the index may be modified so that they function as directory entries.
Name: ["Wagner R.E."]

Title: The neural efficiency analyzer: A technological breakthrough for intelligence measurement?
Abstract: Professor John Ertl's Neural Efficiency Analyzer, an innovative test instrument claimed to give an unbiased assessment of intelligence is decribed and discussed. Potential value of the instrument is recognized but the prediction of scholastic achievement based upon measures of neural events is challenged.
Name: ["Parker J.L."]

Title: Redundancy Reducing Block Coding of Controllable Binary Sources - A New Method of Data Compression. | [REDUNDANZMINDERNDE BLOCKCODIERUNG STEUERBARER BINAERQUELLEN - EIN NEUES VERFAHREN ZUR DATENKOMPRESSION.]
Abstract: A new method is described for compressing data by means of graphs (code trees) and algorithms (flow sheets). The method consists of the conversion of the Shannon-Fano-Huffman code and coordinating code words of the same length with long blocks of more frequent symbols and with short blocks of symbols having lesser frequency. The method comprises the run-length coding as a special case . Like the Shannon-Fano-Huffman code, the method, with increasing length of code word, converges upon the limit value given by the entropy. The factors of attainable compression are given in tabular form.
Name: ["Fey P."]

Title: APPLICATION OF REAL-TIME DIGITAL AUTOMATIC GAUGE CONTROL IN ALUMINUM PROCESSING.
Abstract: This paper develops a linear process model for automatic gage control for hot rolling of aluminum on a multistand continuous hot rolling mill. The controller is developed to meet specifications for real-time digital control through the use of z and w plane techniques. The digital controller is simulated to determine stability and suitability. The gage control system has been tested, with favorable results, on the fifth stand of a continuous hot rolling mill.
Name: ["Hyland Wayne W.", "Green Walter L."]

Title: RESTRICTED-GOAL SYNTAX-AIDED PATTERN-RECOGNITION EXPERIMENT.
Abstract: For recognizing two- and three dimensional patterns in industrial environment, a device using an industrial TV camera and a small computer has been constructed, which recognizes the shapes and salient edges of objects and describes their relations. The paper presents the equipment, the algorithms recognizing figure elements elaborated, and the organization of the system list.
Name: ["Vamos T.", "Vassy Z."]

Title: COMPUTER SIMULATION FOR TIME OPTIMAL OR ENERGY OPTIMAL ATTITUDE CONTROL OF SPIN-STABILIZED SPACECRAFT.
Abstract: An original technique for determining the optimal magnetic torque strategy for control of the attitude of spin stabilized spacecraft is presented. By employing Lagrange multipliers and the Calculus of Variations, optimal control equations are derived which define minimum time and minimum energy attitude maneuvers. Computer program algorithms to numerically solve these optimal control equations are also described. The performance of this technique is compared with a commonly employed planning method.
Name: ["Woolley Robert D.", "Werking Roger D."]

Title: LEARNING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Three papers and an extensive bibliography of learning control are presented. The topics discussed provide a state-of-the-art in learning systems with emphasis on their application to control problems. Individual papers are indexed separately.
Name: ["Symp"]

Title: ARTIFACTS IN RECONSTRUCTIONS MADE FROM A FEW PROJECTIONS.
Abstract: For the molecular biologist or radiologist, the question that arises is whether a given feature could be an artifact introduced by the reconstruction algorithm, or, stated differently, could a feature, which was part of the object, have been removed during reconstruction? An iterative algorithm, such as ART (Algebraic Reconstruction Technique), provides the possibility of answering these questions. First a reconstruction is made in the ordinary fashion. Then the iterative algorithm is restarted with the reconstruction modified to lack or contain the feature. One then sees whether or not the feature is restored in the new reconstruction. By testing different features the space of possible reconstructions is explored.
Name: ["Gordon Richard"]

Title: INDUSTRIAL ROBOTS - SECOND GENERATION.
Abstract: New robot designs will have up to six independently-controlled articulations, handle up to 300 pounds and memory options will range from 128 program steps to 1024 steps. They will also provide the inherent capability of accurate, continuous path traversing and of hand synchronization with a moving target. Programs are stored in digital form and may be accumulated in libraries of tape cassettes for easy retrieval. An inbuilt capability for interfacing with computer is available for applications where this memory expansion may be useful.
Name: ["Cakebread R.F."]

Title: TESTS FOR COMPLETE LOGIC CHECK OF COMBINATION AUTOMATA WITH INPUT-SIGNAL BRANCHING.
Abstract: A structurally based procedure is proposed for putting together the minimum sufficient sequence of check tests for a combination automaton with input-signal branching.
Name: ["Sklyarevich A.N."]

Title: VARIABLE-CYCLE LENGTH CLOCK WITH REALTIME LENGTH CONTROL.
Abstract: A data processing system is shown that has the ability to vary the processor cycle length not only by microcode, but also by realtime needs within the system. The variable-clocking scheme described has the ability to alter its cycle length at any time during the cycle. It accomplishes this end in two different ways to take care of problems that might occur, due to the fact that the cycle has been partially executed before the decision to extend can be made.
Name: ["Zurla F.A."]

Title: UNIFORM HASHING ALGORITHM.
Abstract: A hashing algorithm is described that achieves a uniform distribution of the virtual space onto the real space. If the functions defined in the algorithm have the further property of uniform random distribution, additional properties are satisfied.
Name: ["Arnold R.F.", "Bass W.E.", "Hartung M.H.", "Snow F.D.", "Stephens III R.D."]

Title: The automatic evaluation of magnetic tape recordings by OSCILLOSTORE | [AUTOMATISCHE AUSWERTUNG VON MAGNETBAND- AUFZEICHNUNGEN MIT DEM OSCILLOSTORE]
Abstract: A combined analog magnetic tape unit and modified OSCILLOSTORE fault recorder offers an optimum solution from the price and performance points of view for small and medium-sized installations. The unit permits the automatic evaluation of only those points on a magnetic tape which contain data deviating from a preprogrammed value. This means that the data actually included in the evaluating process are considerably reduced since often only a fraction of a percent of the data recorded in the course of a series of measurements actually contains important information. | A combined analogue magnetic tape unit and modified Oscillostore fault recorder offers an optimum solution from the price and performance points of view for small and medium sized installations. The unit permits the automatic evaluation of only those points on a magnetic tape which contain data deviating from a preprogrammed value. This means that the data actually included in the evaluating process are considerably reduced since often only a fraction of a percent of the data recorded in the course of a series of measurements actually contain important information. The author describes the combined unit and a number of possible applications.
Name: ["Sima H."]

Title: LINEAR SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION WITH PHYSICAL CONSTRAINTS.
Abstract: A model is presented that allows the user to identify the impulse response of a lumped parameters linear system, when an input function and an output function are given together with the maximum estimated memory of the system.
Name: ["Todini E."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION WITH PULSE TYPE INPUTS HAVING APPLICATION TO THE MINERAL PROCESSING INDUSTRY.
Abstract: New improved methods for the estimation of the impulse response from measured input and output signals are presented. These methods are especially suited for heavily damped systems and allow stable reliable solutions even when the measured signals contain large errors. No special form for the input signal is necessary, and no special hardware is required. Modeling errors are minimized by the use of spline functions and discrete models which are form free and allow good representation to any arbitrary curve. As these models are linear in their coefficients, rapid direct solutions are achieved. Applications of these methods in the field of flotation are outlined.
Name: ["Anderssen A.S.", "White E.T."]

Title: AUTOMATION SPEEDS SPECTRUM ANALYSIS.
Abstract: The automatic spectrum analyzer can increase the usefulness of a conventional spectrum analyzer by dictating its operation from a small digital controller (computer). Advantages include greater speed and accuracy which expand the measurement capability. The tedious details of instrument set up and data recording are handled automatically. If the automatic spectrum analyzer, the superheterodyne detector is digitally programmed to tune to a given frequency, set its if bandwidth, if gain, input attenuation, and post detection bandwidth. The tuned detector of an automatic spectrum analyzer can be thought of as a generalized power density meter. It can tune to an arbitrary set of frequencies and measure signal strength. It can do a frequency search, and if a signal is present, it will find it and determine its frequency and amplitude. The system can tune to the harmonic frequencies and measure distortion. It can set at one frequency and record changes in signal level with time. On modulated signals, the system can narrow its bandwidth to measure modulation parameters. The analyzer can also serve as the heart of a receiving system. The if preceding the normal envelope detector can be brought out such that the user can employ a special-purpose detector to recover the desired modulation. By adding a programmable signal source, the automatic spectrum analyzer becomes a flexible stimulus response test system.
Name: ["Cunningham Michael"]

Title: AUTOMATIC AIRCRAFT GUIDANCE LAW FOR MID-AIR COLLISION AVOIDANCE.
Abstract: This paper obtains the automatic optimal guidance law and the guided optimal trajectories for two aircraft to avoid mid-air collision in the terminal area. The paper consists of two parts. The first part is to formulate the two aircraft collision problem into the framework of control theory. In the second part, maximum principle is used to obtain a numerical procedure. Two cases of head-on collision are simulated by a computer APL Program.
Name: ["Huang Sheng-Chao", "Joshi A."]

Title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE APPROACH TO AUTOMATIC SPEECH RECOGNITION.
Abstract: This paper describes an automatic speech recognition machine which combines algorithms for acoustic signal processing, pattern recognition, syntactic and semantic analysis in an interactive hierarchy. The most important feature of this cooperative structure is that any level of processing may, at any time, invoke the aid of another level toward the ultimate goal of understanding what was said. The machine has been implemented in the form of a computer program for an IBM 360/50 and is currently being tested on a large data base.
Name: ["Levinson S.E."]

Title: HAWAII INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON SYSTEM SCIENCES, 6TH, PROCEEDINGS, 1973.
Abstract: Following is a continuation of the list of titles and authors: Multistage Learning Paradigm for Computer Recognition of Speech. By George M. White. Interactive Programming System with Speech Input. By Chacko C. Neroth and Herbert B. Baskin. Machine Recognition of Handprinted Characters. By D. L. Caskey and C. L. Coates Jr. Comparison of Different Filter Structures for Restoration of Images. By B. R. Hunt and H. C. Andrews. Note on the ErSignal of Block Quantizers. By M. Tasto and P. A. Wintz. Resolution Improvement of Remote Sensing Data. By A. Caprihan and W. W. Mendell.
Name: ["White George M.", "Neroth Chacko C.", "Baskin Herbert B.", "Caskey D.L.", "Coates Jr. C.L.", "Hunt B.R.", "Andrews H.C.", "Tasto M.", "Wintz P.A.", "Caprihan A.", "Mendell W.W."]

Title: COMPUTERIZED MULTIANGULAR TOMOGRAPHY.
Abstract: Radiographic diagnostic evaluation of numerous speciic pathogenic entities in medicine and dentistry can be significantly enhanced through the use of recently developed mathematical data processing techniques. A method is described to nondestructively section a human organ, at any desired angle of orientation, using computer processed data derived from a series of ordinary radiographs.
Name: ["Altschuler Bruce R.", "Perry R.Michael", "Altschuler Martin D."]

Title: PRIOR SOLUTIONS: EXTENSIONS OF CONVEX NUCLEUS SOLUTIONS TO CHANCE-CONSTRAINED GAMES.
Abstract: The theory of n-person cooperative games in characteristic function form is extended to games in which the values of the characteristic function for the various coalitions are random variables with known joint distribution functions. Based on the ideas of zero order decision rules and chance-constrained programming, classes of ‚Ä≥prior‚Ä≥ solutions are defined. As ‚Ä≥prior‚Ä≥ solutions, the classic notions are extended to these stochastic games of core, Shapley value and nucleolus by means of their convex nucleus extremal characterizations, and their properties are investigated.
Name: ["Charnes A.", "Granot Daniel"]

Title: NEAR-OPTIMAL STATE ESTIMATION FOR INTERCONNECTED SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A new algorithm is proposed for estimating the state of a nonlinear stochastic system when only noisy observations of the state are available. The state estimation problem is formulated as a modal-trajectory maximum-likelihood estimation problem. The resulting minimization problem is analogous to the nonlinear tracking problem in optimal control theory. By viewing the system as an interconnection of lower-dimensional susbystems and applying the so-called epsilon -coupling technique, which originated in the study of the sensitivity of control systems to parameter variations, a near-optimal state estimation algorithm is derived which has the properties that all computations can be performed in parallel at the subsystem level and only linear equations need be solved.
Name: ["Cline T."]

Title: INVESTIGATION OF SOME LOGICAL SOFTWARE FILTERS FOR SMOOTHING IMPULSE NOISE.
Abstract: Impulse noise which can be introduced from the process under control, for example by electric pick-up from switching circuitry or by faulty multiplexing is discussed. In each situation erroneous readings are obtained which appear as spikes on the measurement record. The paper describes an evaluation of the performance of some logical software filters designed to reduce the effects of this impulse noise in measurement and control loops.
Name: ["Roberts P.D."]

Title: INTERNATIONAL JOINT CONFERENCE ON PATTERN RECOGNITION, 1ST, PROCEEDINGS, 1973.
Abstract: This conference report contains 90 papers and summaries of papers, covering the following topics: mathematical methods, character recognition, biomedical applications, picture processing, speech recognition, syntactic methods, adaptive pattern recognition, scenes and structures, and remote sensing. Most of the papers have been indexed separately.
Name: ["Conf"]

Title: SELF-OPTIMIZATION OF TASK ALLOCATION IN SHARED MAN/COMPUTER CONTROL.
Abstract: A technique for autonomously allocating control between an ‚Ä≥intelligent‚Ä≥ aiding system and a human operator is presented. A criteria function based on operator utilities and task related performance measures is used to adaptively optimize the allocation under changing operational conditions. The technique incorporates the following functions: (1) Adaptively estimate operator utilities; (2) Search for, and obtain, an optimum control allocation policy; (3) Adapt criteria function parameters to time variations in operational conditions.
Name: ["Freedy A.", "Weisbrod R.", "Weltman G."]

Title: An algorithm for computer control of fast-stepping motors
Source: Journal of Physics E: Scientific Instruments
Abstract: Stepping motors under computer control are often required to go as fast as reliability permits, which generally entails acceleration to a high speed followed by deceleration to a destination. For reliable and efficient operation the acceleration must not exceed a given limit; however the motor must not waste time at very low speeds. Since a single computer instruction forms an appreciable part of the delay between pulses at high speed the algorithm which calculates this delay must be very concise. In addition, it must be virtually free of cumulative errors since the tolerance on the mean delay time can easily be less than 0.01% at high speed. Such an algorithm is given.
Name: ["Denne W.A.", "Fuller B."]

Title: Markov model of learning: Length of the first run of correct responses
Source: Acta Universitatis Palackianae Olomucensis Facultatis Medicae
Abstract: The properties of the characteristic of learning were studied, defined as the length of the first run of correct responses. Formulae for the probability distribution and the mean value of this characteristic were derived. Further, the formulae for the amount of information about the parameters of the model were derived, as contained in the sample space of the studied characteristic. This information was compared with the information about these parameters contained in the sample space of the original nonreduced record of learning. In this way, the possible loss or gain of information resulting from the introduction of the studied characteristic of learning could be evaluated.
Name: ["Komenda S."]

Title: Markov model of learning: Length of the first run of correct responses, when only n trials of the process are known
Source: Acta Universitatis Palackianae Olomucensis Facultatis Medicae
Abstract: The properties of the characteristic of learning were studied, defined as the length of the first run of correct responses provided that the process was recorded only in its first n trials. The formulae for the probability distributions and expectations were derived, as also formulae for the amount of information about the parameters of the model contained in the sample space of the studied characteristic. The corresponding numerical results made it possible to evaluate the dependence of these quantities on the size of reduction of the empirical records.
Name: ["Komenda S.", "Tesarikova E."]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR FINDING THE MINIMAL LENGTH HAMILTONIAN PATH IN A GRAPH.
Source: Econ Comput Econ Cybern Stud Res
Abstract: In order to solve certain problems in economy by means of up-to-date computation techniques, use has to be mode of some algorithms conductive to a convenient solution. The algorithm described is meant to find the minimal length Hamiltonian path in a graph. The problem has been considered widely in the specialty literature because it frequently arises in some complex problems such as production effectual programming and particularly combination problems.
Name: ["Mierlea V."]

Title: ROBOT SUPPLYING GRAPHITE ELECTRODE TO AN ELECTRIC-ARC FURNACE.
Abstract: Replacement of used, graphite electrodes in an electric arc furnace is a difficult and time-consuming operation. A robot was designed for the purpose of accomplishing this work by remote control and an experimental model has been built. This electrode-supplying robot has no protruding arms outside its body, thus differing from ordinary industrial robots. An electrode will be loaded into the body of the robot, and chucked by the three rubber-tired wheels which may be regarded as the three manipulators of the robot. The chucking force of the rubber-tired wheels is automatically controlled to the proper level, and the elasticity of the rubber tires will prevent excessive pressure on the brittle electrodes. Such pressure often arises when screwing a new electrode tightly into the old one. The robot has absorbed a dangerous job under conditions of extreme heat and height, and has brought about a reduction in the number of operators from three to one.
Name: ["Mori M.", "Noda A.", "Ito K.", "Tsuboi K.", "Shimogo J.", "Kozuka G."]

Title: BEHAVIOR OF THE HUMAN OPERATOR IN A PROCESS CONTROL TASK.
Abstract: A study of the decision-making process of the human operator engaged in a control task is described. The analysis is based on the examination of verbal protocols and on the observation of subjects engaged in the control of a physical system with which they are familiar, simulated on a computer system. A preliminary study resulted in a model representing the main characteristics of the decision-making process.
Name: ["Doutriaux Jerome"]

Title: ON-LINE TWO-LEVEL COMPUTER CONTROL OF LARGELY UNCERTAIN PLANTS.
Abstract: A computer control technique for controlling a class of largely uncertain multivariable plants using model tracking method is presented. The approach uses a ‚Ä≥two-level‚Ä≥ controller, with a feedforward controller on its first-level, and a conditional feedback controller on its second-level. The design procedure employs the deterministic type Lyapunov signal synthesis procedure which can be implemented on a suitable digital computer, and does not need an explicit knowledge of the plant.
Name: ["Nikiforuk P.N.", "Gupta M.M.", "Kanai K.", "Wagner L."]

Title: PIECEWISE APPROXIMATION OF PLANE CURVES.
Abstract: Piecewise approximation is described as a way of feature extraction, data compaction and noise filtering of boundaries of regions of a picture and of waveforms. Algorithms which minimize the error of approximation for a fixed number of segments are reviewed. A new fast algorithm is proposed which allows for variable number of segments. After an arbitrary initial choise segments are split or merged in order to drive the error norm under a prespecified bound. Results of computer experiments with cell outlines and electrocardiograms are reported.
Name: ["Pavlidis Theodosios", "Horowitz Steven L."]

Title: Developing monitoring techniques for an on-line information retrieval system
Abstract: One of the least understood and most ignored aspects of implementing on-line software is the problem of effective monitoring. This problem takes on many facets: gathering data on user interactions and errors, storing and processing these data, and generating summary reports which can be used to pinpoint deficiencies and to suggest modifications and improvements. Northwestern University has developed techniques to monitor an on-line information retrieval system, by using that system both to monitor itself and to process the data collected. RIQS (Remote Information Query System) is both a batch and on-line generalized, information retrieval system which operates on the CDC 6400. It is used by faculty and students for developing and searching data bases in medicine, political science, computer science, anthropology, astronomy, university administration and planning, etc. An on-line monitor program was developed to produce a RIQS-compatible data base of user interactions with RIQS-ONLINE. Using RIQS, this data base can then be interrogated and searched to generate reports, to create plots, or to produce input for a statistical package.
