Typical parameters which are studied include total real-time per user access to RIQS, real time and central processor time per query, number of records searched, number of records retrieved, number of search terms used, type and size of reports generated, number and type of language or syntax errors made by user, etc. This paper illustrates the use of these techniques by providing summary reports and plots from use of RIQS-ONLINE during the current academic year. System improvements are suggested from analysis of these reports. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Mittman B.", "Dominick W.D."]
Keywords: ["70", "information retrieval", "on-line monitoring", "remote information query system", "software monitoring"]

Title: Optimal control of stationary Markov processes
Abstract: Sufficient conditions are given for the optimal control of Markov processes when the control policy is stationary and the process possesses a stationary distribution. The costs are unbounded and additive, and may or may not be discounted. Applications to Semi-Markov processes are included, and the results for random walks are related to the author's previous papers on diffusion processes. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Morton R."]

Title: STABILITY AND CONTROL ASPECTS OF A PERFORMANCE ADAPTIVE SELF-ORGANIZING CONTROL ALGORITHM.
Abstract: Sufficient conditions for the stability of self-organizing control algorithms based on a subgoal approach are given. A method is presented which aids in the a-priori choise of the structure of the feedback control law under the assumption that on-line or off-line identification of the structure of the plant has been accomplished. Subsequent to closing the loop, bounds, which depend on the control law chosen, on the performance index may be estimated. Illustrative examples are presented.
Name: ["Saridis G.N.", "Fensel P.A."]

Title: CLOUD TYPE PATTERN RECOGNITION USING ENVIRONMENTAL SATELLITE DATA.
Abstract: Cloud type pattern recognition is performed on high-resolution scanning radiometer data from the polar orbiting NOAA-1 (National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration)environmental satellite. Data from the visual and infrared portions of the electromagnetic spectrum are used in a supervised classification analysis of 2100 cloud observations over the tropical eastern Pacific Ocean. Linear discriminant functions, derived from the multivariate normal density function, provide the basis for a Bayesian conditional-probability classifier. The results of dependent and independent Bayesian classification indicate greater overall accuracy is achieved when the combined visible and infrared predictors are used in the analysis.
Name: ["Booth A.L."]

Title: DEVELOPMENT OF AUTOMATIC GROUP SUPERVISORY ELEVATOR CONTROL AND ITS FUTURE.
Abstract: A newly developed automatic group supervisory elevator control system which constantly processes data on passengers and traffic demand in real time, enables elevators to quickly respond to calls by comprehensive decisions and commands (i. e. forecasting control), predetermines the elevator to respond to a call and issues a forecasting signal by means of a hall light which produces a good psychological effect upon waiting passengers.
Name: ["Inuzuka Isao", "Yuminaka Takeo", "Ikeda Eiji"]

Title: USE OF SIMULATION TO TEST THE VALIDITY AND SENSITIVITY OF AN ANALYTICAL MODEL.
Abstract: Simulation is used to test formally the validity of some assumptions made in solving models by analytical techniques and to test the sensitivity of the system to the arrival distribution. The ppresentation refers to a simplified real-time model in which there are a finite number of customers linked to a central processor via common carrier lines and a terminal. The analytical solution in the literature is to derive shown results for each stage of the system and add them up to obtain the behavior of the system. Assumptions must then be made at each stage. Simulation has been used to solve the same system in terms of the same measure of efficiency, i. e. the response time. However, the system is solved as a whole, the output from one stage becoming the input to the second stage. Confidence limits have been obtained for the response time in order to test the results obtained from analytical techniques. Simulation has also been used to test the sensitivity of the system to a change in the arrival distribution. Using analysis of variance, the effect of the arrival pattern and of the interaction is determined.
Name: ["Bernard Prosper M."]

Title: GENERALIZATION ON PATTERNS USING KOLMOGOROV COMPLEXITY.
Abstract: Given a domain D of patterns, and an unknown classifying function f, what is sought is an intelligent way to learn f as the correctly classified elements in D are presented one by one. This question is asked in a gambling context in which a gambler, starting with one unit, sequentially bets a portion of his current capital on the classification of the new pattern. The optimal gambling system is found when f is known a priori to belong to some family F. A universal optimal learning scheme is also exhibited.
Name: ["Cover Thomas M."]

Title: ART: Mathematics and applications. A report on the mathematical foundations and on the applicability to real data of the algebraic reconstruction techniques
Abstract: Some properties of the algebraic reconstruction techniques (ART) for reconstructing objects from their projections (e.g. electron micrographs) are discussed. Some generalizations of previously published ART algorithms are given. In particular, ART is extended to handle weighted projection data. An early conjecture about ART is proved for one of the algorithms: it converges to the most uniform solution of the constraint equations provided by the projection data. Other convergence properties of the ART algorithms are discussed and proved. Some new ART algorithms are described. These are believed to converge to optimal reconstructions consistent with the projection data. The importance of choosing the correct ray widths in case of real projection data is demonstrated, and a method for calculating correct ray widths is given. A method is proposed for estimating the optimal number of iterations in a reconstruction. The performance of ART on real data is demonstrated both in the absence of and in the presence of noise. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Herman G.T.", "Lent A.", "Rowland S.W."]
Affiliations: [' State University of New York at Buffalo', 'Bell Aerospace Division of Textron', ' State University of New York at Buffalo']

Title: METHODS OF EDGE DETECTION IN VISUAL SCENES.
Abstract: Several methods of detecting edges in visual scenes by a digital computer are presented. There are two broad procedures of edge detection, called one- and two-pass methods. Examples illustrating some of the methods in each category are given. Visual pattern recognition is a process whereby a digital computer uses a visual scene as an input and deduces certain properties about the content of the input data. The usefulness of visual pattern recognition is obvious when one considers how much the human decision process is dependent on vision as the major input medium. Several applications of visual pattern recognition are briefly reviewed. One area of considerable current interest is the automatic extraction of information from biomedical images. Another major research area of interest is the automatic analysis of multi-channel spectral data from airborne scanners. From the digitized data, the types and conditions of agriculture are automatically determined by using pattern recognition techniques. Other applications of this research effort include the discovery of minerals.
Name: ["Underwood Stephen A.", "Aggarwal J.K."]

Title: ALGORITHMS FOR STATE ESTIMATION IN LARGE INTERCONNECTED POWER SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Several algorithms for computing the weighted least square state estimate for large interconnected power systems are considered. A power-system state estimator is an on-line program that is capable of processing raw telemetered data in real time and producing the statistically best estimates for the present values of all system variables of interest (some of which cannot be measured). The main objective of on-line state estimation is to provide a reliable real-time data base for all on-line application programs related to security and economic objectives. In addition, an important off-line application of state-estimator program is the simulation of various data-acquisition system alternatives to evaluate the cost versus performance of the data base corresponding to each alternative. Some theoretical and practical advantages and disadvantages of the algorithms are briefly described.
Name: ["Tse E.", "Larson R.E.", "Peterson N.M."]

Title: Glossary and index to remotely sensed image pattern recognition concepts
Abstract: The purpose of the glossary is to state in the simplest possible way the general meaning or word usage for many of the terms in image pattern recognition. There is no intent to provide definitive statements for terms such as "resolution" but rather only statements about the general nature of what resolution is. There is no intent to provide mathematical formulas involving integrals or derivatives in any of the statements. Those who need the mathematics can get it from technical papers or texts. The glossary is designed to be read by those generally unfamiliar with the area and provide for them an overall perspective. The organization approaches that of programmed learning material and can be smoothly (I hope) read from beginning to end. Those needing to look up a specific term can do so via the index. There is some overlap of terms in this glossary with those glossaries or definitions in radiometry and aerial photography. There is no intent that the way the terms are described here replace the way they are described in those glossaries and definitions. The overlap is provided here so that the reader can get a perspective of a cluster of terms frequently used in our field. The perspective is intended to start from what the image concept is through the recording of an image by some sensor, the possible conversion of image format and the simple analog or more complex digital processing which must be done on the imagery. In short, the perspective is one of image pattern recognition. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Haralick R.M."]

Title: CONVERGENCE THEORY FOR OPTIMIZATION ALGORITHMS USING APPROXIMATIONS.
Abstract: A general theory of convergence for optimization algorithms in which approximations are used, is presented. The theory indicates how the accuracy of the approximations can be controlled adaptively in order to insure convergence. The application of the theory to a parameter optimization problem for a nonlinear dynamical system is briefly discussed.
Name: ["Klessig R."]

Title: An Improved Algorithm for the Generation of Nonparametric Curves
Abstract: Generation of curves using incremental steps along fixed coordinate axes is important in such diverse areas as computer displays, digital plotters, and numerical control. Direct implementation of a nonparametric representation of a curve, f(x, y) = 0, has been shown to be attractive for digital generation. The algorithm in this paper is developed directly from the nonparametric representation of the curve, allows steps to be taken to any point adjacent to the current one, and uses decision variables closely related to an error criterion. Consequently, the algorithm is more general and produces curves closer to the actual curve than do previously reported algorithms. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Jordan B.W., Jr.", "Lennon W.J.", "Holm B.D."]

Title: Automatic Parametric Optimization by Means of a Mixed Algorithm, as Demonstrated by the Example of the Radial Slider-Crank Mechanism. | [AUTOMATISCHE PARAMENTEROPTIMIERUNG MIT HILFE EINES GEMISCHTEN ALGORITHMUS AM BEISPIEL DER ZENTRISCHEN KURBELSCHLEIFE.]
Source: Wissenschaftliche Zeitschrift der Technischen Unversitat Dresden
Abstract: If the initial approximations which can lead to solutions are unknown in an optimization problem, the method of a mixed algorithm, that unites the advantages of the stochastic and systematic procedure, is suitable. Within a linked space for optimization variables, a random initial approximation is obtained, from which a determined procedure of search for a local minimum is derived. The Fletcher and Powell method is used successfully in this search. After explaining the formulation of the problem and of the optimization task, a one-dimensional search is undertaken and optimization examples are presented which are tested on a DDP 516 computer.
Name: ["Wachler Klaus"]

Title: NEW APPROACH TO SIMULATING STABLE STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A technique is introduced for analyzing simulations of stochastic systems in steady-state. Confidence intervals are obtained for a general function of the steady-state distribution.
Name: ["Crane Michael A.", "Iglehart Donald L."]

Title: TWO NEW ADAPTIVE EQUALIZER STRUCTURES.
Abstract: A mean square gradient search algorithm is introduced for the adaptive control of a ‚Ä≥Canonic Form‚Ä≥ equalizer. It was previously thought that such an algorithm was not possible due to the fact that there are twice as many variable parameters to adjust than there are correlation measurements to control them. This problem is overcome by the new algorithm. In addition, another new equalizer termed the ‚Ä≥Decision Feedforward‚Ä≥ equalizer is proposed. This new equalizer allows the data decisions to be used for correcting both the ‚Ä≥precursors‚Ä≥ and the ‚Ä≥tails‚Ä≥ of a distorted pulse signal in contrast to the ‚Ä≥Decision Feedback‚Ä≥ equalizer which corrects only the ‚Ä≥tails‚Ä≥ of the received pulses.
Name: ["Brackett P.O."]

Title: APPLICATION OF UNITARY TRANSFORMS TO VISUAL PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: The main problem in classifying visual patterns is to extract useful features from the vast amount of information contained in even a simple scene. Several workers have proposed a feature extraction method which involves linear transformation of the pattern data. The question studied here concerns the number of terms of the transformation that are necessary to achieve a good representation of the picture information. Ideal forms for picture statistics are developed for the Haramard and Fourier transformations along with the corresponding compression characteristics. Also, some experimental results from 1024-element binary valued patterns are given and discussed in terms of the theory.
Name: ["Mundy J.L.", "Joynson R.E."]

Title: AUTOMATED THEMATIC MAPPING AND CHANGE DETECTION OF ERTS-1 IMAGES.
Abstract: This paper describes a system that combines multispectral and spatial pattern recognition techniques to produce thematic maps. This system has been applied to ERTS-1 MSS images, and the results obtained are discussed.
Name: ["Gramenopoulos Nicholas"]

Title: Bayesian acceptance-sampling schemes for two-sided tests of the mean of a normal distribution of known variance
Source: Journal of the American Statistical Association
Abstract: This article is concerned with the problem of deciding whether the mean Œ∏ of a normal distribution of known variance lies in a specified finite interval Œ∏<sup>-</sup> Œ∏<sup>+</sup>). Consideration is given to prior information on Œ∏ and to quadratic and piecewise linear utility structures. Computer-aided methods are described for obtaining the optimal decision rule given a sample of observations and for obtaining the optimal sample size when the sampling cost is a linear function of the sample size. Some simpler approximate methods are also described. ¬© Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Dayananda R.A.", "Evans I.G."]
Affiliations: [' Vidyodaya University of Ceylon', ' University College of Wales']

Title: QUASI-GRADIENT SEARCH METHODS IN A SET OF SPECIFIED DIRECTIONS.
Abstract: Search methods are proposed in which at each step the direction of trial motion is chosen at random from some finite set of specified directions using the realization of only one random number. This set is chosen in such a way that information on unsuccessful trial search steps is used to compute estimates for the gradient of the function to be minimized. Detailed computational schemes are presented, along with results of computational experiments which confirm that the accuracy in determining gradient estimates and the effectiveness of the proposed methods are high.
Name: ["Zak Yu.A.", "Kondrashin G.P."]

Title: Computer Recognition of the Continuant Phonemes in Connected English Speech
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: A method of phoneme recognition of connected speech is described. Input to the system is assumed to consist of the 24 continuant phonemes in connected English speech. The system first categorizes each successive 20-ms segment of the input speech utterance as either voiced fricative, voiced nonfricative, unvoiced fricative or no-speech, utilizing a measure of the relative energy balance between low and high frequencies. Next, the recognition of each 20-ms segment is performed from a distribution of axis-crossing intervals of speech prefiltered to emphasize each formant frequency range. Segmentation is performed from the results of the recognition of each 20-ms segment and from changes in categorization. Finally, the results of the recognition of each 20-ms segment between each pair of segmentation boundaries are combined and the phonemic sound occurring most frequently is printed out. The system has been trained for a single male speaker. Preliminary results for this speaker and for four 3-4-s sentences indicate: a correct categorization decision for about 97 percent of the input 20-ms segments, a correct recognition for about 78 percent of the input 20-ms segments, and an overall correct phoneme recognition for about 87 percent of the input phonemes. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Niederjohn R.J.", "Thomas I.B."]

Title: RELIABILITY MODEL USING MARKOV CHAINS FOR UTILITY EVALUATION OF COMPUTER SYSTEMS ABOARD SHIP.
Abstract: The introduction of computers aboard ships to provide a high degree of automation necessitates calculation of computer system reliability to evaluate the utility of the system. The reliability aspect of the system is simulated by a model using Markov chains. Having defined the system state space and the transition rates, the model provides evaluation of the state probabilities. Evaluation of system utility is based on computer task values and the failure probabilities. Application of the analysis model to an existing system reveals information useful in assigning redundancy, eliminating bottlenecks and allocating spare parts.
Name: ["Boe Carsten", "Heimly Tor", "Mathiesen Tor-Christian"]

Title: AIRCRAFT CONFLICT DETECTION IN AN ASSOCIATIVE PROCESSOR.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: A major problem in Air Traffic Control is detecting when two aircraft are on a potential collision course soon enough to take some corrective action. Many algorithms are being developed which may lead to automating the process of conflict detection. However, these algorithms typically require large amounts of computing resource if they are to be performed in real-time. This paper describes some techniques which may be used by an associative processor to perform the conflict detection operation.
Name: ["Downs H.R."]

Title: BIAS AND COVARIANCE FORMULAE FOR FILTER ERROR ANALYSIS AND MODEL SENSITIVITY.
Abstract: In conjunction with the fact that neglected plant states, system nonlinearities, and uncertain plant parameters may cause significant biasing in data filter state estimation. Bias formulas are derived for simulating this effect of these error sources on the state estimates. It iis shown that fairly general filter error sensitivity is obtained using a bias and covariance error analysis rather than the standard covariance error analysis. This technique reduces the effective error model dimensionality for suboptimal filter performance analysis. In addition, the bias formulas can be used in parallel with standard Kalman covariance formulas to provide an efficient technique for evaluating measurement system performance and model sensitivity trades.
Name: ["Warren Anthony W."]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR DETERMINING OPTIMUM FUEL MANAGEMENT DECISIONS WITH GENERALIZED CYCLE REQUIREMENTS.
Abstract: A method of simulating optimal fuel management decisions for cycles of varying length and energy output is described. It is developed for the purpose of providing the power system planner with the minimum fuel cycle cost achievable when operating a nuclear unit in accordance with a particular refueling outage and energy production schedule. A pattern search method is used to generate a sequence of decision alternatives leading to the optimal alternative. Optimal incore fuel placement is simulated in one dimension by formulating the internal fuel management problem as the assignment problem of linear programming. Core neutronics is treated in one dimension. Several applications are presented.
Name: ["Forkner S.L.", "Specker S.R."]

Title: PROPOSED METHOD FOR THE ANALYSIS OF DERMATOGLYPHIC PATTERNS.
Abstract: Dermatoglyphic patterns refer to the configurations formed by dermal ridges on the fingers, palms, toes, and soles. There is a recognized relationship between the dermatoglyphic patterns and certain developmental defects in individuals. Previous methods of dermal pattern analysis are rather subjective and tedious to perform. this paper proposed a hybrid optical-digital system for the quantitative analysis of the dermal patterns. The proposed system extracts dermatoglyphic features through the medium of an optical Fourier transform and a solid-state photodiode array. Preliminary classification results for a grup of 11 individuals Trisomy-21 (Down's Syndrome) and 10 individuals selected from a normal control group are given.
Name: ["Ausherman Dale A.", "Hall William D.", "Moyers Robert E.", "Fairchild Ronald C.", "Mitchel Ralph H."]

Title: TACTILE PERCEPTION FOR ROBOT DEVICES.
Abstract: The current breeds of production robot are limited in their applications largely by the fact that very few as yet have any feedback from the workpiece. As the price of mini-computers with adequate hardware facilities for real time control is now reaching a level compatible with the fixed program controller, it is feasible to consider more general control of existing hardware. A standard production robot equipped with tactile sensors both on its manipulators and elsewhere combined with a computer control would allow the construction of programs which adapt the control to suit the workpiece encountered. Such a machine would be capable of working with a mix of workpieces in random orientations.
Name: ["Larcombe M.H.E."]

Title: ANALOG SIMULATION FOR SPATIO-TEMPORAL CHARACTERISTICS OF VISUAL SYSTEM.
Abstract: Functioning of the visual system was analysed by spatio-temporal characteristics based upon Enroth's model, Broca-Sulzer phenomenon and Mach effect. In order to get the excitatory and inhibitory potential of the intermediate cell layer in the retina, the exponential value in the model equation was calculated based on physiological theory neuro-phenomena. To show the visual characteristics by analog simulation for generating stimulus waveforms and analysis, visual adaptation was recorded as an electrical stimulation in the form of step functions. There is shown to be a satisfactory agreement within experimental errors between those data obtained and the theoretical values, which are psyco-physiological.
Name: ["Park S.H.", "Kim K.S."]

Title: BAYESIAN NONLINEAR FILTERING ALGORITHM FOR LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH UNKNOWN TIME-VARYING NOISE STATISTICS.
Abstract: The problem of estimating the state of a linear dynamic system driven by additive gaussian noise with unknown time varying statistics is considered. Estimates of the state of the system are obtained which are based on all past observations of the system. These observations are linear functions of the state contaminated by additive white gaussian noise with unknown time varying statistics. The case of scalar measurements is given first and the more general solution for vector measurements stated. A previously developed algorithm designed for use in the case of an unknown Kalman gain and thus the system state in the presence of unknown time varying noise statistics. Numerical examples for both the scalar and vector measurement cases are given.
Name: ["Alspach D.L."]

Title: STABILITY OF SYSTEMS WITH NONLINEAR FEEDBACK THROUGH RANDOMLY TIME-VARYING DELAYS.
Abstract: It is shown that the existence of a certain type of stochastic Lyapunov Functional with non-positive average right-derivative along the solution process is a sufficient condition for the almost-sure sample stability of a class of nonlinear stochastic delay-differential equations with delay and coefficient matrices generated by suitably well-behaved strong Markov processes. The results are applicable to an important class of modern control systems: multi-variable digital control systems which are built around a central real-time data-processing computer which integrates the overall system operation, but ‚Ä≥services‚Ä≥ the system on a time-shared basis.
Name: ["Bell Isle A.P."]

Title: DUAL CONTROL FOR LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH CONTROL DEPENDENT PLANT AND MEASUREMENT NOISE.
Abstract: A control algorithm giving a linear feedback control law has been developed for stochastic systems with control dependent measurement and system noise. This control policy reduces to two known optimal control policies in the cases where the solution is known. The first of these is when the control dependent noise goes to zero giving the well known separation principle. The second case is when no measurement noise occurs. This control policy should be useful in numerous practical cases, in particular in man in the loop studies where the previous control policies must assume no measurement noise. The assumptions of small control effort can represent the case of a manually tuned system where the human only tunes an automatically set control law. For this type of system, the system measurement noise will increase as the man stops observing and performs his control functions and a human input to the control system will always increase the apparent driving noise.
Name: ["Alspach D.L."]

Title: NONSUPERVISED LEARNING CLASSIFIERS WITH OPTIMAL PERFORMANCE.
Abstract: Two types of nonsupervised learning algorithms which lead to optimal classification are presented. The approach adopted in the first type is based on a clustering technique, and a separating hyper-plane is constructed using the first principal component under the assumption that input patterns are clustered with a Gaussian distribution. In the second type, the classification algorithm is obtained by consistent estimators of a mixture distribution of patterns. An analysis is made about the learning process and it is shown that the machines converge to the Bayes' minimum error classifier. Also, some results of a computer simulation are presented in order to show that these machines have a reasonable performance in the classification of unlabelled patterns.
Name: ["Shimura M.", "Imai T.", "Mizoguchi R."]

Title: STRUCTURAL DESCRIPTIONS, TRANSFORMATIONAL RULES, AND PATTERN ANALYSIS.
Abstract: Two equivalent notations are defined for describing the structure assigned to graph-like patterns by web grammar derivations. The notion of a transformational rule for webs is defined and the use of transformational rules for describing structural relations among webs that cannot be indicated by context-free web grammars is illustrated.
Name: ["Underwood William E.", "Kanal Laveen N."]

Title: CLASS OF DISCRETE ORTHOGONAL TRANSFORMS.
Abstract: For a given N-periodic sequence, a class of of log//2N discrete orthogonal transforms ranging from Walsh-Hadamard transform to discrete Fourier transform are defined. The power spectra invariant to sequential shift of the sampled data for these transforms are developed. Generalized expressions for factoring these transform matrices are provided. Based on these matrix factors, efficient algorithms for fast computation of the transform coefficients are developed. By introducing a number of zeros as the elements in the transform matrices, a modified version of the transforms is developed. Some of these transforms have been used in image processing speech analysis ans synthesis, and in spectral analysis of digital systems. In particular, the power spectra of the generlized discrete transforms have been used as features of a EKG pattern classifier offering various degrees of resolution.
Name: ["Rao K.R.", "Ahmed N.", "Schultz R.B."]

Title: Optimum Quantization of Memoryless Gaussian Sources. | OPTIMALE QUANTISIERUNG GEDAECHTNISFREIER GAUSSQUELLEN.
Abstract: Since amplitude quantization of analog sources yields a distortion that depends on the level distribution of the quantizer, several criteria of quantizer fidelity are examined. It is shown that well-known optimum quantizers, e. g. the quantizer for minimum mean-squared error (Max-quantizer) and the quantizer for maximum output entropy, can be derived from a general concept of optimum quantizing. The performance of nonuniform quantizers is discussed, along with the problem of entropy coding of the quantizer output. The investigations are based on analytic solutions and iterative computing procedures. The results are compared with those that can be obtained by using uniform quantizing characteristics and with those given by the rate distortion function of memoryless gaussian sources.
Name: ["Zelinski Rainer", "Noll Peter"]

Title: APPLYING MULTIPLE-VALUED ALGEBRA CONCEPTS TO NEURAL MODELING.
Abstract: The intent of this paper is to present a new approach to neural modeling which overcomes some of the problems inherent in the binary model (or threshold gate model). A review of neurophysiology is presented, the deficiencies of the threshold gate model are explained, and a new model is introduced.
Name: ["Mattrey Robert F.", "Givone Donald D.", "Allen Charles M."]

Title: ONLINE SYSTEM PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENTS WITH SOFTWARE AND HYBRID MONITORS.
Abstract: System performance monitors are the only tools that can measure the computer system behavior in the system's real environment. Monitors collect data that can serve as a basis for computer tuning, computer system model design, workload analysis, model validation, or just finding out more about how the system really works. A software monitor that requires less than 700 bytes of main memory collects statistics about utilization of special online system resources and about the scheduler mechanism, detects system deadlocks, and measures online executive overhead. Since a software monitor would cause an intolerable system degradation and hardware monitoring is not directly applicable for such measurements, a hardware/software monitor interface was implemented which enables recording of software events by a hardware monitor. The monitoring artifact is thus kept close to zero. This technique was applied to measure time a task spends in various states and it has many other uses.
Name: ["Svobodova Liba"]

Title: MODELING THE HUMAN IN A TIME-VARYING ANTI-AIRCRAFT TRACKING LOOP.
Abstract: Optimal control and human response theory are combined to develop a computerized, predictive model of the input-output tracking response of the human gunner in an anti-aircraft artillery (AAA) loop. The model includes representations for the various human limitations (e. g. , time-delay, randomness) that act to degrade system performance. The model extends earlier work in manual control by considering rapidly varying system dynamics, arbitrary non-stochastic inputs, and dynamic attentional allocation between two tracking axes. Model predictions of tracking error covariance are compared with data obtained from trained gunners in independent experiments that simulated the Vulcan Air Defense System (VADS). The agreements are claimed to be excellent for both elevation and azimuth axis tracking, over a range of target passes from easy to difficult. The predictions are obtained using a single set of man-model input parameters that are typical of human response limitations. It is concluded that the modeling approach can be used with confidence in a systems analysis study of weapons effectiveness.
Name: ["Kleinman David L.", "Perkins Tony"]

Title: ESTIMATION OF DATA COMPRESSION WHEN A FIXED-APERTURE PREDICTOR IS USED.
Abstract: Estimates are obtained for the average number of digital readings to be transmitted when a fixed-aperture predictor is used, for both discrete and continuous readout of the signal at the input.
Name: ["Efimov V.M.", "Livshits Z.A."]

Title: SOME RESULTS OF NON-PARAMETERIC CLUSTERING ON LARGE DATA PROBLEMS.
Abstract: Some results of non-parameteric clustering of large data problems are discussed. The algorithm calculates all required thresholds from the actual data, thus eliminating a priori estimates.
Name: ["Northouse Richard A.", "Fromm Frederick R."]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR DETERMINING RELIABILITY ESTIMATES FOR DISCRETE CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Systems whose structures can be described by monotonic functions are considered. An algorithm is presented for determining reliability estimates for such systems. A theorem is proved that makes it possible to employ a recursion procedure to determine the set of minimal paths between two nodes of a nonoriented graph.
Name: ["Apraksin Yu.K.", "Kiryukhin V.V."]

Title: CHRONOLOGICAL PROCESSING OF LOGICALLY DISTINCT EVENTS.
Abstract: A method is presented by which a variable number of events may be processed in their order of occurrence, providing functional and performance enhancements over existing event processing facilities. Increased function is provided by the chronological presentation of completed events to the application. Performance gains are realized by independent handling of each event throughout processing. This is accomplished by utilization of a 'pop-up' stack of completed events.
Name: ["Davidson G.A."]

Title: SYSTEM-INDEPENDENT TRACING FOR PREDICTION OF SYSTEM PERFORMANCE.
Abstract: The technique of obtaining traces characterizing application programs (jobs) is defined, independently of the system on which the tracing was performed. The job profiles so obtained can then be used to drive the simulation model of a computer system, in which the software (operating system) and the hardware used are modeled.
Name: ["Beretvas T.", "Miles E.L.", "Rasch G.B.", "Wicks R.J."]

Title: ASYMPTOTIC PROPERTIES OF MARKOV CHAIN PARAMETER ESTIMATES.
Abstract: Asymptotic normality and asymptotic effectiveness of Bayes and generalized Bayes estimates of an unknown Markov chain parameter are established for a certain smoothness of the transition density and a sufficiently quick intermixing. The results obtained might be useful in the development of optimal reception techniques for communication channels with dependent noise.
Name: ["Apokorin D.S."]

Title: ON COMPRESSING MULTIVARIATE DATA.
Abstract: This paper develops a method of linearly compressing N uncorrelated p multiplied by 1 data vectors, each with equal mean, to M(M less than N) p multiplied by 1 uncorrelated vectors. The mean of the original data vectors is preserved and the covariance matrices of the compressed vectors are equal and minimal in a specified sense.
Name: ["Pore M.D.", "Lewis T.O.", "Odell P.L."]

Title: MODEL REFERENCE ADAPTIVE CONTROL FOR CERTAIN CLASSES OF DISTRIBUTED PARAMETER SYSTEMS.
Abstract: This paper presents the design of model-reference adaptive control for two classes of distributed parameter systems using the Lyapunov stability approach. Class I is represented by the general parabolic systems of partial differential equations in state variable form, whereas class II is restricted to hyperbolic systems in phase variable form.
Name: ["Shahein H.I.H.", "Shen D.W.C."]

Title: SINGULAR PERTURBATION ANALYSIS OF FREE-TIME OPTIMAL CONTROL PROBLEMS.
Abstract: A singular perturbation theory for free-time optimal control problems is developed, introducing a scaling parameter as an additional parameter. This makes possible the extension of existing theory to include control-inequality constraints. An application to the problem of the optimum temperature policy for a stirred-tank reactor with rapidly-decaying catalyst is mentioned.
Name: ["Kao Y.K.", "Bankoff S.G."]

Title: TWO-DIMENSIONAL RECURSIVE FILTERS FOR DIGITAL PROCESSING.
Abstract: It is shown how two-dimensional recursive digital filters can be used to process two-dimensional sampled data. Filtering algorithms can be implemented using either the direct form of the two-dimensional z-transform or a state variable description. Two-dimensional band-pass type filters can be designed by mapping one-dimensional filters into the two-dimensional frequency plane. There are many problems that call for digital filtering of sampled two-dimensional data. For example, the geophysical industry uses two-dimensional filtering for processing seismic records and gravity and magnetic data. Two-dimensional filtering can also be used for the enhancement of photographic data such as weather photos, air photos, and medical X-rays.
Name: ["Shanks John L.", "Read Randol R."]

Title: System for Computerized Processing of Electrocardiograms. | ELEKTROKARDIOGRAMOK SZAMITOGEPES FELDOLGOZASANAK EGY RENDSZERE.
Abstract: Systems engineering problems of an EKG diagnostic bank based on a small computer are discussed, describing the hardware and software system of a realized pilot bank. The system is linked to telephone lines for signal transmission, ensuring two-way communication between the physician and data bank and input and processing of transmitted signals in real-time. The EKG signals are transmitted in three channels in the telephone line, and, after demodulation and analog-to-digital conversion, they are fed into the computer. The processing consists of the automatic selection of the essential, and of a decision-making process which realizes isolation according to certain shape-classes. Decision-making capability of the system is achieved either by given criteria or by learning via adaptive means, which is realized in off-line systems by learning algorithms. This latter procedure is facilitated by the periodic processing of stored data.
Name: ["Bak Miklosne", "Balogh Barnabas", "Nagy Andras B.", "Csanki Ferenc", "Devai Ferenc", "Kobzos Laszlo"]

Title: Analysis of Combinational Probability Transformers. | ANALIZA KOMBINACYJNYCH PRZEKSZTALTNIKOW PRAWDOPODOBIENSTWA.
Abstract: An analytical method is considered including certain problems associated with the synthesis of a probability transformer. The analysis is based on the formalism of orthogonal solutions in Walsh series. It is assumed that the transformer is a combinational logic circuit which is excited by a ‚Ä≥white‚Ä≥ random source, characterized by an equal distribution of probability and independence of responses on particular binary positions. Another problem formulated and solved in terms of spectral approach is a relationship between a continuous random variable and binary variable used to simulate it. A binary distribution providing the best approximation in the ‚Ä≥least-squares sense‚Ä≥ of the continuous density is defined.
Name: ["Laski Janusz"]

Title: MINIMAL REALIZATION ALGORITHM FOR MATRIX SEQUENCES.
Abstract: An algorithm is given for solving the Pade approximation problem for matrix sequences over an arbitrary field. The algorithm is a multivariate version of one first proposed by E. R. Berlekamp and J. L. Massey in a coding theory context, the extension being obtained using matrix-fraction descriptions of multivariable systems. The algorithm is recursive and seems to have some computational advantages. Furthermore, results are in a form that permits easy determination of state-space models from the transfer functions, solving what is called the partial realization problem. The algorithm also shows how to obtain a characterization of the invariants of this problem.
Name: ["Dickinson B.W.", "Morf M.", "Kailath T."]

Title: THEORY OF AN ADAPTIVE QUANTIZER.
Abstract: In an adaptive quantizer that has been used for speech encoding, the entire amplitude range expands or contracts by a multiplicative constant after each input sample. The constant, M//i, depends only on the magnitude of the current quantizer output. Assuming independent identically distributed input samples, it is shown that the sequence of quantizer ranges is a stochastically stable process. There is derived a key design equation, SIGMA p//i(x) log M//i equals 0, where p//i(x) is the steady-state probability that a quantized sample lies in the i**t**h magnitude level when the ratio of quantizer range scale to rms signal level is x. A designer may specify x and solve this equation for multipliers that provide the desired steady state performance. there are many such sets of multipliers and it is shown that the adaptation time constant associated with each set depends on M//N/M//1, the ratio of largest to smallest multiplier.
Name: ["Goodman D.J.", "Gersho A."]

Title: GRAPHICS, PROBLEM SOLVING AND VIRTUAL SYSTEMS.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: This article explores some basic concepts for problem solving through interactive computing. Characteristics of the interactive access process and over-all system concepts are discussed. The evolution of a recognition automaton is proposed based on current work toward a multi-console, interactive graphics Design Terminal.
Name: ["Dunn R.M."]

Title: EVALUATING JOB SHOP SIMULATION RESULTS.
Abstract: The problem of predicting the effectiveness of simulation results as applied to job shop production is discussed. A measure of effectiveness is developed which allows both absolute and relative evaluation of different scheduling techniques and the conditions for profit maximization under a customer service constraint are presented. The development is based upon a model of the shop process which assumes random scheduling behavior and which serves as the reference point for evaluating schedules. 5 refs.
Name: ["Franklin II Carter L."]

Title: STATE-SPACE BASIS FOR SEQUENTIAL PATTERN CLASSIFICATION.
Abstract: Detection and classification of patterns which are characterized by unknown parameters and state variables must be accomplished in conjunction with a method for estimating those quantities. In this paper a sequential procedure for performing this combined task, in the case of linear vector dynamic systems, is discussed. The method assumed that a particular sequence of noisy observations was generated by one of N possible dynamic systems, each of whose state transition and control matrices is known. It is shown that the statistics of the innovation process can be pre-computed, even when the assumed dynamic system is not correct. Specific difference equations are developed for computing the first and second ensemble moments. Similar difference equations are developed for computing the time correlation of the innovation sequences in the presence of model differences.
Name: ["Martin W.C.", "Hopkins W.D."]

Title: HEURISTIC APPROACH TO THE DESIGN OF MINIMUM ADAPTIVE RECOGNITION NETWORK.
Abstract: The proposed heuristic approach permits a rational choice of the transformation function or operator for an input superfluous information by using the two feedbacks from the recognition network's output to its inner structure during the learning procedure. After that, the third feedback from the network's weight components to its inputs makes it possible to minimize both the number of the network components and their respective input components which are needed for proper decisions of the network.
Name: ["Kvitashvili A."]

Title: DIVISION ALGORITHM FOR NEGABINARY NUMBERS THAT YIELDS THE QUOTIENT DIGIT BY DIGIT.
Abstract: A division algorithm for negabinary numbers that yields the quotients digit by digit is proposed. The appropriate digit of the quotient is equal to unity when a given condition is met. A check of this condition requires less expenditure of hardware than the addition of two numbers.
Name: ["Zaznova N.E."]

Title: Automatic Control of Cement Kilns. | [AUTOMATISCHES STEUERUNG EINES ZEMENTDREHOFENS MITTELS PROZESSRECHNER.]
Abstract: Design and algorithms for automatic process control of rotary kilns are presented. The calculation is based upon the discrete transient characteristics of the plant. The continuous automatic switching has also a provision for manual override control.
Name: ["Skopal J."]

Title: COMPUTER IMAGE PROCESSING SYSTEM NETWORKS.
Abstract: Implementation of a computer image processing system is costly in terms of equipment outlay, software development and the sporadic utilization of such equipment. However, the similarities of user requirements in many computer image processing applications suggest the cost-effectiveness of employing a computer network. The design considerations of such a network including input, output, systems interactive capabilities, communications and applications software are described in terms of biomedical image processing applications with which the authors have become involved recently. Acquisition, storage and transmission of data from a variety of image sources for subsequent processing are also discussed.
Name: ["Hopf Herbert H.", "Shapiro Murray", "King Marvin"]

Title: PATTERN RECOGNITION PROGRAMS WITH LEVEL ADAPTATION.
Abstract: Different types of patterning which exist in such diverse types of data as speech, text, and pictorial scenes are described. Several programs which process such data are discussed in terms of contextual, syntactic, semantic, and problem-domain dependent factors. Each of these factors constitutes a potential level of computer processing. By introducing different processing levels each having certain special characteristics (success on some data, inability to resolve other data), there is isolated a general technique for producing a level adaptive program system.
Name: ["Klinger A."]

Title: Generation of Complete Trees. | [GENERACJA DRZEW KOMPLETNYCH.]
Abstract: An algorithm by J. P. Char for the generation of trees in a passive network is discussed and formalized. A new algorithm which is based on the one by Char is proposed for the generation of complete trees, including signs, employing an edge-numbering convention. The proposed algorithm is claimed to be simple, and its computer realization can be accomplished easily. An illustrative example is included.
Name: ["Konkol Krystian"]

Title: RESOURCE ALLOCATION UNDER UNCERTAINTY VIA STOCHASTIC CONTROL METHODS.
Abstract: For a class of resource allocation problems under uncertainty, a sizable improvement in performance or saving in resources can be achieved when the allocation is made using stochastic control methods that have the closed-loop property. This property consists of the following: at every stage the decision is done using the past measurements on the results of the previous actions and the statistics of the future measurements. In this way the present decision takes into account the value of future information. A suboptimal algorithm having the above property and modest computational requirements has been derived, and its effectiveness shown in an example.
Name: ["Bar-Shalom Y.", "Larson R.E.", "Grossberg M.A."]

Title: MULTIVARIABLE SYSTEM SYNTHESIS WITH STEP DISTURBANCE REJECTION.
Abstract: A constructive procedure is presented for the synthesis of linear multivariable systems whose entire internal state and output are corrupted by unknown step disturbances. It is assumed that the dynamical behavior of the system is expressed in any one of three ‚Ä≥equivalent‚Ä≥ ways. In terms of the transfer matrix representation, T(s), the synthesis procedure, which employs ‚Ä≥integral feedforward control‚Ä≥ , is shown to be capable of producing any stable, desired closed loop transfer matrix, T//d(s), which can be expressed as the product of T(s) and any proper rational matrix, T//c(s), while simultaneously eliminating the steady-state effect of step disturbances at the output of the system. Furthermore, the synthesis scheme outlined employs only the known, directly measurable input and output signals.
Name: ["Wolovich W.A."]

Title: CONTROL OF DISCRIMINATION LEVEL AND RECOGNITION ERROR IN SEQUENTIAL PATTERN CLASSIFICATION.
Abstract: A measure of the ability of a pattern classifier to discriminate among different pattern classes is introduced. The use of this measure then defines a compromise between pattern discrimination and recognition error. The measure is particularly useful in sequential pattern classification in allowing control of discrimination level versus recognition error. The trade-off between discrimination level and recognition error is demonstrated for data used in a medical diagnosis problem.
Name: ["McLaren R.W.", "Han K.S.", "Lodwick G.S."]

Title: APPLICATION OF LEARNING ALGORITHMS TO HYPOTHESES TESTING PROBLEMS.
Abstract: By partitioning the observation space (which is one dimensional) and by suitably defining the events called reward and penalty the basic problem of testing between two hypotheses is cast as a learning problem in stochastic automata. That is, testing between two hypotheses is converted into a problem of identifying the state of the stochastic automaton corresponding to the minimum penalty probability. Once this is done, the application of the learning algorithm developed for the 2-state stochastic automaton to the two hypotheses testing problem becomes immediate. Given the allowed upper bounds on the error probabilities of the two kinds, a method for the design of the algorithm which will ensure a decision within the specified error, is given.
Name: ["Thathacher M.A.L.", "Varahan S."]

Title: MATRIX RICCATI EQUATIONS AND SYSTEMS STRUCTURE.
Abstract: A new algorithm for solving discrete-time optimal control problems has been presented and related to recent developments in linear system theory and recursive estimation. This algorithm is shown to be a special case of the ‚Ä≥structure algorithm‚Ä≥ used for characterizing properties of linear systems.
Name: ["Payne H.J.", "Silverman L.M."]

Title: SUBSPACE METHOD IN PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: The usual algorithms in pattern recognition assume that an n-dimensional domain in the n-dimensional representation space corresponds to each of the classes. The subspace model assumes that an m-dimensional subspace (m less than n) passing the origin corresponds to a class. The shortcomings of the original version of the subspace model were eliminated in the version that is explained in the present paper. The new version assigns mutually orthogonal subspaces to classes, where the number of classes can be equal to or larger than 2. It also provides a special ‚Ä≥reject‚Ä≥ subspace.
Name: ["Watanabe Satosi", "Pakvasa Nikhil"]

Title: SYNTACTIC APPROACH TO FINGERPRINT PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: A syntactic approach to the recognition of fingerprint patterns is presented. The fingerprint impressions are subdivided into sampling squares which are preprocessed for feature extraction. A class of context-free languages is used to describe the fingerprint patterns. The recognition is accomplished using sequential parsing technique to reduce the time requirement.
Name: ["Moayer B.", "Fu K.S."]

Title: NONLINEAR ADAPTIVE RECURSIVE IMAGE ENHANCEMENT.
Abstract: A nonlinear method of estimating pictorial data from noisy observations is considered. The data is assumed to be composed of an object with one texture in the background. An edge detection technique using likelihood functions is used to decide if an incoming picture element is a member of the object or the background. Then the picture element is directed to one of the two Kalman filters designed based upon the statistics of the object or the background accordingly.
Name: ["Nahi N.E.", "Habibi A."]

Title: FINITE-TIME OBSERVER FOR NONLINEAR DYNAMIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: This paper introduces finite-time observers for a class of nonlinear dynamic systems. The concept of observability is first shown to be a necessary condition for the existence of a finite-time observer for the system. Then a finite-time observer for an important class of systems is constructed with a novel structure which avoids the use of differentiators.
Name: ["Kou S.R.", "Tarn T.", "Elliott D.L."]

Title: OBSERVERS FOR SYSTEMS WITH UNKNOWN AND INACCESSIBLE INPUTS.
Abstract: Observer theory for constant-coefficient, linear systems is extended to systems with unknown, inaccessible inputs. Two types of observers for such systems are defined, and simplified criteria for their existence are developed. A theorem regarding the structure of these observers is given which allows the application of results for systems with single unknown inputs to systems with multiple unknown inputs.
Name: ["Meditch J.S.", "Hostetter G.H."]

Title: SEGMENTED ALGORITHM FOR SOLVING A CLASS OF STATE CONSTRAINED DISCRETE OPTIMAL CONTROL PROBLEMS.
Abstract: A segmented algorithm for solving state constrained optimal control problems is presented. Its main feature is that it may be implemented on an array of digital computers. Such an implementation exhibits two attractive properties. The first one is that the computational time is reduced due to the parallelism of computations achieved. The second property is that a graceful degradation of performance is realized, i. e. , the array produces approximate solutions in the presence of hardware faults.
Name: ["Meyer G.G.L."]

Title: FEEDBACK CONTROL PROCESS IN AGRICULTURAL PEST MANAGEMENT.
Abstract: A three-component agro-ecosystem consisting of a single prey (host), predator (parasite), and crop is described by means of a linear vector difference equation involving a control term. Deviation of the state of the system from a threshold, and the use of chemical control agents are subject to economic penalties. Dynamic programming is used to determine the optimal pest control policy as a function of the state of the system, so that a quadratic cost function is minimized. Stratified random sampling is used to estimate the state of the system. A simulation of the model, utilizing a digital computer, is presented.
Name: ["Ford-Livene Carlos"]

Title: On the Controllability of Discrete Linear Systems with Output Feedback
Abstract: A discrete time linear system Xt+l = Axt + But'y = Cxt' with output feedback ut = GtYt‚Äô can be regarded as a nonlinear system with ‚Äúcontrol‚Äù G t, Weak sufficient conditions are given for the existence of a finite sequence of gains for which every initial state can be driven to the origin. For a one input, one output system, the question of what terminal states can be reached from a given initial state is resolved. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Mullis C.T."]

Title: OPTIMAL FILTERING FOR SYSTEMS GOVERNED BY FUNCTIONAL DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS.
Abstract: Both linear and nonlinear filters are derived for systems governed by coupled partial and integro-differential equations. The framework used is sufficiently general that the optimal filters for (i) lumped parameter systems having multiple time varying or constant time delays, and (ii) coupled lumped and hyperbolic distributed parameter systems, and (iii) lumped parameter systems with functional time delays, evolve as special cases. Although the filtering equations are the final result, the corresponding smoothing equations are developed as well, and us with a decomposition theorem to produce the optimal filter. The performance of the filter is illustrated through application to a well stirred chemical reactor with external heat exchange.
Name: ["Yu T.K.", "Seinfeld J.H.", "Ray W.H."]

Title: ADAPTIVE TYPE CONTROLLER FOR NONLINEAR MULTIVARIABLE PROCESSES.
Abstract: This article presents a computer control technique for controlling a largely uncertain multivariable plant using a model tracking method. The design technique presented employs the deterministic type Lyapunov signal synthesis procedure which can be implemented on a suitable digital computer, and does not need an explicit knowledge of the plant model.
Name: ["Nikiforuk P.N.", "Gupta M.M.", "Kanai K.", "Wagner L."]

Title: EXPERIMENTAL AUTOMATION OF AIR-TRAFFIC CONTROL.
Abstract: It is reported that Eurocontrol, the European Organization for the Safety of Air Navigation, has recently inaugurated at Bretigny, France, a powerful ATC simulation system to be used for the development and evaluation of future automated systems. The multi-computer, multi-display system incorporates considerable data-processing innovation, aimed at enabling the simulation of the air-traffic environment of any geographical location, and the test and evaluation of any chosen ATC procedure. Extensive recording and analysis features are built in to permit subsequent off-line analysis of the results of these simulations.
Name: ["Worby R.H."]

Title: APPLICATION OF MANY-VALUED LOGIC TO FAULT DETECTION.
Abstract: A brief discussion of the application of many-valued logic to the design of reliable digital systems is presented. Specifically, its use in the detection of faults in completely specified synchronous sequential machines is illustrated. Many-valued concepts are shown to be valuable both in the development of efficient fault sequences and in the economical realization of the corresponding easily testable machines.
Name: ["Sheppard Donald A."]

Title: Theory of Digital Automata. | [TEORIA AUTOMATOW CYFROWYCH.]
Abstract: The main problems of the theory of digital automata are briefly surveyed and Polish achievements in this field are reviewed. In particular, the principal investigations of the abstract synthesis, structural synthesis, combination network synthesis, reliability synthesis, and general problems are pointed out. A comparison with world achievements shows that some problems, such as block synthesis of automata, uniform structures, fault-tolerating automata, digital system testing, machine synthesis of automata, and some problems of sequential system synthesis have received little attention. An attempt is made to forecast future trends in this sphere and to outline a program of research aand development.
Name: ["Traczyk Wieslaw"]

Title: BOUNDS ON THE PERFORMANCE OF COMPUTING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: In this paper, results are derived which contribute to a complexity-based, applied theory of computation. The principal results are a set of computational inequalities which establish boundaries on the storage-time tradeoffs which are permissible on general purpose computers. These boundaries are used to determine efficient machine configurations and efficient programming strategies.
Name: ["Savage John E."]

Title: A Projected Gradient Method for Automatic Equalization in the Discrete Frequency Domain
Abstract: In a recent paper [1] we reported on a new mean-square error automatic equalizer utilizing Rosen's gradient projection theorem to optimize parameters in the discrete frequency domain. Here we develop another projection method to optimize the discrete frequency parameters. The algorithm converges (in the mean) for any channel, even in the presence of noise. It is shown that for the channels Considered, convergence is equivalent to comparable time domain equalizers. The method makes use of fast Fourier transform (FFT) algorithms for computation of the iteration matrix, the gradient, and the projection operation. Use of the FFT for parameter iterations reduces the necessary computations per parameter to a number proportional to log2 M compared to.M for a time domain equalizer, where M is the number of equalizer parameters. The method results in fewer computations per parameter for each iteration, but a somewhat slower rate of convergence than the method employing Rosen's gradient projection. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Walzman T."]

Title: RANKING AND SELECTION PROCEDURES WITH CORRELATED OBSERVATIONS AND SIMULATION.
Abstract: The use of ranking and selection procedures to set the length of computer simulation runs has been suggested. However, ranking and selection procedures to date have generally assumed the observations are independent; hence, since in simulation the data encountered are often correlated, those procedures may not be fully appropriate. In this paper the effect of correlated data on the sample size (simulation run-length) requirements of a selection procedure, is studied assuming a first-order autoregressive model for the dependence within a population and independence across populations. Several suggestions are made as to desirable theoretical developments being pursued, and as to heuristic procedures recommended in the meantime.
Name: ["Dudewicz Edward J.", "Zaino Jr. Nicholas A."]

Title: NONRECURSIVE ALGEBRAIC SOLUTION FOR THE DISCRETE SMOOTHED ERROR COVARIANCE MATRIX.
Abstract: The algebraic solution for the discrete Riccati equation may be exploited to obtain nonrecursive solutions for the discrete smoothed error-covariance matrix. The system matrix required to obtain this result is given, and the corresponding matrix for the continuous case may be found in an analogous manner.
Name: ["Monzingo Robert A."]

Title: Comments on ‚ÄúMinimization of Fuzzy Functions‚Äù
Abstract: This correspondence points out the insufficiency of the method for minimization of fuzzy functions as presented in a recent short note.<sup>1</sup> Two lemmas, which are the basis for a new minimization technique [2], are represented. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Kandel A."]
Keywords: ["fuzzy function", "fuzzy logic", "minimization", "prime implicant of fuzzy function", "minimization fuzzy"]
Affiliations: [' New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology']

Title: Optimal choice of basis for a floating-point arithmetic | Optimale Basiswahl f√ºr eine Gleitkomma-Arithmetik
Abstract: Choosing an internal floating-point representation for a binary computer with given word-length is influenced by two factors: the size of the range of admissible numbers and the precision of the respective floating-point arithmetic. In this paper "precision" is defined by a statistical model of rounding errors. According to this definition base 4 floating-point arithmetic on an average produces smaller rounding errors than all other floating-point arithmetics with a base 2<sup>k</sup>, provided that the ranges of numbers have equal size. ¬© 1973 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Kreifelts Th."]

Title: STATE ESTIMATION FOR CONTINUOUS-TIME SYSTEM WITH INTERRUPTED OBSERVATION.
Abstract: The estimation problem is considered for linear continuous-time systems with the interrupted observation mechanism which is characterized in terms of the jump Markov process taking on the values of 0 or 1. The minimum variance estimator algorithm is derived. The approach adopted is to express the jump process in terms of the initial value and the jump times instead of its instantaneous values and in order to apply D. G. Lainiotis' formula, to regard the initial value and jump times as the unknown system parameter vector. The parameter vector is, however, infinite dimensional so that Lainiotis' formula cannot be applied directly. This is because the formula is applicable only to linear systems with a finite dimensional parameter vector. Therefore, the minimum variance estimator algorithm is derived by using some limiting procedure. The resultant optimal algorithm is infinite dimensional, so that feasible approximate algorithms should be developed for practical implementation. A simple illustrating example is also worked out.
Name: ["Sawaragi Y.", "Katayama T.", "Fujishige S."]

Title: STOCHASTIC PENALTY FUNCTION OPTIMIZATION.
Abstract: A stochastic penalty algorithm is presented, which can be used to find a constrained optimum point for a concave or convex objective function subject to a nonlinear constraint which forms a connected region, even when the objective function itself is not available, but only a noisy estimate of it. When the constraint consists of one linear equation, the author proves convergence to the constrained optimum value and bounds the rate of convergence of the algorithm to the constrained optimum value. This algorithm is then applied to the nonlinear problem of automatically making an array of detectors form a beam in a desired direction in space when unknown interfering noise is present so as to maximize the signal-to-noise ratio subject to a constraint on the super-gain ratio.
Name: ["Winkler L.P."]

Title: The off the shelf system - a packaged information management system
Abstract: The Off The Shelf System (OTSS) is a packaged information management system for hierarchical data bases. OTSS provides, without computer programming, processes to enter and alter data in such a data base, make complex retrievals of data from the data base, and specify various security mechanisms to limit access to, or alteration of, a data base. OTSS also provides a mechanism for extending the available processes on a project by project basis. OTSS has been implemented using Master Links and the Natural Dialogue System. | The Off-The-Shelf System (OTSS) is a packaged information management system for hierarchical data bases. OTSS was designed to operate on any hierarchical data base regardless of its structure and regardless of the data fields stored in the data base. Retrieval processes are available to print, alter, rank, plot, distribute, compute statistics, and perform regression analysis of data. These processes are specified to OTSS in a key-word English-like language in an interactive dialogue environment. OTSS allows for simple alteration of the retrieval process from request to request by selective replacement, deletion, or addition of statements to the dialogue description of the process to be performed. As part of the package, OTSS provides a data-base-independent security mechanism. This mechanism allows a data base administrator to restrict access or alteration of a data base and use of certain process and language facilities in OTSS on a user-by-user basis. A user can be restricted to a logical hierarchical subsection of the data base and to only certain data items stored in that subsection. The user can be further restricted to using only certain processes of OTSS such as printing, ranking, or altering processes, but not plotting or distributing. In addition, OTSS provides the ability to extend the processing capabilities of the system by allowing a programmer to add new processes to the system on a project-by-project basis. The processes so installed are available to the project installing them, and do not become a permanent part of OTSS. OTSS was implemented using the Master Links data base management system and the Natural Dialogue System, a system for designing and implementing interactive computing languages in a dialogue environment.
Name: ["Heindel L.E.", "Roberto J.T."]

Title: SELF-SCALING VARIABLE METRIC ALGORITHMS WITHOUT LINE SEARCH FOR UNCONSTRAINED MINIMIZATION.
Abstract: A new class of quasi-Newton algorithms is introduced for unconstrained minimization in which no line search is necessary and the inverse Hessian approximations are positive definite. These algorithms are based on a two parameter family of rank two updating formulas used earlier with line search in self-scaling variable metric algorithms. It is proved that in a quadratic case the new algorithms converge at least weak superlinearly. A special case of the above algorithms was implemented and tested numerically on several test functions. In this implementation, however, cubic interpolation was performed whenever the objective function was not satisfactorily decreased on the first ‚Ä≥shot‚Ä≥ (with unit step size), but this did not occur too often except for very difficult functions. The numerical results indicate that the new algorithm is competitive and often superior to previous methods.
Name: ["Oren Shmuel S."]

Title: PROBLEM OF COMPROMISE CONTROL IN TWO-LEVEL HIERARCHICAL SYSTEMS ALLOWING FOR RANDOM PERTURBATIONS.
Abstract: The authors consider the problem of choosing a compromise control in two-level hierarchical systems allowing for random perturbations. The solution is based on the method of equivalent transformations to deterministic form of a stochastic programming problem. The proposed algorithm is illustrated by an example.
Name: ["Volkovich V.L.", "Lavrinenko E.P."]

Title: HARDWARE MONITOR VIEW OF REACTOR PROBLEMS.
Abstract: The Neurotron hardware monitor was used to collect instruction count statistics and related machine performance data for reactor problems included in the Argonne National Laboratory benchmark problem collection. These measurements, made during IBM 360/75 execution, are studied to determine similarity of individual problems, and a Euclidean metric is applied in an attempt to identify job clusters with like attributes.
Name: ["Butler Margaret K."]

Title: DATA REDUCTION TECHNIQUE, FOR PATIENT MONITORING
Abstract: The application is considered of semiconductor memories in patient monitoring equipment. This is a technique for classifying values of a monitored parameter taken over a period of time. The result is a distribution curve hereafter referred to as the histogram. This histogram can be produced by some commercially available equipment from such information as electrocardiograms, electroencephalograms, respiration, electromyograms, etc. , and is considered a valuable diagnostic tool. Present methods have an important limitation, concerning the availability upon request of the histogram. That is due to their non-overlapping sampling time intervals, which shift the statistic consistency towards the end of the measuring period thus confining printing or observation of the result to a quite inflexible recycling sequence. The work described here proposes to avoid this shortcoming by optimizing the interfacing with the input/output equipment and by adding more flexibility to the existing state of the art. Essentially, it is an updated manner of processing, the data being continuously refreshed so that the resulted histogram will belong to a constant interval running back from the moment of observation of printing.
Name: ["Ghelfan Pavel", "Edelstein Dany", "Brauner Raul"]

Title: HYBRID NEURAL MODELING SYSTEM.
Abstract: A hybrid neural modeling system is described, which provides the investigator an inexpensive means of simulating certain aspects of nervous subsystem functioning. ‚Ä≥Hands on‚Ä≥ control of the system gives him considerable flexibility while saving him time and cost.
Name: ["Pottala Erik W."]

Title: TERMINAL MODELS OF DIGITAL GATES ALLOWING WAVEFORM SIMULATION.
Abstract: Initial investigations are described into the terminal modeling of TTL digital gates for waveform simulation. This scheme generates network simulation differential equations in the normal form so that analysis is not tied to any specific existing program. The model's properties are discussed as well as its advantages in a general logic analysis routine.
Name: ["Bass S.C.", "Peak S.C."]

Title: ADAPTIVE DIGITAL MTI SIGNAL PROCESSING.
Source: IEEE Electron and Aerosp Syst Conv, Rec
Abstract: The design of an adaptive digital MTI system, which automatically compensates for platform motion and the doppler offset of weather clutter and chaff returns is described. This adaptive MTI uses two, range gated, independent feedback loops. One is a slow loop which, based on samples of fixed ground or sea clutter returns, controls a compensating frequency offset of the coherent oscillator (COHO). The other is a fast loop with a response time of 20-40 range cells, which estimates the doppler offset of weather clutter as a function of range and controls a digital phase-shifter at the COHO output to compensate for the corresponding pulse-to-pulse phase-shift. Theoretical results illustrating the expected performance of this MTI system are presented and practical design problems are discussed.
Name: ["Hansen V.G.", "Campbell R.B.", "Freedman N.", "Shrader W.W."]

Title: APPROXIMATE LOGIC.
Abstract: The purpose of this research is to investigate a general framework where assertions about approximate behavior of complex processes can be defined and evaluated. Different formulations of the infinite value propositional calculus are outlined and investigated. A notion of approximate predicate calculus is obtained. Interpretations are defined. In each case the new notions are compared with the corresponding ones in traditional logic. Finally one particular interpretation is investigated. Conditions for the interchange of quantifiers are given.
Name: ["Tsichritzis D."]

Title: METHOD OF SUCCESSIVE QUANTILE SEARCH IN PROBLEMS OF MEASURING THE STATISTICAL PARAMETERS OF STOCHASTIC PROCESSES.
Abstract: The method of successive quantile search in the problems of measuring the statistical parameters of stochastic processes is considered. It is shown that the method can be implemented in statistical analyzers of stochastic processes. The number and size of the comparison levels is chosen on the basis of a priori data on the range of possible values of the random quantity to be measured and of the requisite estimation accuracy.
Name: ["Os'minin A.A.", "Krasheninnikov V.R.", "Evplov A.S.", "Nerubatskii V.A.", "Turobov V.P."]

Title: ENTROPY MINIMAX PROCESSING OF INCOMPLETE DATA SETS.
Abstract: The purpose of this note is to describe a means of analyzing data sets in which some independent variable data is missing for some of the points in a sample, where the method of multivariate analysis used is entropy minimax. The means described is based upon a cluster approach as distinguished from continuous approaches such as those involving potential functions, and is free of any prior assumptions concerning mutual independence of features.
Name: ["Christensen R.A."]

Title: ADAPTIVE ON-LINE CLASSIFICATION OF MULTI-SPECTRAL SCANNER DATA.
Abstract: A possible solution to the analysis of the massive amounts of multi-spectral scanner data from the Earth Resource Technical Satellite (ERTS) program is proposed. This solution is offered as an adaptive on-line classification scheme. The classifier is described as well as its controller which is based on ground truth data. Cluster analysis is presented as an alternative approach to the ground truth data. Adaptive feature selection is discussed and possible mini-computer implementations are offered.
Name: ["Fromm Frederick R.", "Northouse Richard A."]

Title: A sequential method for system identification in hierarchical structure
Abstract: Implicit in all of hierarchical systems theory is the idea that it is generally easier to deal with several low order systems than with one system of high order. The basic idea of hierarchical systems theory is to decompose a large dimensional system into smaller dimensioned sub-systems in such a way that the overall system objectives can be met. This paper is concerned with the application of hierarchical system theory to the identification problem. Specifically, the equations associated with a given identification problem are recast such that they may be decomposed into infimal subproblems of system identification which can be coordinated using hierarchical systems theory. The maximum a posteriori approach to system identification is taken. This leads to a two point boundary value problem solution which determines optimum state and parameter estimates and estimates of any unknown prior statistics. Invariant imbedding is used to resolve this two point boundary value problem such that a recursive or sequential solution to the identification problem is obtained. Several examples indicate the use of the identification algorithms. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Smith N.J.", "Sage A.P."]

Title: An hypothesis generation model for judgment in nonmetric multiple-cue probability learning
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present a two-phase hypothesis generation model to describe behavior in multiple-cue probability learning tasks with nonmetric cues. The model assumes that on each trial the subject generates two sets of hypotheses: (a) a hypothesis concerning which cue dimension (or pattern) will lead to a correct prediction on that trial and (b) a hypothesis concerning which response will be correct given the cue dimension attended to on that trial. Five-hundred-twelve subjects were assigned to 20 groups in a binary choice task involving two binary cue dimensions. Each group observed cues which differed in validity. Analysis of the data indicated that subjects attend to both cue dimensions in making judgments even when one cue has zero validity. A test of the fit of the observed data to the asymptotic response proportions predicted by the model indicated a reasonable fit. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Castellan Jr. N.J.", "Edgell S.E."]

Title: On hierarchical estimation and system identification using the MAP criterion
Abstract: This paper presents a general treatment of hierarchically structured maximum-a posteriori (MAP) estimation and system parameter identification algorithms for large-scale systems. Continuous-time and discrete-time algorithms for hierarchical estimation and system identification in large-scale systems are derived for several supremal infimal coordination methods. Consolidation and unification of previous results in hierarchical systems theory as applied to system identification are accomplished. Numerical examples are considered to demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithms which are potentially of considerable utility in computer modeling of large systems. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Fry C.M.", "Sage A.P."]

Title: TRANSITIONS IN EXTENDIBLE ARRAYS.
Abstract: Arrays are among the best understood and most widely used data structures. Yet there are no satisfactory techniques for handling algorithms involving extendible arrays (where, e. g. , rows and/or columns can be added dynamically). In this paper, the problem of allocating storage for extendible arrays is examined in the light of earlier work on data graphs and addressing schemes. A formal analog of the assertion that simplicity of array extension precludes simplicity of transition (marching along rows/ columns) is proved.
Name: ["Rosenberg Arnold L."]

Title: TOWARD A MARKOVIAN TRAFFIC CONTROL EVALUATION SYSTEM.
Abstract: The objective of the paper is to present a technique for evaluating traffic control alternatives and resultant performance changes in a complex traffic system. Field examples from the merging section of the Baltimore Harbor Tunnel are presented and analyzed through a multistage optimization process, termed Markovian decision theory. Changes in flow-density relationships, employment of traffic cones, and a hypothesized metering example are discussed as preliminary tests of the technique.
Name: ["Haefner Lonnie E.", "Warner III John A."]

Title: MARKOV CHAIN MODELS FOR ANALYZING MEMORY INTERFERENCE IN MULTIPROCESSOR COMPUTER SYSTEMS.
Abstract: This paper discusses various analytical techniques for studying the extent of memory interference in a multiprocessor system with a crosspoint switch for processor-memory communication. Processor behavior is simplified to an ordered sequence of a memory request followed by an interval of processing time.
