The techniques discussed include discrete and continuous time Markov chain models as well as several approximate analytic methods.
Name: ["Bhandarkar Dileep P.", "Fuller Samuel H."]

Title: AUTOMATED EXPLORATION OF THE DESIGN SPACE FOR REGISTER TRANSFER (RT) SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A design Automation System for the RT level of design is described. The System explores the design space by finding alternative implementations for a user given behavioral specification. The alternative solutions are obtained by transformations on a graph model. These transformations effect trade-offs between the cost of the hardware and the speed of the algorithm. Heuristic routines are used to reduce the design space by exploring only those alternatives whose characteristics approach a user given set of goals.
Name: ["Barbacci Mario R.", "Siewiorek Daniel P."]

Title: ESTIMATE FOR THE OPERATIONAL RELIABILITY OF FINITE AUTOMATA.
Abstract: An algorithm is presented for estimating the state probability functions of a finite automaton whose model is in the form of a transition matrix (or graph). The method does not require the determination of the eigenvalues of a characteristic polynomial and provides an engineering procedure for evaluating the reliability of finite probabilistic automata.
Name: ["Matveev A.A."]

Title: Analysis of the Additive-Type Threshold Model of Learning. | ANALIZA ADDYTYWNEGO PROGOWEGO MODELU UCZENIA.
Abstract: A method is presented for analyzing an additive threshold model for learning of conditional reactions associated with the so-called classical conditioning. The method leads to the identification of all functions of the model, without taking advantage of some arbitrary assumptions.
Name: ["Pacut Andrzej"]

Title: A constrained optimization model of risky decisions
Abstract: A decision model is formulated for individual choices between gambles whose probabilities and payoffs are explicitly stated. The decision situation is characterized as R<sub>N</sub> = (X, P, Z, T, Œ±) where X is a payoff matrix, P is the objective probability distribution over the states of nature, Z is a class of objective functions, T is tolerable regret and 1 - Œ± is the maximum probability for accepting regrets greater than T. Given R<sub>N</sub>, the problem of selecting a strategy is the solution of a chance constrained optimization problem. The solutions for choice situations having two alternatives and n states of nature are developed in a series of theorems. Some implications for experimentation and possible applications are discussed. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Barron F.H.", "Mackenzie K.D."]

Title: GATE EQUIVALENT MODEL FOR COMBINATIONAL LOGIC NETWORK ANALYSIS.
Abstract: An algebraic model for combinational logic networks is presented which is isomorphic to the original network structure down to the level of interconnected logic gates. Thus both the structure and logical function of the network are characterized by a single algebraic expression. This dual nature of the model makes it especially useful as a tool of fault analysis, since it simplifies the problem of recognizing relations between structural defects (faults) and their logical consequences. The model has been found applicable to a variety of specific problems.
Name: ["Reese Randall D.", "McCluskey Edward J."]

Title: AUTOMATIC BATCH CONTROL FOR COATING PREPARATION SYSTEM.
Abstract: Requirements for an automated coating preparation system are considered and sequential automation to integrate batch processes and to produce a nearly continuous output is described. It is concluded that many batch processes including the startup and shutdown of continuous systems utilize a preprogrammed control cycle. The programmed control systems are used to assure a repeated product result. The preprogrammed sequences provide the rigid control enforcement needed to efficiently reproduce a constant quality, batch after batch. There are many system approaches to a programmed control cycle presently in operation, each with a varying degree of success.
Name: ["Hambleton Dana"]

Title: CONSTRAINING HYPERPLANE TECHNIQUE FOR STATE VARIABLE CONSTRAINED OPTIMAL CONTROL TECHNIQUES.
Abstract: A new approach to the numerical solution of optimal control problems with state-variable inequality constraints is presented. It is shown that the concept of constraining hyperplanes may be used to approximate the original problem with one where the constraints are of a mixed state-control variable type. The efficiency and the accuracy of the combination of constraining hyperplanes and a second-order differential dynamic programming algorithm are investigated on problems of different complexity, and comparisons are made with the slack-variable and the penalty-function techniques.
Name: ["Martensson Krister"]

Title: DISPERSIONAL IDENTIFICATION EQUATION OF NONLINEAR PLANTS.
Abstract: The main result of this paper is dispersional identification of nonlinear plants in a class of models with finite memory T. Thus the result is an extension of the identification equation to the class of noninertial models discussed by the authors elsewhere. The results make it possible to obtain the cross regressional function estimation of the optimal model response in relation to the input disturbance. The concept of d-stationary and d-stationarily related random processes is introduced which is an analog of stationarity in a wide sense for processes with nonlinear regression. Examples of nonlinear plants are considered for which the dispersional identification method leads to an accurate result.
Name: ["Bunich A.L.", "Raibman N.S."]

Title: SEMI-AUTOMATED SYSTEM FOR PLOTTING AND COMPUTER CATALOGING OF REMOTE SENSING IMAGERY.
Abstract: As part of a total aerial image data handling system, a computer-assisted system for plotting and descriptor cataloging of aerial imagery has been developed and is in operational use at the NASA-Ames Research Center for the Earth Resources Aircraft Project (ERAP). The system employs two graphics tablets interactively on line to a digital computer as input devices to derive frame coordinates by correlating image points to map points. Various software programs and operating routines allow the operator to semiautomatically plot an image by selecting two or more points within the image most easily matched with map detail. The computer performs the necessary transformations of scaling and orientation to calculate the center and corner coordinates of the frame. Twenty-five other descriptors for each frame are also entered into the computerized data base using predictive techniques requiring a minimum of operator time for verifications or corrections. System hardware, software, operating procedures, precision, and production rates are described. The data base generated by the system is accessed by an image selection system which rapidly retrieves individual images based on geographic location.
Name: ["Gnauck Gary E.", "Hurd Donald J.", "Kroeck Richard M."]

Title: ON THE SMALLEST NUMBER OF PROGRAM MODULES NEEDED TO DUPLICATE DYNAMIC INDEPENDENT INTERACTIONS.
Abstract: By considering the resources of a software system as the nodes of a random network and then examining long-term paths on this network, it is possible under certain circumstances to find a simpler network (fewer nodes) that has the same path properties. The smallest possible network with the ‚Ä≥same path structure‚Ä≥ could then serve as a fundamental index of the complexity of the larger (more nodes) network with some dynamic behavior. This paper examines only the simplest case for which this is possible and omits complex proofs.
Name: ["Flynn R.J."]

Title: DYNAMIC COMPUTER CONTROL OF A HOT WIDE STEEL STRIP MILL.
Abstract: A recently introduced automation project in Scotland is reported. The mill, 1727 mm wide, was designed for a total output of 1. 5 million tons per year and was first commissioned in 1962. The computer control scheme covers material tracking through the furnaces and up to the coilers, and automatic sequencing in the mill. The dynamic functions of computer control are emphasized, including automatic gage control and finishing-temperature control. The mill setups are calculated, based on rolling strategies using mathematical models, and are output from the computer to the mill drives. Future developments in the application of computer automation to the control and monitoring of a complete steel-rolling plant are surveyed.
Name: ["Shaw D.A.", "Eades C.G."]

Title: TIME-DOMAIN ANALYSIS OF CHARACTERISTICS OF THE HUMAN OPERATOR IN A SIMPLE MANUAL CONTROL SYSTEM.
Source: J Fac Eng Univ Tokyo Ser B
Abstract: An attempt to find the characteristics of the human operator in a simple manual control system by applying a method of statistical analysis in the time-domain is described. First, the closed-loop system concerned is considered approximately to be a second order system, and its natural period and the damping ratio are determined. Secondly, the gain and the delay of the human controller are estimated on the assumption of the crossover model. The adaptive response of the operator to a change in the controlled dynamics is also discussed by using the same model.
Name: ["Isobe Takashi", "Kobatake Hidefumi"]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR SYNCHRONIZING ENTRANCE RAMP VEHICLES AND FREEWAY GAPS.
Abstract: An algorithm for synchronizing ramp vehicles into freeway gaps is developed. It is thought to be an improvement over existing synchronization algorithms because the derivation takes into account the phenomenon of vehicular interaction which is fundamental to any realistic description of the merging process. Attention is focused on identification of new platoons and characterizing gap propagations within a platoon. The probability of synchronizing a ramp vehicle with an ordered gap of a platoon is formulated in terms of the platooning freeway vehicles' speeds and arrival times at a shoulder lane detector and is maximized to generate the optimal release time of the ramp vehicle. A numerical example is included.
Name: ["Klee H.I."]

Title: MEASURING AND MODELLING MAN-COMPUTER INTERACTION.
Abstract: The Dialogue Monitor has been developed as a tool for the measurement of computer service. The objectives of such measurement are defined. A set of models and measures is developed. Operation of the Dialogue Monitor and analysis of the data obtained are briefly discussed.
Name: ["Abrams Marshall D.", "Lindamood George E.", "Pyke Jr. Thomas N."]

Title: Bayes estimation of a convex quadratic
Abstract: The estimation of a quadratic regression curve when the quadratic coefficient is known to be positive is treated by a Bayesian method. The method extends easily to deal with a general linear model under parameter constraints. ¬© 1973 Oxford University Press.
Name: ["O'hagan A."]
Keywords: ["bayes", "constrained parameters", "linear regression", "multivariate normal distribution", "multivariate t distribution"]

Title: Optimal digital simulations for random linear systems with integration constraints
Abstract: A generalized approach involving concepts from optimization theory is developed for realizing optimal digital simulations for linear, time-varying, continuous dynamical systems having random inputs by modifying discrete input signal variances. The minimization of a cost functional based on the state covariance matrices of the continuous system and its discrete model leads to a two-point boundary value problem which can be solved by known numerical techniques. The result is a systematic procedure for determining optimal digital simulations under the constraints that the numerical integration formula and integration step size have been specified in advance. An example is presented to illustrate the procedure, including a verification using Monte Carlo simulation runs. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Rowland J.R."]

Title: Application of a mathematical model for the control and optimization of a distillation plant
Abstract: The principles of optimizing process control are elucidated by weighing the merits of hill-climbing, feedback, methods against model, feedforward, methods. It is shown that the advantages of the two methods can be employed at both the optimizing and the stabilizing control levels of a chemical plant. A simple static model containing appropriately chosen non-linearities is being used in a feedforward control loop and updated regularly by feedback in an openloop computer control system, results of which are given. Finally, it is shown that such a model can also be used for statistical evaluation of computer control methods. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Duyfjes G.", "van der Grinten P.M.E.M."]

Title: Automaton models of performance
Abstract: This work illustrates the use of a stochastic automaton model for describing the temporal steps taken by a student in solving simple arithmetic prolems. The method provides a hierarchial classification of problems by difficulty expressed in terms of the structural features of the problems. The model parameters represent the error rates due to these features. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Offir J.D."]

Title: Optimal inference and a redundancy measure for overlapping data sets
Abstract: A redundant sampling feature is added to the binomial data-generating process so that K observers hold a number of samples, say C, in common and then report to a central decision-maker. Analysis specifies the optimal rule for inference which provides for the proper discounting of the partially redundant reports, and numerical results are obtained. In a first case C is assumed known to the decision-maker; in a second, no prior information is available regarding the sampling overlap. An information-theoretic measure of decisional redundancy is obtained for the K = 2 process, and redundancy is discussed in the context of applied decision systems. Several research topics are suggested. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Hershman R.L."]

Title: Hybrid computer solution of queueing systems
Abstract: Digital computers have been widely used for solving queueing problems. However, when the complexity of the problem increases the computational time and cost rise exponentially. A hybrid computer approach has been developed where the rise in cost caused by the complexity of the problem is negligible. The errors of the hybrid system were not cummulative and therefore it was capable of duplicating the solution of the digital computer within the accuracy of 2 %. The optimization af a n stage stochastic service system has been used as an example. The success of this method of solution has opened a whole new dimension toward the application of hybrid computations to queueing problems. ¬© 1973 Presses Acad√©miques Europ√©ennes, Brussels.
Name: ["Khalil T.M.", "Valisalo P.E.", "Copsey A."]

Title: Bayesian statistics applied to the optical estimation of background in routine nuclear counting procedures
Abstract: Bayesian estimation theory is applied to the problem of determining a best estimate of the background count rate in routine counting procedures. The optimal estimation procedure is carried out using a practical loss function and a conjugate prior probability distribution. The Bayes estimate is obtained by using data, prior information and tabulated values of the chi-square probability function. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Raeside D.E."]

Title: Interaction information and Markov chain
Abstract: The problem of multivariate information analysis is considered. First, the interaction information in each dimension is defined analogously according to McGill [4] and then applied to Markov chains. The property of interaction information zero deeply relates to a certain class of weakly dependent random variables. For homogeneous, recurrent Markov chains with m states, m ‚â• n ‚â•3, the zero criterion of n-dimensional interaction information is achieved only by (n - 2)-dependent Markov chains, which are generated by some nilpotent matrices. Further for Gaussian Markov chains, it gives the decomposition rule of the variables into mutually correlated subchains. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Takano S."]

Title: A cellular logic array for image processing
Abstract: A cellular logic image processor employing 192 cells in a 16 by 12 hexagonal array is described. The processor has been constructed and its performance assessed. The various classes of functions which can be implemented in the cellular array are discussed and sample programs explained in detail. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Duff M.J.B.", "Watson D.M.", "Fountain T.J.", "Shaw G.K."]

Title: A method for accelerated discrete filtering of speech signals
Source: USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics
Abstract: An algorithm is described for the discrete filtering of speech signals; it consists of successive smoothing of the initial signal and substantially reduces the volume of computations when obtaining the spectrum. It is shown that the filtered signal m is described by a trigonometric polynomial and contains a frequency spectrum 1 m times the initial speech signal spectrum. According to the present discrete filtering algorithm, the speech initial spectrum is represented in the form of non-uniform frequency bands. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Karpov O.N."]

Title: On the optimal observation problems. PMM vol. 37, n‚âó5, 1973, pp. 771-786
Source: Journal of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: We investigate the observation problems for linear systems operating in the presence of noise not accessible to measurement [1 - 3], The formulation to be considered covers in a single form both the minimax game situations as well as certain cases of a probabilistic description of observable systems. The desired optimal observation operation is formed in two ways: either a priori, when one and the same operation is selected for all possible realizations of the signal being observed, or a posteriori, when the operation is formulated on the basis of the value realized of this signal. The difference of the two observation methods mentioned are compared and discussed. In particular, the classes of functional constraints on the unknown noise and the class of optimal observation operations when the optimal unimprovable result is achieved, are indicated. The relation of the class of operations indicated with the set of linear observation operations is examined. The paper is closely related to the investigations in [4-7]. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Kats I.Ia.", "Kurzhanskii A.B."]

Title: MAN-MACHINE PHOTOGRAMMETRIC SYSTEMS AND SYSTEM COMPONENTS.
Abstract: Under the influence of ideas from control and communication theory, new trends have developed in the design of photogrammetric data-processing systems. In this paper a number of concepts applied to the design of such systems are discussed, with emphasis on the digital man-machine systems and system components. The main characteristics of contemporary photogrammetric systems are outlined in regard to both their hardware and software, including some remarks on automation and orthophoto-techniques. The general descriptions are supported by examples from two systems: one predominantly digital and the other predominantly analog. These examples concern the instrumental developments in the Photogrammetric Research laboratories of the National Research Council of Canada.
Name: ["Jaksic Z."]

Title: A variance algorithm for constrained minimization with linear constraints
Source: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: This paper presents a quadratically convergent, rank one, variance algorithm for constrained minimization with linear constraints. The algorithm does not require a linear search for a local minimum in every iteration. Linear searches are made only when needed for stability and convergence. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Chattopadhyay R."]

Title: A stable fixed lag smoothing algorithm
Abstract: The paper presents a new dynamic fixed-lag smoothing algorithm that is uniformly asymptotically stable under the same conditions which guarantee uniform asymptotic stability of the Kalman filter for the given system. It is shown that the smoothing algorithm obtained through a state augmentation approach can be manipulated along with the well known filtering algorithm to derive the proposed smoothing algorithm. Besides stability, the computational requirements of the new algorithm are also discussed in detail and compared with those of the other stable fixed-lag smoothers. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Biswas K.K.", "Mahalanabis A.K."]

Title: Real time recursive prediction of river flows
Abstract: A method is presented for predicting flows in a river. A stochastic model with a set of undetermined parameters is postulated, and these parameters are estimated in real time using the available flow data, and the model is used for prediction. The predictor is recursive and yields the predicted values of flows at a future time instant based upon all presently available information. In addition, a method is given for comparing optimal predictors obtained from different stochastic models. We use the prediction schemes to obtain one-day-ahead forecasts of the Wabash River in the U.S.A. by using the daily riverflow data, paying particular attention to the choice of the order of the stochastic difference equation. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Kashyap R.L.", "Rao A.R."]

Title: POLYNOMIAL ESTIMATORS FOR SYSTEMS WITH POLYNOMIAL NONLINEARITIES.
Abstract: An estimation problem is considered in which the system and observation equations have only polynomial nonlinearities, and the form of the estimator is constrained to be a linear combination of finite polynomials of the observation. The optimal estimator, in the form of a set of weighting functions, is obtained by application of the orthogonality principle to an expanded observation space. The concept of an expanded covariance is introduced, and a sequential version of the estimator is generated by partitioning the estimator into a predictor and corrector. A set of residuals is defined and the estimation problem reduced to the sequential updating of the residual weighting vectors. The concepts are illustrated with special cases and an example.
Name: ["Masenten W.K.", "Stubberud A.R."]

Title: Comment on an algorithm that generates fuzzy prime implicants by Lee and Chang
Abstract: This correspondence points out the insufficiency of the algorithm to generate the set of all fuzzy prime implicants of a fuzzy formula as presented in Lee and Chang (1971). Two theorems, which are the basis of a new technique that generates the complete set of fuzzy implicants, and used for the minimization of fuzzy functions, as presented in Kandel (1972), are discussed. ¬© 1973 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Kandel A."]
Affiliations: [' New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology']

Title: On recognition algorithms which are caution-threshold-extremal
Source: USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics
Abstract: THE problem of the best choice of recognition algorithm is discussed; the choice is based on the computation of estimates, starting from a generalized error functional. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Dadashev T.M."]

Title: A state variable approach to digital image processing
Abstract: Digital filtering of images is considered. A recursive filter design for two-dimensional separable filters is discussed which is based on state variable methods. Advantages of this design are guaranteed stability, and shorter word length than filters designed by bilinear mapping techniques, greater computational efficiency and easier design as compared with nonrecursive filters. Results are shown for filtering high frequency additive noise from a low spatial frequency image and for filtering a low frequency multiplicative noise from a high spatial frequency image. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Zimmermann F.S.", "Gupta S.C."]

Title: Automata for direct radix conversion
Abstract: Modular logic circuits are described that directly transform on a digit by digit basis a number from one radix to another. Each device-an automaton-is of combined Moore-Mealy design of which the Moore output is a coefficient in the transformed radix, and the Mealy output is an untransformed residue passed on to the next identically designed circuit. Each logic circuit is completely independent of word length, and transformation relative to the input string is exact at each instant of time with all transformed digits simultaneously available. For fractional number conversion, any specified accuracy can be obtained merely by the addition of more modular logic circuits to the chain. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Lanning W.C."]

Title: STRUCTURE DETERMINATION AND PARAMETER IDENTIFICATION FOR MULTIVARIABLE STOCHASTIC LINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The problem of using output data to identify a constant, multivariable, stochastic linear system which has unknown dimension, system matrices, and noise covariances is considered. A general stochastic model is not identifiable since the output data determine an equivalence class of systems, all of which have steady-state Kalman filters with the same impulse response and innovations covariance. If the system matrices of the Kalman filter are chosen in a certain unique canonical form, it is possible to obtain consistent estimates of the Kalman filter parameters. A procedure is given for consistently estimating these parameters. The method is non-iterative, in that the system order is estimated directly from the data. Once the order is estimated, the transition matrix and observation matrix are found, and then the gain matrix and noise covariance are estimated with an exponentially convergent algorithm. This latter algorithm also solves the adaptive filtering problem.
Name: ["Tse Edison", "Weinert Howard L."]

Title: An algorithm for approximation of functions
Source: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: This paper considers a problem of approximation of functions proposed by Bellman [1]. The results include a representation lemma for the solutions and an algorithm for computing such solutions. A sufficient condition for the convergence of the algorithm to the optimal solutions is shown to be related to the uniqueness of solutions of a pair of functional equations. To the author's knowledge, not much is known about these functional equations and these may prove to be of interest in future research. An example is included to illustrate the algorithm. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Chattopadhyay R."]

Title: A parallel processing solution to the adaptive Kalman filtering problem with vector measurements
Abstract: The adaptive Kalman filtering problem with vector measurements is considered. A computational algorithm is derived which gives estimates of the state of a linear dynamic system driven by additive white Gaussian noise with unknown covariance Q and observed by a linear function of the state contaminated by additive white Gaussian noise with unknown covariance R. The computational algorithm is inherently parallel in nature and it is noted that the algorithm should be implemented in a special purpose parallel processing digital computer made up of a number of filters similar to steady state Kalman filters each with a different gain. It is shown that the estimates of the state and the estimates of the unknown covariances Q and R can be made arbitrarily close to the optimal nonlinear Bayesian estimates by an appropriate choice for the number of parallel paths in the computer. When the filtering algorithm is implemented in a parallel processing computer the total processing time for state estimation in the unknown noise environment is only slightly increased over that required for a steady state Kalman filter. A numerical example with a five dimensional state and two dimensional measurement vector is presented. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Alspach D.L."]

Title: Fixed-lag demodulation of discrete noisy measurements of FM signals
Abstract: This paper considers an application of some recent results of fixed-lag smoothing algorithms to the demodulation of discrete noisy measurements of FM signals. The problem is attacked by first modelling the communications system in terms of a finite dimensional nonlinear stochastic system and relating the resulting model to an estimation problem for which approximate solutions can be obtained. Performance results are presented, using the modified truncated second order filtering algorithm. The results illustrate that if delay is allowed in arriving at an "on-line" optimum estimate, significant improvement can be obtained by even a very moderate fixed-lag. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Tam P.K.S.", "Tam D.K.S.", "Moore J.B."]

Title: An information retrieval system using keyword dialog
Abstract: This paper describes an approach to information retrieval through keyword dialog. The problems of using English for information retrieval are delineated. The querying capability of an existing system using the keyword dialog is illustrated with actual computer output. Some of the major advantages of this approach are: it reduces ambiguities in requests; it allows the user to think in smaller functional units; it allows the user to edit previous requests. The high usage during a 6-month trial demonstrated that this approach is a viable alternative to using uncontrolled English. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Chai D.T."]

Title: AMS: A SOFTWARE MONITOR FOR PERFORMANCE EVALUATION AND SYSTEM CONTROL.
Abstract: The first part of this paper describes AMS, a software monitor that is activated by both timing information and system events. The structure of the monitor is described and typical results are displayed. The last half of the paper examines the potential use of this type of monitor as an integral part of a dynamic control algorithm. A simulation model serves as an experimental vehicle to quantitatively evaluate some of the potential improvements which are possible when system performance data is used in a dynamic control algorithm.
Name: ["Bauer Madeline J.", "McCredie John W."]

Title: The likelihood function of additive learning models: Sufficient conditions for strict log-concavity and uniqueness of maximum
Abstract: Luce introduced a family of learning models in which response probabilities are a function of some underlying continuous real variable. This variable can be represented as an additive function of the parameters of these learning models. Additive learning models have also been applied to signal-detection data. There are a wide variety of problems of contemporary psychophysics for which the assumption of a continuum of sensory states seems appropriate, and this family of learning models has a natural extension to such problems. One potential difficulty in the application of such models to data is that estimation of parameters requires the use of numerical procedures when the method of maximum likelihood is used. Given a likelihood function generated from an additive model, this paper gives sufficient conditions for log-concavity and strict log-concavity of the likelihood function. If a likelihood function is strictly log-concave, then any local maximum is a unique global maximum, and any solution to the likelihood equations is the unique global maximum point. These conditions are quite easy to evaluate in particular cases, and hence, the results should be quite useful. Some applications to Luce's beta model and to the signal-detection learning models of Dorfman and Biderman are presented. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Dorfman D.D."]

Title: OPTIMIZATION OF DESIGN PARAMETERS IN A VIRTUAL MEMORY SYSTEM.
Abstract: Performance of a virtual memory computer system operating in multiprogramming environment, critically depends upon the optimal sizing of the various levels in the memory hierarchy as well as on optimally controlling the level of multiprogramming. The main input to the system is the program behavior of the typical programs to be run on the machine. The program behavior of a program is adequately represented by the relationship between E denoting the average uninterrupted processor execution time and S, denoting the main memory space alloted to the program. An S-shaped curve typically characterizes this relationship. A queueing model representing the input/output (I/O) activity as a function of the size of the main memory is developed for a memory system with two memory levels. It is assumed that I/O requests generated at the central processing unit (C. P. U. ) are uniformly distributed among the auxiliary memory units. A closed solution for the C. P. U. idle time is obtained and the effect of main memory size, the level of multiprogramming and the number of auxiliary memory modules, on the C. P. U. idle time is studied.
Name: ["Arora Sant R.", "Kachhal Swatantra K."]

Title: KALMAN FILTERING WITH NO A-PRIORI INFORMATION ABOUT NOISE: WHITE NOISE CASE.
Abstract: The scope of Kalman Filtering in presence of white noises of unknown statistics is extended by establishing a kind of separation theorem which allows one to solve the overall problem of identifying the noise statistics in two steps: (1) identify noise covariances or optimal predictor gain G, and (2) identify noise means, in that order. Of course, implementation of the Kalman Filter is the final step. Step 1 has been solved by extending Mehra's approach to correlated process and measurement noises. In step 2, two new algorithms are proposed for identifying the noise means required before Kalman Filtering. These algorithms use the results of Part I of this paper. To be compatible with the algorithms of Part I, the algorithms are also nonrecursive. They are based on the maximum-likelihood approach. The cost function resulting from this approach is considerably simplified before deriving the algorithms, which affords a great insight into the problem at hand. Uniqueness of bias estimates is considered in the light of the invertibility of dynamic systems. An example partially illustrates the algorithms. A significant advantage of this approach is the ability of suboptimally identifying the noise means even when the noise intensities cannot be uniquely determined.
Name: ["Godbole S.S."]

Title: COMPUTER MODELS FOR AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL SYSTEM SIMULATION.
Abstract: A functional error analysis and modeling study of the air traffic control (ATC) system is described. The dominant functional error sources in the ATC system are identified and computer simulation models are developed which will be utilized for the evaluation of advanced ATC system concepts. The models are constructed to be as realistic as possible without placing excessive computational requirements on their implementation. The models are developed in four categories: aircraft dynamics, air data system, navigation systems and surveillance systems. The performance of most of the models has been numerically verified by digital computer simulation.
Name: ["Hoffman William C.", "Hollister Walter M.", "Simpson Robert W."]

Title: A new approach to feature selection based on the Karhunen-Loeve expansion
Abstract: After surveying existing feature selection procedures based upon the Karhunen-Loeve (K-L) expansion, the paper describes a new K-L technique that overcomes some of the limitations of the earlier procedures. The new method takes into account information on both the class variances and means, but lays particular emphasis on the classification potential of the latter. The results of a series of experiments concerned with the classification of real vector-electrocardiogram and artificially generated data demonstrate the advantages of the new method. They suggest that it is particularly useful for pattern recognition when combined with classification procedures based upon discriminant functions obtained by recursive least squares analysis. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Kittler J.", "Young P.C."]
Keywords: ["covariance matrix", "discriminant function", "feature selection", "karhunen-loeve expansion", "least squares fit"]

Title: An Algorithm for the Optimal Solution of Linear Inequalities and Its Application to Pattern Recognition
Abstract: An algorithm for the optimal solution of consistent and inconsistent linear inequalities is presented, where the optimality criterion is the maximization of the number of satisfied constraints. The algorithm is developed as a nonenumerative search procedure based on two new theorems established in this paper. It is shown that the number of iterative steps before termination is strictly less than that required by an exhaustive search. Experimental results with various types of data establish the computational tractability of the procedure under nontrivial conditions. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Warmack R.E.", "Gonzalez R.C."]
Affiliations: [' University of Tennessee', ' University of Tennessee']

Title: GLOSS: A HIGH LEVEL MACHINE.
Abstract: The GLOSS machine consists of an unlimited number of processors each of which is either active or dormant. Every active processor is either bound to some state or is performing a state transition. A state, like an integer or a character string, is treated as a data object. Thus state transition operators are not considered black boxes as they would be in a functional definition of programming languages. The architecture of the GLOSS machine allows complex control and environment operations to be done in a simple and transparent way. As a result a programming language is easy to implement on the GLOSS machine, and the GLOSS machine gives a reasonably lucid definition of the complex control and environment operations of programming languages.
Name: ["Herriot Robert G."]

Title: HIERARCHICAL MACHINE MODEL FOR THE SEMANTICS OF PROGRAMMING LANGUAGES.
Abstract: This paper presents a method for modeling programming languages by supplying a hierarchical, structured framework for defining program and data structures. A particular language, or class of languages, may be defined relative to a particular graph structure, or set of graph structures, that best describes the actual structures of the language. Each graph structure has associated with it a set of construction and accessing primitives, thus defining the basic machine upon which the semantic functions are defined. The semantic functions defined the language by describing the effect of execution of the various components of the language upon the basic machine. This is done by first defining a control mechanism via set of control functions, and then defining a set of component functions that describe execution of the language components relative to that control mechanism.
Name: ["Basili Victor R.", "Turner Albert J."]

Title: ON STABILITY OF A FIXED-LAG SMOOTHER IN CONTINUOUS-TIME SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The stability of a fixed-lag smoother is investigated in continuous-time linear systems. The fixed-lag smoother is shown to be asymptotically stable if the corresponding optimal linear filter is asymptotically stable. Numerical difficulties appearing often in the realization of the smoothing can be attributed to the behavior of the adjoint system associated with the filter. Two methods are presented to circumvent the numerical difficulties in the operation of the fixed-lag smoother.
Name: ["Koivo A.J.", "Repperger D.W."]

Title: Mosaic patterns of neuronal probabilistic ensembles and brain functioning
Abstract: An attempt is made in this paper to find mosaic distribution patterns of neuron ensembles in cortical structures that can reflect changes in the functional state of the brain cortex and different types of specific activity. An indirect statistical method of defining ensemble distribution patterns in different functional states of the brain is used, and the whole pattern of neuronal responses is constructed by means of a computer. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Kogan A.B."]

Title: A Continuous Two-Dimensional Model of Threshold Learning
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: We present a model of threshold learning that represents discrete one-dimensional learning processes by a continuous two-dimensional learning process. The model gives us an overall view of the learning dynamics of an expanded range of training procedures, and provides insight into the training of multidimensional linear pattern classifiers. In our model the expected performance is measured by learning curves, and the confidence in this expected performance is measured by variance curves. Previous work on the continuous approximation has been restricted to one-dimensional learning processes. The theory developed here promises to lead to improved training procedures and improved rules for determining when to stop training. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Sklansky J.", "Merryman P.M."]

Title: Digital approximation of continuous-data control systems by point-by-point state comparison
Abstract: This paper presents a point-by-point state comparison method of approximating a continuous-data system by a sampled-data system. The problem is to attempt the matching of the states of the two systems at the sampling instants. A partial matching has to be conducted if the systems have more states than controls. A weighting matrix is used to regulate the partial matching and weights placed on each state. The digital approximation is affected by use of forward gain E(T) and feedback gain G(T) in the sampled-data system. It is shown that, in general, these gains can be approximated by truncated Taylor series expansions. An illustrative example is given using the one-axis dynamics of the Skylab satellite. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Kuo B.C.", "Singh G.", "Yackel R."]

Title: Conversion of programs between computers: Interpreters, simulators and compilers
Source: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: The concepts of interpretive simulation of one machine by another and of direct translation of computer programs are examined. Definitions are suggested for these processes, in terms of relationships between abstract machines. Given that one object machine can simulate, in an interpretive sense, another source machine, we seek to define the conditions under which the object machine can have a program which is a direct translation of the one in the source machine. It is shown that under the suggested definitions this is generally the case, even though the direct translation may be no more efficient than the interpretive simulation. ¬© 1973 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Nudds D."]

Title: A Multiprogramming Queue
Abstract: A simple computer system is described, which consists of a CPU and I/O unit and which works in a multiprogramming manner. The model assumes that the system works under heavy load so that the incoming queue is never empty, that the service times at the two units are exponentially distributed independent random variables, and that the number of iterations of the programs is geometrically distributed. Head of the line priority of programs which are being processed over newcomers is considered. Steady state distribution of the states of the system is numerically solved under the assumption of a finite waiting room. The suggested system is compared with one working in ‚Äúbatch mode‚Äù and with an equivalent multiprogramming system with a constant number of programs. The latter comparison shows that the suggested priority rule improves the expected response time without affecting the throughput and the utilizations of the CPU and the I/O unit. The model induces an interesting dependence phenomenon which is discussed at length. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Adiri I.", "Hofri M.", "Yadin M."]
Affiliations: ['IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center', 'Teehnion‚ÄîIsrael Institute of Technology']

Title: INTEGRATED PLANT AND CONTROL SYSTEM DESIGN FOR THE OPERATION OF A MINE AT MINIMUM COST.
Abstract: A dynamic programming technique is applied to the optimization of the control strategy and plant rating for a coal mine. A linear model of the mine is developed which includes the random coal-winning process, conveyor transportation times, the winding shaft, bunkers and the thermal loading of the coal cutting machines. A quadratic cost model is developed whose coefficients are related directly to basic engineering and economic parameters. The resulting control system is shown to demand centralized d. d. c. to effect essential time-delay and drift-free integration functions. The simulation system performance is shown to be highly satisfactory, but calls for surface storage which considerably exceeds that employed in current U. K. practice.
Name: ["Edwards J.B.", "Marshall S.A."]

Title: Two entropies of a generalized sorting problem
Source: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: In this paper we introduce a class of generalized sorting (ordering) problems called "classifications." To each "classification," we associate two quantities: informational entropy (average information quantity) and operational entropy (measure of computational complexity, that is, number of comparisons necessary to "classify" a given sequence of items). The relationship between these quantities is discussed. For a certain classification involving n items, its operational entropy is shown to be approximately n¬∑log<sub>2</sub>n although its informational entropy is constantly equal to 1, independent of the number of items n. ¬© 1973 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Nozaki A."]

Title: THEORY FORMATION BY MACHINE - A GENERAL FRAMEWORK OF THE GOLEM SYSTEM.
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to give a unifying framework to some constructive methodological models of Scientific research, in order to obtain a computer system which would allow not only to test different general methodological systems but also practically help to mechanize some aspects of scientific research. The proposed computer system is called the GOLEM-Generator of Observational Laws from Experiments and Models.
Name: ["Glanc Alois"]

Title: PREFILTERING VERSION OF THE KALMAN FILTER WITH NEW NUMERICAL INTEGRATION FORMULAS FOR RICCATI EQUATIONS.
Abstract: A prefiltering version of the Kalman filter is derived for both discrete and continuous measurements. The derivation consists of determining a single discrete measurement that is equivalent to either a time segment of continuous measurements or a set of discrete measurements. This prefiltering version of the Kalman filter easily handles numerical problems associated with rapid transients and ill-conditioned Riccati matrices. Therefore, the derived technique for extrapolating the Riccati matrix from one time to the next constitutes a new set of integration formulas which alleviate ill-conditioning problems associated with continuous Riccati equations. The prefilter extends Potter's square root filtering, with all its advantages, to continuous measurement problems. It is claimed that prior to this work, no technique existed for numerically integrating the general ill-conditioned, time-varying and continuous Riccati equation.
Name: ["Womble M.E.", "Potter J.E."]

Title: OPTIMAL OPEN-LOOP FEEDBACK CONTROL FOR LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH UNKNOWN PARAMETERS.
Abstract: The problem of controlling a class of linear systems with unknown parameters is considered. The optimal open-loop strategies are obtained for linear systems with unknown parameters in the system matrix with a quadratic performance index. The method of solution is based upon the use of the Hamilton-Jacobi theory. The results may be useful in applications whereby high accuracy is required but there is uncertainty as to certain gains and time constants. The application of control for precision pointing and tracking is a viable area for applying the results. The required control gain is found by the solution of a matrix partial differential equation which is a function of the measurement function. The form of the equation changes as the measurement function changes.
Name: ["Asher R.B.", "Sims C.S.", "Sebesta H.R."]

Title: DESIGN OF TREE NETWORKS FOR DISTRIBUTED DATA.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: The problem of locating information resources and choosing a topology for a network of distributed data files has been formulated in a model that, while simple, retains important practical features such as discrete capacity assignment, economy of scale, and distinction between query and update transactions. Even for a simplified model it appears that heuristic approaches to design are required, and a sample algorithm has been formulated and tested for the special case of tree design.
Name: ["Casey R.G."]

Title: ON THE INVESTIGATION OF ALTERNATIVE REGRESSIONS BY PRINCIPAL COMPONENT ANALYSIS.
Abstract: In a multiple regression problem, let the px1 vector x consist of the dependent variable and p-1 predictor variables. The correlation matrix of x is reduced to principal components. The components corresponding to low eigenvalues may be useful in suggesting possible alternative subregressions. This possibility is analyzed, and formulas derived for the derivation of subregressions from the principal components.
Name: ["Hawkins Douglas M."]

Title: DESIGN OF A WAVEFORM PARSING SYSTEM.
Abstract: A syntax-directed approach is proposed for the extraction of pattern features from one-dimensional spatial or temporal series of events. The approach is offered as a synthesis of formal and ad hoc methods. Existing techniques in the parsing of formal languages are shown to apply to the problem of analyzing series which exhibit certain structure. An example is given detailing this approach as applied to the recognition of carotid pulse waves.
Name: ["Stockman George C.", "Kanal Laveen N.", "Kyle M.C."]

Title: Method for Optimal Estimation of Space-Time Physical Processes - 1. | METODA OPTYMALNEJ ESTYMACJI PRZESTRZENNO-CZASOWYCH PROCESOW FIZYCZNYCH - 1.
Abstract: The problem of optimal estimation of space-time processes is stated and analysed on the grounds of the deterministic dynamic and observation model of such phenomena, use being made of an estimation quality index, which is proposed. The mathematical model of dynamics and observation of processes, characterized by a region which is constant in time, is discussed in its general form. the general problem of optimal estimation of the function of state is formulated for such a process, proposing as an estimation quality index a certain functional, constituting a measure of agreement between the mathematical model and the real process. The problem thus formulated is transformed into a general problem of dynamic optimization, the conditions and problems of accurate and approximate solution being discussed in brief.
Name: ["Maslowski Andrzej"]

Title: ALGORITHM AND HARDWARE FOR SEARCHING ON A KEY IN A CONTENT ADDRESSABLE MEMORY.
Abstract: It is desirable to be able to search the data word on a key field made up of a plurality of key bits. The purpose of this algorithm is to perform that search such that the address of the first data word having the key field will be found and the address of that data word presented.
Name: ["Ouchi N.K."]

Title: COORDINATED ADAPTIVE FILTERS FOR MOTION SIMULATORS.
Abstract: A new approach to providing motion drive signals to a flight simulator utilizing coordinated adaptive filters is presented. Some motivation for the use of coordinated washout is discussed, along with conditions that determine the burden of coordination. The coordinated adaptive filters are derived, based on continuous steepest descent, and the application of the filters to simulated flight data is demonstrated.
Name: ["Parrish Russell V.", "Dieudonne James E.", "Martin Dennis J.", "Bowles Roland L."]

Title: N-STEP, 2-VARIABLE SEARCH ALGORITHM FOR THE COMPONENT PLACEMENT PROBLEM.
Abstract: This paper deals with the methodology of component placement and is based on the results of considerable operational experience. A tutorial presentation of tree search placement algorithms is provided, and an improved placement procedure is described which is demonstrated to be effective in generating near optimal solutions to the component placement problem. These solutions are completely reproducible and are obtained at an acceptable expenditure of computational resources. An additional objective is an assessment of performance of the class of near optimal algorithms. In particular, the question - how close to optimal are the near optimal solutions - is examined.
Name: ["Heider Charles H."]

Title: DESIGN OF DIGITAL ALGORITHMS FOR PROCESS CONTROL.
Abstract: A procedure for analytically deriving direct digital control parameters for digital process control is presented. The performance index chosen for the design is based upon achieving minimum settling time control. The state transition technique is employed. The procedure determines the DDC parameters from a knowledge of the process as indicated by the process reaction curve. It is totally computer programmable. The final digital algorithm in the form of the velocity algorithm, or a related second order transfer function. Applications to control of processes without and with dead-time are shown.
Name: ["Martens H.R.", "Jaliwalla S.A."]

Title: LOW COMPLEXITY FINITE MEMORY DECISION RULES.
Abstract: By examining a particular hypothesis testing problem under a finite memory constraint, general guidelines are derived for the design of asymptotically optimal, low complexity, finite memory decision rules. Asymptotically optimal here means that only a fixed number of bits need be added to memory to achieve the optimal error probability. Thus the fraction of bits ‚Ä≥lost‚Ä≥ by these low complexity rules tends to zero as memory size becomes large. The rules developed are similar to quantized sequential probability ratio tests.
Name: ["Hellman M.E."]

Title: PARAMETER ESTIMATION OF ARMA MODELS USING A COMPUTATIONALLY EFFICIENT MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD TECHNIQUE.
Abstract: A method is presented for estimating the parameters of a fixed order autoregressive moving average model, based on maximization of an appropriate likelihood function. The resulting static optimization is accomplished with a modified Newton numerical algorithm. Under suitable initial conditions for the model, the gradient and Hessian matrices of each iteration can be computed analytically. Because of the highly nonlinear character of the likelihood function, starting values of the algorithm are important. Extensions of the method to more complicated models are described. Some numerical examples illustrate the properties of the method.
Name: ["Sarris A.H.", "Eisner M."]

Title: State assignment for realizing modular input-free sequential logical networks without invertors
Source: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: Appearance of integrated circuits has made of great importance a problem of working out a technique of synthesis which make it possible to form the resulting logic network from identical integrated units involving a minimum number of external links. The proposed assignment made for input-free sequential logical networks has the following features.o(1)The whole sequential logical network consists of n subnetworks, exciting each of n memory elements and having identical internal structure. Besides for any two input binary sets which set i-th and j-th memory elements, respectively, such a shift on s positions exists (s‚â•1) where i-th input set coincides with j-th input set.(2)i-th memory element logical network (i=1,...n) is identified as two-level logic specified by the following parameters <Œ≥<sub>1</sub>, Œ≥<sub>2</sub>, Œ≥<sub>3</sub>>, where Œ≥<sub>1</sub> is a number of gates in the first level Œ≥<sub>2</sub> is a number of inputs for each gate Œ≥<sub>3</sub> is complete number of input variables(3)The i-th logical network (i=1,...n) does not contain any invertors. ¬© 1973 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Kartashev S.P."]

Title: ON THE SOLUTION OF A MINIMAX TERMINAL STATE ESTIMATION PROBLEM - A HILBERT SPACE APPROACH.
Abstract: The solution to a continuous-time LQG (Linear-Quadratic-Gaussian) minimax terminal state estimation problem is obtained using a Hilbert space approach. Minimax state estimation problems can be regarded as two person zero sum differential games with imperfect state information. The motivation for the terminal state estimation problem considered here is provided by a radar data processing problem. The latter problem is associated with tracking an uncooperative target which is under the control of an intelligent adversary. The only information available to the tracker is the dynamics of the target, the statistical description of the initial state of the target, and the statistics of the additive observation noise corrupting the radar data. The minimax decision rule is determined via the method of least favorable prior distributions. The minimax estimator is shown to be a linear functional of the observed data, and the least favorable prior distribution is shown to be a degenerate Gaussian stochastic process.
Name: ["Hexner G.", "Mintz M."]

Title: GLOBAL-LOCAL APPROACH TO CLUSTER ANALYSIS.
Abstract: A global to local philosophy is presented as a methodology for cluster analysis. The global algorithm is presented as an estimator of initial cluster centers, while the local algorithm is presented as a refinement procedure of the global algorithm's estimate. Global-local techniques are discussed and experimental results are presented.
Name: ["Northouse R.A.", "Fromm F.R.", "Eigen D.J."]

Title: NONLINEAR FREQUENCY DOMAIN TECHNIQUES FOR SMOOTHING AND ENHANCEMENT OF RADIONUCLIDE IMAGES.
Source: Soc of Photo-opt Instrum Eng, Semin Proc
Abstract: Several approaches to image processing are discussed which overcome some particular difficulties associated with digital processing and display of clinical radionuclide images. Several nonlinear techniques which extend the usefulness of linear digital filters are discussed. In particular, nonlinear techniques are developed for processing radionuclide scans which produce significantly fewer artifacts (or false-positive lesions) than are encountered using previous linear techniques. The results of applying these methodologies to a variety of phantom data and patient images are shown.
Name: ["Kirch Dennis L.", "Brown Donald W.", "Trow Richard S."]

Title: MULTI-DIMENSION AUTOMATIC CONTROL SYSTEMS OPTIMIZE MACHINING RATES.
Abstract: The problem of optimizing machining parameters on the basis of optimum efficiency criterion with implementation of automatic control systems is discussed. An example is presented for optimization of machining axles in copying lathes with hydraulic control.
Name: ["Solomentsev Yu.M."]

Title: AUTOMATIC GENERATION OF GRAPHS.
Abstract: The generation of nonseparable graphs has been investigated. The main problem in the generating procedure is to avoid producing a number of identical graphs. This has given reason to present some of the known identification methods. No general algorithmic method exists except the permutation method, which is efficient only for small dimensions of graphs (the number of nodes equal 10 or less). The permutation method has been used in the isomorphism test implemented in the generating procedures. Two methods for generating graphs have been presented. The first method called NEWARC starts with a number of graphs and creates new graphs with an increased number of edges. The second method uses NEWARC as a part of the performance as well as another partial generating procedure called NEWNODE. The latter creates one new node and one new edge in a start graph at a time. The generating method is applied on a sufficient set of start graphs consecutively one after another. Sufficiently means the possibility of obtaining all nonseparable graphs of desired dimensions by means of this method. It has been implemented as the computer program GGEN7.
Name: ["Proskurowski Andrzej"]

Title: DESIGN OF OPTIMAL CONTROLLERS FOR DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS USING FINITE DIMENSIONAL STATE OBSERVERS.
Abstract: An observer theory is applied to the distributed parameter control problem for both distributed and boundary control. The procedure is based on an eigenfunction expansion approximation to the state of the controlled plant. The observer is employed to reconstruct the time functions used in the eigenfunction expansion and uses only vector observations taken from measurements of the distributed state at a certain number of prespecified points of the spatial domain. The study has been restricted to a one-dimensional spatial domain in order to keep the dimensionality of the vectors associated with the observer small. A simple example is solved to illustrate the procedure.
Name: ["Stavroulakis P.", "Sarachik P.E."]

Title: DATA COMPARISON OF RECTANGULAR ARRAYS.
Abstract: A development of the eigenvector decomposition of a rectangular array is given from two different, but equivalent points of view. An l-term approximation obtained by means of a heuristic approximation strategy has been shown to be mathematically equivalent to an l-term approximation obtained from a least-squares optimization problem; hence, the l-term eigenvector expansion of matrix P//O obtained herein is optimal in a least-squares sense. It is stated that the eigenvector decomposition of a rectangular array appears to have application to storage of tables of aerodynamic coefficients, digital imagery data compression, and voice print identification. Because of its relation to the method of principlal components, it is also applicable to large scale systems, specifically to the problem of determining low-order models for such systems.
Name: ["Mendel J.M.", "Riley J.D.", "Evans H.W."]

Title: ADAPTIVE CONTROL IN TRANSPORTATION.
Abstract: Recent progress in the implementation of adaptive control systems in transportation is summarized. In transportation applications an adaptive control system combines five basic functions: (1) surveillance, to detect traffic; (2) communications, to relay surveillance data and control signals; (3) performance evaluation, to compare the difference between the desired and current operation; (4) on-line data processing, to determine the control signals and scheduling; and (5) overall system operation, i. e. , the functional summation of (1), (2), (3) and (4). The applications discussed include control of freeway ramps, urban street traffic, air traffic, and urban rapid transit.
Name: ["Darling Jr. E.M.", "Ricci R.C.", "Colella A.M."]

Title: STATE SPACE IMAGE MOTION RESTORATION.
Abstract: A recursive procedure, based on state space techniques, is presented to solve the restoration problem of images degraded by motion in one direction. For motion degraded images that are not noise free a recursive smoothing scheme is developed based on prior knowledge of the second order statistics of the original image in terms of the correlation function of the line scanner and the use of a Kalman-Bucy filter. More general space variant motion can also be treated using the techniques given here the difference being that the corresponding matrices will be time variant.
Name: ["Aboutalib A.O.", "Silverman L.M."]

Title: INFORMATION THEORY AND PRIVACY IN DATA BANKS.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: The problem of providing privacy and security in retrieval systems falls into two rather modern disciplines: information theory and computer science. In this paper the concern is primarily with the former, i. e. , how to relate security of data records in computerized retrieval systems and data banks with Shannon's information-theoretic treatment of secrecy systems for natural language messages in communication systems. In doing so, it is useful to establish first the analogy between retrieval systems and certain communication channels.
Name: ["Reed I.S."]

Title: A forecasting model for mosquito population densities
Abstract: A heuristic model to forecast mosquito densities is constructed from light trap data using an autoregressive integrated moving average process. The model predicts mosquito densities up to 6 days in the future. Using the model a simulation study was performed to examine the influence of several pesticide application strategies on mosquito populations.
Name: ["Hacker C.S.", "Scott D.W.", "Thompson J.R."]

Title: A digital computer nerve model for network simulation
Abstract: A simple mathematical neuron model which is based on commonly accepted approximations and is designed for economical digital computer implementation is described. The model's properties are compared with those of real neurons and other more sophisticated models described in the literature. The simulation of two small networks which have been proposed as fundamental neural structures in the generation of the flight motor control stimuli in some insects using this model is shown to yield results which are superior to those of previously published simulations. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Wood R.A.", "Jones N.B.", "Porter N.H."]

Title: Visual information obtained from flashes and from afterimages
Abstract: A method of calculating the information gain when a grating target is discriminated against a featureless background is developed. This is extended to more general types of structure. The variation of the amount of information available in normal vision, in flashes, and in after-images following flashes has been measured. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Dirchburn R.W.", "Drysdale A.E."]

Title: STOCHASTIC IDENTIFICATION OF NON-LINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A stochastic identification scheme is presented for a class of non-linear systems described by ordinary differential equations. These systems when excited by wideband Gaussian noise generate an output which is near-Markov in nature. Using sampled-data information the Markovian properties of the output can be estimated and then used to compute the various nonlinear functional relationships within the system.
Name: ["Miller W.C.", "Shridhar M."]

Title: STRUCTURE OF A DIRECT HIGH-LEVEL LANGUAGE PROCESSOR.
Abstract: This paper gives a brief description of the structure of a direct high-level language processor (DHLLP) and of how the various elements in the processor function. The DHLLP consists of a language processor which performs the basic interpreting task of the system and four other processors for doing auxiliary tasks. The scanner processor scans the input string. The arithmetic processor performs arithmetic and logical operations. The input/output processor performs the input/output operations, and the memory processor handles the memory access requests. A brief description of the structure of each of these processors is given, as are the solutions to the particular problems inherent in implementing an interpretive system directly in hardware. After each of the processors has been defined, the final section compares the results with the direct execution systems such as the Symbol machine and the Aerospace HOL Computer that uses a preprocessor that converts the source code into a ‚Ä≥more convenient‚Ä≥ internal form.
Name: ["Bloom Howard M."]

Title: INSPECTION OF SHEET MATERIALS: MODEL AND DATA.
Abstract: Results of experiments, conduced as a part of a series of studies, aimed to evaluate the visual inspection of flat glass for faults, are presented. A model combining visual search and decision theory is postulated and tested on the inspection of flat glass for discrete faults. The findings were used to derive model parameters and the model to be used in predicting the performance in the factory situation.
Name: ["Drury Colin G."]

Title: Optimal Observer Techniques for Linear Discrete Time Systems
Abstract: This chapter investigates the idea of using Luenberger's minimal-order observer as an alternate to the Kalman filter for obtaining state estimates in linear discrete-time stochastic systems. One of the major results presented in the chapter is the development of the general solution to the problem of constructing an optimal minimalorder observer for linear discrete-time stochastic systems where optimality is in the mean-square sense. The approach taken in the development which follows leads to a completely unified theory for the design of optimal minimum-order observers and is applicable to both time-varying and timeinvariant linear discrete systems. ¬© 1973, ACADEMIC PRESS, INC.
Name: ["Novak L.M."]

Title: A Square-Root Data Array Solution of the Continuous-Discrete Filtering Problem
Abstract: The Dyer-McReynolds [1] discrete square-root filter-ing algorithm is extended to accommodate continuous dynamics. Differential equations are given to represent the time evolution of the filter data array. These equations are nonlinear, but it is shown that the nonlinearities act to enhance the stability of the solution. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Bierman G.J."]

Title: Analysis of energy demand distribution within anthropomorphic systems
Source: Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement and Control, Transactions of the ASME
Abstract: The paper presents the fundamentals of a synthesis approach to the gait of an anthropomorphic robot. The mathematical algorithms necessary to obtain the drake torques in the powered joints of the exoskeleton anthropomorphic robot are also presented. Driving torques are calculated for some presented gait types. From known got characteristics the dynamics imposed on one part of the system (prescribed synergy) are determined and the corresponding synergies of the complete anthropomorphic ett-skeleton-patient system are calculated. A brief summary of experimentally obtaind energy data gathered by previous investigators is presented and the results of energj analysis for two adopted gait types are discussed. ¬© 1973 by ASME.
Name: ["Vukobratoviƒá M.", "Hristic D.", "Ciric V.", "Zecevic M."]

Title: Use of an inverted file structure for interactive retrieval of computer program abstracts
Abstract: Standard Oil Company of California‚Äôs Program Abstracts System will interactively search for, and list by title and mnemonic, all Company computer programs belonging to a particular category or technical application area in the filed of petroleum exploration and production. If one or more titles are of interest, the user can request a display of those abstracts. Retrieval is by search of an inverted index made up of a fixed set of terms covering application areas, programming languages, processing mode, and machine designations. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Buschman A.C."]

Title: NON-LINEAR ANALYSIS OF A POSITION CONTROL SYSTEM.
Source: J Inst Eng (India), Electron Telecommun Eng Div
Abstract: The stability problem of a simple position control system is studied with particular reference to nonlinear performance. A describing function of the synchro pair is obtained considering the voltages induced in the rotor of the synchro control transformer under oscillating conditions. A stability analysis of the system is then made using the describing function technique.
Name: ["Mukhopadhyay P.", "Venkatesan K."]

Title: Cone-Bounded Nonlinearities and Mean-Square Bounds‚ÄìEstimation Upper Bound
Abstract: This paper is the first in a series of three, the remaining two of which will appear at a later date. Performance bounds are derived in this series of papers for causal state estimation and regulation problems employing mean-square criteria. The systems considered are partially observed finite-dimensional continuous-time stochastic processes driven by additive white Gaussian noise. The particular systems to which the bounds apply are those which, when modeled by Ito differential equations, contain drift (¬∑dt) coefficients which are, to within a uniformly Lipschitz residual, jointly linear in the system state and externally applied control. The bounds derived in the complete series of papers include both upper and lower bounds for causal state estimation and for a quadra tic regulator problem. The upper bounds pertain to the performance of some simple, almost linear designs reminiscent of the designs which are optimal in the linear case. The lower bounds pertain to the optimum performance attainable within a broad class of candidate designs. This paper treats the upper bound for estimation. The second paper presents the estimation lower bound. The estimation performance bounds are independent of the control law, giving a particularly simple form to the control performance bounds which are developed in the third, and final, paper. All the bounds converge with vanishing nonlinearity (vanishing Lipschitz constants) to the known optimum performance for the limiting linear system. Consequently, the bounds are asymptotically tight and the simple designs studied are asymptotically optimal with vanishing nonlinearity. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gilmian A.S.", "Rhodes I.B."]

Title: ADVANCED CONCEPTS IN CONTROL ROOM PLANNING.
Abstract: Nuclear power plant control rooms have been characterized by long operating panels, a multitude of large control switches, numerous large indicators and limited utilization of digital computers. It is reported how a company reevaluated its control room philosophy and, with the assistance of systems suppliers evolved a new one. The result is an ultramodern control room with multiple CPUs dedicated to various plant operating functions and a profusion of crt displays in adaptable formats.
Name: ["Milam W.G.", "Peterman G.J.", "Sulouff M.D."]

Title: ROBOTS HANDLING MORE JOBS ON INDUSTRIAL ASSEMBLY LINES.
Abstract: Increasing numbers of manufacturers throughout the world are building automatic manipulators to handle boring and dangerous factory tasks. Early applications in relieving human operators from dull and even dangerous tasks associated with such things as die casting and forging machines have been expanded to include painting, welding, processing dangerous explosives, handling glass and ceramics, palletizing bricks, and loading and unloading machine tools.
Name: ["Rosenblatt Alfred"]

Title: Automation of the Blast Furnace Process. | [AUTOMACAO DO PROCESSO DO ALTO-FORNO.]
Abstract: The automation of the blast furnace process using an on-line computer is discussed. The automation is based on a model of the process which reflects the furnace behavior and must adapt itself continuously to the real process. Some process models are characterized, with particular emphasis on the AEG process model.
Name: ["Barouning Friedrich"]

Title: Optimization of Personnel Training Systems at Steam Power Plants. | [OPTIMIZATSIYA SISTEMY OBUCHENIYA PERSONALA NA TEPLOVYKH ELEKTRICHESKIKH STANTSIYAKH.]
Abstract: The present system of personnel training at steam power plants in the USSR is criticized and a mathematical model for an optimal training sytem is constructed. Automation of the teaching process to develop individual training is considered. An algorithm of the training system is optimized. Six variants of a teaching program are tested. It is found that the quickest results of the training system are obtained when 80% of the total volume of information is absorbed by the student. It is concluded that modeling of a training system makes it possible to discover quantitative indices characterizing the work of such systems and on their basis to work out the technical task for a teaching machine.
Name: ["Barykova N.G.", "Klushin Yu.A.", "Chistyakov S.F."]

Title: SOME REMARKS ON THE CLASSIFICATION OF LIMIT CYCLES IN DIGITAL FILTERS.
Abstract: Classification schemes for limit cycles in digital filters are considered. In particular, the scheme based on symmetry considerations is completed. A classification scheme based on the concept of the accessibility of limit cycles is introduced. With this scheme, several problems concerning limit cycles are solved, among which a lower bound on the maximum amplitude of limit cycles in second-order filters with two rounding nonlinearities is given.
Name: ["Claasen T.A.C.M.", "Mecklenbraeuker W.F.G.", "Peek J.B.H."]

Title: EXAMPLE OF FUNCTION OPTIMIZATION VIA HYBRID COMPUTATION.
Abstract: Iterative techniques for function optimization have been considered extensively for use in all-digital computation. Relatively little has been done to take advantage of the much higher integration speed of hybrid computation systems. This paper demonstrates application of one simple procedure in a hybrid environment and compares the results to those obtained by an efficient digital procedure. Even though a much more efficient procedure is used on the digital, time-saving factors between 8 and 2 are obtained via the simpler hybrid implementation.
Name: ["Volz Richard A."]

Title: Multiform Partial Symmetry and Linearity
Abstract: It is known from a paper by Das that multiform total symmetry is equivalent to linearity. In this correspondence the results of Das are generalized and a simple proof is given to show that even for multiform partial symmetries the corresponding subfunctions are linear subfunctions. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Khabra N.S."]
Affiliations: [' University of Ottawa', ' University of Calcutta']

Title: Cancellations in Multivariable Continuous-Time and Discrete-Time Feedback Systems Treated by Greatest Common Divisor Extraction
Abstract: This correspondence considers a multivariable system with proper rational matrix transfer functions G<sub>o</sub> and G<sub>f</sub> in the forward and feedback branches, respectively. It develops a strictly algebraic procedure to obtain polynomials whose zeros are the poles of the matrix transfer functions from input to output (H<sub>y</sub>), and from input to error (H<sub>e</sub>). G<sub>o</sub> and G<sub>f</sub> are given in the polynomial matrix factored form N<sub>0</sub>D<sub>0</sub><sup>-1</sup> and D<sub>f</sub><sup>-1</sup>N<sub>f</sub>. The role of the assumption det [I + G<sub>f</sub>(‚àû)G<sub>0</sub>(00)] ‚â• 0 and the relation between the zeros of det [I + G<sub>f</sub>G<sub>0</sub>] and the poles of Hy and He are indicated. The implications for stability analysis of continuous-time as well as discrete-time systems are stressed. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Desoer C.A.", "Schulman J.D."]

Title: A Search Memory for Many-to-Many Comparisons
Abstract: This paper describes a unique associative memory mechanism in which a data base may be simultaneously searched by comparison with a substantial number of key words, or ‚Äúcomparands,‚Äù as contrasted with the usual one-comparand-at-a-time limitation. Possible search criteria include the six arithmetic relations, plus certain logical ‚Äúbit-set‚Äù relations. At some cost in both hardware and speed, each of the comparands may be provided with an associated mask field and/ or search specification. Optionally, the set of comparands may be included within the set of data items, thus allowing cross among thecomparands. all cases, the comparisons location and length the comparison field may be freely programmed withinthe available word size, and a master mask may be provided, without time penalty. Algorithms for one-comparand searches and ‚Äúmemory arithmetic‚Äù operations can also be implemented with little additional hardware. The mechanism is bit-serial, word parallel, so that search time is proportional to the number of bits actively compared, but independent of the number of comparands or data items. At each bit position to be compared, the set of data/comparand pairs is partitioned into four cases, corresponding to the four possible combinations of bit values. Each case is processed separately, one after another, but with all similar items being processed in parallel for each case. Each of the different comparison criteria defines a function, which in turn specifies how to modify the search results at each step.
