A table of function definitions is provided, listing most useful searches. The effective minimum number of comparands is measured by the number of single-comparand searches that could be completed in the time required for a many-to-many search. The maximum limit is purely a practical hardware and software consideration. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Digby D.W."]

Title: Application of the Optimal Control Model for the Human Operator to Reliability Assessment
Abstract: A model for the human controller in continuous manual control tasks is described. The model is based on modern control and human response theories. Techniques for predicting closed-loop system performance and relative workload for the task are presented. The implications for reliability assessment in corresponding man-machine problems are discussed. Finally, an example that involves prediction of pilot performance and workload, and their relation to mission success, for a STOL landing-approach is given. ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers. Inc.
Name: ["Baron S."]

Title: EVALUATION OF THE MATRIX EXPONENTIAL e<sup>hV</sup>.
Source: NTZ Nachr Z NTZ Commun J
Abstract: The matrix exponential e**h**V which is important for system analysis in state space is approximated by the Taylor power series of the ‚Ä≥mxm‚Ä≥ Frobenius type matrix V, truncated to the degree ‚Ä≥n‚Ä≥ . The polynomial is then evaluated with a very efficient algorithm which uses only ‚Ä≥m. n‚Ä≥ arithmetic operations.
Name: ["Wehrhahn Erich A."]

Title: SPEECH SCRAMBLING AND SYNCHRONIZATION.
Abstract: The pseudorandom code time-division speech scrambler is described. It provides moderate security for speech transmitted on analog in-band channels. The scrambler is synchronized by a crystal oscillator and a message-start signal. Work on cryptanalysis, subjective testing, computer simulation and a new pseudonoise transform is included.
Name: ["French Richard Charles"]

Title: Prediction of Human Operator Performance
Abstract: The Kalman Filter technique is applied to the problem of predicting human operator performance in the execution of a wide variety of tasks described by an exponential improvement model. Reliable predictions can be used as a guide by management on the efficiency of task design, operator selection, and operator training functions. Results of industrial case studies involving mechanical and electrical assemblies show that realistic predictions can be made even when the model parameters are nonstationary. Steady-state detection is also included in the paper to permit the isolation of the ‚Äúimprovement plateau‚Äù phenomenon which indicates a false performance ceiling. In such instances both the initial improvement phase and the recovery phase are described by exponential models. ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers. Inc.
Name: ["Sriyananda H.", "Towill D.R."]
Affiliations: [' University of Wales Institute of Science and Technology']

Title: Sequential Estimation with a Finite Statistic
Abstract: A procedure is given for optimizing the sequential estimation of a random variable in the mean-square sense, with the constraint that the data must be summarized by a finite-valued statistic. This finite-valued statistic can be considered to be the memory of the processor. The estimate is constrained to be a function of the contents of the memory and the time of the estimate. An example is given to illustrate the results. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Koplowitz J.", "Roberts R.A."]

Title: A moment-derived stochastic estimation and control algorithm for bounded-noise systems‚Ä†
Abstract: A new algorithm is developed for the combined estimation and feedback control of linear, discrete, dynamical systems having bounded input and measurement noise disturbances. The algorithm evaluates the conditional-mean state estimate by a Bayes-law computation in which density functions are approximated by moments. The resulting non-linear estimator is combined with a Riccati controller to complete the approximately optimal feedback control law. Numerical results for a scalar application are presented, and an indication of the sensitivity to information on the noise bounds is provided. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Clark G.M., Jr.", "Rowland J.R."]
Affiliations: [' General Research Corporation', ' Oklahoma State University']

Title: On Performance Analysis of Retrieval Functions
Abstract: Threshold-type retrieval functions have been suggested by many people and used widely in clustering algorithms. In this paper, a discriminating capacity is defined for these retrieval functions. Explicit methods for computation are presented. The discriminating capacity is useful as a quantitative measure for the retrieval power of each function and can serve as a guide for selection. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Chien R.T.", "Mark E.A."]
Keywords: ["boolean function", "clustering algorithms", "document retrieval functions", "threshold function", "retrieval power"]

Title: A Nonlinear Transformation for Digital Picture Processing
Abstract: A nonlinear picture-to-picture transformation is introduced and compared with a straightforward linear transformation. The criterion for comparison is based on the desire to smooth noisy or textured regions while retaining edge definition. Selected examples from a large number of simulations are presented. The transformation presented is believed to be superior to many techniques presently being employed. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Newman T.G.", "Dirilten H."]
Keywords: ["averaging schemes", "edge curve detection", "gradient plots", "gradient-oriented masks", "interpolation for local averaging"]
Affiliations: [' Texas Tech University', ' Texas Tech University']

Title: PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS OF SIMULATION AND OTHER AIDS IN IMPROVING TRAIN OPERATIONS AND SERVICE.
Abstract: Presents the practical use made by a major U. S. railroad of a large scale network simulation model. This model of the traffic flow over the entire railroad network of major yards and connecting trackage has been designed and developed in close coordination with the Operating Department of the railroad. Examples of its use in forecasting the feasibility and impact of changing train schedules, pre-blocking and new run-through train operations are described. Other computer aids including on-line monitoring of car movements to automatically divert and re-route cars according to customer instruction, along with on-line techniques to assist in the control of empty equipment by automatic re-routing to distribution points are described.
Name: ["Alward S.A."]

Title: A Bayesian method for histograms
Abstract: A Bayesian procedure for the simultaneous estimation of the probabilities in a histogram is described. A two stage prior distribution is constructed which assumes that probabilities corresponding to adjacent intervals are likely to be closely related. The method employs multivariate logit transformations, and a covariance structure similar to that assumed in the first order autoregressive process. Posterior estimates are obtained which combine information between the intervals and have the practical effect of smoothing the histogram.
Name: ["Leonard T."]

Title: PROSPECTS FOR INDUSTRIAL ROBOTS IN AUTOMATED WAREHOUSES.
Abstract: Studies show that picking costs in warehouses represent 60% of annual costs, as compared with 5% for storage. Handling systems for both stationary and mobile robots to pick and also stack customers orders are evaluated. Results show that for picking operations alone, manual handling can be reduced by 50%.
Name: ["Anstrom A."]

Title: DECOMPOSITION OF A DATA BASE AND THE THEORY OF BOOLEAN SWITCHING FUNCTIONS.
Source: IBM Journal of Research and Development
Abstract: The notion of a fundamental relation among the attributes of a data set can be fruitfully applied in the structuring of an information system. These relations are meaningful both to the user of the system in his semantic understanding of the data, and to the designer in implementing the system. An important equivalence between operations with functional relations and operations with analogous Boolean functions is demonstrated in this paper. The equivalence is computationally helpful in exploring the properties of a given set of functional relations, as well as in the task of partitioning a data set into subfiles for efficient implementation.
Name: ["Delobel C.", "Casey R.G."]

Title: Admissible clustering procedures
Abstract: SUMMARY: The present paper extends the results of Fisher & Van Ness (1971). Table 1 more than doubles the size of the corresponding earlier table. In addition a theorem is proved showing an incompatibility between sum of squares methods and the very appealing well-structured admissibility. Finally, a section is included discussing equal admissibility which arises from the idea that it is impossible to distinguish two clusters which have the same population distributions. ¬© 1973 Oxford University Press.
Name: ["Van Ness J.W."]

Title: OPTIMALITY CONDITIONS FOR VARIOUS FORMS OF WRITING A CONTROL PROCESS.
Abstract: An investigation is made of the objective function and the plant equation in terms of their influence on optimality conditions and the algorithm for solving discrete optimization problems. Modifications of algorithms based on sufficient conditions for optimality are proposed for various forms of plant equation.
Name: ["Dorogov N.N.", "Maykov G.P.", "Tsirlin A.M."]

Title: ADAPTIVE SYSTEMS FOR CONTROL OF MARKOV CHAINS WITH REVENUES.
Abstract: A problem of adaptive control of finite ergodic Markov chains with revenues is posed and solved. The control system is an automaton possessing certain optimality properties.
Name: ["Zasukhin V.S."]

Title: Automatic Readout of Data. | [AUTOMATISCHE ERKENNUNG VON SCHRIFTZEICHEN.]
Abstract: Problems dealing will direct readout systems of digits, particularly the recognition of handwritten characters are discussed. The solutions of some problems are explained and recommendations for improvement in readout system given.
Name: ["Zimmermann Rolf"]

Title: COKO III: The Cooper-Koz Chess Program
Abstract: OKO III is a chess player written entirely in Fortran. On the IBM 360-65, COKO III plays a minimal chess game at the rate of.2 sec cpu time per move, with a level close to lower chess club play. A selective tree searching procedure controlled by tactical chess logistics allows a deployment of multiple minimal game calculations to achieve some optimal move selection. The tree searching algorithms are the heart of COKO's effectiveness, yet they are conceptually simple. In addition, an interesting phenomenon called a tree searching catastrophe has plagued COKO's entire development just as it troubles a human player. Standard exponential growth is curbed to a large extent by the definition and trimming of the Fisher set. A clear distinction between tree pruning and selective tree searching is also made. Representation of the chess environment is described along with a strategical preanalysis procedure that maps the Lasker regions. Specific chess algorithms are described which could be used as a command structure by anyone desiring to do some chess program experimentation. A comparison is made of some mysterious actions of human players and COKO III. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Kozdrowicki E.W.", "Cooper D.W."]
Keywords: ["alpha beta", "artificial intelligence", "auxiliary minimal game", "chess algorithms", "command structure"]
Affiliations: [' University of California at Davis', 'Bell Telephone Labs']

Title: Dual decompositions and effective coordination of dynamical systems
Abstract: Hierarchical Control is an attractive solution when the optimization of a large scale system is requested. This paper introduces a consistent approach to the coordination problem in the dynamic case. Two basic transformations on the system afford real decomposition into subproblems by means of the generalized Lagrangian. Two specific hierarchical structures fulfilling efficiently the INPRE and INBAL principles are deduced. This method gives a convenient realization algorithm in both cases. Moreover, these principles are shown, in a sense, to be dual. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Gueguen C.J.", "Manich-Mayol F."]

Title: Examples of Learning Systems
Abstract: This chapter discusses the examples of learning systems and illustrates the practical possibilities of learning systems. The applications of learning algorithms in the construction of various learning systems are discussed. Specific examples of learning systems of pattern recognition, classification, identification, filtering, and control are presented. The chapter focuses on the learning systems for solving the problems of standardization and fault detection. Learning systems can be built in the form of a special analog, discrete or hybrid devices or realized on digital computers. The algorithms of learning take the form of the corresponding digital computer programs. Experimental results are presented for several specific systems. The chapter presents the examples that not only emphasize the variety of learning systems, but also expose the general idea that lies in the foundation of the construction of learning systems. ¬© 1973, Academic Press Inc.

Title: State estimation for partially observed Markov chains
Source: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: Recursive equations are derived for the conditional distribution of the state of a Markov chain, given observations of a function of the state. Mainly continuous time chains are considered. The equations for the conditional distribution are given in matrix form and in differential equation form. The conditional distribution itself forms a Markov process. Special cases considered are doubly stochastic Poisson processes with a Markovian intensity, Markov chains with a random time, and Markovian approximations of semi-Markov processes. Further the results are used to compute the Radon-Nikodym derivative for two probability measures for a Markov chain, when a function of the state is observed. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Rudemo M."]

Title: BEHAVIOURAL APPROACH TO OBTAINING A DOUBLY CONSTRAINED TRIP DISTRIBUTION MODEL.
Abstract: An alternative method of producing a doubly constrained trip distribution similar to that of a gravity model is described. This alternative model differs from conventional models in that it has an explicit, though naive, behavioral rationale. It also produces a doubly constrained distribution more rapidly than these conventional models, partly because it involves fewer iterations and partly because each successive iteration involves fewer zones than that preceding it. In the one full-scale test for which data are available, the new model efficiently simulates a survey derived distribution, while tests with hypothetical systems show that it produces a distribution which can be closely identified with that produced by a conventional model.
Name: ["Arrowsmith G."]

Title: MARKOV PROCESS WITH LOCAL INTERACTION.
Abstract: A stochastic system consisting of locally interacting components subjected to irreversible transformations is analyzed. It is shown that the distribution function of the states of the system at each instant has with respect to the spatial parameter a certain analog of the Markov property.
Name: ["Mityushin L.G."]

Title: Analytical Calculation of Steady Oscillations in Multistep Control Loops by the Zypkin Method. | ANALYTISCHE BERECHNUNG VON DAUERSCHWINGUNGEN IN MEHRPUNKTREGELKREISEN NACH DEM ZYPKINVERFAHREN.
Abstract: For a control loop with an I-T//t plant and a multi-step relay characteristic (multi-point controller) possible steady oscillations are calculated analytically. For this reason a method of J. A. Zypkin is extended. The mode of execution is shown for a seven-point controller. Then the calculated steady oscillations are represented in the state plane.
Name: ["Bauer W.L."]

Title: WEB GRAMMARS AND WEB AUTOMATA.
Abstract: Web grammars proposed by J. L. Pfaltz and A. Rosenfeld are capable of generating sets of directed graphs, each having a symbol on every vertex. In this paper, generalized webs having a symbol on every arc are defined. Based on the concept of these generalized webs, the web grammars are redefined, and the standard form is established for any normal monotone context-sensitive web grammar. Moreover, the web automata capable of recognizing sets of normal monotone context-sensitive web languages are constructed.
Name: ["Ezawa Yoshinori", "Abe Norihiro", "Mizumoto Masaharu", "Toyoda Jun-ichi", "Tanaka Kohkichi"]

Title: OPTIMAL STATIONARY FEEDBACK CONTROL WITH SPECIFIED RELATIVE STABILITY.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: A systematic procedure is presented for designing optimal feedback control systems with the poles restricted either to the left of the line Re(s) equals minus alpha or in a cone tan** minus **1 left brace I//m(s)/Re(s) right brace equals plus or minus theta . Simple transformations of the complex variable s are utilized to find a characteristic polynomial for the desired closed-loop system. It is then shown that this polynomial can be used with the frequency-domain optimality condition and the observability condition to find a proper quadratic index. It is also shown that it may be necessary to include a product of the control variable and the state variable in the quadratic index so that arbitrary pole placement may be possible.
Name: ["Pal J.K.", "Mahalanabis A.K."]

Title: Logical design for sequencing of fast transform algorithms
Abstract: Current interest in the hardware implementation of fast transform algorithms, has prompted a closer look at the sequencing and addressing systems involved. A novel logical design is presented for these systems which minimizes computational hardware and performs satisfactorily atconsiderably faster clock rates than other conventional systems. Modularity and simplicity of the design are further useful features. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Durrani T.S.", "Hart C.G."]

Title: Selection of the Structure and Increments of Quantization for Time and Space Coordinates When Constructing a Nonlinear Digital Model of Steam - Water Duct of a Boiler. | [VYBOR STRUKTURY I SHAGOV KVANTOVANIYA PO VREMENNOI I PROSTRANSTVENNOI KOORDINATAM PRI POSTORENII NELINEINOI TSIFROVOI MODELI UCHASTKA PAROVODYANOGO TRAKTA PAROGENERATORA.]
Abstract: Problems of structure and quantization increments ensuring acceptable exactness of a solution with minimum use of computer time are considered for the temperature channel and the flow and pressure channel of a nonlinear digital model of a boiler section. This model is synthesized on the basis of a specialized computer language. Examples of modeling various boiler sections are given. It is concluded that problems of selection of quantization increments have to be solved independently for the temperature channel and for the flow and pressure channel. Differences in quantization increments for the spatial coordinate for different channels are realized by structural methods.
Name: ["Bubashkin A.S."]

Title: TERNARY THRESHOLD LOGIC NETWORKS REALIZING THREE-VALUED MULTITHRESHOLD FUNCTIONS.
Abstract: A ternary logic function is viewed in this paper as a threshold function, and its realization by threshold networks is investigated. The properties and interdependence of the threshold and the connecting weight are examined. Some specific algorithms of parameter determination for realizing arbitrary ternary logic functions are presented and explained.
Name: ["Imamiya Atsumi", "Noguchi Shoichi", "Oizumi Juro"]

Title: Image reconstruction from finite numbers of projections
Source: Journal of Physics A: General Physics
Abstract: Several results are obtained appertaining to the reconstruction of a two- dimensional image from a finite number of projections. Several schemes are considered for interpolating between the given data. When a trigonometrical Fourier series is used for angular interpolation then one finds, firstly, a consistency condition whereby a posteriori estimates can be made of the errors in the given data, and secondly, a basic image which contains only that information common to all physically permissible interpolation schemes. This basic image is necessarily free of misleading artefacts but it is computationally slow. Several computationally rapid interpolation schemes (based on the fast Fourier transform algorithm) are found to give good quality images, provided the given number of projections is sufficient to resolve the major details of the true image. A computational example is presented showing that a contrived image can be accurately reconstructed from a single projection.
Name: ["Smith P.R.", "Peters T.M.", "Bates R.H.T."]

Title: Automatic Generation of Programs for Data Transformation. | AUTOMATISCHE ERZEUGUNG VON PROGRAMMEN ZUR DATENTRANSFORMATION.
Abstract: A common job in the data processing field is to translate given data files. In the past special programs were usually written to do special data translating job. An approach to automatic generation of data translation programs is suggested which supposes input data items to be phrases of a formal language and the formal language to be described by a metalanguage. The metalanguage used in this approach describes the syntax structure of the input data and their preparation for output data as data translation rules. It is developed from the notation of formal languages belonging to Chomsky-type 3 (finite-stage languages). The data translation rules which must be defined according to the different data translations are converted by a program generator into data translation programs. COBOL was used for programming a prototype of the program generator as well as for the data translation programs.
Name: ["Mueller B.", "Winkler H."]

Title: Methods of Filing and Retrieving Information in a Memory. | METHODES DE RECHERCHE EN MEMOIRE.
Abstract: The methods of filing and retrieving information in a memory are considered. Some important criteria to evalute the methods and the characteristics of the files that are used, and the minimum number of information which is necessary to store one subset of X values chosen on a set N are defined. This minimum is shown to be X Log N/X under some reasonable conditions. Some classical and new algorithms using among other things the notion that address can be one important part of the information are presented and extended. Finally since one of these methods yields one ordered set, its properties with those of actual merging methods are compared.
Name: ["Guiho G."]

Title: Stability Criterion for N-Dimensional Digital Filters
Abstract: The stability requirement for one-dimensional recursive filters is well known. A stability theorem for n-dimensional recursive filters is proved wherein the denominator of the filter is an n-dimensional power series. A Tauberian theorem due to Wiener yields the desired result in the general case. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Justice J.H.", "Shanks J.L."]
Affiliations: [' University of Tulsa', ' Amoco Production Company']

Title: Performance of the A Priori Stochastic-Optimal Feedback Control Law
Abstract: For a stochastic control system with noisy observations, some interest has been shown in mechanizing the optimal open-loop control law as a suboptimal feedback control law. Examples have appeared in the literature to show that the performance of this feedback control law is better than the performance of the optimal control function without feedback. It is shown here that in general this unproven observation is true. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Early R.H.", "Early B.N."]

Title: Hybrid Modeling of Systems with a Variable Structure. | GIBRIDNOE MODELIROVANIE SISTEM S PEREMENNOI STRUKTUROI.
Abstract: Problems of modeling dynamic systems characterized by the variability of internal connections and interdependences are considered. In order to obtain mathematical description of the systems of the said class a coincident system of differential equations is composed, containing binary variables. A formal apparatus of minimization of the number of computing operators of equations is proposed, making it possible to realize a mathematical model with a minimum of equipment on a hybrid computing system.
Name: ["Fel'dman L.P.", "Sleptsov A.I."]

Title: TWO-STAGE ALGORITHM FOR SEQUENTIAL DECISION PROBLEMS.
Abstract: The Progressive Optimality Algorithm for solution of dynamic programming problems is introduced. An application to a practical production planning problem illustrates the operation of the algorithm. Solutions using both analytical and heuristic methods are compared with previous published solutions to illustrate the effectiveness of the algorithm.
Name: ["Howson H.R.", "Sancho N.G.F."]

Title: On Divergence and Probability of Error in Pattern Recognition
Abstract: An upperbound on the probability of error in classifying a pattern using Bayesian decision criterion is obtained in terms of its divergence and it is shown that the maximization of the divergence of the pattern minimizes this upperbound. Furthermore, a relationship between the divergence of a pattern and its nearest neighbor classification risk is presented. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Babu C.C."]

Title: Cooley-tukey-type algorithm for the haar transform
Abstract: It is shown that the Haar transform can be computed using a Cooley-Tukey-type algorithm that is implemented in 2(N-1) additions/subtractions. This algorithm is derived by relating the Haar transform to the modified Walsh-Hadamard transform using a simple bit-reversal scheme. ¬© 1973, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Ahmed N.", "Natarajan T.", "Rao K.R."]
Affiliations: ['Electrical Engineering Department Kansas State University', 'Electrical Engineering Department University of Texas']

Title: DISCRIMINATION OF RANDOM FIELDS AGAINST BACKGROUND NOISE.
Abstract: Statistical inference theory is applied to the discrimination problem for random fields. The integral equation to which the problem is reduced is subjected to an analytical investigation.
Name: ["Ramm A.G."]

Title: DISCRETE REPRESENTATION OF SIGNALS WITH AN UNBOUNDED GENERALIZED SPECTRUM.
Abstract: A theorem is formulated and proved, making possible the discrete representation of signals with an unbounded generalized spectrum and the same spectral properties as real signals. This general result is used to derive an exact expression and error estimates for the model of a signal with a bounded generalized spectrum.
Name: ["Medvedev V.A.", "Oleinikov B.I.", "Stepanov B.M.", "Filinov V.N."]

Title: On Sequential Refinement Schemes for Recursive Digital Filter Design
Abstract: A linear synthesis technique is developed for a recursive digital filter which approximates the desired discrete impulse response. Sequential schemes which can be used to refine the preliminary filter design are developed for three distinct cases in which the output sequence number, the filter order, and the number of the numerator coefficients of the transfer function are allowed to vary separately. By the use of matrix inversion lemmas, the new sets of filter coefficients are obtained sequentially based on the old estimates and the new data without having to repeat the entire design procedure. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Chao K.-S.", "Lu K.-S."]

Title: Capacity of Gaussian Channels with Several Inputs and Outputs. | [ZUR KAPAZITAET GAUSSCHER KANAELE MIT MEHREREN EIN- UND AUSGAENGEN.]
Abstract: For given power density spectrum of the input process, and restricting the signal power of the output process, the capacity of the channel with transmission matrix H(f) is maximized using the formula of the Gaussian multiport channel. The Matrix H(f) shows, for example, how the signal power is distributed to the different channels when diversity transmission is assumed.
Name: ["Dieterich Guenter"]

Title: The Predictability of Certain Optimum Finite-Impulse-Response Digital Filters
Abstract: Some of the properties of optimal solutions to the finite-impulse-response low-pass filter design problem are discussed. These solutions are optimum in the sense of discrete Chebyshev approximation over a union of closed compact sets, i.e., the error of approximation exhibits at least (N + 3)/2 alternations (of equal amplitude) over the frequency ranges of interest, where N is the duration of the filter impulse response in samples. It has been shown that, in certain special cases, the solution can exhibit (N + 5)/2 alternations of equal amplitude. These solutions have been called extraripple filters because of the extra alternation that is present. How these extraripple solutions can, within bounds, be scaled to yield additional solutions, which are stilll optimal over new frequency ranges, is shown. Thus an infinite number of optimal low-pass filters may be obtained directly from a finite number of extraripple solutions. An interpretation of the various types of optimal filters, in terms of locations of the zeros of the z-transform polynomial, is also given. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Rabiner L.R.", "Herrmann O."]

Title: A Semi-Markovian Population Model with Application to Hospital Planning
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics
Abstract: A semi-Markovian population model can be used to describe patient movements in a health-care delivery system. The recovery progress of a patient at any time is defined by one of a finite number of ‚Äústates.‚Äù The movement of a patient among the states is governed by a discrete-time semi-Markov process which is called a ‚Äúpath.‚Äù The inputs to the system are various patient ‚Äúgroups.‚Äù Each group is characterized by a distinct input distribution with known mean and variance. Assuming that the input distributions are relatively stable in the long run, estimates of the means and variances of steady-state census mix are derived. On a short-term basis, the model will accommodate daily fluctuations in input distributions and use an information vector, which summarizes the state of the system at the time of prediction, to improve the estimation. An illustrative example using field data is presented. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Kao E.P.C."]

Title: A fuzzy relative of the ISODATA process and its use in detecting compact well-separated clusters
Abstract: Two fuzzy versions of the fc-means optimal, least squared error partitioning problem are formulated for finite subsets A' of a general inner product space. In both cases, the extrcmizing solutions are shown to be fixed points of a certain operator T on the class of fuzzy A-partitions of X, and simple iteration of T provides an algorithm which has the descent property relative to the least squared error criterion function. In the first case, the range of T consists largely of ordinary (i.e. non-fuzzy) partitions of A' and the associated iteration scheme is essentially the well known ISODATA process of Ball and Hall. However, in the second case, the range of T consists mainly of fuzzy partitions and the associated algorithm is new; when X consists of k compact well separated (CWS) clusters, Xt, this algorithm generates a limiting partition with membership functions which closely approximate the characteristic functions of the clusters Xj. However, when X is not the union of k CWS clusters, the limiting partition is truly fuzzy in the sense that the values of its component membership functions differ substantially from 0 or 1 over certain regions of.V. Thus, unlike ISODATA, the "fuzzy" algorithm signals the presence or absence of CWS clusters in A'. Furthermore, the fuzzy algorithm seems significantly less prone to the "cluster-splitting" tendency of ISODATA and may also be less easily diverted to uninteresting locally optimal partitions. Finally, for data sets.V consisting of dense CWS clusters embedded in a diffuse background of strays, the structure of X is accurately reflected in the limiting partition generated by the fuzzy algorithm. Mathematical arguments and numerical results are offered in support of the foregoing assertions. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Dunn J.C."]

Title: On Minimization of Fuzzy Functions
Abstract: The study of fuzziness in combinational switching systems by means of a suitable fuzzy algebra is discussed. The insufficiency of the methods for simplification of fuzzy functions as presented by Lee and Chang [9] and by Siy and Chen [10] is discussed. A new technique for minimization of fuzzy functions is developed. Special properties of fuzzy functions are discussed and their relationships to two-valued logic are investigated. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Kandel A."]
Keywords: ["essential fuzzy prime implicant", "fuzzy algebra", "fuzzy function", "fuzzy iterated consensus", "fuzzy logic"]
Affiliations: [' New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology']

Title: An experimental differential p.c.m. encoder-decoder for Viewphone signals
Abstract: A fully digital differential pulse code modulation (d.p.c.m.) system has been constructed to provide a flexible and stable basis for subjective optimization of a technique for efficient coding of video telephone picture signals. The experimental encoder accepts a precoded 8-bit p.c.m. input and delivers a 4-bit d.p.c.m. output which may be corrupted by simulated channel errors before decoding and display. The implementation of the system is described and photographic results of the coding technique are presented. ¬© 1973, The Institution of Electronic and Radio Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gerrard G.A.", "Thompson J.E."]

Title: METHODS OF SOLUTION OF QUANTUM DETECTION AND MEASUREMENT PROBLEMS.
Abstract: An extremal problem is studied that is a quantum generalization of the problem of minimization of the average risk in Bayesian nonquantum decision theory.
Name: ["Grishanin B.A."]

Title: Comments on ‚ÄúIdentification of Totally Symmetric Boolean Functions‚Äù
Abstract: A modification in the algorithm for the detection of totally symmetric functions as expounded by the author in an earlier note<sup>1</sup> is presented here. The modified algorithm takes care of a limited number of functions that escape detection by the previous method. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Biswas N.N."]

Title: Limit-Cycle Oscillations in Floating-Point Digital Filters
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: In a digital filter realized with fixed-point arithmetic, there is a peculiar phenomenon known as limit-cycle oscillation, which is due to roundoff errors. For floating-point arithmetic, it has been conjectured that its amplitude is negligibly small, if it does exist. This paper shows that limit-cycle oscillations can exist in floating-point digital filters and that their amplitude can be large. Also, conditions for the existence of limit-cycle oscillations are derived. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Kaneko T."]

Title: Roentgen-videometric methods for the determination of ventri-colarvolume using a video light pen and digital contour memories | R√∂ntgenvideometrische Verfahren zur Ventrikelvolumenbestimmung unter Verwendung eines Video-Lichtgriffels und digitaler Konturenspeicher
Abstract: In order to obtain a better judgement o'f the physical performance of the heart one requires continuous simultaneous measurements of the pressure and volume of the various heartchambers, especially those of the left ventricle. Different methods of volume-determination are contrasted in this publication and possibilities to automate these wearisome measurements are given. A realized System is specified, in which the contour points traced with a light pen are digitally recorded. By this means the contour tracing of a whole sequence of successive biplane angiograms is very facilitated, because there is no tracing of the whole contour necessary but only of those segments which have changed in comparison to the preceding picture. The ventricular volume can be determined from the sum of elliptical disks, whereby the length of the axes are infered from the two heart aspects. This well known method is modified here in such a way that a precise centring and scaling of the two aspects is not required and that the ventricular volume can nevertheless be determined in a simple manner by a connected Computer. ¬© 1973 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Zimmermann R.", "Bussmann W.-D.", "Ameline W.", "Schmidt M.", "Effert S."]
Affiliations: ['Dornier GmbH', 'Institut f√ºr Allgemeine Elektrotechnik und Datenverarbeitungssysteme', 'Rogowski-Institut der TH', 'Abteilung Innere Medizin I']

Title: Recognition in a homogeneous medium
Abstract: An experimental technique of recognition in conditions of a homogeneous medium is proposed. By homogeneous is meant a medium consisting of stimuli which are perceived as multiplicities of perceptively equivalent elements. Stochastic models are constructed making it possible to predict the probability for the ensemble of subjects. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Farmakovskii V.V."]

Title: SIMULATION OF PACKET-SWITCHING NETWORKS CONTROLLED ON ISARITHMIC PRINCIPLES.
Abstract: An account is given of simulation experiments on an isarithmically controlled packet-switching network. The isarithmic principle (a method of congestion control by placing an upper limit on the number of data packets in transit at one time) has been developed in such a way as to mimize the amount of ‚Ä≥empty‚Ä≥ packet traffic, while retaining much of the flexibility of the original concept. It is suggested that one of the important performance measuring criteria is the average time spent by traffic in awaiting admission to the network; it is shown how this time can be minimized by best choice of the number of packets permitted to be in transit at one time and of the length of queues of ‚Ä≥empties‚Ä≥ awaiting traffic. It is further suggested that the performance (measured in terms of throughput rate and end-to-end delay) of the network being studied (a ladder-shaped network of 18 nodes and 31 links) is not improved by applying adaptive routing, though some form of this must be provided to cope with fault conditions.
Name: ["Price W.L."]

Title: BAYES' DECISION RULE FOR RAPID DETECTION AND ADAPTIVE ESTIMATION SCHEME WITH SPACE APPLICATIONS.
Abstract: A sub-optimal filter applicable to systems which have unknown impulses at unknown instances of time is described. An adaptive filter has been discussed by the authors in a previous paper. A modification for that filter is shown to be sub-optimal. Computer results have been included to point out the improvement.
Name: ["Sanyal P.", "Shen C.N."]

Title: PROJECTION OPERATOR ALGORITHM FOR OPTIMAL CONTROL PROBLEMS WITH UNSPECIFIED INITIAL STATE VALUES.
Abstract: An automatic gradient projection algorithm is developed to treat optimal control problems with unspecified initial values for some state variables and with an unspecified interval of the independent variable. Repeated use of the projection operator allows a one-dimensional minimization among controls which satisfy the terminal state constraints to be employed as the step size selection procedure. The projection operator is developed for a control space which is the Cartesian product of control parameters, those governing the initial values of the state variables and the independent variable interval length, and the control functions of the dynamical system so that the proposed algorithm iterates on all control parameters and control functions simultaneously. Two numerical examples, including a minimum time-to-climb V/STOL problem, are given to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed algorithm.
Name: ["Rajtora Stanley G.", "Pierson Bion L."]

Title: AUTOMATIC ORGANIZATION OF FILES - 2. TRANSLATION PACKAGE.
Abstract: An overview is presented of the TRANSLATION package of the SOLID System. The SOLID System is a high-speed, fully automatic, information and question-type, independent, self-organizing, management/retrieval system. The TRANSLATION package is responsible for performing some of the supervisory and monitoring functions in the information and data base-dependent portion of the system called the FRONT part. The TRANSLATION package is the interface between the user and the main frame of the SOLID System. It is responsible, in part, for the ease with which anyone can use the SOLID System and with the versatility of SOLID.
Name: ["Perry James T.", "de Maine Paul A.D."]

Title: DETERMINISTIC AND ADAPTIVE ROUTING POLICIES.
Abstract: Efficient routing policies are required for both design and operation of distributed, packet-switched computer networks. In the network design pocess, deterministic policies, which are time invariant, easy to analyze and simple to represent, are generally used. For the routing of packets in a real network, on the other hand, adaptive policies, which can adjust to traffic fluctuations and component failures are implemented. Therefore, a computer network is typically optimized with respect to a deterministic policy and then operated with an adaptive policy. In the first part of this paper the two policies are compared using analytical and simulation methods, and it is shown that, in uniform traffic situations, the flow patterns generated are very similar. This result justifies the use of deterministic policy in the design phase. In the second part of the paper, the inadequacy of traditional adaptive policies in handling particular traffic situations is pointed out. As a solution, a new centralized adaptive policy is proposed, which combines and positive features of both deterministic and adaptive routing. The feasibility of such centralized policy implementation on a real network, and its efficiency with respect to the traditional implementation is discussed.
Name: ["Gerla Mario"]

Title: DELAY PLANE, OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS OF SUBJECTIVE PROPERTIES - 2.
Source: AES: Journal of the Audio Engineering Society
Abstract: Objective analysis of subjective sound properties is possible only by expanding analysis beyond the conventional approach of time domain and frequency domain. A case has been presented that time and frequency, rather than being the only valid coordinates of representation, are in fact only two valid functional representations out of an indefinitely large number. A useful working audio tool has been presented in the form of a C**2 space which can be manipulated when presented as a two-dimensional chart, called the delay plane. This paper draws heavily from the mathematics of normed linear spaces. The first two sections on definition and Hilbert space summarize the salient engineering features of this branch of mathematics and provide a digest version for the needs of this paper as well as a minimum background for audio engineers. The necessary mathematical basis for a heuristic working concept is presented.
Name: ["Heyser Richard C."]

Title: SEQUENTIAL SEARCH OF AN OPTIMAL DOSAGE: NON-BAYESIAN METHODS.
Abstract: A class of one-sided (sequential) stochastic approximation procedures which have possible applications in many fields is represented. A motivational background could be simply described in terms of a biomedical problem. A drug could be administered at various dosages. High dosages although desirable increase the level of toxicity. The dosage-toxicity relationship is not completely known. Sequential experimentation is used to approach from below the highest possible dosage one may give without causing too much toxicity.
Name: ["Eichhorn B.H."]

Title: CONSTRAINED SEQUENTIAL-BLOCK SEARCH IN SIMULATION EXPERIMENTATION.
Abstract: The application of sequential-block search techniques to simulation experimentation with constrained systems is described. Two basically different approaches are examined. One approach combines designed experiments, multiple regression, and mathematical optimization to predict a constrained optimum solution, which is then checked by further experimentation in the region of the predicted solution. A second approach employs a sequential optimum-seeking technique, such as gradient search or sequential simplex search, modified to accommodate constraints. These techniques are illustrated with a simple inventory system modeled with the GASP-II simulation language. A comparison of the effectiveness of these approaches is presented.
Name: ["Biles William E."]

Title: RELATING TIME AND PROBABILITY IN COMPUTER GRAPHS.
Abstract: Program behavior is discussed in terms of Petri Nets. Using probabilistic information, an experimental method is given to determine the time spent in each state. To illustrate the method, two examples are given for program graphs.
Name: ["Johnson Robert R."]

Title: TOPOLOGICAL ANALYSIS, CLASSIFICATION, AND ENCODING OF CHINESE CHARACTERS FOR DIGITAL COMPUTER INTERFACE - 2.
Abstract: A possible three-stage system for classifying and encoding Chinese characters is proposed. The rationale for such a system is also given. The details of each stage are further discussed, and the possible hardware implementation (for the first stage in particular) is illustrated in greater detail. Finally, a heuristic scheme for encoding Chinese characters for ordinary dictionary usage is suggested as a by-product of the investigation.
Name: ["Wang Paul P."]

Title: A Note on a Modified Ternary Simulator Capable of Initializing All Fault Machine Memory Elements
Abstract: Generation of test patterns and diagnostics for complex digital modules often involves a ternary (0, 1, u) simulation program. A non-Boolean technique, presented herein, initializes u (unknown) values in such a way that diagnostic resolution and accuracy is enhanced. A pure ternary simulator lacks this initialization capability. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Gravitz M.E."]

Title: Optimal linear smoothing : Continuous data case
Abstract: Recently, Lainiotia (1971 c), using the so-called ‚Äò partition theorem ‚Äô, has obtained an optimal linear smoothing algorithm in explicit, closed-form expressions that are attractive, both from a computational and an analysis point of view. Lainiotis (1971c‚Äòpartition smoothing‚Äô algorithm is re-examined herein, and its computational and analytical advantages studied. It is compared to the previously established two-filter smoothing algorithm of Mayne (1966), Fraser (1967), and Mehra (1968), as well as to the ‚Äò innovation smoothing ‚Äô algorithm of Kailath and Frost (1968) Subsequently, the so-called ‚Äò iterative ‚Äô or ‚Äò reprocessed ‚Äô smoothing scheme, used extensively as a data reduction process in the Apollo Space Programme, is studied using the ‚Äò partition smoothing ‚Äô algorithm. The resulting explicit and closed-form expressions are readily amenable to interpretation and optimization, and are, moreover, both theoretically interesting as well as practically useful. The statistical and limiting properties of the ‚Äò partition reprocessed smoothing ‚Äô algorithm are obtained and are thoroughly examined. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Lainiotis D.G."]
Affiliations: [' The University of Texas at Austin']

Title: VALIDATION OF STOCHASTIC DIFFERENCE EQUATION MODELS FOR EMPIRICAL TIME SERIES.
Abstract: A multiple hypothesis test has been developed for comparing the validity of a number of linear stocchastic difference equations for the given empirical time series. The linear stochastic difference may have autoregressive, observable input, and deterministic trend terms with unknown coefficients. The test involves the recursive evaluation of the empirical prediction error of the sequence for each model. Both theoretical and empirical justifications for the method are given. From the computational view, the test is quite compact since the test statistics can be computed in a recursive manner.
Name: ["Kashyap R.L."]

Title: RANDOM-SEARCH ALGORITHMS WITH LINEAR CONSTRAINTS.
Abstract: Algorithms are proposed for solving the problem of minimizing a convex function with linear constraints, by using methods of projecting a randomly chosen direction of motion at each step. An algorithmic procedure is described and a number of particular cases and illustrative examples are considered. It is shown that the proposed algorithms make it possible to solve the linear programming problem by methods of random search over a finite number of steps.
Name: ["Zak Yu.A."]

Title: Learning Pattern Recognition Systems
Abstract: This chapter discusses the learning pattern recognition systems. Learning systems that realize optimal algorithms can be called Bayes systems. If the algorithms are not optimal, such systems can be called asymptotically adaptive Bayes systems. The classical Bayes approach and its resulting decision rules, lead to the comparison of the likelihood ratio with the thresholds that depend on the decision rules. They require sufficient a priori information. The adaptive Bayes approach implies approximation of the discriminant function by a certain finite series of linearly independent functions. Unlike the traditional adaptive approach that minimizes the functional defining the goal of learning, the adaptive Bayes approach minimizes the difference between the correct, but unknown discriminant functions and its approximation. The adaptive Bayes approach imposes a certain modification in the viewpoint of statistical decision theory. If a priori information is complete, then the Bayes rules should be used. ¬© 1973, Academic Press Inc.

Title: SIMULATION IN THE DESIGN OF UNIT CARRIER MATERIALS HANDLING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The values and benefits of simulation are discussed as applied to the design of a track system for a unit carrier, a vehicle used to transport one or more items to a certain destination. In a unit carrier system these discrete, individual vehicles carry an item or items along fixed routes, each relatively independent of the other vehicles in the system. The design of the automatic baggage handling system for the Seattle-Tacoma International Airport is used as an example of such a unit carrier system. Design requirements include input rates of baggage loading stations and car destination patterns over a relatively fixed system geometry. A simulation model is used to evaluate overall performance including empty car availability and minimized network flow. Design of the trackage controls as well as tuning of the entire baggage handling system are aided by use of the model.
Name: ["Siesennop W.Wayne", "Callies Fritz A.", "Campbell Neal S."]

Title: BIOLOGICAL APPLICATIONS OF PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: The application of a pattern recognition system for analyzing lateral or profile x-ray films of the human head by extracting accurate coordinate points from the films - i. e. , image enhancement - is discussed.
Name: ["Walker Geoffrey F.", "Kowalski Charles J."]

Title: MINIMIZATION OF PROBABILISTIC AUTOMATA REPRESENTING FINITE INFORMATION MEDIA.
Abstract: The constructive viewpoint in mathematics is used to consider the problem of representing finite information media by probabilistic automata with a minimum number of internal states for a fixed radius of isolation delta . It is shown that the problem has a solution for all delta , except, perhaps, for a finite number of values.
Name: ["Lapin'sh Ya.K."]

Title: A widely convergent minimization algorithm with quadratic termination property
Source: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
Abstract: We have constructed a DSDS whose properties imply the convergence of a conjugate gradient method, which is a modification of the Fletcher and Reeves method and has the quadratic termination property. The convergence is global for functions continuously differentiable, bounded from below, having bounded level sets and one and only one critical point. However these assumptions are not restrictive, since if the function is simply continuously differentiable, the algorithm converges to a local minimum point if the initial point is chosen in any bounded level set containing one and only critical point. ¬© 1973, Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Treccani G."]

Title: Discrete-Time System Identification by the Correlation Method
Abstract: The pseudorandom binary sequence is applied to the parameter estimation of discrete-time systems. The proposed method, based on the correlation analysis, gives a computationally simple and effective way of parameter estimation. The estimates of the parameters are shown to be asymptotically unbiased. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Funahashi Y.", "Nakamura K."]

Title: INTERACTIVE PATTERN RECOGNITION: A DESIGNER'S TOOL.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: The Air Force's Rome Air Development Center has produced a unique tool for solving automatic recognition problems, called the On-Line Pattern Analysis and Recognition System (OLPARS). In this article five of the twelve applications of the OLPARS have been discussed with the intention of showing how a system designer or a research worker can use interactive pattern recognition systems as tools to solve automatic target identification problems and as statistical analysis packages.
Name: ["Simmons Jr. Edward J."]

Title: ON THE CAPACITY OF NOISY CHANNELS WITH ARBITRARY SIGNAL COSTS.
Abstract: Four types of information capacity of general noisy channels with arbitrary input signal costs are considered and theorems on their asymptotic equality are proved, both for unconstrained and constrained inputs. The considered capacities are relevant to transmission of fixed and variable costs, respectively. In particular, for the transmission length cost assignment, the results amount to a general proof of the intuitive statement that the capacity bound for the length of reliable transmission is valid asymptotically also for the average length of variable length transmission. Examples with memoryless channels are given, including channels with feedback.
Name: ["Csiszar I."]

Title: The application of an image compression - feature transgeneration technique to the computer aided diagnosis of brain tumors
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The application of a technique for image compression and feature transgeneration to the automated diagnosis of brain tumors from brain scintigrams is discussed. This technique essentially consists of partitioning the original image into nonoverlapping subimages and applying feature transgeneration to each subimage. This technique is applied to achieve image data compression or reduction and feature generation that is optimal for classification rather than for representation. In developing and improving the technique, emphasis was placed on a specific application, the detection of brain tumors from scintigraphic images. Some performance results for the classification of normal/abnormal classes of brain scans and for the control of false negatives are presented. Some possible extensions, modifications, and implications of this work are briefly described.
Name: ["Han K.S.", "McLaren R.W.", "Lodwick G.S."]

Title: MINIMAX STRATEGIES IN STATISTICAL GAMES CORRESPONDING TO RECOGNITION PROBLEMS.
Abstract: An examination is made of methods of finding minimax strategies in statistical games which correspond to recognition problems with an arbitrary number of classes and discrete features, and also with two classes when the features are discrete or continuous and normally distributed. In the general cast, the game is solved by reducing it to a linear programming problem. In the case of two classes, the solution is based on the properties of Bayesian strategies. Computational algorithms realizing the proposed methods are included.
Name: ["Dudenko L.N."]

Title: EFFECT OF INEXACT DATA ON THE LEAST SQUARES EXTRAPOLATION OF NONSTATIONARY PROCESSES.
Abstract: The initial information used in the extrapolation of various processes is known only to a certain degree of accuracy and reliability. It is proposed that the Monte Carlo method be used for taking into account the effect on the extrapolation result of a probabilistic error of the original data. A set of programs has been compiled on a Ural-14 digital computer for least squares extrapolation of time series of the parameters of electric, heat, and fuel consumption, with determination of the trend and of the random component. Specific experimental and industrial calculations were performed that showed the strong effect on the extrapolation result of probabilistic error in the original data.
Name: ["Derzskiy V.G.", "Polyakov V.B."]

Title: On the Expected Duration of a Search for a Fixed Pattern in Random Data
Abstract: search to find a given L-ary sequence in a semi-infinite stream of random L-ary data. The search time is found to be an increasing function of the lengths of the ‚Äúbifices‚Äù of the pattern, where the term bifix denotes a sequence which is both a prefix and a suffix. An expression is obtained for the expected duration. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Nielsen P.T."]

Title: APPROXIMATE SYNTHESIS OF FREQUENCY-SELECTIVE SIGNAL PROCESSORS.
Abstract: A method is presented of selection of the weight function of a linear integral transformation defined on a limited signal interval. Using it, it is possible to obtain a spectral curve of pre-assigned form. The method is convenient in digital spectral analysis of processes in control systems.
Name: ["Kitaygorods'kiy A.B.", "Ivanova L.K."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF COMPLEX AUDIO SPECTRA BY MEANS OF FREQUENCY MODULATION.
Source: AES: Journal of the Audio Engineering Society
Abstract: A new application of the well-known process of frequency modulation is shown to result in a surprising control of audio spectra. The technique provides a means of great simplicity to control the spectral components and their evolution in time. Such dynamic spectra are diverse in their subjective impressions and include sounds both known and unknown.
Name: ["Chowning John M."]

Title: Suboptimal adaptive control of a class of non-linear systems‚Ä†
Abstract: The problem of controlling a class of nonlinear systems with uncertain parameters and imprecisely defined system and measurement noise terms is considered. A sub-optimal adaptive control algorithm is developed as a solution to coupled linear modelling and control optimization problems. Features of the algorithm are the forward-recursive generation of the modelling and control processes and necessity for past and present values of states and parameters alone in order to implement the algorithm (i.e. no precomputed nominal trajectory is required). These features make the algorithm ideally suited to real-time control applications Real-time control of a non-trivial fifth-order system, (a model of a plasma torch furnace) is considered and the results of an experimental study are presented. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Luxat J.C.", "Lees L.H."]
Affiliations: [' University of Windsor', ' University of Witwatersrand']

Title: Causality, stability and inverse systems
Abstract: A definition of linear systems is given in terms of convolution operations using a sequence of Markov matrices. A sequence of (block) Toeplitz matrices is constructed from the set of Markov matrices and is shown to act as a sequence of input-output maps for system records. Inverse systems and minimum phase systems are defined and properties including causality and stability established. These results are used to examine system input sequences which produce zero output sequences. Applications in identification theory are indicated. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Caines P.E."]

Title: EMPIRICAL COMPARISON OF MODELS FOR SHORT RANGE FORECASTING.
Abstract: Results of a simulation study of the short-range forecasting effectiveness of exponentially smoothed and selected Box-Jenkins models for sixty-three monthly sales series are presented. Tabular data are presented to show the average percent error, and the ranking of the models for both the one-month forecast and the cumulative six-month forecast for the sixty-three actual sales series. The average value of the smoothing parameter is shown for the models smoothed with the recurrence equations. The average percentage of errors for each model for five synthetic data series, plus forecasting results on the series, are also described.
Name: ["Groff Gene K."]

Title: Punish/Reward: Learning with a Critic in Adaptive Threshold Systems
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: An adaptive threshold element is able to ‚Äúlearn‚Äù a strategy of play for the game blackjack (twenty-one) with a performance close to that of the Thorp optimal strategy although the adaptive system has no prior knowledge of the game and of the objective of play. After each winning game the decisions of the adaptive system are ‚Äúrewarded.‚Äù After each losing game the decisions are ‚Äúpunished.‚Äù Reward is accomplished by adapting while accepting the actual decision as the desired response. Punishment is accomplished by adapting while taking the desired response to be the opposite of that of the actual decision. This learning scheme is unlike ‚Äúlearning with a teacher‚Äù and unlike ‚Äúunsupervised learning.‚Äù It involves ‚Äúbootstrap adaptation‚Äù or ‚Äúlearning with a critic.‚Äù The critic rewards decisions which are members of successful chains of decisions and punishes other decisions. A general analytical model for learning with a critic is formulated and analyzed. The model represents bootstrap learning per se. Although the hypotheses on which the model is based do not perfectly fit blackjack learning, it is applied heuristically to predict adaptation rates with good experimental success. New applications are being explored for bootstrap learning in adaptive controls and multilayered adaptive systems. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Widrow B.", "Gupta N.K.", "Maitra S."]

Title: ITERATIVE PROCEDURE FOR THE SINGLE-MACHINE MULTI-PRODUCT LOT SCHEDULING PROBLEM.
Abstract: This paper describes an iterative procedure for directly determining near optimal frequencies of production for the products and the associated fundamental cycle time which, in many cases, can be used directly for constructing production schedules. In cases where feasible schedules cannot bconstructed using the values from the iterative procedure, the procedure provides a basis for changing the production frequencies and the fundamental cycle time to obtain feasible schedules.
Name: ["Doll C.Loren", "Whybark D.Clay"]

Title: The Design of Optimal Compensators for Linear Constant Systems with Inaccessible States
Abstract: This paper considers the problem of designing an optimal linear time-invariant dynamic compensator for the regulation of an nth-order linear time-invariant plant. The usual quadratic cost on the state and control is averaged over initial plant state values. The globally optimal compensator gains and dynamic order are determined by showing that this problem is mathematically identical to a steady-state stochastic control problem whose optimal solution is known. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Rom D.B.", "Sarachik P.E."]
Affiliations: [' New York University', 'Bell Laboratories', ' New York University Science']

Title: ON A CLASS OF STOCHASTIC OPTIMIZATION PROBLEMS WITH A SPECIFIED GROWTH PATTERN.
Abstract: Author considers a system which consists of several subsystems. The outputs of these subsystems satisfy linear difference equations which specify the growth pattern of the output of the system over time. The state of each subsystem is described by a finite Markov chain, the transition probabilities of which are subject to our control. Associated with the Markov chain of each subsystem is a cost per unit output of the subsystem, and the cost is incurred as the subsystem occupies one of the J states in each epoch. The problem of minimizing the total expected cost with respect to the transition probabilities over a sufficiently long period of time is shown under certain conditions to reduce a collection of n independent programs. Each of these can be solved by column generation techniques.
Name: ["Nakamura Masao"]

Title: On the Adaptive Control of Linear Systems Using the Open-Loop-Feedback-Optimal Approach
Abstract: This paper considers the suboptimal stochastic control of linear discrete-time dynamical systems with uncertain or stochastically varying parameters. The suboptimal scheme is based upon the use of the open-loop-feedback-optimal (OLFO) method. The state and parameter estimates are generated by an extended Kalman filter algorithm. Numerical results for first-order systems are presented. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Ku R.", "Athans M."]

Title: DISCRETE MATCHED FILTER FOR SIGNALS IN THE FORM OF WALSH FUNCTIONS.
Source: Telecommunications and Radio Engineering (English translation of Elektrosvyaz and Radiotekhnika)
Abstract: An algorithm of an optimal discrete filter for signals in the form of Walsh functions, required for processing N input values of N log//2 N computational operations is considered. Its connection with the well-known algorithm for the fast Walsh transformation is pointed out. Methods of constructing such a filter are described.
Name: ["Trakhtman V.A."]

Title: Fuzzy planner: Reasoning with inexact concepts in a procedural problem-solving language
Abstract: All contemporary deductive problem-solving paradigms deal with a world in which assertions are true (false) and action-rules valid (invalid). This simplified situation is inadequate for realistic applications which include inexact information. This report describes a precise computationally specific method for coupling two different many-valued logics with a procedural problem-solving system (micro-PLANNER). Solutions to deductive problems can be found which meet specific criteria of validity. This particular scheme enables the system to dynamically compute the truth-value of a subgoal during the search process. Thus, the validity of a subgoal may be used to direct the heuristic search procedure. Fuzzy PLANNER is a promising medium for experimenting with different many-valued logics to find the ones most appropriate for different problem domains. However, the notions elaborated here are relevent to any procedural problem-solving language. ¬© 1974 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Kling R."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF STATIONARY LINEAR SYSTEMS OF GIVEN STRUCTURE USING INTEGRAL PERFORMANCE CRITERIA.
Abstract: The optimal parameters of a stationary linear system under an integral performance criterion are determined for initial conditions belonging to an (n plus 1)-dimensional manifold specified by a positive-definite quadratic form.
Name: ["Aslanyan A.E."]

Title: Optimum Rank Rule for Signal Detection in Noise with Unknown Distribution.
Abstract: 8 refs. In Russian.
Name: ["Prokof'ev V.N.", "Shishkin A.D."]

Title: Textural Features for Image Classification
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: Texture is one of the important characteristics used in identifying objects or regions of interest in an image, whether the image be a photomicrograph, an aerial photograph, or a satellite image. This paper describes some easily computable textural features based on graytone spatial dependancies, and illustrates their application in category-identification tasks of three different kinds of image data: Photomicrographs of five kinds of sandstones, 1:20 000 panchromatic aerial photographs of eight land-use categories, and Earth Resources Technology Satellite (ERTS) multispecial imagery containing seven land-use categories. We use two kinds of decision rules: One for which the decision regions are convex polyhedra (a piecewise linear decision rule), and one for which the decision regions are rectangular parallelpipeds (a min-max decision rule). In each experiment the data set was divided into two parts, a training set and a test set. Test set identification accuracy is 89 percent for the photomicrographs, 82 percent for the aerial photographic imagery, and 83 percent for the satellite imagery. These results indicate that the easily computable textural features probably have a general applicability for a wide variety of image-classification applications. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Haralick R.M.", "Dinstein I.", "Shanmugam K."]
Affiliations: [' University of Kansas', ' Wichita State University']

Title: ALGORITHM FOR THE SPECTRAL ANALYSIS OF MANY-COMPONENT SUBSTANCES.
Abstract: In the algorithm proposed for the spectroscopic analysis of many-component substances, each stage of the analytical procedure is optimized and use is made of optimum-experiment theory which enables one to obtain estimates of the composition with a minimum dispersion within the class of linear estimates, and also to minimize the systematic errors in the analysis.
Name: ["Makulov N.A."]

Title: DIGITAL-SUMMATION THRESHOLD-LOGIC GATES: A NEW CIRCUIT ELEMENT.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: Threshold-logic gates are memoryless, multiple-binary-input single-binary-output circuits that operate by an arithmetic summation process to determine the 0 or 1 gate output state. The availability of such gates would be of great advantage to ditigal system design. A new approach to the circuit realization of such gates is presented, i. e. to use digital-summation techniques within the gate circuitry, as distinct from the analog-summation techniques previously employed. The adoption of digital summation removes the former circuit-tolerance problems, and allows gates with great potential usefulness to be readily designed.
Name: ["Hurst S.L."]

Title: LINEAR ALGORITHM FOR COMPUTING THE OPTIMUM UNIVERSITY TIMETABLE.
Abstract: An algorithm for computing a timetable for a university department is discussed. The problem is formulated in terms of costs associated with features of the timetable, including the interaction between courses. The algorithm finds a globally optimal solution using a linear mathematical model.
Name: ["Akkoyunlu E.A."]

Title: Universal Noiseless Coding
Abstract: Universal coding is any asymptotically optimum method of block-to-block memoryless source coding for sources with unknown parameters. This paper considers noiseless coding for such sources, primarily in terms of variable-length coding, with performance measured as a function of the coding redundancy relative to the per-letter conditional source entropy given the unknown parameter. It is found that universal (i.e., zero redundancy) coding in a weighted sense is possible if and only if the per-letter average mutual information between the parameter space and the message space is zero. Universal coding is possible in a maximin sense if and only if the channel capacity between the two spaces is zero. Universal coding is possible in a minimax sense if and only if a probability mass function exists, independent of the unknown parameter, for which the relative entropy of the known conditional-probability mass-function is zero. Several examples are given to illustrate the ideas. Particular attention is given to sources that are stationary and ergodic for any fixed parameter although the whole ensemble is not. For such sources, weighted universal codes always exist if the alphabet is finite, or more generally if the entropy is finite. Minimax universal codes result if an additional entropy stability constraint is applied. A discussion of fixed-rate universal coding is also given briefly with performance measured by a probability of error. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Davisson L.D."]

Title: DISCOVERY OF PHYSICAL LAWS BY GMDH METHOD WITH THE ABSENCE-OF-BIAS CRITERION.
Abstract: By using an external complement (selection criterion) in multilayer GMDH selection algorithms, it is possible to obtain a unique (objective) mathematical model of a complex plant on the basis of a small number of experimental data. The choice of the selection criterion must be appropriate. The most exact models for simple prediction can be obtained using the regularity criterion. For the discovery of laws governing the behavior of plants (a ‚Ä≥physical model‚Ä≥ ), it is recommended that a new selection criterion be used, namely, that the estimates of the coefficients must be unbiased. In the case of open-loop plants and exact data (without noise), the results yielded by the regularity criterion and by the unbiasedness criterion will be the same, so that these criteria are then equivalent. Three examples of discovery of laws are presented.
Name: ["Ivakhnenko A.G.", "Shervashidze V.V.", "Shelud'ko O.I.", "Patereu S.G.", "Ivakhnenko N.A."]

Title: Dynamic Analog Synthesizer of Human Vocal Tract. | SYNTHETISEUR ANALOGUE DYNAMIQUE DU CONDUIT VOCAL.
Abstract: Starting with a brief survey of the principle of the terminal analog speech synthesizer, a description of a dynamic analog synthesizer of the human vocal tract is given. Special emphasis is put on the realization of the elementary cell of the artifical electrical line. This realization is characterized by its command simplicity and facility. Finally, some possible improvements as well as studies on a complete system for speech synthesis is given.
Name: ["Guerin B."]

Title: Technological Basis for Automation of Continuous Control of Start-Up of Power Units with Once-Through Boilers. | TEKHNOLOGICHESKAYA OSNOVA AVTOMATIZATSII NEPRERYVNOGO UPRAVLENIYA PUSKOM ENERGOBLOKOV S PRYAMOTOCHNYMI KOTLAMI.
Abstract: Algorithms of control of start-up operations of power units with once-through boilers are considered. Principal features of the algorithms and requirements with respect to automatic devices at each stage of start-up and with regard to standardized technology are pointed out.
Name: ["Kozlov V.N.", "Leizerovich A.Sh.", "Livshits M.A.", "Doverman G.I."]

Title: Complete Test Sets for Logic Functions
Abstract: The problem of designing fault detecting test sets from the functional description rather than the structural description of the networks realizing the logic function is studied. The concept of an expanded truth table for logic functions is introduced. It is proved that the set of minimal true vertices and maximal false vertices of the expanded truth table constitutes a test set to detect any number of stuck-at-faults in a network belonging to a class of restricted networks, called unate gate networks. It is further indicated that even in the presence of redundancies in the network, the test sets given remain valid. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Reddy S.M."]
Keywords: ["complete test sets", "expanded truth table", "fault detect", "ing test sets", "logic network"]

Title: INTERACTIVE USE OF A TIME-SHARED PROCESS CONTROL COMPUTER IN ELECTROPHOTOGRAPHIC SENSITOMETRY.
Source: IBM Journal of Research and Development
Abstract: The usefulness of electrophotographic exposure sensitometry as means of characterizing and evaluating new photoconductor materials has been extended by coupling the experiment to an on-line computer. This automated system provides several new functional capabilities not realistically attainable in manual operation and drastically reduces the time lag in the exchange of information between research workers who prepare materials and those who evaluate the materials. These various improvements have been achieved by extensive use of interactive graphic techniques and a user-oriented data-base organization.
Name: ["Schechtman B.H.", "So S.S.", "Luttman E.W."]

Title: REGIONS OF ABSOLUTE STABILITY OF NONLINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A procedure is given for determining the arbitrary parameter q in the frequency criterion for absolute stability as a function of the system parameters, using mathematical programming.
Name: ["Aysagaliyev S.A."]

Title: Dynamic Programming as Applied to Feature Subset Selection in a Pattern Recognition System
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: This paper proposes dynamic programming search procedures to expedite the feature subset selection processes in a pattern recognition system. It is shown that in general the proposed procedures require much fewer subsets to be evaluated than the exhaustive search procedure. For example, a problem of selecting the best subset of 4 features from a set of 24 features requires an evaluation of (4) = 10626 subsets by using the exhaustive search procedure; on the other hand, it requires only 175 and 136 subsets to be considered by employing the proposed Procedures I and II, respectively, to solve the same problem. While the number of subsets to be evaluated for the dynamic programming search procedures is slightly greater than that for the without-replacement search procedure, the best feature subset selected by the proposed methods may, however, not necessarily contain all of the best single features selected in the previous stages. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Chang C.-Y."]

Title: A Heuristic Relaxation Method for Nonlinear Mapping in Cluster Analysis
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A relaxation method mapping high-dimensional sample points to low-dimensional sample points is discussed. This method tries to preserve the local interdistance of sample points. Some special heuristi√©s have been introduced to handle the difficulty arising from a large amount of data. Experimental results with handwritten character data and Iris data show that the method runs fast, converges rapidly, and requires a small amount of memory space. Title: Breadth-first search: Some surprising results
Abstract: Although breadth-first search procedures cannot explore truly large search spaces, actual implementations of such procedures can result in surprisingly powerful problem-solvers that outperform more sophisticated heuristic search procedures. We describe two breadth-first search procedures. The first one, S&R, proves theorems from Principia of Whitehead and Russell, and is compared to two versions of the Logic Theorist. Previous estimates of the size of the search space are significantly reduced. When theorems are proved in an optimal order, this order differs markedly from that found in Principia, while more general theorems than those of Principia are often found. The second system, S&M, adapts breadth-first search to locally infinite search spaces in systems of rewriting rules. S&M is compared extensively to the heuristic theorem-prover of Quinlan and Hunt, and to some other theorem provers. ¬© 1973.
