Title: Fast algorithms for the elimination of common subexpressions
Abstract: We give two algorithms for computing the set of available expressions at entrance to the nodes of a flow graph. The first takes O(mn) isteps on a program flow graph (one in which no node has more than two successors), where n is the number of nodes and m the number of expressions which are ever computed. A modified version of this algorithm requires O(n<sup>2</sup>) steps of an extended type, where bit vector operations are regarded as one step. We present another algorithm which works only for reducible flow graphs. It requires O(n log n) extended steps. ¬© 1973 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Ullman J.D."]

Title: MAN MACHINE INTERACTION IN MINICOMPUTER CONTROLLED TESTING APPLICATION.
Abstract: This paper organizes a theory of man machine interaction in which the total system utilizes the strength of human operators to augment the computational and measurement abilities of the computer. The systems used as examples include a minicomputer controlled test cell for evaluating the performance of a complex hydraulic system in a family of earth movers. Man-machine interaction is carried on via a video terminal (machine to man) and a keyboard (man to machine). In this system, the computer directly (via sensors) monitors the earth movers and communicates with the two inspectors in English via the CRT's. The second system discussed utilizes a test language for the development of special test procedures on a stand-alone programming console.
Name: ["Edwin Allan I."]

Title: AIRCRAFT TRANSITION ALGORITHM FOR CONFLICT PREDICTION, WITH SPECIFIC REFERENCE TO THE NORTH ATLANTIC AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL SYSTEM.
Source: Toronto Univ Inst Aerosp Stud UTIAS Tech Note
Abstract: The purpose of this project was to extend presently available digital fast-time Air Traffic Control conflict prediction simulation models. A simulation algorithm was designed for compatibility with the Gander Automated Air Traffic System (GAATS). The algorithm, intended for application to a multiple aircraft strategically controlled environment, functions to search, detect and resolve conflict situations during enroute aircraft transitioning. The simulation model includes meteorological data, route structure, flight trajectory construction, and a conflict resolution option.
Name: ["Mohr D.J."]

Title: AUTOMATIC PATH SPECIFICATION FOR THE AMC 71 MOBILITY MODEL.
Source: Stevens Inst Technol, Davidson Lab, Rep
Abstract: This report contains the description of a computer-based method for determining the family of routes from which the Route Selection Program of the AMC 71 Mobility Model can choose to determine the minimum-travel-time path of a vehicle over some terrain. It specifies what data and in what format it must be presented in order for the computer programs to construct a file that the Route Selection Program needs. Currently, the method is restricted to rectangular maps. The family of paths, which includes lateral path segments, can be altered without repeating the laborious initial work required to digitize and compile the map description. Also included is a brief study of the effects of changing the parameters of the path family on the overall transverse time of several vehicles.
Name: ["Jurkat M.Peter"]

Title: MODIFIED QUASILINEARIZATION ALGORITHM FOR OPTIMAL CONTROL PROBLEMS WITH NONDIFFERENTIAL CONSTRAINTS - 1. THEORY.
Abstract: This paper considers the numerical solution of optimal control problems involving a functional I subject to differential constraints, nondifferential constraints, and terminal constraints. The problem is to find the state x(t), the control u(t), and the parameter pi so that the functional is minimized, while the constraints are satisfied to a predetermined accuracy. A modified quasilinearization algorithm is developed. Its main property is the descent property in the performance index R, the cumulative error in the constraints and the optimality conditions.
Name: ["Miele A.", "Mangiavacchi A.", "Aggarwal A.K."]

Title: TRANSFORMATION OF FLOW DIAGRAMS INTO MAXIMALLY PARALLEL FORM.
Source: Sagamore Comput Conf on Parallel Process, Proc, Pap, Sagamore Lake
Abstract: The algorithmic transformation of flow diagrams into a goto- and variable-free parallel program representation is described. It is shown, how the control mechanism for these parallel programs works and that it exhibits dynamically maximum parallelism in a certain, well-defined sense. The method presented is new and gives the optimum that can be achieved in intra-task parallelism.
Name: ["Urschler G."]

Title: VARIATION IN VEHICLE HANDLING CAPABILITY UNDER GUSTY CONDITIONS.
Abstract: Vehicle handling characteristics are investigated both on the stability and the man-vehicle system. The closed loop system analyzed in this paper is made up of a model of a human operator which was developed at the Cornell Aeronautical Laboratories from actual driver responses obtained under simulated road conditions, and a lateral stability model of an automobile which has been modified to incorporate the effect of nonlinear tire performance. Both models are combined in this paper and are assumed to accurately represent a vehicle travelling down a level, straight road at a nominal speeed of 96. 5 k/hr where it suddenly encounters a transverse gust of wind. The purpose of the system model is to determine the stability of the man-machine combination under these conditions and thus also determine a measure of the handling characteristics using servo analysis techniques.
Name: ["Mahig J."]

Title: HOW TO RECOGNIZE A ‚Ä≥GOOD‚Ä≥ FORECAST.
Abstract: This paper adopts the viewpoint of the decisionmaker who has to evaluate a forecast he has been given. This viewpoint reflects the basic nature of all serious forecasts - they are of value only as inputs to decisions. They have no intrinsic value for any other purpose. The forecaster who has prepared a forecast for a decisionmaker should expect that his forecast will be given the type of analysis described herein, and should prepare that forecast in such a way that it will satisfy the analysis. There are a number of means for evaluating a forecast. The one presented here is known as an Interrogation Model, because it is based on asking a series of questions about the forecast. The sequence of questions is designed to provide an efficient search of the given forecast for those items which are critical in a specific situation. The model involves four steps: interrogation for need, interrogation for underlying cause, interrogation for relevance, and interrogation for reliability. For each step, specific questions are posed and their scope and significance are explained.
Name: ["Martino Joseph P."]

Title: Multiple-stage probabilistic information processing
Abstract: Human performance on hierarchical inferences may be suboptimum. As a means of improving this performance, it is suggested that a hierarchical inference task be decomposed into a series of simpler intuitive inferences linking each stage in the hierarchy and that assessments of these inferences be formally combined using the optimum hierarchical model. The results of laboratory experiments with this procedure show that it can improve performance over a completely intuitive approach. A case study in which the procedure was applied to a real world inference problem is also described and some practical difficulties are identified. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Gettys C.", "Michel C.", "Steiger J.H.", "Kelly C.W.", "Peterson C.R."]

Title: On the Application of Discrete Transformations for Redundancy Reduction. | UEBER DIE ANWENDUNG DISKRETER TRANSFORMATIONEN ZUR REDUNDANZREDUKTION.
Abstract: This paper presents a method of encoding discrete sources of information for redundancy reduction using code words with fixed length. Considering a model of a linear encoded speech signal, the presented method was compared with a zero-order hold and with a Huffman encoding. The method is less efficient than the Huffman encoding but much more efficient than the zero-order hold.
Name: ["Sappl E."]

Title: SPOKEN DIGIT RECOGNITION USING MULTI-CATEGORY LINEAR DISCRIMINANT FUNCTION.
Abstract: The ultimate goal of this research is speech recognition of a limited vocabulary in real time. A few parameters whicch represent vowel features were extracted from the output of a filter bank (Gaussian characteristics with Q equals 2) utilizing a multi-category linear discriminant function. The plane constructed from the first two of the parameters was found to give a good approximation to the F//1-F//2 diagram. This plane was applied to real time spoken digit recognition, the correct recognition rate being 80% without learning.
Name: ["Yasuhiro Teruo"]

Title: Testing flow graph reductibility
Source: Proceedings of the Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
Abstract: Many problems in program optimization have been solved by applying a technique called interval analysis to the flow graph of the program. A flow graph which is susceptible to this type of analysis is called reducible. This paper describes an algorithm for testing whether a flow graph is reducible. The algorithm uses depth-first search to reveal the structure of the flow graph and a good method for computing disjoint set unions to determine reducibility from the search information. When the algorithm is implemented on a random access computer, it requires 0(E logE) time to analyze a graph with E edges, where logx = minCillog11}. The time bound compares favorably with the 0(E log E) bound of a previously known algorithm. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Tarjan R."]

Title: Type two computational complexity
Source: Proceedings of the Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
Abstract: A programming language for the partial computable functionals is used as the basis for a definition of the computational complexity of functionals (type2 functions). An axiomatic account in the spirit of Blum is then provided. The novel features of this approach are justified by applying it to problems in abstract complexity, specifically operator speed-up, and by using it to define the illusive notion of the polynomial degree of an arbitrary function. New results are obtained for these degrees. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Constable R.L."]

Title: Recovery semantics for a DB/DC system
Source: Proceedings of the Annual ACM Conference, ACM 1973
Abstract: Presented is a unified, systematic view of integrity/recovery as it relates to a data-processing system - whether man, machine, or both. The concept, sphere of control (SOC), as a bound around a process, is developed to permit describing and solving many of the rather aggravating problems of auditability, repeatability, reproducibility, scheduling, consistency, recovery and general integrity. Identified are the relationships among resources and SOCs, the types of resource status which must be maintained, and the effects that dependency versus commitment has on process scheduling and recovery strategy. Virtually ignored are the problems of lost storage for which redundancy is a solution, mainly because information already exists in this realm. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Davies C.T., Jr."]

Title: Application of Optimal Smoothing Techniques to the Calibration of an Inertial Navigation System. | DIE ANWENDUNG OPTIMALER GLAETTUNGSTECHNIKEN BEI DER KALIBRIERUNG EINES TRAEGHEITSNAVIGATIONSSYSTEMS.
Abstract: Theoretical and experimental results are presented, showing that - compared with conventional gyrocompassing techniques - the application of optimal smoothing leads to a higher accuracy of the determination of gyro and accelerometer errors of an LN3-2A inertial platform. A description of the optimal smoother, consisting of a forward-KALMAN-filter and a backward-filter, is given. A calibration scheme is investigated, which avoids platform rotation. With this procedure the rapid determination of the sensor errors is possible with high accuracy.
Name: ["Winter H."]

Title: Methods for Parameter Insensitive Control System Design with Application to a Control Configured Vehicle (CCV). | METHODEN ZUR AUSLEGUNG EINES PARAMETERUNEMPFINDLICHEN REGELUNGSSYSTEMS UND IHRE ANWENDUNG FUER EIN AERODYNAMISCH INSTABILES FLUGZEUG (CCV).
Abstract: Methods for the design of parameter insensitive control systems are applied to control the longitudinal motion (flight path control) of a control configured vehicle (CCV). For nominal flight conditions the controller design is simplified by introducing reference trajectories and optimizing over the controller coefficients. Maintaining the nominal control system properties, its sensitivity with respect to plant parameter variations then is reduced in a direct way by a suitable readjustment of the controller structure and/or controller coefficients. Detailed simulation results illustrate the properties of the different control system designs.
Name: ["Hirzinger Gerd", "Kreisselmeier Gerhard", "Pietrass Alfred"]

Title: TELEOPERATORS: MANUAL/AUTOMATIC SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS.
Abstract: One particular type of man-machine system: the teleoperator is considered. The teleoperator is defined as a remotely controlled, cybernetic, man-machine system designed to extend and augment man's sensory, manipulative, and cognitive capabilities. In addition to being a man-machine system, the important distinguishing attributes of the teleoperator system are that it is remotely controlled, it exists for the purpose of extending and enhancing man's sensory, motor and cognitive capabilities and it offers total lower operational costs. The essential subsystems of a teleoperator system include the man, the remotely controlled device at the worksite, and the communications link between these two. The man is always in the control loop of a teleoperator system - as an active controller or as a supervisor, managing the performance of the system under some form of computer control. The remotely controlled device is the machine which actually performs the work for which the system is designed. The device incorporates sensors, feedback systems, manipulators, end effectors, guidance systems, communications devices, and mobility system as needed. The communicative link incorporates provision for transferring commands and control inputs from the man to the machine and for relaying system status information and feedback data back from the machine to the man. Proposed applications discussed include space exploration, industrial operations, prosthetic and orthotic devices, and health care.
Name: ["Janow Carl", "Malone Thomas B."]

Title: Convergence of optimum seeking procedures
Abstract: This paper is concerned with the analysis of problems connected with the convergence of optimum seeking procedures, and particularly with the method of planning the rate of convergence and thus influencing the quality of procedures. Local linearization of the relevant dynamic process is performed and quite general results are thus obtained. A solution of multistep algorithms is also presented. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["≈ΩEn√ç≈†Ek V.R."]

Title: Maximum likelihood identification of gaussian autoregressive moving average models
Abstract: SUMMARY: Closed form representations of the gradients and an approximation to the Hessian are given for an asymptotic approximation to the log likelihood function of a multidimensional autoregressive moving average Gaussian process. Their use for the numerical maximization of the likelihood function is discussed. It is shown that the procedure described by Hannan (1969) for the estimation of the parameters of one-dimensional autoregressive moving average processes is equivalent to a three-stage realization of one step of the Newton-Raphson procedure for the numerical maximization of the likelihood function, using the gradient and the approximate Hessian. This makes it straightforward to extend the procedure to the multidimensional case. The use of the block Toeplitz type characteristic of the approximate Hessian is pointed out. ¬© 1973 Oxford University Press.
Name: ["Akaike H."]
Keywords: ["autoregressive moving average process", "block toeplitz matrix", "hessian", "identification", "maximum likelihood"]

Title: Bayesian sequential estimation of a poisson process rate
Abstract: SUMMARY: This paper provides numerical and analytical solutions to the problem of estimating the rate of a Poisson process. Optimal designs are obtained for various loss functions and the method of analysis is valid for any other loss function. The cost of sampling plays a fundamental role and since there are many practical situations where there is a time cost and an event cost, a sampling cost per observed event and a cost per unit time are both included. ¬© 1973 Oxford University Press.
Name: ["El-Sayyad G.M.", "Freeman P.R."]
Keywords: ["dynamic programming", "poisson process", "preposterior analysis", "sequential decision theory", "sequential sampling"]

Title: The naive rule for reconstructing a noisy Markov chain
Abstract: SUMMARY: An observer desires to record a realization of a stationary two-state Markov chain X, but experimental conditions are such that he instead sees a realization of a sequence Y subject to error. The objective is to reconstruct X. The naive reconstruction rule is that rule which assumes that X is a sequence of independent random variables and selects X<sub>i</sub>, the reconstructed X<sub>i</sub>, using only Y<sub>i</sub>. A necessary and sufficient condition is given for the naive rule to be the optimal reconstruction rule. ¬© 1973 Oxford University Press.
Name: ["Devore J.L."]
Keywords: ["naive reconstruction rule", "observable error sequence", "optimal reconstruction of a stochastic sequence", "unobservable markov chain", "reconstruct naive"]

Title: n-Dimensional array languages and description of crystal Symmetry-II
Source: Proceedings of the Indian Academy of Sciences - Section A
Abstract: In this paper the array models are generalized to n-dimensions and these are seen to preserve a natural hierarchy among different families corresponding to a partial ordering induced in n-tuples of integers. The n-dimensional array models are closed under union, concatenation (in all directions), Kleene closure (in all directions) and Œµ-free general homo-morphlsm. Symmetry operations such as translation, reflection about co-ordinate planes, rotation through angles œÄ/2 and œÄ about the co-ordinate axes, inversion about the origin and conjugation are examined. Three-dimensional matrix models are used to generate space groups of three-dimensional crystallography. Certain regular solids such as the cube, the tetrahedron, the octohedron, prisms and pyramids are generated using the array models to describe the growth of crystals. ¬© 1973 Indian Academy of Sciences.
Name: ["Siromoney R.", "Krithivasan K.", "Siromoney G."]

Title: PROBLEM OF APPLYING INFORMATION THEORY TO EFFICIENT IMAGE TRANSMISSION.
Abstract: Shannon's theory of source encoding with a fidelity constraint, more commonly known as rate distortion theory, was specifically intended to provide a theoretical basis for efficient transmission of information such as images. Twenty five years have passed with only minor impact of the theory on the problem. The author points out what the theory has to contribute to the problem, two difficulties that impeded application of the theory to image transmission, and current efforts to solve these difficulties.
Name: ["Sakrison David J."]

Title: SOME RESULTS IN COMPUTER-AIDED TEST GENERATION.
Abstract: Computer-aided generation of production tests for logic involves four steps. These steps are: 1) Logic description, or describing the logic in a form suitable for computer processing; 2) Test pattern generation, which may be automatic or manual; 3) Simulation of test patterns to determine expected outputs; and 4) Translation of the resulting stimulus-response sequence to a form understandable by the tester. The steps in the process are discussed, and the system capabilities required for each are described.
Name: ["Hickman John I.", "Shiner John F.", "Fike John L."]

Title: Optimal strategies for a class of adaptive search processes
Source: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
Abstract: Optimal strategies are investigated for a class of one-dimensional search processes in which the objective is to find a point which is near, but not beyond, a boundary of uncertain location. Problems of this type are encountered in the analysis of mining operations. Upper and lower bounds for the optimal expected payoff are derived, and the optimal search strategies are described explicitly for a large subclass of these processes. Results are obtained by formulating the search as a multistage decision process and using a dynamic programming approach. ¬© 1973 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Willman W.W."]

Title: A class of loss functions of catenary form
Abstract: The catenary form of loss function is considered in the framework of Bayesian decision theory. The mathematical tractability of this form seems to be unrecognized; it contains quadratic loss as a limiting case. For various probability distributions expressions are given for posterior analysis, and limiting properties are investigated. ¬© 1973 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Raeside D.E.", "Owen R.J."]
Keywords: ["bayesian estimation theory", "loss functions", "non-mean-square error criterion", "parameter estimation", "quadratic loss function"]

Title: Mechanizable proofs about parallel processes
Source: 14th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory
Abstract: This paper attempts to use formal semantics of a class of parallel processes in order to carry out mechanizable proofs about them. The formalism used is LCF (Logic for Computable Functions, Milner [22]), with slight extensions. The processes we consider communicate by sharing memory, rather than by signals on communication lines. Parallelism is treated as nondeterminism. We state properties such as mutual exclusion of critical sections, absence of deadlocks, determinacy, and we show examples of proofs. ¬© 1973 IEEE.
Name: ["Cadiou J.M.", "Levy J.J."]

Title: A model implementation for protective domains
Source: International Journal of Computer & Information Sciences
Abstract: A combination hardware/software mechanism is presented which supports very general capabilities for the protection of and controlled access to sharable information structures. It is defined through symbolic algorithms in terms of the dedicated model hardware. The model centers on two key concepts, that of the tenant, who is a "storage holding" entity, and that of the domain, which is an "information accessing" entity. The domain, defined as "a capsular collection of mutually accessible information structures having a single common external protective interface," is an integral part of the hardware logic. It is contended that the definition of a mechanism to enforce access authorizations must include an underlying philosophy specifying the conditions under which such access authorizations may be granted. Such a philosophy is suggested. It is based on the principle of ownership according to which any area of storage is at all times held by a single tenant who has the exclusive right to grant/revoke access privileges to his proprietary information structures, i.e., information residing in proprietary storage. ¬© 1973 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Spier M.J."]

Title: ASYMPTOTIC BEHAVIOR OF THE LINEAR PROGNOSIS ERROR FOR A CLASS OF STOCHASTIC PROCESSES.
Abstract: Estimates are obtained for certain quantities, related to the error of prognosis, for a certain class of stochastic processes. It turns out that these quantities decay according to a power law.
Name: ["Genis A.L."]

Title: Variable-precision exponentiation
Abstract: A previous paper presented an efficient algorithm, called the Recomputation Algorithm, for evaluating a rational expression to within any desired tolerance on a computer which performs variable-precision arithmetic operations. The Recomputation Algorithm can be applied to expressions involving any variable-precision operations having O(10<sub>-p</sub> + ‚àë | Œµ<sub>i</sub> |) error bounds, where p denotes the operation's precision and Œµ<sub>i</sub> denotes the error in the operation's ith argument. This paper presents an efficient variable-precision exponential operation with an error bound of the above order. Other operations, such as log, sin, and cos, which have simple series expansions, can be handled similarly. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Richman P.L."]

Title: RECOGNITION OF MISSPELLED KEYWORDS.
Abstract: An algorithm for use by compilers in recognizing misspelled keywords is described.
Name: ["Kellerman E."]

Title: Nonlinear Filter Evaluation for Estimating Vehicle Position and Velocity Using Satellites
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: Approximate nonlinear filtering theory is applied to the estimation of vehicle position and velocity in three demensions using sequential range measurements to three known locations. The particular case studied is a satellite air traffic control system which utilizes range measurements to two geostationary satellites and an altitude measurement. Three approximate filters are examined as suboptimal realizations of the minimum-variance filter and simulation results are presented to show that simple first-order approximation is an adequate representation. The parametric relationship between state covariance, measurement noise, vehicle maneuver structure, data rate, and system geometry is presented. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Wilson S.G."]

Title: Multiprocessor self diagnosis. Surgery, and recovery in air terminal traffic control
Source: Proceedings of the 4th ACM Symposium on Operating Systems Principles, SOSP 1973
Abstract: In order to meet the increasing need for more complex automated air terminal systems, Sperry Univac developed a unique failsafe-fahsoft multiprocessor executive program that will serve as the software basis for enhancements to present day ARTS ill systems. The executive provides the overall control of the multiprocessor data processing subsystem, failure detection and recovery sequence, and the execution of the air traffic control tasks. ¬© Proceedings of the 4th ACM Symposium on Operating Systems Principles, SOSP 1973. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Walther W."]

Title: ON THE REPRESENTATION OF WALSH FUNCTIONS AND FAST WALSH TRANSFORM ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: For the binary-ordered Walsh-Paley functions, sequency-ordered Walsh-Kaczmarz functions and Kronecker-ordered Walsh-Hadamard functions, the definitions and mathematical properties which are significant for practical applications are established in a systematic way and the mutual mappings of each of these systems onto each other are presented. The theory of linear transformations with Walsh functions is described and a method for the systematic construction Fast Walsh Transform algorithms is given. This method is applicable for all systems of ordering of the Walsh functions. By means of this method some Fast Walsh Transform algorithms are presented in a novel wayas certain matrix factorizations. For the computation of Walsh functions, Walsh matrices, and Fast Walsh Transforms a collection of ALGOL 60 procedures is also given.
Name: ["Kremer H."]

Title: FAST-CONVERGING EQUALIZER ALGORITHM FOR DIGITAL COMMUNICATION.
Abstract: A new equalizer algorithm is discussed which improves the convergence speed of the tap gains of a transversal filter type automatic equalizer which is generally used in the field of data communications in order to equalize the frequency characteristics of channels. Typically ZF (zero force) and MSE (mean square error) equalizers have been used. An algorithm for rapidly obtaining the optimum tap gains of ZF equalizer, which is simple in construction and easy to implement, is described. In this algorithm, simultaneous linear equations whose coefficients are the values of the single test pulse sampled at T-second intervals and whose unknown numbers are the optimum tap gains are solved by calculating the approximate inverse matrix, when the initial distortion satisfies a certain criterion.
Name: ["Tachibana Makoto", "Sata Hiroshi"]

Title: System of Optimal Planning of Underground Mining Work and Stages of Its Introduction. | [SISTEMA OPTIMAL'NOGO PLANIROVANIYA PODZEMNYKH GORNYKH RABOT I ETAPY EE VNEDRENIYA.]
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii, Gornyi Zhurnal
Abstract: Possibilities are considered for the introduction of a system of optimal planning of mining work at underground ore mines. On the basis of an analysis of optinum planning problems it is shown that some of them can be solved manually. Others require periodical use of a computer, though once a year or once a month only, which makes utilization of computing centers in different cities for their solution feasible. This justifies the division of the process of introduction of this system into four stages. Introduction of the system by stages considerably extends the field of its application at ore mines and creates favorable conditions for future introduction of automatic control systems, including an optimal work planning system at the enterprises.
Name: ["Roginskii F.N."]

Title: MEASUREMENT OF THE IMPEDANCE BY AUTOMATIC ADJUSTMENT OF A PHYSICAL MODEL.
Abstract: A description is given of the construction of an instrument for measuring the impedance using a physical model. The model has to be adjusted in such a way that its differential equation corresponds with that of the unknown impedance; that is, the impedance measurement employs parameter-estimation techniques. For the implementation of model and adjustment mechanism, standard hybrid computer components are used. The test signal also is easily implemented and is composed in such a way that it is possible to measure three parameters of the impedance simultaneously with little dependence between the parameter adjustments. Some attention is paid to the stability problem.
Name: ["van de Ven H.H.", "Gisling A.P.", "Eykhoff P."]

Title: Enumerative Source Encoding
Abstract: Let S be a given subset of binary n-sequences. We provide an explicit scheme for calculating the index of any sequence in S according to its position in the lexicographic ordering of S. A simple inverse algorithm is also given. Particularly nice formulas arise when S is the set of all n-sequences of weight k and also when S is the set of all sequences having a given empirical Markov property. Schalkwijk and Lynch have investigated‚Äô the former case. The envisioned use of this indexing scheme is to transmit or store the index rather than the sequence, thus resulting in a data compression of (log|S|)/n. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Cover T.M."]

Title: NEW CODE TRANSLATOR FOR THE LETTER-SORTING SYSTEM - 1. POSTCODES AND THEIR USE.
Abstract: Operational experience obtained from using the code-sorting system for handling letter mail has led to changes in its concept and, hence, to changes in facilities required of the machines. The decision to concentrate all sorting into about 100 offices has led to changes in the British Postcode and to changes in the way machine codes printed on envelopes are used to control the sorting operation. Part 1 describes some of the features which have influenced the development of the Postcode and explains how codes are used to control the sorting of letter mail. Subsequent parts will describe the design of the new translator which has been developed to provide the new facilities now seen to be required.
Name: ["Andrews J.D."]

Title: The Representation and Matching of Pictorial Structures Representation
Abstract: The primary problem dealt with in this paper is the following. Given some description of a visual object, find that object in an actual photograph. Part of the solution to this problem is the specification of a descriptive scheme, and a metric on which to base the decision of ‚Äúgoodness‚Äù of matching or detection. We offer a combined descriptive scheme and decision metric which is general, intuitively satisfying, and which has led to promising experimental results. We also present an algorithm which takes the above descriptions, together with a matrix representing the intensities of the actual photograph, and then finds the described object in the matrix. The algorithm uses a procedure similar to dynamic programming in order to cut down on the vast amount of computation otherwise necessary. One desirable feature of the approach is its generality. A new programming system does not need to be written for every new description; instead, one just specifies descriptions in terms of a certain set of primitives and parameters. There are many areas of application: scene analysis and description, map matching for navigation and guidance, optical tracking, stereo compilation, and image change detection. In fact, the ability to describe, match, and register scenes is basic for almost any image processing task. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Fischler M.A.", "Elschlager R.A."]

Title: FULLY-AUTOMATED FREIGHT TRAINS: FIVE SYSTEMS SHOW THE WAY.
Abstract: It is reported that North America has two standard-gage automated mineral railways in commercial operation on which no train crews are employed, and others are under construction. The author analyzers the cybernetic elements required for the operation of these unmanned freight trains, and points out that it could be possible to apply the same techniques to railroads with more elaborate traffic patterns.
Name: ["Mellitt Brian"]

Title: Methods for Simulating Continuous Dynamic Systems on an ODRA 1204 Computer. | METODY SYMULACJI NA MASZYNIE CYFROWEJ CIAGLYCH OBIEKTOW DYNAMICZNYCH.
Abstract: Three methods are presented for simulating dynamic systems with continuous input signals. They are based on the following methods of solving ordinary differential equations: the difference method, the method of fundamental solutions and the Runge-Kutta method. These methods are compared as to computing time and accuracy. All calculations have been carried out on an ODRA 1204 electronic digital computer. Advice is offered on choosing the most suitable method for a given simulation problem.
Name: ["Kowalska Elzbieta", "Studzinski Jan"]

Title: Stochastic Automata Models with Applications to Learning Systems
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The performance of variable-structure stochastic automata in stationary random environments has been extensively studied for the case when the environment's response is 0 or 1 (P model). A method is suggested for extending the updating schemes known for the P model to the S model, where the environment's output can lie in the interval [0,1], and a class of optimal nonlinear schemes for the S model is derived. Computer simulations reveal the superior performance of the S model in multimodal search even when the bounds on the performance function are unknown. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Viswanathan R.", "Narendra K.S."]

Title: MICROPROGRAMMED COMPUTER DESIGN AND EVALUATION SYSTEM.
Abstract: The system is a powerful tool for either architecture or hardware design. The design with quantitative evaluation is performed and the production documents can be obtained. The system consists of two subsystems. MPGS, a software subsystem, translates the description of a target machine written in a high level language into the equivalent microprogram sequences on a host machine. Many convenient features are provided to generate efficient code for similation, such as user defined translation control, and file management facilities. GPMS, a hardware subsystem, is a microprogrammed simulator, which rapidly simulates various models by changing its writable microprogram memory. In addition, simulation time and resource usage information of a model are measured during simulation. This cooperative software and hardware features make it possible to design a computer on more accurate evaluation data.
Name: ["Yamamoto Masahiro", "Hattori Mitsuhiro", "Yano Michiko", "Hakozaki Katsuya", "Kagiyama Keiichiro", "Fujino Kiichi"]

Title: Quasi-Optimum Digital Phase-Locked Loops
Abstract: Quasi-optimum digital phase-locked loops (DPLL) are derived utilizing nonlinear estimation theory. Nonlinear approximations are employed to yield realizable loop structures. Baseband equivalent loop gains are derived, which, under high signal-to-noise ratio conditions may be calculated off line. Additional simplifications are made that permit the application of the Kalman filter algorithms to determine the minimum mean-square error (MSE) loop filter. Consideration is given to sampling rate and implementation requirements. Performance is evaluated by a theoretical analysis and by simulation. Theoretical and simulated results are discussed and a comparison to analog results is made. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Polk D.R.", "Gupta S.C."]

Title: REFLEX Method for Empirical Optimization
Source: Industrial and Engineering Chemistry Process Design and Development
Abstract: While model development is rarely expedient, practical techniques for computer-based control and optimization without such models are notably few, and the unique character of model-based process control and optimization has prompted considerable theoretical attention. Empirical optimization methods are typically less restricted in applicability than error-free methods, but it is customarily assumed that the empirical methods are inherently inefficient. The REFLEX empirical optimization method presented is shown to be both efficient and directly applicable to model-free process control optimization. Both on-line and off-line tests of the REFLEX operation are given as appropriate measures of the performance of the optimization method. ¬© 1973, American Chemical Society. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Glass R.W.", "Bruley D.F."]

Title: Concerning Statistical Synthesis of Temperature and Antisurge Control Systems for Stationary Gas Turbine Plants. | O STATISTICHESKOM SINTEZE SISTEM TEMPERATURNOGO I PROTIVOPOMPAZHNOGO REGULIROVANIYA STATSIONARNYKH GTU.
Abstract: Using the example of the antisurge control system of a single-shaft gas turbine plant, a selection of the optimum values of the automatic control system parameters satisfying contradictory requirements with respect to these parameters is carried out. Linearized equations of the dynamics of the antisurge control system for gas turbine plant operation in a network with randomly changing load and presence of interference at the antisurge regulator input serve as the basis of calculation. The choice of the optimum parameters of the linear system of antisurge control is made on condition of minimization of the dispersion of the total mean quadratic error of the fuel valve.
Name: ["Shvets V.M."]

Title: Adaptive control utilizing optimally sensitive design techniques
Abstract: In the recent literature a control problem in which both the initial state vector as well as a vector of constant plant parameters ore unknown ha3 been treated utilizing sensitivity techniques referred to as optimally sensitive control. In this paper the concepts of optimally sensitive control as developed by Kokotovic, Perkins, Cruz and others are extended to the problem in which the state dynamics contain a vector of stochastic inputs which can be represented as Martingale processes. The resulting optimally sensitive system is shown to be an effective and realistic adaptive controller for systems containing unknown time-varying parameters. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the resulting control system at identifying and adapting to the levels of the unknown time-varying inputs. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Pedersen K.C.", "Nardizzi L.R."]

Title: Observer-Estimators for Discrete-Time Systems
Abstract: The theory of observer-estimators for linear discrete- time systems is described. Both deterministic and stochastic cases are considered; in particular, the case that some observations are noise free while others are noisy is considered. Asymptotic properties for both time-varying and time-invariant systems are analyzed and the influence of observability and detectability assumptions is considered. The results unify approaches to deterministic and stochastic state estimation problems for linear discrete-time systems. Optimal filtering in the presence of colored noise is considered as a special case. ¬© 1973 IEEE
Name: ["Tse E."]

Title: PERIODIC MODES IN PULSE WIDTH MODULATED CONTROL SYSTEMS BY A MODIFIED DISCRETE SEQUENCE METHOD.
Source: J Inst Telecommun Eng New Delhi
Abstract: A modified discrete sequence method is presented to identify possible periodic modes in a pulse with modulated (PWM) control system. The technique is based on expressing periodinc sequences in terms of exponential functions in the discrete sense and balancing the harmonics. With the recognition that a PWM system can be reduced to a sampled data system with saturations, the above exponential series is applied to the study of specific modes. This method makes it possible to determine whether a PWM control system has periodic modes and, if it does, to identify them exactly.
Name: ["Datta K.B."]

Title: HOW NEURAL ADAPTATION CHANGES CHROMATICITY COORDINATES.
Abstract: In a discussion of results on color-matching data previously obtained by Crawford and Richards, it is shown how the neural organization of the retina is related to color matching. Known neural interactions in the visual system suggest that observers do not set equal quantum absorptions on the two sides of the color field, and a model of the interaction is shown to account for the departures from the principles of trichromatic theory.
Name: ["Ingling Jr. Carl R.", "Drum Bruce A."]

Title: RECONSTRUCTION OF THE STATISTICAL STRUCTURE OF A DISCRETE SIGNAL.
Source: Telecommunications and Radio Engineering (English translation of Elektrosvyaz and Radiotekhnika)
Abstract: The results of measurements of the statistics of errors and distortions in a communications channel depend on how well the structure of the test signal approximates the structure of actual messages. Therefore the statistical structure of a pseudo-random sequence should approximate the real sequence with a given degree of accuracy. The principles of simulating the statistical structure of a signal are described taking into account the features of the code used. The method discussed permits the use of simple technical tools in order to solve the problem of reconstructing the statistical structure of a real signal in general form which is applicable to both the testing of communications channels and the investigation of digital data transmission systems by the simulation method.
Name: ["Brusilovskiy K.A."]

Title: ALGORITHMS FOR IDENTIFICATION OF OBJECTS WITH DISTRIBUTED PARAMETERS.
Abstract: A procedure is shown for simulating processes with distributed parameters by using integral operators. The identification of a mathematical model of a real object, in both statics and dynamics, is done using the theory of random functions. The procedure is illustrated with an example of simulation of an absorption process in a plate-like column.
Name: ["Antsypovich I.S.", "Lipatov L.N.", "Shkatov F."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF NONLINEAR CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The time expenditures are estimated in solving identification problems for nonlinear control systems by least squares. For the identification of nonlinear stochastic control systems a gradient search method is proposed. The computational algorithm of this method uses the methods of sensitivity theory.
Name: ["Kozeyev V.A."]

Title: A stereo field map with implications for disparity processing
Abstract: The neural basis for stereopsis may be divided into at least 2 components: one mechanism that processes divergent disparities and a second mechanism that processes convergent disparities. The most clearcut evidence for the presence of these 2 components is the finding that some individuals lack either one or the other. However, when the ability to process both convergent and divergent disparities is present in the same individual it is more difficult to demonstrate the presence of 2 separate mechanisms. The mechanisms for stereopsis are shown to consist of at least 2 components in the same individual. This demonstration is based upon a new kind of perimetry whereby field maps for stereopsis are plotted for both convergent and divergent disparities. Extensive measurements on one observer show that the zone of the visual field over which convergent disparities are processed may differ quite distinctively from the zone of the visual field over which divergent disparities are processed.
Name: ["Richards W.", "Regan D."]

Title: A new model for randomly organized associative memory
Abstract: We shall define associative recall as follows: 'Associative recall is an operation in which a memorized item is recalled by an arbitrary, sufficiently large known part of it' In our models for associative recall, memory traces are superimposed on certain engram elements in distributed form. In most models, memorized signals are reconstructed during recall. Reconstructivity places severe demands on physical systems, e.g., neural networks. In this model the reconstruction of items can be made virtually. ¬© 1973 Informa UK Ltd All rights reserved: reproduction in whole or part not permitted.
Name: ["Kohonen T."]

Title: Probabilistic recursive functions
Source: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society
Abstract: The underlying question considered in this paper is whether or not the purposeful introduction of random elements, effectively governed by a probability distribution, into a calculation may lead to constructions of number-theoretic functions that are not available by deterministic means. A methodology for treating this question is developed, using an effective mapping of the space of infinite sequences over a finite alphabet into itself. The distribution characterizing the random elements, under the mapping, induces a new distribution. The property of a distribution being recursive is defined. The fundamental theorem states that recursive distributions induce only recursive distributions. A function calculated by any probabilistic means is called 0-calculable. For a class of such calculations, these functions are recursive. Relative to Church‚Äôs thesis, this leads to an extension of that thesis: Every ‚Äòeffectively calculable function is recursive. In further development, a partial order on distributions is defined through the concept of * 'inducing.‚Äù It is seen that a recursive atom-free distribution induces any recursive distribution. Also, there exist distributions that induce, but are not induced by, any recursive distribution. Some open questions are mentioned. ¬© 1973 American Mathematical Society.
Name: ["Irwin M."]

Title: On the application of probabilistic distance measures for the extraction of features from imperfectly labeled patterns
Source: International Journal of Computer & Information Sciences
Abstract: A commonly used approach for feature selection is to select those features that extremize certain probabilistic distance measures. In most of the procedures it is assumed that the labels of the patterns are perfect. There are many practical situations in which the labels of the patterns are imperfect. This paper examines the applicability of the extremization of the Bhattacharyya distance, the divergence, equivocation, Kalmogrov variational distance, and Matusita distance as criteria for selecting the effective features from imperfectly identified patterns. ¬© 1973 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Babu C.C."]

Title: Scheduling of computer programs for optimal machine utilization
Abstract: This paper discusses the problem of developing schedules for the execution of computer programs in a batch oriented multiprogramming environment. An approximate approach to the problem is developed by heuristically reducing the dimensionality of the problem to a sequential optimization problem. The superiority of this heuristic criterion over five other commonly used criteria is shown. A numerical example is given. ¬© 1973 BIT Foundations.
Name: ["Thesen A."]

Title: Ein Darstellungsproblem bei der Vermaschung alternativer Parallelwege in Entscheidungsnetzen und seine L√∂sung
Abstract: In case of being connected by crossing paths alternative parallel paths in a decision network lead to a special node problem. At the points of confluence we find a difficulty in figuring of a node parameter. The present paper describes that problem and gives its solution. A practical example is given. ¬© 1973 Physica-Verlag.
Name: ["Burger H.", "Oesterer D."]

Title: COMPUTER CONTROL OF COLOR TELEVISION CAMERAS.
Abstract: Computer control of color television cameras is discussed. The relative merits and demerits of the individually controlled color camera system versus the centrally controlled color camera system are tabulated. Even in the centrally controlled system, a number of degrees are conceivable, depending on the scale. For instance: (i) A system of controlling a small number of cameras with an exclusive digital controller, (ii) A system of controlling a comparatively large number of cameras (several to several dozens) with an all-purpose minicomputer (control of devices other than cameras may be included), (iii) Large-scale control using a large-scale computer system, (iv) Hierarchy system combining (ii) and (iii). In this report, system(ii), which controls several to several dozen cameras using an all-purpose minicomputer of 8000 to 16,000 words, is discussed. The technique of detecting the position and level information in the picture at high speed and high accuracy from the video signal with noise, and a control algorithm for efficient and proper control on the basis of information obtained from the detector system have been discussed. The system is capable of completing the adjustment of the registration and color balance, which is necessary in the initial camera set up, in one to two seconds.
Name: ["Wakui Kotaro", "Murakami Keinosuke", "Endo Tsugio", "Kutsuwada Isamu", "Ozeki Kenji"]

Title: Error detection in precedence parsers
Abstract: We consider methods by which a precedence matrix may be modified without severely degrading the error-detecting capability of a parser utilizing the matrix. Two different definitions of "the same" error detection capability are considered. The first, called "exact equivalence", permits only useless parts of the precedence matrix to be modified. The second, called simply "equivalence", allows the modified matrix to perform some reductions, but never to shift an input symbol, after the original has detected an error. We give necessary and sufficient conditions for a modified precedence parser to be equivalent or exactly equivalent to the canonical parser. We then consider the interesting case where the modification is caused by replacing the precedence matrix by linear precedence functions. A simple algorithm to find (if they exist) exactly equivalent linear precedence functions for a given precedence matrix is presented. ¬© 1973 Springer-Verlag New York Inc.
Name: ["Aho A.V.", "Ullman J.D."]

Title: An extension of the theory of learning systems
Abstract: The author's inquiry [1] on learning systems is generalized in the following respects: The process of learning, instead of coming to an end when the learning goal has been reached, is supposed to last for ever, so that the above "definitive" learning as well as phenomena such as forgetting, re-learning, changing the goal etc. become describable. We take over the notion of semi-uniform solvability of a set Œì of learning problems (2.2), but now (trivial cases excluded) the whole capacity of a learning system is never s. u. solvable. Finite such sets Œì are. The notion of a solving-basis of some Œì is introduced and we can state necessary conditions that Œì possess such a basis (2.14), so that examples of sets Œì without a basis can be provided. On the other hand, any s. u. solvable Œì has as basis. The notion of uniform solvability (3.1) reinforces that of s. u. solvability, and there are given sufficient conditions for Œì to be uniformly solvable (3.6). In some "finite cases", s. u. solvability, existence of a basis and uniform solvability coincide (3.7-3.9). At last we give the construction for the weakest learning system solving a uniformly solvable problem set (3.12-3.19). ¬© 1973 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Menzel W."]

Title: Determining parameter values in the generalized image system
Abstract: Generalized image analysis is considered as a logical algebraic extension of Guttmanian image analysis. Under the assumption that a reduced-rank description of the images is desired, a procedure is developed which achieves the scale-free property by simultaneously rescaling in the metrics of both the images and anti-images, and which produces images and anti-images that are maximally independent in terms of the dimensions needed to account for them. ¬© 1973 Psychometric Society.
Name: ["Koopman R.F."]

Title: Texturerkennung und Texturreproduktion
Abstract: The recognition of textures involves multiple local filtering and subsequent averaging of the image to produce a feature space in which textures are represented as cluster centers. Results are presented for a two variate algorithm involving the features "brightness" and "roughness". Both regular and random textures generated by program are used. The final result of classification is expressed in terms of the original textures: the computer "paints" what it has seen - and makes rather understandable errors at the borders between different textures. ¬© 1973 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Triendl E.E."]

Title: On the random error propagation in relatively large networks
Abstract: A relatively large network is one which covers a large area whereas each observation only involves points within a small local area. For such networks an efficient method is described to establish the lower bounds for the spectral norm of the covariance matrix of the rigorously adjusted co-ordinates. The method utilizes a classification of observations and networks which is thought to be interesting in itself. The weakness of pure angular networks is revealed to stem from the fact that such networks offer little resistance to conformal distortions of the network. A numerical example is given. Asymptotic results for block-type networks are obtained which apply among others to photogrammetric bundle block networks. ¬© 1973 Academia, Publishing House of the Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences.
Name: ["Meissl P.", "Kub√°ƒçek L."]

Title: An approach via state estimation to differential games with information time lag
Abstract: This paper deals with zero-sum two-person differential games in which one player has a deferred information on the state vector. This player mends this lack of information by using an adaptative deterministic extrapolation to estimate the plant state, and then, makes his decisions by means of the datas so obtained. An analysis of the phenomenon yields a criterion for optimizing the estimation which is based upon the Hamiltonian estimation of the perfect information game. A class of extrapolators is given by its dynamical equation. Then, the initial game is reduced to a new game containing pure time delay in the state and the controls. ¬© 1973 Physica-Verlag Rudolf Liebing KG.
Name: ["Jumarie G."]

Title: Optimization of costly measurements in stochastic decision processes
Abstract: Two kinds of problems regarding measurement optimization in stochastic decision processes, when measurements are costly or constrained not to exceed a given number, have been investigated in the last years: the first one refers to the optimum timing of observations on the state vector of the process, while the second refers to the convenience of buying information on the random actions exerted by a stochastic environment. In this paper the two problems are considered from a unified point of view. In other words, the decision maker has to determine the optimal observation policy, under the assumption that both state and random vectors are measurable. A solution based on the application of dynamic programming is discussed for a general class of multistage processes. Analytical results are then obtained for scalar linear systems with quadratic cost on state and control. In this case, an efficient algorithm to determine the optimal sequence of measurements is presented, on the base of which a sensitivity analysis with respect to the process parameters is also carried out. ¬© 1973 Physica-Verlag.
Name: ["Puliafito P.P.", "Zoppoli R."]

Title: Preference aggregation and statistical estimation
Abstract: This paper deals with various connections that are found to exist between statistical estimation methods for decision-making and rules of group choice in the social choice area. Initially the aggregation of individual opinions is formulated as a pattern recognition problem; firstly it is shown that individual preferences lead to a natural representation in terms of binary patterns. Then we proceed to show how the search for a group preference pattern can be conducted by classifying the input preference patterns into various 'pattern classes' and using the resulting classification boundaries to define the area of mutual agreement over some of the available alternatives. This leads to a decision-theoretic problem which consists in defining a decision rule (for classification) that is least likely to lead to misrecognition of arbitrary preference patterns. A maximum likelihood solution is obtained and compared with some well-known rules of group decision-making. Other solutions are also possible, on the basis of different optimality criteria, and their social choice interpretation is suggested. Finally, a method using Coleman's linear model for attributes is applied to yield group decision rules by feature weighting of election issues. ¬© 1973 D. Reidel Publishing Company.
Name: ["Blin J.-M."]

Title: On the uniqueness of search directions in variable-metric algorithms
Source: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
Abstract: Generalized variable-metric algorithms presented in Ref. 1 produce a unique search direction independently of parameters in the algorithms under several conditions. They generate a unique sequence of minimizing points for the given initial conditions if the objective function is quadratic. ¬© 1973 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Adachi N."]
Affiliations: [' Faculty of Engineering in Kyoto University']

Title: Control extension in a recursive language
Abstract: Techniques for language extension are of interest today as a means for language design experimentation without language proliferation. Attention thus far has been focused on methods for data structure definition and manipulation. The problem of program control extensibility has been recognized by workers in the field but less thoroughly treated. This paper outlines an approach to control extensibility applicable on the source language level to appropriate programming languages. Using the recursive language LISP as an example, extensions are defined that provide call by name function parameters, generator functions (as in IPL-V), non-deterministic functions, and general coroutines. LISP facilitates this exercise by features including dynamic scope of variables, source programs manipulatable as data, simplicity of program state representations, and control over context of function evaluation. The results of this paper suggest criteria for evaluating base languages in extensible programming systems, as well as a possible insight into formal program analysis. ¬© 1973 BIT Foundations.
Name: ["Lindstrom G."]

Title: Scheduling Algorithms for Multiprogramming in a Hard-Real-Time Environment
Abstract: The problem of multiprogram scheduling on a single processor is studied from the viewpoint of the characteristics peculiar to the program functions that need guaranteed service. It is shown that an optimum fixed priority scheduler possesses an upper bound to processor utilization which may be as low as 70 percent for large task sets. It is also shown that full processor utilization can be achieved by dynamically assigning priorities on the basis of their current deadlines. A combination of these two scheduling techniques is also discussed. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Liu C.L.", "Layland J.W."]
Keywords: ["deadline driven scheduling", "dynamic scheduling", "multiprogram scheduling", "priority assignment", "processor utilization"]

Title: On the design of optimal output feedback control systems‚Ä†
Abstract: For a linear control system with quadratic performance index the optimal control takes a feedback form of all state variables. However, if there are some states which are not fed in the control system, it is impossible to obtain the optimal feedback control by using the usual mathematical optimization technique such as dynamic programming or the maximum principle. This paper presents the optimal control of output feedback systems for a quadratic performance index by using a new parameter optimization technique. Since the optimal feedback gains depend on the initial states in the output feedback control system, two cases where (1) the initial states are known, and (2) the statistical properties of initial states such as mean and covariance matrices are known, are considered here. Furthermore, the proposed method for optimal output feedback control is also applied to sampled-data systems. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Yahagi T."]

Title: The optimum traversal of a graph
Abstract: For a given graph (network) having costs [c<sub>ij</sub>] associated with its links, the present paper examines the problem of finding a cycle which traverses every link of the graph at least once, and which incurs the minimum cost of traversal. This problem (called the graph traversal problem, or the Chinese postman problem [9]) can be formulated in ways analogous to those used for the well-known travelling salesman problem, and using this apparent similarity, Bellman and Cooke [1] have produced a dynamic programming formulation. This method of solution of the graph traversal problem requires computational times which increase exponentially with the number of links in the graph. Approximately the same rate of increase of computational effort with problem size would result by any other method adapting a travelling salesman algorithm to the present problem. This paper describes an efficient algorithm for the optimal solution of the graph traversal problem based on the matching method of Edmonds [5, 6]. The computational time requirements of this algorithm increase as a low order (2 or 3) power of the number of links in the graph. Computational results are given for graphs of up to 50 vertices and 125 links. The paper then discusses a generalised version of the graph traversal problem, where not one but a number of cycles are required to traverse the graph. In this case each link has (in addition to its cost) a quantity q<sub>ij</sub> associated with it, and the sum of the quantities of the links in any one cycle must be less than a given amount representing the cycle capacity. A heuristic algorithm for the solution of this problem is given. The algorithm is based on the optimal algorithm for the single-cycle graph traversal problem and is shown to produce near-optimal results. There is a large number of possible applications where graph traversal problems arise. These applications include: the spraying of roads with salt-grit to prevent ice formation, the inspection of electric power lines, gas, or oil pipelines for faults, the delivery of letter post, etc. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Christofides N."]

Title: The dynamic clusters method in nonhierarchical clustering
Source: International Journal of Computer & Information Sciences
Abstract: Given a finite set E ‚äÇR<sup>n</sup>, the problem is to find clusters (or subsets of "similar" points in E) and at the same time to find the most typical elements of this set. An original mathematical formulation is given to the problem. The proposed algorithm operates on groups of points, called "samplings" ("samplings" may be called "multiple centers" or "cores"); these "samplings" adapt and evolve into interesting clusters. Compared with other clustering algorithms, this algorithm requires less machine time and storage. We provide some propositions about nonprobabilistic convergence and a sufficient condition which ensures the decrease of the criterion. Some computational experiments are presented. ¬© 1973 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Diday E."]

Title: Equivalence of the box-jenkins-astrom control law to the kalman linear regulator
Abstract: The letter demonstrates the equivalence of the BJA control law to the Kalman linear regulator for a class of single-input single-output stochastic LQP control problems. The result is obtained by comparing explicitly the two control laws derived for the same problem. ¬© 1973, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hughes D.J."]

Title: Approximation of two-person games with information exchange
Source: USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics
Abstract: The stability of the best guaranteed result and the approximation of the sets of strategies in games with information exchange are discussed. A method is outlined for solving bimatrix games with a fixed sequence of moves. ¬© 1975.
Name: ["Molodtsov D.A.", "Fedorov V.V."]

Title: On Functional Satisfying a Data-Processing Theorem
Abstract: It is shown that the rate-distortion bound (R(d) ‚â§ C) remains true when ‚àílog x in the definition of mutual information is replaced by an arbitrary concave (‚à™) nonincreasing function satisfying some technical conditions. Examples are given showing that for certain choices of the concave functions, the bounds obtained are better than the classical rate-distortion bounds. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Ziv J.", "Zakai M."]

Title: MULTIPLE REGRESSION APPROACH TO OPTIMAL DRILLING AND ABNORMAL PRESSURE DETECTION.
Abstract: Recent developments in onsite well monitoring systems have made possible the routine determination of the best mathematical model for drilling optimization and pore pressure detection. This modeling is accomplished through a multiple regression analysis of detailed drilling data taken over short intervals. Included in the analysis are the effects of: bit diameter and bit weight, rotary speed; bit wear; pressure differential across the hole bottom; bit hydraulics; formation compaction; and formation strength. This paper presents procedures for using the regressed drilling model for selecting bit weight, rotary speed and bit hydraulics, and calculating formation pressure from drilling data. The application of the procedure is illustrated using field data.
Name: ["Bourgoyne Jr. A.T.", "Young Jr. F.S."]

Title: REINFORCEMENT LEARNING MODELS AND THEIR APPLICATIONS TO CONTROL PROBLEMS.
Abstract: The importance of reinforcement learning concepts in psychological learning theories has been recognized by control scientists. Elementary concepts of reinforcement learning, a stochastic reinforcement-learning model, a representative reinforcement-learning control system, applications of such a system, and the utility and limitations of reinforcement-learning control systems are discussed.
Name: ["Mendel J.M."]

Title: A General Approach to Linear Mean-Square Estimation Problems
Abstract: An explicit and easily implemented solution is given to the general problem of linear mean-square estimation of a signal or system process based upon noisy observations, under the assumption that the auto-and cross-correlation functions of the signal and the observation processes are known. Also a number of specific estimation problems are briefly discussed. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Cambanis S."]
Affiliations: [' University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill']

Title: On self-learning systems
Abstract: The fundamental problem on self-learning is discussed. The characteristics and the capability of two representative organizers obtained by the Karhunen-Loeve system and the stochastic approximation method are described and their relationship with Bayes' solution is discussed. The organization obtainable by the KL system is realized by calculating the difference of the features between the categories and by classifying the system so as to maximize this difference. This procedure is shown to be optimal. Further, the sufficient condition for this procedure to be the Bayes' solution is derived. For the organization attainable by the stochasfic approximation method, two functional to be evaluated are introduced and the system is organized so as to minimize these functionals. The necessary and the sufficient conditions for these procedures to be Bayes' solution are obtained for the mixture of normal distributions with identical covariance matrices. The several simulations on a digital computer are performed for both cases. The results of these simulations indicate the validity of our learning systems. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Noguchi S.", "Tomita S.", "Watanabe T."]

Title: Intelligent behaviour systems based on semantic networks
Abstract: This paper develops a hypothesis concerning the structure and interaction principles of main psychological programs in form of semantic networks. Models for the brain information mechanisms are proposed, including planning, decision making, complex concept forming and situation evaluation. Some experimental studies are described. ¬© 1973, MCB UP Limited
Name: ["Amosov N.M.", "Kasatkin A.M.", "Kasatkina L.M.", "Kussul E.M.", "Talaev S.A.", "Fomenko V.D."]

Title: SMALLEST MANY-VALUED LOGIC FOR THE TREATMENT OF COMPLEMENTED AND UNCOMPLEMENTED ERROR SIGNALS.
Abstract: It is shown that the smallest many-valued logic whose AND truth-table and OR truth-table have both complemented and uncomplemented entries other than 0, 1, consists of six entries. An alternate logic is given which has increased generality, but consists of nine distinct entries. A corresponding algebra and unary operations are discussed.
Name: ["Breuer Melvin A.", "Epstein George"]

Title: COMPUTER BASED DECISION SYSTEMS IN XEROX CORPORATE PLANNING.
Abstract: This paper presents a corporate decision-aiding system, a family of timeshared models, developed for Xerox of Canada Limited (XCL) in an effort to link the functional areas for communication, planning, and control purposes. Using the approaches of statistical forecasting, heuristics, and simulation, the XCL Decision System assists and guides management all the way from deriving product demand forecasts to simulating the day-to-day operations of the firm to formulating divisional financial statements to preparing corporate operating and medium-range plans. Developed in a short time span and at low cost, the system is used extensively in Canada and has been adopted, in part, by U. S. corporate and regional offices.

Title: ALGEBRAIC SOLUTION OF THE SERVOMECHANISM PROBLEM WITH EXTERNAL DISTURBANCES.
Abstract: A new servo theory is proposed which make use of simple linear algebraic methods, rather than optimal control methods, to formulate, study, and solve the multi-variable linear servomechanism problem. The result is a new, algebraic procedure for designing high-performance output-feedback servo controllers for multi-input, multi-output, possible time-varyng linear plants. Moreover, when the plant is also subjected to external disturbances, the servo controllers designed by this new procedure will continue to provide consistently accurate tracking of complex servo command inputs - even though the disturbances are persistent acting, unknown and unmeasurable.
Name: ["Johnson C.D."]

Title: COMPUTER AIDED PLACEMENT AND ROUTING OF HIGH DENSITY CHIP INTERCONNECTION SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A novel set of inter-related algorithms has been presented which enables a range of different component sizes to be interconnected with optimum packing. These may be either circuits on a silicon chip, chips on a hybrid assembly, conventional component packages on a printed circuit board, or hybrid assemblies on a back-plane. The algorithms developed are very powerful since they are free from the constraints imposed by a hardware tailored system, i. e. , the topography is defined by the logic rather than the technology. These constraints, however, may be incorporated where required. Initially the logic array is placed on a continuous plane. From this state, it is gradually transmuted through various cellular structures defined, initially, by the components and finally by a combination of the components and their associated tracks. The culmination is an arrangement which, at all stages, is determined by the logic and not the technology.
Name: ["Crocker N.R.", "McGuffin R.W.", "Naylor R.", "Vosper H."]

Title: DYNAMIC PATH SYNTHESIS AND OPTIMAL CONTROL.
Abstract: Dynamic Path Synthesis refers to a class of linkage synthesis problems in which constraint paths between specified positions are determined in such a way as to optimize some measure of the resulting dynamic behavior. These problems can be transformed into nonlinear optimal control problems which are generally non-autonomous. The physical nature of the system allows general comments to be made regarding uniqueness, controllability, and singular control. The ideas are developed in the context of a two-link device yielding a fourth order non-linear control problem, for which a numerical example is presented.
Name: ["Starr P.J."]

Title: DIGITAL ADAPTIVE CONTROL OF MACHINE TOOLS.
Abstract: Describes a theoric and experimental research on adaptive control of the metal cutting process. The problem is considered as an optimal control problem and an optimalizing strategy for resetting the index of performance of the process of its extremum value is developed. The stability and performance of the adaptive loop are tested by simulation methods and from these studies a control program for a digital time-shared process computer is derived. Final experiments performed by connecting the process computer to a special purpose analog simulator.
