Title: Response routing in selcuk networks and lashley's dilemma
Abstract: Given a large net of modules of limited logic and memory in which connectivity is primarily to near neighbors with one-way channels, the question is asked of how responses to a generally broadcast request can be routed to the site of the request. A routing procedure which does not require site information is proposed. The procedure is based on the Selcuk Principle which maintains that in properly constructed networks routing can be achieved with each module remembering only on which input channels the request had first arrived. The procedure is successfully applied to a neural network model proposed by Eccles and to one advanced by Burns. The strongest requirement of the proposed procedure is that there be switching among output channels and this appears consistent with the findings of Chun, Raymond & Lettvin (1970) that there is selective invasion of axonal arborization. Since the Selcuk Network scheme achieves response routing on the basis of strictly local information, pursuant to the broadcast of a general message, it has applicability to content-based addressing and to computer-to-computer communication nets. It also constitutes an approach to pattern recognition whereby the image on the ‚Äúretina‚Äù is transformed into a time spectrum of responses, the analysis of which yields information on angle, size, curvature, and position of the edges. ¬© 1973, Academic Press Inc. (London) Limited. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Sahin K.E."]

Title: DYNAMIC PERFORMANCE OF A COMPUTER NUMERICAL CONTROL SYSTEM FOR MULTI-AXIS CONTOURING MACHINE TOOLS.
Abstract: Presents a control design approach for a computer numerical control (CNC) system as a stand-alone contouring controller. Indicates the required real time speed and accuracy requirements for CNC software and develops an appropriate software structure. Shows hybrid computer simulation results which indicate that CNC dynamic performance is superior to conventional NC systems. A mathematical machine tool model and feed axis drive system was developed and used as a vehicle for studying the control system design. Physical parameters were chosen based on an 86-in. Bullard vertical turret lathe because of available data. Continuous d-c electric motors were assumed as lead-screw drives for the two axes machine tool model system.
Name: ["Middleditch A.E.", "Paul F.R."]

Title: On the optimal evaluation of a set of n-linear forms
Source: 14th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory
Abstract: At the heart of a number of arithmetic complexity problems are some basic questions in tensor analysis. Questions regarding the complexity of multiplication operations which are n-linear are most easily studied in a tensor analytic framework. Certain results of tensor analysis are used in this paper to provide insight into the solution of some of these problems. Methods are given to determine a partial ordering on the set of tensors corresponding to a partial ordering with respect to complexity on the set of n-linear operations. Different classes of algorithms for evaluating n-linear operations are studied and a generalized cost criterion is used. Algorithms are given for determining the rank of a class of third order tensors and a canonical form for such tensors is presented. Bounds on the complexity of a wide class of operations are also derived. ¬© 1973 IEEE.
Name: ["Dobkin D."]

Title: Bayesian analysis of error components regression models
Source: Journal of the American Statistical Association
Abstract: This article examines the use of a two-way, random-effects, model with correlated errors and additional explanatory variables in combining cross-section with time series data. This model has been analyzed from a Bayesian viewpoint. Methods are developed for computing posterior distributions of slope coefficients. The advantage of our approach over sampling theory approaches is briefly discussed. It has been shown how one can obtain reasonable inferences about slope coefficients which are the parameters of interest, in the presence of nonestimable nuisance parameters by judicious use of sample and prior information. ¬© Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Swamy P.A.V.B.", "Mehta J.S."]
Affiliations: [' Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System', ' Temple University']

Title: Applications of computers and mathematical models to the study of neuronal systems nuclear and neuronal pulse spectrometry
Abstract: Transfer of methods between physics and biophysics based on a formal similarity between nuclear data and random nerve spikes, is shown. The following examples are described: on-line measurement of biophysical signals using the methods of nuclear pulse spectrometry; Monte Carlo model of nerve-muscle junction and comparison with nuclear models, and minicomputers in experiments. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Souƒáek B."]

Title: Bounds on Suboptimality in the Control of Linear Dynamic Systems
Abstract: A simple inequality giving both upper and lower bounds on suboptimalityis developed and shown to be applicable in estimating 1) the cost of uncertainty in plant parameters, and 2) the cost of decentralized control in interconnected systems, In this second problem the results yield a ‚Äúweak coupling‚Äù condition guaranteeing the stability of a simple decentralized control scheme. Name: ["Bailey F.N.", "Ramapriyan H.K."]

Title: STATISTICAL METHOD OF PREDICTING THE TREND OF AIR POLLUTION.
Abstract: A statistical method of predicting the trend over the periods of interest is described. It is provided the mechanism of pollutant diffusion is considered as a black box. The method is based on the theory of pattern recognition. A predictive scheme requring detailed estimates of an index of environmental pollution some hours ahead is shown.
Name: ["Maeda K.", "Fukuda T.", "Uemura K."]

Title: EXHAUST POLLUTION MINIMIZATION IN SMALL ENGINES USING ADAPTIVE DIGITAL CONTROL.
Abstract: Advances in digital computer technology have brought the application of on-line digital control systems to bear on the problem of exhaust gas pollution from the internal combustion engine. One application, adaptive digital control of fuel consumption based on a feedback of an analysis of exhaust gases, is explained. A small gasoline engine is modified with a fuel injection system, thus the engine, digital computer, and gas analyzer interface is developed. The engine's exhaust pollutants, based on real time operating conditions, are minimized while performance is retained. The delay time limitations experienced by the feedback transducer are demonstrated by a transient mode of operation. The relevance of this investigation and some future applications are discussed.
Name: ["Kehres John K.", "Allan III John J."]

Title: PATH IDENTIFICATION PROCEDURE FOR NETWORKS.
Abstract: A generalized procedure has been advanced for path identification in complex multiloop interconnect directed networks. Reference to transportation networks has been made for the sake of specificity in this paper although the proposed method is equally applicable to all types of directed networks. Typically, one may utilize such procedures for developing information aimed at an efficient traffic rerouting between a given origin-destination pair. The rerouting may be necessitated by situations such as vehicular congestion or adverse weather conditions along a previously assigned nodal segment. A network example illustrates the application of proposed algorithm.
Name: ["Garg D.P."]

Title: THE EFFECT OF MODELING ERRORS ON LINEAR STATE RECONSTRUCTORS AND REGULATORS
Abstract: The effect of imprecise knowledge of system parameters on the reconstruction error of linear observers and on the stability of a class of linear regulators is examined. An upper bound on the reconstruction error for linear unforced systems is obtained. It is shown that in the regulator problem consideration of parameters uncertainty leads to the inclusion of step disturbances. An upper bound that guarantees stability of a class of closed-loop regulators is obtained. It is also shown that if a reulator is designed based on a low-order dynamic model, then by properly choosing a linear control law, the output of the actual process can be made to approximate a desired output response despite uncertainty in the parameters of the actual process.
Name: ["Thau F.E.", "Kestenbaum A"]

Title: SEQUENTIAL GRADIENT-RESTORATION ALGORITHM FOR OPTIMAL CONTROL PROBLEMS WITH NONDIFFERENTIAL CONSTRAINTS - 1, 2.
Abstract: This paper considers the numerical solution of optimal control problems involving a functional I subject to differential constraints, nondifferential constraints, and terminal constraints. The problem is to find the state x(t), the control u(t), and the parameter pi so that the functional is minimized, while the constraints are satisfied to a predetermined accuracy. The approach taken is a sequence of two-phase processes or cycles, composed of a gradient phase and a restoration phase. The gradient phase involves a single iteration and is designed to decrease the functional, while the constraints are satisfied to first order. The restoration phase involves one or several iterations and is designed to restore the constraints to a predetermined accuracy, while the norm of the variations of the control and the parameter is minimized. Several numerical examples are demonstrated.

Title: MERGE CONTROL IN AUTOMATED TRANSIT SYSTEM NETWORKS.
Abstract: Assuming that the longitudinal control of vehicles is accomplished by what is known as the moving-cell or point-follower approach, the merge control problem becomes one of determining necessary point-skip maneuvers to assure that points equi-distant from a merge junction are not simultaneously occupied by vehicles. This paper describes an original algorithm for intersection control which can satisfactorily resolve such merge conflicts 95 percent of the time for system traffic densities approaching 80 percent of capacity by monitoring the status of only twelve points on each line. The algorithm is suitable for programming in a small digital computer; one of which is conceptually located at each intersection.

Title: OPTIMISING AUTOMATIC TRACKING OF MULTILAYER BOARDS.
Abstract: Some known automatic tracking techniques for multilayer printed circuit boards such as Maze-Running, Line-Search, and Channel-Allocation are critically reviewed and compared. Consideration if given to the prohibitive core and time requirement for a real life environment involving an approximately 500x500 track matrix associated with the request for orthogonally connecting about 2500 pin-pairs, on each board. The evolution of an effective algorithm and list-structure capable of successfully handling this problem is then discussed. Finally, several side issues of major significance are introduced. The efficient pre-sorting of the order in which wires are submitted to the main algorithm has been found to make a significant contribution to the efficiency of the entire system. Profile analysis is developed as a technique for comparing the relative merits of various topological placements of the logic network.
Name: ["Adshead H.G."]

Title: DESIGN ANALYSIS OF COMPUTER SYSTEMS BY SIMULATION.
Abstract: Viewed grossly, a computer system has a processing capability which may be statistically characterized in terms of throughput for an average or typical workload. While such a measure may suffice for situations where both the components of the system and the workload can be accurately reduced to factors in statistical relations, it becomes inadequate as a tool in design environments where a generality of applications is to be considered. One has then to follow two complementary approaches of isolating intrinsic characteristics of the problem environment and of choosing a set of parameters which may be used to alter the processing capability of the system. In both these approaches, a computer-based analysis provides about the only means of obtaining quantitative results based upon which qualitative changes can be made. This is well illustrated by the contributions such simulations have made to the design of memory systems; to a lesser extent, simulations have also provided results to aid processor design in general. However, design analysis of computer systems has not been as successful due to the large number of variables and the tremendous diversity of applications. Some attempts to solve this problem are discussed and some suggestions for further work are made.
Name: ["Joseph M."]

Title: Fuzzy sets concept in rank-ordering objects
Source: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: A method of rank-ordering objects using a fuzzy algorithm is described. Each object can be rank-ordered and discriminated by fuzzy functions which characterize the relations of each pair of alternatives. The fuzzy algorithm proposed here is useful in classifying objects of which classes do not possess sharply defined boundaries. In this paper, the author gives the proofs of several theorems on fuzzy functions introduced here. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Shimura M."]

Title: FINDING ANTILOGARITHMS IN THE FINITE FIELD GF(2<sup>n</sup>) WITH APPLICATIONS TO PN SEQUENCE GENERATION.
Abstract: The design of pseudo-noise (PN) generators for correlation analysis of linear dynamic systems entails the problem of generating all shifted (i. e. delayed0 versions of the PN sequence. A delay operator D is introduced. It is shown that all delay operators left brace D**k right brace together with addition and multiplication form an extension field, in which the desired delayed version can be readily computed. Both a combinatorial and a sequential circuit for carrying out these computations are presented.
Name: ["Van Lantschoot Eric J.M."]

Title: Conditional dependence and decomposition strategies in diagnostic inference systems
Abstract: This paper discusses the application of decomposition rules to Bayesian man-machine diagnostic inference systems. An experiment is reported which investigates the use of such decomposition rules in dealing with conditionally dependent data. The experiment, unlike its predecessors, employs an intuitive inference task where the veridical odds can be closely estimated. One major conclusion of this research is that logically equivalent decomposition rules are not necessarily of equal difficulty. Consequently, recommendations as to the superority of a particular decomposition rule should not be made; the systems designer's choice of a particular decision rule should be based on the types of data and conditional dependencies encountered in his particular situation. Such considerations may lead to the adoption of hybrid decomposition rules of a type not previously used. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Steiger J.H.", "Gettys C.F."]

Title: SIMPLE ALGORITHM FOR POLE ASSIGNMENT IN A MULTIPLE INPUT LINEAR TIME INVARIANT DYNAMIC SYSTEM.
Abstract: This paper is concerned with the development of a simple algorithm for solving the problem of pole assignment in a multiple input linear time-invariant dynamic system, by means of state variable feedback. Unlike other existing methods which solve the same problem, the proposed algorithm does not require the transformation of the system equations to a special canonical form or the reduction of the multiple input system to an equivalent single input system. Analogously, the dual problem of constructing an asymptotic state estimator for a multiple output system is solved, with the solution enjoying analogous advantages.
Name: ["Chidambara M.R.", "Broen R.B.", "Zaborszky J."]

Title: A comparison of the Shannon and Kullback information measures
Abstract: Two widely used information measures are compared. It is shown that the Kullback measure, unlike the Shannon measure, provides the basis for a consistent theory of information which extends to continuous sample spaces and to nonconstant prior distributions. It is shown that the Kullback measure is a generalization of the Shannon measure, and that the Kullback measure has more reasonable additivity properties than does the Shannon measure. The results lend support to Jaynes's entropy maximization procedure. ¬© 1973 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Hobson A.", "Cheng B.-K."]

Title: Graphics and digitizing automatic transduction of drawings into data bases
Source: AFIPS Conference Proceedings - 1973 National Computer Conference and Exposition, AFIPS 1973
Abstract: This process is a realization of an economical, accurate, and easy method for capturing drawings for use in computer graphics systems. The implication is a far more productive utilization of computer graphics console time with emphasis on image manipulation, editing, and analysis rather than on image creation. The value of automatic digitization lies in its ability to rapidly and accurately transduce drawings into computer data bases. Such ability implies that drawings may directly act as the original source of information for the various purposes for which they were conceived. That is, the data base will be in one-to-one correspondence with its own drawing and may therefore hopefully provide the same information to the computer that the drawing does to the human. The dream of computer graphics is of man and machine working intimately toward the solution of complex problems by combining the visual power of the human with the computational power of the computer. This dream is indeed realizable provided that the data upon which it must feed is readily accessible, for the strength and viability of any computer system is measured by the data which it processes. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery, Inc. All rights reserved.

Title: APPLICATION OF PATTERN SEARCH TO COMPLICATED MULTIVARIABLE PROBLEMS WITH CONSTRAINTS.
Abstract: Presents the use of the pattern search optimization technique to solve multivariable problems with constraints. Modifications to increase the efficiency of the originally published technique are made and discussed. Pattern search is then used to determine the minimum amount of heat rejected from a nuclear power cycle - an 11-variable problem with constraints on both the independent variables and the merit function.

Title: VIBRATION CONTROL USING SEMI-ACTIVE FORCE GENERATORS.
Abstract: A type of force generator which can respond to general feedback signals from a vibrating system in order to control the vibration but which does not require the power supply of a servomechanism is described. Computer simulation studies show that the performance comparable to that of fully active vibration control systems can be achieved with the semi-active type of device. Physical embodiments of the concept are discussed and compared to hardware used in active and passive vibration control systems.

The asymptotic convergence rate is derived for the former case and a convergence acceleration technique is proposed. Title: The complexity of some non-classical logics
Source: 14th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory
Abstract: Decision procedures for validity in intuitionistic propositional calculus and modal propositional calculus are given which require a running time proportional to a polynomial in the length of the formula on a nondeterministic Turing machine. Using a theorem of Cook's and well-known transformations from intuitionistic to classical and modal to intuitionistic logics, the validity problem for intuitionistic and modal logics is shown to be polynomial equivalent to the validity problem for classical logic. ¬© 1973 IEEE.
Name: ["Cherniavsky J."]
Affiliations: ['State University of New York at Stony Brook']

Title: REMOTE CONTROL OF PLANETARY SURFACE VEHICLES.
Abstract: A remotely manned system consisting of an earth-based control center and a remote rover system on the planetary surface is assumed to extend to the remote site the sensory, manipulative and certain intellectual capabilities of humans here on earth. Required system functions, including scientific payload functions, vehicle functions and ground-based human control functions are discussed and the effects of communication delay and increased remote automaticity on system performance are investigated. To accomplish the required operations for scientific exploration, the control of the remote system requires the development of techniques to deal with problems of long communication time delays so that the performance in terms of operation speed can be increased to acceptable levels. Increased operational performance can be achieved primarily by increasing the rate of useful information flow in the man-machine sensor-control loop, or by increasing the autonomous capabilities of the remote system or by both.

Title: A notion of helping and pseudo-complementation in lattices of honest subrecursive classes
Source: 14th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory
Abstract: A notion of one computable function (not) helping the computation of another is defined in terms of the lattices of honest subrecursive classes. It is said that two honest computable functions do not help each other's computation if the intersection (meet) of the subrecursive classes which they generate is the zero subrecursive class; that is, two functions do not help each other's computation if they have trivial information content in common. One honest subrecursive class is said to be the pseudo-complement of another if it is the maximum class which has trivial information content in common with the other. A technical characterization is given of those honest subrecursive classes for which there are non-zero honest subrecursive classes with trivial information content in common with them. Further, it is shown that for every non-zero honest subrecursive class there is an effective, increasing sequence of honest subrecursive classes which have trivial information content in common with it, and this sequence is cofinal upwards with the set of all honest subrecursive classes which have trivial information content in common with it. Although there is always an upper bound to the set of classes which can have trivial information content in common with it, there may or may not be a maximum class with this property. ¬© 1973 IEEE.

The topics discussed include: linear pattern matching algorithms; efficient algorithms for determining an extremal tree of a graph; efficient compilation of linear recursive programs; equivalence problems in monadic recursion schemes; mechanizable proofs about parallel processes; chow parameters in pseudothreshold logic; on multiple input change hazard-free combinational switching circuits without feedback; multiple-input change asynchronous machines using controlled excitation and flip-flops; and on finding and updating shortest paths and spanning trees.

Title: Dependence of the time of recognition of visual images in cats on the values of the signal to noise ratio
Abstract: The quantitative expression of the noise-proof stability of visual recognition in cats in conditions of a time deficit has been studied. The dependence of the time of recognition of the visual images on the signal to noise ratio is closely exponential. ¬© 1974.

Title: On the optimality and limiting properties of the bayes solution of a system of linear algebraic equations
Source: USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics
Abstract: The problem of solving a system of linear algebraic equations when the a priori information is specified statistically (the problem of estimating a parameter from the results of direct and indirect measurements) is considered. We prove the existence and uniqueness of the Bayes solution in the class of (linear) unbiased estimates, and the optimality of the solution in certain classes of disturbances and values of the estimated parameter. The Bayes approach is extended to the case when the information is inaccurately specified (in a sense defined in the paper). Aspects of the convergence of the estimates in classes and at a point are discussed. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Murav'eva M.V."]

Title: Indexing language structure for automated retrieval
Abstract: A proposal for a computer-aided method of building up an indexing language is made. The method involves linking the terms relevant to any special retrieval system into the UDC, preferably in the form of the Standard Reference Code when it becomes available. Links between the terms are intended to be established in such a way that, provided indexing input sessions are accomplished via a video terminal, a hybrid thesaurus-classification could be built up by a form of "learning process" in the course of regular indexing. The proposed means of establishing links between terms are described, the associated computer system is outlined, and an example of indexing language build-up procedure is presented. Possible uses for natural language search, using the thesaurus-classification as a "switching language", and for automatic classification, are suggested as long-term aims. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Wall R.A."]

Title: AUTOMATIC FILE COMPRESSION.
Abstract: This paper describes a software system developed by the author which attempts to reduce substantially the storage space occupied by large files on secondary storage devices. The system analyses a sample of the file to be compressed to determine which character strings occur most frequently, chooses a new alphabet by extending the machine's character set to include some selected character strings, and then, using the Huffman minimum redundancy coding technique, generates a set of variable length codes for the new alphabet. The file contents are then represented in storage using the new codes. The system is completely automatic and machine independent.
Name: ["McCarthy J.P."]

Title: HAWAII INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON SYSTEM SCIENCES, 6TH, PROCEEDINGS, 1973.
Abstract: Following is a continuation of the list of titles and authors: Approach to Pattern Classification When Little Is Known. By Terrence L. Fine. Title: On the Reconstruction Error of Sampled Data Estimates
Abstract: In the sampling and reconstruction of a random process a discrepancy may occur between its multiplicity and that of its reconstructed version. It is shown that under general conditions an error due to this discrepancy is not present in the total error due to sampling and reconstruction. The problem is studied in the more general framework of tracking a random process of arbitrary multiplicity with one of unit multiplicity; there too, the tracking error can be made arbitrarily small. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Ephremides A.", "Brandenburg L.H."]

Title: Multivariable PID estimation and control in systems with biased disturbances
Abstract: A solution is given to yield reset control action in multivariable control systems, where the controller consists of a state reconstructor and feedback from estimated process and environmental states. Integral action in the estimation loop follows from the assumptions about the disturbance model, and if a special choice for the "feed-forward" matrix operating on the estimated environmental states is made, integral, or reset, control action results. The classical least squares optimal control with modeling of the environment is illustrated using a linearized model of a plug flow tubular reactor as a basis for the design. As a second example which illustrates the reset control action, i.e. the tracking of a constant reference vector with zero control error, a simple third order linear system is used. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Balchen J.G.", "Endresen T.", "Fjeld M.", "Olsen T.O."]
Affiliations: [' Division of Automatic Control', ' Division of Noratom-Norcontrol', ' Division of Automatic Control']

Title: Inductive inference: A recursion theoretic approach
Source: 14th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory
Abstract: There are several situations that we are trying more or less to model. One arises from the standard IQ test in which a person is given a finite sequence of integers and asked to produce the next integer in the sequence. Another is provided by the following grossly simplified view of one aspect of physics: Consider a physicist who is trying to find a law to explain a growing body of experimental data. This data is presented as a set of pairs (x,y). Here, x is a description of a particular experiment, e.g., a high energy physics experiment; y is a description of the results obtained, e.g., the particles produced and their respective properties. The law describing these phenomena is essentially an algorithm for computing the function f(x) = y. What an inductive inference machine does is to request and obtain data in the form of pairs (x,y) and then use this to look for an algorithm i that computes (an extension of) f. Other examples arise in grammatical inference, pattern recognition, etc. This paper develops inductive inference along the lines of Solomonoff [9], Gold [4], and Feldman [3]. What is new and distinguishes our work from theirs is our attempt to characterize the set of functions that can be identified by an inductive inference machine. In the process, we have discovered (Theorem 4, part 1) that inductive inference machines can be considerably more powerful than we previously thought possible. ¬© 1973 IEEE.
Name: ["Blum L.", "Blum M."]
Affiliations: [' University of California', ' University of California']

Title: Statistical indicators of optimality
Source: 14th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory
Abstract: Neighborhood search has been used with some success in providing approximate solutions to discrete optimization problems. The technique produces solutions which may be locally but not globally optimal. For a particular class of problems this paper describes a method for analyzing the relative effectiveness associated with different neighborhoods in terms of the probability that a local optimum is in fact global. The analysis is then applied to the 5-city Travelling Salesman Problem for which two neighborhoods of like size are compared. It is found that local optimality with respect to one of these neighborhoods is roughly twice as likely to indicate global optimality as is local optimality with respect to the other. It is felt that further development of the techniques described in this paper might lead to computer designed heuristics for certain discrete optimization problems. ¬© 1973 IEEE.
Name: ["Savage S."]

Title: Fixed interval smoothing with discrete measurements
Abstract: A recursive form of the Bryson-Frazier (1963) smoothing equations for a linear continuous dynamic system with linear discrete measurements is presented. The now algorithm exhibits a duality with the Kalman filtering equations. As a result of this duality it is possible to convert existing Kalman filtering programmes into smoothing programmes by redefining variables. Storage and computational requirements for the new algorithm are less than that for the Rauch-Tung-Streibel (1965) continuous smoother or the Fraser (1067) two-filter continuous smoother. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Bierman G.J."]

Title: Adaptive beamforming in the spectral domain
Source: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society, AP-S International Symposium (Digest)
Abstract: The adaptive array process is cast into a constrained optimization problem in the spectral domain. Basically, the process allows the array to maintain constant gain in a desired look-direction while simultaneously rejecting undersired interference. The solution to the problem leads to two versions of a "spectral-domain constrained least-mean-squares" (SD-CLMS) iterative algorithm. Convergence considerations lead to optimization of the algorithm in the noiseless case. Smoothing techniques are recommended for the noisy case. A numerical example is included. ¬© 1973 Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Daniel S.M."]

Title: GENERAL ALGORITHM FOR SERVICE PROCESSES LEADING TO ERLANG'S LOSS FORMULA.
Abstract: This paper describes an algorithm or numerical procedure for calculating the loss (call congestion) in a finite number of steps. A practical communications engineering application based on this procedure is given for loss calculations and dimensioning of server groups in Telex, TWX, and similar data dial networks. It is shown that the distribution functions of call inter-arrivals differs from the case of Poisson input as usually assumed in telephone traffic, which results into higher loss (call congestion) than the case of random telephone traffic. Refs.
Name: ["Badran Farid M."]

Title: CURRENT TRENDS IN INFORMATION PROCESSING FOR OBSERVED POINT PROCESSES.
Abstract: The additive white Gaussian noise model is used routinely in the study of communication and control systems. There are two principal reasons: (1) the model provides an accurate description for receivers and sensors found in many of these systems; and (2) the model is analytically tractable. Point process models are useful for these same reasons, but it is only recently that they have begun to emerge, with increasing frequency, in the communication and control literature. Many of the elegant and useful results known for the additive Gaussian model have natural counterparts for the point process models. In this paper, the author describes briefly some of the applications which have led to the rising interest in point processes, review point process models which are currently under investigation, and compare results known for the additive Gaussian and point process models.
Name: ["Snyder Donald L."]

Title: OPTIMAL FEEDBACK CONTROL OF LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH LEAST pth AND MINIMAX COST FUNCTIONS.
Abstract: The problem of finding time-invariant optimal feedback controllers for linear dynamic systems with least pth and minimax cost functions is considered. Since analytical methods for solution are not available, the parameters of the optimum open-loop realization are determined using a search routine, and then the optimal feedback coefficients are obtained by a simple transformation. The method is applicable to both the regulator and the servomechanism problem. An example in the control of a nuclear reactor is considered.
Name: ["Sinha Naresh K.", "Bereznai George T."]

Title: ANALYSIS, SIMULATION AND REALIZATION OF AN AUTOMATIC DIGITAL WIRELINE EQUALIZER SYSTEM.
Abstract: The problem of rapid automatic digital equalization of a highly distorting wireline channel is considered. An appropriate training signal received through the channel is sampled and subsequently processed by a 100-tap transversal filter comprising the equalizer. The resulting equalizer output signal is compared to a properly synchronized locally available reference signal representing the training signal processed by a reference channel of desired frequency characteristics. Errors between these two signals motivate a steepest descent controller to iteratively synthesize the equalizer's impulse response that minimizes the mean-squared error by exercising optimal relaxation along gradient directions. As the mean-squared error approaches its minimum the composite of channel plus equalizer approaches the reference channel characteristics within some tolerance. The problem is formulated deterministically in convenient matrix notation leading to the development of a mathematical block diagram of the equalizer system. A computer-simulated numerical example demonstrates the effectiveness of the SD-equalizer in equalizing a highly distorting channel within a few seconds of real time. The concept of ‚Ä≥learning surface‚Ä≥ is introduced, offering a graphical description of the evolution of the equalizer's impulse response throughout the training process. Implementation considerations are shown to lead to an equally effective and nearly optimal, but considerably simplified, system. Experimental observations agree with simulation results. Finally, smoothing techniques allow for effective equalization in the presence of noise.
Name: ["Daniel Sam M.", "Scott R.J."]

Title: OUTPUT ADAPTIVE DYNAMIC MODEL FOR ESTIMATING TURBULENCE.
Abstract: In modern aircraft, a highly accurate inertial navigation system is utilized for precision tracking and navigation. The application of this requires an accurate evaluation of the performance prior to utilization. This paper considers the development of a dynamic normal mode model for a fighter aircraft, obtained by use of an adaptive learning model to describe the aircraft system. The aircraft response to turbulence is characterized by a single model based upon the normal modes of aircraft vibration. The model is derived in terms of the Lagrangian equations of motion of the aircraft. This allows the total deflection at each point on the aircraft to be represented as a summation of the deflection at the point due to each of the generalized coordinates. The input to the system is taken to be atmospheric turbulence. The learning model is systematically adjusted to provide, from the input turbulence, an output signal.
Name: ["Epps J.B.", "Liberty S.R.", "Ferry D.K.", "Seecat R.H."]

Title: OPTIMUM LINEAR SYSTEM REDUCTION VIA THE PHASE-VARIABLE CANONICAL FORM.
Abstract: An algorithm is given to reduce the order of linear multivariable time-discrete systems. The lower order model is constrained to have a state matrix in the phase-variable canonical form. It is demonstrated that in some situations a non-derogatory model may be used to approximate a derogatory system. The method of steepest descent is used for the reduction of a system of medium size. It should be noted however, that alternative optimization techniques which converge much faster than the steepest descent method are readily applicable. The small number of parameters in the phase-variable form makes it feasible to use such minimization procedures.
Name: ["Zohdy M.A.", "Aplevich J.D."]

Title: DATA COMPRESSION: THEORY AND PRACTICE.
Abstract: The branch of information theory that treats data compression problems is called rate-distortion theory. Given a data source and a quantitative measure of distortion between the original and compressed versions of the source output, the theory specifies the minimum compressed data rate R(D) at which an average distortion of D is attainable. Any performance (D,R) in the distortion-rate plane that can be achieved by a practical data compression scheme necessarily lies above this rate-distortion function, R(D). After presenting the rudiments of rate-distortion theory, the author compares the performances both with one another and with the absolute performance limit prescribed by the R(D) curve. Particular emphasis is placed on data compression algorithms inspired by information-theoretic techniques such as algebraic coding, tree coding, and trellis coding.
Name: ["Berger Toby"]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF STATE MODELS OF DIFFUSION PROCESSES.
Abstract: Petroleum and natural gas extraction policy cannot always rely on surface data such as geology and current wellhead measurements. The underground petroleum reservoir is neither an infinite nor a static system. It is, in fact, a very dynamic system and hence extraction policies should reflect the dynamic properties of the system in order to maximize some aspects of the extracted mineral. Of considerable value, then, would be the ability to find a dynamic model of the reservoir and how it will respond to various dynamically changing resource management policies. Since the petroleum reservoir is a distributed parameter system, it was decided to attempt the identification of a state variable model for a simple one dimensional diffusion process. A least squares identification technique is shown to be useful in obtaining an accurate lumped parameter model of a diffusion process.
Name: ["Jacquot Raymond G.", "Jennings James W.", "Kure John W."]

Title: DESIGN OF TWO-DIMENSIONAL NONRECURSIVE DIGITAL FILTERS.
Abstract: This paper describes four techniques for designing two-dimensional nonrecursive digital filters (i. e. filters whose unit sample responses are zero outside of a finite area). These methods include: the use of window functions, frequency sampling, the straightforward application of linear programming, and a new algorithm. The first three methods are extensions of techniques for designing one-dimensional nonrecursive digital filters and are described only briefly. Of these three, only the third one can be used to design filters that are optimal in the sense that the maximum absolute value (Tchebycheff norm) of the error has been minimized. The new algorithm can also be used to design optimal filters. This algorithm is iterative in nature and it uses linear programming as an optimization technique. However, it uses only a small number of constraint points at each iteration.
Name: ["Fiasconaro James G."]

Title: PROGRAM STRUCTURE FOR A TRANSPORTABLE MILITARY COMMUNICATION SWITCHING SYSTEM.
Abstract: The program organization for the U. S. Army's AN/TTC-38 stored program-controlled tactical communication switch is described. The effort to keep the design simple and efficient resulted in a real-time program which places a minimum reliance on interrupts. The control is basically asynchronus, and uses multi-programming techniques to allow the processing of individual calls to time-share the system. Overloading causes the system to degrade gracefully: the program looks for new work at a slower rate but the real-time constraints of calls being processed are always met. Thus, while subscribers requesting service will experience some delays, no incorrect calls or lost calls result. The success of this implementation is due in large part to the fact that the control concepts mesh perfectly with the architecture of the processor whose design was also affected by the requirements of the application.
Name: ["Dempsey P.J.", "Roder J.", "Rosene A.F."]

Title: FINDING CLIQUES IN GRAPHS.
Abstract: A clique in a graph is a maximal complete subgraph. In an obvious way, a clique in a graph G corresponds to a maximal independent ( equals internally stable) set of vertices in the complement of G. Hence problems concerning cliques and problems concerning maximal independent sets of vertices are essentially the same. This paper, which is expository, deals with two questions. First of all why would anyone need to find the cliques in a graph, and secondly, grated the need for it, what algorithm can one use to find them? Among problems for which it may be necessary to find the cliques in a graph, are those of the determination of clusters (sec left bracket 2 right bracket , left bracket 5 right bracket ), graph colouring problems left bracket and the problem of constructing time-tables. Many algorithms have been proposed for finding cliques. Those discussed are the straightforward bottom-up algorithm of Bednarek and Taulbee, and the rather better algorithm of Bierstone, as modified by Corneil and Mulligan. Mention is also made of the use of pseudo-Boolean programming for problems of this kind.
Name: ["Read Ronald G."]

Title: LINEAR MINIMUM-VARIANCE FILTERS APPLIED TO PHASE-LOCK LOOPS.
Abstract: A new technique is presented for design of first-order phase-lock loops which employs the theory of linear minimum-variance filtering for systems with state-dependent noise. If the first-order phase-lock loop is described in rectangular coordinates, the system dynamics are described by a second-order Ito equation with state-dependent noise due to the oscillator instability. The measurement is linear with additive channel noise. Using the continuous linear minimum-variance estimator, the rms error in phase is degraded 3% from the error variance of the classical (optimal) phase-lock loop above threshold. However, since the scheme is not dependent upon linearity assumptions, the performance below threshold is superior to the classical design as demonstrated by a Monte Carlo analysis.
Name: ["Gustafson Donald E.", "Speyer Jason L."]

Title: OPTIMAL PIVOTING ORDER FOR THE SOLUTION OF SPARSE SYSTEMS OF EQUATIONS.
Abstract: Several papers have been published on the solution of sparse systems of equations. Results have indicated that considerable computational and storage savings as well as reduction of round-off errors can be achieved in solving large sparse systems. It has also been shown that the order in which the variables are eliminated strongly affects the fill-in and the number of long operations required. An efficient algorithm for determining absolutely optimal ordering is not known. The algorithms proposed so far determine a near-optimal ordering, i. e. , they chose the optimal pivot for each step but give no guarantee that such a choice will lead to an overall optimum in the subsequent step. The algorithm proposed in this paper falls into the same general class but resulted in fewer operations on many tested matrices.
Name: ["Nakhla M.", "Singhal K.", "Vlach J."]

Title: SOME COMPUTER-ORIENTED ALGORITHMS FOR DIRECTED GRAPHS.
Abstract: This paper is mainly related to work done with two algorithms. One is a path and loop ennumeration algorithm for oriented graphs, and the other is for finding multiple non-touching loops. Gains, or operation sequences, have been determined simultaneously with the paths, loops and non-touching loops. Application to formulation of state equations using S. Mason's rule have been shown. A coding method for non-commutative edge-weights is introduced and applied to sequential networks. Similar coding was used to simplify non-touching loop determination.
Name: ["Ozguner Umit"]

Title: ADAPTIVE CONTROL OF ENGINE TEST RIGS.
Abstract: The paper discusses the basic objectives of control system design and illustrates the use of root-locus technique in the stabilization of the speed control loop of a petrol engine test rig. The practical limitations of using conventional control technology are explained and a case for the use of self adaptive control presented. Details are then given of the adaptive control system currently being developed at Queen Mary College, London, England. Experience with the use of adaptive control has indicated that the usual 'tuning' of an engine test rig can be successfully carried out automatically. The modeling technique has proved surprisingly accurate despite high levels of random noise. Repeatability of results is very high being determined mainly by the repeatability of rig operating conditions.
Name: ["Taylor J.G."]

Title: Discrete optimal control with multiple constraints I Constraint separation and transformation technique
Abstract: The discrete optimal control problem with multiple inequality constraints on functions of the state and/or control variables is presented. A new transformation technique for dealing with problems in which the number of constraint functions does not exceed the number of control variables is derived. The application of this technique results in a set of control constrained system equations of the same dimensionality as the original system equations. This transformation technique is then extended by the introduction of the principle of constraint separation to cater for the more general problem in which the constraint functions outnumber the control variables. It is shown that the time interval may be split up into segments over which the number of dominant constraints does not exceed the number of control variables. The necessary conditions for extremals and the interpoint boundary conditions at the switchover points are derived and a numerical switching algorithm is presented. It is shown that the state and adjoint variables are single-valued at the switchover points and that all sub-optimal trajectories are feasible in that they will not violate the constraints imposed. Two practical examples are solved in which the constraint functions outnumber the control variables. The solution to the second example is compared with that obtained by using a penalty function approach. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Ritch P.S."]

Title: DYNAMIC COMPUTER CONTROL OF ENGINE TEST RIGS.
Abstract: This paper describes briefly the computer automated test beds that have been developed at Queen Mary College (London, England) over the past four years. The reasons for the choice of control philosophy are given as well as some of the problems that have had to be solved on the way to achieving a versatile and reliable test facility. The capabilities of the system for controlled dynamic cycles are described and present and future work relating to adaptive control and optimization is outlined.
Name: ["Soliman J.I."]

Title: AUTOMATION OF TEST RIGS USING PROCESS CONTROL COMPUTERS.
Abstract: The reasons why and how process-control computers are used for test rig purposes is explained with application examples taken from the motor vehicle industry. Organization possibilities for the hardware either as centralized or decentralized units are explained with the basic characteristics of the Siemens process control computers Models 320 and 330. The ever increasing engineering costs coupled with the reduction in the basic investment costs of the hardware have influenced the thinking in terms of software. A programming system known as PDC ‚Ä≥Proving Direct Control‚Ä≥ offers the end user a complete and quickly variable standard programming system designed for test rig and test bay automation. Computer-aided testing is described for both development and production testing, whether in the laboratory, on the test track, or even in the wind tunnel.
Name: ["Aggett Gerald", "Heck Rolf"]

Title: LR-regular grammars-an extension of LR(k) grammars
Source: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: LR-regular grammars are defined similarly to Knuth's LR(k) grammars, with the following exception: arbitrarily long look-ahead is allowed before making a parsing decision during the bottom-up syntactical analysis; however, this look-ahead is restricted in that the essential "look-ahead information" can be represented by a finite number of regular sets, thus can be computed by a finite state machine. LR-regular grammars can be parsed deterministically in linear time by a rather simple two-scan algorithm. Efficient parsers are constructed for given LR-regular grammars. The family of LR-regular languages is studied; it properly includes the family of deterministic CF languages and has similar properties. Necessary and sufficient conditions for a grammar to be LR-regular are derived and then utilized for developing parser generation techniques for arbitrary grammars. ¬© 1973 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["ƒåulik II K.", "Cohen R."]

Title: Metrics on spaces of finite trees
Abstract: With the increasing popularity of hierarchical clustering methods in behavioral science, there is a need for ways of quantitatively comparing different tree structures on the same set of items. We employ lattice-theoretic methods to construct a variety of metrics on spaces of trees and to analyze their properties. Certain of these metrics are applied to data from Fillenbaum and Rapoport (1971) on the semantic structure of common English kin terms. This application shows that tree metrics can be used to select a componential analysis which is maximally consistent with an empirically derived set of trees. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Boorman S.A.", "Olivier D.C."]

Title: DYNAMIC COMPUTER CONTROL OF ENGINE TEST RIGS.
Abstract: This paper describes briefly the computer automated test beds that have been developed at Queen Mary College (London, England) over the past four years. The reasons for the choice of control philosophy are given as well as some of the problems that have had to be solved on the way to achieving a versatile and reliable test facility. The capabilities of the system for controlled dynamic cycles are described and present and future work relating to adaptive control and optimization is outlined.
Name: ["Soliman J.I."]

Title: Suboptimal control of nuclear reactors using low-order models‚Ä†
Abstract: A realistic model of a nuclear reactor is non-linear and of order 9. As such a model is not suitable for on-line computation of optimal control, many authors have tried using simplified models of lower order. This paper shows that these classical reduced-order models are not satisfactory for control purposes, as their responses deviate considerably from that of the actual system. Optimum second-order models are then derived and used for suboptimal control of the plant. It is shown that these suboptimal controls approach the actual optimum sufficiently closely. The entire scheme for updating the model and using it to compute the suboptimal controller can be performed on-line, thereby realizing the adaptive control of the reactor power level. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Sinha N.K.", "Berezna G.T."]

Title: On tape-bounded complexity classes and multi-head finite automata
Source: 14th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory
Abstract: The principal result described in this paper is the equivalence of the following statements; (1) Every set accepted by a nondeterministic oneway two-head finite automaton can be accepted by a deterministic two-way k-head finite automaton, for some k. (2) The context-free language Lp (described in the paper) is recognized by a (log n)-tape bounded deterministic Turing machine. (3) Every set accepted by a L(n)-tape bounded nondeterministic Turing machine is recognized by a L(n)-tape bounded deterministic Turing machine, provided L(n) ‚â• log n. This work extends results reported earlier by Hartmanis [2], Savitch r9,10], and Lewis, Stearns, and Hartmanis [6]. ¬© 1973 IEEE.
Name: ["Sudborough I.H."]

Title: On a class of additive learning models: Error-correcting and probability matching
Abstract: A general model for learning signal detection in a Yes-No task is considered in which (a) the decision criterion shifts upward and downward by equal steps, and (b) the probability that the criterion shifts on a trial depends on the stimulus-response pair on that trial. Conditions are given for this process to have a unique stationary distribution, and the behavior of the process, as the step-size decreases to zero, is studied. The special model where criterion shifts may occur only on error trials can account for the probability matching behavior and for the interaction between signal strength and signal probability typically observed when the payoff matrix is symmetrical. Further, when the shift probability is assumed to be an increasing function of the distance of the sensory input from the criterion, the stationary mean criterion values are less extreme than the values that yield probability matching. It is shown that the model provides a way of incorporating payoff matrix asymmetry. Finally, the standard error in the maximum likelihood parameter estimates is calculated and a statistic is proposed for discriminating the error-correcting model from the more general model. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Thomas E.A.C."]

Title: Min and max hierarchical clustering using asymmetric similarity measures
Abstract: The min and the max hierarchical clustering methods discussed by Johnson are extended to include the use of asymmetric similarity values. The first part of the paper presents the basic min and max procedures but in the context of graph theory; this description is then generalized to directed graphs as a way of introducing the less restrictive characterization of the original clustering techniques. ¬© 1973 Psychometric Society.
Name: ["Hubert L."]

Title: Estimating the expected probability of misclassification for a rule based on the linear discriminant function: Univariate normal case
Abstract: The problem is to estimate the average probability of misclassifying an observation from a given population in the context of the two group classification problem when populations are univariate normal with unknown means and common known variance, and the rule is based on the linear discriminant function. Several estimators are compared with respect to asymptotic MSE and with respect to the distribution of the absolute error between estimator and parameter, and conclusions drawn about the best estimators. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Sorum M."]
Keywords: ["classification", "linear discriminant function", "probabilities of misclassification", "probability misclassifying", "probability misclassification"]

Title: RKHS Approach to Detection and Estimation Problems‚Äï‚ÄïPart V: Parameter Estimation
Abstract: Using reproducing-kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) techniques, we obtain new results for three different parameter estimation problems. The new results are 1) an explicit formula for the minimum-variance unbiased estimate of the arrival time of a step function in white Gaussian noise, 2) a new interpretation of the Bhattacharyya bounds on the variance of an unbiased estimate of a function of regression coefficients, and 3) a concise formula for the Cramer-Rao bound on the variance of an unbiased estimate of a parameter determining the covariance of a zero-mean Gaussian process. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Duttweiler D.L.", "Kailath T."]

Title: Tyeoriya i praktika uluchshchyennogo myetoda poiska | [Theorie und Praxis eines verbesserten Suchverfahrens]
Abstract: Nelder/Mead have developed a search procedure for function minimization. The method is critically reviewed and illustrated by some formal examples. Further development has been done in Heidelberg and is incorporated in the computer program Reflex. Reflex is applied in two examples (adaptation of the log-normal distribution to an empirical income distribution; time-variant predicting filter). ¬© 1973 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Tiede M."]

Title: A simulation of memory for chess positions
Abstract: This paper describes an information-processing model, MAPP, implemented as a computer program, that simulates the processes subjects use to remember and reproduce chess positions they have seen briefly. The model incorporates processes adapted from PERCEIVER, an information-processsing theory of eye movements in chess perception, and EPAM, a theory of rote verbal learning. The data from MAPP show good agreement with the performance of strong chess players in identical tasks. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Simon H.A.", "Gilmartin K."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF BIOLOGICAL CASCADES OF LINEAR AND STATIC NONLINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A method is presented for the identification of any nonlinear biological device consisting of a cascade of a linear, a static nonlinear, and a linear system. Following a single application of a white Gaussian input, explicit frequency domain solutions for the linear transfer functions are obtained in terms of the Fourier transforms of the first and second order input-output cross-correlations. Easily-tested necessary conditions, which do not require identifying the component systems, are found for a biological system to be represented by such a cascade or by special cases of it.
Name: ["Korenberg Michael J."]

Title: COMPUTER AUGMENTATION OF HUMAN CREATIVITY.
Abstract: A program is described in which an individual user interacts conversationally with a digital computer through a terminal, using standard English languagee phrases for input and output, in such a way that the idea or new concept generation of the user is supported, stimulated and augmented by the machine. Questions involving I/O approaches, basic modes of the algorithm files, tables and varius storage approaches, man/machine dialogue control in real time and English language interpretation and reconstruction are discussed. Sample dialogue is presented from preliminary programming in APL PLUS.
Name: ["Nevill Jr. G.E.", "Charles Jr. J.R.", "Crowe R.A."]

Title: VOCAL TRACT PARAMETER IDENTIFICATION USING SEQUENTIAL ESTIMATION TECHNIQUES.
Abstract: A new method of speech digitization based on the identification of vocal tract parameters using modified versions of the Kalman filter and the Stochastic Approximation sequential estimation algorithms is presented. Subjective listening tests indicate that the synthesized speech is highly intelligible. A detailed discussion of the computational requirements of the algorithms is given; the algorithms are shown to be real time feasible using parallel processing methods. Finally, it is noted that the most promising application of sequential estimation algorithms seems to be to systems that encode and transmit the error in the estimate of the speech waveform.
Name: ["Melsa J.L.", "Jones S.K.", "Gibson J.D."]

Title: FORMANT EXTRACTION HARDWARE USING ADAPTIVE LINEAR PREDICTIVE CODING.
Abstract: A hardware system for formant extraction using adaptive linear predictive coding has been constructed which measures formant frequencies, formant bandwidths, pitch, voicing and mean squared amplitude from speech signals. It operates on-line in one-eighth real time with a recorded speech signal and feeds the output parameters either into memory for later off-line display or to a Honeywell DDP-116 computer for on-line analysis. The Formant Extraction Hardware (FEH) includes a Data General NOVA 1200 minicomputer with 8192 words of core memory, a 12 bit A/D converter for sampling the speech signals, a sampling clock, an input low-pass filter, and an output interface system.
Name: ["Welch John R.", "Oetting John D."]

Title: Equivalence problems in monadic recursion schemes
Source: 14th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory
Abstract: The inclusion problem for the class of monadic recursion schemes is shown to be undecidable, thus answering an open question of Paterson [5], The proof depends upon a construction similar to one used in showing that the question "is L<sub>1</sub> ‚äÜ L<sub>2</sub> ? " is undecidable for context-free languages L<sub>1</sub>, L<sub>2</sub>. ¬© 1973 IEEE.
Name: ["Friedman E.P."]

Title: REAL-TIME IMPLEMENTATION OF A LINEAR PREDICTIVE CODING SYSTEM.
Abstract: This paper describes the implementation of a Linear Predictive Coding system in real-time on a programmable processor. The processor used has a word length of 16 bits, makes use of integer arithmetic, and has a memory access time of 100 nsec. The algorithm chosen for implementation is an adaptation of the technique introduced by B. S. Atal of Bell Labs. The system makes use of a minimum distance function pitch extractor and a novel method of maintaining system stability. Much attention has been give to block scaling of the processed data in order to provide the accuracy required in the limited precision machine. Computationally efficient matrix solution and synthesis algorithms are also discussed.
Name: ["Klayman C.", "Kaufman G.", "Snyder A.", "Teacher C.", "Welch J.", "Brandenstein W.", "Tremain T."]

Title: MODEL SIMPLIFICATION OF LINEAR DYNAMIC SYSTEMS BY CONTINUED FRACTION EXPANSION TECHNIQUE.
Abstract: It is often desirable and sometimes necessary to reduce the order of linear dynamic systems in the analysis and design of control systems. Several methods are available to reduce the dimensionality of the system. Among the various methods, the one due to C. Chen and L. Sheih is considered most powerful and requires less computational time. In their technique of model simplification the given higher order transfer function is expanded into continued fraction expansion and some of the quotients are ignored depending upon the order of the required model. A systematic justification for this procedure via sensitivity considerations is provided in this paper. This approach indicates that the simplification is applicable to control systems which can normally be considered as low pass filters.
Name: ["Vittal Rao S."]

Title: EFFICIENT COMPUTER ANALYSIS OF ADJOINT SIGNAL FLOW GRAPHS.
Abstract: It is shown that a simple relation exists between the system equations of a signal flow graph of a linear system and those of the adjoint signal flow graph. Moreover, the LU factors, (L is a lower triangular matrix and U is an upper triangular matrix), of the coefficient matrix of the adjoint signal flow graph can be obtained directly from the LU factors of the coefficient matrix of the original signal flow graph. Furthermore, it is shown that the eigenvalues of the adjoint signal flow graph and those of the original signal flow graph are the same, and that a simple relation exists between the transformation matrix which diagonalized the system matrix of the adjoint signal flow graph and that of the original signal flow graph. Hence, in sensitivity calculations, the computing time required to analyze both signal flow graphs is reduced by nearly 50 percent.
Name: ["Lee Arnold Y."]

Title: ADAPTIVE SPEECH COMPRESSION FOR PACKET COMMUNICATION SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Packet communication systems offer many significant advantages for low duty factor user populations. These advantages can be applied to voice communication. Additional data compression beyond that achievable with the new linear predictive encoding techniques can be obtained by exploiting the asynchronous character of the packet communication channel. The adaptive data compression algorithm DELCO achieves a compression factor greater than 2 while maintaining high quality.
Name: ["Magill D.T."]

Title: Chow parameters in pseudothreshold logic
Source: 14th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory
Abstract: The Investigation of Chow parameters is extended to pseudothreshold functions. Pseudothreshold logic is a generalization of threshold logic. Chow parameters are a set of n + 1 integers derived from a Boolean function of n variables. The main results are: 1. Two different pseudothreshold functions with the same Chow parameters have the same optimum structure. Thus, the optimum structures of pseudothreshold functions can be cataloged using Chow parameters. 2. The set of positive threshold functions is a subset of the set of positive, zero-free, pseudothreshold functions which is a subset of the nonnegative, nontrivial pseudothreshold functions which in turn is a subset of the measure minimum functions. 3. The set of positive threshold functions is a subset of the intersection of the set of positive Chow unique functions and positive, zero-free, pseudothreshold functions. 4. The sets of positive Chow.unique functions and the positive, zerofree, pseudothreshold functions are subsets of the Chow maximum functions which in turn is a subset of the positive Boolean functions. ¬© 1973 IEEE.
Name: ["Baugh C.R."]

Title: LMMSE ESTIMATION OF EXPONENTIALLY CORRELATED PROCESSES IN DEGRADING ENVIRONMENTS WITH VIDEO APPLICATIONS.
Abstract: A model is derived and evaluated for estimating a continuous uniformly sampled exponentially correlated random process in noise which is uncorrelated or has exponential correlation at points separated by integral multiples of the sample interval. The linear minimum mean-squared error fidelity criterion is used to specify a model with improvement curves given and comments provided on performance. Matrix results are derived to provide the required vector of weights for the 2j plus 1 sample estimator. Application is made to the processing of real-time video.
Name: ["Gilbert Alton L.", "Carden Frank F."]

Title: System identification in large scale systems with hierarchical structures
Abstract: Due to its systems control orientation, the theory of multilevel hierarchical control developed by Mesarovic and others appears especially promising for identification and modeling of large scale systems consisting of relatively independent subsystems with strong and weak intersystem coupling. Standard techniques of optimum systems control and estimation theory may be used to resolve system problems described in this format. Determination of system structure and identification of system parameters form an inherent part of this procedure. To achieve advantages by hierarchical system concepts, it is necessary to decompose a large scale system into a number of smaller parts in such a manner that individual subsystem estimation, identification and control is feasible and to coordinate the subsystems in order to obtain the overall system goal. While decomposition is in theory easy, in practice it must be accomplished such that subsystem structure preserves constraints, information structures and acceptable authority structures. The success of coordination will thus, in practice, be affected by the particular system decomposition chosen. This paper presents the results of an investigation of system identification, using the maximum a posteriori criterion, of system parameters within a hierarchical structure. Examples demonstrate the use of the system identification algorithms. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Guinzy N.J.", "Sage A.P."]

Title: MINIMAX TERMINAL STATE ESTIMATION FOR LINEAR PLANTS SUBJECT TO A TOTAL ENERGY CONSTRAINT.
Abstract: A linear-minimax terminal state estimator is derived, for a discrete linear plant which is subject to a total energy constraint, using a standard quadratic loss function. This linear-minimax decision rule is derived using the method of least favorable prior distributions. It is shown that there exists a least favorable prior distribution for the unknown control law, which is defined by a discrete probability measure with support which lies entirely on the boundary of the hyperellipsoidal parameter space which defines the space of admissible control policies. This discrete distribution is supported by 2**k points, which receive equal probability, and which are determined by the solution of a certain nonlinear algebraic matrix equation. The exponent k is equal to the rank of the covariance matrix of this least favorable prior distribution.
Name: ["Hexner Gyorgy", "Mintz Max"]

Title: ALGORITHMS FOR OPTIMAL TREE NETWORKS.
Abstract: A few of the standard techniques of constrained optimization are analyzed in relation to tree network design.
Name: ["Chandy K.M."]

Title: NEW ALGORITHMS FOR UNCONSTRAINED OPTIMIZATION.
Abstract: In this paper a family of algorithms for unconstrained optimization based on homogeneous function is presented. It is shown that this family of algorithms reaches the minimum of a homogeneous function in n plus 2 iterations and does not require finding the minimum on the one-dimensional search. The D. Jacobson W. Oksman algorithm can be derived from this family of algorithms as a special case.
Name: ["Charalambous Christakis"]

Title: SUB-OPTIMAL LINEAR SYSTEM REDUCTION ALGORITHM.
Abstract: A modification of the B. L. Ho algorithm is presented for sub-optimally approximating the parameters of multi-input, multi-output time-discrete linear systems. The cost function is taken to be the sum of squared errors of the impulse response.
Name: ["Aplevich J.D."]

Title: DECISION GRAPHS FOR INFORMATION PROCESS.
Abstract: Identifying and classifying information are important tasks in many areas such as data processing in census studies, process controls in information processing systems, the recognition of patterns, and so on. A procedure is developed to design a reasonable testing process to identify information from a given decision table. This problem is attacked by the use of linear graph theory so that more general cases of identifying information can be covered.
Name: ["Mayeda Wataru"]

Title: SIMPLE PARTITIONED MARKOV CHAIN MODEL AND TROPOSCATTER CHANNEL.
Abstract: A simple partitioned Markov chain model is briefly reviewed. The usefulness of the model will be impaired if the number of states of the model is too large. Two error sequences from troposcatter channel are examined. The results show that a four state model is sufficient to represent the troposcatter channel.
Name: ["Tsai Stephen"]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF NONRECURSIVE DIGITAL FILTERS APPROXIMATING THE FREQUENCY RESPONSE OF A GIVEN RECURSIVE DIGITAL FILTER.
Abstract: The use of bilinear z-transform method shows that for every well defined digital approximation problem there is a corresponding analog filter problem. So the enitre analog filter theory is useful in the design of digital filters. The filters resulting from the use of bilinear z-transform design method are all recursive digital filters. But the nonrecursive digital filters have certain advantages over the recursive digital filters with respect to stability and the ease of implementation etc. This paper presents a method of finding a nonrecursive digital filter, which approximates the frequency response of a given stable recursive digital filter, thus establishing a method of using the wealth of information available in the analog filter theory for the design of nonrecursive filters as well.
Name: ["Chalapatirao K."]

Title: A standard form for sequential stochastic control
Abstract: Causal discrete-time stochastic control problems with nonclassical information patterns are not necessarily sequential in the sense that the order of the various control actions is fixed in advance. When this sequential condition does hold, then they can be reduced to a (theoretical) standard form which enables the establishment of a maximum principle, a reachable set concept and dynamic programming, all in a straightforward and transparent way. ¬© 1973 Springer-Verlag New York Inc.
Name: ["Witsenhausen H.S."]

Title: EFFICIENT METHOD FOR COMPUTER AIDED ANALYSIS OF LINEAR TIME INVARIANT NETWORKS.
Abstract: A computer method, based on the eigenvalue approach for obtaining frequency responses and time-domain solutions of linear time-invariant networks, is presented. For most cases, this method yields substantial saving in computation time.
Name: ["Wang K.U.", "Wang H.T.H.", "Phoomvuthisarn S."]

Title: ON SOME GAMES IN A FINITE-STATE SEQUENTIAL MACHINE CONTEXT.
Abstract: Discussed are certain conceptual problems for games in a finite-state machine context, also referred to as automata games in literature. The notion of a pregame is introduced as a convenient way of dealing with the problems of dynamic games. Two examples are given, and ‚Ä≥rational‚Ä≥ strategies and outcomes determined for different conditions.
Name: ["Ragade R.K."]

Title: COMPUTATIONAL CONSIDERATIONS AND ROUTING PROBLEMS FOR LARGE COMPUTER COMMUNICATION NETWORKS.
Abstract: In this paper, the computational aspects of the large network routing problem are considered. Both hierarchical and nonhierarchical networks are studied, and computation, storage and overhead traffic requirements are examined. Several hierarchical routing algorithms are proposed. These algorithms are based on a decomposition approach and provide significant savings in memory space and computation time when compared to other techniques which have been implemented or proposed. These algorithms can operate efficiently for distributed networks with 1000 or more nodes each of which is active in the routing process.
Name: ["Gerla M.", "Chou W.", "Frank H."]

Title: NEW STATISTICAL METHOD OF NONLINEAR SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION.
Abstract: A statistical method is proposed for directly identifying the Volterra kernels of any time-invariant physically realizable nonlinear system of finite of infinite order. Following a single application of a special random input, the first order Volterra kernel is found by a single first order cross-correlation, the second order Volterra kernel by an additional second order cross-correlation, and so on. Several applications and extensions are discussed, and the suitability of the method for biological modeling is considered.
Name: ["Korenberg Michael J."]

Title: DESIGN OF SIMPLE MODEL REFERENCED CONTROLLERS FOR APPROXIMATE PARAMETER INVARIANCE.
Abstract: A synthesis method is presented in this paper for the design of a controller for a class of model reference systems in which the plant is not known exactly or is subject to large parameter variations. The design introduces in the system external stable networks whose parameters become dominant compared to the plant parameters.
Name: ["Constantinides Christos T.", "Hval Magne"]

Title: APPLICATIONS OF LOWER-TRIANGULAR TRANSFORMATIONS IN CODING AND RESTORATION OF TWO-DIMENSIONAL SOURCES.
Abstract: Transformations of two-dimensional random processes by lower-triangular operators that uncorrelates processes with separable autocovariance functions are discussed. The significance of this transformation is its computational efficiency, involving no transformation delays, and the fact that for markov processes the transformation is accomplished recursively. For markov processes the transform coding sytem using the lower-triangular operator results in a DPCM encoder thus unifying DPCM with the transform coding techniques. Wiener filtering of markov processes using lower-triangular transformation results in a suboptimal Wiener filter which requires significantly less multiplication operations than other discrete Wiener filters.
Name: ["Habibi Ali"]

Title: APPROXIMATE ACCESS DELAY COMPUTATIONS IN MULTIPOINT PRIVATE LINE NETWORKS WITH POLLING.
Abstract: A communications network is considered consisting of a number of data stations (terminals) successively polled and served by a computer. The computer and the transmission line are modeled as a single server whose constant service time includes transmission and processing times. Requests for service by the computer arrive randomly at each station according to Poisson distributions and only one request per station may be transmitted during a single polling cycle. An approximation to the average access delay, defined as the time from which a request reaches the head of its queue at the station (and no request from its queue is being processed) until it begins service, is presented. Supported by some GPSS simulation results, the approximation appears applicable to any number of stations, any distribution of traffic among the stations, and a full range of system utilizations.
Name: ["Pack Charles D.", "Whitaker Bruce A."]

Title: NONLINEAR SYSTEMS IDENTIFICATION TECHNIQUE USING PIECEWISE LINEAR APPROXIMATIONS.
Abstract: A technique for identifying a class of nonlinear systems is presented. The technique uses the response-error method of identification and piecewise linear segments to approximate the nonlinear terms in the equation. The technique consists of searching over the breakpoints of the piecewise linear approximation for the optimum values to improve the approximation over that of fixing the breakpoints at equally spaced intervals and searching over the parameters of the linear segments. Using this technique fewer piecewise linear segments are needed to approximate a nonlinear element. This technique is not restricted to piecewise linear segments, there is no theoretical reason why piecewise smooth functions that are polynominal approximations over each segment cannot be used, though only the linear approximations over each segment are considered in this paper. Of course, as the degree of the approximation is increased, the number of parameters to be identified likewise increases. An example is given illustrating the technique and its advantage over using fixed break points.
Name: ["McKinley Jr. Henry J."]

Title: PRECOMPUTED STATE DEPENDENT CONTROL.
Abstract: Presented is a method of control which is applicable to multiple-input multiple-output nonlinear time-invariant systems in which desired behavior can be expressed explicitly as a trajectory in system state space. The method, called Precomputed State Dependent Control, is basically a synthesis technique in which a suboptimal control law is developed off-line, prior to system operation.
