This law is obtained by conducting searches at a finite number of points in state space, in the vicinity of some desired trajectory, to obtain a set of constant control vectors which tend to return the system to the desired trajectory. These vectors are used to evaluate the unknown coefficients in a control law having some assumed analytic form. The resulting coefficients are used in the on-line computation of control vectors.
Name: ["Johnson M.Ray"]

Title: A versatile method for the nonte carlo optimization of stochastic systems
Abstract: The paper discusses a versatile family of Monte Carlo methods for the sequential optimization of stochastic systems. The method selects a sequence of successive one-dimensional search directions, defines a (stochastic) search in each of the directions, where the data used for both the one-dimensional search and the direction determination are merely noise-corrupted observations on the system. The method is more general than stochastic approximation, it converges to a stationary point even in the presence of multiple minima, and it uses rather natural logics. A convergence theorem is proved. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Kushner H.J.", "Gavin T."]

Title: DIGITAL PROCESSING OF RADIOGRAPHIC IMAGES.
Abstract: This report provides a description of some of the techniques for image handling and image processing on the computer. Both the frequency and spatial domain designs and implementations of digital filters are covered. Examples of digitally processed synthetic test patterns as well as radiographs are shown to illustrate the techniques. The software developed implementing the processing algorithms is documented.
Name: ["Bond A.D.", "Ramapriyan H.K."]

Title: EFFECTS OF VARIATION OF SPEED ON VEHICLE HANDLING DURING WIND GUST.
Abstract: The closed loop system analyzed in this paper is made of a model of a human operator which was developed at the Cornell Aeronautical Laboratories from actual driver responses obtained under simulated road conditions, and a lateral stability model of an automobile which has been modified to incorporate the effect of nonlinear tire performance. Both models are combined in this paper and are assumed to accurately represent a vehicle traveling down a level, straight road at various speeds where it encounters gusts of wind or varying magnitude. The purpose of this system model is to determine the stability of the man-machine combination under these conditions and thus determine the variation in stability using servo analysis techniques. The results obtained appear to reasonably characterize the system and indicate that under certain idealized conditions, servo analysis techniques appear applicable to man-machine systems.
Name: ["Mahig Joseph"]

Title: HAWAII INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON SYSTEM SCIENCES, 6TH, PROCEEDINGS, 1973.
Abstract: Following is a continuation of the list of titles and authors: Application of System Theoretic Concepts to the Simulation of Large Scale Adaptive Systems. By Tuncer I. Oren. On the Simulation of Time-Sharing Computing Systems. By B. J. Wesley and J. Tartar. On Constructive Methodology for Information Retrieval. By Alois Glanc. Information System Performance Prediction and Evaluation. By H. Ling and V. Y. Lum. Information Processing System for the MedicaExamination Program Under the Federal Coal Mine Health and Safety Act of 1969. By Harry O. McKinney, Wayne A. Muth and Larry F. Boyce. Computer Control Interface for an Automated Ophthalmic Refraction System. By Chacko Neroth, Paul Chang and Elwin Marg.
Name: ["Oren Tuncer I.", "Wesley B.J.", "Tartar J.", "Glanc Alois", "Ling H.", "Lum V.Y.", "McKinney Harry O.", "Muth Wayne A.", "Boyce Larry F.", "Neroth Chacko C.", "Chang Paul", "Marg Elwin"]

Title: ON INVERSE OPTIMAL CONTROL PROBLEM AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC CYBERNETICS.
Abstract: Some aspects of the inverse optimal control problem are considered for linear discrete-time multi-control regulatory processes. A closed-loop system with a known control policy is given; the problem is to determine performance indices for which the given control law is optimum. A sufficient condition for the solution of the inverse problem is developed, and an explicit solution is obtained for a special case of interest in socio-economic regulatory processes. The developed techniques for the selection of ‚Ä≥favorable‚Ä≥ performance criterion is illustrated through examples.
Name: ["Lee Kwang Yun", "Park Jonggoo"]

Title: Algorithms of Optimal Learning
Abstract: This chapter discusses the algorithms of optimal learning. The performance indices of learning are considered, the methods of obtaining quasi-optimal, optimal, and suboptimal learning are given in the chapter, with their properties and characteristics explained. Any learning system that satisfies the conditions of the convergence criterion can reach the goal of learning, but the criterion of convergence establishes very broad boundaries of convergence. An algorithm of learning is considered to be an algorithm of optimal learning if the distance is minimal at each instant. For continuous and hybrid algorithms, there are no constrains characteristic of the discrete algorithms. Hybrid algorithms can provide optimal estimates using discrete data in the cases where the discrete algorithms are only quasi-optimal. However, the application of the algorithms of optimal learning is confronted with enormous difficulties that are connected to the necessity of computing an initial value of the estimate and the matrix parameters in the algorithm. Therefore, the algorithms of optimal learning cannot be used in practice. ¬© 1973, Academic Press Inc.

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF ONE CLASS OF NONLINEAR STOCHASTIC DISCRETE OBJECTS.
Abstract: A solution is presented to the problem of evaluating the parameters of one class of Markov processes described by a system of nonlinear stochastic difference equations with right sides that are linear with respect to the parameters. Bayesian estimates and maximum-likelihood estimates are investigated. The precision of the estimates is computed. A procedure for solving strongly nonlinear problems is considered.
Name: ["Ruban A.I."]

Title: SIMULATION OF SEQUENTIAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS WITH IN-PROCESS INVENTORY.
Abstract: A general class of simulation models of production lines is studied to formulate theories on system behavior. All of the systems have normally distributed processing times as an approximation to conditions often encountered in the manufacturing environment. Results show that the behavior of such systems is a function of buffer capacity, the system coefficient of variation, and the number of stages in the system, and that the pattern of variation among the individual stages has no significant effect on the behavior of the system. From the results, it appears possible to obtain an excellent approximation to optimum buffer size for any system meeting the general assumptions of the model. Insight can also be gained into the cost of constraints on buffer sizes less than optimum.
Name: ["Anderson David R.", "Sellers Brian D.", "Shamma Mohammed M."]

Title: SIMPLE MULTIVARIABLE DECOUPLER FOR DDC.
Abstract: Linear regression analysis is used to determine a discrete multivariable process model from process response data. This simple model describes the classical P, V or modified V canonical models. A decoupler can be designed, for these processes, which preserves classicial first order models and allows the process industries to use PID controllers on these decoupled systems.
Name: ["Sayers Jr. Herbert D.", "Moore Charles F."]

Title: DIGITAL FILTERING OF STOCHASTIC NETWORK DECISION NODE NOISE.
Abstract: Digital filtering techniques are utilized to counteract serial correlation in random number sequences generated during discrete-event stochastic network simulations. An algorithm is described which monitors departures from Bernoulli decision node branch probabilities and compensates for observed serial correlation. Relationships between branch probability and system performance are then explored.
Name: ["Roffman Martin M.", "McNamee Lawrence P."]

Title: INTRINSIC RANDOM FUNCTIONS AND THEIR APPLICATIONS.
Abstract: The intrinsic random functions (IRF) are a particular case of the Guelfand generalized processes with stationary increments. They constitute a much wider class than the stationary RF, and are used in practical applications for representing non-stationary phenomena. The most important topics considered are: existence of a generalized covariance (GC) for which statistical inference is possible from a unique realization; theory of the best linear intrinsic estimator (BLIE) used for contouring and estimating problems; the turning bands method for simulating IRF; and the models with polynomial GC, for which statistical inference may be performed by automatic procedures.
Name: ["Matheron G."]

Title: TCS ENVIRONMENT SIMULATION.
Abstract: Software used in modern stored program control switching systems must be free of errors when an exchange goes into operation. Environment simulation provides an efficient checkout tool for such software debugging. The simulator developed for TCS provides a variable and repeatable environment to check the system software over a wide range of conditions. When an error has been detected and the program patched, the simulation can be repeated to check the patch.
Name: ["Foucault C.C.", "Cerny D.J.", "Ponce de Leon L."]

Title: PROBLEM GENERATION AND SOLUTION.
Abstract: A survey of an operational generative CAI system for teaching problem solving is presented. Experience using the CAI system in an introductory digital systems course is summarized. This system forms the foundation for Artificial Intelligence research on teaching problem solving using generative CAI. The current system suggests a model which is used to describe the design of a general system for problem generation and solution.
Name: ["Perry J.M.", "Koffman E.B."]

Title: DETERMINING SAMPLING EQUIPMENT LOCATIONS BY OPTIMAL EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN WITH APPLICATIONS TO ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND ACOUSTICS.
Abstract: The problem is treated of estimating vector fields governed by linear differential or functional equations from data collected at a finite number of locations. Direct application of optimal regression experimental design makes the uncertainty in the estimates as small as possible with a given measurement effort and specifies where the measurements should be taken. Error bounds are developed for the variances of estimates of the maximum intensity of a given function and the location giving this maximum. Applications are given to problems in air pollution monitoring and acoustics.
Name: ["Gustafson S.A.", "Kortanek K.O."]

Title: MULTIPATH SENSITIVITY OF A LINEARIZED ALGORITHM USED IN TIME-DIFFERENCE-OF-ARRIVAL LOCATION SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Any location scheme using Time-Difference-of-Arrival (TDA) measurements is inherently nonlinear, requiring the point of intersection of two hyperbolic sheets. However, because the ‚Ä≥best‚Ä≥ solution technique may be quite time consuming, linearization methods are often employed wherever possible. The method described is a direct linearization of the location geometry which transforms the intersection-of-hyperbolas problem into one of finding the intersection of straight lines with an auxiliary, quadratic constraint. The linearized algorithm so developed has been implemented for use in essentially line-of-sight applications. However it is shown that when a narrow-band, phase measuring technique is used to make TDA measurements in an urban environment, propagation errors may be large enough to violate the underlying linearizing assumption upon which the algorithm is based.
Name: ["Nicholson David L."]

Title: Collision detection programs for a computer-controlled Thermatron 80 radiotherapy machine
Abstract: A Thermatron 80 cobalt-60 radiotherapy machine has been installed in the Department of Therapeutic Radiology at the Tufts-New England Medical Center. A DEC PDP-11 computer directs this machine under closed-loop control. Initial control use of the system is to automate patient set-up, saving time and also to obtain better accuracy and control of this positioning. The machine has six degrees of freedom within which it is possible for patient- machine as well as machine-machine collisions to occur. In order to prevent this possibility, programs have been developed which, given the initial and final configurations of the six degrees of freedom and their intermediate position trajectories, determine if a collision will occur.
Name: ["Kreifeldt J.G.", "Seymour R.", "Hsieh L.", "Neurath P.W."]

Title: RELIABILITY MODEL USING MARKOV CHAINS FOR UTILITY EVALUATION OF COMPUTER SYSTEMS ONBOARD SHIPS.
Abstract: The reliability aspect of the system is simulated by a model using Markov chains. Having defined the system state space and the transition rates, the model provides evaluation of the state probabilities. Evaluation of system utility is based on computer task values and the failure probabilities. Application of the analysis model to an existing system reveals information useful in assigning redundancy, eliminating bottle-necks and allocating spare parts.
Name: ["Boe Carsten", "Heimly Tor", "Mathiesen Tor Christian"]

Title: Improved algorithm for low-order digital convolution
Abstract: A new algorithm, based on the minimisation of add and multiply operations, is presented for the implementation of a class of low-order real digital-convolution products. ¬© 1973, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Terrell P.M.", "Rayner P.J.W."]

Title: EVALUATION OF FIVE PARAMETER ESTIMATION ALGORITHMS FOR A NONLINEAR REACTOR MODEL VIA MONTE CARLO SIMULATION.
Abstract: The validity of parameter estimation using the normal process record was tested for 5 algorithms by generating simulated records with known statistics via Monte Carlo simulation for 3 models of a well stirred tank reactor. For the model linear in the coefficients, the quasilinearization method gave unbiased estimates with large dispersion whereas the sequential filter gave biased estimates with even greater dispersion. Neither algorithm proved satisfactory for the model nonlinear in the coefficients.
Name: ["Hensley H.D.", "Himmelblau D.M."]

Title: Integrated techniques for functional and gate-level digital logic simulation
Abstract: Digital simulation is defined as the process of exercising a realistic software model of a digital system, with sets of input stimuli, to generate signal behavior versus time. Simulation processes can be categorized by their simulation atom. Gate-level simulation                              <sup>1,2,3,4</sup>                              is simply one in which the atoms of simulation are gates. Functional simulation                              <sup>5,6,7,8</sup>                              simulates larger units, such as adders, decoders, registers, etc. It appears that gate-level simulators can perform accurate simulation                             <sup>4, 9</sup>                             . However, they present some operational limitations, such as the maximum number of gates that can be simulated. Further- more, the host computer time often becomes intolerable for large nets. An additional problem is encountered when the logical net is encoded for input to the simulator. Clerical errors in encoding the net, and their detection and correction, can cause costly delays. Finally, for gate-level simulators, MSI-LSI functional modules must be expanded to a gate-level description. The logical solution to the above limitations is the use of functional simulation techniques.                          ¬© 1973 Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Inc..
Name: ["Szygenda S.A.", "Lekkos A.A."]

Title: TREE TRANSDUCTIONS AND FAMILIES OF TREE LANGUAGES.
Abstract: It is shown that the composition of any n bottom-up transductions can be realized by the composition of n plus 1 top-down transductions, and similarly, the composition of any n top-down transductions can be realized by the composition of n plus 1 bottom-up transductions. The families of tree languages are studied which can be obtained from the recognizable sets (sets accepted by finite tree automata) by the composition of n top-down or bottom-up transductions, n greater than equivalent to O. Finally, the closure properties of the top-down and bottom-up families in both the tree hierarchy and the string hierarchy are investigated.
Name: ["Baker Brenda S."]

Title: COMPUTER ASSISTANCE FOR WRITING INTERACTIVE PROGRAMS: TICS.
Abstract: An on-line and interactive programming system, TICS (for Teacher-Interactive Computer System) is described, which is aimed at facilitating the authoring of interactive computer programs. The system includes particular features for creating instructional software, and in that application it is intended for direct use by persons whose expertise lies in the subject matter being addressed, but not necessarily in computer programming. To that purpose, the system provides a greater degree of computer-assistance for the authoring process itself than has been afforded in earlier languages and programming systems of similar orientation. TICS is implemented within the M. I. T. Multics time-sharing system.
Name: ["Kaplow Roy", "Schneider David", "Smith Jr. Franklin C.", "Stensrud William R."]

Title: SELF-LIMITING ELECTROOPTIC VARIABLE DENSITY FILTERS.
Abstract: A new type of electrooptic variable density filter is reported. It uses a photoconductive film deposited on a transparent lead lanthanum zirconate titanate (PLZT) ferroelectric ceramic plate. In conjunction with a simple bias circuit, a nonlinear filter behavior which limits the transmitted light in a continuously variable manner is achieved. The basic principle of operation is that the resistance of the photoconductive film controls the fraction of the bias voltage applied to the underlying electrooptic material thereby determining the birefringence and, consequently, the optical density of the filter. The term ‚Ä≥self-limiting‚Ä≥ is appropriate since no external sensing or control circuitry is required. The theory of operation of the device is developed for both static and dynamic light conditions, and experimental results on prototype devices are presented. Several applications for this new device are suggested.
Name: ["Schueler D.G.", "Smith W.D."]

Title: ANALYSIS OF ALGORITHMS, A CASE STUDY: DETERMINANTS OF POLYNOMIALS.
Abstract: This article considers the problem of computing the determinant of a matrix of polynomials; two algorithms (expansion by minors and Gaussian elimination) are compared, examining each under two models for polynomial computation (dense univariate and totally sparse). Results are discussed.
Name: ["Gentleman W.M.", "Johnson S.C."]

Title: ON THE ESTIMATION OF THE TRANSFER FUNCTION PARAMETERS OF PROCESS- AND NOISE DYNAMICS USING A SINGLE-STAGE ESTIMATOR.
Abstract: The bias aspects of least squares estimators are dealt with. It is shown that the frequently used generalized least squares technique does not suffer from bias problems but requires a comparatively large number of noise parameters to be estimated. This is due to the fact that the noise is modeled as an autoregressive series. An updating scheme is proposed, which enables modeling of the noise filter as a mixed autoregressive moving-average series. This approach has the important advantage that in principle a smaller number of parameters has to be estimated. Moreover, the process- and noise parameters are determined using a single-stage estimator instead of separated estimators as applied in the generalized least squares scheme.
Name: ["Talmon J.L.", "van den Boom A.J.W."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF COMPLEX SYSTEMS IN TERMS OF REDUCED MODELS.
Abstract: The paper deals with the approximation of systems by means of models within a specified class on the basis of input and output. Discrete linear time-invariant systems are considered. Output data are assumed corrupted by a noise, unknown except for a bound on its energy. A guaranteed cost criterion of approximation is used.
Name: ["Donati F.", "Canuto E."]

Title: MOMENT AND DISTRIBUTION SENSITIVITY OF A TRAFFIC QUEUE CONTROLLER.
Abstract: Parameter optimization has been applied to the control of vehicles entering a highway in order to reduce traffic jams. Sensitivities to changes in mean flows and in distributions for the random arrivals are examined both parametrically and via Monte Carlo simulations. Analytical performance variances are presented, and an adaptive scheme is proposed using a novel mean flow estimator.
Name: ["Shaw Leonard"]

Title: SURVEY OF REDUCED ORDER SENSITIVITY MODELS.
Abstract: Techniques for reducing the order of sensitivity models are surveyed. Work on sensitivity points methods are described. Methods of obtaining reduced order models using state representations of systems are presented. Some recent results on controllability and observability of sensitivity models are presented.
Name: ["Perkins William R."]

Title: PRESENTATION AND MAJOR DESIGN ASPECTS OF THE CYCLADES COMPUTER NETWORK.
Abstract: A computer network is being developed in France, under government sponsorship, to link about twenty heterogeneous computers located in universities, research centers, and data processing centers. Goals are to set up a prototype network in order to foster experiment in various areas, such as: data communications, computer interaction, cooperative research distributed data bases. In order to speed up the implementation, standard equipment is used, and modifications to operating systems are minimized. Rather, the design effort bears on a carefully layered architecture, allowing for a gradual insertion of specialized protocols and services tailored to specific application and user classes. Host-host protocols, as well as error and flow control mechanisms are based on a simple message exchange procedure, on top of which various options may be built for the sake of efficiency, error recovery, or convenience. Depending on available computer resources, these options can be implemented as user software, system modules, or front-end processor packages. CYCLADES uses a packet-switching sub-network, which is a transparent message carrier, completely independent of host-host conventions. While in many ways similar to ARPANET, it presents some distinctive differences in address and message handling, intended to facilitate interconnection with other networks. In particular, addresses can have variable formats, and messages are not delivered in sequence, so that they can flow out of the network through several gates toward an outside target.
Name: ["Pouzin Louis"]

Title: PARTITIONING FOR LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH ARBITRARY STRUCTURAL SYMMETRIES. A GENERALIZATION OF THE BISECTION TECHNIQUE.
Abstract: Group theoretical concepts are applied to the analysis of linear systems having arbitrary structural symmetries. These concepts make possible the identification of the smallest subsystem that supports a set of symmetry basis solutions thereby simplifying to a large extent the computations involved in finding the system equations. An application of the proposed method to electrical network analysis is shown as an example.
Name: ["Rubin Harvey", "Even Reed K."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF NONLINEAR SYSTEMS HAVING PRESCRIBED PERIODIC SOLUTIONS.
Abstract: Methods for synthesizing an autonomous nonlinear system having a prescribed periodic solutions are presented. A third-order differential equation is developed which has the prescribed periodic solution as its steady-state solution. A second-order differential equation is presented which has the periodic solution as its unique C**1 steady-state solution. In additon to solving the synthesis problem, this second order autonomous system exhibits a new phenomenon where trajectories intersect at certain points in the phase plane - called tunnel points - in finite time.
Name: ["Chua Leon O.", "Green D.N."]

Title: SIMULATION - A TOOL FOR PERFORMANCE EVALUATION IN NETWORK COMPUTERS.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: A simulation model is presented for a hypothetical geographically distributed network computer. The approach is to design a general n node network simulator and then to particularize the input parameters to describe ILLINET (the computer communications network at the University of Illinois.
Name: ["Bowdon Sr. Edward K.", "Mamrak Sandra A.", "Salz Fred R."]

Title: MONTE CARLO TECHNIQUES IN STUDYING ROBUST ESTIMATORS.
Abstract: Recent work on robust estimation has led to many procedures which are easy to formulate and straightforward to program but difficult to study analytically. In such circumstances experimental sampling is quite attractive, but the variety and complexity of both estimators and sampling situations make effective Monte Carlo techniques essential. This discussion examines problems, techniques, and results and draws on examples in studies of robust location and robust regression.
Name: ["Hoaglin David C."]

Title: CHINESE CHARACTER RECOGNITION BY HIERARCHICAL PATTERN MATCHING.
Abstract: A new algorithm, named ‚Ä≥Hierarchical Pattern Matching‚Ä≥ , is proposed and is proved useful and practical for Chinese character recognition. The basic idea of this method exists in the process of hierarchical pattern matching from a macroscopic to a microscopic viewing field and in reducing the candidate categories step by step from macro, or less detailed pattern stages, to micro, or more detailed pattern stages. The experimental results for the 881 Chinese character-set are given.
Name: ["Yamamoto S.", "Nakajima A.", "Nakata K."]

Title: CLASSIFICATION OF THE INTERACTIVE WORKLOAD FOR A VIRTUAL MEMORY COMPUTER SYSTEM.
Abstract: A log of user transactions with the T. J. Watson Research Center TSS/360 system was developed. A stratified sampling technique was used to generate a representative sample of user transactions (workload). Prinicpal component analysis was employed to classify the workload based on computing resource demand measurements. The results of the analysis were used in experiments conducted to tune the performance of the system.
Name: ["Anderson Jr. Harold A.", "Galati G.L.", "Reiser Martin"]

Title: An algorithm to estimate sub-optimal present values for unichain markov processes with alternative reward structures
Source: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
Abstract: A new algorithm to obtain a sub-optimal policy and estimate of present values for a class of discounted discrete Markov processes having alternative reward structure in an infinite horizon have been discussed. Based on initial estimates of steady-state probability and gain, this algorithm determines a policy and estimates the present value vectors which could either be used as it is or in conjunction with FR-algorithm or H-algorithm depending upon the accuracy requirement. In both the later cases it generally accelerates the process of computation. ¬© 1973, Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Das Gupta S."]

Title: An Innovations Approach to Least-Squares Estimation-Part VII: Some Applications of Vector Autoregressive-Moving Average Models
Abstract: We use the innovations method to solve some linear estimation problems for stochastic processes described as the solution of high-order linear difference equations driven by colored noise. Such models are often called vector or multivariable auto-regressive-moving average (ARMA) models. We illustrate how the use of ARMA models can provide some simplifications and some new results in the problem of state estimation in colored noise. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Aasnaes H.B.", "Kailath T."]

Title: Regression operator in infinite dimensional vector spaces and its application to some identification problems
Source: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
Abstract: The main purpose of this paper was the transfer of the notion of regression into the theory of Banach valued random variables. This approach enables the formulation of identification problem in the domain of the infinite dimensional probability theory. In the special case, when the random variables are Hilbert valued we state that the regression operator minimizes the square mean error. This makes the proof of the approximation theorem possible in the case of the linear bounded regression operator. Given further the statistical approximation theorem enables practically the identification of linear systems. The problem unsolved in this paper is as well the approximation of the nonlinear regression operator. It seems to the author that the general formulation of identification problem presented in his paper should help with solving also these problems. ¬© 1973, Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Szymanski A."]

Title: SYSTEM FOR OPTIMIZING MACHINE-TOOL CONTROL PROGRAMS.
Abstract: A system which automatically corrects the cutting process relationships for modifying an n. c. machine control program is described. Correction is done by comparing information in the computer memory with data obtained during the machining operation of the initial stage, by means of a feedback control loop.
Name: ["Gaevskii Yu.S."]

Title: Retrieval operations and data representations in a context-addressed disc system
Source: Proceedings of the 1973 Meeting on Programming Languages and Information Retrieval, SIGPLAN 1973
Abstract: This paper attempts to demonstrate that simple expansion of the processing capabilities of fixed disc read and write heads can avoid the multi-level mappings from high-level retrieval language to machine language and from user oriented data representation (information structure) to machine oriented data representation (storage structure) which are found necessary in conventional von Neumann computers. The processing capabilities built in the disc read and write heads for each disc track allow information files to be segmented and data items stored on all segments to be searched, modified, inserted, deleted, rearranged and rewritten simultaneously as a set of discs are rotating. Information structures such as the network structure, the hierarchical or tree structure and the relational structure are discussed and their implementations and basic search operations in the disc system are described. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Su S.Y.W.", "Copeland G.P., Jr.", "Jack Lipovski G."]

Title: On the notion of relevance in information retrieval
Abstract: The paper presents a new point of view about the ‚Äúrelevance‚Äù concept. The logic of information retrieval is analysed (two-valued, many-valued and infinite-valued logic) and the truth-value is interpreted as the relevance value. The logical system which seems to be most appropriate to describe the process of information retrieval is the continuous logic suggested by McNoughton. In- this case the answer of the information retrieval system is interpreted as a fuzzy set. ¬© 1973, MCB UP Limited
Name: ["Negoita C.V."]

Title: PERFORMANCE OF LQG CONTROL SYSTEMS USING OPTIMAL k-STEP-AHEAD CONTROL LAWS.
Abstract: The performance of stochastic LQG control systems using a class of linear and constant but sub-optimal control laws over an indefinite operating time is investigated. The class is that of optimal k-step-ahead control laws, as defined in the paper: it includes the Box-Jenkins-Astroem minimum variance control laws. Analytic expressions are obtained for the expected value of a quadratic performance criterion in a linear system using any constant linear control law. These are used to compare the relative performances of sub-optimal and optimal control laws in several examples. The results lead to conclusions about what characterizes systems where the sub-optimal k-step-ahead control law (i) is close to optimal, (ii) is far from optimal, and (iii) causes instability.
Name: ["Hughes D.J.", "Jacobs O.L.R."]

Title: ADAPTIVE EQUALIZATION
Abstract: The concepts of adaptive filtering theory are used in the development of the basic equations of the adaptive equalizer. The distortion function chosen for minimization is the mean square error. The digital implementation of the adaptive equalizer in a high speed PAM modem is described. That modem has successfully worked at 14,400 bits per second on voice telephone channels of the Autovon Network.
Name: ["Poe W.R."]

Title: CRITERION BASED ON AN INFORMATION THEORETIC MEASURE FOR GOODNESS OF FIT BETWEEN CLASSIFIER AND DATA BASE.
Abstract: A criterion for characterizing an iteratively trained classifier is presented. The criterion is based on an information theoretic measure that is developed from modeling classifier training iterations as a set of cascaded channels. The criterion is formulated as a figure of merit and as a performance index to check the appropriateness of application of the characterized classifier to an unknown data base and for implementing classifier updates and data selection respectively.
Name: ["Eigen D.J.", "Davida G.I.", "Northouse R.A."]

Title: ON BLOB RECONSTRUCTION.
Abstract: Convex blobs (e. g. biological cells, fine particles, etc. ) often appear to an optical input device as an ensemble of overlapped units. Hence a problem is to single out every blob belonging to the ensemble so as to allow quantitative measurements on each blob. Two algorithms are suggested that, using some heuristic hints on the features of the pre-existing contour, reconstruct the blob. Local and global information on the initial contour are considered and a running example showing the operation of each algorithm on the same input blob is described. The adequacy of the proposed solutions could be investigated by studying the results obtained by humans on the same task.
Name: ["Arcelli C.", "Levialdi S."]

Title: DESCRIBING DATA IN COMPUTER NETWORKS.
Abstract: Three major classes of data descriptor messages are discussed (for language processors, for input/output devices, and for resource allocation) that are required by computer networks where the details depend on the variety of systems in a network and on file complexity. Three classes of networks, namely remote job entry networks with compatible operating systems and computers, networks for transmitting arbitrary data sets between systems that have the same internal data representation but different hardware and operating systems, and networks for transmitting arbitrary data sets between arbitrary systems are also discussed. Requirements for the three classes of networks are compared. Further details of networks of systems with the same internal structures but different hardware and operating systems are given.
Name: ["Fredericksen D.H."]

Title: Stochastic extension and functional restrictions of ill-posed estimation problems
Source: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
Abstract: In Theorem 1 it is shown that under mild conditions the minimum-variance smoothed-estimation of a Gaussian process y(t) with covariance Ry(t,œÑ) from noise-corrupted measurements z(t)=y(t)+n(t), t‚ààT, with n(t) Gaussian with covariance R<sub>n</sub>(t,œÑ), is equivalent to a purely deterministic optimization problem, namely, findingy ‚àà H (R<sub>y</sub>) that minimizes the functional (Formula presented.) Here „Äà¬∑,¬∑„Äâ<sub>R</sub> denotes inner-product of the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS)H(R). Theorems 2 and 3 deal with the more general situation where y is a set of linear measurements on an unknown function w(Œ±), Œ± ‚àà A. The above stochastic-deterministic equivalence provides valuable insight and important consequences for modelling. An example shows how this equivalence allows one to make use of Kalman-Bucy filtering in a purely deterministic problem of smoothing. ¬© 1973, Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Mosca E."]

Title: ON SEQUENTIAL REFINEMENT SCHEMES FOR RECURSIVE DIGITAL FILTER DESIGN.
Abstract: A linear synthesis technique is developed for a recursive digital filter which approximates the desired discrete impulse response. Sequential schemes which can be used to refine the preliminary filter design are developed for three distinct cases in which the output sequence number, the filter order and the number of the numerator coefficients of the transfer function are allowed to vary separately. By the use of matrix inversion lemmas, the new sets of filter coefficients are obtained sequentially based on the old estimates and the new data without having to repeat the entire design procedure.
Name: ["Chao Kwong-Shu", "Lu Keh-Shew"]

Title: Linear and nonlinear programming
Abstract: This chapter discusses the application of flow graphs to optimization problems. First, a linear programming (LP) algorithm in which signal-flow-graph (SFG) methods rather than matrix manipulations are used is developed and applied. Then, nonlinear optimization problems are described and optimization procedures are developed based on gradient methods and the LP algorithm. This technique is a variation of Zoutendijk's method of feasible directions. The chapter discusses a general form of LP problems and presents a simplex solution using SFG methods. This is done by Gauss‚ÄìJordan elimination in a simplex algorithm. One of the difficulties with the method is the necessity of redrawing the flow graph at every iteration, which was resolved simply by keeping the A matrix and the number of the basic variable JB(I). ¬© 1973, Academic Press Inc.

Title: Elements of Statistical Decision Theory
Abstract: This chapter focuses on the elements of statistical decision theory. Learning becomes necessary when a priori information is insufficient and so small that the results of statistical decision theory cannot be used directly. Bayes systems form a class of optimal systems. Sufficient a priori information is needed for their realization. If a priori information is given, the problems of recognition and classification consist of computing and comparing the likelihood ratio and threshold. Minimization of different criteria of optimality is reduced to a corresponding change of thresholds. Several ways to overcome lack of a priori information are (1) processing current information in order to determine necessary data and (2) applying the min-max decision rule that guarantees the best decision under the worst conditions. If the conditions are close to the worst conditions, this approach provides an acceptable solution. A decision system that has a larger margin of error than what is desirable is obtained. ¬© 1973, Academic Press Inc.
Name: ["Fisher R."]

Title: Synthesis of an adaptive observer using lyapunov's direct method
Abstract: An adaptive scheme is synthesized to estimate the state vector and identify all the parameters of a Single-input single-output nth order linear system, from only the input‚Äîoutput data. The scheme is proved to be asymptotically stable in the whole, thus ensuring the convergence of the identification process. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Kudva P.", "Narendra K.S."]

Title: Tree Systems for Syntactic Pattern Recognition
Abstract: An approach of representing patterns by trees rather than by strings is described. A review of tree systems that include tree grammars, transformations, and mappings on trees and tree automata is briefly presented. The tree system is then applied to the problem of syntactic pattern recognition. Tree grammars are used for pattern description, and tree automata are used for classification. Illustrative examples include the application of the tree system to the classification of bubble chamber events and some English characters. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Fu K.-S.", "Bhargava B.K."]
Keywords: ["bubble chamber events", "picture recognition", "syntactic pattern recognition", "tree automata", "tree grammars"]

Title: OPTIMUM DISTRIBUTION OF REDUCTION STAGES IN AN AUTOMATED ROLLING-MILL CONTROL SYSTEM.
Abstract: The problem of optimum distribution of reduction stages in a continuous cold-rolling mill is solved by successive analysis and optimization of variants. A nonadditive criterion is considered in the problem with fixed trajectory ends. An algorithm is given for solving the problem on a general-purpose computer in an automated mill control system.
Name: ["Mozgovaya E.A.", "Orzhel A.D.", "Olefir F.F."]

Title: QUANTIZATION EFFECTS IN DIGITAL FILTERS.
Abstract: The principal effects of quantization of input data, of filter coefficients, and of finite arithmetic precision, are each treated in detail as they affect filter performance. The effects described include noise and limit cycles.
Name: ["Kaiser James F."]

Title: OPTIMAL CONTROL OF A VARIABLE SPIN SPEED CMG SYSTEM FOR SPACE VEHICLES.
Abstract: A control system is suggested for providing the very highly accurate pointing stability required for certain future NASA spacecraft missions. For example, one proposed mission of NASA requires the pointing stability to be plus or minus 0. 005 arc-second during the experiment observation time which can last for several hours. The proposed system consists of three double gimbal control moment gyros with changeable rotor momenta. These changeable rotor momenta, within the range of about plus or minus 10% of the momentum bias, will provide the system with the required highly accurate control capability. An optimal control law for the suggested system is specified. However, since no direct method of solution is known for this complicated system, a computation technique using successive approximations is used to develop the required solution. The method of calculus of variations is applied for estimating the changes of index of performance as well as those constraints of inequality of state variables and terminal conditions. Thus, an algorithm is obtained by the steepest descent method and/or conjugate gradient method. Numerical examples are given to show the optimal controls.
Name: ["Liu T.C.", "Chubb W.B.", "Seltzer S.M.", "Thompson Zack"]

Title: INFORMATION APPROACH TO EVALUATING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF A COMPUTER/MACHINE ALGORITHM SYSTEM.
Abstract: The authors propose to use the DELTA I-method ( DELTA I being the average risk) to make an overall evaluation of the characteristics of a computer/machine algorithm system and to give a formalized compact description of this system. The approach is illustrated with examples of machine algorithms and descriptions and evaluations of the efficiency of the characteristics of the addition operation.
Name: ["Korchagin V.G.", "Sadomov Yu.B.", "Khokhlov L.M."]

Title: INTERCHANGEABILITY OF THE ROUTH AND JURY TABULAR ALGORITHMS FOR LINEAR SYSTEM ZERO LOCATION.
Abstract: The Routh and Jury tabular schemes for determination of linear system zero location relative to the left half plane and unit disc respectively are formulated as special cases of two algorithms for finding the greatest common divisor of two polynomials. Two recent extensions of the tabular methods are expressed similarly, and this enables a previously unknown 'duality' property of the two zero location algorithms to be demonstrated, namely, that a Routh-type array can be applied to the unit disc problem, and a Jury-type array to the left half plane problem, and these applications occur in a precisely symmetrical fashion. Extensions are given for complex polynomials, and remarks are made on the problem of coefficient growth during array construction.
Name: ["Barnett S."]

Title: ESTIMATION OF STATE VARIABLE MODELS USING INPUT-OUTPUT DATA.
Abstract: Starting from a comparison, analysis, and review of some existing methods for the identification of minimal realization of linear time-invariant multivariable dynamic systems, a modification of a previously published method is suggested which permits considerable saving in computation. The modification is based on an important property of linear systems which allows the order of the minimal realization to be determined in advance by direct processing of available input-output data.
Name: ["Bingulac S.P.", "Djorovic M."]

Title: CUTTING PLANE ALGORITHM FOR THE FIXED CHARGE PROBLEM.
Abstract: The fixed-charge problem arises in a host of industrial applications and plant location problems. An algorithm is devised for solving this problem with linear constraints. The algorithm employs especially constructed cuts to locate the global optimum point. Computational results are included.
Name: ["Taha Hamdy A."]

Title: ON BIAS REDUCTION IN FILTERING PROBLEMS WITH NON-LINEAR MEASUREMENTS BY FIRST ORDER ITERATIVE METHODS.
Abstract: A study is presented concerning first-order filtering methods for estimation problems with measurement which are nonlinear functions of the state. A qualitative interpretation of the linearized, the extended, and the iterated Kalman filters is first given in the scalar case. The superiority of the iterated filters for bias reduction, as compared with the classical filters, is then proved when the measurement noise is very small relative to the estimate error or for a large number of measurements. These results are illustrated by a numerical simulation of the attitude restitution of a spinning satellite.
Name: ["Huynh Huu Thanh"]

Title: METHOD FOR MODELLING THE PROCESS DYNAMICS DIRECTLY IN THE TIME DOMAIN.
Abstract: Time functions are derived which make it possible to identify the ‚Ä≥decisive time interval‚Ä≥ (DTI) wqhich is a portion of the step response having the major influence on the dynamic behavior of a system. Methods are presented for matching the DTI of the step response of a system to that of a suitably selected model structure.
Name: ["Frigyes A."]

Title: Describing an algorithm by Hopcroft
Abstract: We give an algorithm, its correctness proof, and its proof of execution time bound, for finding the sets of equivalent states in a deterministic finite state automaton. The time bound is K ¬∑ m ¬∑ n ¬∑ log n where K is a constant, m the number of input, symbols, and n the number of states. Hopcroft [3] has already published such an algorithm. The main reason for this paper is to illustrate the use of communicating an algorithm to others using a structured, top-down approach. We have also been able to improve on Hopcroft's algorithm by reducing the size of the algorithm and correspondingly complicating the proof of the running time bound. ¬© 1973 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Gries D."]

Title: Closed Loop Formulations of Optimal Control Problems for Minimum Sensitivity
Abstract: The dynamical behavior of many physical processes can be described by differential equations. The ability of such a description to correctly predict the actual system response is directly related to the accuracy of the mathematical model. Errors in the model can result from unsatisfactory initial approximations and from actual component variations after the model has been produced. When a differential equation is used for controller design, the resulting control may greatly depend on various parameters in the model. If these parameters remain at their design values, the control input to the actual process will produce the desired output. However, if the actual system deviates from the model, the desired output may not be realized. Modeling accuracy is particularly important in the practical application of optimal control theory. There are many quantities related to the optimization problem, such as the cost functional, constraint boundaries, and terminal manifold, which are affected by parameter variations. ¬© 1973, ACADEMIC PRESS, INC.
Name: ["Crane R.N.", "Stubberud A.R."]

Title: COMPUTER CONTROLLED ELECTRON MICROPROBE ANALYSER.
Abstract: A new computer program to facilitate chemical analysis with a computer-controlled electron microprobe analyser has recently been developed. Complete control of three analysing channels is provided so that the task of performing the necessary fine adjustments to the equipment is considerably simplified in both routine and non-routine cases. By entering simple commands at a teletype, the computer can be instructed to set or display measuring parameters, locate and measure x-ray intensity peaks, move the specimen, and monitor the specimen absorbed current. Further, programs can be constructed, either in the computer memory, or on paper tape, to carry out lengthy and complex sequences of operations. With a single initialisation of the system, a complete analysis of up to twenty-four elements, at many specimen positions, may be stored. Thus, the operator is relieved of the continual supervision and adjustment which is necessary with a manual system. At present, a small dedicated computer is used, but the operating system is written in such a way that it could easily be made part of a larger time-shared system.
Name: ["Grinton Geoffrey R."]

Title: DEMULTIPLEXING CONSIDERATIONS IN COMPUTER/COMMUNICATIONS SYSTEMS.
Abstract: As the architecture of time sharing computer networks becomes more distributed, the design problems of the multiplexor/demultiplexor systems have become more important. In this paper, consideration is given to the trade-offs required between the CPU scheduling algorithm and the demultiplexing buffer characteristics in order to optimize the computer communications network. The demultiplexing buffer is analyzed by means of a queueing model with batch Poisson arrivals and multiple distinct constant servers. The relationship among the buffer size, buffer overflow probability, average message length and CPU scheduling algorithm is derived.
Name: ["Durr L."]

Title: COMPUTER-AIDED EQUATION FORMULATION AND SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS FOR DISCRETE SYSTEMS.
Abstract: System equations are formulated in terms of the submatrices of the summing and branching matrices of signal flow graphs for multi-input, multi-output discrete systems. A theorem similar to Tellegen's Theorem in network theory is presented for signal flow graphs. As in network theory, the application of this theorem leads to defining the adjoint signal flow graphs for discrete systems. From this, a sensitivity calculation of output variables with respect in a system parameter is developed which is equivalent to the analysis of two signal flow graphs, the original one and its adjoint. These results lead to straightforward algorithms which may be implemented in a general automated discrete system analysis and design computer program.
Name: ["Lee Arnold Y."]

Title: ON SURVIVABILITY CALCULATIONS OF PROBABILISTIC COMMUNICATION NETWORKS.
Abstract: The probability of survival H of a communication network is defined as the probability of maintaining communication between every pair of stations so that it is the algebraic sum of the probabilities of all the possible states, in each of which a complete tree of the network graph exists. Computation of approximate values of survivability are made and with the aid of computers, a number of communication networks are investigated to determine maximum error of the approximation formula.
Name: ["Chan S.G.", "Enginler S."]

Title: CONTROL OF CHANNEL ASSIGNMENT IN TACTICAL TDMA SATELLITE COMMUNICATION.
Abstract: In a multiple-user, demand-accessed satellite system, two areas of fundamental concern are resource organization (sharing of capacity through multiple access) and resource allocation (control of access). This paper is based on a particular TDMA organization designed for tactical satellite communications. The resource control aspect, that is, control of on-demand access to the repeater, is complicated by diverse terminal capabilities and traffic requirements, and an ever changing level of system utilization resulting from random, independent link initiations and terminations. A definition of optimal channel assignment under such circumstances is presented in this paper. An assignment algorithm which meets this definition when assigning channels from a channel organization like the one presented is developed and explained.
Name: ["Doggett John E.", "Kinal George V.", "Talbot Stuart H."]

Title: OPTIMAL DESIGN OF A HELICOPTER PRECISION HOVER CONTROL SYSTEM.
Abstract: Modern control theory is employed to analytically determine the limit of positional precision with which a helicopter can be hovered. Approaches based on Liapunov's second method and a squared root locus method are formulated to this optimal control problem. Both of these methods avoid iterative solution of the matrix Riccati equation. The squared root locus method is developed as a computer algorithm which generates optimal control designs as a function of performance index and helicopter for stability/control derivatives. Practical design constraints can readily be interpreted from the results of this formulation.
Name: ["Puri N.N."]

Title: Phototype II: A job selection simulation model
Source: Proceedings of the 1st Symposium on Simulation of Computer Systems, ANSS 1973
Abstract: Optimization of a multiprogramming computer configuration is a complex task. The most common approach in establishing a mix of resources and a classing/initiator configuration is to make an educated guess and, over a period of time, to make refinements through a series of increasingly more educated guesses. This paper describes an alternate approach to optimization of resources and job selection through simulation. This use of simulation departs from the accepted simulation philosophy in that by using actual utilization statistics as control parameters, the model represents a computer system functionally rather than abstractly. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Byrne T.A.", "Piercey A.V.", "Myers F.L."]

Title: Non-canonical parsing
Source: 14th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory
Abstract: Although the field of "canonical parsing" (i.e. parsing in which we always reduce the leftmost phrase of a sentential form) has been extensively studied, the field of noncanonical parsing has been relatively untouched. In this paper, we first motivate the whole study by presenting a language which is intrinsically non-canonical and then we develop a general model of bottom-up parsing which incorporates the capability of making non-canonical reductions. These parsers have the important properties of operating in linear time and of being implementable on "traditional" automata. Finally, in section 3 we extend several existing parsing methods to utilize our ideas and examine the relationships between the various classes so produced. ¬© 1973 IEEE.
Name: ["Szymanski T.G.", "Williams J.H."]

Title: RECURSIVE DIGITAL FILTER SYNTHESIS IN THE TIME DOMAIN.
Abstract: The nonlinear minimization problem which results from recursive digital filter design with phase constraints is simplified somewhat by working in the time domain. This paper describes techniques which utilize the time samples of the desired response as target values for an iterative minimization. Initial values for the alpha and beta (feedforward and feedback) coefficients can be obtained by one of several reliable methods and fed into iterative routines which lead to a locally optimal solution for the coefficients. The initial guess procedures, stemming from regression-like equations, only require the solution of a set of linear equations. In addition, the iteration procedures described in this paper lead to recursive filter designs requiring little computer time. Examples are presented to illustrate a range of applications.
Name: ["Brophy F.X.", "Salazar A.C."]

Title: COMPUTER-ASSISTANCE FOR LOCAL TRUCKLOAD SCHEDULING DECISIONS.
Abstract: Describes a computerized scheduling algorithm for local truckload operations called LOTSA. This algorithm comprises a portion of a computer software package known as DSPTCH. DSPTCH, currently under development and testing, is seen as a prototype of the computer-assisted decision-making needed to resolve the general local truck scheduling problem.
Name: ["Heisterberg R.J.", "Reed Jr. Ruddell"]

Title: n-dimensional array languages and description of crystal symmetry-I
Source: Proceedings of the Indian Academy of Sciences - Section A
Abstract: Following the general linguistic approach proposed by Narasimhan to pattern recognition we proposed two generative models, viz., the matrix models and the more powerful two-dimensional array models. In this paper we generalize the matrix models to n-dimensions and establish that the n-dimensional matrix models are closed under union, concatenation, Kleene closure, ‚àà-free homomorphism, inverse homomorphism and intersection with regular matrices. Symmetry operations such as translation, reflection and half-turn are examined. ¬© 1973 Indian Academy of Sciences.
Name: ["Siromoney R.", "Krithivasan K.", "Siromoney G."]

Title: Interval arithmetic for guaranteed bounds in linear programming
Source: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
Abstract: In this note, we show how interval arithmetic can be used to give a solution to the linear programming problem which is guaranteed to be on the safe side of the true solution, where roundoff error is taken into account. ¬© 1973 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Stewart N.F."]

Title: A Survey of Some Theoretical Aspects of Multiprocessing
Abstract: In this paper, several theoretical aspects of multiprocessing are surveyed. First, we look at the language features that help in exploiting parallelism. The additional instructions needed for a multiprocessor architecture; problems, such as mutual exclusion, raised by the concurrent processing of parts of a program; and the extensions to existing high-level languages are examined. The methods for automatic detection of parallelism in current high-level languages are then reviewed both at the inter and intra statement levels. The following part of the paper deals with more theoretical aspects of multiprocessing. Different models for parallel computation such as graph models, Petri nets, parallel flowcharts, and flow graph schemata are introduced. Finally, prediction of performance of multiprocessors either through analysis of models or by simulation is examined In an appendix, an attempt ~s made toward the classification of existing multlprocessors. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Baer J.L."]
Keywords: ["array processors", "automatic detection of parallehsm", "flow graph schemata", "graph models", "multlprocessing"]

Title: Debugging aids for hybrid- computer programmers
Abstract: We discuss here proposals for two new debugging aids for hybrid-computer programmers. For digital programs, ‚Äúrelevant‚Äù post-mortem dumps have long been advocated.<sup>1</sup>We propose extending this philoso phy to analog dumps. We describe means of making selective dumps via analysis of the topological structure of analog programs. We also propose a novel analog static-check procedure which takes advantage of the greater computational facilities afforded by a digital computer to solve algebraic equations. The analog-dump and static-check methods recommended here, at worst, help hybrid programmers with their debugging efforts by automating certain common tac tics. Many errors can thereby be automatically detected and precisely located. In conclusion, we suggest how correction of these errors can be auto mated to some extent. ¬© 1973, Sage Publications. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Lew A."]

Title: SCHEDULING JOBS ON PARALLEL PROCESSORS WITH DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING
Abstract: The problem of scheduling jobs on M‚Äêparallel processors is one of selecting a set of jobs to be processed from a set of available jobs in order to maximize profit. This problem is examined and a dynamic programming solution is presented which decomposes it into a sequencing problem within an allocation problem. The computation required for solution is found to depend on the sequencing problem as it is affected by the waiting cost function. Various forms of the waiting cost function are considered. The solution procedure is illustrated by an example, and possible extensions of the formulation are discussed. Copyright ¬© 1973, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved
Name: ["Gupta J.N.D.", "Maykut A.R."]
Affiliations: ['U. S. Postal Service', 'U S Army Missile Command']

Title: Preliminary classification of mass spectral patterns using a simplified learning machine
Abstract: A simplified learning machine technique is presented which is suitable for forming preliminary classification of patterns. This technique allows preliminary compression of data prior to the training process, and generates a reliable classifier even when there are linearly inseparable data in the training set. This method has been used to form an eight-feature pattern classifier which identifies, directly from their mass spectra, compounds of the structure (RO)<sub>2</sub>P(=X)Y where R is H, Me, or Et; X is O or S; and Y is any functional group. ¬© 1973, CSIRO. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Mathews R.J."]

Title: A unified approach to global program optimization
Source: Conference Record of the Annual ACM Symposium on Principles of Programming Languages
Abstract: A technique is presented for global analysis of program structure in order to perform compile time optimization of object code generated for expressions. The global expression optimization presented includes constant propagation, common subexpression elimination, elimination of redundant register load operations, and live expression analysis. A general purpose program flow analysis algorithm is developed which depends upon the existence of an "optimizing function." The algorithm is defined formally using a directed graph model of program flow structure, and is shown to be correct. Several optimizing functions are defined which, when used in conjunction with the flow analysis algorithm, provide the various forms of code optimization. The flow analysis algorithm is sufficiently general that additional functions can easily be defined for other forms of global code optimization. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Kildall G.A."]

Title: The architecture of CASSM: A cellular system for non-numeric processing
Source: Proceedings - International Symposium on Computer Architecture
Abstract: This paper presents the architecture of a contextaddressed cellular system for non-numerlc information processing, using an inexpensive, large-capacity circulating memory device. The system allows data to be represented in a structure very close to the form as the user perceives it (information structure) and allows the search operations of high level queries to be implemented directly. The information structures currently used in existing information systems are described. Then the architecture of the system as a whole is presented, as well as the implementation of these information structures as basic data types and hardware management of storage allocation and garbage collection. The paper intends to demonstrate that distributing intelligence throughout a rotating memory device can decrease the time required for search operations in large data bases. And that the search strategy and storage management functions can be efficiently carried out in hardware, greatly simplifying the software of information systems. Thus, data not only becomes faster but easier to access, verify, insert and delete. ¬© 1973 Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Inc..
Name: ["Copeland G.P., Jr.", "Lipovski G.J.", "Su S.Y.W."]

Title: PERFORMANCE CAPABILITY OF RESPONSIVE ELECTRONIC VEHICULAR INSTRUMENTATION SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The operation of a proposed aid to disabled motorist system is described. Microscopically monitoring traffic flow data with a responsive electronic vehicular instrumentation system, REVIS, is shown by digital simulation to result in decreased mean wait time for the arrival of aid at the scene of an incident. The system additionally allows for the telemetering of data between the vehicle and inroad detectors; its fundamental real time function being achieved without motorist intervention.
Name: ["Nadan J.S.", "Wiener Richard"]

Title: APPLICATIONS OF AUTOMATIC VEHICLE LOCATION SYSTEMS TO RAILROAD OPERATIONS.
Abstract: The LORAN based AVM system currently offers the best combination of high location accuracy, large area coverage, low cost and high dependability. Location accuracies of plus or minus 100 ft at ranges of 1000 miles from Coast Guard operated LORAN navigation transmitter stations are attainable over virtually all of the eastern half of the United STates. The vehicle based equipment is portable and can be attached to a vehicle such as a locomotive within minutes. LORAN's unique combination of high accuracy and long-range performance attributes make it an ideal system for displaying to a dispatcher or yardmaster the locationof all locomotives and trains under his control as well as information on their speed and the distance betweenthem. Most prominent among these applications are terminal areas where the LORAN-AVM system can be used to maintain surveillance over the activities of switching engines.
Name: ["Jakobsberg Wolfgang"]

Title: A method for construction of suboptimal non-linear regulators by minimax algorithm‚Ä†
Abstract: A method is proposed for an approximate construction of the optimal state regulator for an autonomous non-linear system with quadratic performance index. The method is bused upon the instantaneous linearization technique developed by Pearson. In the method of instantaneous linearization, the non-linear system is approximated by a state-dependent linear model. However, the solution is not optimal in general because of the arbitrariness of the linearized model. The purpose of the present paper is to correct the shortcomings of this method. First, an optimality condition for the control law obtained by the method of instantaneous linearization is derived. Secondly, by making use of this condition, a systematic procedure is presented to determine a suboptimal feedback control for a second-order system. A minimax algorithm is used to design the linearized model closely approximating the original system within a prescribed region in the state space. The validity of the present method is shown by examining typical examples. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Sannomiya N."]

Title: INDIVIDUAL ITEM FORECASTING MODEL EVALUATION
Abstract: A computer simulation experiment was conducted to evaluate and compare seven individual item forecasting models across five different demand patterns. Results indicate the best model varies depending upon the demand pattern, the time period forecast, the noise level of the demand pattern, and to a lesser extent the measure of forecast error. Across all demand patterns, exponential double smoothing was best for the long run forecast and at least second best for the short run regardless of noise level in the demand patterns. Analysis of models within a demand pattern yielded, in most cases, several models as ranking equally well. The adaptive model developed here did not perform as well as some other models. For example, it ranked no better than third on a step function demand pattern. Copyright ¬© 1973, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved
Name: ["Adam E.E., Jr."]

Title: Experimental evaluation of optimal multivariable servo control in conjunction with conventional regulatory control
Abstract: The problem considered is that of driving a multivariable process controlled by conventional feedback control algorithms, from some initial state, to a specified final state such that a linear performance index is minimized. The formulation is based on a linear, discrete, time-invariant model of the process plus a minimum-time or sum of the absolute errors criterion and is solved using a standard linear programming algorithm. Constraints on the state and/or control variables can be incorporated to guarantee practical, physically realizable control policies. Experimental and simulated results show that the technique is easy to implement, and that the use of different criteria produces significantly different process transients. Experimental data from a computer-controlled, pilot plant evaporator show that the method is practical and produces better results than conventional methods. ¬© 1973, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Nieman R.E.", "Grant Fisher D."]

Title: Collection properties influencing automatic term classification performance
Abstract: Retrieval performance with automatic term classifications for three test collections has been variable: it has been effective in one case and ineffective in two. This paper attempts to discover why. It describes experiments designed to show how classification performance depends on (a) the supply of terms for matching in request and document descriptions, (b) the supply of terms for classification in document descriptions and term vocabulary and (c) the supply of strong connections between terms. The classification failures for the two collections cannot be attributed to inadequacies in these respects. It is shown that the real difference between the collections is in the separation of relevant from non-relevant documents. The separation for the two collections is so poor that classification cannot be expected to succeed. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Jones K.S."]

Title: AUTOMATION IN MANNED AEROSPACE SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Proceedings includes 24 papers on the current capabilities and potentials for automating manned aerospace systems as well as on the tools currently available and under development for assigning system functions to man, machine and man and machine, so as to best satisfy aerospace system requirements and constraints. Following is a list of titles and authors of 24 papers presented: Man's Role in Integrated Control and Information Management Systems. By J. L. Nevins and I. S. Johnson. General Guideline for the Design of Manned Aerospace Vehicles. By J. Wanner. Influence of Cost and Technical Risk on the Design of the Avionics System for the Space Shuttle. By H. T. Wright. Automatic Acquisition and Tracking Methods Employed in the Joint Services In-Flight Data Transmission System (JIFDATS). By T. N. Leiboff. Determination of an Optimal Trajectory in the Presence of Risk. By A. Tiano, P. Dagnino and M. Piatteli. Space Station Information System Requirements - A Case History of Man-Machine System Definition. By C. R. Gerber. Automated Techniques for Spacecraft Monitoring. By H. R. Segnar. Some Development Trends in the Integration of Electronic Systems in the Swedish Aircraft 37 Viggen. By B. Sjoberg. Multiloop Attitude Control System for a Satellite with Flexible Booms. By R. Di Lorenzo and E. De Bernardis.
Name: ["Nevins J.L.", "Johnson I.S.", "Wanner J.", "Wright H.T.", "Leiboff T.N.", "Tiano A.", "Dagnino P.", "Piatteli M.", "Gerber C.R.", "Segnar H.R.", "Sjoberg B.", "Di Lorenzo R.", "De Bernardis E."]

Title: Bayes estimation of a convex quadratic
Abstract: The estimation of a quadratic regression curve when the quadratic coefficient is known to be positive is treated by a Bayesian method. The method extends easily to deal with a general linear model under parameter constraints.
Name: ["O'Hagan A."]

Title: A theory for the induction of mathematical functions
Abstract: Presents a detailed theory for how humans induce mathematical functions to explain observed data. The theory is based on both solution times and verbal protocols. It proposes that induction is a heuristically directed generate-and-test process. The order in which hypotheses are generated is mostly independent of the data. Each hypothesis is maintained until it is negated, but a false hypothesis that matches part of the data is frequently retested. A computer simulation program, incorporating these processes, accurately predicted solution times for Ss on different sets of problems without any changes in parameters. In addition, the program's solution protocols were indistinguishable from human protocols. (25 ref.) (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2006 APA, all rights reserved). ¬© 1973 American Psychological Association.
Name: ["Huesmann L.R.", "Cheng C.-M."]
Keywords: ["solution times  verbal protocols theory induction of mathematical functions for explanations of observed data", "induce mathematical", "induction mathematical", "theory based", "proposes induction"]

Title: REAL-TIME NUCLEAR POWER PLANT PARAMETER IDENTIFICATION WITH A PROCESS COMPUTER.
Abstract: A dynamic least squares on-line identification algorithm is implemented on a process computer and applied to a simulated process and real process data. The pressure dynamics and the core dynamics of the halden Boiling Water Reactor are studied with the help of this algorithm. Digitally designed filters were used for filtering the process input and output signals.
Name: ["Roggenbauer Helmut"]

Title: SIMULATION OF HUMAN LEARNING AND HUMAN DECISION MAKING.
Abstract: The ultimate goal of this project is to devise a methodology which emulates human problem solving and decision making in complex situations requiring value judgements of qualitative information. Inherent in the process of sophisticated decision making in a dynamic world is learning. The methodology employed has been incorporated in several programs and these programs have achieved some success against humans. The methodology utilizes game theory techniques, computer modeling and simulation, Bayes' Theorem, and builds on A. Samuel's successes with a linear evaluation function.
Name: ["Clema Joe K.", "Fynewever Mark S."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION OF VERY NOISY DYNAMIC PROCESSES USING MODELS WITH FEW PARAMETERS.
Abstract: The variances of the parameter estimates of a dynamic process can be reduced by using models with as many equal parameters as possible. This is shown for continuous processes by using the Cramer-Rao inequality. A very simple method for identifying a dynamic process with three unknown parameters is also given.
Name: ["Isermann Rolf"]

Title: DETECTION OF MALFUNCTION USING A PROCESS CONTROL COMPUTER SIMPLE NOISE POWER TECHNIQUES FOR INSTRUMENTS.
Abstract: The general problems of malfunction detection by the computer and by the process operator are discussed. A technique for the detection of malfunction, namely the analysis of the average power of the noise, i. e. , noisiness, of instrument signals is considered. The advantage of the technique is that it is general, is applicable to many types of instrument and can be used on single instruments. It is claimed to have given promising results in limited laboratory and industrial trials.
Name: ["Anyakora S.N.", "Lees F.P."]

Title: Boundary detection and volume determination of the left ventricle from a cineangiogram
Abstract: This paper is concerned with a method to detect left ventricular boundaries and the subsequent volume computation from a cineangiogram by a digital computer. It will first describe three digital techniques: (1) to restore the original dimensions by a logarithmic transformation; (2) to reduce noise by averaging images; and (3) to subtract images after and before dye injection, and then a boundary detection method based on statistical principles and heuristics. A method to locate the aortic valve will also be described. Experimental results on several cine frames will be presented to demonstrate the feasibility of these techniques. Once the boundary of the ventricle is determined, the computation of the volume is performed by the usual Simpson's rule. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Chow C.K.", "Kaneko T."]
Keywords: ["boundary detection", "cardiac cineangiogram", "detection of aortic valve", "digital image processing", "dynamic threshold method"]

Title: Every discrete input machine is linearly simulatable
Source: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: This paper extends the work of Herman (1971) to show that all discrete input sequential machines (whether finite or infinite state) are linearly simulatable over fields of infinite characteristic. Since this permits the computation of nonrecursive functions, it is concluded that allowing nonlinear output decoding with infinite state linear machines leads to a triviality (as opposed to the case of finite state linear machines where it does not). ¬© 1973 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Zeigler B.P."]

Title: State-space approach in problem-solving optimization
Source: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (including subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics)
Abstract: In this paper we have proposed a new description of SSPS, called syntactic description, which constitutes a framework useful to structure a rich content of informations about a given problem. The semantic description has been shown to be equivalent to the syntactic description of SSPS. A method has been briefly outlined, which is based on the semantic description, and which makes possible to extract, in an automatic way, i. e., by computation, the heuristic information useful to guide the search in the state space. The future research work shall be addressed to the exploitation of the semantic description as a powerful basis on which to formulate procedures apted to solve the main goal of automatic problem-solving. In particular the direction of heuristic guided search and learning will be investigated. ¬© 1973, Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Vincentelli A.S.", "Somalvico M."]

Title: USE OF SYMBOLIC COMPUTER GRAPHICS IN DYNAMIC MODELS OF BIOLOGICAL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Computer-based graphical techniques are now available which permit a biologist or medical researcher who is not a computer specialist to construct and test mathematical models of biological systems. These techniques are useful in studies of systems consisting of a number of interconnected elements, where each element consists of a simple well-defined operation. Tracer, chemical, and cellular kinetic studies as well as electrical and fluid-flow networks have been simulated by this method. Models are created by arranging symbols, lines, and labels to describe graphically the desired arrangement of elements. When a graphical model has been completed, it can be automatically translated into a program. Since the user generates the text definition of his elements, he can choose to define these in any programming language for which a compiler is available.
Name: ["Horovitz Mark W."]

Title: Identification of predictor and filter parameters by ARMA methods
Abstract: The present paper describes procedures for recursive joint identification of the parameters of mixed autoregressive-moving-average models and for the determination of their order. The procedures given are subsequently extended to joint the estimation of the transition and the covariance parameters of single output and multi-output Kalman‚ÄîBucy filters in cases where both input and measurement noise sequences exist. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Krause D.J.", "Graupe D."]
Affiliations: [' North Dakota State University', ' Colorado State University']

Title: An upper limb prosthesis orthosis power and control system with multi level potential
Source: Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery - Series A
Abstract: An electrical power and control unit was designed to power paralyzed or prosthetic upper limb joints in the mode of an artificial muscle.
