The system permits placing the components in any desirable location on the patient, interchanging terminal devices, actuating more than one joint by a single motor, and easy interfacing with a wide variety of orthotic and prosthetic components,  including those of modular endoskeletal design. Sensor options for control signal acquisition include a new skin motion sensor for shoulder disarticulation amputees and an improved myoelectric sensor.
Name: ["Schmeisser G.", "Seamone W."]

Title: HIGHER LEVEL LANGUAGE FOR MICRO-PROGRAMMING.
Abstract: A brief review is presented of some high level languages for microcoding. A new language is given that provides an efficient way for detecting and locating parallel processable independent actions for possible representation in microinstruction.
Name: ["Ramamoorthy C.V.", "Tabandeh M.", "Tsuchiya M."]

Title: CONTINUED FRACTION METHODS FOR THE REDUCTION OF LINEAR TIME-INVARIANT SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Continued fraction methods are given for the reduction in order of single input/output linear time-invariant systems. It is shown how the algorithm of Chen and Shieh (see Engineering Index 1971 p 283 abstract 25903) may be used twice to derive biased reduced order models. It has been shown that Jordan-type continued fractions may be used to derive reduced order models, which are equivalent to those derived by a Cauer-type expansion. The advantage of using a Jordan-type continued fraction is that it is easier to compute and invert, especially when applied to the reduction of multivariable systems.
Name: ["Shamash Y."]

Title: Possible improvement in television-signal prediction due to interframe correlation
Abstract: An analysis of t.v. signals as a 3rd-order Markoff source has been made. Possible improvements achieved by a 3rd-order prediction is also examined. ¬© 1973, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Isailoviƒá J."]
Keywords: ["filtering and prediction theory", "markov processes", "television", "video signals", "improvement television"]

Title: ON-LINE OPTIMIZATION PROCEDURE FOR AN URBAN TRAFFIC SYSTEM.
Abstract: A method is described for the on-line optimizing closed loop control of urban traffic systems. The method of approach is to use the theory of hierarchial systems as developed by M. D. Mesarovic and the decomposition of the system follows the pattern used in Madrid, Spain by H. H. Fuehrer.
Name: ["Macleod C.J.", "Al-Khalili A.J."]

Title: MULTIPLE-OUTPUT NAND NETWORKS SYNTHESIZED IN SECONDS WITH COMPUTER PROGRAM THAT ACCOUNTS FOR FAN-IN AND FAN-OUT LIMITS.
Abstract: The article discusses an efficient computer algorithm for the synthesis of multiple-output, multiple-level NAND (NOR) combinational networks that accounts for the practical fan-in and fan-out limits of these logic gates. The program's ability to handle many variables and to realize solutions with near minimum numbers of gates makes it ideally suited for practical computer designs.
Name: ["Su Stephen Y.H."]

Title: STOCHASTIC ANALYSIS OF EMG SIGNALS FOR MULTI-FUNCTIONAL PROSTHESIS CONTROL PURPOSES.
Source: Ky Univ Off Res Eng Serv Bull K UKY BU104, Carnahan Conf on Electron Prosthet, Proc
Abstract: A stochastic analysis of EMG signals is described in terms of a time-series analysis. Following an analysis of the p. d. f. of the innovation of the EMG signals, an ARMA model for various recorded EMG signals is derived, and subsequently a K-B filter model is obtained. It is demonstrated that recognition of various limb functions is facilitated via this analysis and the resultant identification, as is required for multifunctional EMG control of prostheses. Realization problems are discussed.
Name: ["Graupe Daniel", "Cline William K.", "Kaplon Ted K."]

Title: ON THE STABILITY OF A DISTRIBUTED PARAMETER PROCESS WITH POISSONIAN NOISE.
Abstract: A class of stochastic distributed-parameter processes is dealt with. The class is represented by a one-dimensional distributed parameter feedback system where the gain is corrupted by a random noise of the Poisson type. Sufficient conditions, for weak stability of the systems solutions, are observed.
Name: ["Yavin Yaakov"]

Title: Dynamic programming and parallel computers
Source: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
Abstract: The computational theory of dynamic programming is examined from the viewpoint of parallel computation. A discussion of various forms of parallelism, the corresponding parallel algorithms, the applicability of the algorithms to different types of optimization problems, and their advantages over serial computation is presented. In addition, parallel aspects of various dimensionality reduction techniques such as state increment dynamic programming, successive approximations, and shift vectors are also given. ¬© 1973 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Casti J.", "Richardson M.", "Larson R."]

Title: SOME MODERN CONTROL ASPECTS OF AUTOMATICALLY STEERED VEHICLES.
Abstract: Discusses the modern control concepts of controllability and observability as applied to linearized models of rubber tired vehicles having both front wheel and four wheel steering systems. Front wheel steered vehicles are completely controllable and observable (for a typical lateral position measurement) except for possibly one velocity. Using a full order linear observer to provide state estimates, one can arbitrarily locate the system eigenvalues. Four wheel steering results in complete controllability for all velocities. Feedback gains are found which decouple the lateral position and yaw responses for certain initial conditions while preserving arbitrary eignevalue location capability. This arbitrary role allocation capability is also preserved when the rear steering angle is constrained to be the negative of that at the front.
Name: ["Pasternack Sam"]

Title: DIGITAL FILTERING FOR ANALYSIS OF STRUCTURAL VIBRATIONS.
Abstract: A digital signal analysis system to aid in compiling vibration test data is described. This method for digital filtering of time series data has proved to be fast, effective, and an easily implemented method of analyzing structural properties. In addition to providing the design engineer with all of the traditional forms of output offered by analog systems, the computer-based nature of the digital filter system facilitates the use of large-scale dynamic simulations requiring mode identification and other analytical software.
Name: ["Malen D.E.", "Vaughan E.A."]

Title: An algorithm for finding the synthetically important rings of a molecule
Source: Journal of the Chemical Society, Perkin Transactions 1
Abstract: An algorithm for finding rings in the computer representation of molecular structures is presented. The method generates only chemically important rings. The difficulties of deciding on the best algorithm are discussed.
Name: ["Malcolm B."]

Title: Stochastic generation of regular distributions
Abstract: A new class of models is proposed to describe the dynamic processes leading to the establishment of regular spatial patterns of structures in natural systems. Simple mathematical arguments are used to compute the saturating densities of the distributions, and these results are verified by computer simulation of model systems.
Name: ["Glass L."]

Title: Exhaust pollution minimization in small engines using adaptive digital control
Abstract: Advances in digital computer technology have brought the application of on-line digital control systems to bear on the problem of exhaust gas pollution from the internal combustion engine. One application, adaptive digital control of fuel consumption based on a feedback of an analysis of exhaust gases, is explained. A small gasoline engine is modified with a fuel injection system, thus the engine, digital computer, and gas analyzer interface is developed. The engine's exhaust pollutants, based on real time operating conditions, are minimized while performance is retained. The delay time limitations experienced by the feedback transducer are demonstrated by a transient mode of operation. The relevance of this investigation and some future applications are discussed.
Name: ["Kehres J.K.", "Allan III J.J."]
Affiliations: ['U. S. Army Tank-Automotive Command', 'University of Texas']

Title: A Computational Algorithm for the Optimal Control of Continuous-Time Stochastic Systems
Abstract: An algorithm for computing optimal controls for a class of continuous-time stochastic systems is presented. For a linear example, it is shown that the generated control is precisely the optimal control. Numerical results for a nonlinear example suggest that the generated control is at least locally optimal. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Tacker E.C.", "Sanders C.W., Jr.", "Linton T.D."]
Affiliations: [' Louisiana State University', ' Louisiana State University']

Title: On finding lowest common ancestors in trees
Source: Proceedings of the Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
Abstract: Trees in an n node forest are to be merged according to instructions in a given sequence, while other instructions in the sequence ask for the lowest common ancestor of pairs of nodes. We show that any sequence of On) instructions can be processed " on line" in 0(n log n) steps on a random access computer. If we can accept our answer "off-line", that is, no answers need to be produced until the entire sequence of instructions has been seen seen, then we may perform the task in 0(n G(n)) steps, where C'n) is the number of times we must apply log2 to n to obtain a number less than or equal to zero. A third algorithm solves a problem of intermediate complexity. We require the answers on line, but we suppose that all tree merging instructions precede the information requests. This algorithm requires 0(n log log n) time. We apply the first on line algorithm to a problem in ende optimization, that of computing immediate dominators in a reducible flow graph. We show how this computation can be performed in 0(n log n) steps. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Aho A.V.", "Hopcroft J.E.", "Ullman J.D."]

Title: Identification and modelling of large-scale systems using sensitivity analysis
Abstract: This paper considers the parametric identification of large-scale systems from noise-corrupted output observations. Computational tractability is achieved using perturbation techniques for decoupling and system-order reduction. The influence of the state variable model assumed for the original system on the performance of the identification system is discussed. Examples are given which demonstrate the effectiveness of the identification techniques. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Guinzy N.J.", "Sage A.P."]

Title: Automatic Operations Planning-Interrelation between Processor and Postprocessors. | [AUTOMATISK OPERATIONS-BEREDNING.]
Abstract: Distribution of technological calculations among processor and postprocessor is discussed. The discussed calculations are determination of operations, operation sequence, clamping devices and clamping surfaces, machining sequence, tools, machining data and tool paths. Collision problems are also considered. The modification of postprocessors far automatic control of machine tools is also treated.
Name: ["Berg G."]

Title: NON-PARAMETRIC LEARNING OF DISTRIBUTION FUNCTIONS USING STOCHASTIC APPROXIMATIONS.
Abstract: A non-parametric learning scheme of the cumulative distribution function F(x) of patterns is presented and discussed. It is shown that the cumulative distribution function can be non-parametrically learned by a novel scheme in which the variable domain integrator is necessary. A finite mixture distribution can be parametrically constructed without the supervisor. This kind of unsupervised parametric learning scheme possesses considerable practical merit compared to conventional ones.
Name: ["Isomichi Yoshinori"]

Title: STUDIES TO DESIGN AND DEVELOP IMPROVED REMOTE MANIPULATOR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: This report describes a philoscophy of remote manipulator control based upon several levels of automatic supervision which derives manipulator commands from an analysis of sensor states and the taks requirements. Principle sensors are manipulator joint position, tactile, and motor currents. The tactile sensor states can be displayed visually in perspective or replicated in the operator's control handle or perceived by the automatic supervisor. Studies are reported on control organization, operator performance and system performance measures. Refs.
Name: ["Hill J.W.", "Sword A.J."]

Title: Correlated Clutter and Resultant Properties of Binary Signals
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: A simple Markov process model of binary, digitized radar clutter returns is assumed. Probability distributions for the number of hits in n observations are developed for small n with a binary parameter describing the process derived for Rayleigh distributed clutter. Tables of distributions are included, along with an example to show the effects of correlation on the false-alarm probabilities of a sliding-window detector. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Bogush A.J., Jr."]

Title: Pitch Extraction Method. | UNE METHODE D'EXTRACTION DU FONDAMENTAL.
Abstract: The voiced sound signal is considered as the response of a system consisting of a number of resonators and excited by a pulse series. So, every excitation pulse is characterized by an abrupt increase of the signal energy. A specially introduced function measures the signal energy variations and delivers a weight pulsion when this variation takes a peak value. Then a regularity test algorithm selects useful pulses.
Name: ["Maissis A."]

Title: A Bayesian approach to interactive retrieval
Abstract: This paper presents a probabilistic model for interactive retrieval. Specifically, it applies the principles of Bayesian statistical decision theory : (1) the use of both prior (subjective) and sample information about the relationship of document descriptions to query relevance, and (2) maximization of the expected value of a utility function, to the problem of optimally restructuring a search strategy in an interactive environment. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Tague J.M."]

Title: Optimal observation of linear plants whose dynamic properties are known
Source: Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement and Control, Transactions of the ASME
Abstract: The paper is concerned with determination of the state components in the case of measurements of output and control signals of the plant with errors. The optimal operators have been considered, which in the case of least favorable measurement errors give a minimal value of error of component to be defined. Particularly a case of signal measurement with errors which differ from each other has been considered. It has been shown that optimal operators are certain linear operators. The way of selecting these optimal operators from linear operators has been also shown. Namely it has been proved that for all cases which are considering the so called mini-max principle preserve its validity. Other theorems which can help to select optimal operators are formulated. ¬© 1973 by ASME.
Name: ["Qessing R."]

Title: REPRESENTATION OF PATTERN CLASSES USING FUZZY SETS.
Abstract: The construction of a pattern space over the family of fuzzy sets contained in a set is considered. Fuzzy features and fuzzy pattern classes are defined in the family of fuzzy sets. Since the family of fuzzy sets contained in a set forms a distributive lattice, a fuzzy pattern space is constructed by applying to the distributive lattice the same technique of representing a pattern class in terms of members of partitions as in a pattern space defined over a Boolean lattice.
Name: ["Kotoh Kaoru", "Hiramatsu Keiji"]

Title: ANALYSIS OF TIME-DISCRETE QUEUING SYSTEMS WITH TRANSIENT PHENOMENA.
Abstract: The aim of the study is transient analysis of waiting times and call numbers of a queuing system which has a single processor and periodically interrupts its service for a fixed time interval, called the pause period. A service time for a call is a multiple of a certain time unit (the time quantum) and commences at the initial epoch of some quantum. The processor operates for a period of N quantums in a row and pauses for a next period of M successive quantums. The operating and pause periods alternate, and an incomplete service for a call is continued in the immediately following processing period. The behavior of this queuing system is transient in the sense that probability distributions of all numbers or waiting times are all time dependent. A radio-call communication system is modeled as this system.
Name: ["Satoh Shohei"]

Title: FINITE-MEMORY SEQUENTIAL MACHINES AND INFORMATION-LOSSLESS SEQUENTIAL MACHINES.
Abstract: The properties of finite-memory sequential machine and information-lossless sequential machines are discussed. The following conclusions are derived: a q-symbol shift register of length m can generate a periodic sequence of length less than q**m; there exist the minimum output memory sequential machines and the minimum input memory sequential machines; there exist a sequential machine satisfying the upper bound of k in k-lossless sequential machines; and the relation between the information-lossless sequential machine and its inverse (or quasi-inverse) machine is clarified.
Name: ["Kambayashi Yahiko", "Yajima Shuzo"]

Title: CORRELATION SPECTRAL ANALYSIS OF LINEAR SAMPLED-DATA STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A correlation spectral theory is elaborated relative to transformation of a nonstationary random process by a one-dimensional parametric nonstationary sampled-data stochastic system of the first kind. The required characteristics of the system are described, and a relationship is established between the correlation functions and the spectra of the signal, the response, and the system. The well-known results of spectral correlation analysis for one-dimensional linear sampled-data systems are particular cases of the results obtained in this paper.
Name: ["Geranin V.O."]

Title: A Backtrack Procedure for Isomorphism of Directed Graphs
Abstract: A reasonably efficient procedure for testing pairs of directed graphs for isomorphism is important in information retrieval and other application fields in which structured data have to be matched. One such procedure, a backtrack procedure based on a representation of directed graphs by linear formulas, is described. A procedure for finding a partial subdigraph of a digraph that is isomorphic to a given digraph is also described. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Berztiss A.T."]
Keywords: ["backtrack programming", "digraph isomorphism", "representation of digraphs", "procedure isomorphism", "isomorphism directed"]

Title: STATISTICAL QUALITY CRITERION FOR FEATURE RECOGNITION.
Abstract: A simple and easily grasped quality criterion for feature recognition is proposed, in the case of ordered selection of useful objects, from a group of nuisance objects, with respect to a random feature.
Name: ["Yumashev S.G."]

Title: INVARIANT RULE FOR NONCOHERENT DETECTION OF A SIGNAL IN THE PRESENCE OF NOISE OF AN UNKNOWN LEVEL.
Abstract: The problem of noncoherent detection of a signal is examined in the presence of uncorrelated Gaussian noise of an unknown level. It is shown that a most powerful detection rule with respect to the signal-to-noise ratio does not exist for the case of nonfluctuating signals and signals with an unknown and variable amplitude. A locally most powerful detection rule is derived which is invariant with respect to simultaneous variations of signal and noise power.
Name: ["Prokof'yev V.N."]

Title: Chapter VIII: Learning Filters
Abstract: This chapter presents the principles of designing learning filters that can extract or transform desired signals in a best way after a period of learning in the conditions of insufficient a priori information. Learning filters differ from the learning pattern recognition systems and learning models. In the case of learning models, for each value of the input signal, corresponding output signal is known. The learning filters are considered as the systems that extract desired signals from the background noise. Frequently, the filters have to transform the signals, that is, to provide specified values of the signals and their corresponding derivatives or integrals. The synthesis of optimal filters is only possible under sufficiently complete a priori information, that is, when statistical characteristics of the signal and noise are known in advance. When a priori information is incomplete, the classical method of synthesizing optimal filters become inconvenient, and they have to be replaced by the adaptive approach. ¬© 1973, Academic Press Inc.

Title: CONSTRUCTION OF A MARKOV MODEL OF THE USEFUL SIGNAL FOR AUTOMATIC TRACKING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A procedure for constructing a Markov model of the useful signal for automatic tracking systems is examined. The differential equations of the model generating the useful signal, which is connected with the properties of the object, are determined by use of the formula for Ito's stochastic differential.
Name: ["Korobov N.N.", "Dolgiy A.A.", "Rubtsov B.V."]

Title: Solution of the Stochastic control problem in unbounded domains
Abstract: Bellman's dynamic programming equation for the optimal index and control law for stochastic control problems is a parabolic or elliptic partial differential equation frequently defined in an unbounded domain. Existing methods of solution require bounded domain approximations, the application of singular perturbation techniques or Monte Carlo simulation procedures. In this paper, using the fact that Poisson impulse noise tends to a Gaussian process under certain limiting conditions, a method which achieves an arbitrarily good approximate solution to the stochastic control problem is given. The method uses the two iterative techniques of successive approximation and quasi-linearization and is inherently more efficient than existing methods of solution. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Robinson P.", "Moore J."]
Affiliations: ['Department of Electrical Engineering University of Maryland', 'Department of Electrical Engineering University of Newcastle']

Title: USE OF OPEN-LOOP STRATEGIES IN THE SYNTHESIS OF SUBOPTIMAL ALGORITHMS FOR CONTROL OF STATIC PLANTS.
Abstract: A synthesis method is proposed for suboptimal control algorithms for a class of static plants under conditions of incomplete information. With this method it is fairly easy to take into account the need for observing the plant during the control process. This is done by estimating the losses due to such observation in the case of open-loop controls. As an example, a linear plant is considered. The method is convenient if the level of a priori information about the plant is fairly high.
Name: ["Bakan G.M."]

Title: STATISTICAL PREDICTION OF RANDOM PROCESSES ON THE BASIS OF SELF-ORGANIZATION OF PREDICTION EQUATIONS - 2. SYSTEMATIC MULTIPLE DIFFERENTIAL PREDICTION WITH SEPARATION OF TWO TRENDS.
Abstract: The minimum number of characteristic variables of a complex system is determined, for which the estimates obtained by regression analysis are not biased. The system prediction is made simultaneously for this (or a larger) number of variables. The regression equations can be obtained (by the GMDH) for the variables, as well as for their time derivatives or integrals. The differential regression equations are a description of a physical model of the deterministic part of the process. Multiple prediction signifies step-wise integration of differential regression equations. Unstable differential procedures are automatically selected by the program for short-term predictions, whereas more stable procedures are selected for long-term predictions. The prediction accuracy can be increased considerably by preliminary separation of two trends (for the variables and for their deviations), with appropriate choice of regularization methods. The regularization methods differ, in accordance with the rules of grouping the experimental points into a training and a checking sequence. In the example of six predictions of different duration, it is shown that there exists an optimum value of the ‚Ä≥sampling period‚Ä≥ that minimizes the error calculated on the second checking sequence. A hypothesis is advanced according to which the first checking sequence should contain the points corresponding to the vertices of the first harmonic of the random process.
Name: ["Ivakhnenko A.G.", "Todua M.M.", "Chukin Yu.V."]

Title: PROBABILISTIC CRITERION FOR OPTIMALITY OF ALGORITHMS FOR APPROXIMATION OF FUNCTIONS OF RANDOM VARIABLES.
Abstract: A probabilistic criterion for optimality of algorithms is constructed for the approximation of functions of random variables, and an optimal algorithm is determined on the basis of this criterion.
Name: ["Khlobystov V.V."]

Title: A model for pattern recognition by cell networks
Abstract: A study is made of certain properties of a model cell network based on lateral inhibition. It is demonstrated that specific patterns of input activity, termed eigenpatterns, will pass through the network without distortion. Under certain conditions the network will show selectivity for one particular eigenpattern, and the degree of this selectivity is under the control of non-specific parameters of the network. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Findlay J.M.", "Daniell G.J."]
Affiliations: [' University of Durham', ' University of Southampton']

Title: ON THE TREE HEIGHT OF CONTEXT-FREE LANGUAGES.
Abstract: A tree height is defined as the height of a derivation tree of a word in a context-free language. Various properties of the tree height are investigated from the viewpoint of its asymptotic behavior with respect to lengths of words in context-free languages. Furthermore, for the sake of study of the tree height, some generalized classes of linear context-free grammars are introduced and their hierarchical structures of generative capabilities are investigated.
Name: ["Noshita Kohei", "Takaoka Tadao"]

Title: RECOGNITION OF WORDS USING STRUCTURAL RELATIONSHIPS WITH EXPLICIT TIME.
Abstract: A proposal to construct voice pattern recognizers on the basis of pattern structural properties is analyzed. The results of computer simulation with regard to recognition of ten word-figures, are examined.
Name: ["Gudonavichyus R.V.", "Zayezdnyy A.M.", "Chitavichyus A.B."]

Title: ON AN ALGORITHM OF DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING.
Abstract: A computational algorithm of dynamic programming is proposed which allows a decrease of the number of elements of Bellman optimal sequences due to the decrease of one of the constraints by two. To determine the optimal result, the functional equation is solved twice, in the direct and reverse directions, which compensates the decrease of the value of one of the constraints. A numerical example is presented and an estimate of the volume of computations is given.
Name: ["Alekseeva S.M.", "Alekseev O.G."]

Title: CLASSIFICATION OF SYSTEMS OF ONE-DIMENSIONAL ITERATIVE AUTOMATA BY ITS INFORMATION TRANSMISSION CAPABILITY.
Abstract: In this paper, systems of one-dimensional iterative automata are classified into three classes, Classes I, II and III, according to their information transmission (from right to left) capabilities, and the properties of these classes are clarified. A system of one-dimensional iterative automata is composed of cells (S, f) where S is a set of states and f is a state transition function from S**3 into S. Class I consists of systems in which the leftmost cell receives no information from the right cells at a certain distance regardless of initial conditions. In systems of Class III, the leftmost cell receives the information from all cells at any distance. A system whose information transmission depends on its initial conditions belongs to Class II.
Name: ["Kobuchi Yoichi", "Nishio Hidenosuke"]

Title: Model for neural regulation of the heart
Source: Annales Academiae Scientiarum Fennicae - Series V Medica
Abstract: This work is aimed at the construction of a functional model for regulation of the heart in connection with the central nervous system (CNS), based upon experimental results obtained by the author. Such a model would provide understanding of cardiovascular regulation as a function of inhibitory and excitatory neural components.
Name: ["Hakumaki M.O.K."]

Title: A Computationally Simple Procedure for Imagery Data Compression by the Karhunen-Lo√®ve Method
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: Of the several methods that have been proposed for imagery data compression, the Karhunen-Lo√®ve procedure minimizes the meansquare error between the original and reconstructed imagery data. In spite of its optimality property, the Karhunen-Lo√®ve procedure has not been widely used because of its computational complexity. The main difficulty is in the computation of the eigenvectors and the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix of the imagery data since the dimension of the covariance matrix is usually large. A computationally short procedure for calculating the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix is presented. We show that the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the N √ó N bisymmetric covariance matrix can be obtained from the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of two N/2 x N/2 submatrices. Since the eigenvector calculations are proportional to the third power of the matrix dimension, the proposed procedure reduces the computations by a factor of four. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Shanmugam K.", "Haralick R.M."]

Title: DISCRETE OPTIMAL CONTROL IN LINEAR STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS WITH RANDOM DATA SAMPLING.
Abstract: A piecewise-constant (on the intervals on which the parameters are constant) control is sought which minimizes a quadratic quality criterion for a linear stochastic system whose matrices are switched after random time intervals. Existence conditions for a stationary regulator are presented.
Name: ["Darkhovskiy B.S.", "Leybovich V.S."]

Title: Irreducible canonical realizations from external data sequences
Abstract: A direct procedure for obtaining a minimal realization of a linear multivariable time-invariant discrete system is described, by considering input/output data sequences as initial characterization. The main feature of the procedure is to lead to a well-defined canonical form of the state-space matrix triple with a remarkable saving of computing effort An example is given in order to display the mechanization of this approach. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Bonivento C.", "Guidorzi R.", "Marro G."]

Title: ASSOCIATIVE PROCESSOR.
Abstract: Associative processing is enhanced by encoding the binary or other data signals into a higher level code such as hexidecimal, decimal, etc. , performing the associative processing, and then decoding the high-level coded output of the associative processing back to binary or other data coding.
Name: ["Jones J.W.", "Sears J.F.", "Taylor K.G."]

Title: SELECTION OF OPTIMUM STRUCTURE OF TABULAR MODEL OF CONTROLLED PLANT.
Abstract: The large amount of data is the main obstacle of the use of tabular models in cybernetic control systems for multivariable technological processes. The problem of minimizing the amount of data is solved by structural combination of a coarse global model with a set of precise local models. Possible configurations of two- and three-dimensional tabular models with central symmetry are obtained in the form of regular point systems.
Name: ["Protsenko M.M.", "Skurikhin V.I.", "Yakovenko L.P."]

Title: A method for adaptive traffic control
Abstract: Present methods for determining optimal settings for signal networks are too time consuming to be implemented on-line with contemporary computers. The bulk of the computation involves signal coordination between intersections. It is proposed that global signal coordination may be achieved adaptively using appropriately chosen local control algorithms. This is demonstrated for certain simple networks using an algorithm that minimizes stops to vehicles in platoons. The results are valid for essentially light traffic. For several cases it is shown that a system consisting of signals controlled independently with the algorithm converges to a periodic asymptotic state exhibiting global signal coordination. The convergence proof is simultaneously a proof of the system's stability. No claim is made that the particular algorithm studied here is suitable for implementation in the field. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Rosdolsky H.G."]

Title: ADAPTIVE REGULATION OF MULTIVEHICLE GUIDEWAY TRANSIT.
Abstract: This paper examines automatic speed and headway control for a train of vehicles traveling in a fixed guideway at equally spaced intervals. The control law established ensures longitudinal stability for both individual vehicle and vehicle train. The law is adaptive in the sense that system behavior is rendered independent of vehicle loading, wind velocity, and nominal static friction.
Name: ["Powell B.K."]

Title: REARRANGEMENT OF ITEMS IN A WAREHOUSE.
Abstract: The paper gives a two-state algorithm that produces the sequence of item movements necessary to achieve the desired rearrangement and incur the minimum cost (or time) spent in the rearranging process; the result is optimal in the restricted case where the rearranging must be done in a number of cycles, each one being of a short time duration.
Name: ["Christofides Nicos", "Colloff I."]

Title: ONLINE OPTIMAL CONTROL OF ARC IMPEDANCE FOR AN ELECTRIC-ARC-FURNACE MODEL.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: The dynamic behavior of an electrode-position control system for an industrial direct electric-arc furnace is investigated. The electrode-positioning servomechanism is modelled as an electromechanical system with transfer-function relationships and nonlinear valve characteristics defining the hydromechanical system. the electrical-power-transmission-system model is based on single-phase circuit equations and incorporates an empirical arc-discharge characteristic. A dynamic representation of the supply system is also used which incorporates a linear model of an equivalent synchronous machine including both transient and subtransient effects. Dynamic performance of the conventionally controlled system is investigated by analog hybrid simulation of the nonlinear-system model. Optimal and suboptimal control of a linearized model is also studied, and methods of solution based on dynamic programming and the algebraic matrix Riccati equation are compared. To investigate online calculations of optimal control, various forms of performance functional are considered. Conventional 4-mode control and linear optimal control of arc impedance are applied in real time by process computer to the analog-simulated nonlinear-system model. The study demonstrates a relative improvement in the dynamic performance of arc current, and hence power, with changing bath conditions and varying arc-discharge characteristics.
Name: ["Nicholson H.", "Roebuck R."]

Title: Sensitivity of the Performance of Optimal Stochastic Systems
Abstract: Sensitivities of cost of an optimal nondeterministic system with noise-corrupted measurements are compared. It is shown that closed-loop realization of optimal control gives lower sensitivity than an open-loop realization. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers. Inc.
Name: ["Kang H.S.", "Mahalanabis A.K."]

Title: Performance deterioration of optimal regulators incorporating kalman filters
Abstract: In this paper, the performance deterioration of optimal regulators caused by the introduction of Kalman filters as state estimators is investigated. It is shown that, in the ease of single-input single-output systems, the performance deterioration cannot be made arbitrarily small unless the optimal control law can be implemented by direct output feedback. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Arimoto S.", "Porter B."]

Title: OPTIMAL CONTROL SETTINGS FOR RANDOM DISTURBANCES.
Abstract: An isolated step-function disturbance is generally assumed in work on optimal controller settings, but most process systems receive new upsets before the effects of previous ones have died out. The authors show that frequent disturbances require different controller settings, which converge to the classical values as the interval between disturbances becomes long compared to system response.
Name: ["Sood M.", "Huddleston H.T."]

Title: Design of a Self-Checking Microprogram Control
Abstract: In designing a self-checking processor, it is essential to recognize the types of failures that are most probable. Matching the checking techniques with the type of faults that are expected to occur should yield the best result with the least amount of hardware. The microprogram control will consist of integrated circuits: large-scale integration (LSI) for the memory and small-scale integration (SSI) for the associated control logic. Because of the density of chips on a plug-in package and the physical proximity of the devices on an integrated circuit, multiple faults within a single circuit are highly probable. The types of faults within a circuit have been analyzed and found to be of the type which would tend to affect the bits in a unidirectional manner. Also the failed bits would probably be adjacent rather than randomly dispersed throughout-the microprogram store word. The checking technique implemented takes advantage of the error characteristics mentioned above. This led to the choice of using m-out-of-n codes for the control fields of the microprogram instruction words. This code permits the detection of all multiple unidirectional errors. However, for the address field, it is desirable to maintain the data in binary form. Consequently, a check code which is systematic is essential to give this flexibility. By recognizing that the multiple bit faults tend to affect adjacent bits, we can take advantage of this fact by interleaving the binary address field with the m-out-of-n codes in the microprogram store. Any multiple adjacent bit faults would then affect both the binary address field and the m-out-of-n code. There-fore, a single parity check bit is adequate to detect single bit faults in the binary field with multiple adjacent bit fault detected by the m-out-of-n check. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Cook R.W.", "Sisson W.H.", "Storey T.F.", "Toy W.N."]

Title: Boolean Bar - Bar Algebra. | [ALGEBRE BARRE - BARRE OU ‚Ä≥BARBARE‚Ä≥ DE BOOLE.]
Abstract: When designing a logic circuit it is often necessary to introduce some transformation in order to accommodate with the requirements of the technology being chosen. A graphical method, called bar-bar algebra, very simple and easy to use, has been elaborated making it possible to transform a logic circuit to obtain an equivalent one but with different operators. The method is based mainly on a simplified representation of the different gates that are in use and on some elementary rules established by analogy with binary algebra relations. The transformation of a circuit is then obtained only adding, shifting or canceling small bars representing inverters or the attribute of a gate on a drawing of the circuit. The method has been extended to the exclusive ‚Ä≥OR‚Ä≥ operator and leads to a rapid optimization of anyt logical circuit however complicated.
Name: ["Messeca E."]

Title: Empirical Bayes Approach to M-ary Detection
Abstract: An empirical Bayes procedure is introduced for M-ary detection in a statistically undefined noise background. The Bayes decision rule, which depends on a set of nuisance parameters, is formed first from sample qualitative information so that the requirement of known noise distribution can be relaxed. The rule is then approximated by estimating the nuisance parameters. The resulting empirical procedure possesses the desirable property of consistency and is simple to implement. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Chen Y.-B."]

Title: Improvement of automatic abstracts by the use of structural analysis
Source: Journal of the American Society for Information Science
Abstract: We have undertaken to extend the capabilities of the abstracting system described by Rush, Salvador and Zamora by adding to the system a modification procedure that could be employed to make the abstracts produced by the system more acceptable to the reader. Results of this study are reported in this paper. Our purpose is to present a rationale for the modification phase of an abstracting system and to describe several modification rules whose implementation is an initial step toward the automated production of abstracts that contain sentences written especially for the abstract. We have described several methods for improving the readability of abstracts produced by computer program. The research described in this paper was performed as a part of a larger project whose aim is the development of an operational automatic abstracting system. 18 references are given.  Copyright ¬© 1973 Wiley Periodicals, Inc., A Wiley Company
Name: ["Mathis B.A.", "Rush J.E.", "Young C.E."]

Title: TRANSLATION INVARIANT TRANSFORM WITH UNIFORM AMPLITUDE BOUNDS FOR PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Source: J Inst Telecommun Eng New Delhi
Abstract: A transform called R (for rapid) transform which is invariant under cyclic permutation of the signal samples has been proposed in literature. The R-transform domain can be partitioned into sets of samples such that samples belonging to any one set have the same amplitude bounds. A transform which is invariant under cyclic permutation of the signal samples and has uniform amplitude bounds is proposed in this paper.
Name: ["Moharir P.S."]

Title: On the Design of Gradient Algorithms for Digitally Implemented Adaptive Filters
Abstract: The effect of digital implementation on the gradient (steepest descent) algorithm commonly used in the mean-square adaptive equalization of pulse-amplitude modulated data signals is considered. It is shown that digitally implemented adaptive gradient algorithms can exhibit effects which are significantly different from those encountered in analog (infinite precision) algorithms. This is illustrated by considering the often quoted result of stochastic approximation that to achieve the optimum rate of convergence in an adaptive algorithm the step size should be proportional to 1/n, where n is the number of iterations. On closer examination one finds that this result applies only when n is large and is relevant only for analog algorithms. It is shown that as the number of iterations becomes large one should not continually decrease the step size in a digital gradient algorithm. This result is a manifestation of the quantization inherent in any digitally implemented system. A surprising result is that these effects produce a digital residual mean-square error that is minimized by making the step size as large as possible. Since the analog residual error is minimized by taking small step sizes, the optimum step-size sequence reflects a compromise between these competing goals. The performance of a time-varying gain sequence suggested by stochastic approximation is contrasted with the performance of a constant step-size sequence. It is shown that in a digital environment the latter sequence is capable of attaining a smaller residual error. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gitlin R.D.", "Taylor M.G."]

Title: APPROXIMATION OF DISCRIMINANT FUNCTIONS IN A NEIGHBORHOOD OF ZERO VALUES.
Abstract: Two adaptive Bayesian algorithms are given. One is designed for a teaching sample of fixed size, and the other (recursion) for a sample of increasing size.
Name: ["Zenkov V.V."]

Title: Inverse problem for linear systems containing uncertain parameters
Source: Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement and Control, Transactions of the ASME
Abstract: The concept of fuzzy dynamic programming and of guaranteed cost control initiated by Chang is applied to the inverse problem of guaranteed cost control for linear systems containing uncertain parameters. Obtained, for a class of linear systems with uncertain parameters, is a frequency-domain criterion which, analogous to that for the deterministic system, is sufficient for the control law to be of guaranteed cost type. The author presents an iterative method which, if convergent, enables one to solve the inverse problem for the general linear systems. ¬© 1973 by ASME.
Name: ["Panda S.P."]
Affiliations: [' The University of Michigan', ' State University of New York at Stony Brook']

Title: Minimizing wasted space in partitioned segmentation
Abstract: A paged virtual memory system using a finite number of page sizes is considered. Two algorithms for assigning pages to segments are discussed. Both of these algorithms are simple to implement. The problem of choosing the page sizes to minimize the expected value of total wasted space in internal fragmentation and in a page table, per segment, is then solved for a probability density function of segment size which may be expressed as a convex combination of Erlang densities. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gelenbe E.", "Boekhorst J.C.A.", "Kessels J.L.W."]

Title: On Coding and Filtering Stationary Signals by Discrete Fourier Transforms
Abstract: This correspondence concerns real-time Fourier processing of stationary data and examines the widespread belief that coefficients of the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) are ‚Äúalmost‚Äù uncorrelated. We first show that any uniformly bounded N √ó N Toeplitz covariance matrix TN is asymptotically equivalent to a nonstandard circulant matrix CN derived from the DFT of TN. We then derive bounds on a normed distance between TNand CN for finite N, and show that|TN-CN|2 = o(1/N) for finite-order Markov processes. Finally we demonstrate that the performance degradation resulting from the use of DFT (as opposed to Karhunen-Lo√®ve expansion) in coding and filtering is proportional to|TN-CN| and therefore vanishes as the inverse square root of the block size N when N ‚Üí ‚àû. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Pearl J."]

Title: PREDICTING RAILROAD BANKRUPTCIES IN AMERICA.
Abstract: Author discusses the urgent need for an early-warning system covering the historically failure-prone railroad industry and to develop a tool for providing such a system. A multivariate statistical technique called linear discriminant analysis is utilized to identify and quantify those financial measures which are effective indicators of bankruptcies. A model which combined several financial statement ratios proved to be extremely accurate in predicting railroad bankruptcies at one and two annual financial statement dates prior to failure. Subsequent tests on additional railroad samples confirm the validity of the model. Currently existing railroads in America are assessed for their bankruptcy potential by this diagnostic model.
Name: ["Altman Edward I."]

Title: A model for a document retrieval system
Abstract: There are some proper characteristics of a document retrieval system among various kinds of information retrieval systems. One of them is that a query described by a user has some degree of vagueness in itself. One of them is that a certain measure of similarity between a query and a document must be introduced. Another is that a proper consideration must be imposed on the occurrence of keywords and the relations existing between keywords. This paper describes the theoretical model of a document retrieval system by giving logical meaning to the "vagueness" and the "similarity", with the frequency of occurrences of keywords and the relations among them taken into consideration. Furthermore, there are some other important problems in a document retrieval system implementation point of view. The procedures as well as various kinds of data formats are described in order to implement the above model as a computerized document retrieval system, including SDI (Selective Dissemination of Information) system. ¬© 1973.

Title: Constrained Minimax Estimate of a Normal Mean
Abstract: For Bayes estimation of a normal mean, if prior mean and prior covariance are known, a minimax estimate is obtainable by assuming the prior distribution to be normal. The minimax is constrained by the given prior mean and covariance. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Shulman A.D."]

Title: Unsupervised Tracking of Maneuvering Vehicles
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: The design of adaptive filters for the tracking of high-performance maneuvering targets is a fundamental problem in real-time surveillance systems. As is well known, a filter which provides heavy smoothing can not accurately track an evasive maneuver, and conversely. Consequently, one is led to the consideration of adaptive methods of filter design. This paper presents an improved self-adaptive filter algorithm for on-line solution of the above problem. Basically, this algorithm utilizes the orthogonality property of the residual time series to force the filter to automatically track the optimal gain levels in a changing environment. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Hampton R.L.T.", "Cooke J.R."]

Title: Observability and optimal measurement location in linear distributed parameter systems‚Ä†
Abstract: Observability and the optimal location of measurements are developed for a class of linear distributed parameter systems whose solutions can be represented by eigen-function expansions (the so-called modal form). A key question studied is the effect of measurement locations on the observability of this class of systems. Since observability is realty a prerequisite to state estimation, an algorithm is developed to determine a set of measurement locations which, in some sense, lead to the beat state estimates. This is accomplished by minimizing the trace of the steady-state covariance matrix of the state estimates. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Yu T.K.", "Seinfeld J.H."]

Title: Suboptimal input signals for linear system identification
Abstract: It is well known that inputs for identification experiments can be synthesized on the basis of optimizing a certain performance criterion, such as variances of parameters, estimates of weighting functions and probabilities of transmission error. Such signals give the best possible performance for given constraints of input energy, observation time and nature of noise. The question arises whether one can choose signals on the basis of other possibly more intuitive or physical criteria and see what kind of performance they give w.r.t. optimal inputs and common signals, as unit step inputs. These signals, which fit between the two extremes are here referred to as suboptimal. The measure of performance is here taken to be the sum of parameter variances. It is shown that suboptimal inputs on the basis of maximizing the output signal/noise ratio, matching the system bandwidth and of pseudo-random binary noise nature can be selected for a given system. It is, however, also indicated that this is not a general method, since for certain systems no suboptimal performance was reached. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["LjubojeviƒÜ M."]

Title: Common phrases and minimum-space text storage
Abstract: A method for saving storage space for text strings, such as compiler diagnostic messages, is described. The method relies on hand selection of a set of text strings which are common to one or more messages. These phrases are then stored only once. The storage technique gives rise to a mathematical optimization problem: determine how each message should use the available phrases to minimize its storage requirement. This problem is nontrivial when phrases which overlap exist. However, a dynamic programming algorithm is presented which solves the problem in time which grows linearly with the number of characters in the text. Algorithm 444 applies to this paper. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Wagner R.A."]

Title: The Viterbi Algorithm
Abstract: The Viterbi algorithm (VA) is a recursive optimal solution to the problem of estimating the state sequence of a discrete-time finite-state Markov process observed in memoryless noise. Many problems in areas such as digital communications can be cast in this form. This paper gives a tutorial exposition of the algorithm and of how it is implemented and analyzed. Applications to date are reviewed. Increasing use of the algorithm in a widening variety of areas is foreseen. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers. Inc.
Name: ["Forney G.D., Jr."]

Title: Image processing by self-generated spatial and spectral masks
Abstract: Parallel, analog image processing techniques are described which enable images to be decomposed into subimages that contain objects that are spatially and spectrally equivalent. The decomposition is achieved by generating binary aperture masks directly from the image, with the aid of predetermined signature functions. The versatility of this approach is experimentally demonstrated for some simple scenes. The technique holds promise for on-board, computer-controlled processing of remotely obtained images. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Stark H.", "Barker R.C.", "Garcia E.", "Lee D."]

Title: Automated Processing of Deflection Measurements. | DEPOUILLEMENT AUTOMATISE DES MESURES DE DEFLEXIONS.
Source: Lab Cent Ponts Chaussees, Bull Liaison Lab Ponts Chauesses
Abstract: Features of the solution adopted to develop a more advanced method of processing of data supplied by LPC deflectographs to obtain information on the results of the nondestructive testing for road works.
Name: ["Siffert M."]

Title: Use of SPOOF's in the Analysis of Faulty Logic Networks
Abstract: In general, one cannot predict the effects of possible failures on the functional characteristics of a logic network without knowledge of the structure of that network. The structure- and parity-observing output function (SPOOF) described in this paper provides a new and convenient means of characterizing both network structure and output function in a single algebraic expression. A straightforward method for the determination of a SPOOF for any logic network is demonstrated. Similarities between SPOOF's and other means of characterizing network structure are discussed. Examples are presented that show several useful applications of this new tool. It is shown that the SPOOF provides an easy means by which the effects of any ‚Äústuck-at‚Äù fault-single or multiple-on the functional characteristics of a logic network can be determined. In addition, one may, using SPOOF‚Äôs, determine just which faults, if any, can occur in a network to affect its output function in a given way. Other likely applications of SPOOF‚Äôs, not yet fully explored, are indicated and areas for future re-search are suggested. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Clegg F.W."]
Keywords: ["fault", "fault detection and diagnosis", "fault equivalence", "tolerant computing reliability of digital systems spoofs", "logic network"]

Title: Multiple-channel models of human vision: Bandwidth considerations
Abstract: Physiological constraints and mathematical properties of the Fourier transform imply that frequency-selective channels in the visual system must have nonzero bandwidth. Existing experimental results for aperiodic patterns, interpreted in light of a multiple-channel model, indicate not only that nonzero bandwidths must be used in such a model, but also that bandwidths vary with the characteristic frequency of the channels. ¬© 1973 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Quick Jr. R.F.", "Reichert T.A."]

Title: Minimal Event-Node Network of Project Precedence Relations
Abstract: A procedure for constructing a minimal event-node network to represent a set of precedence relations without parallel activities is presented. A minimal event-node network is an event-node network in which both the number of nodes and the number of arcs are the minima to preserve the given precedence relations. Counterexamples are given to show that the algorithm presented by A.C. Fisher, J.S. Liebman, and G.L. Nemhauser (1968) produces event-node networks which are not minimal. Since our procedure includes the set-covering problem, the time required may grow exponentially with the number of given activities. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Corneil D.G.", "Gotlieb C.C.", "Lee Y.M."]

Title: Recent Studies in Automatic Text Analysis and Document Retrieval
Abstract: Many experts in mechanized text processing now agree that useful automatic language analysis procedures are largely unavailable and that the existing linguistic methodologies generally produce disappointing results. An attempt is made in the present study to identify those automatic procedures which appear most effective as a replacement for the missing language analysis. A series of computer experiments is described, designed to simulate a conventional document retrieval environment. It is found that a simple duplication, by automatic means, of the standard, manual document indexing and retrieval operations will not produce acceptable output results. New mechanized approaches to document handling are proposed, including document ranking methods, automatic dictionary and word list generation, and user feedback searches. It is shown that the fully automatic methodology is superior in effectiveness to the conventional procedures in normal use. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Salton G."]
Keywords: ["automatic indexing", "automatic text processing", "computational linguistics", "information retrieval evaluation", "language analysis"]

Title: Solving flight-path optimization problems on a minicomputer
Abstract: The problem of determining maximum-range flight paths for a jet transport during climb is investigated. The motivation for this effort is the fact that the number of air cargo flights is ever increasing. Thus even a small improvement in efficiency can have a large effect in total dollar savings. The objective is to guide the aircraft so that it will reach a prespecified cruise altitude and velocity and obtain maximum range in the process. The amount of fuel to be used is prespecified. Motion is in a vertical plane with lift coefficient being the control variable. The system of differential equations describing the motion of the plane is fifth order and nonlinear. The conjugate gradient procedure is used to solve the problem. The complexity is such that 36,000 storage locations are required for the most straight-forward application of the procedure. Through various approximations this requirement is reduced to 250 locations. Simulations showed that performance is not degraded through the approximations. The magnitude of the problem is thus reduced to that which could be solved by an on-board minicomputer. This is a major step toward the realization of optimal feedback control. The other requirement is that computation time be short enough to permit on-line solutions. This computation time is directly proportional to the number of iterations required for convergence to the optimal. This in turn is a function of the severity of the disturbance. If the disturbance is not too severe, one iteration may be sufficient for calculating the new optimal trajectory. This could be done within a fraction of the time required for the entire maneuver thus effectively yielding optimal feedback control. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Thomasson F.Y.", "Cook G."]

Title: Experimental visual prosthesis
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: Of the methods available which seek artificially to replace the sensory input lost through blindness, the approach which should ultimately be of greatest value is that by which visual information is fed directly to the brain. The paper reviews earlier work in this field and describes a new prosthesis. | Of the methods available which seek artificially to replace the sensory input lost through blindness, the approach which should ultimately be of greatest value is that by which visual information is fed directly to the brain. Title: An Explicit Approach to Minimal Realization from System Markov Parameters
Abstract: A new method for determining a minimal realization of a finite-dimensional linear system from data comprising a set of Markov parameters is presented. The method is based on treating the Markov parameter matrices as the elements of vectors in an ¬© 1973 IEEE

Title: Table-Model Computer with Problem-Oriented Language. | [TISCHRECHNER MIT PROBLEMORIENTIERTER SPRACHE.]
Abstract: The first part shows in a general way the advantages of a problem-oriented language. The description of the operation of Tektronix table calculator and a few calculation examples show the first implementation of this language. The second part describes the new Hewlett-Packard Model 9820 A miniature computer which allows a still more simple programming. Simple examples show, how the application of a table-model computer and a problem-oriented language can save on computation time in the analysis of applied mathematics problems and makes it often possible to avoid the use of a computer specialist.
Name: ["Schilt H."]

Title: Partition of Boolean Functions for Realization with Multithreshold Threshold Logic Elements
Abstract: In this paper, the concept of ‚Äúprimary partition‚Äù of Boolean functions has been introduced. A systematic method of obtaining the multithreshold realization of Boolean functions based on this new concept is presented. The problem essentially reduces to a table lookup procedure; the computational labor in finding the minimum-threshold minimum fan-in solution is substantially reduced. Title: Optimal Least Squares Time-Domain Synthesis of Recursive Digital Filters
Source: IEEE Transactions on Audio and Electroacoustics
Abstract: A method for finding the coefficients of an nth-order linear recursive digital filter, which gives the best least squares approximation to a desired pulse response over a finite interval, is presented. A relationship is derived between the approximating error corresponding to an optimal set of numerator coefficients and the error produced by an overdetermined set of linear equations, which is a function of the denominator coefficients only. This relation provides a computational algorithm for calculacing the optimal coefficients by iteratively solving weighted sets of linear equations in terms of the denominator coefficients only. Both theoretical and numerical results are presented. Also, bounds are found on the interval in which the norm of the optimum error must lie. Title: CHECK YOUR LOGIC BEHAVIOUR WITH AUTOMATIC TEST GENERATION.
Abstract: A properly designed simulator program can calculate the expected outputs from a circuit, failures within the circuit, and when or if a sequential circuit is initialized, but it cannot develop the input patterns necessary to detect a particular failure or to initialize a memory element. The true test-generation system can close the gap between failure coverage that might exist on a particular circuit and the failure coverage needed. Two true test generation techniques are discussed, namely the D algorithm and the so-called Boolean difference.
Name: ["Marlett R.A."]

Title: Structure of Search Methods. | [STRUKTUR VON SUCHVERFAHREN.]
Abstract: The term ‚Ä≥structure of a file‚Ä≥ is discussed and defined dynamically. The structure depends on the method of searching used at execution time. It is assumed that a search method is implemented by a computer program P on which a digraph G(P) can be defined. This digraph G(P) is called the structure of the search strategy. It is shown that well-known methods, such as sequential search, chained files, hash-coding, are based on the same G(P). Other methods, such as indexed sequential organization, can be described as links of several G(P)s.
Name: ["Muehlbacher J."]

Title: Disjunctive and conjunctive operators for Boolean functions
Abstract: A theoretical study of disjunctive and conjunctive operators, called p and q differentials, is undertaken to derive various properties of Boolean functions. The attempt is first to subsume a set of results, relative to the concept of prime implicant of a Boolean function, in a single consistent theory very close to the Boolean differential calculus. Title: On the Stability of a Fixed Lag Smoother
Abstract: The aim of this correspondence is to show that the fixed lag smoothing algorithm reported earlier by the authors is asymptotically stable and is computationally better than the other stable smoothers reported recently. ¬© 1973 IEEE
Name: ["Biswas K.K.", "Mahalanabis A.K."]

Title: SAFETY ANALYSIS FOR AUTOMATED TRANSPORTATION SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The paper outlines an approach for analyzing the safety characteristics of vehicular ground transportation systems operated under computer surveillance and control. Time delays in emergency control, resulting from discrete sensor spacing, finite sampling time, and loss of telemetered data, are analyzed and expressions for the attendant increase in the minimum headway are developed. The general approach and the specific techniques are illustrated with numerical examples.
Name: ["Rahimi A.", "Hajdu L.P.", "Macomber H.L."]

Title: Representation of a Real Function of Two Variables by Perspective Transformation of Its Contour Lines. | DARSTELLUNG EINER REELLEN FUNKTION ZWEIER VERAENDERLICHER DURCH PERSPEKTIVISCHE ABBILDUNG IHRER NIVEAUKURVEN.
Abstract: A method is described enabling a very exact and instructive plane representation of a surface which is defined by a real function of two variables. This representation is obtained by the perspective transformation of any curves situated on the surface. Visibility criteria and a method for representation of plane curves, which acts according to the properties of the curves, are discussed.

Title: ON THE SYNTHESIS OF MULTIVARIABLE SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The general question of compensating a linear multivariable system via linear state variable feedback (lsvf) in ccombinationn with input dynamics is considered. It is shown that, since lsvf and input dynamics can both be represented by proper feedforward compensation, any design based on feedforward compensation alone can usually be realized in a more efficient manner through the combined use of ‚Ä≥low-order‚Ä≥ feedforward compensation (input dynamics) and lsvf. A major result is the frequency-domain synthesis algorithm for ‚Ä≥separating‚Ä≥ any proper feedforward transfer matrix in order to achieve the more efficient compensation scheme. Examples which illustrate the employment of the algorithm to the questions of decoupling and exact model matching are included.
Name: ["Wolovich William A."]

Title: An analytical method for the filtering error evaluation of sub-optimal filters in a noisy non-linear dynamic system
Abstract: This paper presents an analytical method for the filtering error evaluation of sub-optimal filters in a noisy non-linear, discrete-time system. The a posteriori probability density for the filtering error process conditioned upon measurement data sequence is expanded into a series of orthonormal Hermite functions and the bias of estimate obtained from sub-optimal filters is computed recursively as the mean of this probability density. Numerical example presents a comparison of the bias obtained from several sub-optimal filters. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Soeda T.", "Yoshimura T.", "Fukunaga S."]

Title: INTERACTIVE GRAPHIC SYSTEM FOR MODELING SYMBOLIC NETWORKS.
Abstract: SNAP (System of Network Analysis Programs) is an interactive graphic system which is general enough to handle any network regardless of its physical interpretation and is capable of determining which application program is appropriate to process the particular network. The system currently includes four application programs; continuous systems simulation, electrical circuit analysis, Boolean expression reduction, and logical circuit simulation. A conversational drawing program within the system enables users to create a network of symbols using a light pen and a crt without issuing explicit drawing orders. Experience with SNAP has shown that if the drawing phase is separated from the analysis phase in a computer-aided design system, the resulting system can easily be modified or expanded. The SNAP system had such a separation from its very beginning, allowing substitution of the IDOL (Implied Drawing Orders Language) drawing program for the less efficient DIM (Display Image Manipulator) drawing program without requiring alteration of any code in the analysis program. New analysis programs were added to the system without changing any code in the drawing program. Current applications of the system include development of models for biological phenomena such as human eye movements, creation of models which simulate the spread of epidemic disease, and regional simulation to determine the effect of housing configurations on various factors in the environment. The system has also been used for algae modeling, simulation of pattern rrecognition in neuronal nets, and vehicle aerodynamics simulation.
Name: ["Morse Stephen P."]

Title: Flowchart techniques for structured programming
Abstract: With the advent of structured programming and GOTO-less programming a method is needed to model computation in simply ordered structures, each representing a complete thought possibly defined in terms of other thoughts as yet undefined. A model is needed which prevents unrestricted transfers of control and has a control structure closer to languages amenable to structured programming. We present an attempt at such a model. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Nassi I.", "Shneiderman B."]
Affiliations: [' State University of New York at Stony Brook']

Title: Freeway-Traffic Data Processing
Abstract: Two basic data processing problems associated with freeway traffic are formulated: estimation of traffic variables (section mean speed and density) and detection of occurrence of an incident or accident within a given section of the road. The existing traffic sensors and the current estimation techniques and their shortcomings are reviewed. Stochastic models for traffic variables are developed and used to design optimum recursive estimators. The incident detection problem is introduced as a potential area where many interesting research topics exist. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Nahi N.E."]

Title: Stochastic Computing. Principles and Prospects of Application. | CALCUL STOCHASTIQUE. PRINCIPE ET PERSPECTIVES D'APPLICATION.
Abstract: Basically, in a stochastic computer, information is represented by random pulse signals. Although studies have only recently been undertaken in this field, they have already given rise to applications due to the development of microelectronics. The principles of stochastic representation of data are set forth and the main stochastic operators are described. Stochastic encoding and decoding of data is explained and the field of application of stochastic computers is examined. They are particularly suited for cases where reliability and security rather than precision and speed are primarily required.

Title: Representation of contours and regions for efficient computer search
Abstract: A novel computer-searchable representation for the three basic pictorial features, contour maps, region coverage, and line structures, is described. The representation, which has practical storage requirements, provides a rapid means of searching large files for data associated with geometric position as well as with attribute value. An application of this representation to handling terrain information illustrates its utility. The algebraic properties of the data structure make it computationally easy to determine whether a point lies within a closed boundary; compute the area contained by a closed boundary; generate the closed boundary representing the union or intersection of two closed boundaries; and determine the neighboring boundaries to a point and the minimum distances between them and the point. ¬© 1973, ACM. Title: Fast State Minimization of Incompletely Specified Sequential Machines
Abstract: Existing techniques for finding minimum state covers of an incompletely specified sequential machine are streamlined to yield a single minimum cover with significantly less computation. Abstract: This paper is concerned with establishing the existence of a recursive sequence x which exhibits a ‚Äúcontinuous‚Äù trade-off between the length of programs (information) which compute the finite initial segments of x and the computation resources (e.g. computation time) required by these programs for such computation. ¬© 1973, ACM. Title: System Theoretical Criteria of the Formalization of Program Structures (Software Concept). | [SYSTEMTHEORETISCHE KRITERIEN DER FORMALISIERUNG VON PROGRAMMSTRUKTUREN (EIN FORWARE-KONZEPT).]
Abstract: A method based on elementary and general criteria by which the complexity of programs can be broken up into a network of sequential or recursive processes is discussed. The structure of these processes can be defined by static state-relations by means of so-called operations and variables, representing modular processes and quantities of states; these definitions simultaneously imply also the structure of the data resulting from a process, so that the user can combine the processes to be activated corresponding to specific needs in the same way one would use building blocks.

Title: The use of grammatical inference for designing programming languages
Abstract: Both in designing a new programming language and in extending an existing language, the designer is faced with the problem of deriving a ‚Äúnatural‚Äù grammar for the language. We are proposing an interactive approach to the grammar design problem wherein the designer presents a sample of sentences and structures as input to a grammatical inference algorithm. The implemention is presently restricted to a subclass of operator precedence grammars, but a second algorithm is outlined which applies to a larger class of context-free grammars. ¬© 1973, ACM. Title: TRAFFIC DENSITY ESTIMATION FOR SINGLE AND MULTILANE TRAFFIC.
Abstract: Modifications are proposed for an algorithm that estimates the number of vehicles on a section of highway from a time series of flow and velocity measurements. The effect of alternate assumptions concerning the nature of the velocity field between points of measurement is explored. A simplification is proposed to avoid solution by successive approximation of certain transcendental equations.
Name: ["Knapp Charles H."]

Title: USE OF DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING TECHNIQUES FOR DETERMINING RESOURCE ALLOCATIONS AMONG R/D PROJETS: AN EXAMPLE.
Abstract: An example of the use of dynamic programming for R&D resource allocation in the aerospace industry is described. Procedures for developing the required input data are described, and a quantitative comparison is made of the effectiveness of resource allocation by dynamic programming vis-a-vis a conventional method. It is shown that dynamic programming can result in significant improvements in program effectiveness.
Name: ["Kepler C.Edward", "Blackman Wade"]

Title: A spatial filtering technique for improved holographic character recognition
Abstract: Conventional holographic pattern recognition systems suffer from the disadvantage that, in dealing with highly ordered patterns such as Arabic numerals or the letters of the Roman alphabet it is sometimes impossible to distinguish between patterns with a high degree of similarity (eg the capital letters 'E' and 'F' or 'B' and 'P'). The present paper analyzes a simple case and shows how the insertion of a suitable spatial filter in the Fourier transform plane can reduce the unwanted cross-correlation signal between dissimilar patterns to zero, without removing the desired auto-correlation signal between similar patterns. Although no attempt is made to generalize the analysis, it seems probable that in cases involving the recognition of a small number of patterns with a strong 'family resemblance' a compromise filtering arrangement could be developed which would lead to a substantially improved performance. ¬© 1972.
Name: ["Pursey H."]

Title: Some Comments on the Use of Ambiguous Decision Tables and Their Conversion to Computer Programs
Abstract: This paper comments upon recently published work on decision table translation using methods similar to the rule-mask technique. The applicability of these methods under various possible conventions on overall table meaning is discussed, and it is argued that there is a place both for the multi-rule and the single-rule (or action set) convention in decision table usage. ¬© 1973, ACM. Title: DATA SIMULATION FROM PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTIONS.

Abstract: Review of the techniques for generating random numbers from probability distributions and to review some applications of these randomly generated numbers in models having probabilistic components. The use of the simulated observations in stochastic models is discussed.

Title: COMPARISON OF TWO PERSONNEL PREDICTION MODELS.
Abstract: The paper describes, compares, and contrasts two mathematical models of personnel movement through a hierarchical organization. The first model is a Markov chain. The emphasis is on a cohort model based on people's lifetime behavior in the system. Data from student enrollments is used in comparing the models, and predictions are made and compared with numbers from real situations.

Title: Geophysical interpretation - A pattern recognition system
Abstract: The general interpretation system is defined by a cyclic chain of deductions and inductions within the premises of the general pattern recognition system. The major problem of adducing the best-fitting model for the determination of target parameters through their field response can be achieved by designing an adaptive pattern recognition scheme. Such a scheme has been resolved into three major areas: Prognosis, Sophistication and Diagnosis. Sophistication has been considered as the key to simulate natural settings. The dependence of this sophistication on the type of physical parameter involved has been shown through statistical approach of Kernel approximation. ¬© 1973.

Abstract: Mathematical models for prediction of the performance behavior in the technological process methods are reviewed. An algorithm for the probability calculus is introduced. The use of various mathematical methods for process control, automatic control and measurementsis outlined.
Name: ["Engelmann H.G.", "Kretzschmar B."]

Title: Experimental Study of Information Measure and Inter-Intra Class Distance Ratios on Feature Selection and Orderings
