Abstract: This paper describes the results of experimental investigation of two-feature evaluation criteria, i.e. inter-intra class distance ratio and information content measure. These two indirect statistical measures take into account higher order statistical redundancies among the feature being evaluated. The algorithms are first presented and then they are applied and compared to recognize handprinted alphanumeric characters. Both Highleyman'S data and raw data obtained in the Signal Processing Laboratory at Case Western Reserve University, Cleveland, Ohio, were used for the study. It is believed that the criteria can be used for other applications and can especially be used where the statistical independency among features is not assumed. Name: ["Michael M."]

Title: IMPROVED DISCRIMINANT TRAINING AND FEATURE EXTRACTION FOR THE GENERATION OF SIMULATED MASS SPECTRA OF SMALL ORGANIC MOLECULES.

Title: APPROXIMATELY BAYESIAN CLASSIFICATION IN THE ABSENCE OF A PRIORI INFORMATION.
Abstract: A probabilistic classification problem with a teacher is studied in the absence of a priori information regarding the probabilistic characteristics of the input situations. Equations determining the minimum of the mean Bayesian risk in a class of given decision rules are obtained, and adaptive algorithms for solving them are constructed.
Name: ["Opoytsev V.I."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS FOR CONTROLLING COMPLEX TECHNOLOGICAL PROCESSES.
Abstract: An examination is made of the synthesis of a control system of an industrial object whose mathematical expectation is linear in the controlling influences. The problem is solved under conditions of incomplete information regarding the probabilistic nature of the random variables in the mathematical model. The control law is sought in the form of a linear decision rule. Approximate deterministic equivalents are given for the stochastic problems in the form of convex programming models.

Title: SKELETONIZATION OF BINARY IMAGE.

Name: ["Rutchka A."]

Title: SIMULATION OF LOGICAL-DIFFERENTIAL SYSTEMS ON A DIGITAL COMPUTER.
Abstract: The concept and formal definition of logical differential systems are given on the basis of set-theoretic partition of a class of continuous-discrete systems. A deterministic mathematical model of functioning of logical-differential systems is proposed. It is shown that the dynamics of the logical-differential systems can be regarded as the functioning of a special class of automata. One possible method of numerical simulation of logical-differential systems using a digital computer is proposed. The characteristics of a special program developed for the digital computer M-220 in the algorithmic language LYaPAS, with arithmetic broadening, are presented.
Name: ["Perchuk V.L.", "Fisun N.T."]

Title: METHOD FOR SHIFTING FROM LOGICAL DIAGRAMS OF ALGORITHMS TO AN ASYNCHRONOUS LOGICAL GRID.
Abstract: An examination is made of a method of coding the internal states of an automaton, such that to each state corresponds a memory element of special form. A method is proposed for simplifying the structure of such an element, and decreasing the number of them. The method can find broad application in cases in which the algorithm of functioning of the automaton is described in the language of logical schemes of algorithms. The control object is represented in the form of an operational automaton, and the distribution function of the displacements is introduced for describing it.
Name: ["Millerova M.G."]

Title: ON SEQUENTIAL DETECTION OF SIGNALS AGAINST A NOISE BACKGROUND.
Abstract: Sequential detection methods that are based on simultaneous detection and filtering are examined. Sufficient coordinates are found for the case in which the signal and noise are functions of Markov processes. The structure of optimal and quasioptimal sequential detectors is clarified. The apparatus of Markov processes is used to study the characteristics of sequential detection. Specific examples of synthesis and analysis of sequential procedures are examined. The relationship between the detection and filtering characteristics is brought out.
Name: ["Sosulin Yu.G.", "Fishman M.M."]

Title: On the stability of a stochastic non-linear differential system
Abstract: A stochastic control system is studied by applying the general theory of stochastic integral equations. A theorem is proven which guarantees the existence of a unique random solution x(t; œâ) of a stochastic differential system in the form where œâ‚ààŒ©, the supporting set of a probability measure space (Œ©, B, P), and T* is a non-linear operator. In addition the random solution x(t; œâ) is shown to be exponentially stable in mean square under the conditions of the theorem. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Padgett W.J."]

Title: DISTRIBUTION OF AN ESTIMATE OF THE MEAN QUEUE LENGTH IN A MULTILINE QUEUEING SYSTEM.
Abstract: A formula is derived for the variance of a sample estimate of the mean length of a queue in a multiline Poisson queueing system with waiting. The result obtained can be used for a priori estimates of the accuracy of statistical simulation of complex systems of similar structure.
Name: ["Polyak D.G."]

Title: Solvability of the halting problem for certain classes of Turing machines
Source: Mathematical Notes of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR
Abstract: One method of proving that some Turing machine is not universal is to prove that the halting problem is solvable for it. Therefore, to obtain a lower bound on the complexity of a universal machine, it is convenient to have a criterion of solvability of the halting problem. In the present paper, we establish some of these criteria; they are formulated in terms of properties of machine graphs and computations. ¬© 1973 Consultants Bureau.
Name: ["Pavlotskaya L.M."]

Title: OPTIMAL SCHEDULING POLICIES FOR SOME SIMPLE TRANSPORTATION SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A transportation system is described with one vehicle and several service points. Travel times between adjacent stops are random variables whose distribution functions are unchanged over a given period of time. The problem is to devise the scheduling strategy that minimizes average waiting time for passengers of the system. The special case of a two-stop line is analyzed in detail. An approximate optimal policy for systems with two terminals, very closely related to the one-terminal optimal strategy, is suggested.
Name: ["Barnett Arnold", "Kleitman Daniel J."]

Title: An integrated non-parametric sequential approach to multi-class pattern classification
Abstract: A now method of pattern classification, evolved by integrating in a sequential mode a non-parametric feature selection criterion with an explicit learning scheme, is presented. This feature selection criterion is based on the well-known concept of inter-class and intra-class Euclidean distances as a measure of the separability of the pattern classes in a given feature space. An ‚Äò effective figure of merit‚Äô is denned and the feature subset in which this figure of merit attains the maximum value is construed as the best feature subset. Usually in most of the existing techniques, a single feature subset is chosen as the hest for the multi-class problem as a whole. A distinctive departure from this practice has been made here in that an individual best feature subset is determined for each of the pattern classes. The values of the effective figure of merit for the best feature subsets of the different pattern classes are sorted to determine the best separable pattern class. The learning scheme developed here is employed in conjunction with the feature selection scheme to train the weight vector of the beat separable class. This learning is explicit in that the weight vector is moved in the appropriate feature subspace to search for the position of minimum classification error amidst the training sample clusters with the errors being monitored explicitly throughout the learning phase. This weight vector is then used to classify the training set and those samples (from the remaining classes) which are classified as unknown form the reconstituted training sample set. This procedure of selecting the best feature subset of the best separable pattern class and training the weight vector of that class is continued sequentially until alt the pattern classes have been considered. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Dasarathy B.V."]

Title: Automated spectral analysis of neurophysiological data using intermediate magnetic tape storage
Abstract: A software package for the Digital Equipment Corporation Lab-8 Computer is described which performs frequency domain analysis of biological input-output signals where each signal may consist of either a continuous analog record or a series of point events in time such as action potentials. The data to be analysed is first stored in digital format on a DECtape magnetic tape storage device and is then accessed by a series of programs which sample the data, perform the fast Fourier transform upon the sampled data and then compute averaged spectral estimates from the Fourier coefficients. Intermediate data samples and final spectral estimates are stored on a DF32 magnetic disc unit as files within the Disc Monitor System. Ancillary programs are provided which allow visual and numerical examination of the data at various stages of the process. Access to the data and arithmetic manipulation of the data is provided through the interpretive language FOCAL. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["French A.S."]

Title: CHOICE OF THE STRUCTURE OF A DIAGNOSIS DEFECT SYSTEM IN A DIGITAL COMPUTER.
Abstract: An examination is made of the problem of organizing the diagnosis of defects in a digital computer, with an arbitrary finite number of levels of exchange of a part that has failed, as an integer-valued linear programming problem.
Name: ["Trufanov S.V."]

Title: ON OPTIMAL DISPATCHING IN SINGLE-CHANNEL QUEUEING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: An examination is made of a single-channel queueing system with waiting, at the input of which there appear n simple flows of orders, differing in cost of losses due to wating per unit time. The distribution law of the servicing time is the same for all n flows. An algorithm is constructed for setting up m less than n relative priorities on the set of n flows, that is optimal with respect to the overall losses due to waiting. The computational efficiency of the algorithm is estimated.
Name: ["Eydinov R.M.", "Afanas'yev L.A."]

Title: STABILITY ESTIMATES FOR NON-STATIONARY SYSTEMS WITH OPTIMAL REGULATORS AND CHANGING OBJECT PARAMETERS.
Abstract: Linear systems optimized on the basis of a quadratic criterion are considered. A method is proposed for estimating the system stability with fixed regular parameters and changing object parameters. Examples which illustrate the efficiency of the method are presented.
Name: ["Vanyurikhin G.I.", "Zhitarev V.K."]

Title: Control of Linear Systems, with Bounded Correcting Variables by Means of Stepping Minimization of a Norm. | [STEUERUNG LINEARER SYSTEME MIT BEGRENZTER STELLGROESSE DURCH SCHRITTWEISES MINIMIEREN EINER NORM.]
Abstract: Calculation of the input stepping functions of linear systems with bounded correcting variables leads to an undetermined system of equations, if deadbeat-response is required. For this system of equations an algorithmic solution is given. First, an estimate of the number of sampling intervals which are necessary for the control is made. Starting from this estimate the particular control steps are derived by minimization of a norm which is formed from the control vector remaining at any particular time.
Name: ["Ziegler E."]

Title: CONTROL WITH PREDICTION OPTIMIZATION IN SIMPLE CONTINUOUS PLANT MODELS.
Abstract: A control system with optimization of prediction is studied that satisfies the basic principles of self-organization. A simple linear prediction model is used that acts only in a local (limited) interval equal to the prediction time. Its simplicity makes it possible to use Pontryagin's maximum principle for optimization, and to ascertain the main properties of the system under consideration, in particular, to discover an asymptotic law according to which an increase in prediction time causes the optimal control to change less and less, while the stability of the system increases (either monotonically or with damped oscillations) to a steady-state value.
Name: ["Ivakhnenko A.G.", "Tolokhnyanenko V.A."]

Title: DIRECT ALGORITHM FOR IMITATION OF MARKOV SEQUENCES.
Abstract: A direct algorithm is studied for imitation of Markov sequences using the recursion relation x//n// plus //1 equals f(x//n), where f(x) is a piecewise-linear function defined on a unit interval. It is shown that, under certain restrictions on f(x), there exists a partition of the interval left bracket 0, 1 right bracket into a finite number of subintervals, such that the set of all possible sequences of number defined by this recursion, and factored according to that partition, is isomorphic to the set of realizations of some homogeneous nondegenerate Markov chain with a finite number of states. Conversely, for an arbitrary homogeneous nondegenerate Markov chain with a finite number of states, there exists a piecewise-linear function f(x) such that the set of corresponding sequences is isomorphic to the set of realizations of that chain. The proposed algorithm is easily realized on a digital computer, and requires no external random (or pseudorandom) inputs.
Name: ["Sandler Ye.A."]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR SYNTHESIS OF CONTROL LAWS FOR NONLINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: An algorithm for synthesis of control laws is considered that is based on construction of the solution of a nonlinear system of equations in a DELTA t-interval, with the aid of series, and minimizing the norm of the deviations of the actual trajectory from the assigned trajectory. An example is presented, illustrating the use of this algorithm.
Name: ["Gryshutin V.G.", "Plashenko O.M."]

Title: Human Factor Aspects for Data Traffic with Telephone Subscriber Devices. | HUMAN-FACTOR-GESICHTSPUNKTE FUER DEN DATENVERKEHR MIT FERNSPRECH-TEILNEHMERGERAETEN.
Source: NTZ Nachr Z NTZ Commun J
Abstract: Data traffic with telephone subscriber devices raises a variety of human factor problems concerning the organization of the data services, the procedures and the design of the subscriber devices. The information flow generated by the subscriber (several bit/sec) is relatively small; the data - like telephone numbers - are mostly redundance-free. A display for the purpose of input check lowers the error rate. With the aid of the card reader, data entry is reproducible and also faster and more reliable than by hand. If human factor problems will be satisfactorily solved, data traffic should hardly be more difficult for the user than a telephone call.
Name: ["Flohrer Walter", "Noe Werner"]

Title: A spatially-oriented information processor which simulates the motions of rigid objects
Abstract: An iterative circuit array is described, which can simulate the forced motions of rigid objects. The array acts as a highly-parallel information-processor, which is especially suited to spatial problems involving the motions of objects. Relevance to spatial representation in A.I. is proposed. Electronic simulation of an aspect of "visual thinking" is described. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Baker R."]

Title: Linear Convex Stochastic Optimal Control with Applications in Production Planning
Abstract: Linear stochastic systems with convex performance criteria and convex, compact control regions are studied. The admissible control region is assumed to be a continuous function of the (perfectly) observed state. Optimal feedback controls are shown to exist within the class of Borel measurable functions of past states. In fact, they are shown to be continuous functions of the present state. Using dynamic programming the optimal return function is shown to be convex. Asymptotic results for stable systems are derived. These results are then used to explore several problems in aggregate production and work-force planning. Computational aspects of the results in the context of the smoothing problem are discussed. ¬© 1973 IEEE
Name: ["Kleindorfer P.R.", "Glover K."]
Affiliations: [' Massachusetts Institute of Technology', ' Massachusetts Institute of Technology']

Title: Algorithms for Designing Fault-Detection Experiments for Sequential Machines
Abstract: In this paper we present algorithms for designing fault-detection experiments for sequential machines with special emphasis on the case in which the machine does not possess a distinguishing sequence. The length of an experiment is reduced through: 1) identifying each state with its own unique input/output set rather than using a common set for all states; 2) utilizing overlapping of the required input/output sequences so that a portion of the experiment serves more than one purpose; and 3) verifying the reference condition in which the machine is placed at many points in the experiment by as short a locating sequence as possible. Important distinctions are made between locating sequences of the type introduced in previous work and those defined and used here. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Farmer D.E."]

Title: Distribution Coding in the Visual Pathway
Abstract: Although a variety of types of spike interval histograms have been reported, little attention has been given to the spike interval distribution as a neural code and to how different distributions are transmitted through neural networks. In this paper we present experimental results showing spike interval histograms recorded from retinal ganglion cells of the cat. These results exhibit a clear correlation between spike interval distribution and stimulus condition at the retinal ganglion cell level. The averaged mean rates of the cells studied were nearly the same in light as in darkness whereas the spike interval histograms were much more regular in light than in darkness. We present theoretical models which illustrate how such a distribution coding at the retinal level could be ‚Äúinterpreted‚Äù or recorded at some higher level of the nervous system such as the lateral geniculate nucleus. Interpretation is an essential requirement of a neural code which has often been overlooked in modeling studies. Analytical expressions are derived describing the role of distribution coding in determining the transfer characteristics of a simple interaction model and of a lateral inhibition network. Our work suggests that distribution coding might be interpreted by simply interconnected neural networks such as relay cell networks, in general, and the primary thalamic sensory nuclei in particular. ¬© 1973, The Biophysical Society. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Sanderson A.C.", "Kozak W.M.", "Calvert T.W."]

Title: REDUNDANCY REDUCING FACSIMILE CODING SCHEME.
Source: NTZ Nachr Z NTZ Commun J
Abstract: A special run-length code for an efficient coding of black-white facsimile pictures, like weathermaps or printed matter, is described which allows considerable reductions in channel or storage capacity. Along the scan line black and white runs or segments of runs are coded with code words of different lengths. Reconstructing the runs or segments of runs from a transmitted code word can be accomplished instantaneously without observing subsequent code words. Coding with only two different word lengths and instantaneous decoding leads to a relatively simple hardware implementation of this run length coding. On the other hand by using an appropriate run segmentation rule and by matching the two word lengths to the run length probabilities this code achieves a relatively high compression factor of 80 percent of the upper bound of in-line run length coding for weathermaps.
Name: ["Musmann Hans Georg", "Preuss Dieter"]

Title: Approximation algorithms for combinatorial problems
Source: Proceedings of the Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
Abstract: Simple, polynomial-time, heuristic algorithms for finding approximate solutions to various polynomial complete optimization problems are analyzed with respect to their worst case behavior, measured by the ratio of the worst solution value that can be chosen by the algorithm to the optimal value. For certain problems, such as a simple form of the knapsack problem and an optimization problem based on satisfiability testing, there are algorithms for which this ratio is bounded by a constant, independent of the problem size. For a number of set covering problems, simple algorithms yield worst case ratios which can grow with the log of the problem size. And for the problem of finding the maximum clique in a graph, no algorithm has been found for which the ratio does not grow at least as fast as 0(n ), where n is the problem size and e 0 depends on the algorithm. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Johnson D.S."]

Title: Quantization errors in calculation of volumes areas and coordinates in medical images
Source: Proceedings of SPIE - The International Society for Optical Engineering
Abstract: In the computer processing of dynamic images (cinefilm, TV) data volume and rates are usually excessively high. This is because of the addition of two spatial demensions to the normal time-domain processing problem. It has therefore been necessary to reduce the spatial and intensity resolution of the converted images. This paper examines the errors resulting from these quantization trade-offs, as applied to several medical image processing problems. ¬© 1973 SPIE.
Name: ["Winter D.A.", "Reimer G.D."]

Title: Adaptive Estimation for a Linear System with Interrupted Observation
Abstract: This short paper is concerned with the Bayesian estimation problem for a linear system with the interrupted observation mechanism that is expressed in terms of the Stationary two-state Markov chain with unknown transition probabilities. Derived is the approximate minimum variance adaptive estimator algorithm coupled with the estimation of the unknown transition probabilities. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Sawaragi Y.", "Katayama T.", "Fujishige S."]

Title: DIAKOPTICS AND SYSTEM OPERATIONS: AUTOMATIC GENERATION CONTROL IN MULTIAREAS.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: A procedure for the instant-by-instant control of all the generation, or the so-called automatic generation control, of power pools is described. The multicomputer configuration formed by the multiplicity of individual company computers present is utilized in the procedure. The method is an extension of the present basepoint-and-participation-factor approach used in the USA for the control of the generation in a single area. The paper first summarizes the single-area method, and then presents the necessary multiarea theory; this is followed by the multiarea-dispatch algorithm and the procedure for the automatic generation control of power pools. It is shown that the dispatch algorithm and the hierarchy of multilevel control can be readily extended to a multiplicity of power pools or so-called 'superpools'.
Name: ["Happ H.H."]

Title: STORAGE MAPPING OF DIRECTED GRAPHS.
Abstract: A method is described for economically mapping directed graphs as matrices into a computer storage.
Name: ["Koch K."]

Title: Representation of fuzzy functions
Abstract: Fuzzy functions of n variables are studied. The unique representation of a fuzzy function as the join-irredundant sum of join-irreducible elements is presented: two algorithms are given for obtaining that representation either from any fuzzy expression or from a truth table of the function. A parametrical representation of the lattice of fuzzy functions compatible with a given Boolean function is studied through some disjunctive and conjunctive differentials introduced earlier for Boolean functions. Two algorithms for computing the prime implicants and the prime implicates of a fuzzy function are derived. | This paper is devoted to the study of fuzzy functions of n variables. The unique representation of a fuzzy function as the join irredundant sum of join irreducible elements is presented: two algorithms are given for obtaining that representation either from any fuzzy expression or from a truth table of the function. A parametrical representation of the lattice of fuzzy functions compatible with a given Boolean function is studied through some disjunctive and conjunctive differentials introduced earlier for Boolean functions. Finally two algorithms for computing the prime implicants and the prime implicates of a fuzzy function are derived.
Name: ["Davio M.", "Thayse A."]

Title: Quantization of Pictorial Color Information; Nonlinear Transforms
Abstract: The use of hue and saturation signals to carry pictorial color information in digital systems is explored. The subjective performance of a linear quantization scheme for hue and saturation is investigated and compared to other schemes, using a graphical representation in a space of uniform subjective color discrimination. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Frei W."]

Title: Computerized optimal control system design for boost vehicles
Abstract: An optimization technique has been developed which combines the practical features of hybrid simulation of the dynamic systems with the systematic approach of modern control theory. Standard hybrid computer optimization methods using high-speed repetitive simulations and gradient minimization schemes have been extended to obtain time-varying optimal gain schedules and reduce the sensitivity of the optimized system to parameter and disturbance uncertainties. In this approach the performance index is expressed in meaningful engineering terms that reflect the interactions among all major design disciplines. The basic optimization technique is developed and its application to the space shuttle is presented. Control gain schedules, vehicle design and performance characteristics resulting from the technique are compared with controllers developed by conventional methods. ¬© 1973 by the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Inc.
Name: ["Trautwein W.", "Livingston J.M."]
Affiliations: ['Lockheed Missiles and Space Company Inc.', 'NASA Marshall Space Flight Center', ' Huntsville Research and Engineering Center', ' Aero Astrodynamics Laboratory']

Title: Recursive Image Enhancement-Vector Processing
Abstract: A new approach to design of a recursive image enhancer is introduced when the image is characterized statistically by its mean and correlation function. A vector linear dynamical model is derived to represent the statistics of the processor output when several lines of the picture are processed simultaneously. Based on the vector model, a Kalman filter is designed and utilized to recursively enhance the image. The vector processing results in a simpler and more accurate image enhancement algorithm in comparison with scalar processing. Two examples, one with very low signal-to-noise ratio, are used to illustrate the effectiveness of the procedure. Finally, the performance of the vector and scalar estimators is compared. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Nahi N.E.", "Franco C.A."]

Title: Edge Detection in Simple Scenes Using A Priori Information
Abstract: A system of programs is described for the detection of the straight edge lines in simple scenes. Distinct lines are detected by a procedure that is relatively inexpensive. The more subtle lines are then located by a search that is much more costly per unit area, but which is only applied to certain areas suggested by the locations of the lines already found. The considerable efficiency of this approach to edge detection is discussed both theoretically and in relation to the performance of the present system. The heuristics used in proposing possible subtle lines are described in detail. In addition, considerable attention is devoted to other aspects of the procedure such as: local edge-detection operators, vertex finding, and the extraction of lines from local evidence. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Griffith A.K."]

Title: Progress in Picture Processing: 1969‚Äì71
Abstract: Developments in the field of picture processing by computer during 1969-71 are surveyed. The topics covered include picture compression, image enhancement, pictorial pattern recognition, scene analysis, and picture grammars. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Rosenfeld A."]

Title: Implementation of a High Level Language Machine
Abstract: Computing machines which directly execute the statements of a high level language have been proposed in the past. This report describes the actual implementation of such a machine: it is a computer whose ‚Äúmachine language‚Äù is APL. The machine is fully operational and correctly executes almost all of the APL operations on scalars, vectors, and arrays. The machine automatically allocates memory, executes statements, calls functions, converts numbers from one type to another, checks subscripts, and automatically detects many types of programmer errors. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hassitt A.", "Lageschulte J.W.", "Lyon L.E."]

Title: A class of universal linear bounded automata
Abstract: In this paper we construct for each integer n, an lba which is universal for all lba's whose set of tape symbols numbers no more than n. We also obtain the corresponding result for deterministic lba's. These results are used to show that for each n there is a set accepted by a deterministic lba, but not by any deterministic lba with fewer than n symbols in its alphabet. The fundamental idea is to modify the construction of the universal Turing machine so that it becomes universal for an appropriate class of linear-bounded automata. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Feldman E.D.", "Owings Jr. J.C."]
Affiliations: [' University of Maryland', ' University of Maryland']

Title: Fixed-lag smoothing for nonlinear systems with discrete measurements
Abstract: Approximate nonlinear filtering formulas are applied to yield fixed-lag smoothing results for nonlinear systems with discrete noisy observations. A signal process model is defined which allows the required fixed-lag estimates to be obtained as filtered estimates. The smoothing results are only approximations since the nonlinear filtering theory used is based on simplifying approximations, but assuming that the simplifications are valid, then the fixed-lag smoothed estimate is a better one than simply a filtered estimate. In some circumstances the improvement may be quite substantial. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Moore J.B.", "Tam P.K.S."]

Title: NEW LOOK AT ADAPTIVE CONTROL.
Abstract: An adaptive control system is one which operates in an environment that changes over time in an unpredictable fashion. It can be justified only where conditions warrant its use. In general, a process is a candidate for adaptive control when there are changes over time in the input/output relationship of the process. These variations may result from disturbances to the process, raw material variations, wear of equipment components, etc. When there are unpredictable changes in the process or its environment which affect system performance, adaptive control represents a logical approach to the problem of compensating for these changes.
Name: ["Groover Mikell P."]

Title: Identification of the Static Behavior of Very Noisy Dynamic Processes. | IDENTIFIKATION DES STATISCHEN VERHALTENS STARK GESTOERTER DYNAMISCHER PROZESSE.
Abstract: Various identification methods for the static behavior of very noisy dynamic processes are described. The scatter of the static parameter errors caused by the noise signals are compared with the minimum possible value in accordance with the Cramer-Rao-Frechet Law. It is further shown how the static behavior of slow time-variant processes can be measured. Some methods can also be applied to nonlinear processes.
Name: ["Isermann R."]

Title: New Algorithm of Optimal Dynamic Control. | [UN NOUVEL ALGORITHME DE COMMANDE DYNAMIQUE OPTIMALE.]
Abstract: Applications of the theory of optimal dynamic control to industrial processes remain always extremely limited, the main reason for this being the more or less arbitrary choice of the structure of the dynamic model. This article presents a control with quadratic criteria and receding horizon, realized from a model with pulse response. A critical study of the quadratic control method is presented, and a very simplified solution using a short horizon of optimization has been chosen. The algorithm is completed by adding a new stochastic predictor allowing the system to react in front of random disturbances. A very precise dynamic identification is not particularly necessary.
Name: ["Lebourgeois F.", "Menendez A."]

Title: Actor induction and meta-evaluation
Source: Conference Record of the Annual ACM Symposium on Principles of Programming Languages
Abstract: The PLANNER project is continuing research in natural and effective means for embedding knowledge in procedures. In the course of this work we have succeeded in unifying the formalism around one fundamental concept: the ACTOR. Intuitively, an ACTOR is an active agent which plays a role on cue according to a script. We use the ACTOR metaphor to emphasize the inseparability of control and data flow in our model. Data structures, functions, semaphores, monitors, ports, descriptions, Quillian nets, logical formulae, numbers, identifiers, demons, processes, contexts, and data bases can all be shown to be special cases of actors. All of the above are objects with certain useful modes of behavior. Our formalism shows how all of these modes of behavior can be defined in terms of one kind of behavior: sending messages to actors. An actor is always invoked uniformly in exactly the same way regardless of whether it behaves as a recursive function, data structure, or process. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hewitt C.", "Bishop P.", "Greif I.", "Smith B.", "Matson T.", "Steiger R."]

Title: COMBINATION REPLACEMENT ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: This configuration replaces data on a combination of both the least used and first in, first out replacement algorithms.
Name: ["Chia D.K.", "Sigworth K.L."]

Title: Sufficiently Informative Functions and the Minimax Feedback Control of Uncertain Dynamic Systems
Abstract: The problem of optimal feedback control of uncertain discrete-time dynamic systems is considered where the uncertain quantities do not have a stochastic description but instead are known to belong to given sets. The problem is converted to a sequential minimax problem and dynamic programming is suggested as a general method for its solution. The notion of a sufficiently informative function, which parallels the notion of a sufficient statistic of stochastic optimal control, is introduced, and conditions under which the optimal controller decomposes into an estimator and an actuator are identified. A limited class of problems for which this decomposition simplifies the computation and implementation of the optimal controller is delineated. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Bertsekas D.P.", "Rhodes I.B."]

Title: An automaton in the nonstationary random environment
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to consider the behavior of a finite automaton in a nonstationary random environment. The behavior of finite deterministic automata in stationary random environments was considered by Tsetlin. In this paper, the probabilistic automaton is introduced as a random environment in order to generalize the stationary random environment. The interaction between the probabilistic automaton and the two-state deterministic automaton is considered in the case where the probabilistic automaton has two inputs and two states and, besides, is completely isolated by the 0th approximation. And the limiting state probability distribution of this finite automaton is also obtained. Moreover, it is shown that, if the probabilistic automaton is completely isolated by the (0, k)th approximation and satisfies some conditions, then the finite automaton can behave expediently against the probabilistic automaton. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Tsuji H.", "Mizumoto M.", "Toyoda J.", "Tanaka K."]

Title: HYBRID COMPUTER SOLUTION OF QUEUEING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Digital computers have been widely used for solving queueing problems. However, when the complexity of the problem increases the computational time and cost rise exponentially. A hybrid computer approach has been developed in which the rise in cost caused by the complexity of the problem is negligible. The errors of the hybrid system were not cummulative and therefore it was capable of duplicating the solution of the digital computer within the accuracy of 2%. The optimization of an n-stage stochastic service system has been used as an example. A circuit diagram for simulating a 5-stage stochastic servicing system, and the results obtained with it are presented.
Name: ["Khalil T.M.", "Valisalo P.E.", "Copsey A."]

Title: Model for Visual Pattern Recognition Based on Decision Theoretical Criteria. | [MODELLE ZUR VISUELLEN ZEICHENERKENNUNG AUF DER GRUNDLAGE ENTSCHEIDUNGTHEORETISCHER KRITERIEN.]
Abstract: Tanner and Swets have shown that statistical decision theory offers a useful model for the behavior of sense organs. The present study describes three experiments in which the performance of human observers in three visual tasks (contrast sensitivity in homogeneous and noisy backgrounds, and detection of detail) can be described with the help of a decision theory model. A significant finding is that the results of psychophysical measurements are significantly dependent on the observer's criterion and on the probability of detection that is used.
Name: ["Schwegler F.", "Husemann K."]

Title: CONSTRUCTION OF AN ALGORITHM FOR STABILIZATION OF A DEFORMING SPACECRAFT USING A DIGITAL COMPUTER.
Abstract: An algorithm is presented for the control of mechanical systems based on a standardized model, written in differential form. A sufficiently simple system, described by linear differential equations, was chosen as the standardized model. A study is made of the algorithm and the methods of formation of the assigned properties of its transmission function are shown. The realization of the algorithm assumes the presence in the control circuit of a digital computer.
Name: ["Sidorov I.M.", "Krangacheva L.B.", "Lebedev V.G."]

Title: STRONG CONSISTENCY OF A NONPARAMETRIC ESTIMATE OF A DENSITY FUNCTION.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: If one has n observations from the probability density f then one nonparametric estimate of f(x) is essentially to divide an integer k(n) by the volume of the smallest sphere centered at x which contains at least k(n) of the n observations. Loftsgaarden and Quesenberry gave conditions on f and the sequence k(n) which ensured that this estimate converges in probability to f(x). Similar conditions which ensure convergence with probability 1 are given here.
Name: ["Wagner Terry J."]

Title: ON ESTIMATING RANDOM PROCESSES WITH FINITE MEMORY.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The use of finite-valued statistics in sequential estimation is extended to include estimation of stationary and nonstationary random processes. Numerical results indicate the tradeoffs that occur between memory size, observation quality, signal correlation, and observation time.
Name: ["Tooley John R.", "Roberts Richard A."]

Title: DETERMINATION OF PREDICTION EQUATION COEFFICIENTS USING THE CRITERION OF ‚Ä≥PROBABILITY OF OCCURRENCE IN THE DEVIATION CORRIDOR ‚Ä≥.
Abstract: It is proposed to construct a model of a random process by approximating the distribution function and the correlation function. It is shown that this problem can be solved by a uniform Chebyshev approximation. A formula is obtained for the quantization step for which the hypothesis of consistency of the original sample with the obtained model is valid.
Name: ["Chukin Yu.V."]

Title: Optimal Stochastic Linear Systems with Exponential Performance Criteria and Their Relation to Deterministic Differential Games
Abstract: Two stochastic optimal control problems are solved whose performance criteria are the expected values of exponential functions of quadratic forms. The optimal controller is linear in both cases but depends upon the covariance matrix of the additive process noise so that the certainty equivalence principle does not hold. The controllers are shown to be equivalent to those obtained by solving a cooperative and a noncooperative quadratic (differential) game, and this leads to some interesting interpretations and observations. Finally, some stability properties of the asymptotic controllers are discussed. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Jacobson D.H."]

Title: Growing and pruning a pattern classifier
Abstract: In the past, automatic procedures for the design of pattern classifiers have usually used a machine of fixed size. These procedures require that prior to learning we know, or can guess, the complexity of the decision surface used by the teacher. Techniques have been discovered for changing the complexity of a pattern classifier by adding or removing parts of it. These methods, respectively called "growing" and "pruning" use well established learning rules applied alternately with the addition or removal of comput,ing equipment. Growing is thus a process by which we can increase the complexity of a classifier until it fits the problem. Pruning removes computing equipment from a classifier whose performance is satisfactory, but inefficient. The paper describes our experimental evaluation of these procedures. These studies have shown that these techniques are capable of designing a classifier which closely models a complex teacher with a minimum of storage. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Batchelor B.G."]

Title: A Picture-Coding Algorithm for the Merli Scan
Abstract: A method is proposed and evaluated for coding a notched scan that jumps back and forth between adjacent scan lines of a normal raster. Alternate points in the line are coded using the normal differential quantizer algorithm while the remaining points use a nonlinear predictor proposed by Graham. The advantage of the algorithm over normal differential quantization is that the prediction strategy is improved while the advantage over other two-dimensional strategies is that the effect of transmission errors is confined to the line pair being processed and does not spread vertically. For coarse coding there is a significant improvement in picture quality when compared with normal differential quantization while for high-quality pictures there is a small reduction in entropy. The effect of transmission errors is investigated and shown to be similar to the effect with normal differential quantization. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Limb J.O."]

Title: The Design, Implementation, and Evaluation of a Working Set Dispatcher
Abstract: The behavior of a computer system is largely dependent upon the algorithms employed to allocate the system resources to the processes competing for them. Recent research in time-sharing paging systems has developed the working set model for program behavior, and a resource allocation strategy based on this model has been proposed. Two implementations along these principles have been reported, but it seems that in neither case have further results been announced. This report discusses the design and implementation of a dispatcher based on the working set principle, presents data to permit analysis of its behavior, and indicates future directions of research on methods of controlling a computer system. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Rodriguez-Rosell J.", "Dupuy J.-P."]
Affiliations: [' Royal Institute of Technology', 'IBM France Scientific Center']

Title: AN AUTOMATED SHIP MAINTENANCE SYSTEM
Abstract: Any shipboard computer system meets its system objectives only when it is totally operational. When it is down due to a system failure it is a useless collection of electronic components. In present and future ship computer systems, maintainability is not only desirable, it is mandatory. Also system maintainability must keep pace with the increased sophistication and complexity of the systems themselves. To meet this maintainability requirement, system designers must consider system maintenance at the time of system design and development. In the philosophy of an automated maintenance system such as the one discussed in this paper, the system design and development process is geared to making all operating system information, which could be used in system maintainability, available in an orderly meaningful manner. This process means designing the system software to monitor system status and performance data, to use this data along with preventive maintenance scheduling and fault prediction analysis in performing total system evaluation. This evaluation process then results in the definition of recommended preventive testing or the required fault detection and isolation testing. During the latter stages of fault isolation testing and continuing through fault correction, the system is also responsible for making the available reconfiguration recommendations for the failure being corrected. Following the correction of a system failure the system is automatically reconfigured to the normal operating system. Data appropriate to the system failure is categorized and, recorded to be used in future fault prediction and preventive maintenance scheduling. All of this occurs in real‚Äêtime and on‚Äêline, in conjunction with the normal operation of a system program. This capability is provided for during the software design period. While not totally automatic or totally comprehensive, it provides maintenance personnel with the information required to determine what is happening within the system. This data combined with other features mentioned greatly reduces the essential and critical tasks of the maintenance personnel. Finally the entire process results in the required expansion of critical system availability. ¬© 1973 by the American Society of Naval Engineers
Name: ["STECKMAN G.L."]

Title: Model for Double Proportionality for Estimating Nonnegative Matrices, Particularly Input-Output Tables. | [MODELL DER DOPPELTEN PROPORTIONALITAET ZUR SCHAETZUNG VON NICHTNEGATIVEN MATRIZEN, INSBESONDERE INPUT-OUTPUT-TABELLEN.]
Abstract: A biproportional model for estimating nonnegative transaction matrices, especially input-output tables, is described. A complete matrix for a given period in time is known as base. The unknown matrix for a second period is to be estimated on this base from known marginal totals and certain given elements. The problem can be solved by constructing an initial estimate of the matrix followed by an iteration process. The algorithm has been formulated in FORTRAN IV and tested on a Siemens 4004/55 computer.
Name: ["Schintke J."]

Title: A search technique of control rod pattern for smoothing core power distributions by fuzzy automaton
Source: Journal of Nuclear Science and Technology
Abstract: This paper deals with a new search technique for optimum using a fuzzy automaton, which has been developed for the purpose of determining a desirable rod pattern for smoothing the core power distribution. Using the algorithm thus developed, the optimal input vector applied to a controlled system whose characteristics are unknown is determined automatically from a learning operation of the fuzzy automaton when an initial guess and a hypothetical range of optimal input vector are given. The characteristics of this algorithm are examined for an example of its application to a simple problem. The optimal control rod pattern for smoothing the core power distribution is also determined by this algorithm in a simulation study using the three-dimensional boiling water reactor simulator ‚ÄúFLARE‚Äù. It is concluded that optimum points are obtained with sufficient convergence and with only a small increase in the number of iterations and computation time accompanying an increase in the number of components of the input vector. The predicted optimal control rod pattern in the simulation study can be considered reliable. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Serizawa M."]

Title: Using verbs to automatically determine text descriptors
Abstract: This paper describes a method of automatic indexing which may also be viewed as a simulation of how a person classifies documents. In this method, the sentences of a passage are isolated and converted into an intermediate predicate formalism. The verb, which names the predicate, is assigned a priority. Predicate priorities, derived primarily from the verb priorities, are used as distance indices in converting the predicates from an entire passage to a graph structure. Elementary notions from graph theory are applied to determine the descriptors of the passage. The method is illustrated with a story that has been processed automatically. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Tharp A.L."]

Title: Restoration of Pictures by Quadratic Programming and by Fourier Transformation in the Complex Domain
Abstract: Two methods for digital restoration of pictures blurred by imperfections of the optical system and by random noise are suggested. Method one is based on the a priori information that a picture has nonnegative intensity and leads to quadratic programming. In method two, the finite extent of the picture is shown to make Fourier transformation in the complex domain useful. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Philip J."]

Title: Processing algorithm for a nonlinear signal in non Gaussian noise
Abstract: In deriving the probability coefficient in the case of non-Gaussian noise the primary difficulty is to find the multivariate probability density of the non-Gaussian noise. To circumvent this difficulty it is assumed that any stationary random process can be approximated as exactly as desired by Markovian processes. The aim is to find the conditional probability density of this non-Gaussian Markov process.
Name: ["Dunayev A.S.", "Voronin V.I.", "Mukhamedyarov R.D."]

Title: PERFORMANCE ESTIMATION OF KOLMOGOROV-SMIRNOV FILTER AND ITS APPLICATION TO PROCESSING OF TEXTURE PATTERNS.
Abstract: This paper introduces the KS filter (and the CvM filter) as a means of picture preprocessing and examines the properties. The KS filter (CvM filter) gives, as the output corresponding to each point of the picture, Kolmogorov-Smirnov (Cramer-von Mises) statistics derived from the intensities of the input picture in a small region with that point as the center. The paper first evaluates the detecting capabilities of these filters in discriminating the differences in the statistical properties of the input pictures, and then verifies experimentally these capabilities in applications to randomly produced artificial patterns and actual pictures (chest X-ray pictures).
Name: ["Kato Osamu", "Toriwaki Junichiro", "Fukumura Teruo"]

Title: VARIABLE SAMPLING FREQUENCY - A NEW ADAPTIVE TECHNIQUE.
Abstract: A novel scheme for adaptive plant control is reported which comes in handy where process dynamics vary randomly with time. A simple digital algorithm samples plant status less ofen when variations are slow, and more often as they increase in speed. It is claimed that control action economy and good predictability of plant behavior are achieved. The approach used is simple when compared with some of the more complex adaptive approaches.
Name: ["Sutherland Jr. A.A."]

Title: GENERATION AND REDUCTION OF DIAGNOSTIC DATA.
Abstract: The diagnostic data for detecting faults in a logical circuit can be regarded as a set of vectors with elements being 0, 1, and chi . It is shown that the reduction of diagnostic data becomes the problem of mapping this set of vectors to another set of vectors with fewer dimensions. The procedure of locating the fault then turns out to be that of determining the inclusive relation among the vectors. In the next step, properties are pointed out which the mapping must have in order to make such a reduction of the diagnostic data. A mapping which is practically useful and expressed by a logical function, and a tabular-form mapping which is expressed by a conversion table and a generation rule, are introduced, and their properties are examined.
Name: ["Kojima Kazuo", "Tanaka Chiyoshi", "Kanada Hajime"]

Title: A class of learning systems
Abstract: Recently, an increasing amount of work is being done on learning systems, i.e., systems capable of improving their performance during operation in such a way as to Optimally solve recognition, identification, filtration and control problems. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Tsypkin Y.Z."]

Title: A Region Coloring Technique for Scene Analysis
Abstract: A method of converting a picture into a ‚Äúcartoon‚Äù or ‚Äúmap‚Äù whose regions correspond to differently textured regions is described. Texture edges in the picture are detected, and solid regions surrounded by these (usually broken) edges are ‚Äúcolored in‚Äù using a propagation process. The resulting map is cleaned by comparing the region colors with the textures of the corresponding regions in the picture, and also by merging some regions with others according to criteria based on topology and size. The method has been applied to the construction of cloud cover maps from cloud cover pictures obtained by satellites. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Strong J.P., III", "Rosenfeld A."]
Affiliations: ['Goddard Space Flight Center', ' University of Maryland']

Title: Concurrent Programming Concepts
Abstract: This paper describes the evolution of language features for multiprogramming from event queues and semaphores to critical regions and monitors. It suggests that the choice of language concepts should be guided by two simple principles: First, ~t should be possible to understand a concurrent program in timeindependent terms by an effort proportional to its size; secondly, it should be possible to state assumptions about invarmnt relationships among program components and have these assumptmns checked automatically. The central problems of multiprogramming are illustrated by annotated algorithms written in a weU-structured programming language. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hansen P.B."]

Title: LOGISTIC DISTRIBUTION AS AN APPROXIMATION TO THE NORMAL CURVE.
Source: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Abstract: For psychophysical calculations with a small computer lacking an error-function routine it is shown that logistic distribution yields a satisfactory approximation to the normal probability function. Application is to statistics of optical and acoustical signal recognition by human observers.
Name: ["Jeffress Lloyd A."]

Title: Recognizing familiar patterns
Abstract: In this paper we are concerned with the recognition by machine of familiar patterns, which have either been encountered beforehand or are very similar to some pattern which the machine has seen previously. We shall assume that each pattern has been coded, to form a vector, X, containing only numeric descriptors. In order to design our machine we are given a finite number of these vectors, which will be used to develop some notion of ‚Äúfamiliar.‚Äù New vectors will then be classified by the machine as ‚Äúfamiliar‚Äù or ‚Äúnot like anything ever seen before.‚Äù. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Warren P.W.", "Batchelor B.G."]

Title: COMPUTER CONTROL OF ON-OFF ELECTROTHERMAL PROCESSES.
Abstract: A control scheme is described for improving the performance characteristics of an on/off electrothermal process by means of a model of the process. Although the process itself operates on open loop, the switching sequence is closely controlled by the operation of a closed loop incorporating the model and the process controller. The temperature drift may be virtually eliminated by representing the model electronically. The scheme proves useful when the process has a large inherent delay or when it is not convenient to derive transduced signals from the output temperature for the purpose of control.
Name: ["Murgatroyd J.L.", "Goodman D."]

Title: A theory of the epigenesis of neuronal networks by selective stabilization of synapses
Source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
Abstract: A formalism is introduced to represent the connective organization of an evolving neuronal network and the effects of environment on this organization by stabilization or degeneration of labile synapses associated with functioning. Learning, or the acquisition of an associative property, is related to a characteristic variability of the connective organization: the interaction of the environment with the genetic program is printed as a particular pattern of such organization through neuronal functioning. An application of the theory to the development of the neuromuscular junction is proposed and the basic selective aspect of learning emphasized.
Name: ["Changeux J.P.", "Courrege P.", "Danchin A."]

Title: PREDICTING DELAYS IN TIME-SHARING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: It is shown how blocking and delay theory from telephone traffic engineering can be used to predict the probability and average lengths of delays in a time-sharing system. The author considers a particular family of delay curves, known as the Erlang C curves, of interest because of analogies which can be drawn to time-sharing computer systems. The assumptions made in deriving the Erlang C curves and the applicability of these curves to delay prediction in time-sharing systems are analyzed. Finally, the author advises that the level of service against which a time-sharing system is to be designed should be detrmined through use of user-attitude surveys designed to measure acceptable standards of system performance as seen from the user's viewpoint. General forms of queueing theory equations for a ssingle-server system are presented in an appendix.
Name: ["Thomas G.R."]

Title: An Actively Adaptive Control for Linear Systems with Random Parameters via the Dual Control Approach
Abstract: A new method is presented for controlling a discrete time linear system with possibly time-varying random parameters in the presence of input and output noise. The cost is assumed to be quadratic in the state and control. Previous algorithms for the above problem when the system had both zeros and poles unknown were of the open-loop feedback type, i.e., they did not take into account that future observations will be made. Therefore, even though these schemes were adaptive, their learning was ‚Äúaccidental.‚Äù In contrast to this, the new approach uses an expression of the optimal cost-to-go that exhibits the dual purpose of the control, i.e., learning and control. The effect of the present control on the future estimation (‚Äúlearning‚Äù) appears explicitly in the cost used in the stochastic dynamic programming equation. The resulting sequence of controls, which is of the closed-loop type, is shown via simulations to appropriately divide its energy between the learning and the control purposes. Therefore, this control is called actively adaptive because it regulates the speed and amount of learning as required by the performance index. The simulations on a third-order system with six unknown parameters also demonstrate the computational feasibility of the proposed algorithm. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Tse E.", "Bar-Shalom Y."]

Title: On a Game Problem Involving Systems with Time Delay
Abstract: A dynamic programming approach is used to obtain feedback solutions to a game problem involving linear systems having a time delay. As is known, the optimal feedback gains in linear time delay systems with quadratic criterion are determined by partial differential equations [1]. In the particular case studied here, the solution to these equations can be obtained by first separating variables and then solving the resulting simpler equations. The optimal feedback control also has the advantage that it can be realized on-line. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Koivo A.J.", "Repperger D.W."]

Title: Efficient Exercising of Switching Elements in Combinatorial Nets
Abstract: The work described in a previous paper, ‚ÄúEfficient Exercising of Switching Elements in Nets of Identical Gates,‚Äù is continued. Sections 1, 3, and 4 of the previous paper are prerequisites to the current work. Exercising, or ‚Äútesting,‚Äù the gates of a net is equivalent to performing fault diagnosis in the case in which each fault is detectable. Where F is any set of switching functions, this paper establishes a necessary and sufficient condition on an arbitrary function set G such that all trees composed only of functions from F will accept G; choosing G as the ‚Äútesting‚Äù functions P(T, r) of the previous paper, this is the condition under which all such trees can be tested by r (or fewer) patterns. The case of ‚Äústuck-at‚Äù faults is then investigated at length. It is shown that: (a) all trees can be tested for stuck-at faults by three patterns, and nearly all by two patterns; (b) for some interesting classes of functions, all nets can be tested by two patterns‚Äîin general, many nets can; (c) for any set of functions which are functionally complete and suitably closed under constant inputs, there are nets which require arbitrarily many patterns. The latter result suggests that nets requiring arbitrarily many patterns exist for nearly all interesting choices of functions and of faults. For ‚Äúinput dependence‚Äù tests, a result is cited to show that economical testing of nets of nand (nor) gates of mixed sizes is possible. Finally, for the case of exhaustive testing, experience suggests that economical tests exist for most nets composed from functions of F wherever F is a bounded set‚Äîi.e. a set of functions for which there is a fixed upper bound on the number of patterns required to test any tree. The (individually) bounded functions are completely characterized; then the bounded sets of symmetric functions are completely characterized. The latter prove to be those sets for which: (a) each function is individually bounded (i.e. not ‚Äúand,‚Äù ‚Äúor,‚Äù or constant); and (b) F contains at most one of the following: (1) ‚Äúnot,‚Äù (2) a ‚Äúnand‚Äù function, (3) a ‚Äúnor‚Äù function. Thus bounded sets of functions are the rule, not the exception, and economical testing appears to be generally possible. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Richards D.L."]

Title: Resolution of a holographic shape recognition system
Abstract: Parameters characterizing the scale change, rotation angle and aspect angle of the image being analyzed by a system are described. The limiting values of these parameters in terms of a recognition quality criterion are computer calculated. | Parameters characterizing the scale change, rotation angle and aspect angle of the image being analyzed by a system are described. The limiting values of these parameters in terms of a recognition quality criterion are computer-calculated.
Name: ["Fedorov B.F.", "Dorokhov B.Y."]

Title: Parallel Program Schemata and Maximal Parallelism II: Construction of Closures
Abstract: The phenomenon of maximal parallelism is investigated in the framework of a class of parallel program schemata. Part II is concerned with the actual realization of closures of schemata represented as ‚Äúflowcharts.‚Äù In the case that the flowchart is acyclic there is always a closure which is finite-state realizable. However in the case of cyclic flowcharts this is not generally true. Then realizations which are not finite-state are investigated. Of special concern is the class of counter realizations and the class of queue realizations, both a type of ‚Äúreal-time‚Äù automaton. It is shown that these form a proper hierarchy in the set of realizations for closures of flowcharts. A class of flowcharts is then presented all of which have queue realizations of their closure. It is shown that for this class, the existence of a finite-state realization for the closure is decidable. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Keller R.M."]

Title: BIT-PLANE ACCESSARIES OF TRANSFORM DOMAIN SIGNAL PROCESSING.
Source: J Inst Telecommun Eng New Delhi
Abstract: In digital signal processing in the transform domain, it is important to study the effects of quantization in the transform domain on the signal reconstructed by inverse transformation. Adaptive quantization schemes are developed earlier for Fourier transform domain and Hadamard transform domain, using the knowledge that in the transform domain adaptive set-dependent bounds can be obtained on the sample amplitudes. This paper discusses various pre-processing and post-processing techniques that reduce the errors and favorably change the distribution of errors in the reconstructed signal or reduce the effective bit-rate without affecting the errors in the reconstructed signal.
Name: ["Moharir P.S."]

Title: Wide-Sense Adaptive Dual Control for Nonlinear Stochastic Systems
Abstract: A new approach is presented for the problem of stochastic control of nonlinear systems. It is well known that, except for the linear-quadratic problem, the optimal stochastic controller cannot be obtained in practice. In general it is the curse of dimensionality that makes the strict application of the principle of optimality infeasible. The two subproblems of stochastic control, estimation and control proper, are, except for the linear-quadratic case, intercoupled. As pointed out by Feldbaum, in addition to its effects on the state of the system, the control also affects the estimation performance. In this paper, the control problem is formulated such that this dual property of the control appears explicitly. The resulting control sequence exhibits the closed-loop property, i.e., it takes into account the past observations and also the future observation program. Thus, in addition to being adaptive, this control also plans its future learning according to the control objective. Some preliminary simulation results illustrate these properties of the control. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Tse E.", "Bar-Shalom Y.", "Meier L."]

Title: The logical analysis of continuous, non-linear biochemical control networks
Abstract: We propose a mapping to study the qualitative properties of continuous biochemical control networks which are invariant to the parameters used to describe the networks but depend only on the logical structure of the networks. For the networks, we are able to place a lower limit on the number of steady states and strong restrictions on the phase relations between components on cycles and transients. The logical structure and the dynamical behavior for a number of simple systems of biological interest, the feedback (predator-prey) oscillator, the bistable switch, the phase dependent switch, are discussed. We discuss the possibility that these techniques may be extended to study the dynamics of large many component systems. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Glass L.", "Kauffman S.A."]
Affiliations: [' University of Rochester', ' University of Chicago']

Title: Output Feedback Gains for a Linear-Discrete Stochastic Control Problem
Abstract: For the finite-horizon linear-discrete quadratic stochastic control problem, the control is restricted to be a memoryless linear transformation of the measurement. The two-point boundary value problem that specifies the feedback gain matrices is derived, and an algorithm for solving it is given. An example is solved comparing the cost of the suboptimal control to the optimal control. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Ermer C.M.", "Vandelinde V.D."]

Title: A Note on the Modified Kalman Filter for Channel Equalization
Abstract: An application of the Kalman filter to equalization of a digital communication channel is described. The resultant modified Kalman equalizer (KE) is a nonlinear system in which the channel tap gains are estimated via a decision feedback approach and the initial state variable is estimated by a prediction process. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Mark J.W."]

Title: Hyperplane Search Algorithms for the Solution of Integer Programming Problems
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: An algorithm is presented for solving all-integer linear programming problems which successively searches hyperplanes parallel to the optimal hyperplane containing the solution to the associated linear programming problem with the integer restrictions suppressed. These hyperplanes are searched for integer solution points using a dynamic programming formulation. Numerical examples of this technique and some computational results are also presented. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Cooper L."]

Title: TWO-WAY FINITE AUTOMATA ON CONTROL SETS.
Abstract: The control of two-way finite automata (2FA) is discussed and the classes of languages accepted by them are characterized. First, the relationships between 2FA on control sets and two-way pushdown automata (PDA) are examined. It is shown that when the control sets are regular, the class of languages accepted by 2FA on those sets is equal to the class of regular sets, and that when the control sets are context-free, the class of languages accepted by 2FA on those sets of equal to the class of languages accepted by two-way PDA. Next, the relationships between 2FA on control sets and two-way sequential transduction are examined and it is shown that there they are closely related. Finally, giving certain characterization of languages accepted by 2FA on control sets, some new results are obtained and several earlier results on two-way PDA are reconfirmed.
Name: ["Takanami Itsuo"]

Title: On the near-optimality of the shortest-latency-time-first drum scheduling discipline
Abstract: For computer systems in which it is practical to determine the instantaneous drum position, a popular discipline for determining the sequence in which the records are to be accessed is the so-called shortest-latency-time-first, SLTF, discipline. When a collection of varying-length records is to be accessed from specified drum positions, it is known that the SLTF discipline does not necessarily minimize the drum latency time. However, we show that the total time to access the entire collection for any SLTF schedule is never as much as a drum revolution longer than a minimum latency schedule. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Stone H.S.", "Fuller S.H."]

Title: ADAPTIVE ESTIMATOR WITH LEARNING FOR A PLANT CONTAINING SEMI-MARKOV SWITCHING PARAMETERS.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: An adaptive state estimator with learning has been developed to help solve the problem of state estimation of an unreliable linear system operating in Gaussian noise. By definition, the unreliable plant has certain parameters that can vary randomly within a finite set of possible values at times which are unknown to an observer. In modeling the stochastic system, it will be assumed that the variations in the plant configuration can be described by a semi-Markov process. By incorporating the semi-Markov process into a Bayesian estimation scheme an adaptive state estimator was developed which could handle the switching plant or switching environment problem without computer storage increasing as time progresses.
Name: ["Moose Richard L.", "Wang Paul P."]

Title: EMPIRICAL SPECTRAL ANALYSIS OF GAUSSIAN HOMOGENEOUS RANDOM FIELDS.
Abstract: Estimates of the spectral densities of Gaussian homogeneous random fields specified on two-dimensional and p-dimensional integer-valued lattices are investigated. The parameters are found for the weighting functions of the spectral density estimates so as to minimize the mean-square error of estimation (or its upper bound) under given a priori assumptions regarding the degree of smoothness of the estimated spectral density.
Name: ["Alekseev V.G."]

Title: WAVEFORM RECONSTRUCTION FROM ELEMENTS SPECIFIED AT A FINITE NUMBER OF POINTS.
Abstract: The problem of reconstructing the waveform of a signal having a finite spectrum from specified values of the signal and its derivatives at a finite number of points is solved for the case of a priori constraints on the spectrum.
Name: ["Kas'yanyuk S.A."]

Title: INVESTIGATION OF A PROGRAM FOR THE SYNTHESIS OF A MULTILEVEL CLASSIFICATION.
Abstract: Experiments are described in which the behavior of a multilevel classification program is investigated as a function of the complexity of the problems to be solved and of the training and examination conditions. Several experiments are devoted to the comparison of singlelevel and multilevel training. The preference of multilevel training is inferred from those experiments. Several examples of the multitudinous classifications synthesized by the program are given.
Name: ["Rashkinis A.V."]

Title: AUTOMATA THAT DISTINGUISH RANDOM MEDIA.
Abstract: The interrelationship of the asymptotic optimality of a sequence of automata and aggregates of automata is investigated. It is proved that asymptotically optimal sequences of automata can generate both asymptotically optimal and poorly behaved sequences of aggregates on one and the same set of media for an aggregate. The proof is based on the fact that a statistic distinguishing random media corresponds to a sequence of automata that asymptotically distinguishes those media.
Name: ["Koganov A.V."]

Title: HETEROCHROMATIC ADDITIVITY, FOVEAL SPECTRAL SENSITIVITY, AND A NEW COLOR MODEL.
Abstract: Experiments show that heterochromatic additivity failures for foveally viewed trichromatic lights can be predicted using a vector model derived from bichromatic additivity data; that near-threshold bichromatic additivity failures are similar to threshold-level failures; and that foveal spectral sensitivities obtained by direct brightness matching and threshold methods are greater for the long- and short-wavelength ends of the spectrum than those obtained by clicker photometry. A new opponent-colors model appropriate for threshold-level color vision is expressed as a transformation of the CIE standard observer.
Name: ["Guth Sherman L.", "Lodge Howard R."]

Title: OUTPUT-PREDICTION EQUATION WITH MINIMUM-TIME CONTROL OF LINEAR MULTIVARIABLE SYSTEMS.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: An equation is developed for the prediction of the output of a linear time-invariant multivariable system that is based on process past inputs and outputs. To demonstrate that the output-prediction equation is a realistic model of process dynamics, a derivation is included to establish the inputs necessary to generate a minimum-time deadbeat response. A computer simulation study illustrates the applications to a 4th-order process.
Name: ["Sandoz D.J.", "Walker P.A.W."]

Title: DESIGN TECHNIQUE FOR NONLINEAR EQUALISERS.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: A theoretical analysis, using the properties of linear vector spaces, is applied to the design of a nonlinear equalizer. The design minimizes the probability of error in the detection of a serial digital signal, subject to the accurate equalization of the time-invariant channel, when the signal is received in the presence of additive white Gaussian noise with a high snr. The equalizer contains a conventional combination of linear feed-forward and nonlinear feedback transversal filters. Certain commonly used assumptions are made concerning the transmitted signal and the channel, but it is not assumed that the channel can necessarily be equalized by a linear feedforward transversal filter of limited length. A simple example shows the advantage in tolerance to additive Gaussian noise, which is achieved by the nonlinear equalizer over the corresponding linear equalizer, in a particular case where accurate equalization of the channel is achieved by the linear equalizer.
Name: ["Clark A.P."]

Title: Determination of the Dynamic Characteristics of a System with Code-Impulse Regulator. | WYZNACZANIE CHARAKTERYSTYK DYNAMICZNYCH UKLADU Z REGULATOREM KODOWO-IMPULSOWYM.
Abstract: Method of analysis of a discrete automatic control system with a code-impulse regulator is discussed. The algorithm of the code-impulse regulator operation is determined and a method of determining the dynamic characteristics of the control system is presented. Theoretical consideration is supplemented by an example illustrating the procedure in determining the response of the system to step forcing.
Name: ["Smirnow Andrzej"]

Title: A Linear Bit Synchronizer with Learning
Abstract: An adaptive sequential bit synchronizer for a random square-wave data process is proposed in this paper. The probability distributions of the signal parameters and noise process are assumed unknown. The synchronization algorithms, implemented on a small computer, are capable of accurately estimating pulse transition time, pulse amplitude, and pulsewidth simultaneously by invoking the Gauss-Markov theorem. Numerous simulations indicate that the performance of the synchronizer is satisfactory from the points of view of the amount of data required and the speed of convergence.
