Title: EFFECTIVE HEURISTIC ALGORITHM FOR THE TRAVELING-SALESMAN PROBLEM.
Abstract: Procedure for generating optimum and near-optimum solutions for the symmetric traveling-salesman problem is discussed. The procedure is believed to have wide applicability in combinatorial optimization problems.
Name: ["Lin S.", "Kernighan B.W."]

Title: Optimal Demodulation of PAM Signals
Abstract: Kalman filtering theory is applied to yield an optimal causal demodulator for pulse-amplitude-modulated (PAM) signals in the presence of white Gaussian noise. The discrete-time data (or sampled continuous-time data) are assumed to be either a stationary or non-stationary Gaussian stochastic process, in general nonwhite. Optimal demodulation with delay is also achieved by application of Kalman filtering theory. The resulting demodulators (fixed-lag smoothers) are readily constructed and their performance represents in many cases a significant improvement over that for the optimal demodulator without delay. The fixed-lag smoothing results are in contrast to those for amplitude-modulated signals (AM) where only approximate fixed-lag smoothing is possible, and this with considerable design effort. The performance of the optimal PAM demodulator is shown to be equivalent to that of an optimal discrete filter for the discrete data. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Moore J.B.", "Hetdakul P."]

Title: Rational pattern classification when very little is known
Abstract: The problem of pattern classification when very little is known about the pattern source is structured through a set of axioms describing desirable properties for a classifier that involve no probabilistic assumptions or hypotheses. The derived classifier is then studied under the hypothesis that the pattern source is probabilistic and its long-run performance found to strongly converge to that of the Bayes classifier under reasonable restrictions. The sparse results of a pilot study on the comparative small sample performance of the derived classifier are found to be encouraging but not definitive. This work is an outgrowth of previous work on extrapolation when little is know. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Fine T.L."]

Title: Forecasting the Development Trends of Electric Power Consumption, Taking into Account Probable Errors of Initial Data. | [PROGNIZIROVANIE TENDENTSII RAZVITIYA ELEKTROPOTREBLENIYA S UCHETOM VLIYANIYA VEROYATNOI POGRESHNOSTI ISKHODNOI INFORMATSII.]
Abstract: In forecasting any process, the initial data are known only to a certain degree of accuracy and reliability. It is proposed to use the Monte Carlo method to take into account the influence of probable erroneousness of the initial data on forecasting results. A set of programs has been worked out on the ‚Ä≥Ural-14‚Ä≥ digital computer for extrapolating, by the least square method, time series of indices of power consumption, singling out the trend and the random component. Particular experimental and industrial calculations have been made making it possible to draw a conclusion regarding the importance of the influence of probable error-rate of the initial data on the extrapolation result.
Name: ["Derzskii V.G.", "Polyakov V.B."]

Title: An approach to the control of processes with pure time delay
Abstract: The advent of on-line digital computers and relatively large-storage supervisory computers allows the possibility of improved control of processes containing pure time delay (distance/velocity lag). Such processes frequently occur in industrial plants and their control is also complicated by the fact that both the magnitude of pure time delay and the values of the parameters of the minimum-phase elements in the process may vary with time. Furthermore extraneous disturbances of time varying and unknown power spectra will cause further control difficulties. This paper contains an outline of a new general approach to this problem in which a digital computer is used as the main control element to implement a scheme designed to optimize the performance of such systems. ¬© 1973, The Institution of Electronic and Radio Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Atkinson P.", "Fellgett P.B.", "Swann T.G."]
Affiliations: [' University of Reading', 'University of Reading', 'Marconi-Elliot Computer Systems Limited']

Title: NONLINEAR OPTIMAL CLASSIFICATION OF OBSERVATIONS IN THE RECOGNITION OF RANDOM PROCESSES.
Abstract: An examination is made of the problem of recognizing a random process THETA //t on the basis of observation of a realization of a random process xi //t connected with the useful signal. The proposed observation classification method is optimal in the sense of minimum mean risk. Observation classification methods are investigated for various special loss functions and various forms of the useful signal.
Name: ["Shpilevskiy E.K."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF OPTIMAL CONTROLS FOR LINEAR NON-STATIONARY OBJECTS.
Abstract: Linear systems with variable parameters are considered. The problem is discussed of analytical synthesis of a control law which provides a given or best (in the sense of some criterion) quality of the closed-loop system. A compensation method is proposed which significantly simplifies the solution of the problem for a class of non-stationary systems. For an integral quadratic quality criterion, the synthesis is reduced to solving a matrix Riccati equation with constant coefficients. An example illustrates the possibilities of the method.
Name: ["Vanyurikhin G.I."]

Title: Speech Analysis by Kalman Filtering. | ANALYSE DE LA PAROLE PAR FILTRAGE OPTIMAL DE KALMAN.
Abstract: A method is presented for the evaluation of a reduced number of parameters characterizing a vocal signal by means of identification of the transfer function of a phonation system. The identification of a stable transfer function of the vocal track is performed with minimum variance criterion by using optimal Kalman filtering. the corresponding recurrent algorithm offers a stable model and permits simultaneous deduction of the source wave form and pitch periods.
Name: ["Gueguen C.J.", "Carayannis G."]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR SOLVING MULTICRITERION LINEAR PROGRAMMING PROBLEMS WITH EXAMPLES.
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to develop a useful technique for solving linear programs involving more than one objective function. Motivation for solving multicriterion linear programs is given along with the inherent difficulty associated with obtaining a satisfactory solution set. By applying a linear programming approach for the solution of two person - zero sum games with mixed strategies, it is shown that a linear optimization problem with multiple objective functions can be formulated in this fashion in order to obtain a solution set satisfying all the requirements for an efficient solution of the problem. The solution method is then refined to take into account disparities between the magnitude of the values generated by each of the objective functions and solution preferences as determined by a decision-maker. A summary of the technique is then given along with several examples in order to demonstrate its applicability.
Name: ["Belenson Sheldon M.", "Kapur Kailash C."]

Title: EXAMINATION OF THE USE OF ADPATIVE FILTERING IN FORECASTING.
Abstract: Adaptive filtering is a technique for preparing short- to medium-term forecasts based on weighting of historical observations, in a similar way to moving average and exponential smoothing. However, adaptive filtering, as it has been developed in electrical engineering, attempts to distinguish a signal pattern from random noise, rather than simply smoothing th noise of past data. This paper reviews the technique of adaptive filtering and investigates its applications and limitations for the forecasting practitioner. This is done by looking at the performance of adaptive filtering in forecasting a number of time series and by comparing it with other forecasting techniques.
Name: ["Wheelwright Steven C.", "Makridakis Spyros"]

Title: A Decision‚ÄîDirected Adaptive Tracker
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: In the design of a tracking filter for air traffic control (ATC) applications, a maneuvering aircraft can be modelled by a linear system with random noise accelerations. A Kalman filter tracker, designed on the basis of a variance chosen according to the distribution of the potential maneuver accelerations, will maintain track during maneuvers and provide some improvement in position accuracy. However, during those portions of the flight path where the aircraft is not maneuvering, the tracking accuracy will not be as good as if no acceleration noise had been allowed in the tracking filter. In this paper, statistical decision theory is used to derive an optimal test for detecting the aircraft maneuver; a more practical suboptimal test is then deduced from the optimal test. As long as no maneuver is declared, a simpler filter, based on a constant-velocity model, is used to track the aircraft. When a maneuver is detected, the tracker is reinitialized using stored data, up-dated to the present time, and then normal tracking is resumed as new data arrives. In essence, the tracker performs on the basis of a piecewise linear model in which the breakpoints are defined on-line using the maneuver detector. Simulation results show that there is a significant improvement in tracking capability using the decision-directed adaptive tracker. Name: ["McAulay R.J.", "Denlinger E."]

Title: On joint detection, estimation and system identification: discrete data case
Abstract: The recent results of Lainiotis (1971 a, b, 1971) on single-shot, as well as multishot, joint detection, estimation and system identification for continuous data and dynamics are extended to multishot, discrete data and discrete dynamical systems. The results are given for the signals generated by the linear dynamical systems with unknown parameter vectors and driven by white gaussian sequences, where the observation contains additive white gaussian noise. Specifically, it is shown that the above problem constitutes a class of non-linear mean-square estimation problems. By utilizing the adaptive approach, closed-form integral expressions are obtained for simultaneously optimal detection, estimation and system identification. In addition, several approximate algorithms that utilize linear Kalman estimators are presented to limit the storage requirement to finite size and reduce computational requirements. The results presented in this paper are applicable to both independent and Markov signalling sources. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Lainiotis D.G.", "Park S.K."]

Title: Rejection of Uncertain Characters. | ZUR ZURUECKWEISUNG ZWEIFEHLHAFTER ZEICHEN.
Source: NTZ Nachr Z NTZ Commun J
Abstract: The rejection problem in the context of K-class-classification is considered. The considerations are based on a two-stage concept with the first stage consisting of the actual K-class classifier generating only a preliminary decision, followed in the second stage by a special 2-class classifier supervising the decision process and accepting or rejecting the preliminary decision by means of check-data extracted from the decision process. Several reject criteria of practical importance are discussed and compared experimentally. The problem of optimizing the reject threshold is considered from the viewpoint of risk minimization.
Name: ["Schuermann Juergen"]

Title: Approximation of discrete linear systems
Abstract: Given a multi‚Äìinput, multi‚Äìoutput linear time‚Äìinvariant discrete‚Äìtime system or its weighting matrices, equations are derived to characterize a system of lower dimension which optimally approximates the given system with respect to the sum of squared output errors of the impulse response. These equations are shown to imply that in principle a modified B. L. Ho algorithm can be used to find the approximation. The connection with projection methods of approximation is demonstrated, Some comments on computational difficulties are included. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Aplevich J.D."]

Title: Speech Data Rate Reduction Part II: Applicability of Sensitivity and Error Analysis
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: This paper deals with the application of modern estimation techniques to the problem of speech data rate reduction. It is desirable to adaptively identify and quantitize the parameters of the speech model. These paramaters cannot be identified and quantized exactly; the performance of the predictor is thereby degraded and this could prevent data reduction. In many cases it is desirable to emply a suboptimal predictor in order to simplify the algorithms, and predictor performance is again degraded. This paper develops sensitivity and error analysis as a potential method for determining quantitatively how speech data reduction system performance is degraded by imprecise parameter knowledge or suboptimal filtering. An intended use of the sensitivity and error analysis algorithms is to determine parameter identification and model structure requirements of configuration concepts for adaptive speech digitizers. First, sensitivity and error analysis algorithms are presented that form the basis for the remainder of the work. The algorithms are then used to determine how imprecise knowledge of vocal tract parameters degrades predictor performance in speech. Transversal filters have previously been proposed for this application. The sensitivity analysis algorithms are then used to determine when and by how much the transverse filter is suboptimal to the Kalman filter. In particular, the question of how effectively a higher order of all-pole model approximates a system with zeros is answered, as this question is of considerable importance in speech. Finally, the physical significance of the innovations process in speech data rate reduction is studied. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Gunn J.E.", "Sage A.P."]

Title: System identification using almost periodic functions: Application to non-linearities with memory
Abstract: A method for measuring by crosscorrelation the impulse responses of the linear portions of a system containing a zero-memory non-linearity is shown to be applicable to certain typos of non-linear characteristic with memory. Several situations are analysed and some experimental results presented. A computer programme is given for calculating the parameters of the input signal from a given tabulated non-linear characteristic. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Simpson R.J.", "Power H.M."]

Title: An Algorithm for Optimal Prefix Parsing of a Noiseless and Memoryless Channel
Abstract: We discuss the prefix encoding of a Q-ary source (Q=2) into an L-symbol channel alphabet with L = Q. We present an optimal encoding scheme that minimizes the expected cost per symbol in the case of equally probable source symbols and arbitrary channel symbol costs. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Lempel A.", "Even S.", "Cohn M."]
Affiliations: ['Technion-Israel Institute of Technology', 'Weizmann Institute of Science', 'Sperry Rand Research Center']

Title: On identification of non-stationary parameters by fixed point smoothing-the case of coloured noise
Abstract: The paper presents a new approach to the problem of identification of non-stationary model parameters. It is shown that a recursive algorithm for the smoothed parameter estimates can be obtained through an application of the Kalman filtering algorithm to an augmented system. As an illustration of the versatility of this approach, estimates of non stationary model parameters of a system with non-white process noise are also derived in the paper. Finally, formal solutions of the problem of identification of non-stationary parameters of a continuous time system are presented. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Sinha A.K.", "Mahalanabis A.K."]

Title: Tree-Manipulating Systems and Church-Rosser Theorems
Abstract: Subtree replacement systems form a broad class of tree-manipulating systems. Systems with the ‚ÄúChurch-Rosser property‚Äù are appropriate for evaluation or translation processes: the end result of a complete sequence of applications of the rules does not depend on the order in which the rules were applied. Theoretical and practical advantages of such flexibility are sketched. Values or meanings for trees can be defined by simple mathematical systems and then computed by the cheapest available algorithm, however intricate that algorithm may be. We derive sufficient conditions for the Church-Rosser property and discuss their applications to recursive definitions, to the lambda calculus, and to parallel programming. Only the first application is treated in detail. We extend McCarthy's recursive calculus by allowing a choice between call-by-value and call-by-name. We show that recursively defined functions are single-valued despite the nondeterminism of the evaluation algorithm. We also show that these functions solve their defining equations in a ‚Äúcanonical‚Äù manner. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Rosen B.K."]

Title: ANALOG AUTOMATIC ADVISER FOR OPTIMAL CONTROL OF CELLULOSE WASHING.
Abstract: A statistical model of the cellulose washing process is presented, and also a control model. An analog automatic adviser has been developed for realizing the control model, on the principle of passive summation of currents and digital measurements of voltages. An automatic hybrid control system is described for the cellulose washing process; it uses an analog automatic adviser as its open loop.
Name: ["Grubov V.I.", "Golub O.P.", "Dem'yanenko V.I.", "Tseshkovs'kiy E.V."]

Title: On the Choice of Poles and Zeros in the Transfer Matrix of Decoupled Multivariable Control Systems - 1. | [FESTLEGEN DER POLE UND NULLSTELLEN BEI DER SYNTHESE LINEARER ENTKOPPELTER MEHRGROESSENREGELKREISE - 1.]
Abstract: A new algorithm for the synthesis of a decoupled linear time-invariant multivariable system is presented. This algorithm has two advantages over the present procedures: it uses mainly frequency-domain techniques which can be directly employed in synthesizing the diagonal transfer matrix; and the given algorithm is more simple than earlier ones and can be carried out by using pencil and paper methods and some few standard computer programs even when the system is of higher order. A theorem is proved which provides a meaningful interpretation of the choice of additional zeros in the diagonal transfer matrix in connection with the problem of unobservable modes in the closed loop system and the problem of possible reduction of control effort. The outlined synthesis procedure applies not only to decoupling by means of static feedback but by dynamic compensation as well.
Name: ["Cremer M."]

Title: PHASE PROCESSING OF RANDOM SIGNALS.
Abstract: A method of transforming optical signals that are continuous random processes (differing from noise in the shape of their power spectra) by means of a phase filter is described. It is shown that the signal at the output of the phase filter is invariant with respect to the input amplitude spectrum, and, in addition, is automatically normalized.
Name: ["Emdin S.Ya.", "Kundin A.I.", "Teterin V.V."]

Title: Model of some stages in schematic picture recognition (Russian)
Abstract: A model of recognition of schematic pictures based on analysis of data on the human and higher animal visual system is described. Primary stages of model functioning are local feature extraction, synthesis of fragment of description, and advancement and check up of hypothesis.
Name: ["Krol V.M.", "Levashov O.V.", "Reclitis V.K.", "Tanengolts L.I."]

Title: A Numerical Algorithm for Identifying Spread Functions of Shift-Invariant Imaging Systems
Abstract: Numerical optimization techniques are applied to the identification of linear, shift-invariant imaging systems in the presence of noise. The approach used is to model the available or measured image of a real known object as the planar convolution of object and system-spread function and additive noise. The spread function is derived by minimization of a spatial error criterion (least squares) and characterized using a matric formalism. The numerical realization of the algorithm is discussed in detail; the most substantial problem encountered being the calculation of a vectorgeneralized inverse. This problem is avoided in the special case where the object scene is taken to be decomposable. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Ekstrom M.P."]

Title: Stability considerations on the expanding subinterval performance adaptive SOC algorithm
Abstract: Self-organizing control system (SOC) [1] algorithms are designed to control a system with completely or partially unknown dynamics, operating in a stochastic environment, so as to obtain an effective (optimal or otherwise acceptable) performance. Such an effective performance is obtained by on-line reduction of the uncertainties involved in the control of the system. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Saridis G.N.", "Fensel P.A."]

Title: Dynamic Scheduling of Large Digital Computer Systems Using Adaptive Control and Clustering Techniques
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: This research is directed toward the development of a scheduling algorithm for large digital computer systems. To meet this goal methods of adaptive control and pattern recognition are applied. As jobs are received by the computer, a pattern recognition scheme is applied to the job in an attempt to classify its characteristics, such as a CPU-bound job, an I/O job, a large memory job, etc. Simultaneously, another subsystem, using a linear programming model, evaluates the overall system performance, and from this information an optimized (or desired) job stream is determined. When the processor requests a new job, it is chosen from the various classifications in an attempt to meet the optimal (or desired) job stream. After the jobs are completely processed, their characteristics are compared to the projected classification produced by the pattern discriminant function. The results are then returned to the discriminant function to update the decision mechanism, a minimum-distance discriminant function. From a systems point of view, this results in an adaptive or self-organizing control system. The overall effect is a dynamic scheduling algorithm. Simulation studies indicated that the scheduler was able to adapt to changing work loads, and it improved the turnaround times significantly. These simulation studies were based on a multiprocessor-uniprogram environment. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.

Title: A Model-Driven Question-Answering System for Mixed-Initiative Computer-Assisted Construction
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: This paper describes a pragmatic question-answering system which was developed for experimental use in a computer-assisted instruction environment. The two primary design goals of this system are 1) the representation of dynamic processes along with their causal inter-relationships, and 2) the generation of responses in units of discourse greater than simple sentences. A method of modeling processes with augmented finite-state automata is discussed and is shown to permit efficient inferencing as well as provide a satisfactory deep structure for paragraph generation. Coupled with the dynamic process model is a semantic/conceptual network which contains static or factual information. Examples of the inferencing techniques using both the automaton model and the semantic network are given. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Brown J.S.", "Burton R.R.", "Zdybel F."]

Title: REALIZATION OF n-STATE HOMOGENEOUS MACHINES USING n - 1 NEURONS.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A procedure for realizing a strongly connected finite-state machine (FSM) by neural networks is described. It contains two steps. The first step is to convert any (nonhomogeneous) machine into a homogeneous machine. It is shown that such a conversion can always be achieved. The second step is to realize an n-state homogeneous machine using n - 1 neurons. The procedure is completely general and can be applied to any single- or multiple-input FSM. Examples are given to illustrate the procedure. If the specification is a set of regular events instead of an FSM, one can always obtain an FSM realizing it. Hence the method presented here can be applied to the realizing of regular events by neural networks which may be helpful for the representation and analysis of certain aspects of brain functions.

Title: Stochastic algorithms in system identification
Abstract: In order to identify a linear system with a discrete non-parametric model a class of algorithms which is closely related to the Kalman filter is considered. With an input signal of appropriate statistics these algorithms are easy to calculate and are characterized by a speed of convergence which is comparable to that of a Kalman filter given an imperfect, a priori knowledge of the error covariance matrix. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.

Title: PROBABILISTIC GMDH ALGORITHM WITH SEQUENTIAL DISCRIMINATION OF INPUT FEATURES.
Abstract: A new algorithm for classification (pattern recognition) of Bayesian type has been constructed, in which the decision functions gradually become more complicated. This algorithm is useful in the case of an input feature space of large dimension, and a fairly small number of interpolation points. The input features are assumed to be statistically dependent. It is shown that in some cases a recognition algorithm that has been trained by a finite sample will yield a higher accuracy (compared to all other GMDH algorithms) if only part of the input features are used. The algorithm is constructed on the basis of statistical decision theory, which (as is well known) in the case of an infinitely long training sample provides a method of pattern recognition of optimum accuracy. The transition from statistically dependent input features to independent features is carried out by orthogonalization of those features. As an example, this algorithm is used for optimal diagnosis of poisoning by four classes of pesticides.

Title: On Symmetric Functions with Redundant Variables-Weighted Functions
Abstract: Any switching function may be transformed into a completely symmetric switching function with some of its variables repetitive. In this paper we shall discuss certain properties, easily detectable in decomposition charts, that may be applied to reduce the number of repeated variables when such a transformation is performed. An algorithm utilizing lookup tables based on these properties has been devised enabling us with relative ease to transform an arbitrary switching function of four variables into a completely symmetric switching function with the least number of variables. The algorithm may be generalized to n-variable switching functions provided that the corresponding lookup tables are made available. To eliminate the tediousness associated with repeating the variables, we introduce a novel class of functions-weighted functions-that also emphasize the similarity between completely symmetric functions and multithreshold threshold functions. Title: STABILIZATION OF DYNAMIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A stabilizing control is constructed for a linear automatic control system with nonideal measuring units and actuators. It is assumed that stabilizing control is known in the case of ideal measuring units and actuators. The method of constructing the control is based on Lyapunov functions, and illustrated by an example of rotational motion of a rigid body.
Name: ["Smirnov E.Ya."]

Title: OPEN-LOOP TRAJECTORY SHAPING FOR SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION WITH CONSTRAINTS.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The choice of an open-loop input signal to be used in driving a stochastic system to a desired nominal terminal state can be optimized to improve estimation performance as well as to minimize a nominal cost function. An example is presented for a first-order system with an unknown time constant being estimated with an augmented Kalman filter.
Name: ["Schmidt George T."]

Title: DESCRIPTION OPTIMIZATION BY ORTHOGONALIZATION OF THE DATA OF A PASSIVE EXPERIMENT.
Abstract: A procedure is proposed for optimizing a description, based on orthogonalization of a system of functions. It minimizes the systematic and random errors and shortens the sorting process.
Name: ["Boloshin S.B.", "Osipov A.V.", "Semenov G.A."]

Title: OPERATING SYSTEM FOR DYNAMIC PARALLEL ALLOCATION OF COMPUTATIONS IN A CONTROL COMPUTER SYSTEM.
Abstract: The operating system of a control computer is analyzed from the standpoint of optimum parallel allocation of computational tasks. The multichannel system developed produces real-time results.
Name: ["Barskiy A.B.", "Savvin I.M."]

Title: FILTRATION OF RANDOM SEQUENCES WITH GAPS USING OPTIMAL DISCRETE FILTERS WITH CONSTANT MEMORY.
Abstract: An examination is made of optimal minimum means square error filtration of random sequences with independent omissions of individual observations in the case of a polynomial model of the useful signal on a finite interval. Operating algorithms, block diagrams, and methods of analyzing the quality of optimal filters with constant memory are proposed.
Name: ["Korshunov Yu.M.", "Stepanenko V.N."]

Title: Reliable Boundary Value Supervision with a Process Computer. | [SICHERE GRENZWERTUEBERWACHUNG MIT PROZESSRECHNER.]
Abstract: The supervision of process values with regard to critical limits is a common task in process-computer-applications. If measurement-errors are present, then wrong decisions can not always be avoided. It may happen, that limit crossings are not detected immediately, or alternatively, that crossings are reported, though none are present. In this paper a method for process supervision is proposed which, in a certain sense, is optimal with regard to the risk of wrong decisions. The method is based on mathematical statistics. it is shown, that the supervision in many cases can be accomplished by examination of a linear combination of a sequence of measured values. In spite of the statistical refinements, the on-line computations are still not extensive, compared to other, more usual supervision procedures.
Name: ["Kohlas J."]

Title: ABSOLUTELY EXPEDIENT LEARNING ALGORITHMS FOR STOCHASTIC AUTOMATA.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A general but simple condition of symmetry of the nonlinear functions figuring in the reinforcement scheme is shown to be necessary and sufficient for absolute expediency (monotonic decrease of the expectation of the average penalty in all stationary random media). Various schemes are simulated and the results are compared. An adaptive updating of the parameters in the scheme to obtain faster convergence is proposed.
Name: ["Lakshmivarahan S.", "Thathachar M.A.L."]

Title: A Unified Method for the Reconstruction of Sampled Data
Abstract: Many digital systems have need for continuous-type output for oscilloscope display, process control, or hybrid computation. This paper presents a generalization and unification of the theory of extrapolation and reconstruction of sampled data. This generalization allows implementation of a recursive algorithm or digital filter in conjunction with the continuous data reconstruction. The general procedure is demonstrated for the implementation of an nth-order recursion relation using polynomial or exponential data reconstruction requiring only a single resetting integrator for the general nth-order reconstructor. Name: ["Durling A.E.", "Bullock T.E."]

Title: HOMECOMINGS OF MARKOV PROCESSES.
Abstract: If x//0 is a particular state for a continuous-time Markov process X, the random time set, when X is in the state x//0, is often of both practical and theoretical interest. Ignoring trivial or pathological cases, there are four different types of structure which this random set can display. To some extent, it is possible to treat all four cases in a unified way, but they raise different questions and require different modes of description. The distributions of various random quantities associated with the random time set can be related to one another by simple and useful formulas.
Name: ["Kingman J.F.C."]

Title: Analysis of an Information System Model with Transfer Penalties
Abstract: A general model of systems consisting of ‚Äúcontrol units‚Äù and ‚Äúpassive units‚Äù is established. These units could be instructions and data in computer programs, for example, or information processing modules and files in data management systems; other applications are also suggested. The model contains both structural and behavioral information. The sets of units of the model are partitioned, and the resulting subsets correspond to different groups of elements of real systems. Certain classes of communications between the subsets result in ‚Äúboundary crossings,‚Äù with which penalties are associated. An analysis of the model is performed, in order to determine the expected frequency of boundary crossing. Synthesis of the subsets in order to reduce the number of boundary crossings is discussed, under the presumption that the other parameters of the model remain fixed. Name: ["Lowe T.C."]
Keywords: ["boundary crossing", "computer network", "data management", "information retrieval", "information system model"]

Title: DESIGN OF AN INFORMATION RETRIEVAL SYSTEM FOR PHOTOGRAPHIC CHEMISTRY, TECHNOLOGY, PROCESSES, AND MATERIALS.
Abstract: A computer and microfilm-based indexing and retrieval system for the photographic patent literature is described. The system is designed to capture word concepts consistently by use of a highly structured thesaurus, in which the indexing terms are well defined and in which relationships between terms are displayed in hierarchial form. The system can be searched by computer and also by using microfilm indexes produced by COM equipment on 16-mm film. Copies of the full text of the indexed patents have been microfilmed and are available in roll or aperture-card formats. This system forms the basis for a cooperative indexing effort in which all members of the photograpic industry are being invited to participate.
Name: ["Graham Robert W.", "Roberts Harry E."]

Title: MINIMAX PURSUIT PROBLEM WITH LAG IN INFORMATION.
Abstract: An examination is made of the game problem of putting a system to be controlled on a given set when there is a lag in the information of the first player. It is assumed that the right-hand member of the differential equation describing the system motion depends on the controlling influences in a nonlinear manner. A control of the first player is constructed that guarantees that the system will get onto the given set by some initial instant. The conditions for existence of this control are formulated.
Name: ["Shishmakov V.S."]

Title: ESTIMATION OF THE THROUGHPUT OF A MULTIPROCESSOR COMPUTER WITH COMMONLY ACCESSIBLE MEMORY.
Abstract: A method of distributing the assignments (dispatching) in a multiprocessor computer, consisting of homogeneous processors operating with a commonly accessible memory, is examined. For this method, estimates are obtained for the throughput of the computer as a function of the dispatching time, the number of processors, and the time for completion of a single assignment. The estimates are substantiated by simulation results.
Name: ["Kazantsev P.N.", "Kornev M.D."]

Title: System Identification Using Prony's Method. | SYSTEMIDENTIFIKATION MIT DEM PRONY-VERFAHREN.
Abstract: A method for the identification of single-input single-output systems represented by rational algebraic transfer functions (degree of the numerator polynomial less than that of the denominator) out of time domain is described. For that purpose a method is used for the approximation of time-discrete weighting functions by series of exponential functions with complex arguments (Prony). It is shown that systems containing multiple poles can be treated with the Prony method too. The degree of the denominator polynomial of the transfer function can be determined automatically while solving the set of linear equations necessary for the computation of the poles. If the weighting function is not known a deconvolution with the Prony-method is possible provided simple excitations like step or ramp functions are used. The algorithm has been implemented in ALGOL 60. Three examples show the effects of statistical errors of the samples of the weighting function on the computation of the poles and the systems degree, the efficacy of the method to a non-ideal system and the deconvolution in the case of step excitation.
Name: ["Lacroix Arild"]

Title: ON FEATURE EXTRACTION FROM IMPERFECTLY LABELED PATTERNS.
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The application of an estimation technique for the extraction of features from imperfectly labeled patterns is examined. Furthermore, an upperbound on the estimation error of perfectly labeled samples is obtained in terms of the estimation error of imperfectly identified patterns.
Name: ["Babu C.Chitti"]

Title: Feature Evalution with Measures of Probabilistic Dependence
Abstract: In this paper, measures of probabilistic dependence are derived from distance measures and are applied to feature evaluation in pattern recognition. The main properties of the measures are derived and are discussed in their application to feature-class dependency. Relations between the measures and error probability are derived. Experiments using feature subsets extracted from Munson's handprinted data are performed to compare the feature-evaluating capabilities of the measures both relative to each other and relative to error probability. Name: ["Vilmansen T.R."]

Title: MINIMIZATION OF RING-SUM EXPANSIONS OF BOOLEAN FUNCTIONS.
Abstract: Paper introduces the set of 3**n canonical expansions of an n-variable Boolean function; an algorithm is presented that makes it possible to compute the minimal canonical expansions. A new equivalence relation on the set of n-variable Boolean functions, the D-equivalence, is defined; the four-variable Boolean functions are classified according to this relation. This provides a complete solution of the general minimization problem for n equals 4, and an improved approach for n greater than, or equal to, 5.
Name: ["Bioul G.", "Davio M.", "Deschamps J.P."]

Title: Finite-Time Performance of Some Two-Armed Bandit Controllers
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A class of asymptotically √ë‚Äù-optimal two-armed bandit controllers is given, and two criteria for comparing the long-term finite-time performance of controllers in this class are proposed. The performances of three particular controllers are compared using the criteria, and the analysis is confirmed by computer iteration if the appropriate probability recurrence relations. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Witten I.H."]

Title: Making the fast Fourier transform really fast
Abstract: The combination of a new mathematical tool (the fast Fourier transform) and specially designed computer hardware speeds up processing by 10,000 to 1 over standard methods. Now, spectra of communications signals can be calculated economically in real time. | The fast Fourier transform processor implements the principle of the Fourier transform by utilizing a unique algorithm (a step-by-step rule to get a solution to a problem) for calculating the transform. The algorithm is what makes the computation ‚Ä≥fast.‚Ä≥ In the transformation of a time representation of a signal to its frequency representation (or vice versa), the exact Fourier transformation of a time function is expressed mathematically as an ‚Ä≥integral‚Ä≥ that runs continuously from all past time to all future time. Digital computers, however, cannot evaluate such an integral directly; instead, they must approximate it by summing up a finite series of discrete terms. Because the sequential processor has the drawback that, as higher speeds are sought, the arithmetic unit and memory become expensive, consideration has been given to the ‚Ä≥cascade‚Ä≥ processor. In ‚Ä≥cascading,‚Ä≥ data are passed through the fast Fourier processor in a continuous flow such that work is distributed among the stages. Cascading greatly reduces the speed at which the arithmetic operations must be performed, and eliminates the expensive input and output memory that would be needed to process a continuous flow of data using sequential processing. It has been found that by making the central arithmetic units (CAUs) operate somewhat faster than the minimum rate for cascade processing - but still considerably slower than the rate for sequential processing - one CAU could be shared by several stages. Switching networks feed data for each stage to the CAUs from temporary-storage memories. The effect of sharing the complex arithmetic units is to materially reduce the cost of the processor.
Name: ["Fuss P.S.", "Stuart Jr J.C."]

Title: Outline of a New Approach to the Analysis of Complex Systems and Decision Processes
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The approach described in this paper represents a substantive departure from the conventional quantitative techniques of system analysis. It has three main distinguishing features: 1) use of so-called ‚Äúlinguistic‚Äù variables in place of or in addition to numerical variables; 2) characterization of simple relations between variables by fuzzy conditional statements; and 3) characterization of complex relations by fuzzy algorithms. A linguistic variable is defined as a variable whose values are sentences in a natural or artificial language. Thus, if tall, not tall, very tall, very very tall, etc. are values of height, then height is a linguistic variable. Fuzzy conditional statements are expressions of the form if A then B, where A and B have fuzzy meaning, e.g., if x is small then y is large, where small and large are viewed as labels of fuzzy sets. A fuzzy algorithm is an ordered sequence of instructions which may contain fuzzy assignment and conditional statements, e.g., x = very small, if x is small then y is large. The execution of such instructions is governed by the compositional rule of inference and the rule of the preponderant alternative. By relying on the use of linguistic variables and fuzzy algorithms, the approach provides an approximate and yet effective means of describing the behavior of systems which are too complex or too ill-defined to admit of precise mathematical analysis. Its main applications lie in economics, management science, artificial intelligence, psychology, linguistics, information retrieval, medicine, biology, and other fields in which the dominant role is played by the animate rather than inanimate behavior of system constituents. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Zadeh L.A."]

Title: PROBABILISTIC SHORT-TERM RIVER YIELD FORECASTS.
Abstract: A predictive model, employing a first order autoregressive structure, which enables estimation of the probability distributions of streamflow volumes in future seasons, is developed. the model is applicable to streams that have intraseasonal runoff volumes describable by lognormal probability distributions.
Name: ["Burges Stephen J.", "Johnson Allen E."]

Title: Stability under Random Perturbations. | [Ueber STABILITAET BEI ZUFAELLIGEN STOERUNGEN.]
Source: Wissenschaftliche Zeitschrift der Technischen Unversitat Dresden
Abstract: The problem of stability of dynamic systems affected by random disturbances of the ‚Ä≥white noise‚Ä≥ or the Gaussian process type is considered. Different approaches to these problems are presented and also some questions of control of such systems for the purpose of optimal stabilization are discussed.
Name: ["Freidlin Mark Jiosefowitsch"]

Title: Coordination and Sensitivity Analysis of a Multilevel Control System with Interaction in the Indicator of Quality. | [KOORDYNACJA I ANALIZA WRAZLIWOSCI WIELOPOZIOMOWEGO UKLADU STEROWANIA Z INTERAKCJAMI WE WSKAZNIKU JAKOSCI.]
Abstract: The case considered is that in which the indicator of quality of a control system is not a simple sum of local indices. For such a case the multilevel structure of the system is considered. The method of decomposition ensuring the global optimality of solutions of local problems consists of a suitable modification of local indices. The problem as well as its decomposition is stated for a Hilbert space. The control problem is given in the form of a precisely formulated example. A coordination method is presented which is based on the variable operator method. The latter is specially useful for determining the sensitivity of a multilevel system with respect to coordination variables. The effect of modification of local indices on the system sensitivity is discussed. An example of a control system for purifying the natural environment is given.
Name: ["Dontchev Asenn L."]

Title: Freeway Traffic Surveillance and Control
Abstract: In the past decade, automatic freeway surveillance and control systems have been introduced in several cities in the United States. Effective use of the hardware that has been implemented requires a sound mathematical basis for evaluation and optimization studies. In this paper, the nature of freeway congestion and the structure of systems which have been implemented to relieve this congestion are discussed. Mathematical models of freeway traffic which allow consideration of on-ramp metering control are developed. Finally, several freeway traffic-control problems are discussed, current approaches are described, and formulations of improved (optimal) approaches are developed. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Isaksen L.", "Payne H.J."]

Title: The reallocation of hash-coded tables
Abstract: When the space allocation for a hash-coded table is altered, the table entries must be rescattered over the new space. A technique for accomplishing this rescattering is presented. The technique is independent of both the length of the table and the hashing function used, and can be utilized in conjunction with a linear reallocation of the table being rescattered. Moreover, it can be used to eliminate previously flagged deletions from any hash-coded table, or to change from one hashing method to another. The efficiency of the technique is discussed and theoretical statistics are given. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Bays C."]

Title: An heuristic strategy for multimodal search‚Ä†
Abstract: A heuristic search is described which has the aim of finding practically all extrema of a given non-linear functional. A standard unimodal descent algorithm is employed for finding individual extrema. This basic algorithm is applied repeatedly using various computed initial points and starting directions. Through an additional vise of several learning cycles most available extrema can be found. Numerical experiments indicate that the method is certainly very efficient for functionals of dimensions 15‚Äì 20 with 20‚Äì25 extrema. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["OpaƒåiƒÜ J."]

Title: MARKOVIAN DECISION PROCESSES WITH UNCERTAIN TRANSITION PROBABILITIES.
Abstract: The processes are assumed to be finite-state, discrete-time, and stationary. The rewards are time discounted. Both a game-theoretic and the Bayesian formulation are considered. An implicit enumeration algorithm is discussed for the Bayesian formulation where upper and lower bounds on the total expected discounted return are provided by the max-max and max-min optimal policies.
Name: ["Satia Jay K.", "Lave Jr. Roy E."]

Title: Computer-assisted expert interrogation: A report on current methods development
Abstract: This paper describes a major program currently under way at the Institute for the Future to develop and test a system for on-line interaction among experts via a network of computer terminals. The authors review the Institute's existing methods for eliciting and processing expert judgments, then discuss the operational procedures by which these methods have conventionally been implemented. In light of the shortcomings of these existing procedures, the authors argue an urgent need for on-line group modeling capabilities as the next leap forward in judgmental-research methodology. A description is given of the Institute's recently completed prototype computer interrogation system, whereby remotely situated respondents can participate in Institute inquiries via the ARPA computer-communication network and the University of Southern California's PDP-10 computer. Problems encountered thus far are discussed, as are future plans for system refinement and extension. The paper concludes with some brief philosophical observations on the state of our art, acknowledging that much work remains to be done on the still-primitive tools of decision-making. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Lipinski A.J.", "Lipinski H.M.", "Randolph R.H."]

Title: The internal machine
Source: Proceedings of the ACM-IEEE Symposium on High-Level-Language Computer Architecture, HLLCA 1973
Abstract: Two results are presented in this paper: an enlargement of the concept of machine languages and a way to design computers based on an inner machine oriented toward interpretation of machine languages in general. In Part I we discuss attributes of "directly interpretable languages" and processing mechanisms related to their interpretation. "Sequential extraction" allows an instruction to be of arbitrary form, while "linear decoding" allows us to organize the interpreting routines into structures. This leads to powerful machine language level capabilities. Using the mechanisms of Part I, we build in Part II the case for the "internal machine" approach to computer design. The internal machine (unlike microprocessors) is not oriented towards low level (gate, register) manipulation of data, but its operations reflect elementary actions related to the process of interpretation. The advantages of the internal machine include simplicity, programming interface (as opposed to the interface offered by microprocessors), and the ability to handle directly interpretable languages. One can choose among many architectures for the internal machine. An organization based on the execution stack is suggested as the most general solution. The essential "general purpose" organizations of the internal machines lend themselves to extensions and specializations which provide extra efficient handling of specific subprocesses related to interpretation. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Welin A.M."]

Title: A Two-Space Solution to the Hidden Line Problem for Plotting Functions of Two Variables
Abstract: A fast algorithm for eliminating hidden linies from perspective representations of single-valued functions of two variables is presented. Compared with the most widely used algorithm for this problem, the algorithm presented here is as versatile, but much faster. Compared with a recently published algorithm for this problem, the algorithm presented here is more powerful and as fast. Compared with more general algorithms, the one presented here is much less complicated, since this algorithm is tailored to this problem. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Wright T.J."]

Title: INDUSTRIAL DYNAMICS MODEL FOR START-UP MANAGEMENT.
Abstract: Efficient start-up management can result in considerable productivity increases compared to improvements possible in ‚Ä≥steady-state‚Ä≥ activities. Provided adequate targets are set and updated in accordance with realistic productivity expectation, management can interact rapidly in order to achieve optimum performance. Such a management process is dependent on the availability of suitable methods of predicting future productivity and estimating present productivity in the presence of random fluctuation due to many causes. This paper develops a predictive start-up model which performs both these functions. At each observation time, observed productivity is compared with predicted productivity as estimated from previous data, the difference being used to update the model parameters in a manner analogous to exponential smoothing. The model is applied to a number of start-up problems and is shown to track the parameters in an acceptable fashion. Long- and short-term productivity predictions resulting from the model are shown to be a useful management aid.
Name: ["Towill Denis R."]

Title: Hierarchical Storage in Information Retrieval
Abstract: A probabilistic analysis is employed to determine the effect of hierarchical storage organizations on information retrieval operations. The data storage hardware is assumed to consist of n-levels of linearly connected memory hardware with increasing data access times and increasing data storage capabilities. A system might, for example, consist of fast semiconductor memory, computer core memory, extended core storage, disk memory, and data cells. Equations are derived to predict the effect of such a system on data access times using sequential files, random access files, and structured files employing multiple-hierarchical linked lists. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Salasin J."]

Title: COLUMN GENERATION ALGORITHM FOR OPTIMAL TRAFFIC ASSIGNMENT.
Abstract: A algorithm for solving a class of nonlinear traffic assignment problems is presented. The fundamental advantage of the algorithm is that it does not require the a priori generation of all paths joining each origin-destination pair. The algorithm is capable of handling large networks. Computational experience that contrasts column generation with the a priori generation of all paths and compares two different quadratic programming algorithms is reported.
Name: ["Leventhal T.", "Nemhauser G.", "Trotter Jr. L."]

Title: On the H-Matrix System Representation
Abstract: The H-matrix representation of the input/output behavior of an asymptotically stable constant parameter linear system is discussed. The concept of a canonical representation and the measurements required to determine this representation directly are treated. The minimal complete realization problem is solved for the H-matrix representation based on exponential signals, and connections between this approach and the identification and realization theories based on the Hankel matrix of Markov parameters are exhibited. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Audley D.R.", "Rugh W.J."]
Affiliations: [' Wright-Patterson AFB.', ' The Johns Hopkins University']

Title: On the Precision Attainable with Various Floating-Point Number Systems
Abstract: For scientific computations on a digital computer the set of real numbers is usually approximated by a finite set accuracy F ‚Äúfloating-point‚Äù numbers. We compare the numerical accuracy possible with different choices of F having approximately the same range andrequiring the same word length. In particular, we compare different choices of base (or radix) in the usual floating-point systems. The emphasis is on the choice of F, not on the details of the number representation or the arithmetic, but both rounded and truncated arithmetic are considered. Theoretical results are given, and some simulations of typical floating-point computations (forming sums, solving systems of linear equations, finding eigenvalues) are described. If the leading fraction bit of a normalized base-2 number is not stored explicitly (saving a bit), and the criterion is to minimize the mean square roundoff error, then base 2 is best. If unnormalized numbers are allowed, so the first bit must be stored explicitly, then base 4 (or sometimes base 8) is the best of the usual systems. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Brent R.P."]

Title: AUTOMATIC PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE FOR N. C. LATHES.
Abstract: Economic aspects of small-batch production program of lathes are considered with regard to automatic control. A description of specific control programs and algorithms for tool set-up is given.
Name: ["Vul'fson I.A."]

Title: SINGLE SERVER QUEUE IN DISCRETE TIME - NUMERICAL ANALYSIS 1.
Abstract: This is the first of a sequence of papers dealing with the computational aspects of the transient behavior of queues in discrete time. It is shown that for a substantial class of queues of practical interest, a wealth of numerical information may be obtained by relatively unsophisticated methods. This approach should prove useful in the analysis of unstable queues which operate over a limited time interval, but is by no means limited to such queues. Mathematically the service unit is modeled in terms of a multivariate Markov chain, whose particular structure is used in iterative computation. Many important queue features may then be derived from the n-step transition probabilities of this chain.
Name: ["Neuts Marcel F."]

Title: Minimum-norm control of linear systems with partially known initial conditions
Abstract: The problem of controlling a linear system with initial conditions known to lie in a bounded set of the state space, and which is otherwise unknown, is treated in this paper by a modification of the techniques associated with the L-problem of moments. The set of initial conditions is assumed to be a convex polytope. The problem is reduced to devising a control function whose components are bounded functions over a given interval which maps the vertices of the polytope into a closed ball with the center at the origin, and has the least norm (sup-norm) among all control functions to do so. It is possible to apply a modified version of the techniques used to solve the L-problem of moments, and in this manner the optimal control, if it exists, is characterized and existence and uniqueness conditions are derived. A by-product of the analysis is an efficient computational method for optimal control. The procedure is shown by a numerical example. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Dharmasagar Rao V.", "Rubio J.E."]
Affiliations: ['Space Science and Technology Centre Indian Space Research Organisation']

Title: Deadlock Free Syntax Analysis - 1, 2. | SACKGASSENFREIE SYNTAXANALYSE - 1, 2.
Abstract: Pseudo-LL(k)-grammars are related to the LL(k)-grammars. They permit a top-down syntax analysis without deadlocks, even in the presence of left-recursive rules and alternatives with a series of common start symbols. To test a grammar for the PLL(k)-property, one first writes it in top-down form or lets a program translate it from Backus-Naur form into top-down form. One investigates then whether the terminal strings of length k of all rest-alternatives are disjoint. These strings can be defined recursively so that they are relatively easy to compute, particularly if k equals 1. If the grammar is stored in a tree-like structure, one can state an algorithm that computes for k equals 1 the necessary start symbols and performs the PLL(1)-test. Sentences of Pll(1)-grammars can be parsed with a simple recursive algorithm that operates through the tree-like structure and is thus independent of a particular grammar (syntax-oriented parser). It turns out that almost all grammars of practical programming languages can be transformed into PLL(1)-grammars without destroying their original shape. There remain only very few constructions that are not PLL(1) (in Algol 60 a single one). The PLL(1)-concept therefore seems to offer a convenient way to generate fast, small and reliable top-down parsers for context-free grammars.
Name: ["Rechenberg P."]

Title: Adaptive control of linear stochastic systems
Abstract: An adaptive control algorithm for linear systems with unknown constant parameters and quadratic performance criterion has been obtained. The control is nonlinear in the estimate of the state of the plant and is given as the weighted integral of the model conditional optimal controls with the a-posteriori probabilities as weights. The control scheme is separated into a bank of model-conditional deterministic control gains, and a corresponding bank of known nonlinear functions of the model conditional, causal, mean-square state-vector estimate. The separation here can be viewed as a decomposition of the control into a bank of model conditional optimal non-adaptive linear controls, one for each admissible value of the unknown parameter, and the bank of a-posteriori model probabilities which incorporate the learning nature of the adaptive control. The computational requirements are reduced by a great extent for the special case when the uncertainity is only in the measurement matrix. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Deshpande J.G.", "Upadhyay T.N.", "Lainiotis D.G."]

Title: Automatic Stabilization of the Vibration Level of the Drilling Machines. | [AVTOMATICHESKAYA STABILIZATSIYA UROVNYA VIBRATSII BUROVYKH STANKOV.]
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii, Gornyi Zhurnal
Abstract: A new principle of designing a systen of automatic control of the rasp drilling process is explained. The permissible (according to industrial hygiene norms) level of vibrations of the drilling machines is adopted as control criterion. In a particular case, the system can be adjusted to any capacity of the machine. The system realizes the most effective method of removing a machine from the vibration zone. Industrial tests of the system, carried out at the main open pit mine of the Kachkanarskig ore dressing combine, and maintenance experience have proved its efficiency and reliability.
Name: ["Marasanov Yu.P.", "Borovkov V.A.", "Shtrombasser R.S.", "Kovin V.P."]

Title: On the generative power of transformational grammars
Abstract: Mathematical modeling of phrase structure grammars has yielded many results of benefit to linguists in their investigation of these grammars, such as Chomsky's characterization in terms of self-embedding of those context-free languages which are not regular. The recent shift of focus in linguistic theory to transformational grammars has not been accompanied by a similar application of mathematical techniques to transformations. Our present purpose is to foster such studies by providing general definitions which model grammatical transformations as mappings on trees (equivalently, labeled bracketings) and investigating questions of current linguistic interest, such as the recursiveness of languages generated by transformational grammars. The first result of our research is that, despite the linguistically motivated, complex restrictions placed on transformational grammars, every recursively enumerable set of strings is a transformational language (Theorem 5.1). We demonstrate that this power of transformational grammars to generate non-recursive languages results from their ability to cycle their rules, applying transformations an unbounded number of times (Corollary 6.6). Analysis of decision procedures for grammars with bounded cycling reveals a connection between the amount of cycling permitted by a grammar and the complexity of the recursive set it generates; if cycling is bounded by any elementary recursive function (primitive recursive function, function in ‚àÑ<sup>n</sup> for n > 3), then the language generated has characteristic function in the same class (Corollary 6.7). One application of these results provides empirical support for the notion that natural languages are recursively, in fact elementarily, decidable. Our results also isolate one feature which must be further restricted in a linguistically motivated way if transformational theory is to achieve its goal of delimiting precisely the natural languages. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Peters Jr. P.S.", "Ritchie R.W."]

Title: A dual structured data base system
Source: Proceedings of the 1973 Meeting on Programming Languages and Information Retrieval, SIGPLAN 1973
Abstract: DUDABS demonstrates the ability to separate the data base into the two distinct classes (unique/common) of data, with the classical capabilities such as appending, modifying, and listing. The reverse polish scanning of unique expressions has proven to be an excellent method to implement the retrieval for the DUDABS system. It effectively and systematically reduces the size of the data base to be searched from the entire set to a much smaller subset. Results of this minimization become evident as one realizes that by this reverse polish process, a full sequential search of the data base is generally avoided. Depending on the application and prior knowledge of its characteristics, the amount of advantage over a single structured system can vary widely. In particular, it was demonstrated that the balance of the tree is extremely important. This dual structure can be used to decrease retrieval times or storage requirements. The relative value to a user of storage requirements verses retrieval time can guide him in structuring his data base. If each structure is not used correctly, the resulting data base degenerates greatly. But, with accurate prediction of the classification of the items in an application, a better design can be achieved than using either structure alone. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Clark W.O.", "Shannon L.L."]

Title: GENERATION OF SIMULATED MASS SPECTRA OF SMALL ORGANIC MOLECULES BY COMPUTERIZED PATTERN RECOGNITION TECHNIQUES.
Abstract: An empirical method employing computerized pattern recognition techniques has been applied to the generation of simulated mass spectra of small organic molecules. Molecular structures are represented in computer-compatible form through the use of a fragmentation code which assigns code designations to specific groups of atoms and/or bonds within the molecules. Using such descriptions of molecules, pattern classifiers have been developed to predict the presence or absence of mass spectral peaks in each of 60 nominal m/e positions and to give a measure of the intensity of peaks in 11 of these.
Name: ["Schechter Joseph", "Jurs Peter C."]

Title: On filtering in delay systems with continuous dynamics and discrete‚Äêtime observations
Abstract: Filter equations for linear delay systems with continuous‚Äêtime dynamics and discrete‚Äêtime measurements are derived by separating the estimation problem into prediction between measurements and updating at a measurement. The result is the analog of the well‚Äêknown Kalman filter for the nondelay case. A computational technique for implementing the filter is indicated and illustrated by an example of a scalar system with a delay in the dynamics as well as measurement. Copyright ¬© 1973 American Institute of Chemical Engineers
Name: ["Padmanabhan L."]

Title: DESIGNING A BINARY RECIPROCATOR.
Abstract: There are mathematically describable functions that can be implemented in ways which are not necessarily replicates of manual methods. The advent of large scale iintegration makes it reasonable to search for these novel methods in functions which see frequent use. These statements are exemplified in the process of arithmetic division. The manual approach, which has always been reflected in machine architectures. The existence of another feasible way of dividing, more in keeping with the LSI environment, was not known. Such a method has been discovered through the use of systematic scanning with an automatic network synthesizer. It has been found that the complete definition of the process of digital reciprocation (dividing into unity) (i. e. , Boolean functions made of all possible quotients) is not as irregular as might have been supposed. It has also been shown that the demonstrated regularities can be employed to reduce the complexity of a dividing switching network. Since regular networks of this nature are almost ‚Ä≥natural‚Ä≥ subjects for LSI implementation, it follows that a feasible LSI-oriented digital reciprocator logic has been produced.
Name: ["Logan J.Robert"]

Title: Adaptive Detection Probabilities for Fluctuating Target Models in Nonhomogeneous Gaussian Noise
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: Under the assumption that the average noise power may vary from cell to cell, new, more easily computed expressions are given for the probability of detecting a fluctuating target by means of a cell-averaging CFAR test. The generalized chi-square family of fluctuating targets is considered with the Swerling I and III models given as special cases. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gibson A.E."]

Title: Algorithm dynamics
Source: Proceedings of the Annual ACM Conference, ACM 1973
Abstract: A technique for measuring simple structural properties of algorithms is described. Using these measures, it is found that for a non-trivial class of algorithms there is a quantitative relationship between operators and operands and their usage. Properties of "Full" and "Reduced‚Äù algorithms are then explored, and shown to predict the quantitative relationship observed. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Halstead M.", "Bayer R."]

Title: AUTOMATIC CONTROL PLUS MANUAL EQUALS AUTOMANUAL CONTROL.
Abstract: An automatic controller and a human operator are each highly developed and effective control systems, but incompatible. However, the problem is eliminated in a system that uses a predictor as the man-machine interface. This article takes a look at the test results of a system in which a new method was developed for combining manual control with automatic, and which produces better results than the automatic controller alone.
Name: ["Kelley C.R.", "Beggs J.D.", "Prosin D.J."]

Title: A Nonrecursive List Moving Algorithm
Abstract: An efficient, nonrecursive algorithm is given for moving any LISP-type list. In particular, the algorithm requires no storage other than the new nodes into which the lists is to be moved, and no additional bits per node for marking; the algorithm runs in time proportional to the number of nodes in the list. The original list structure is destroyed as it is moved. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Reingold E.M."]

Title: PATTERN RECOGNITION PROBLEM IN APPLIED GEOCHEMISTRY.
Abstract: Available pattern recognition techniques, drawn mainly from the field of electrical engineering, are reviewed, and the application of feature selection, pattern classification (discriminant analysis) and pattern analysis (cluster-seeking techniques) methods in exploration geochemistry are discussed. Examples are drawn from regional stream-sediment multi-element survey data.
Name: ["Howarth R.J."]

Title: Some regular state sets in the system of one-dimensional iterative automata
Abstract: For the system of one-dimensional iterative automata, each set of all passive, Garden-of-Eden, and branching point state configurations is defined and shown to constitute a regular set. This regularity is proved to hold for the fixed, cyclic, open and reflexive boundary conditions. For proving theorems, a new device called N-automaton is introduced. Relationship with the gsm mapping is also discussed. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Kobuchi Y.", "Nishio H."]

Title: Chapter VII: Learning Models
Abstract: This chapter elaborates certain learning models. Learning models that change their structure and parameters in order to approach the behavior of the systems under study, can be used for system identification. After reaching their goal of learning, learning models give the characteristics of the studied systems. Learning models permit identification of linear and nonlinear systems under normal operating conditions. They can be used to obtain linear approximations of essentially nonlinear systems. The simplicity of the block diagrams of nonlinear learning models and their external similarity with the block diagrams of linear learning models can lead to an incorrect impression that linear and nonlinear models do not differ very much from each other. The most complicated methods are related to the decomposition, that is, to substitution of a complex problem of large dimensionality by several simpler problems of smaller dimensionality that have independent solutions. Until such methods are found, simple nonlinear learning models have to be used. ¬© 1973, Academic Press Inc.

Title: Fuzzy multi-stage decision-making, fuzzy state and terminal regulators and their relationship to non-fuzzy quadratic state and terminal regulators
Abstract: Bellman and Zadeh recently considered fuzzy multi-stage decision processes, the concept of fuzziness emanating from Zadeh‚Äôs earlier work on fuzzy sets. Here we extend their results to processes involving continuous state and decision variables, and discuss three alternative definitions of policy membership functions, two of which were previously proposed by Bellman and Zadeh. Also discussed (example) is the mathematical ‚Äò equivalence ‚Äô between some fuzzy and non-fuzzy processes which, although profoundly different models philosophically, have the same optimal policies and optimal state realizations. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Gluss B."]
Affiliations: [' University of Illinois at Chicago Circle']

Title: A computer generated aid for cluster analysis
Abstract: A computer generated graphic method, which can be used in conjunction with any hierarchical scheme of cluster analysis, is described and illustrated. The graphic principle used is the representation of the elements of a data matrix of similarities or dissimilarities by computer printed symbols (of character overstrikes) of various shades of darkness, where a dark symbol corresponds to a small dissimilarity. The plots, applied to a data matrix before clustering and to the rearranged matrix after clustering, show at a glance whether clustering brought forth any distinctive clusters. A well-known set of data consisting of the correlations of 24 psychological tests is used to illustrate the comparison of groupings by four methods of factor analysis and two methods of cluster analysis. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Ling R.L."]

Title: Proceedings of the 1973 Meeting on Programming Languages and Information Retrieval, SIGPLAN 1973
Source: Proceedings of the 1973 Meeting on Programming Languages and Information Retrieval, SIGPLAN 1973
Abstract: The proceedings contain 17 papers. The topics discussed include: a translating computer interface for a network of heterogeneous interactive information retrieval systems; specifying queries as relational expressions; on the construction of effective vocabularies for information retrieval; comparative analysis of interactive retrieval systems; fol: a language for implementing file organizations for information storage and retrieval system; an evaluation of languages for the implementation of information storage and retrieval systems; from a data description point of view; and retrieval operations and data representations in a context-addressed disc system.

Title: RKHS Approach to Detection and Estimation Problems‚ÄïPart IV: Non-Gaussian Detection
Abstract: We introduce the reproducing-kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) associated with the characteristic functional of a random process and use it to develop a general RKHS theory for non-Gaussian detection. Previously known results for choosing between processes with Gaussian and Poisson statistics are obtained as specializations of this theory. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Duttweiler D.L."]

Title: Pipeline array for square-root extraction
Abstract: Pipelining an arithmetic process is a well known technique for improving the computation speed of the arithmetic algorithm. In the letter is proposed a pipeline version of the array for the extraction of square roots of binary numbers. It is shown that a significant speed improvement (on a throughput basis) can result by this modification of the conventional logic arrays. ¬© 1973, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Majithia J.C."]

Title: On the analytic formalism of the theory of fuzzy sets
Abstract: The extension of standard concepts of set theory (like union, intersection, etc.) to the theory of fuzzy sets is not obvious. Several policies for answering questions of this type have been discussed, but it appears that the operations of max and min play a central role in the arithmetic of fuzzy sets. Letting Œº<sub>A</sub>(x) denote our willingness to accept x as a member in the fuzzy set A, Zadeh defines intersection A ‚à© B and union A ‚à™ B of the two fuzzy sets A and B by A ‚à© B = {(x; min {Œº<sub>A</sub>(x), Œº<sub>B</sub>(x)})} and A ‚à™ B = {(x; max {Œº<sub>A</sub>(x), Œº<sub>b</sub>(x)})}. The object of this paper is to show that these definitions are not only natural, but under quite reasonable assumptions the only ones possible. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Bellman R.", "Giertz M."]

Title: On the Numerical Reconstruction of Images From a Microwave Hologram
Source: IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques
Abstract: A new technique for the numerical reconstruction of images from a long-wavelength hologram is proposed. The technique is to calculate images by the fast Fourier transform (FFT) algorithm with the hologram data sampled by a straight line approximation. This sampling technique is convenient to reduce the number of the sampling points, and the image can be reconstructed with less data than the conventional equally spaced sampling method, A one-dimensional hologram is constructed at S band and an image is reconstructed by the proposed method. These results are discussed and compared with the results of the conventional numerical reconstruction. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Nagai K.", "Aoki Y.", "Suzuki M."]

Title: Optimal Trajectories for Multidimensional Nonlinear Processes by Iterated Dynamic Programming
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A trajectory optimization technique for multidimensional nonlinear processes is presented. Problems which are cast in a discrete-time mold are considered. The method is based on dynamic programming and employs a combination of the technique of functional approximation and the method of region-limiting strategies. The cost function at each stage is approximated by a quadratic polynomial in a region which is restricted to be of a size judged appropriate to reduce the error in the approximation. Minimal costs are evaluated at a set of points, called base points. A new control trajectory and an improved state trajectory are then generated within an extrapolation region. The iterative application of this procedure yields an optimal trajectory. Contained in the algorithm is a simple procedure which eliminates matrix inversion to determine the coefficients of the approximating polynomial. The present algorithm is applicable to problems with one bounded control action. It accounts for inequality constraints on state variables in a straightforward manner. The algorithm is applied to solve a number of trajectory optimization problems. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Arora J.K.", "Pierre D.A."]

Title: BAYESIAN APPROACH TO AUTOCORRELATION ESTIMATION IN HYDROLOGIC AUTOREGRESSIVE MODELS.
