Source: Mass Inst Technol, Dep Civ Eng, Ralph M. Parsons Lab Water Res Hydrody
Abstract: Three general approaches leading to the marginal posterior probability distribution function for the autocorrelation coefficient of the first order annual autoregressive model are presented. The performance of the Bayes estimators for the quadratic, symmetric linear and asymmetric linear loss functions is evaluated by Monte Carlo methods. The general framework for the derivation of a loss function for a hydrologic water resources system design problem is presented.
Name: ["Lenton Roberto L.", "Rodriguez-Iturbe Ignacio", "Schaake Jr. John C."]

Title: Determination of Derivatives by a Model with Automatic Parameter Setting. | BESTIMMUNG VON DERIVATIVEN DURCH EIN MODELL MIT AUTOMATISCHER PARAMETEREINSTELLUNG.
Source: Dtsch Luft Raumfahrt, Mitt DLR Mitt 73-25
Abstract: An analog circuit which continuously adapts model parameters to unknown system characteristic values is used to determine derivatives of an aircraft from flight data. The results of an evaluation with a linear and a nonlinear model are plotted and evaluated. The plane used for comparative test results was Dornier 27.
Name: ["Koehler R."]

Title: Evolution-Linearizing Routine to Represent Numerical Data by Arbitrary Functions. | EVOLUTIONS-LINEARISIERUNGS-PROGRAMM ZUR DARSTELLUNG VON NUMERISCHEN DATEN DURCH BELIEBIGE FUNKTIONEN.
Abstract: A new method is presented for interpolation of digital data or for interpretation of the same by means of theoretical models. This method may replace the method of linear estimation, offering a better procedure for handling the convergence, fit-precision and the computation-time.
Name: ["Plaschko P.", "Wagner K."]

Title: A high-speed algorithm for computing conditional probabilities of substrings of sequentially observed data
Abstract: An algorithm is described that computes relative frequencies of occurrence of all arbitrarily long substrings of sequential data, such as are obtained from experiments in learning/memory and verbal interaction. The algorithm offers high speed and provides systematization for the computation of empirical conditional probabilities. Use of this algorithm allows application of probabilistic and information theoretic disciplines to reveal dependencies between events separated arbitrarily in time. ¬© 1973 Psychonomic Society, Inc.
Name: ["Nirenberg L.M.", "Haber J.", "Moise S.L."]
Affiliations: [' Brain Research Institute', 'Health Sciences Computing Facility', 'University of California']

Title: Optimization of Systems of Partial Boolean Functions. | ZUR OPTIMIERUNG VON SYSTEMEN PARTIELLER BOOLESCHER FUNKTIONEN.
Abstract: An appropriate technique for the optimization is presented by means of which one nonredundant total solution, at least, can be obtained in a particularly rational manner. Some pertinent algorithms are given.
Name: ["Zander H.J.", "Heltzig H.F."]

Title: On the Problem of Information Classification as a Prerequisite to Information Processing with Computers. | [ZUM PROBLEM DER KLASSIFIKATION VON INFORMATIONEN ALS VORAUSSETZUNG UND ERFORDERNIS EINER RECHNERGESTUETZEN INFORMATIONSVERARBEITUNG.]
Source: Wissenschaftliche Zeitschrift der Technischen Unversitat Dresden
Abstract: On the example of an information system for research administration, a method is developed for information classification which is a prerequisite both of the analysis and synthesis of an information system as well as the corresponding information processing based on a computer.
Name: ["Belke Wolfgang", "Doehn Inge", "Kasper Frank"]

Title: On-line prediction of hydrologic system
Abstract: A theory of the on-line prediction of runoff from a hydrologic system is developed, in a general form, applying the Kalman filtering theory well known in the field of automatic control. It overcomes the shortcomings of the conventional methods of runoff forecasts that the unit-hydrograph, the excess run-off rate and the pattern of rainfall intensity distribution are not determined uniquely but change from storm to storm. The method utilizes effectively the most reliable hydrologic information (i.e. rainfall and runoff data of the present storm) by the on-line processing. Some examples of estimation of unit-hydrograph and prediction of runoff are presented to show the effectiveness of the method
Name: ["Hino M."]

Title: Eyeball Parameter Estimation with a Computer
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: Great promise is shown by combining man and computers via interactive graphics to solve problems neither could solve alone. The behavior of man in this problem-solving combination must be studied just as any computer problem-solving system. The example problem studied is parameter estimation. After collecting observational data, a mathematical model of the data generation process is constructed which generates predicted data which varies according to some parameters of the model. The problem is to find parameters which ‚Äúfit‚Äù predicted data to collected data. Three methods are typically used to solve this problem: calculate parameters as a function of the observational data, ‚Äúgrid search‚Äù the parameter space, and ‚Äúhill climb‚Äù in the parameter space. In all these procedures, ‚Äúfeel‚Äù of the data and model are lost. Systematic differences may be present which suggest data collection errors or a need to reformulate the model. An interactive graphics curve-fitting procedure has been developed which both fits curves and gives the man some feel of the process. Collected data are displayed. The man then iteratively enters trial parameters and immediately observes the predicted data along with the collected data (and other predicted data curves). Collected data for problems with two parameters were generated using linear, sinusoidal, exponential, and logrithmic models to which random error and sometimes systematic error components were added. Collected data for problems with four parameters were generated using a model of short-term memory and random error. The two-parameter problems were fit by subjects with no a priori knowledge of the models they were using. The four-parameter problems were fit by psychology graduate students who had studied the model. Both classes of subjects performed well on most problems, but there were individual differences attributable to the problem type and error type. The sinusoidal models proved harder to fit than others, but the median parameter estimates of the subjects were all quite close to grid search estimates. Visual fitting of the two-parameter models proved approximately ten times faster in central processing unit (CPU) model time than grid search CPU time. Savings for the four-parameter model was substantially greater. Three groups of users have satisfactorily used the system in practical work. For this task, the man-graphic problem-solving system proved economical, accurate, and provided insight into both models and data. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Garnatz D.K.", "Hunt E."]

Title: FUNCTION MINIMIZATION ALGORITHM.
Abstract: Described is an iterative process of fitting a hyperparaboloid to a set of reference points to predict the function minimum, and periodically refining the semimajor axes of the paraboloid, so it will converge towards a good approximation of the defined function in the vicinity of its minimum.
Name: ["Gaston C.A."]

Title: THEORETICAL CONSIDERATION OF THE PROBLEM OF TWO CORRELATIVE RANDOM WALK PROCESSES IN MULTIDIMENSIONAL SIGNAL SPACE AND ITS DIGITAL SIMULATION.
Abstract: A statistical analysis is made of random signals in connection with two random walk processes in multidimensional signal space. It is assumed that correlations between random signals at two distinct time points can be expressed as linear and nonlinear correlations between corresponding random vectors of two different N-dimensional random walk processes. Specifically, the joint probability density and the conditional probability density functions of two resultant vectors whose expansion coefficients represent the correlations between two random walk processes are derived. Further, digital simulation is made of two different N-dimensional random walk processes to confirm the validity of the theory.
Name: ["Ohta Mitsuo", "Nishimura Masafumi", "Hiromitsu Seijiro", "Mashimo Tohru"]

Title: PHONEME RECOGNITION IN CONNECTED SPEECH - 2. RECOGNITION, TRAINING, AND SELF-ORGANIZATION ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: It is shown that the problem of phoneme recognition of connected speech, formulated in Part 1 (Avtomatyka (Sov. Auto. Cont,) No. 6, 1972), can be solved in principle by the standard procedure of dynamic programming. However, this is not feasible in practice, since it requires a large memory. The author proposes an algorithm that reduces these requirements by two orders of magnitude. The algorithm consists of a computational scheme of dynamic programming that uses the concepts of potentially optimal control, and potentially optimal index and recognition response. Training is considered in relation to the presence or absence of the teacher's indications with regard to the sequence of phonemes in the training sample, or with regard to their number. It is shown that the training problems are in fact problems of self-organization, since the teacher does not specify the limits of the phonemes in the training sample. Iteration algorithms for training with finitely many steps are described in detail.
Name: ["Vintsyuk T.K."]

Title: DECISION PROCESS OF STOCHASTIC SEQUENTIAL MACHINES.
Abstract: T. T. Nieh (see Engineering Index 1969 p 181 abstract 48331) has defined a cost function for the input symbol and a gain function for the output symbol of the Mealy-type stochastic sequential machine. He proposed a system in which the gain for an input sequence of length n is equal to the sum of gains at each step of the sequence and discussed the magnitude of gain. He did not, however, provide insight into the method of deriving the optimum input sequence for the system. This paper describes a method whereby the optimum input sequence for the Moore-type stochastic sequential machine can be determined with less time using a computer. In order to circumvent the drawbacks in forward and backward methods, the proposed method combines the two. Proportional or linear prediction is used for estimating the remain rate of the admissible vector, which is required in determination of the coupling step. The results of computer simulation indicate that proportional prediction is the simplest, leading to satisfactory results.
Name: ["Kutsuwa T.", "Kosako H.", "Kojima Y."]

Title: FLOW GRIDS AND THEIR USE IN THE REALIZATION OF FINITE AUTOMATA.
Abstract: The concept of a flow grid is introduced, and its operation described. It is shown that a flow grid realizes an idempotent finite automaton (one that keeps its state upon repeated application of the same input). A method is proposed that, for each idempotent automaton, constructs a flow grid realizing it. A generalization of the concept of a realization (realization with stretching in time) is introduced. A method is proposed for realization of an arbitrary finite automaton, in general not idempotent, with stretching 2. Estimates are given for the complexity of grids constructed by the methods indicated.
Name: ["Gendler M.B."]

Title: PARTIAL RESTORATION OF IMAGES FROM AERIAL PHOTOGRAPHS USING EXPERIMENTALLY DERIVED FOURIER FILTERS.
Abstract: An experiment is reported in which clear quantitative improvements were made in images from conventional aerial photographs using linear processing with experimentally derived Fourier filters. These filters are found from the images produced by known two-tone objects such as symbols painted on flat uniform surfaces. A sequence of noise suppression and linear filtering steps has been developed and implemented using a computer for calculating a processing filter and for using that filter to improve digitized images. Comparison of images before and after processing indicates that well-defined improvements are made.
Name: ["Carter William H."]

Title: On Decentralized Linear Stochastic Control Problems with Quadratic Cost
Abstract: A decentralized stochastic optimal control problem is considered where agents have different a priori information on the system initial state. Agents are assumed to exchange their control values but not their state vector observation values. It is shown that this leads to a suboptimal control law, with correction terms being added to the well-known optimal proportional feedback control signal obtainable under the information centralization assumption of linear dynamics with quadratic cost, when person-by-person satisfactory team decisions are considered. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Aoki M."]

Title: Identification and control of muftivariable stochastic feedback systems
Abstract: This paper considers the problem of simultaneous identification and control of stochastic processes characterized by linear dynamic models with unknown systems parameter coefficients. Stochastic approximation is used to derive consistent identification algorithms for the case in which arbitrary feedback controls are present. These identification methods can also be used for determining the order of the system, if the latter is unknown, as well as the exact canonical structure for the multivariable case. An approximation to the optimal control solution is obtained by explicitly separating the functions of identification and control, and asymptotic convergence to a stochastic optimal controller is attained without on-line structural modification. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Lobbia R.N.", "Saridis G.N."]

Title: Organization of the Queuing Discipline in Queuing Systems Using Models of the Collective Behavior of Automata
Abstract: An analysis of queuing systems with infinite queues shows that the quality of the system operation determined, for example, by the average length of a queue, can be improved by the introduction of priorities. In this case the highest priority number is given to a subscriber with the shortest average service time. However, in order to organize a system of priorities, it is needed first, to know the probabilistic characteristics of the input flows, and, second, a special system of queue control. Often in a number of practically important cases the probabilistic characteristics of inputs are not known beforehand or vary with time. This chapter describes a queuing system in which the priorities are worked out directly in the channels without any a priori knowledge of input characteristics. As a result, each channel, in the course of its operation, selects a subscriber with the smallest average service time, and in case, the service times are close to one another‚Äìa subscriber with the densest flow. ¬© 1973, Academic Press Inc.

Title: ALGORITHMS FOR OPTIMIZATION OF COVERINGS.
Abstract: An algorithm is proposed for finding a quasioptimal covering or packing of a bounded set S of space points by parallel displacement (translation) of a given bounded set G. This algorithm is suitable for use in special-purpose dynamic systems. It is examined in detail.
Name: ["Kuznetsov I.N."]

Title: OPTIMISING THE STATIC PROPERTIES OF AN AUTOMATIC CONTROL SYSTEM FOR ONCE-THROUGH BOILERS.
Abstract: Methods are considered for optimization of static conditions of automatic control systems for once-through boilers. Using the method of piecewise linear approximation with respect to the PK-39 boiler units of the Troitsk central power station, a table of special-purpose function is calculated and a table of optimal transitions is completed. One of the variants of realization of the table of optimal transitions, using units for selecting the maximum, is presented. It has been partly put into operation at the Troitsk power plant.
Name: ["Volgin V.V.", "Bessonov V.V."]

Title: ON THE CONTROL OF STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Methods are considered of deriving optimal adaptive algorithms in the one-step control problem. As an example, the problems of adaptive control of a linear object is solved.
Name: ["Mamaev D.D."]

Title: The influence of human factors on the performance of a real-time speech recognition system
Source: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Abstract: The performance of real-time speech recognition systems is observed to depend upon the environments in which they are used. Human factors, caused for example by operator frustration, significantly affect success rates. A set of experiments with a word recognition system is described which quantifies this change, whilst the system is being used to control the movement of a displayed cross on a screen. ¬© 1973, Acoustical Society of America. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Carpenter B.E.", "Lavington S.H."]

Title: LEARNING CONTROL IN REMOTE MANIPULATOR AND ROBOT SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Introduces the principles and functional organization of control systems of robots and manipulator systems and emphasizes the unique role of learning in system operation. Of particular interest are the properties of trainable control policies which provide the ability to change behavioral patterns with changing environmental statistics and allow performance improvement as experience is acquired. Current applications of learning techniques in robots and manipulators are described, and an example of an interactive man-learning control system is presented.
Name: ["Freedy Amos"]

Title: ON-LINE LEARNING CONTROL ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: Five algorithms have been selected to represent the learning control systems for which convergence to an optimal solution can be established mathematically. Such a consideration covers the major part of the on-line learning control systems. The algorithms included have been chosen by the author as the most representative of the on-line learning control algorithms because each one of them utilizes one of the most successful learning techniques known.
Name: ["Saridis George N."]

Title: Linear pattern matching algorithms
Source: 14th Annual Symposium on Switching and Automata Theory
Abstract: In 1970, Knuth, Pratt, and Morris [1] showed how to do basic pattern matching in linear time. Related problems, such as those discussed in [4], have previously been solved by efficient but sub-optimal algorithms. In this paper, we introduce an interesting data structure called a bi-tree. A linear time algorithm for obtaining a compacted version of a bi-tree associated with a given string is presented. With this construction as the basic tool, we indicate how to solve several pattern matching problems, including some from [4] in linear time. ¬© 1973 IEEE.
Name: ["Weiner P."]

Title: CALCULATING THE IMAGE CONTRAST OF POINT OR LINE OBJECTS.
Abstract: Exact expressions for the image contrast K are determined and the object dimensions are found for which the equations for a point and for a line are valid.
Name: ["Sokol'skiy M.N."]

Title: DEVELOPMENT OF NEW PATTERN-RECOGNITION METHODS.
Source: U S Air Force Syst Command, Aerospace Res Lab
Abstract: New methods in pattern recognition are studied in relation to classical approaches using techniques of multivariate statistical analysis. The application of these techniques to specific problems in physical, engineering, behavioral, and other sciences is reviewed. The problems of improved data description and dimensionality reduction are tackled by means of clustering approaches. Several improved clustering methods are developed for general pattern recognition: a new approximate procedure for computing the minimal-spanning tree, a new application of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for cluster validity, and a new application of relativistic principles in measures of relationship. Experiments using interactive graphic displays to illustrate these new methods are described, and application of computer programs to meteorological problems is demonstrated. New methodology for research in developing new pattern-recognition methods is illustrated by the development of a closed-loop generation and description language. The same language as that used by the clustering system to describe data is used to generate data. Thus, comparisons of performance of successive research versions of pattern-recognition systems can be easily made, which will facilitate their adaptation from research to application versions.
Name: ["Hall D.J.", "Huffman D.A.", "Duda R.O.", "Wolf D.E."]

Title: SUCCESSIVE OVERRELAXATION ITERATIVE TECHNIQUE FOR AN ADAPTIVE EQUALIZER.
Abstract: This study deals with an adaptive strategy for the equalization of pulse-amplitude-modulated signals in the presence of intersymbol interference and additive noise. The successive overrelaxation iterative technique is used as the algorithm for the iterative adjustment of the equalizer coefficients during a training period for the minimization of the mean square error. Analytically, convergence of the relaxation algorithm was proven in a noisy environment and the coefficient variance was demonstrated to be bounded. Numerical simulations conducted indicate that the relaxation algorithm consistently converged much faster than the gradient techniques; hence, it requires much less time in the training period than do the gradients.
Name: ["Kosovych Ostap S."]

Title: MATHEMATICAL AND COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEMS IN LINEAR DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING.
Abstract: This book deals with applications of linear dynamic programming to solution of optimal problems (specifically optimal random problems) of production. A set of mathematical models, describing various modes of functioning of individual processes and their aggregates is derived, and several techniques for quantitative and qualitative analysis of such models are presented. These modeling techniques are then applied to the analysis of Bellman's simple automobile production problem, modified by incorporation of a feedback flow of factors of production, whereby the optimal plan and schedule for production of a new aircraft is desired. Similar plans are derived for a warehouse and for demand on bank credit.
Name: ["Krivenkov Yu.P."]

Title: MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD IDENTIFICATION AND OPTIMAL INPUT DESIGN FOR IDENTIFYING AIRCRAFT STABILITY AND CONTROL DERIVATIVES.
Abstract: A new method of extracting aircraft stability and control derivatives from flight test data is developed based on the maximum likelihood criterion. It is shown that this new method is capable of processing data from both linear and nonlinear models, both with and without process noise and includes output error and equation error methods as special cases. The first application of this method to flight test data is reported for lateral maneuvers of the HL-10 and M2/F3 lifting bodies, including the extraction of stability and control derivatives in the presence of wind gusts. Several simple examples are first given and then the results of an extensive stability and control derivative identification simulation for a C-8 aircraft are detailed.
Name: ["Stepner David E.", "Mehra Raman K."]

Title: UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT OF SEVERAL TECHNIQUES FOR THE REPRESENTATION OF RANDOM VECTORS AND DATA SETS.
Abstract: Linear vector space theory is used to develop a general representation of a set of data vectors or random vectors by linear combinations of orthonormal vectors such that the mean squared error of the representation is minimized. The orthonormal vectors are shown to be the eignevectors of an operator. The general representation is applied to several specific problems involving the use of the Karhunen-Loeve expansion, principal component analysis, and empirical orthogonal functions; and the common properties of these representations are developed.
Name: ["Bundick W.Thomas"]

Title: TRANSFORMATION IN PROBLEMS OF DETERMINING THE PARAMETERS OF CONTINUOUS DYNAMIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A sequence of transformations is considered which are performed on a system of linear differential equations, and which are based on the properties of regular transfer functions. It is shown that, using the transformations, the parameters of continuous systems ccan be determined by solution of a system of linear algebraic equations. An example is presented of the application of a non-search identification algorithm.
Name: ["Ivanovskiy R.I."]

Title: Tridimensional representation of surfaces interpolated from a table of values contained in a central memory: (Application to the analysis of electroencephalographic frequencies, using a small computer) | Visualisation tridimensionnelle de surfaces interpolees a partir d'un tableau de valeurs contenu en memoire centrale: (Application √† l'analyse de fr√©quence d'electroenc√©phalogrammes: R√©alisation sur petit ordinateur)
Abstract: We describe a system running on a mini-computer which has the following advantages: 1. (1) allows the interpolation of a surface from several points, by an x 3rd degree function and a y 3rd degree function; 2. (2) projects a three-dimensional space on a plane; 3. (3) visualises it, thus giving a very instructive view of several data, making easier for users the interpretation of experimental or mathematical results. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Laviron A.", "Echallier J.F."]

Title: STRUCTURAL SYNTHESIS OF FILTERS FOR INDIRECT MEASUREMENT OF VARIABLES ON THE GENERALIZED GMDH ALGORITHM.
Abstract: Using GMDH algorithms based on self-organization (selection) principles, it is possible to synthesize the most diverse filters, such as smoothing or prediction filters, algebraic or differential filters, linear or square-law filters as well as filters represented by a complete Kolmogorov-Gabor polynomial. Moreover, it is possible to retain in them any arguments needed ( ‚Ä≥protection of variables‚Ä≥ ). However, any restriction in the freedom of choice of the algorithm will reduce the filter accuracy. As an example, results are presented of synthesis of smoothing filters for an actual industrial plant. The filters are intended for rapid indirect measurement of variables; in the absence of the filters, measurements could be made only in the laboratory with a delay of two to three hours.
Name: ["Ivakhnenko A.G.", "Todua M.M.", "Fomichev A.A."]

Title: OPTIMAL PROPERTIES OF A CERTAIN CLASS OF CONTROL AUTOMATA.
Abstract: A definition of a certain class of infinite probabilistic automata is given. It is shown that, in the control of homogeneous random sequences with independent values, they possess the property of delta -optimality. An ergodic theorem is proved for them.
Name: ["Sragovich V.G."]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR FINDING THE MINIMAL LENGTH HAMILTONIAN PATH IN A GRAPH.
Source: Econ Comput Econ Cybern Stud Res
Abstract: In an attempt to further reduce the computing time associated with finding a minimal path in a graph, the author examines this problem from the viewpoint of reducing computer time.
Name: ["Mierlea V."]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR GLOBALLY-OPTIMAL NONLINEAR-COST MULTIDIMENSIONAL FLOWS IN NETWORKS AND SOME SPECIAL APPLICATIONS.
Abstract: An algorithm is described that finds globally optimum flows in networks having nonlinear costs of arc flows, the flows being finite-dimensional vectors such as multicommodity flows. The algorithm is an extension of a theory of R. E. Allsop for minimizing total delays in a traffic network; it is also intimately related to results in nonserial dynamic programming.
Name: ["Korsak Andrew"]

Title: Linear stochastic optimal control under information rate constraints
Abstract: The discrete-time, linear, stochastic optimal control problem is considered under information rate constraints on the feedback loop. The feedback loop, including sensor, is modelled as a communication channel which provides a specified amount of information (in the Shannon sense) about the state of the linear plant at each discrete-time instant given the current and past observations and past controls. No further specific structure for the sensor is assumed. The expected value of a positive definite quadratic loss function is used as the performance criterion to be minimized. This leads to a double minimization problem in which the performance criterion is minimized over the set of admissible controls and the set of conditional probability densities for the state given the observations and controls which achieve the specified information. A set of recursion relationships for the solution of this problem is derived using the techniques of calculus of variations and dynamic programming. The solution indicates that the optimum sensor is linear in the state with additive Gaussian noise with parameters which achieve the specified information rate; and, with the appropriate parameters in the measurement equation, the solution reduces to the well-known solution for the linear plant-quadratic cost problem with linear measurements and additive Gaussian noise. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Lefevre R.J.", "Stear E.B."]

Title: Optimal Discrete Systems with Pure Delays
Abstract: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the optimization of multivariable discrete systems containing pure delays in dynamics, in performance index, and in constraints are investigated. Using nonlinear programming, it is shown that a discrete maximum principle similar to the one derived by Pearson and Sridhar [1] is valid for a subclass of these problems, that is, systems with linear dynamics, convex inequality constraints, and convex performance index. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Mariani L.", "Nicoletti B."]
Affiliations: [' University of Padua', ' University of Naples']

Title: CONVEX PROGRAMMING MODEL FOR OPTIMIZING SLBM ATTACK OF BOMBER BASES.
Abstract: A convex programming model allocating submarine-launched ballistic missiles to launch areas and providing simultaneously an optimal targeting pattern against a specified set of bomber bases. Flight times of missiles from launch areas to bases vary and targets decrease in value over time. A nonseparable concave objective function is given for expected destruction of bombers. An example is presented.
Name: ["Bracken Jerome", "McGill James T."]

Title: INVERSE FILTERING FOR LINEAR SHIFT-VARIANT IMAGING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Two techniques are introduced for inverse filtering of linear shift-variant imaging systems. The first technique requirs that the linear system be decomposed into a distortion of the input plane followed by a shift-invariant operation and terminated by a distortion of the output plane. The second technique relies upon the assumption that the system may be specified by several shift-invariant impulse responses. It is shown tht such systems may be inverted by the same techniques used to invert the Wiener-Hopf integral equation.
Name: ["Robbins G.M.", "Huang T.S."]

Title: Design of Failure Search Algorithms for Electromechanical Mine Systems on the Basis of A Priori Reliability Data. | [POSTROENIE ALGORITMOV POISKA NEISPRAVNOSTEI V SHAKHTNYKH ELEKTROMEKHANICHESKIKH SISTEMAKH NA OSNOVE APRIORNOI INFORMATSII O NADEZHNOSTI.]
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii, Gornyi Zhurnal
Abstract: A procedure is presented for constructing failure search algorithms on the basis of a method of expert evaluation. The necessity of using the proposed method is shown and a particular numerical example is given. The economic effect of the utilization of failure search algorithms in mine conditions is estimated.
Name: ["Gimel'shein L.Ya."]

Title: Interpreting pictures of polyhedral scenes
Abstract: A program that achieves the interpretation of line drawings as polyhedral scenes is described. The method is based on general coherence rules that the surfaces and edges must satisfy, thereby avoiding the use of predetermined interpretations of particular categories of picture junctions and corners. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Macworth A.K."]

Title: Mathematical Modeling of the Simplest Forms of Behavior
Abstract: This chapter presents certain problems related to the mathematical models of simple forms of behavior. By studying movements that can be objectively measured, certain characteristic features that govern the mechanism of control of complex systems can be revealed. Some of these characteristic features are capable of being modeled. Without gaining an understanding of the more complex features of behavior, any kind of exact and accurate knowledge of control processes cannot be obtained. The chapter discusses the simplest forms of collective behavior, which is reduced to the well-investigated behavior of the individual. The behavior of a single human, one member of a group (one machine, one animal) is defined in a very simple way. This definition makes it possible to construct more complicated models. The most important feature of collective behavior is the possibility of an agreement. ¬© 1973, Academic Press Inc.

Title: DISTRIBUTION OF THE NUMBER OF REQUESTS IN A QUEUEING SYSTEM WITH ‚Ä≥WARMUP‚Ä≥ .
Abstract: A method is proposed for calculating the stationary probabilities of the states of an M vertical G vertical 1 queueing system in which a request entering the unoccupied system has a service time distribution PHI ( tau ) and in all other cases has a service time distribution F( tau ).
Name: ["Ryzhikov Yu.I."]

Title: Unsupervised learning structure and parameter adaptive pattern recognition with discrete data
Abstract: This paper presents the problem of unsupervised learning structure and parameter adaptive pattern recognition. Different near optimal solutions that alleviate the infinite or exploding memory requirements of the optimal solution are suggested. The learning capabilities of these methods are compared with that of the optimal supervised scheme by presenting an example. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Rajasekaran P.K.", "Srinath M.D."]

Title: MATRIX ALGORITHM FOR THE SYNTHESIS OF MINIMAL ENCODING NETWORKS FOR LINEAR CONVOLUTIONAL CODES.
Abstract: An algorithm for the synthesis of minimal-memory encoding networks on a code matrix or on the transfer function of a linear convolutional (recurrent) code is described. The operation of the algorithm is illustrated by examples. The results are extended to a broader class of convolutional codes.
Name: ["Zarovnyi V.P."]

Title: UPPER BOUND FOR THE POWER OF AN AUTOMATON STATE CODE.
Abstract: An upper bound on the power of an automaton state code is obtained on the basis of two race models for q-stable delay elements. The upper and lower bounds on the power of the automaton state code are compared with the corresponding bounds for ordinary noise-immune block codes, and some new problems are discussed.
Name: ["Sagalovich Yu.L."]

Title: ERROR PROBABILITY EXPONENT FOR A FEEDBACK SYSTEM WITH THE USE OF A CONCATENATED CODE.
Abstract: A system with (noiseless) feedback and advanced correction based on a concatenated code is analyzed. An upper bound is derived for the error probability in the system and for the average code combination length for a given concatenated code decoding algorithm in the case of a memoryless channel.
Name: ["Zhigulin L.F.", "Zyablov V.V."]

Title: Nonlinear-Discrete Data Systems Extension of the Known Sector of Stability
Abstract: A simple and elegant method for widening the domain of stability of nonlinear sampled-data systems to an appreciable extent is presented. The order of the difference equation is artificially increased in order to examine the behavior of the system in the time domain for a longer duration than indicated by the dynamics of the system. The utility of some of the well-known methods can be considerably enhanced by the technique described here. The method is illustrated by several examples, some of which are difficult to solve by the existing methods. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Janakiraman P.A.", "Rao P.V."]

Title: Chemical facilitation in dynamic models of neural macrostates
Abstract: A mathematical model for the neuron is introduced for convenient modelling of neural macrostates. The state and dynamics of the neuron are characterized by the level of transmitter substance acting on its input. The model is continuous in time rendering the use of differential equations possible. The model is best applicable to neuron pools to describe their activity as a single totality. ¬© 1973 Informa UK Ltd All rights reserved: reproduction in whole or part not permitted.
Name: ["Pohjavirta A."]

Title: A Minimization Algorithm for the Design of Linear Multivariable Systems
Abstract: A new algorithm for the design of linear multivariable systems is presented. This algorithm constructs a set of minimal-order (McMillan degree) solutions to a proper rational matrix equation. The algorithm has direct application in exact model matching, inverse systems, and dynamic observers. In particular, application of the algorithm is made to the construction of a minimal-order inverse system. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Wang S.-H.", "Davison E.J."]

Title: DESIGN AND ANALYSIS OF BOILER-TURBINE-GENERATOR CONTROLS USING OPTIMAL LINEAR REGULATOR THEORY.
Abstract: The demand for improved dynamic response of fossil-fired power plants has motivated a comprehensive program of control system design and analysis. Previous papers have reported the development of a nonlinear mathematical model of a drum-type, twin furnace, reheat boiler-turbine-generator system which is suitable for control system analysis and has been extensively verified by field test. On the basis of this model, local stability, observability, and controllability have been examined over the load range, using linearization and modal analysis. An approach to control system design has been developed based on optimal linear regulator theory and which recognizes the limitation of an imperfect model. This approach produces ‚Ä≥integral-type‚Ä≥ action which guarantees zero steady-state errors. The controller does not require complete state feedback. Improved performance has been demonstrated by comparison with the existing control structure through simulation using the nonlinear process model.
Name: ["McDonald John P.", "Kwatny Harry G."]

Title: ANALYSIS OF STOCHASTIC STABILITY OF IMPULSE CONTROL SYSTEMS IN A FREQUENCY RANGE.
Abstract: A study is made of impulse systems with pulse-amplitude modulation and randomly varying parameters, both with and without random disturbances. Proofs are given for theorems on the mean-square stability of such systems. These proofs constitute a generalization of the theorems of V. A. Yakubovich to the stochastic case. Frequency criteria for stochastic stability, in the form of stochastic analogs of the frequency criteria of Jury-Lee, are obtained.
Name: ["Tunik A.A.", "Lychak M.M."]

Title: GRADIENT OPTIMIZATION METHODS WITH MEMORY.
Abstract: The author considers methods for developing gradient methods with memory, which are multistep search methods of conjugate directions. In the methods developed, the direction of search at each step is formed as a linear combination of the gradient and the k preceeding search directions, where k is the depth of the memory. The basic properties of these methods are investigated. The quadratic convergence of gradient methods with memory is proved. The results of experimental comparisons of various search methods for the minimization of test functions which simulate a ravine and the presence of perturbations are given.
Name: ["Meleshko V.I."]

Title: Some simple spike separation techniques for simultaneously recorded neurons
Abstract: Segregating the spike trains from two simultaneously recorded neurons can be accomplished by several simple methods involving a laboratory oscilloscope's trigger circuits. The principle of "amplitude discrimination later in the spike waveform" is discussed; simple methods for implementing it on an oscilloscope or a llaboratory computer are presented. The problem of declining spike heights during a burst is discussed, and criteria are presented for maintaining the segregation of such a bursting neuron from other simultaneously recorded neurons. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Calvin W.H."]

Title: An Application of the Minimum Discrimination Information Estimate for Detecting Gaussian Signals
Abstract: The minimum discrimination information estimate is used to compute the log-likelihood ratio, or logarithm of the Radon-Nikodym derivative, when the Gaussian signal has one of two covariance functions. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Melnick E.L."]

Title: TWO-PATTERN RECOGNITION PROBLEM FOR A NOISY CHANNEL, SOLVABLE BY EXTENSIVE GAME THEORY.
Abstract: The two-pattern recognition problem with the possibility of a null situation is investigated. The problem is stated in an extensive game context; the optimal strategies of the observation system are determined, a recognition criterion is found, and the role of the null situation is assessed.
Name: ["Nesteruk V.F.", "Porfir'eva N.N."]

Title: A model for iterative computation
Abstract: Iterative procedures have many advantages for computation; for instance, an approximation to the final answer is provided even if the computation stops abruptly. A model for iterative computation is proposed where a procedure G executed repeatedly "converges" to a function f{hook}. A notion of approximation of functions on the integers is used based on densities. Some results on the power of iteration and iterative extensions are obtained. The relation between iteration and composition is investigated. Heuristic procedures are defined. Many interesting problems remain open. The area is very interesting, since a combination of tools from Analysis and Automata theory can be used. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Tsichritzis D."]

Title: OPTIMAL SEARCH USING TWO NONCONCURRENT SENSORS.
Abstract: Search for a stationary target is considered for a situation in which two sensors are available, but cannot be used simultaneously. The cost (in time) of switching from one sensor to the other is ignored, and each sensor is assumed to have perfect discrimination. For a specified class of searches an optimal allocation of search effort is obtained. In the case of a circular normal prior target location distribution, an example is presented in which one sensor is assumed to have a fixed sweep width and the other a stochastic sweep width. An optimal plan is found for this example. This plan produces an allocation of search effort which is expended in a disk by one sensor and in a bounding annulus by the other.
Name: ["Persinger Carl A."]

Title: Identification and prediction of a class of non-Gaussian time-series via transformation
Abstract: Whereas optimal prediction of Gaussian sequences requires the employment of a linear filter with consistently identifiable parameters and with Gaussian white noise input, the optimal predictor of non-Gaussian sequences is n nonlinear filter, having an independent noise input. Since the latter cannot be identified directly without prior knowledge of the non-linearity, the optimal linear predictor is usually identified where a non-Gaussian white noise input is considered and which is fully optimal only when that input turns out to be independent in all moments. However, if the non-Gaussian sequence is the outcome of a Gaussian sequence passed through a zero memory non-linearity or through non-linear measurement elements, a transformation of the non-Gaussian sequence into a Gaussian one is possible, such that optimal non-linear prediction may be approximated to any required degree, as is shown by the analysis of the present work. Furthermore, the parameters of that predictor may be consistently identified in the absence of any parameter information. ¬© 1973 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Graupe D.", "Krause D.J."]

Title: A simulation model of an information retrieval system
Abstract: This paper describes a simulation model which is used as a tool for designing and evaluating literature searching systems. The simulation program creates a well specified collection of documents and analyzes the effect of changes in query file characteristics on system output performance. First a thesaurus of term relations is generated. Then, employing the thesaurus, routines generate pseudo-documents and pseudo-queries. These pseudo-documents and pseudo-queries are then compared to see the effect of various query file parameter changes on the quantity of material retrieved. Evaluation of the simulation output indicates that there are small differences between the results of the experimental runs. It is concluded that one method for generating pseudo-queries is not clearly better than another. It is believed, however, that the simulation model as an approach to the evaluation of retrieval systems provides a limited but useful framework for the evaluation of information retrieval systems. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Cooper M.D."]

Title: EQUIVALENCE OF MULTIDIMENSIONAL TRANSFORMS AND REVERSION METHODS OF SOLVING NONLINEAR EQUATIONS.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: The multidimensional-transform method and the reversion method of obtaining the respone of nonlinear control systems are compared. It is proved that, for a fairly general class of systems, the reversion method and the transform method not only yield the same solution, but also that the linear approximation and the higher-order approximations to the solution by both the methods are identical. This identification makes it possible to predict the stability of nonlinear systems in the transformed domain under rather restricted conditions.
Name: ["Anjaiah B.", "Reddy D.C."]

Title: Statistical Estimates of Bounded Optical Scenes by the Method of ‚ÄúPrior Probabilities‚Äù
Abstract: A method is developed for producing a maximum-likelihood estimate of an optical object scene that simultaneously is bounded above and below by known radiance levels. The a priori object statistics are assumed unknown and so must be estimated if a maximum-likelihood estimator is to be found. Recourse is made to a counting procedure in the spirit of Jaynes‚Äô [2] approach to estimating a ‚Äúprior probability‚Äù distribution. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Frieden B.R."]

Title: OPTIMIZING CONTROL OF MACHINE TOOL (3RD REPORT, ON-LINE CONTROL OF TOOL LIFE IN TURNING).
Abstract: THE ON-LINE ADAPTIVE CONTROL OF TOOL LIFE IN ORDER TO REALIZE A PREDETERMINED TOOL LIFE FOR A MATERIAL OF WHICH THE TOOL WEAR CHARACTERISTIC IS UNKNOWN HAS BEEN IMPLEMENTED FOR TURNING.THE INCREASE OF TOOL WEAR IS INDIRECTLY DETECTED ON-LINE BY MEANS OF A SPECIALLY DESIGNED CUTTING FORCE DETECTOR.AN INVESTIGATION OF THE DATA PROCESSING, ESPECIALLY OF SAMPLING TIME AND PERIOD OF THE DETECTED DATA, WAS CONDUCTED IN ORDER TO ASSURE COMMERCIALLY JUSTIFIED RELIABILITY OR ACCURACY.ON-LINE DATA ANALYSIS AND CONTROL ARE EXECUTED BY A COMPUTER AND A NUMERICAL CONTROLLER EQUIPPED WITH A SPEED CONTROL SYSTEM.LTHE EXPERIMENT HAS SHOWN THAT THE ADAPTIVE CONTROL OF TURNING OPERATION IN VIEW OF TOOL LIFE CAN BE ACHIEVED BY THE ON-LINE IDENTIFICATION OF TOOL WEAR RATE WHILE SAMPLING THE SIGNALS VIA THE VARIATION OF CUTTING FORCE OVER A SHORT PERIOD.(A).
Name: ["HONDA T.", "TAKEYAMA H.", "SEKIGUCHI H.", "TAKADA K."]

Title: PULSE TRAIN CONTROL OF ELECTRO-HYDRAULIC SERVO-SYSTEMS.
Source: PROC 29TH NAT. CONF. ON FLUID POWER (ILLINOIS INST. OF TECHNOL., CHICAGO, U.S.A.)
Abstract: IN THIS PAPER, A COMPUTER-CONTROLLED POSITION STEPPING SYSTEM USING AN ELECTRO-HYDRAULIC SERVOVALVE AND A HYDRAULIC MOTOR IS DESCRIBED.A MINICOMPUTER IS USED AS A CONTROLLER WHICH GENERATES ACCURATELY-TIMED TRAINS OF PULSES THAT ARE SENT TO THE POSITION STEPPING MOTORS IN ORDER TO ACHIEVE BOTH POSITIONING AND CONTINUOUS-PATH CONTROL.THE FEATURES OF THE SYSTEM AND THE RESULTS OF ACCURACY TESTS FOR BOTH POSITIONING AND CONTOURING ARE PRESENTED.
Name: ["POO A.N."]

Title: SPEECH RECOGNITION.
Abstract: A sophisticated computer facility is being used to study speech and develop word recognition algorithms. The approach is unique in that it does not require modified procedures for recognizing different speakers or new vocabularies. Consisting of a hierarchy of tests, the recognition process starts with the most certain speech elements and progresses to more difficult ones.
Name: ["Medress Mark F."]

Title: Synthesis of an Optimal System of Control of a Closed-Circle Plant. | [SINTEZ OPTIMAL'NOI SISTEMY UPRAVLENIYA OB''EKTOM S ZAMKNUTYM TSIKLOM.]
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii, Gornyi Zhurnal
Abstract: Plants with recirculations of substances are among the most widespread units in industry. It is known that such installations are not easy to automate, and quite frequently the required quality of control by means of standard regulators cannot be ensured. For this reason, the problem of controlling such processes is topical at present. A Bayes' problem is considered of optimal control of plants with closed cycles in the presence of random noise in the feedback channel on the basis of the theory of dual control. An overall minimum for the given functional is achieved by means of parametric minimization. The algorithm for an optimal regulator in a discrete and a continuous variant is obtained when the plant is acted upon by a disturbance in the form of a Markovian random process for the case when the control signal is limited with respect to the modulus.
Name: ["Khainish S.V."]

Title: Tutor-A Turing machine simulator
Abstract: TUTOR is a high speed Turing machine simulator, written in IBM System 360 Assembler Language. Turing machines are represented by flow diagrams using H. Hernes table of machines as the basic elements. Composite machines so represented may themselves be used as elements of other machines, thus incorporating the concept of subroutines. In this paper the relationship of a flow diagram to the basic concept of a Turing machine is developed, the functions of the basic machines are described, and a complete programmer's guide is included. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Pierce J.C.", "Singletary W.E.", "Vander Mey J.E."]

Title: OPTIMAL CONTROL FOR A CERTAIN CLASS OF DISTRIBUTED PARAMETER SYSTEMS.
Source: J Inst Eng (India), Electron Telecommun Eng Div
Abstract: The problem of optimal control is considered for a certain class of distributed parametric system with a constraint on the spatial derivative of the response. Using approximation theory it has been shown that the optimal control exists and a simple method has been suggested for it computation.
Name: ["Agarwal D.C."]

Title: An Algorithm for Nonsupervised Pattern Classification
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: An algorithm for classifying a data set into an initially unknown number of categories is presented. It is composed of a procedure for selecting initial points, a mode estimation procedure, and a classification rule. An integer valued function is defined on the sample space and a gradient search technique is used for estimating its modes. A procedure for mode estimation in the case of an infinite data set is also proposed. Sufficient conditions for the convergence to the neighborhood of the modes have been stated. The algorithm was used for clustering multicategory artificially generated data sets and was compared with an optimal classification scheme. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gitman I."]

Title: Standard Operations of Data Processing - A Methodical Concept for the Development and Realization of Automated Data Processing Systems. | [STANDARDOPERATIONEN DER INFORMATIONSVERARBEITUNG ALS EIN METHODISCHES KONZEPT BEI DER ENTIWCKLUNG UND REALISIERUNG VON ASIV.]
Source: Wissenschaftliche Zeitschrift der Technischen Unversitat Dresden
Abstract: A methodical concept for creating parts of technological system foundations for an automated data processing system (ADPS) to deal with information processes in the management processes is presented. It is assumed from the beginning that research into the principles, oriented towards realization of ADPS, would immediately yield useful contributions to the rationalization of data processing.
Name: ["Belke Wolfgang"]

Title: On the application of the fuzzy sets separation theorem for automatic classification in information retrieval systems
Abstract: This paper deals with a new clustering technique using the concept of fuzzy set introduced by Zadeh. A cluster is defined as a subset characterized by a membership function which associates with each element a real number in the unit interval. A membership function is proposed and a method to select the cluster elements is derived using the separation theorem of the fuzzy sets. The clusters obtained by this way are controlled overlapping groupings. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Negoit«é C.V."]

Title: N-fold fuzzy grammars
Abstract: A new form of fuzzy grammar, which is called an n-fold fuzzy grammar, is defined and some of its properties are investigated. The n-fold fuzzy grammars are a generalization of fuzzy grammars defined by Lee and Zadeh, where the grade of application of the rule to be used next is conditioned by the n(‚â•1) rules used before in a derivation. The n-fold fuzzy grammars whose rules are of context-free form can be shown to generate context-sensitive languages by setting a threshold appropriately. Fuzzy grammars by Lee and Zadeh with context-free rules, however, cannot generate context-sensitive languages. As to n-fold fuzzy grammars, we mainly focused our attention on n-fold fuzzy grammars with type 3 rules as a preliminary step. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Mizumoto M.", "Toyoda J.", "Tanaka K."]

Title: Time Bounds on Space Computations
Abstract: A physicomathematical basis is used to establish bounds TD(n) on the time needed to compute n-argument functions by spatially distributed primitive devices or composite systems D. The axioms used concern the speed, packing density, and noisethreshold of the energy with which any computing device detects or alters the physical representation of information. The principal result is that TD(n) grows at least as n1/3. Composite systems consisting of spatially distributed identical components are examined in light of this bound. Inherent bounds on the computing time of n-argument functions are then combined with TD(n), resulting in a measure of computational efficiency which bounds computing time to processor size. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Dertouzos M.L."]
Keywords: ["complexity of space-time computations", "energybased axioms for space-time tradeoffs", "time bounds on space computations", "computations physicomathematical", "space computations"]

Title: Learning of Fuzzy Formal Language
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A learning model of fuzzy formal language is proposed and discussed. We continue training the learning machine by giving sets of sentences sequentially. As a result of parsing of the given teaching sentences, the learning machine reinforces fuzzy grades of membership of productions in an inherent fuzzy grammar of the machine. The convergence of the proposed model is considered, and it is shown that the grades of membership of desired productions are intensified by choosing an adequate teaching sequence of the sentence set. Furthermore, a concept of ‚Äústrongly equivalent,‚Äù in which two grammars are not distinguished by any teaching sequence, is introduced. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Tamura S.", "Tanaka K."]

Title: Optimal control of linear stochastic systems with applications to time lag systems
Abstract: Optimal control of linear stochastic systems of general type, perturbed by a stochastic process with independent increments, is considered. The performance functional is quadratic, and various different types of observation processes, providing either complete or incomplete information about the system, are discussed. It is shown that (with the conditions imposed) the optimal control is linear in the observed data and can be determined by solving a deterministic problem with a similar dynamic structure. These results are applied to the control of linear stochastic functional differential equations, both with complete and incomplete state information. In the latter case, a separation theorem is shown to be valid: The problem is decomposed into the corresponding deterministic control problem and a problem of estimation. The optimal feedback solution of the deterministic problem is derived. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Lindquist A."]
Affiliations: [' Systems Theory The Royal Institute of Technology']

Title: OPTIMAL OBSERVATION OF LINEAR PLANTS WHOSE DYNAMIC PROPERTIES ARE KNOWN.
Abstract: The paper is concerned with determination of the state components in the case of measurements of output and control signals of the plant with errors. The optimal operators have been considered, which in the case of least favorable measurement errors give a minimal value of error of component to be defined. Particularly a case of signal measurement with errors which differ from each other has been considered. It has been shown that optimal operators are certain linear operators. The way of selecting these optimal operators from linear operators has been also shown. Namely it has been proved that for all cases which are considering the so-called mini-max principle preserve its validity. Other theorems which can help to select optimal operators are formulated.
Name: ["Gessing R."]

Title: Optimization of the Sampling Period of Discrete Models of Continuous Plants. | [OPTYMALIZACJA OKRESU PROBKOWANIA DYSKRETNYCH MODELI OBIEKTOW CIAGLYCH.]
Abstract: A continuous linear dynamic plant with known autocorrelation function of an input signal. The accuracy of modeling is characterized by the variance of the simulation error. It is shown how the simulation error variance depends on the input signal autocorrelation function and the cross-correlation function between input and output signals. A detailed solution is given for the simulation of the first order time lag system. It is assumed that its input signal is generated by the first order filter excited by white noise. The following plots are given: the simulation error variance versus sampling peiod, optimal sampling period versus the order of a model, minimal simulation error variance versus the order of a model for different input signals. In conclusion, a warning is given against choosing too small sampling period.
Name: ["Arczewska Wanda", "Manczak Kazimierz"]

Title: Combined System of Automatic Control of Mine Hoists. | [KOMBINIROVANNAYA SISTEMA AVTOMATICHESKOGO REGULIROVANIYA SHAKHTNYKH POD ‚Ä≥EMNYKH MASHIN.]
Abstract: An analysis of disturbances acting on a mine hoist installation is carried out. Possible ways of designing combined automatic control systems localizing the main disturbances are shown. Principles of formation of the braking moment under various conditions of operation of the hoisting installation are set forth. A functional circuit of the automatic control system is given.
Name: ["Popovich N.G."]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR INTEGER LINEAR PROGRAMMING - A COMBINED ALGEBRAIC AND ENUMERATION APPROACH.
Abstract: An algorithm was developed for integer programming problems. It transforms the integer programming problem to an algebrically equivalent C. Hermite canonical problem, and then employs the J. Fourier-T. S. Motzkin eliminajtion. These algebraic operations transform the problem into a form that leads to an efficient implicit enumeration scheme to calculate an optimal solution.
Name: ["Bradley Gordon H.", "Wahi Pran N."]

Title: Application of the Lyapunov Function for the Study of the Convergence of Unconstrained Minimization Methods. | ZASTOSOWANIE FUNKCJI LAPUNOWA DO BADANIA ZBIEZNOSCI METOD MINIMALIZACJI BEZ OGRANICZEN.
Abstract: Algorithms are defined as discrete dynamic systems and convergence criteria are derived via the second method of Lyapunov. It is shown that methods of static optimization making use of linear search belong to this class of algorithms. Formerly obtained convergence theorems are adapted for these methods. Some methods using gradient evaluation are found to be convergent even if the minimized function is not unimodal on every straight line, provided that during the linear search the local minimum closest to the starting point is found. Some of the results can be generalized for the case of Hilbert spaces.
Name: ["Kurcyusz Stanislaw"]

Title: Some Methods of Identification in Closed-Loop Systems. | O NEKOTORYKH METODAKH IDENTIFIKATSII V ZAMKNUTNYKH SISTEMAKH.
Abstract: Methods of elimination of displacement when identifying the parameters of a plant in a closed-loop control system are considered. Convergence and accuracy of the algorithms are analyzed. Results of experiments are presented.
Name: ["Perel'muter V.M."]

Title: A process for reducing duster representations and retrieval costs
Source: Proceedings of the Annual ACM Conference, ACM 1973
Abstract: This centroid vector reduction process produces vectors which require substantially less storage space than those vectors produced by previous approaches. Furthermore, this decrease in vector length significantly reduces the time required to calculate correlation measures with query vectors. Additionally, these savings in time and storage are gained without adversely affecting retrieval effectiveness. The reduction of the processing time of the basic correlation comparison operation strongly affects the retrieval costs of searching a large clustered file in an online document retrieval system. In such an environment the response time of the system to the user's query plays a major role in overall system performance. As the time per query-document correlation increases due to increased information in the centroid representations, the number of comparisons possible per unit time decreases. Thus, to achieve financially feasible retrieval from, large collections with response times fast enough for an online environment, while still maintaining satisfactory recall-precision levels, a centroid vector reduction process not only becomes necessary but assumes a critical role. The process described in this paper is an important asset to the clustered file organization. However, the desirability of clustered file organizations for information retrieval systems can be further enhanced by reducing the time required to retrieve from secondary memory those documents associated with the clusters whose centroids exhibit sufficiently high correlations with the user's query. To reduce this time the clusters to be retrieved must be arranged a priori in an optimal fashion in external storage. Although work has been initiated in this area for nonoverlapping clusters [5], an investigation of the relation between the homogeneity of clusters and their physical proximity in secondary storage is being undertaken for the more realistically feasible case of overlapping clusters. ¬© 1973 Association for Computing Machinery, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Crouch D.B."]

Title: A Dimensionality Reducing Model for Distributed Filtering
Abstract: The necessity of filtering noisy data generated by multidimensional processes arises in many diverse settings. The direct application of the Kalman-Bucy results is hindered by dimensionality difficulties inherent in multidimensional problems. This paper shows that for linear steady-state problems significant dimensionality reductions can be accomplished, thus making routine the solution of many interesting problems. ¬© 1973 IEEE
Name: ["Angel E.", "Jain A.K."]

Title: Minimum-Bias Windows for High-Resolution Spectral Estimates
Abstract: The class of window pairs w(t) ‚Üî W(œâ) is considered such that w(t) = 0 for |t| > M and W(œâ) ‚â• 0. It is shown that in this class, the window (ommited formula) yields spectral estimates with minimum bias. Furthermore, the variance of the resulting estimate is smaller than that obtained with the known windows of the same size. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Papoulis A."]

Title: Application of Hybrid Computers. | [HYBRIDRECHNERANWENDUNGEN.]
Source: Wissenschaftliche Zeitschrift der Technischen Unversitat Dresden
Abstract: After some fundamental remarks on hybrid computer technology, its typical applications are indicated. Especially, the solution of problems from the theory of optimal processes by means of hybrid computers is considered. The basis for the solution is Pontryagin's maximum principle which is particularly suited for processing on a hybrid computer. After a general formulation of the maximum principle, various search algorithms for the unknown initial conditions of the adjoint variables are compared for a linear time-optimal problem.
Name: ["Knoefel Siegfried"]

Title: Improving the m-Path Search Procedure. | VERBESSERUNG DES m-WEG-SUCHVERFAHRENS.
Abstract: Considering linear lists with items ordered by keys m-way searching is a known searching technique. to minimize the average number of search operations the linear list is usually divided into distinct blocks containing a constant number of items such that the block dsize is equal to the number of blocks. In this paper another choice for the size of the blocks is proposed which minimizes the average searching time without increasing the programming effort.
Name: ["Six H.W."]

Title: COMPUTER ALGORITHM FOR ROUTING OVERSIZED TRUCKS.
Abstract: The basic input to the algorithm consists of the network description in terms of speed and distance on constituent links, and in addition, the height and weight limits on each link, and the height and weight of the truck to be routed between specified origins and destinations. The algorithm computes the minimum time path on the basic network or on the residual network subsequent to removal of all links having an allowable height and weight less than the corresponding parameters for the truck to be routed.
Name: ["Pant Shiva K.", "Wegmann Frederick J."]

Title: SIMPLE ALGORITHM FOR COST OPTIMIZATION OF A THREE DECISION VARIABLE SYSTEM.
Abstract: To illustrate the use of the algorithm described a three-stage wastewater treatment plant is optimized. The same algorithm can be used to optimize any three decision variable problem. To show its versatility it is used to illustrate the optimization of a trickling filter using the Eckenfelder equation.
Name: ["Ordon Chester J."]

Title: On the Solution of a Matrix Equation in the Theory of Luenberger Observers
Abstract: An explicit solution is presented for a matrix equation involved in the design of a Luenberger observer to realize an acceptable approximation to a desired state-variable feedback law u = uo + Kx for the system dx/dt = Ax + Bu, y = Dx. ¬© 1973 IEEE
Name: ["Power H.M."]

Title: Tan-Like State Assignments for Synchronous Sequential Machines
Abstract: Recently, Tan developed a heuristic state assignment algorithm for asynchronous sequential machines. In this paper a state assignment algorithm based on Tan's is developed for synchronous sequential machines. It shares with Tan's algorithm the advantages of simplicity of execution and economy of logic elements in the resulting realizations. Copyright ¬© 1973 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Curtis H.A."]
Keywords: ["logic circuit realizations", "state assignment algorithms", "synchronous sequential machines", "algorithm asynchronous", "assignments synchronous"]

Title: TECHNIQUE FOR THE SOLUTION OF MASSIVE SET COVERING PROBLEMS, WITH APPLICATION TO AIRLINE CREW SCHEDULING.
Abstract: Method of attack by using a set covering algorithm repeatedly on much smaller matrices extracted from the overall problem is outlined. Approach has been used on an airline crew-scheduling problem, with good practical success on test cases involving close to 1000 rows.
Name: ["Rubin Jerrold"]

Title: ON AN ASYMPTOTIC PROPERTY OF THE LEAST-MEAN-SQUARE-ERROR DESIGN CRITERION IN PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: A wide theoretical justification is given to the use of the so-called least-mean-square-error design criterion in pattern recognition. It is shown that the least-mean-square error yields an upper bound on the error probability of the Bayesian decision rule. The tightness of the bound is discussed. Practical consequences are considered from the viewpoint of the feature-selection and -ordering problem.
Name: ["Devijver P.A."]

Title: COMPUTER METHODS OF DIPLOG CORRELATION.
Abstract: This paper presents an automatic diplog processing system that incorporates several new techniques and allows alternative processing paths. The rationale for selecting the product-moment method as the primary correlation technique is given and the algorithm for variable window-length correlation and infinite-clip methods are discussed. Several approaches to grading and screening of picks to improve the appearance of the machine-ocorrelated diplogs are also examined. The derivation of flexible vector analysis equations for dip calculation is presented.
Name: ["Schoonover L.G.", "Holt O.R."]

Title: Extraction d'invariants morphologiques d'une information par correlation optique et filtrage spatial
Abstract: The set of characters on a page of text may be described as a two-dimensional random distribution of morphological constants (linguistic data and spread function of the writer) to which a gaussian noise is superimposed. Processing the whole page by using optical correlation and spatial filtering techniques allow one to extract these constants, thus supplying a recognition test of the writer. The general principles are explained, and the distinction of two type writer founts is experimentally verified. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Duvernoy J."]

Title: Algorithm for Automatic Layout of Printed Boards in Two Steps Using Threaded Lists. | [EINZWEISTUFIGES VERFAHREN ZUM AUTOMATISCHEN ENTFLECHTEN VON LEITERPLATTEN MIT GEFAEDELTEN LISTEN.]
Abstract: A program for wiring layout of printed boards is reported. The program is used as part of a comprehensive system for automated design of digital networks. Applied algorithms, spectrum of applicability, and performance of the program are discussed.
Name: ["Rottmann W.", "Lang O.", "Pfadler W."]

Title: A theory of discrete patterns and their implementation in SNOBOL4
Abstract: The notion of a discrete pattern is formalized and certain properties deduced. A pattern is shown to be a generalization of a formal language. Algorithms for implementing the kinds of patterns in SNOBOL4 are given. The general approach is to create, in-so-far as possible, a bottom-up parse from a top-down specification. ¬© 1973, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gimpel J.F."]

Title: TECHNICAL CONTRIBUTIONS FINDING NEGATIVE CYCLES.
Abstract: A simple transformation on the distances associated with edges incident to a vertex is used as a basis for locating negative cycles in a directed graph. Computational experiments indicate that it is faster than several potentially competitive methods when used as a subroutine in an assignment problem algorithm proposed by M. Klein. The transformation may also be used to convert a graph into one with nonnegative edges provided the graph has no negative cycles.
Name: ["Klein M.", "Tibrewala R.K."]

Title: An analog computer study of fast, isolated movements
Abstract: The peripheral part of the motor control system is modelled on an analog computer. The model consists of an inertial load connected to an antagonistic muscle pair with their muscle spindles and neural connexions. It has Œ± inputs as well as Œ≥ inputs. The model is used for studying the hypothesis that simple on-off activities control fast isolated movements. It is found that the model responses on activation of the Œ≥ input alone are not realistic ones. A fair simulation may be obtained if the Œ± input and the Œ≥ input are activated simultaneously. Results suggest a diminished muscle spindle sensitivity during the movement. ¬© 1973 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Dijkstra Sj.", "van der Gon Denier J.J."]

Title: SEARCH FOR DEFECTS IN COMPLEX CONTROLLED SYSTEMS.
Source: Telecommunications and Radio Engineering (English translation of Elektrosvyaz and Radiotekhnika)
Abstract: The existing methods of searching for defects were developed mainly for relatively simple controlled systems. The search for defects in complex systems which consist of a large number of functionally related units, such as, for example, switching apparatus and other discrete automatic devices, is a problem of independent interest and is considered in this paper. First, the search principle is discussed. Then, the method of analysis of the controlled system is described, as well as synthesis of logical search systems. An example of a controlled system consisting of eleven elements which are placed on three removable modules is considered. A logical diagram is realized which can pinpoint the module containing the defective element.
Name: ["Garkusha I.I."]

Title: A perturbation method for the analysis of impulse propagation in a mathematical neuron model
Abstract: A perturbation method is presented for the calculation of signal propagation velocities in a mathematical neuron model. Impulse frequencies and waveforms are also determined. The method uses a non-linear conduction model containing a small parameter, such that analytical solutions are possible, yet the inherently non-linear physiological phenomena involved, can be explained. A simple two-variable membrane equation is used, but the method is generally applicable to various more complete systems. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Noldus E."]

Title: Optimal trees for a class of information retrieval problems
Abstract: A review is given of the use of doubly-chained trees for information retrieval. It is shown that for several reasons related to the actual implementation of such a scheme and to properties of functions related to the retrieval process, the chaining steps, by which expected search time is measured, may be of different cost depending upon whether the step is vertical (equal compare result) or horizontal (unequal compare result). Since previous results are for equal cost steps, the problem of constructing an optimal retrieval tree under the new circumstances is formulated mathematically and a very rapid solution procedure is given. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Stanfel L.E."]

Title: Central regulation of temperature in cold environments. I. A dynamic model with two temperature inputs
Abstract: A preoptic-hypothalamic network representing neural regulation of temperature in cold-stressed animals has been modeled using CSMP (a program for real time processes). The calculated outputs of this model can be readily compared with experimental data, and the neural regulator can be integrated with other homeostatic regulators. The calculated outputs consist of signals for activating shivering and nonshivering heat production as two inputs, hypothalamic and cutaneous temperature, are varied in time. To simulate the effect of a pyrogen-induced fever, a parameter in the model is varied to alter the temperature sensitivity of one class of hypothalamic neurons. Finally, calculations are included to allow a critical comparison of this model with other thermoregulatory models for cold-stressed animals. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Horowitz J.M.", "Erskine L.K."]
Affiliations: ['Department of Animal Physiology University of California']

Title: THRESHOLD SIGNALS IN MOVING TARGET SELECTION SYSTEMS WITH AMPLITUDE LIMITING.
Source: Telecommunications and Radio Engineering (English translation of Elektrosvyaz and Radiotekhnika)
Abstract: Moving target selection systems with amplitude limiting are analyzed by statistical modeling on a computer. The efficiency of such a system is compared with that of a similar system without limiting.
Name: ["Popov D.I."]

Title: VISIBILITY OF STRUCTURED AND UNSTRUCTURED IMAGES.
Abstract: Two experiments were made to study a model of the human visual system operating near threshold. A grain modulation transfer function using unstructured grain images is defined as the reciprocal modulation required to just see a grain image of a given spatial frequency. The visual system is 1/25 as sensitive to this as to the sine wave modulation transfer function. Results of the experiments are consistent with a simple multichannel linear model.
Name: ["Greenwood Robert E."]

Title: Strong Consistency of an Estimate of the - Asymptotic Error Probability of the Nearest Neighbor Rule
Abstract: Let R be the asymptotic error probability of the nearest neighbor rule (NNR). A particular estimate of R from n-classified samples, known to converge to R in probability as n increases to infinity, is shown to actually converge with probability 1 to R whenever the NNR itself converges with probability 1. ¬© 1973, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Wolverton C.T."]

Title: Near-optimal control of high-order systems using low-order models
Abstract: This paper considers the use of low-order models for the determination of an approximate optimal control of a high-order system. For a number of such models of a given system, derived using different methods, the approximate optimal control input is calculated. The result of the application of these inputs to the system is compared with the actual optimum. It is shown that optimum low-order models provide a near-optimal control, which may serve as a good first approximation to the optimum. Together with a suitable scheme for on-line identification these models may be used effectively for adaptive control. ¬© 1973 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Sinha N.K.", "De Bruin H."]

Title: Time-Dependent Boolean Functions and Their Realization. | VREMENNYE BULEVY FUNKTSII I IKH REALIZATSIYA.
Abstract: Time-dependent Boolean functions of two variables x and t are considered. On their basis mathematical description of timing operators by another set are presented. These Boolean functions are realized in the simplest manner on R, C elements and semiconductor logical elements. For this reason realization of timing relay devices, whose synthesis is accomplished by using time Boolean functions, is given only on these elements.
Name: ["Polyakov V.E.", "Trotsenko A.A."]

Title: Principles of automatic analysis of sleep records with a hybrid system
Abstract: A program for automatic sleep staging of whole nights polygraphic records of human subjects is described. The electronic system consists of an analog component, performing a first reduction of data, and a digital one, a small general purpose computer. The computer program assesses first the technical quality of the record, by recognition of artefacts, which may impair the diagnosis procedure. It performs second a two steps analysis, based upon electroencephalogram, muscle activity and eye movements. The first step of analysis is a recognition of elementary patterns on the tape and the second step is a calculation of a minute by minute sleep stage diagnosis, based upon these elementary patterns. This program has been tested by comparisons with human scoring of the same records, and has proved to have a good accuracy. This system is actually used as a clinical tool in the exploration of sleep disturbances. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Gaillard J.M.", "Tissot R."]

Title: An Adaptive Estimation Algorithm for Time-Varying Bit Synchronizers
Source: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
Abstract: This paper presents an adaptive estimation algorithm for bit synchronization, assuming that the parameters of the incoming data process are time varying. The data are linearly related to the state variable to be determined. By employing the Gauss-Markov theorem, the optimal recursive estimate (including the nonstationary property of the system), which is a matrix operation on the transformed data, is obtained.
