The theoretical analysis of the behavior of the adaptive loop was performed with the aid of the analog computer MEDA 81T, and the obtained oscillograph records are presented.
Name: ["Kazmierkowski Marian Piotr"]

Title: USE OF GENERALIZED PERFORMANCE CHARACTERISTIC OF HUMAN OPERATOR IN ESTIMATING THE EFFICIENCY OF ERGATIC CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: It is suggested that the generalized performance characteristic of a human operator be used for quantitative estimation of the efficiency of ergatic systems. This does not require the development of special mathematical methods.
Name: ["Meleshev A.M.", "Pavlov V.V."]

Title: RECURSIVE SHORT-TERM LOAD-FORECASTING ALGORITHM.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: The problem of forecasting the integrated-load demand of an interconnected power system is studied. It is proposed that the harmonic-series model for the weekly load pattern be expressed in the state-variable form. This then permits the use of Kalman-filtering techniques, for load-prediction purposes. It is shown that this approach leads to an improvement in the forecasting reliability, without increasing the online computational requirements. The results of a particular study are presented.
Name: ["Sharma K.L.S.", "Mahalanabis A.K."]

Title: Image processing in pathology. I. Fundamentals of the procedures | AUTOMATISCHE BILDVERARBEITUNG IN DER PATHOLOGIE. I. ALLGEMEINE METHODISCHE GRUNDLAGEN
Abstract: This paper presents the mathematical foundations for the application of automatic image processing in pathology. Problems of image preprocessing, object features, group arrangements and classification are discussed. A review of the literature concerned with the subject is presented. Based on the fundamentals described, concrete material (liver sections, electron microscopic photograms, and smears of the cervix uteri) are analysed.
Name: ["Arnold F.", "Kunze K.D.", "Meyer W.", "Voss K.", "Weber K.H.", "Simon H."]

Title: Arithmetical operations performed by nerve cells
Abstract: A simple neurone model is constructed and analysed mathematically to see what types of operation it can perform on its synaptic inputs. The neurone consists essentially of a soma together with semi-infinite dendrite. Provided their conductance changes are sufficiently small, excitatory synapses are linearly additive and inhibitory synapses are linearly subtractive, irrespective of location. Inhibitory synapses, producing large conductance changes and located preferably on the soma, are ideally suited to carry out division. The extension of this model to the more complex situation of branching dendritic trees is briefly examined and its relevance to real nerve cells is discussed. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Blomfield S."]

Title: THEORETICAL FOUNDATIONS OF INFORMATION RETRIEVAL SYSTEM DESIGN.
Abstract: The basic character of the theoretical foundations of information retrieval system design, still a matter of controversy, can be described in a general way once the distinction has been made between reference retrieval and data retrieval. It is suggested that the underlying theory of reference retrieval is probability theory, while the theoretical underpinnings of data retrieval involve a combination of numerical computation, deductive logic, and linguistics.
Name: ["Cooper W.S."]

Title: An Economical Hardware Realization of a Digital Linear Predictive Speech Synthesizer
Abstract: Speech analysis/synthesis algorithms utilizing linear prediction coefficients have certain advantages over those employing formant-based techniques. For example, 4-kHz speech samples may be synthesized using a basic sequence of 10 multiply/adds followed by a single addition of the current sample of the excitation function. Real-time software synthesis of 4-kHz speech is possible (using this technique) on certain 16-b minicomputers, but the central processing unit (CPU) overhead may approach 100 percent. We describe an economical (<600-dollar) hardware realization of a 4-kHz digital linear predictive speech synthesizer which requires, at most, a CPU overhead of about 40 percent real time. The device is constructed of standard TTL/MOS logic and consists (essentially) of a high speed 2's complement multiplier/adder capable of calculating a 26-b product (l0-b speech samples, 16-b coefficients) in 0.33 ¬µs, and a dual shift register. In addition, a procedure is discussed which enables the device to be used both as a formant synthesizer for vowels or voiced consonant production, and as a predictive synthesizer for other speech sounds. This procedure, hybrid synthesis, permits the utilization of formant concatenation techniques and reduces the coefficient storage required to specify vowels/voiced consonants by about 60 percent. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Gough M.J.", "Morris L.R."]

Title: AUTOMATIC CONTROL OF END-EXPIRATORY CARBON DIOXIDE.
Abstract: The design of a computer controlled system for precise manipulation of inhaled carbon dioxide on a breath-to-breath basis. The system incorporates a closed-loop servo-controlled breathing chamber and a digital computer. The chamber control loop consists of a CO//2 analyzer, a servo motor, and a CO//2 inlet valve and yields a 90% response time under 1. 5 seconds. Thus, all chamber concentration changes can be made while the subject exhales. Commands for the desired chamber CO//2 concentration are dictated to the chamber loop by a digital computer via a digital-to-analog converter. The flexibility offered by this type of system enables the experimental control of a subject's end-tidal CO//2 by means of a second control loop with the digital computer as the controlling element. A basic computer control algorithm is discussed and preliminary results are presented.
Name: ["Ward Denham S.", "Michels David B.", "Swanson George D.", "Bellville J.Weldon"]

Title: Automatic Detection of Crack Initiation in a Fatigue Test. | [DETECTION AUTOMATIQUE DE LA PREMIERE FISSURATION AU COURS D'UN ESSAI DE FATIGUE.]
Abstract: A method is described which makes it possible to easily detect initial cracking by direct strobomicroscopic observation. Based on this method, an automatic technique is derived which makes unnecessary continuous checking and allows accurate detection of all early minute cracks which cannot be detected by any classical method.
Name: ["Ledocq J."]

Title: VARIATIONAL METHOD FOR APPROXIMATING THE RESPONSE OF NONLINEAR STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A method is introduced for determining approximate properties of the response of nonlinear stochastic systems. The method is based in concept on the variational methods of mechanics and allows the consideration of classes of systems not readily subject to analysis by existing techniques. Three examples are presented illustrating the application to nonlinear systems with non-stationary inputs, non-Gaussian inputs and with time delay. The main limitation of the technique is the necessity for assuming a meaningful form for the approximate solution in terms of arbitrary random variables.
Name: ["Zirkle L.D.", "Clark L.G."]

Title: OPTIMAL CONTROL ALGORITHM WITH TRANSPORTATION DELAY.
Abstract: A practical approach to implementing a linearized model with transportation delay to simulate industrial process dynamics is discussed. The model is derived from quadratic performance criteria from optimum control theory, and the literature must be consulted for derivation detail. The objective is to show how such a model may be modified to accommodate practical restrictions such as control input limits and unmeasurable disturbances.
Name: ["Lin C.S."]

Title: DYNAMIC MODELING AND CONTROL OF SOME CONGESTION-PRONE SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A new way of modeling the behavior of a congestion-prone system by a nonlinear differential equation is introduced. The use of the model in determining optimal operating policies for such a system is discussed.
Name: ["Agnew Carson E."]

Title: ANALOG ADAPTIVE CONTROLLER FOR ON-LINE IDENTIFICATION AND CONTROL OF A FIRST-ORDER PROCESS WITH TIME-VARYING GAIN.
Abstract: A simple and practical adaptive controller was described for on-line gain identification and control of a first-order flow process with time-varying gain and with pure delay present in the measurement of the control variable. An identification system is used in series with the main process and the identification is essentially based on the fact that the system input being fixed, the time taken for the control variable to go from one preselected value to another is inversely proportional to the system gain. The controller can be fully implemented on a moderate size analog computer with patchable logic. It identifies the gain without disturbing the normal operation of the plant.
Name: ["Gupta Surendra R.", "Coughanowr Donald R."]

Title: A record oriented, grammar driven data translation model
Source: Proceedings of the ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data
Abstract: The Data Translation problem is the problem of translating data from one computer stored form into another, either with or without changing its original logical structure. A lot of work have been established in this field, but most of them are geared to the data encountered in the commercial and business environment. Another kind of data, namely the self-defining data which is very common in the humanities data processing environment, has received very little consideration. This paper examines both and proposes an unifying approach-a top down grammar driven method-to the generalized data translation problem. ¬© 1974 ACM.
Name: ["Liu S.", "Heller J."]
Affiliations: [' State University of New York at Stony Brook']

Title: ON THE SET OF OPTIMAL CONTROLS FOR MARKOV CHAINS WITH REWARDS.
Abstract: On the base of a recurrence formula for the expected reward of a finite Markov chain (that is, an extension of Laurent expansion for expected discounted reward, as well as the recurrence relation for expected nondiscounted reward), necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for controlled Markov chains with sensitive discounted and sensitive averaging criteria are established. Employing the obtained optimality conditions criterion equivalence between these two types of optimality criteria is shown.
Name: ["Sladky Karel"]

Title: A study of response times under various deadlock algorithms and job schedulers
Source: Proceedings of the 1974 Annual ACM Conference, ACM 1974
Abstract: A trace-driven model is used to study the effects of various schedulers and deadlock control algorithms, and their interactions, on response times in a general-purpose operating system. Jobs' requests for memory and processors are extracted from a production load and used to drive a detailed simulation program. The simulation results show that response time is more sensitive than CPU utilization to differences between schedulers and deadlock control algorithms. Preemptive scheduling improves response time but degrades CPU utilization. Preemptive deadlock control algorithms improve both measures of performance. There are significant interactions between schedulers and deadlock control algorithms. Deadlock control algorithms can not be expected to optimize resource utilization. 1974 ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Sherman S.W.", "Howard J.H., Jr.", "Browne J.C."]
Affiliations: ['Institute for Computer Applications in Science and Engineering', 'University of Texas at Austin']

Title: METHODS OF ESTIMATING THE CORRECTING CAPACITY OF FUNCTIONS OF THE ALGEBRA OF LOGIC.
Abstract: Methods of analyzing the correcting capacity of functions of the algebra of logic are described. The apparatus of discrete functional transformations is used to estimate this capacity on the set of arithmetic and nonarithmetic errors. Certain classes of Boolean functions are examined from the point of view of their correcting capacity for errors of given multiplicity.
Name: ["Karpovskiy M.G.", "Moskalev E.S.", "Troyanovskiy A.A."]

Title: PROBABILISTIC MODEL OF INVENTORY CONTROL WITH A RECURRENT FLOW OF CLIENT'S ORDERS OF RANDOM SIZE.
Abstract: In the model under consideration, the demand for individual articles of a single type is described by an accumulation process, in which the instants at which the clients' orders are placed form a recurrent flow, and the sizes of these orders constitute mutually independent random variables with the same distribution. To replenish the inventory, the warehouse places vendor's orders in accordance with policy of two levels. All vendor's orders are filled with a constant lag. A stationary distribution is found for the inventory level, and an explicit expression is found for the stationary rate of operating expenditures.
Name: ["Rubal'skiy G.B."]

Title: EXTREMAL, OPTIMAL, ADAPTIVE, AND SELF-ADJUSTING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A design method is proposed for an efficient control system of a complex queueing process. It consists in building up the structure of the system through suboptimal levels (according to the criterion of minimum losses).
Name: ["Zaychenko Yu.P.", "Pechurin M.K."]

Title: ON THE STABILITY OF AUTOMATIC CONTROL SYSTEMS WITH RANDOM STATIONARY PARAMETERS.
Abstract: The authors determine the stability regions, and confidence intervals for a given confidence probability, in the plane of two random parameters of the ACS (the synthesis problem). They also propose a method for determination of the probability of stable operation of the system for a given set of numerical characteristics of the random parameters, including those used to construct the stability region (the analysis problem). In order to estimate the scattering field of the stability boundaries, a method is used which is based on consideration of the coupling moments of the random parameters in a series expansion of the system solution, which is applicable to both linear and nonlinear systems.
Name: ["Glikman B.F.", "Lintsov Ye.A.", "Solov'ev V.V."]

Title: FAULT TOLERANT CELLULAR SPACES.
Abstract: The following problem is treated: When an arbitrary cellular space (CS) is given, design a fault tolerant CS which simulates it in real time. A CS is said to be fault tolerant if it behaves normally even when its component cells are subject to a certain kind of failure. The problem is formulated precisely in terms of cellular automata theory and makes definite some necessary concepts like simulation, misoperation, error, K-separated error, etc. When there is introduced a new multi-dimensional error correcting code and it is utilized for designing the fault tolerant CS. The theory is first explained by using a typical 2-dimensional example, while general considerations are taken up later. Among various outstanding features of biological systems, fault tolerant behavior is one of the most interesting capabilities. Though the cellular space is uniformly interconnected and homogeneous contrary to real living organisms, it would serve as the first step toward more complicated fault tolerant systems.
Name: ["Nishio H.", "Kobuchi Y."]

Title: SOLUTION OF BRANCHED AND CYCLIC PROBLEMS BY MULTI-PROCESSOR COMPUTER SYSTEMS.
Abstract: For a large number of branches and cycles with ambiguously identified operands and strong functional dependence among subsequent tiers (in cycles), the functional graph becomes implicit and its analysis is difficult in many cases. For this type of problem there is a need to develop a special parallel form of representation which would be free of such inadequacies. Such a form is proposed in this paper. It is given the name of parallel development, and is based on the idea of control graph standardization and on extraction, maximum possible isolation, and paralleling of all admissible operations paths of the computational process.
Name: ["Spatyy P.S."]

Title: CONSTRUCTION OF STABLE IDENTIFICATION ALGORITHMS FOR LINEAR STATIONARY SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Consideration of stable estimation of the impulse response of a linear stationary system on the basis of a Wiener-Hopf integral equation of the first kind. Simpler estimator functionals (or Euler's equations) than usual are proposed. Using this approach, it is possible to shorten considerably the identification time.
Name: ["Biryukov V.F."]

Title: INCREASING THE EFFICIENCY OF A DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING METHOD IN OPTIMAL STAND-BY PROBLEMS.
Abstract: To decrease the number of terms in sequences when solving optimal control problems by dynamic programming, a proposal is made to introduce for each term of the sequence a lower bound for the possible solution. To determine an approximate solution and lower bounds, the method of undetermined Lagrange multipliers is used. A combined application of the methods of dynamic programming and of Lagrange multipliers cuts down the field of search and ensures optimality of the result obtained. The computational procedure proposed is illustrated with an example.
Name: ["Alekseyev O.G."]

Title: A top down analysis technique for parallel systems
Source: Proceedings of the 2nd Symposium on Simulation of Computer Systems, ANSS 1974
Abstract: The top-down analysis technique provides a new approach for the synthesis of system models. A modified, context-free grammar is used as a means of formally describing the operation of the system which can be translated into a Markov chain model or a simulation by mechanical means. To demonstrate the use of a grammar as a system notation, the top-down analysis of a multi-processor computer system is presented. ¬© 1974 ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Clymer J.R.", "Perdue R.E."]

Title: Physically-Distinct Derivation of the Information Flow for Arbitrary Densities of Distribution of Signals. | [PHYSIKALISCH-ANSCHAULICHE ABLEITUNG DES INFORMATIONSFLUSSES BEI BELIEBIGEN VERTEILUNGSDICHTEN DER SIGNALE.]
Abstract: The transmitted information per unit of time is calculated for the case of arbitrary continuously distributed densities of signals transmitted over a system. By means of some examples, it is shown that the information flow, for specified distribution density of the interfering signal, becomes a maximum when the system total output signal shows a Gaussian distribution in an interval derived in the paper. It is shown that the derived relationship agrees better with Shannon's equation for channel capacity the larger the snr.
Name: ["Krauss M."]

Title: Suboptimum Linear Feature Selection in Multiclass Problem
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A suboptimum method of linear feature selection in multiclass problem is presented. The set of features is selected in sequential manner based on an upper bound on the probability of error. The proposed method is applied to a problem of classifying Japanese vowels. Computer simulation results are presented and discussed. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Ichino M.", "Hiramatsu K."]

Title: On using statistical analysis of SMF data to build usable simulation models of large-scale computer systems
Source: Proceedings of the 2nd Symposium on Simulation of Computer Systems, ANSS 1974
Abstract: This paper describes a technique of building workload models from SMF data. In a stable production environment, two classes of jobs were modeled, one employing a synthetic jobstream to model the "background noise", and one employing individual models of "important" jobs. Univariate statistical analysis of SMF data provided the job profiles for the synthetic jobstream, and provided relationships between CPU time and I/O counts of each file for the "important" jobs. The resultant workload was simulated with the System Analysis Machine (SAM) language. ¬© 1974 ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Merrill H.W.B."]

Title: SIMULATION OF ORGANISMS BASED ON L SYSTEMS.
Abstract: It is demonstrated that a simulation program (CELIA) based on L systems is an appropriate tool for studying the development of biological organisms and for testing hypotheses concerning such development. The demonstration involves the simulation of some grafting experiments on hydra which were done in order to test their regulatory properties. The simulation is based on a diffusion-inhibition model which embodies the principle of positional information. The L systems referred to were introduced by A. Lindenmayer in 1968 as a mathematical framework within which intercellular relationships can be discussed, computed and compared.
Name: ["Herman Gabor T.", "Schiff Gordon L."]

Title: New On-Line Identification Algorithm. | EY UJ ON-LINE IDENTIFIKACIOS ALGORITMUS.
Abstract: A new on-line identification method for discrete linear systems is described which applies the Astrom-Bohlin maximum likelihood technique to the Clarke approximate noise model and, based on this, to an on-line algorithm. The basic concept of the maximum likelihood method is described together with its application to the general and approximate noise model and the on-line algorithm.
Name: ["Gertler Janos", "Banyasz Csilla"]

Title: DATA COMPRESSION IN DISCRIMINATING STOCHASTIC PROCESSES.
Abstract: Discrimination of stochastic processes generates a need of observation data reduction concerning the length of the realization to be considered as well as the variety (alphabet) of the instantaneous process states to be identified. In this paper a method for such data compression is given based on the theory of asymptotic discernibility of two stationary random processes as developed by the author for processes with memory.
Name: ["Perez Albert"]

Title: Stochastic Prediction Method Based on Growth Curves. | [A NOVEKEDESI GORBEKEN ALAPULO SZTOCHASZTIKUS PREDIKCIO EGY UJ MODSZERE.]
Abstract: The new method of curve-fitting and stochastic prediction published in this paper can be applied to the efficient estimation of the development in time of the utility traits of animals. The very essence of the method is the adaptation of the loss function of the fitting and of the separation of environmental effects to the properties of such data. An adequate mathematical model, machine computations and selection tables were prepared to assess at an early period the meat productivity of sheep.
Name: ["Fischer Janos", "Telegdi Laszlo", "Csukas Endre"]

Title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation of Parameters in Multivariate Gaussian Stochastic Processes
Abstract: We outline a proof of the strong consistency of the maximum likelihood estimate of the parameters of Gaussian random processes possessing linear autoregressive moving average or state space representations. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Caines P.E.", "Rissanen J."]

Title: Routing a fleet of M vehicles to/from a central facility
Abstract: In a previous paper, algorithms for optimally routing a single vehicle were presented. In this paper, the problem of routing a fleet of M vehicles serving fixed demand for transportation from many origins to a single destination is considered. The M vehicle General Routing Problem (abbreviated M‚ÄêGRP) is the core of many real routing problems, such as school bus routing for a single school (many‚Äêto‚Äêone) and garbage truck routing to a central dump. It is shown that the M‚ÄêGRP on a given graph is equivalent to a GRP on a modified graph. From this result, it is shown that single vehicle routing algorithms can be applied to the M vehicle routing problem. Copyright ¬© 1974 Wiley Periodicals, Inc., A Wiley Company
Name: ["Orloff C.S."]

Title: ONE-STEP IRREDUCIBLE REALIZATION OF A QXP RATIONAL MATRIX.
Abstract: Preliminary results are presented concerning a one-step realization procedure for finding an irreducible state model (A,B,C,D) from a q-by-p rational transfer-function matrix G(s) having multiple poles without first forming a controllable (observable) model and then reducing it to a controllable as well as observable one. A matrix A of a new form with the Jordan form as its special case is introduced to overcome the subtleties of the realization problem. The degree of G(s) may be greater than the degree of the least common denominator of all the entries of G(s). It is possible to consider additional network synthesis constraints in determining matrix C column by column and matrix B row by row. The procedure can be applied to the synthesis of networks to reduce the number of physical elements needed. Digital computers can be used to further simplify the computation.
Name: ["Huang Hsien-Lu"]

Title: Matrix Representations for Sorting and the Fast Fourier Transform
Source: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
Abstract: The different versions of the fast Fourier transform (FFT) are described here for arbitrary base in terms of the matrix factors of the discrete Fourier transform matrix T<sub>N</sub>. The Kronecker product notation and the ideal shuffle base r permutation operator form the basis for a unifying theory through which the various versions of the FFT can be viewed. The properties of the ideal shuffle base r permutation operator are used to arrive at FFT versions with such desirable properties as in-place computation or identical geometry from stage to stage. The FFT versions previously described in the literature are derived here. At the same time, algorithms for the sorting of FFT data in digit-reversed order are generated. These are explored and new sorting versions amenable to hardware implementation with sequential memory are presented. As an example of how the unifying theory is used, a number of FFT versions with identical geometry from stage to stage are derived. The hardware necessary for these algorithms is described for the base 4 case with N = 1024 data points. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Sloate H."]

Title: Comparative Study of a Discrete Linear Basis for Image Data Compression
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: Transform image data compression consists of dividing the image into a number of nonoverlapping subimage regions and quantizing and coding the transform of the data from each subimage. Karhunen-Lo√®ve, Hadamard, and Fourier transforms are most commonly used in transform image compression. This paper presents a new discrete linear transform for image compression which we use in conjunction with differential pulse-code modulation on spatially adjacent transformed subimage samples. For a set of thirty-three 64 √ó 64 images of eleven different categories, we compare the performances of the discrete linear transform compression technique with the Karhunen-Lo√®ve and Hadamard transform techniques. Our measure of performance is the mean-squared error between the original image and the reconstructed image. We multiply the mean-squared error with a factor indicating the degree to which the error is spatially correlated. We find that for low compression rates, the Karhunen-Lo√®ve outperforms both the Hadamard and the discrete linear basis method. However, for high compression rates, the performance of the discrete transform method is very close to that of the Karhunen-Lo√®ve transform. The discrete linear transform method performs much better than the Hadamard transform method for all compression rates. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Haralick R.M.", "Shanmugam K."]
Affiliations: [' University of Kansas', ' Wichita State University']

Title: PRACTICABLE SOLUTION FOR THE QUADRATIC ASSIGNMENT PROBLEM.
Abstract: A practical algorithm is presented for dealing with a wide range of Quadratic Assignment Problems. It is applicable to arbitrarily large values of n, permitting hand solutions. The algorithm is applicable to problems involving a general cost function, and to the combined problem (locating multiple new facilities with respect to multiple existing facilities, such that both linear and quadratic assignment costs are considered. The algorithm provides a practicable choice criterion with expected efficiency evaluation, so that it is possible to predict the effectiveness of the algorithm, and at times prove that a solution is optimal.
Name: ["Nanda Ravinder", "Weingarten Allen"]

Title: ITERATION SKIPPING IN PRIMAL INTEGER PROGRAMMING.
Abstract: An examination of computational results using the simplified primal integer programming algorithm of F. Glover reveals the existence of long sequences of iterations following a specific pattern. The paper examines the structure of these sequences so that both the termination of a sequence and the tableau at that point can be predicted. It then constructs an algorithm that exploits this structure by performing the iterations of the sequence implicitly and presents computational results.
Name: ["Arnold Larry R.", "Bellmore Mandell"]

Title: Approximate Linear Realizations of Given Dimension via Ho's Algorithm
Abstract: Ho's Algorithm generates exact realizations of finite-dimensional linear systems, given exact data. We discuss here a variant of the algorithm that generates approximate realizations of specified dimension from approximate data. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Zeiger H.P.", "McEwen A.J."]

Title: On pursuit and feedback in optimal stochastic control-explicit control laws
Abstract: In this paper a non-gaussian discrete time stochastic pursuit problem is solved. Then this solution is applied to a class of linear stochastic feedback problems with arbitrarily generated disturbances and incomplete state information. As a by-product, we obtain a generalized version of the well-known "separation theorem." In particular, the solution is applied to obtain explicit feedback laws for systems with imperfectly known disturbance parameters. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Wernersson √Ö."]

Title: Information flow in one-dimensionalmarkov systems
Source: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society
Abstract: The information flow in discrete Markov systems provides a method for determining that such a system has a unique invariant measure. Estimates are obtained for the information flow and conditions under which there is a unique invariant measure for a one-dimensional Markov system are obtained. ¬© American Mathematical Society 1974.
Name: ["Dawson D.A."]
Keywords: ["discrete markov system", "information flow", "invariant measure", "flow dimensionalmarkov", "flow discrete"]

Title: Asymptotic Statistics of Periodogram-Type Spectral Estimates for the Output of Nonlinear Devices
Abstract: The high resolution statistics of a periodogram-type spectral estimate for a periodic deterministic signal plus Gaussian noise are well understood. If, however, the signal plus noise is first passed through a nonlinear memoryless device (such as a hard limiter), the situation becomes much more complicated. The main result of this correspondence is the derivation of the high resolution limit of the joint statistics of the I and Q components of a periodogram for a certain class of nonlinear devices with a deterministic periodic signal and Gaussian noise as input. This result permits the calculation of the asymptotic central moments of the spectral estimate formed from the foregoing periodogram. It then becomes possible to subject a device employing this technique for spectral estimation to a detailed performance analysis. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Fitelson M.M."]

Title: ELECTRICALLY-REPROGRAMMABLE ANALOG TRANSVERSAL FILTER.
Abstract: The charge-coupled device (CCD) and metal-nitride-oxide silicon (MNOS) technologies may be combined to provide discrete analog signal processing (DASP) in contrast to conventional digital signal processing (DSP). In DASP, analog data samples are stored, transferred and operated on by analog means, whereas in DSP, digital or quantized samples are handled with binary logic. A major advantage of DSP is retained in DASP; namely, the precise transport delay particularly in relation to coherent signal processing. The dynamic range of an analog bit in DSP may be thought of as composed of 6-db equivalent DSP digital bits. A transversal filter is a basic building block in DASP and such a filter may be constructed with a CCD multi-tapped, delay line. A method is presented to sense nondestructively and to obtain an electrically variable multiplication of the surface charge in a CCD storage well. Thus, an analog transversal filter is constructed with reprogrammable, analog tap weights for DASP or also digital tap weights. Applications include Fourier transformers, matched filters and correlators, and adaptive filters.
Name: ["Lampe Donald R.", "White Marvin H.", "Fagan John L.", "Mims James H."]

Title: MODEL FOR THE EVALUATION OF LARGE SCALE DATA RETRIEVAL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The stochastic model described is designed to measure the retrieval workload of most data retrieval systems. Hence, if a user can neglect the effect of file updating, the stochastic model can be used effectively to compare alternative data retrieval systems and select the most appropriate one. Thus far the model has been applied to several areas of research including the effect of query complexity on the design of large scale data retrieval systems. The model described by this paper does not use ‚Ä≥real‚Ä≥ data base records. Instead, an abstracted form of the data base is used. The data base abstraction is based on important data base statistics which give a summary of the data base. Due to this statistical representation, the model is called a stochastic model. Rather than examining each data base record, the stochastic model computes measures of system performance by analyzing the statistics of the data base.
Name: ["Siler Kenneth F."]

Title: SIMULATION SYSTEM FOR BRAIN MODELING.
Abstract: A highly parameterized, general purpose simulation system for brain structures has been coded in FORTRAN. Detailed three-dimensional models involving up to 8000 neurons and 80,000 synapses can be specified and simulated. Individual model elements are not enumerated. Instead the parameter scheme uses spatial lattices and intersecting probability distributions to position neurons and synapses with any desired degree of precision or randomness. The system has been used to study neural activity in a cerebellar cortex model involving 2000 neurons and 20,000 synapses and to evaluate an integrated circuit picture-processing array made of 2700 logic elements and 5400 connections.
Name: ["Wittie Larry D."]

Title: ON THE SWITCHING INSTANTS IN TIME-OPTIMAL CONTROL WITH SOME HARMONIC DISTURBANCES.
Source: Bull Acad Pol Sci, Ser Sci Tech
Abstract: The minimum-time control problem for a single-input, single-output linear, time-invariant plant affected by a given external harmonic disturbance is considered. This disturbance is supposed to be defined as a function of time alone, and there are no restrictions concerning the place in which the disturbance affects the system. An effective procedure for determining the switching instants is given.
Name: ["Pelczewski W.", "Lawrynowicz J."]

Title: APPLICATION OF AN ELECTRONIC IMAGE ANALYZER TO DIMENSIONAL MEASUREMENTS FROM NEUTRON RADIOGRAPHS.
Abstract: Means of obtaining improved dimensional measurements from neutron radiographs of nuclear fuel elements are discussed. This report describes the use of video-electronic image analysis relative to edge definition in radiographic images. Based on this study, an edge definition criterion is proposed for overcoming image unsharpness effects in taking accurate diametral measurements from radiographs. An electronic density slicing method for automatic edge definition is described. Results of measurements made with video micrometry are compared with scanning microdensitometer and micrometric physical measurements. An image quality indicator for estimating photographic and geometric unsharpness is described.
Name: ["Vary Alex", "Bowles Kenneth J."]

Title: On-line digital computer control of slurry-conditioning in mineral flotation
Abstract: A computer control strategy for an operating metallurgical process is described in this paper. A real process is modelled by a set of stochastic differential equations with state-dependent noise, and a practical non-linear filter is developed for the estimation of the model parameters and the state variables. A separation principle is invoked and a sub-optimal control strategy is implemented. Operating experience has shown that the estimation and control algorithms are effective. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["King R.P."]

Title: Abstract computability and its relation to the general purpose analog computer (Some connections between logic, differential equations and analog computers)
Source: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society
Abstract: Our aim is to study computability from the viewpoint of the analog computer. We present a mathematical definition of an analog generable function of a real variable. This definition is formulated in terms of a simultaneous set of nonlinear differential equations possessing a ‚Äúdomain of generation.‚Äù (The latter concept is explained in the text.) Our definition includes functions generated by existing general-purpose analog computers. Using it we prove two theorems which provide a characterization of analog generable functions in terms of solutions of algebraic differential polynomials. The characterization has two consequences. First we show that there are entire functions which are computable (in the sense of recursive analysis) but which cannot be generated by any analog computer in any interval‚Äîe.g. (Formula Presented). Second we note that the class of analog generable functions is very large: it includes special functions which arise as solutions to algebraic differential polynomials. Although not all computable functions are analog generable, a kind of converse holds. For entire functions, (Formula Presented) the theorem takes the following form. If f(x) is analog generable on some closed, bounded interval then there is a finite number of bk such that, on every closed bounded interval, ∆í(x) is computable relative to these bk. A somewhat similar theorem holds if ∆í is not entire. Although the results are stated and proved for functions of a real variable, they hold with minor modifications for functions of a complex variable. ¬© 1974 American Mathematical Society.
Name: ["Pour-El M.B."]
Keywords: ["algebraic differential polynomial", "cauchy-peano existence theorem for differential equations", "computable function of a real variable", "gamma function", "general purpose analog computer"]

Title: ON SOME ESTIMATION PROBLEMS IN PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: Two estimations are investigated for which the results of the algorithms are useful in pattern recognition. The targets of estimations are the L//2 norm squares of a probability density and an optimal Bayes decision function. Two examples for the application of these quantities in pattern recognition are presented.
Name: ["Gyorfi L."]

Title: EVT APPLIED TO THE DESIGN OF VARIABLE THRESHOLD DETECTORS.
Abstract: This paper describes how Extreme Value Theory (EVT) may be utilized to estimate the false alarm probability (P//F//A) of a fixed or variable threshold detector using a limited number of data samples. First, a general discussion of the EVT concept as applied to fixed threshold detectors is given. The technique is then shown to be directly applicable to variable threshold CFAR (constant false alarm rate) detectors and new results are obtained which permit one to design CFAR detectors when the noise distribution at the detector input is unknown or only partially known. To demonstrate the EVT concepts described in the paper, EVT is applied to a known noise distribution, namely the Weibull distribution. An evaluation of the EVT approach is given under the assumption of a Weibull noise distribution and a complete mathematical analysis of the accuracy of the EVT approach is given. Finally, the utilization of EVT concepts in the design of CFAR detectors is discussed and results of a computer simulation are presented.
Name: ["Novak L."]

Title: Determination of Matrices of Linear Transformations of the State Variables for Linear Stationary Systems. | WYZNACZANIE MACIERZY PRZEKSZTALCEN LINIOWYCH ZMIENNYCH STANU W LINIOWYCH UKLADACH STACJONARNYCH.
Abstract: A general method is presented for determining the matrices of linear transformations of the state variables for multi-input multi-output linear systems. The matrix of linear transformations can be calculated as a result of postmultiplication of the controllability matrix of the considered system by the inverse matrix of a controllability matrix of a transformed system.
Name: ["Kaczorek Tadeusz"]

Title: DIGITAL IMAGE DEBLURRING.
Abstract: Results are presented on the digital homomorphic estimation of the frequency response of a two-dimensional linear system through which images have been passed and blurred. Almost no a priori knowledge concerning the system is required, and only one blurred image is necessary for a successful estimation. For those blurs that have phase reversals, such as motion blurs and out-of-focus blurs, a simple method of calculating the correct phase has been developed. The image may be restored by filtering either the intensity version or the density version of the image.
Name: ["Stockham Jr. T.G.", "Cannon T.M."]

Title: Admissibility conditions for a class of quadrature formulas with random nodes
Source: Mathematical Notes of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR
Abstract: The present note is concerned with the theory of the Monte Carlo method. We consider the problem of the admissibility of quadrature formulas with random nodes. Based on the formulation of an admissibility condition we obtain a new class of such formulas. ¬© 1975 Consultants Bureau.
Name: ["Granovskii B.L."]

Title: Matrix Method of Identification of Indistinguishable States in Nondeterministic Sequential Machines. | [MACIERZOWA METODA IDENTYFIKACJI STANOW NIEROZROZNIALNYCH W NIEDETERMINISTYCZNYCH MASZYNACH SEKWENCYJNYCH.]
Abstract: The state minimization problem for nondeterministic sequential machines (nondeterministic transducers) is considered. An algorithm for determining the minimal form of a given nondeterministic sequential machine is presented. The minimization procedure is based on the matrix description of nondeterministic sequential machines as well as properties of finite vector space.
Name: ["Szabatin Jerzy"]

Title: Investigation of Dynamic Characteristics of the Human Operator in Man-Machine Systems (A Survey). | [ISSLEDOVANIYA DINAMICHESKIKH KHARAKTERISTIK CHELOVEKA-OPERATORA V CHELOVEKO-MASHINNYKH SISTEMAKH. (OBZOR).]
Abstract: A number of models of the human operator involved in the ‚Ä≥eye - hand‚Ä≥ channel tracking problems are considered, with application mainly to the problems of aircraft and motor vehicle control. The advantages and shortcomings of the models are pointed out and prospects for further research are outlined. Possible practical applications are presented. Particular attention is paid to the quasilinear models, in particular to the cut-off frequency model. Examples of correction of the transfer function in the direct input branch, containing human operator, are given.
Name: ["Netushil A.V.", "Kornyushko V.F.", "Chupakhin A.S."]

Title: Two linear lower bounds on the complexity of Boolean functions | Zwei lineare untere Schranken f√ºr die Komplexit√§t Boolescher Funktionen
Abstract: We establish two linear lower bounds on the minimal number of 2-ary Boolean operations that are necessary to compute certain Boolean functions. The first bound depends on the structure of primimplicants of the Boolean function. The second bound depends on the structure of the set of subfunctions. Both lower bounds yield the exact cost of an optimal computation in certain cases. ¬© 1974 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Schnorr C.P."]

Title: GRAPH SEARCH APPROACH TO THE DETERMINATION OF TEST SEQUENCES FOR LSI SEQUENTIAL CIRCUITS.
Abstract: SCIRTSS, a sequential circuit test search system is described. The functioning of the program is described, its strengths and weaknesses are pointed out, and the results of its application to 6 circuits are presented. Work with SCIRTSS so far has convinced the authors that it is indeed possible to write a program which will automatically or nearly automatically generate test sequences for highly sequential and in general very complex sequential circuits. SCIRTSS itself has been successful in generating tests for almost all faults in a fairly large class of circuits. The two features most responsible for making SCIRTSS feasible are (1) the representation of a stored fault so that the search can be divided into two parts and (2) the use of an economical design language based search routine.
Name: ["Hill Fredrick J.", "Belt John E.", "Carter Ernest A.", "Huey Ben M."]

Title: CONTINUOUS DIGESTER LEVEL CONTROL USING DISCRETE LEVEL INDICATION.
Abstract: The discrete level indication, present in many continuous digesters, is used in a special algorithm to give precise level control. An unconventional nonlinear filter is used to counter noise in the level measurement. Improved K No. control is shown to follow the level controller application. The algorithm presented here manipulates a primary variable, which moves the level up and down in a cyclic fashion. Variables suitable as primary variables include the outlet device, the wash upflow, and the weak black liquor entering the bottom of the digester. A backup variable is stepped when a high level appears, and is held until the condition is corrected. The backup variable is commonly the blow flow.
Name: ["Cohen Ernest M.", "Ryan Thomas L."]

Title: EVALUATION OF VARIOUS SCHEDULING DISCIPLINES BY COMPUTER SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The assignment of patients to examination rooms in a diagnostic radiology department can be categorized as a job-shop scheduling problem. This paper shows a way of using a GPSS (General Purpose Simulation System) discrete event simulation model to test, analyze and find the best heuristic scheduling algorithms that can be applied to patient flow in a diagnostic radiology department. Four main measures of performance are considered: waiting time before examination, total time in the system, utilization of staff and equipment, and the number of patients in the system at the end of a working day. Among the scheduling disciplines tested include the following six: smallest number of patients in each queue, smallest work load in each queue, shortest processing time (SPT), truncated SPT (with priorities), common queue (patients join a single queue versus multiple queues based on examination type), and truncated common queue.
Name: ["Lev Benjamin", "Caltagirone Robert J."]

Title: EXTENSION OF SCAN-RESCAN PROCESSES USING DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING IN SEARCH PROBLEMS.
Abstract: In this extension of previous work, a loss function for multi-level intensities is investigated. Using this loss function, a total Bayes mean risk for pattern recognition of abnormalities is defined. The policies are based upon the Bayesian hypothesis testing and Bayesian parameter estimation. To attain the best empirical result from the standpoint of both accuracy and time consumption, the above mean risk function at the rescanning stage is minimized by formulating the optimum time allocation to each cell in the search area. Another application of the technique, applied to the sampling inspection of an aggregate of lots, is also considered. A considerable saving in the total sample size is achieved by the scan-rescan procedures.
Name: ["Bellman Richard", "Sugiyama Hiroshi", "Kashef Bayesteh"]

Title: STABILITY CRITERION FOR RECURSIVE FILTERS.
Source: IBM Journal of Research and Development
Abstract: A new criterion is derived that relates the stability of two-dimensional recursive filters to the properties of its cepstrum. It provides a procedure for the decomposition of unstable recursive filters having nonzero, nonimaginary frequency response into stable recursive filters. The optimal solution of the decomposition problem is discussed, including numerical implementation and nonrecursive solutions. Several numerical examples show the potentialities and limitations of the rules for decomposition and for truncation of the operators.
Name: ["Pistor P."]

Title: EMBEDDING A GRAPH IN A PLANE WITH LOCAL CONSTRAINTS.
Abstract: An algorithm for testing the planarity of a graph with local constraints is presented here. This is more useful than the ordinal algorithm for laying out an electrical circuit on a plane without crossovers, especially in cases the circuit contains multi-terminal elements, because it is not necessary to represent physical constraints about terminal sequence as for the graph model.
Name: ["Uyehara Takao", "Shiraishi Hiroshi", "Takahashi Osamu", "Kojima Takamoto"]

Title: ON-LINE IDENTIFICATION OF PERIODIC SYSTEMS FROM AN INPUT/OUTPUT DATA, THE DETERMINISTIC CASE.
Abstract: The construction of a dynamic system from an input/output sequence is considered. An input/output sequence is said to be identifiable if there exists a realization of the sequence and the realization is unique, up to an equivalence class of algebraic equivalent systems. A sufficient condition is derived for an input/output sequence to be identifiable, and an algorithm for the realization process is provided. Two major assumptions made by others are removed. The algorithm is useful for an on-line identification process.
Name: ["Liu R.W.", "Suen L.C."]

Title: PENALTY METHOD OF DETERMINING AUTOMATICALLY A NC CUTTER PATH.
Abstract: It is predicted that in future it will be possible to connect computer-aided design (CAD) and computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) systems. As a result, it is expected that a number of problems will arise which will be difficult to solve. One of the important problems involved within the connection appears to be the automatic determination of a NC cutter path for a given geometrical pattern (shape). A new method of determining such a cutter path is proposed and it is named the ‚Ä≥Penalty Method‚Ä≥ .
Name: ["Kakazu Y.", "Okino N.", "Hoshi K."]

Title: COORDINATING AGGREGATE AND DETAILED SCHEDULING DECISIONS IN THE ONE-MACHINE JOB SHOP - 1. THEORY.
Abstract: A formal model of the one-machine job-shop scheduling problem with variable capacity is presented. The paper generalizes sequence-theory results to this case, analyzes various lower-bounding structures for the problem, outlines a preliminary branch-and-bound algorithm, and illustrates several features of the algorithm and bounding structures by an example.
Name: ["Gelders L.", "Kleindorfer P.R."]

Title: Optimization of structured programs
Abstract: The class of programs which do not contain goto statements has a structure which lends itself to optimization by an optimizer that is fast, efficient and relatively easy to program. The design of such an optimizer is described, along with some of the results obtained using this optimizer‚Äîone such result being that very little code optimization is achieved. The conjecture is made that this is true because gotoless programming languages lend themselves to more compact and concise object code at the source language level. Copyright ¬© 1974 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd
Name: ["Zelkowitz M.V.", "Bail W.G."]

Title: Roundoff Error in Multidimensional Generalized Discrete Transforms
Source: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
Abstract: The analysis of rounding error in the one-dimensional fast Fourier transform (FFT) is extended to a class of generalized orthogonal transforms [1] with a common fast algorithm similar to the FFT algorithm. This class includes the Binary FOurier REpresentation (BIFORE) transform (BT) [2], the complex BT (CBT) [3], and the discrete Fourier transform (DFT). Expressions for the mean square error (MSE) in the two-dimensional BT, CBT, and FFT are derived. In the case of white input data, the mean square error-to-signal ratio is derived for the multidimensional generalized transforms. The error-to-signal ratio for the one-dimensional FFT derived by Kaneko and Liu is modified with improvement. Some comparisons among BIFORE, DFT, and Haar transforms are also included. The theoretical results for the two-dimensional FFT and BIFORE have been verified experimentally. The experimental results are in good agreement with the theoretical results for lower order sequences, but deviate as the order increases due to the actual manner of rounding in the digital computer. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Chan O.W.C.", "Jury E.I."]

Title: RADIAL GRAMMARS AND BIOLOGICAL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A. Lindenmayer has introduced developmental models that generate sequences of cellular descriptions of developing organisms. The L-systems describe developing organisms at given instants of time as arrays of symbols in one, two or three dimensions, each symbol corresponding to a cell. The authors have previously developed two-dimensional generative models for the description of digital pictures and kolam patterns. Complicated patterns of kolam, a South Indian folk art, appear similar to patterns found in nature for example, on the shell of the starred tortoise (Testudo elegans). The two models previously defined are powerful enough to describe a large class of patterns which have basically a rectangular format. In this paper is introduced a third model which can describe a class of pictures which have a circular format, starting from one center and growing at several points on the circumference. These models are briefly described. The first model is referred to as the matrix model, the second as the array model and the third, the radial. Examples are presented to show that several variations of the models can be interpreted to describe the symmetry or growth of many living organisms.
Name: ["Siromoney Gift", "Siromoney Rani"]

Title: NEURAL CODING THROUGH MASS ACTION IN THE OLFACTORY SYSTEM.
Abstract: A method is given for describing the dynamics of interactions in neural masses, where such interactions are manifested in the EEG ( ‚Ä≥brain waves‚Ä≥ ). The experimental data come from the vertebrate olfactory system which is the simplest system generating EEG waves. The results show how the EEG is generated in this system, and how it may be interpreted in relation to sensory processing.
Name: ["Freeman Walter J."]

Title: AUTOMATED GENERATION OF SELF-METRIC SOFTWARE.
Abstract: Self-metric software are programs that record their behavior statistics automatically during their execution. They are generated from existing software by inserting software measurement instruments into the program at appropriate locations after an automatic analysis by the system. An algorithm to locate and insert the optimal (minimal cost) set of activity counters for generating the program activity profile is given. The use of the model for measuring execution time, branching characteristics, code activities, path activities, and other program statistics are discussed. The applications of these statistics in program testing, optimization, and program restructuring for virtual memory are presented.
Name: ["Cheung R.C.", "Kim K.H.", "Ramamoorthy C.V.", "Reddi S.S."]

Title: OPTIMAL MULTILEVEL CONTROL SCHEME FOR LARGE SCALE DYNAMIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: An optimal multilevel control approach - as applied to Large Scale Dynamic Systems (LSDS) - is presented. A feasible decomposition technique is adopted to uncouple the interacting subsystems. To achieve a global solution, the coordination process is carried out using a conjugate gradient technique especially adapted for such class of problems. The proposed method proves to be most powerful in computational efforts with quadratic convergence that can be achieved in a finite number of steps. Theoretical investigations are supported by a typical system application.
Name: ["Mahmoud M.S.M.", "Bilal A.Y."]

Title: EFFICIENT IMPLEMENTATION OF RECURSIVE DIGITAL FILTERS.
Abstract: The application of multidimensional techniques and the Fermat number transform to block recursion for the efficient implementation of recursive digital filters is considered. A new structure for implementing filters with poles near the unit circle. The Fermat Number transform can implement finite length convolution with no error and with a minimum number of multiplications. A new recursive filter structure is presented that has reduced coefficient sensitivity and round off noise problems for transfer functions with poles very near the unit circle.
Name: ["Burrus C.S.", "Agarwal R.C."]

Title: SOME PROBLEMS OF ADAPTIVE OPTIMAL PROCESS CONTROL.
Abstract: Tsypkin has shown an algorithm based on dual control for the adaptive control of a dynamic nonlinear single input - single output system - with known dynamic lag series, connected with the input and quadratic performance index (loss function). This method has been generalized for adaptive control of multiple input - single output system. Since then this idea has been developed and investigated in detail. In this paper the problems of choosing convergence matrices of dual control with two perceptrons (identification and control) and sensitivity model, furthermore the influence of a priori knowledge of dynamics on adaptive control is considered. By means of the developed PCSP (Process Control Simulator Program), the issue of adaptive control are simulated in several cases of different strategies. These experiences can be used in the development of process control software.
Name: ["Keviczky Laszlo", "Banyasz Csilla", "Kocais Janos"]

Title: ON REPLACING STATE CONSTRAINTS WITH CONTROL CONSTRAINTS IN OPTIMAL CONTROL THEORY.
Abstract: The relation between systems with state constraints and those with control constraints which depend upon the state is examined. The notion of a smooth control constraint map is introduced and its properties are studied. A sequence of such maps is utilized to obtain approximate solutions to the state constrained optimal control problem. Convergence of these approximate solutions is shown to hold for a large class of systems. An application to a predator-prey system of the Lotka-Volterra type is presented.
Name: ["Rocklin Sol M."]

Title: QUASILINEARIZATION ALGORITHM FOR SOLVING A CLASS OF OPTIMAL CONTROL PROBLEMS WITH MULTIPLE INEQUALITY CONSTRAINTS.
Abstract: A quasilinearization algorithm is proposed to solve a class of optimal control problems with multiple constraints. The constraints are inquality constrains on functions of the state and control variables, and bounds on the values of the control variables. Necessary conditions for optimal control of the formulated problem are derived. Some of them are used in the iterative procedure to determine whether nominal trajectory is on the boundaries of the inequality constraints. A problem is solved to illustrate the proposed method.
Name: ["Yeo B.P."]

Title: SEGMENTING AND RECOGNIZING CONTINUOUS SPEECH.
Abstract: A segmentation and recognition method for continuous speech signals is described. The performance achieved by this method is high compared to the performance realized by other existing methods, and the technique is easily adaptable to various input forms.
Name: ["Das S.K."]

Title: AUTOMATION OF AUTORADIOGRAPHIC ANALYSIS IN THE NEUROSCIENCES.
Abstract: A cooperative research program is described which has as its objective the automated characterization of neurological tissure regions from autoradiographs by utilizing medium resolution image processing techniques. An experimental system is discussed which includes raw imagery, scanning equipments, feature extraction algorithms, and regional characterization techniques. An approach is presented for validating these techniques and the intial experimental results obtained from the analysis of an autoradiograph of a region of the hypothalmus. An extension of these automated techniques to other biomedical research problems is discussed.
Name: ["Bisignani W.T.", "Greenhouse S.C.", "Entingh D."]

Title: NEURON AS A SEQUENTIAL MACHINE.
Abstract: Some of the operational and anatomical parameters of the pyramidal neuron are related to those of the sequential machine. Attention is drawn to the versatility of the sequential machine to be able to represent continuous cellular processes. One's choice of suitable timing between state transitions, the input set groupings, and how much detail about neural operations is desired in the sequential machine dictate how complex the sequential machine will be. Seemingly minor additions of detail can result in quite large increases in the size and complexity of the sequential machine. Probably only primary (major) effects are of interest to most people such that secondary and tertiary effects will be imbedded in the machine. Yet all the continuous neural processes appear to have realistic, discrete, finite realizations within the framework of the theoretical sequential machine.
Name: ["Schneider Richard E."]

Title: Reconnaissance automatique des potentiels d'unit√© motrice
Abstract: A system for the automatic recognition of motor unit potentials is presented; it makes possible the retrieval of the dates of discharge of a single unit in a graph in which several units are collated simultaneously. This system operates by autoinstruction, i.e. the system operates when a single sample of the unit sought is fed into the computer in plain language. The percentage error is low where the unit sought is of characteristic shape, time-stable, and in quiet surroundings. ¬© 1974 International Federation for Medical & Biological Engineering.
Name: ["Caspi P.", "Legoffic J.P.", "Richalet J."]
Keywords: ["recognition of motor-unit potentials", "recognition motor", "automatique des", "motor unit", "unit potentials"]
Affiliations: ["Groupe d'Etudes et de Recherches en bio-Syst√®mes Cit√© Fournier"]

Title: OPTIMUM FILTERING AND DETECTION IN IMPULSE NOISE.
Abstract: Under mild conditions, the maximum a posteriori and minimum-mean-square-error estimates are obtained of a Gaussian random process when observed in the presence of shot noise and white Gaussian noise. The solution of the detection problem for a known-signal in shot noise plus white Gaussian noise is also given.
Name: ["Ohlson John E."]

Title: Hierarchical structuring for system identification
Abstract: Hierarchical system theory deals with the decomposition of large or unwieldy systems into smaller subsystems which are conceptually and computationally easier to manipulate. System identification-the determination of unknown system parameters-is an area of system theory in which hierarchical structuring may be particularly useful. For example, as system identification techniques are applied to societal systems, the dimensionality of the problem may become so large as to cause computational difficulties. For such problems, hierarchical techniques may offer a significant reduction in computational requirements. This research investigates hierarchical structuring for system identification. The maximum a posteriori (MAP) identification criterion yields a two point boundary value problem (TPBVP) which is cast into a hierarchical structure. Two different methods-quasilinearization and invariant imbedding-are used to solve the subproblems which are then coordinated to achieve the overall problem solution. Several examples are solved to demonstrate the use of the developed algorithms. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Smith N.J.", "Sage A.P."]

Title: EFFICIENT COMPUTATIONAL PROCEDURES FOR CLOSED QUEUEING NETWORK MODELS.
Abstract: Efficient computational procedures are described to compute the normalization constant and the marginal queue length distributions for closed queueing network models where the equilibrium state probabilities have a produce form solution.
Name: ["Muntz R.R.", "Wong J.W."]

Title: Coupling between a symmetric and an asymmetric neural system
Abstract: Coupling of asymmetric and symmetric neural systems is found such that induced bias in the latter furnishes clues to the transmission pathways of the former.
Name: ["Jaffe J."]

Title: ON RESWITCHING OF REARRANGEABLE CLOS NETWORKS.
Abstract: A formalized mathematical model of the 3-stage Clos network is presented. An algorithm of control of such a network is given. This algorithm gives a new constructive proof of the Slepian-Duguid theorem. The algorithm reroutes not more than r-1 calls, where r denotes the number of switches in the first section. It is also shown that the Clos structure is never optimal. The algorithm was implemented on an Odra 1304 computer.
Name: ["Lipski Witold", "Pioro Michal"]

Title: Application of the Linear Optimal Theory in Designing Control Systems. | [A LINEARIS OPTIMUM ELV ALKALMAZASA SZABALYOZASI KOROK TERVEZESEHEZ.]
Abstract: A computer oriented procedure based on the linear optimal theory for designing conventional control loops is described.
Name: ["Bakonyi Peter", "Ercsenyi Andras"]

Title: Bayes-Optimum Two-Stage Hierarchic Recognition Systems. | [BAYES-OPTIMALE ZWEISTUFIGE HIERARCHISCHE ERKENNUNGSSYSTEME.]
Abstract: Structural methods of recognition describing objects by a finite quantity of discrete elements, and by relations existing between them, have been considered so far to be fundamentally different from known numerical methods (vectorial concept), for which optimum solutions are available. In this paper, they are shown to be two-stage hierarchic systems of recognition. They are considered to be optimum according to Bayes if the given (sufficient) conditions are met.
Name: ["Fuchs S."]

Title: DIRECT DESIGN FROM INPUT-OUTPUT DATA OF SUBOPTIMAL FEEDBACK LOOPS FOR LINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A describing technique for linear time-invariant systems in terms of input-output relations is proposed. The method allows the direct design of suboptimal feedback controllers from the knowledge of input-output data. State equations of the system to be controlled are not required.
Name: ["Genesio Roberto", "Pome Roberto"]

Title: CHOICE OF BASE ELEMENTS IN STRUCTURAL SYNTHESIS ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: For a given multi-output device (system of Boolean functions) and a particular structural synthesis algorithm, a technique is suggested for choosing between two functionally complete sets of elements that result in simpler implementation of the given multi-output device. A decision rule is constructed for Boolean functions given in tabular form. Experimental verification of the Gavrilov - Kopylenko algorithm is reported.
Name: ["Tolmacheva A.Ya."]

Title: ADAPTIVE MODELS FOR ON-LINE CONTROLLED PROCESSES.
Source: Siemens Forsch Entwicklungsber, Res Dev Rep
Abstract: The economy and efficiency of industrial processes can be optimized with the aid of a self-learning model. Lack of knowledge of process parameters is compensated for by iterative adaptation of the model. The number of learning cycles required is kept within reasonable limits by adaptively accelerating the rate of convergence.
Name: ["Troendle Hans Peter"]

Title: Low sensitivity feedback gains for deterministic and stochastic control systems
Abstract: The problem of obtaining output feedback gains to minimize a quadratic performance criterion which includes sensitivity variables is discussed. The equivalent stochastic problems are also studied and when a Kalman filter is allowed, the minimum variance estimate of the state is employed to implement the control. A set of non-linear matrix equations are obtained which constitute the necessary conditions that must be satisfied for an optimal solution. For the deterministic case it is shown that when no sensitivity is considered and the matrix which relates output and input is invertible, the usual Riccati formulation is obtained. The problem is also reformulated using a compensator and it is shown that it can be cast into an instantaneous feedback form. ¬© 1974 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Stavroulakis P.", "Sarachik‚Ä° P.E."]

Title: AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL SCHEME THROUGH SIMULATION.
Abstract: A simulation model is developed to effectively assist in planning air traffic control operations in the terminal area. The analysis applies unique concepts to the air terminal system, employing a discrete events simulation philosophy through the GASP simulation language. The study includes pertinent factors associated with actual air traffic operations such as multiple runway dependency, landings and take-offs, aircraft flight characteristics, interaction between approaches, traffic control standards, wave-offs, arrival and departure structures, and so forth. A systems approach has been taken in designing the model so that the components of the system and their complex interactions are represented realistically. The validation of the model indicates that the discrete event modeling philosphy can adequately simulate air terminal operations.
Name: ["Yu Jason Chiahsin", "Akhand Shamsul Alam"]

Title: Fuzzy sets and neural networks
Abstract: It is possible that a better model for the behavior of a nerve cell may be provided by what might be called a fuzzy neuron, which is a generalization of the McCulloch-Pitts model. The concept of a fuzzy neuron employs some of the concepts and techniques of the theory of fuzzy sets which was introduced by Zadeh [2, 3] and applied to the theory of automaton by Wee and Fu [6], Tanaka et al. [7], Santo [8] and others. In effect, the introduction of fuzziness into the model of a neuron makes it better adapted to the study of the behavior of systems which are imprecisely defined by virtue of their high degree of complexity. Many of the biological systems, economic systems, urban systems and more generally, large-scale systems fall into this category. In the nearly three decades since its publication, the pioneering work of McCulloch and Pitts [1], has had a profound influence on the development of the theory of neural nets, in addition to stimulating much of the early work in automata theory and regular events. Although the McCulloch-Pitts model of a neuron has contributed a great deal to the understanding of the behavior of neural-like systems, it fails to reflect the fact that the behavior of even the simplest type of nerve cell exhibits not only randomness but, more importantly, a type of imprecision which is associated with the lack of sharp transition from the occurrence of an event to its non-occurrence. In this paper, some basic properties of fuzzy neural networks as well as their applications to the synthesis of fuzzy automata are investigated. It is shown that any n-state minimal fuzzy automaton can be realized by a network of m fuzzy neurons, where ‚îålog<sub>2</sub> n‚îê ‚©Ω m ‚©Ω 2n. Examples are given to illustrate the procedure. As an example of application, a realization of Œª-fuzzy language recognizer using a fuzzy neural network is presented. The techniques described in this paper may be of use in the study of neural networks as well as in formal languages, pattern recognition, and learning. ¬© 1975 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Lee S.C.", "Lee E.T."]
Affiliations: [' University of Houston', ' State University of New York']

Title: Human factors design criteria in man-computer interaction
Source: Proceedings of the 1974 Annual ACM Conference/Annual Meeting, ACM 1974
Abstract: The need for better understanding of human behavior in the Management Information Systems (MIS) environment has been recognized. One method of examining this behavior is to describe man as an information processor and focus on his ability to store, retrieve and utilize information. The use of design criteria which explicitly recognize man's limitations in these areas can enhance overall system performance. Consideration of several criteria to be used in the design of interactive languages is given. Finally, the hypothesis that with an interactive system "perceived" response time is more important than actual response time is presented. Results of preliminary experiments are included. ¬© 1974 ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Testa C.J.", "Dearie D.B."]

Title: FILE SEARCHING WITH A PARALLEL PROCESSOR.
Abstract: A technique is described for using a parallel array computer to perform searching operations in a hash indexed table. Some evaluations of the efficiency of this technique are given.
Name: ["Downs H.R."]

Title: OPTIMUM MEAN-SQUARE ESTIMATE FOR DECODING BINARY BLOCK CODES.
Abstract: By the use of abstract Fourier analysis on groups, the optimum mean-square error decoding rule is developed for a fixed block code. The optimum 1-1 encoding rule to be used with this optimum decoder is derived and a procedure for simultaneous optimization over both encoding and decoding rules is given. It is shown that there is a linear encoding rule which is optimum. A system which implements the optimum decoding rule is outlined. The decoding rule developed here is a mapping from binary n-tuples directly into the real numbers with the optimization being over all possible mappings into the real numbers. As such the system developed here replaces both the error-correction and digital-to-analog conversion components used in most-numerical data transmission systems.
Name: ["Wolf Gary A.", "Redinbo G.Robert"]

Title: CELL KINETICS AND CELLSIM.
Abstract: CELLSIM is a cell kinetics simulation system which is intended to facilitate the application of computer simulation in the field of cell cycle kinetics. The user interfaces to the system through a simple problem-oriented language which uses the conventions and the vocabulary common to the cell biologist. Therefore, a cell biologist should be able to develop his own computer simulation models after very little instruction. An added dividend to the use of this language is that the assumptions and the logic of the model are apparent to other researchers who examine the program. This simulation system uses a number of built-in collection algorithms that automatically re-group and re-assign cells when the cell population approaches the memory limit of the computer system on which it is being run. These algorithms have been designed so that they have a minimum of disturbance on the models being simulated. Thus a researcher can simulate a cell model for any length of simulated time without concern for exceeding memory limits.
Name: ["Donaghey Charles E."]

Title: EFFICIENT ALGORITHM OF FINDING A MINIMAL TRIANGULATION OF A GRAPH.
Abstract: A new method for finding a minimal triangulation of a graph is presented. This efficient new algorithm has a running time proportional to the product of the number of vertices and the number of edges.
Name: ["Fujisawa Toshio", "Orino Hideo"]

Title: STABILIZATION OF LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH UNKNOWN SYSTEM PARAMETERS AND TIME DELAYS.
Abstract: A stability criterion for linear systems with time delays is obtained. Based on this criterion, a method of designing controls which stabilize a class of linear systems containing time delays and unknown system parameters is described. Sufficient conditions for the stabilizability of such systems are developed.
Name: ["Ho Chen-Yao"]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF ARRAYS OF MAITRA CASCADES.
Abstract: A method for testing Boolean functions with don't cares for Maitra cascade realizability is described. This method is extended to formulate a simple algorithm for synthesizing arrays of Maitra cascades. Maitra cascades are iterative interconnections of 2-input, 1-output cells. Each cell is a logic gate which realize at its output any one of the sixteen functions of two variables. The cascade in which no input variable is fed through more than one input is termed an irredundant cascade.
Name: ["Bandyopadhyay S.", "Das S.R.", "Basu S.", "Choudhury A.K."]

Title: Almost Uniform Distributions for Computer Image Enhancement
Abstract: The use of a gray level transformation which transforms a given empirical distribution function of gray level values in an image into a uniform distribution has been used as an image enhancement as well as for a normalization procedure. This transformation produces a discrete variable whose empirical distribution might be expected to be approximately uniform since it is related to the well known distribution transformation. In this correspondence, an extension of the theorem is given which shows that the theorem ‚Äúalmost‚Äù holds for an ‚Äúalmost‚Äù continuous input distribution. The application of the discrete distribution transformation to computer image enhancement is considered. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Hall E.L."]
Keywords: ["computer image enhancement", "distribution transformation", "uniform distribution", "distribution used", "uniform distributions"]

Title: COMMENTS ON MODELS OF MULTI-PROCESSOR MULTI-MEMORY BANK COMPUTER SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Processor degradation produced by access conflicts in multi-processor, multi-memory bank computer systems is considered. Hardware and software parameters which influence performance are outlined and discussed. The incorporation of these parameters in analytic and simulation models is discussed with a view to the predictive merit of the model. Finally a general simulation model of a multi-processor is presented, and results based on its use are analyzed and compared with those of other models. Results relate to the mode of instruction referencing, to the type of bussing between processors and memory modules, to the synchronization of memory modules, to the number of commands per instruction reference, and to the relationship between probabilistic and simulation models.
Name: ["Franta W.R.", "Houle Philip A."]

Title: CONTROL WITH PREDICTION OPTIMIZATION USING DISCRETE LINEAR PREDICTION MODELS OF THE PLANT.
Abstract: The prediction is optimized in a sliding prediction interval. The equations of motion of a closed-loop system are derived, and the effect of the prediction time on the motion and stability of a closed-loop control system with prediction optimization is studied. An asymptotic law is obtained according to which (in the case of a sufficiently long prediction time) the decision taken at the running instant does not change when the prediction time increases. The optimal control is obtained with the aid of Pontryagin's maximum principle; this is possible in the optimization of processes that can be predicted using linear models. In the cases of problems of large dimension, and of nonlinear filters, it is necessary to use self-organization.
Name: ["Ivakhnenko A.G.", "Tolokhnyanenko V.A.", "Yaremenko A.G."]

Title: PROPOSED METHOD FOR GENERATION OF MINIMUM-HARDWARE STATE ASSIGNMENTS.
Abstract: A new procedure is proposed for obtaining minimum or near minimum hardware internal state assignments for asynchronous sequential machines. The procedure is algorithmic and requires a minimum of computation.
Name: ["Sawin III Dwight H."]

Title: MINIMIZATION OF BOOLEAN FUNCTIONS WITH ‚Ä≥DON'T CARES‚Ä≥ SUBJECT TO CONSTRAINTS.
Abstract: An algorithm is given for computing the irredundant sums of Boolean Functions and don't cares subject to constraints. It is shown that extensions of known algorithms are sufficient to solve the problem.
Name: ["Herzog Otthein", "Reusch Bernd", "Riedemann Eike"]

Title: Computerizied Control for Machine Production. | GEPGYARTO RENDSZEREK SZAMITOGEPES IRANYITASA.
Abstract: Development of computerized control systems for automomous subsystems in machine production is discussed.
Name: ["Hatvany Jozsef"]

Title: O( vertical V vertical multiplied by (times) vertical E vertical ) ALGORITHM FOR MAXIMUM MATCHING OF GRAPHS.
Abstract: An algorithm is presented which finds a maximum matching in a graph with n nodes and m edges within time k//1mn plus k//2, where k//1 and k//2 are constants.
