It is also shown that a maximum degree-constrained subgraph can be found within time k//3m**3 plus k//4, where k//3 and k//4 are constants. Use of random access computer is assumed in the computation of the time bounds.
Name: ["Kameda T.", "Munro I."]

Title: ON A SUBSYSTEM OF THE NEURAL NETWORK BEHIND THE BASILAR MEMBRANE.
Abstract: A simplified model of a part of the neural network behind the basilar membrane is described. An approach based on automata theory is made to simulate some facts about single nerves and neurons known in physiology. Results are obtained by simulations on a digital computer.
Name: ["Vollmar R.", "Spreng M."]

Title: LEARNING IN MODIFIABLE F-S AUTOMATA.
Abstract: This paper aims at the investigation of an automata theoretic model of learning systems. Learning is considered as an adaptive, goal directed process which is induced by information from the system's environment. The learning goal is, in general, an activity which, prior to a learning phase, cannot be realized as the system's behavior merely by changing its state. Nevertheless, the system that learns reaches its goal. This, however implies modifiable (state-transition) structures. First are defined automata which are able to modify their structures (modifiable automata), and introduce a performance measure (modification tolerance). Then is investigated the adaptive behavior of two classes of modifiable automata, viz. automata which gradually change their structures (inert modifiable automata) and automata which are stable, i. e. have isometric or metric-decreasing next-state relations (modifiable F-S automata). This leads, for instance, to an approximate fixed point theorem characterizing the potential adaptiveness of certain modifiable F-S automata and to learning processes which give rise to a gradual adaptation of these automata.
Name: ["Dal Cin M."]

Title: FINGERPRINT IMAGE ENHANCEMENT SYSTEM.
Abstract: In automatic fingerprint identification systems, the pattern is converted into an electrical signal. The analog signal is then digitized into levels and then converted into binary signals, for the digital system to perform the pattern recognition. The problem encountered is how to decide whether the signal is either a logic 1 or 0, since there is no reference level to compare with. A logic system is presented that provides a reference level for each point on the print. The reference level for each point is obtained by comparing the average of the gray scale value of a square region surrounding the point. The gray scale of the point is then compared with this average value, to decide whether the point should be called at level 1 or 0.
Name: ["Ting Y.M.", "Ho A.P."]

Title: INTRODUCTION TO L SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The mathematical theory of L systems is introduced by surveying typical problem areas and results within the theory. It assumes knowledge of the rudiments of formal language theory. The theory of L systems was originated by Lindenmayer as an attempt to build mathematical models for the development of simple filamentous organisms. An L-system is a formal description of strings of finite automata, which resemble the behavior of biological cells in that individual automata can change state, subdivide into several new automata, or die out.
Name: ["Rozenberg G."]

Title: STATISTICAL METHODS FOR COMPARING THEOREM PROVING ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: A binary relation on a set of theorem-proving algorithms is defined, using some basic notions of statistics and probability theory. This relation is proved to generate a linear ordering in any given set of theorem-proving algorithms, and serves as an attempt to formalize somehow the often used phrase: ‚Ä≥Algorithm A is better than algorithm B‚Ä≥ , at least in the case of theorem-proving algorithms. A number of assertions describing some basic properties of this relation is stated and proved.
Name: ["Kramosil Ivan", "Zwinogrodzki Zbigniew"]

Title: GENERALIZATION OF THE PROPOSITIONAL CALCULUS FOR PURPOSES OF THE THEORY OF LOGICAL NETS WITH PROBABILISTIC ELEMENTS.
Abstract: The definition of logical nets with probabilistic elements is given. To describe these nets, the logical-probabilistic expressions, as a probabilistic extension of propositional calculus, are introduced. Some fundamental properties of these logical-probabilistic expressions are investigated.
Name: ["Havranek Tomas"]

Title: ARBITRARY POLE PLACEMENT WITH LIMITED NUMBER OF INPUTS AND OUTPUTS.
Abstract: In controller design problems, the quantitative description of the desired controlled system behavior is often given by specifying the closed loop poles. An output-variable, feedback control policy for a linear system of order n, with m outputs and p inputs, is described by u equals minus Gy. Matrix G contains p multiplied by m parameters which may be used to dictate the locations of the closed loop poles. The limiting condition for arbitrary pole placement, without some form of state estimation, is p multiplied by m equals n since the p multiplied by m independent controller parameters may be used to specify the n poles. However, there is no systematic procedure for the design of controllers subject to limiting condition. In this paper, a technique based on model system description is used to design static output-variable feedback controllers with limited number of inputs and outputs. It is shown that arbitrary closed loop pole placement is possible if p plus m greater than equivalent to n plus 1 for sufficiently well coupled systems.
Name: ["Loscutoff W.V."]

Title: OPTIMUM CELLULAR REALIZATION OF SYNCHRONOUS SEQUENTIAL MACHINES WITH UNIFORM INTERCONNECTIONS.
Abstract: The state behavior realization of sequential machines by uniform cellular arrays is considered. It is shown that, if some combinational network is allowed between a cell and its nearest neighbor, than a 2-dimensional cellular array of 2-state cells exists, universal over all sequential machines. A 1-dimensional cellular array is also exhibited, universal over all single input machines which display a mild connectedness property. Finally, it is shown that for any k, there exists a uniform cellular array consisting of k 2-state cells universal proof is exhibited that no n-dimensional cellular array exists, capable of realizing the state behavior of any synchronous sequential machine, without employing either multiple encoding or combination logic cells.
Name: ["Hyman Edward", "Kashef R.Sohrab"]

Title: Review of Pattern Recognition in Medical Diagnosis and Consulting Relative to a New System Model
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A review of pattern recognition applied to medical diagnosis and consulting is presented. Papers (127‚Äîreferences) are evaluated with respect to a new medical system model incorporating concepts of consulting and decision making, the latter based on a Bayesean approach incorporating problem knowledge. This model introduces the consultant as an essential component of the decision system. The model is that of a system with subsystems. A subsystem contains a set of classes, and each class has a class-feature relationship. Features (defined as functions of measurements), complex features, and class-feature relationships provide for introducing a priori medical knowledge and dimensionality reduction. Special features such as significant features, rule-in or rule-out features, and time-dependent features, and special classes such as subclasses and intermediate classes are introduced. Etiology, a method of tracing from one subsystem to another subsystem, also is part of the system. With respect to this model, papers in numerous application areas are reviewed. No single paper fulfills many of the system's properties, and this may be why there are very few, if any, of the results described in these papers being used in health care delivery. Part of the paper is a complementary literature review of 127 papers on computer assisted medical diagnosis and consulting. Name: ["Patrick E.A.", "Stelmack F.P.", "Shen L.Y.L."]

Title: Distributed relaxation processes in sensory adaptation
Abstract: Dynamic description of most receptors, even in their near-linear ranges, has not led to understanding of the underlying physical events - in many instances because their curious transfer functions are not found in the usual repertoire of integral-order control-system analysis. We have described some methods, borrowed from other fields, which allow one to map any linear frequency response onto a putative weighting over an ensemble of simpler relaxation processes. One can then ask whether the resultant weighting of such processes suggests a corresponding plausible distribution of values for an appropriate physical variable within the sensory transducer. To illustrate this approach, we have chosen the fractional-order low-frequency response of Limulus lateral-eye photoreceptors. We show first that the current "adapting-bump" hypothesis for the generator potential can be formulated in terms of local first-order relaxation processes in which local light flux, the cross section of rhodopsin for photon capture, and restoration rate of local conductance-changing capability play specific roles. A representative spatial distribution for one of these parameters, which just accounts for the low-frequency response of the receptor, is then derived and its relation to cellular properties and recent experiments is examined. Finally, we show that for such a system, nonintegral-order dynamics are equivalent to nonhyperbolic statics, and that the efficacy distribution derived to account for the small-signal dynamics in fact predicts several decades of near-logarithmic response in the steady state. Encouraged by the result that one plausible proposal can account approximately for both the low-frequency dynamics (the transfer function s<sup>Œ∫</sup>) and the range-compressing statics (the Weber-Fechner relationship) measured in this photoreceptor, we have described some formally similar applications of these distributed effects to the vertebrate retina and to analogous properties of mechanoreceptors and chemoreceptors.
Name: ["Thorson J.", "Biederman-Thorson M."]
Affiliations: ['Max-Planck-Institut f√ºr Verhaltensphysiologie', ' Oxford University', 'Old Marlborough Arms']

Title: INTERACTIVE MAN-MACHINE APPROACH TO THE COMPUTER LOGIC PARTITIONING PROBLEM.
Abstract: The problem of partitioning computer logic has been attacked in the past by manual and automatic techniques. Described here is an interactive approach which combines aspects of both approaches and creates results which are better than those obtainable by either approach independently. An overview of the system is presented, several algorithms are discussed and experimental results are given.
Name: ["Hanan M.", "Mennone A.", "Wolff Sr. P.K."]

Title: AUTOMATED INSPECTION OF ELECTRONIC ASSEMBLIES.
Abstract: Automated Visual Inspection Systems for electronic assemblies are investigated. Three major phases are considered: scanning devices, software algorithms, and possible computer systems.
Name: ["Harlow C.A.", "Henderson S.E.", "Rayfield D.A.", "Johnston R.J.", "Dwyer III S.J."]

Title: HIGH SPEED IMAGE ANALYSIS.
Abstract: Optical Power Spectrum (OPS) measurements can often be used to drastically reduce the amount of information to be processed by an automatic image analysis system. This data reduction makes it possible to process at the rate of 1000 image areas per second or faster. This is frequently millions of times faster than can be accomplished with conventional (all digital) processing techniques. The Optical Power Spectrum (or Fraunhofer diffraction pattern) is formed by a simple laser and lens. It is a measure of the frequency content of the image and thus provides information about the presence and sharpness of edges and about the size of objects in the image. The utility of these high-speed techniques has been demonstrated for a number of applications including cloud screening, area correlation, detection of Black lung disease in chest X-rays, the determination of image quality, and terrain classification.
Name: ["Jensen Niels", "Kasdan Harvey", "Mead Donald C.", "Thomasson James"]

Title: Simulation as a Tool for Assessment of the Interface Man-Machine, with the Aid of Digital Computers. | EINE SIMULATIONSMETHODE ZUR UNTERSUCHUNG UND VERBESSERUNG DER WECHSELWIRKUNGEN AN DER SCHNITTSTELLE MENSCH-MASCHINE MIT HILFE EINES DIGITALRECHNERS.
Abstract: A method is presented able to serve as a useful tool for simulation of system processes in man-machine systems with special emphasis on the interactions at the man-machine-interface. A dynamic functional model of the man-machine-system and its intended mission environment was simulated on a digital computer. The simulation model includes operator functions, such as information selection, decision making etc. , and a selection of relevant system and environmental processes.
Name: ["Doering B."]

Title: INTEGER ARITHMETIC PATH EXPANSION ALGORITHM.
Abstract: Graphical display systems are often built around a minicomputer with limited word size, core, and instruction repertoire. Thus, plotting algorithms which do not need floating point software or hardware are particularly valuable. Extending the integer arithmetic functional plotting concepts, integer algorithms are presented for the calculation of Euclidean distance, plotting of lines perpendicular and parallel to a given line segment, and the calculations of the intersection of two (slant) lines, all to an accuracy of one screen unit. These algorithms are combined into an algorithm to plot the outline of a path expanded from a centerline of straight-line segments, with unrestricted orientations. The algorithms have been implemented on a PDP-8 minicomputer with a Tektronics 611 storage scope. They are routinely used to display integrated circuit mask descriptions.
Name: ["Weber T.A.", "Schweikert D.G."]

Title: Results in the application of pattern recognition methods to nuclear reactor core component surveillance
Abstract: Pattern recognition methods were applied to analyze and interpret neutron noise data from the High Flux Isotope Reactor (HFIR) at ORNL. The results show that it is feasible to detect some core component failures by means of machine-discernible differences in the time-dependent noise power spectra. These neutron spectra (signatures) were analyzed by using acluster-seeking algorithm to derive a set of templates for automatic computer evaluation of the reactor's mechanical integrity and soundness. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Gonzalez R.C.", "Fry D.N.", "Kryter R.C.", "Gonzalez R.C."]
Affiliations: ['Oak Ridge National Laboratory', ' University of Tennessee']

Title: ESTIMATION IN MULTISERVER QUEUING SIMULATIONS.
Abstract: The paper presents methods for computing point and interval estimates of descriptors of simulated queuing systems. In particular it is shown that computation of three sample quantities suffices to generate point and interval estimates for twelve system descriptors.
Name: ["Fishman George S."]

Title: GRAPH GRAMMARS FOR THE SPECIALIZATION OF ORGANISMS.
Abstract: The use of the theory of graph grammars is presented for the description of the process of specialization of organisms (as represented by graphs) as productions in a graph grammar and derivation of graphs. The basic notions are developed of graph grammars which are based on categorical concepts, especially the one of pushout. After an introduction to the underlying biological idea, the graph grammar concept is applied to a simple example of specialization, then an algorithm for the general specialization process is given. Two theorems about subderivations and derivations of homomorphic images are given.
Name: ["Ehrig Hartmut", "Tischer Karl Wilhelm"]

Title: Indirect Adaptive System with a Model in a Speed Control Loop of a Converter Drive. | POSREDNI UKLAD ADAPTACYJNY Z MODELEM W OBWODZIE REGULACJI PREDKOSCI NAPEDU PRZEKSZTALTNIKOWEGO.
Abstract: A synthesis method of an identification algorithm is presented for systems with learning models. The synthesis of an adaptive speed control system of a converter drive with a separately excited dc motor is outlined. This controller assures time invariant dynamic properties of the control system for the case when the electromechanical time constant and field flux value are fluctuating. Theoretical considerations are supported by the results of tests of the designed system, directly recorded by an analog computer.
Name: ["Kazmierkowski Marian P."]

Title: Fuzzy-PLANNER: Reasoning with inexact concepts in a procedural problem-solving language
Abstract: All contemporary deductive problem-solving paradigms deal with a world in which assertions are true (false) and action-rules valid (invalid). This simplified situation is inadequate for realistic applications which include inexact information. This article describes a precise computationally specific method for coupling two' different many-valued logics with a procedural problem-solving system (micro-PLANNER). Solutions to deductive problems can be found which meet specific criteria of validity. This particular scheme enables the system to dynamically compute the truth-value of a subgoal during the search process. Thus, the validity of a subgoal may be used to direct the heuristic search procedure. Fuzzy-PLANNER is a promising medium for experimenting with different many-valued logics to find the ones most appropriate for different problem domains. However, the notions elaborated here are relevant to any procedural problem-solving language. ¬© 1975 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Kling R."]

Title: Classification of Stoping Pillars for Long-Term Control of the Development of Mining Work in Coal Mines. | [KLASSIFIKATSIYA VYEMOCHNYKH STOLBOV DLYA PERSPEKTIVNOGO UPRAVLENIYA RAZVITIEM GORNYKH RABOT NA SHAKHTE.]
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii, Gornyi Zhurnal
Abstract: A model of representation of mining and geological information on stoping pillars for purposes of long-term control of the development of the mining work is set forth. The method is based on two principles: the principle of the ‚Ä≥output classification‚Ä≥ and the ‚Ä≥typification‚Ä≥ principle. It is proposed to use methods of the pattern recognition theory as the mathematical tool permitting realization of these principles. Relying on the recognition methods, a classification algorithm is compiled and a program for a ‚Ä≥Minsk-22‚Ä≥ computer is constructed in accordance with it.
Name: ["Vorob'ev B.M.", "Komkov V.V."]

Title: SIMULATION OF PASSENGER MOVEMENTS THROUGH A TRANSIT STATION.
Abstract: The simulation model being developed is a discrete-system, event-oriented representation of the movement of individual passengers through a transit station. The model is stochastic in nature with the entities of the system being the individual passengers whose movement through various activities in the station give rise to the events which drive the simulation. Station activity subsystems, such as the ticketing areas, passenger movement areas and platforms, are represented by links, nodes, and areas. The outputs from the model are Time Impedance Measures (e. g. , Walking Times, Time spent in queue, and Total In-Station Time) and Occupancy or Density Levels (sq ft. per person) in the movement and queueing areas of the station.
Name: ["Fausch Peter A.", "Dillard David", "Hoffmeister John F."]

Title: Nearer to the sites where the data originate! First steps toward progressive solutions of data documentation | [HIN ZU DEN ORTEN DER DATENENTSTEHUNG! ANSATZE ZU FORTSCHRITTLICHEN LOSUNGEN DER DATENERFASSUNG]
Abstract: Information problems are often considered and solved, isolated and independent from the real processes which generate these problems. The data processed, originate both temporally and spatially in the very process from which this problem solving isolates itself. The development of mechanical and electronic data processing therefore requires a renewed reference to real process, to the sites where data originate. The author lists the problem involved in data documentation and reviews conventional solutions. The possibilities for progressive solutions of data documentation are mapped out. Three ideas are presented and discussed whose implementation will improve data processing: acceleration of data processing with the use of new hardware; rationalisation of data processing through the elimination of superfluous intermediate and control processes; abridging communication distances. The author concludes that the first steps towards these improvements are organisational rather than technical.
Name: ["Mann D."]

Title: An abstract machine theory for formal language parsers
Abstract: The usual data necessary for any abstract machine theory is given in categorical terminology. In these terms, an abstract machine theory for formal language parsers is developed, exposing the essential nature of any left-to-right parsing scheme. A weak classification of all parsers for a given language is developed and the usual notions of initial machine, reachable machine and minimal machine apply. Minimality is an extremely weak notion in this theory, although it is equivalent to a simple form of immediate error detection for parsers. Remarks on the construction of parsing procedures are given. ¬© 1974 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Benson D.B."]

Title: Stable Fixed-Lag Smoothing of Continuous-Time Processes
Abstract: Attempts to realize optimal fixed-lag smoothers for continuous-time processes have encountered two major difficulties: the presence of delay lines in the smoother, and the instability of most smoothers. This paper considers suboptimal smoothers which still outperform filters and have performance very close to the optimum. Design procedures are exhibited for smoothers that are both finite-dimensional and asymptotically stable, with the procedures depending on the delay line being approximated by a finite-dimensional dynamical system. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Chirarattananon S.", "Anderson B.D.O."]

Title: COMPUTATION OF APPROXIMATELY OPTIMAL CONTROL SIGNALS FOR SYSTEMS WITH TIME DELAYS.
Abstract: A computational algorithm is presented for a class of optimal control problems involving time delays. The approach is to restrict the control signal to a class of piecewise constant time functions with a prescribed number of switching times, compute the optimal member of this class, and then repeat with a larger number of switching time. By allowing the number of switching times to increase beyond bound a sequence of restricted optimal control signals is developed whose limit approaches the unrestricted optimal control signal. In practice the computations are terminated after a finite number of repeats, thus leading to the approximate nature of the solution. The results of two examples are included to illustrate the technique.
Name: ["Horwitz L.B."]

Title: DISCRETE AND CONTINUOUS COMPLEMENTARY FILTERING.
Abstract: Consideration is given to a class of filters which are of significant practical importance, having the capabilities of generating estimates of the desired state variables, using a structure which is relatively uncomplicated. It is shown that under certain steady state conditions the filters clearly exhibit what has been referred to as a complementary property. Both continuous and discrete versions of the problem are considered. The complementary filtering technique presented is useful for those situations in which one does not have a complete dynamical description of the random system generating the state variables to be estimated. It is also useful when attempting to generate estimates using a rather simple filter structure, even though enough information might be available concerning the process so that better results could be obtained using a filter structure of greater complexity.
Name: ["Sims Craig S."]

Title: Model reference adaptive control based on liapunov's direct method: Part II: Hybrid Computer Simulation and Experimental Application
Abstract: A Model Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC) system is evaluated via hybrid computer simulation and experimental application to a computer-controlled, pilot plant evaporator. In both the simulation and experimental studies, the MRAC system performed well and was insensitive to unmeasured process disturbances, to the choice of the initial control policy and to changes in plant operating conditions. In addition to providing an algorithm for adapting control systems to accommodate changing process parameters, MRAC also provides a systematic approach for tuning or developing multivariable control systems for time-invariant processes. ¬© 1974, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Kent Oliver W.", "Seborg D.E.", "Grant Fisher D."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF LINEAR RECURSIVE FILTERS OPTIMAL IN THE MINIMAX SENSE.
Abstract: A method is described for the design of recursive minimax digital filters. The procedure involves an iterative algorithm which is a modification of the second Remes algorithm which enables one to design both recursive and nonrecursive digital filters exhibiting minimax behavior over the continuum rather than a finite set of points. The normalized magnitude square of the frequency response is considered, but the procedure may be extended to other filter parameters.
Name: ["Holtz Howard"]

Title: Zur Extrapolation in Markoffschen Entscheidungsmodellen mit Diskontierung
Abstract: The paper deals with Markovian decision models (discrete Markov chains, semi-Markov processes, regenerative processes) with finite state and action space in the case of discounting future rewards. A unified method is derived to obtain upper and lower bounds for the optimal objective function based on iterates of value iteration or successive overrelaxation. Finally some numerical tests for the resulting algorithms are given. ¬© 1974 Physica-Verlag.
Name: ["Schellhaas H."]

Title: ON THE INFORMATION STABILITY OF STATIONARY ERGODIC PROCESSES.
Abstract: Conditions are derived under which two jointly stationary and ergodic sequences of random variables have a finite information rate and are information stable. The results are extended to the case of continuous-parameter stochastic processes.
Name: ["Kadota T.T."]

Title: ON MULTI-THRESHOLD FUNCTION AND MULTI-THRESHOLD ELEMENT NETWORKS.
Abstract: Properties of multithreshold function (MTF), the synthesis of the given switching function by cascade multithreshold element (MTE) network and the size of MTE networks are considered. In these networks, each MTE has the different weight vector for the input variables and the same number of thresholds. The fundamental networks treated here are cascade, 2-level and feedforward MTE networks.
Name: ["Imamiya Atsumi", "Noguchi Shoichi", "Oizumi Juro"]

Title: VALIDATION OF COMPUTER SIMULATION MODELS USING PARAMETRIC TIME SERIES ANALYSIS.
Abstract: A statistical testing procedure is suggested to perform the comparison of the time-dependence structure between realistic and simulation-generated data. The time series technique concerned can be used to perform forecasting, which is usually more efficient and cheaper than ordinary simulation methods, under various experimental conditions.
Name: ["Hsu Der-Ann", "Hunter J.Stuart"]

Title: HEURISTICALLY ORIENTED APPROACH TO SCHEDULING BATCH PRODUCTION ORIENTED COMPUTER SYSTEMS.
Abstract: An objective function is provided and an approach is outlined to heuristically scheduling production oriented batch computer systems based upon the existence of a fast (approximately 100 times faster than real time) means for predicting the performance of a given system for a given schedule.
Name: ["Kimbleton Stephen R.", "Baker Kenneth R."]

Title: INPUT DESIGN FOR MODEL DISCRIMINATION WITH APPLICATION TO RESPIRATORY CONTROL.
Abstract: Input design is considered for discrimination among a set of alternative structural models all competing to characterize the same physical process. The class of models considered consists of a set of nonlinear differential equations whose output can only be observed at discrete times through a noisy observation. The input is constrained by physical considerations and the design is considered in terms of the probability of error in model selection. The results provide rationale for designing experiments for human respiratory controller, model discrimination studies.
Name: ["Swanson George D.", "Bellville J.Weldon"]

Title: DUAL MULTIPLE-RESOURCE ASSIGNMENT ALGORITHM.
Abstract: The multiple-resource assignment problem has given a set of resources left brace resource 1, resource 2,. . . , resource n right brace , and a set of categories, left brace category 1, category 2,. . . , catetory m right brace , with m less than equivalent to n, and a rating matrix that represents the value of assigning resource i to category j. An algorithm is presented that finds all the best assignments in O(nm) steps. In many situations it is important to find the assignment or set of assignments with maximum value.
Name: ["Tiernan James C."]

Title: DIGITAL SIMULATION OF STATIONARY GAUSSIAN LOADS.
Source: Pol Acad Sci Inst Fundam Tech Res Nonlinear Vib Probl
Abstract: This study is concerned with a digital simulation technique for representing a non-white stationary Gaussian random process. A filtered white noise random process is obtained by passing an approximate white noise random process through a linear filter. As applications, jet engine sound pressures, boundary layer pressure fluctuations and gust loadings in atmospheric turbulence are simulated by using various types of first and second order linear filters.
Name: ["Kanematsu H.", "Nash W.A."]

Title: Sample interval and spot shape for digital image processing systems
Source: Proceedings of SPIE - The International Society for Optical Engineering
Abstract: During the past decade substantial advances in processing speed, memory size and software have occurred in computer technology. Similar advances have resulted in highly sophisticated communication systems. These developments have enabled digital electronic methods to become a practical photographic image processing technique. For example, a recently developed change detection system (Ref. 1) is capable of processing 400,000 image points per second. This and other digital image processing systems generally result from special purpose applications of algorithms developed on large scale, general purpose digital computers. ¬© 1974 SPIE.
Name: ["Glish J."]

Title: Finding Optimal Demand Paging Algorithms
Abstract: A cost is defined for demand paging algorithms with respect to a formal stochastic model of program behavior. This cost is shown to exist under rather general assumptions, and a computational procedure is given which makes it possible to determine the optimal cost and optimal policy for moderate size programs, when the formal model is known and not time dependent. In this latter case it is shown that these computational procedures may be extended to larger programs to obtain arbitrarily close approximations to their optimal policies. In previous models either unwarranted information is assumed beyond the formal model, or the complete stochastic nature of the model is not taken into account. ¬© 1974, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Ingargiola G.", "Korsh J.F."]
Affiliations: ['California Institute of Technology', ' School of Business Adminsitration', 'California Institute of Technology']

Title: Intelligent Automatic Game Partner for the Game of Nim.. | [EIN INTELLIGENTER MASCHINELLER SPIELPARTNER FUER DAS NIM-SPIEL.]
Abstract: As a contribution to machine intelligence, a game automaton for the Nim game is described. The automaton simulates the failure-inherent human game strategies. Game records compare the automaton to human game partners, at the same time showing the human players' learning behavior.
Name: ["Wernicke J."]

Title: Certain Method for the Synthesis of Boolean Generators of Random Signals. | O PWENEJ METODZIE SYNTEZY GENERATOROW BOOLOWSKICH SYGNALOW PRZYPADKOWYCH.
Abstract: A new synthesis method is described which is based on the use of logic networks with feedback loops. It is shown how to construct the generator of a random Boolean variable y(t) with a given distribution function. It is proved that the frequency of output switchings for such a network is limited and stable (on the average). The algorithm used to solve the problem is illustrated with a simple example.
Name: ["Ruszczynski Andrzej"]

Title: Minimum Variance Control for Linear Discrete Systems - 1. | LINEARIS DISZKRET IDEJU RENDSZEREK MINIMALIS SZORASU IRANYITASA - 1.
Abstract: The paper discusses the minimum variance control of constant parameter, linear, discrete time systems. Disturbances reaching the system are taken into consideration as a stochastic process of rational spectrum reduced to the output. The individual chapters are giving algorithms for the cases of systems with known and unknown parameters. Beyond the methods already known, a new method is also presented suited for solving control with minimum variance. This process uses the generalized method of least squares for the adaptive estimation of the parameter of the optimum controller.
Name: ["Hetthessy Jeno", "Keviczky Laszlo"]

Title: Minimax Predictors for Signals Having a Bonded kth Derivative
Abstract: Predictors are derived which minimize the maximum possible mean-squared prediction error for signals observed in white noise and having a bounded kth derivative. Expressions are given for the resulting worst-case error and a suboptimal solution is presented which, for the case k = 2, performs nearly as well as the optimal and is far easier to implement. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Kelsey D.W.", "Haddad A.H."]
Affiliations: [' Coordinated Science Laboratory University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign']

Title: Time Optimal Multivariable Control of LInear Sampled Data Systems with Bounded Correcting Variables. | [ZEITOPTIMALE MEHRFACHREGELUNG LINEARER ABTASTSYSTEME MIT BESCHRAENKTEN STELLGROESSEN.]
Abstract: The problem of time optimal control of linear sampled data systems with several bounded control variables is formulated. It is shown, that the convexity of certain controllable state sets allows the synthesis of a multi-variable controller by a series of those standard controllers that were proposed by Ludyk. As an example, a standard controller is described for an important class of systems in a form that is independent of the system order and that can be programmed easily.
Name: ["Brueck P."]

Title: GRADIENT - REGRESSION SEARCH PROCEDURE FOR SIMULATION EXPERIMENTATION.
Abstract: A gradient search procedure for simulation experimentation with constrained systems is examined. This procedure combines gradient search with curvilinear regression in moving toward a constrained optimal solution for a system involving n controllable variables. In a direction-determining block, at least n plus 1 simulation trials are performed around a current base point to establish an improving direction. Then in a step determining block, t simulation trials are performed along the improving direction to establish the most favorable step in moving to the next base point. This sequential block process, in which each block is executed in one input to the computer, is repeated until an approximate solution is found which satisfies all system constraints.
Name: ["Biles William Ernest"]

Title: SAND SHIFTING VIEWED AS A GAUSS-MARKOFF PROCESS.
Abstract: Sand movement by wind saltation, creep and water erosion is modelled as a Markoff chain and as a Gauss-Markoff sequence. Computer simulation results are given.
Name: ["Gold S.J.", "Wood W.H."]

Title: ON THE FACTORIZATION OF SEMI-SEPARABLE KERNELS.
Abstract: Necessary and sufficient conditions are derived for the nonnegative-definiteness of semi-separable symmetric kernels containing a weighted identity operator. A limiting approach is used to obtain a special factorization of such kernels. This factorization obeys a minimum property, and the limit approach permits the approximation of such kernels by covariances of the outputs of finite-dimensional linear systems driven by white noise.
Name: ["Krasner Norman", "Kailath Thomas"]

Title: Bayes' Approach to Electric Power System State Estimation. | BAIESOV PODKHOD K OTSENKE SOSTOYANIYA ELEKTROENERGETICHESKOI SISTEMY.
Abstract: Consideration is given to the problem of calculating the parameters of the operating conditions of en electric power system by using the data of inexact measurements in a statistical formulation (by measurement at a particular moment in time) and in a dynamic formulation (by a series of successive measurements). The mathematical tool is based on a combination of Bayes' approach and of the fundamental principles of the reduced gradient methods. It is concluded that this method is effective and adaptable; it provides a sufficiently free choice of coordinates for solving a problem; it is well suited to the operation with data acquisition systems carrying out successive interrogations of sensors.
Name: ["Gamm A.Z."]

Title: SUBOPTIMAL CONTROL OF THE CONTINUOUS-TIME LINEAR REGULATOR WITH UNKNOWN GAIN DYNAMICS.
Abstract: The suboptimal control of linear continuous-time stochastic systems with Gauss-Markov unknown gain parameters is considered. The types of controllers considered are: 1) open-loop-feedback-optimal control, 2) enforced separation control, and 3) a combination of per-interval control with switching to enforced separation control after the gain uncertainty decreases below a certain threshold. Correlated noises and costs between the sampling instants are considered. Qualitative properties of the OLFO system are discussed. Simulation results dealing with the control of stable and unstable third-order plants are presented.
Name: ["Adams Thomas L.", "Emad Fawzi P."]

Title: IMPLEMENTED TECHNIQUES FOR HANDLING SPIKES IN AN ASSIGNABLE DELAY SIMULATOR.
Abstract: A technique is developed to perform spike and hazard analysis in a less pessimistic approach than has been used previously. It was implemented as an extension of the TEGAS2 simulation system and is capable of associating different turn-on and turn-off propagation delays with an element. A hazard can be defined as the situation in which two or more inputs to a particular gate arrive at slightly different times, causing an anomaly in the output of the gate. A spike is the result of an attempt to change the output of a gate at a rate faster than its turn-on or turn-off propagation delay time. Methods for detecting timing problems are investigated and analyzed.
Name: ["Szygenda S.A.", "Lekkos A.", "Fike J."]

Title: A computer-based system of speech-training AIDS for the deaf‚ÄîA progress report
Source: AFIPS Conference Proceedings - 1974 National Computer Conference, AFIPS 1974
Abstract: This paper is a progress report on an effort to develop a computer-based system of speech-training aids for the deaf. The project was begun with the assumption that an attempt to design such a system would probably fail, and that a more promising approach would be to attempt to evolve one through use. Accordingly, a system incorporating some of the capabilities that it was thought would be useful for speech training was developed, and installed at the Clarke School for the Deaf where it is now being used on an experimental basis in a remedial speech-training program. The expectation was that the capabilities of the system would be modified and extended as attempts to use it provided insights concerning what features it should have. To ensure that such insights do in fact guide the system's evolution, developers and users are engaged in a continuing dialogue concerning the desirability and feasibility of specific modifications and extensions, both in the training procedures that are used in conjunction with the system and in the characteristics of the system itself. ¬© ACM-CONFERENCE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Nickerson R.S.", "Kalikow D.N.", "Stevens K.N."]

Title: A model for the evaluation of large scale data retrieval systems
Abstract: The model described in this paper provides a methodology for evaluating large scale data retrieval systems by measuring the retrieval work load associated with a set of user queries, a specified file organization, and a given data base. ¬© Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Siler K.F."]

Title: ON-LINE DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEM FOR SMALL DUPLEX PROCESSORS.
Abstract: The Metaconta switching system is controlled by two ITT 1600 processors operating in a duplex configuration. To minimize machine down-time in the event of a failure, a diagnostic technique has been developed that enables the working machine to test the failing one. The system has a supervisory program in the core store that reads diagnostic data from paper tape and performs the tests specified by the tape. This is an on-line diagnostic technique because only a small percentage of total processing time is spent on fault detection while the operational processor continues to handle the full load of calls. System software is organized so that the traffic handling capacity of the exchange is unaffected even when running during peak hours. When the diagnostic procedure conclusively identifies a fault, an error message is output indicating the names of the printed boards which could contain the fault. If no fault is detected, a message states this. A simple assembly type language and assembler have been developed for the diagnostic test data. To ensure accurate fault location, the diagnostic test data were verified over a considerable period.
Name: ["Rijmenams Rene J.", "Callahan David G."]

Title: GENERALIZED LINEAR ESTIMATE OF FUNCTIONS OF RANDOM MATRIX ARGUMENTS.
Abstract: The optimal linear estimation problem in a generalized formulation is considered for a function of observational data matrix being a sum of random matrix signals and of a matrix of observation errors or noise. The criterion of optimality is the minimization of the penalty which is a linear combination of the squares of the norms of two kinds of errors: of the error matrix which would take place in estimation without noise and of the matrix of actual estimating errors. Results are applicable also in the case of deficient rank of covariance matrices and/or of signal model. Correlation of signals with the noise is allowed. A priori statistics of signals can be incorporated to improve the estimates. It is shown that different known generalizations of least squares estimates are special cases of the minimum penalty estimate.
Name: ["Kovanic Pavel"]

Title: A rotational procedure for separation of trait, method and interaction factors in multitrait-multimethod matrices
Abstract: A rotational procedure is derived for handling factor matrices of multiway classification data. The solution is formulated in terms of multitrait-multimethod data. Given a factor structure of a multitrait-multimethod correlation matrix, ordered by traits within methods, a method factor is defined as one that has constant entries in each method section, a trait factor as one that has periodic entries, and an interaction factor as one that has variable entries both for traits and methods. A rotation is derived for separation of trait, method, and interaction factors. A numerical illustration is given to show that the procedure may also be employed for rotation to a hierarchical structure. ¬© 1974, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Levin J."]

Title: DEGREE OF A POLYNOMIAL MATRIX AND EXPLICIT FORMULA FOR THE ORDER OF COMPLEXITY OF LINEAR ACTIVE NETWORKS.
Abstract: Through the definition of the degree of a polynomial matrix, it has been possible to characterize an index rho which measures the degree of improperness of the polynomial matrix, which in turn determines the degree of the determinant of the polynomial matrix. The results are used to express explicitly the order of complexity of linear active networks.
Name: ["Ho Y.S.", "Roe P.H."]

Title: SELF-SCALING VARIABLE METRIC (SSVM) ALGORITHMS - 1, 2.
Abstract: A new criterion is introduced for comparing the convergence properties of variable metric algorithms, focusing on stepwise descent properties. This criterion is a bound on the rate of decrease in the function value at each iterative step (single-step convergence rate). Using this criterion as a basis for algorithm development leads to the introduction of variable coefficients to rescale the objective function at each iteration, and, correspondingly, to a new class of variable metric algorithms. Effective scaling can be implemented by restricting the parameters in a two-parameter family of variable metric algorithms. Conditions are derived for these parameters that guarantee monotonic improvement in the single-step convergence rate. Also introduced are some possible implementations of Self-Scaling Variable Metric Algorithms based on the theory that is presented. These implementations are analyzed theoretically and discussed qualitatively. A special class of SSVM algorithms is introduced, which has the additional property of being invariant under scaling of the objective function or of the variables. Experimental results are provided for a particular case of this class. This case has been tested in comparison to the DFP algorithm on a variety of functions with up to 50 variables. The results indicate that the new method has substantial advantage for functions with a large number of variables.
Name: ["Oren Shmuel S.", "Luenberger David G."]

Title: NEW AIR FORCE MASTER PERSONNEL RECORD SYSTEM.
Abstract: The Federal Government has many extremely large document centers that store vast quantities of paper or hardcopy information for management and/or archival purposes. In some instances, these documents must be stored, maintained and retrieved at either the document, single-page or sub-page level at extremely high update rates. This storage problem is further complicated by the legal requirements to keep either hardcopy or silver halide film for archival purposes. The problems faced by the records manager of a large scale, high usage, hardcopy records system are discussed, using the Military Personnel Record System, under the control of the Air Force Military Personnel Center (AFMPC), as an example of such a system. In 1969, the Rome Air Developmlent Center (RADC) undertook a research project to determine the best available method of automating the paper records at AFMPC and developing, acquiring and testing a pilot of that system. The system selected - AFMPC Microform System - is described in detail. Each subsection - Automatic Data Processing, File Conversion, and Image Storage and Retrieval - is broken down into its component parts and their function is described. Information collected, statistics and interim results found are given.
Name: ["Osinski Anthony E.", "Thayer R.H."]

Title: OPTIMAL BACKBOARD ORDERING THROUGH THE SHORTEST PATH ALGORITHM.
Abstract: A search is reported for such an ordering of mother boards of a large scale system that the total length of the inter-connecting wires be minimal. It is shown that a directed and weighted, linear graph may be produced, on which this problem is equivalent to finding the shortest path between a unique source and a unique sink. An algorithm for tracing the shortest path is presented. This algorithm takes advantage of the special features of the auxiliary graph and reduces significantly the computational effort required.
Name: ["Cederbaum I."]

Title: EFFICIENT COMPUTER ALGORITHM FOR THE SIMULATION OF STIFF LINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: It is proposed to achieve efficiency in the time-domain analysis of a single-input, single-output linear time-invariant system with widely separated time constants by applying stiffly stable integration formulas to a system representation whose computational complexity grows only linearly with the number of natural modes. The idea of obtaining sparsity by representing the system as a cascade of subsystems is joined with the modified Gear-Nordsieck formulas proposed by B. Brayton, et al (see Engineering Index 1972 596 Abstract 57267) to obtain a variable-stepsize-and-order method suitable for stiff linear systems. A byproduct of the cascade representation is the ability to bypass subsystems which have practically reached a steady state (a ‚Ä≥shortcut formulas ‚Ä≥).
Name: ["Tan Cary C.", "Pottle Christopher"]

Title: Computational complexity of probabilistic turing machines
Source: Proceedings of the Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing
Abstract: Probabilistic Turing machines are Turing machines with the ability to flip coins in order to make random decisions. We allow probabilistic Turing machines small but nonzero error probability in computing number-theoretic functions. An example is given of a function computable more quickly by probabilistic Turing machines than by deterministic Turing machines. It is shown how probabilistic linear-bounded automata can simulate nondetermin-istic linear-bounded automata. ¬© Association for Computing Machinery. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gill J.T., III"]

Title: Time Analysis with Digital Simulation.
Abstract: Peculiarities of the digital simulation of digital filters are investigated after having defined the term of digital filter. Rules for calculating with pseudo fixed-point numbers treated as floating points are derived. The possibility of calculating with a shortened word length is considered.
Name: ["Harder W."]

Title: CONVERGENCE RATE ACCELERATION OF SUCCESSIVE APPROXIMATION ALGORITHMS IN REAL-TIME CASE.
Abstract: Some of the results of the study of non-asymptotically optimum procedures are reported. In this case the optimum of convergence rate is formulated by F. N. Saridis. This paper shows an unusual principle of study for cases of stochastic and real time.
Name: ["Bencsik Istvan"]

Title: OPTIMAL ALGORITHMS IN EVALUATING ARITHMETIC OR LOGICAL EXPRESSIONS IN PARALLEL.
Abstract: An optimal algorithm is introduced for generating the syntactic tree of an arbitrary program statement in the form of an arithmetic or a logical expression such that the execution time is minimum in a parallel processing environment. In addition, a scheduling discipline is developed for scheduling these detected parallel processable tasks in a pipeline system under the model of n jobs and two facilities, namely, memory fetch and task execution units. The optimal algorithms thus developed can also be applied to a non-pipeline multiprocessor system.
Name: ["Ramamoorthy C.V.", "Li H.F."]

Title: Simulating Stable Stochastic Systems, I: General Multiserver Queues
Abstract: A technique is introduced for analyzing simulations of stochastic systems in the steady state. From the viewpoint of classical statistics, questions of simulation run duration and of starting and stopping simulations are addressed. This is possible because of the existence of a random grouping of observations which produces independent identically distributed blocks from the start of the simulation. The analysis is presented in the context of the general multiserver queue, with arbitrarily distributed interarrival and service times. In this case, it is the busy period structure of the system which produces the grouping mentioned above. Numerical illustrations are given for the M/M/1 queue. Statistical methods are employed so as to obtain confidence intervals for a variety of parameters of interest, such as the expected value of the stationary customer waiting time, the expected value of a function of the stationary waiting time, the expected number of customers served and length of a busy cycle, the tail of the stationary waiting time distribution, and the standard deviation of the stationary waiting time. Consideration is also given to determining system sensitivity to errors and uncertainty in the input parameters. ¬© 1974, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Crane M.A.", "Iglehart D.L."]

Title: TIME-OPTIMAL CONTROL OF LINEAR PLANT AFFECTED BY DISTURBANCE BEING POLYNOMIAL FUNCTION OF TIME.
Source: Bull Acad Pol Sci, Ser Sci Tech
Abstract: The minimum-time control of a single-input, single-output linear time-invariant plant affected by a given external disturbance being a polynomial function of the time is considered. The method for determining the switching instants is presented, based on our complex-analytical procedure.
Name: ["Pelczewski W.", "Lawrynowicz J."]

Title: ADAPTIVE PATTERN PROCESSING IN THE VISUAL SYSTEM.
Abstract: A neuronal network capable of learning pattern discrimination is proposed. Basic characteristics of the component neurons largely reflect well-established physiological principles and their individual plastic properties are consistent with recent findings concerning visual experience and synaptic changes detected by electron-microscopy. Pattern discrimination within the network is robust under rather severe input-pattern degradation.
Name: ["Trehub Arnold"]

Title: Note on analogue memory automata
Abstract: A hybrid automaton that has an analogue memory, that is, an analogue memory automaton (AMA), is proposed. Further, a multiplicative AMA (MAMA) that has only analogue multiplication function is presented. As a special case of MAMA, a counter machine and counter language are considered. Furthermore, a MAMA event is defined as a final value of the analogue memory of MAMA, and it is shown that the MAMA event is a subclass of the probabilistic event. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Tamura S.", "Tanaka K."]

Title: APPLICATION OF LOGICAL-PROBABILISTIC EXPRESSIONS TO THE REALIZATION OF STOCHASTIC AUTOMATA.
Abstract: Methods are suggested for the realization of stochastic automata and probabilistic operators. These methods are based on the notion of logical-probabilistic expression. It is pointed out that T. Havranek's articles on logical-probabilistic expressions, appearing in Numbers 1 and 2 of Kybernetika 10 (1974) consecutively, are necessary reading for full understanding of this study.
Name: ["Havranek Tomas"]

Title: Problems in Adaptive Control Optimization for Machine Tool Processes. | AZ OPTIMALIZALO ADAPTIV SZERSZAMGEPIRANYITAS NEHANY PROBLEMAJA.
Abstract: Optimization of machine tool processes. The objective is to give the foundations necessary for the realization of optimizing adaptive control systems. The present first part of the paper, contemplated to consist of several parts, is discussing the case when machining conditions are not changing considerably and the mathematical model of the system can be regarded as exactly known. In this case a deterministic optimizing problem is to be solved. The solution of this basic problem has an important role also in the case of adaptive systems elaborated for changing conditions. In the paper new methods are proposed for determining the values of optimum feed and cutting speed in the case of a given depth of cut, and on the basis of this, by using the method of dynamic programming, for the determination of optimum partition of passes in the case of turning.
Name: ["Frey Tamas", "Somlo Janos"]

Title: On reducing computational burden in the Kalman filter
Abstract: A minimum variance linear filter which estimates only a part of the state is presented in this paper. The undesired part of the state is eliminated by a simple linear transformation. A filter is derived for the new reduced order plant dynamics which contain one-step-correlated noise and a simple delay. Comparison to the Kalman filter shows that the new reduced order filter can give a substantial reduction in computational burden and storage requirements. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Samant V.S.", "Sorenson H.W."]

Title: LEARNING STATE ESTIMATION AND CONTROL OF POWER SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Learning algorithms based on stochastic approximation are developed for state estimation and optimal allocation control of a power system subjected to random uncertainties characterized by an absence of a priori information on their probability distributions. The stochastic approximation algorithms are considered learning algorithms, since they provide more information about the system and its performance, while in operation. The algorithms converge to the optimal solution in stochastic sense and may be implemented on-line by the dispatch center digital computer.
Name: ["Yousif Salah M."]

Title: ON THE USE OF FUNCTIONAL ANALYTIC METHODS FOR HYBRID COMPUTING PROBLEMS.
Abstract: The paper introduces some basic notations of normed function spaces suitable for the treatment of hybrid computing problems. A triangularization procedure of a linear differential equation is introduced which enables a two-sweep solution of the associated two-point boundary value problem. The application of a simple iterative algorithm for the nonlinear boundary value problem is investigated. The CSDT-method for the solution of partial differential equations of the evolution type is considered and generalized to higher order approximations. The recursive solution method of nonlinear boundary problems is used for a model of the sheet forming process in a two-wire paper machine. The solution of partial differential equations with higher order methods is illustrated for a simple transport equation.
Name: ["Wahlstrom Bjorn"]

Title: NUMERICAL SOLUTION OF SEMICLOSED EXPONENTIAL SERVER QUEUING NETWORKS.
Abstract: A class of exponential server queuing networks, called semiclosed networks, is introduced. In a semiclosed network, the number of customers K is a random variable such that K** minus less than equivalent to K less than equivalent to K** plus . Arrival rates may be variable and the service rates load dependent. An efficient and numerically stable summation algorithm, based on a multidimensional Horner scheme is given with an operation count of O(NK** plus **2) where N is the number of servers.
Name: ["Reiser Martin", "Kobayashi Hisashi"]

Title: Design approaches to adaptive control systems for arm prostheses
Source: Proceedings of the 1974 Annual ACM Conference, ACM 1974
Abstract: The arm amputee is limited in his ability to generate and receive the information necessary to achieve smooth, coordinated control of a multijoint prosthesis. To augment his information processing capability, various applications of reflex feedback loops in the prosthesis itself and computer aiding with micro computer technology appear to make it possible to develop sophisticated arm prostheses at reasonable cost. Based on a review of various techniques utilized for prosthetic control, a combination is proposed that makes use of myoelectric pattern recognition, local reflex control, and adaptive computer aiding with heuristic and algorithmic generation of multijoint trajectories. 1974 ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Lyman J."]

Title: Integrated voice/data compression and multiplexing using associative processing
Source: AFIPS Conference Proceedings - 1974 National Computer Conference, AFIPS 1974
Abstract: The Associative Communications Multiplexer (ACM) concept is based upon the Associative Processor (AP). For the purposes of the following discussion, an AP will be defined as an ensemble of processing Elements (PEs), each capable of storing information, comparing that information with an internal or externally applied comparand argument, and performing arithmetic operations between the various internal and external operands. The same operation---store, compare, or process---may be executed on the differing local data, simultaneously in all or any subset of processing elements. A single control unit, with internal program memory, supplies instructions in parallel to all PEs to control their operations. ¬© ACM-CONFERENCE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Wald L.D."]

Title: WAVE MODEL OF TEMPORAL LEARNING AND HABITUATION IN THE DENTATE GYRUS OF THE MAMMALIAN BRAIN.
Abstract: A circuit model is proposed for brain structure which is capable of storing information dynamically and of using this information to learn temporal sequences of inputs. Given inputs A and B separated by time d, a network that learns this sequence must somehow represent A and B and code the interval between them such that the sequence may be reproduced when necessary. Readout of temporal memory may be accomplished by the network itself or by another system that can decipher the memory's code. The first possibility is chosen here so that when stimulus A is presented to the network after it has learned the A-B sequence, a representation of B will be read out after d sec. The general structure of the network and its operation are described first, then the details of stimulus representation and readout, and the handling of delays.
Name: ["Stanley J.", "Kilmer W."]

Title: DISCRETE SPEED CONTROL FOR AUTOMATIC CURVE DIGITISER WITH NEARLY CONSTANT TANGENTIAL VELOCITY.
Abstract: The paper presents the design, philosophy and practical realisation of a solid state instrument capable of automatically acquiring, following and digitising a given closed contour. The functional modules of the instrument are: (a) Sensor and contour encoder/decoder; (b) Central decision actuation sequencer/controller which also incorporates the module which essentially senses the direction of the tangent to the given curve and generates the proper speed command signal (fast-slow) to keep the tangential-following speed nearly constant; (c) Basic signal sources and associated electronics for auto-manual modes of operation. Such an instrument has numerous applications in industrial and biomedical electronics - for example in the numerical control of machine tools and in applications involving the analysis, processing and pattern recognition of medical data and neurophysiological signals.
Name: ["Ganguly Udaya S.", "Poussart Denis"]

Title: An analytical model for information processing systems
Source: AFIPS Conference Proceedings - 1974 National Computer Conference, AFIPS 1974
Abstract: Information processing systems are an important sector in the application of computer technology to the fields of on-line data processing and the management of large complicated data bases. With an increase in the number of systems being designed and used, there has been an increasing emphasis on the modeling and performance evaluation of such systems. In Reference 4 Nunamaker presented a procedure for the design and optimization methodology of such systems. In some cases, the evaluation procedure was reduced to the evaluation of file structure and data base organization. Kobayashi gave an algebraic modeling of information structures. In this paper, we carry out the study of mean response time by taking into consideration host processor environment, user characteristics and the data base structure. Total system response time is the main goal of this investigation. ¬© ACM-CONFERENCE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Huang S.-C.", "Goel A.L."]

Title: Set-theoretic view of data-base representation
Source: Proceedings of the ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data
Abstract: To achieve what I believe to be an acceptable Information Management System, I propose that a set-theoretic view of a data-base be adopted. Most potential data-base users use the language of set-theory in their day to day references to the objects and relationships of their data-bases. Instead of twisting these natural language references to "collections", a representation that is modelled on sets should be implemented. Among the many advantages to be gained by adopting this approach are: Non-redundant storage of data common to two or more application environments, controlled access to the entire data-base by any data-dependent key, rapid selection and isolation of easily specified subsets of data, and the extraction of only those datanecessary to satisfy specific needs. This description of data-base representation will include some conceptual aspects and will address specific problems related to the computer-based data-base. Some of the areas that will be addressed are security, integrity, accessibility, and flexibility. ¬© 1974 ACM.
Name: ["Beitz E.H."]

Title: Scheduling for Minimum Total Loss Using Service Time Distributions
Abstract: An analytic model of a single processor scheduling problem is investigated. The scheduling objective is to minimize the total loss incurred by a finite number of initially available requests when each request has an associated linear loss function. The assumptions of the model are that preemption is allowed with negligible loss of processor time, and that the distribution of actual service times is known for each class of requests. A request is associated with a class by any of its characteristics except its actual service time. A contrived example demonstrates that one reasonable scheduling rule does not always minimize expected total loss. The major results of the paper are the definition of a new scheduling rule based on the known service time distributions, and the proof that expected total loss is always minimized by using this new rule. Brief consideration is given to generalizations of the model in which new requests arrive randomly, and preemption requires a non-negligible amount of processor time. ¬© 1974, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Sevcik K.C."]

Title: Topological Formulation of Symbolic Network Functions and Sensitivity Analysis of Active Networks
Source: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
Abstract: A new and efficient algorithm for topological formulation of network functions in symbolic form for a general linear (passive or active) network is presented. This algorithm, which is based on the concept of graph partitioning developed by Dunn and Chan, has all of the advantages of the existing topological formulas, such as overcoming the problem of sign evaluation and greatly reducing the number of term cancellations and the number of topological terms. In addition, and perhaps the most important, it presents a step-by-step procedure for formulating network functions that can readily be adapted for computer implementation. Finally, it is shown that the theoretical results developed herein are most suited for sensitivity analysis of linear active networks. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Shieu S.-D.", "Chan S.-P."]

Title: APL ALGORITHM TO SOLVE SPARSE SYSTEMS OF EQUATIONS.
Abstract: An essential tool for the design (and thus fabrication) of computer circuit hardware is a means for analyzing circuits and circuit devices. The modified nodal approach satisfies this need. In applying the MNA to problems, a unique sparse system of equations results. A method is proposed to solve this system efficiently when programmed in APL.
Name: ["Brennan P.A.", "Ho C", "Ruehli A.E."]

Title: OPTIMAL CONTROL FOR LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH BOUNDED CONTROL AND STATE VECTOR.
Source: Siemens Forsch Entwicklungsber, Res Dev Rep
Abstract: Using the general maximum principle of Pontryagin, so-called time optimal controls with bounded control and state variables are computed for linear time invariant systems. These controls assure that a system can be brought from its initial state to a required final state in the shortest possible time. Controllers are designed on this basis (structural optimization). This feedback structure will be compared with the well-known conventional start-up controllers.
Name: ["Theilmann Bernd"]

Title: Model reference adaptive control based on liapunov's direct method: Part I: Theory and Control System Design
Abstract: The Liapunov design approach for mode! reference adaptive control (MRAC) is extended to include adaptive integral and setpoint control modes. The feasibility of the Liapunov approach is illustrated by designing a multivariable MRAC system based on a fifth-order state space model of a pilot scale, double-effect evaporator. Simulation results are presented to demonstrate that the MRAC approach gives satisfactory control for a wide range of adaptive loop gains and despite very poor initial control policies. ¬© 1974, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Kent Oliver W.", "Seborg D.E.", "Grant Fisher D."]

Title: AUTASIM: A system for computerred Assembly of Simulation Models
Abstract: The AUTASIM System (Automated Assembly of Simulation Models) is described. The system is designed to rapidly assemble discrete event, stochastic simulation models of node network systems. Systems of this type are distribution systems, plant operations, systems for the provision of services, transportation systems, and combinations of these. Models can be used for comparative analysis of new concepts and proposed systems with other systems. The main AUTASIM components are a Module Library of computer programs, a program called the Model Assembler and a Model Description Language. The Library contains functional and simulation service modules which are the building blocks for the simulation models created. The Model Assembler program reads a coded model description, selects the required modules from the Library, and creates the necessary linkage routines for a complete model program. The Model Description Language, AUTASCRIPT, is defined. The operation of the FORTRAN coded Model Assembler and linkage control programs is described, as is the GASP based model simulation control. ¬© Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Burger R.T."]

Title: APPROXIMATION OF GENERAL NONRECURSIVE FILTERS USING NONLINEAR PROGRAMMING.
Abstract: This paper describes an approach to the approximation of the frequency domain magnitude response of a transversal or finite impulse response (FIR) filter with arbitrary phase response and time-domain constraints; this contrasts to techniques for such filters with linear phase. A nonlinear programming algorithm is described for achieving approximations to the desired design allowing disjoint constraints to be placed on the filter coefficients. Examples of results are shown.
Name: ["Marshall Fred C."]

Title: DIRECT COMPUTATION OF CANONICAL FORMS FOR LINEAR SYSTEMS BY ELEMENTARY MATRIX OPERATIONS.
Abstract: Algorithms are presented for obtaining several canonical forms for multi-input, multi-output time-invariant linear systems. Only elementary row and column operations on the state matrix A, the input matrix B, and the output matrix C are used, in contrast to earlier methods, most of which require the explicit computation and inversion of similarity transformation matrices.
Name: ["Aplevich J.D."]

Title: Adaptive non-linear bayesian estimation for bounded-noise systems‚Ä†
Abstract: An adaptive non-linear filtering algorithm is developed for handling linear, time-invariant, discrete, dynamical systems with bounded input and measurement noise disturbances. The new result yields the conditional-mean state estimate by combining the Bayesian decision rule, a reachable set concept and a technique of approximating probability density functions by their moments. The adaptive feature is needed because only the input noise bounds, rather than the complete input density function, are assumed to be known. Numerical comparisons on a second-order system are presented to demonstrate that the non-linear filtering algorithm adapts itself to yield considerably more accurate results than those obtained by applying the best linear filter. ¬© 1974 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Kuo T.-S.", "Rowland J.R."]
Affiliations: [' National Taiwan University', ' Oklahoma State University']

Title: Minimization of the Number of States of Finite Automata. | [MINIMALIZACJA LICZBY STANOW AUTOMATOW SKONCZONYCH.]
Abstract: The synthesis of sequential circuits is considered. Fundamental definitions of automata theory are presented, and some relations are defined about the set of states. Theorems and definitions used for practical solutions of state minimization are given and illustrated by an example. Five algorithms are included which are the base for computer programs.
Name: ["Polytech Warsaw Pol"]

Title: ROBOT TO LEARN NATURAL LANGUAGES.
Abstract: Work is reported on a design for a robot which could learn a natural language such as English. The project requires that the essential features of language acquisition be identified and formalized. An objective is to show how much language competence can be acquired by a robot with a perceptual and motor system, but with no pre-programmed linguistic information. This paper deals only with the problems involved in specifying the development of a semantic and syntactic system. The robot is to operate in a restricted environment with a small set of readily discriminable objects. The robot ‚Ä≥converses‚Ä≥ with its teacher by teletype about the objects, attributes and events in this world - a giant chessboard room.
Name: ["Block H.D.", "Moulton J.M.", "Robinson G.M."]

Title: ON THE FEEDBACK DECOMPOSITION OF QUASIPERFECT AUTOMATON.
Abstract: It is proved that, using the feedback decomposition as well as the series-parallel one, the minimum unit of a quasiperfect automaton becomes a reset automaton of order 2 or a counter of order 2.
Name: ["Ae Tadashi"]

Title: TIMING ANALYSIS FOR DIGITAL FAULT SIMULATION USING ASSIGNABLE DELAYS.
Abstract: The techniques described are generally applicable to any time domain, parallel fault, digital logic simulation system. The particular implementation was done on the CC-TEGAS3 system and quoted results are from this system. The CC-TEGAS3 system is a time domain digital logic simulation system comprised of different models that can be used for simulating digital networks with varying degrees of accuracy and cost. The first technique to be considered provides accuracy of fault simulation when using assignable nominal delays for different element types. The second technique provides for handling fault induced activity in a network, in such a way as to considerably reduce the amount of simulation time required.
Name: ["Thompson E.W.", "Szygenda S.A.", "Billawala N.", "Pierce R."]

Title: CLASSIFICATION OF THE VERTICES OF AN UNDIRECTED COMMUNICATION GRAPH G GENERATING A CONGRUENCE RELATION ON G.
Abstract: A communication graph problem, which is a special kind of vertex coloring problem of an undirected graph, is considered, along with the problem when there exists a vertex classification of a communication graph G generating a congruence relation T on G such that the homomorphic image of G, with respect to T, is a tree. A necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of such kind T on G is given.
Name: ["Nieminen Juhani"]

Title: DESIGN AND EVALUATION SYSTEM FOR COMPUTER ARCHITECTURE.
Abstract: A system is described which was developed as a powerful tool for design and evaluation of various processors or architectures at the register transfer level simulation. The major modules of the system consist of a microprogrammed simulator and a hardware monitor for measurement. Simulation models are implemented on the simulator by loading microprograms, which represent a model, into the writable microprogram memory. The simulation speed is faster, by an order of four, than the register transfer level software simulators. Therefore, it becomes possible to run and evaluate many programs on the simulator. Some evaluation data can be obtained directly by the built-in simulator measurement functions, and the hardware monitor, operatively coupled with the simulator, provides a variety of performance data during simulation. Some application examples of tradeoff problems on firmware/hardware design, system software/hardware and high level language processor are described.
Name: ["Hakozaki Katsuya", "Yamamoto Masahiro", "Ono Takaki", "Ohno Naoya", "Umemura Mamoru"]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR LARGE SET PARTITIONING PROBLEMS.
Abstract: An algorithm is presented for the special integer linear program known as the set partitioning problem. This problem has a binary coefficient matrix, binary variables, and unit resources. Furthermore, all of its constraints are equations. In spite of its very special form, the set partitioning problem has many practical interpretations. The algorithm is of the branch and bound type. A special class of finite mappings is enumerated rather than the customary set of binary solution vectors. Linear programming is used to obtain bounds on the minimal costs of the subproblems that arise. Computational results are reported for several large problems.
Name: ["Marsten Roy E."]

Title: PRACTICAL SOLUTION OF LARGE MIXED INTEGER PROGRAMMING PROBLEMS WITH UMPIRE.
Abstract: A discussion is presented of some branch and bound methods implemented in the UMPIRE mathematical programming system for solving practical integer programming problems. Details of computational experience with these methods are given. It was found that the nontrivial integer programming problems encountered tend to fall into two classes. The first class of problems is characterized by a relatively small number (less than 100) of binary integer variables embedded in a very large and difficult linear program, with a few thousand constraints and complex matrix structure. The second class of problems tends to have many more integer variables (perhaps several hundred), frequently organized into special ordered sets and expressing complex logical relationships, but embedded in a much simpler linear program with 500-1000 constraints. Problems in the first group in particular do not generally behave well using a simple-minded ‚Ä≥penalty‚Ä≥ approach for reasons made clear and a number of heuristic estimation procedures are used to guide the branch and bound search. The most important devices used are ‚Ä≥priorities‚Ä≥ , the ‚Ä≥best projection criterion‚Ä≥ and ‚Ä≥pseudo-costs‚Ä≥ . Some or all of these heuristics can also be very useful in tackling the second group of problems, where it is important to reach a good solution quickly to limit the search.
Name: ["Forrest J.J.H.", "Hirst J.P.H.", "Tomlin J.A."]

Title: SEGMENTATION PROCESSES IN VISUAL PERCEPTION: A COOPERATIVE NEURAL MODEL.
Abstract: Since the visual field, in general, contains many more than one object, at some stage prior to recognition of an object there must occur a separation into subsets of the set of features detected, such that each subset contains features corresponding to a single object or a meaningful group of objects. A neural model for the segmentation of a visual scene by excitatory and inhibitory interaction between feature-detecting neurons in a neural network is discussed. Analytic equations are developed for the neural mechanism of segmentation. The model is tested by computer simulation of the process of binocular depth perception in Julesz random-dot stereograms, where the segmentation process generates the surfaces at different depths.
Name: ["Dev Parvati"]

Title: ON 'FORGETFUL' CELLULAR AUTOMATA.
Abstract: Cellular automata (CA) are considered as a first approach to the representation of neural networks and the development of some simple types of organisms - as done by Lindenmayer systems - by formal methods. When defining CA it can be seen that they represent very crude models of biological information processing. The models can be improved by including further properties observed in the systems being modeled. Here an attempt is made to build in forgetfulness.
