Little is known about the occurrence of this phenomenon in nature, so it is assumed in this paper that nature works according to a principle of effectiveness: Information that has not been reused during a certain period is supposed to be of little relevance and therefore it may disappear. Cellular automata are modified in such a way that states of a single automaton become unreachable if they have not been accessed during a certain period, depending on a function phi : The automaton will then assume the quiescent state. These 'forgetful' cellular automata may differ in the function phi , the interconnecting scheme and the cardinality of the state set.
Name: ["Hoellerer W.O.", "Vollmar R."]

Title: Cooperative phenomena in binocular depth perception
Abstract: Novel stereoscopic demonstrations lead to a simple model that explains many of these complex phenomena in stereoscopic vision, including disorder order transitions, hysteresis, and multiple stable states.
Name: ["Julesz B."]

Title: A Biological Approach to Pattern Recognition
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: This paper describes a layer structured system suitable for pattern recognition which operates similar to the afferent nervous system of vertebrates. The ‚Äúsystem theory of homogeneous layers‚Äù has been developed to describe signal transmission and signal processing between neuronal layers. Feature extraction in the sense of spatial filtering is performed by such a layered system with a few hierarchical stages. The last stage contains adaptive coupling which is adjusted by a learning process. The system has been simulated with a computer and parts of it with a coherent light arrangement. Its performance in recognizing handprinted characters (alphanumerics) is highly satisfactory and corresponds approximately to the human capability for this task. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Marko H."]

Title: SCHEDULE-CONSTRAINED JOB SCHEDULING IN A MULTIPROGRAMMED COMPUTER SYSTEM.
Abstract: Current methods used for scheduling jobs into a multiprogrammed computer are yielding suboptimal results with respect to schedule performance and resource utilization. The schedule-constrained job scheduling program is defined as the problem of deciding what jobs should coexist in the memory of a multiprogrammed computer to insure satisfactory schedule performance and adequate resource utilization. To solve the schedule-constrained job scheduling problem, the author has developed and tested seven scheduling algorithms using a digital simulation model.
Name: ["Cook Thomas Murray"]

Title: TRANSFORM IMAGE CODING SPECTRUM EXTRAPOLATION.
Abstract: In transform image coding, one of the means for achieving compression is to discard transform coefficients according to a given strategy. The reconstruction is usually obtained by setting the discarded coefficients to zero. Observing that the transform coefficients are usually partially correlated, a more sophisticated reconstruction scheme is studied, in which the missing coefficients are extrapolated instead of set to zero. Computer simulations show significant quality improvement of reconstructed images.
Name: ["Pratt William K."]

Title: STATISTICAL ESTIMATES OF DECOMPOSITION OF PROBABILISTIC AUTOMATA.
Abstract: Asymptotic estimates are obtained for the number of probabilistic automata, with rational transition probabilities, that admit various forms of decomposition in the set of all automata of some class when its parameters satisfy certain relationships.
Name: ["Giorgadze A.Kh.", "Burshteyn L.V."]

Title: RECURSION THEOREMS AND AUTOMATA WHICH CONSTRUCT.
Abstract: A brief outline is presented of John von Neumann's construction of a particular machine (based on cells containing 29-state automata) that both simulated an arbitrary Turing machine and reproduced itself. The von Neumann machine was constructed as a cellular or tessellation automaton. The particular kind of tesselation automata considered in this paper (Turing machine automata) will automatically construct other machines in a non-trivial fashion and will automatically have computing ability in addition to constructing ability. Analogies with biological phenomena are indicated.
Name: ["Case John"]

Title: MODEL HIERARCHY FOR VIRTUAL MEMORY SYSTEM INVESTIGATION.
Abstract: A hierarchy of simple models is presented for an idealized version of an IBM VS/370 computer system. The idealized system consists of a main memory, an auxiliary memory, and a processor. Demand paging is employed with an LRU (Least Recently Used) replacement algorithm. A hierarchy of simulation and analytic models is developed which represents the system at several levels of detail. These models are compared and their suitability for representing the system for various purposes is discussed. Several interesting observations concerning the performance of the LRU page replacement algorithm are presented.
Name: ["Placy Emily C.", "Strauss Jon C."]

Title: EXPONENTIAL MARKOV STOCHASTIC MODEL.
Abstract: A system stochastic model described by Kolmogorov's differential equations which lead in the steady state to the system balance equations is presented. Applications of this model to some engineering simulation situations are briefly treated.
Name: ["Yousif Salah M."]

Title: UTILIZATION OF AN INFORMATION SYSTEMS SIMULATOR FOR LINE BALANCING.
Abstract: A simulation technique for production line-balancing has been developed to utilize an Information Systems Simulator developed at Lehigh University. A precedence diagram is constructed from the work elements of the line and translated into a partially ordered file. The file system enables the user to determine, store, and maintain pertinent information such as the ultimate followers of each task, the total number of immediately preceding tasks, tasks larger than the desired cycle time, and other information essential for decision-making. The algorithm can process an almost unlimited number of activities and requires less than 30,000 words of core storage. Where perfect balance is impossible, the balancing algorithm can obtain the ‚Ä≥best‚Ä≥ balance through the use of prescribed station flexibility.
Name: ["Shiveley M.Wayne", "Simonds James W."]

Title: PREEMPTIVE SCHEDULES FOR A RESTRICTED FLOW-SHOP PROBLEM.
Abstract: The problem of scheduling different processors on a set of tasks whose behaviours are known in advance is investigated. As this scheduling problem is known to be polynomial complete if preemptions are forbidden the preemptive case is studied. The usefulness of the results obtained is demonstrated by an example from the operating systems area.
Name: ["Schindler Sigram", "Lemaire Wolfgang"]

Title: STUDY OF SELECTIVE OPTIMIZING COMPILER TECHNIQUES.
Abstract: The concept of a selective optimizing compiler which uses execution time profiles to automatically select time consuming code for extensive optimization is developed. Code optimization techniques, global over the small segments of selected code were measured individually. Measurement results and a brief analysis of the relative effectiveness of each technique are presented. Code selection techniques are derived from static and dynamic program behavior measurements combined with time saved measurements. These lead to design guidelines for a selective optimizing compiler for FORTRAN.
Name: ["Katkus Gene R."]

Title: CONSENSUS VS. COMPETITION IN NEURAL NETWORKS: A LOOK AT THREE MODELS.
Abstract: The rationale underlying this work is to examine equivalent network mechanisms in three neural models, all of which involve competition or consensus or both among units. A look at these three networks, whose units seem to be doing opposite things, can clarify the relation between a network's structure and its desired output. In one case all modules are to give the same or similar output; in another case only one module is to give above threshold output; and in the third and most complex case strings of modules of a given length and given location are to give above threshold output. In each case the final output is closely related to weighted spatial averaging functions specific to each model.
Name: ["Montalvo Fanya"]

Title: FAULT TOLERANT CELLULAR AUTOMATA.
Abstract: The cellular automaton may be regarded as one of the simple mathematical models of the nerve network in the brain and by the study of this field, one can expect to develop a new powerful method in the field of the information processing. Some methods are presented for designing a cellular automaton with error correction or detection capabilities using geometrical coding. The concept of the group graph is introduced to represent the uniformity precisely and it is assumed that the cellular structure is defined by means of it. Assuming the condition that at most one cell misoperates in any tessellation K of the cellular space, i. e. , K-sm condition, general design algorithms or detection capabilities are given. Some examples are presented for the cellular automaton with 2-dimensional lattice and the hexagonal cellular structures.
Name: ["Harao Masateru", "Noguchi Shoichi"]

Title: ALL-DIGITAL ADAPTIVE VOCODER.
Abstract: Equipment has been available for a number of years which enables low-speed, digital voice communication after band-width reduction of the speech signal. This voice coding (vocoder) equipment generally encodes key parameters of the speech power spectrum and subsequently re-synthesizes this spectrum at the receiver. A significant number of problems have been encountered with conventional vocoding equipment implemented with analog techniques. Many of these problems have been solved by the predictably, precise performance of all-digital processing techniques. The first part of this report reviews general speech characteristics and voice coding techniques to provide background for clear understanding of the new processors' capabilities. The second section describes the functions of a voice analyzer and data converter, VADAC. Finally, a summary of the findings of the VADAC development program is presented as a guide to continued speech processing research.
Name: ["Walker John R.", "Paxton William S."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION, STRATEGY AND SIMULATION FOR THE ADAPTIVE CONTROL OF MACHINE-TOOLS.
Abstract: A method of analysis is proposed which uses the results of digital computer calculations for verifying the validity of the selected performance index with a view to meeting certain requirements.
Name: ["Selim I.H.", "Moisan A."]

Title: NEW ALGORITHM FOR EIGENVALUES AND EIGENVECTORS.
Abstract: A new method of finding the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of an arbitrary complex matrix is presented. The new method is a similarity transformation method which transforms an arbitrary N multiplied by N matrix to a Jordan canonical form in N-1 or less transformations.
Name: ["Beavers Jr. Alex N.", "Denman Eugene D."]

Title: APPLICATION OF PARAMETRIC TIME SERIES IN SIMULATION MODELING.
Abstract: A parametric time series model is employed to simulate the number of aircraft present in an air traffic control sector. The procedures discussed for modeling the response of a continuous variable over time have been presented by George E. P. Box and Gwilym M. Jenkins in their text Time Series Analysis Forecasting and Control (1970). This work, the identification, parameter estimation and associated tests of adequacy are illustrated using data from a low altitude control sector. The fitted model provides a useful algorithm and reflects the time dependency which exists between the number of aircraft measured in consecutive time periods. The simulation is part of a larger air communications system simulation which is under development.
Name: ["Polhemus Neil W.", "Hunter J.Stuart"]

Title: FACSIMILE RUN LENGTH CODING USING RUN LENGTH PREDICTION.
Source: Siemens Forsch Entwicklungsber, Res Dev Rep
Abstract: An efficient run length coding scheme is described in which an attempt is made to code each run length with a single-block codeword. The choice of the length of this codeword is based on a prediction of the run length to be coded, making use of the existing vertical or, more generally, two-dimensional correlation between neighboring run lengths of the same color. The coding scheme is applied to different test patterns. Considerable gains in compression factor over three existing coding schemes are realized.
Name: ["Stern Peter Andre", "Heinlein Walter E."]

Title: AUTOMATA THEORY AND NEURAL MODELS.
Abstract: The author's basic aim is to bridge the gap between studies of behavior or overall function (psychology) and the study of the units of explanation, the neurons (as afforded by neuroanatomy and single-cell neurophysiology). The brain exists to enable an organism to interact with its world in an adaptive way - in trying to formulate problems for the neural modeller. He continually refers (with varying measures of approval) to the slogan that ‚Ä≥the brain is an action-oriented layered somatotopically organized computer‚Ä≥ . A brief overview is presented of different approaches to, and levels of, neural modeling to aid the reader in appreciating the complexity of developing and adapting techniques to different problems.
Name: ["Arbib Michael A."]

Title: OPTIMUM DESIGN OF AUTOMATIC CONTROL SYSTEMS WITH THE AID OF DIGITAL COMPUTER.
Abstract: Utilization of digital computers in optimum design of automatic control systems is discussed. DDS (Digital Dynamics Simulator) and DDS-OPT (DDSOptimization Version) are problem-oriented software especially suited for analysis and design of automatic control systems. The optimum design of hot strip mill control systems using this software is presented. DDS is a kind of block diagram simulator enabling the user to easily compute the response of the control system if the structure of the control system is given in the form of numerical tables. DDS-OPT is a DDS appended with the function of optimization mode. In this mode, design parameters are automatically adjusted to obtain optimum response. As the method of searching the optimum point, a parallel tangent method is used in DDS-OPT. By this searching method, the number of required searches increases only about proportionally to the number of design parameters. The hot strip mill control system is studied to optimize design parameters under the constraints on impact drop, recovery time, offset error and motor current. The performance index is defined as the sum of the absolute error and the penalty values. These penalty values are defined as the excess values over the constraints of the design object. The optimum designs are executed with 2 design parameters, with 6 design parameters and with changing the condition of the design constraints. Computer design gives better performance than design aided by human decisions.
Name: ["Mitsumaki Tatsuo", "Mizuno Katsuhiro", "Haruna Koichi", "Namiki Shigeyuki"]

Title: COMPUTER-AIDED ANALYSIS OF SYSTEMS WITH MULTI-ARGUMENTED.
Abstract: A method for the computer analysis of systems with multi-argumented nonlinearities is advanced. The method is based on extensions of the definitions of summing and branching matrices and the formulation of the system equations from generalized signal-flow graphs. In addition, sensitivity relations using adjoint signal-flow graphs based on a theorem similar to Tellegen's Theorem are developed.
Name: ["D'Angelo", "Lee Arnold Y."]

Title: Routenwahl in Liniennetzen
Abstract: The paper formulates an algorithm for finding all shortest and all most comfortable routes in structured networks (traffic-networks). The Berlin underground-network has been taken as an example to explain the algorithm. ¬© 1974 Physica-Verlag.
Name: ["Ajzen H.", "Rokeach L."]

Title: HOLOGRAPHIC INSTALLATION FOR ANALOG PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: An installation is described for holographic pattern recognition, which incorporates a system for photoelectronic recording of the correlation signal. The installation uses a spatially compatible filter and two versions of the recording system: static and dynamic. The unit may be used for recognition of varied objects that are characterized by the light intensity distribution in the autocorrelation signal (for example, particle tracks in a bubble chamber, optical spectrograms, the data obtained by photographing, etc. ).
Name: ["Aleksakov G.N.", "Bykovskii Yu.A.", "Larkin A.I.", "Markilov A.A."]

Title: Bayesian point estimation and prediction
Source: Annals of the Institute of Statistical Mathematics
Abstract: In the Bayesian viewpoint, point estimation and prediction are treated from a decision-making standpoint. If a loss function can be determined which associates a loss with every possible error of estimation or prediction, then the optimal estimator or predictor is that value which minimizes expected loss. In most applications, the loss function is assumed to be linear or quadratic in the error of estimation or prediction, although there are many practical situations in which these simple functions are quite inappropriate. In this paper, we investigate the properties of Bayesian point estimates under other loss functions; both the general case and two special cases (power and exponential loss functions) are considered. For the special cases, we also investigate the sensitivity of Bayesian point estimation and prediction to misspecification in the loss function and discuss the practical implications of the results. ¬© 1974 Institute of Statistical Mathematics.
Name: ["Britney R.R.", "Winkler R.L."]

Title: A data structure formalization through generating functions
Abstract: In this paper we exhibit a representation of the data structures allowing the automatic construction of the generating form of a family starting from its description by nieans of words. The generating form of a family of data structures is useful in the proof of structure properties and of one-one and many-one mappings between structures. Some examples of this use are given. At last this paper contains a generative extension of the P√≥lya theorem, i. e. a theorem which allows one to write the generating function of the family of distinct confignrations, with respect to a given permutation group, which can be built on a finite set of figures. ¬© 1974 Instituto di Elaborazione della Informazione del CNR.
Name: ["B√∂hm C.", "Dezani-Ciancaglini M."]
Affiliations: ["Istituto di Scienza dell'Informazione dell'Universit√† di Torino"]

Title: SELECTION OF HYBRID COMPUTATION METHODS IN THE FIELD OF DYNAMIC DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS.
Abstract: In this paper a comprehensive theoretical basis is formulated concerning the hybrid computer approximation of partial differential operators. The investigation leads to a theorem that enables the identification of consistency and error properties of general hybrid serial methods. The theorem is applied to several well-known hybrid serial methods and the results presented can be directly used as a guide for selecting the optimal implementation.
Name: ["Bosgra Okko H.", "Buis J.Paul"]

Title: Fast Convolution Using Fermat Number Transforms with Applications to Digital Filtering
Source: IEEE Transactions on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
Abstract: The structure of transforms having the convolution property is developed. A particular transform is proposed that is defined on a finite ring of integers with arithmetic carried out modulo Fermat numbers. This Fermat number transform (FNT) is ideally suited to digital computation, requiring on the order of N log N additions, subtractions and bit shifts, but no multiplications. In addition to being efficient, the Fermat number transform implementation of convolution is exact, i.e., there is no roundoff error. There is a restriction on sequence length imposed by word length but multidimensional techniques are discussed which overcome this limitation. Results of an implementation on the IBM 370/155 are presented and compared with the fast Fourier transform (FFT) showing a substantial improvement in efficiency and accuracy. ¬© 1974 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Agarwal R.C.", "Burrus C.S."]

Title: COMPUTER SIMULATION IN ELECTRO-OPTICAL IMAGE PROCESSING.
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present, by outlining some recent research work, how computer simulation has already been successfully applied in electro-optical image-processing applications. It is demonstrated that general-purpose high-speed digital computers have reached the stage of development where it is becoming feasible to perform sophisticated mathematical operations on images in reasonable time, therefore allowing the trade-off of optical properties, technology characteristics and digital signal processing capabilities in an easy manner.
Name: ["Stucki P."]

Title: Measuring the Empirical Properties of Sets
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: An important problem which frequently arises is the problem of measuring the degree to which a collection of objects has the empirical properties of its elements. Examples of this are found in the question of whether a network of switches is on or off, the degree to which a group of factories pollutes the air, and even the probability of success defined on an empirical frequency distribution. While each of these questions may be addressed with an esoteric formalism, there exists no general methodology for addressing the general problem because the properties of a set's elements are not defined on the set itself. For example, the set of all tall buildings is neither tall nor a building. Rather, it is an abstraction and has only those properties defined on such abstractions, e.g., cardinality. The purpose of the present paper is to develop a broad new formalism for addressing the noted general problem in a very general way. To begin with, the property p defined on the object x is formalized as a function p(x) = [0, 1] which may be ‚ÄúBoolean‚Äù (binary valued) or ‚Äúformal‚Äù (many valued or fuzzy). A set P may likewise have such a property to the degree p(P). Such a set is referred to as a ‚Äúproperty set,‚Äù and these are partitioned into two general categories: ‚Äúproperty systems‚Äù and ‚Äúcollectives.‚Äù A property system is characterized by the fact that its elements are related through the operators and or or. The degree to which a property system has a property defined on its elements is found as in fuzzy set theory. As a result, a property may be Boolean for a property system under the necessary and sufficient condition that it is Boolean for all elements of the property system. Another result is that the associative law holds for forming a property system so that its elements may be collected all at once or a few at a time. A collective has a property to the average degree that its elements have the property. As a result, all properties are formal for a collective and the associative law does not hold for forming collectives. Thus the elements of a collective must be collected all at once. However, the primary distinction between a property system and a collective is that the degree to which a collective has a property is monotonically increasing as the number of its elements which have that property as well as the degree to which they have it; whereas, for a property system, this is measured as the greatest or least degree to which any one element has the property. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Allen A.D."]

Title: FINITE DATA REDUCTION IN THE CASE OF A LONG SEQUENCE OF OBSERVATIONS.
Abstract: A case is considered when a finite number of simple hypotheses and a sequence of observation xi //1, xi //2,. . . , xi //N is given, so that under all possible hypotheses the xi //i's are independent and identically distributed random variables, and N is a very large integer. However, only m symbols (say the numbers 1, 2, . . . , m) may be used to describe the value of each individual random variable. The problem is to find an m-valued statistic T such that the sequence T xi //1, T xi //2, . . . , T xi //N should contain as much information as possible, at least in an asymptotic sense. An optimality criterion based on the Chernoff information number is introduced. For an optimal m-valued statistic, the rate of convergence to the prior uncertainty of the information contained in the sequence T xi //1, T xi //2, . . . is the maximum which equals the Bayesian error-exponent. An iterative procedure is presented providing, step by step, a better statistic, and terminating in the optimal one in many cases. The results are illustrated in the exponential case.
Name: ["Nemetz T."]

Title: On the Approximation of Linear Control Systems with Time Lag. | OB APPROKSIMATSII LINEINYKH UPRAVLYAEMYKH SISTEM S POSLEDEISTVIEM.
Abstract: An optimal control which minimizes a quadratic functional in a linear system with delay is discussed. Two approximation methods are proposed which can be used to solve the task of optimal control and functional minimization. It was possible to determine the difference between the approximate and exact solutions by the terms of the coefficients of the equations.
Name: ["Kolmanovsky V.B."]

Title: PARAMETER OPTIMIZATION OF STOCHASTIC AUTOMATA OPERATING IN RANDOM ENVIRONMENTS.
Abstract: Two methods of determining the lower bounds of the convergence rate of finite stochastic automata are presented. The rate of convergence, defined as the percentage decrease in the distance between the transient probability distribution and the equilibrium probability distribution in each step, is determined as a function of the elements of the probability transition matrix. Formulas of parameter optimization for a class of stochastic automata for fast convergence and maximum expediency are derived.
Name: ["Yeh Hsi-Han"]

Title: Stochastic Program for a Man-Machine Design of Intermediate Range. | [PROGRAMME STOCHASTIQUE POUR LES PLANS HOMMES-MACHINES A MOYEN TERME.]
Source: Rev Fr Autom Inf Rech Oper
Abstract: In this article, a global intermediate range man-machine planning model is proposed. The dynamic and probabilistic nature of the problem is taken into account by the use of decision rules within a probabilistic programming context. A convex separable program is thus obtained. Two approximate solution methods are then presented, and it is shown that they reduce to linear programs. A detailed analysis is included for the case when the forecasted demand is a normally distributed random variable.
Name: ["Martel Alain"]

Title: QUASI-NEWTON ALGORITHM FOR SOLVING OPTIMAL CONTROL PROBLEMS ON A HYBRID COMPUTER.
Abstract: Quasi-Newton methods are known to be powerful techniques for minimizing functions of several parameters. Their features are a large convergence region together with a fast convergence rate near the optimum. In this paper a one-parameter class of quasi-Newton methods is extended to the optimization in function spaces. The inherent algorithm is implemented on a hybrid computer to reduce computing time. Some convergence properties of the algorithm are investigated.
Name: ["Kraft D.", "Sander N."]

Title: DIGITAL CONTROL PROCEDURES AND MODERN CONTROL ALGORITHM EXPERIENCE USING A HYBRIC COMPUTER TO TEST A ‚Ä≥DIRECT DIGITAL CONTROL‚Ä≥ APPLICATION TO A THERMAL POWER UNIT.
Abstract: A model of a power plant has been implemented on the analog section of a hybrid computer, and a control structure has been implemented on the digital section. The results of this approach are presented, with reference to a method of automating tuning and to a non-interacting control structure.
Name: ["Beato Alberto", "Chicca Giovanni", "Possenti Andrea", "Quatela Sergio", "Segimiro Alberto"]

Title: NEW HEURISTIC TEST GENERATION ALGORITHM FOR SEQUENTIAL CIRCUITS.
Abstract: A new heuristic algorithm for the computation of tests to detect failures in sequential logic circuits is described. The values of logic blocks in a logic circuit are expressed in boolean vectors with six elements and main process of the algorithm is the operations among these values. Presented in this paper are basic principles for the algorithm, their application procedure with an example and experience with the system as implemented.
Name: ["Arima Toshihiro", "Tsuboya Mitsukuni", "Amamiya Goro", "Okuda Jiro"]

Title: GENERATED CUT FOR PRIMAL INTEGER PROGRAMMING.
Abstract: The paper gives a sufficient condition in the form of a linear program for the existence of a cut, and proposed an algorithm for generating such cuts. The process of cut generation is imbedded into a convergent primal algorithm to be used in an attempt to overcome the proof-of-optimality problem experienced with the primal algorithm.
Name: ["Arnold Larry R.", "Bellmore Mandell"]

Title: On optimal nonlinear estimation - Part II: Discrete observation
Abstract: A general representation for the joint conditional probability density of an arbitrary random signal process under discrete-time observation is obtained. This representation forms the cornerstone of the paper, and from it all other results are deduced. The conditional densities of prediction and smoothing are expressed in terms of filtering via the application of the general representation. The prediction and smoothing of a random process with linear dynamics and arbitrary a priori distribution are given to illustrate the applicability of the previous results in obtaining effectively computable formulas. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Lo J.T.-H."]

Title: Automatic isolation and analysis of nasals and nasalized vowels in continuous speech
Source: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Abstract: Nasals and nasalized vowels comprise approximately 14% of the phonemes used in English Speech. An algorithm is described for locating and identifying nasals and preceding nasalized vowels. Spectral analysis is performed on a computer using a linear prediction model containing both poles and zeros, to locate the formants and antiformants of these phones. The effectiveness of this approach is compared to that of an all pole (LPC) model, using formant bandwidth data to locate the antiformant. The identification of nasalized vowels is based on the hypothesis that the formants of an unnasalized vowel, when nasalized, tend to move away from the antiformant of a succeeding nasal. Experimentation has indicated that automatic techniques can be employed to isolate nasals and preceding nasalized vowels in continuous speech; linear prediction can be used to effectively analyze the spectra of these phones; and speaker dependent tables of formants and antiformants extend these results to multiple speaker environments.
Name: ["Gillmann R.A.", "Ritea H.B."]

Title: ON APPROXIMATING REAL FREQUENCY DATA BY REALIZABLE NETWORK FUNCTIONS.
Abstract: The problem of efficiently approximating real frequency data, which represents either measured information of a physical system or idealized curves to be realized by rational positive real (PR) or bounded real (BR) functions is considered. The final rational function is guaranteed in advance to satisfy the conditions of physical realizability. All the steps of approximation are executed in the real frequency domain. Illustrative, numerical examples are given.
Name: ["Kotiveeriah P.", "Carlin H.J."]

Title: COMPUTER GENERATION OF REAL TIME HALF-TONE THREE DIMENSIONAL OBJECTS.
Abstract: A minicomputer system is described for generating realistic images of three-dimensional colored objects with the resolution of studio quality television. The object descriptions consist of a set of opaque intersecting polyhedra with each of the planar polygonal faces possessing some arbitrary color. Software for hidden surface removal, surface intersections, surface shading and scan conversion is described. An improved display processor for faster display is outlined.
Name: ["Staudhammer John"]

Title: AUTOMATIC ANNOUNCEMENT OF CHANGED TELEPHONE NUMBERS.
Abstract: To relieve the telephone information service, a technique has been developed which permits the new number to immediately be announced. Moreover, disconnection of the former station and connection to the announcing unit (AU) can be effected by remote control at any time. The essential facilities for this automatic announcement service are a multi-track announcing unit and an AU connecting matrix to interconnect the announcements of the individual tracks in the proper sequence. The control functions are performed via an electronic data processing system in which the correlation between the old and the new numbers is stored. The technical approach presented in this paper appears also to be suitable for the absent subscriber service making use of an automatic announcement with a limited vocabulary.
Name: ["Eckhardt Guenther"]

Title: ON-LINE CONTROL OF THE CUTTING STATE BY THE PATTERN RECOGNITION TECHNIQUE.
Abstract: The pattern recognition technique is successfully applied to the on-line control of cutting situations, such as the formation of continuous long chips, coiled chips and properly broken chips with the aid of a chip breaker. The recognition of cutting situations has been made possible by using six different parameters as the pattern vector, extracted from the power spectrum of the cutting force and cutting conditions.
Name: ["Matsushima K.", "Sata T."]

Title: DECONVOLUTION WITH OBSERVERS.
Abstract: Discrete time observers are used to design deconvolution filters for known overlapping signals. Selection of the observer gains depend on the noise environment and the degree of resolution desired. The observer approach provides a recursive filter that is readily adjusted to range from an inverse filter to a matched filter. Examples are given to illustrate the design approach.
Name: ["Bona B.E."]

Title: DIGITAL CONTROL OF AN ANALOG MARKETING MODEL.
Abstract: This paper discusses the concept of digital control of inventory and ordering procedures for a marketing system of three levels representing the retailer, the distributor, and the factory. An analog model consisting of three interacting control loops (one for each level), to simulate the flow of orders from retailer to distributor, and from distributor to factory, and a corresponding flow of goods in the reverse direction has been constructed using hybrid computing circuitry. Digital algorithms have been applied in a manner designed to control the undesirable amplification of the sales disturbance, and to maintain factory activity consistent with retail sales. Results indicate that the inventory and requisitioning responses have conflicting requirements.
Name: ["Clemence C.R."]

Title: ALTERNATE ROUTING IN COMPUTER-COMMUNICATION NETWORKS.
Abstract: Routing of messages, using a multiplicity of paths, is discussed. A gradient projection algorithm is used to recursively determine the optimum relative usage of the paths available. This algorithm is relatively simple to apply and, in the examples studied, converges quite rapidly.
Name: ["Schwartz M.", "Cheung C.K."]

Title: FINGERPRINT IMAGE ENHANCEMENT SYSTEM.
Abstract: Reproducing a fingerprint accurately in binary form is difficult because the analog signal rides on a DC noise signal which is due to the variations of the background density of the print. This problem is overcome by means of a circuit that establishes a dynamic threshold level. The circuit can be extended, if necessary, so that the dynamic average level is established on the area of which the center point is the point of interest. Another advantage of this system is that it enhances the analog signal rather than the digital signal.
Name: ["Ting Y.M.", "Wilson W."]

Title: SEQUENTIAL CONJUGATE GRADIENT-RESTORATION ALGORITHM FOR OPTIMAL CONTROL PROBLEMS - 1. THEORY.
Abstract: This paper considers the problem of minimizing a functional I which depends on the state x(t), the control u(t), and the parameter pi . Here, I is a scalar, x an n-vector, u an m-vector, and pi a p-vector. At the initial point, the state is prescribed. At the final point, the state and the parameter are required to satisfy q scalar relations. Along the interval of integration, the state, the control, and the parameter are required to satisfy n scalar differential equations. A sequential conjugate gradient-restoration algorithm is constructed in such a way that the differential equations and the boundary conditions are satisfied at the end of each complete conjugate gradient-restoration cycle.
Name: ["Heideman J.C.", "Levy A.V."]

Title: Algorithm 20. A powerful algorithm for the K-th best route in a graph | [Algorithmus 20 Ein leistungsf√§higer Algorithmus zur Bestimmung von K-k√ºrzesten Wegen in einem Graphen]
Abstract: A computer programming algorithm is presented which is based on Yen's principle [1] for finding the K loopless paths that have the shortest lengths from one fixed node to another in a network. Several modifications and extensions permitted to construct an extremely efficient algorithm, with regard to the number of necessary memory addresses as well as to the need of operations. The computer time increases linearly with K and is mostly less than the time of Hoffman-Pavley's algorithm [2], moreover, each of the generated paths is loopless. The algorithm published in this paper may be one of the best methods available till now for the solution of the K-shortest paths problem. ¬© 1974 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Weigand M.M."]

Title: Certain Problems Associated with Probabilistic Programming. | O PEWNYCH ZADANIACH PROGRAMOWANIA PROBABILISTYCZENGO.
Abstract: The use of probabilistic programming to construct models of optimal control of static linear plants is considered. It is assumed that both additive and multiplicative disturbances can occur in a control system. Values taken by the control performance index can be disturbed too. Some statistical optimization criteria are introduced. It is shown that probabilistic programming problems can be used, in general, to nonlinear programming problems.
Name: ["Molisz Wojciech"]

Title: AUTOMATIC TEST-GENERATION AND TEST-VERIFICATION OF DIGITAL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The system of programs, described in this paper, was developed over a period of four years. The primary input to the programs is a component level netlist type description of PC boards and a gate-level description for MOS LSI chips. This is processed through the system whose final output is a test deck for test-generation and detect list for test-verification. The models and assumptions used are defined. Next, the flow of test-generation, the process of finding a test-string to detect a specific failure, is described. Then the flow of test-verification, which determines the detect list for a given test-procedure is discussed. This is followed by a description of the algorithms, operational features of the program and the results obtained.
Name: ["Verma J.P.", "Selove D.M.", "Tessier J.N."]

Title: GENERATION OF THE ADMISSIBLE BOUNDARY OF A CONVEX POLYTOPE.
Abstract: The purpose of the paper is to develop a constructive algorithm for generating the admissible boundary of a convex polytope, when the polytope is the convex hull of a given (finite) set of points, as well as to mention some related results. One application is to the sensitivity of decisions to changes in the prior distribution for problems in statistical decision theory.
Name: ["Shachtman Richard"]

Title: Ways of Devising Automatic Control Systems for Gold Mining Enterprises and Specific Features of their Design. | PUTI SOZDANIYA ASU NA ZOLOTODOBYVAYUSHCHIKH PREDPRIYATIYAKH I OSOBENNOSTI IKH POSTROENIYA.
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii, Gornyi Zhurnal
Abstract: Principal ways of designing automatic control systems (ACS) for gold mining enterprises, the purpose of creating new ACS, the main content of the new control problems, specific features of the organizational structure and the techniques of working gold deposits are considered. Several ways of approach to the priorities in the mining work and to the introduction of the ACS are proposed.
Name: ["Bagautinov G.A.", "Kimel'man E.A.", "Shabalin P.Kh.", "Kompaneitsev E.A.", "Smirnov V.S."]

Title: A simple algorithm for the time‚Äêoptimal control of chemical processes
Abstract: A simple algorithm for the time‚Äêoptimal control of chemical processes during setpoint changes, in processes which can be described by a second‚Äêorder lag plus dead time model, is described. Knowledge of the unsteady state model parameters is not required because the algorithm uses a dimensionless phase plane on which the switching curves are independent of system parameters for a given forcing function. The algorithm gives the parameters of a second‚Äêorder lag plus dead time model as a by product of the setpoint change. It is easily tuned and is relatively insensitive to changes in the process dynamics. The algorithm does not require a large computer or long computing times and has been implemented on both analog and digital computers in controlling computer simulated systems. Copyright ¬© 1974 American Institute of Chemical Engineers
Name: ["Beard J.N., Jr.", "Groves F.R., Jr.", "Johnson A.E., Jr."]

Title: FACSIMILE CODING USING TWO-DIMENSIONAL RUN LENGTH PREDICTION.
Abstract: An efficient run length coding scheme in which an attempt is made to code each run length with a single-block codeword is discussed. The choice of the length of this codeword is based on a prediction of the run length to be coded making use of the existing vertical or, more generally, the existing two-dimensional correlation between neighboring run lengths of the same color. The coding scheme was applied to different test patterns yielding high compression factors for all types of patterns used (typewritten test, handwritten text, line drawing, weather chart, newspaper halftone picture) and different sampling resolutions.
Name: ["Stern P.A.", "Heinlein W.E."]

Title: The force density method for form finding and computation of general networks
Source: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering
Abstract: A new method for network analysis, the "force density method", is presented. This concept is based upon the force-length ratios or force densities which are defined for each branch of the net structure. It is shown that the force densities are very suitable parameters for the description of the equilibrium state of any general network: the associated node coordinates of the structure are obtained by solving one single system of linear equations. A Gaussian transformation of the topological branch-node matrix yields the equation matrix. A method based on force densities renders a simple linear "analytical form finding" possible. If the free choice of the force densities is restricted by further conditions, the linear method is extended to a nonlinear one. A damped least squares approach is then introduced. In this version the method may be applied to the detailed computation of networks. Moreover, an interesting cross-connection between geometrical minimum way nets and prestressed unloaded structures is derived using the force densities. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Schek H.-J."]

Title: Information Flows in Hierarchical Systems
Abstract: Relations between information flows and structure are discussed for two major classes of systems which have information-processing functions. It is shown that for both classes hierarchical structure is ideally suited for efficiency in the information processing. A partition law of information flow is developed which shows that the sum of the information flows through atomic components of a deterministic system can be partitioned into flow within the system devoted to system coordination, input flow which affects the output (throughput), and input flow which is blocked by the system. ¬© 1974, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Conant R.C."]
Affiliations: [' University of Illinois at Chicago Circle']

Title: Learning as a generative process<sup>1</sup>
Abstract: A cognitive model of human learning with understanding is introduced. Empirical research supporting the model, which is called the generative model, is summarized. The model is used to suggest a way to integrate some of the research in cognitive development, human learning, human abilities, information processing, and aptitude-treatment interactions around the notion of transfer of experience and abilities. ¬© 1974, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Wittrock M.C."]

Title: A design scheme for incomplete state or output feedback with applications to boiler and power system control
Abstract: The problem of designing a linear feedback when all state variables are not available is discussed. The design scheme is based on computation of a complete state feedback and a reduction to a specified structure. The reduction is made by approximation of the eigenspace corresponding to a set of dominant eigenvalues. The method consists of successive choices of weightings on this space. The method is applied to the control of a boiler and a three-machine power system. In the power system case the complete state feedback can be replaced by local output feedback without significant decrease in performance. The examples indicate that the proposed method is a realistic design method for multivariable systems. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Bengtsson G.", "Lindahl S."]

Title: A firmware organization for minimal error evaluation in numerical computations
Source: Proceedings of the Annual International Symposium on Microarchitecture, MICRO
Abstract: The use of numerical arithmetic developed for general use in continuous space, on computers where numerical values are represented by a finite number of significant digits leads to errors that tend degenerate as computing progresses. The principle of the permutation-perturbation method is that, while in algebra a given algorithm provides a single result r, the same algorithm carried out on a computer provides a set R of numerical results that are all representative of the exact algebraic result r. The perturbation procedure acts on the data and result of each elementary operation, and the permutation acts on the order on which operations are carried out. A statistical procedure is used to generate r and its accuracy from a few elements of the set R. In practice the method consists in adding (or not adding) a bit in low order position of each operand and the partial and final results of a computation. The permutation procedure consists in permuting (or not) the non-associative operators in the algorithm. The software simulation of the P-P algorithm has given excellent results. We describe in this paper our approach towards incorporating this concept as a microprogrammed module. It is expected that the study will be a step towards a machine structure that will yield an evaluation of the error together with the numerical results of an algorithm. ¬© 1974 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hyder S.S.", "Ung V.", "Vignes J."]
Affiliations: [' Universit√© Paris VI', ' Universit√© de Montr√©al']

Title: DEEP STRUCTURES OF BIOLOGICAL NETWORKS.
Abstract: Techniques are given to determine a new observable property of biological systems, the deep structure, by exploiting correspondences between nonlinear equations describing biological control networks and Boolean switching networks. The deep structure is an experimentally observable property of biological networks.
Name: ["Glass Leon"]

Title: On Modifying Logic Networks to Improve Their Diagnosability
Abstract: This paper considers the use of control logic to reduce the number of tests required by a logic network and to simplify test generation. The properties of EXCLUSIVE-OR (EOR) circuits as control elements are examined. Systematic procedures are presented for modifying any combinational or sequential network so that the resulting network requires only five tests. These tests can easily be generated using a set of predefined test patterns of length five. The design of diagnosable networks using a limited amount of control logic is also discussed. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Hayes J.P."]
Keywords: ["control logic", "diagnosable logic network", "fault diagnosis", "improving diagnosability", "test reduction"]

Title: LOCOMOTIVE SIMULATOR.
Abstract: A train simulator consists of: an exact reproduction of a locomotive cab with controls and fixtures; an instructor station and console with gages duplicating those of engine console, indicator lights for monitoring operation, and switches for setting up and controlling the training events and runs; a visual system, using a multiple of projectors; a motion system; a sound system; a computer system. Realistic simulation provides the maximum amount of engineer interest and motivation necessary to efficient learning and retention of skills, and provides high transfer of learning from simulator to real train operation. The digital computer is given information specifying the number and types of engines in consist, number of cars and weights, numerical data on track gradient, curves, speed limits, and milepost locations. During simulation, the computer calculates a complete force balance for each car, up to 200 cars in a train, and up to 164 separate values on each car ten times a second, and determines amount and direction of slack action, coupler force, locomotive tractive effort, braking effort, train speed, wheel action, effects of sand on adhesion, plus other effects a real train would experience. This computational ability provides the real time reaction which allows the trainee to obtain in a few weeks, experience under a wide variety of conditions, which would otherwise require years to acquire.
Name: ["Culbertson D.L."]

Title: DEVELOPMENT OF FAST ALGORITHMS VIA INNOVATIONS DECOMPOSITIONS.
Abstract: Certain decompositions of the innovations process of a time-series are designed to obtain a statistical shift-invariance property that enables an imbedding derivation of some fast algorithms for least-squares estimation and matrix factorization.
Name: ["Sidhu G.S.", "Kailath T.", "Morf M."]

Title: SIMULATION OF COMPUTER SYSTEMS USING AUTOMATICALLY GENERATED LOAD DESCRIPTIONS.
Abstract: Discrete event simulation of computer systems, with emphasis on the load or task modeling phase of such simulation is discussed. A relatively new technique, called trace-driven modeling, is presented. The technique shows promise of being capable of accurately modeling the behavior of tasks executing in a computer system. A description of a trace-driven model of the CDC 6500 computer system in use at the Purdue University Computing Center is presented. Data which displays the degree of accuracy attainable with this model is included.
Name: ["Schwetman Herbert D."]

Title: √úber die Vernetzungsstruktur von maschinen
Abstract: By adding some technologically motivated postulates to the definition of finite automata, we gain a mathematical model which permits interesting insights into the network structure of computing machines. In particular we show that the design of a strongly wired part (CPU) and a weakly wired part (storage) is advisable from the viewpoint of cost minimisation. We can also deduce some results about the interdependence of wiring density and computation time. ¬© 1974 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Kaufholz G."]
Affiliations: ['Fachbereich Angewandte Mathematik und Informatik der Universit√§t des Saarlandes']

Title: COMPUTER CONTROL OF BATCH DIGESTERS USING A KAPPA NUMBER MODEL.
Abstract: An integrated computer based control system for Batch Digester Automation is described. It is shown balances, and computer control enabled the mill to increase target Kappa number by more than 10 points with a significant reduction in its standard deviation, and eliminated variations in steam flow to the digester house. The system includes automatic scheduling, steam flow leveling, automatic cooking control; and Kappa number control through the use of a kinetic model of the delignification process. The kinetic model is used to schedule the spacing of start of cooks subject to steam flow constraints by adjusting the cooking temperature, and to predict the Kappa number continually throughout the cook. Scheduling is handled through digester house heat balances,and is enforced through the automatic temperature and pressure control systems. Steam flow regulation is implemented via feedforward and feedback control and is required to compensate for inaccuracies in the steam leveling and scheduling calculations. Results of the implementation at the Interstate Paper Company, Riceboro, Georgia digester house are presented in this paper.
Name: ["Wells C.H.", "Johns E.C.", "Chapman F.L."]

Title: PREDICTIVE MEAN SQUARE ERROR AND STOCHASTIC REGRESSOR VARIABLES.
Abstract: When prediction is the main objective, predictive mean square error (p. m. s. e. ) seems to be a more reasonable criterion. Two approaches are considered to improve the p. m. s. e. of the predicted response when predictor variables are stochastic and, in particular, follow a multivariate normal distribution. The first technique, the subset approach, uses only a subset of the available predictor variables to predict the response. A decision rule to select the subset is given. In the second method, the lambda approach, the regression coefficients are scaled down by a suitable constant. An estimator of the constant is suggested. Both techniques are illustrated by an example.
Name: ["Narula Subhash C."]

Title: COMPUTER SIMULATIONS OF A DYNAMIC VISUAL PERCEPTION MODEL.
Abstract: Computer based pattern recognition and scene analysis systems are typically designed to operate on static input, and this is analyzed in a sequence of steps from feature enhancement and extraction to the isolation and recognition of meaningful patterns. The perceptual system of humans, however, must operate in a rapidly changing environment as objects, eyes, and observer are continually moving. Once an object is recognized, it must be actively remembered as it moves about the field of view. It is suggested here that perceived objects are dynamically represented by maintained patterns of neural activity. In the model discussed, information is represented by activity in iterative nets. A portion of that activity will represent the object's position, and this subregion of activity must move as the object moves. It is shown that iterative nets need not be complex to perform interesting processing. With the model described, it is suggested how human visual system may keep track of moving objects and perceive object motion when image motion is combined with eye and observer motion. The model exhibits several movement illusions known to psychologists.
Name: ["Burt Peter J."]

Title: ON THE OPTIMUM DECISION RULE FOR THE RADAR SIGNAL PROCESSING.
Abstract: The optimum decision rule for processing of the primary search pulse radar information is derived and its statistical characteristics are determined. The derivation is based on the real assumption that the starting value of radar signal phase is a random variable.
Name: ["Vrana Ivan"]

Title: CONVERGENCE THEOREM ON THE ITERATIVE SOLUTION OF NONLINEAR TWO-POINT BOUNDARY - VALUE SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The nonlinear two-point boundary value problem occurs quite naturally in studies in many diverse science branches. For obtaining the approaching solution of the nonlinear problem the nonlinear problem is often replaced with a sequence of linear problems in such a manner that the sequence of solutions to the linear problems approach in a limiting sense the solution of the nonlinear problem. The convergence theorem proved here establishes the application of the modified Newton's method for solving the nonlinear two-point boundary-value problem.

Title: Construct validity of test items measuring acquisition of information from line graphs
Abstract: Tested a system, based on 2 types of information and 3 types of informational units, for classifying graph information and generating test items to assess learning. 36 undergraduates served as Ss. An analysis of variance indicated differences in learning predictable from the classification system; however, a multitrait-multimethod matrix analysis failed to provide evidence of trait validity for the system's informational constructs. In view of these results, a graph information-processing strategy is proposed in which Ss utilize data point information. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2006 APA, all rights reserved). ¬© 1974 American Psychological Association.
Name: ["Price J.R.", "Martuza V.R.", "Crouse J.H."]
Keywords: ["construct validity test items measuring acquisition of information from line graphs college students", "graphs tested", "tested based", "validity test", "test items"]

Title: PROBABILITIES OF ERRORS IN THE CLASSIFICATION OF OBSERVATIONS.
Abstract: An examination is made of the problem of estimating the probabilities of errors in the classification of observations. It is assumed that the sets of observations obey many-dimensional normal distribution laws with unequal covariance matrices which are either diagonal or preliminarily diagonalized by some nonsingular transformation. Under these conditions, the distribution law of the classification function is derived in the form of a Gram-Charlier series expansion. The results obtained enables one to find the probabilities of erroneous classification when the sample space is partitioned into two classes. For the case in which the number of classes exceeds two, a procedure is proposed for obtaining upper bounds for the probabilities of pairwise ‚Ä≥mixing up‚Ä≥ of the classes. The results of solution of classification problems on a digital computer are given as examples.
Name: ["Natkovich Yu.S.", "Prokof'yeva T.V."]

Title: SPEECH FEATURE EXTRACTION BY A MODULATED FOURIER FUNCTION.
Abstract: A well-known method of estimating the speech spectrum envelope is to employ the Fourier transform of the impulse response h(t) of the inverse filter obtained by solving Wiener's inverse filter problem. Noting that if t is made sufficiently large, the impulse response of the inverse filter converges toward zero, the authors have considered expansion of h(t) in terms of a system of damped oscillating orthogonal functions (a modulated Fourier system). It is shown that the modulated Fourier system permits representation of features with fewer terms than are needed with Fourier transforms and, further, feature patterns having poles can be obtained in the same manner as formants. The report also discusses the effectiveness of the proposed method when implemented by means of equipment that provides for feature extraction by parallel processing.
Name: ["Miki Nobuhiro", "Yoshimoto Chiyoshi"]

Title: SEARCH ALGORITHM FOR THE MINIMUM NUMBER OF VERTICES IN AN ORIENTED GRAPH THROUGH WHICH PASS ALL CIRCUITS OF THE GRAPH.
Abstract: Special simulation languages exist, such as MIDAS, DSL-90, and CSSL. One distinctive feature of these languages is the special procedure of sorting of operators. The basis of one of these procedures is given, beginning with representation of a dynamic system as an oriented graph with circuits, but without loops. Suppose that the circuits have common vertices, and that there exists a minimal set of vertices through which pass all circuits of the graph. One can easily show that there can be several such sets. The algorithm to be given here finds one of them.
Name: ["Likhachev V.M."]

Title: RANGE FILTERS FOR PROCESSING OF CONTINUOUS-TONE PICTURES AND THEIR APPLICATIONS.
Abstract: A new filter is proposed for extraction of features from continuous-tone pictures and its applications are discussed. Called a range filter (RF), it is a nonlinear and basically nondirectional filter which is based on the statistic ‚Ä≥sample range,‚Ä≥ and has high detection ability despite its rather simple structure. The RF is defined and three different interpretations concerning the RF are presented. As examples of applications chest X-ray films and texture patterns are discussed. Consideration is given to the possible extensions and variations of this filter. Since the RF can easily be realized both in software and hardware, its potential in image processing is high.
Name: ["Suenaga Yasuhito", "Toriwaki Jun-ichiro", "Fukumura Teruo"]

Title: SYNTHESIS FOR EASILY DIAGNOSABLE LOGIC CIRCUITS.
Abstract: Presentation of a synthesis of easily diagnosable logic circuits with high availability. This circuit consists of a set of blocks of identical structure and a collector array of Exclusive-OR elements. The authors show that when the number of blocks is odd, only (n plus 4) fault-detecting tests are sufficient; and when the number is even, (n plus 6) tests are sufficient to detect a single fault, where n denotes the number of input variables. This circuit is shown to possess some control terminals in blocks which permits a faulty block or faulty collector to be located easily. It is also shown that if a faulty point is located, the faulty circuit can be repaired systematically only by use of control terminals.
Name: ["Yamamoto Masaru"]

Title: An integer arithmetic path expansion algorithm
Abstract: Graphical display systems are often built around a minicomputer with limited word size, core, and instruction repertoire. Thus, plotting algorithms which do not need floating point software or hardware are particularly valuable. Since the usual (CRT) graphical display has limited resolution, the typical floating point evaluations of square roots and transcendental functions are often unnecessarily accurate. Extending the integer arithmetic functional plotting concepts, integer algorithms are presented for the calculation of Euclidean distance, plotting of lines perpendicular and parallel to a given line segment, and the calculations of the intersection of two (slant) lines, all to an accuracy of one screen unit. These algorithms are combined into an algorithm to plot the outline of a path expanded from a centerline of straight-line segments, with unrestricted orientations. The algorithms have been implemented on a PDP-8 minicomputer with a Tektronics 611 storage scope. They are routinely used to display integrated circuit mask descriptions. ¬© 1974 ACM.
Name: ["Weber T.A.", "Schweikert D.G."]

Title: Time-Discrete Wiener-Kalman Filters. | ZEITDISKRETE WIENER-KALMAN-FILTER.
Abstract: For time-discrete filters, it is shown how the (nonstationary) Wiener problem can be transformed into the Kalman configuration under very general assumptions. Such a transformation is of special importance when nonstationary processes are considered or in case of investigating the transient behavior of the estimation filter in the presence of finite estimation intervals.
Name: ["Hartmann I.", "Landgraf Ch."]

Title: Character string manipulation ni apl
Source: Proceedings of 6th International Conference on APL, APL 1974
Abstract: Use of t-hc NMSU EXECUTE enhancement at PCS (since September 1973) has opened the way to many new applications and programming techniques. Most of these applications? have besn in the drea ot packages where the user communicates indirectly with APL through a higher-level 'language; tailored to a specific task. One such prog rain is the PCS APL/RJS system. In the HJE system the user is under firm program control with all his inputs in the character input mode, These inputs are scanned with the API. character handling primitives and program control paths are altered to .satisfy the request. As the interfo.ce languages become ‚Ä¢ more sophisticated, it often becomes useful to create or modify apl programs under program control and cause them to be executed. The enhancement of APL character string manipulation and some programming application areas are the subject of this paper. ¬© 1974 ACM-CONFERENCE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Moore C.R."]

Title: ON THE EXISTENCE OF MOMENTS OF STATIONARY LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH MULTIPLICATIVE NOISE.
Abstract: Conditions are derived under which a control system described by a linear stochastic differential equation with multiplicative noise possesses a stationary probability distribution with finite pth moment. Both the Ito and Stratonovich interpretations are considered.
Name: ["Haussmann U.G."]

Title: A gradient method for computing optimal bang-bang controls
Abstract: An established technique for computing optimal hang-bang controls is to minimize the cost of the bang-bang control with respect to the switching times and final time using a direct search method. In this paper, explicit expressions are obtained for the gradient of tilt: cost of a bang-bang control with respect to theso parnmetcrs. This ennbles the minimization to be performed more accurately, and also more rapidly, using a gradient search method such as that of Davidon. The lise of this approach to compute time-opnimal controls for Iifth-order system, and to minimize integral- square-error for It third-order system is described. ¬© 1974 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Sirisena H.R."]

Title: POSITIVITY CONDITIONS AND INSTABILITY CRITERIA FOR FEEDBACK SYSTEMS.
Abstract: An instability theorem is obtained for feedback systems which is analogous to the ‚Ä≥positve operator‚Ä≥ theorem for L//2-stability, and from this theorem instability counterparts to many known stability criteria can be obtained. In particular, a counterpart to the circle criterion is given, and results are given for systems with a time-varying gain with restricted rate of variation in the feedback loop. The most significant feature of the result is that it allows one to use ‚Ä≥multiplier‚Ä≥ techniques to obtain instability criteria.
Name: ["Skoog Ronald A."]

Title: A Quantitative Analysis of the Utilization of Associative Memories in Data Management
Abstract: An associative approach to data management is developed, and a methodology for measuring the performance and effectiveness of this approach is provided. Mathematical models which quantitatively describe retrieval, storage requirements, updating, and flexibility are developed for both a class of current sequential systems and an associative system. Utilizing these models, a comparison is made between the two systems under certain assumptions so that for given classes of data management problems, one can determine which system is more favorable. The comparison reveals that, in general, the associative system outperforms current inverted list systems that use pointers. In the area of retrieval, it is shown that for single criteria searches the performance improvement is proportional to the logarithm of the list length. For multicriteria searches involving the union or intersection of items, a significantly higher performance improvement is obtained. For example, ratios of 50 to 1 are common. It is shown that current systems require at least twice as much storage as the associative system. Also, updating may be significantly faster. For example, to update one item in a list of 16, the ratio of interrogations is about 30 to 1. However, when all items in the list are updated, the ratio is only about 3 to 1. Flexibility is a measure of how easily a data management system responds to modified requirements such as new query classes, different data structures, etc. It is shown that the associative system can easily adapt to modified requirements, thereby providing a high degree of flexibility, whereas in current sequential systems, flexibility is relatively poor. For example, in the associative system, indexing is potentially available at the bit level without a storage penalty. On the other hand, in current systems indexing requires a high degree of data redundancy. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["DeFiore C.R.", "Berra P.B."]

Title: Application of Stochastic Control Theory to Resource Allocation Under Uncertainty
Abstract: The subject of this paper is the application of stochastic control theory to resource allocation under uncertainty. In these problems it is assumed that the results of a given allocation of resources are not known with certainty, but that a limited number of experiments can be performed to reduce the uncertainty. The problem is to develop a policy for performing experiments and allocating resources on the basis of the outcome of the experiments such that a performance index is optimized. The problem is first analyzed using the basic stochastic dynamic programming approach. A computationally practical algorithm for obtaining an approximate solution is then developed. This algorithm preserves the ‚Äúclosed-loop‚Äù feature of the dynamic programming solution in that the resulting decision policy depends both on the results of past experiments and on the statistics of the outcomes of future experiments. In other words, the present decision takes into account the value of future information. The concepts are discussed in the context of the general problem of allocating resources to repair machines where it is possible to perform a limited number of diagnostic experiments to learn more about potential failures. Illustrative numerical results are given. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Bar-Shalom Y.", "Larson R.E.", "Grossberg M.A."]

Title: Sequel: A struciured english query language
Source: Proceedings of the ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data
Abstract: In this paper we present the data manipulation facility for a structured English query language (SEQUEL) which can be used for accessing data in an integrated relational data base. Without resorting to the concepts of bound variables and quantifiers SEQUEL identifies a set of simple operations on tabular structures, which can be shown to be of equivalent power to the first order predicate calculus. A SEQUEL user is presented with a consistent set of keyword English templates which reflect how people use tables to obtain information. Moreover, the SEQUEL user is able to compose these basic templates in a structured manner in order to form more complex queries. SEQUEL is intended as a data base sublanguage for both the professional programmer and the more infrequent data base user. ¬© 1974 ACM.
Name: ["Chamberlin D.D.", "Boyce R.F."]
Keywords: ["data base management systems", "data manipulation languages", "information retrieval", "query languages", "english query"]

Title: A Stability Criterion for Nonautonomous Difference Equations with Application to the Design of a Digital FSK Oscillator
Source: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
Abstract: We derive, by use of the Lyapunov theory for difference equations, a criterion for the asymptotic stability of a system governed by a nonautonomous difference equation of second order. The results are pertinent to the design of a simple digital frequency-shift-keying (FSK) oscillator. A feature of our analysis that is of major importance is the technique used in our application of the Lyapunov theory. It is shown that the technique yields the best stability criterion that can be obtained by the use of any positive definite quadratic form as a Lyapunov function. Thus we show how one might overcome one of the major obstacles to the practical application of the Lyapunov theory, i.e., the problem of choosing an appropriate (in some meaningful sense) Lyapunov function. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Willson A.N., Jr."]

Title: Contribution to the solution of sequencing problems in process industry
Abstract: The nature of sequencing problems of the Travelling salesman problem type is examined. Mathematical methods applicable to this particular sequencing problem are surveyed and characteristic individual as well as common properties are described Based upon dynamic combinatorial and heuristic programming, algorithms have been developed for a sequencing problem in a rayon-wool factory. Special properties of these algorithms are presented as well as computing experiences. ¬© 1974, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Solem O."]

Title: Bayesian Density Functions for Gaussian Pulse Shapes in Gaussian Noise
Abstract: The probability density function for the amplitude of a Gaussian-shaped pulse of unknown arrival time is derived together with its mean and variance, when the time argument of the pulse is randomly distributed according to a Gaussian probability distribution or a uniform distribution. Then using the amplitude density as a prior distribution, the marginal density function for the pulse plus stationary Gaussian noise and its attendant expression for the probability of detection are derived. Applications to the calculation of detection probabilities in the presence of pulse peak location errors are cited. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Clow R.", "Hansen E.", "McNolty F."]

Title: REPRESENTABILITY OF AUTOMATA BY DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A general method is described for the representation of abstract mapping processes by dynamical systems. In particular it is shown that the defining maps of a finite automaton can be so represented. This kind of result has a number of interesting applications to biology and to mathematical structures.
Name: ["Rosen Robert"]

Title: A direct search for time-optimal control in stochastic systems ‚Ä†
Abstract: A feedback control policy is formulated for minimization of the expected length of time required for the state of a stochastic dynamic system to first reach a desired terminal region. The control variables are constrained and it is assumed that noise-free observations of the system state are available at all times. Dynamic programming leads to a non-linear partial differential equation that is very difficult to solve. Instead the difference between the stochastic and the more tractable deterministic equations for the switching hyperplane is represented by a truncated power series, and the optimal switching hyperplane for a ‚Äò bang-bang ‚Äô controller is then computed through a search on the power series coefficients using repetitive simulations. Numerical results for the location of the stochastic switching curves for a specific second-order system with additive gaussian white noise are presented and discussed. ¬© 1974 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Lee W.-K.", "Luecke R.H."]

Title: Problem of Automation of Mathematical Modeling of Nonlinear Electric Systems with Distributed Parameters on Analog Computers. | K VOPROSU AVTOMATIZATSII MATEMATICHESKOGO MODELIROVANIYA NA AVM NELINEINYKH ELEKTRICHESKIKH SISTEM S RASPREDELENNYMI PARAMETRAMI.
Abstract: Based on the structural method of modeling, by means of analog computers, of electric systems with distributed parameters and of sensitivity functions with respect to different parameters, a method is proposed which can be used for the automation of mathematical modeling of electric systems with distributed parameters. A simplified method of structural modeling and expressions for finding the dispersion and the mathematical expectation of the modeling error are presented. An analog block diagram for modeling sensitivity functions is proposed.
Name: ["Kuliev Z.Ya.", "Myachin S.I."]

Title: Method of Determining a Diagnostic Procedure Using a Matrix of System Units Connections. | METODA WYZNACZANIA PROCEDUREY DIAGNOSTYCZNEJ NA PODSTAWIE MACIERZY POLACZEN BLOKOW UKLADU.
Abstract: A method of determining a dynamic diagnostic procedure is proposed. It is described by two algorithms which can be easily implemented on a digital computer. The average diagnosis cost corresponding to the obtained procedure is close (or often equal) to minimal. An algorithm necessary for obtaining an optimal diagnostic procedure is derived, using the method of dynamic programming.
Name: ["Krawczyk Henryk"]

Title: IMPACT OF MICROPROCESSORS ON CONTINUOUS SIMULATION.
Abstract: With the advent of low cost microcomputer hardware the possibility now exists for the development of systems of parallel microprocessors. For simulation purposes the system of processors may take a form similar to that of an analog or hybrid computer with one processor performing an integration, another a multiple variable summation, etc. This paper presents a possible configuration for such a system and discusses briefly some problems to be resolved as well as some suggestions for multiprocessor integrations.
Name: ["Johnson Everett L."]

Title: A program for rapid and automatic functional group recognition
Source: Journal of the Chemical Society, Perkin Transactions 1
Abstract: An algorithm has been devised which, when applied to a canonical connection table description of an organic molecule, produces the functional groups therein. The procedure has been programmed for all non-heterocyclic molecules containing chlorine, sulphur, phosphorus, oxygen, nitrogen, and carbon atoms.
Name: ["Esack A.", "Bersohn M."]

Title: Initial design concepts for an advanced design automation system
Abstract: Most design automation systems attempt to automate only a small part of the physical description. Much is left to the designers. An exploratory design automation system is being developed at the University of Southern California. The system is intended to be highly interactive and has several features which will enhance the possibilities of automatic physical description. Different approaches and algorithms required to accomplish the future system are outlined. ¬© 1974 ACM.
Name: ["Breuer M.A.", "Friedman A.D."]

Title: Finite memory algorithms for testing bernoulli random variables
Abstract: This paper solves the basic multiple hypothesis-testing problem with a time-varying finite-state automaton. Let X<sub>1</sub>, X<sub>2</sub>,..., be a sequence of iid Bernoulli random variables with unknown parameter p = Pr(X<sub>i</sub> = 1). The K-hypothesis testing problem is investigated under the following assumptions: the X<sub>i</sub>'s are observed sequentially, and summarized after each new observation by an m-valued statistic T<sub>n</sub>1,...,m which is updated by an algorithm of the form T<sub>n</sub> = f<sub>n</sub>(T<sub>n</sub>-1, X<sub>n</sub>). Two automata are exhibited which make only a finite number of errors with probability one: ‚Ñ≥<sub>1</sub>, a 2K-state machine resolving perfectly the K simple hypotheses H<sub>k</sub>: p = p<sub>k</sub> (k = 1,..., K); and ‚Ñ≥<sub>2</sub>, a 4-state machine solving the difficult testing problem H<sub>0</sub>: p = p<sub>0</sub> versus H<sub>1</sub> : p ‚â† p<sub>o</sub>. The algorithms do not require artificial randomization. The rate of convergence is related to the Kullback discrimination information between the hypotheses. ¬© 1974 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Hirschler P.R."]

Title: A data description language approach to file translation
Source: Proceedings of the ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data
Abstract: Successive generations of computers and software systems have resulted in the inability of one computer system to process data created under a different software system on possibly a different hardware system. The Data Translation Project at The University of Michigan is involved in research and development on this problem. Informally, data translation is defined as the process whereby data created under a particular system is transformed so that it can be read and processed on another system which may be on different hardware.
