Our approach to this problem is to develop a high level data definition language for the user to describe the data in its existing (source) form and also in its desired (target) form; various source to target form relationships must also be described by the user. These definitions are then input to a generalized program (a data translator) which reads the source data in its source form and writes the desired target data. ¬© 1974 ACM.
Name: ["Merten A.G.", "Fry J.P."]

Title: NEW ADAPTIVE RECEIVER STRUCTURE FOR QUANTIZED PAM SIGNALS.
Abstract: The receiver is comprised of a transversal equalizer followed by a Viterbi decoder. The equalizer is used to equalize in a mean-square-error sense to an optimized channel model which has a small number of interfering symbols. The Viterbi decoder is used to detect the interesting symbols.
Name: ["Cantoni A."]

Title: Possible electronic processing of hemodynamic measuring data | MOGLICHE ELEKTRONISCHE VERARBEITUNG HAMODYNAMISCHER MESSDATEN
Source: Zeitschrift fur die Gesamte Innere Medizin und Ihre Grenzgebiete
Abstract: Suggestions for the use of differentiators, integrators, multiplicators and dividing units for the processing of hemodynamic measuring data are put forward. Examples of typical curves demonstrate the value of these electronic structure units. A comprehensive hemodynamic working program for testing drugs assisting or affecting the coronary circulation is difficult to make without these electronic auxiliary units. Evidence of hemodynamic parameters can be improved, additional information obtained and the evaluation of these established circulatory factors is rationalized.
Name: ["Gunther K.", "Urbaszek W."]

Title: THERMAL POWER PLANT TOTAL AUTOMATION SIMULATOR.
Abstract: A thermal power plant simulator for the development of advanced total automation systems has been completed. The intended automation covers such functions as optimum control, emergency processing, and adaptive control. The scope of research and the system configuration of the simulator are described.
Name: ["Takenouchi Hajime", "Hori Akifumi", "Miyaoka Sadataka", "Mizutani Hiroshi", "Maruyama Hidehisa", "Nakata Akira", "Iioka Michihiro", "Nakano Yoshiyuki", "Nishida Takehiko"]

Title: A Black-White. Representation of a Gray-Scale Picture
Abstract: A hardware-implemented algorithm combining dynamic thresholding and edge detection allows black-white representation of gray-scale images for computer storage. The output resembles a highly detailed sketch, with resolution and contrast superior to a halftone representation. The same algorithm can be applied to text and line drawings, so that all three types of images can be stored using the same compression algorithm. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Morrin T.H."]

Title: Flexible building of specialized information retrieval systems application 70 the management of apl functions as a programming aid
Source: Proceedings of 6th International Conference on APL, APL 1974
Abstract: This paper describes an Information Retrieval system designed as a flexible "kit" in order to build various specialized and personalized information retrieval systems more easily. All these systems (including of course the "father system11) are based upon free-text descriptions of the- objects handled in a given application. For each word chosen as a keyword, the user can give synonyms and enter a defi nition ; in each definition itself, keywords can also be defined; and so on.,. This defining procedure recursively available to any depth within the same entry function, is the main source for the thesaurus capabilities of the system. A new approach to Computer Assisted Instruction is described as a consequence of these facilities to build and to manage individualized IR systems. By applying an early version of the system to its awn functions ; we obtained an on-line updating tool for the development of the application, Issuing easily updated write-ups as well as supporting interactive consultation. These facilities are now available for the development of other packages, completely unrelated to the system. Some technical information (file structure, use of APL SV9 etc...) and examples are given in the text. ¬© 1974 ACM-CONFERENCE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Pages J.-C.", "Mauboussim A."]
Affiliations: ['IBM Paris scientific center', ' Universite de Paris']

Title: Search for problem adjusted models of decision | [SUCHE NACH PROBLEMANGEPASSTEN ENTSCHEIDUNGSMODELLEN]
Abstract: It is advantageous to adjust the decision making process to the respective problem. The outlay, however, must correspond with the useful results to be attained. Models which assist in reaching target oriented and non contradictory decisions may be found in an approximated process. Four steps are proposed for each cycle; examination of the existing information conditions, model building or modification, examination of the organizational and technical prerequisites, and seeking for further simplification possibilities.
Name: ["Laager F."]

Title: COMPUTER CONTROL FOR LD CONVERTER.
Abstract: Converters (or LD converters) are crucible type rotary furnaces. A computer control system has been developed for this converter which provides data processing, operator's guide, linkage with other computers, and forecast control functions. A wide range of displays on color cathode ray tubes with keyboards attached is employed. Requests are made to the computer by keyboard operation and the computer answer is displayed on the crt. Models are used in the operation for research and development but the process control is in the hands of the local operators. The experience and judgement of the operators are utilized.
Name: ["Kitahama Saburo", "Hattori Kazuo", "Mori Kiyoshi", "Matsugami Kazuo", "Ogino Shinichi"]

Title: CLIQUE DETECTION ALGORITHMS BASED ON LINE ADDITION AND LINE REMOVAL.
Abstract: Two new clique detection algorithms are presented. One utilizes (a) the cliques of a subgraph of the graph having the same points, and (b) the set of lines of the graph not in the subgraph. The other utilizes (a) the cliques of a supergraph of the graph having the same points, and (b) the set of lines of the supergraph not in the graph. The development of the theorems underlying the algorithms, which relate the cliques of a graph to those of the subgraph obtained by the removal of a line from the graph, are also presented. These algorithms are intended primarily for application to a special problem which arises in certain graph theoretical cluster analysis schemes: a sequence of graphs, all having the same points, is generated; each is subjected to a cluster analysis requiring the cliques of the graph.
Name: ["Osteen Robert E."]

Title: Assisting network users with a Network Access Machine
Source: Proceedings of the 1974 Annual ACM Conference/Annual Meeting, ACM 1974
Abstract: Accessing networks of heterogeneous computer systems can often be cumbersome due to differences in command languages and conventions. Approaches toward improving these conditions are identified and a specific solution - a "Network Access Machine" - is described in detail. The "Network Access Machine" is a minicomputer-based system that acts as a network access point for a user at his terminal and assists the user through the automatic execution of access procedures. This minicomputer facility allows the user to specify (or to have specified) his own network commands. The minicomputer expands these commands into command sequences executable on a specified network and host connected to that network. Further, system and network responses are analyzed to assure agreement 'with those anticipated for specific commands. Conditional and parameterized expansions allow the use of the same commands on different host computers and different networks. ¬© 1974 ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Blanc R.P."]

Title: Tree Encoding for Symmetric Sources with a Distortion Measure
Abstract: A simple algorithm is developed for mapping the outputs of a source into the set of code sequences generated by a tree code. The algorithm is analyzed for a special case in which the source produces discrete independent equiprobable letters, and the distortion measure satisfies a symmetry condition. Letting R be the code rate and D* be the minimum average distortion for that rate as given by Shannon's rate-distortion theorem, we show that the algorithm is capable of achieving average distortion as close to D* as desired. Furthermore an upper bound is developed on the average amount of computation for the algorithm. Asymptotically as the average distortion „Äàd„Äâ approaches the theoretical limit D*, the bound on average computation has the form exp [a/‚àö„Äàd„Äâ ‚àí D*] for some constant a. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Gallager R.G."]

Title: State Minimization of Incompletely Specified Sequential Machines
Abstract: A simple procedure for the state minimization of an incompletely specified sequential machine whose number of internal states is not very large is presented. It introduces the concept of a compatibility graph from which the set of maximal compatibles of the machine can be very conveniently derived. Primary and secondary implication trees associated with each maximal compatible are then constructed. The minimal state machine covering the incompletely specified machine is then obtained from these implication trees. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Biswas N.N."]

Title: Structured programming and automatic program synthesis
Abstract: When a computer is used to synthesize a program, there is usually too much information for it to handle. In this paper, we propose the use of stepwise refinement technique, based upon the concept of structured programming, to overcome this difficulty. ¬© 1974, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Lee R.C.T.", "Chang S.K."]

Title: Stabilization of a class of non-linear systems with incomplete state information‚Ä†
Abstract: In this paper a controller design incorporating a non-linear state reconstruotor is considered for a class of unstable non-linear plants. A basic assumption is that if all state variables x of the process to be controlled were available for measurement, then there is some control law Œ¶(x) that would result in an asymptotically stable closed-loop system. When only a limited number of measurements are available, it is shown that a non-linear state reconstructor can be used to provide estimates x of the process state. Conditions are given for the stability of the controlled system using Œ¶(x). Simulation results of the performance of a non-linear regulator are included. ¬© 1974 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Thau F.E."]
Affiliations: ['The City College of The City University of New York']

Title: STABILITY CRITERIA FOR DISTRIBUTED NONLINEAR SAMPLED-DATA SYSTEMS DEFINED BY GREEN'S FUNCTIONS.
Abstract: Sampled-data, nonlinear, distributed systems, which exhibit a structure similar to that of the standard closed loop with lumped parameter, are investigated from the viewpoint of their input-output stability. These systems are governed by operational equations involving discrete Laplace-Green kernels. Their feedback gains are bounded by upper and lower values which depend explicitly on the time and the distributed parameter. The main result is: an input-output stability theorem is given which applied both in L// infinity (O, infinity ) and L//2(O, infinity ). In the special case of systems with distributed periodical time-varying feedback gains, a stability criterion is given which applies in Marcinkiewicz space M//2(O, infinity ). This result which involves the mean square value of the feedback gain is generally less restrictive than the L//2(O, infinity ) stability criterion mentioned above.
Name: ["Jumarie G."]

Title: Analysis of Mass Service System with Switching on Threshold. | RASCHET SISTEMY MASSOVOGO OBSLUZHIVANIYA S POROGOM VKLYUCHENIYA.
Abstract: An algorithm is proposed to calculate the stationary probabilities of the states of an M/G/1 type system. Processing in the system starts when q greater than 1 requests have accumulated and stops when the queue is completely exhausted. The generating function of the probabilities and the factorial moments of the queue length are produced. The Laplace transform of the waiting time distribution and the initial moments of this distribution are obtained and the selection method of the optimal q value is referred to. 3 refs.
Name: ["Ryzhikov Yu.I."]

Title: The variable cell length listprocessor VARLIST
Source: Proceedings of the 1974 Annual ACM Conference/Annual Meeting, ACM 1974
Abstract: A listprocessing system which allows assignment of cells of any length, expressed in a discrete number of computer words, is proposed for a wider range of problems than just for the algebraic manipulation systems for which it was designed. Erasure of lists is done while preserving contiguity of space by means of an internal and external linkage technique. A compacting routine which copies used blocks into empty blocks can be applied provided that the liststructures have a canonical form which can be identified through the type field so that all pointers can be accessed for readdressing. An application program outside the mathematical area is discussed. ¬© 1974 ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Klip D.A."]

Title: Neuronal network discriminating local stimuli (Russian)
Abstract: The task of neuronal discrimination of local stimuli (for example a pure colour, a prick, etc) is considered. The local stimulus at the output of a neuronal network corresponds to such state of the network where only one of its neurons is activated while all the others are inert. The discrimination of this state essentially checks whether the stimulus is local and if so, what its intensity is and where it is localized. Solving the problem in the source space of stimuli might be quite cumbersome because of the high dimensionality of the source space. Special linear transformation of the source space into a three dimensional one is described which under the condition of nonnegativity of the stimuli preserves all the information necessary for solving the problem. This transformation can be easily realized with the help of a three neuronal network. The conditions under which the network must have four or five neurons are considered. The results obtained give some interpretation of the three component theory of color vision.
Name: ["Gutman S.R."]

Title: RTL THE FIRMWARE DESIGN AUTOMATION SYSTEM.
Abstract: The RTL (Register Transfer Language) design-automation system provides the tools for microprogrammed processor development. By design, it solves the problem of the multitude of different and changing microprogramming techniques and designs. With RTL, one general design language and its supporting software can be used for a wide range of firmware designs, replacing the usual creation of a new language, generation of supporting software, and training of microprogrammers for each new firmware design. It also means the designer is free to make major design changes throughout the design cycle. This removes the traditional delay between firmware specifications and the delivery of supporting software. This is the major feature offered by RTL. Since RTL uses a register level language for documentation, it provides for a concise, precise, easily understood design description. Simulation can be an efficient process. Parallelizm and gross timing are easily represented and simulated. This provides the ability to document both the firmware and supporting hardware in separate sections while allowing them to interact during simulation.
Name: ["Hasterlik Robert L."]

Title: DEVELOPMENTAL TREE ADJUNCT GRAMMARS.
Abstract: Developmental systems using certain tree generating systems are described. These systems achieve the types of results generated by the so-called recurrence systems, but yielding, hopefully, simpler grammatical descriptions. Context-sensitive rules are used in the subtree replacement system - as contrasted with the context-free tree adjunct grammar rules. In the spirit of developmental systems, rules are simultaneously applied at all applicable locations.
Name: ["Levy Leon S.", "Joshi Aravind K."]

Title: TIME-SHARED ILP ALGORITHM FOR STRICTLY LIMITED RESOURCE ALLOCATION PROBLEMS.
Source: Am Soc Eng Educ COED Trans
Abstract: This paper presents a time-shared integer linear programming (ILP) algorithm specifically developed to provide a convenient method for oobtaining the optimal integral allocation of strictly limited resources with linear diophantine objective and constraints. The geometric character and time-shared orientation of this procedure make it useful as both an instructional and analytical tool. For purposes of comparison, the results to nine allocation test problems are given as obtained by this procedure (CPS-PL/I) and a branch-and-bound algorithm (FORTRAN IV) of the batch processing variety.
Name: ["Davis Robert P.", "Shamblin James E."]

Title: FEASIBILITY OF CONTINUATION METHODS FOR NONLINEAR EQUATIONS.
Abstract: A general theorem is proved which establishes the feasibility of the basic numerical continuation process under near minimal conditions. This result is then applied to several iterative methods. The problem of estimating t-parameter step length a priori is examined and several results are given. A generalized numerical continuation process is introduced which includes previous approaches such as the Davidenko method. The theory is applied to a nonlinear two-point boundary value problem that arises in diffusion theory and numerical results are given.
Name: ["Avila Jr. J.H."]

Title: Remote Determination of the Profiles of the Atmospheric Structure Constant and Wind Velocity Along a Line-oF-Sight Path by a Statistical Inversion Procedure
Source: IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation
Abstract: A statistical inversion procedure is developed for remotely determining the average transverse wind velocity and the atmospheric structure constant at N arbitrary points along a line-of-sight path. Linear integral equations are given relating the amplitude correlation function and the amplitude and phase structure functions with the unknown structure constant and wind velocity. It is shown that the standard matrix inversion leads to large variations, as high as 1011percent errors, in the unknown for small data error of one percent; thus the problem is ill posed. The errors are reduced to a suitable level by a statistical procedure that is dependent upon a priori knowledge of the statistics of the unknowns. For the structure constant, a procedure developed by Franklin and others is used, while the wind velocity is determined by modifying the method to include the errors in the structure constant. Computer simulation is used to estimate the error., It is shown that, with an input error of one percent, the rms error in the unknown is only on the order of ten percent. To show the effectiveness of the method, experimental data obtained by a Stanford group are used to determine the wind velocity and the structure constant along the path, yielding reasonable results. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Heneghan J.M."]

Title: A Unified Representation of Differential Pulse-Code Modulation (DPCM) and Transform Coding Systems
Abstract: We consider a transform coding system that uses lower-triangular transformation to uncorrelate the data. Based on this transformation we propose a generalized differential pulse code modulation (DPCM) system and show that at high bit rates in performs almost as well as coding by the method of principal components (Karhunen-Loeve transformation). This study connects the transform coding system to the DPCM encoder by showing that thep roposed system simplifies to a standard DPCM encoder for Markov data. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Habibi A.", "Hershel R.S."]

Title: INPUT OF ANALOG SIGNALS TO THE ‚Ä≥NAIRI-2‚Ä≥ ELECTRONIC COMPUTER.
Abstract: An attachment is described which matches analog-digital converters to the ‚Ä≥Nairi-2‚Ä≥ electronic computer. Microprogram control of the attachment is used and ensures input of a 7 to 12-digit parallel binary code with a maximum rate of 25,000 measurements/sec into the electronic computer.
Name: ["Ganapetyan M.A.", "Sarkisyan E.S."]

Title: PROBABILITY ESTIMATE OF THE ERROR OF CORRECTING SIGNAL PHASE BY DIGITAL METHODS.
Source: Telecommunications and Radio Engineering (English translation of Elektrosvyaz and Radiotekhnika)
Abstract: A statistical method for estimating the error of a digital phase correcting device due to splitting of the input signals into discrete parts and the limited number of digits is considered. Theoretical expressions are obtained for the case when the input signal is a normal stationary process.
Name: ["Mush B.S."]

Title: A model for visual recognition of alphanumerics
Abstract: In this paper we propose a hypothetical scheme for recognizing the alphanumerics. The scheme is based on the known physiological structure of the visual cortex and the concept of a short Lino extractor nouron (SLEN). We assumo four basic typca of such units for extracting vertical, horizontal, right and left inclined straight line segments. The patterns reconstructed from the scheme show perfect agreement with the test patterns. The model indicates that the recognition of letters T and H requires extraction of the largest number of features. ¬© 1974 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Jayaram Tjdupa K.", "Murty I.S.N."]
Affiliations: [' Indian Institute of Science', ' Indian Institute of Science']

Title: A new heuristic test generation algorithm for sequential circuits
Abstract: This paper describes a new heuristic algorithm for the computation of tests to detect failures in sequential logic circuits. In the algorithm, the values of logic blocks in a logic circuit are expressed in boolean vectors with six elements and main process of the algorithm is the operations among these values. Presented in this paper are basic principles for the algorithm, their application procedure with an example and our experiences through the implemented system. ¬© 1974 ACM.
Name: ["Arima T.", "Tsuboya M.", "Amamiya G.", "Okuda J."]

Title: FESTO SYSTEM 1000 PROGRAMMABLE CARD CONTROL FOR A KAUFELDT ROBOT.
Abstract: The control systems for robots have been applied ranging from process control plant to sophisticated machine tools. In all instances, they have demonstrated high reliability coupled with cost effectiveness. The control of a manipulator such as the Kaufeld unit is well within the capability of the logic system and presents no more difficulty than any other form of automation system. It provides an extremely good example of the effectiveness of pneumatic position sensing coupled to a highly developed control technology. Positioning repeatibility is 1/10 mm.
Name: ["Jones B.", "Klink W."]

Title: Comparison of Some Classification Techniques
Abstract: The so-called table look-up classification procedure and a modification of it are discussed. These and several other classification techniques are evaluated and simulation results comparing some of the techniques are displayed. Indications are that the table look-up technique is quite useful in classifying large sets of data, such as in remote sensing data analysis. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Odell P.L.", "Duran B.S."]
Keywords: ["classical bayes technique", "classification techniques", "discriminate analysis", "monte carlo simulation", "multivariate normal density function"]
Affiliations: ['University of Texas at Dallas', ' Texas Tech University']

Title: MAPPING LINEAR SHIFT REGISTERS INTO TWO-DIMENSIONAL SHIFT REGISTER ARRAYS.
Abstract: An APL program, conveniently named ROUTE, maps linear shift register configurations into two-dimensional shift register arrays, in such fashion that an arbitrary subset of separated shift register positions may be topologically clustered along an edge of the array. This may be useful for instance in graphic information scanning operations, requiring grouping of signals representing successive scanned segments of a character symbol.
Name: ["Ostapko D.L."]

Title: ELIMINATING THE HUMAN TOUCH.
Abstract: The hand lapping process is controlled predominantly by torque information, although force and vibration information are used for transverse control and lap change purposes. All the information coming through the operator's fingertips can be measured, analyzed and used for control purposes just as a human uses the information. The slow response times of a human being are a limiting factor in the hand process control so that use of automatic controls can speed up the process significantly. The use of this approach has allowed successful automation of the process with improvements in quality, scrap rate and economics. It is reasonable to assume that any process which is controlled by the human hand acting as sensor and control can similarly be automated.
Name: ["Buckley B.R.A.", "Smith J.D.", "Welbourn D.B."]

Title: Errors in Regular Languages
Abstract: Random occurrences of three types of errors in the input to a finite automaton are considered: an a error is a deletion of one symbol from the input string; a Œ≤ error is an insertion of one extra symbol; and a Œ¥ error is a change of one symbol into another symbol. A method using operators for determining regular expressions defining error-corrupted strings is developed and is employed in the construction of a finite automaton, the outputs of which are stochastically generated by Bayes‚Äô Rule (with certain approximations) to take into account the frequencies with which strings appear as inputs and the probabilities of errors. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Thomason M.G."]
Keywords: ["bayes rule", "error operators", "errors in inputs", "finite automata", "regular expressions"]

Title: Quantization Complexity and Independent Measurements
Abstract: It is known that, in general, the number of measurements in a pattern classification problem cannot be increased arbitrarily, when the class-conditional densities are not completely known and only a finite number of learning samples are available. Above a certain number of measurements, the performance starts deteriorating instead of improving steadily. It was earlier shown by one of the authors that an exception to this ‚Äúcurse of finite sample size‚Äù is constituted by the case of binary independent measurements if a Bayesian approach is taken and uniform a priori on the unknown parameters are assumed. In this paper, the following generalizations are considered: arbitrary quantization and the use of maximum likelihood estimates. Further, the existence of an optimal quantization complexity is demonstrated, and its relationship to both the dimensionality of the measurement vector and the sample size are discussed. It is shown that the optimum number of quantization levels decreases with increasing dimensionality for a fixed sample size, and increases with the sample size for fixed dimensionality. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Chandrasekaran B.", "Jain A.K."]
Affiliations: [' Ohio State University', ' Ohio State University']

Title: Optimum Sequential Detector Performance on Intersymbol Interference Channels
Abstract: Tight upper and lower bounds on the average probability of error are obtained for the nonlinear optimum sequential detector with zero ‚Äúlook ahead.‚Äù A linear upper bound is obtained that is very tight over a wide range of signal-to-noise ratios and a wide range of values of the intersymbol interference. The structure of the linear detector whose performance is given by the linear bound is determined and shown to take the form of a semi-infinite transversal equalizer. The tap values of the equalizer are related to the channel impulse response and the performance of realizable truncated equalizers is obtained in the form of the average probability of error versus equalizer length. ¬© 1974 IEEE
Name: ["Fritchman B.D."]
Affiliations: [' Lehigh University', ' University of Maryland', 'Naval Research Laboratory']

Title: PARADIGM FOR SEMANTIC PICTURE RECOGNITION.
Abstract: The paper presents the results of research into the development of a semantic-based picture recognition technique. The need for such a technique is reflected in the limitations of syntactic picture recognition techniques, which are discussed in detail. The motivation for developing a semantic-based technique arises from a few intuitive notions described in the paper. A paradigm for semantic picture recognition is realized in the development of a general procedure which makes explicit use of contextual information and bases recognition on intensional class descriptions.
Name: ["Baird Michael L.", "Kelly Michael D."]

Title: ROBOTS REDUCE EXPOSURE TO SOME INDUSTRIAL HAZARDS.
Abstract: The advantages offered by industrial robots in hazardous operations are discussed. In addition they improve productivity in manufacture. The industrial robot, as considered here, is a general-purpose, programmable, parts-handling machine that will also control and synchronize the equipment or production machinery with which it works. As with a human, it can be ‚Ä≥taught‚Ä≥ a job, can ‚Ä≥remember‚Ä≥ instructions it has been given, can be ‚Ä≥retaught‚Ä≥ when the job content changes, and can be transferred to a different job when the first job ends.
Name: ["Heroux Norman M.", "Munson Jr. George"]

Title: Information structure in dynamic multi-person control problems
Abstract: The role of Information Structure (Who knows what?) and its design (Who should know what?) in many person or decentralized optimization problems have been relatively neglected in stochastic control as well as game theory. This paper serves as an introduction which surveys work done in this area as well as some recent results in team theory and the value of information. The aim of the paper is primarily conceptual with the purpose of clarifying some basic issues in this area. ¬© 1973.
Name: ["Ho Y.C.", "Chu K.C."]

Title: Self-Organizing Probability State Variable Parameter Search Algorithms for Systems that Must Avoid High-Penalty Operating Regions
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: Self-organizing probability state variable (PSV) parameter search algorithms possessing long-term memory have been formulated to cope with systems that must avoid high performance-penalty operating regions. The information gained from all previous experiments is efficiently encoded in multivariate probability distribution functions (pdf‚Äòs). This long-term memory capability enables the PSV algorithms to avoid effectively future experiments in high penalty regions. The systems considered are resource-limited, and catastrophic failure may occur if parameter values lying in high penalty regions are implemented. Those cases in which the high penalty regions are not known in advance were investigated. The PSV algorithms have the capability of adaptively learning the location and hypervolume of these regions as the search proceeds. The algorithms are explicitly guided in their internal strategies as a function of the remaining system resources and the updated probability distribution functions. Clustering analysis is used both in the discovery of new operating regions and for updating the pdf's. As a by-product of this research, clustering was also investigated as a presearch scheme. It is shown that this procedure has great promise as a means of assessing the complexity of an optimization problem. Experimental results are presented to demonstrate the utility of the self-organizing PSV search algorithms. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Mucciardi A.N."]

Title: Recursive solutions for the estimation of a stochastic parameter
Source: Journal of the American Statistical Association
Abstract: Some applications of the Wiener-Kolmogorov and Bayes approaches are discussed with regard to the construction of recursive equations for the best linear estimator of a stochastic parameter. Solutions are given for the prediction, filtering and smoothing cases when the parameter follows a vector Markov process and is observed with error. The Bayes solution is used to generate a canonical factorization of the autocovariance generating function of the observed series. Generalization of these techniques to other models is also discussed. ¬© 1974, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Blight B.J."]

Title: Design principles for digital autopilot synthesis
Abstract: This paper presents a control system synthesis technique for direct, computer-aided design of digital control system software with performance improvements in the areas of: sample time determination, control/structural interactions, noise effects (including gusts), dynamic response characteristics, and reduced sensor requirements. The design approach uses a newly developed set of digital control synthesis computer programs (known as DIGISYN). DIGISYN is based on stochastic control and estimation theory. Control requirements are specified as upper bounds for the state vector error and the desired vehicle response to either control commands or external disturbances. Using a system dynamics model that includes parasitic modes, DIGISYN collectively considers system and sensor noise and external stochastic disturbances (e.g., wind gusts) to determine the maximum permissible sample time, the optimal state estimator, and a set of feedback gains to yield the desired response characteristics. The unique feature of this approach is that sample time is determined by propagating the state covariance matrix until the specified error bounds are exceeded. The rationale for using this method to determine sampling time is that corrective action to reduce the system errors is only applied at the end of each sample period. This paper discusses an application of DIGISYN to pitch-plane control of the Grumman V/STOL Design 607A and verifies performance via a digital time history simulation. ¬© 1974 American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Inc. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Herman H.", "Gran R."]

Title: CONTROL OF ORIENTATION OF SOLID BODIES BY USING RODRIGUES-HAMILTON PARAMETERS.
Abstract: Control of the orientation of solids with arbitrary distribution of mass is considered through use of the Rodrigues-Hamilton parameters as kinematic parameters. A very simple control is designed that ensures asymptotic stability of the orientation process.
Name: ["Lebedev D.V."]

Title: ON THE ABSOLUTE STABILITY OF A CLASS OF MULTIVARIABLE SYMMETRICAL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: In this work a class of nonlinear composite systems for which the study of absolute stability in the frequency domain becomes particularly simple is defined. Systems belonging to this class are formed by symmetrical interconnection of stable linear subsystems with interconnecting transfer functions satisfying a certain nonlinearity sector condition.
Name: ["Monauni L."]

Title: SUFFICIENT CONDITIONS OF OPTIMALITY OF PROCESSING QUANTUM SIGNALS.
Abstract: Sufficient conditions of optimality of reception of quantum signals are derived from both Bayes and information criteria. It is shown that for a linear channel with Gaussian boson noise these conditions are satisfied by coherent measurement of the received superposition.
Name: ["Belavkin V.P.", "Vantsyan A.G."]

Title: BRIEF NOTE ON MINIMAX OPTIMAL TREES.
Abstract: The paper addresses the problem of finding doubly-chained tree structures for data storage which are best in the sense of minimizing maximum search time as opposed to the usual objective of minimizing average search time. The feasibility of pursuing the latter invariably rests upon assuming a uniform distribution of inquiries, which is often not a valid assumption. As a result, some situations might be treated more appropriately by seeking solutions that minimize maximum search times. It is shown that for the case of equally costly horizontal and vertical search steps, the solution found for minimizing the average is at the same time a minimax solution. In the more general case, that is not necessarily so, but a minimax solution is easily found.
Name: ["Stanfel L.E."]

Title: Sensitivity reduction in modal control systems
Abstract: The conventional modal control theory is concerned with the problem of determining a state feedback matrix-valued gain which drives the system eigenvalues to prescribed positions. When the parameters of the open-loop system involve certain variations, the closed-loop eigenvalues, obtained by using a feedback gain determined as above, also contain variations. In the present paper the problem of choosing an additional state feedback gain such as to reduce the closed-loop eigenvalue variations as much as desired is solved. Specifically, upon the assumption that a nominal set of parameter values is given, and that a feedback modal control law which drives the eigenvalues of the nominal closed-loop system to the desired positions is known, two alternative expressions for the required additional reduced eigenvalue sensitivity feedback controller are derived. Both cases of known and unknown system state vector are considered. The theory is illustrated by several examples. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Tzafestas S.G.", "Paraskevopoulos P.N."]
Affiliations: [' Computer Center Nuclear Research Center Democritos']

Title: Optimal Control of Stochastic and Adaptive Processes. | COMMANDE OPTIMALE DE PROCEDES STOCHASTIQUES ET ADAPTATIFS.
Source: Rev Fr Autom Inf Rech Oper
Abstract: It is indicated that the optimal control of stochastic and adaptive processes offers classes of problems, which are generally difficult - both from the conception and computation points of view. The intent of this paper is to discuss some difficulties underlying some classes of those problems and to review possible approximations for their solution. Also mentioned are some hints about other interesting classes of stochastic and adaptive control processes for which only meager results are currently available.
Name: ["El-Fattah Y.M."]

Title: EFFICIENT ALGORITHM FOR THE PARTITIONING OF TREES.
Source: IBM Journal of Research and Development
Abstract: This paper describes an algorithm for partitioning a graph that is in the form of a tree. The algorithm has a growth in computation time and storage requirements that is directly proportional to the number of nodes in the tree. Several applications of the algorithm are briefly described. In particular it is shown that the tree partitioning problem frequently arises in the allocation of computer information to blocks of storage. Also, a heuristic method of partitioning a general graph based on this algorithm is suggested.
Name: ["Lukes J.A."]

Title: Finite-Memory Classification of Bernoulli Sequences Using Reference Samples
Abstract: It is shown that in two-way Bernoulli classification problems deterministic machines can perform as well as optimal randomized machines if their memory is increased by less than one bit. This is accomplished by allowing the algorithm to observe samples from both classes, thus in effect using the data source itself to provide the necessary randomization. An application to a simple communication problem is indicated. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Shubert B.O."]

Title: Part ii minimal realization
Abstract: PA complotely new algorithm for calculating a state space minimal realization of a rational transfer function matrix is given. Tho algorithm consists of four major steps: Calculation of the least common denominators of the columns of the transfer function matrix; calculation of the greatest common right divisor of two polynomial matrices; factoring the divisor from the two matrices; and expansion of the resulting relatively right prime matrices into constant matrices. The transfer function matrix need not be proper and the result of the calculations leaves the polynomial part of the transfer function matrix unaltered, thus allowing a useful check on the accuracy of the computations to be incorporated. The results of several examples show that this new algorithm is superior in terms of computing time to other methods and is very accurate. ¬© 1974 Taylor and Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Pace I.S.", "Barnett S."]

Title: DRS-A User Oriented Information Retrieval System
Abstract: DRS (Data Retrieval System), a user-oriented computerized information retrieval system, is described. The system allows data base generation and information retrieval by users without programming and systems knowledge. As an illustration, a chemical information system using the Wiswesser Line Notation (WLN) is generated, and retrieval examples are given using this data base. Because of its easily understandable English command language, DRS is suitable for a wide variety of information retrieval systems. Polaroid was instrumental in many of the advanced features of DRS developed during the past three years. ¬© 1974, American Chemical Society. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Szonyi G."]

Title: PROBABILISTIC ESTIMATING.
Abstract: Using the mathematics of random variables, a procedure is developed for calculating the variance of the total estimate of project cost. Input consists of three-value estimates of the individual budget work items. Correlation among work items is shown to produce a significant part of total variance. A simplified technique for these calculations is suggested.
Name: ["Spooner James E."]

Title: Information Rates and Data-Compression Schemes for Poisson Processes
Abstract: In this paper, we derive rate-distortion functions under proper magnitude-error fidelity criteria and study instrumentable data-compression schemes for Poisson processes. In particular, we derive information rates and obtain rate-distortion relationships for practical data-compression schemes, for the reproduction of the unordered sequence of Poisson event occurrences, for the reproduction of the sample functions of the Poisson counting process, and for the reproduction of the sequence of intervals between the event occurrences of a Poisson process. The reproducing processes are taken to be point (or jump) processes themselves. The performances of the various data-compression schemes presented here are compared with those of the ideal schemes (as presented by the rate-distortion functions) and are shown to be close to the latter over wide regions of distortion. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Rubin I."]

Title: Upper Bounds on Sequential Decoding Performance Parameters
Abstract: This paper presents the best obtainable random coding and expurgated upper bounds on the probabilities of undetectable error, of t-order failure (advance to depth t into an incorrect subset), and of likelihood rise in the incorrect subset, applicable to sequential decoding when the metric bias G is arbitrary. Upper bounds on the Pareto exponent are also presented. The G-values optimizing each of the parameters of interest are determined, and are shown to lie in intervals that in general have nonzero widths. The G-optimal expurgated bound on undetectable error is shown to agree with that for maximum likelihood decoding of convolutional codes, and that on failure agrees with the block code expurgated bound. Included are curves evaluating the bounds for interesting choices of G and SNR for a binary-input quantized-output Gaussian additive noise channel. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Jelinek F."]

Title: The dimension of stability of stochastic automata
Abstract: The concept of the dimension of stability of stochastic automata is introduced and examined. We are concerned with the minimal-state form of the automaton and the dimension of stability. Natural automata are defined, for which the dimension of stability is not less than the difference between the number of states and the number of states of its minimal-state equivalent. For minimal state automata, the upper bound on the dimension of stability is given, and we demonstrate minimal-state automata for which the dimension of stability reaches this upper bound. An estimate of the dimension of stability of automata that are not necessarily minimal state is based on this result for minimal-state automata. ¬© 1974 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Rytter W."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF ADAPTIVE SYSTEMS WITH A STANDARD MODEL BY LYAPUNOV'S DIRECT METHOD.
Abstract: An algorithm for an adaptive system using a standard model is synthesized by Lyapunov's direct method. The Lyapunov function is constructed in the form of a quadratic form, the coefficients of which are sensitivity functions of the system. The dynamic properties of such algorithms depend on the characteristics of the control influences to a smaller degree than is the case with adaptive systems in which the coefficients of the quadratic form are assumed to be constant.
Name: ["Prokopov B.I."]

Title: GENERALIZATION OF ROUTH ALGORITHM BY LYAPUNOV'S SECOND METHOD.
Abstract: The degree of relative stability is used as one of the measures for stability of real-coefficient ordinary differential equations, and can be examined by the stability criteria for complex-coefficient ordinary differential equations. The well-known Hurwitz criterion is based on characteristic polynomials of the system. This paper shows the applicability of Lyapunov's second method to the stability analysis. A generalized Routh algorithm is formulated and proved using the second method of Lyapunov.
Name: ["Hamada Nozomu", "Takahashi Schin-ichi"]

Title: SELECTION OF FEATURE ENSEMBLE AND SYNTHESIS OF MULTILAYER PERCEPTRON USING SELF-ORGANIZATION.
Abstract: The synthesis of multilayer perceptrons using self-organization is considered, the procedure consisting of two parts: At first the most effective composition of the feature ensemble is obtained using multilayer selection, and after that a multilayer perceptron model is constructed by GMDH algorithms. Optimization can also be realized using self-organization.
Name: ["Ivakhnenko A.G.", "Koppa Yu.V."]

Title: Coupling between cortical potentials from different areas
Abstract: At any instant, the electroencephalogram can be classified as to (i) polarity and (ii) direction of change in polarity. This classification provides a way to measure coupling between cortical areas. The technique is simple, yet of wide potential utility for studying functional relationships between cortical areas. The results of applying this technique suggest how the potentials giving rise to the electroencephalogram may play a role in information processing in the central nervous system.
Name: ["Callaway E.", "Harris P.R."]

Title: Evaluating the equality or inequality of symbol strings in API
Source: Proceedings of 6th International Conference on APL, APL 1974
Abstract: Employing concepts from the field of artificial intelligence, this paper presents a new modified implementation of Kellerman's algorithm to evaluate the equality of two symboi strings; A linear dichotomizer was simulated in APL, providing new data on the performance of the above algorithm when used with adaptive learning machines. ¬© 1974 ACM-CONFERENCE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Macdonald G."]
Affiliations: ['State University of New York at Binghamton']

Title: CONDITIONALLY GAUSSIAN RANDOM PROCESSES.
Abstract: A class of non-Gaussian processes ( theta //t, xi //t, 0 less than equivalent to t less than equivalent to T) is defined by means of nonlinear Ito stochastic differential equations with the property that the conditional finite-dimensional distribution functions of the process ( theta //s, s less than equivalent to t) subject to the condition ( xi //s, s less than equivalent to t) are with probability 1 Gaussian. This fact yields effective results in statistical problems of random processes, in particular a nonlinear generalization of the Kalman - Bucy filtering problem.
Name: ["Liptser R.Sh."]

Title: UPPER BOUNDS FOR THE NUMBER OF POINTS OF A BINARY CODE WITH A SPECIFIED CODE DISTANCE.
Abstract: An upper bound is obtained for the number of points of a binary code of length n and code distance d; the new bound improves the Elias bound by a factor that grows exponentially with n; a new upper bound is also obtained for the number of points of a binary equilibrium code.
Name: ["Sidel'nikov V.M."]

Title: FUZZY SETS AND NEURAL NETWORKS.
Abstract: Although the McCulloch-Pitts model of a neuron has contributed a great deal to the understanding of the behavior of neural-like systems, it fails to reflect the fact that the behavior of even the simplest type of nerve cell exhibits not only randomness but, more importantly, a type of imprecision which is associated with the lack of sharp transition from the occurrence of an event to its non-occurrence. In this paper, some basic properties of fuzzy neural networks as well as their applications to the synthesis of fuzzy automata are investigated. It is shown that any n-state minimal fuzzy automaton can be realized by a network of m fuzzy neurons. Examples are given to illustrate the procedure. As an example of application, a realization of lambda -fuzzy language recognizer using a fuzzy neural network is presented. The techniques described in this paper may be of use in the study of neural networks as well as in formal languages, pattern recognition, and learning.
Name: ["Lee Samuel C.", "Lee Edward T."]

Title: SIMULATION OF A COMMAND AND CONTROL DATA PROCESSING AND DISPLAY SYSTEM.
Abstract: Recently, a system simulator was developed to be used in determining the throughput and response-time capabilities of a data processing and display system for a proposed Tactical Air Control Center Automation. The simulator specifically addresses the hardware and software of the data processing subsystem. It shows the utilization of various hardware and software components of the data processing subsystem and keeps track of the lengths of all the subsystem queues; it exhibits the critical paths in the flow of data. The simulator also provides sensitivity tests to such parameters as CPU speed, assignment of priority, and various software features, thus allowing the system architect to evaluate alternative susbsystem designs.
Name: ["Warren C.S."]

Title: PROGRAM GIVES FILTER TIME RESPONSE.
Abstract: A short program is presented which gives a filter's time-domain response when the input is a connected series of waveform segments and the system transfer function is described by a ratio of polynomials in the complex frequency domain. The program provides a tabular listing of the output and algebraic expressions that describe the response of the network to each segment of the input. The type of output furnished is particularly useful for work with pulsed data systems, in which the network's time response is often as important as group-delay and frequency-attenuation characteristics.
Name: ["Lecklider Thomas H."]

Title: Parallel Balancing of Binary Search Trees
Abstract: A method for the balancing of binary search trees on a highly parallel computer is described. This method can be adapted for execution on a multiprocessor computer system. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Chang S.-K."]
Keywords: ["binary search trees", "highly parallel computer", "information retrieval", "parallel computation", "sorting"]

Title: A gentralized learning" game
Source: Proceedings of 6th International Conference on APL, APL 1974
Abstract: APL is used to describe a "learning" game, generalized to a class of rules. ¬© 1974 ACM-CONFERENCE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Peelle H.A."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF CONTROL LAWS FOR MULTIVARIABLE SAMPLED-DATA SYSTEMS INCORPORATING INTEGRAL FEEDBACK.
Source: Rev Fr Autom Inf Rech Oper
Abstract: It is shown that the introduction of integral action into the laws for the feedback control of a class of linear multivariable sampled-data systems can under certain conditions destroy the controllability of such systems. Since the destruction of controllability characteristics is clearly of great significance in connection with the synthesis of feedback control laws which effect eigenvalue assignment in systems of this class, the first objective of this paper is to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the controllability of multivariable sampled-data systems incorporating integral action. The second objective is to present an explicit eigenvalue-assignment algorithm for the synthesis of feedback control laws for systems of this class so that good transient as well as good steady-state response characteristics can be achieved.
Name: ["Porter B."]

Title: An Extension of the Stochastic Linear Regulator Problem
Abstract: The stochastic linear regulator problem is extended to cover the case of non-Gaussian white noise. Using martingale theory, it is proved that the linear optimal regulator is also optimal for non-Gaussian white noise. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Kwakernaak H."]

Title: AUTOMATIC FREQUENCY RESPONSE CORRECTING NETWORK FOR STANDARD VF CHANNELS.
Source: Telecommunications and Radio Engineering (English translation of Elektrosvyaz and Radiotekhnika)
Abstract: The constructional principles of the AKU-3 automatic correcting network for standard vf-channels employed for data transmission are discussed, together with its main parameters, namely, the correcting capacity, the band of corrected frequencies, the accuracy of correction of amplitude-frequency response and group delay response distortion, automatic adjustment time, and noise immunity of the adjustment system. Experimental test data are given for the AKU-3 operating in long channels jointly with the amplitude differential-phase modulation with partial sideband suppression (APM-SSB) and double differential phase-shift keying (DDPSK) modems for data and facsimile transmission.
Name: ["Myastsov B.N.", "Berkovich D.A.", "Lev A.Yu.", "Tsirel'son D.A."]

Title: English as a very high level language for simulation programming
Abstract: An automatic programming system which produces simulation programs from information obtained through natural language dialogue has been implemented under CP/CMS on the IBM 360/67. In the current version the information obtained from an English conversation about a simple queuing problem is used to build a language independent entity-attribute-value data structure. From this structure both an English description of the problem and a GPSS simulation program for it can be produced. This processing is done by a FORTRAN program which interprets sets of decoding and encoding rules written in a specially developed grammar-rule language. The paper includes a complete sample problem with a discussion of its processing and examples of decoding and encoding rules. ¬© 1974, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Heidorn G.E."]

Title: MARKOVIAN LEARNING PROCESSES.
Abstract: Real-valued Markov processes with steps of the form DELTA X//n equals THETA //i( lambda //i minus X//n) or DELTA X//n equals delta //i, i equals 1,. . . , nu , arise frequently in the theory of human and animal learning. This paper first surveys results pertaining to the asymptotic behavior of such processes as n approaches infinity . Next, general theorems are given that cover limiting behavior as n approaches infinity and, simultaneously, theta //i approaches 0 or delta //i approaches 0. Finally, an example of a two-dimensional learning process X//n is presented.
Name: ["Norman M.Frank"]

Title: Least-Squares Estimator for Hereditary Systems with Time-Varying Delay
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: A constructive solution to the estimation problem of linear hereditary systems with time-varying delay is presented using a leastsquares fit to the contaminated data. The utilization of optimum control theory yields a split boundary value problem, which is transformed to an initial-value problem by utilizing the theory of Fredholm resolvents. Applications of the theory to man-machine systems, for example, are indicated. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Koivo H.N."]

Title: ADAPTIVE QUANTIZATION IN DIGITAL CONTROL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Adaptive quantization has been shown to be very useful in digital systems for reducing the quantization noise. A digital control system is simulated with (a) no quantizer, (b) with uniform step quantizers, and (c) with adaptive quantizers. It is observed that an appreciable improvement in the system performance may be achieved by using adaptive quantization. The upper bound on the percentage quantization error is introduced to replace the upper bound on the absolute value of the error. The process graph technique is applied to calculate the upper bound on the percentage error.
Name: ["Jain Ramesh", "Chatterjee B."]

Title: AUTOMATA WITH LABELED TREE INPUTS.
Abstract: Description of a new tree automaton arising in the discussion of determination of the equivalence of programs with tree-type data structure and investigation of its properties. A two-way tree automaton (2ta) which operates on a tree in two directions, a class of Turing machine (tTM) which is obtained by replacing the tape with a labeled tree, a two-way pushdown automaton (2tPDA) and marked one-head tree automaton (mta) are introduced. Results are discussed.
Name: ["Tokura Nobuki", "Kasami Tadao"]

Title: PPKR - A Program Package for the Convex Feedback Method. | PPKR - EIN PROGRAMMPAKET FUER DIE METHODE DER KONVEXEN RUECKFUEHRUNG.
Abstract: A survey is given of the Convex Feedback Method for optimal control of linear systems with quadratic performance index. This relatively new method (H. A. Nour Eldin, 1971) may take place of the Riccati-Feedback for many applications. The PPKR, described in this paper, solves general open-loop control problems with the new method. Special attention is paid to the fast computation of the time response of linear, time invariant systems with piecewise constant control input.
Name: ["Ebert K."]

Title: OPTICAL-DIGITAL SYSTEM FOR AUTOMATIC PROCESSING OF CHEST X-RAYS.
Abstract: A prototype optical-digital system for automatic processing of chest X-rays and preliminary results are presented. The system consists of a digital image scanner used for locating the lung fields and texture measurements, a diffraction pattern sampling unit which provides both annular ring and wedge samples of the Fraunhofer diffraction pattern of lung areas, and a microcomputer for control and computation of decision functions. The film is positioned by a computer-controlled film transport to provide an overall automated system. The system will be used for screening chest X-rays of coal miners for pneumoconiosis.
Name: ["Hall Ernest L.", "Kruger Richard P.", "Turner A.Franklin"]

Title: Variability and Covariability of Modified Spectral Estimators
Source: IEEE Transactions on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
Abstract: The use of data windows in digital spectral analysis causes a covariance between spectral components in the periodogram. The variability of the smoothed spectral estimator, obtained by a graded summation of adjacent periodogram values, is increased. These effects are analyzed for white Gaussian signals. ¬© 1974 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Persson J."]

Title: ESTIMATION OF PARAMETERS IN DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The estimation of spatially- and temporally-varying parameters in nonlinear distributed systems has been considered from an optimal control standpoint. Necessary conditions for optimality have been derived for the optimal control problems arising from estimation of the location of the boundary of a distributed system. Based on the necessary conditions, steepest descent and conjugate gradient computational methods for iteratively determining the optimal estimates have been presented. The theory presented is seen to have wide applicability to distributed identification problems arising in transport, geophysical, and wave propagation phenomena.
Name: ["Seinfeld John H.", "Chen Wen H."]

Title: OPTIMAL SCHEDULING RULES FOR A SINGLE PROCESSOR.
Abstract: New results are presented for the optimal scheduling of a single processor when randomness is present. The objective is to minimize the expected waiting costs of jobs per unit time. The various factors considered are the types of waiting cost functions, available information about the jobs, types of scheduling rules allowed, and type of arrival process. The principle results relate to the generality of SPT/C type rules, particularly to cases where arrivals are completely general.
Name: ["Schrage Linus"]

Title: STORING EXTENSIBLE TABLES IN ASSOCIATIVE MEMORIES WITH FIXED WORD-LENGTHS.
Abstract: The fast search capability of associative memories makes them ideal for storing tables that must be searched frequently. A scheme is proposed which can be used for storing extensible tables with variable-length fields in a conventional associative memory. Algorithms for common operations on tables are given and their efficiency is evaluated.
Name: ["Parhami Behrooz"]

Title: METHOD FOR IDENTIFYING PARAMETERS OF ANALYTICALLY MODELLED SYSTEMS.
Source: Technion, Israel Inst Technol TAE Rep
Abstract: Parameters of dynamic systems are often determined by fitting an analytic model to experimental data with a least squares procedure. The method of differential corrections is an efficient numerical technique for minimizing the fit error, however it has a narrow domain of convergence. It is proposed here to increase this domain by applying the continuation method in its iterative form. An auxiliary parameter is introduced into the fit quadratic function. This yields a family of minimum problems depending on a parameter. The desired solution is obtained by a continuation procedure which uses the method of differential corrections at intermediate steps. An example is presented.
Name: ["Kirszenblat A.", "Chetrit M."]

Title: PRACTICAL FILTER FOR SYSTEMS WITH UNKNOWN PARAMETERS.
Abstract: This paper deals with the problem of a practical filter for discrete-time, dynamic systems with unknown parameters whose variation cannot be estimated in advance. The modeling errors caused by unknown parameters clearly degrade the filter performance and sometimes lead to divergence of estimation errors. Divergence is said to occur when the calculated covariance of estimation errors becomes very small compared with the actual covariance. A practical filter that modifies the calculated covariance is developed as a technique for controlling the divergence. This is done by testing whether or not the actual residual of each stage is likely to have come from the calculated distribution, and the calculated covariance is modified when the test is rejected. The numerical results of digital simulation indicate that divergence of estimation errors is observed when the a priori information for dynamic systems is in error and that the divergence is prevented by the proposed filter.
Name: ["Soeda T.", "Yoshimura T."]

Title: CLASS OF QUADRATICALLY CONVERGENT ALGORITHMS FOR CONSTRAINED FUNCTION MINIMIZATION.
Abstract: The problem of minimizing a function f(x) subject to the constraint phi (x) equals 0 is considered. Here, f is a scalar, x is an n-vector, and phi is an m-vector, where m less than n. A general quadratically convergent algorithm is presented. The conjugate-gradient algorithm and the variable-metric algorithms for constrained function minimization can be obtained as particular cases of the general algorithm. It is shown that, for a quadratic function subject to a linear constraint, all the particular algorithms behave identically if the one-dimensional search for the stepsize is exact.
Name: ["Huang H.Y.", "Aggarwal A.K."]

Title: FEEDBACK CONTROL PROCESS IN AGRICULTURAL PEST MANAGEMENT.
Abstract: A three-component agro-ecosystem consisting of a single prey (host), predator (parasite), and crop is described by means of a linear vector different equation involving a control term. Deviation of the state of the system from a threshold, and the use of chemical control agents are subject to economic penalties. Dynamic Programming is used to determine the optimal pest control policy as a function of the state of the system, so that a quadratic cost function is minimized. Stratified random sampling is used to estimate the state of the system. A simulation of the model, utilizing a digital computer, is presented.
Name: ["Ford-Livene C."]

Title: Bayesian inference for variance components using only error contrasts
Abstract: Patterson & Thompson (1971) proposed estimating the variance components of a mixed analysis of variance model by maximizing the likelihood of a set of error contrasts. In the present paper, a convenient representation is obtained for that likelihood. It is shown that, from a Bayesian viewpoint, using only error contrasts to make inferences on variance components is equivalent to ignoring any prior information on the fixed effects and using all the data. ¬© 1974 Oxford University Press.
Name: ["Harville D.A."]
Keywords: ["bayesian inference", "error contrasts", "maximum likelihood", "mixed linear models", "variance components"]

Title: Frame selection systems and languages for medical applications
Abstract: A frame selection system and a frame programming language were implemented to support medical information system applications. A frame selection system is an interactive computer system which enables the user to enter data via a CRT terminal, by using a selection device to point at items or phrases displayed on the screen. A frame is a set of choices representing the alternatives available to the user at each stage of a selection process. A model was developed to study the capabilities of frame selection systems.
Name: ["LeBeux P.J."]

Title: On the choice of an experiment for prediction in linear regression
Abstract: Bayesian decision theory is used to obtain optimal designed and random regression experiments. If a choice is possible, it is shown how to decide between them. This is done if the data obtained are to be analyzed in order that a future value of the dependent variable can be predicted using the best subset of the independent variables.
Name: ["Brooks R.J."]

Title: Estimation of discrete multivariate densities for computer aided differential diagnosis of disease
Abstract: A Bayesian approach is taken to the problem of estimating a multivariate discrete density. Prior distributions on the space of multivariate densities are formulated to reflect the idea that the density is near a particular one, or near one which has independent variates. Given a sample of multivariate observations, an approximation to the posterior distribution of the unknown density is developed, and simple formulae for a density which approximates the mode of this posterior distribution are given. The estimate is developed in particular when the variates are binary and the prior distribution reflects that the variates are nearly but not exactly independent. The degree of apparent lack of independence in the sample determines how far from the usual estimate assuming independence this estimate will be. The proposed estimate can be thought of as interpolating between the histogram or 'cell frequency' estimate and an estimate assuming independence.
Name: ["Brunk H.D.", "Pierce D.A."]

Title: Approximate Bayesian inference with incompletely specified prior distributions
Abstract: An approximate method is suggested for evaluating the decision rules of Watson (1974) for situations where only a partial specification of the prior distribution can be given. The method is applied to the problem of estimating the mean of a distribution of unknown form, under quadratic loss. ¬© 1974 Oxford University Press.
Name: ["Goldstein M."]
Keywords: ["approximate nonparametric estimation", "bayesian inference", "decision theory", "partial information", "prior distributions"]

Title: DEVELOPMENT OF ADAPTIVE SYSTEMS IN GERMANY AND FRANCE.
Abstract: The paper shows the development of adaptive control systems in Germany and France. After a review of the historical development, typical theoretical principles and some representative examples of adaptive control systems in several fields of application are discussed. The paper shows that important results were obtained both from theoretical and experimental point of view by investigators in both countries.
Name: ["Landau I.D.", "Unbehauen H."]

Title: A statistical analysis of retrieval tests: A bayesian approach
Abstract: A model is proposed to explain the retrieval characteristics of an IR system. It is assumed that, for a given system and a given question, there are probabilities of retrieving relevant or non-relevant documents, but that these probabilities are not necessarily the same for different questions. A Bayesian method is outlined for estimating these probabilities, on the basis of a model relating them. The method is applied successfully to some Cranfield data. Potentialities of the method are discussed. ¬© 1974, MCB UP Limited
Name: ["Robertson S.E.", "Teather D."]

Title: Foundation of evaluation
Abstract: The mathematical theory of measurement is used to construct a framework for the evaluation of information retrieval strategies. The model arrived at is based on precision and recall. After a detailed examination of the kind of conditions the model can be expected to satisfy a plausible measure of effectiveness is derived. Finally, a number of other measures are shown to be special cases of it. ¬© 1974, MCB UP Limited
Name: ["Van Rijsbergen C.J."]

Title: COMPUTER PROGRAM FOR NONLINEAR REGRESSION USING LEAST SQUARES.
Abstract: The Bureau of Mines, at its Denver, Colo. , research center, has developed a computer program to solve nonlinear regression problems. The program is written in a general form so that, regardless of the functional relationship assumed, the unknown parameters may be evaluated by the Newton-Raphson method of iteration. Variances and covariances of the parameters are derived, based on the propagation of errors. A creep function is established from shale test data as an example of program utility. Program accuracy is compared to the accuracies of other programs in present-day use.
Name: ["Langland Robert T.", "Yabe Norman N."]

Title: DIGITAL ADAPTIVE FLIGHT CONTROLLER DEVELOPMENT.
Abstract: A design study of adaptive control logic suitable for implementation in modern airborne digital flight computers has been conducted. Two designs are described for an example aircraft. Each of these designs uses a weighted least squares procedure to identify parameters defining the dynamics of the example aircraft. The two designs differ in the way in which control law parameters are determined. One uses the solution of an optimal linear regulator problem to determine these parameters while the other uses a procedure called single stage optimization. Extensive simulation results and analysis leading to the designs of this study are presented.
Name: ["Kaufman Howard", "Alag Gurbux", "Berry Paul", "Kotob Samir"]

Title: COLOR TELEVISON CAMERA CONTROL BY A MICROCOMPUTER.
Abstract: The authors have made studies of automatic adjustment techniques for color TV cameras using a minicomputer, and have recently developed a small scale control system containing a microcomputer. In this system a single microcomputer controls the several color TV cameras used in one outside broadcasting vehicle or one studio by ‚Ä≥one-touch‚Ä≥ operation, thereby replacing the complicated adjustment setup usually required for color boradcast TV cameras.
Name: ["Wakui Kotaro", "Murakami Keinosuke", "Kawai Teruo", "Ohzeki Kenji"]

Title: STOCHASTIC THEORY OF LEARNING SYSTEMS - FOUNDATIONS OF TRAINABLE PATTERN-RECOGNITION SYSTEMS.
Abstract: This report treats learning systems for pattern recognition. The treatment is characterized by the stochastic nature. The reason why the stochastic approach is employed is that the learning processes are set forward by a stochastic train of inputs. Therefore, even if the processors are deterministic, their behaviors are of a stochastic nature. The most powerful method for these treatments is what is called the stochastic approximation or the potential function method. The stochastic approximation method is illustrated. And a new modification of the method is proposed by the author. The learning system of probabilistic mapping is considered. This system is aimed at associating some patterns with given patterns. The non-parametric learning of probability distribution is then examined, as is the learning system for the finite-mixture distribution. This learning system is usable as a pattern categorizer trained by itself. Finally, the relation between these new learning systems and pattern recognition is discussed. Moreover two gedenken systems to recognize patterns are presented.
Name: ["Isomichi Yoshinori"]

Title: THEORY FOR OPTIMAL Pl-CONTROL OF MULTIVARIABLE LINEAR SYSTEMS.
Source: Acta Polytech Scand Math Comput Mach Ser Mach Ser
Abstract: The linear-quadratic control problem with a performance index for regulator problems in the process industry is treated for step disturbances. In the performance index weight is put on the output vector, on the time derivative of this vector, and on the time derivative of the control vector. The resulting control law is of proportional-integral-type. Conditions for the existence of the control law and for the stability of the controlled system are derived. Furthermore, the control problem is extended to regulation of the mean value of an output vector. Some properties of the derived control laws are illustrated through digital simulation for two systems. One is a system of the fifth order; the other is a system of the 12th order describing the dynamics of a 10 plate distillation column.
Name: ["Gustafsson Sten E."]

Title: COMPUTER EXPERIMENTS ON PERIODIC SYSTEMS IDENTIFICATION USING ROTOR BLADE TRANSIENT FLAPPING-TORSION RESPONSES AT HIGH ADVANCE RATIO.
Abstract: Systems identification methods have recently been applied to rotorcraft to estimate stability derivatives from transient flight control response data. While these applications assumed a linear constant coefficient representation of the rotorcraft, the computer experiments described in this paper used transient responses in flap-bending and torsion of a rotor blade at high advance ratio which is a rapidly time varying periodic system. It was found that a simple system identification method applying a linear sequential estimator also called equation of motion estimator, is suitable for this periodic system and can be used directly if only the acceleration data are noise polluted. In the case of noise being present also in the state variable data the direct application of the estimator gave poor results, however, after prefiltering the data with a digital Graham filter having a cut-off frequency above the natural blade torsion frequency, the linear sequential estimator successfully recovered the parameters of the periodic coefficient analytical model.
Name: ["Hohenemser K.H.", "Prelewicz D.A."]

Title: MODELING AND FORECASTING OF FIRE PHENOMENA.
Abstract: The tests introduce the use of trigonometric series as models for forecasting. These models have an advantage over others in that no individual term in the series can contribute more than the value of its coefficient as a function of time. Therefore, for long projections in time, or forecasts, there are no higher-order terms of t to dominate the forecast as is the case with algebraic polynomials, for example. The authors demonstrate that these models are applicable to the analysis of nonstationary time series as well as stationary series.
Name: ["Maxwell F.D.", "O'Regan W."]

Title: Toward a theory of automatic information processing in reading
Abstract: A model of information processing in reading is described in which visual information is transformed through a series of processing stages involving visual, phonological and episodic memory systems until it is finally comprehended in the semantic system. The processing which occurs at each stage is assumed to be learned and the degree of this learning is evaluated with respect to two criteria: accuracy and automaticity. At the accuracy level of performance, attention is assumed to be necessary for processing; at the automatic level it is not. Experimental procedures are described which attempt to measure the degree of automaticity achieved in perceptual and associative learning tasks. Factors which may influence the development of automaticity in reading are discussed. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["LaBerge D.", "Samuels S.J."]

Title: GENERALIZED DATA STRUCTURES FOR DATA TRANSLATION.
Abstract: The DIAM model is a powerful model of data which is simultaneously general and based on as few primitive notions as possible. However, certain structures common to database management systems are not easily modelled in DIAM as originally defined. The paper proposes several extensions to handle these cases, while, at the same time, not extending the basic idea of a few primitive constructs. The paper also contains a few examples of the use of this model in a data translation situation.
Name: ["Taylor Robert W."]

Title: FORMALISM FOR DATA TYPES.
Abstract: A formalism for data types and data elements is presented. A mechanism is developed for ‚Ä≥lifting‚Ä≥ data type attributes to data element attributes. A rule is specified for controlling the correction of data type and data element attributes.
Name: ["Conner Michael"]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF PROGRAMS FROM THEIR PROPERTIES, AND THE INSANE HEURISTIC.
Abstract: The design of a computer system which will attempt to synthesize programs given their properties is described. Examples of functions synthesized are: PLUS, TIMES, ABSDIF and POWER on non-negative integers and APPEND and REVERSE on lists. For pedagogical reasons, the emphasis is placed on minimal sets of properties needed to synthesize a function.
Name: ["Siklossy L."]

Title: COMPLEMENTARY SIMULATION SYSTEM USING PHYSICAL AND DIGITAL TECHNIQUES.
Abstract: In many ways physical and digital fault simulation techniques complement each other. Simulation of faults where both methods apply provides a means for detecting processing errors and determining the limitations of each technique. A complementary simulation system was developed to provide simulation by each method, requiring a minimum of manual effort. The complementary simulation system has been used in the development of diagnostic tests for an ESS memory unit. Results indicate that substantial agreement between physical and digital simulation is obtainable, and that maximum diagnostic performance can be achieved by integrating the results of both processes.
Name: ["Goetz F.M."]

Title: An interactive digital image processing system
Source: Proceedings of SPIE - The International Society for Optical Engineering
Abstract: A mini-computer system has been implemented to perform interactive image processing. The computer system presents an in-tegrated modular approach to hardware development as well as software development. Digitally controlled scanners are interfaced with the system and are treated as extensions of core memory.
