Abstract: It is known that the optimal controller for a linear dynamic system disturbed by additive, independently distributed in time, not necessarily Gaussian, noise is a linear function of the state variables if the performance criterion is the expected value of a quadratic form. This result is known to hold also when the noise is Gaussian and is multiplied by a linear function of the state and/or control variables. In this paper it is proved that the optimal controller for a discrete-time linear dynamic system with quadratic performance criterion is a linear function of the state variables when the additive random vector is a nonlinear function of the state and/or control variables and not necessarily Gaussian noise which is independently distributed in time, provided only that the mean value of the random vector is zero (there is no loss of generality in assuming this) and the covariance matrix of the random vector is a quadratic function of the state and/or control variables. The above-mentioned known results emerge as special cases and certain nonlinear other special cases are exhibited. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Jacobson D.H."]

Title: Computer algorithms for analyzing patient data
Source: AFIPS Conference Proceedings - 1974 National Computer Conference, AFIPS 1974
Abstract: This topic deals with the computer-assisted evaluation of the questions of which several alternative diagnostic states might apply to a particular patient. We are also concerned here with the choice of therapy once a disease presence has been established. The computer-assistance scenario of this type must take into account both the types of diseases for which it is being instituted and possibly large amounts of patient data. ¬© ACM-CONFERENCE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Clive J."]

Title: Un modello di Œª-calcolo fortemente equivalente agli schemi ricorsivi
Abstract: This paper is oriented toward the strong equivalence between programs. We examine the procednre calls in the Cuch (the language defined by merging Church's Œª-calculus and Curry's combinators). We known that the Cuch with the Gross variant, we can model all kinds of procednre calls. Moreover, we show that also any computation rule, defined for the recursive procedure calls, can be strongly embedded into the Cuch. ¬© 1974 Instituto di Elaborazione della Informazione del CNR.
Name: ["Simone C."]

Title: State estimation for linear deterministic distributed systems
Abstract: The paper considers linear distributed systems whose state belongs to a separable Banach space, namely X. The state x of the system is assumed to be adequately approximated by its projection x<sub> N</sub> on a certain finite dimensional subspace X<sub> N</sub> (N given a priori), which is a member of a set of denumerable dense subspaces in X. A definition is given for the system's approximate observability. An algorithm is provided for computing an estimate x<sub> N</sub><sup> ^</sup> for x<sub> N</sub> . An example of a diffusion system with homogeneous (Dirichlet) boundary condition and one point (noise-free) measurement transducer is considered. The problem of numerical instability is studied. The effect of a number of important factors on the estimation problem is investigated. An extensive computational experience is presented. ¬© 1974 Instituto di Elaborazione della Informazione del CNR.
Name: ["El-Fattah Y.M."]

Title: DESIGN OF A FINITE IMPULSE RESPONSE FOR THE VITERBI ALGORITHM AND DECISION-FEEDBACK EQUALIZER.
Abstract: Methods of computing the performance of the zero-forcing and decision-feedback equalizers and the Viterbi algorithm maximum likelihood detector are reviewed. The design of a finite impulse response forward equalizer which minimizes the noise variance is considered for the purpose of limiting the complexity of the Viterbi algorithm and limiting error propagation in the decision-feedback equalizer. It is shown that on coaxial cable channels, and perhaps more generally on channels with severe intersymbol interference, that the reduced noise enhancement of the decision-feedback equalizer far outweighs the effects of error propagation on the overall error probability when a short finite impulse response is used.
Name: ["Messerschmitt David G."]

Title: Grammatiche context-free su spazi metrici compatti
Abstract: The Rabins cut-point theorem gives some conditions on acceptance of a probabilistic langnage by a finite state automaton. In the present, paper we will generalize Rabin's results by studying the possibility of reducing a coutext-free or right-linear grammar with infinite non-terminal symbols to an equivalent grammar with a finite number of non-terminal symbols. We will show that reducibility is related to some topological properties of non-terminal symbols, which we will consider as a metric space. Finally, as an application, we will use the above methods in the study of certain classes of weighted languages. ¬© 1974 Instituto di Elaborazione della Informazione del CNR.
Name: ["Bertoni A."]

Title: Filtering of discrete time series by symmetric least-squares operators
Source: Journal of the International Association for Mathematical Geology
Abstract: Least-squares operators with real and symmetric coefficients are shown to be equivalent to low-pass digital filters. By viewing these operators as digital filters one gains considerable insight into their properties. This in turn leads to a better understanding of their usefulness and limitations in data smoothing. It is shown that complete removal of noise from a given input time series is possible with the use of least-squares operators if spectral overlapping between signal and noise does not exist. Power-spectral analysis which provides information about the frequency composition of the input data is essential for successful application of least-squares operators. ¬© 1974 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Chan S.H.", "Leong L.S."]
Affiliations: [' University of Malaya', ' Science University Malaysia']

Title: EXTREMAL PARAMETER DISTRIBUTIONS IN STOCHASTIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A study is made of dynamic systems with random parameters, about which only the set of their values and certain moment characteristics are known. An estimate is made of the influence of such random parameters on the system quality indices, determining the ‚Ä≥worst‚Ä≥ and ‚Ä≥best‚Ä≥ distribution functions. It is shown that, when this information regarding the parameters is available, for finite-dimensional dynamic systems, the extremal distribution will be discrete, so that the problem is reduced to determination of the extremum of a function of a finite number of variables. An explicit solution is obtained for certain cases.
Name: ["Vladimirov S.A.", "Volkov L.N."]

Title: ENCODER/RESOLVER ARRAY FOR CONTENT ADDRESSABLE MEMORY.
Abstract: This Encoder/Resolver array is used for setting out priorities and identifying multiple match addresses during a Content Addressable Memory (CAM) search operation. Propagation delay and total array loading are minimized.
Name: ["Davidson E.E."]

Title: On the equivalence of maximum principle open-loop controllers and Carath√©odory feedback controllers for time-delay systems
Source: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
Abstract: The optimal feedback gain matrix derived from the maximum principle for linear time-delay systems with quadratic cost satisfies an integral equation. On the other hand, if the extended Carath√©odory lemma is used to solve the same problem, the optimal feedback gains satisfy a set of partial differential equations. It is shown that the resulting feedback gains are equivalent. ¬© 1974 Plenum Publishing Corporation.
Name: ["Koivo H.N."]
Affiliations: [' University of Minnesota', ' University of Toronto']

Title: OPTIMAL BIDDING IN SEQUENTIAL AUCTIONS.
Abstract: When a bidder's strategy in one auction will affect his competitor's behavior in subsequent auctions, bidding in a sequence of auctions can be modeled fruitfully as a multistage control process in which the control is the bidder's strategy while the stage characterizes the competitor's behavior. This paper presents such a model in which the state transition represents the competitors' reaction to the bidder's strategy. Dynamic programming is used to derive the infinite horizon optimal bidding strategy. It is shown that in steady state this optimal stategy generalizes a previous result for equilibrium bidding strategy in ‚Ä≥one-shot‚Ä≥ auctions.
Name: ["Oren Shmuel S.", "Rothkopf Michael H."]

Title: IMPROVING IDENTIFICATIONS IN THE FILE SEARCHING OF MASS SPECTRA.
Abstract: A statistical theory which permits quantitative prediction of file search results is used to compare algorithms in terms of their sensitivity to error. In this method, a code found in the library is modified sufficiently to produce misidentification. For two very simple goodness of fit criteria, it is possible, for any code, to predict both what type of error will cause misidentification and the magnitude of the error that can be tolerated before misidentification occurs. In this way, it is possible to more quantitatively compare two algorithms in terms of their sensitivity to error.
Name: ["Grotch S.L."]

Title: Two …õ-Optimal Nonlinear Reinforcement Schemes for Stochastic Automata
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: Two nonlinear reinforcement schemes [2], [8] for variable-structure stochastic automata are discussed. It is proved that they can ensure …õ-optimality under certain conditions. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Sawaragi Y.", "Baba N."]

Title: Deterministic Acceptors of Regular Fuzzy Languages
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: The one-to-one relationship between finite automata, regular (type-3) languages, and regular expressions is well known. This correspondence demonstrates the use of regular expressions for describing deterministically finite fuzzy automata and regular fuzzy languages, and introduces a normal form for the production of a regular fuzzy grammar when the ‚Äúmax(min)‚Äù form is used. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Thomason M.G.", "Marinos P.N."]

Title: A general-purpose computer program for obtaining improved simulation solutions
Abstract: Many operations research problems confronting the military decision maker are either too expensive lor experimental solution or too complicated for analytical treatment. For such problems, computer simulation often proves useful. However, any attempt to determine the best problem solution by means of simulation relies, in general, on a search of the relevant parameter space. Because it was postulated that application of a mathematically-based search should produce simulation solutions superior to those obtained by standard methods, a computer program was developed to provide such a search. This executive program can easily be interfaced with a simulation to monitor an adaptive search for the best solution. In addition to performing the mathematical calculations to support the search, it maintains all the accounting functions required during the optimization process. This paper describes the program logic, summarizes its applications to date, and discusses implications of its performance. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Smith D.E."]

Title: Automatized programming of nonlinear differential systems in a hybrid computer. Hybrid simulation of a world model
Abstract: A method is discussed how to study by means of hybrid computation the behaviour and (optimal) control of a wide class of non-linear differential systems without changing the analogue patching. A hybrid computer implementation has been set up for studies in the field of world dynamics. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Dekker L.", "Kerckhoffs E.H.J."]

Title: COMPUTER CONTROLLED ACQUISITION, PROCESSING AND DISPLAY OF MYOCARDIAL PERFUSION IMAGES.
Abstract: A computer controlled color coded photographic system for processing and display of myocardial perfusion images is presented. The system combines quantitative and analog properties into a single permanent display, excellent for pattern recognition. It has been in routine use for the past three years in displaying the images of myocardial perfusion. The cost is reasonable if a computer system is already available in the Nuclear Medicine Laboratory.
Name: ["Jansen Carl", "Adams Ralph", "Grames George M.", "Carlsen Ernest N."]

Title: Combination of spatial networks using an estimated covariance matrix
Abstract: When combining satellite and terrestrial networks, covariance matrices are used which have been estimated from previous data. It can be shown that the least-squares estimator of the unknown parameters using such an estimated covariance matrix is not necessarily the best. There are a number of cases where a more efficient estimator can be obtained in a different way. The problem occurs frequently in geodesy, since in least-squares adjustment of correlated observations estimated covariance matrices are often used. If the general structure of the covariance matrix is known, results can often be improved by a method called covariance adjustment. The statistical model used in least-squares collocation leads to a type of covariance matrix which fits into this framework. It is shown in which way improvements can be made using a modified approach of principal component analysis. As a numerical example the combination of a satellite and a terrestrial network has been computed with varying assumptions on the covariance matrix. It is shown which types of matrices are critical and where the usual least-squares approach can be applied without hesitation. Finally, a simplified representation of covariances for spatial networks by means of a suitable covariance function is suggested. ¬© 1974 Bureau Central de L'Association Internationale de G√©od√©sie.
Name: ["Schwarz K.-P."]

Title: An economical algorithm for distinguishing blocks in a graph
Source: USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics
Abstract: AN ALGORITHM for organizing the search for blocks in a connected graph is presented. The estimate of the number of operations of the algorithm is of minimum possible order: O(p), where p is the number of arcs of the graph. ¬© 1975.
Name: ["Dinits E.A.", "Zaitsev M.A.", "Karzanov A.V."]

Title: COMPUTER SYSTEM FOR THE CARDIOVASCULAR LABORATORY.
Abstract: An integrated computerized diagnostic cardiology system is described, which provides a means of assembling a comprehensive patient data base and allows implementation of automated logical decision-making. Automated medical decision making (HELP: Health Evaluation through Logical Processing) aids the physician in obtaining necessary measurements and in making an accurate diagnosis. Diagnostic techniques which quantitate left ventricular dynamic function and regional contractility have been incorporated into the system and provide additional information upon which a diagnosis can be based.
Name: ["Clayton Paul D.", "Urie Paul M.", "Marshall Hiram W.", "Warner Homer R."]

Title: Sequential Algorithm for the Determination of Maximum Compatibles
Abstract: This correspondence describes an algorithm which finds the maximum compatibles (maximal complete subgraphs of a symmetric graph) sequentially and in lexicographic order. The algorithm is intended for use in digital computers, where it requires only a small program and very little memory space. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Stoffers K.E."]
Keywords: ["compatibility matrix", "hasse diagram", "lexicographic ordering", "maximal complete subgraphs", "spanning tree"]

Title: SYNVER: A system for the automatic synthesis and verification of synchronization processes
Source: Proceedings of the 1974 Annual ACM Conference/Annual Meeting, ACM 1974
Abstract: The automatic synthesis of systems of synchronized processes and the proof of the synchronization's correctness is discussed. A general system, SYNVER, is proposed. Its input is a problem description and its output is a set of communicating processes proven correct. A high-level assertion language is presented in which certain types of synchronization problems may be described in a natural but formal way. Heuristics are developed for SYNVER so that it may infer from the problem description what data structures and what operations are necessary to realize the described synchronization. From this information, the code pertaining to synchronization is synthesized. Finally, SYNVER applies verification techniques to prove that the assertions made about the synchronization of the processes are not only consistent, but are also realized by the code synthesized. ¬© 1974 ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Griffiths P."]

Title: Optimum Features and Graph Isomorphism
Source: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
Abstract: An algorithm is presented to test the graph isomorphism for undirected linear graphs. The graph isomorphism between two or more graphs can be tested by obtaining their optimum codes. The algorithm relabels the nodes of graphs to obtain optimum codes. The optimum code is the code of maximum weight obtained from the upper triangle of the adjacency matrix of the given graph. The method of ordering the nodes of a graph to produce a code invariant to isomorphism is related to invariant features in feature extraction [7], [15]. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Shah Y.J.", "Davida G.I.", "McCarthy M.K."]

Title: The application of a symbolic mathematical system to program verification
Source: Proceedings of the 1974 Annual ACM Conference/Annual Meeting, ACM 1974
Abstract: Program verification is a relatively new application area for symbolic mathematical systems. We report on an interactive program verification system, based on the inductive assertion method, which system is implemented using an existing symbolic mathematical language and supporting system, Reduce. Reduce has been augmented with a number of capabilities which are important to program verification, particularly transformations on relational and Boolean expressions. We believe these capabilities would be valuable in other contexts and should be incorporated more widely into symbolic mathematical systems for general use. The program verification application can serve as a guide to an appropriate definition of such capabilities, particularly with regard to the need to distinguish between undefined program variables and polynomial indeterminates. Additional capabilities which would benefit the program verification application include representation of user-defined functions by internal forms which directly incorporate properties such as commutativity and associativity (as is commonly done with plus and times), and a comprehensive facility for defining conditionally applicable transformations. ¬© 1974 ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["London R.L.", "Musser D.R."]

Title: Some ideas on semantic memory in automatic learning of heuristics
Abstract: This paper is concerned with the problem of computer semantic memory, i. e. with the problem of representing general knowledge about, a given world. The sematic memory issue is raised in the context of machiue learning of heuristics and the connection with the problem of machine representation of knowledge is emphasized. The guidelines for the implementation of a sematic memory are presented and attention is given to the design of the processes for storing and retrieving information. The problem of knowledge representation is tackled in its, general form, so that the proposed semantic memory may be of interest also in other fields, like Natural Lauguage Understanding, Question Answering, Theorem Proving. ¬© 1974 Instituto di Elaborazione della Informazione del CNR.
Name: ["Sirovich F."]

Title: ON THE STRUCTURE AND PERFORMANCE OF A LINEAR DECISION FEEDBACK EQUALIZER BASED ON THE MINIMUM ERROR PROBABILITY CRITERION.
Abstract: In recent years, the structure of a decision feedback equalizer (DFE) constrained to have linear feed forward filter (FFF), linear feedback filter (FBF), and error free past decisions has been considered based on the minimum mean-square distortion criterion, minimum mean-square error criterion, and maximum SNR with zero forcing constraint. This paper considers the structure of a DFE with these constraints based on the minimum bit error probability criterion which appears to be the most relevant criterion for independent digital data error analysis. It is shown that the FFF consists of a matched filter in tandem with a TDL operating to reduce intersymbol interference (ISI) from future bits and a FBF consists of a TDL operating to cancel completely the ISI from past bits in the absence of decision error.
Name: ["Shamash E.", "Yao K."]

Title: PERFORMANCE OF SELECTED LINEAR AND NONLINEAR RECEIVERS IN ELF NOISE.
Abstract: A model for ELF impulsive noise environments is described in detail and some of its properties discussed. A useful and intuitively satisfying model for impulsive noise processes typical of the ELF environment has been shown to consist of the sum of a low-density shot process and white Gaussian noise (WGN). Attention is then directed toward the performance of selected linear and nonlinear receivers operating in noise environments as described by this model. Approximate expressions are determined for the error probability performance of linear matched filter reception binary antipodal signals. These results are extremely useful in providing qualitative insight into the manner in which error probability depends upon the various parameters of the underlying noise model. Simulation results are presented indicating the error probability performance of a number of selected nonlinear receiver structures useful in combating the effects of impulse noise. Finally optimum zero memory nonlinear (ZMNL) receiver characteristics are determined and illustrations are presented to indicate behavior as a function of noise model parameters.
Name: ["Modestino J.W.", "Sankur B."]

Title: Equivalenza tra grammatiche, sistemi di equazioni in variabili di linguaggio e serie formali
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate conditions for the equivalence of three different manners of defining a language: a context-free grammar, a system of equations whose variables are languages, a system of equations whose variables are formal sums. In order to achieve this goal, the well-known concept of formal sum is introduced; moreover the existence and uniqueness of the solution of a system of equations is proved by means of Banach's classical fixed-point theorem. ¬© 1974 Instituto di Elaborazione della Informazione del CNR.
Name: ["Gatto M.", "Mandrioli D."]
Affiliations: ['Istituto di Elettrotecnica ed Elettronica del Politecnico di Milano']

Title: MODEL OF REACH CAPABILITIES OF MAN.
Abstract: A mathematical modeling technique for simulation of human motion is reviewed, and the technique is utilized to develop an approach to the analysis of reach. The modeling technique uses the Euler angles as geometric variables. The reach analysis approach involves the optimal location of intermediate joints to attain maximum reach.
Name: ["Luming Henry", "Krause Horst E."]

Title: Note sulla derivata di un programma
Abstract: In this paper, we consider while-program-schemata, as defined, for example, in [1] [2] [3], interpreted over a domain of functions and predicates over the real numbers. We observe that the (real) functions computed by programs of this kind are representable by (non recursive) Algol-like expressions which are, in general, too complicated to be treated with the methods of classical mathematical analysis. As an example of how to extend classical analytical concepts to functions computed by programs, we give a method for constructing in an algorithmic way a program which computes the derivative of the function computed by a given program, if such a derivative exists. A simple example is given. ¬© 1974 Instituto di Elaborazione della Informazione del CNR.
Name: ["Antoni G.D.", "Polillo R."]

Title: OPTIMUM QUANTIZATION OF SPEECH FOR CONSTANT WORD LENGTH CODING.
Abstract: A quantization method is presented which exploits the intersample statistical dependencies between speech samples to achieve a higher signal to noise ratio (SNR), for a given transmission rate, than by conventional methods. To accomplish this, it is first necessary to measure the conditional probability density for each state of the assumed stationary Markov model. A minimum mean squared error quantizer is then employed which switches in a quantizing characteristic matched to the corresponding Markov state conditional probability density. Such a quantizer will be called a switched quantizer and provides an optimum method of quantization under the constraint of assigning constant length code words to the quantizer representative levels. In a computer simulation using telephone quality speech and a switched quantizer at first constrained to have 64 characteristics, the increase in SNR over that of a three past sample prediction DPCM system using a logarithmic quantizer is 6. 6 dB. When the constraint on the number of quantization characteristics is reduced to four, the gain in SNR becomes 4. 9 dB.
Name: ["Cohen F.A."]

Title: KALMAN FILTER EQUALIZER FOR QPSK DIGITAL COMMUNICATIONS CHANNEL.
Abstract: The discrete complex Kalman filter is considered as an equalizer for quadrature-phase-shift-keyed (QPSK) systems in the presence of additive noise and intersymbol interference. For a known linear time-invariant channel with finite duration impulse response, the finite n-dimension complex Kalman filter equalizer is able to reduce the degradation caused by ISI. When the channel is unknown, an adaptive Kalman equalizer is used in which the channel complex tap gains are estimated by decision feedback. A two component multipath channel QPSK system is used as an example. Using the Chernoff upper bound to calculate the error probabilities, the computer simulation shows that both the Kalman filter equalizer and adaptive equalizer have better performance than the integrate-and-dump correlator with no equalizer.
Name: ["Lee T.S.", "Cunningham D.R."]

Title: CONTROL OF CONGESTION IN MESSAGE SWITCHED NETWORKS.
Abstract: The problem of congestion in message switched data communication networks is discussed, and a queueing model and some analytic results are presented. The queueing model for a logical link and the analysis performed on it provide a quantitative method for evaluating and comparing various schemes which can be employed to prevent a single link from causing congestion in a message switched network. Using this method, the behavior of networks employing end to end and local controls is investigated. The effectiveness of controls in preventing congestion is demonstrated and the tradeoff between reduced service to the link user and improved service to other users is identified. Both types of control schemes are shown to provide similar performance with respect to this tradeoff. Finally, the increased need for controls with increasing network demand is demonstrated.
Name: ["Pennotti Michael C.", "Schwartz Mischa"]

Title: ADAPTIVE PCM SPEECH TRANSMISSION.
Abstract: A digital speech compression system design is described which is capable of exploiting both the time varying bandwidth and voice activity properties of a typical telephone speech conversation. The system is designed to accept a 4. 096 Mb/s TDM frame made of up 64 PCM voice channels each sampled with 8 bits at an 8 kHz rate. The 64 channels are ultimately multiplexed into a single PCM data stream at a 1. 296Mb/s data rate representing an approximate 3. 2/1 reduction in the data rate. The data stream consists of twenty PCM channels with a probability of freezeout of 0. 05% (negligible) and a probability of downgrading (reduced channel quality) of 0. 8%. Control word coding is specified to assure error free transmission. The overall bit rate of 1. 296Mb/sec, therefore, includes coded control information and sync. 5 refs.
Name: ["Whelchel John E.", "Mayefskie Gerald F.", "Stroud Robert H.", "Eger Thomas E."]

Title: COMPUTER RECOGNITION OF DIPLOG PATTERNS. A TOOL FOR STRATIGRAPHIC ANALYSIS.
Abstract: Many types of subjective decisions can be made by the computer by suitable training, and in particular the computer can pick out patterns in a Diplog vector plot quite accurately. By picking the patterns automatically and generating azimuth frequency plots, many man hours can be saved. When designing such a pattern recognition system the following principles will be useful: eliminate unnecessary attributes of the test class as possible. Combine attributes into features where it is applicable; select the training sample carefully to represent boundary areas; and where possible, plot the feature space and the training objects.
Name: ["Schoonover Larry G."]

Title: MACHINE PROCESSING FOR REMOTELY ACQUIRED DATA.
Abstract: A general discussion intended to introduce the prospective user to multivariate data analysis techniques as applied to the processing of remotely acquired earth observational data is presented. Not only are numerically-oriented remote sensing systems discussed, but attention is given to image-oriented systems, the other main branch of remote sensing, in order to establish the relationship between the two. Plates, diagrams, and curves are appended.
Name: ["Landgrebe D.A."]

Title: PLASTICS AND ROBOTS: A MARRIAGE OF NECESSITY.
Abstract: This paper discusses the possibility of the use of robots in plastics processing plants. These applications illustrate but a few to which the robot is well suited in injection molding. In addition, the robot can load insert into the molds, present parts for paint spraying after removing them from the molding machine, feed trim presses, palletize or package the parts and virtually anything that the human operator does repetitively. One figure shows the Unimate robot situated between two large molding machines, each of which produces two automobile bucket seat backs. After removal, the robot places the parts into an automatic trimming and drilling fixture. The robot then rotates to the other molding machine and repeats the process. The Unimate automatically cycles both molding machines and the trimming fixture as part of its program. Two illustrations show an application in which the robot is handling large elastomer rubber injection molded parts. This is a particularly challenging job because of the unwieldy and floppy nature of the part and because it has a great affinity to stick to the mold.
Name: ["Munson Jr. George E."]

Title: IDENTIFICATION AND AUTOREGRESSIVE SPECTRUM ESTIMATION.
Abstract: In recent years there has been increasing interest in autoregressive spectrum estimation. This procedure fits a finite autoregression to the time series data, and calculates the spectrum from the estimated autoregression coefficients and the one step prediction error variance. For multivariate time series, the estimated autoregressive matrices and one step prediction covariance matrix produce estimates of the spectra, coherences, phases, and group delays. The use of H. Akaike's Information Criteria (AIC) for identification of the order of the autoregression to be used makes the procedure objective. Experience has indicated that AIC works very well for model identification when compared to more subjective procedures such as the examination of partial F-statics, and that using both autoregressive spectrum estimation and classical spectrum and superimposing the plots gives a much stronger feeling for the shape of the true spectrum being estimated. The results of some of these analyses are presented.
Name: ["Jones Richard H."]

Title: Scheduling in systems with two scarce resources
Source: Proceedings of the 1974 Annual ACM Conference/Annual Meeting, ACM 1974
Abstract: Few optimality results have been reported for the scheduling of computer systems with more than one resource. This paper considers a system with two independently-scheduled scarce resources, which may be thought of as a CPU and an I/O channel, and two active programs with distinct service burst time characteristics. Schedules requiring preemption no more frequently than when-a program requests service at a resource are shown to be sufficient to achieve maximum average utilization (the unweighted average of the utilizations of the two resources). A rule that specifies schedules of this form when applied at both resources is defined and proven optimal. Finally, the more general problem of maximizing weighted utilization is treated. ¬© 1974 ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Lazowska E.D.", "Sevcik K.C."]

Title: RAPID ESTIMATION AND DETECTION SCHEME FOR UNKNOWN DISCRETIZED RECTANGULAR INPUTS.
Abstract: An algorithm to detect unknown discretized rectangular inputs and to estimate the state simultaneously, has been described. The discretized rectangular input is represented by a sequence of equal magnitude impulseive inputs to the state. Four alternate hypotheses are formed at every stage of observation and Bayes risks are compared to determine the correct one. A minimum variance estimate of the inputs is used to improve the estimate of the state. Computer results from a numerical example are shown to demonstrate that a possible divergence of the Kalman filter can be prevented by incorporating the detection scheme.
Name: ["Sonalkar R.V.", "Sken C.N."]

Title: SMALL COMPANY PRODUCTION CONTROL USING A VISIBLE RECORD COMPUTER.
Abstract: A system of production control has been designed to operate on an inexpensive Philips P358 Visible Record Computer, so that it is suitable for small and medium sized companies, particularly those engaged in batch production. It incorporates an adaptive loading procedure, enabling realistic delivery dates for customers' orders to be determined. Other features of the system include accurate stock recording, the preparation of works order documentation, progress control and the preparation of a Forward Load Report.
Name: ["Galgut Paul E."]

Title: OPTIMAL CONTROL OF LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH INCOMPLETE MEASUREMENTS USING AN N<sup>th</sup> ORDER OBSERVER.
Abstract: The optimal control of linear systems where measurement of all the state variables is not possible is investigated from the viewpoint of observer theory. Observers whose dynamic order equals the dimension of the plant state vector are examined and necessary conditions for the optimal observer dynamics and control feedback gains are derived.
Name: ["Bailey R.A.", "Schmitendorf W.E."]

Title: COMPUTER AUTOMATED ULTRASONIC INSPECTION SYSTEM FOR AIRCRAFT FORGINGS.
Abstract: A computer-automated ultrasonic immersion inspection system is described which will be used to inspect aircraft forgings. The system is capable of automatically inspecting objects with nonplanar surfaces, such as tapers, fillets, and large radii. Modes of operation include both pulse echo and Delta scan inspection, with computer control of scanning, data acquisition, processing, and display. Flaw signals are input in the rf form to allow defect characterization.
Name: ["Yee B.G.W.", "Allison J.E."]

Title: INPUT DESIGN FOR PARAMETER IDENTIFICATION - 1. A NEW FORMULATION AND A PRACTICAL SOLUTION.
Abstract: A new formulation and a practical and useful solution to the input design for identification of system parameters are presented. The new formulation is directly relevant to the following question: for a given measurement system and with prescribed physical constraints on the input and output magnitudes, what should the input functions be and for how long should the data record be taken to enable identification of system parameters to a specified accuracy? Time optimal control theory is used in the formulation of this important problem. Necessary conditions for the optimal control input are discussed. By converting the calculation of the Cramer-Rao lower bounds into a sequential operation, a practical and useful solution is then presented. Application of this new input design approach is made to the identification of aircraft stability and control parameters.
Name: ["Chen Robert T.N."]

Title: APPLICATION OF DISTURBANCE OBSERVER TO COMPUTER CONTROL OF BLENDING PROCESS.
Abstract: A practical control algorithm which can be used for regulation of a linear time delay process with linear control constraints subject to unknown disturbances is presented. The algorithm is written via velocity form suitable for use in DDC or supervisory type industrial control with existing hardware output interface equipment. An example of seven component gasoline blending is presented to illustrate the closed loop control performance. The classical integrator control and unknown disturbance observer are derived and incorporated into the proposed algorithm.
Name: ["Lin C.S.", "Gardner N.F."]

Title: DESIGN AND SELECTION OF A SUPERVISORY CONTROL SYSTEM.
Abstract: This paper describes the process of designing and selecting a digital supervisory control system for the Cities Service Pinto Valley Concentrator. Selection was made through an analysis of hardware, software, experience, maintenance, delivery, and cost consideration. The resulting system consists architecturally of a central multiprocessing computer driving three process input-output stations, the operator interface, and peripheral devices. The real time multiprocessing system is supplied by the computer system vendor. The process input-output and data handling software is supplied by the total systems' vendor; and the control, display, and reporting software by the user.
Name: ["Arney Terry O."]

Title: APPLICATION OF FUZZY ALGORITHMS FOR CONTROL OF SIMPLE DYNAMIC PLANT.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: A scheme is described in which a fuzzy algorithm is used to control plants, in this case, a laboratory-built steam engine. The algorithm is implemented as an interpreter of a set of rules expressed as fuzzy conditional statements. This implementation on a digital computer is used on-line, to control the plant. The merit of such a controller is discussed in the light of the results obtained.
Name: ["Mamdani E.H."]

Title: MANAGEMENT PLANNING AND CONTROL SYSTEMS INCORPORATING MICROANALYTIC PROCESS SIMULATION MODELS.
Abstract: The application of computer-based management systems incorporating: sensor-based information acquisition, extensive over-time data bases, judgemental as well as quantitative inputs, and digital discrete process and decision simulation models. Theoretical and experimental evidence supporting the use of such systems is drawn from the chemical, aerospace, and electronics industries. Strengths and weaknesses of specific model structures are illustrated, and characteristics of computer systems required to support effective model utilization are defined. Managerial and operating problems encountered are also described.
Name: ["Amstutz Arnold E."]

Title: INFORMATION SYSTEM FOR SCHEDULING SENSOR EQUIPPED ENVIRONMENTAL SURVEILLANCE AIRCRAFT.
Abstract: Common pitfalls are presented and an example is given which illustrates how certain problems were avoided in the design of an Optimal Pollution Surveillance Schedule Generating System (OPGENS) to be used by the U. S. Coast Guard in directing ultraviolet and infrared sensor equipped aircraft on pollution surveillance missions over the navigable waterway system of the United States. This example is appropriate because OPGENS incorporates both sophisticated Operations Research models and complex Management Information Systems concepts. The primary model in OPGENS is based on work done with Markovian Decision Processes, and the solution algorithms incorporated are variations on formal mathematical programming approaches found in the Management Science literature.
Name: ["McKell Lynn J.", "Wright Gordon P."]

Title: TEXT PROCESSING AND INFORMATION RETRIEVAL - REPORT ON WORKSHOP 4.
Source: Networks for Res and Educ, Sharing Comput and Inf Resour Nationwide, Semin conducted by EDUCOM, Pap and Discuss
Abstract: Systems designed to capture, store, and selectively retrieve textual information and data bases requiring large-file capability were analyzed. The emphasis was on users of systems that incorporate text processing, indexing, and searching operations and that allow the user to build as well as retrieve from files.
Name: ["Massy William F."]

Title: ON THE SIMPLE EYES OF INDUSTRIAL ROBOT APPLYING THE CORRELATION TECHNIQUE.
Abstract: Preliminary results of a study are presented which was conducted in order to develop sensors to recognize the shapes of an object. The paper describes the newly devised simple eyes which consist of a couple of TV cameras with telephoto lens, a polarity coincidence correlator and servomechanisms to control them. The eyes can perceive whether an object exists ahead or not, and measure, when an object exists, the distance between the object and the eyes.
Name: ["Matsushima Kozo", "Furuichi Chieko", "Osogoe Toshikuni"]

Title: STATE SPACE REPRESENTATIONS OF DISTRIBUTED FLUID LINE DYNAMICS.
Abstract: Demonstrates the convenience of using a systematic straightforward procedure to obtain meaningful dynamic information for a class of complex distributed parameter fluid line networks. System transients in the time domain are determined by means of state space techniques. Digital computer implementation yields a simple but consistent way of obtaining overall system time solutions. A step-by-step analysis procedure flow chart is shown in Apendix I which illustrates the basic approach for modeling, approximating and selecting digital techniques for simulating the dynamic response of fluid line systems.
Name: ["Yao H.", "Goodson R.E.", "Leonard R.G."]

Title: OPTIMAL ADAPTIVE SAMPLED-DATA REGULATOR.
Abstract: Adaptive sampling often provides a more accurate model of sampled-data processes when sampling is not triggered by a timer, but occurs when one or more outputs attain preset threshold values. In this paper, the optimal linear regulator problem with adaptive sampling is formulated and both open and closed loop solutions are determined. A comparison of a system's performance with adaptive and with periodic sampling is presented.
Name: ["Schlueter Robert A.", "Levis Alexander H."]

Title: OVERMODELING OF DYNAMICAL PROCESSES.
Abstract: Description of the physical and mathematical consequences stemming from an engineer's inadvertent selection of ‚Ä≥more than enough‚Ä≥ process variables x//1 to represent the process state. This situation, called ‚Ä≥overmodeling‚Ä≥ , is studied for both linear and nonlinear dynamical processes, and general results are obtained,
Name: ["Johnson C.D."]

Title: PSEUDOINVERSION IN DIGITAL IMAGE RESTORATION.
Abstract: Restoration of images degraded by known phenomena is a field that has met with little success. At least part of this lack of success in restoration is due to two basic problems: historical-analog-image processing reliance on Fourier or spatial plane concepts; and, more recently (in digital processing), limited computer capability. Perhaps more importantly, digital image processing has largely ignored the powerful tools available from the field of numerical analysis and in particular, techniques for pseudoinversion of degradation matrices. Hence, the basic purpose of this paper is to present a limited review of some concepts in generalized matrix inversion and to demonstrate the utility of procedure with specific examples.
Name: ["Patterson Claude L.", "Buechler Gunther", "Andrews Harry C."]

Title: Some recent investigations of a new fuzzy partitioning algorithm and its application to pattern classification problems
Abstract: Recent results pertaining to a newly developed fuzzy partitioning algorithm are surveyed. The algorithm has potential value as a heuristic tool for identifying clusters within large finite data sets, and more specifically, for estimating the parameters in a mixture of unimodal probability densities, given a finite sample drawn from the mixture. The topics treated are: fuzzy partitions, conventional clustering algorithms, fuzzy clustering algorithms, asymptotic behavior of optimal fuzzy partitions with increasing cluster separation, scalar measures of partition fuzziness, and unsupervised learning and parameter estimation. ¬© 1975 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Dunn J.C."]

Title: BOUNDS FOR IDENTIFICATION ERROR AND A QUANTITATIVE MEASURE OF IDENTIFIABILITY.
Abstract: Upper and lower bounds for identification error are established for finite observation samples. It is shown that the behavior of both the upper and lower bounds are described completely by a resolvability function which describes the degree of resolvability between different parameters in the parameter set. This allows one to derive identifiability conditions by investigating the asymptotic behavior of this function. Moreover, the resolvability function gives a quantitative measure of identifiability.
Name: ["Tse Edison"]

Title: EVALUATION OF REAL-TIME ALGORITHMS FOR OMEGA PROPAGATION PREDICTION.
Abstract: Published OMEGA Predicted Propagation Corrections (PPC's) are generally recognized as providing the most accurate means of correcting received OMEGA signals. However, computation of the published PPC's involves use of two sophisticated computer routines - one involving extensive propagation physics modeling, the other is a complex mathematical adjustment requiring online access to a large data base. Real-time implementation of these routines in shipboard or airborne computers is not practical and thus, a number of algorithms have been developed in an attempt to obtain correction values which closely match published PPC's, yet impose a considerably less severe computer burden. In this paper, various of these algorithms - including functional approximations and simplified propagation physics models - are evaluated in terms of their accuracy relative to published PPC's and their relative computer burdens. The propagation models used in the PPC computation process are briefly examined in order to highlight areas of possible simplification for real-time applications.
Name: ["Beavers Jr. Alex N.", "Gentry Daniel E.", "Kasper Jr. Joseph F."]

Title: DUAL EFFECT, CERTAINTY EQUIVALENCE AND SEPARATION IN STOCHASTIC CONTROL.
Abstract: Various policies in fixed end-time stochastic control are discussed. The emphasis is on the difference between the feedback and closed-loop policies. It is shown how the closed-loop policy has the important property that it can be actively adaptive, while the feedback policy can be only passively adaptive. The feature of being actively adaptive is possible when the control has a dual effect. The intimate connection between the neutrality (lack of dual effect) and certainty equivalence properties for a class of problems is proved. This new result is then used to widen the class of problems for which it was previously known that the certainty equivalence property holds.
Name: ["Bar-Shalom Yaakov", "Tee Edison"]

Title: Optimal control of linear multivariable systems with quadratic performance index, and the inverse optimal control problem
Abstract: For a linear order time-invariant system with scalar control variable and quadratic performance index, a procedure is given for computing the optimal value of the feedback vector Instead of determining, as a first, step, the N(N+1)/2 elements of a symmetric matrix, the values of k are computed directly, leading to substantial simplifications, and making the method well suited for higher-order systems. In contrast to other methods starting from the same premise, no restrictions are imposed on the form of matrix. In addition, and based on the previous considerations, a solution of the inverse optimal control problem is also presented. The form of the weighting matrix in the performance index can be chosen arbitrarily (e.g. as diagonal). In contrast to other known procedures, the computations are straightforward, and again no restrictions are imposed on the form of the system. ¬© 1974 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Buelens P.F.", "Hellinckx L.J."]

Title: LONGITUDINAL CONTROL IN GUIDED TRANSPORTATION SCHEMES USING THE MOVING-CELL PHILOSOPHY.
Abstract: The longitudinal control of vehicles in automated transportation systems using the moving-cell approach is considered. A linear, sampled-data controller has been derived which has been shown to yield good vehicle response characteristics; the responses being optimal with respect to a defined quadratic performance index. An extended system model has been proposed which considers the problem of inaccessible state variables and which attempts to deal with the effects of random disturbances and measurement noise. The resulting optimum controller and linear state estimator have been shown to be extremely effective at maintaining the vehicle at or near to its desired position, and at smoothing out fluctuations in the rate of change of propulsive force, despite very noisy measurements and large input disturbances.
Name: ["Rumsey A.F.", "Powner E.T."]

Title: COMPARISON OF USER REACTION TO AUTOMATED INSTRUCTION PRESENTED BY A COMPUTER AND BY AUDIO-VISUAL MEANS.
Abstract: This paper describes the result of simulating the kind of highly flexible CAI system that is on the borderline of current technology. Factors determining optimum man-computer interaction with naive users were explored. It is concluded that the ordinary person has little difficulty in adapting to a simple interface with the computer, but different factors appear to determine the extent to which a particular interface is suitable for young and old subjects.
Name: ["Bevan N.S.", "Evans C.R."]

Title: POSTURAL STABILITY OF THE TWO-DEGREE-OF-FREEDOM BIPED BY GENERAL LINEAR FEEDBACK.
Abstract: The use of linear feedback to stabilize the two-degree-of-freedom model of a biped is considered. Linear feedback is used not only for stabilization but also for placing the system poles and for altering the system characteristics. The use of constraints to reduce the number of external inputs required to control the model is investigated. The effect of various linear feedback strategies on the nonlinear model is studied via computer simulation.
Name: ["Golliday Jr. C.L.", "Hemami H."]

Title: APPLICATION OF GEOMETRIC PROGRAMMING TO THE POWER SYSTEM ECONOMIC DISPATCH OPTIMIZATION.
Abstract: A new method is outlined for obtaining an approximate optimized solution of the economic dispatch problem of a power system using the output of a standard loadflow computer program along with a geometric programming algorithm. This digital-computer method is much faster than the existing methods, requiring only about thirty seconds on an IBM 360-75 system to obtain a loadflow solution as well as optimize the economic dispatch problem for a system of 203 buses, and requires little additional core storage over the requirements of the loadflow routine.
Name: ["Sarma Mulukutla S.", "Bayless Charles E.", "Stanek Eldon K."]

Title: SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION USING FOKKER-PLANCK TECHNIQUES.
Abstract: An identification scheme is presented for a class of nth-order linear systems described by state equations with constant coefficients. When these systems are excited by a Gaussian process an approximation to the Fokker-Planck equation can be derived for the system, as the state vector is near-Markov in nature. Using sampled-data information the Markovian properties of the system can be estimated and then used to compute the coefficient matrices appearing in the state equations.
Name: ["Miller W.C.", "Shridhar M.", "Jullien G.A.", "Loh N.K."]

Title: ON THE PROPERTIES OF CONVERGENCE OF STATISTICAL SEARCH.
Abstract: The convergence of statistical (random) search for the minimization of an arbitrary function Q(w) is treated. It is shown that random search can be regarded as a gradient algorithm in the q-domain. Using the gradient to define the minimum of the function, the convergence is discussed at length-including convergence WP1, convergence in the mean and epsilon -optimality. The proof of convergence is based upon the theorems of convergence of random processes of E. Braverman and L. Rozonoer. The relationship between random search and order statistics is explained. Finally, emphasis is put on the applicability of the theorems for the design of hierarchical search systems and statistical search with a mixture.
Name: ["Devroye Luc P."]

Title: NULL-STEERING ARRAY FOR RPV APPLICATION.
Abstract: In today's search for smarter tactical drones, usually referred to as RPV's (remotely piloted vehicles), there has become a need for secure interference-resistant two-way links. Small single adaptive arrays can aid in signal acquisition, and in later communication, when there is high power interference. The interference is reduced by adaptively steering antenna pattern nulls toward the interference. A brief review of adaptive algorithms for performing this array control is given. A three-element adaptive array has been built and its experimental performance is presented. Typical patterns for various desired and jamming signals are shown. Also, data is presented showing the array adaptive nulling performance with modulated signals. The design of a lightweight, miniaturized null-steering array featuring hybrid integrated circuit techniques is also described.
Name: ["Rassweiler G.G.", "Martin G.P.", "Payne L.M.", "Lehman D.F."]

Title: ERROR PROPAGATION IN DECISION-FEEDBACK EQUALIZERS.
Abstract: The reception of discrete-time and discrete-level data that has been amplitude modulated onto a pulse train and transmitted over a noisy channel with dispersion has been extensively studied. Among the various receiver structures that have been proposed and analyzed, one that is particularly attractive and of much current interest is that of the decision-feedback equalizer. An upper bound on the true probability of error of a receiver employing decision feedback is derived. The bound is readily evaluated numerically and appears to be reasonably tight for typical channels. Its functional form is simple enough to be useful in developing a general understanding and intuition for error propagation.
Name: ["Duttweiler D.L.", "Mazo J.E.", "Messerschmitt David G."]

Title: KALMAN-TYPE PROCESSING FOR ADAPTIVE ANTENNA ARRAYS.
Abstract: A technique is presented for applying Kalman filtering methods to adaptive array processing. For relatively simple problems (e. g. , small communication arrays) adaptive array control algorithms based on gradient or random search methods yield suitable processing techniques. However, for more complex problems such as the multi-mission RPV (Remotely Piloted Vehicle) command and control system, more sophisticated processing is required. For such applications adaptive processing methods based on Kalman-type (recursive estimation) methods offer important potential advantages. The basic application procedure for adaptive arrays is presented and the simulation of a communication array in an interference environment indicates the effectiveness of the method.
Name: ["Baird Jr. Charles A."]

Title: ASYNCHRONOUS LOGICAL NETS WITH FEEDBACK FOR DYNAMIC SYSTEMS MODELLING.
Abstract: This paper formulates the logical equivalence principle of general form equations to the system of logical ones. Also introduced are Boolean matrices of mathematical operations. Digital logical devices for control systems are discussed.
Name: ["Borkovskiy Boris A.", "Katkov Alexander F.", "Romantsov Vladimir P."]

Title: BIT RATE REDUCTION BY AUTOMATIC ADAPTATION OF QUANTIZER STEP-SIZE IN DPCM SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A DPCM system with adaptive quantization is described. Theoretical considerations on the optimum parameters that determine the quantizer adaptation in order to minimize the quantizing noise are developed. The performance of a 32 kbit/sec computer simulation of such a system is shown and the particular type of output quantizing noise examined. Attention is devoted to subjective evaluation of the output quality, even in presence of channel errors.
Name: ["Castellino P.", "Modena G.", "Nebbia L.", "Scagliola C."]

Title: DIFFERENTIAL GAMES WITH SYSTEM UNCERTAINTY AND IMPERFECT INFORMATION.
Abstract: The solution to the linear differential game with system uncertainty and imperfect information is given. The system uncertainty is assumed contained within a time-invariant parameter vector which is partitioned into two subvectors. The first subvector is known to the pursuer but unknown to the evader. Similarly, the second subvector is known to the evader but unknown to the pursuer. Guaranteed cost strategies are found. A feature of each player's strategy is that it is an adaptive strategy as it includes a parameter adaption procedure to learn the uncertain parameter.
Name: ["Asher Robert B.", "Sims Craig S.", "Sebesta Henry R."]

Title: ENTROPY OF SPEECH SIGNALS AND RATE DISTORTION FUNCTION.
Abstract: Following the results of recent measurements of the amplitude probability densities of continuous band-limited speech signals new mathematical representations are discussed. The differential entropies are derived and estimates of the rate distortion function are given.
Name: ["Wolf Dietrich"]

Title: ON-LINE, DIGITAL PITCH PERIOD EXTRACTOR FOR SPEECH SIGNALS.
Abstract: A method for pitch detection is presented which derives pitch or pitch periods from speech signals in the time domain using a two-step nonrecursive digital filter. First, the higher formants are attenuated by a gap-function low-pass filter; the second step presents a filter whose first zero is situated around F1. The output signal of this filter shows a structure similar to the waveform of the vocal cords with only one significant maximum remaining per pitch period. This maximum is detected and marked a preliminary pitch period limitation. In a final step, these markers are shifted into an optimum-phase position. The method has been run on a computer and has been implemented as a digital hardware device for on-line pitch detection.
Name: ["Hess Wolfgang J."]

Title: MAN-MODEL INTERACTIVE COMPUTER SYSTEM FOR ANALYSIS OF COMPLEX SOCIETAL PROBLEMS.
Abstract: A decision evaluation and conflict resolution system is being developed for eventual use by planning and policy making organizations. The system is being implemented on a portable interactive graphic computer system. The system features the capability of integrating societal system models with models of human judgment and interpersonal conflict. A number of alternative United States energy policies are being evaluated with the system to determine their probable relative impacts upon the U. S. economy and their degree of acceptability among decision makers and the public.
Name: ["Burnett Robert A.", "Dionne Paul J.", "Eschbach Eugene A.", "Reardon William A.", "Miller Jr. L.Charles", "Summars David A."]

Title: COMPUTATIONAL METHOD FOR THE DESIGN OF LINEAR SYSTEMS WHICH INCLUDE A MODEL OF THE HUMAN OPERATOR.
Abstract: A stochastic parameter-optimization procedure is presented for the design of linear systems which include a model of the human operator. The model of the human operator is lumped-parameter and includes a remnant disturbance if desired. Mathematical properties of solutions to novel algebraic equations are derived and are used to construct a computational algorithm. An extensive example of the application of parameter optimization techniques is included.
Name: ["Merriam III C.W."]

Title: ADAPTIVE TIMING RECOVERY IN DIGITAL SYNCHRONOUS DATA RECEIVERS.
Abstract: Synchronous data communication systems with Nyquist signaling or with partial response techniques require at the receiver a precise timing recovery circuit which adjusts the sampling instant in such a way as to minimize the remaining linear disturbances (intersymbol interference introduced by the channel). Previously suggested methods have the disadvantage of requiring knowledge of the input signal on a continuous basis rather than at discrete, symbol-spaced instants only. In order to avoid this drawback, a new, general method for adaptive timing recovery in synchronous data receivers has been developed. Timing information is derived entirely from samples taken at the symbol rate. The new method is thus highly attractive for time-discrete, all-digital receiver structures. The proposed algorithms are simple and economic to implement and convergence is very fast.
Name: ["Mueller Markus", "Mueller Kurt H."]

Title: COMPUTER CLASSIFICATION OF LIVER SCAN DATA.
Abstract: A method is proposed for automatic classification of scintigraphic data of the human liver. Three way classification is carried out into normal, tumor, and cirrhosis categories. A six dimensional pattern vector derived from the scan data is used in the classification program. The results demonstrate the potential applicability of the method in a clinical environment.
Name: ["Jain V.K.", "Meade R.C.", "Madden J.A."]

Title: REDUCTION OF PLANTS COMPLEX MODELS BY IDENTIFICATION TECHNIQUES.
Abstract: A modeling technique which considers a simulated detailed mathematical model as a priori knowledge of a plant is used to obtain an equivalent low order discrete linear model efficient for small variations of the output data collected from the plant, maximum likelihood identification method and hybrid computer to identify parameters and optimize order of the simple model.
Name: ["Malek N.R.Abdel", "Cianciolo T."]

Title: DATA ACQUISITION SYSTEM FOR HEARING DISEASE DETECTION.
Abstract: This paper presents the application of a pseudo-hybrid computer to the detection of hearing diseases in small children. The method is unique, especially in the way the interface is arranged to eliminate noise.
Name: ["Claes W.", "Davis R.G.", "Marren B.M.", "Nero F."]

Title: HYBRID TEST OF AN OPTIMAL DECOUPLING CONTROL ALGORITHM.
Abstract: A method for the on-line design of a control system for multi input-multi output processes, with requirements of optimality and classical figures of merit (settling time, overshoot) is proposed. The main result is that the dynamic behaviour of the outputs can be easily modified even during the on-line control of the process.
Name: ["Descusse J.", "Boumard J.", "Sarlat D.", "Mezencev R."]

Title: ENGLISH LANGUAGE INTERACTION COMPUTER GRAPHICS SYSTEM.
Abstract: A system is discussed for allowing natural language interaction capability on a color computer graphics facility. The system will allow a non-computer oriented operator to construct and manipulate colored two or three-dimensional images through keyboard English conversations with the computer augmented with an electronic sketchpad and a set of variable control dials.
Name: ["Eastman Jeffrey Ford"]

Title: USE OF REGRESSION OPERATOR IN DESIGN OF NONLINEAR DYNAMIC SYSTEMS BY MEANS OF HYBRID COMPUTATION TECHNIQUE.
Abstract: The paper is an attempt to apply the concept of the regression operator in Hilbert space to design and test of dynamic systems. The method of the approximation of a nonlinear regression operator as well as the proofs of the convergence of the method are given. The input and output signals are presented in the forms of series expansions in orthonormal bases. In turn, each component of an output signal is presented in the form of the linear combination of orthonormal polynomials of many variables. It is shown that if the input signal is the gaussian distributed random variable then the Hermitte polynomials can be used to the approximation of the unknown operator of the system. This fact determines the way of the identification of the designed system in the digital part after its modelling in the analog part. The algorithm of identification is hence derived. Random variables generated in the digital part serve as the desired gaussian input signal. The determined approximated operator may be applied to the real system control by means of a digital computer.
Name: ["Szymanski Andrzej"]

Title: FILTERING INERTIAL SYSTEM ERRORS TO IMPROVE TERMINAL SECTOR NAVIGATION.
Abstract: An analysis is given for estimating the inertial measurement unit's error states in an aided terminal guidance mode. Position observations measured by a radar area correlation system and a radar altimeter are processed in an extended Kalman filter to yield the suboptimal estimates of the inertial measurement unit's errors.
Name: ["Pastrick Harold L."]

Title: BIPED GAIT SIMULATION STUDIES.
Abstract: Basic problems of biped gait simulation are considered. The mechanical structure of the biped body is reduced to the mathematically simple inverted pendulum. Simple control laws are formulated and the gait process is analyzed independently for two component motions, viz, lateral and longitudinal. From the mathematical point of view the gait process reduces to the solution of a sequence of second order differential equations. Results of the simulation performed on an analog computer with parallel logic, are presented in the form of time solutions as well as phase-plane trajectories.
Name: ["Morawski Janusz M."]

Title: BLOCK CODING OF CONTROLLABLE BINARY SOURCES FOR DATA COMPRESSION.
Abstract: Code redundancy and compression factors of the inverse of the Shannon-Fano-Huffman-Code are investigated. A flow graph for programming an algorithm due to J. P. M. Schalkwijk and examples with application to data compression are given.
Name: ["Fey Peter"]

Title: HMO, AN INTEGRATED HARDWARE MICROCODE OPTIMIZER.
Abstract: Discussion of an algorithm for optimizing the density and parallelism of microcoded routines in microprogrammable machines. Besides the algorithm itself, the algorithm's uses, design integration problems, architectural requirements, and adaptability to conventional machine characteristics are also discussed and analyzed. Even though a hardware implementation of the algorithm is proposed, the algorithm is viewed as an integral part of the entire microcode generation and usage process, from initial high-level input into a software microcode compiler down to machine-level execution of the resultant microcode on the host machine. It is believed that, by removing much of the traditionally time-consuming and machine-dependent microcode optimization from the software portion of this process, the algorithm can improve the overall process.
Name: ["Bondi James O.", "Stigall Paul D."]

Title: An interactive man-machine approach to the computer logic partitioning problem
Abstract: The problem of partitioning computer logic has been attacked in the past by manual and automatic techniques. We describe an interactive approach which combines aspects of both approaches and creates results which are better than those obtainable by either approach independently. An overview of the system is presented, several algorithms discussed and experimental results are given. ¬© 1974 ACM.
Name: ["Hanan M.", "Mennone A.", "Wolff P.K., Sr."]

Title: Using simulation to evaluate system performance
Abstract: This paper presents some recent results obtained from using simulation to evaluate computer system performance when alternative job priority assignment algorithms are considered. Performance data are given for both individual computing centers and network computers.‚àóA pay-for priority scheduling algorithm for the individual centers is explored and load leveling techniques for transmitting jobs between centers are evaluated. The effects of these algorithms on system performance are demonstrated through the use of a simulation model. ¬© 1974 ACM.
Name: ["Bowdon E.K."]

Title: Simulation system for brain modeling
Abstract: A highly parameterized, general purpose simulation system for brain structures has been coded in FORTRAN. Detailed three-dimensional models involving up to 8,000 neurons and 80,000 synapses can be specified and simulated. Individual model elements are not enumerated. Instead the parameter scheme uses spatial lattices and intersecting probability distributions to position neurons and synapses with any desired degree of precision or randomness. The system has been used to study neural activity in a cerebellar cortex model involving 2,000 neurons and 20,000 synapses and to evaluate an integrated circuit, picture-processing array made of 2,700 logic elements and 5,400 connections. ¬© 1974 E-flow IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Wittie L.D."]

Title: APPLICATION OF PATTERN RECOGNITION TO FLIGHT TEST DATA ANALYSIS.
Abstract: The techniques of pattern recognition are applied to process theoretical and actual flight test trajectory data. The computation is automated so that the results are two-dimensional plots and clusters which permit one to validate analytical trajectory models, detect spurious data, and identify problem areas. Numerical results are presented to illustrate the effects of scaling parameters, eliminating parameters and using different two-dimensional projections.
Name: ["Chew K.", "Campbell D.M.", "O'Dell M.D.", "Vaning W.S."]

Title: IDEA OF CONTROLLED DEVIATION AND ITS USABILITY TO ANALOG MODEL PARAMETERS OPTIMIZATION.
Abstract: A new unimodal, multivariable function minimization method is proposed. A construction of the method takes into account the peculiarities of analog calculation. This feature coupled with good effectiveness and algorithm simplicity recommend the method to the realization of a hybrid automatic optimizer.
Name: ["Galar Roman", "Kasprzak Waclaw", "Piesiak Stanislaw"]

Title: The Microprogrammable Multi-Processor (MMP) system for simultaneous emulation of interoperating computer systems
Source: Proceedings of the Annual International Symposium on Microarchitecture, MICRO
Abstract: A Teleprocessing Design Center (TDC) has been established within the Communications/Automatic Laboratory of the US Army Electronics Command (ECOM) at Fort Monmouth, New Jersey, for the purpose of supporting experimentation in developing and validating Army Tactical Data Systems (ARTADS) configurations. The TDC is collocated within the Communications/Automatic Data Processing Laboratory with the Communications System Design Facility which includes circuit and message switching systems, systems and technical control facilities, and transmission media. The heart of the TDC is the MMP system which will provide the capability of simultaneously emulating up to two interoperating ARTAD systems. This paper describes that system, including the hardware and key software modules, and provides a detailed look at its use in emulating one of the ARTAD systems, namely the Tactical Fire Direction System (TACFIRE). Of particular interest is the system nature of this emulation, since not only the processor itself, but each and every one of the diverse peripheral units will be emulated. ¬© 1974 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Mattson R.", "Salisbury A."]
Affiliations: ['US Army Electronics Commend', 'Army Tactical Data Systems']

Title: An algorithm for the construction of the graphs of organic molecules
Abstract: A description and a formal proof of an efficient computer implemented algorithm for the construction of graphs is presented. This algorithm, which is part of a program for the automated analysis of organic compounds, constructs all of the non-isomorphic, connected multi- graphs based on a given degree sequence of nodes and which arise from a relatively small "catalog" of certain canonical graphs. For the graphs of the more common organic molecules, a catalog of most of the canonical graphs is known, and the algorithm can produce all of the distinct valence isomers of these organic molecules. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Brown H.", "Masinter L."]

Title: Micro control hardware and high level languages interpretor: An attempt of macro supported by firmware
Source: Proceedings of the Annual International Symposium on Microarchitecture, MICRO
Abstract: The aim of this paper is to try and describe a new technique for implementing microprograms to form a dynamic interpretor of macro-languages. It demonstrates the connexion between the control address mechanism in micro-instruction and the structure of a dynamic interpretor. The proposed mechanism, which is like the Eastwood fetch/generator instruction (1), is founded on a microprocedure call generator. The control store and control mechanism of the CPU are split into two specific levels : the first one, MIDEF (MIcroprocedure DEFinition) level is for defining short microprocedures, the second, MICALL (MIcroprocedure CALL) level, for linking these micro procedures together, MICALL being the fetch/generator mechanism. Independence between microprocedures at MIDEF level allows to link microprocedure dynamically at MICALL level in order to interpret directly new MACRO instructions. This paper describes briefly the options that the EPRON (2) project has taken. EPRON being our test-tool for interaction between hard-, firm- and software. ¬© 1974 IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Demarteau J."]

Title: SOME RESULTS ON SOURCE ENCODING COMPLEXITY.
Abstract: Some approaches to encoding time-discrete finite sources are considered. Reliabilities of different schemes vs. decoding complexity are compared. No formal definition of the complexity is given and comparison is rather qualitative. It is shown that there are schemes for which the number of decoding computations per source symbol is upperbounded by a constant, whereas the error probability approaches zero exponentially with block length increasing. For simplicity the binary memoryless source is assumed.
Name: ["Koshelev Valery N."]

Title: COMPARISON OF STABILITY CRITERIA FOR INTERCONNECTED SYSTEMS WITH PULSE FREQUENCY MODULATION.
Abstract: Stability criteria for systems containing an arbitrary number of pulse frequency modulators are considered, which fall under three basic categories, namely, Lyapunov's second method, frequency domain method and a direct method for global finite pulse stability (GFPS) introduced earlier by the authors. The criteria are compared with respect to effectiveness (in terms of size of left bracket parameter- right bracket region sufficient for stability), generality (in terms of classes of applicable systems) and ease of application. The direct GFPS criterion is the simplest to apply and, at the same time, provides bounds on the number of pulses emitted by each modulator. Comparative examples yielded greater stability regions (of parameters) from the direct GFPS criterion than from (optimal application of) a recent frequency domain criterion of A. Kh. Gelig. A criterion based on Lyapunov's second method could provide good stability regions, but is difficult to apply, especially for higher-order systems.
Name: ["Gulcur Halil O.", "Meyer Andrew U."]

Title: The use of simulation and gaming in information systems research
Abstract: Research in management information systems and in information, communication or intelligence systems in general has grown significantly within the past decade. Yet although significant work is evident at both the theoretical level with the development of information economics and statistical decision theory and at the technical level as is evidenced by the development of complex on-line networks and advanced information storage and retrieval systems, little research which has focused upon information systems has utilized gaming and simulation techniques. Such techniques have been used by the authors in a series of related studies into information systems and decision processes. The paper contains two major experimental studies. The first is a series of information economics experiments where discreet event simulation is utilized to estimate the ex ante value of more timely information in a fifteen period decision process which contains four random environmental variables. The ex ante value and the information value which is realizable given the actual decision environment are then used as a standard with which to compare actual, realized information values obtained in controlled experiments. The empirical results obtained include evidence with respect to the value of more timely information, the value of detailed budgetary feedback and the impact of these information differences on learning rates. The second main study described in this paper considers gaming used to analyze an on-llne directive planning system. In this context it is not possible to estimate information value, but experimental data with respect to user attitudes, type and degree of information utilization and the impact of decision approach is obtained. ¬© 1974 E-flow IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Mock T.I.", "Vasarhelyi M.A.", "Fellingham J.C."]

Title: Simulation of computer systems using automatically generated load descriptions
Abstract: A complete description of a computer system must include three groups of components: I. The hardware components 2. The software components (the operating system), and 3. The load components (the stream of tasks to be processed). When computer systems are simulated all of these components are found as features of the simulations. The hardware normally appears as a collection of tables and associated operational data. The operating system appears both as tables and as scheduling or assignment algorithms. The load is represented either as a sequence of requests for service (use of system resources) or as a set of functions which can generate such a sequence of requests. In many applications, the description of the load turns out to be the most difficult task. This paper discusses some techniques and procedures which have been used to automatically generate the required load descriptions. The emphasis is on a request sequence generator which uses data found in a system event trace. One such technique, called trace-drlven modeling, has been implemented at the Purdue University Computing Center. This implementation is discussed and its usefulness and accuracy are illustrated with actual data. ¬© 1974 E-flow IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Schwetman H.D."]

Title: REAL TIME IMAGE REDUNDANCY REDUCTION USING TRANSFORM CODING TECHNIQUES.
Abstract: Several image coding systems based upon transform coding are studied. Analysis and simulation show that in many applications these systems are capable of image coding at about one to two bits per pixel with acceptable image quality and tolerance to channel errors. Simulation studies indicate that a bit rate reduction to about 1. 5 bits/pixel can be obtained for monochrome image transform coding in 16 multiplied by 16 pixel blocks. Color images require about 2. 0 bits/pixel. With standard DPCM systems, monochrome images are coded with 2. 5 to 3. 0 bits/pixel. Implementation studies and tests that have been performed indicate that the systems can be implemented for real time television operation using recently developed technologies.
Name: ["Habibi Ali", "Pratt William K.", "Robinson Guner", "Means Robert", "Whitehouse Harper", "Speiser Jeffrey"]

Title: APL\INFO : A system for automatic documentation
Source: Proceedings of 6th International Conference on APL, APL 1974
Abstract: An experimental system for automatic documentation is presented which allows an easy communication between user and nystem by means oC a sophisticated guary language, together with an high degree of conversationally, permitted by the use of APL.
