The main characteristics of the query language used are: It is a superset of APL, in the sense that it uses a double level (linguistic and metalinguistic) in the request It allows to define a real "search program" defined in terms of logical conditions defined bv the user It allows a search based on koy-vords and/or on keyword forms, holding on account morphological flexions . ¬© 1974 ACM-CONFERENCE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Dellorco P.", "Bartoho L."]

Title: A gradient-regression search procedure for simulation experimentation
Abstract: This paper examines a gradient search procedure for simulation experimentation with constrained systems. This procedure combines gradient search with curvilinear regression in moving toward a constrained optimal solution for a system involving n controllable variables. In a directiondetermining block, at least n+l simulation trials are performed around a current base point to establish an improving direction, Then in a step determining block, t simulation trial s are performed along the improving direction to establish the most favorable step in moving to the next base point. This sequential block process, in which each block is executed in one input to the computer, is repeated until an approximate solution is found which satisfies all system constraints. ¬© 1974 E-flow IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Biles W.E."]

Title: INPUT-OUTPUT STABILITY CRITERIA FOR A BROAD CLASS OF STOCHASTIC NONLINEAR DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS DEFINED BY GREEN'S FUNCTION.
Abstract: This paper deals with the input-output stability of a class of nonlinear distributed systems defined by their Laplace-Green's functions or, similarly from a practical point of view, by their distributed transfer functions. The time-dependent nonlinear feedback element is distributed and bounded by two limiting gains which depend explicitly upon the distributed parameter. These systems are disturbed by a state-and space-dependent Gaussian noise which is added to the input of their linear components. This noise depends explicitly upon the output of the system via its own nonlinear feedback gain. Some input-output stability criteria are stated, which can be considered as being stochastic distributed versions of the circle criterion available for deterministic lumped parameter systems.
Name: ["Jumarie Guy"]

Title: REAL-TIME ADAPTIVE AIR POLLUTION MODELING.
Abstract: The author presents a new model, called the AFT (adaptive-filtering transport) model, for prediction and control of urban SO//2 air concentrations. The airshed is modeled by the pollutant mass conservation equation, a partial differential equation (PDE) in four independent variables. This equation is solved by the method of fractional steps, in which a four-dimensional PDE is split into three successive two-dimensional PDE's and solved numerically by extensions of finite difference techniques. The new feature is an adaptive process noise, in order to take into account uncertainties in the system parameters, incomplete measurements, and approximation errors. An adaptive or self-correcting algorithm, suitable for on-line use, is incorporated into the program to make corrections to the state variable vector and selected model parameters, based on incoming data from monitoring stations.
Name: ["Bankoff S.G.", "Hanzevack Jr. E.L."]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR COMPUTER GUIDANCE OF A MANIPULATOR IN BETWEEN OBSTACLES.
Abstract: A mathematical algorithm is proposed that will generate an incremental motion for each position of the manipulator. Repeated use of this algorithm will automatically direct the mechanical arm (manipulator) to a specified destination avoiding collisions with obstacles.
Name: ["Loeff Luis A.", "Soni A.H."]

Title: USE IN PROBABILISTIC DESIGN OF PROBABILITY CURVES GENERATED BY MAXIMIZING THE SHANNON ENTROPY FUNCTION CONSTRAINED BY MOMENTS.
Abstract: A general algorithm is described for obtaining the maximum entropy distribution constrained by moments in functional form. It is based on Jaynes' principle. The distribution is proposed as a useful tool in probabilistic design. The maximum entropy distribution is generated for a large number of analytical distributions, and compared with the original. The results appear to confirm that it can represent well most populations when four or five moments are used. The maximum entropy distribution is also compared with the Johnson and Pearson empirical distributions. The results are favorable in the two examples given. The practical convenience of the method in probabilistic design is illustrated by an example in structures.
Name: ["Siddall J.N.", "Diab Y."]

Title: THREE MILLION HOURS OF ROBOT FIELD EXPERIENCE.
Abstract: A survey of the advantages obtained by assembly machines that have accumulated over 3 million hours of operation is presented. Consideration is given to the intrinsic and to the logged reliability of a sophisticated, digitally-controlled machine, its field service cost, and the life of such a machine in typical factory environments.
Name: ["Engleberger J.F."]

Title: DYNAMIC OF THE HUMAN KIP-UP MANEUVER.
Abstract: Results of experimental and analytical investigation of a human motion problem are presented. Kip-up maneuvers by a human performer are recorded photographically. A three rigid link model is constructed for the performer using Hanavan's inertia model of a human being. Comparisons of the observed motion with solutions of the mathematical model equations are presented. A ‚Ä≥minimum-time‚Ä≥ performance of the performer is then compared with an approximate analytic solution for the three-link model. Differences between the observed motions and the analytic solutions are discussed. Some changes in the model are suggested.
Name: ["Ghosh T.K.", "Boykin W.H."]

Title: Statistical analysis of discrete-event simulations
Abstract: This paper surveys past and ongoing work by the authors in statistical analysis of simulations. An earlier developed technique for analyzing simulations of GI/G/S queues and Markov chains is shown to apply to discrete-event simulations which can be modeled as regenerative processes. It is possible to address questions of simulation run duration and of starting and stopping simulations because of the existence of a random grouping of observations which produces independent identically distributed blocks in the course of the simulation. This grouping allows one to obtain confidence intervals for a general function of the steady-state distribution of the process being simulated. The technique is illustrated with a simulation of a retail inventory distribution system. In some simulations, more than one random grouping may exist which produce independent identically distributed blocks. In this cas% it is shown that the simulator may choose any such grouping without fear of obtaining less efficient confidence intervals. That is, simulations of the same time duration will produce confidence intervals which are asymptotically the same in length. Finally, approximation techniques are presented which may be appropriate for simulations in which it is not possible to find a random grouping as above. ¬© 1974 E-flow IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Crane M.A.", "Iglehart D.L."]
Affiliations: ['Control Analysis Corporation', ' Department of Operations Research']

Title: SELF-GENERATING ANALYSIS ALGORITHM FOR COMPUTER BASED DESIGN OF MECHANISMS.
Abstract: Describes the classification scheme and analysis algorithms used in a computer-aided design system for planar mechanisms. A rectangular coordinate classification scheme intended for use with a graphic man/computer interface is presented. An iterative solution technique is also discussed and a detailed description of the method of solution equation generation is provided.
Name: ["Reed W.S.", "Garrett R.E."]

Title: AUTOMATIC PARAMETER IDENTIFICATION APPLIED TO A RAILROAD CAR DYNAMIC DRAFT GEAR MODEL.
Abstract: One of the most important components in simulating track-train dynamics is the mathematical model of the connection between two cars, the draft gear-coupler combination. In this paper an automatic parameter identification technique is presented which can be used to generate a nonlinear functional relationship of dynamic draft gear characteristics using experimental data.
Name: ["Ward E.D.", "Leonard R.G."]

Title: EFFICIENT ALGORITHM FOR GENERATION OF SPARSE TOPOLOGICAL MATRICES.
Abstract: A new algorithm for the generation of optimally sparse fundamental circuit and cutset matrices is described. This efficient method is based on Gaussian-Jordan elimination with optimum ordering and the topoloical relation between a fundamental cutset matrix and the incidence matrix.
Name: ["Wang K.U.", "Ko Shang-Bin"]

Title: A stimulus-driven model of concept identification
Abstract: The discrete events assumed to occur in problem solving behavior (where an unpracticed person is trying to identify the rule being used in the binary classification of objects) have been modeled using SNOBOL4. The main assumption of this cognitive simulation is that attention given to unexpected characteristics of succeeding objects drive the behavior of the S (subject). Specifically, the simulated Ss with smaller short-term memories indicated a strong recency effect: Rules represented by values occurring in the last positions in the instance were significantly easier to identify. For the largest memory size used, a significant primacy effect was seen. ¬© 1974 E-flow IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Newsted P.R."]

Title: Spatial Entropy
Abstract: A major problem in information theory concerns the derivation of a continuous measure of entropy from the discrete measure. Many analysts have shown that Shannon's treatment of this problem is incomplete, but few have gone on to rework his analysis. In this paper, it is suggested that a new measure of discrete entropy which incorporates interval size explicitly is required; such a measure is fundamental to geography and this statistic has been called spatial entropy. The use of the measure is first illustrated by application to one‚Äêand two‚Äêdimensional aggregation problems, and then the implications of this statistic for Wilson's entropy‚Äêmaximizing method are traced. Theil's aggregation statistic is reinterpreted in spatial terms, and finally, some heuristics are suggested for the design of real and idealized spatial systems in which entropy is at a maximum. 1974 The Ohio State University
Name: ["Batty M."]

Title: ALTERNATIVE APPROACHES TO INTEGRATED AIRBORNE OMEGA/INERTIAL NAVIGATION.
Abstract: Integrated OMEGA/Inertial navigation systems appear attractive in airborne applications since the excellent short-term accuracy of an inertial navigator is well-complemented by the intermittent availability of bounded, moderately accurate OMEGA position fixes. There are a number of different approaches which can be taken to accomplish the desired system integration; three such approaches are considered. The first involves a straightforward output reset, the second is essentially a Kalman-based variant of rate-aiding and the third involves conventional optimal integration. These schemes are evaluated using models for various navigation system errors to yield predictions of system position and velocity error behavior. Additionally, the schemes are compared on the basis of operational factors such as ease of implementation and computer utilization.
Name: ["Gentry Daniel E.", "D'Appolito Joseph A.", "Kasper Jr. Joseph F."]

Title: FORMULATION OF A DECISION MODEL TO SELECT OPTIMUM CROP PRODUCTION PRACTICES.
Abstract: Concept of crop production optimization is described. A problem is formulated by transforming a set of crop growth equations into constraints for a mathematical program, which also includes operational and resource constraints. An objective function is written for maximizing profit for a single crop. The decision variables are rates and timing of both nitrogen and irrigation applications and harvesting dates. Diagrams demonstrate model building.
Name: ["Jones James W.", "Wensink Robert B.", "Sowell Robert S.", "Hesketh John D."]

Title: An application of parametric time series in simulation modeling
Abstract: A parametric time series model is employed to simulate the number of aircraft present in an air traffic control sector. Borrowing from the work of Box and Jenkins, the identification, parameter estimation and associated tests of adequacy are illustrated using data from a low altitude control sector. The fitted model provides a useful algorithm and reflects the time dependency which exists between the number of aircraft measured in consecutive time periods. The simulation is part of a larger air communications system simulation which is under development. ¬© 1974 E-flow IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Polhemus N.W.", "Hunter I.S."]

Title: Schedule-constrained of scheduling in a multiprogrammed computer system
Abstract: The schedule,constrained job scheduling problem is defined as the problem of deciding what jobs should coexist in the memory of a multiprogrammed computer to insure satisfactory schedule performance and adequate resource utilization. At the present time, the job scheduling function in many multiprogrammed computer systems is being accomplished in a suboptimal manner. In computer installations that must pay strict attention to schedule performance, the scheduling module of the operating system, because it does not consider schedule constraints, cannot be allowed to schedule jobs as they beome available for processing. Instead, human judgment must override the operating system by deciding which jobs should be input to the computer. To solve the schedule-constrained job scheduling problem, the author has developed and tested seven scheduling algorithms using a digital simulation model. ¬© 1974 E-flow IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Cook T.M."]

Title: Classification based on dichotomous and continuous variables
Source: Journal of the American Statistical Association
Abstract: A Bayes procedure for classifying an observation consisting of one dichotomous variable (X) and a continuous vector Y is applied to a model assuming that the conditional distribution of Y given X is normal. The procedure reduces to two linear discriminant functions, one for each value of X. An example utilizing data on critically ill patients is given. Extension to one polytomous variable or several dichotomous variables is discussed. ¬© 1974, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Chang P.C.", "Afifi A.A."]

Title: Fuzzy systems and artificial intelligence
Abstract: Many concepts of problem solving theory are better understood in an abstract algebraic framework which also applies in automata theory. Because many systems of practical interest fall outside the scope of linear theory, it is desirable to enlarge as much as possible the class of systems for which a complete structure theory is available. The fuzzy system approach is presented as a basis for the design of systems far superior in artificial intelligence to those we can conceive today. The concepts of controllability, observability and minimality are developed, and conditions for the realization of an input-output map by such a system are given. Several problems, all directly or indirectly related to fuzzification, arise in considering this broader class of systems. ¬© 1974, MCB UP Limited
Name: ["Negoita C.V.", "Ralescu D.A."]

Title: IEEE CONFERENCE ON DECISION AND CONTROL, 1974, INCLUDING SYMPOSIUM ON ADAPTIVE PROCESSES, 13TH, PROCEEDINGS.
Abstract: The proceedings consists of 172 papers dealing with a wide variety of aspects of learning methods for large scale systems, computational algorithms, applications of systems theory to resource problems, estimation error analysis, digital filtering, adaptive control theory and applications, aerospace applications, optimal control, multilevel world modelling, stochastic systems, linear systems, model reference adaptive systems, control of uncertain systems, mini-max problems and differential games, engineering-economic systems, system identification and simulation, image processing, contributions to systems engineering by women, major decision and control issues in military and air traffic control systems, stochastic control and management science, estimation and identification in power systems, applications of structural modelling, and urban systems applications. Individual papers are indexed separately.
Name: ["Conf"]

Title: FORWARD CONTROL WITH THE IMPULSE CORRECTING FEEDBACK DERIVED FROM THE TIME TREND OF THE OUTPUT DIFFERENCE.
Abstract: The paper presents a control algorithm, designed for technological processes, the dynamic properties of which are mainly defined as dead time delays. It is based on the forward control principle; the control coefficients are optimized by an impulse feedback loop.
Name: ["Zitek Pavel"]

Title: PARAMETER ESTIMATION FOR NONLINEARLY OBSERVED DYNAMIC SYSTEMS: A MODIFIED QUASILINEARIZATION APPROACH.
Abstract: The estimation of parameters and initial states for nonlinearly observed dynamic systems is considered. A Fletcher-Powell deflected gradient search technique is incorporated into the quasilinearization procedure to facilitate direct solution of the nonlinear algebraic system which results when the quasilinearization method is applied to nonlinearly observed dynamic systems. The proposed method requires no matrix inversion. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that the radius of convergence for initial parameter estimates (guesses) with this approach can be much greater than that obtainable utilizing methods which require linearization of the observation equations. The method also is suitable for linear observations. A numerical example is given.
Name: ["Ownby Michael L.", "DiStefano III Joseph J."]

Title: NONLINEAR ADAPTIVE EQUALIZER FOR DATA TRANSMISSION OVER HF CHANNELS.
Abstract: A system is described which consists of a number of cascaded decision-directed equalizers, each one having a different nonlinear characteristic. Received data samples are estimated with respect to a threshold, after part of the intersymbol interference has been subtracted. This threshold is linearly decremented from stage to stage, reaching zero at the final stage. A technique such as this which uses estimates from previous stages also permits the cancellation of intersymbol interference due to pre-echo in the channel. Computer simulations have shown that even for single-stage working, the system can adapt to a wide range of channels, including those with two equal strength multipaths. For a different range of channels, two to seven stages of equalization appear to be optimum.
Name: ["McBride W.J.", "Rosie A.M.", "Monds F.C."]

Title: SAMPLED-DATA APPROACH TO THE SIMULATION OF NONLINEAR NETWORKS.
Abstract: A new technique is presented for the discrete-time simulation of nonlinear networks. The approach involves modeling of the network as a nonlinear flowgraph, and inducing additional state variables to account for the nonlinear elements. Once the complete state-variable description is obtained, a simple recursion process will generate the time-domain solution. This method permits general network models to be incorporated with standard transfer of state-variable models (both continuous- and discrete-time) such that a total system simulation is possible. A detailed example is presented.
Name: ["Vanlandingham H.F.", "Grigsby L.L."]

Title: EFFICIENT USE OF MINI-COMPUTERS IN INDUSTRIAL ROBOT CONTROL.
Abstract: This paper shows how a robot may be modified to allow multiple unit control by a single computer as an alternative to logic control systems.
Name: ["Larcombe M.H.E."]

Title: Fixed-Memory Recursive Filters
Abstract: This correspondence presents three algorithms for computing least-squares estimates based on fixed amounts of data. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Buxbaum P.J."]

Title: PS: A TOOL FOR BUILDING PICTURE-SYSTEM MODELS OF COMPUTER SYSTEMS.
Abstract: PS is a tool for designing computer systems by using picture systems as models. These models are particularly valuable for constructing, debugging, and communicating computer system mechanisms early in the design cycle. A picture-system model of a computer system consists of a picture-set containing a picture for each state of the computer system relevant to the mechanism being modeled, a distinguished initial picture corresponding to the initial state of the computer system, and a set of transitions which defines for each picture the set of pictures which may follow it. The goal of this research is to automate the production and analysis of picture-system models so that these models can be used on a broader basis as a means of communicating computer system mechanisms at various levels of abstraction.
Name: ["Isaacson Portia"]

Title: TECHNIQUE TO IMPROVE THE PERFORMANCE OF A NONLINEAR FILTER WITH AN APPLICATION TO SATELLITE-AIDED AIRCRAFT NAVIGATION.
Abstract: This paper evaluates performance of a filter that transforms nonlinear measurements in the coordinate system of the state before using in the the filter. The bias and computational performance of this mechanization are compared with the conventional extended Kalman (EK) filter. The bias in the EK filter is a function of the covariance of the estimation error, while in the state-coordinate-system (SCS) it depends on variance of the transformed measurement noise, which is independent of the estimation error and depends only on the nonlinearity. Thus when the initial covariance of the state is large, the SCS filter has less bias than the EK filter. This reduction in the bias is achieved at a cost of additional computations required to implement the transformation. The improved performance of the filter due to the coordinate transformation is then demonstrated with an example of satellite-aided aircraft navigation.
Name: ["Joglekar Anil N."]

Title: Approximate evaluation techniques for the single-link and complete-link hierarchical clustering procedures
Source: Journal of the American Statistical Association
Abstract: A technique is presented for testing the hypothesis that a hierarchical sequence of partitions constructed by the single-link or complete-link clustering method could have been obtained because of ‚Äúnoise.‚Äù Two rank orderings of the object pairs are compared. One of the orderings is obtained from the initial proximity values; the second is derived from the levels at which an object pair first appears within a single subset within the hierarchy. The hypothesis that the given set of proximity values have been assigned randomly is tested by referring the Goodman-Kruskal rank correlation y statistic to an approximate permutation distribution. ¬© 1974, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Hubert L."]

Title: Representation of Curved Surfaces by Approximation of Measuring Points. | DARSTELLUNG GEKRUEMMTER FLAECHEN DURCH APPROXIMATION VON MESSPUNKTEN.
Abstract: Milling of curved surfaces on the NC-controlled milling machines is discussed. It is shown that, with the aid of electronic data processing, the design and manufacture of curved surfaces can be automated provided that a mathematical surface representation suitable for computer processing is available. A method is proposed which provides such surface representation by approximation of measured points.
Name: ["Henning Hermann"]

Title: Interconnections for Parallel Memories to Unscramble p-Ordered Vectors
Abstract: Several methods have been considered for storing arrays in a parallel memory system so that various useful partitions of an array can be fetched from the memory with a single access. Some of these methods fetch vectors in an order scrambled from that required for a computation. This paper considers the problem of unscrambling such vectors when the vectors belong to a class called p-ordered vectors. This class of vectors is defined in such a way that elements that should be adjacent in an unscrambled vector are p elements apart in the p-ordered vector. Interconnections are described that can be used to unscramble p-ordered vectors. The usefulness of the interconnections depends on the number of memory modules in the system. Certain advantages result from using a prime number of memory modules. In this case, pairs of interconnections exist that can unscramble p-ordered vectors in a number of steps that grows as the square root of the number of memory modules. Other results are discussed for more general memory sizes. Lower and upper bounds are given for the number of steps to unscramble the worst case vector when a pair of these interconnections is used. An algorithm is given that has produced optimal pairs of interconnections for all sizes of memory that have been tried. The algorithm appears to find optimal pairs for all memory sizes for which the algorithm is applicable, but no proof has yet been found. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Swanson R.C."]
Keywords: ["array storage allocation", "data alignment", "group generators", "illiac iv", "memory interconnections"]

Title: Numerical test of stability of large sparse matrices and dynamical systems
Abstract: The stability of an n-square complex matrix A is determined by the number a = max {Re (a<sub>1</sub>)}, where the a<sub>1</sub> are the eigenvalues. A practical numerical technique is developed for computing the number √¢ of any normal matrix (AA& = A&A). When applied to an arbitrary matrix, the technique yields a number not less than √¢, and hence, if the number is negative, the matrix is stable. The technique is particularly efficient when A is a large sparse matrix. ¬© 1974, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Zakian V.", "Papaconstantinou C."]

Title: NEW ALGORITHM FOR THE INVERSION OF RATIONAL MATRICES.
Abstract: An algorithm is given which primarily depends on the construction of the determinant of a polynomial matrix. The method utilizes manipulations with real numbers only, thus making it more efficient to program the inversion procedure on a digital computer.
Name: ["Emre Erol", "Abdullah Khaldun", "Huseyin Ozay"]

Title: Easily Testable Two-Dimensional Cellular Logic Arrays
Abstract: An algorithm to synthesize two-dimensional AND-EOR arrays is given. The design criterion chosen is to minimize the number of columns in the two-dimensional cellular arrays. It is also shown that AND-EOR arrays, synthesized using the algorithm presented, can be modified such that 2n + 5 test vectors will detect any single fault in the array realizing an n-variable function with only one observable output. Furthermore, this test set is shown to be independent of the function being realized by the cellular array under test. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Saluja K.K.", "Reddy S.M."]
Keywords: ["cellular arrays", "controllable inputs", "fault detection", "minimization algorithms for cellular arrays", "single faults"]

Title: Simulation of Speech Signals. | SIMULATION VON SPRACHSIGNALEN.
Abstract: It is shown that Gaussian processes can be combined in such a way that a stochastic process is generated which shows significant properties of real speech signals. The one- and two-dimensional amplitude distribution densities as well as the autocorrelation function are discussed. The process is well suited for simulating speech signals in communication systems and can easily be realized in hardware.
Name: ["Brehm Helmut", "Juengst Ernst Werner", "Wolf Dietrich"]

Title: A model for visual shape recognition
Abstract: Suggests that many examples of stimulus equivalence may be explained by angle and length-ratio feature detectors whose outputs are generalized over the visual field. Problems of interference between a number of figures simultaneously present, and of localizing the figure that is being recognized, require a mechanism of selective attention. This could involve the temporal segregation of signals from different figures as they pass through the recognition circuits. The figure to which attention is directed feeds a signal back to an earlier stage to enhance the corresponding input before the generalization process deprives it of its spatial information. (22 ref) (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2006 APA, all rights reserved). ¬© 1974 American Psychological Association.
Name: ["Milner P.M."]
Keywords: ["model of visual shape recognition", "recognition suggests", "stimulus equivalence", "examples stimulus", "model visual"]

Title: Neuron system for comparing images and standards invariantly to affined transformations (Russian)
Abstract: A multilayer neuron system is considered with the help of which the similarity between the standard and image can be evaluated invariantly to affinic transformations. The comparison is carried out at the characteristic points, distinguished on detector nets. The evaluation of similarity degree, interlocation, orientation and the scale of the standard and image, results from the passing of the information concerning the input signal through normalizing neuron nets, whose transmitting functions are determined. Nets constituting the system consist of formal neurons of the simplest types. The system belongs to the class of the systems of parallel action, i.e., the result is produced immediately after the image appears. Considerations are presented concerning its possible  learning.
Name: ["Gutman S.R."]

Title: LARGE TIME BANDWIDTH PRODUCT PROGRAMMABLE SAW PSK MATCHED FILTER MODULE.
Abstract: A description is given of the theory and design of an inherently large time bandwidth (TB) product ( greater than 1000) programmable Surface Acoustic Wave (SAW) matched filter module with the capability of processing signals considerably longer than those accommodated in existing 128 tap programmable analogue matched filters (PAMF's) alone. The module employs serial-parallel signal processing techniques, segmenting a continuous long PN-PSK code into short blocks for recognition in a SAW PAMF, which is reprogrammed as each individual code segment enters it. The resulting series of correlation peaks is coherently summed in a recirculating delay line integrator (RDLI). Also given is a theoretical analysis of the RDLI performance, presenting computer derived results to illustrate the dependence of performance both on number of recirculations and number of transducer periods. A description is given of the performance of a prototype module capable of processing PSK coded sequences of lengths up to 2047 chips with 5 MHz bandwidth.
Name: ["Grant P.M.", "Brown J.", "Collins J.H."]

Title: LEARNING, PREDICTION AND DECISION-MAKING IN URBAN SYSTEMS ANALYSIS.
Abstract: The study of urban systems involves learning, prediction and decision-making. This paper introduces learning automaton concept for urban modeling, and discusses an urban control system which makes use of information processing feedback for decision-making and mathematical models for learning and prediction.
Name: ["Tou Julius T."]

Title: DYNAMICAL MODEL OF CONFLICT - 1, 2.
Abstract: Problems of selecting and quantifying the variables for a socio-political model, and interactions between that and an economics model are discussed. Optimal control theory is invoked to see if decision-rules can be synthesized that will allow regions A and B to satisfy their goals while keeping the index of hostility low. This is clearly a constrained optimization problem, and any success will indicate that the methods of Systems Science are fertile material for the difficult problems raised by the human control of man. Functions, diagrams, and curves illustrate analysis.
Name: ["Noton Maxwell", "Charlwood F.J.", "Edmead F.", "Janes F.R.", "M'Pherson P.K.", "Mitchell C.R."]

Title: USE OF A GENERAL-PURPOSE TIME-SHARED COMPUTER IN ACCELERATOR CONTROL.
Abstract: A general purpose real-time data acquisition and control system implemented on a PDP-10 time shared computer and interfaced to devices via PDP-8 peripheral processors and a serial transmission scheme has been constructed. The design objectives of Fortran coded time-shared access to the accelerator have been achieved under the manufacturer's monitor with the addition only of shareable device handlers. The time-sharing monitor has allowed the development and operation of alternative control systems in parallel with continued use of an earlier system. Program development has been facilitated by the convenient access provided by the operating system and the multiple terminals available for programming and testing.
Name: ["Barton M.Q.", "Culwick B.B.", "Curtiss J.A.", "Dabrowski J.J.", "Frankel R.S.", "Harrison W.E.", "Martin F.R.", "Smith J.D.", "Warkentien R.J.", "Weitman I."]

Title: Optimal scheduling of independent tasks on heterogeneous computing systems
Source: Proceedings of the 1974 Annual ACM Conference/Annual Meeting, ACM 1974
Abstract: In this paper, the problem of optimal scheduling of independent tasks on heterogeneous computing systems is considered. Optimal scheduling algorithms which produce preemptive schedules with minimal completion times and non-preemptive schedules with minimal mean flow times are described. A bound on mean flow times also provides us with information concerning the relative merit of different multiprocessor systems. ¬© 1974 ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Liu J.W.S.", "Yang A.-T."]
Keywords: ["multiprocessor systems", "preemptive scheduling algorithms", "optimal scheduling", "scheduling independent", "tasks heterogeneous"]
Affiliations: [' University of Illinois', ' Advanced Manufacturing Development Group']

Title: Sequences of similarity judgments as time series
Abstract: Sequences of similarity judgments made to pairs of geometrical patterns with three variable elements were obtained from 22 subjects. Each subject made 100 judgments to a series which embodied random input, step transitions and impulse shifts. Three different instructions concerning the use of information from previous trials were used. Time series analyses gave linear transfer function coefficients whose ratios reflected the strategy employed by a subject. Evidence of local nonstationarity in the response gain functions is examined. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Gregson R.A.M."]

Title: Statistical Method for the Prediction of Matching Results in Spectral File Searching
Abstract: In file search techniques, the distribution of mismatches quantitatively measures the fit of a particular unknown against a given library. A simple theoretical method is developed to predict, a priori, this distribution. With this procedure, for any unknown code and library, the mean number of mismatches can be calculated exactly. For a given library and coding scheme, the mismatch distribution for most unknown codes closely follows a common curve which is easily calculated from statistical properties of the library. When this common curve is normalized to a constant mean, the observed matching behavior is well predicted. The theory should permit the user to more clearly assess the effects of errors on file search performance and suggest techniques by which recognition performance may be optimized. ¬© 1974, American Chemical Society. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Grotch S.L."]

Title: Apparatus for studying bisensory learning rates in man/machine systems
Abstract: An apparatus for studying learning rates in a simulated industrial or machine control environment is described. Four channels of signals are produced which activate either a light source, dials (meters), a vibrotactile unit, or all of these displays in combination on each channel. Input to the displays is by tape recorded signals of varying intensities. The occurrence of a stimulus signal and the response to it are recorded on a multiple channel event‚Äêrecorder. The apparatus is intended to facilitate research into the bisensory presentation of signals. 1974 Australian Psychological Society
Name: ["Morris J.L.", "Diespecker D.D."]

Title: TRANSFORMATIONS AND INFERENCE OF TREE GRAMMARS FOR SYNTACTIC PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: The authors present an extension of their work (see Engineering Index 1974 abstract 052281) employing tree systems for syntactic pattern recognition. A model for tree transformational grammar and an inference algorithm for tree grammars are presented. Their applications to syntactic pattern recognition are briefly discussed.
Name: ["Bhargava B.K.", "Fu K.S."]

Title: SELF-INTERFERENCE, NATURAL CODES AND DECODING ALGORITHMS.
Source: IEEE Electron and Aerosp Syst Conv (EASCON '74), Rec
Abstract: The application of probabilistic decoding algorithms to the problem of intersymbol interference is presented. The channel or equipment generated intersymbol interference is modeled by a natural tree code of constraint length equivalent to the time dispersion in baud intervals. The Viterbi algorithm can then be used as a maximum likelihood decision processor. Emphasis is also given to ancillary modem functions which must perform in a severe self-interfering environment, for instance, modulation, channel adaption, synchronization, diversity, etc. This approach can safeguard the performance available if no intersymbol interference was generated.
Name: ["Goutmann Michel M."]

Title: RANDOM SIGNAL FLAW DETECTION.
Abstract: A random signal flaw detection technique is described which provides an increase in sensitivity of several orders of magnitude compared to conventional pulse echo detection systems. The increased sensitivity may be conveniently exchanged for increased range since the random signal system does not suffer the range ambiguity problems common to systems which transmit coherent signals. The system uses a random signal correlation and time integration to realize an enhancement of the signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 10,000. Experimental results demonstrate that the range resolution of the random signal system is independent of signal duration, permitting operation with a peak-to-average power ratio close to unity. Data is also presented on the sensitivity of the system showing that irregularities far smaller than the resolution limit of the system are easily detected.
Name: ["Newhouse V.L.", "Furgason E.S.", "Bilgutay N.M.", "Cooper G.R."]

Title: REGULAR DECOMPOSITION AND PICTURE STRUCTURE.
Abstract: This paper describes the recursive partitioning and accessing of two-dimensional scene data. The regular decomposition defines successive quadrants of either the entire picture or a previous picture quandrant, and a four-successor tree results. Experiments using decimal encodings of tree elements for computer graphics display generation and for interaction with a complex scene shown on a video terminal are discussed here and the capability of the technique for representing picture structure is explored.
Name: ["Klinger Allen"]

Title: ON THE INFERENCE OF TREE GRAMMARS FOR SYNTACTIC PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: An algorithm for the inference of tree grammars from sample tree structures is presented. The algorithm, which operates on one pattern tree at a time, is divided in three parts. The first part produces an initial tree grammar capable of generating only the input pattern. In the second part the grammar is generalized by taking into account regularity and self-embedding. In the third part the grammar is simplified by merging equivalent productions. The parsing properties of the resulting grammar are also considered.
Name: ["Gonzalez R.C.", "Thomason M.G."]

Title: APPROACH TO OPTIMIZATION OF HORIZONTAL MICROPROGRAMS.
Abstract: Problems involved in optimization of horizontal microprograms are described. Existing techniques are applied to detect microprogram paralellism in a sequential source microprogram to allow subsequent optimization of the microprogram in a horizontal format. An algorithm for optiizationof horizontal microprograms is derived. An upper bound for microprogram execution time is determined. The results derived in this paper are very general so that they are applicable to any machine with a horizontal microinstruction format (including a vertical format which is a special case of a horizontal format). An example is given to illustrate the algorithm.
Name: ["Tsuchiya M.", "Gonzalez Jr. M.J."]

Title: BOUNDS AND APPROXIMATIONS FOR ERROR PROBABILITIES IN CHARACTER RECOGNITION.
Abstract: The use of Bayes decision functions is investigated for computer character recognition. Bounds for P//e in noncontextual and contextual character recognition have been obtained. In the case where no context is used, the bounds obtained are reasonably tight and easy to compute. For contextual character recognition, the goodness of the bounds cannot be verified because of the fact that P//e is too complicated to compute. As to the problem whether the use of context can reduce the error probability, the answer remains unknown. However, it can be shown that if the Markov chain is nonstationary, some indications can be found that reduction of P//e by using context is possible. The error bounds obtained in this paper can be used in both analysis and design of character recognition systems. For a given recognition system, those upper bounds and arithmetic means may be used as approximations for the corresponding average error probabilities. On the other hand, if a recognition system is to be designed with a prescribed precision, then the upper bounds may be used for feature selections, in determining whether or not the given requirement is feasible.
Name: ["Lee Elisa T."]

Title: MICROPROGRAMMED STORAGE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM.
Abstract: The development of a storage management scheme for MEMBERS, an emulated stack machine incorporating a virtual store and paging, is described. The approach used employs an analog of the 'working set' concept. The use of microprogramming for the implementation of the storage management system is discussed and some preliminary estimates of its performance are given.
Name: ["Macres P.", "Coulouris G.F."]

Title: PROPORTIONAL-INTEGRAL DERIVATIVE REALISATION OF OPTIMAL LINEAR-QUADRATIC REGULATORS.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: A new method is presented for the realization of optimal linear-quadratic regulators, for linear time-invariant systems, using the concept of proportional-integral derivative (p. i. d. ) feedback. It is shown that an optimum complete-state-feedback regulator-system response can be alternatively obtained with incomplete feedback, by introducing the derivative-control action. Considering also the integral feedback, needed to cancel the unknown input disturbances, the method can be viewed as a design method for a class of optimal multivariable p. i. d. controllers with a prescribed closed-loop system response. The paper presents an analytical derivation and discusses the properties of such controllers. An illustrative numerical example is also included.
Name: ["Calovic M.S.", "Cuk N.M."]

Title: ACCELERATED FRANK - WOLFE ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: A class of iterative procedures is presented, called accelerated Frank - Wolfe algorithms. It is shown that a subclass, namely the nontrivial proper algorithms, is of special interest. An algorithm parametrized by an integer q is exhibited and it is then seen that for every q greater than 0, the algorithm is a nontrivial proper accelerated Frank - Wolfe algorithm.
Name: ["Meyer Gerald G.L."]

Title: Development of New Estimation Algorithms by Innovations Analysis and Shift-Invariance Properties
Abstract: It is shown how certain innovations decompositions can be used to obtain an alternative derivation of some new estimating algorithms, based on Chandrasekhar-type equation. Such equations were originally obtained in radiative-transfer theory by using some invariance principles due to Ambartsumian and Chandrasekhar. Stationary processes have a natural shift invariance, but we show here how state-space descriptions can be used to bring out such invariances for nonstationary processes generated as the response to white noise of constant-parameter state space models. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Sidhu G.S.", "Kailath T."]

Title: PROPERTIES OF BASIC NETWORK QUANTITIES AND ESTIMATION OF THEIR PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTIONS.
Abstract: Basic network quantities phi are defined, and their relation to flow, tension and guage is clarified. When intervals I(e) are subject to random variation, phi becomes a random variable whose distribution F// phi ( theta ) is difficult to determine in general due to cutset or path correlation even when intervals are independent of each other. Under independence assumption of intervals I(e), estimation techniques F// phi ( theta ) by means of opening, shortening and duplication of edges are developed.
Name: ["Onaga Kenji"]

Title: PROBLEM SOLVING: MARKOV CHAIN METHOD.
Abstract: It is explained how the theory of Markov chains aids in analyzing both short-term and long-run behavior of various systems, and, in turn, facilitates decision making and planning. An example problem demonstrates how the method is applied and the kind of results that can be expected.
Name: ["Feder Paul I."]

Title: On the Modeling of Demand Paging Algorithms by Finite Automata
Abstract: Two finite automata are devised for modeling two classes of demand paging algorithms. The first one of one input and three outputs models the class of algorithms with a constant amount of allocated space. The second one of one input and six outputs models the class of algorithms with a variable amount of allocated space. Some evaluation techniques are developed following each model. The memory states of the first class algorithm with the Least Recently Used (LRU) replacement policy and the working set model of the second class are recursively defined by strings of the loaded pages. The adopted replacement policy and the state string updating procedure are imbedded in the recursive definition of memory states. Properties of some algorithms are developed to fit the finiteness assumption of a reference string. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Yang C.C."]
Keywords: ["demand paging algorithm", "finite automaton", "least recently used replacement policy", "memory management", "missing-page rate"]

Title: The caret functions: Efficient algorithms for tha scans and reductions of sight boolean functions
Source: Proceedings of 6th International Conference on APL, APL 1974
Abstract: This paper describes an efficient algorithm for the APL scans for eight Boolean functions, those whose symbols employ the caret in some orientation. The APL reduction function for each can be derived from the scan algorithm. ¬© 1974 ACM-CONFERENCE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["McDonnell E.E."]

Title: An Algorithin for Estimating a Portion of the State Vector
Abstract: An algorithm is developed for estimating a portion of the state of a linear dynamical system. The dimension of the filter used in the estimation procedure may be considerably smaller than the dimension of a Kalman filter used to estimate the entire state vector. Thus, an on line computational advantage is achieved. The savings may be significant if the dimension of the segment of the state vector which is of interest is much smaller than the dimension of the entire state vector. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Sims C.S."]

Title: BINARY TOEPLITZ-KRONECKER TRANSFORMS AND THEIR APPLICATIONS.
Abstract: Two binary orthonormal Toeplitz kernels of order two and four binary orthonormal Toeplitz kernels of order four exist. Their inverses also belong to these groups of two and four kernels, respectively. A large number of binary orthonormal transforms can be formed by Kronecker products of these Toeplitz kernels. Fast computational algorithms exist for all these transforms based on the fact that they are derived by Kronecker products of Toeplitz kernels. These algorithms lend easily to hardware implementation with the feature of modular assembly such that when one module is replaced by another, a different Toeplitz-Kronecker transform is obtained. This feature is exploited for the programmed transform domain secrecy coding schemes.
Name: ["Moharir P.S."]

Title: Arbitrary pole placement with limited number of inputs and outputs
Source: Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement and Control, Transactions of the ASME
Abstract: In controller design problems, the quantitative description of the desired controlled system behavior is often given by specifying the closed loop poles. An output-variable feedback control policy for a linear system of order n, with m outputs and p inputs is described by u = ‚àí Gy. Matrix G contains p √ó m parameters which may be used to dictate the locations of the closed loop poles. The limiting condition for arbitrary pole placement, without some form of state estimation, is p √ó m = n since the p √ó m independent controller parameters may be used to specify the n poles. However, there is no systematic procedure for the design of controllers subject to limiting condition. In this paper, a technique based on modal system description is used to design static output-variable feedback controllers with limited number of inputs and outputs. It u shown that arbitrary closed loop pole placement is possible if p + m ‚â• n + 1 for sufficiently well coupled systems. ¬© 1974 by ASME.
Name: ["Loscutoff W.V."]

Title: SCOPE 3HM, a High Performance System for Time Critical Simulations. | [SCOPE 3-HM, EIN HOCHLEISTUNGSSYSTEM FUER ZEITKRITISCHE SIMULATIONEN.]
Abstract: Complex time critical simulations require high performance digital computing systems in order to satisfy the response time needs of the real-time programs for a multiple of concurrent users. This paper discusses both the hardware and software components of the time critical system SCOPE 3 HM that has been developed by Control Data for the CD 6000/CYBER 70 computer line.
Name: ["Loens K.", "Weigl J."]

Title: Three-dimensional displays using computer-generated holograms
Abstract: A hologram of a three-dimensional object is synthesized by a computer using the technique of holographic stereograms. A sequence of perspective views of an object is calculated and their Fourier transform holograms are synthesized by a computer. Each hologram is arranged in the order of the view points to produce the final composite hologram. The experimental reconstruction of the three-dimensional object can be successfully performed. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Yatagai T."]
Affiliations: ['The Institute of Physical and Chemical Research']

Title: Algorithm of the Newton - Rafson Method for Solving Nodal Voltage Equations in an Inverted Form. | ALGORITM METODA N'YUTONA-RAFSONA DLYA RESHENIYA URAVNENII UZLOVYKH NAPRYAZHENII V OBRASHCHENNOI FORME.
Source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenij i Energeticheskikh Ob''edinenij Sng. Energetika
Abstract: In determining flow distribution in electric networks, the use of the Newton - Rafson method for solving equations of nodal voltages in an inverted form is proposed. To reduce the required volume of computer memory, it is proposed to solve a system of linear equations equivalent to the initial one, during each iteration, with little-filled matrix of coefficients. The possibility of utilizing minimization of the norm of the vector-function of capacity disbalances in the nodes, by using the linear search method of equation solving based on Fibronacci numbers, is considered.
Name: ["Manusov V.Z.", "Lykin A.V.", "Sidorkin Yu.M."]

Title: Process Computer in Charge of Parcel Distribution and Sorting Systems. | [PROZESSRECHNEREINSATZ BEI PAKETVERTEILANLAGEN.]
Abstract: The duties performed by a process computer in a parcel distribution and sorting system are described by way of example of a destination control. The necessary flexibility in assigning the destination coding to the various discharge points can only be implemented with a computer. The structure of the program system specially developed for this purpose renders the software independent of the mechanical construction and configuration of the distribution routes.
Name: ["Deschner Wolfgang", "Optiz Werner"]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR THE COMPUTATION OF OPTIMUM-LAG SPIKING FILTERS.
Abstract: An algorithm is derived for the calculation of digital filters which perform approximate deconvolution in the least squares sense together with optimum lag between the first sample of the input signal and the position of the spike in the output array. The algorithm is based on the Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization technique especially adapted to problems that can be formulated by means of a rectangular cyclic coefficient matrix such as is the case with discrete convolution. This technique makes it possible to determine the optimum spike position as soon as the orthogonalization has been performed, without having to calculate filters and actual outputs. The algorithm performs fewer arithmetic operations than conventional techniques and therefore needs less computer time, as is shown by means of numerical examples.
Name: ["DeMeersman Roger", "De Voogd Nicholas"]

Title: DIGITAL COMPUTER SYNTHESIS OF OPTIMAL CONTROL ALGORITHMS FOR MULTIVARIABLE PLANTS.
Abstract: Computer-sided analytic design of controllers for multivariable plants is considered, and a flow diagram of the algorithm, as well as results of optimization of a chemical engineering process, are presented.
Name: ["Salyga V.I.", "Domrin V.D.", "Gorodis'ka V.O."]

Title: Approximations to stochastic programs with complete fixed recourse
Abstract: The probability distribution of the data entering a recourse problem is replaced by finite discrete distributions. It is proved that the convergence of the objective functions of the approximating problems to that one of the original problem can be achieved by choosing the discrete distributions in quite a natural way. For bounded feasible sets this implies the convergence of the optimal values. Finally some error bounds are derived. ¬© 1974 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Kall P."]
Affiliations: [' und mathematische Methoden der Wirtschaftswissenschaften der Universit√§t Z√ºrich']

Title: Linear scale-factor error and optimum filter bandwidth for correlation accuracy
Abstract: Theoretical results are presented for the effect of linear scale factor on the alignment accuracy of two 1-dimensional random signals. For the low-signal/noise-ratio Gaussian correlation function, the optimum resolution is obtained as T|Œµ|/‚àö6, where T is the map length and Œµ is the fractional scale-factor error. ¬© 1974, The Institution of Electrical Engineers. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Webber R.F.", "Delashm W.H."]
Keywords: ["correlation methods", "filtering and prediction theory", "correlation accuracy", "gaussian correlation", "bandwidth correlation"]

Title: Separating Bias and State Estimates in a Recursive Second-Order Filter
Abstract: When recursively estimating the state of a nonlinear process using a second-order filter to process data from many sensors, the method of augmenting the state vector with those sensor systematic errors for which estimates are desired can result in a new vector of extremely large dimension. To avoid the computational problems arising from operations with large dimension matrices it is desirable to decouple the state and systematic error estimation. An efficient method of generating the estimates separately has been derived for the linear filter [1]. For the second-order filter [2] the separation can also be accomplished although unless the observation model is linear, the estimates are coupled during the discrete update stage of the two stage filter. If the observation model is linear, the estimates are completely decoupled just as in the linear filter. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Shreve E.L.", "Hedrick W.R."]

Title: An Identification Procedure for Discrete Multivariable Systems
Abstract: A new procedure is presented for the identification of discrete linear multivariable systems. Using Lyapunov's direct method the asymptotic stability of the overall system is established when the inputs are sufficiently general. It is shown that the procedure may also be extended for the identification of a certain class of nonlinear systems. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Kudva P.", "Narendra K.S."]

Title: ANALYSIS OF A CLASS OF NONLINEAR TIME-VARYING DISCRETE SYSTEMS USING MULTIDIMENSIONAL PARAMETRIC Z-TRANSFER FUNCTIONS.
Source: Proceedings of the Institution of Electrical Engineers
Abstract: A method of analyzing a class of nonlinear time-varying discrete systems having polynomial-type nonlinearities is presented. The analysis makes use of Volterra-series representation and multidimensional parametric z-transfer functions. The method is further extended to determine the output response between sampling instants through the use of multidimensional parametric modified z-transfer functions. The terminal-state theorems for multidimensional parametric z transforms are presented. This new method of analysis is applied, for illustration, to a practical time-varying discrete system involving a nonlinear feedback element.
Name: ["Bansal V.S.", "Mali S.L."]

Title: Model Reference Adaptive Control with an Augmented Error Signal
Abstract: It is shown how globally stable model reference adaptive control systems may be designed when one has access to only the plant's input and output signals. Controllers for single input-single output, nonlinear, nonautonomous plants are developed based on Lyapunov's direct method and the Meyer-Kalman-Yacubovich lemma. Derivatives of the plant output are not required, but are replaced by filtered derivative signals. An augmented error signal replaces the error normally used, which is defined as the difference between the model and plant outputs. However, global stability is assured in the sense that the normally used error signal approaches zero asymptotically. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Monopoli R.V."]

Title: Improvement of System Response by Reducing Quantization Error Through Adaptive Sampling
Abstract: The employment of quantization in a control system can lead to the introduction of error in the output. This correspondence presents a method for reducing the quantization error by the use of adaptive sampling. An example is provided to fully illustrate the application of the method and to demonstrate the output error reduction. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["McDaniel W.L., Jr.", "Bennett W.E."]
Affiliations: [' Mississippi State University', ' Virginia Polytechnic Institute']

Title: Adaptive control using stochastic approximation
Abstract: Adaptive control of systems with uncertainty can be implemented without complete identification of the plant if the cost function is measured continuously and the parameters of the controller are adjusted, using an efficient gradient method, to obtain optimum performance. As, in practice, only noisy measurements of the cost function are available, one has to use stochastic gradient methods. In this paper some efficient stochastic approximation algorithms are proposed for adaptive control. ¬© 1975 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.
Name: ["Sinha N.K.", "Prasad T."]

Title: Asynchronous Control Arrays
Abstract: This paper introduces a class of programmable cellular arrays, called control arrays, and presents a technique for programming these arrays to realize asynchronous control systems. Control arrays are two-dimensional uniform networks composed of a collection of identical cells that can be independently programmed to one of two internal states. A control system is a device that controls one or more operations by means of initiation and termination signals that are transmitted through bidirectional control links. A control system model is developed by augmenting the marked graph model in order to represent constraints on the generation of these control signals. Finally, an array synthesis procedure for realizing control systems with control arrays is presented. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Jump J.R."]
Keywords: ["asynchronous control systems", "concurrent operations", "control structure", "marked graph", "programmable cellular array"]

Title: Comparing complexity classes
Source: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: Complexity classes defined by time-bounded and space-bounded Turing acceptors are studied in order to learn more about the cost of deterministic simulation of nondeterministic processes and about time-space tradeoffs. Here complexity classes are compared by means of reducibilities and class-complete sets. The classes studied are defined by bounds of the order n, n<sup>k</sup>, 2<sup>n</sup>, 2<sup>n</sup>. The results do not establish the existence of possible relationships between these classes; rather, they show the consequences of such relationships, in some cases offering circumstantial evidence that these relationships, do not hold and that certain pairs of classes are set-theoretically incomparable. ¬© 1974 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Book R.V."]

Title: The Effects of Races, Delays, and Delay Faults on Test Generation
Abstract: Test sequences constructed by most test generation procedures often create time dependent results when applied to a circuit. These dependencies often invalidate the test. The main cause for this situation is that the test generation procedures and circuit models employed do not take into account many aspects of delay associated with a circuit. In this paper we present modeling techniques to be used by conventional test generation procedures to alleviate some of these problems. These models include the cases of equal, unequal and ambiguous delay values. Both inertial and transport delays are considered. Both static and dynamic output behavior is studied, though we restrict inputs to fundamental mode operation. Finally, a new type of fault, called a delay fault, is introduced, and a model developed so that a test to detect this class of fault can be generated via conventional test generation techniques. In summary, this paper attempts to outline procedures and identify problem areas so that test generation is more of a science rather than a hit and miss process, and so that the correctness of results need not always be verified via simulation or physical fault injection. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Breuer M.A."]
Affiliations: [' University of Southern California', 'Hughes Aircraft Company']

Title: METHODS OF SCHEDULE THEORY IN TECHNOLOGICAL CHECKING PROBLEMS.
Abstract: An examination is made of the travelling-salesman problem for the case in which the salesman's travelling time is limited, and less than the length of the minimum cycle. His route is to include the maximum possible number of cities. A branch-and-bound algorithm is proposed for solving the problem.
Name: ["Alekseyeva S.M."]

Title: THEORETICAL AND EXPERIMENTAL INVESTIGATION OF A MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD RECEIVER.
Abstract: Approximate expressions are derived for the detection characteristics of a quasi-deterministic signal and for estimates of its unknown, nonenergy parameters. Experimental results of a verification of the derived relations are given.
Name: ["Marshakov V.K.", "Trifonov A.P."]

Title: SIMPLEX ALGORITHM ON A LINEAR GRAPH - A UNIFIED VIEW OF THE EXTREMAL PATH AND CUTSET PROBLEMS ON A GRAPH.
Abstract: The problem of obtaining the length of a path between a specific pair of nodes on a graph or minmax values of cutset is interesting by itself, but it is a very important problem because it appears as a subproblem for various others. As a solution to this problem, a graphic approach based on labeling method and an algebraic approach represented by linear programming (LP) have been used. In this paper, the above problem is formulated as LP by using Kirchhoff's law represented by fundamental cutset matrix or fundamental loop matrix of a graph, and a new graphic approach having one-to-one correspondence with the simplex method is suggested. It is shown that the problem can be treated in a unified manner. It is further shown that the concepts of base, axis transformation, duality, degeneracy in the simplex method can be related to graph theory.
Name: ["Goto Satoshi", "Ohtsuki Tatsuo"]

Title: LAMP: System Description
Abstract: A general description of the Logic Analyzer for Maintenance Planning (LAMP) system is presented. LAMP is a digital‚Äêlogic simulation and analysis system used for logic‚Äêdesign verification, for generation and evaluation of fault‚Äêdetection and diagnostic tests, and for generation of the trouble‚Äêlocation manual (or fault dictionary) data. It is implemented on the IBM 360/370 TSS and OS machines (for both interactive and batch operations), and has been in active use at Bell Laboratories in the development of electronic switching systems, data set facilities, transmission equipment, and advanced integrated circuit technologies. ¬© 1974 The Bell System Technical Journal
Name: ["Chang H.Y.", "Smith G.W., Jr.", "Walford R.B."]

Title: On the selection of secondary indexes
Source: Proceedings of the 1974 Annual ACM Conference, ACM 1974
Abstract: The selection of secondary indexes to use for speeding up the access to information is one of the key problems in data organization. While in general, the provision of indexes facilitate data retrieval, we are also expected to pay a certain amount of various costs. Therefore, the gains and costs to index an attribute or field must be analyzed on individual basis. Lumi and King<sup>2</sup> in their papers, analyzed the problem of single attribute indexes with maintenance. Stonebraker<sup>3</sup> analyzed a similar problem allowing the indexes to be combined, but taking into consideration only retrieval time. Here we would like to follow the approach of Lum and King but propose a much simpler version which can be used as a rule of thumb for index selection. 1974 ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Lum V.Y."]

Title: PHONETIC TO GRAPHEMIC TRANSFORMATION BY USE OF A STACK PROCEDURE.
Abstract: The problem of establishing the graphemic form of machine-derived phonetic strings is considered in the context of continuous speech recognition. The derived transcriptions processed are of sentence length and contain substitutions, insertions, and omissions introduced by classification and segmentation stages as well as free variation by the speaker. Translation is formulated in terms of the heuristic development of a phonetic path through a finite directed graph specified by the sublanguage used. A left-to-right translation procedure based on the stack algorithm is described and some qualitative results from a software implementation presented. In the algorithm, search at the phonetic level is guided by an incremented function of the log-likelihood of the contaminated phonetic sequence given a form of the hypothesized transcription.
Name: ["Rabinowitz Arthur S."]

Title: The application of artificial intelligence techniques to biologic cell identification
Abstract: An interactive system for measuring and classifying cells is discussed. Techniques developed in several artificial intelligence systems are used to provide for a computer controlled microscope and peripheral hardware a language and control mechanism to permit the interactive description of cell models. In particular, the system will initially be applied to the analysis of bone marrow smears. An example is given to illustrate the descriptive modeling capability.
Name: ["Shapiro B.", "Lemkin P.", "Lipkin L."]

Title: OPTIMUM ESTIMATION OF OCEAN WAVE HEIGHTS USING ACCELEROMETER DATA.
Abstract: The problem of estimating ocean wave heights given accelerometer and pressure measurements from a spar buoy is described. The correlated ocean waves are represented as a second order system driven by white noise. The buoy dynamics in the vertical are represented as a second order system driven by the waves or by white noise. Some results are given for models with state vectors of order three and four using real data.
Name: ["Severance Robert W."]

Title: UNIFIED THEORY ON COMPUTER-AIDED ANALYSIS OF SYSTEMS AND NETWORKS.
Abstract: Methodologies on computer-aided analysis and design of systems parallel to those of networks are developed. Basic elements of a signal-flow graph representing a system are defined. Equations are formulated in terms of the two topological matrices, the summing matrix and the branching matrix, for a signal-flow graph. Topological constraints analogous to Kirchhoff's laws are stated. State equations of a linear dynamic system analogous to those of an LCR network are obtained. A theorem similar to Tellegen's theorem is obtained for signal-flow graph and a method is developed for sensitivity computation by employing the concept of adjoint signal-flow graph. Based on these parallels between networks and systems, a unified theory on computer-aided analysis and design of networks and systems is accomplished.
Name: ["Lee A.Y."]

Title: Identification of Human Driver Models in Car Following
Abstract: This paper presents the development of two new mathematical models of driver behavior in single-lane car following situations. Optimum parameter values in each of these models were obtained using standard parameter identification algorithms. The basic approach to model development was to derive the model structure using optimal control theory. The problem was formulated as a model-tracking problem and a quadratic cost function was minimized. Model parameters were optimized by comparing model behavior with freeway data obtained on Interstate 71 in Ohio by Clear and Treiterer. The results indicate that the models fit the data very well during acceleration and deceleration phases, but not during constant velocity regions. To obtain a better fit during transitions between acceleration and deceleration phases, a second model was postulated based on the hypothesis that the driver tracks not only the car directly in front of him,but also cars directly ahead of the lead car. An adaptive controller structure with a mode switching algorithm has been derived and its parameters optimized. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Burnham G.O.", "Seo J.", "Bekey G.A."]

Title: AUTOMATED SPIROMETRY SYSTEM.
Abstract: A reliable automated spirometry system for use in rapid and accurate testing of populations in the field is described. The system consists of an electronic spirometer, 4-channel FM tape recorder, storage oscilloscope, FVC-FEV//1 calculator, and code word generator. The FVC calculator and code word generator were developed in-house for use with commercially available equipment. The system stores the flow and volume signals on the FM analog tape and has a backup system using polaroid photographs in the event of tape recorder failure. Approximately 7,000 coal miners have been studied using this system with only minor problems. Storage of the data on analog tape will allow reprocessing of the data as new techniques of analysis become available.
Name: ["Hankinson John L.", "Rose William D."]

Title: GENERAL PROGRAM FOR SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION AND ANALYSIS USING A DESK-TOP MINI COMPUTER.
Abstract: This paper describes an assembler language program written for the Nova line of mini computers. The program enables one to analyze, on- or off-line, the statistical properties of a system's input-output signals, to compute the impulse function and the frequency response and to predict the system's output under a given input.
Name: ["Montagner G.J.", "Trott G.W."]

Title: IMAGE DATA COMPRESSION BY HADAMARD-HAAR TRANSFORM.
Abstract: A hybrid version of the Haar and Walsh-Hadamard transform (HT and WHT) called Hadamard-Haar transform (HHT)//r is defined and developed. (HHT)//r results from the Kronecker product of the well known Haar and Walsh-Hadamard transforms and as such the base functions of (HHT)//r are linear combinations of Haar functions. Efficient algorithms for fast computation of the (HHT)//r and its inverse are developed. Specific examples illustrating the (HHT)//r, its properties, and the fast algorithms are included. The objectives of developing the (HHT)//r are to provide another tool for applications in digital signal and image processing, which have gained prominence in recent years, and to compare its utility and performance with those of the other discrete transforms. Digital computer programs for fast implementation of (HHT)//r and for evaluating these performance criteria are developed. Based on these criteria, it is shown thaat the (HHT)//r offers a compromise between the HT and the WHT.
Name: ["Rao K.R.", "Narasimhan M.A.", "Revuluri K."]

Title: GAME-THEORETIC CONTROL AND PROBLEMS OF STABILITY.
Abstract: Control problems associated with an ordinary dynamical system under conditions of conflict or uncertainty are discussed. A stable game-theoretic scheme of control is constructed with a theoretical foundation being described. The scheme which includes an imitating model plant - the so-called leader - is based on a mathematical formalization of the problems under consideration. The proposed scheme unites the methods of the theory of stability of motion with those of the theory of differential games.
Name: ["Krasovskii N.N."]

Title: ELECTRONIC SYSTEM TO PRODUCE ARTIFICIAL VISION FOR THE BLIND.
Abstract: An electronic system to produce artificial vision for the blind by electrical stimulation of the visual cortex is proposed. The system, which is based on extensive recent physiological data, consists of two parts; an external portion consisting of special purpose image sensing and signal processing circuity, and an internal portion (to be completely biologically implanted) containing an array of surface electrodes to stimulate the cortex, and the necessary electrode driver circuits. Both signal and power are coupled from the external to the internal parts of a link. The artificial vision produced by this system would be analogous to a ssports arena ‚Ä≥scoreboard‚Ä≥ .
Name: ["Dobelle W.", "Fordemwalt J.", "Hanson J.", "Hill D.", "Huber R.", "Mladejovsky M.", "Smith K."]

Title: EFFICIENT ALGORITHMIC PROCEDURE FOR OBTAINING A MINIMUM l<sub> </sub>infinity -NORM SOLUTION TO A SYSTEM OF CONSISTENT LINEAR EQUATIONS.
Abstract: An algorithmic procedure is described for determining a minimum l// infinity -norm solution to the system of consistent linear equations Ax equals y, where A is a m multiplied by n matrix of rank m, y is a known m multiplied by 1 vector and x is an unknown n multiplied by 1 vector. The algorithm's development is based on some fundamental concepts from functional analysis. Its computational efficiency is shown to easily exceed that of the linear programming formulization of the same problem.
Name: ["Cadzow James A."]

Title: SOME THOUGHTS ON ASSOCIATIVE PROCESSING LANGUAGES.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: This paper proposes language forms, based on the PL/1 language, which will give the programmer the capability to directly use all of the features of an associative processor without having to revert to assembly language coding. Many of the statements will translate into one or two lines of machine code, but this is necessary to use of the full power of the machine.
Name: ["Patterson William W."]

Title: GRAPHICAL METHOD FOR COMPUTER CHOICE OF A HYPOTHESIS ABOUT THE DISTRIBUTION OF A RANDOM QUANTITY.
Abstract: A graphical method is considered for choosing a hypothesis about the distribution of a random empirical quantity with the aid of a digital computer. An algorithm and ALPHA-language program are proposed for various distributions. They are intended for calculating and printout on the alphanumeric printer of a BESM-3M computer of regions in the ( beta //1, beta //2)-plane.
Name: ["Milyuna M.K."]

Title: NUMERICAL SOLUTION OF QUEUING NETWORKS WITH DIFFERENT CLASSES OF CUSTOMERS.
Abstract: Networks of queues are important models for the analysis of computer systems, both for hardware and software. A description is given of efficient algorithms for the numerical solution of a new class of queuing network models.
Name: ["Kobayashi H.", "Reiser M."]

Title: ON INVERSE OF LINEAR DISCRETE-TIME-VARYING SYSTEM.
Abstract: The extension of the inverse problem to a linear nonstationary discrete-time system is given. It has importance for the synthesis of discrete-time or sampled-data time-varying systems.
Name: ["Soukup Vaclav"]

Title: USER MICROPROGRAM DEVELOPMENT FOR AN LSI PROCESSOR.
Abstract: Microprocessor customizing has resulted in more efficient microprocessor systems, where it is possible to augment the existing machine instruction set, modify the interrupt servicing or input/output handling, or have the microcomputer directly execute a high-level language. Adjusting system architecture to the specific application simplifies programming and improves throughput. Key to these improvements is user microprogramming. The additional level of flexibility and expandability provided by microprogrammable microprocessors is explored in this article, along with potential applications of the microprogram technique. Important characteristics and configurations of a user microprogram development system are also described.
Name: ["Weissberger Alan J."]

Title: HYBRID COMPUTER SYSTEM SIMULATING INELASTIC SEAM BEHAVIOR.
Abstract: This paper describes a combination electrical resistance network analog and digital computer system - a hybrid computer - for simulating nonlinear, inelastic behavior of portions of mine pillars or abutments, or of artificial support such as packs, props, or backfill. The hybrid system combines the speed of analog computation with the decision-making capability of the digital computer and has many implications for rational planning of underground excavations in seam- or vein-type deposits. As an example of the utility of the system, the predictions of the hybrid are compared with actual field observations from Project Salt Vault. In this instance, inelastic seam behavior results from time-dependent deformations in the salt.
Name: ["Hardy M.P.", "Crouch S.L.", "Fairhurst C.", "Sinha K.P."]

Title: DECOMPOSITION THEOREM FOR FINITE AUTOMATA.
Abstract: A theorem is proven that establishes the existence conditions for a decomposition in the general case. A constructive method is given for an abstract network of automata, which realizes a specified automaton.
Name: ["Keevallik A.E."]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF DYNAMIC SYSTEM BY RANDOM SEARCH WITH GUIDE SPHERE.
Abstract: It is shown that the error in a gyroscopic device can be reduced significantly if it is allowed to move in a certain way with respect to a vibrating base. The optimal angles of rotation are found by random search with a guide sphere.
Name: ["Bachkalo B.I."]

Title: Method of Computer-Aided Assignment of Welded Parts to Welding Equipment. | [EINE METHODE ZUR RECHNERGESTUETZTEN ZUORDNUNG VON SCHWEISSTEILEN ZU SCHWEISSANLAGEN.]
Abstract: The application of the mathematical-logical modeling to describe the complexity of welding systems and their factors is discussed. A technique is proposed which enables an unambiguous assignment of the welding equipment to the welding systems with respect to the characteristics of welded joints.
Name: ["Mosny Martin"]

Title: FOURIER REALIZATION OF THE OPTIMAL PHASE DEMODULATOR.
