Abstract: An optimal phase demodulator is realized by sequentially calculating the Fourier Coefficients of the conditional density of the phase and phase rate given the observations. The point mass method of carrying the density and its resultant estimate is shown to be the same as that of the Fourier Filter. The advantage of the Fourier Filter is that it produces estimates eight times faster than the point mass filter while retaining fidelity.
Name: ["Bucy R.S.", "Youssef Hussein"]

Title: LEARNING HARDWARE-SOFTWARE SYSTEM FOR THE RECOGNITION AND PICK UP OF OBJECTS.
Abstract: A computer hardware-software system is described that recognizes and picks up objects. The hardware includes computer, sensing device (TV camera, ultrasonic detectors, fiber optic detectors, etc. ), and manipulator. The software consists of an algorithm specifically tailored for recognition and picking up of an object, through minimization of an objective function.
Name: ["Ayoub E.E."]

Title: SUBOPTIMAL CONTROL OF LINEAR SYSTEMS WITH INACCESSIBLE STATES VIA REDUCED ORDER MODELS.
Source: J Inst Eng (India) Electron Telecommun Eng Div
Abstract: Implementation of the optimal control law to regulator feedback problems requires reconstruction of the inaccessible states of the system. However, if the available state variables are sufficient for stabilizing the system and if simplicity is desirable as against the complexity of constructing an observer, a suboptimal linear regulator can be designed with the available state variables only. This paper reviews some important methods for reconstructing unavailable states and proposes a new method for designing control systems with inaccessible states. The suggested procedure utilizes a reduced order model of the original system. The concept is illustrated by a numerical example.
Name: ["Vittal Rao S."]

Title: CONSTRAINED OPTIMAL NONLINEAR REGULATORS FOR SINGLE-STATE FEEDBACK.
Abstract: The regulator problem for single input-output linear plants in which only the plant output is available for control is considered. A method is presented to specify an optimal nonlinear controller characteristic, constrained to lie within a given Popov sector, that yields improved performance over that obtained by proportional controllers. System performance is measured by a quadratic performance index, and performance is compared with that of both proportional and optimum linear state regulators.
Name: ["Gay T.A.", "Hoberock L.L."]

Title: EFFECTS OF MOTION ON THE PARAMETERS OF THE HUMAN OPERATOR ENGAGED IN A ROLL AXIS TRACKING TASK.
Abstract: A multiple-input single-output linear state variable model is used to determine the extent to which a human controller involved in a compensatory tracking task uses cues other than the visual error signal to improve his tracking performance. The control system used in this study is a roll axis chair designed to simulate roll in a high performance aircraft. The additional cues studied are the angular position and angular velocity of the human controller.
Name: ["Neff J.A.", "Junker A.M."]

Title: NETWORK MODULES TO SIMULATE QUANTIZED ENTITY FLOW.
Abstract: Systems and processes which can be described by unit commodity flow (quanta) or information flow (bits) are modeled in terms of frequently recurring network components. A modular and mutually compatible set of network components is formulated and properties of these modules are examined in terms of interacting queues, probabilistic and deterministic branching nodes and similar characteristics. A classification of modules provides a user-oriented library of components. The resulting modelling technique is ideally suitable for digital simulation of industrial systems which can be described in terms of entity flow.
Name: ["Dabaghian L.", "Akiba Y.", "Happ W.W."]

Title: TOWARD THE GENERAL PURPOSE-SPECIAL-PURPOSE SIMULATION PROGRAM.
Abstract: An approach is suggested for the realization of generalized simulation programs, each such program being characterized by its applicability in diverse studies on the various members of some specific class of systems. Basic simulation concepts are defined and used to establish the general criteria underlying the design of such programs.
Name: ["Vaccari Erminia", "Delaney William"]

Title: STARAN parallel processor system software
Source: AFIPS Conference Proceedings - 1974 National Computer Conference, AFIPS 1974
Abstract: This paper is concerned with the features and concepts of system software for a parallel associative array processor-STARAN. Definitions of parallel processors have appeared often. Essentially they are machines with a large number of processing elements. They have the capability to operate on multiple data streams with a single instruction stream. STARAN is a line of parallel processors with a variable number of processing elements. ¬© ACM-CONFERENCE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Davis E.W."]

Title: Properties and calculation of transmission zeros of linear multivariable systems
Abstract: A new definition of transmission zeros for a linear, multivariable, time-invariant system is made which is shown to be equivalent to previous definitions. Based on this new definition of transmission zeros, new properties of transmission zeros of a system are then obtained; in particular, it is shown that a system with an unequal number of inputs and outputs almost always has no transmission zeros and that a system with an equal number of inputs and outputs almost always has either n-1 or n transmission zeros, where n is the order of the system; transmission zeros of cascade systems are then studied, and it is shown how the transmission zeros of a system relate to the poles of a closed loop system subject to high gain output feedback. An application of transmission zeros to the servomechanism problem is also included. A fast, efficient, numerically stable algorithm is then obtained which enables the transmission zeros of high order multivariable systems to be readily obtained. Some numerical examples for a 9th order system are given to illustrate the algorithm. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Davison E.J.", "Wang S.H."]
Affiliations: [' University of Toronto', ' University of Colorado']

Title: NEW APPROACH TO CONTINUOUS DIGESTER CONTROL.
Abstract: The approach is based on linear stochastic control theory and new results in the area of adaptive control. The digester process is very complex and can be described as a nonlinear, multivariable, time varying stochastic system. However as the nonlinear structure is rather well known, it is fully possible to use the properties of linear systems. The developed control algorithm handles the multivariable and the time varying aspects in a powerful way. The strategy which does not require any other a priori knowldege about the process than the nonlinear properties is, in fact, a self-adjusting regulator. The central part of the algorithm is very compact and easy to apply in practice.
Name: ["Cegrell Torsten", "Hedqvist Torbjorn"]

Title: The use of Boolean algebra in the study of neural networks
Abstract: The McCulloch Pitts theory is modified to make it compatible with a frequency code. This is accomplished by defining a stimulus to an input as a discharge of action potentials at the maximum frequency for that input, and no stimulus as the complete absence of firing. A response is defined as the firing of an output at the maximum rate which results from the stimulation of any combination of inputs. This modification provides an all or none definition of stimulus and response, as required for Boolean algebra, which is still consistent with a frequency code. Detailed procedures are described for converting the response patterns of network outputs into Boolean equations, and for producing hypothetical network diagrams from these Boolean equations. A third procedure allows any network with known synaptic connections to be described by Boolean equations.
Name: ["Harris C.L."]

Title: Code for a General Purpose System Identifier and Evaluator (GPSIE)
Abstract: The modeling process may be viewed as a three-step iteration: 1) hypothesize a structure, 2) estimate (identify) unknown parameters, and 3) test for consistency between the model and available data. This paper describes a new, publicly-available computer program which performs the second and third tasks. The program, called General Purpose System Identifier and Evaluator (GPSIE), can handle nonlinear, time-varying, multiple input-output systems of arbitrary dimensions. The user supplies an array of data and a subprogram in PL/I or Fortran defining the model structure of interest. GPSIE searches for the maximum-likelihood estimates of any unknown parameters, and computes statistical measures of consistency between the model and the data. Options allow the user to deal efficiently with many kinds of systems. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Peterson D.W.", "Schweppe F.C."]
Affiliations: [' Massachusetts Institute of Technology', ' Massachusetts Institute of Technology']

Title: INTEGRATED APPROACH TO THE DESIGN OF FAULT TOLERANT COMPUTING SYSTEMS.
Abstract: This paper offers an introduction to a research effort in fault tolerant computer architecture which has been organized at the University of Southwestern Louisiana. This first area of concentration involves the systematic design of fault tolerant computing systems via a multi-level approach. Efforts are being initiated also in the areas of diagnosis of microprogrammable processors via firmware, fault data management across levels of virtual machines, development of a methodology for realizing a firmware hardcore on a variety of hosts, and delineation of a minimal set of resources for the design of a practical host for a multi-level fault tolerant computing system.
Name: ["Caillouet Jr. L.Philip", "Shriver Sr. Bruce D."]

Title: ECONOMIC SCHEDULING USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.
Abstract: Since the load of a power system is constantly changing, one or more of the generation units must be in a dynamic state at any given time. Also, changes in such quantities as ambient temperature and feedwater temperature affect the overall system efficiency, thus the incremental cost given by a cost curve is at best only an approximation of the actual incremental cost. The purpose of this work is to describe a new technique which would allow real time estimation of the present incremental cost and a prediction of future incremental cost for a given input signal. It uses supervised learning methods rather than classical modeling techniques to represent system input-output characteristics. During execution, the desired input-output response is obtained by combining the direct search methods of operations research and pattern recognition.
Name: ["Taylor F.J.", "Schroder D.C."]

Title: EMULATION OF COMPUTER NETWORKS BY MICROPROGRAMMABLE MICROCOMPUTERS.
Abstract: A method is suggested for implementing microprogrammable microcomputer systems as a sophisticated tool (emulators) for decreasing the economic risk involved in development of large computer networks. Two levels of emulation are proposed for different network configurations. At the first level each microprocessor emulates one of the large computers in the real network. At the second level of emulation, an additional microprocessor emulates the front-end processor associated with each large computer. The Intel 8080 microprocessors are selected for implementing the systems described.
Name: ["Cohen David", "Liu Ming T."]

Title: DATA REDUCTION FOR MULTIPLE CORRELATED SOURCES.
Abstract: Most of the previous work in data reduction has been concerned with the efficient representation of the output of a single information source. Due to the recent upsurge of interest in communication networks, where several sources are simultaneously communicating with one or more receivers, an important problem to be considered is the simultaneous removal of redundancy from several information sources. Results of past work on this problem will be reviewed and it will be shown how these results can be applied to several new configurations.
Name: ["Wolf Jack Keil"]

Title: OPTIMUM TEARING OF LARGE SYSTEMS AND MINIMUM FEEDBACK SETS OF A DIGRAPH.
Abstract: Optimum tearing of a complex network or system at an appropriate place and minimum feedback sets of a digraph are dealt with concerning the minimization of computation steps and storage.
Name: ["Kuh E.S.", "Cheung L.K."]

Title: A predictive model for ambulatory patient service time
Abstract: This paper reports results from one area of research on the general problem of resource scheduling and utilization in medical ambulatory care at the Lahey Clinic Foundation in Boston. Major areas in which it is possible to reduce scheduling errors in ambulatory care are noted, and research results in the development of more effective models of predetermining patient service time are reported. Previous work with regard to service time has been centered around the development of the need for individual appointments usually spaced at mean service time intervals. In this report an analysis is made of the variables that determine the expected length of a patient visit. Improved and implementablc models for the determination of expected service time based on the criteria of mean absolute error of prediction are noted. ¬© Lippincott-Raven Publishers.
Name: ["Rockhart J.F.", "Hehzog E.L."]
Affiliations: [' Lahey Clinic Foundation', ' Lahey Clinic Foundation']

Title: ROETEXT: a system for automatic text processing in diagnostic radiology | ROETEXT: EIN SYSTEM FUR DIE AUTOMATISCHE TEXTVERARBEITUNG IN DER RONTGENDIAGNOSTIK
Abstract: The configuration and function of the automatic text processing system ROETEXT is described. The system allows automatic typing, coding, and storing of radiological reports in computer compatible form. The standardized reports as well as precoded descriptors and diagnoses are collected in a text manual and stored in a text storage unit. The radiologist uses either a precoded standard report or compiles a report using precoded descriptors and diagnoses, and notes corresponding code numbers, consecutively, on a working sheet. These data, including variables, patients' personal data and report identification data, are entered into the system by a clerk typist. In the generation of the final roentgenological report document as well as of the computer compatible tape, 2 operational steps can be distinguished. In the first step a working tape containing codes of all components of the final report document is punched out and a working sheet is printed out. The second step is fully automatized. By means of the working tape, the text of the final report is retrieved from the text storage unit, the report documents are typed continuously on the form feed, and a computer compatible tape containing patients' data and coded roentgenological diagnoses is punched out.
Name: ["Novak D."]

Title: Optical image enhancement in nuclear medicine
Abstract: Radioisotopes are injected intravenously and their distribution imaged externally using scintillation detectors. The isotope concentration is different in abnormal tissue than in surrounding normal tissue. Recorded images are distorted by collimators which result in a known approximately circularly symmetric Gaussian shaped spread function. In the past, the authors used computers to correct recorded images for this distortion using both linear and non linear filtering techniques. Later, they used an optical system to carry out linear filtering. Now they are using a new optical/digital hybrid system to accomplish non linear filtering. This new system is described. | Nuclear Medicine is a relatively new and rapidly expanding field dealing with the use of radioisotopes in patients for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes. Radioisotopes are injected intravenously and their distribution imaged externally using scintillation detectors. This procedure is the so-called radioisotope scanning. The isotope concentration is different in abnormal tissue than in surrounding normal tissue. Recorded images are distorted by collimators which result in a known approximately circularly symmetric Gaussian shaped spread function. In the past, the authors have used computers to correct recorded images for this distortion using both linear and non-linear filtering techniques. Later, they used an optical system to carry out linear filtering. Now they are using a new optical/digital hybrid system to accomplish nonlinear filtering. This new system is described.
Name: ["Brown D.W.", "Kirch D.L.", "Trow R.S.", "Lefree M.T."]

Title: Computer generation of random normal deviates for Monte Carlo work
Abstract: A procedure is described for computer simulation of random sampling from a normally distributed population with prespecified mean and standard deviation. Evaluation of the number generator for both randomness and normality showed statistical characteristics adequate for Monte Carlo work, as well as for evaluation of psychological and behavioral models involving random error components. The computer program is included.
Name: ["Woodward J.A.", "Overall J.E."]

Title: Natural language information storage and retrieval system for nuclear medicine: Two years' experience
Abstract: For 2 yr an information storage and retrieval system originally designed for pathology diagnoses was also used for nuclear medicine reports. An input translator accepts the free text which is automatically indexed. A thesaurus automatically expands a search request to include related terms. Logical searches cross referencing these 2 patient data files result in increased specificity of retrieved material. Expansion of the data base by laboratory and medical record summaries in natural language will further improve cross referencing and increase specificity of searches.
Name: ["Stein M.A.", "Okubo R.", "Bennett L.R.", "Winter J."]

Title: A Practical Application of a Real-Time Isolated-Word Recognition System Using Syntactic Constraints
Source: IEEE Transactions on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
Abstract: In this paper we describe an application of a real-time isolated-word recognition system, to the recognition of sentences of a language used in numerical command of machine tools. The acoustic level operates with dynamic matching procedure and knowledge about syntactics and semantics of the language is used to predict the incoming words. With such a syntax-directed system, real-time recognition of sentences pronounced word-by-word is very accurately achieved, even for several speakers. This system will then be adapted to the recognition of connected speech, as well as in the design of new languages for man-machine voice communication, Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Haton J.-P."]

Title: Recovery of randomly sampled signals by simple interpolators
Abstract: The mean square error performance of simple polynomial interpolators is analyzed for wide-sense stationary signals subjected to randomly timed sampling represented by stationary point processes. This performance is expressed in dimensionsless parametric terms, with emphasis on asymptotic error behavior at high dimensionless sampling rates Œ≥. The form of the asymptotic error expression, and particularly its dependence on Œ≥, is shown to vary according to the number of points utilized, together with the differentiability properties of the signal. One point extrapolation yields a mean square error varying with Œ≥<sup>-2</sup> if the signal is differentiable, and as Œ≥<sup>-1</sup> if the signal is not. Similarly, two-point (polygonal) interpolation error exhibits linearity in Œ≥<sup>-4</sup>, Œ≥<sup>-3</sup> or Œ≥<sup>-2</sup>, according as the signal is twice, exactly once, or nondifferentiable. Specific examples are offered to furnish insight into actual error magnitudes. It is shown, for instance, that introduction of jitter in the sampling sequence increases the error by only a negligible amount. Exponential decay of the sample values is compared with stepwise holding; little is gained for a nondifferentiable signal, while for a differentiable signal the error performance deteriorates from Œ≥<sup>-2</sup> to Œ≥<sup>-1</sup> at high sampling rates. When more than two points are used in a polynomial fitting recovery scheme, specific computations or error become excessively difficult. However, it is proved that the asymptotic mean square error varies with Œ≥<sup>-2n</sup> when n points are utilized, and the signal is continuously differentiable at least n times. Finally, we compare the mean square errors of one and two sample schemes as described above with those attained by causal (extrapolating) and noncausal (interpolating) Wiener-Kolmogorov optimal filters. We demonstrate nontrivial instances in which the Wiener-Kolmogorov mean square error varies as Œ≥<sup>-1/2</sup>, so that any of the simple recovery schemes considered exhibits superior performance at high sampling rates. This is explained by noting that the latter represent time-varying filters, whereas the Wiener-Kolmogorov filter is timeinvariant. ¬© 1974 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Beutler F.J."]

Title: Error and Sensitivity Analysis of Stochastic Approximation Algorithms for Linear System Identification
Abstract: Propagation of errors in identifying constant coefficient parameters of a discrete time linear system, using stochastic approximation algorithms, is investigated. Error and sensitivity analysis algorithms are derived for the cases when there is structural modeling error as well as when the a priori statistics of identified parameters, and plant and measurement noise, are incorrectly specified. The error and sensitivity analysis algorithms are useful as a design tool to better specify appropriate identification algorithms for actual implementation. The error and sensitivity analysis algorithms are applied to several examples including identification of eight predictor coefficients for adaptive digitized speech transmission. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Alam M.A.", "Sage A.P."]

Title: A comparison of list schedules for parallel processing systems
Abstract: The problem of scheduling two or more processors to minimize the execution time of a program which consists of a set of partially ordered tasks is studied. Cases where task execution times are deterministic and others in which execution times are random variables are analyzed. It is shown that different algorithms suggested in the literature vary significantly in execution time and that the B-schedule of Coffman and Graham is near-optimal. A dynamic programming solution for the case in which execution times are random variables is presented. ¬© 1974, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Adam T.L.", "Chandy K.M.", "Dickson J.R."]

Title: LARGE-SCALE PROGRAMMING PROPERTIES OF MENU PLANNING AND SCHEDULING.
Abstract: In contrast with the classical formulation of the diet program in textbook and feed-mix models, the mathematical programming formulation of optimum and acceptable human diets takes the form of interrelated menu planning and scheduling models where the scheduling constraints are in the thousands and clearly outnumber the nutritional constraints. The requirement for providing structure, compatibility and variety on the menu schedule corresponds to a general graph theoretical problem of compatible mapping. Some aspects of this can be handled through the solution of a restricted assignment problem which is treated as the subproblem of the system. Another large-scale programming property arises from the occurrence of variable coefficients in the master problem due to the fact that the entities subject to programming are often equivalent classes of menu items forming convex sets of ingredient and nutrient composition vectors. The need for solving such problems correctly is routinely faced in all forms of volume feeding organizations, especially in hospitals, schools, and military food service systems. Inefficiencies in the traditional methods of menu planning have been shown to reach 20% of food cost.
Name: ["Balintfy Joseph L."]

Title: ANALYSIS OF THE EFFICIENCY OF A MULTIPROGRAM COMPUTER SYSTEM ALLOWING FOR CENTRALIZED CONTROL.
Abstract: A Markov model of the operation of a single-processor multiprogram computer system is used as a basis for determining the load factor of the central processor depending on the number of programs processed in parallel (multiprogramming level), the configuration of the external devices, and the centralized-control algorithm for the programs.
Name: ["Volovnik G.A."]

Title: Analysis of global pattern features
Abstract: A fundamental method for analysing the global features of visual patterns is presented. Pattern features are considered to be synonomous with non-random distributions in the pattern statistics. In particular, the statistics of the chords of the patterns are considered, leading to the histograms of the chord lengths and angles. Peaks in these histograms indicate the presence of structure in the pattern. It is demonstrated how the points of the pattern contributing to this structure can be enhanced and/or extracted. It is argued that this is a more fundamental way of obtaining pattern features than other ad hoc methods. The chord space approach allows analytic solutions to be easily obtained for idealized patterns such as circles, parallel lines, etc. A method for implementing the algorithms on a parallel processor is indicated. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Moore D.J.H.", "Parker D.J."]

Title: APPLICATION OF MARKOV-PROCESS THEORY TO THE ANALYSIS OF ADAPTATION-ALGORITHM DYNAMICS.
Abstract: An approach to the analysis of adaptation-algorithm dynamics is considered. It consists of constructing approximate models of the algorithms. A formal definition of the adaptive system is given. The models described are employed to investigate the dynamics of a no-search gradient algorithm, as well as a random-search algorithm. Estimates are obtained for the practical rate of convergence of these algorithms in the problem of adaptive identification of a static object.
Name: ["Derevitskii D.P.", "Fradkov A.L."]

Title: MINIMAL REALIZATION OF TERNARY THRESHOLD FUNCTIONS.
Abstract: Threshold functions up to three variables are studied. Partition of the set of threshold functions according to a set of transformations is defined. A table of classes of equivalence is provided, giving the required information on minimum weights and safe thresholds for a given function, by table inspection and simple theorems.
Name: ["Nazarala Jorge", "Moraga Claudio"]

Title: COMPUTERIZED EEG SPIKE DETECTION.
Abstract: One of the first problems to be considered in the design of an automated system for detecting spikes in EEG's is that there exists no adequate definition of an EEG spike. The most reasonable way of defining spikes appears to be on the basis of human detection. Preliminary experiments showed that human detection is quite variable. Disagreement between the experts on individual spikes is not necessarily very important clinically. Rather, a comparison on a patient basis would be more important than a comparison on the basis of individual spikes. In an initial study, over 50 properties which were considered to be potentially useful in the automated detection of spikes were programmed and tested on a smaller data set of spikes from a single patient detected by a single expert. Electromyographic (EMG) signals resemble spikes, and often occur as noise antifacts in EEG records. Algorithms for detecting EMG noise were also programmed and tested on this initial data set.
Name: ["Gose Earl E.", "Werner Sarah", "Bickford Reginald G."]

Title: COMPARISON OF THE MODEL STRUCTURE AND PREDICTIVE POWER OF AGGREGATE AND DISAGGREGATE MODELS OF INTERCITY MODE CHOICE.
Abstract: This paper reports the construction of both disaggregate and aggregate models of intercity mode choice; data from the Edinburgh-Glasgow Area Modal-Split Study were used. The models are then compared in terms of their structure (i. e. , the variables included) and their ability to predict modal split. The disaggregate models provide a better statistical explanation of mode-choice behavior.
Name: ["Watson Peter L."]

Title: High level operations in automatic programming
Source: Proceedings of the ACM SIGPLAN Symposium on Very High Level Languages
Abstract: We discuss the thesis that one good way of achieving non-procedural or problem-oriented languages is by constructing higher and higher level procedural languages. We present a set of operations embedded in a programming language VERS2 which represent a higher level of description than currently exists. These include iterators (operations which, if written out, would normally involve an iteration over a group of objects), pattern matching facilities, implicitly specified data structures, and the ability to place constraints on data structures. ¬© 1974 Authors.
Name: ["Earley J."]

Title: A heuristic approach to inductive inference in fact retrieval systems
Abstract: Heuristic procedures are presented which have been developed to perform inferences by generalizing from available information. The procedures make use of a similarity structure which is imposed on the data base using nonnumerical clustering algorithms. They are implemented in a model fact retrieval system which uses a formal query language and a property-list data structure. A program of experiments is described wherein the procedures are used with test data bases which are altered by deleting part of the data and by purposely introducing false data. It is found that the system can infer the correct response under a variety of conditions involving incomplete and inconsistent data. ¬© 1974, ACM. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Skinner C.W."]

Title: ON STEP ADAPTATION IN RANDOM-SEARCH ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: A step-adaptation algorithm in which the step length has a continuous distribution law is proposed. An adaptation procedure is described for cases in which the region of variation of the control variables cannot be determined in advance and when there are constraints. It is shown that adaptation algorithms in which the step length is continuously distributed are a generalization to the case of successive step subdivision. The step-adaptation procedure is illustrated with a variety of examples.
Name: ["Volynskii E.I.", "Filatov G.V."]

Title: HEURISTIC METHODS: STRUCTURES, APPLICATIONS, COMPUTATIONAL EXPERIENCE.
Abstract: A brief review is given of heuristic methods, dividing them into two large groups: the methods that lead to a first feasible solution (FFS), and the methods that iteratively improve existing solutions (IIS). Their further subdivisions are considered and compared. They are illustrated by means of the travelling salesman problem. A brief survey is then given of several problems and of the corresponding heuristic methods suggested in the literature, such as: the quadratic assignment problem, the LP-transportation problem, the integer programming problems, the job shop scheduling problems and problems of resource scheduling.
Name: ["Mueller-Merbach Heiner"]

Title: FROM ADAPTIVE CONTROL CONSTRAINT TO A PILOT SYSTEM FOR OPTIMIZATION.
Abstract: Adaptive Control (AC) systems are divided into Adaptive Control Constraint (ACC) and Adaptive Control Optimization (ACO). In Germany several universities are working on a joint project for developing a pilot system for ACO which should be finally - besides CNC, DNC, data acquisition and processing - one part of a general hardware - software system in the sense of a computer-aided manufacturing system. In the first part different sensors are discussed. The second part handles the off-line and on-line optimization, especially the process simulation and software-developments for direct digital control and optimization.
Name: ["Stute G.", "Eitel H."]

Title: The development of adaptive systems in Germany anil France
Source: Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement and Control, Transactions of the ASME
Abstract: The paper presented shows the development of adaptive control systems in Oermany and France. After a review of the historical development, typical theoretical principles and some representative examples of adaptive control systems in several fields of application are discussed. The paper shows that important results were obtained both from theoretical and experimental point of view by investigators in both countries. ¬© 1974 by ASME.
Name: ["Landau I.D.", "Unbehauen H."]
Affiliations: [' Laboratoire d‚Äô Automatique Saint Martin d‚ÄôHeres', 'Universitat Stuttgart']

Title: RANDOM-SEARCH ALGORITHM FOR SOLUTION OF MANY-EXTREMAL PROBLEMS.
Abstract: An examination is made of a modification of an algorithm with return after an unsuccessful step. It is proposed to arrange the series of trial probes inside some ellipsoid with known center and extremal probability density law. The advantages of use of an extremal probability density over a uniform law, and the global properties of the proposed algorithm, are discussed. Two variations of the algorithm are investigated: first, with a variable ratio of the axes of the ellipsoid, but with their direction fixed, and second, with constant shape of the ellipsoid which varies its position in space. The results of operation of each of these variants for a many-extremal function, and the results of solving practical problems, are given.
Name: ["Volynskiy E.I.", "Pochtman Yu.M."]

Title: K-SIMULATION FOR CIRCUIT ANALYSIS.
Abstract: In digital simulation of logic networks, it is often convenient to know whether application of a given input sequence would produce a given logic state on a particular output, caring neither when nor for how long this state exists. An economical method of performing this calculation called K-simulation is described. K-simulation agrees with results of three-valued simulation which uses the value ‚Ä≥X‚Ä≥ as the initial state of sequential logic.
Name: ["Anstett R.H.", "Snethen T."]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR CONTROL OF GLIDING DESCENT OF A SPACECRAFT FROM EARTH ORBIT.
Abstract: An algorithm is proposed for the autonomous discrete control of the gliding descent of a spacecraft (SC) from earth orbit. The angles of roll and attack serve as the control parameters. The results of modeling on an electronic computer are presented. It is shown that in view of the simplicity and sufficiently high precision of control, the given algorithm can find application for control systems for which one of the main requirements is related to a weight restriction.
Name: ["Nogov O.A.", "Korostashevskii G.N.", "Sindyukova L.I."]

Title: Plane autonomous state classifiers as measuring devices
Abstract: Object systems are studied on which plane autonomous state classifiers act as measuring devices. Several conclusions are drawn regarding the structure of the object system. The problem of coupling a PASC with an object system is considered in detail. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Engel A.B."]
Affiliations: [' State University of New York at Buffalo']

Title: SICLOPS: A SYSTEM OF COMPUTER PROGRAMS FOR RECTIFIED MAPPING OF AIRBORNE SCANNER IMAGERY.
Abstract: The system has been developed to perform geometrically corrected line-by-line mapping of airborne multispectral scanner data to ground coordinates and to estimate ground areas. SICLOPS is an acronym for Scanner Imagery Correction and Line-by-line Orientation ProgramS. As inputs, SICLOPS accepts aircraft attitude and positional information furnished by ancillary aircraft equipment, plus ground truth information giving the location, in map grid coordinates, of a number of recognizable landmarks on the ground. The geometric correction and mapping procedure locates the scan lines, or the pixels on each line, in terms of map grid coordinates. The area estimation procedure gives ground area for each pixel or for a predesignated parcel specified in map grid coordinates.
Name: ["Spencer M.M.", "Wolf J.M.", "Schall M.A."]

Title: CLUSTERING ALGORITHM FOR UNSUPERVISED CROP CLASSIFICATION.
Abstract: The algorithm described in this paper automatically determines the initial value for cluster centers and thresholds, by analyzing the hystograms of the observations to be clustered. Thus, in this procedure the initial centers are close to the final ones and convergence is obtained in only a fraction of the iterations required by conventional heuristic clustering procedures. A table look-up procedure yields a further reduction in the computer time required to run this algorithm.
Name: ["Borriello L.", "Capozza F."]

Title: The computation of lightness by the primate retina
Abstract: It is proposed that one function of the retina is to compute lightness using a two-dimensional parallel algorithm. There are three stages: (1) a centre-surround difference operation: (2) a threshold applied to the difference signal: (3) the inverse of (1), whose output is lightness. The operation of the midget bipolar-midget ganglion channel is analysed in detail, and a functional interpretation of various retinal structures is given. Requirements of the theory are stated concerning the arrangement and connexions of cells, and the signs of the synapses, in the inner plexiform layer. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Marr D."]

Title: Transition processes of human operator's model parameters in learning memorizing process and learning process (Japanese)
Abstract: The human operator's learning processes are classified into a learning memorizing process and a learning process, in accordance with whether the randomly appearing forcing function is the same on each trial or not. Under this classification, the transitions of the operator's model parameters in the 2 processes are analyzed and compared. The model is composed of gain, time delay, neuromuscular lag and first order lead and lag. The model parameters are found to vary between the learning memorizing process and the learning process, with the input bandwidth, and with the operator's practice. Some of these results are compared with those of the cross over model. The accuracy of the proposed model is substantiated by checking the agreement between the model output and the operator's output by the correlation coefficient and the power ratio.
Name: ["Hashimoto T."]

Title: A non parametric ranking method for the statistical evaluation of sensory data
Abstract: Sensory data are rarely normally distributed and should therefore be statistically analyzed by non parametric techniques. A computer program was devised for generating tabular data by which up to 20 samples can be compared following evaluation by as many as 75 panelists. When samples are initially ranked, rank sums for each sample may be compared to appropriate entries in the tables directly. If scalar values are assigned by panelists, the technique is still useful, but the values must first be converted to ranks.
Name: ["Kramer A.", "Kahan G.", "Cooper D.", "Papavasiliou A."]

Title: The Tactile Vision Substitution System: applications in education and employment
Abstract: The Tactile Vision Substitution System converts the visual image from a narrow angle television camera to a tactual image on a 5 inch square, 100 point display of vibrators placed against the abdomen of the blind person. This arrangement allows for the free use of the hands at the same time that the machine is in use. The possible applications of the system in education include the teaching of certain spatial concepts, e.g., monocular cues, and as an attachment to a microscope to allow for the examination of slides. In employment, the system could be used in those jobs in electronics requiring the use of an oscilloscope (to which it can be attached) or in assembly work involving the microscope, e.g., microcircuitry.
Name: ["Scadden L.A."]

Title: Evaluation of neuronal spike trains in neurophysiological experiments
Abstract: A simple method of analysis of spike train data from single neurons which avoids loss of relevant information is described. Examples of its usefulness in describing stochastic properties and detecting non-stationarities are presented. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Murphy J.T.", "Kwan H.", "Mackay W.A.", "Wong Y.C."]
Keywords: ["neuronal spike trains", "stochastic analysis", "trains neurophysiological", "evaluation neuronal", "neuronal spike"]

Title: Stochastic modeling of neural discharge
Abstract: Spontaneous neuronal discharge has been simulated using a Poisson distributed random number generation to provide excitatory post synaptic potentials of variable duration. Respective values of pulse height and threshold potential are given in the main program. The resulting neural spike train is used to compute an interspike interval distribution and an expectation density function which are plotted as a function of threshold potential. The twenty curves thus obtained are displayed in perspective on a storage CRT. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Mansourian B.G.", "Phan Tan T."]
Keywords: ["depolarization", "expectation density function", "inter-spike interval distribution", "nerve membrane potential", "neural model"]

Title: Optimal systems of a combination of control and observation. PMM vol. 38, n‚âó 1, 1974, pp. 12-24
Source: Journal of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics
Abstract: We examine linear controllable systems under the condition of incomplete information on the current phase state, when at each instant only certain functions of the phase coordinates are accessible to measurement. We assume that noise, for which there is no special description, enters into the controllable system and into the measurement (observation) channel. Only the exact deterministic constraints which this noise satisfies, are known. At each instant the optimal controls are synthesized from the information on the whole previous history of observation on the basis of a minimax criterion for a convex function of phase coordinate values at the termination instant of the process. Thus, in the paper we examine a specific information game problem of conflict control [1], The peculiarity of the problem manifests itself in the fact that here we are required to optimize as an aggregate both the synthesis process of the optimal control as well as the process of continuous estimation of the magnitudes of the current phase coordinates. The latter leads to the use of both the extremal constructions of the theory of differential-game problems of dynamics [1, 2] as well as the functional constructions for minimax problems of position observation and prediction [3, 4]. Fundamental attention is given to the constructive formation of the solution within the framework of convex analysis [5, 6]. The investigations in [7-9] were devoted to a different formulation of problems on the combination of control and observation. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Kurzhanskii A.B."]

Title: Classification: Purposes, principles, progress, prospects
Abstract: There is an intimate interrelation between principles and procedures in classification, and modern work in this field has been profoundly affected by the development of electronic computers. Besides the delineation of natural systems and the achievement of economy of memory and ease of manipulation, the primary purpose of classification is the description of the structure and relationship of groups of similar objects. Successful classifications generate scientific hypotheses, although much classificatory work has applied, practical goals. The acceptance of polythetic taxa is a major conceptual advance and has directly led to classifications based on many, equally weighted characteristics. The specification of data for classification by computer will enhance objectivity but not eliminate cultural and subjective biases. Techniques of classification include cluster analysis and ordination, and numerous ways of representing classifications have been elaborated recently. By the application of graph theory to some classificatory problems it has been possible to reconstruct evolutionary branching sequences. Computer classification has been successfully applied across a broad range of disciplines.
Name: ["Sokal R.R."]
Affiliations: [' State University of New York at Stony Brook']

Title: A system for the computer simulation of clinical reasoning
Abstract: A system is presented for computer simulation of the logical processes used by the physician in clinical medicine. The medical logic in a given area is formulated in modular fashion, where each module states the inference to be drawn and the clinical data on which the inference is based. The complex reasoning in diagnosis or therapy is reduced to a series of logical inferences each of which depends on a small number of clinical findings. Since all findings will not necessarily be present in each patient, the Boolean subsets of the findings sufficient for confirming the inference are expressed by threshold logic. A numerical weight is assigned to each finding such that the sufficient subsets will have a total score exceeding a preset threshold. The system programs are: EDIT, to convert the physician formulated medical logic modules into appropriate computer files; LIST, to aid in correcting and standardizing the medical terminology; QUERY, to allow on-line entry of patient data; and TEST, to analyze the patient data and report the patient's status. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Wiener F."]

Title: A computer program for quantitating data related to central control of respiration
Abstract: The genesis of the rhythmicity of the respiratory center has been widely studied. However, there has been little investigation of the effects on the respiratory center of diverse physiological states. A computer program has been written in an attempt to quantify some of the characteristics of the medullary respiratory control neurons (e.g., peak frequency, burst duration, interburst interval, time to peak frequency, and number of spikes per burst), and the associated changes in breathing pattern (i.e., respiratory rate, peak inspiratory and expiratory air flow rates, and tidal volume) in response to inputs producing a known reflex change in respiration. The computerized determination of this data has made it possible to help meet the objective of correlating the activity of single medullary respiratory neurons with breathing pattern. The program described in this paper utilizes the time intervals between extracellularly recorded action potentials from single medullary respiratory neurons and the associated ventilatory responses mentioned above. The means by which this data is processed are described. A discussion is presented of the problems related to performing the data reduction prior to statistical correlation of the neuron and ventilation variables. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Lam C.F.", "Carter H.T.", "Katz S."]
Affiliations: [' Medical University of South Carolina', ' Medical University of South Carolina']

Title: Experiments with syntactic traces in information retrieval
Abstract: A new concept called syntactic trace is introduced. Syntactic traces consist of syntactic similarity patterns and data base pointers. The similarity patterns contain indications about polygram-substrings that searchable parts of the different documents which are connected by means of the pointers have in common. An experimental computer program called STORES (Syntactic Trace Organized Retrospective Enquiry System) has been developed; it makes use of an access-strategy based on the syntactic traces. The results show that just a minor part of the total data base has to be processed in order to find exactly all possible hits for a given information enquiry in the form of a boolean expression. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["De Heer T."]

Title: Storage and manipulation of data by computers for determinative bacteriology
Abstract: Determinative bacteriology inherently involves acquisition and manipulation of many small pieces of information. Much of this information is codable directly in binary (i.e., 'yes' or 'no') form. Digital computers are uniquely suited to perform the desired data processing. Although at least one extensive coding system with some associated computer programs has been developed, much remains to be done before a universally applicable microbial data system is available. Some of these remaining computer technology tasks are the development of complete systems for data handling, data compression methods and common specifications for data communication. Common specifications are also required for the methods for elucidating the bacterial characteristics which are to be encoded. Some classes of data cannot be coded reasonably in binary form. In such cases, different coding methods will have to be developed along with computer techniques to manipulate and analyze these classes. Some examples of these classes, each with their unique problems, are sources of isolation, nucleic acid hybridization, serological typing, and genetic mapping.
Name: ["Krichevsky M.I.", "Norton L.M."]

Title: Information systems for experimental social programs: a health services example
Abstract: The organizational forms and data requirements of experimental social programs contribute to the necessity for the development of new general purpose file management and data processing systems. The organizational aspects of social research dictate that information systems be capable of performing both periodic reporting and special analytic tasks while remaining flexible enough to change as the experimental program develops. Restrictions imposed by the nature of social services data require a hierarchically organized data base and a variable length list structure. This paper describes the Hierarchical Information Processor (HIP) constructed and used by an experimental health services program. HIP is a PL/1 based macrocompiler programming language that allows a user to have access to a hierarchically structured data base to prepare either reports or special files for input to statistical packages. Segments of HIP include: a data base accessing code or dictionary, an extractor program, a table creation program, and a report generation program. Syntax and a sample program are included.
Name: ["Moore Jr J.R.", "Hershey J.C."]

Title: Automatic control of installations for experiments relating to physiological research of the visual system
Abstract: A mini-computer controls several installations where rabbits perform pattern-discrimination tests. Each installation runs independently of the others, permitting each rabbit to behave at its own speed (which is an essential part of the test). The number of installations can easily be extended without changing the program. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["van der Mark F.", "Meijer J.H.C."]

Title: Analysis of the code relating sequence to conformation in globular proteins: theory and application of expected information
Abstract: An information theory analysis of the folding of a globular protein is proposed. The folding is seen as a transfer of information between 2 messages, the primary sequence and the biologically active conformation. It is shown how the information transferred was estimated by inspection of proteins of known primary sequence and conformation. In this estimation, concerted use of subjective (Bayesian) probabilities leads to a more robust approach which can be employed whether the number of proteins of known sequence and conformation is large or small. Further, it is demonstrated that the problem then becomes a very simple algebraic formulation for information estimates. Finally, it is shown how this process of information theory analysis can be reversed to predict the conformation of a protein by using its primary sequence and the above information estimates obtained from other proteins. The present paper provides the theoretical basis for the derivation and application of a stereochemical alphabet and for investigation of the effects of residues on the conformations of their neighbors.
Name: ["Robson B."]

Title: HABERT - A system for evaluating x rays with the aid of a computer | HABERT - EIN SYSTEM ZUR COMPUTERUNTERSTUTZTEN RONTGENBEFUNDUNG
Abstract: The HABERT system presents a computer aided X ray evaluation for radiological diagnoses. The input of findings is followed by the output of a report in clear sentences with simultaneous storage. The system is constructed in such a way that it presents possible alternative diagnoses to the radiologist. This gives the opportunity to use programmed learning.
Name: ["Ecker F.", "Gothier W.", "Katzenberger K."]

Title: Localized oscillations in neural networks I. General considerations with nonlinear differential equations
Abstract: The linearized McCulloch & Pitts equation for neural network is shown to have localized oscillations. The localization is shown to be preserved or enforced by the introduction of nonlinearity. Reminiscence and association of memories are supposed to be related to the resonance phenomena of these localized oscillations. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Sait√¥ N.", "Oosima M."]
Affiliations: [' Waseda University', ' National Institutes of Health', ' Waseda University']

Title: A computer method for the analysis of ocular refractive data
Abstract: Numerous analytical investigations of data from vision examinations have been reported in the past century, most of which were limited to small samples because calculations often had to be performed by calculators or by hand. A method of coding and assembling ocular refractive data derived from vision examinations is described. This method can be used on large samples, allowing a wide variety of mathematical calculations, and data assembly correlations to be accomplished by a computer in a fraction of the time required for similar hand calculations.
Name: ["Woodruff M.E.", "Adamack T.", "Samek M."]

Title: A note on the Bayesian sequential estimation of a binomial parameter
Abstract: This paper is concerned with the Bayesian sequential estimation of a binomial parameter under quadratic loss and constant observation cost. A method of obtaining an approximation to the optimal design is suggested which is simpler to compute with little increase in risk. Finally, the effect of truncation is discussed.
Name: ["Jones P.W."]

Title: Digital electronic control of automatic ventilators
Abstract: Respiratory therapy depends in large measure on the existence of various devices such as those intended for automatic ventilation of the lungs. A digital system for use in ventilator control is described. The basic principle of this system is that every respiratory cycle is divided into a fixed number of counts. The control of the ratio of inspiration time to expiration time is accomplished by selecting a variable time out of the fixed time interval and designating it inspiration time. The remaining counts become expiration time. Respiratory rate is adjusted by varing the total time interval, and ratio by selecting a different inspiration time. The output of a DAC (Digital/Analog Converter) driven by the counters is adjustable and proportional to tidal volume. By inserting read only memories between the ratio scalars and the DAC input, a large number of different inspiration waveforms are generated. | A digital system for use in ventilator control has been developed. The basic principle of this system is that every respiratory cycle is divided into a fixed number of counts. The control of the ratio of inspiration time to expiration time is accomplished by selecting a variable time out of the fixed time interval and designating it inspiration time. The remaining counts become expiration time. Respiratory rate is adjusted by varying the total time interval, and ratio by selecting a different inspiration time. The output of digital to analog converter (DAC) driven by the counters is adjustable and proportional to tidal volume. By inserting read only memories between the ratio scalars and the DAC input, a large number of different inspiration waveforms are generated.
Name: ["Engelman Jr F.A.", "Cook A.M."]

Title: The recognition problem with time constraints
Source: USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics
Abstract: A RECOGNITION system with a fixed recognition time and a fixed maximum permissible waiting time is considered. The extremum of the probability of the exact classification of such a system as a function of the recognition time is investigated. The ergodic case is investigated. For the same case a study is made of the conditions of the closeness of the probability of exact classification of the recognition system with Gaussian time constraints to the probability of exact classification of a recognition system with fixed constraints. ¬© 1975.
Name: ["Kol'tsov P.P."]

Title: Synthesis of Autonomous Automata with Variable Structure.
Abstract: A multilevel method of the synthesis of variable structure automata is presented. It is shown that this method requires the minimal number of elementary automata and answers a learning time close to the minimum. It is found that multilevel automata can be used to control queueing processes.
Name: ["Ruszczynski Andrzej"]

Title: MANAGEMENT OF URBAN FREEWAY TRAFFIC.
Abstract: Surveillance system goals and techniques for achieving these goals are reviewed with particular emphasis on the problem of managing unexpected capacity-reducing incident situations. Recent research has demonstrated the feasibility of detecting incidents from traffic flow data, which is desirable for surveillance purposes because this information can be used to implement control strategies which attempt in real-time to divert some freeway traffic to alternate routes. Some of the operational problems involved with freeway traffic management are discussed, particularly the generation of false alarms by detection algorithms and driver willingness to be diverted to alternate routes.
Name: ["Cook Allen R."]

Title: APPROACH TO NONLINEAR SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION BASED ON B SPLINES.
Abstract: A dynamical system, described by a nonlinear integral operator of a general type and driven by a random input, is considered. It is assumed that only certain statistical properties of the input as well as a record of the output are available. The structure of the system is retrieved from the data by representing the unknown kernel of the integral operator in terms of an appropriate set of tri-variate B splines and estimating the parameters in this representation by a least square procedure.
Name: ["de Figueiredo Rui J.P."]

Title: INVESTIGATION OF SOME MULTIDIMENSIONAL EXTREMAL CONTROL SYSTEMS BY COMPUTER SIMULATION.
Abstract: Various methods for finding the extremum of a unimodal function by an extremal control system are considered. Several procedures for generalizing this system into a multidimensional one (from the point of view of autonomy of its individual subsystems) are proposed. Comparative characteristics of these procedures and their asymptotic behavior when the dimension of the system is increased, as obtained by computer simulation of the system, are presented.
Name: ["Sholokhov V.G.", "Grinchenko S.N."]

Title: Fan-In Constrained Tree Networks of Flexible Cells
Abstract: This paper is concerned with the synthesis of irredundant tree networks with two input single output flexible cells. An algorithm is developed which tests whether a given Boolean function is tree realizable; if it is tree realizable, a best tree is generated which realizes the function. It is shown that for each realizable function there exists a nontrivial unique partition from which a best tree can be constructed. Finally, the number of functions realizable by irredundant trees is determined. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Insttute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Chakrabarti K.", "Kolp O."]
Keywords: ["admissible partition", "best tree", "disjunctive decomposition of a function", "flexible cells", "irredundant tree"]

Title: ON A SET-THEORETICAL APPROACH TO SEMANTICS OF CONTEXT-FREE LANGUAGES.
Abstract: A method for semantic definition of context-free languages which is based on fixpoint methods is demonstrated by two examples. There are similarities to descriptions with the Vienna definition language. The abstract interpreter, however, is defined as a function and not as a mechanism performing computations.
Name: ["Hattinger G.", "Plate H.", "Reinke R."]

Title: ALGORITHM FOR THE SOLUTION OF A LOCATION PROBLEM WITH METRIC CONSTRAINTS.
Abstract: In many location problems, the solution is constrained to lie within a closed set. In this paper, optimal solutions to a special type of constrained location problem are characterized. In particular, the location problem with the solution constrained to be within a maximum distance of each demand point is considered, and an algorithm for its solution is developed and discussed.
Name: ["Schaefer Margaret K.", "Hurter Jr. Arthur P."]

Title: On the selection of parameters in Self Scaling Variable Metric Algorithms
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of selecting the parameter in a family of algorithms for unconstrained minimization known as Self Scaling Variable Metric (SSVM) Algorithms. This family, that has some very attractive properties, is based on a two parameter formula for updating the inverse Hessian approximation, in which the parameters can take any values between zero and one. Earlier results obtained for SSVM algorithms apply to the entire family and give no indication of how the choice of parameter may affect the algorithm's performance. In this paper, we examine empirically the effect of varying the parameters and relaxing the line-search. Theoretical consideration also leads to a switching tule for these parameters. Numerical results obtained for the SSVM algorithm indicate that with proper parameter selection it is superior to the DFP algorithm, particularly for high-dimensional problems. ¬© 1974 The Mathematical Programming Society.
Name: ["Oren S.S."]

Title: A Geometric Model for Stochastic Automata
Abstract: This paper is concerned with the problem of equivalence and dominance relations between sequential stochastic machines. We first introduce the transition output stochastic automaton together with the notion of pseudoautomaton. In Section III, we establish some fundamental properties concerning the rank of a stochastic automaton. This yields the definition of a geometrical stochastic automaton (GSA), using the notion of polyhedral cones introduced in Section II. Section V is a systematic investigation of the set of GSA‚Äôs, mainly concerned with the relations between two GSA's. In Section VI we establish relations between a GSA and a stochastic automaton. Section VII proves the interest of the geometrical model by applying properties of GSA's to stochastic automata, to solve an open problem concerning minimization. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Insttute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Bancilhon F."]

Title: Convergence properties of the generalised least squares identitication method
Abstract: Convergence properties of the generalized least squares method are analyzed. The method can be interpreted as optimization of a likelihood function. The number of local maximum points of the likelihood function is examined. It is shown that this number is influenced by the signal to noise ratio. This theoretical result is illustrated by numerical examples using plant measurements. It is also proved that the method gives consistent estimates under suitable conditions. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["S√∂derstr√∂m T."]

Title: The role of sequential probabilities in lipreading
Abstract: A model of visual speech perception is proposed to account for the possible interaction between visual input and information stored within the individual concerning probability of occurrence of phenomes and their sequential or transitional probabilities. The model suggests that visual speech reception involves the formulation of hypotheses about incoming information and the confirmation or rejection of these hypotheses on the basis of subsequent inputs. An 'Instant Replay' capability is proposed to generate new hypotheses after previous ones have been rejected. An extremely low recognition threshold, based on the redundance of the language, is proposed which simplifies the operation of the model. One possible advantage of the model is that it suggests some easily testable ideas which may have implications for the training of hearing handicapped individuals.
Name: ["Lowell E.L."]

Title: A method of reaction to a syntactical error in a syntactically oriented translator
Source: USSR Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics
Abstract: AN ALGORITHM is proposed which permits a syntactical analysis to be continued after any syntactical error, one-symbol errors being corrected, and a choice, in some sense optimal, of the corrected version being made. ¬© 1975.
Name: ["Kaplunov M.I.", "Filatov V.I."]

Title: Simulation of Operations at a Face as First Step Toward Face Control. | [STREBSIMULATION ALS VORSTUFE FUER DIE STREBSTEUERUNG.]
Abstract: Paper describes a mathematical model that has been developed for the purpose of investigating the possibility of installing a central control station of face operations by means of monitoring and controlling programs. It is aimed at securing guidance toward elimination of down time, thus increasing the utilization rate of face equipment.
Name: ["Sill Dieter"]

Title: OPTIMUM CONTROL OF DISTRIBUTED PARAMETER SYSTEMS BY DIGITAL COMPUTER.
Abstract: In recent years the problem of optimizing control systems has become highly significant. In the case of systems of distributed parameters the discrete variational calculus and discrete maximum principle is used to give a calculation algorithm which can be directly programmed. The calculation method described finds a wide application in solving the problem of optimum control of different physical processes, that is, with the knowledge of parameters determining the system properties the optimum control vector as a function of space and time can be calculated.
Name: ["Lengyel L.", "Vajta Jr. M."]

Title: The imbedded state space approach to reducing dimensionality in dynamic programs of higher dimensions
Source: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
Abstract: By exploiting discontinuity properties of the maximal convolution it is possible to drastically reduce dimensionality in finite dynamic programs. In fact, we show how the search over the usual M-dimensional state space can be reduced to a one-dimensional search over an imbedded state space. The versatility of our approach is illustrated on a number of example problems. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Morin T.L.", "Esogbue A.M.O."]
Affiliations: [' Northwestern University', ' Georgia Institute of Technology']

Title: ON THE OPTIMALITY OF THE BAYES PREDICTION POLICY IN TWO-ECHELON MULTISTATION INVENTORY MODELS.
Abstract: It is proved that the Bayes prediction ordering policy developed is an optimal policy, in the sense that it minimizes the total expected discounted cost of ordering for any finite planning horizon.
Name: ["Zacks S."]

Title: EXPECTED NUMBER OF STEPS IN SUCCESSIVE APPROXIMATION TYPE ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: It is difficult to ensure convergence for asymptotically optimum algorithms in case of real time. This paper shows how the convergence rate is possible to be numerically determined in time. To decide the applicability of real time or evaluate the convergence speed and accuracy of an algorithm, it is solved only for specific cases. An algorithm nearly optimal for solving a task can rarely be used to solve other tasks. As the procedure used for examining error probability in the MONTE-CARLO methods applies to the case of any arbitrary signal distribution, so the described calculation simulating the convergence speed of the successive approximation-type algorithms is generally valid not regarding the task-dependence.
Name: ["Bencsik I."]

Title: Problem of Application of Laplace Transforms to Linear Control Systems with Variable Parameters. | [K VOPROSU PRIMENENIYA PREOBRAZOVANIYA LAPLASA K LINEINYM SISTEMAM AVTOMATICHESKOGO REGULIROVANIYA S PEREMENNYMI PARAMETRAMI.]
Abstract: Analytical results are obtained which make it possible to indicate a class of automatic control systems with variable parameters for which Laplace transforms can prove to be an effective means of analysis. This is namely for linear automatic control systems with a limited variable matrix of coefficients of the differential equation describing these systems. A general approach in applying the Laplace transform to systems with polynomial and fractional-linear coefficients is outlined. Equations are presented for deriving the parametric transfer function for the said class of systems. Theorems about the behavior of the parametric transfer function as a function of a complex variable are obtained.
Name: ["Malashenko V."]

Title: IMAGE EVALUATION OF IMAGE INTENSIFIERS.
Abstract: An objective image evaluation of image intensifiers consists of measuring the parameters that effect detection or recognition probabilities. The most important parameters are the cathode sensitivity, the noise figure, integration time constants and image transfer characteristics. The first three parameters have no equivalent in optical systems. To qualify image transfer characteristics in optical systems, the concept of the optical or modulation transfer function is well established. Also, in image intensifiers, the MTF is widely used as a quality criteria. Quite some efforts have been spent to determine the functional dependence of detection probabilities on the MTF, and to justify the concept of the MTF for image intensifiers. The result are at least doubtful.
Name: ["Pollehn Herbert K."]

Title: An adaptive information retrieval system using partial file inversion
Abstract: The retrieval of information by means of freely-chosen descriptors may be handled efficiently by creating an inverted file organization in an adaptive manner, entries in this file being generated by sequential searching of the master file, when required. A system design utilizing this concept and incorporating features to generate file keys of wide generality, to minimise sequential searching, and to regulate the size of the inverted file, is described. Operational parameters which can be varied to tune the system for efficient operation are discussed. Some potential applications of this type of retrieval system are presented. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Reardon B.C."]

Title: REAL-TIME IDENTIFICATION OF CONTINUOUS LINEAR SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A method is presented of estimating the coefficients of linear differential equations based on measuring the input and output signals of identified systems. In comparison with other methods this method offers relatively very accurate results. It does not require a special type of input signal and is suitable for real-time identification under operating conditions.
Name: ["Zampa Pavel"]

Title: Testing flow graph reducibility
Source: Journal of Computer and System Sciences
Abstract: Many problems in program optimization have been solved by applying a technique called interval analysis to the flow graph of the program. A flow graph which is susceptible to this type of analysis is called reducible. This paper describes an algorithm for testing whether a flow graph is reducible. The algorithm uses depth-first search to reveal the structure of the flow graph and a good method for computing disjoint set unions to determine reducibility from the search information. When the algorithm is implemented on a random access computer, it requires O(E log<sup>*</sup>E) time to analyze a graph with E edges, where log<sup>*</sup>x=min{i{norm of matrix}log<sup>(i)</sup>x‚â§1}. The time bound compares favorably with the O(E log E) bound of a previously known algorithm. ¬© 1974 Academic Press, Inc.
Name: ["Tarjan R.E."]

Title: ON A NEW DECOMPOSITION SOLUTION OF THE SPARSE SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The contribution deals with the decomposition of large-scale systems described by the large sparse sets of the algebraic equations of the given structure. Use is made of the zero elements of the relevant matrix to reduce the number of the arithmetical operations by the computation of the system. The derived method employs the graph theory approach. The results form the introduction of the fluidum concept, the formulation of the operation criterion and the derived optimization algorithms. The formulated conclusions generalize the present conception of the Kron decomposition method.
Name: ["Bakule Lubomir"]

Title: FUZZY REPRESENTATION, CNF MINIMIZATION AND THEIR APPLICATION TO FUZZY TRANSMISSION STRUCTURES.
Abstract: Generalizations of binary switching networks are described, emphasizing special minimization techniques needed in order to extend Boolean procedures to fuzzy contact systems and to fuzzy transmissions. The elementary properties of the specific fuzzy algebra are analyzed in great detail and a matrix treatment of fuzzy contact systems is investigated.
Name: ["Kandel Abraham"]

Title: The brain wave equation: a model for the EEG
Abstract: Both spontaneous and evoked potentials measured on the surface of the head are believed due to postsynaptic potentials in vertically oriented neurons in the cortex. Potential differences between surface locations at any given time are due to the instantaneous difference in synaptic activity between the corresponding vertical regions. Because of the high correlation of activity between regions separated by distances large compared to the radius of influence of single neurons, communication between these locations must be by means of action potentials. In order to quantify the dynamics of interaction of 10<sup>10</sup> cortical neurons, use is made of the concept of a neural mass. The neural mass consists of sufficiently large number of neurons so as to exhibit certain average properties which are independent of its exact inner circuitry. An integral wave equation is derived to describe the spatial-temporal variation of cortical potential. Solutions are obtained indicating that electrical oscillations, which are independent of the location and time history of subcortical input, can persist in the cortex. The nature of these oscillations depends on the relative abundance of excitatory and inhibitory connections between neural masses and on the physiological state of the brain. The latter is partially determined by velocity distribution functions for action potential propagation. A dispersion relation for brain waves is shown to exist for certain ranges of the connection parameters. In some limiting cases, weakly damped waves occur with œâ=ck, where c refers to a characteristic velocity for the distribution functions. Preliminary experiments indicate qualitative agreement with this result. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Nunez P.L."]

Title: A model of activity I and sleep
Abstract: Two models of activity and sleep are presented, each of which is based on the notion of an internal state of arousal. The first model is essentially an activity drive model which fails because it predicts that the organism will never sleep. The second model makes more direct physiological assumptions about the build-up of arousal in the brain. For reasonable parameters, arousal builds up so far beyond the optimal level that the only way to bring it back into bounds is to cut off all external stimulation. Thus the model predicts a circadian rhythm not because of a biological clock but as the byproduct of the interaction between two processes (activity and arousal) neither of which is separately periodic in function. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Hunter J.E."]

Title: CONVERGENCE OF THE LOGARITHM OF THE LIKELIHOOD RATIO TO A WIENER PROCESS IN THE PROBLEM OF DETECTING AN ARBITRARY SIGNAL IN WHITE NOISE.
Abstract: It is shown that a necessary and sufficient condition for the convergence of a finite-dimensional distribution of the logarithm of the likelihood ratio to the distribution of a Wiener process whose mathematical expectation and variance are equal to the limits of the corresponding moments of the distribution, is the mean-square convergence of the energy of the output data of the block of optimal estimation (with a special choice of time scale) to its mean value. Expressions for the probability densities of a transition are obtained.
Name: ["Sosulin Yu.G.", "Fishman M.M."]

Title: FAMILY OF DISCRETE HAAR TRANSFORMS.
Abstract: A new class of discrete orthogonal transforms called generalized Haar transforms, (GHT)//r is defined and developed. The base functions of (GHT)//r are linear combinations of Haar functions. Pertinent properties of (GHT)//r such as, linearity, uniqueness, dyadic autocorrelation, and dyadic shift invariance are developed. By factoring the transform matrices into a number of sparse matricces efficient algorithms for fast computation of (GHT)//r and its inverse are developed. By subjecting these algorithms to successive bit-reversal operations, a single processor such as the Cooley-Tukey type can be used for implementing all the transforms. Specific examples illustrating the (GHT)//r, its properties and the fast algorithms are included.
Name: ["Rao K.R.", "Narasimhan M.A.", "Revuluri K."]

Title: AUTOMATIC RECOGNITION OF FRICATIVES AND PLOSIVES IN CONTINUOUS SPEECH.
Abstract: A linear prediction method, the Low-Coefficient LPC, produces meaningful spectra, that serve as input to a computer program that isolates and classifies fricatives and plosives in continuous speech. Method and results are presented.
Name: ["Molho Lee"]

Title: MAN-COMPUTER PROBLEM SOLVING IN COMPUTER COMMUNICATION NETWORKS.
Abstract: Development and operation of computer-communication networks involve a number of optimization problems. Often such problems cannot be solved using mathematical programming procedures and must be handled by means of heuristic methods. This paper presents a suboptimum problem solving method based on a man-computer procedure termed the heuristic branching method, whereby man determines probable directions of search, while the computer executes the problem-solving procedure and evaluates the results obtained. These data are used by the human operator in further problem solving iterations for adjusting the recommendations given to the computer.
Name: ["Samoylenko S."]

Title: FUZZY SET AND AUTOMATA THEORY APPLIED TO ECONOMICS.
Abstract: Fuzzy set and automata theory is shown to be useful in modeling qualitative aspects of economic systems. The individual consumer's preference structure, a basic concept in microeconomics, is represented by fuzzy sets and operations on fuzzy sets. Fuzzy automata are used to model individuals' formulations of their voting strategies in social choice theory.
Name: ["Hatten Mary Louise", "Whinston Andrew B.", "Fu K.S."]

Title: PARTIALLY OBSERVABLE MARKOV DECISION PROCESS MODEL OF MEDICAL DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT.
Abstract: This paper models medical diagnosis and treatment as a partially observable Markov decision process with a terminating state. After formulating the problem the paper concentrates on results describing the form of the optimal policy under reasonable sufficient conditions.
Name: ["Hockstra Dale"]

Title: ON DETERMINATION OF OPTIMAL TIME OBSERVATION OF NONSTATIONARY STOCHASTIC PROCESS.
Abstract: Optimum time observation of nonstationary random signal is dealt with considering that a nonstationary random signal y(t) with the constant average value u and cross correlation function R//x//y(t, tau ) is obtained as an output of nonstationary filter excited by Gaussian white noise x(t).
