The filter formed is described by weight function g( tau ,t) (or by transfer function G(s,t)) with coefficients changing in time.
Name: ["Kuszta Boguslaw"]

Title: EDUCATION IN SYSTEMS AND CONTROL THEORY - AN INTERACTIVE SYSTEM.
Abstract: A time-sharing, interactive system is presented which uses graphical displays as man machine interfaces. In a first stage, the system is only devoted to the education in linear control theory and application. With the automatic control language as a guide, the authors first worked out a high level interactive language, oriented towards model description: differential systems, matrices, vectors, transfer function equations. Then, to this external description, an internal problem representation has been effected, thus allowing at any time, a proper image of the problem resolution state. The implementation difficulties of such a computer system are described in the paper. Different ways of taking advantage of this educational interactive system are also described.
Name: ["Calvez J.P.", "Elloy J.P.", "Thomas Y."]

Title: SYSTEMS OPTIMIZATION WITH UNKNOWN CRITERIA.
Abstract: The goals represented in criterion functions for systems optimization make undependable bases for systems design. A system's goals are not well-defined and are difficult to predict in advance of experiences with the designed system. Systems almost always pursue many noncomparable and partially inconsistent goals, and these goals may be represented by criterion functions, by constraints, and even by control policies. Systems designers should strive to preserve the legitimacy of multiple goals and should avoid relying upon prior information. The process of systems optimization should be treated as a sequential search in which delays are accepted in order to elicit information about the system and its environment.
Name: ["Starbuck William H."]

Title: MICROPROGRAMMABLE MULTI-PROCESSOR (MMP) SYSTEM FOR SIMULTANEOUS EMULATION OF INTEROPERATING COMPUTER SYSTEMS.
Abstract: The heart of a Teleprocessing Design Center that has been established within the Communications/Automatic Laboratory of the US Electronics Command (ECOM) at Fort Monmouth, New Jersey is the microprogrammable multiprocessor system which will provide the capability of simultaneously emulating up to two interoperating Army Tactical Data Systems. This paper describes that system, including the hardware and key software modules, and provides a detailed look at its use.
Name: ["Mattson Roy", "Salisbury Alan"]

Title: CELLULAR ARRAYS FOR ASYNCHRONOUS CONTROL.
Abstract: A microprogrammable array for realizing an asynchronous control structure is presented. The arrays realize structures which allow sequencing of operations, conditional branch, subroutine call, fork operation to create parallel processes, join of parallel processes, merging of control, and arbitration with semaphore primitives to achieve controlled access to limited resources. The circuits obtained are asynchronous and speed independent. The microprogrammed array is a cellular form of C, S, NOR, XOR synthesis of Petri Nets.
Name: ["Patil Suhas S."]

Title: ON STORAGE OPTIMIZATION OF HORIZONTAL MICROPROGRAMS.
Abstract: Micro-instruction generation for horizontally microprogrammable computers is examined in order to reduce the number of required micro-instructions for a loop-free segment of micro-operations. The micro-instruction generation process is analyzed and two optimization methods are presented. The first method is algorithmic in that it will always generate the minimum micro-instruction set for a given subblock of micro-operations. The other method is heuristic and does not always result in the minimum micro-instruction set. The methods are shown to achieve better results than those of the existing methods.
Name: ["Yau S.S.", "Schowe A.C.", "Tsuchiya M."]

Title: AUTOMATIC CLASSIFICATION METHODS APPLIED TO MULTISPECTRAL PHOTOGRAPHY.
Source: Conf on Earth Resour Obs and Inf Anal Syst, Remote Sensing of Earth Resour
Abstract: An evaluation of automatic processing methods is reported, as applied to multispectral photography, which was obtained in a program concerning the airborne mapping of recent geology. The imagery was obtained with a cluster of five cameras, then digitized by a computer controlled densitometer, and processed further by a digital computer. Preprocessing of the data appeared to be essential in order to remove systematic distortions. Several classification methods, both statistical and non-statistical, were implemented and applied to the imagery of a test area. The methods studied comprise the maximum-likelihood decision rule, the sequential decision rule, the minimum distance to mean criterion, the linear discriminant method and a non-supervised clustering method. For classification purposes the maximum-likelihood decision rule appears to be most suitable.
Name: ["Beers J.N.P.", "van Kuilenburg J."]

Title: COMPUTER CONTROL OF SUBMERGED ARC FERROALLOY FURNACE OPERATIONS.
Source: Electr Furn Proc Metall Soc AIME
Abstract: Closed loop computer control of two large ferrosilicon furnaces, their auxiliary subsystems, mix batching system and total plant power demand has been implemented at the Ashtabula, Ohio, plant of the Ferroalloys Division of Union Carbide Corp. All phases of the control are technically successful. At the Alloy, W. Va. , plant the computer control application of the new metal silicon furnace, its auxiliaries and the automated mix batching system is nearing completion. Monitoring of all phases of the operation, and data collection and logging are already operating. A description of computer hardware, control software and operator and process interfaces are included in the discussion. Observation of the computer controlled operations of the ferrosilicon furnaces to date indicates that the anticipated operating improvements will be fully realized.
Name: ["Wilbern W.L."]

Title: On the integral equations of the linear theory of recurrent lateral interaction in vision
Abstract: In a spatially homogeneous visual system with linear, recurrent, lateral interactions that fall off with distance at large distances, the response field is related to the excitation field through a functional equation involving convolution of the response with an "interaction kernel" which characterizes the system. We discuss here the general theory of solutions of such equations in Bochner's F<sub>k</sub>-spaces, and we present explicit solutions for some special cases in which the interaction kernel is "bimodal," i.e., achieves its maximum absolute value at a non-zero distance of separation of sensory points. Bimodal kernels are of interest because they appear to be in qualitative accord with physiological data, and, as is known, a linear recurrent system with such a kernel can yield a transfer function whose maximum value is finite and occurs at a finite, non-zero, spatial frequency. Such a recurrent system with a bimodal kernel and a regular transfer function can, however, also show "oscillations," i.e., multiple turning points, in the response to a simple step-function excitation field. To help study this last phenomenon, we derive resolvent functions for integral equations in a class which generalizes the classical Lalesco-Picard equation. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Coleman B.D.", "Renninger G.H."]

Title: Numerical taxonomy with fuzzy sets
Abstract: A recently developed fuzzy clustering technique is utilized to analyze the substructure of a well known set of 4-dimensional botanical data. A solution obtained without prior knowledge of labelled pattern structure is offered in support of our contention that the technique proposed affords a comparatively reliable criterion for a posteriori evaluation of cluster validity. ¬© 1974 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Bezdek J.C."]

Title: A real time picture processor for use in biologic cell identification. I. System design
Abstract: The class of special purpose picture processors has common characteristics which set it apart from conventional general purpose computers. The authors argue for the implementation of a fast serial processor of gray scale images having easy access to a tessellated gray scale neighborhood, where the tessellation of a neighborhood is the movement of that neighborhood through the image array in some deterministic way. Such a machine would be very useful in an interactive system used for problems such as the design of effective procedures for automated cell classification.
Name: ["Lemkin P.", "Carman G.", "Lipkin L.", "Shapiro B.", "Schultz M.", "Kaiser P."]

Title: Image processing in pathology. II. Object isolation and contour fitting | AUTOMATISCHE BILDVERARBEITUNG IN DER PATHOLOGIE. II. OBJEKTISOLIERUNG UND KONTURAUSGLEICH
Abstract: In image processing there is often the problem that single objects have to be isolated from object clusters. For this purpose a new procedure is proposed: following the isolation of object clusters, their contour curve is determined in individual contour points. Isolated contour segments of single objects are then subjected to an elliptical equalization. The method is demonstrated by means of an example.
Name: ["Voss K."]

Title: Ein verallgemeinertes adaptives Modell zur Beschreibung von Lern- und Identifikationsprozessen
Abstract: From the similarity in mathematical structure of the linear learning model of Bush and Mosteller and of identification methods based on the gradient method, an adaptive model encompassing both problems is derived which allows the statistical description of learning processes in stationary or non-stationary environment and of identifying processes for linear, time-variable systems with a distorted output signal. ¬© 1974 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["H√∂ge H."]
Affiliations: ['Mitteilung aus dem Zentrallaboratorium f√ºr Nachrichtentechnik der Siemens AG']

Title: An automatic microscope system for differential leukocyte counting
Abstract: Described are the operation and special purpose hardware of a practical system for an automatic differential leukocyte count. The system is based on an extended memory configuration minicomputer. Major features of the system are: a high speed, 3 axis, servo controlled microscope stage; a cell location sensor; a special slowed scan; a 2 spectral band television camera for direct computer input; and a focus signal generated from the camera, with the loop closed through the computer. The camera and monochrome monitor scan a 256 x 256 element frame 15 times/sec. The original or modified images may be displayed from the computer memory. The performance goal is the processing of one cell/sec, with the identification of 17 or more cell types.
Name: ["Dew B.", "King T.", "Mighdoll D."]

Title: Multivariate clustering procedures with variable metrics
Abstract: Several multivariate clustering methods are analyzed in which each cluster may have a different metric depending on its covariance matrix. Numerical experiments show that the only reliable method among these is one using a metric suggested by Rohlf [1970] based on the within cluster covariance matrix normalized for unit determinant. (12 references.)
Name: ["Maronna R.", "Jacovkis P.M."]

Title: SYSTEM FOR PROGRAM SYNTHESIS FROM EXAMPLES.
Abstract: An autoprogrammer is an interactive computer programming system which accepts as input example calculations and which yields computer programs for doing those calculations. Such a system provides the user with a sort of scratch pad and command system for executing the examples, and it synthesizes programs on the basis of a recorded history of the steps required to do those computations. This paper briefly describes an autoprogramming system which is currently under development by the authors.
Name: ["Biermann A.W.", "Krishnaswamy R."]

Title: Some properties of randomly connected networks of neuron-like elements with refractory
Abstract: Dynamic properties of randomly connected networks consisting of neuron-like elements with refractory are investigated from a macroscopic point of view. Equations describing the transition of the activity level of the network - a macroscopic state - are derived under some hypotheses on the stochastic properties of the network. The equations are characterized by a set of parameters which are determined by distributions of the threshold values of elements and the weighting values of connection between elements. It is shown that a network behaves like a monostable, bistable or astable circuit when its refractory period is less than one time unit and that a network is monostable or bistable when its refractory period is longer than two time units. An oscillatory network, on the other hand, is always realized if the network has a feedback mechanism which decreases the excitability of neurons when high activity level is sustained. Some results of computer simulation of randomly connected neuron networks are also presented. ¬© 1974 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Yoshizawa S."]

Title: MICROPROGRAMMED OPERATIONS FOR A THREE-VALUE LOGIC SIMULATOR.
Abstract: An application of microprogramming to improve the performance of the three-value simulation part of a logic design verification system is described. Emphasis is placed on developing a theory of computing three-value logic functions in such a way that identical independent functions may be computed in parallel. As a result, it is possible to simulate a number of nearly identical machines simultaneously.
Name: ["Squires Stephen L."]

Title: RAPID EXECUTION PROGRAM TO CALCULATE FOUR MEASURES OF DISTRIBUTION AND WARN OF NON - NORMALITY.
Abstract: A program is defined that outputs a warning directly on the data summary when the distribution of the collected data deviates from the Gaussian by an amount sufficient to invalidate the statistical inference.
Name: ["Quigley S.R.", "Davis D.W.", "Collins L.S."]

Title: PHONOLOGICAL COMPONENT OF AN AUTOMATIC SPEECH-RECOGNITION SYSTEM.
Abstract: One of the problems encountered in speech recognition is that of associating with each of the possible phonetic realizations of a particular utterance, the probability of that production as a realization of the utterance. To deal with this problem in the speech-recognition system being constructed at IBM, the authors developed a phonological-rule component which employs: (1) A lexicon of American English phonemic base forms; (2) A set of phonological rules to account statistically for phonemic and major allophonic variation resulting from idiolect, dialect, style and pace, and (3) An algorithm for applying the rule to the base forms for the generation of phonological variants. The generation and format of the base forms, the statistical raison d'etre of the rules, and the logistics of the algorithm for applying the rules are described.
Name: ["Cohen P.S.", "Mercer R.L."]

Title: AN INTELLIGENT TERMINAL PROCESSOR.
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to describe the design and architecture of a current CPU design. Some aspects of processor architecture which have tended to produce compact and powerful machine code in this machine are discussed. Microprogramming has become a more powerful and economic design tool with the availability of inexpensive user-programmable ROM integrated circuits. In this paper, an application of ideas related to microprogram sequence generation is explained. As a direct result of this sequence generation technique, large benefits are shown in effective microprogram capabilities.
Name: ["Hatch David"]

Title: SOME ASPECTS OF AN INTERACTIVE DIALOGUE-GENERATION FACILITY.
Abstract: There is a rapidly growing demand for computer access by persons who are not computer professionals. This demand is being met by the development of a wide variety of man-computer dialogues. The need for rapid development of large numbers of dialogues creates a need for special-purpose systems. In this paper, an interactive programming system for the generation of man-computer dialogues is introduced. The types of dialogues this system can generate, and the tools provided by the system for dialogue generation, are discussed.
Name: ["Stallings William"]

Title: APPLICATION OF STOCHASTIC OPTIMIZATION THEORY TO FAMILY PLANNING AND FERTILITY CONTROL.
Abstract: A dynamic stochastic optimization model of human fertility control is formulated and analyzed in the context of a well-known stochastic optimization problem. Conditions for optimality and a separation result are presented for the optimization model, and implications of generalizations of the optimization model on the resultant dynamic programming equation are discussed.
Name: ["White Chelsea C."]

Title: ADAPTIVE MODELING OF PSYCHOTROPIC DRUG EFFECTS.
Abstract: Adaptive modeling techniques developed for aerospace and industrial applications are also finding their way intothe evaluation of psychotropic (mind-influencing) drugs. This paper presents recent applications of adaptive modeling algorithms to evaluation of drug-induced EEG changes. The adaptive techniques are applied to EEG time waveform data to model nonlinearly two quantities: the bioavailability of a compound and the equivalent dosage of two different compounds. These quantities are modeled as functions of the post-pre drug changes in frequency content of the EEG waveform.
Name: ["Mucciardi Anthony N."]

Title: USING INTEGRAL PERFORMANCE CRITERIA FOR APPROXIMATE SYNTHESIS OF OPTIMAL CONTROL FUNCTION OF SECOND-ORDER DYNAMIC SYSTEMS.
Abstract: Nearly optimal switching lines are constructed for various cases of linear oscillatory systems and one nonlinear oscillatory system.
Name: ["Priezzhev A.V."]

Title: Real-Time Evaluation of Fluctuating Parameters. | [REAL-TIMEOVE HODNOCENI FLUKTUJICICH PARAMETRU.]
Source: Sb Ved Pr Vys Sk Banske Ostrave Rada Hutn
Abstract: The problem of real-time analyses of stochastic signals is discussed. The existing methods of measuring and evaluating parameters with random character are outlined and a number of practical examples are presented. The possibilities of evaluation with the aid of code symbols are dealt with and special devices developed for this purpose are shown.
Name: ["Janousek Ivo"]

Title: Evolutionary learning circuits
Abstract: This paper presents a theory of the central nervous system based on information processing concepts suitable for describing molecular biological systems. The main features of the theory are (1) the CNS consists of various types of unit regions of which there are many interchangeable replicas; (2) each region contains neurons whose firing is determined by excitase enzymes which recognize specific patterns of inputs and which may be coded by genes which are either heritable or culturable; (3) the CNS has selection circuits which test and evaluate individual regions and which control the production of culturable excitase genes on the basis of this evaluation. The genes whose production is stimulated diffuse out of the regions in which they are produced to transform other, competent regions of the same type. The function of the excitase molecules is the same in these new regions because the tissue structure and cellular properties are the same. This makes it possible for trial and error learning to be mediated by the same mechanisms as natural evolution, except that it is more efficient due to the selection circuits. Systems operating on the above basis are capable of performing any operation performable by a conventional computer, but with certain important restrictions on programmability. Such systems are also (structurally) simpler than conventional information processing devices and more amenable to learning and evolution. The theory makes a number of definite predictions about the CNS, some of which correspond to known facts and others of which are testable. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Conrad M."]

Title: Bedside processors handle intensive care in hospitals
Abstract: Automatic, around the clock monitoring of patients' life functions by computerized systems has been a dream of the future to most hospitals. But centralized, minicomputer based systems cost too much, and their failure could be catastrophic. But a new distributed intelligence system, based on low cost LSI microprocessors and hard wired controllers, puts independent control elements at each patient's bedside.
Name: ["Editorial"]

Title: A Markov process model for dynamic control of emissions
Abstract: A simple model is developed to evaluate the potential of emission control policies that depend upon meteorological forecasts. An optimal control policy is derived for this model and related analytical results are obtained. A more realistic model leading to a linear programming formulation is discussed and illustrated by means of an example.
Name: ["Patel N.R."]

Title: MORE ON THE MUTUAL INFORMATION PRINCIPLE FOR PRIOR MODELING.
Abstract: Some new results are presented on the use of the Mutual Information Principle (MIP) (see Engineering Index 1973 abstract 026567) for modeling random variables (r. v. 's), while utilizing all available information. The finite range, discrete r. v. case with absolute value error function is solved. An interpretation of the role of the error function is presented. The solution to the continuous r. v. prior modeling is given a linear systems interpretation. Finally, the MIP is extended to conditional prior PDF via a communication channel modeling illustration.
Name: ["Noonan Joseph P.", "Tzannes Nicholas S."]

Title: NEW DEVELOPMENTS IN WATER SHED POLLUTION FORECASTING USING ADAPTIVE TRAINABLE NETWORKS.
Abstract: An example is given of recent applications of Adaptive Trainable Network modeling techniques to demonstrate their utility. In this example, network models are presented that forecast total phage concentration in the Potomac River as a function of simply measured environmental variables such as river flow rate, river staging, tide levels, precipitation, and average daily temperature. It is shown that the networks are able to make these forecasts with an average accuracy of 95. 2% throughout a 12-day forecasting period.
Name: ["Mucciardi Anthony N."]

Title: DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION OF A SYSTEM TO TRANSLITERATE THAI BY COMPUTER.
Abstract: This paper describes the construction of a computer system that accepts Thai words as input and produces as output a Romanized transliteration. The components of the system are an IBM 1800 computer, a Thai and a Roman character printing Shinko teletype, a string processing language and an interpreter program for this language.
Name: ["Warotamasikkhadit Udom", "Londe David", "Kanchanawan Nitaya"]

Title: Model of a plausible learning scheme for CA3 Hippocampus
Abstract: There is ample evidence that mammalian Hippocampus, defined as ammon's horn sectors 1 through 4, can learn. In particular, sector CA3 is presumed able to learn to produce a wide range of appropriate output patterns in response to extrinsic inputs arriving over the mossy fiber, temporo-ammonic, septo-hippocampal, and commissural systems. The neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of CA3 have been studied extensively, but the information conveyed by its signals and the way its circuit actions represent decisionary and memory functions remain elusive. Several roles have been posited for the Hippocampus in the guidance of animal behavior, but they are not inter-related in any clear way, and seem separated by several levels of abstraction from the circuit actions which actually embody decisionary and memory functions. We present a plastic circuit model of the CA3 sector and discuss its computer simulation as a caricature of developmental and neurophysiological processes. In particular, we concentrate on plausible ways in which excitatory and inhibitory interneurons can learn to properly influence articulate pyramidal cell output patterns under the guidance of only diffuse positive or negative reinforcement. Statistical learning in interneuronal-to-pyramidal synapses is posited to occur in one cell cluster after another until the overall circuit matures. A kind of intra-pyramidal Markovian learning is also posited and simulated, with quite remarkable results. A list of critical assumptions each of which is testable in principle is given, so the model can be thoroughly tested. The effect of each assumption is documented by computer simulation data. ¬© 1974 Springer-Verlag.
Name: ["Kilmer W.", "Olinski M."]

Title: Histoquantitation using computer data cards
Abstract: This paper describes a new approach to histoquantitation which makes fuller use of the visual expertise of the microscopist, provides a permanent visual two‚Äêdimensional coded record, and allows mathematical exploitation of the collected data. The microscopic image of the specimen is traced directly onto computer data cards. A simple sketch records accurate quantitative data for areas and boundaries of as many components of the image as required, in a matrix of 840 points. Spatial relationships are maintained. The matrix is transferred by an Optical Mark Data Card Reader into a computer for extraction of a maximum of information. 1974 Blackwell Science Ltd
Name: ["Meinhard E."]

Title: Stochastic models for single neuron firing trains: a survey
Abstract: The spontaneous firing activity of single neurons can be viewed in the framework of stochastic modelling. Of special interest in this regard is the point process defined by the times at which neuronal discharges occur. In this paper, point process models for the spike (discharge) train of spontaneous active neurons are considered. The main physiological features included in most of these models are excitation, inhibition, temporal summation, and decay. Since all the point processes considered are stationary, interest is focused on the interspike interval distribution associated with each model. The aims of this paper are 2 fold: to survey an extensive yet disparate literature on stochastic models for neuron firing; and to introduce this literature to biomathematicians and statisticians who may be called upon to analyze neural data collected by their biological colleagues.
Name: ["Fienberg S.E."]

Title: Programs and "programs" for sequential patterns in motor behavior
Abstract: Sequences of discrete movements that are relatively slow offer a problem of temporal structure to the brain. Some attempts to analyze the structure of such tasks as finger tapping and producing rhythmic sequences are discussed. In general the available models have dealt with temporal behavior in a strictly serial fashion. More recently higher-order structural aspects have become accessible. As an illustration of this approach the analysis of a piano composition of Erik Satie, Vexations, is discussed. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Michon J.A."]

Title: HYBRID SIMULATOR FOR DISCRETE CONTROL CORRECTION.
Source: IEEE Electron and Aerosp Syst Conv (EASCON '74), Rec
Abstract: This paper presents the results of a hybrid simulation of the synchronization of a digital data communication network by the method of discrete control correction. Three network nodes were constructed from modular integrated circuit hardware. The remaining nodes, simulation control and monitoring were implemented with a small general purpose minicomputer. The results presented illustrate the versatility of the simulator as well as the verification of stability in the discrete control correction technique.
Name: ["Perreault D.A.", "Mukundan R.", "Krishnan K.R."]

Title: SOLUTION OF THE BASIC CONTROL PROBLEM BY THE GRADIENT DESCENT METHOD.
Abstract: The typical engineering problem of determining the controls which insure satisfaction of dynamic system requirements specified in inequality form is formulated. This control problem, termed basic, reduces to a minimax problem. The solution of the minimax problem by the gradient descent method is examined.
Name: ["Bogomolov A.I.", "Sirazetdinov T.K."]

Title: SEVERAL ROLES OF MAN AS A SUPERVISOR OF ROBOTS.
Abstract: This paper proposes a taxonomy of roles played by the human supervisor of computer-controlled machines. The five principal categories of supervision proposed are: Communicating, planning, monitoring, intervening, and trusting. The paper briefly reviews some of the concepts and techniques by which the interaction between the supervisor and computer is augmented, as related to the five roles. The supervisory control paradigm employed is quite general, though as a specific example the paper considers a mechanical arm-hand directly controlled by a computer and performing simple assembly manipulation tasks.
Name: ["Sheridan Thomas B."]

Title: SPEAKING OF LEARNING MODELS.
Abstract: Psychological learning models are applied to the problem of real-time computer recognition of spoken words over a telephone. The learning and recognition properties of this approach are analyzed. Experimental results for a vocabulary of fourteen words spoken by fourteen children over a home telephone gave correct classification above 90 percent.
Name: ["Danforth Douglas g.", "Rogosa David R.", "Suppes Patrick"]

Title: Possibility for Direct Static Optimization of a Special Class of Linearizable Systems Having a Hierarchic Control Structure. | [EINE MOEGLICHKEIT ZUR DIREKTEN STATISCHEN OPTIMIERUNG EINER SPECIELLEN KLASSE LINEARISIERTER SYSTEME MIT HIERARCHISCHER STEUERUNGSSTRUKTUR.]
Abstract: The optimization of special systems is considered where the subsystems possess quadratic quality functions with respect to input and output magnitudes of the individual systems. The total quality function is additively structured from the quality subfunctions while the interaction relationships and the process characteristics are linear functions. For this class of systems, a programmable algorithm for the direct determination of the input quantities of the individual systems is presented so that the activities of the subsystems represent the optimum of the total system.
Name: ["Friedrich Bernd"]

Title: AUTOMATED ACCESS TO NETWORK RESOURCES. A NETWORK ACCESS MACHINE.
Abstract: A user accomplishing a task independent of a speciic host is inundated by the diaglogue necessary to gain access to a specific machine's resources. Several viable solutions exist to this user-oriented problem. This paper explores the Network Access Machine (NAM) developed at the National Bureau of Standards Institute for Computer Sciences and Technology. NAM expands user created macros to produce the interactive dialogue necessary to access the required resource on any heterogeneous network or on a remote access system. Real time analysis of system responses by the NAM gives the user flexibility in creating access procedures for the particular resources of individual computer systems.
Name: ["Rosenthal Robert", "Watkins Shirley W."]

Title: REAL-TIME COMPUTER SYSTEM FOR INTERACTIVE CONTROL OF MULTIPLE INDEPENDENT BEHAVIORAL EXPERIMENTS.
Abstract: The system, based on a PDP-11, is designed for the control and analysis of experiments in animal behavior. It uses a new language developed for use by scientists lacking training in computer programming. It permits simultaneous development and execution of on-line programs, as well as the summarization of stored data from prior experiments.
Name: ["Scroeder K.", "Hitch S.", "Migler B.", "Beer B."]

Title: SIMPLE ACCURATE POSITIONING SYSTEM FOR AN INDUSTRIAL ROBOT.
Abstract: A detailed description is given of a positioning system which basically consists of a number of mechanical stops attached to indexable bars such that there are a minimum number of 6 positions per axis. These stops are positioned as required and include a fine positioning adjustment. It is found that this system gives a positioning accuracy far greater than those commonly used with robots. The design of the hydraulic system and the control system for the fast to slow traverse are given together with test results obtained from a prototype system. The method of programming and the advantages and disadvantages are specified in a final discussion. In particular, how the system can be used in fairly complex operations such as palletizing is discussed.
Name: ["Rooks B.W.", "Tobias S.A."]

Title: COMPUTER ENHANCEMENT OF ACOUSTIC IMAGES.
Abstract: The quality of images available from acoustic systems is not always satisfactory to human observers. A digital image-processing technique, employing minicomputers and relatively inexpensive input-output equipment, has been used for image enhancement and noise removal in images produced by a Bragg-diffraction system. This paper describes the technique and shows the results of applying the method in the case of a particularly simple image of a hook.
Name: ["Takagi Mikio", "But Tse Nie", "Heidbreder Glenn R.", "Lee Chin-Hwa", "Wade Glen"]

Title: GRAPH INTERPRETATION OF ORDERING STRATEGIES IN GAUSSIAN ELIMINATION.
Abstract: The applications and the implications of Gaussian Elimination (G. E. ) in electric networks analysis are reviewed. The graph theoretic formulation of the optimization problem when pivots are taken on the main diagonal is described, and the optimization problem which arises when pivots are taken out of the main diagonal is formulated in a graph theoretic way. In order to describe the problem in this way, a theorem on the decomposition of non symmetric permutations and a theorem, which relates the cycle structure of the graph associated to M and column permutations, are given. A general schema of algorithm is described and some possible improvements are discussed.
Name: ["Sangiovanni Vincentelli A.", "Santomauro M."]

Title: SIMPLEX-LIKE ALGORITHM FOR CONTINUOUS-TIME LINEAR OPTIMAL CONTROL PROBLEMS.
Abstract: This paper is one of a group of three presenting a set of constructive techniques for the synthesis of solutions to linear control problems in the time continuum. Such problems are infinite-dimensional in principle, and usually give rise to very large systems under discrete approximation. The proposed constructs, although finite in structure, attack the problem without any inherent approximate discretization of the time continuum. The fundamental concepts of ‚Ä≥Generalized Functions‚Ä≥ and representation theory (under an extended concept of ‚Ä≥basis‚Ä≥ ), dealt with in two companion papers, are brought together in a construct which shows how to move from a starting ‚Ä≥basis‚Ä≥ to a new and improved ‚Ä≥basis‚Ä≥ . The construct is used successfully in solving a variety of small test examples.
Name: ["Drews William P."]

Title: ACQUISITION BEHAVIOR OF A DISCRETE NONLINEAR FREQUENCY ESTIMATOR.
Abstract: The acquisition and tracking of a noisy sinusoidal signal is an important problem in many areas of communications and control. Paper applies nonlinear estimation theory to this problem, and develops an estimator which estimates the frequency and phase of a sinusoidal signal from discrete observations. This estimator is essentially an adaptive discrete phase lock loop, with a second order time varying loop filter. Some results of a simulation study of the acquisition behavior of this estimator are presented.
Name: ["Pyle Robert H."]

Title: DIGITAL SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION AND ITS APPLICATION TO DIGITAL FLIGHT CONTROL.
Abstract: On-line system identification of linear discrete systems for implementation in a digital adaptive flight controller is considered by the conventional extended Kalman filter and a decoupling process in which the linear state estimation problem and the linear parameter identification problem are each treated separately and alternately. Input requirements for parameter identifiability are established using the standard conditions of observability for a time variant system. Experimental results for simulated linearized lateral aircraft motion are included along with the effect of different initialization and updating procedures for the priming trajectory used by the filter.
Name: ["Kotob S.", "Kaufman H."]

Title: NONLINEAR FILTERING APPLIED TO THE MODELING OF EARTHQUAKE DATA.
Abstract: A Taylor series approximation to the coefficients of a time varying differential equation is appended to the system state vector to create a nonlinear differential equation. A filtered estimate of the augmented state equation that results provides estimates of the original state, the unknown coefficients, and the variance of the system excitation noise (which is assumed white). The problem is one of determining an adequate approximation to the resulting nonlinear filter. Four different filters, which are closely related, have been tried. They are the extended Kalman filter; the Schwartz-Bass filter, which results from a second order approximation to the nonlinearities; a symmetric density assumption filter (i. e. , the conditional density is assumed symmetric), which for this problem reduces to the Schwartz-Bass filter; and a third moment filter, which results from retaining the third conditional moment equation and eliminating the fourth moment by assuming it can be written in terms of the second moment. The results of applying these filters to a typical earthquake record is presented.
Name: ["Gran Richard", "Kozin Frank"]

Title: TERNARY CELLULAR ARRAY.
Abstract: A cellular array that can realize any combinational ternary switching function is described. The cells are identical, each with a single ternary control input. Assigning these inputs to constants, variables, and the Post negations of variables determines the function to be realized. Several results concerning notation, evaluation, universal arrays, symmetric functions, and a few special functions are presented.
Name: ["Miller D.M.", "Muzio J.C."]

Title: Identification and Autoregressive Spectrum Estimation
Abstract: In recent years there has been increasing interest in autoregressive spectrum estimation. This procedure fits a finite autoregression to the time series data, and calculates the spectrum from the estimated autoregression coefficients and the one step prediction error variance. For multivariate time series, the estimated autoregressive matrices and one step prediction covariance matrix produce estimates of the spectra, coherences, phases, and group delays. The use of Akaike's information criterion (AIC) for identification of the order of the autoregression to be used makes the procedure objective. Experience gained from analyzing large amounts of data from the biological‚Äô and physical sciences has indicated that AIC works very well for model identification when compared to more subjective procedures such as the examination of partial F -statistics, This experience has also indicated that using both autoregressive spectrum estimation and classical spectrum estimation and superimposing the plots gives a much stronger feeling for the shape of the true spectrum being estimated. The results of some of these analyses are presented. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Jones R.H."]

Title: SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION ON DIGITAL TECHNIQUES. NEW TOOLS FOR DYNAMIC ANALYSIS.
Abstract: Recent developments in theories, computation softwares and instrumentations for frequency analysis and systems identification involving digital computations are reviewed and their applications to metal cutting process and machine tool dynamics are discussed. A description is presented of fundamental principles of the time series analysis and computing algorithms which involve complex Fourier Transform, fast Fourier Transform (FFT), correlation functions, and identification of dynamic systems based on conventional and generalized models which may be calculated in both frequency and time domains. Applications to machine tool dynamics, such as Fourier analysis of machine tool vibrations, evaluations and measurements of the cutting process dynamics, and transfer function measurements of machine tool structures are described with examples.
Name: ["Moriwaki T.", "Hoshi T."]

Title: SEQUENTIAL ADAPTIVE PREDICTIVE CODING OF SPEECH.
Abstract: This paper discusses a new method of speech digitization using sequentially adaptive algorithms in the adaptive predictive coding system proposed by B. Atal and M. Schroeder. The system can operate with a bit rate of 7 to 8 kilobits per second with a reproduced speech quality equivalent to 5 bit log PCM. While no effort has been made to minimize computational effort associated with the algorithm, the computational requirements are modest.
Name: ["Melsa J.L.", "Cohn D.L.", "Gibson J.D."]

Title: COMPUTER RECOGNITION OF AERIAL MULTISPECTRAL PHOTOGRAPHY USING OPTICAL DENSITY OF OBJECT.
Abstract: To maintain uniform performance in computer recognition of aerial multispectral photography, a simple calibration technique of atmospheric effects, exposure conditions, and film processing conditions is studied based on a concept of photographic photometry. Together with a grey step-wedge on the ground, the objects are photographed by a 4-band multispectral camera. From the wedge density data, an overall radiant energy transfer function of the system and the effects of atmospheric scattering can graphically be obtained for each multispectral band. The scanning density data of the image on the film are fed into a computer and converted into the reflection density data through the overall radiant energy transfer function of the system, and a computer recognition is carried out using the reflection density data.
Name: ["Yasuda Yoshizumi", "Emori Yasufumi"]

Title: MULTIPROGRAMMING APPROACH TO A SEQUENCE CONTROLLER.
Abstract: A new programmable logic controller is proposed with which a complex control system can be designed without resorting to an intuitive solution. In the present programmable logic controller, a number of simple, basic modules of sequential mechanism can be combined to form a complex sequence system; the complete system is synthesized during executions of programs by a multiprogramming method in which a number of parts sequence programs are controlled by scanning. Thus, even a complex system can be designed with ease, and the design time of a sequence control system can be reduced greatly.
Name: ["Hamano Goro"]

Title: FAST KARHUNEN LOEVE TRANSFORM FOR FINITE DISCRETE IMAGES.
Abstract: Some new results for digital signals defined over a finite interval are presented. It is shown that such signals may be represented by noncausal boundary value difference equations, and for a first order finite Markov sequence, the Karhunen Loeve (KL) transform which is normally given by a set of non-periodic sinusoidal functions reduces to periodic sine functions if the boundary conditions are given. Since periodic sine functions may be computed via fast Fourier transforms, this leads to a fast KL transform in signal processing problems such as optimum Wiener filtering, optimum coding, etc. , in the KL transform domain, and opens many other possibilities in digital signal processing.
Name: ["Jain Anil K."]

Title: CLOUD SCREENING FROM AERIAL PHOTOGRAPHY APPLYING COHERENT OPTICAL PATTERN RECOGNITION TECHNIQUES.
Abstract: A technique is discussed for cloud screening of aerial photography in which digital pattern recognition is used to process signals from a segmented spatial frequency detector in a coherent optical system. Relatively simple feature selection algorithms reduce the dimensionality of sample data, while providing effective cloud/non-cloud class separation in two-dimensional feature space. Several classification algorithms demonstrated cloud screening classification accuracies in excess of 95% on two sets of small-scale aerial photography obtained with mapping cameras. Analysis of the results has identified hardware modification in the coherent optical system which should lead to higher levels of performance.
Name: ["Lukes George E."]

Title: COMPUTER ASSISTED SYSTEM FOR COLLECTION OF BEHAVIORAL DATA.
Abstract: Collecting and recording simple events becomes difficult when large numbers of events and high rates of occurrence exist. A small computer is ideally suited to coping with this problem and the response time of the computer is so much faster than behavioral events that considerable manipulation of data can be carried out between them. This note describes a small computer interfaced to a series of ‚Ä≥plus-mazes‚Ä≥ in which the activity of test animals in a standard environment can be monitored.
Name: ["Marples T.G.", "Dodds J.R."]

Title: Sensitivity of the Performance Index to Shortening the Scope of Planning in a Linear-Quadratic Problem. | WRAZLIWOSC WSKAZNIKA JAKOSCI NA SKROCENIE HORYZONTU PLANOWANIA W PROBLEMIE LINIOWO-KWADRATOWYM.
Abstract: Optimal control problems are considered for which the optimal terminal state is of no interest and the scope of optimization T is not restricted. Many technological processes are of that type. In principle, such processes are controlled in the repetitive way with the repetition period T//p. The possibility of determining a suboptimal control on the basis of the suboptimization scope T*(T* less than T) instead of T is considered. The aim of the paper is to determine a relationship associating T, T*, T//p, process parameters and the value of the performance index. As a result, a numerical algorithm making it possible to evaluate the loss in the performance index as a function of T, T* and T//p is worked out.
Name: ["Krawczyk Jacek Bogdan"]

Title: SYNTHESIS OF MAITRA CASCADES.
Abstract: Application of a canonical synthesis method to network synthesis with the aid of the Maitra cascade is considered. The necessary and sufficient conditions for realizability of a Boolean function are found. Two synthesis algorithms are indicated.
Name: ["Blokh A.Sh.", "Pavlovskii A.L."]

Title: IMPROVED VERSION OF THE TABLE LOOK-UP ALGORITHM FOR PATTERN RECOGNITION.
Abstract: A new version of the table Look-Up Approach has been developed which is faster, requires significantly less core memory, and retains full precision of the input data. The new version can be used on low-cost minicomputers having 32K words (16 bits each) of core memory and fixed-point arithmetic; no special-purpose hardware is required. An initial FORTRAN version of this system can classify an ERTS computer-compatible tape into 24 classes in less than 15 minutes.
Name: ["Eppler W.G."]

Title: PATTERN RECOGNITION FOR CREDIT GRANTING.
Abstract: One key aspect of consumer credit evaluation is the prediction of payment behavior for new loan customers. This prediction can be modeled as a two-class pattern recognition problem where a variety of features are obtained from the loan application. This paper presents a feature selection technique designed to identify those features which contain the greatest information about the outcome of the loan. The technique, based on the information theory concept of average mutual information, makes no assumptions about any parametric distribution of the class outcomes in feature space.
Name: ["Boyle Brian F."]

Title: Parameter Estimation in Multivariate Stochastic Difference Equations
Abstract: We will review the principal methods of estimation of parameters in multivariate autoregressive moving average equations which have additional observable input terms in them and present some new methods of estimation as well. We begin with the conditions for the estimability of the parameters. In addition to the usual method of system representation, the canonical form I, we will present two new representations of the system equation, the socalled canonical forms II and III which are convenient for parameter estimation. We will mention, in some detail, the various methods of estimation like the various least-squares methods, the maximum likelihood methods, etc., and discuss them regarding their relative accuracy of the estimate and the corresponding computational complexity. We will introduce a new class of estimates, the so-called limited information estimates which utilizes the canonical forms II and III. The accuracy of these estimates is close to that of maximum likelihood, but their computation time is only a fraction of the computation time for the usual maximum. likelihood estimates. We will present a few numerical examples to illustrate the various methods. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Kashyap R.L.", "Nasburg R.E."]

Title: Some Recent Advances in Time Series Modeling
Abstract: The aim of this paper to describe some of the important concepts and techniques which seem to help provide a solution of the stationary time series problem (prediction and model identification). Section I reviews models. Section II reviews prediction theory and develops criteria of closeness of a ‚Äúfltted ‚Äú model to a ‚Äútrue‚Äù model. The central role of the infinite autoregressive transfer function g is developed, and the time series modeling problem is defined to be the estimation of g., Section III reviews estimation theory. Section √çV describes autoregressive estimators of g., It introduces a criterion for selecting the order of an autoregressive estimator which can be regarded as determining the order of an AR scheme when in fact the time series is generated by an AR scheme of finite order. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Parzen E."]

Title: Automatically controlled recording and processing of thalamic unit discharges in human stereotaxic operation
Abstract: The paper concerns 2 topics in the application of a data processing system that enables automatic exploration of unit discharges along the electrode track through the thalamus, and on line processing of pulse and analog signals obtained from the same electrode. The system would not only make physiological identification of the location more efficient but also make  it more quantitative and accurate.
Name: ["Saito Y.", "Ohye C."]

Title: Canonical Forms for the Identification of Multivariable Linear Systems
Abstract: The advantage of using a unique parameterization in a numerical procedure for the identification of a system from operating records has been well established. In this paper several sets of canonical forms are described for state space models of deterministic multivariable linear systems; the members of these sets having therefore the required uniqueness property within the equivalence classes of minimal realizations of the system. In the identification of a stochastic system, it is shown how the problem depends also upon determining a unique factorization of the spectral density matrix of the system, and the sets of canonical forms obtained for the deterministic system are extended to this case. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Denham M.J."]
Affiliations: [' Imperial College of Science and Technology']

Title: Plane autonomous state classifiers
Abstract: The theory of autonomous state classifiers in framed in the context of dynamical systems. Plane autonomous state classifiers are studied in depth within this context. A comprehensive theory of autonomous state classifiers is obtained. The relation of this theory to the problem of generalizing a saddle point is considered. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Engel A.B."]

Title: Dual Control Linear Discrete-Time Dynamic System. | STEROWANIE DUALNE LINIOWYM DYSKRETNYM OBIEKTEM DYNAMICZNYM.
Abstract: The paper is concerned with the dual control of a linear discrete-time single-input single-output system with constant but unknown parameters. The goal of a control action is to minimize the output variance. It is known that for such a case it is impossible to derive an effective formula determining a control strategy for the N-step control problem. To overcome this difficulty, a simple approximate control strategy is used. At every step of control, the output variance for one step ahead is minimized. The derivation of the proposed strategy is presented and the convergence of parameter estimators is proved. Results of this discussion imply that the strategy derived converges to that for a system with known parameters. Numerical examples were solved in order to illustrate typical inputs and outputs responses of a controlled plant. It is shown that there is the high dependence of system responses in the first control interval upon initial values assumed for the controller.
Name: ["Nahorski Zbignew"]

Title: EFFECTS OF HYPOTHESIS SHIFTING ON THE SOLVING OF INSIGHT PROBLEMS.
Abstract: Insight problems differ from others within the class of ill-defined ones in that achieving a solution is dependent on entertaining and testing one key hypothesis. It is hypothesized and shown here that attainment of this key hypothesis is in part a function of the processor's hypothesis selection activity. A model that includes the probability of selecting a new hypothesis as a parameter is tested in comparison with one that excludes such a parameter against obtained data.
Name: ["Badre Albert N."]

Title: MULTITHRESHOLD PERIODIC TERNARY THRESHOLD LOGIC.
Abstract: A new functionally complete logic is presented, the multithreshold periodic ternary threshold logic, (MPT), and its main characteristics are disclosed. Necessary and sufficient conditions are given for a 2-place function to be MPT; it is shown that there are 1593 2-place MPT functions, and a list of equivalent classes of MPT 2-place functions is provided. Extension theorems are given for n-place functions (n** greater than 2) and for MPT realizations of non MPT functions.
Name: ["Gutierrez Jorge", "Moraga Claudio"]

Title: COMPUTER SORTING OF ADR NON-ACTION INFORMATION.
Abstract: Methods used for computer sorting of ‚Ä≥non-action‚Ä≥ messages generated by Automatic Disturbance Recording Equipment (ADR) are described. Non-action messages are a written record, in telegraph code, of the condition of selected key relays in a common control marker when it force releases because of failure to switch a call satisfactorily. Problems encountered with manual sorting and early computer programs for sorting ADR messages are discussed. A field trial of the standard method of message sorting using an on-line minicomputer is reported.
Name: ["Cotterell I.R.", "Doherty R."]

Title: ON-LINE REPRESENTATION OF THREE VARIABLE DATA.
Abstract: The lack of user-oriented, packed displays is a major obstacle in applying modern computer technology to patient monitoring. A new method of display is described which uses an available output device, a thermal strip chart recorder, to produce a voiceprint-like pattern of 2 variables versus time. It is small, inexpensive, and can easily fit inside a plug-in module along with signal processing circuitry. It can reduce channel and paper use while preserving input data. Examples of this device used with an EEG spectral processor are presented as well as ideas as to possible future uses of such a display method.
Name: ["Fleming Robert A.", "Smith N.Ty"]

Title: Decision theory and artificial intelligence: I. A semantics-based region analyzer
Abstract: Mathematical decision theory can be combined with heuristic techniques to attack Artificial Intelligence problems. As a first example, the problem of breaking an image into meaningful regions is considered. Bayesian decision theory is seen to provide a mechanism for including problem dependent (semantic) information in a general system. Some results are presented which make the computation feasible. A programming system based on these ideas and its application to road scenes is described. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Feldman J.A.", "Yakimovsky Y."]

Title: Progress in diagnosing electrocardiograms
Abstract: Measurements which are used in an automated vector cardiogram processing system to classify the repolarization of the ventricle are described. Results of a classification program in which these measurements are used for independent patient material are presented.
Name: ["Talmon J.L.", "Van Herpen G."]

Title: STARAN PARALLEL PROCESSOR SYSTEM SOFTWARE.
Source: AFIPS Natl Comput Conf Expo Conf Proc
Abstract: A brief description has been given of software packages that compose the system for the operational STARAN parallel associative array processor. Also described is the additional software that makes STARAN operational when integrated with HIS-645 or XDS SIGMA 5 sequential computers. The goal of all the software is to provide tools to use STARAN in the stand-alone and integrated modes. Many modules have been discussed.
Name: ["Davis Edward W."]

Title: CALCULATION OF THE TRAFFIC CAPACITY OF A PRIVATE DATA NETWORK.
Abstract: A private data network is analyzed, and a model is derived for the programming system of the processing unit. A stochastic model which accounts for the random nature of message generation is set up. In the calculation model the network is viewed as a queueing system consisting of a number of devices. By means of approximate analytical methods and simulations, the response time and CPU utilization can be calculated. Comparisons between the analytical and simulation results, concerning the polling waiting time, show good agreement for the cases with low traffic. The simulations yield a higher response time than the analytical solution.
Name: ["Fakhr El Din Mohamed E.", "Peiram Lars"]

Title: SOME ASPECTS OF VECTOR OPTIMIZATION.
Abstract: Aspects of system optimization with respect to several criteria are considered. Algorithms are proposed which reduce the solution to a process of solving a sequence of programming problems for a specified (by experts, in this case) preference ranking of vector-criterion values and specified weighting coefficients of the criteria as functions of the values they attain.
Name: ["Gurin L.S."]

Title: DECENTRALIZED FILTER FOR INTERACTING DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS.
Abstract: A decentralized filter is derived for interacting dynamical systems. Its performance and relation to the standard Kalman filter are discussed. Some extensions of this filter are indicated.
Name: ["Sanders Jr. Charles W.", "Tacker Edgar C.", "Linton Thomas D."]

Title: EXACT AND APPROXIMATE, LINEAR AND NONLINEAR FIXED-INTERVAL, FIXED-POINT AND FIXED-LAG SMOOTHING WITH MEASUREMENTS INVOLVING CORRELATED NOISE.
Abstract: Fixed-interval, fixed-point, and fixed-lag nonlinear as well as linear smoothing algorithms with measurements involving correlated noise are developed. The smoothing algorithms for linear system are exact. The linear fixed-interval smoothing algorithm with measurements containing correlated noise agrees with existing algorithms. The smoothing algorithms for nonlinear system are approximate.
Name: ["Liang D.F.", "Christensen G.S."]

Title: VARIABLE-VALUED LOGIC: SYSTEM VL<sub>1</sub>.
Abstract: The paper defines the concept of a variable-valued logic (VL) system and discusses in detail one specific system called VL//1. The main motivation for the development of the VL system concept is to construct a well-defined, general formal system unifying various combinatorial problems and adequate, in particular, for problems of 'learning from examples' (problems which are of special interest to areas of pattern recognition and machine intelligence).
Name: ["Michalski R.S."]

Title: Quantification of abnormal EEG spike characteristics
Abstract: A digital computer technique is presented whereby abnormal scalp EEG transients are magnified and processed so that detailed characteristics of their morphology can be precisely quantified. A set of six parameters describing these characteristics is proposed, and data from a quantitative analysis of abnormal spikes chosen from three human epileptics are presented. Finally, the advantages of the presented method are discussed. ¬© 1974.
Name: ["Ktonas P.Y.", "Smith J.R."]

Title: ONE ADAPTIVE APPROACH TO THE SYNTHESIS OF SYSTEMS FOR AUTOMATIC DIAGNOSTIC CLASSIFICATION OF ELECTRONIC CIRCUITS USING THE CONSTANT-VOLTAGE MODE.
Abstract: A system is proposed for automatic diagnostic classification of continuous-action electronic circuits with a finite number of diagnosed states. A potential function is used as the closeness criterion, while the potentials measured at a finite number of test points are used as the information criteria. The basic stages in an algorithm for machine realization of the approach are considered.
Name: ["Marinov Yu.P.", "Khristova B.K."]

Title: Resolving time of scintillation camera computer system and methods of correction for counting loss. I. Measurement of resolving times of a delay line type camera and an on line computer system (Japanese)
Abstract: In quantitative dynamic studies, a scintillation camera is widely used with an on line computer system or a data processor of fixed program. However, dynamic data are often inaccurate due to a considerable resolving time inherent in the camera and in the data processing system. Separate determinations were made of the resolving times of a delay line type scintillation camera and an on line computer system (TOSBAC 3400 Model 31 DAC system). The counting rate characteristics of the camera were measured against varying intensities of a radioactive source, and fitted by exponential function by which a resolving time of 5.5Œºsec was determined. The data acquisition rate of the computer system was investigated in terms of display counting rate of the camera. The equation of constant dead time was well fitted to the experimental acquisition rate which gave a system resolving time of 10 Œºsec. In dynamic image data, the speed of data transfer from core memory to magnetic disk was the limiting factor for the highest rate and for the smallest time of each frame. Finally, possibilities are suggested for improving the high counting rate performance of the camera computer system.
Name: ["Fukuhisa K.", "Iinuma T.", "Matsumoto T."]

Title: ON METHODS OF OPTIMUM INPUT SIGNAL SYNTHESIS.
Abstract: In this paper it is investigated how to generate optimal input signal series for the identification of linear discrete-time system in order to improve the accuracy of the estimate. The determinant of the covariance matrix or the inverse of information matrix is considered as a measure of the error in the parameter estimate. Very simple methods are suggested for the minimization of these criteria in case of amplitude constrained input signal.
Name: ["Keviczky L."]

Title: Suboptimal Control in the Presence of Disturbances - 2. Tracking Problems for Linear Time-Invariant Stable System with Fixed Terminal Time. | STEROWANIE PRAWIE OPTYMALNE W OBECNOSCI ZAKLOCEN - 2. ZAGADNIENIA NADAZANIA DLA LINIOWEGO STACJONARNEGO I STABILNEGO UKLADU PRZY HORYZONCIE SKONCZONYM.
Abstract: For the first part, see Engineering Index, Jan 1975 Monthly, p 97, Abstract No. 001259. In this second part concerned with optimal and suboptimal tracking problems, a certain quite general form of a functional involving costs of tracking errors as well as control costs is assumed as a performance index. It is shown that for the class of systems considered there exists a uniquely defined optimal control.
Name: ["Gessing Ryszard", "Latarnik Michal"]

Title: LARGE-SCALE LINEAR PROGRAMMES WITH HIDDEN CYCLIC STRUCTURE.
Abstract: This paper examines how a class of large-scale linear programming problems can be transformed into equivalent problems which have a decomposition structure. The constraint matrices have a cyclic structure which cannot be detected immediately. An algorithm for detecting such structures and a procedure for constructing the new programs are presented. The same technique can be applied for decomposition of networks, to detect cyclic structures of input-output matrices, and to detect periodicity of irreducible Markovian chains. An example is presented.
Name: ["Brucker Peter"]

Title: Graph Representation and Diagnosis for Multiunit Faults
Abstract: A method using graph theory is proposed for the detection and the location of a multiunit fault in a system. The method requires only a slight increase in the number of internal monitoring terminals over the number required for the 1-unit fault diagnosis. A graph representation of a system initially leads to a rectangular diagnostic matrix. An algorithm is developed for constructing a square reachability matrix from the diagnostic matrix. A graph derived from the reachability matrix permits diagnosis of multiunit faults. Copyright ¬© 1975 by The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Nakano H.", "Nakanishi Y."]

Title: FILTERING FOR COUNTING PROCESSES, A MARTINGALE APPROACH.
Abstract: The filtering problem for counting process observations is considered. The method used is the theory of martingales and stochastic integrals. Two equations are defined in terms of martingales, forming the stochastic system. The observation equation associates the counting process with a rate process. The second equation expresses in general terms the evolution of the rate process. The representation of these equations is derived with respect to the family of sigma -fields generated by the observations. The filtering, prediction and smoothing problem are considered using the least squares error criterion. Stochastic differential equations for the optimal estimates are derived. The results are discussed and a simple example is given.
Name: ["Van Schuppen J.H."]

Title: Elimination of M Hazard in Realizations of Partially Defined Boolean Functions. | ELIMINACJA M - RYZYKA W REALIZACJACH FUNKCJI BOOLOWSKICH CZESCIOWO OKRESLONYCH.
Abstract: A pertinent algorithm is formulated. A method is presented for generating a set of prime implicants, which are essential for the realization of partially defined functions in the form of the sum of products free from logic hazards.
Name: ["Sapiecha Krzysztof"]

Title: Analog to digital conversion of information: a structural model of the basic functional unit of the central nervous system
Abstract: This paper presents a model for information representation and transmission in the time and frequency domains in a central nervous system structure. The basic functional unit of the central nervous system is assumed to be a population of substructures whose logical operation in time and frequency domains is analog with digital readout. This model allows information, (the smallest unit defined by Œîf x Œît = 1/2 and f(o) x t(o) = 1/2 (Barrett), to be transmitted linearly in either a modified or unmodified form through a substructure which functions as a information storage and detection device independent of absolute energy amounts in the physical stimulus. Whittaker's interpolation theory provides the basis for a description of the unit's functioning, a representation which is also basic to information theory. The model presented is applied most readily to the auditory pathway, but could also be applied to any sensory pathway of the central nervous system, excluding the visual pathway which is uniquely designed for contrast registration.
Name: ["Barrett T.W."]

Title: Linear Time-Dependent Systems
Abstract: In studies of linear open-loop systems, the assumption of time invariance is often tacitly made. In this paper we show how a time dependent system can arise quite naturally. The estimation of time dependent transfer function, on the basis of a single realization, when the input/output processes are nonstationary is considered. We also consider the problem of testing a given open-loop system for time dependence. The tests described here make use of the concept of the ‚Äúevolutionary cross spectra,‚Äù and rests essentially on testing the ‚Äúuniformity‚Äù of a set of vectors, whose components consist of the ‚Äúevolutionary gain spectra‚Äù and ‚Äúevolutionary phase spectra.‚Äù Using a logarithmic transformation on the evolutionary gain spectra, we show that the mechanics of the tests are formally equivalent to a two-factor multivariate analysis of variance (MAN-OVA) procedure. Numerical illustrations, from the real and simulated data, of the proposed tests are included. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.
Name: ["Rao T.S.", "Tong H."]

Title: Stochastic Theory of Minimal Realization
Abstract: In this paper it is shown that a natural representation of a state space is given by the predictor space, the linear space spanned by the predictors when the system is driven by a Gaussian white noise input with unit covariance matrix. A minimal realization corresponds to a selection of a basis of this predictor space. Based on this interpretation, a unifying view of hitherto proposed algorithmically defined minimal realizations is developed. A natural minimal partial realization is also obtained with the aid of this interpretation. ¬© 1974, IEEE. All rights reserved.

Title: EFFECTIVE ALGORITHM FOR DRAWING OF PLANAR NETWORKS.
Abstract: An algorithm is presented which is applicable to arbitrary graphs. It tests planarity, and gives the actual disposition of the graph on the plane as the final result.
Name: ["Kljuic B.", "Salcic Z."]

Title: Statistical Diagnosis and Synthesis of Reliability and Maintainability Data About Electro-Mechanical Equipment. | DIAGNOSTIC STATISTIQUE ET SYNTHESE DES INFORMATIONS RELATIVES A LA FIABILITE ET A LA MAINTENANCE D'UN MATERIEL ELECTROMECANIQUE.
Abstract: Two applications of pattern recognition theory are described for maintenance control and automated diagnosis. Correspondence analysis, considered as a feature extraction method, is used in order to analyze data sets originating in equipment monitoring; it is thereby possible to display causality relations between those parameters which influence the operational behavior of the system. Automated statistical diagnosis has been achieved in quasi-real time, thanks to a generalization of the nearest neighbor rule. Its application to automated quality control of electro-mechanical parts has produced 92% correct classification rate for acceptable items. The paper discusses the applicability of these methods to accelerated prototype testing.
Name: ["Pau Louis Francois"]

Title: Sequential Retrieval. | WYSZUKIWANIE SEKWENZYJNE.
Abstract: With reference to the Bellman's problem concerned with optimization of seraching n boxes for a ball, a general model of the sequential retrieval has been considered. Basic properties of the optimal strategy have been given. For some particular cases, a local optimization criterion has been formulated which makes it possible to determine the optimal strategy quite easily.
Name: ["Subieta Kazimierz"]

Title: Minimum Variance Control for Linear, Discrete Time Systems - 2. | LINEARIS DISZKRET IDEJU RENDSZEREK MINIMALIS SZORASU IRANYITASA - 2.
Abstract: The generalized least squares method of Clarke is used for the adaptive estimation of optimal control parameters to solve the minimum variance control problem for systems with unknown and constant parameters.
Name: ["Hetthessy Jeno", "Keviczky Laszlo"]

Title: HIERARCHICAL CONCEPT FOR MAN-MACHINE COMMUNICATION.
Abstract: The Cerebellar Model Articulation Controller (CMAC) is a computer based control system in which high-level task-oriented commands can be broken down into a series of elemental motor actuator signals. CMAC is a general purpose adaptive control concept which can be arranged in a hierarchical structure, so as to facilitate the man-machine communication problem. For example, CMAC can solve the coordinate transformation problem so that commands can be given in terms of desired end point trajectories. Furthermore, CMAC can handle many feedback variables such as measurements of misalignment of parts, variable mass loading, irregularities in materials, and constraints imposed by an external environment.
Name: ["Albus J.S.", "Evans J.M.", "Johnsen E.G."]

Title: Mathematical Model of a Retrieval Process. | MODEL MATEMATYCZNY PROCESU WYSZUKIWANIA.
Abstract: Concepts of the formalized analysis of a retrieval process are presented. The state of a retrieval process is identified as information about an object. An analysis of the expected cost of a retrieval with given strategy is performed. It is shown that the optimization criterion, i. e. , minimization of the expected cost of a retrieval, satisfies the Bellman optimality principle.
Name: ["Subieta Kazimierz"]

Title: Identification Processes for Dynamic Systems with Separated, Static Nonlinearity. | [IDENTIFIKATIONSVERFAHREN FUER DYNAMISCHE SYSTEME MIT SEPARIERTER STATISCHER NICHTLINEARITAET.]
Abstract: Two identification techniques are presented for a special class of nonlinear systems. the theoretical and practical investigations of their algorithms show that the first technique leads to useful results only upon application of a broadband test signal with wide control limits and Gaussian distribution. Positive results can be expected with the second technique if an optimal strategy of the search process can be met.
Name: ["Badelt W."]

Title: EXPERIMENTAL COMPARISON OF RANDOM-SEARCH ALGORITHMS.
Abstract: Results of computational experiments are reported for an investigation into the effectiveness of certain local random-search algorithms used to solve arbitrary extremal problems. Several types of search algorithms are considered: with ‚Ä≥randomness penalty,‚Ä≥ in subspaces, with self-training based on the best trial, with self-training (modified). Statistical estimates are obtained for several indices characterizing the effectiveness of the algorithms.
Name: ["Lazarev I.B.", "Valuiskikh V.P."]

Title: ESTIMATING MARKOV TRANSITION PROBABILITIES FROM MICRO-UNIT DATA.
Abstract: The standard method of deriving maximum-likelihood estimates for transition probability matrices is outlined. Statistical tests for determining the Markov property, the specific order of a chain and the homogeneity of a set of matrices are applied to data relating to manufacturing establishments. Refinements to the maximum-likelihood procedure are examined in the context of fractional disaggregation of long-period matrices and in the framework of fitting smoothing surfaces to observed transition probabilities.
Name: ["Collins Lyndhurst"]

Title: A Threshold Selection Technique
Abstract: Threshold selection for picture segmentation is relatively easy when the frequency distribution of gray levels in the picture is strongly bimodal, with the two peaks comparable in size and separated by a deep valley. This report describes a method of handling cases in which the peaks are very unequal in size and the valley is broad. A Laplacian operation is applied to the picture to determine pointsthat lie on or near the edges of objects. Threshold selection becomes easier when the frequency distribution of gray levels of these points is used. Copyright ¬© 1974 by The Insttute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc.
Name: ["Weszka J.S.", "Nagel R.N.", "Rosenfeld A."]

Title: Some Properties of Methods of Conjugate Gradients and Variable Operators Applied to the Minimization of Functionals in a Real Hilbert Space. | [NIEKTORE WLASNOSCI METOD GRADIENTOW SPRZEZONYCH I ZMIENNYCH OPERATOROW W ZASTOSOWANIU DO MINIMALIZACJI FUNKCJONALOW W RZECZYWISTEJ PRZESTRZENI HILBERTA.]
Abstract: A theoretical analysis is presented for the problem of the convergence of conjugate gradient and variable operator algorithms in a real Hilbert space. For a dynamic optimization problem, consisting of the minimization of the performance index for differential state equations, the general form of a computing algorithm is given. Results of applying the derived algorithms to particular dynamic optimization problems are presented.
Name: ["Winnicki Andrzej"]

Title: DIAGNOSIS BY LOGISTIC DISCRIMINANT FUNCTION: FURTHER PRACTICAL PROBLEMS AND RESULTS.
Abstract: Further results on logistic discrimination are given. When zeros occur in the one-way margins of discrete observations a problem arises. This is discussed, a solution is suggested and an application of the approach is given in a medical setting.
Name: ["Anderson J.A."]

Title: SUBCLASSES AND CLASSES OF BOOLEAN FUNCTIONS.
Abstract: The concept of a subclass of functions is introduced. It permits a sharp reduction in the process of examination associated with the determination of all classes of Boolean functions. A method for determining these classes is given.
Name: ["Yakubaitis E.A."]
